name: WE ARE FOOTBALL 2024
detailed_description: Welcome to WE ARE FOOTBALL 2024 – the NEW football management experience from the creators of the legendary On the Ball and EA SPORTS FIFA Manager Series! Dive into the world of football like never before. Choose an existing club or start your own. Manage either men or women, lead your club to new heights, and become the next manager legend! Be there with your team on the pitch. In our immersive 3D game engine, you can directly influence the action on the pitch through instructional shouts. Simulate the same game a thousand times over, witness matches 50 years into the future or switch between games in conference mode on match day. Relive highlights, analyze goals, and enjoy a comprehensive season summary. WE ARE FOOTBALL 2024 offers an extensive feature set to adapt the game to your needs, including a powerful external editor to set up league systems, clubs, players, managers, employees, referees, sponsors, fan chants, derbies, and more. Configure the game to your skill level and preferences with over 100 options and difficulty settings to make this YOUR road to glory. Now immerse yourself in the thrill of football management with WE ARE FOOTBALL 2024 ! KEY FEATURES User Interface and Technical Enhancements: Clear menu with tabs and customizable wing menus for easy navigation In-game editor for changing club and player data at any time Over 12,000 generic AI-generated pictures and aging youth players for realism 21:9 monitor support Hotseat multiplayer for up to 4 players Game Content: 3 game modes for club play: Free club selection, club creation, and career mode Develop your own managerial skills and use individual skill development trees for each player Diverse manager functions (finance, sponsors, HR, organization, fan support, and more) Organize your own tournaments and preseason tours Extensive options for play styles, formations, and other tactical instructions Modern training and realistic training schedules, including training groups Team chemistry with player relationships, hierarchies, and effects of player hobbies Simply click on players to watch their previous goals Comprehensive youth area with screening days, headhunting campaigns, youth boarding schools, and expandable international youth centers for early talent discovery Improved transfer market where your personal reputation as a negotiator counts Stadium editor that lets you expand, upgrade, and customize your home ground Expandable 3D club grounds with new buildings and many new details and improvements Optional simulation of the manager's private life, including family and children who can start a professional football career or become a department head at your club National Team Integration: Separate European Championship and World Cup modes for both men and women Option to choose a national team to manage directly at the start of the game or long-term takeover offers for national teams during gameplay Match: 3D match display with 9 cameras, slow motion, replay, live rating changes, and optional action boxes with additional information within scenes See your tactical instructions implemented on the pitch New 'Tactical Analysis' option provides information on how the result came about Short or long 3D scenes and an alternative quick calculation Intervene during the match in decision-making situations by giving commands to the players Editor: Edit any country in the world with both women’s and men's leagues Fully editable league systems with promotion/relegation regulations, cups, and playoffs Automatic creation of leagues, teams, and players Extensive editors for logos and jerseys with integration options for your own graphics Automatic conversion of existing WAF databases

_childDocuments_.review: Updated in July 20th.I have been playing football manager games since PC Fútbol / PC Calcio 3.0 and Ultimate Soccer Manager 2, we're talking 1994-1996. I dismayed when Dynamic Multimedia went bankrupt, then I discovered Total Club Manager and Championship Manager, and after that  with the same exact game released over and over again for 60 (!) bucks.Football Manager got lazy simply focusing on tactics and transfers, with no economy, no stadium building, no merchandising, no immersive interface whatsoever. Both PC Fútbol 5.0 and Ultimate Soccer Manager 2 already excelled at this back in 1996, and I guess . Their concept of improvement was adding extremely annoying, repetitive and time-consuming press conferences after every three clicks, like wtf?. You get to manage your own club in a much more comprehensive way, building your own stadium or training grounds, and enjoying a delightful view of the club's museum.  and pleasant than FM's Excel interface, and there's simply a lot more to do.  and more intuitive,  and more intuitive,  and more intuitive, and you can even prepare your own rehearsed plays - something that a tactics-only game like FM has repeatedly failed in adding, even though, again, Ultimate Soccer Manager 2 had it back in 1996.There are many areas where this game can improve. , but it has a more casual, more intuitive approach that can work wonders if well polished. Some of the areas where I think the WAF2024 can be better are:• . Players fitness is more balanced now, but it's still a headache sometimes. It multiplies stamina x energy, but I think it should simply average both. Also, having your keeper exhausted after a match makes little sense. • . There is not a single screen with your whole team performance over the season, only individual screens. • . The classic FM 1 shot 1 goal defeat, with the opponent's GK MOM, still happens way too often.• . Players sometimes admit their contract is too lucrative, but still ask for an increase in wages for an extension. Agents quit negotiations all the time. You can't offer a larger/smaller release clause, and can only accept or reject their offer. Players ask for 15M wages, you refuse, sell them, and now they earn 3.8M at their new club. More player flexibility and dialogue options would be appreciated, like 'who do you think will pay these wages?', or 'f*ck you, you f*cking brat!'.We have the grounds for an excellent 'football manager' kind of game, and it's already pretty neat and playable. , and it's very easy to tell it was made with a lot of love. You can see the way your own players improve after every match,  (FM's players are just a bunch of whiny little b*tches), and , not to milk you. Many complaints FM has never taken seriously are fixed from the start in WAF2024.I am even happier because , the same way they greatly improved We Are Football, even months before the release of their new game. I could see how they implemented a lot of fixes based on what their userbase suggested. They love football, they listen, and they are the future of football management games. Football Manager is a closed chapter for me, and I will only reopen it when (if) they ever decide to actually improve the game.If you love football management games,  My sincere thanks to Winning Streak Games and THQ Nordic for doing what noone else could for the past 20 years!

_childDocuments_.review: What to make of this game...?After about 30 hours in and watching a great LetsPlay I think I never had so much fun with such a "bad" game. I wish I could giva a neutral review but right now it is a little bit more like miss than hit. For now at least, I'm positive it will be patched some day later and I'll be thrilled to change my review once it happens. First of all: Certain parts of the game are absolutely fun and it is a very good and - in my case - stable manager as I had no crashes whatsoever. I LOVE it that women were included and I have deep respect for having options and features like climate neutrality. The game has a lot of good ideas, some are excellent, some are just bad  implemented.My main reasons for a bad review at this point are:- the game runs extremely slow when it comes to calculating the week. I have an excellent gaming PC but this kills so much fun, especially if you are only simulating 19 leagues like I do and not using any mods.- the game explains nothing and is very often clunky. For example: My striker has achieved a 1 in training, scored 3 goals, got another 1 in the game and still looses 16 points progress after the matchday. Or: My team is now on first place, scored goals, the overall happiness is high with the majority of players and we still loose ALOT of team spirit every day. I have no idea why...- Bugs: It has a lot. Most featured one is that it is shown that my team is on the attack but instead it is the other team attacking. Or I cannot organize a trainings camp, completely greyed out or I send a player to my fanclub and in the weekly suggestions and still says I have to do so and so on and so on. Or another headscratching example: I do ALL my transfers myself. 2 players are suddenly injured in one week and my team stretches a bit thin (with a full bench and only 2 non-nominated players left). Suddenly two players I never heard of are created out of thin air  (no transfer period, due to low league no second team, 31 years old and clearly no youth player) and which I have to pay from now on. Where did the guys come from???  Profile says they are in the team since 2 years (which is a blatant lie...), they are super weak and costs more than I want to pay. These, exact these things are what makes the game sooo frustrating. But it gets worse - their happiness is 0 intoxicating the whole team and instantly join the "we hate our manager"-team in the overview. Now I have to kill their contract and pay a fee. So unbelievable frustrating. - Things I can't wrap my head around: I create an own club and start (without being able to do anything) with 20 workers. My office can only maintain 10 but in the first year there is no way to make enough money for another office. So at the end of the year OSHA comes around and I have to pay so much money that I'm basically ruined. The thing is: It is NOT possible to terminate any worker contracts. It is also not possible to change positions, e.g. making my co-trainer youth-trainer. I have to terminate his contract. Also the workload is insanely buggy. My youth-trainer has a skill of 7, an effortskill of 8 and has to manage 4 - in words: four! - young players and has a workload of 187% ... - Also also: The player behaviour is insane...  Contrary to reality (just look at Darmstadt), my players in the lower leagues are mortally offended when everything in the club isn't always running smoothly and they immediately lose satisfaction, team spirit, switch to the anti-coach camp and loose points. A real team would know that playing in a higher league is an adventure that should be enjoyed (and makes money), but in the game everyone acts as if they were FC Bayern, who had just been relegated...If I talk to the players, they're offended, if they let them be, they're offended, I wish him to get well soon, that's basically a declaration of war,  I change players during the match as we are one team and the player is already tired - you guess it: I made myself a mortal enemy. Again: In the lower leagues AND at the easiest difficulty! We're not talking about the Riberys, Messis or Ronaldos of this world.  Even the youth trainers hate me for doing my job and watch my talents play... It is so frustrating in an unnecessary way...And don't get me started about broken promises and stuff. Best example: During winter break a player was bought and transfered to my team, I promised him to let him play. The next week (still in the winterbreak where are NO games!) he was instant furious as I broke my promise to let him play... and so on and so on. You get the drill.Another great example: It is a sunny day, I was minding my own clubowner-business as one of my beloved players stumbles into my office asking for more money. I said: "Lets talk."Now: HE, yes, you read that right, HE makes an offer what he wants me to pay him. The offer was ffair, I accept. HE, yes, HE storms out of my office, crying his eyes out as my offer(!)  meaning: HIS offer was too low, he feels underpayed and now his happiness is down to the bottom because HIS offer I accepted was too low for him... you can't make those stuff up...THEN another matchday, another issue. My striker is a little down and I cheer him up by saying: "You will score a goal today, my man." He does not. He is instead DEADLY furious I had the audacity of having faith in him. He wants me to apologize. Apologize to him that I ever had faith in him tthat he could score a goal. A. man. in. his. thirties. A man who earns more than all of us will ever had in their life. A man I specifically bought to strike goals is now offended and hysterically wanting me to apologize for me thinking he COULD be able to MAYBE strike a goal. I would sell him but as ALL players are like this, I entirely stopped talking to everyone.  AND THEN: A player is unhappy and wants me to change his contract. I promise him to do so. But the button is greyed out gameplaywise. So why will the player come up to me if there isn't a chance to do so??And this and way more repeats every day...- Transfers: A player is worth, let's say: 1 Million. Another club wants to buy him and offers the ridiculous amount of 2 Euro. (Yeah, this is an exaggeration but in this game it happens WAY more as you may thinkg). Instead of saying "I want what he is worth, I only can change what I want about 20 times in supersmall steps, basically NEVER be able to even reach what the player is worth. So I have to sell every player way under what he is worth and this is frustrating.- Tactics: Seem to have no influence at all. Same goes for weakpoints, settings, Ultrabonus and so on. I absolutely miss any form of feedback or help. - Training: It is almost impossible to train. I work on my weakpoints but loose way faster points in everything not trained as I can balance them out generating even more weakpoints. - 3D Visualization: Yeah, I can live with it being outdated... but seriously: I tested a female club and half of my players have the half-bald head of a boomer-team of a German alpine village club? Come on... - Fans: Every week the happiness of my fans is reduced to zero even though we keep winning, I'll visiting my fanclub every(!) week (again: lower leagues, there is basically maybe one fanclub :D) and it is sooo tedious to click on the same 5 buttons every week. And the list goes on and on and on. On first glance this game is sooo good, so fun, so cool.But if you really want to PLAY this game, it grows ever so frustrating with every minute.I love it that this manager is so much easier to learn and I see what the game could be one day. Just one more push, just some adjustements and this game will be great. Some more control options and WAY more coolness of players in the lower leagues and I'll be sold forever. :)Once this happens I will sooo gladly change this review as I wish the team so much success and all the best! Keep up the good work, I'm rooting for you so hard right now!

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the Football manager it has pro and cons.But the pro outweigh the cons by a landslide so i decided to give it a recommended.Pro :1. It is cheap. At least on my country. Must be the no.1 Pro since the cost is like 10 times cheaper than FM2024 here when the editor combined.2. This game has Editor included. And has workshop content.3. It has Stadium management. Means you can build your own stadium, your home base. They're costly, and pretty much you can't do a lot unless you're playing for very long, choosing a top dog club, or editing the starting club. The stadium and the home base aren't just cosmetics, they actually affect your management effort.4. You can simulate to have a waifu, a pet, children, and commit non graphic adultery.5. You can change the player's picture and name. Even if you want to upload anime, or car picture maybe.6. UI and music are OK, comparatively equal or better than FM2024. It is more on the pop side of choice when FM is looking more professional presentation. But in terms of text readibility, WAF is much better for my eyes.7. To be frank I'm not expert of any football manager. But i believe, WAF2024 gives me the right amount of match result i could expect, according to my managerial effort. Compared to FM2024. Like if my team is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stronger than the enemy team, and team synergy is being good, i could expect something like 5-0, even 7-0 within a match. Where at FM, i feel like the result is always toned down into normal zero. So I'd say, the game is more predictable.Yes, sometimes RNG could give me middle finger here. Like idk why happens that way, but it is not frequent.8. You can play as more than just one manager. Also, your record is being saved into the game. Let's say i'm creating Anton as a new manager. Played Anton at certain club until the contract terminated. You may consider it is the end of Anton's career. But his progress is saved into the game. Like his level, his personal earning, his wife and pets, everything. So you can start a new game using Anton, as strong as where you leave him.Cons:1. The match graphics are less to be desired. The animation quality is like night and day when compared to FM. FM2024 has more fluid and believe-able ball and human animation. Where here you can chuckle why the movement is weird. Especially during goal, there's a gap in a second before it actually tells you, hey, it was a goal. The camera angle choices also are questionable. Either too far, or highlighting unimportant part of the scene. The tackling scene are ankward, players don't change their stance when sprinting. Sometimes the ball itself teleports. Sometimes, the scene happens way too unrealistically fast. Like two goals in the same minute....If you're a person who doesn't care the match 3D presentation, you can turn it off altogether making the match a lot faster. IMHO i sometimes prefer this way. Since there're dozens of them piling within a season.By far, i think this is the most negative point of the game. That is, if you compare it to FM.There are much worse football manager games out there for this.2. There's no Indonesian team, at all. So no liga Djarum, or piala Sukarno etc. Do not expect Indonesian stadium or cities either. However, you can write it down at the editor.Tried to create Jakarta city, it gave me the picture of Borobudur temple. Okay. At least not blank :OIt isn't just Indonesia, maybe your country isn't listed in the game database as well.I listed Indonesia since i think football is quite big here. Not internationally perhaps, but one thing for sure, Indonesian have die hard supporters. Until some of them die, and it became a problem...3. The editor, has no display scaling. It made to be fix at 1080p at 100% windows text scaling.At 1440p i recommend to use 125% scaling to read the editor. If you're using 150% scaling at 1440p like i did, some of the buttons are unreadable. It always on windowed mode, but this strange window you cannot drag upwards to read the missing bottom part. It even refuses to be full screen when i used 'Loseless scaling' to force it full screen at its correct aspect ratio.*Loseless Scaling is another program you can find on Steam.The editor also patch ALL the database when you just need to adjust a little. Which could take some time to finish.Neutral :1. The workflow is different to that FM2024. You may or may not like it. Myself, I could adapt.2. There's no stats like dribble, pass, stamina like an RPG stat screen. Instead all players are determined by a single character level plus several special skills he or she have mastered. Other than that, talent, and personality.It isn't like ROBERTO PASS 70 DRIBBLE 56 KICK 80More like ROBERTO Level 8, learned long pass, corner, and tackling skill. Talented, and has a team player personality.The character level and skill could grow during training given if the character still can improve.The long pass, corner etc is like his special skill. It's not like he can't make a long pass or tackling without it. But is more proficient than a regular person.Frankly i personally consider this as a positive after playing the game for a long time. Since it is far easier to see each player qualities in a glance rather than reading a bulk of statistics. But it can be a learning curve? To some people. It took me some time to adapt.3. Small part of the game is comical in nature. They're good and still leaving most of the content is coherent, more like trying to make a stress relief for you. But depends on who are you, may says differently.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to others. Its worth the money.  But heres the Pros and Cons PROS - Quicker then Football Manager- More to do with other aspects of the football club then Football Manager which appeals to a lot of players- Fun aspects of the game like sprinkers and streakers and random bits which are just funny and it doesn't take itself that seriously - You can run all leagues and your machine will still run better then 30-40 leagues of FM2024 (I'm a massive fan of FM24)- Youth camps, Seeing 12-13 years olds com into your under 17 side. - The developers are reading/listening to comments... good to see- I like the fact you can view all goals within the game and it loads up straight away. - The amount of data/Stats is excellent. 2 points per game table is not required but i'm glad its in there as is a cool feature. CONS- Editor isn't great. I want to add Cups to nations, The Editor doesn't allow you to do this- Training issues with stamina (Perhaps just me, But its seems to be a bit buggy) - Too much randomising in teams winning things. Fenerbache aren't going to win the CL in the 2nd season of the game- No World Club Cup.- German Leagues options need to be cut (Sometimes we don't want to run them all) - German Lower League have no state cups- DFB Pokal & FA Cup formats are wrong, (No bundesliga teams should draw each other in the 1st round, FA Cup starts from last 64 excluding a lot of lower league sides which doesn't add to the experence) - Better graphics are needed. Away fans don't celebrate when their team scores a penalty All in all this is a developing game, The developers have their heads screwed on and its worth spending money on for a fun quick game where you can rise through the divisions. 7.5/10 Good work

_childDocuments_.review: Right, so I've played the first WAF game as well but only ever with the Zocker patches applied (for official team and player names). I don't know if this is a Zocker patch issue or a game mechanics issue, but the following problem is still occurring on WAF 2024 as it did on WAF:1) Player fee negotiations are so incredibly basic and awful. When a player isn't transfer listed, the internal / 'hidden' price that will be accepted for a player will always be 200% of their market value (clubs will ask for more than 2x the price but you can always negotiate it down to 200%, but never below it). Or when they are transfer listed, you can negotiate price down to half the market value which'll always be accepted (but again, never a penny below half price). The only 'variation spice' you get in terms of lower than half price fees only occur on transfer deadline day, and that's it.2) Certain main positions will very rarely, if ever, be listed on the transfer market by *any clubs* regardless of any filters being activated or not, namely Goalkeepers and Strikers / Defensive forwards (though for some reason no one has DF as a main position to begin with, lol). It's always a CM and CD galore transfer market.3) Release clauses activating way later on in time after the contract has been signed (and the way that loans function on WAF). First and foremost, does this even happen in real life? Because as far as I knew (and also how it works on FM), a release clause is active the moment the contract is signed. But I guess it ties in with another annoying 'game rule' which is that when a player comes back from loan, you cannot loan them out again for an entire season. Players have a veto in this game, which allows them to flat out block you offering them for sale "because they came here to prove themselves", and they will even say this for an entire season long once returning from loan. The way this functions was probably done with the purpose of preventing the player from making profit on signings (window flipping) in a way that is not training a player's stats (and their value) up before selling them and to give the marketing part of the game more weight for the player to bother with for financial profits.Anyway, if the devs are going to stick with these delayed release clause activations then it should 1) be written as "activates on 1 January 2027" instead of "From: 01/01/2027 and when a release clause is not active yet, the text of this should be colored in red (and in green when it is active).4) Player dissatisfaction with pay the moment their stats improve. Boy this is so dang annoying; what even is the purpose of signing a contract from say 2026 to 2030 when players already start to 'demand' more money in 2026, not even a few months in to their new contract at a club, just because their stats went up shortly after you signed them? Imagine a scenario like that in real life, it would make being a football manager even more unbearable than it already is with all the spoiled brat diva behavior nowadays. Guess what, beneficial things should happen to clubs as well and that means the devs should move up player dissatisfaction behavior about their salary half-way into their contract at minimum, even if their stats went up way before that time.5) Contract discrepancies, causing players to always charge you more than when signing on for any other club and always demanding more money per week on new contracts compared to their current/former contract, despite any factors that should normally cause players to take a pay cut on a new contract e.g. they're in their 30s, are no longer in their prime, hampered development due to bad performance or long term injury etc. Even when you try to sign a player on a free transfer, they will demand an insane signing on fee (way higher than what they'd ask if you paid a club a transfer fee), which pretty much null and voids any financially beneficial point of signing players for free. This is how much of a mess player contracts are in this game. Example: I had Musiala charge me a 68m signing on fee lol.And there are more issues that I can't be bothered to type out, but this altogether negatively affects the experience for me. The thing is that these above issues were *exactly* the same in the previous WAF game, so unless either the base game aka the devs fixes this properly (or the Zocker.de patch creators if this is caused by them) then I won't be buying this game again and can't recommend it to anyone who is looking for an experience which isn't *this* immersion killing and basic, especially when it comes to the transfer dealings / contract handling parts.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. In my opinion that explains the very positive feedback here rather than the game being a very good game.I come from thousands upon thousands of hours of football manager over the past 25 years. I also played games like Ultimate Soccer Manager years ago and some of the others as well. There is a feeling of jadedness towards FM a lot of people are experiencing, the game has failed to develop really in the 6 -8  years and a lot of the mechanics and game play is becoming predictable, for me anyway. There is definitely a place for a competitor to FM but this just doesn't seem to be it.There is doubt and confusion at every turn in WAF24. The game starts in a way that makes you question the games professionalism from minute 1. You load up and the title screen has very loud obnoxious menu music that is essentially 4 bars on repeat. Though there is a sound on/off toggle at the top, you instinctively look for a settings menu and soon find there isn't one. This just isn't right and sets the tone in my opinion.The game seems to cover a lot of ground in terms of nations, leagues, teams etc. but its not like FM where the leagues will have their own rules specific to them etc. I imagine these are just labels in the same spreadsheet split into country and leagues, the players are all auto generated unless you use a easily accessible database mod which adds players and faces to the game. There is no issue at all with this, if the game is sound.Career mode tries to recreate the FM method of selecting your background experience by asking you weird multiple choice questions rather than letting you pick your background, its not game breaking, but it needs explanation to be honest, whatever you choose your going to be offered a crap lower league team in a random country.This is all the by the by, what matters here is the gameplay, mechanics and the flow of the game and to me it just is not intuitive.This game needs some sort of tutorial in my opinion. You can simply click along and action backroom staff suggestions, even buy players etc. but you dont really understand why or what you are doing or the effects it has a lot of the time. It seemed that players possibly have some sort of RPG levelling system where there training increases there XP each week and they progress towards unlocking traits maybe? It isnt clear. There are action points, you get 4 at the start and it seems you can use them in negotiations, but there is no way of knowing how you acquire more and if you can use them freely or if you should save them. You dont know other places they may be usable.Tactics are a complete mystery. There are several option or sliders, but they make little to no sense to me.  Options like 'I need tough guys today', or 'dont foul in the box' etc. There are 10 of these in one sub area that would look like where you would put the main tactical ethos, however in reality it seems to be just what FM would have as 3 options for tackling intensity essentially.Another example is pressing. You can press in about 10 different way, 'frequently', 'targeted', 'varied' etc. but there is no real explanation on what these means, for example when do they press when targeted? Is it automatic? Outside of these sliders there is very little else to do or control tactics from what I could see.This leads into the match engine which is basically old school text with 3D highlights. It is not like FM where you can watch the whole game and see the team attempt (in theory) to play your strategy. You just need to have faith here that the mechanics are sound as you have no way of seeing them in action even partially.I am not going to go too much into this because I didn't play much, I refunded after 2 hours, so will leave it here on tactics and engine.The worst thing for me is the UI. It is absolutely abysmal. I mean shocking. There is no obviously accessible menu available at all times. Sometimes your only option is to continue. Want to save or quit? Unlucky. Want to change settings? Gotta wait for the option to appear. There does seem to be a home hub where this all is, but just is not always available. I think they could offset this in a big way with a tutorial where the game flow is explained and therefore you can understand where you are and exactly when the home hub area will come available. It seems to also have a weird tactical RPG action point system on things you can do. You have 44 hours available in your working week. and most options take up some of this time. Some of your time is automatically assigned so essentially you can schedule about 4-8 actions per week depending on what they are.  Want to offer a player a contract? Thats 2 hours, on Tuesday. Want to research a transfer market (scouting I assume?), That'll be 2 hours on Sunday. Want to look for a new kit sponsor... you guessed it.In principal, there is nothing wrong with this, in FM you can essentially do this stuff completely unrestricted and is that truly realistic? Could I feasibly offer 30 players a contract in one day as well as set up scouting assignments for every position in my team, have a board meeting and then a team meeting  all in one hour window. No its equally unrealistic. But it doesn't feel like it matters really.Again there is nothing wrong with what they are doing, it just needs explanation and understanding of consequence.I will say, there is a essentially a manual somewhere that has walls of text on most things. I actually was not able to intuitively find it and never saw it in my play through, I only saw it whilst watching someone else review, which is mad. There should be help question marks at the very least linking you to this all over this game in lieu of any tutorial. Should be flashing in front of you at least when starting out.I could go on, but in 2 hours I am not going to go too far as I don't feel further qualified. The crux here is simple. A game like this is a massive time sink, its something you want to spend a lot of time and invest in. However there needs to be faith that it will be worth your time and rewarding and WAF24 just fails to provide the user with this largely due to a lack of clarity and what I see as some fairly poor basic design choices. I wanted to play this and it be good because I had become somewhat jaded with FM and was even prepared to accept a lower quality more simple game, however in the end, all WAF24 did was create an itch only FM currently can scratch and I spent last night reinstalling all the graphics packs, mods and back playing it now, instantly drawn in and invested.There absolutely is a place for an arcadey alternative to FM that has the extra bells and whistles FM does not have, even with a slightly simplified match engine and tactical system, but WAF24 fails to let the user know what it exactly is and how to get the most out of it and in my opinion is not able to fill this void on these grounds.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent football manager game. If you like manager games, and think the FM series is too cumbersome, this is a game well worth checking out. It plays much faster and you don't need to go through a million spreadsheets just to advance ingame time.The official database and portrait packs in the Workshop are easy to install and make the game so much better. You also have a player editor ingame, so if you have a generic named youth player, you can edit him/her to your heart's content. The AI generated picture, which ages accordingly, is one of the best features in games ever imho. You also have an option to play with family mode, which means you can add your own spouse and children, which you have to spend time with during your campaign. This is optional but also nice feature.Another great feature is being able to expand your stadium and club grounds. You can then fly over it and see your accomplishments. You can also take a tour through your club's museum, if you have built one. All additions to your stadium are also seen in the ingame match engine and look great. You have complete control over sponsors, the aforementioned stadium improvements, training camp locations and more. Although if you don't want to do it yourself, you can also delegate it to one of your assistents. You are free to select formations, and even drag and drop players to certain field locations should you want to customise the standard formations. You can also hire department heads and even offer players to other clubs.Players have star ratings and also prospect ratings so that you can see if a player is exceptionally gifted. Pre-match tactics can be issued before any match and you can also do halftime talks and give players bonuses and incentives to play better in crucial matches. The match highlights look simple, don't expect FIFA24 graphics, but have a great charm and work well. The game plays better than the FM series imho and you should really give it a shot. There is much more to tell but you just have to experience it, I, for one, am loving every minute of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Football Manager for sports - WAF 2024 for fun! I've heard this summary in a twitch stream and it is so true. Where FM is more of a deep simulation of all aspects that are influencing a single football match, WAF 2024 is more like a RPG: You are developing your club and your players over a very long span of time, unlocking new options and tools along the way. You are extending your roster, your stadium, your fan base, your club grounds. If you want to, you can even create your own club, starting from the lowest league (men or women) – if you invest some time into your private life, you can see your family grow and your offsprings becoming players in your own team. On this scale, a single win or loss does not count that much, the whole game is more about creating a solid base for sustainable long-term success.To me, it is like playing Crusaders Kings compared to Total War. Sure, each individual match (battle ^^) is not as detailed as it is in FM / Total War. Instead of taking ages for simulating every minutiae, WAF and Crusader Kings are focussing on the very basics: Is my grand strategy setup sustainable enough to win in the long run? Compared to it's predecessor, WAF 2024 goes quite some mile to make sure match day still represents your decisions and lives up to your expectations. There is a new (outdated but serviceable and fast) 3D engine that shows highlight scenes from the match, like goals, shots, offside, … Given that you can easily speed through a season within a single evening, there is some degree of repetition here, but the scenes represent your tactics and your player skills faithfully in an abstract way. Unless you’re working in football on an professional level, you will see most tactical options available to you that you would bring up in a typical pub discussion. Be careful: While it’s skill setup is more basic than FM (with players having RPG like skills for shooting, tackles, headers, etc. in a range from -- to  ++), there are for more psychological ‚traits‘ to keep in mind when setting up your dream team. For instance, if you have hired a team of players with high extraversion and confidence, you might have a lot of great team leaders, but team hierarchy will suffer. Players with low confidence are better team players, but they suffer penalties when struggling to keep the league. Players with high openness learn new positions faster, but they are also more inclined to leave you early.But wait, there’s more: There are not only five psychological traits, but you need to judge proneness for injuries, how rough your player goes into tackles, the amount of swag he is bringing in for your jersey sales and social media and much more. I’ve played a lot of football managment games over the years, but this game has by far the most interesting decisions to take into account when signing a new player. While it’s match day presentation is far away from any recent AAA release, there are lots of little touches that show real love fort the beatiful game: Fans are waving banners, there are authentic chants for most bigger European clubs, players are celebrating when scoring last minute and from time to time your coach even gets the chance to yell into a scene, deciding ist outcome. The upside of the dated graphics: WAF 2024 is super fast, you can go into EVERY match on the whole planet and watch all goals of a season in hindsight. Results are usually plausible, with the occasional outlier – like in the real world. Even after multiple dozens of seasons team setups stay reasonable and leagues resemble the current balance of power in football.It is also a funny game from time to time. There are winks and nods to the more crazy aspects of football, like one of your player secretly advertising himself in social media debates, or a mole giving away all your secrets to the press. I’ve spent three digits hours with this game and I still see surpries and little secrets – some of them unlock only after quite some time of playing. Just to give you an idea: There is a 200 pages ingame guide (currently German-only, but translations are shared in Discord and the developers are working on a translation.)Two things you should keep in mind: First, there are no offical licenses, but you can go to Steam Workshop and you willl find a great solution with a single click. Second, there is a crazy amount of additional customization available in the gamis. Not only you can finetune difficulty to your liking (even disabling any layoffs), but you can customize many aspects of your stadium for free, change player and club names on the fly, add your pets and wife to your game and much more. To me it is a real pinnacle of what I like in football management game and I recommend it wholeheartedly to everyone who wants to try a fresh take after years and years of FM domination. (And as an additional plus: You’re supporting a small eleven people indie team that is actively listening to its community. Devs are very active here and on Discord, an update is already in the making and there is a good chance that you will get an immediate dev response when asking any question).To summarize: Grand-strategy football mangement / RPG hybrid - 10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: This game desperately needs a tutorial, one that isn't in the PDF format. It tries to do many things differently than conventional football managers, which is great... if it provides the necessary tools to teach players HOW it actually works. For example, contract negotiations. It seems to have moved to a "live negotiation" instead of the standard weeks of offer/counter-offer that most football managers uses. I clicked on "longer term" and it immediately gave me an X. However, the "reduce term" button is greyed out. Why? There is no indication whether the player just refuses to extend the contract or I need to "balance" it with more money. After a few clicks, I try to revert to the last contract to start again then the player immediately ended the negotiation.That is just one example, the game is filled with mechanics that are unexplained or hidden in layers or unrelated UI. Buying share and selling share are on completely different area of the UI, training goal isn't really grouped together and you have to open each player one at a time, move to the goal tab, then select goal, etc. etc.It's just a mess of a cool concept. It feels a bit like they kept adding idea without really organizing it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's lovely to have a football management game that goes beyond what's happening on the pitch and with the playing squad, and explores the broader club management aspect too.Those club management elements are reasonably well done. Massive infrastructure changes are expensive and take time (with a configuration option to make them immediate) as you'd expect, and there are always tweaks you'd want to do.Unfortunately the on pitch simulation is too lightweight. Team tactics are formation based with some basic probability/percentage sliders for 'whole team' tactics; there's no way of giving individual player instructions, or implementing anything remotely sophisticated that resembles current leading manager tactics.That also constrains the ability to influence team success. A good manager will win with a mediocre team - but not in this game. Player ability matters far more, and that's all down to the squad.Training is another challenge area. The training configuration and level of control is excellent, with the ability to give the whole team a training focus each week, and also work on individual players' skills and positions. Unfortunately training is exceedingly short term, where a team's competence in (e.g.) the offside trap will literally halve in a matter of weeks because they were training on set pieces, attacking, tackling, etc. This makes it a whac-a-mole attempt to avoid anything getting too bad, rather than supporting a serious team strategy.On top of that are multiple bugs, and sadly the game's discord channel took all of the reports in its bug channel and deleted the lot with no comment. That doesn't encourage community engagement, or give any confidence that any of those bugs will be fixed.So there are good things about this game and it does differentiate itself from competitors through that wider set of responsibilities for the player (to the extent they choose - in game assistants can pick up most/all tasks) but overall it feels short of a full experience, and sadly just not good enough on the bit that matters: Football management.

_childDocuments_.review: "Believe" - Ted Lasso.This game has satisfying depth as far as a simulation is concerned. If you were to buy this game, expect a lot of fun trying to flex your manager muscle while learning about the nuances of football and dealing with player, boardroom dramas. While it doesn't totally ignore gamers who're looking for a lower commitment experience, it's a *lot* better if you're willing to invest some time peeling away the layers of the game.To be fair, I've never played WAF's more expensive counterpart and this is my first football manager. I'm about 120+ hours in when I write this. I do have a soft corner when it comes to indie games.What's striking is,* Depth of the training system / player potential development / player skills. It's got me asking questions on what's possible and is fun to connect the dots. I hope my club will at some point nurture a Maradona, or a Pele all the way. There's still a lot to learn and experiment with. The link between player skills and the tactics created around them is something I'm working out.* Club Management Delegation system is pretty solid with a few rough spots, so that you can focus on those aspects of football management that you enjoy the most.* Manager Personal Development feels like it's going in the right direction with scouting networks getting better with time and research.* Scouting - you don't need a huge budget to field a competitive team but it takes a little while to learn the 'search' ropes and find players with good value.* The player & manager communication system is smart enough for choices to matter in the near-term but I suspect has little impact on the match outcome. No real reward if you were to accurately (and constructively) criticize a poor first-half performance in the locker room.* Absolutely fun half-time locker room speeches in an English accent that are surprisingly relevant to the situation at hand. Not perfect always but still a good surprise.A few things that I find unnecessarily opaque and challenging:Stamina and Energy: If I don't field a player (not on bench, not on first team), I don't see them recovering energy quicker even when grouped under 'regeneration'. After a match, the game will rush through the next 2 days making it impossible to figure out if players who didn't play are regenerating (or not). This makes the peak season difficult to navigate as you're forced to consistently field tired players. I've found that you can't beat this by increasing squad depth as the higher competition and reduced match time decreases player satisfaction rapidly. Match performance analysis feels underwhelming and unintuitive: This is the single most important area that needs to be done right at the outset. While there's a clear correlation between ball possession and how well you'll do / end-result. However, that feels like it's the *only* real-time link between cause and effect. I think this makes it harder for managers to judge if the tactics they've adjusted are having a positive / negative net-effect. As a result, I'm at a loss trying to figure out what change(s) resulted in a truly bad performance, versus an unfortunate loss that I should write down to RNG. I would've _loved_ to see zone-wise possession data, ball wins, passes completed to help figure out what's going on. Post-match media comments. They feel repetitive, shallow and uninformative. An opportunity lost.I was expecting the team-rival scouting / video analysis to reveal better insight into who I'll be playing next. Sadly, even after 9/10 analysis I'm still stuck with boiler plate training suggestions (tackles, free kicks ...). I would've liked to see, 'shut down long passes by marking so and so ...' or other tactical suggestions that can help tailor training and match-prep.Lastly delegation: I have a simple ask, please allow the Head of HR to negotiate demands in salary increases from department heads. That'll free me up to focus on the football. WAF has good community support (even better if you know German) and I really hope the devs find my review helpful. It'd not be fair to expect an evolved product overnight and I'm watching for regular updates on this one. This game is *good* and the love for football on the developers part helps set it apart from the rest. Auf wiedersehen!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm currently on season 3 in this game, and I started from the bottom, working my way up to my first promotion. If you see other reviews with playtimes below 2 hours, I can assure you they haven't taken the time to truly learn the game. The tactical aspect of this game is more casual; you don't need to overthink it. It basically:-Analyzing your team's quality-Choosing the tactics and formation that best suit your team-Setting your training routine according to your tactics (Passing, Counter-attack, etc.)-Maintaining the team's fitness-Balancing the team's personalities (Leader, Artist, Team player, etc.)Following these steps will generally meet or exceed the board's expectations.What sets this game apart are the aspects that Football Manager doesn't offer:-Balancing your work and personal life-managing the club's facilities-Establishing a deeper personal connection with your players-Developing your favorite players beyond their potential-More role play aspects that I can't mention one by oneOverall, this game is excellent and holds immense potential. From what I know, the developers are still actively patching the game and adding more features. I'd rate it a solid 7.5/10.

name: Kingdom Eighties
detailed_description: Check out this upcoming game! About the Game Grab your bike, pedal off and beat back the Greed to save your town. Kingdom Eighties is a story-based tower defense spin-off to the award-winning Kingdom series set in the 80s. This is a singleplayer adventure with base building and strategy elements, rad aesthetics and a soundtrack inspired by the sweet synth tunes of the ‘80s. Something disturbing has broken free from the shadows and it's up to you as The Leader to drive the evil back by recruiting your friends and other kids from the neighborhood. Together you will build your defenses and protect the town from the relentless attacks by the mysterious Greed monsters that are trying to steal your family heirloom, the Crown of Creation. ​​For what nefarious purposes, who knows? Muster and Deploy the Neighborhood Watch Gather your three unique companions, each with special skills, and recruit other kids to build defenses, collect coins and… run a lemonade stand and a pizza shop (among many other things)! Manage the people you recruit, unlock tools and more importantly gear your crew up for the horrors that come at night. Captivating story about something dangerous lurking in the shadows A force, dormant for centuries, has somehow broken free in the ‘80s; Kingdom Eighties is a comic-sized story about the small town Monarch that has come under threat by an unknown evil. It has fallen upon you, as The Leader, to defend it and save the day. Rally the Summer Camp when an evil force of goopy Greed monsters attack and try to break your defenses. Where did they come from and where the heck are all the adults? Uncover clues and discover what happened to everybody else as you repel and fight the Greed back. Pixels, Neon Lights and Synths Kingdom's iconic, handcrafted art style is back, now with a neon touch coming directly from the ‘80s aesthetics. Chill and vibe with the synthy OST from Andreas Hald, and travel back to the wonder days of bike riding and summer camps, when everything seemed possible. Survival Mixtapes Mode In the true arcade style, Kingdom Eighties features a new game mode: Survival Mixtapes! Bring your best tactics and strategies to fend off progressively harder waves of Greed in four different episodes including “Back to the Suburbs” and “Greed, First Goo”. Make on-the-fly decisions as certain buildings’ special abilities are disabled and levels feature random mounts. This game mode is sure to put your skills to the test!

_childDocuments_.review: Although the Kingdom games are mostly rehashes at a reasonable price, there's always been something to keep me buying the latest iteration of the series, the most recently being the co-op experience. Unfortunately this game removes many elements and simplifies the entire game while giving it an 80s reskin.I'll try to list what they've added and what they've removed.+ There are 2 new enemies added to the game, one is similar to the breeder but instead is slightly larger and slams its body down instead as it's only function, and the other are little ranged plants that spit at your wall (but easily killed by a single swipe from your companion).- The crown stealer has been removed (Completed the game on hard never saw one).- The breeder no longer has an armoured variant (Completed the game on hard never saw one).- Greed armour system seems to be reduced as now some wear funny hats but it barely protects them making them easier to deal with.+ Replacing most money earning mechanics is a job system. When placing walls past certain buildings you can pay 3 coins to open up various skinned stores for kids to generate coins from (pizza place/arcade cabinet/etc). These are all functionally the same but are operated by both builders and kids without a bow/hammer.- Farming has been removed (except for some bushes which are functionally identical to the job system). Crops/Grass growing for wheat functionality is gone.- There is little incentive to push both lanes (I didn't realise you even could) as you linearly push left or right and activate a scripted animation cutscene which sometimes abruptly teleports you to the next level.- Less wall and tower upgrades- Far less buildings- Island specific upgrades are gone along with their buffs.- Island specific villagers are gone with their ability to unlock certain buildings/mechanics.+ 3 NPCs follow you around the game on their bike permanently once unlocked (mandatory to progress). These function as unlocks for upgraded walls, unlocking lane pushing, and unlocking turrets. 2 of them do periodic charge attacks on a cooldown.- Less mount variety, with one being a reused and buffed unicorn from Kingdoms Two Crowns.- Gems have been removed but not replaced with anything, making coins the only real currency now.- Banking has been removed.- Knight mechanic has been simplified (you can no longer send them to push/attack and they seem to just shield retreating archers if the wall falls instead of attacking).- Co-op has been removed.- Boat mechanic has been removed and if you can travel to previous levels I couldn't figure it out.- Maps have been removed/additional gamemodes and there are only 4 short maps to complete that could probably take you an hour to finish if you know what the script trigger to move to the next level is (just push the dumpster as soon as it's available).- Maps are linearly designed so there's no reason to return to them, if you even can. Unlike previous instalments there were upgrades that could only be obtained via backtracking. This is no longer the case where you can fully grab everything you see straight away and just push to the next map without coming back to your base, removing that feeling of persistence/accomplishment, or excitement in finding something you can come back to later.The best thing about this game is probably the 80s soundtrack they've added, but that's about it for me. Artistically both the environment and background graphics are poorly done this time around where it's difficult to tell what is gameplay vs art asset. Unlike their previous games where forest elements and buildings were clearly distinct, this game blends in many 80s pixel art into a convoluted mess making it difficult to interact with things.The worst thing is the simplified gameplay from an already simple game. Before you would upgrade your town until you could hire shield guards that would allow you to eventually push out a lane. They kept most of this in, you still get an upgraded kid that can guard a lane (although I don't know why this is useful as they no longer attack at the wall and seem to only defend retreating archers by blocking if the wall falls), but you can no longer push with these "knights". Instead you are given a dumpster to push with your always following helper, a reskin of the bomb into a cave mechanic, but this time it's a portable defensive item that replaces the knights lane pushing. Your objective is to push into the cave and instead of blowing it up which was satisfying, you now get into the cave to collect something, or worse yet push to the cave to collect some items around it, then leave it to complete a scripted sequence.The game is far shorter, with far less decision making and building, and far less to do. The minor quality of life addition to builders and jobless people now participating in jobs to earn money would have been a nice addition if it didn't replace everything else and trivialise the game. Even decisions around cutting down trees are pointless now as the homeless people are now generated in buildings you can surround and easily manage (with the exception of the final level where they bring back camps for some reason). You just push out, build walls anywhere, push the scripted lane, and move onto the next level. I don't even think there's a way to return to a previous level as there's no boat mechanic.Overall this is a lazy addition to the series that takes away far more than it adds, removes one of it's most request features co-op, and simplifies the game into triviality. The art style of the environment has been poorly thought out and the addition of drawn cutscenes doesn't really add anything to the game and honestly detracts from it as the quality looks like something from early flash animations, ironically coming full circle to the game's humble beginnings as a flash game.P.S. the game still has jittery frame updates while you are moving making the scrolling appear unsmooth. This has been reported across every game they've released and I posted about it 3 years ago and yet every game still suffers from it, truly showing how little they update their engine or seemingly pay attention to user feedback.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game if you've never played Kingdom before. Boring and basic if you have. Imho, Eighties is basically an episodic and linear story that has the gameplay of a stripped down, nearly naked Kingdom game. I'm recommending it because the game somewhat accomplishes what it advertised. I'm assuming most of us who are buying this are probably Kingdom fans though; if you are, change and reduce your expectations to have an enjoyable experience.As a standalone, Eighties can be an okay purchase if you're looking to play a simple, story-forward game that you can definitely finish in less than 10 hours (in normal mode). Just buy it at a discount lol. It's for you if you enjoy a game with light plot, great aesthetics and soundtrack, and limited gameplay. Also, consider that there's not a lot of replayability. Once you've reached the end and have watched all of the cutscenes, the game is over. There's nothing left to do or explore. And even if you play it again, you don't make any active choices to change the course of the story so its not like you'll unlock a new type of ending. You either defeat the greed or restart at some level. And sure, even though all of the other Kingdom games are like this, the heavy emphasis on the story makes Eighties feel way more concluded and final once you get to the end. For Kingdom fans (especially Two Crowns fans who enjoy the other DLC), like no. There's no easy way to play Eighties and not compare its lack of features to previous iterations. Many of the unique features you'd find in Two Crowns like the pikemen/ninja/fishermen, farm/farmers, and certain structures (war horn, farm/stable, catapult, portals, etc) don't exist in Eighties and there are no good alternatives imo. I assume these reductions are because it doesn't work with the plot. Since the monarch is a teen in the eighties, there's no way you'd have a farmer or banker in your camp alongside the "workers/kids" you recruit (not without creative writing at least). My most critical note is that because there's not a lot to do, I got drowsy twice during my whole playthough and took a nap on both occasions. And to be super nitpicky, I so hate how the mounts move. So annoying to have to move back-and-forth numerous times just because the mount has an extended stop and doesn't fully stop moving once you literally lift your finger off the button. There are a few more nitpicky things but….ugh.Sigh. I really wanted to love it. I don't regret the purchase but I also won't be playing it again. As beautiful as it is, I bought Eighties for interesting new gameplay which it sort of delivered. I didn't buy it just to experience subpar Kingdom gameplay in a new skin. Oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Kingdom, or any of the other games, I absolutely recommend you try out this title. The art style is beautiful, the music is spot on and the core gameplay has remained largely unchanged compared to the previous instalments.Unfortunately, that is where my praise for this game must end. Because despite the aforementioned positives I still did not quite enjoy my time playing this game.For starters, it is really short. A couple hours in and I've already seen everything the game has to offer, now I simply need to play the final mission and finish up the story. Which is truly a shame, because the devs took the time to flesh out the story and background of the entire series. As everything becomes connected after seeing the cut scenes. I also disliked the unlockable characters, not because they're boring but because one of them is insanely OP. Yeah I'm talking about Wiz. Sure, you don't get the ability to build archer towers, which is a major debuff, but once you get my boy Wiz you can build very powerful auto turrets. Which not only do a lot of damage but also have insane range, and can be swapped to a mortar to get even more insane range. This makes every level you play after getting Wiz trivially easy. The effort it takes to unlock these characters is absolutely vaporised by the sheer power these characters bestow upon you, which is a bit unbalanced in my opinion. The story itself is fine, I liked it actually. It's basically the Kingdom games but set in the future, in a time where humanity has long forgotten their sins of the past. But the one thing that completely ruined it for me were the cutscenes. I mean come on, no voice acting! Like are you serious?! They make it look like a cartoon, so they thought it would be smart to also have us read them like a cartoon. And I can understand that line of thinking, but someone must have noticed how utterly boring and flat the cutscenes are without any sort of voice acting. And it's not the reading itself that I dislike about them, it's the surprise of getting a cutscene in the first place and the subsequent anticipation of something amazing only to realise I'm watching glorified pages out of a comic book. The games difficulty is also completely off compared to other titles. The game warned me of this, suggesting that veterans play on higher difficulty, which I did. And still the game was incredibly easy, I lost my crown a whole 1 time and got it back 2 seconds later because my good friend K absolutely murder the poor sod that took it. This was on the first island, not once did I lose it after that. The difficulty isn't helped by the stupidly OP towers that Wiz lets you build and the robot he builds for you when going on the attack. It feels like the devs wanted to make a version of Kingdom that was nigh impossible to lose, which I think kind of go's against what the other games were trying to achieve. You don't beat this game by merit, you beat it because it was meant to be completed without breaking a sweat. Now finally the pricing. In case you hadn't noticed I'm not quite that positive about my experience, but the price was the one of the few aspects that I genuinely thought was okay. I bought the game on sale, for 8,84 euro's. The original price would have been 11,79 euro's, so I got a nice 25% discount. Thanks steam. Even though I got a discount I do believe the pricing is fine. You don't get much for what you pay, but it's not a total scam. It's obvious a lot of time and effort went into making this game, and for what I experienced I think 12 euro's is an 'okay' price. Not a great price, or a good deal, but an okay price for a game that has a lot of potential. I sincerely hope the devs read some of the reviews, and realise where they made mistakes. Because if they update this game to make it actually more indepth and enjoyable and lenghten the overall experience, I believe it has a bright future.Also, you can only employ children. Which is kinda cool.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a time where I’d choose a neutral review if I had one. To put it shortly: Is this a bad game? No, certainly not. Would I buy it if I’d known this beforehand? Also no.Graphics and music are fine. The pixel art is absolutely gorgeous as usual, and it’s my golden standard for pixel art quality. The only downside is that it can be too busy in certain aspects, particularly when it comes to differentiating employed vs unemployed workers. The music is serviceable; it gets the job done, but it’s not as memorable as the previous entries.When it comes to gameplay, there’s been a significant downgrade. Several features have been either cut (Bankers, Catapults, Fliers, Crown Stealers, Statues, Hermits, Gems, revisiting islands) or extremely simplified (Towers, Knights, Ways of getting money), with no significant improvements, to the point it feels like something in between New Lands and Two Crowns.There’s also balancing issues. First, the new towers are brutally overpowered, to the point that it makes archers almost redundant, even during Blood Moons. They cannot be destroyed, have a fairly high damage output and cost a single payment of 5-7 coins. Prioritizing towers makes even Cursed a cakewalk, to be honest. The new enemy, which is basically a Breeder-sized enemy that cannot create new people, can be very easily kited and killed.The only aspect that had some work added in the game when compared to previous entries would be the story, which is fairly generic (Not that I’m expecting to have my mind blown) and the addition of a metric ton of eighties references (Along with another slathering of self-references). They are decently done, and YMMV on whether or not they enhance the game. I’m a bit past 80’s nostalgia myself, but I’ve seen much worse attempts.All in all, a very short game with no replay value, with a lot of cut features and quite a bit of balancing issues. I’d only recommend it for the most ardent of fans, and even then, keep your expectations in check.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I somewhat liked the Game, and it could have gone both Yes or No on the recommend, however I can't recommend it over its predecessor of Two Crowns. The Enemy doesn't attack them, they are fairly cheap and very effective, compared to the same value in archers. The best defence is just not expanding and putting turrets everywhere.Regarding generating Money: You still have archers that hunt animals (though seeing children as large as a teenagers shin kill squirrels and such in cold blood will always be weird to me), as well as a new system of chores.You don't have Fishermen, Farmers or the merchant, stripping the option for generating money quite limited, compared to the previous game.The Chores themselves are fine, there is a nice bit of visual variation between them, but as you only have one resource there's not really much mechanical difference.Visually it looks good and the addition of the bicycle band is a nice visual for actually working as a group with other children instead of just being a rich monarch.However the setting having children murder small animals in cold blood and fighting against demons doesn't really fit that well, I think.All in all it's a stripped down version of the previous game with a nice looking, but kind of ill fitting Skin.

_childDocuments_.review: Since I first stumbled upon the original Kingdom, it's been my go-to for that cozy gaming experience – you know, the one that lures you in with its calming tunes, charming pixel graphics, and a gameplay mix that's simple yet surprisingly intricate.Over the years, I've dipped my toes into different versions of the game, each bringing its own unique twist. My top pick? Definitely the Shogun expansion. Exploring new islands, encountering fresh monsters, riding mounts, and constructing towers – every iteration felt like an exciting new adventure.Now, let's talk Eighties – the latest addition to the Kingdom family. This time, it's not just about building and surviving; there's a narrative weaving through each stage, turning each island into a chapter. Four chapters later, and you've got yourself a game with an ending. It's not the strongest story you'll experience, yet it works.But, here's the thing that bugs me a bit – the game's a bit on the short side. Complete all four chapters with a regular playthrough, not diving too deep into every nook and cranny, and you're looking at roughly 5-6 hours. And that's me being optimistic. For a 12 euro price tag, it feels a tad brief. Sure, you can stretch it out with replayability, aiming for all the achievements like I did, but there's a limit.Now, there's this "mixtape" mode they threw in – a survival setup where you replay specific chapters, with extra rules and a tougher difficulty. Not exactly my cup of tea, but I'm sure it's got its own fanbase.One thing that kind of bugged me was the fact that there's no co-op mode. Honestly, games like Kingdom, especially ones with this vibe, should totally have a coop feature – it's like a given. I've got some sweet memories of chilling on the couch with my GF, diving into the Kingdom series together, and not having a coop mode in Eighties just felt a bit off.Let's dive a bit more into what makes Kingdom: Eighties so special—the whole 80s vibe is just spot on, I've got to admit. The game manages to capture that nostalgic feel perfectly, with loads of nods to classic movies, series, and games. It's like a blast from the past with all these neat details in different scenes, making the whole experience feel super immersive.And can we talk about the music? Oh man, it's on another level. The Kingdom series has always nailed it in the music department, and Eighties is no exception. The tunes are crazy good. I caught myself more than once just standing in-game, soaking in the 80s vibes from the soundtrack. It's like being transported to this whole other world, whether it's the woods or the busy streets.So, this 80s setup they've got going on isn't just a backdrop. It's the heart of the game. The references, the details, and that killer soundtrack—it all adds up to an experience that deserves to be played. Kingdom: Eighties becomes this trip down memory lane, a visual and musical feast that really pays homage to the awesomeness of the 1980s. It's those little touches that make it more than just a game; it's a memorable journey back in time, and that's what sets it apart in the Kingdom series.I appreciate you taking the time to read through my review. I hope you'll find this and my other reviews somehow helpful! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Huge disappointment as a long-term fan of the series. Coming in at probably about 6 hours of gameplay or less, this entry doesn't show any of the same sort of love and care as previous entries in the series. There are 5 levels you play in sequence and this is the entire game, with no other gamemodes or even the ability to pop back and forth between locations.I played this game on Hard and it was still definitely the easiest Kingdom experience I have ever had. You can steamroll every level by just slowly walking backwards behind your mobile garbage bin while your archers and other acquaintances shoot - you will discover by accident that just retreating a bit is basically a guaranteed win strategy, where you can then take a second to recover (one of your acquaintances will take just a couple seconds to fully repair your shield when you are out of combat) before powering back on. I would often knock down like two or three portals at once in a single raid without stopping to go back and check on how my kingdom was going, and all of the "oh god, I wonder how my other wall is going" tension of the previous games that was core to this series' appeal is gone. Also gone are any sort of character/crest customisation options, other game modes, or the ability to hop back and forth between locations. This game has no bells and whistles.The pixel art is very competent as always, but I found the art assets a lot less compelling in this game because of how confused the setting is. You're a group of teenagers recruiting small children to form an army, and in a huge missed opportunity this absurd setting *isn't* played for a joke during the game's very thin story. I did not find this to be the cool aesthetic experience I was maybe hoping it might be - do not go into this thinking it will be Kingdom: Hotline Miami or anything. I have more things to say but the game doesn't really merit a longer review.

_childDocuments_.review: Downgrade:I am a massive fan of the kingdom games, I've played all the two crowns DLC's, replayed them multiple times, beat the game on cursed and basically squeezed out as much as I can of them, but I still come back to play, whether it being challenges, or beating the campaign again on a harder difficulty, there is so much repeatability in two crowns.When I bought this game, I was pretty excited, it looked cool and I thought I would grab it, it wasn't overly expensive and I thought that it would be fine considering it is part of the kingdom franchise, I had no worries, but when I started playing, my excitement for it dropped.first of all, there are almost no new features, the siege dumpster was cool, but essentially just a re skin of knights which is fair since there has to be a way to take out portals, towers are too powerful, being able to set up a conga line from across the map, making even cursed a breeze, you can't tell the difference between hired and not hired people and some other tedious things.If this was the first time I played a kingdom game, I probably would've rated it positive since it still isn't bad and as is better than most other games, but playing previous kingdom games and playing this just felt like a waste of money, it would've been better off as DLC, scrap the story, it isn't very interesting anyway but it was a nice change, get rid of this no going back to old stage crap and price it at £3 or $4 then I would probably enjoy it since it has enough changes for the price.Overall, I didn't dislike it too much, but it wasn't good either, it didn't hit the same as previous games, in addition to there only being 4 stages to go to, I beat the game on both normal and cursed but still after 17 hours feel like I haven't got my moneys worth. I think the main reason the reviews aren't just negative is because its people new to the kingdom series and this is the first game they have played, if you have played and enjoyed prior series then don't buy this, it is a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like other games in the series, but with a little bit of a story thrown in. Not only does it feel like the other Kingdom games, but it has 80s shout-outs and nostalgia that ARE NOT just surface level. If you were there, you will understand better what is going on and probably chuckle once or twice.If you weren't there, there are things in there for you too, like a specific vibe similar to a very popular streaming show, which sets a great mood for the game. Something that is different is that there are levels, each with an objective. You can choose to complete these quickly or you can do as much as possible on each level, it is up to you and this will determine how long the game lasts. Either way, it should be entertaining and not too serious. In short, if you enjoyed the other Kingdom games, get this one. If you are a fan of the 80s, get this one. If you don't care about either of these things but are still considering the game, get it.  It isn't expensive and it can help you kill some time.

_childDocuments_.review: Again wishing for a "meh" rating on steam. It's not bad, but it's no where near as good as some of the other games bought out by this franchise. I mean I was sold on having one of these games with more of a storyline, but the storyline is kinda bland and boring and very linear to the point that I was getting quite tempted just the skip the cut scenes which is not a good thing considering its meant to be the core of this game. I'm sure this game could be made into something amazing with a storyline added, but this isn't it.Some of the things you're building/using are hard to work out what they are until you use them resulting in lost coins. It's kind of annoying when you have to abandon missions and redo them because the game has decided that you need to pay people you've already recruited to do something right at the end of the task. There's a lot of time wasting as you wait for trees to be cutable so you can build further out and sometimes the builders seem to move in slow motion to arrive. It feels like the game doesn't respect your time and it's being dragged out in places to make it feel longer which doesn't equal better value for money if it messed up the enjoyment of the game. It doesn't even look like you need to be particularly careful of your crew, as unlike other versions where if you let them stay out too late by getting them to do extra tasks beyond the wall they can get wiped out, a lot of the time it looks like they just won't go out there or leave in time to be back before dark. It kind of feels like a reskin with a lot of the challenging and interesting features stripped out.  There's no cool rides that I've seen so far. Just variations on bikes that don't seem to be significantly better or worse than one another and many seem to look almost the same. I actually couldn't really work out which one (if any and they're not just cosmetic) was the best to use. Your friends come with you and have a tendancy to mow down enemies that are about, also removing a lot of the tension you get in the other games about exploring too far beyond the walls.Anyway, it's not a bad game, it's just that it has a lot of things that seem to make it significantly worse and less enjoyable than it's previous incarnations, and nothing that's been really improved. The series really does need something to make it feel more fresh, but unfortunately this game hasn't managed to pull that off.  I'll probably finish it eventually, but its not on my must play list right now.
