_childDocuments_.review: I'm ultimately recommending this game, but I have mixed feelings. I'll start by saying I'm a huge fan of this series. I discovered it by accident and I've since sunk in several hundred hours into Kingdom Two Crowns, but I've played Classic and New Lands as well. What I love most about Two Crowns is it can be calming to play. I have a very stressful job so it's nice to be able to quickly turn on Kingdom and play the Shogun map. What I love most is the simplicity.Kingdom Eighties is the opposite of simplicity. There's way too much going on and I feel overwhelmed. I can tell that the devs put a lot of hard work into it and it's really creative. I love all the little movie/tv easter egg details. Other reviewers have discussed what new roles are available for making money since farmers are gone, so I won't go into depth there. There's a lot of witty stuff like recycling centers, fishing, life guarding, etc. There's a lot of humor to be found, but again, for me, it goes against the simplicity of what I liked in the first game. There's a lot going on with background buildings and things to build. Two Crowns is also about gradually building upwards, incorporating new features, upgrades, and people as you play along. This game kind of dumps everything on top of you all at once, with very little gradual progression.It can also be hard to tell whether your defenses are adequate. I liked the sticks to stone to steel progression of the first game. This one has a bunch of stuff clumped together that makes it hard for me to know what level the defense is at a glance. I need to physically check to see how much the next improvement costs before I can decide whether it's adequate. This game, unlike the others, actually has a bit of a story to it with characters. I think it's really cool how they tie the previous games into this one. I won't spoil stuff, but I do like the angle they took. It's quite clever. It's also nice to travel with companions that help you fight and you don't have to worry about them getting attacked/kidnapped (like the dog from previous games).In all, if you're a fan of the series and a fan of eighties films/shows, you'll definitely like this. It's a brilliant combination. But if you're like me and you loved the simplicity of the first games, this one moves way too fast and has too much going on. The music's great, the art's great, and the new characters are great, but I sadly don't think I'll be playing this one as much as I do Two Crowns. I like taking peaceful strolls with my horse through the forest while I listen to the birds and plan out how my kingdom will look. I love feeling like I'm building a civilization in Two Crowns. But this game's not about that, and that's totally fine. They have a story, it's with purpose, and the setting/tempo perfectly reflects that. Kingdom Eighties is ultimately a nice addition to the franchise, but I do hope they make another game like Two Crowns in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I've previously played Kingdom, New Lands, and a little bit of Two Crowns (which I have on pending but I get distracted), and it's no surprise then that I've been waiting for this "sequel"; in quotation marks, since it's something a bit special and could be defined as a "start" to the saga, curiously enough. When I saw its first trailer, where they showed that eighties theme that radiated a retro feel, it captured me completely and filled me with intrigue, so here I am to give it its deserved review.Kingdom Eighties - Summer of Greed, is a base building and defense game, where we'll take the role of "Leader", a boy who will be involved in an epic adventure to save his family, friends, and the whole town from greedy monsters that invade the territory. It is a strategic game where we'll have to manage our main resource, in this case coins, to recruit units, build or improve buildings, and activate events along the way, among other things; everything necessary to fight greed and its legions of horrifying creatures.The , that yes, for the first time in the saga, this game will tell a tale in a more direct way and as an episodic campaign, with old school animated cinematics, which will gradually reveal the story. We'll follow the adventure of the aforementioned "Leader", the playable character, who will learn the secrets of his lineage and its connection with the greed. But thankfully, he will not have to face this adversity alone, as we'll be able to recruit three other characters who will accompany us and help us in this crisis, as well as an army of… children? Yes, ruthless creatures that can make you lose your sanity; perfect choice. I was a bit intrigued about the story, about how it would be told and what would happen in it, and I can say that I was satisfied; it's a story with some good clichés and a very fitting ending. I liked the way they approached it and I hope we can see this reflected in future titles, as I think it's a universe that can get better and better, and I think it's fantastic. I want to mention that this is a step in a great direction, and I want to make special emphasis on what I said so that it is not taken as "in the right direction", since the predecessors of this title are also very entertaining, and although they do not show such a concrete story, they seemed to me to be on the right track as well.The  doesn't change much with respect to the previous Kingdoms, but for those who aren't familiar with the saga, I'll tell you that the mechanics are quite simple. The game is presented to us on a 2D map, where we can move from left to right to explore the sides of our base, which will always be located in the center of the territory. Our main objective is to defend our crown, since losing it to greed will end the game, especially at night when we'll be besieged; all while also fulfilling the main mission of the episode, although it usually involves reaching the end of one side of the map, making our way through the ominous portals and obstacles that summon our enemies. To accomplish this, we'll have to employ units and build defenses, which will be possible by using in-game currency: which is, well, coins. But this is not the only use of these coins, as there are several things to spend them on, such as bicycles. The bikes are the mounts of this title, and as in the previous games, each one has its own abilities. Some are faster, some make you less tired, and some aren't even bikes at all! Skateboards, carts... and many other secret vehicles that are just plain cool, and which I obviously won't spoil.We can also use our coins to have our units, that is, the children, perform various tasks to get us more money in return; besides, of course, being able to assign them to defense or construction, with bows and hammers respectively. Unlike the other titles, farms were replaced with arcade arcades, lawn mowers, and we can even occupy abandoned fast food chains so that our little helpers have something to entertain themselves and in turn generate profits. The children feel much more "villagey" than in the predecessor games, as there aren't many unit variants (no spearmen, to give an example), but this is resolved with the addition of our three new companions. These companions will be recruited little by little at key points in the episodes, and will be a powerful addition to our forces, as they have unique and characteristic skills. We'll have an athletic jock who will take care of everything that involves brute force, an engineer who will lend us her repair skills, and a computer genius who will take care of even crafting robots. I especially loved this last addition, it's a colorful and, above all, cool group of characters that really change the atmosphere of the game with respect to the previous ones, and I thought it was excellent. I feel that the gameplay in general has not lost that simplicity of the Kingdom games, and is still addictive and highly entertaining. The  are very characteristic of the saga, being presented in a very nice and vibrant pixel art, but with new additions such as portraits and handmade cinematics (starting with an excellent animated intro), which have been great. The eighties vibe is palpable throughout the entire screen, from the characters and appearances to the background environments and landscapes, and it feels phenomenal. I saw some enemies that felt new to me, but they have the same touch as in the previous games, very well presented and perfectly accompanying their predecessors.I also want to add that there are references everywhere, to beloved and very nostalgic franchises like Ghostbusters and Back to the Future, and at times it seems like a great love letter to that era, from the author to his childhood; and very well done it should be noted. The , on the other hand, is also awesome. It has very catchy melodies, a lot of synthesizer and retro vibes, ranging from 'chill' tunes to some more tense ones, especially at night. Between the two sections it creates a very pleasing atmosphere, super charismatic, and really only heightened my enjoyment of the game.  In , Kingdom Eighties is a game that stays well rooted to its roots, but adds slight changes that keep its gameplay fresh. Of its most notable additions, the story stands out and lends itself to enjoyment, along with the cast of cool characters that are literally the star of the show. Retro visuals, music that transports you to another era, and a lot of nostalgia for many of us; everything comes together in a game that could be classified as a starting point to the saga. It has a lot of neat aspects, and I recommend it to both fans of the franchise and curious individuals who are still not quite sure, and I hope you come to like it as much as I do.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Kingdom Two Crowns game, me and my best friend played it for several hours until we beat the game, the game was quite ruthless and difficult to play, enemies were getting stronger and stronger with each day, it was fun. Ultimately there was no plot involved, just monsters who are called "greed" and they punish players who don't spend their coins by taking them from their pouch and in the end taking the crown. It's quite clever isn't it? Well, if I liked the previous one, why am I downvoting this one? The problem with this game, is that it's a reskin of a previous game with a few changes here and there, so it feels the same, there nothing new except story points, you play the game and progress through the story, and the story is quite bad and boring to be honest. I would probably like the story if it was voiced or maybe animated better, otherwise I am immensely bored by the story, might as well just put dialogue boxes in the game, without those out of place 'animated' cutscenes. I didn't feel as much satisfaction as I did when I played Kingdom Two Crowns and destroyed a portal, Kingdom Eighties just don't have that feeling of winning the game. In Kingdom Two Crowns there is no story, you destroy a portal and can call it a day, because you don't need to see the story to the end, so me and my buddy didn't go through each island to destroy each portal (because they're all the same anyway, we unlocked every unlockable artifact/character/mount and moved on, because it was tedious). In Kingdom Eighties you have to go through each island (level) to get to the end of the story, nothing much changes, just new places with different mounts (skateboards, bicycles, etc.), some were pretty cool, but that was it, you get bored after a few dozen minutes. Each level has to be defeated by destroying the same portal over and over again. It gets boring real quick after a few levels. I wish the developers would bring some new mechanics, not similar, because it's stupidly boring. Maybe add variations of the portal, maybe add some bosses, not reuse the same minions which we see on every level. Also the game is like really short, with no replayability value, sure you can change difficulty, kick it up a notch, all it would do is make the minions stronger and in bigger quantities, you would just waste more time trying to defeat the monsters. That's just not fun. Also, about the story, I mean, if you do include a story, and make the whole game about it, why don't you give each character some background? Give them actual names? Voice actors? Make them interesting, because you guys did include a story, but it feels so bare and barely interesting and very short. I didn't feel anything about them, if one of them died through the story I wouldn't even blink. Because I don't give a damn about some dude named "Champ", all he does is push the garbage bin, he has some dialogue lines, but I don't even remember any of his lines.

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy the game for a short period of time, the gameplay is identical to the older games in the Kingdom Series, however there are some problems I have with this game, and I cannot recommend it unless you are purely looking for a handful of hours of fun, or to support the Devs.- It's a Kingdom game set in the eighties, I love the new look of the game and the music is great- It runs well with no bugs on my end or any visual glitches- It's not a very expensive game - No replayability after you finish the story (Unless you are hunting achievements). Unlike previous games in the Kingdom series, when I finished the story of this game I felt no reason to go back- The story is rather dry in my opinion, the characters you meet have no names except for what they are suppose to obviously be. Your character is simply Leader and you meet with the others known as Champ, Tinkerer and Wiz. And while they where useful characters to have around, I didnt care at all about them, and everytime there was a cutscene after the first few, I wanted nothing more but to skip.- No Co-op. I understand that the devs might have wanted to try and focus on the story a little more in this, and while the attempt is appriciated, I would've found the game way more entertaining if I could have played with a friend like in previous game entries. (Two Crowns for example)- It's short. I had about 5 hours of play until I cleared the game. I understand I can go back for achievements but I'd rather not. While the game sports some fancy new looks and music compared other kingdom games, it plays identicaly and is only a few hours long. Its cheap at 11€ but the story is dry and the characters forgettable. I do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 15h 3/10 2 I wrote  No Yes, but the game is short and you need to play at least 2 times through it No, except for spending 50 days on one island, but that is mostly waiting with moving to the next level after you beat the enemy. Gladly the game doesn't pause when in the background, so just keep it running.  No Yes, but a very doable one. Complete the game in 50 days, on easy I only needed 21 days when trying to get this achievement. No No Yes, there is an achievement for beating the game on hard and on cursed difficulty. the difficulties stack, so beating it on cursed will also give you the achievement for hard.  NoYay, a new game in the Kingdom series! I love Kingdom: Two Crowns, so I was very hyped for this one. I have seen complaints that it is a reskin, but I don't feel it is. Also, have you seen how many details went into the artwork for this entry? I'm glad it is a separate entry, as that comes with a new achievement list, and not just an achievement for beating the game. What stood out to me the most is how much love went into the artwork. so many small details and it looks all so awesome. I'm more of a nighties kid but I still could feel the vibe this game went for. I also love that each new level had new artwork and a new setting. It wasn't more of the same, it was clearly a new place they moved to.  However, I'm wondering if this might confuse new players. As the Kingdom series isn't known for its explanation and is more of a trial-and-error type of gameplay. And then having buildings that do the same as in the previous level but look a bit different might be confusing. With more focus on the story, I would say this is a good entry point for new players. Also because the difficulty isn't as brutal as in some of the early Kingdom games. And for the veterans, it also sprinkled in a lot of hints to earlier titles and they will be referenced during the game. However, one complaint I have is that the text in the cutscenes is quite fast and there is no voice offer. My main language isn't English, so I'm not a fast reader and I have missed the endings of sentences. I also saw this on a playthrough by a YouTuber that they couldn't finish the text in time before it already moved on. The achievements for Kingdom Eighties are quite easy compared to earlier entries, and I'm personally a fan of that. They still will challenge you, but they are doable and it gives you the feeling that you can reach that sweet 100% completion. I was surprised that you can't go back to earlier levels, as in previous entries you could. So this means there are a bunch of missable achievements. But the game is short and you have to play at least through it twice: Speedrun (within a little over 3h, but on easy it took me only 1,5h) and completing the game on the hardest difficulty. I had so much fun completing Kingdom Eighties and I'm so amazed by the beautiful pixel artwork and still the addictive gameplay the Kingdom series always has.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough game to review.TLDR; I think if you're new to the Kingdom series, Kingdom 80s may be a good start to see if you wanted to play the other games in the series. But it's probably too simple and short for the experienced players.I  the Kingdom series and I feel this is a good addition to the series. The review by Kurtino (and others) contain most of the actual changes and I agree with most of their opinions. But thought I needed to balance it out a bit.Kingdom 80s changes a few core mechanics, generally to be more accessible and easier to play. + I love the addition of a story, even if it doesn't change much gameplay wise. + Each of the 4 islands is themed completely differently, and each has their own slightly different mechanics to complete it.+ I like the ability to change "archer towers" to have different attacks and wish this would be in future games~ Some of the "mounts" seem redundant, and most of them don't have many useful distinguishing features. - The game is short. 4 small islands, usually 2-3 portals per side. I beat the game on cursed difficulty, all portals on both sides, in about 7 hours, and I play fairly defensively.- It can be difficult to tell what is interactable. There is generally more on screen than previous games, and it can be especially difficult to see the "vagrants".- There isn't much in terms of replayability. Without adding new stories, I don't see how they could add DLC to increase replayability. So you're "stuck" with the game as it is.Overall, I found it an interesting take on the Kingdom series and like that they tried to jazz it up and try different things. Even if I think it fell slightly short this time. If it had a couple more islands, I think it would've been received better.If you want a longer game, and more value for money, get Two Crowns instead. If you want a fairly chill entry to the Kingdom series, this is it.

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Eighties is a nostalgic game about paying off kindergartners to help you win summer back for everyone.  Beat it on Normal in 4 hours, then went around getting achievements for a good 8 more - using a keyboard.  Difficulty can be set in game.  This is a good entrance game to the series. Like Kingdom's little bro.  Casual-normal are fair for kids and newcomers, hard is for those who want a little challenge, and Cursed is for everyone else who's played the rest of Kingdom's franchise line.  There's also a survival mode to see how long you can last.Unlike the other games, Kingdom 80s is single-player only.  Assumingly because you play a specific character. Also unlike other Kingdoms, this game follows a story.  Meaning it's linear.  You cannot go back to previous lands.  Each land accompanies a VHS-style cartoon vid leading you onto the next chapter.  There are 4 chapters total, each filled to the brim with fun oldschooled Saturday Morning vibes, rides that are a blast from the past, and all the static flair and vibrant colors you will ever dream of.  The soundtrack is rad.  Perfect for this universe.  The assets have been repixelled for the 80s.   Now there are present-day buildings, pools, and cars.  It's amazing how different it is compared to everything else Fury Studios made with the same assets.  While I like the whole of it, there are some things I'd wish were different: One is I wish there was more of a reason to take out portals on the beach side of the map.  Like the towers, where you can bring more people to the next area or... I don't know... Something .  Two, I wish there were bigger hints on some of the mounts . I loved what they did with this game and the fresh-out-of-the-box newness with it.  Definitely worth my money, and I hope to go back and get the two remaining achievements I'm lacking.  If you've played Kingdom games and like them, just get this already.  You know you'll like it.  And it's different enough to give some fresh air.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply a disappointment, in nearly all aspects. If you want a good Kingdom experience, the first Kingdom and Two Crowns are the only ones worth playing. I regret spending enough time on this to no longer allow a refund. The main problems are:It seems like a blatant diversity quota/ cash grab, as all it gives is different sprites and less content than the previous games. The cutscenes feel extremely out of place, and the characters are bland. Being locked in to a single character as well is disappointing, as it seemed like it would be a 4 person co-op, or at least 4 different stories. Took everything that worked in the previous games and threw them out the window instead of fixing what didn't work. The gameplay ends up feeling more like a roblox tycoon then a Kingdom game, and it feels like if you were really dedicated, you could finish the whole game in an hour.Got rid of the banking system, the trader; who was a good source of early game money, and the gem system.Knights now have almost no real use, as now you have the athlete push a garbage can as a shield, and attacking the portals are trivial, even allowing multiple attacks one after another, making the gameplay loop consist of surviving until you upgrade the town enough to get the garbage can, and then steamrolling the portals.My first time playing this game was on hard difficulty, I can't even imagine how easy then game is on all the lower difficulties.The mounts are all very similar, and don't offer any significant benefits over the others.Archer towers are replaced with sentrys, with 3 variants: Long range mortar type, high damage laser, and regular turret. No way to buff damage, just hp.Enemies are easy to deal with, more so than previous games. The large ones no longer spawn more regular enemies, and the new hermit crab-esque enemy mostly dies before it can do any damage. There are also smaller ranged enemies that follow the large ones and leave when the large enemy dies. Don't seem to make any real difference in the waves except for sometimes making the player drop coins every once in a while.I do not recommend you buy this game if you are expecting something that builds on the previous games, as all it seems to do is ruin anything that was good from them instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge fan of all Kingdom Games so far, but that one is the best one without any doubt!Kingdom Eighties surpasses its predecessors in many ways. While the gameplay principle remains the same (which is intentional as these games aim to maintain familiarity), the actual gameplay itself has been significantly enhanced. I am particularly impressed by the introduction of new settings. We have moved beyond mere survival in forests and now explore cities, neighborhoods, amusement parks, and much more... it truly feels invigorating! Additionally, you're not really journey alone; instead, you interact with fantastic NPC friends who exhibit distinct personalities. These changes serve a purpose, as Kingdom Eighties presents a compelling main storyline that feels immensely satisfying so far. It gracefully guides us through each level, elevating the gameplay to an entirely new level. The cutscenes are absolutely breathtaking!

_childDocuments_.review: For veterans to the series there's some novelty value in the new mechanics, however the gameplay is streamlined (only two worker types to worry about, invulnerable companions that can attack the greed, farms replaced by stores and arcades that rain money like confetti) to the point the difficulty becomes trivial, though given the relative short playing  time (4 chapters) at least it ends before the novelty entirely wears off. For newcomers the easier difficulty might have made it a good starting point, however the lack of content is a problem. It's the cheapest entry in the franchise at present, New  Lands being half again the price and Two Crowns almost double, but both have significantly more content (even without DLC) providing much better bang for the buck - and of course Two Crowns also has multiplayer. The 'synth' soundtrack is largely forgettable. Even the nostalgia bait is reduced to a few background cameos that seem to exist entirely so you can say 'I remember that movie/show'. It's there perhaps the biggest weakness lies; the ingredients are all there to lean into the classic 'kids gang' movies of the 80s like Goonies or ET, however the individuals are barely given any characterisation, the story and plot feel rushed and is largely predictable and boring and as a result I found myself caring less about Leader and his friends/parents that I did the anonymous protagonist of the previous two games, and they didn't get the benefit of faux VHS cutscenes.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the reviews of people claiming this game is "woke". There is not a single woke thing about it, unless you consider the existence of POC inherently woke- in which case, do not play the game at all, because you're a jerk and don't deserve joy. The game itself is campy and fun, in the same world as the other games just in a more modern era featuring the descendant of the old monarchs who fought back against the greed. The story doesn't make much sense, but it's fun to get the cutscenes. You can tell a lot of love went into this game and the team had a lot of fun making it. You need to rethink your old approach to the old games - the main way to make coin here is chores, which can only be done by spreading your walls to keep those chore areas safe for kids to perform them. In some instances, you WANT to keep your recruits unassigned (in fact there's at least one mount that requires a bunch of jobless kids to even be possible to unlock), which makes the gameplay feel fresh and new with mechanics you already know but strategies you have to rethink. That being said, the game is very... very easy. The turrets you unlock on episode 2 make each nightly wave a joke, especially if you give them any amount of armor. Through all four episodes I think I only had a turret get destroyed once. I had enough fun that I'm going to replay the whole campaign on a more difficult setting and see how it's balanced again. But like, woke? No, unless you think black people existing is woke. If so, please go outside and touch some grass. The story is nothing special, but it's not some woke agenda. Anyone saying that is terminally online and running in the wrong crowds.

_childDocuments_.review: Oversimplified, short and easy, i really don't understand why this isn't just another DLC for Two Crowns instead, as it would've fitted there more than as a standalone game, it simply doesn't have anything to justify its existence the way it is.Gameplay, same as the previous entries, but a lot more simplified, and in some aspect worse:-> The progression to unlock things got rushed, you just get all unlocked it by the second act;-> The workers got simplified, no spearman, no farmers, no hermits, all replaced with random plots that generate money without much investment or strategybehind; -> No buff statues, no puzzles to unlock things, just superficial fetch quests and there you go;-> The heroes got a lot more broken then before, to the point you can even finish the entire game by only using them in combat;-> Too short, only 4 acts, and the objectives to progress each act are a joke, especially because of the Broken heroes, but even more because of the oversimplified mechanics-> Some new assets, specifically related to mounts and the kids, but all enemies are reused from previous entries, with only 1 and 1/2 new enemy that's barely noticeable because his gimmick thing don't do anything most of the time, and in everything else he's just another greed Breeder;I guess then that the is story the only reason for this to exist, but there's nothing there to hold it up, just a superficial and poorly written hero's journey, told in static frames i've saw done better everywhere else, even those games that use comics style to tell story can make better use. At least they maintained the same voxel/pixel style as the previous entries.Tho there's something i simply can't wrap my head around: Who hired the person responsible for the cutscenes art? Who was the person that approved those literal farts of cutscenes? How can someone look at those stupid characterizations of the main protagonist and his friends, making them all not only look goofy, but also constantly look like they had just farted and were trying to hide it, in every cutscene they show up, at every glimpse of emotion they try to enact, constantly ruining any semblance of seriousness the story could've had.How could someone look at that atrocious thing and say: "Yeah, that's right, that's fitting for Kingdom series". I can only conclude that either Raw Fury was ripped of by someone, they underpaid someone, or someone was doing some favours around. That kind of low quality thing doesn't belong anywhere near this series, and i simply can't believe Raw Fury wouldnt have any kind of supervision over it, this is just a complete failure on their part...Hope the new DLC for Two Crows end up being better, and that Raw Furry hire more competent to writers and artists, sounds like this didnt ended up as Sweet as was intended

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Eighties is a good continuation of the Kingdom series. It continues the story of a monarch's fight against the greed, in this case in the form of a child called "Leader" in an 80s setting that is strongly reminiscent of Stranger Things but also contains many Eastereggs from other pop culture franchises, such as Jaws, Friday the 13th, Nightmare on Elm Street, Predator but also a cannibal hut from the Forest or the DeLorean from Back to the Future.In terms of gameplay, some things change, so you recruit 3 unique children, who are also named only after their abilities. The Sport Cannon can push trash containers, which act as a barrier when attacking the portals of the greedy. The technician repairs them and can improve turrets. The technician, which you meet only in the 2nd level, makes sure that you can build guns and supports the "Portal Attack Squad" with a Terminator 2-inspired gun on chain drive. Outside of the portal attack, the clique follows you on bicycles and attacks Greed with the same from time to time. Here you don't need to pay attention to health points and the like. This is well chosen and avoids frustration.Otherwise, you recruit generic little kids who take on roles like archer or technician. During the day, however, they also earn money. This differs from level to level. In the 2nd level, a residential area, for example, lawns are mowed, in the mall, the last level, the children work in a donut store.The visuals are typical Kingdom with a good touch of retro and a phenomenal soundtrack that I can only recommend to purchase.What I don`t like is; the game is way to short after someone has settled in. After 4 levels that seem very small, it was over. Also, I recommend veterans to start at least with difficult. I have played through all previous Kingdom parts on different platforms, but wanted to go relaxed and played on easy. There, unfortunately, you are attacked by a maximum of 4 Greed at night, so start at least on Normal, players of the previous parts on Hard.Otherwise, I can recommend the game. I had only one bug, in the first level I could not pick up the Trophy, in my 2nd run, otherwise flawless.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like Kingdom Two Crowns with ~150hours. Other than the bare mechanics, this game is not at all similar to the game I know and love. For an $12.00 game, I expected far more than just 5 or 6 hours of game(and I really took my time as well). Overall, I am really disappointed, I really wanted to like the game. I did not think that the "story-based" style really worked here. Unless you are really bored and just wanna see what is up, I do not really recommend this game, even if you love the prequel.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the games that a middle option would have been apt, but as it stands I can't recommend the game unless it's on sale. Even then, honestly, I don't think you're missing out if you skip this.Here's the rub: I LOVE Kingdom Two Crowns. I've put well over 200 hours into it at the time of writing this review, and it's one of those games I could pick up on a weekend and accidentally play for 6 hours straight. If this is your first introduction to this series, stop, right now, immediately, and go give KTC a try.However, if you played KTC, let me be candid: this could've just been a DLC. I thought I would get some answers about what the greed are, where they come from, why the leaders and the crown entice the greed so much because this was supposed to be a story-based game, but there was none of that. I won't insult the story itself, but it wasn't strong enough to justify this game as a standalone. There were some changes, sure, but outside of the "story," I think they are comparable to the changes between the base KTC and Dead Lands/Nord Lands.Don't get me wrong, I really love the mystery surrounding the greed and I don't feel like I need answers, but I think it's weird that you would make a new filter for an already established game that was meant to be narrative-driven but make the narrative in question feel like an afterthought. A lot of the castle expansion elements have been removed and not replaced with a counter-part, such as the archer/builder/knight buffs, the gems, hermits/hermit abilities, knight upgrades, etc. I dearly, dearly missed the archer buff late game and the knights are absolutely useless. Narratively, it makes sense, since they're children, but like.... why?Anyway, despite my extremely fond feelings towards KLC, I just feel apathetic about this, and I probably would've been better off spending another 6 hours on Dead Lands.

Companions don't get captured and they actively play a part in attacks.  The companions combined with the new way you coordinate offensives against the portals is without a doubt the highlight of the game, now you can push portals to your hearts content using your own characters movement to guide the squad of attackers.

_childDocuments_.review: For someone that has probably put in over 100 hours into two crowns across almost every platform. Someone that has bought two crowns on switch, iPhone, android tablet, Xbox, and PC because I love the game so much this game is an utter disappointment. I didn't even play the game for 2 hours before turning it off because it was so flat and boring and nothing in this game makes me want to start it back up. _childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: This may be a Kingdom Title but does not have the same replay-ability quality as the other series. I have sunk hundreds of hours collectively into Kingdom and Kingdom Two Crowns. Like many fans I was excited for this new entry but found it fell flat. Interesting new mechanics have been introduced and if you enjoy the solo play aspect of original Kingdom, perhaps you will have a better experience with this than I did.The loss of co-op really impacted my enjoyment of the game. Had this game come before Two Crowns, I could imagine myself being in a position to recommend it more... but as it was delivered to the community well after Two Crowns and DLC... Its a no for me. Is the game bad? No, it has its charms and nostalgic hit. If you are looking for a short resource management game with a cute story, pick this up. Otherwise, buy Kingdom Two Crowns. 👑👑
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Not Kingdom at all. Difference you may like.But that's short one for 1-2 evenings at most.All achievements in 3 runs.- 1 on hardest- 1 on easy or normal (50 days)- maybe extra level run on easy to get twins and/or 20 kids, and 1 portal on pacifist.10-18 hours for 100% of the content & 100% achievements.And this game they've been doing for so long...Also, way too easy on "cursed".Game gives almost no challenge at all.The only challenge - is last portal hordes. Last 5-10 minutes of the game.All other stuff is just routine most of the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the Kingdom Two Crowns game, even the New Lands was fun... But Kingdom Eighties was a big step back in gameplay. No more city management, no more people management, no more money management... And worst of all, no multiplayer!?The campaign is about 4 hours of gameplay (if you take your time and unlock everything).You only hire kids for two roles: Builder or Slingshot. That's it.You don't build and upgrade archer towers in this one - You build something else, but they're much simpler (and overpowered!)You don't attack both sides of your base, only one. One side you expand for money, and then fully upgrade the wall and tower... Then just turn around and push the other side without any worry behind you.Granted I can see they put a lot of effort into the story, as there are these cute little cut scenes throughout.I also noticed loads of easterieggs in the environment and the "mounts".I would have loved to see this be an upgrade from Kingdom Two Crowns, and be a much longer game, with more features, more roles, and keep all the fun nostalgia of the 80s.I look forward to Fury Studios next instalment in the Kingdom series... But unfortunately I can't recommend this Eighties "expansion"... Maybe grab it when it comes down to half price or something as a short nostalgic hit.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to post a first impressions type review as there are not many reviews as of yet and I was on the fence about mixing Kingdom with an 80's vibe.So far it's been great! There are a couple of tweaks to the standard Kingdom formula, but the overall concept is the same as previous games. I will say that two levels in I have received an actual objective to complete the level. While this still mostly boils down to the same premise (build up your camp and expand until you're strong enough to face the main enemy base), I did enjoy the addition of the completion goal.  Also, there are new ways to passively generate income within your camp, which was a welcome addition as well. "80's vibes" are super popular right now, so much so that I have started erring on the side of caution when a game goes 80's. However, Kingdom manages to not only nail the 80's vibe but do it in an enjoyable and fun way while adding some pretty cool additions to the standard Kingdom formula. These changes are more than a rad 80's paint job, making this standalone expansion well worth the price of entry, even to series veterans.I still have a while to go, so if anything changes or if I have anything to add  I will update my review, but as of now I do very much recommend this standalone expansion to Kingdom veterans and newcomers alike!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Boring. You can probably squeeze out one play through if you care enough, but this could've been so much more fun with co-op. I remember seeing a post where the devs said multiplayer doesn't fit their vision for the game. Which makes no sense, because you literally have other characters following you around and that could've easily been a friend instead of AI. They should've just had the option to play this game solo or with a friend and nobody would've complained.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played The Kingdom Franchise and wanted a good introductory game or a place to start, then look no further. Kingdom Eighties is a good starting point for those who want to try out the Kingdom games as well as a good game for the fans that enjoy New Lands more than Two Crowns. This game gets the core of New Lands and gives it a new way to use it while also adding new mechanics unique to this version of the game. The Theme of the game is also very charming if you are into the 80's pop culture aesthetic. Scattered throughout the different levels are different references to different media and even some of the things you use are from said places. The music also matches the theme with the soundtrack being more Synth heavy to match the tone of the game. The game does create a Story for this Spin-off with some cut scenes but honestly, I could have gone without the story and cut scenes since these games don't really need one. Nonetheless, it was a nice inclusion for the explanation of how the monsters got to the present day. This game is also much easier than its predecessors. It is incredibly easy to get money in the game (which can become a problem since this game does not have a Banker to store your money in the castle) and at least from what I've seen there is no Winter mechanic. Even on Hard Difficulty, the game was not so challenging but it might have to do with the fact that I am an Avid Kingdom Player and I know the game very well. I think the reason why this game is mixed and not liked as much as the previous entry is because Two Crowns added a lot of cool features to the game that are not present in this one at all. This game is supposed to be similar to New Lands and not Two Crowns. In New Lands, the game was much simpler with fewer features and this game expands on the core of that game while adding new things. It's not a bad thing, I had my fun with it, but if you wanted something like Two Crowns then maybe you might be disappointed. It doesn't help as well that this game is more linear with only 4 maps to complete and if you leave one map you can't go back to it, unlike the previous games, so if you missed something, tough luck. Regardless, as a fan of the gameplay Loop from the Kingdom games, I was satisfied and Enjoyed my time with it. It was as relaxing as all the other games and hit the Nail on the head for what a Kingdom game is supposed to be. It is short though, much shorter than the other games, so if anything Pick it up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Eighties is a must-play for fans of the series! It takes everything we loved from the previous games and cranks it up to eleven. Immersive cutscenes, simple yet challenging gameplay, and a non-hand-holding experience. It's a fun adventure! The awesome pixel art graphics, inspired by neon 80s are complemented by great chill synthwave music. In my opinion, Kingdom Eighties’s price is more than justified.Full YouTube video review available here:
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Played Kingdom Eighties. Big fan of the Kingdom games in general. Fun, challenging and the unique pixel art graphcis with the water graphics just delivers something different. You know when you're playing a Kingdom game. This one though....I won't say it's bad. Because I think that's unfair, and I wish there was a "Meh" button versus a thumbs down,  but it relies super heavy on the Stranger Things 80s nostalgia. Which is cute, it's different, but this game is also by far and away the least challenging to in the series (in my opinion). It doesn't have the depth of gameplay or expand on the Kindgom games world the way each previous iteration has. I beat the whole thing in under 5 hours...and that's not a bug - there's a Steam badge doing it. I'm a long way from a min-maxer, so that was a little unsatisfying.While it's not a bad game, especially if you like the Kingdom games, you can wait for a killer 80% off sale where it's just $3 before buying and not feel guilty about missing anything. I like a good nostalgia trip as much as the next guy...but I think this is one of those too much spice, too little steak issues. Shame - the potential was there for a really great game and really unusual expansion but this just feels so light, like so much was spent on 80s references that they really forgot the core of needing a survival/challenging game. It's okay - but it's a disappointment compared to other recent Kingdom games and what could have been.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great chance to iterate on the format of the kingdom games and mix it up a little, so it's really a shame that none of that happened. It's dismally short, basically identical to past entries, and doesn't even make good use of the theming. For goodness's sake, the intro cutscene has a kid defeat a greed monster with a slingshot, but then in game you just use regular bows & arrows like before. Come on. If you don't own any kingdom games, this isn't the one to start with, and if you do own any kingdom games, you won't have any reason to get this one since it's more of the same, so in the end, I can safely say no one should buy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing. This doesn't have the same amount of features as the original games, and hence doesn't have a lot of replay value that you can sink into it. I played it on easy because I'm old and I don't have as much time to grind away and perfect my skills on games. So I would say I beat it pretty quickly.There are some features that I wish were fleshed out more, like the use of your team-mates during the game. It feels like they are fun, but always there beside you. There is no threat to them, or consequences of losing them. The different bikes are neat but I don't feel like they vary that much like the creatures in the original except for two that I won't expound on so they don't get spoiled.The story is okay. I never felt like I needed a story to go along with gameplay I've come to love, so it was fine and moved the plot along.In the end I'd say this was pretty good, but in no way beats the original, which is a shame because this feels like a lot of love was put into it. This in no way means this game is bad. It was a lot of fun to play, but feels like it's "finished" now and there is nothing more I can do with it, other than playing on higher difficulty levels. The aesthetics and the music that accompany it are a treat, and all the little 80s and 90s easter eggs are a lot of fun to find. Be they just background elements or actual gameplay devices. However, if you liked this you would love Kingdom two crowns which also has a coop mode which is fantastic! I really love the teams that work on these properties and am excited to see what they put out next and would encourage you to support them as well. The products they create are really well done, though this one was sadly short and I hope they include some more gameplay modes in a future update!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of the series you will like it. It's easier than the previous instalments with a story to tell and the environment changes according to the story. There are no problems like fields drying out due to snow (no weather changes) or loosing the chance to increase population if you cut down trees around their settlement. You don't feel alone wandering around in your kingdom though, since you have some friends accompanying you all the time. Really beautiful pixel art with a fun short ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid follower of the Kingdom series, I must express my disappointment with Kingdom Eighties. Compared to its predecessors, this installment falls short and fails to capture the essence that made the previous games so enjoyable. Furthermore, it lacks an engaging endgame experience, a feature that was present in Two Crowns with its exciting Skull Islands and various game modes. It seems like this game was designed solely for quick profit rather than catering to the dedicated fan base that has supported the franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: While there was obviously a lot of labor put into this game, it also lacks innovation, direction and feels like a very secondary product. It's like they got a senior artist and an engineering intern and asked them to cook a mix of Kingdom and Stranger Things. This is a literal reskin of former with a flavor of later. I'm on level 4 now and there're ZERO new mechanics. They basically made the heroes on bicycles sometimes use old mechanics. Lame, lame, wouldn't ask for a refund since I just played for 3 hours, but this is a massive disrespect to your players folks.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

I know it was just something like a campain with story telling but the story is not that great it feels so forces in some areas.And the last think is, its not designed to be repetitive, its forced in some direction and thats all.Overall4/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played any of the Kingdom titles then this is a very good place to start. It's not difficult but it will ease you into the mechanics of the franchise. There is some replayability with the "Camp Stories" where the player can choose a level and see how long they can survive against an un-ending horde. Actually found this a challenge, seemed the difficulty curve ramped excessively.If you are seasoned Kingdoms player and not a completest than perhaps give it a skip unless it's on sale.Nice soundtrack and the usual "retro" graphics.Ultimately - worth a buy if on sale, unlikely to return to it now I've completed on 2 of the difficultly levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: ok, listen; I know this is Day 1 of release. Holy crap though!!! I've already played more then three hours! _childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like Ready Player One. It lists a lot of things that you like, but once you start paying attention it's basically void from meaning.In general, it is a step down from Two Crowns: Graphics in general are confusing, everything blends in - sometimes can't tell things from the from the background or bushes in the foregroundSome units have no use, like the Squires. or the recruited children with no weapons that run straight to the activities, but then wander weaponless for a while.Story makes little sense, it's like "ah we should make the player go from A to B in the story with... uuhm. A canoe? A super slow drawbridge? A van that goes trhough walls!" and it's just a bit over 4hs to complete.And in gameplay terms, it feels that you are being held by the devs as they point you exactly which way to go, with little to no reward if you explore the rest of the islands, no statues-like mechanics, seasons, etc.Overall it's a poor attempt of get some nostalgia and story altogether in a game. Maybe with some fixes and DLCs in the future it can turn over.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, it's just... meh.They didn't really fix any of the issues with the Kingdom series.  There's always been the problem of challenge, either it's mind numbingly easy, or you get completely rolled over with no chance.  There's never anything in between.  And here it's worse than usual.Some random thoughts:  Gems are gone (which is nice).  Still can't queue up multiple builds (so you have to babysit wall construction).  The kids are really hard to see/differentiate.  There's a lot of visual clutter.  The music is.. ok.  Don't imagine it's going to have a lot of replayability.  The kid chores are quite funny and charming.If you're a Kingdom fan you'll probably like it.  For anyone else, Two Crowns is a better game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly love the kingdom series and have played the games over multiple accounts (phone too) for many, many hours. So seeing this was announced instantly got me very hyped. i instant bought it on release day. The sad thing is tho is that the game is way to short. i didn't rush anything, just played with the sense to progress and not really fool around and beat the game in 2,5 hours. I don't really see any replay ability either bcs its more story based (which also was imo pretty lackluster and way to little) and 2 crowns is just way better for replay ability. Imo 11 euros ain't worth it, maybe if they add more content but not right now. Just stick to two crowns.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: The new 'islands'/realms vary in a neat way but overall the game just has very little depth. As a result the game is really, really short and it has very little replay value. I love the art design and new additions like changes to towers, money production and sieging but if anything they make the game much easier.  If this is the 'platform' going forward I'd check it out again but as someone who has played and replayed two crowns a bunch I can't see myself replaying this for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: honestly i'd call this the game you choose if your not sure if you like the style of kingdom gameplay mostly due to the fact 80s is much more forgiving than the other entries for example you only need to worry about archers, builders and knights rather than having all the money gathering jobs.but i will say this 10/10 would send an assorted dozen children into a portal to kill all the monsters inside.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really worse than previous chapters. There's only 1 campaign and it has only 4 missions in it. It will take only 6-9 hours to complete them even on a hard level. There will be no point to re-play it. Gameplay hasn't changed except for some details, which is not bad, it's actually good (except the game is really easier now).Also, I know this game is not about any lore or story, it's about gameplay, however, they did some story and lore here, and it is SO BAD and CRINGE so I cannot keep silence about it. Well, if you are a fan of previous games - you will be most likely satisfied. I've enjoyed myself playing it too, won't lie, but it's mixed with a very big disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend playing Kingdom Two Crowns instead which is way more fun. Not beginner friendly, since it doesn't explain a lot of the mechanics on what they do, just "Stand here". Normal mode is incredibly easy and you will be rolling in huge amount of coins, so you will just end up throwing them in water or trying to save them by throwing so much excessive coins on the ground, though there is not much things to spend them on either. It's also hard to see the kids that you need to recruit because of the cluttered graphics. The 'Catapult' or the Dumpster in this game is worse to use then previous games, because if you want to destroy one side of the portal, you will have to slowly drag it from across the opposite side of the game if you destroyed a portal for the other side previously, as they only give you one, rather than two like the previous game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted more gameplay not less and some weird generic animated story. Beat it in 5 hours which is better than portal I guess. But I don't feel compelled to play it again or do anything more in the game unlike the previous versions I probably played for more than 100 hours and purchased on multiple platforms.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: The game is mostly focused around the story.unlike the previous Kingdom games - Kingdom Eighties makes you go through dialog, cut scenes and character intros to continue on with the game. It can be quite annoying as I'm use to just being able to do whatever I wanted and go wherever in the previous games. It felt like I had fewer options in this one and less freedom to have fun with the game. On the other hand, the art style remains the same which is a huge relief - can't say the same about the cut scenes which feel rather odd and unusual for Kingdom games. Can't say that the characters in cut scenes are what i picture Kingdom characters to look like, but it's not completely terrible either.However, the monsters look just about the same. Few changes were made to make them suit the Eighties aesthetic and few new monsters were also added which i actually quite liked. Specially the crab one.Overall, the game is not bad. Definitely prefer the Kingdom Two Crowns and New Lands games over this one, but I still recommend playing this one to see for yourself what I was talking about. Maybe someone else would enjoy this more than me.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Could be better, but it's alrightI've beaten the game in less than 5 hours by accident. I wanted to explore more, but didn't, and I don't want to after I finished the game. The gameplay is, compared to the originals, really lacking, nothing that could keep my attention for more than 5 seconds.The game is more storyline focused, instead of the "building your own empire" theme the originals had. The Story is sadly easily forgettable and feels like Stranger Things Season 1. The Story that is in there is pretty much only there to serve the gameplay and the setting.I would still recommend it, since I didn't had a bad time playing it, but I would recommend refunding it immediately if you don't enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good and I finished it in about 9.2 hours, on Hard, on my first playthrough.The cutscenes are fine and the overall story was nice.Some parts of the gameplay were kind of irritating. For example there is no way of teleporting and to recruit new troops you have to travel back and forth way to much.Especially the last island this is annoying and it just takes way to long to finish without providing anything new. Something I've noticed and I was really irritated by, was the fact that the time needed to insert coins to buy new stuff was way longer than in any other Kingdom games.Asside from this, I was pretty satisfied after completing the game. I had no performance problems and the game ran smoothly.Some of the new contents were pretty nice additions to the Kingdom series, for example: the coin bucket you unlock after the first island or the Siege Barrier and Siege Turret.Additionally, Instead of archer towers you can build centry turrets which are pretty op and where essential in completing my Cursed playthrough.Apart from this, I really, really enjoyed the different mount options and found myself enjoying every single one of them. In the end I used the Gear Bike the most because I found it to be the most efficient.Lastly, I really liked the way the companions worked and would love to see more adittions to the Kingdom series just like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: It's disappointing to see such a step backwards after the big step forward in Two Crowns. Pros/improvements from Two Crowns:- Visuals - The art and backgrounds are great. In most areas, it's pretty easy to see the difference between the buildings. Not always though.- Music- Pacing - Has a story, sort of, and the levels themselves feel ok although they're too short. Cons- Short - I did two play throughs in 9 hours. I shouldn't have played the second time. I was hoping there was something different I'd find or something I missed the first time. There wasn't. Realistically, this is a 4.5 hour game.- Towers are too OP - Walls close to the start and a long line of towers is gonna whittle down anything you fight so there are just crumbs left at the end. I normally wouldn't mind, but it makes archers mostly irrelevant. - No explanation for the buildings - This is par for the course for this game which is normally fine, but it doesn't work in this one because every stage has different buildings. You beat the level not even sure what some things do pretty consistently. I just activated them then left. Sometimes there were coins when I came back by. - No explanation for the mounts plus a weird way of activating the skills - Good lord do I hate Stickey Keys which activates every 10 seconds when you're using some of the mounts. Overall, this is the first in the series that really disappointed me which is sad because it was the one I was most looking forward to. Oh well. Guess I got my money's sort of worth?
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Game is quite short even for a Kingdom standardPros: - Coin is easier to earn, with multiple stations generating income fast and not locked between seasons.- The towers can serve as a wall, providing more options for retreat.- Overall some new Ideas that can freshen it up for older playersCons:- Game time is relatively short- Enemies dont ramp up in power- Units like knights dont serve a purpose, entirely replaced with new mechanic- The maps all feel the same, no Hermits or additional upgrades unlocked past map 1/2 making the rest a chore.Overall I hope they add more updates to the mechanics of the game as it ended up stale halfway through. . I'm not sure if I can recommend this one if you haven't played through the original one, though it is easier and can serve as an entry point.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Day 1 its not as good as k2c. It is still very good. I think most negative reviews stem from the fact that it doesnt match k2c in quality. What there is is good though.A whole lot of new mechanics, its not just an expansion. Right now, it feels a little unfinished. The story seems simplified and the script is very weak. Some mechanics just seem pointless (knights seem to serve no purpose now??). Removing the gem mechanic probably makes me disappointed the most, I liked this.I haven't seen any game breaking bugs yet, however on higher difficulties, reworked villager spawn can kind of brick your run.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, like all the other Kingdom games. The cut-scenes have cool animation, but they are not needed, and gives the game a different feeling or vibe from the other Kingdom games. I like the new mounts that allow you to destroy the greed.The biggest problem with the game, as others have said, is that it's missing co-op mode. I think co-op would make this game a lot more fun to play.I would recommend this game to people who don't use co-op.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve loved all the other Kingdom games. But for me, this one is kind of boring. The story is lame and none of your decisions matter. As long as you have enough gold, there’s no consequence to chopping down every tree and building every wall.The design is not well thought out at all. The previous kingdom games made it very clear what every building and person did. With this one, the only difference between the people you’ve hired or not are if they’re still at the playground. And you need some unknown number of hired but jobless people because they’ll go to the economy buildings that seem to use between 1-3, with more crowded around, doing nothing.The omission of multiplayer also sucks. It’s why I continue to replay Two Crowns again and again. But this one, I just don’t have interest in playing more.One thing this shares with all the previous games is that it’s too easy. They recommend cursed difficulty for experienced players. But really, cursed here should be the default. The turrets become secondary walls. And if the greed break through, the turrets keep shooting. Again, there’s no decision making. Just max out everything and it’s virtually impossible to lose unless that’s what you’re trying to do by taking as many days as possible.The kingdom games have always had amazing soundtracks. But this one, like every other aspect of the game, is just ok. Sure, it fits the theme. But I don’t find myself wanting to listen to it outside of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic addition to the Kingdom's franchise, new mechanics that are fun to incorporate into existing strategies, GORGEOUS artwork, more 80's nostalgia than you can shake a snap-bracelet at, and challenging new levels that have a great puzzle aspect to them. Music is top tier as always. A great step in the right direction after Kingdoms: Norse Lands, just really crushing it all around. If you've enjoyed playing Two Crowns, you do not want to skip this game. At this rate, I will be buying and playing Kingdoms games as long as they keep making them!!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: The first kingdom game with a narrative scenario-like structure to its levels. Single player only but a positive surprise with overall good tweaks and additions compared to previous entries. Can be beaten in about 4-5 hours with no hassle but offers a more enduring challenge at higher difficulty. Special mentions for the addition of cutscenes, half-a-dozen relevant easter eggs and the a very fitting artstyle and music.I must mention though how for an old kingdom fan some of the game's quirks can feel weird (like squires only being useful for defense) and you might be confused as to how to truly win the last level . Still, especially for its price it's a very solid experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: More of the same but with different mechanics. Still fun and addictive, a bit less repetitive than the previous episodes, more story-based.I only regret that it’s only four chapters, finished it already :'( (in 9 hours). _childDocuments_.review: I have played all of the other Kingdom games and DLC, and find this one a great addition to the collection. You may see negative reviews saying it is just a "reskin" and has nothing new, but this is false: there are plenty of new game mechanics and lots of cool unexpected things to discover if you play long enough and take the time to explore. The game is indeed shorter than Kingdom 2 Crowns, but that is to be expected as it is a fraction of the price, is story-driven, and has none of the additional DLC's and updates that 2 Crowns got over the years (YET!). I finished the game on hard difficulty in 8.5 hours, which is longer than most, as I take my time enjoying things rather than rushing through. I got 65% achievements, and will have to play all the way through at least 2 more times to get 100% achievements, so there is some replay-ability. It is worth the price-tag, even if they don't release new content in the future (which I expect them to do, as is evidenced by how much work they put into 2 Crowns after its release). All-in-all I found it to be very entertaining and loved the many Easter eggs!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Good to see devs experiment with some new ideas, but they feel really half-baked. Which wouldn't be that great of a deal, if the variety that already existed in older games was included here too - but it isn't.Bland story, linear and short campaign, no coop, greatly simplified economy and gameplay on general. Artistically the game got way less coherent in a "pixel soup" way, which maybe was intentional, but it makes the end product look, and feel worse. You can even pick it up in music, with some tracks sounding like they belong in earlier games, and some actually playing into that eighties aesthetic.If you've never played the earlier games, Kingdom Eighties isn't that bad, honestly. Short and sweet, enjoyable experience that doesn't overstay its welcome. But if you did, then I can't recommend it at all, as many good things you might've liked New Lands for are now gone, and what you receive in return isn't nearly as good.

_childDocuments_.review: A big step backwards for the series.  I loved the new graphics for the world and the characters, but it did feel overly cluttered at times.  The animation and the writing during the cut-scenes though, I couldn't stand.  They've removed multiplayer which was one of my favorite aspects of the previous games.  They removed gems leaving coins as the sole currency, which allows you to just get everything right away.  You can no longer go back to previous stages, which you won't need to because, again, no gems.I was truly excited for this release.  Two Crowns is one of my favorite games.  I can't count the number of times that I've replayed it both solo and co-op.  I won't be replaying this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really feel like the linear story fit the game well. Other Kingdom games had implied lore, but ultimately let you fill in why your monarch was doing what they were doing. This game has a story, and it's a very bare-bones story that's essentialy "save these people" and it's not compelling at all. I honestly feel that the story segments detract from the game - everything that was done in the cutscenes could have just been shown more effective in-game without switching art styles. There is also only the option  to play the campaign, and no way to jump between islands in free play like previous games. There's so much less content in Kingdom 80's than there is in Kingdom: New Land. I played for four hours, and I feel like I've seen and done everything there is to see. This game is significantly easier than the other games in the series. Making money is not a challenge, the Greed are not a challenge, and the dumpster and laser robot clear house on nearly anything that's attacking your walls. I was on the offensive more often than I was on the defensive, which is noticeably the opposite to the previous games.

_childDocuments_.review: i've played two of the previous installments in the series and it was great to get used to the gameplay in both. they also felt significant enough to warrant a full release, well worth my time. it's too bad we're not talking about those previous installments instead of this one. they're VERY fun, and if only my partner could get into the gameplay (he might, after beating this one!) i'd beat them again in co-op. the main points of a *Kingdom* game would be the addictive and at first relatively simplistic nature of the gameplay loop. that's basically it, but the stripped down nature of the games is the real appeal of it, the high grade flash game quality of the series. if you want what i consider to be the experience of the series, try another game whose flavor is to your liking--you'll probably love it. here's the rub. this game is a bizarre backstep on a formula that must have been well-trod and practiced by the developers. much of the problems have been explained in detail, in some cases far better than i would have. whatever you see repeated in more than one review is the truth. the positives of this installment are the unique setting, the soundtrack, and the 80's flavor. in my opinion, as lovely as the gameplay art (itself an upgrade from the quality of the other entries, i have to admit) is, i would call the 80's flavor not a compliment to the overall experience, but a distraction in the least and a smokescreen for what has been lobotomized at the worst. in comparison to, say, *Grounded*, which utilizes a 90's setting in a way that reflects on many aspects of the game in a way that feels fun, *Eighties* uses nostalgia and blatant call-backs as a crutch. if i wanted to be cruel, i would call this a cynical cash grab in the vein of trying to rplicate the devotion caused by *Stranger Things*. i didn't see the problems clearly until i was at the last level and realized how short and dumbed down the whole experience really was. by then all that was left was to beat it, much like the experience of eating a cheap enough meal but still feeling unfulfilled and a little greasy as i was staring down the barrel of eating the last few bites of it before i could leave. around $10 is cheap enough, sure, but an experience is still an investment of time and money is still money. if this had been released as a free update in another game or something like a *Blood Dragon* add-on, perhaps that expectation would have turned this into a different experience. the problem is that the dumbing down, even if it was a lower cost of entry than a standalone game, would still be evident. as it stands, the four levels that make up the experience feel like the first half of the real game, in terms of the pacing, the difficulty, and the story. the length does the game a great disservice and i didn't feel really invested in any aspect of the game in a meaningful manner.unfortunately, even though it wasn't a horrific experience i can't think of a way to recommend this, as the better games in the series exist already.

Lack of enemy varietyNo indication of homeless vs recruited childrenReduced the amount of upgrades overallKnights serve no purposeNo special army or worker unitsThe mounts mostly are mostly just mobility upgradesStory is added for the sake of stitching levels together.Game is way too short. _childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting take on the kingdom series but seems a little short, even with all achievements taking less than 20 hours even with me taking my time and 3 playthroughs. I personally found the game a little too easy even on the hardest difficulty. Slight spoilers ahead. Once you unlock the towers, defense becomes a joke since, unlike towers in other kingdom games, these ones do not require builders, making them risk free to build many and far from your walls, plus they dont have levels and only 3 can shut down waves completely even in insane difficulty (at least up to day 10). Plus the vending machines on the last level, while only usable once theyre in groups of three, just make getting money too easy.Some features also seem to have basically no purpose. The "Knights" unlike in the base series lost their ability to attack, so now theyre purely defensive, but it doesnt seem important with the new towers combined with the new tower walls. Also one of the new greed enemies, the shooty guys were probably supposed to be annoying and snipe archers or something, but they just shoot the walls even when the walls are low level, basically acting like slower attacking greed. They do stand further away, which might seem like something interesting, but as soon as you kill their leader - the other new greed weaker "Tanks", they run away even if other greed are present. An argument can be made, that this game was created not for difficulty, but for the new way to play in a story mode and the atmosphere of the 80s, which it seems to do a good job at (not an 80s kid, so cant really say). But if the setting means nothing to you, then it doesnt really help the game.I would only recommend this game if you love the theme, or you have played all a lot of other kingdom games and want a similar, yet with slightly changed and a few new mechanics, game.
