_childDocuments_.review: This has been an interesting take on the Kingdom formula. Let's get the elephant out of the way first: There is no co-op in this game. This was announced over a year ago, so this wasn't a surprise, just a slight bummer after Kingdom Two Crowns. At the time of that announcement, they mentioned the co-op was not included due to how they want to have the game's story play out.So there is a story in this game. Previous games in the Kingdom series were similar to a "rogue-lite" although without really having many of the mechanics of typical rogue-lites. Previously, you had islands you visited, structures you built and the lay of the land could stick around after lengths of time pass while your character is away from the island or dead, and getting killed would send you back to the first of 5 islands, devoid of a story. Kingdom Eighties is not like the older Kingdom games.Kingdom Eighties takes on a 1980's theme, full of references to many 80 movies and pop culture. Instead of the usual 5 islands that would act as a form of progression, hiding secrets that will require you to return to those islands later on via a boat, this island game mechanic has also not returned with the latest game. Instead, you play through 4 levels with linear gameplay (go to A, go to B, collect C, upgrade D, destroy E, etc...) with cutscenes placed in specific locations activated by spending a single coin. The story is sort of a classic 80's movie theme of some "strange things" happening in town, four friends get together, save the town and their parents. It's cheesy like the 80's, but that is the point. This is supposed to be a reason you're buying the game, so keep in mind that if you dislike 1980's style story and references, you're not going to like this game.There are "chores" that your builders can do in order to earn you extra coins if you're running low. These will require an available builder to do. If you have something you need to build and all of your builders are busy doing chores, they will stop doing chores to do other duties. "Archer Towers" are now unmanned, Squires still exist, pikemen do not. There are a lot of differences between this game and the previous games, definitely proving why this could not have simply been a downloadable skin/theme for Two Crowns. Many of the levels even have "vagrant camps" in the form of indestructible buildings that you can't destroy by accident this time. My extended playtime for my playthrough was due to mistakenly destroying the trees bordering the only actual "vagrant camps" in the final level. I was prepared for this earlier, but since indestructible camps appeared in the first few levels, I wasn't expecting it to return on the final level. If you do destroy your "vagrant camps" (okay, we all call them vagrant camps, but they are just all children you are hiring, I'm not gonna admit to child labor here) you can build a house in place of the camp, but it will cost 5 coins per vagrant instead of 1 coin. This is sill better than the alternative, you know this if you've played the previous games.Due to the mistake I made, it took me about 6 hours instead of the typical 4-5 hours that it sounds to be taking other players to complete the campaign. I also didn't know until after finishing the campaign, that this whole time I could have moved the garbage dumpster (mobile barricade, it's required for destroying portals) across to the other half of the map. This wasn't obvious. The dumpster is typically located and pointing in the direction of your level-objective (cave, etc) so you'll have to drag it back towards your home base before you see the npcs turn it around and face it the other way. This is how you clear both ends of the map. You will want to clear both ends of each map. There is no lighthouse, but you will get goodies still, like a larger coin purse. There are also additional mounts (bikes) for you to find. Many will have abilities seen in other kingdom games, such as faster mobility while in the forest, or a machine gun, or a flame trail.This is not the best Kingdom game ever, but it does have the 80's charm and the quality of life changes in this game will likely make this the most accessible Kingdom game for new players unfamiliar with the series to jump right in, and maybe get them interested in New Lands or Two Crowns. I would say this game is worth the current price at 10% off, or even full price, as this is still cheaper than going to a movie theater today. If you are new to the series, it's far more friendly than the previous games. If you are a veteran of this series, maybe give Hard or Cursed difficulties a shot, otherwise you might not think this game challenging enough to scratch the itch.

_childDocuments_.review: Loving It So Far:Only a couple of hours in and finished chapter 2 but much of the good stuff from previous Kingdom games is here mixed with some great new additions and mechanics to make is feel fresh. The addition of a story with cutscenes is the biggest new addition alongside some new mechanics, tools and weapons which I won't spoil. The music is great as it is with all the Kingdom games. _childDocuments_.review: Like summer, this kingdom game is short and sweet. Definitely a must play, not as conventionally hard as the other games in the series but it does bring about its own challenges in the Cursed difficulty and the ever random endless mode aptly called Mix Tapes. Compared to the other games of the series, there is a few of the ever present staples missing like the flying enemies, towers and certain units. While the Greeds did lose the aerial superiority, they made up for it with visibly upgraded units and freaking mortar. Though not to be outdone, losing the towers is a big change but the trade off is you get turrets! OP in every way which contributes to it being easier (which is a testament to how ramped up Cursed difficulty is even with the turrets). A lot of good things and features in this game and I, personally, view it as a sort of fun playable testing phase to bring the good stuff to future games. Definitely satisfied and hopefully they continue the story in this game via future DLCs or, even better, a future game in the form of a sequel or a brand new game altogether. Enjoy! Also, the achievements are pretty straightforward and easy to do bar some of the challenging/grindy ones. Though not as grindy and not as frustrating to get as the ones from past games in the series. This game is also Steam Deck playable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a shorter more linear game than Kingdom: Two Crowns. There are some fun variations on the mechanics such as the siege barrier. The game seems a little easier to me than Two Crowns, but that's what 'hard' and 'cursed' are for. Overall an enjoyable little game.

_childDocuments_.review: I blame Sweet Baby Inc for stealing my money and time :> no wonder this game is BSAfter the release of Baldur's Gate 3 and the immense impact it brought. I believe game devs and studios should now more than ever be on their toes when it comes to the quality of games they try to sell to us. I am already disappointed with how lacking this game was for me. And now more so because I felt cheated out of my time and money in this game.I love the Kingdom games and with Two Crowns, I really thought it would be just another great step forward for the game but it's not. One may argue that the devs have made it clear that this was a stand-alone game and very linear in nature, but this just shows the evident disconnect the devs and publishers have with their consumers.I can attest that most of the people that bought the game despite the lengthy time since Two Crown bought this one BECAUSE of their love of Two Crowns and its DLC. And this game robbing the players of what made the games great in the first place is makes Kingdom Eighties nothing short of a quick cash grab.That said, I mean no ill intent but a clean cut-throat updated review. I highly DON'T recommend this game because I would rather suggest you buy Kingdom Two Crowns or even the original Kingdoms.Because then despite the meager price, you have had your money's worth with the music, the visuals and the gameplay Kingdoms truly has to offer.not this.- cute retro pixel art style- new color palette, love the cute pink trees- the references - a new concept of using bikes as a steed - no more banking system despite the fact there's a LITERAL BANK. I really miss our accountant- very linear gameplay. There's no point in maximizing the structures and walls in an island because you are forced to continue to the next chapter. Thus no replayability.- Can't change your monarch - singleplayer. Seeing the trailer at first, I was excited to see 4 monarchs riding their bikes thinking you can have up to 4 players in a game. It's not- The game carries your hand too much. It's annoying- The cutscenes are fine at the start of the game, introducing to us the story. But not when it's every few minutes. ________________________________________________________This game makes a reference to . Further questioning the decision of making the game singleplayer. Wouldn't it be accurate to the story since that is what supposedly shown?I wish they would make distinctions with the bikes or give them abilities like horns or a basket for carrying.The hermits in the previous games were nice because they give you reason to leave the island, explore, expand, and subsequently return to previous islands to further improve the settlements. I think it would be better that the "hermits" of this era were the NPCs we meet. (1) The jock with the ability to ride bikes alongside the monarch and pulling the seige. (2) The tinkerer/DIY expert unlocking upgrades or repairing buildings and staying primarily at the center of the kingdom taking logistics and banking. and (3) the Wiz in charge with the artillery/weapons making robots and upgrade to our bike. Having all 3 in bikes is cool to look at but they have so much more potential with their function.And since all of them can use bikes and run over greed, there's no survival factor for the monarch because of these "bodyguards". It's way too safe to actually lose your crown.If the game made it so that we loot/find or combine bike parts for the hermits/NPCs to allow the gang to progress to another location, that would be a far more interesting challenge than just "mass child labor".And coop. The game is far more enjoyable as multiplayer. AND profitable for the Devs too because two copies will have to be bought.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many of the other negative reviews posted already, this is a contextual thumbs down. If you've never played a Kingdom game and you like the look of this one, I do recommend this as a sort of "training" game or starter set for the real game in the series, Kingdom Two Crowns. The art style is awesome, the team you build around the protagonist helps out with different tasks which is fun, but ultimately it feels very easy and more repetitive compared to the other games in this series. There are few secrets to uncover or discover; if you're looking for boost statues, for example, you won't find them here (at least not as far as I've gotten in chapter 3 of 4). I keep expecting something new to show up "on the next map," but nothing really does, except for a few art assets. It's a beautiful game, as all of their games are. I thought the concept was fun and I think it's adorable that you hire tiny children to work for you instead of grown peasants/homeless people/campers? I'll probably finish it just to see the ending. The story cut scenes are cute and well executed. Ultimately, the gameplay itself is shallow and disappointing, and I'm sad about it. This was an instant buy for me because of their previous work, but due to the simplicity and emptiness of this title I won't be instant buying in the future. I hope their next one offers a bit more interest.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:-I finished this game in 4h in normal mode.Unlike the other Kingdoms, you only have to worry about one side of the map in this one. So there is this massive drop in difficulty in this entry. If you have already played through any of the previous Kingdoms, play on the hard or cursed difficulty. -The writing and presentation is kinda poor. Voice acting would have been a great addition-Compared to the other games where any mounts other than the starting horse have a purpose, about half the mounts in this one barely affect your gameplay. There is no point in using a mount that leaves a trail of fire that damages enemies but immobilises your allies.-To add to the lack of interesting mounts gameplay-wise, there are no shrines or any kind of events to bring variety to your play-through. Norselands and Deadlands had characters/events that would give different powers/ skills and they were all useful or interesting. There are different characters here but you cant switch and they just follow you around and do their stuff which again, dramatically makes the game easier.Pros:-Excellent art direction as usual.-Excellent music and good sound design.Heavily inspired by Stanger Things with other references here and there.Overall its a big step backward but its the kind of release that will make the devs realise what to do and what not to do in their next gamesBecause of how short the game is and how there's no replay-ability, i cant recommend this game for more than 10$

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to preface this by saying that I love Kingdom as a series and I'm currently working on the final two achievements I need to complete it, but this game is by far my least favorite of them all. The 80s theme is kind of neat and the art and mini movies are wonderful, but personally I wish Raw fury had spent another year developing a fully fleshed out game rather than a pamphlet's worth of gameplay.Also the main character being bi-racial in a well off family (His dad owns a brick phone. Those things cost a literal fortune), with a group of minority kids who are all camp counselors in the 1980s in middle-America is kind of way too on the nose for forced diversity. _childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fine addition to the Kingdom franchise. The devs really outdid themselves on the graphics this time; I counted at least 6 layers of parallax on the final level, possibly 7, and they've beautifully evoked the 80s setting with details like the winding roads lined with streetlights on the mountains, miniature movie posters on the mall cinema, groups of teens on bikes, etc. Half the fun of this particular game is spotting all the references. I saw some grumbling on the discussion forums about how weird it is to have little kids fighting the Greed. Well... it's accurate to the time period. Movies from that era were very willing to depict little kids in harm's way. I immediately thought of Wednesday Addams organizing a riot during the Thanksgiving play in Addams Family Values, or Ke Huy Quan playing Short Round in Indiana Jones: Temple of Doom. I'm sure other people can chime in with better examples, but those are just the two that come to mind first.I hope the mechanic of armies automatically gathering at the correct side for the Blood Moon gets backported to Kingdom Two Crowns, because that was extremely handy.My biggest critique of the game is that it's much, much too easy, even on Cursed difficulty, for someone who has beaten Norse Lands in a single reign. The low difficulty level and forgiving gameplay is the most period-inaccurate thing about this title. Bring back Crownstealers, ramp the waves faster, proc multiple Breeders a night, something! I'm also playing the game less than a week after release, so there's a few issues with polish that will get addressed in the next month or two. The most glaring thing was that the trophy on the first level will occasionally fail to pop after it's paid for. If that happens to you, just save and quit and then reopen the game -  if you move too far, you'll make your last save unplayable and have to restart the level entirely, which is annoying. I also noticed a few small things, like archers sometimes having higher priority on coin pickup than Leader. If you buy it in six months, though, those things should be fixed.I hope there will be some challenge island expansions or DLC for this game. I liked the setting and I wish there was more playable content. In the meantime, it was fun to have a Zombies Ate My Neighbors-type storyline game and I definitely enjoyed it. Good job, you guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

Highly recommend this tubular game!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game but it's way too short. _childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: well, with a lot of regret I leave this negative review and hope the developers see it. First of all, yes, it is a good game, however, compared to the previous ones, it is far below in terms of quality. I will list some points.I have more than 550 hours of kingdom two crowns and it is a game that I am really like. Starting from the base using new lands, two crowns, dead lands and mainly norse lands, these games took everything that was good and improved it, added new mechanics and everything was enriched. A new map in the norse lands was added and that was great, totaling 6. I would like more difficulties or map editors, to have the possibility of having a map with 8 or 9 portals but that is another case, it is as a suggestion .Returning to the kingdom eighties.About graphics - The game is beautiful, certainly made with a lot of love and commitment and is the most beautiful of the series.About mechanics - It looks like a demo to me and has much less stuff than the previous ones. There are only two professions, builders and archers. There is practically no strategy and the advancement also does not allow exploration, everything must follow linearly and in a correct progression, no exploring until the end of the map or recruiting in distant camps, having to attract animals for hunting, using different powers of mounts to help at some point.Main problem - In addition to the difficulty being very easy, there is no coopAbout difficulty - Really very easy. In cursed mode I finished without losing the crown once and I didn't have any challenge, I finished it in just one afternoon of play and most of it advanced mechanically because there was no challenge.About the size of the game - it's very short, small maps and very easy money.in short - It's a great game and very beautiful, but compared to norse lands it is really inferior and limited. Play with an open mind and avoid comparing or you will be frustrated.Suggestions for improvements to other modes, whether this game or updates to the franchise or even new games:1 - First, coop.2 - More difficulty always including the enemies that fly on the blood moons, the guardhouses must be useful to shoot down these monsters (in the norse lands they don't exist, but I would add, currently I play with making challenges of simply finishing the game without losing the crown once, without changing mounts, without using special weapons or powers and without doing berserk - berserkers break the game - , just to create a higher difficulty, so I really miss that, more complex challenges and more enemies, more portals. I want to see 10 walls being broken and need to bribe enemies with money). More portals to be destroyed, something that forces me to have to survive until year  4 or 5 to complete the game and that makes it really difficult.3 - Reinforcing the points I made in the game's mechanics, the different professions greatly enrich the game. Having the strategies of building a farmer instead of an archer to produce money, or using the money to activate an effect of an elder on some tower to generate some special power, these strategy mechanics have a big impact. The game needs more difficulty to add more strategy, wrong actions could be more punishing and careful strategies could be more required in cursed difficulty. I understood that the mechanics and idea is different and this game is narrative, it is another game and with other mechanics, but compared to norse lands it is inferior. The fact of having a bank to store the coins, seasons of the year, all of this adds up to the strategies and creates a more careful, more immersive paceFinally, I really like this game a lot and I have a great affection for it, I leave the negative review here to draw attention and also with regret, because I do not want to evaluate this game negatively. A big thank you for creating this franchiseI hope my criticisms are productive or of some use, I hope it reaches the developers and many thanks again. sorry for the negative review

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was something between yes and no for recommending the game, it's not BAD I did enjoy it, and if you enjoyed the other kingdom games you will probably like this too.The addition of cut scenes and what feels like more of a story was also nice I liked the characters.But it feels much shorter then previous games and without any new mechanics that jump out and help it be it's own thing.Hoping the DLC will help add more but for 10 bucks for 4-6 hours of playtime it's not bad.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very short, with limited replay value, I think, as it standsThat said, it is absolutely charming.  I think the graphics are great, the music is wonderful and the game play is simplified in all the right ways for newer players.  I enjoyed the cutscenes and overall the story was very nostalgic. _childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game I really do, but everything that made this game fun, re-playable and exciting was taken away. _childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Eighties was a different spin on the usual Kingdom games, I disagree with many of the current reviews saying that its "too short" and needs co-op. Personally I've never played any Kingdom game with other people and the 3-5 hour game is very re-playable, especially if you like getting achievements and there's a infinite mode unlocked once you beat the main game. As always with Kingdom games, the art and music is unique and beautiful. Although the plot was weak, I appreciate Raw Fury trying something new. The Stranger Things-esk vibes tied in with Kingdom lore behind it, while also beginning the game at a summer camp felt so interesting and fresh. The beginning and ending animations were great and the characters didn't have a whole lot of depth but it makes sense not to for this kind of game.I do think that the main character the "LEADER", did need more facial expressions for the cut-scenes. The diversity of the main characters within the game was great! There were many throw backs to 80's references and technology which were fun and all the different mounts were awesome to use! (I did have an issue not being able to use any of the special abilities that some mounts had like jumping or shooting)Overall, a solid game with great graphics and music that I would highly recommend! 11/10

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I have spent too many hours on the Kingdom Series and have been waiting for this one with much eagerness. I absolutely love the new mechanics and the new take on the game. The children are a little hard to differentiate between vagrants and funded ones, but that's minor. Game is also considerably more challenging than the original series and I love that about it!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: The devs clearly put a ton of love and attention into this game.I played through yesterday, and my wife has been playing today, and we keep finding new little things. It's great!The fact that every level features variations for the camp, archer and builder stations, job posts, etc is such a cool touch, and definitely took more work to pull off compared to the previous games.The companions are a unique twist. Sort of a combo between a mount ability and unique builder that follows you around. I dig it.The dumpster (siege barrier) is an awesome mechanic. It's way more than just a knight swap like some have said. It's a whole diff vibe to be able to assault a portal and actually stay alive if they launch a counter attack by moving backward and attacking. I hope they add something similar to future "normal" Kingdoms as well. The turrets... Nuff said. Freaking awesome. I love that you can use them as towers that enemies can pass by, or build them up as barricades.The chores mechanic to replace farming makes way more sense with this theme.  In the 80's every kid had chores or some kind of little side hustle. I love the variety of things for them to do as well. From lawn mowing to recycling to serving pizzas... Love all the details that went into making so many unique interactions.So many Easter eggs! For anyone who grew up in that era, there are so many nostalgic things to recognize, from the popular to the mundane. It's all there.YeaSome people loath the 80's aesthetic. I read comments about it being "too much" or "cluttered" or "overwhelming" but... It kinda be like that though. Personally, I think they nailed it. In a good way!I REALLY hope they continue to add to this game like they have with Two Crowns. I woukd love a game mode similar to New Lands, that isn't attached as rigidly to the story. Also Co-Op would great. But as it is now, I still love it. Just hoping this is just the beginning of more updates and expansions to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game, similar to the others in the Kingdom series. Gameplay is more simple, defense with turrets makes it even easier.I really like the 80s vibe (like Stranger Things and cameos of that era, music, neon), addition of a story and diverse scenery. It is a shame it is relatively short (hoping for DLC or similar themed Kingdom games, think Goonies).As to the actual changes to gameplay, the actual destruction of greed gates requires a little bit more strategy, with moving your 'flexible wall' and support back and forth to prevent destruction from a heavy wave. The turrets (as mentioned before) have serious power, that can even withstand blood moons, so there isn't that much of stressful moments if your defense holds, or if you need to build multiple layers. Money is very easy to generate, same as 'hiring', so in the end the whole game is easier.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: The game evokes vibes reminiscent of "Crossing Souls" but appears to be a spinoff of that title. Despite this, it manages to deliver an enjoyable gameplay experience with a passable plot, and it runs smoothly, which is a definite positive for me.While the cutscenes featured throughout the episodes are somewhat lacking in substance, offering no voiceovers and minimal animation, the gameplay compensates for these shortcomings. Although there is a fair amount of repetitive left-and-right movement and coin collection, it doesn't take away from the overall enjoyment of the game. After a few repetitions, you'll find yourself completing the tasks with ease.Overall, Kingdom Eighties offers a fun and engaging gaming experience, despite its similarities to "Crossing Souls" and the limited production values of its cutscenes. If you can overlook these minor drawbacks, you're in for an enjoyable gaming adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I unfortunately had high hopes for this as I have played all of the other games in the kingdom series. Tldr, a lot of mechanics which made the older games in the franchise fun were removed for this game and replaced with nothing. Was not a fan of the low quality and slow moving cut scenes. Felt extremely linear, short, boring and overall just not at all what I was expecting from this franchise. I lack any motivation to replay it.Perhaps younger kids can enjoy this installment of the series, as it genuinely felt as if they might be the target audience with it's watered-down and challenging-less game play.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a quicker Kingdoms experience, this is a good one to pick up, since it's short, sweet, and has... decent replayability, I guess?Otherwise I'd suggest going for Kingdoms Two Crowns. This game doesn't have enough content to justify it's usual sale price.I really want to like this game, but it's just not got the same replayability or length the others in the series did.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: The Kingdom games are entertaining. They are visually appealing, soothing, and have a clear aim, challenge, and overall atmosphere, but I don't see this as a whole new game, but rather a re-skin and degradation from the previous ones. This 1980s look does not suit the game. It's going for that campy older adolescent vibe where you're basically having the kids do all the manual labour and getting paid to simply drink all the time and bully them around. Visually it's nice, but it's a bore in comparison to the mid-evil survival aspect the original goes for. Play the original games unless you want cut scenes and 1980s-style gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like the Kingdom games? Do you like Stranger Things? Are you nostalgic for the 80's in general? Then have I got a game for you!!Kingdom Eighties plays pretty much like all the other Kingdom games but now with an awesome 80's neon coat of paint. Everywhere you look there's an easter egg or reference, everything from Back To The Future, to My Little Pony, to Breakfast Club, to ET. If it happened in the 80's you'll probably notice it here at some point.This game takes the story element from Two Crowns and cranks it up to eleven. Instead of simply just "fix boat leave" there are now different levels with their own narrative focus. The Camp level for example has you recovering the canoe and have to locate a gold trophy to motivate the resident canoe rower into doing the job.One of the biggest complaints I've seen is that the game is just too easy now, and since the game mainly focuses on you completing the main campaign at all costs that is largely true. On top of easier enemies you also get 3 indestructible NPCs that will defend you to the death and you have to try, really try, to actually die and lose the game now.With that said however once you finish the main campaign you unlock Survival Mixtapes, an endless wave mode that is more akin to the brutal difficulty of the original Kingdom game and the Challenge Isles of Two Crowns.So get this game and party on dudes!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I do like the game, but it is a reskin of the previous versions and does not have new features for returning players.I have played all the other games and liked them, although some are more of a DLC than a full game, but I tolerated it because it was cheap and gave enough features.Furthermore, I have over 60h in all games combined and only 5h in this one, in my eyes it does not offer new things to old player.The only reason I would buy this is if the first game you play, but even then I would rather play 2K and the DLC
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet spin-off in the kingdom universe, shows potential but unfortunately misses a couple of important points:1. No co-op, which is a shame because its one of kingdom's best features, and there isn't a really good excuse for removing that.2. It's a really easy and repetitive game, even on hard difficulty, without any big strategic decisions.3. For a story-driven game, there should be an extra effort to write a good and compelling story, with a rewarding and surprising ending. Also it's such a shame that the story wasn't dubbed, as it might make create an emotional connection with these very one-dimension characters.Honestly, I don't regret buying this game, as a fan of the Kingdom series, but it is not the sequel we were rooting for.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: They took the two crowns concept and removed everything that made it great, the couch co-op, the base building (walls are no longer really needed), and made it linear so that you breeze through levels and get automatically transported ahead. But they failed to do this properly, all you really do now 70% of the time is wait for trees to become cuttable, which seems out of place now. It may have been left in intentionally to drive playthrough time up to five hours from about two hours of solid playtime. As a theme alone it would have been great but destroying the underlying game with it is absolutely unforgivable. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of Kingdom games, especially North Lands. To be honest, i pirated all of them, cuz i had no spare money. So this time i decided to buy the game immediately.If i didn't owe the devs for the previous games, i would refund this.This clearly is not another add-on for Two Crowns that i expected, nor it is a developement of the series, this is a spin-off from the series, an experiment, where they butchered the gameplay loop that i liked, and instead tried to give "story" (if you can call what they did a story) and force me into building a giant base that occupies the whole map. Experiment failed, waiting for a next normal Kingdom game.More details to back up my opinion:1. Visuals.Though they are nice, make objects and colors blend together. Kids are so small, that i need to really try to distinguish who is unemployed. I'm playing on a weak laptop with no 2-meter wide screen.2. Gameplay and mechanics.In previous games expanding the base was your decision, here it felt like i'm forced to expand, and very quickly - only few days in, and traveling from one end of the base to another takes forever.Next, expanding made you destroy hobo camps, and building a hobo-home afterwards required investment, so this made you make some decisions, but not anymore.Next, building a farm and buying scythes was compact and required investment, now farms take half of your base and feel forced too. Next, mounts are now easily obtainable, you literally get a new bike for few coins, and not even given time to figure out what it does, you immediately get third one.All this feels like a huge downgrade from previous games.Also i retrieved the boat from the cave, and exited the cave before the kids with the boat, because they were so slow. But this counted as me fleeing, boat remained in cave and my army scattered. A warning on exiting the cave would be nice.3. New features and setting. Picking 80s and kid's summer camp is fine idea i guess, but couldn't they at least think it through? You literally pay little kids to do all the work, hooray for child labor =)Instead of coins you could use badges, so little boy scouts would do anything to get a new shiny badge. Why greed would want badges? Because it's greed, if kids want them, greed wants them too.Why are those kids like 5 years old, couldn't they be like 12-16 to at least resemble a workforce. Also, you fix swimming pools to earn coins off of your own camp kids? Or instead of putting some effort and remaking bows into slingshots, killing into non-lethal badge-earning activity, they just copy pasted archers, making 5 year old kids hunt deers and rabbits. Also, ctrl-c ctrl-v kid knights with shields, seriously?NPC guys that aid you could be nice, but they make the easy game even easier.  And introducing cutscenes without voicing, even a single phrase, feels weird too.Cutscenes! That would be a nice new feature, would i not be playing on a laptop. Because the cutscenes lag super heavily, both video and audio, for a few seconds, then play normally, greatly spoiling the process.So, even though i like Kingdom series and gameplay, even though i like the music, this game feels really awkward compared to predecessors.

They kept saying coop wouldn't work for the experience they had planned.The experience was a linear 4 level campaign, where the first level is basically a tutorial. So, effectively you get 3 short levels of kingdom with new mechanics. These 'new' mechanics are basically just 1 mechanic.  You can make the kids do chores for money. Each one is the same, but has different art per station on each level.You can't send armies out to attack anymore.. but you can still make the armies for no reason? _childDocuments_.review: EXTREMELY SHORT. I played on Hard difficulty and dragged it out as long as I could, exploring every inch of every map, and still didn't make it to 10 hours. It starts out easier than ever: there are only two types of minions, since "knights" can be completely ignored and serve absolutely no discernible purpose and farmers have been removed completely. Coins rain from every building that can produce them, especially the arcade, and can be worked by anyone at all. The banker has also been completely removed, presumably because collecting coins is already absurdly easy. It really served to amplify and highlight the tedium of the core gameplay loop: collect coins, drive to the edge of camp, build a wall or recruit until I'm out of money, then drive back into camp and repeat. The difficulty slowly escalates over time, and, towards the end, monsters were so tough and doing so much damage that even the highest level walls couldn't hold them off for more than a few hits. Playing on Cursed difficulty would not have been fun. Vehicles were all essentially identical, save for a few with unique powers that were so neutered as to be completely useless. The fastest mount is so fast it's uncontrollable, and I ended up switching it back out for a regular bicycle. This hollow shell of a game is littered with "member berries," bits of nostalgic cameo references intended to endear the game to you, but they have no bearing on the story or environment. Mechanically this could just as easily have been in the original medieval world or futuristic sci-fi and would have functioned just the same. Overall I think this would have been better served as a DLC or challenge mode in Two Crowns rather than a separate game. It is less content than the original and fails to distinguish itself from it in any meaningful way.

_childDocuments_.review: I've not been much of a fan of the Kingdom games. I tried them and did not enjoy several of the mechanics. Kingdom: Eighties feels like it was made with my grievances in mind. The economy was my biggest gripe, with coins being difficult to come by and requiring serious investment to get even a slightly reliable income. Either by farms or by clearing space for archers to hunt rabbits. In Eighties, income is streamlined with various buildings added that produce coins with only a minimum investment. I always hated, absolutely hated, beyond reason, that towers in the previous games basically "consumed" an existing archer. Making towers built early in the game become a hindrance and a liability, because you lose active archers basically permanently. In Eighties, there are no archer towers. They've been replaced with very, very cool automated laser towers. Love it.Recruitment was also always such a freaking hassle in the previous games. You couldn't really expand if there was refugee camp, because you would destroy the camp and lose a source of recruitment. I also hated this. Very much. The punishment you received for expanding (the whole point of the game) made some of my playthroughs fundamentally unwinnable. I can't push forward with archers and knights if my only refugee camp is right next to my base and I lose all my potential recruits. In Eighties, recruitment points are not destroyed when you expand past them. They continue to function like normal. This is awesome.I love being able to lead my assault force and my assault force having a reliable means of protection. This was not the case in previous games. Great change too.Having friends/companions that actually DO something is awesome. This is a great change.I'll be honest, I really, really dislike all of the previous Kingdom games. I got them for free from Epic a while back. And even with no actual investment in them, I find them infuriating. Not in a good way. I'm sure I'm playing them wrong and that there is some method or trick that everyone else knows that I don't, but I can barely get past the first island and certainly can't beat the 2nd. And I'm done trying.  I'm done fighting the old games to have fun. But I'm not reviewing the old games. lol. I'm reviewing Eighties. And I've beaten Kingdom: Eighties 3 times already. Twice on Hard and once on Cursed. I love this game. This is the Kingdom game that I always wanted to play, with clear, player-friendly mechanics. And an actual story (A basic but functional one). With actual characters. They give you a goal, they give you interesting events and really, really cool mounts. This game engages the player 1000% better than the old games. And it's not "easy" either, it just doesn't make it hard for the player to enjoy it. Big difference.So, if you're like me and you rather disliked the old Kingdom games for the same reasons, give Eighties a try. They made the exact right improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't really deserve a thumbs down, per se. I would give it a sideways thumb. Being a sequel, I can't NOT compare it to the previous games, which honed their style over time and nailed a simple, elegant, enjoyable, and interesting strategy game. This game introduces a major factor that changes a lot--a story, which does indeed add a lot of enjoyment (although I couldn't help but be annoyed at much use they got out of the same still image of each character--for a story that is hyperfixated on the importance of the main character and their family, you would think that they would have more than two images of them). Perhaps because the story added so many new things, the develops felt the need to simplify other mechanics, which I believe to be to the detriment of this game. Or perhaps because of the intense upgrade in graphics, they felt the need to simplify the game mechanics. Unfortunately, what I found was that the game was lacking the strategic element that the previous games had, only even remotely touching on the familiar need for strategy in the last chapter (and even then, only VERY slightly). Without having to strategically keep sections of forest to keep your camps, plot out how many citizens become farmers, plan out how to survive the seasons changing, constantly keep track of the number of archers you have vs the archer towers you're building, when to spend your money vs invest it in the bank, or when its worth building a teleportation portal----this game is simply missing the strategic challenge. The choice of mount in this game even feels to be largely a waste of time (I ended up with the skateboard until I unlocked the completely broken insane mount in the last chapter), and having one mount be so clearly better than every other mount makes the others feel pointless. The homages in the game are certainly fun to encounter, but I really wish this gameplay didn't leave me bored. I love the addition of the mobile barricade and would love to have seen that incorporated in a game like Two Crowns.While the graphics are clearly a huge step above where they were in previous games, it does make gameplay a real struggle. Kids blend into backgrounds or are concealed by grass, buildings ("camps" and "chores") and various interactables aren't clearly distinguished from non-interactable foreground art and change appearance from chapter to chapter and leave you guessing as to their purpose constantly, non-recruited kids are nearly identical to recruited kids, archers that are attached to a knight appear to be visually identical to unattached archers, heck, at times I would lose Leader amongst the other teens. There is clearly care and attention put into every visual element in the game, but it's unfortunate that it all gets lost in the clutter to diminish the individual pieces. In my opinion, in order to utilize the varying setpieces and all of the different interactables in the game, I would suggest adding small UI pop-ups clarifying the objects: provide stats for the different mounts (since the first three mounts are all bikes that are very similar-looking and drove very similarly, stats would help the player to learn why one would be better than the other), provide a short description for interactables (what is Leader trying to accomplish with this interactable? Are they paying a coin to talk to their mother to progress the story, or to have a kid vandalize a parking meter for money?), providing a title of a location so that you can determine it functions the same as the one on the prior chapter (shoe store vs sandbox "camps"; the various chore stations, etc). Yes, this would be a departure from the simplicity of the series, however, this game is already a departure from that, and it can't rely on the same simple UI when it is far more obtuse.In summary, this game is a fun nostalgic romp through 80s media, lighthearted and simple. It's not something I would advise you play while carrying on a serious conversation with someone, but it doesn't require the level of focus that the previous games did. It's strategy-light with some fun visuals and music. If that's what you're looking for, then sure, I'd recommend. But if you're looking for the challenge of the other Kingdom games with some new mechanics added, then this probably won't be what you want.

_childDocuments_.review: While I generally adore the Kingdom games, Eighties didn't quite stick in the same way the others did. I have several hundred hours in Two Crowns and 100%ed Classic, but I think I will end up finishing Eighties on its hardest difficulty eventually and likely not playing again unless I feel like hunting achievements. I wish I could give an "eh" rating, as I don't think the game itself is necessarily bad, but I'll have to say I wouldn't recommend this title over the others.The core gameplay is what you'd expect from a Kingdom game, meaning you still recruit workers (kids in this game) and try to defend the town you build. This title adds several new "chore" buildings where the kids you recruit can make you extra money, and three companions who follow along behind you. Despite these three other characters existing, there is no multiplayer functionality, and they mostly unlock new buildings and help fight the Greed. The references sprinkled throughout are good for a chuckle or two and I think it's interesting that they tried to take a more story-focused route here with some added art, but it's quite short and lacks the replayability previous titles have imo. It seems like some challenge modes were added, which I admittedly haven't tried yet, so maybe that adds that needed replayability element. I'll update this review if I get around to trying them.On the more negative side, I almost feel like the screen seems too cluttered or busy in this game, which was a huge turn-off for me as it made the environment confusing to keep track of. While in previous titles it was fairly clear what was a background vs. interactable element, I struggled with determining what I could mess with in Eighties sometimes, almost like there was too much detail for the art style. The base difficulty also seems MUCH easier compared to previous titles, and it's almost too easy to get money with the chore mechanic, which removes a lot of the fun when you're someone who liked the challenge in other Kingdom games. I don't feel that the story itself added all that much to the experience, as it was somewhat cute the first time but feels like an odd direction to take with a Kingdom game, standalone or not. The story is told thru "cutscenes" of static images with some unvoiced dialogue written out, though I do think the art in these is pretty alright. It's just not my favorite thing, and it was intended to be the main draw I think. Overall, I don't find Eighties quite as calming and fun to come back to compared to Two Crowns, so I always end up playing the latter instead - which is why I can't really recommend Eighties when it comes down to it. It's fun to play through a few times maybe, but something about the charm and relaxing atmosphere is absent that I can't fully put my finger on. That being said, it's not a *bad* game, so maybe it'll feel better to play if you're newer to Kingdom games, want an explicitly shorter game, or don't mind the difficulty decrease.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is cute, really. I’m pleasantly surprised. A different approach to that of the originals, but with very similar gameplay. I loved the atmosphere, the small details (not just visually), the references etc. Many despise it for being a victim of diversity propaganda. While this seems to be true on some level, it did not bother me much tbh, because it’s an original story, in a completely new setting (so we can’t talk about “color-washing” of previous content). The motive might still be the wrong one, sure, but life’s too short for constantly being pissed off about everything, right? ;) Although, the random height differences between my subjects were a bit irritating, because it made noticing them or distinguishing between jobs much harder in the beginning. It’s ok, but at least put a unit counter somewhere already! :D (TC could use that too btw) Some kind of random map generator (like Lost Islands in TC) would be nice for long-time replayability, because, as of now it’s just a linear 4-map campaign with Survival Mixtapes acting as hardcore mode for the same maps. Although the latter one is in endless mode and the mounts are random, nothing else changes there, so it’s very repetitive. Other than that, I think it’s a solid spin-off. I’ve also yet to encounter any game-breaking bugs, so I definitely recommend this one! Although Two Crowns is still the king of the series, this is still a better deal than New Lands in terms of content-price balance.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game was specifically made for me. As a child of the 80s, I get every reference in this game. While it uses Stranger Things as it's frame, I have seen jokes and references from Ghost Busters, Back to the Future, Gremlins, Transformers (the cartoon, not the Michael Bay abomination), G.I. Joe (same), Robo Cop, Predator, He-Man, and the Never Ending Story. The story is a nice change from the past game and I am impressed with how well the formula works. Everyone over the age of 40 needs to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: A goofy and fun spin on the normal Kingdom play with a rad and dorky 80's theme. There's awesome bikes and mounts, rad moves, a stranger things sort of vibe and lots of radical references.The level themes change quite a lot through the chapters, pixel art is beautiful as always, there's different objectives each time (Although may be hard to figure out exactly what to do for some.. but it's do-able) and.. most importantly..Child labor! You get to steal their lunch money while you wheelie on your bike with the squad, chugging soda's with your fluffy pal! Well.. It's to save the world after all, y'know?This was a crazy fun twist on the Kingdom experience, absolutely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: "Kingdom Eighties" is a fantastic addition to the Kingdom series, offering a creative twist on the setting and atmosphere. The 80s aesthetics and music are beautifully executed, and the animation, style, pacing, achievements, and gameplay are as amazing as usual for this series.Given the low price and unique gameplay, I would recommend it even to those who are simply fans of the Eighties and want to expand their collection of such themed games.Due to its lower difficulty compared to other titles in the Kingdom series, this game is an excellent choice for newcomers to the series or even to gaming in general. However, it still presents a challenge on the highest difficulty level or when trying to achieve certain achievements.Yes, this one has no Coop. In exchange we get a bit of story thrown in._________________ Regarding the many negative reviewsFor those put off by negative reviews, it's important to note that many of these reviews are related to drama surrounding a company hired by Raw Fury for additional writing. Only three people from that company were involved, with a very minor role. Judging the entire game based on this minimal involvement is ridiculous.As for complaints about supposed "wokeness" in the game... I find this to be a take from angry internet snowflakes. There is no political agenda or wokeness present in this game. Having played through the entire campaign, I can confirm that the dialogue and story content do not support such claims. The only dialogue you get is about the attack of the Greed. It seems likely that those making these complaints have not actually played the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: It's great, I love the 80's references. My only complaint is that there is no obvious way to restart a level. When I tried to restart, I actually ended up losing all progress, not just the level. Oops! Guess I have to start all over again. It is the most clever Kingdom game, and if you are in your 40's like me, you will love all the little nods and references.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: very fun game to play. came into this knowing it was not two player co-op. still interesting story and fun gameplay. worth buying. only bad thing maybe is that there is not much replayability like the two crowns game. bought on release day and played for around 6 hrs and its done. have not gone back to it.

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the Kingdom series for nearly a decade. Got this DLC and at first thought it was nothing more than a skin or theme to the old Two Crowns game. But no, it's got much different mechanics, is tuned differently, and feels more like exploring a mystery. The art is next level and as you progress, tells a story on its own. Kudos for making a very original feeling game from the well established Kingdom world! The cutscenes are a bit lame and take you out of play a little, but I do like the Stranger Things and 80s nostalgia vibes. Have put in 3 hours in my first session without thinking about it, looking forward to more!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the game and going.... Man. That mountain looks really familiar. Huh. Oh well.... no really, it looks really familiar.Goes too next level. Dang it! That mountain looks almost exactly... there's no way it is! How would they know about... OH my gosh! It is the mountain in my own back yard!! AAHHHH! They made the mountain in the Bay Area!!!!Plays end of game... you know, I kinda agree with that type of ending. :steaamhappy:Yes, short "game" compared to Two Crowns and other series. But I love the different take of the Kingdom series, I enjoyed the new ways of making money and getting friends. Didn't quite figure out the bikes really, what the difference was besides speed on them. Thoroughly enjoyed the atmosphere, the music and of course the background scenery that I was so familiar with. The "so eighties" outfits and such was an enjoyable moment.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I was at first concerned by the mixed reviews, but then I grabbed the game on sale - and I love it! I played all Kingdom games before and this one is really refreshing and complements the Kingdom universe very well. It is the first Kingdom game with a story that is told by reaching certain milestones on a map or a certain level. Since I was borne in the 80ies, I really loved the nostalgic flare. But If you are younger and liked stranger things, give it a try! The gameplay really reminded me of things like The Goonies and E.T. There are a lot of othere references to the 80ies and movies from that time, but I don´t want to spoil anything.I Played it on normal and it was not really a challenge because I knew the mechanics from the previous games, although some things are difficult. Would I buy it again without discount? Maybe, its quite short and I finished it on normal difficulty in 4 hours. But I don´t know how long I need on harder difficulties, and it seems that I missed some achievements.There is also an endless feature that was introduced after the "story campaign", which sounds also quite fun: how many days can you make with endless waves of enemies?In summary, I am really entertained so far, and after completing the campaign, I will definately play it more here and then, like I did with the other kingdom games as well. Definately a recommendation from my side. And have a look at the Credits until the end :-) !

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: The main character in the game is a teenage boy called "leader" that the game hints at as being a descendant of maybe the monarchs that are the characters played in the previous installments of the kingdoms series. And much like its predecessors the aim is to secure the "kingdom" by recruiting workers and archers, leveling up your kingdom's central camp, taking down trees and building fences and destroying the greed by surviving their waves of attack at night and progressively destroying their portals as you expand and then finally their cave. Here however the kingdom is made up of different areas you progress through as "episodes" starting with camp site, suburbs, downtown and finally a mall area (total of four different areas) as you follow through the campaign.Differences From Previous Kingdoms Games:+ Hero "leader" gathers a group of friends (they are four in total) who follow him around everywhere and have different strengths so the character is not alone.+ Theme obviously (eighties retro theme which includes a variety of locations you progress through episodes wrapped inside a campaign story, that would be representing islands but with no going back to each as you progress through the game) so to sum up location variety and one way progression.- Story presented as short movie flashes you unlock with coins.+ Some game dynamics are different for example you don't have farms so the kids i.e. "workers" pick up certain unlockable jobs such as pizza/popcorn/burger vendors, arcade gamers, etc..+ You only have tents that get destroyed and must be rebuilt as houses in the episode to recruit kids, before that you just recruit them from certain buildings that remain standing as you progress through the zones.     The Artwork: * Artstyle: + Beautiful especially if you're into retro art-styles. As with other kingdoms games Raw Fury doesn't disappoint here. The atmosphere is probably the game's strongest point. - Game is pixelated and there's a lot going on sometimes in terms of colors and objects which can make it a bit overwhelming as your eye trying to distinguish between background and foreground especially as you're moving along which can be sometimes straining for the eyes.* Music: + Nice music, eighties centered.- Personally preferred the previous kingdoms games music.The Writing and Story:- Found this to be the game's weakest points probably, the story feels like it's written by a ten year old. Just bad and very cheesy.The Game-play and Controls:+ Good controls, had no issues at all there+ If you like the game-play in other kingdoms games, this is almost the same.How the game makes you feel:+ Atmosphere a little less chill than previous kingdoms games but maintains the same feel with more colors which can swing either way depending on each person's personal taste and preferences.+ For some reason found it a bit reminiscent of the 1992 home alone: lost in new york video game, especially the mall area.The Ending:- Similar to previous kingdoms games but you get a short video ending as part of the story line which I found is super cheesy.+ Then the credits roll which you can't skip, luckily, because you get to see Sara's photo and this is not something you would want to skip, would recommend buying the game just for that. The personal touch from the devs was nice.- You get the option to continue playing in mixtape mode which is a mode where you don't win and just see how many days/waves of greed you can survive.Playtime and Replayability:- You can finish the game in under 4 hours, it's pretty short- You can replay it... if you like more of the same and would like to go through the same storyline again (yes the very cheesy one - fortunately you have the option to skip those scenes when they come up).Worth your money?Depends... if it's on sale and depending how much you're into eighties themes and would like to experience that and how much you're into kingdoms gameplay style. I don't regret buying it on sale as I have played all the other kingdoms games and did not want to skip this, the graphics are beautiful, and the theme is nice, but you have to think of it as an experience rather than a game. Would recommend buying an older cheaper kingdoms game on sale and seeing if you're into that sort of thing first. ❤ Audience ❤☑ Beginner☑ Casual Gamer☑ Normal Gamer☐ Expert☼ Graphics ☼☐ Bad☐ Alright☐ Good☑ Beautiful☐ Fantastic♬ Music ♬☐ Bad☐ Alright☑ Good☐ Beautiful☐ Fantastic☠ Difficulty ☠☑ Easy☑ Average☑ Easy to learn / Hard to master☑ Hard☐ Unfair§ Bugs §☐ Bugs destroy the game☐ Lots of bugs☐ Few Bugs☐ You can use them for speedrun☑ Nothing encountered☯ Story ☯☐ There is none☑ Bad☐ Alright☐ Good☐ Fantastic⚔ Gameplay ⚔☐ Frustrating☑ Sleepy☐ Boring☑ Fun☐ Challenging۞ Game time / Length ۞☐ Really short (0 - 3 hours)☑ Short (4 - 8 hours)☐ Few hours (10 - 20 hours) [if you focus on the main story]☐ Long (40-60 hours) [if you complete everything]☐ Very Long (61-100 hours)☐ Extremely Long (101+ hours)$ Price / Quality $☐ Full price☑ Wait for Sale☐ Don't buy☐ Refund it if you can

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly like this one better than Two Crowns. I've always been a big fan of the minimalism introduced in the original Kingdom Classic and didn't really like the feature creep that was getting into the series as a whole. Eighties does retain some of those features but it's much closer to New Lands, except that each chapter is much more differentiated in both aesthetics and goals, in addition to the fact that they're taking the series into an entire new art direction with this one.It's a great entry if you're looking for a refresh rather than more of the same. It's also quite a bit cheaper than the other Kingdom titles. There is ample replayability with the survival mixtapes (post-campaign) which offer randomized maps similar to New Lands. _childDocuments_.review: I've been a devoted fan of the Kingdom game franchise, and Kingdom: Eighties didn't disappoint, offering a captivating blend of retro aesthetics and classic gameplay. The 80s-style graphics are a visual treat, evoking a sense of nostalgia that adds a unique charm to the gaming experience.The simplicity and brevity of the storyline were a refreshing change. Kingdom: Eighties doesn't bog you down with a complex narrative, allowing you to dive straight into the action. However, the straightforward plot doesn't compromise on engagement, and the game manages to strike a balance between simplicity and intrigue.The standout feature for me was undoubtedly the retro 80s graphics. The pixel art style perfectly captures the essence of the era, and the attention to detail in the design of characters and landscapes is commendable. It's a visual feast that adds a layer of immersion to the gameplay.One aspect that I found slightly less enjoyable was the inclusion of turrets in the game. While they contribute to the challenge, I felt they disrupted the otherwise fluid and dynamic gameplay. However, this is a minor gripe in an otherwise enjoyable experience.The real test of skill comes with the survival mixtapes. These challenges inject an extra layer of difficulty, requiring strategic thinking and quick decision-making. They add a fresh and exciting dimension to the game, ensuring that even seasoned players face a formidable challenge.In conclusion, Kingdom: Eighties is a delightful addition to the franchise. The 80s aesthetic, combined with the straightforward yet engaging gameplay, makes it a must-grab especially when it's on sale. The overall experience is thoroughly enjoyable.

You will get your friends in exactly same order in exactly same place. And then, it's just grinding the money, building, fixing, re-building, fixing.PS. If you lose your companion (ie dog) to the greed, you will never get it back, because you proceed to next level and cannot rescue it from the greed cave. So, keep your eye on your pet.

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant addition to the Kingdom series, Kingdom Eighties brings a narrative story into play for the first time. You play as The Leader as you collect your friends and marshal your troops of abandoned kids to rescue your hometown from the Greed. The gameplay is largely the same as previous installments, but set against a backdrop of lovingly designed eighties references. The lack of co-op is a loss, but mechanically I understand why it wasn't included. A really fun self-contained expansion! I think it's a pretty solid entry to the series for new players, as the plot and shorter levels make it a bit more accessible than the earlier games.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent take on the Kingdom concept, my favourite so far! (Loved Two Crowns too)Visuals are colourful and filled with fun details and easter eggs. The narrative approach ties all the levels together in a much stronger way than previous games did, also allowing mechanics to evolve organically through the chapters. For example, kids spawn in indestructible camps in Chapter 1 but, by Chapter 4, they spawn in tents following the usual Kingdom rules (cutting trees around tents destroy them), which then must be rebuilt into camps similar to those found in Chapter 1. This creates a smooth learning curve and challenge progression, tying in well with other progressive mechanics in the game. Assault strategies are also more engaging, requiring constant movement to avoid retaliatory waves and push on to other portals.You really shouldn't listen to the masochist gamer crowd, who can't seem to enjoy an interactive experience unless it's punishing to an extreme degree. The challenge level here is actually very satisfying in my opinion, giving you just enough time to enjoy the view, sounds and details of the experience. I grew up in the 80's myself and to me, the extreme difficulty of many games from this era is actually a design weakness. I'm glad some games today have a more thoughtful approach and are able to find other ways to engage and delight players!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a side-scrolling real-time strategy game where you collect coins and spend them (hopefully wisely) to build up your defences, explore, and then bring the fight to your enemy. This game is apparently intended as a prettier, easier introduction to the Kingdom series. I think the developers succeeded in this goal, but veterans of the series may be disappointed.THE GOOD:- Your goals are better described, through cut-scenes, than in previous games in the Kingdom series.- The new mechanic of the siege wall makes it much easier to assault and defend, if you use it correctly- The graphics are the nicest in the series.- Kingdom Eighties punishes failure less harshly. When you fail and get killed you have the option to go back to your previous save, losing 1 day of game time or less.  This won't save you from major strategic errors, but it will definitely save you from tactical blunders or simple input errors.- It's a blast-from-the-past 80's-style story with the kids saving the day while the adults wet their pants. That's a good thing, right?THE BAD:- Kingdom Eighties is significantly easier than previous games in the series.- The mechanics are simpler.- This is overall a nice entry in the series, but for players of the previous games looking for more challenge, or a major spin on the previous formula, it's a bit of a disappointment.THE UGLY:- In the cut-scenes, the characters jiggle strangely.- I didn't notice any bugs or anything offensive.

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Eighties is a stand-alone Kingdom throwback adventure. I got exactly what I was expecting: a 1-dimensional, beautiful, chill kingdom game with an 80's theme. I would not call it an evolution of the Kingdom formula, but it was different enough to be a stand-alone title. You still get to try different mounts, experiment with unlocking perks and upgrades, wander out of your camp in the daytime and secure it at night, etc. Interesting additions/differences:-Unlocking other teens to be able to perform different actions, instead of sages-Mount (bicycle) "Boost" button which was different than double-tapping the direction you want to go... not sure what that actually did on some mounts-Siege mechanics are much better than previous Kingdom games (dumpster shield and smarter "knights")-Can unlock a bigger purse-Hand-crafted levels instead of randomly-generated: very pretty custom levels and backgrounds-Different musical artist than Amos Roddy (but still good)Missing Kingdom "Staples":-No bank-No gems-No ship to repair-No seasons-No farmers/specialty classes outside of workers, archers, and knights... workers (and jobless!) do coin "farming"-No Toytree musicBottom line: if you like Kingdom, especially the older titles, you'll probably like this one too. If you haven't played Kingdom but like the 80s, you might like this game. Minor Gripes:-Lack of randomly-generated levels inhibits replay value. I'm not sure how they would be able to add a mode like "new lands" which would let you jump around endlessly, but I'd play it! -Game was kind of easy: even on "hard", I never had money problems or really felt threatened. Maybe I'll try again on the hardest difficulty another timeEDIT: Thanks for the developer response, I appreciate it and thanks for trying something different! I will try those other modes. I also wanted to say, this Kingdom would be great for newcomers to the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this was a fresh take on the Kingdom series that I really appreciated. We had several games that were very similar to each other in style and mechanics. Kingdom Two Crowns is still the crown jewel of the series- the dev studio has a challenge in topping their work on Two Crowns. With that said, Eighties is a 'standalone expansion' and it does a great job of standing out on its own and even appealing to series newcomers.The series is all about micro-strategy and base building. Operate on a day/night cycle and use your time and money wisely. Find little trinkets as you expand your base. There's little to no emphasis on efficiency in Eighties, however. Hard difficulty was a breeze and enemies had a tough climb to reach me if they even managed to break down my first wall. I might go as far to recommend you play at the highest difficulty if you're returning to the series and enjoyed the feeling of min/maxing your days while controlling your spend.Many mechanics and dynamics are removed from the campaign. A core subset of features and mechanics remain in Eighties and it almost feels like back to basics. Even if you've only played New Lands... there are still things that were in New Lands that don't return in Eighties. All of these thoughts lead me to believe that the scope of this game could've been increased by a notch or two. The level of decision making required by this game was relatively low, and I would've appreciated a wider selection of structures or units to spend on. But, I'm not going to knock the game for it too much- I'm still satisfied with what we got.Yeah, mixing the 80's with the Kingdom format is basically chocolate mixed with peanut butter. There's just so much charm put into every little thing and a lot of comes from the 80s theming. The backgrounds look incredible in this game, and the level of polish in the animations and visuals is commendable. Also, I'm glad to get another great OST out of the series :)

_childDocuments_.review: For new players to the Kingdom series, this is the best game to start with. Buy Kingdom 80s first, then buy Kingdom Two Crowns if you get hooked. For experienced players, K80s is a great update, its worth your time and $$$.  Each of the 4 islands in K80s has a radically different visual style from each other. Animated cutscenes add a ton of personality that was missing before, there are lots of generic 80s easter eggs, and in all each island/level feels like a real place that people lived in before the Greed took over. I especially love that this game gives you a good in-game reason for clearing out all the trees, without feeling like you are causing an Easter-Island-like ecological disaster. Gameplay has been smoothed out even more than K2C, in many little ways that make the game less of a pain but also much easier. I only play on Cursed difficulty, and I've never felt really challenged.  The changes are still welcome, for example, archers (here, instead, they are little kids with slingshots) are mostly accurate without being perfect.  Turrets have a good defensive effect even far away from your outer walls, and you can switch their type on the fly.  The player's "mount" starts with the "recharge stamina anywhere" trait, and as you round out your "gang" with the 3 other bikers, you have defenses to knock the Greed away from your crown.  In other words, every basic mount is the Griffin, which is the only mount we used anyway.  Also, the "bomb run" crew now includes a moving wall instead of knights, which is repaired during lulls in the battle, the trade-off here being that knights are much less useful and I can almost win without knights on the hardest difficulty level.  Also, coins are generated at various stations throughout the levels, meaning less backtracking and more time spend in the action. (Plus, excess engineers will work the coin stations along with any unassigned villages/kids).    In all, this feels like a great "reset" of giving the player the basic features that move the game into the future.  I can't wait to see what

_childDocuments_.review: Why this installment is the best in the franchise... from a massive Kingdom fan:If you're like me and have played all of the previous kingdom games, you were overwhelmed by the trailer for this installment. _childDocuments_.review: I love "Kingdom". I have ever since the first and "Two Crowns" is a game that I own on all of my devices and play regularly, because I Just love the vibe. And I was really, really hyped about "Eighties" as it looked different, fresh and was set in one of my favorite time periods.So it really sucks that I have all of these negative things to say about this one. All the hype and this asking price just sets you up for something completely different. Still though I had fun and this is probably the best starting point for new players. It just could've and should've been way better. So. Narrative driven Kingdom. Awesome idea! I love those types of games so I was excited to check it out. But that's not really what this is. This is a bunch of typical things you do in Kingdom games, disguised as Campaign chapters and masked through some already outdated-looking cinematics without any voice acting.Guys, I'm sorry, but for $11, you should've done far better. And here are some examples:* No voice acting in a game released in 2023 for $11* Basically a spiced-up reskin of an already existing game for $11* The greed look the same and for $11, no: masks don't count* For $11, we're back to Archer priority being messed up and we get missions that involve the futuristic concept of "waiting around"* For $11, you get to have the tutorial ghost explain to you things you've already done, because having the game check for that or an option to pay it a coin to go away would truly be too much, right? * There is literally nothing to do outside of the ~5 hour long Campaign mode, which I guess costs $11You heard that right: no freeplay, no survival, no nothing. At the very least it was very logical and expected of the game's visuals to transfer over to "Two Crowns" as a skin pack, but that doesn't happen either. This is the real heavy hitter in the complaints department and I truly can't wrap my head around this decision. Because all of these beautiful, amazing and vibalicious visuals are just stuck in the "80s" campaign, which I'd never play again honestly. I mean, it's not like theres a reason to, beyond the five difficulties. And that just sucks. It truly does. Because having five difficulties is the best way to show that you have no clue how to ballance your game. I enjoyed my time in "Eighties" land, but I just couldn't stop myself from thinking how much better it should've been. And I truly hope that the concept of a story-driven Kingdom spinoff doesn't die with this one, because it is worth exploring again. But with more attention to detail, please. Also, Raw Fury, if you are reading this: it is time to combine all of Kingdom under one app/launcher (at least on PC). Keep the Classic experience, keep all of the modes, but just unify everything in one place. It is way more convenient and it is also a requirement if you don't want people nagging on you for prices. Because "Eighties" just feels like a $6 DLC pack gone rogue. Kingdom best game forever. Back to Two Crowns. Also, the Greed should go, these green potatoes are getting boring as all heck. Or at least give them new designs so they don't look this silly.
