_childDocuments_.review: Step into a time-warp of pixels and neon lights with Kingdom Eighties, a delightful retro-style game that pays homage to the golden age of gaming. This quirky adventure will have you grinning from ear to ear as you embark on a quest filled with 80s references, challenging puzzles, and a healthy dose of nostalgia. Get ready to groove to the beat and defeat evil in this pixelated wonderland.Graphics and Visuals:One word: RAD! Kingdom Eighties fully embraces its retro roots with pixel art that oozes charm and character. Every element, from the characters to the environments, is lovingly crafted to transport you back in time. The vibrant colors and smooth animations add a touch of modern flair to the classic aesthetics. As you venture through the game's various levels, you'll be greeted by sights that invoke fond memories of the arcade era, making it an absolute treat for both old-school gamers and newcomers alike.Gameplay:Kingdom Eighties sets itself apart from the crowd with its engaging and inventive gameplay mechanics. You'll take control of an intrepid hero who must rescue the iconic princess from the clutches of an evil villain straight out of an 80s action movie. To do so, you'll need to navigate through challenging platformer levels, solve mind-boggling puzzles, and defeat enemies with rad weapons and power-ups.The game strikes a perfect balance between nostalgia and innovation. It's familiar enough to make you feel at home, yet it adds refreshing twists to keep things exciting. Whether it's jumping over gaps, dodging enemy fire, or exploring secret passages, the controls are smooth and responsive, ensuring that you stay immersed in the action-packed adventure.Sound and Music:If you're a fan of synth-heavy tunes and catchy chiptunes, Kingdom Eighties has got you covered. The soundtrack captures the essence of the 80s era, transporting players back to the days of arcades and boomboxes. The upbeat music perfectly complements the action on-screen, enhancing the overall gaming experience. With every jump and every victory, you'll find yourself humming along and grooving to the game's infectious beats.Storyline and Characters:Prepare for a narrative that is equal parts nostalgic and hilarious. Kingdom Eighties doesn't take itself too seriously, and that's precisely why it shines. The characters are delightfully eccentric, with personalities that pay tribute to classic 80s archetypes. From the brave hero with his righteous mullet to the princess who isn't afraid to kick some butt, each character is a nod to the pop culture icons of the past.The story is a rollercoaster of quirky adventures, packed with unexpected twists and turns. It keeps you invested and eager to progress through the game, just to see what hilarity unfolds next. Whether you're laughing at witty one-liners or chuckling at clever references, the humor will have you glued to your screen.Conclusion:Kingdom Eighties is a gem that skillfully captures the essence of the 80s gaming era while infusing it with modern-day creativity. It's a joyful celebration of retro gaming, complete with challenging gameplay, fantastic pixel art, and an infectious soundtrack. With its quirky characters and laugh-out-loud humor, the game stands out from the crowd and guarantees an entertaining experience for players of all ages.So, don your neon headband, crank up the synth, and dive headfirst into the neon-lit adventure of Kingdom Eighties. Get ready for a nostalgic journey that's solid fun from start to finish!

_childDocuments_.review: Great for newcomers! Good for longtime fans.As many others have said, this isn't a step forward for the series; however, it is not a step back either, more of a step to the side. The devs gave it a fresh new aesthetic, while keeping the same art style, streamlined the gameplay a bit to make it more accessible, and gave the us a charming little story to follow.Some longtime fans are underwhelmed due to the lack of much new content (mechanics), and the loss of coop play. I am too, a little. That said, I think what they have done is give newcomers an excellent point of entry to the series. While it's not really the game I wanted them to make, I still enjoyed playing it very much, and recommend it to anyone and everyone. Fans of the other games simply need to adjust their expectations a bit. Can't wait to see where these games go from here!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I have put quite a few hours into the Kingdom series and it's various iterations.  For me, the thing about the Kingdom formula is that it's incredibly easy to fall back into the routine of the game.  I find it incredibly addictive.  I have played on Steam, on my Nintendo Switch and on my PlayStation.  I have played both single player, and multiplayer.  Sure, I can get a little tired of the formula after a while but if I give it some time and fire it back up it's quite easy for me to fall right back into it.  (I will note that my play through of this game took place entirely on a Steam Deck)Kingdom:Eighties manages to bring some fresh and new things to the game but it also remains ... very much the same.  I really enjoy the eighties theme of this one.  The new mechanics are quite enjoyable and actually dial back on some of the more punishing aspects of previous titles.  I rarely found myself struggling to enlist more archers and workers.  The combat also felt a little sped up in this one.  Once you have reached full power you have a movable wall (in the form of a dumpster) AND a powerful mounted gun, making your assaults on the greed more effective then ever.  This did have the side effect of making the overall experience pretty easy for someone who had already mastered most of the in's and out's of previous titles. In Kingdom:Eighties, I rarely felt very challenged.  Your mileage may vary if you are not as familiar with Kingdom.  It's easy to overextend yourself and the game WILL punish you for doing so.  However if you have played the previous games you will know the logical strategy to go with. Like me, you will probably complete the whole thing without failing once.  (The greed never even managed to knock off my crown)The overall experience was also very short.  I think I took my sweet time on some of those levels and I still completed my play-through in about 5 hours.  For some people this short playtime and low difficulty may mean the game is not for you.    Personally, I don't need all my games to take incredibly long to complete.  I have a backlog of incomplete games that I will not live long enough to fully complete, so a game I can actually beat in a few sessions can actually work out quite well for me.  Of all the things in this game to elicit complete delight from me it was the new mounts.  The game keeps them coming at a fast pace, and they get a lot more exciting then a bike!  The unique mounts in this game were fantastic.  The could not believe the last one I got - super cool!  I won't spoil it.I'm looking at the achievements I did not manage to complete on my first play through and considering going back to try to get them.  Kingdom games always keeps me wanting to come back for more, and if this is a sign of how they make continue to shake up the series in the future then I for one am pretty excited about it.  If they continue to tweak the game and give it new flavours, I will keep showing up to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Is the game good? Absolutely.Will I tell my friends to play it? Also yes.Does the game cater to save noise levels and take into account people might be using headset? Hell no.Eighties is at it's core the same as any other kingdom installment plus it's own unique gimmicks which makes it fun to play. However, I had set the volume and music of the game down to 1 and still had to take my headset off at times due to how excessively eardrum burstingly loud the sound was. It's honestly not acceptable to have game music be that loud anymore and I shouldn't need to lower my PC volume if the game is already at it's lowest. In fact if other games can detect and take into account that I'm wearing a headset then this one should too.I'm still giving it a thumb up because it is actually a good game, but giving a thumbs down out of spite because of the volume issue is extremely tempting.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointingly easy even on the highest difficulty.  Practically no strategic depth in the game.The charm of the graphics and 80's references doesn't really save the game.  I was concerned as I was playing through that the game wouldn't provide an interesting gameplay loop that won't just get steamrolled through.Yet even playing on the "highest" possible difficulty, I beat this on my first try without anything to provide even the semblance of an obstacle.It's a shame really, because the kingdom series has always had a charm in it's simplicity.  But if the game doesn't provide a challenge even on the highest possible difficulty, what are veterans supposed to look forward too?  Each new game in the series has been made easier and easier, and all we really want is for the game to challenge us.This is the first game to provide difficulty settings of 5 different ranges, yet the gameplay doesn't have enough depth to make the highest settings even remotely challenging.  Every obstacle in this game gets beaten the exact same way.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good game. If you prefer Two Crowns and think this won't be for you, because it's not a coop, you're wrong. I thought so too, and I was wrong. It's addictive in the best kind of way.- The story is tacky by design, simple, engaging, and has a nice connection to the previous installments, alongside elements that either remained the same, or were redesigned in a familiar way.- Lots of new and different things that might at first feel like this isn't right, it was better previously, but once you'll get a hang of it, you'll see the great point in it all.Two Cons:- Achievements will force you to replay many times over, on various modes of difficulty, which is a bit redundant if you're going from top to bottom.- It's not always clear what's happening, and what you're doing, so the next thing you know, you progressed in the story, and can't go back for whatever you thought you'll pick up after you do just this one more thing over there.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Kingdom series; this was an insta-buy for me. The game loop is roughly the same as in the rest of the series, with some changes (such as chores replacing farming), some new mounts (of various quality), and a more relatable setting. Basically, fresh enough to be worth the while, but not a significant departure.Music has always been a strong point of the series, and, once again, it doesn't disappoint. Yeah, the Stranger Things-like setting has been overdone, but it's nice to finally have a narrative to the series... although it does fall a bit flat. It's minimal, it's cliché, it checks all the tropes, and given how little plot there is, it does stretch credulity, such as a phone call being ended due to no battery... only to work again fine in the next chapter despite the phone user  Also, we all know about the rebel kids  ignoring their parents' advice, but the way it's presented is a bit disappointing. Not even a , just a plain .The gameplay changes, in my opinion, are interesting. Small QoL features such as workers claiming a free bow/hammer even if it's not in the right direction, are worthwhile. On the flip side, the more complex visuals and more detailed scenery/characters make for harder identification. Also, as of this writing, archers sometimes look like super fast Luigis racing across the map at record speed, which is strange. Every negative thing I could've said about the game has been listed. I finished the game at hard in 8 hours in 2 sittings. It's another great quality game in a great series. Pick up Kingdom Classic for free if you haven't played the series yet, but we've got another winner.

_childDocuments_.review: America in the 1980s is as romantic to us as Arthur's Camelot. It is a time of stories, of hope and idealism that perseveres in the face of adversity. With bikes as steeds and the freedom to roam the spirit of adventure lives in that halcyon decade. The Kingdom series has brought the eternal struggle against the universal foe of Greed to many places and cultures, and now it has come to this familiar yesteryear that creeps ever further into legend as time drags on.The core game-play is here, refined and accompanied by great attention to detail. Progression through the stages, however, is linear. There are also only four stages in the main story, but these can be attempted on multiple difficulty levels. In a way, this unusual entry might be a good place for newer players to get into the series and I imagine that there will be more content added to the game in the coming months, though I can't say for sure.I thoroughly enjoyed my play-through on Hard and am considering another attempt on a higher difficulty. There are a few secrets I missed the first time around and am interested in trying to find ways to improve my efficiency. With its bright colors and pleasant music, this game series is probably one of my favorites on Steam, and this is a solid entry with a slightly different approach that I think works pretty well and expands upon the existing lore in interesting ways.

The characters, background and world are beautifully designed and don't even get me started on the pixel art!Cons:*Level 3 was a bit laggy as to the recyclable parts for the truck not spawning in again after the greed stole them, which made me had to reply the whole game as i got stuck.* I was very upset that we didn't get a reward by destroying the beach portals in Chapter 2,3 and 4. It was great that we got something in Chapter one but nothing after that (wish they gave us more types of coin purses)* Level 1 felt a bit rushed as the ghost wouldn't leave me alone until i broke a portal.* They should really have given us a pop up message warning that you are about to leave the current level and if you want to proceed, otherwise you can't unlock everything like the Spaceship...* Story wise, they could have done a lot more as the game has great potential, for example side characters would have been appreciated. They don't have to join the bike gang but could have provided support or even resources along with their own little side story. The main story was also a bit lacking.Overall, the game was great and i had a lot of fun playing it. There are many cons but the game outweighs them all. _childDocuments_.review: Let me prephase, I LOVE the Kingdom series. It's my go-to comfort game, and I've sunk hundreds (REALLLYY stretching the gameplay to its limit) in the series collectively. Unfortunately, Kingdom '80s made a core change that makes the game quite unplayable for the long run. The game is much more linear than the previous games which give you a single mission of "Survive", Kingdom '80s has a linear storyline, which has a finite ending. While you can freeplay beyond that, you can't travel freely between the maps, even if you conquer each stages beach spawner. Which thinking about it now, is a really odd choice to make when you could have inserted more varied, and natural blockers for the opposite end of the map from the main caves. I enjoyed my playthrough of it, and I'm doing a second playthrough right now just to get the achievements I missed and play on Cursed (which I recommend for returning players, it's still kinda ez), unfortunately I highly valued the replayability of the previous games, and this one doesn't have it with the single change it made. All that aside, the game made really good changes otherwise. Unemployed minions (kids which cracks me up) will mingle and do different various activities that earn you income. And arming a small horde of children with bows and slingshots is pretty funny. The  abundant references get kind of annoying and cheesy after a bit, some times even ruining immersion with how on the nose they are  for example.tl;dr: it's a fun new take on the Kingdom franchise, however it's not the definitive upgrade I was hoping for, and the change of removing different playable maps you can return to makes replaying the game more tedious than rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve waited a long time wondering what was next for Kingdom after Two Crowns. When the announcement for Kingdom Eighties was made, I was ecstatic. I’m a kid of that decade and, though I didn’t initially think of the 80’s being a great fit thematically for the series, I couldn’t help but to be both curious and excited. So now, after finishing it, for all the talk about Kingdom Eighties being a re-skin, I guess I just don’t see it. Not entirely, anyway. Sure, many of the elements in Kingdom Eighties serve the same purpose as those in previous games. You still build walls, recruit archers and builders and expand your kingdom (that IS Kingdom, after all). But there’s a few simple, new mechanics for series loyalists to play around with, and even some of the older mechanics are used in slightly different ways.Kingdom Eighties is much more than a new setting, though its new setting is beautiful to look at, and teeming with pop culture references of the decade. I was initially drawn to the series because of its gorgeous pixel art and, as much as I love Eighties’ look, it CAN get a little busy at times, making overlooking something easier to do than in previous games. If I had to choose, I’d still go with the look of its predecessors. The audio rounds out the presentation, and strangely enough, I feel the same way about the soundtrack. Two Crowns and New Lands contain some of my all-time favorite video game tracks. And though Eighties contains a great soundtrack with a very similar feel (but with an 80’s synth flavor), I didn’t hear quite as many standout tracks that stay with me long after I quit playing like I did with New Lands or Two Crowns.Eighties is a much more linear experience, unfolding in four levels. It’s more narrative focused, and the levels reflect that. You play the leader, but are accompanied by three friends, each of them with unique strengths that directly affect your kingdom. The tinkerer, for example, makes repairs and upgrades to specific elements that cannot be repaired/upgraded otherwise. These three friends accompany you everywhere. They either follow you on their bikes or, for the cost of a coin, equip a dumpster (to be used as a moving wall) and a radio-controlled robot with gun blazing (the tinkerer remains on her bike regardless, but in exchange, she can repair/upgrade at all times). You are vulnerable since you hold the crown, but your friends are not, so they go bravely into battle without consequence. Which brings me to one of my only real complaints about Kingdom Eighties: It’s incredibly easy in comparison to its predecessors. This may be welcoming to new players just getting their feet wet, but Kingdom veterans may be disappointed. Much of what you know about the series has been streamlined. Most unlockables, for example, don’t chain together to achieve a goal, but instead just drop free money.I’ll give you a glaring example. Instead of say, farming, which requires you to build a farmer station, recruit a farmer, then build the farm — in Kingdom Eighties you’ll simply spend a few initial coins to open a pizza stand that simply drops free money for you for the remainder of the level. And these examples are everywhere. They’re not representative of the entire game no, but many of Kingdom’s most engaging mechanics have been removed, leaving you feeling like you have less to do.And yet, Kingdom Eighties retains its addictive “just one more day” quality. It’s still a blast to expand and upgrade, and some of the new mechanics involving the main characters make fighting the Greed fun, if not easy. Really, approaching Day 40 battles are a cakewalk compared to Day 40 in Kingdom’s main games. Part of the reason for that is because, in Kingdom Eighties, your towers are unmanned gun towers that, when upgraded, are also equipped with barriers that function as walls. If you build your towers out far enough, the Greed often don’t reach the outer walls of your kingdom at all. Combine this with the moving wall that is your dumpster, and three friends who can fight the Greed and NOT die, Kingdom Eighties offers very little in the way of challenge. There’s no traveling between islands either. Unlike previous Kingdom games, Eighties’ linear structure means that you simply complete each level in order to proceed. Once you accomplish your goal, you don’t return to that level again. The lack of traveling between islands to care for your other kingdoms while strengthening your forces, along with its easy difficulty, makes Kingdom Eighties a very brief game.Kingdom Eighties is enjoyable, retaining a lot of what its predecessors built, but also being a tad bittersweet in that much of what makes these games so engaging is absent. Its streamlined designed is great for new players, but lacks the depth series veterans crave. As long as you’re a fan, you’ll find plenty to like here while simultaneously yearning for more — more involving mechanics AND more game (though if you’ve completed it, it looks as though the Greed aren’t quite finished). So if you’re a fan, it’s doubtful that Eighties will satiate you completely, but it’s still a fun, fresh take on the series that remains true to the Kingdom spirit.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Pixel Art- Soundtrack- 80s Easter Eggs- Fun changes to Gameplay mechanicsCons:- Super Short. You will finish it in a day and be left probably wanting moreI've an inordinate amount of time playing Kingdom Two Crowns when I have plenty of other games in my steam library I haven't touched. Its a bit of a comfort game as there is a nice blend of art design, soundtrack, patience, time and resource management as well as risk taking. At this stage I think I am a pretty safe bet when it comes to purchasing any DLCs or add-ons to the Kingdom Two Crowns universe. With kingdom Eighties I was expecting another skin upgrade; the same game with a few minor tweaks to the strategy and the gameplay.Kingdom Eighties is a whole new overhaul. The art design and soundtrack are on point as usual, with added narrative elements and a new way to acquire coins. This game is a lot more accessible to newcomers as there is much more forward momentum. Gone are seasons and having to travel back and forth between islands, or taking that risk of whether you conquer that new island at the end of autumn. Levels are now stand alone, you don't depend on what you shipped out with from a previous island, you start with the same amount each time.The downside of this is there are only 4 levels. I finished this game pretty completely on 7 hrs. I'll prob do another run through on hard, but after that it probably doesn't have quite the same replay value as other Kingdown Two Crowns titles which have enough variability to them that you can keep coming back and playing again.Absolutely appreciated the work that went into artwork, music, level design and the sheer volume of 80s easter eggs in this game. I look forward to seeing where they go to next and how they can expand the gameplay. However with only 4 levels it is very short, and considering the price you can get much bigger games for that price.

_childDocuments_.review: As it stands, Its just okay compared to two crowns. Fun, but not even as good as most of the special missions in Two Crowns.The theme is awesome. I love that you hire little kids to battle the aliens. For all the flack that people give this, I'm surprised they never watched movies from the 80's like Goonies. Children in danger saving the adults was a primary trope from that era. Fits perfectly.Before I list: I think the main thing holding this back was spending all development on the kingdom side and not the greed side. Green are almost unchanged, but humans get every advantage. Example to prove the point: I think having turrets be unmanned, UNKILLABLE AND act as reinforced walls was a bad decision. As cool as it is, its silly OP.Strange design choices:No flying bad guys (in my play through), no towers manned by army, no reason to ever consider not chopping down a tree, no gems/choices on what to upgrade (every "gem" is actually a key for a specific unlock).These removals make the game very, very straightforward: Build an army, then expand. Other thoughts-The teens you recruit are a cool design idea, but they are op in my opinion. They also interfere with the usefulness of some mounts like the DeLorean which light the ground on fire only for your teens to shove them back from it.-no vagrants? I guess they are teens now? This makes them more straightforward OP instead of strategic/optional. You can't lose teens for example.-No revisiting islands makes the game EVEN MORE straightforward and linear. The old games made islands something you had to return to to finish/harvest.-Why can't I name my Leader or pick their gender? How hard would it be to draw two for cutscenes??-As you advance and unlock things, it sets the expectation there will be some new endgame we are building to. Nope. if anything, its much, much more simplistic. And yeah. I have NO IDEA how 2 player was not an EASY thing to accomplish. What design choice made that hard??? Really struggling to see the logic. Just divide up the teens...

_childDocuments_.review: All the Kingdom games are really fun.  They aren't long games, but worth every penny.  This version of the game took me 7.8hrs on hard. The depth of the mechanics are a bit more shallow than Two Crowns, but it's still fun.  Mainly the economy.On previous games you had to build up your economy in a smart way or you would find yourself over expanded and not enough income or winter would arrive and you wouldn't have enough saved or alternate sources for coin.  In this game, you basically just expand as fast as you want with never any real worry for coin because destroying forest just unlocks places for your kits to generate money. _childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Eighties is, unsurprisingly, more Kingdom with a different theme.It's  I finished it in about 3.5-4 hours on normal difficulty with little to no real problem. Each map is a different location starting with a summer camp and eventually a mall, but there's only a total of 4 levels. Lots of references.It was worth it to me for just over $8 since I went through a 2nd time on hard difficulty and am doing some achievement hunting.The main tweaks are;~You're a teen on a bicycle, trike, or several other rides in the nineteen-eighties instead of adult on a horse or etc creatures but you still get the crown. I love the faint swish-swish swish-swish sound of riding the bikes.~They did away with spearmen/ninja/whatever job. It wasn't that great, and archers do great.~Farms are also good riddance, but replaced with other interesting places your people can make you money such as a pool with lifeguard, popcorn stand, a handful of others, so even when without a job (archer/engineer) they can be useful.~No banker. You find a money pouch upgrade.~You get 3 pals on bikes that each do their own thing which helps fulfill a suggestion or two.~Watchtowers are now laser turrets. No waiting for an archer to run to it; nerd friend builds laser towers. Mechanic friend can upgrade them to act as walls. When your HQ is upgraded all the way you can switch the type of laser from regular medium damage lasers into either slow firing heavy laser that stuns heavier/bigger enemies or an artillery that fires far in an arc instead of direct.~No gems, just coins.Your mileage may vary. Though there was only 4 the levels were interesting, however Kingdom Two Crowns seemed more in-depth even though the levels are more generic to each other.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me about 5 hours to finish the game on normal. Honestly, I'm kinda glad the story wasn't long. When I come away from playing a game of Kingdom Two Crowns and it's been like 15 hours, I feel like I wasted a measurable chunk of my life. When I finally do come back, I forget where I was and start over. To be honest, I've never managed to finish a whole run of Two Crowns because I get burnt out, so this was good for me. It's nice to be able to finish a lot quicker. I would say it lasted just long enough for a story.  It's such a shame to waste this cool aesthetic! Hopefully this will be a patch, but I'm not holding my breath.I think a lot of people are complaining about the simplicity and all, but to me, less is more in this case. I really think that this was meant to get people into the Kingdom Games. (Also why it's a standalone, probably.) Each section is unique and has unique assets, so the artists had a lot of work cut out for them. At times, it did get a bit busy on screen, particularly on the second stage, but I got used to it. For ~$11 after tax, I feel like it was a fun little romp. It's very much like watching an 80s movie. It's all self-contained and resolves itself. The music is good but it didn't stick out to me. (meaning it wasn't annoying either.) There were also a lot of cute cultural references all over. One new thing that I REALLY liked was the movable attack barrier (a dumpster in this case). Honestly this made it SO much easier because now you can kite enemies. I wish that the developers would add this into KTC. They have a habit of not updating old things though. (Ex. The European and Shogun faction in K:TC got left behind, feature-wise, when Dead Lands and Norse Lands came out.) I did really like the companions. It was fun to have a little band of friends riding bikes around with me. I definitely liked Tinkerer's and Champ's punt ability. (I don't know why both of them get that ability and Wiz doesn't. I suppose Tinkerer gets it because Champ has to push the dumpster, but it doesn't make a ton of sense for her.) I think that the allies thing has potential for a party system in a future game! It'd be really cool to mix and match party members. I only really have complaint and that's the lack of voice acting in the cutscenes. Maybe they tried it and it was worse with voice acting, but I imagine that it couldn't cost  much to hire five-ish people for 20-30 lines.Some final thoughts: It would be nice to go back to certain levels (particularly the camp level) and play a bit longer, but I suppose there's nothing stopping you from restarting and hanging out there for longer. I don't know if there's a point to clearing the dock side (/lane), but I did it anyway. You get to see something in the background,  , which I assume is a movie reference. Other than that, it seemed pointless, which isn't a huge deal. oh and allies still get stuck in fire, so I avoided using that specific ability.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice throwback with a stranger things twist. Not much to say other than there is a story mode now with some potential to build on it. Finished it pretty easily on the average difficulty.Companions are added into the game that follow you around as your 'friends' offering unique abilities with repairing, fighting and a movable tower for attacking/raiding the enemy.Certainly not as frustrating as two crowns is where if you lose your crown you gotta start pretty much all over again finding Gems. Instead of gems its just unique objects you find while exploring outside your base. Some are easier to get than others but in story mode you find everything regardless.I recommend playing the game on higher difficulties as unique enemies begin to spawn and becomes a challenge to actually play. I would wait for a sale or better yet a bundle. Not because the game isn't worth the price, just that steam tends to do that to all games.Better than diablo 5/10

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I finished one game on hard.I thought that 'diversity' would be annoying, but frankly I stopped give a damn once I realized I pay little girls 1 coin for an eternity of servitude and found that incredibly hilarious. Feels about as wrong as it is funny.I don't really care about the story component of this game. If you liked Kingdom series for it's gameplay - this is another iteration that adds some stuff, removes some stuff, changes some stuff and is in general very similar either way.Buy if you just want more Kingdom and it looks interesting to you.Don't buy if you are tired of the same formula and expect a leap of change.It's a Kingdom game. Simplified 1D (only left-right) strategy game where you build up defenses, hire units, buy equipment, defend from attacking Greed and try to eventually defeat it.Some of the most important differences between this and Two Crowns:- 80's setting - synth-wave music, lasers and neons- no longer do you have ability to travel between islands, you instead progress through a linear set of levels with a specific objective on each one- there's a story where you play as a descendant of monarchs that fought Greed and now you have to defeat them again after your dad disturbed an ancient Greed cave- you recruit 3 NPCs that join you, attacking Greed and unlocking some abilities and buildings for you- archers now use different weapons, bows, baseballs and slingshots and they are picked at random once they get equipped at the archer's stand (you still only buy bows, but they equip different weapons anyway - go figure)- farming, fishing and berry-picking has been replaced by a jobs system - as you expand you will unlock ability to occupy some objects or stores and your unequipped serfs and builders will start working at those places for a steady income- towers have been replaced by automated laser turrets with 3 different types and they can act like barriers once fortified, but you need to unlock the ability to build them first- some new Greed types have been added, but some have been also removed- you can't send your knights to attack, attacks are now manually controlled similar to how the bomb was following you around in Two Crowns, meaning you have to take part in every attack- many buildings like the bakery, bank, blacksmith were removed- gems were also removed, most upgrades or mounts you find in buildings you liberate from Greed control by cutting trees around it and they only cost coins- you can upgrade your coin pouch size onceI like the synth-wave, neon style and atmosphere in general.You play as a teenager, commanding a horde of preschoolers with slingshots.For some reason like 90% of my 'kingdom' were little girls. So the scenario is: I drop 1 coin, they pick it up and become my forever-slave, happy to work and fight for my reign as the supreme kid. I command an army of little girls with slingshots and trash-can-lid-shields.It's both wrong and funny as all hell. Even more so since this game kinda treats itself quite seriously.In general you can expect similar kind of fun as other games in the series.There's a lot of new buildings and interaction animations for them in the new economy.I find it difficult to believe that a bunch of little shts would shoot at Greed with slingshots.It's really the same game at the other Kingdom titles. I don't personally mind, but it is not something I can easily recommend to everyone who already played Two Crowns.Especially since a lot of stuff have been removed. I especially disliked new attack mechanics - I don't want to personally go up to each portal and watch it getting destroyed. I feel this games is at it's best when it offers you strategic challenges.Once it becomes about personally having to go and micromanage every little thing I tend to zone out.A whole lotta nothing interesting going on here. We have diversity, playing as a mixed kid with black and white parents and we recruit a white jock, an asian mechanic-gurl and a black nerd. Cutscenes try to give them character, but are overall boring to experience. No voice acting, simplistic story.Nothing is wrong with simple, I just feel like this story is shoehorned and doesn't justify it's existence. I mean in previous games we were fighting Greed because it wanted our crown and that was all the context we needed, right? If you want to give this game a story - more should have been done to make it an important part of the experience.You are still choked by how slow you acquire new recruits. At some point you will have more coins than what you realistically spend even if you upgrade everything. You'd want to just accelerate your recruit process, but no - have to wait for kids like you had to wait for vagrants in other Kingdom games.It's eh. It's also cheap. If it looks interesting to you - you will probably have some fun with it.I'd give Kingdom 80's aIt ain't rad, nor wack.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, maybe even best in the series, provides a good chunk of lore for why things happen in previous games.Honestly though it would be interesting to see a four player adaptation considering there are four characters.All in all, good 6 and a half hours, the gameplay was smooth, visuals were stunning, music was ear candy.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR- At BottomFirst let me say if you loved the other games as much as I have...You may not like this game. Many key mechanics that have been developed threw out the kingdom franchise seem to have been removed from the game. Keep in mind when playing this that its a story based experience. Once you leave a "zone" (known as islands in previous games) you don't seem to be able to return to them later on. Despite this i enjoyed the challenge; on my second play threw I cleared out each new area as i went knowing if i missed something i couldn't come back. This combined with how hand holdy the tutorial can be at time makes your first play threw feel vary... "on rail" and fast. As of this time i have completed all but 4 achievements in 10 hours and 3 play thews. At no point in time did i ever feel any level of difficulty however i did really enjoy the story and i think for the current price it is worth its cost. Despite the fact that i have long sens finished two crowns and its achievements i keep coming back to it over and over again; however with kingdom 80's, outside of the dev's adding a more traditional "free roam" variant to the game... once i complete the achievements i don't see myself returning to this game.TLDR: I think the game is worth its cost and has a fun story; however its definitely not for all returning players.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: probably the most engaging Kingdom game so far. each chapter has drastically different sets, so it doesn’t feel entirely repetitive despite its similar gameplay to the previous installments. if you never played a Kingdom game and only plan on getting one of them, get Kingdom Eighties; if you played Kingdom games before and just wanted to try out this new game, you could get it when it’s on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a very good game. I'm assuming anyone who's reading this has already played it's predecessors, to that degree it's in essence quite the same, though different enough to be worth it's price.My only real two complaints about the game are that whilst there is an animated cutscene, every cutscene after that is very much static. I was honestly hoping for more, though I understand that isn't a priority, especially if you replay the game, you're liable to just skip them immediately to save time.The other is - as of writing - there isn't any sort of "challenge" islands so to speak and in lieu of this on my end, I'm attempting to get every achievement in the game, including completing the game on Cursed difficulty. I recommend if you've done either normal or hard first, it's then worth a shot since it is incredibly difficult unless you're very familiar with the game, as it's one of those games where the phrase "easy to learn, hard to master" rings true.In any case, my only recommends to improve the game would be to create challenges similar to the challenge islands in the other games, even if they're distinctly similar to those ones.Overall, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it. If you only play on normal it's pretty easy adventure to get through in 6 hours and it doesn't have co-op like previous game, but these aren't really negatives for me. Overall if you likes other Kingdom games, you will enjoy this one too. If you are new to series, I recommend getting Kingdom: Two Crowns.Next it's time to challenge myself with harder difficulties, let's go!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★★When it comes to gaming experiences, Kingdom Eighties is an absolute gem that takes players on a nostalgic journey through the vibrant era of the 1980s. As I delved into the game, I couldn't help but feel a sense of pure joy and excitement. It's disheartening to see that some reviews have been negative, mostly due to expectations for additional content. However, from my perspective, Kingdom Eighties stands as a work of art and easily ranks as the best game I have played this year.One of the standout features of Kingdom Eighties is its attention to detail. The developers have meticulously recreated the vibrant aesthetics, iconic music, and cultural references that defined the '80s. Every pixel, every synthwave soundtrack, and every neon light evokes a sense of nostalgia that transports players back to that extraordinary era. The game's art style perfectly captures the essence of the time, immersing players in a world that feels both familiar and captivating. If you have a love for the '80s or simply appreciate well-crafted gaming experiences, this game is an absolute must-play. Prepare to be transported to a time where neon dreams and pixelated wonders come to life.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to other games of this series, Kingdom Eighties is simpler and more straightforward. What it lacks in depth, however, it makes up for by being easy to pick up, play, and enjoy. The distinct "Saturday Morning Cartoon" feel is cheesy, but in a good way if you're into that kind of thing. I am, and found it more fun. The other games had a darker, more foreboding feel, but this one has a more fun adventure tone to it which is a nice change of pace.It is short with little variation in game play. Not that I found the originals all that varied either. The greater simplicity actually does make it more enjoyable for me since I don't have to juggle things like seasons while the Greedling horde ramps up to impossible to deal with levels (though on higher difficulties, the horde can certainly get to that level). In that sense, this can be seen as a more "bite sized" version of Kingdom.So yeah, short, sweet, and fun. I enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 19 hours to beat. If you like the series you will enjoy this. I think for the next game - they really need to switch it up. This is more like a fully fleshed out version of their old games into a campaign. What I liked about the previous games this game is lacking, but it also adds enough new things that I enjoyed it on a single play through. I'm just not sure I'll ever play it again. That's a big difference between this game and the last ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: The game might not be a total standout, but it sure keeps its promises. If you're eager to jump into a world full of electronic music, teenage vibes, and hidden monsters, then you're in the right spot. The mood it sets? Top-notch. It's an easy, laid-back game with nice 2D graphics, even though it can get a bit repetitive.This is my first go at a kingdom game, so I can't say if it matches up with other games in the series, but it's been an interesting journey. However, the repeating pattern of the game might keep you hooked until only about level 4. But if you're someone who enjoys the pulsing beats of synthwave and vaporwave, this game might be just what you're looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended it!It's quite enjoyable with a new style of Kingdom series.This version is like a casual one compare to the previous series. If you survive that, this one super casual! Just enjoy the story line and puzzle.This series is good at tricking me when I think what it used to be on the previous one and it should be the same mechanic here, but it's not. Which create a full of surprise on each episode.Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a sequel to two crowns, but it never really claimed to be.  It feels like a neat little spin-off trying out some new mechanics.The story is about as saturday morning as you can get, but if you enjoy Kingdom, you'll enjoy this - there are plenty of little easter eggs to find, and it plays in a suitably different way to be worth the cost.No regrets buying this, I doubt you will have any either for the cost.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom has offered the same game experience for what, 4 games now? This is basically the same. It is however much more episodic and story driven. Each island is custom down to how the coin generating buildings look and the way you beat it is different each time.Instead of getting a farm or a fishing place, you get a copy-paste coin generating building but it can be a pizza place, arcade, whatever. This simplifies the coin generation and gives more way for combat, which is slightly more engaging in that you don't just send knights off, but one of your companions carry a 'big shield' which your units rally behind. You can move it back and forth and to both sides of the screen etc.Overall, a much better, simpler, yet more complex introduction to the Kingdom genre. Two Crowns however is still the best 'raw' arcade-like version of the game. This is a reskin spin-off.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Kingdom Camp!This camp is rulled by a guy in a hoodie, who buys kids at their homes for just 5 bucks and makes them work from dusk to dawn to get more money or trains them as a full-time killing machines that shoot or stab any entity deemed foreign to camp on sight. Yes, even if it is a cute fluffy bunny, it will be shot, skinned, processed and sold by the kids. All the money go to the hoodie boss, no need for any salary at this paradise! Any escapee kid would be given to greeds as a meat shield for the boss.In case of unforseen events he has 3 overseers to help him with the discipline at the camp. One of them is a hacker who cracks security systems and constructs from sticks and stones giant mechanical machines of death shooting lasers at anything considered an enemy. Another one is a tinkerer who can transform an old broken minivan into a military-grade zombie-mobile with just some spare parts. And the last one is the muscle guy, who is ready to bring a bulletproof container under heavy fire for just 1 gold to cover the boss. While on break, these guys find special enjoyment in trampling any small living things designated as enemies - that might be one of the reasons why there are no revolts in the camp at all.The hoodie boss also has very intricate ways of dealing with his enemies - he shoots them full of holes, burns them till only ashes remains, crushes them with heavy machinery and many more. Heck, sometimes he even poops money on them!Once again, welcome to Kingdom Camp, the place noone ever leaves!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I could say a lot of things and go in depth about everything but that would take a while and I haven't even finished Act II. Perhaps I'll do that later. All I can say at the moment is that the second part really made me realise how much has been switched up compared to the old games and it suddenly drew me in. So much so I felt like I needed to give it a positive review already just to do my part at getting others to possibly buy this. Although I do love Two Crowns for it's multiplayer and old timey aesthetic, Eighties takes a fresh and creative new swing on the mechanics and visual aesthetics. And it's already seeming to be engaging me enough even with how little I've played that I can tell I'm going to enjoy it regardless of being limited to single player. Also, considering the inclusion of a nice little story, I can now see why it doesn't need a co op as the game focuses itself on investing you into the charming characters and entire 80's world. The Kingdom games have always been good for a chill time whilst also being slightly terrifying and this does not change that while allowing the overall story to grow and for the gameplay to remain familiar enough to intuit your way through yet still different enough to be worth the title as a whole new game and not just an extended DLC for Two Crowns.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed completing the normal difficulty of the game. As an avid fan of Raw Fury's Kingdom series, I must admit a personal inclination towards Kingdom Two Crowns and its predecessors. However, I cannot overlook the remarkable work put into this game's graphics and pixel art, which truly stand out. While I found immense pleasure in playing the game, I couldn't help but yearn for a deeper and more extensive game play experience, reminiscent of the earlier Kingdoms titles. Nonetheless, my love for this game remains unwavering. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: fun, relaxing, and enjoyable. i finished the story in almost a single session as i have serious issues. Kingdom Eighties is different from the other Kingdom instalments but felt good as it doesn't just resell Two Crowns. it has a main story to focus around, and mechanics that are a little less complicated for new players along with adding more/different buildings with their own unique operations. a large issue arises with its focus on story, to me story games don't have much replay value and lacking non linear islands doesn't help with replay value. unfortunately for people familiar with the kingdom series, it lacks the complex mechanics and environment that the other games have so that it can appeal to younger or different audiences. i did like the dumpster change for sieges, but this left the 4 divisions kind of useless to me
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is an early review because at this point I've only played for 7 hours, but I'm a huge fan of the Kingdoms franchise. My favorite up until now was Two Crowns, but the first one is also great. I've been waiting for this game to come out for so long, like checking the page multiple times a week hoping for updates. I have played over 100 hours of Two Crowns and still come back for more. The Kingdom franchise games are all the same layout with differing details, like vehicles and powers, and they're all side scroller pixel games. They're also some of the most visually beautiful games I've ever played. It's a perfect mix of chill and strategy. Kingdom Eighties is super cute and Stranger Things adjacent, with cute eighties motifs, like the colored string lights, the character layouts, and fun eighties features. It's interesting to have the posse aspect, instead of weapons (so far), they will charge and push back the Greed monsters, which makes it pretty helpful, but honestly not sure if I like the posse vs weapons. All of this review is based on my knowledge of all Kingdom games and how I feel the newest one adds to the franchise. I'm still on my first island, but so far it's pretty straightforward and with their interesting "camper cabins" that produce campers to hire with a coin to be archers, builders, and to work in spots like fishing and a mess hall- it makes everything pretty easy. Honestly I'll most likely go back and play it on difficult, but again, I'm still on the first island. Looking forward to playing more and may update my review as I go. Happy playing, Campers!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Short answer: If you are a fan of the kingdom two crowns series, go ahead and put this game in your cart.Amazing soundtrack just like the first. plays similar to the original one but there are some big key differences. 1. the NPCs you can get help you out often and a lot2. there is in fact a story this time around. pretty decent3. loads of awesome references to the 80s4. your workers earn money by doing chores, rather than trades like the farmer role in the old one. Faster money gain. 5. every island feels different, and with objectives now. Overall a fantastic game. no bugs or problems. It was kinda short coming in at 5 hours but I enjoyed it, and will replay it again. I am interested to see what will come out next with this game and I enjoy supporting these devs. they do a fantastic job.

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: this is one of my favorite game series. _childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, just Wow (Insert GIF of Owen Wilson saying "Wow" here). This Kingdom game is the least buggy at launch. Only issue I had was that one of my bicycle riding friends walked infinitely into the last portal,  which i had just destroyed. It fixed itself upon arriving at the second island. The Kingdom series offer some of the most interesting and creative tower defence styled combat. I've been hooked on Tower Defense games ever since Pixel Junk's Monsters. If you like Tower Defense and haven't played the kingdom series yet, you are missing out.  The first one, Kingdom Classic, is where it all started. It's also free. All the time. I finished the game in 6.4 hours on normal, now to replay through it on hard then on cursed which will put my playtime between 25 to 30 hours approximately. This game is not expensive and has a lot of content to get into! So there you go, go buy Kingdom Eighties right now. You know you want to. While you're at it check out New Lands and Two Crowns. Both are amazing and its neat to see how much they refined the experience from game to game and year to year( spoiler alert - the games get better with each outing.)  Peace out Steam people!!

_childDocuments_.review: If this, the animations, the music, the concept, the mechanics is the end point of me having bought everything in the Kingom series, this makes me very happy, I love this concept, it's great, so... reminiscent and retro.If this, the animations, the music, the concept, the mechanics is the end point of me having bought everything in the Kingom series, this makes me very happy, I love this concept, it's great, so... reminiscent and retro.This next part is a part where I decided to edit my review.It's a short game, certainly a downgrade from two crowns Norse Lands, it's not bad, it's an excellent entry point, the little shack with works mechanic is very good but it lacks things. Clearly the use of coins, solely it's because you don't get to go back to previous areas to recover gems you haven't acquired so they did away withj gems altogether.Not to mention this is another entry in the "Wow so cool, so retro, synthwave and old tech" pieces of media that feel... not right... it's like when Destiny 2 promised me that Lightfall would be "like an 80's action movie about a buddy cop story and a city under siege". This isn't that bad, but it just lacks the proper flair. It doesn't help the fact that once the game is done, it's done. I always enjoy a Kingdom run, really like taking the Stag out for a ride because it's fun to defend multiple islands, get some rides, gather some friends (the special workers) and specially in Norse Lands, find and use some artifacts, but this onef feels like a strip down version of all that.If this is your first Kingdom game or really enjoy the Kingdom series, give it a whirl, otherwise Kingdom: Two Crowns Norse Lands is way, way better.

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit of a kingdom freak so I was pretty excited when this dropped. picked it up right and beat it in a few days. Overall a very fun addition to the kingdom franchise. I was born in the 80's, so the look and references to things like ET and back to the future are a lot of fun. The retro cartoon cut scenes were cool, but I would have been fine without them if it meant the developers could have made this game a little longer. Another one or two lands to rule over would have been nice.which brings me to the negatives. It felt a little short, maybe it's just because I want my kingdom plays to last forever, but one or two more lands would have been nice. Also, it needs a two player mode! Kingdom: Two Crowns was a lot of fun to play with a friend.My hope is there are plans for a DLC or another sequel to give us these experiences.All in all, if you've enjoyed the other kingdom games, you will likely enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom Eighties is a nostalgia game, a side project, a spin off. Its beautiful, fun and overall good.However, its short and its a lot more directed than the other games. Does this mean its bad? Not at all. Its interesting to get some lore on the greed and while corny, its quite comfortable to play.My only issues is that the graphics are a mess in the later stages, they blend in too much with each other, leaving your eyes no where to rest, making the screen feel busy and chaotic. Its something you get used to, but level 2 took a lot of getting used to.Honestly, its a fun little game if you have the time and 12 bucks. You likely wont get a lot of re-play value out of it as it stands, but you'll likely enjoy your time while playing it. Took me around 8 hours to play through on hard, and that was with 2 resets due to the graphics causing me to overlook stuff that were integral. (Not to mention theres no way of knowing what you're spending coins on often. This can lead to issues like when you spend 5 coins on a tower that spawns a wave of enemies).
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: If you absolutely need another fix of kingdom this will scratch your itch, but in reality its the latest in a growing line of Video Game IP's that decides to steer some DLC heavily into childhood nostalgia at whatever cost.Like Far Cry Blood Dragon, and X-Com Chimera squad this is a game that reasons it can trade in its own metacritic score to pepper its world in synthwave colours and jokey winks to the audience.  Thing is that 80s nostaliga is not a replacement when it comes at the cost of the gameplay your fans came for in the first place.The game arrives wihtout any user guides or explanations over what has changed, presumably because it reasons that its treasure hunt is its own reward. the devs on twitter didnt' even reply when asked what the purpose/function of one of the vehicles was.  While perfectly playable, the experience removes a lot of navigation options from warping around the islands to even returning to levels.  billing itself as a strictly 1player and strictly linear experience it just comes across as a frankly bizarre game design decision to lean in on replayablilty over the first 3 titles and then lean hard out of that direction of travel because telling the world 'i grew up on E.T.'Baiting gamers like southparks member-berries was more important than maintaining the high quality bar that has meant every new title from New Lands through to NorseLands built on the successes of last time.Sure they Eighties may attract non kingdom fans, but when the quality is lower than usual those folks won't stick around. if you want a fix of kingdom or the 1980s at whatever cost have at ye, ortherwise you can give it a skip.

_childDocuments_.review: Look- if you were already a fan of Kingdom Series games then you have already bought this.That's what I did. For ten bucks I am very happy with my purchase. Thank you for making this warm and gooey game of Nostalgia.

All in all, especially considering the price tag, not a bad thing to pick up to play for the weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Great 80s references, lots of fun things to discover, but a pretty short game overall.  I've no regrets buying at full price, but only because I've gotten such value out of everything else in the Kingdom series.  Might be worth waiting for a sale on this one, or waiting to see if more content is added.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: After coming down from playing through Two Crowns, and recently picking up Nordlands, I have to admit that my feelings for Kingdom: Eighties is certainly mixed.On one hand you have a charming new aesthetic. The music is lovely, and I'll never once get over seeing the tiny tots running around with their too-big hats completing jobs. The price tag is also lower, every Easter egg to the older games is appreciated, and as someone who never took the chance at playing the multiplayer of Two Crowns, I actually really enjoy having companion characters.But as slim as the price tag is, so is the game play. Mechanics have been dropped, enemies are a breeze to get through, there are very few neat unlockables outside of the introduced mounts, and most of the time I found myself finishing a level and thinking...is this really it? Am I already done? I'll be honest, the replayability seems nonexistent. I feel like there was a great deal of potential here, but it just sort of falls flat. Being able to switch between kids would have been lovely-- I would gladly take on the role of protecting the royal for a change-- and though I liked having a story to follow, it was over so quickly I can't very well recall most of it. I'll be a darn liar saying if a DLC came out I wouldn't snatch that sucker up. This game filled the spot of me needing something to do while doing something else, but the thing was about the older games I kept wanting to go back to play them when I was otherwise occupied. This one I'll finish, and until a DLC is out, it'll be left to dust in my gaming library, I'm afraid. Items removed: -No gems for unlocking unique characters/mounts/puzzles,-No sending out squads to defeat enemies on their own (sending out tots for this on their own might be odd, but then why not send a teen with them?),-No unique unlockable units outside of the companions (which sounds like an odd complaint, but you find out what the companions do pretty quickly, and two of them you get on the very first level. Where's the mystery in that?),-No unique locations to puzzle out (you can unlock small areas for the tots to work at, which gets coin, and their animations are adorable, but it feels bland after awhile),-No returning to previous levels (there's no reason to, I did everything available on every level pretty quickly and that mostly meant "collect item, destroy enemy, leave")All of the above sounds like too much to give anyone a reason to buy the game, but it's still kind of fun. I still adore what this company has done, and I want them to continue putting out gems. This one is more like a neat rock, but it'll be on my shelf alongside the real beauties, all the same. tl;dr: Buy game, it's ten bucks, and it's still worth it, especially coming from a small studio that's at least putting out unique titles. What else are you going to spend ten bucks on? A mediocre burger you'll finish in one sitting? C'mon.

_childDocuments_.review: The Kingdom series is an absolute blast.-Beautiful graphics-Melodic and inviting sound track-Simple to understand and easy to vary mechanics All in all a fun game to take seriously or as a time waster, and all of this is applicable to Kingdom as a series, not just EIGHTIES, with this stand alone you can add to the above:-Fun synth vibes-Stranger Things/Goonies/80's nostalgia aesthetic -A more linear form of progression (if you are familiar with the series, there seems to be less back tracking)-Companions! You travel with a group instead of alone

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the series and someone who grew up in the 80s I knew the game would be good, but I was still surprised to see all the references to 80s pop culture that they managed to cram into this game.They even explain why a medieval series has moved into the 20th century and they do it in the most 80s way possible.If you enjoyed the other games in the series, this one is a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect introduction to the Kingdom series of games (Kingdom, Kingdom Two Crowns, Kingdom Eighties). The other games have WAY WAY more mechanics, and multiple islands you have to bounce around between, and complicated mounts, etc.--> It's short, and a very well rounded and extremely well executed experience. <--It took me like 10 hours to complete it, but you really don't feel shorted, and you don't feel like you want more. _childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game; it's not perfect, but it definitely lived up to my expectations and then some.The things i liked: I love the new siege mechanic, I love the new mounts. The different requirements for recruiting the various companions was fun. good soundtrack (not quite as great as the Two Crowns soundtrack, but that's a pretty high bar to clear). I also just get a giggle about the idea i'm giving bows and arrows to small children, but that might just be me...The things i didnt like so much: I wish there were more achievements to go for, and i'd love for some kind of endless/challenge mode to give a greater amount of replayability once the main story is done.A side note: this game is Very 80s aesthetic. I loved it, lots of bright colors, lots of clutter, lots of LOTS! If you dont like that aeshtetic, you may have a lot less fun.TLDR: fun, well worth the $10, but i wish there was more of everything
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Wish it were longer/a little more robust, but I loved it as a snack-sized Kingdom DLC. Sweet little story, new mechanics were fun, enjoyed the weird variety of rides, music and look were absolutely great.I'd say this one is a little more cozy than other titles in the franchise, but I'd love to see it expanded with more of the features from other Kingdom titles to have the option of bringing the difficulty & replayability more in line with stuff like New Lands.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: While I did enjoy the new mechanics with the customisable turrets and "team" siege with the crew. It was surprisingly easy and forgiving even on the hardest difficulty. There was lots of room to recover from financial ruin or having your entire camp wiped out during a double revenge + blood moon wave.Co-op and character/mount switch was a great addition to Two Crowns, it was a tad unfortunate to see both merged into your ragtag crew of AI friends.  There was so much room for worldbuilding and character backstory that I feel like the story cut-scene is a very "meh" approach to having a story mode. I hope we see some of these gaps filled in during future content updates.Art and music is great as always, there's plenty of cheeky 80's Easter eggs for anyone chasing 80's nostalgia.I don't think I would ever give up on the Kingdom series, but I hope it won't let us down. ;)TLDR- I don't mind recommending K80's to friends who wants to have a fun time and try out the entire franchise later. But I'm going to cautiously hopeful for any future DLCs that could test the true veterans.

_childDocuments_.review: Fellow fans of the series need no introduction, but let's do it anyway, for the rest of you.Kingdom is a side-scrolling strategy game with simple resource management. There's 2 in fact; coin and people. You fight against an eldritch enemy horde called The Greed. Their aim is to take everything away. That's it, that's all you're getting.Kingdom: Eighties is the newest instalment of the series in a brand new setting, that's right, you guessed it, it's the eighties. Can you remember how many pop culture references came from my birth decade? Fury Studios do, you'll find a huge number of them as you play. I mean it. I can't begin to count them all.Okay, let's get to the meat of it. It plays just like the other instalments. You ride left or right, recruit kids with coins, give them hammers or bows and set them to work. Of course there is much more to it. For some, it might help if you think of this as a 2 route tower defence. Build up walls, your archers will go out and hunt during the day and come back to stand behind the safety of your walls at night, while raining arrows upon any attacking Greed.Don't think it will be easy though. You need to expand to get anywhere. Mark trees to be cut down, find areas for the kids to do chores to earn more coin. You're going to need it. You really don't want to be caught without coins in your bag. What will the greed take from you if you have no coin? Your crown of course, that will be a game over.Every 7 days or so the Greed will launch a major assault, you might even see a Greed variant. I hope you remembered to upgrade your walls.One fun change from the previous games is there are no hermits. They were characters that gave unique upgrades to structures. Now we have companions instead, they will ride bikes along with you and provide upgrades, move siege barriers and even attack or knock back Greed who get too close. Useful right?Occasionally you might find a new mode of transport, it'll cost you coins, but they all have strengths and weaknesses. Try them all, I'm sure you'll find the perfect ride for you!So, you've got the basics down, are you enjoying it? I certainly did. I binged it to completion in just under 9 hours on normal mode. That may be rather slow compared to some of you but I turtle in these games. I'm slow and methodical. That's just my personality coming through. That's not to say the game is short. For the price you pay, there is a great amount of content and features you might not notice in your first play-through. Knowing the track record of the developers, they're likely to add more as time goes on. At least, I sincerely hope so.Something else that is new to the series is the story and animated cut-scenes. These really do enhance the experience in my opinion. It's a nice direction that could suit potential future titles very well. We can only wait to see what happens from here on.I'm sure there is much more you'd like to know about Kingdom: Eighties but I don't want to spoil the joy of exploration. Jump in, ride around and discover all the new content and features.I don't usually give ratings but I think this one deserves something quantifiable. So here we go, Kingdom: Eighties has earned a 9/10 from me. The only thing that would earn it the extra point is if they made it longer, I'm sure most will be satisfied as is, but with how much I loved it, I wanted more.

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed the game for what it is, I agree with others that it was too short, removed many mechanics and only added a few new ones. The game was far too simple and each level while aesthetically unique were functionally the same. Game is linear and you only really need to push one direction to complete the level, theres very little incentive to push in both directions, other than to unlock a mount or unlock a job for coin production, possibly due to the very limited procedural generation you may be required to obtain something on the other side of the map. I liked the companions, however they did make the game much easier. My biggest gripe is it really lacks any replayability once youve completed the store. Event if the store was eh, I appreciated they included a small story in a game that otherwise has never had one. The art and music was great, really like the theme of this one. _childDocuments_.review: A fun spin on the traditional Kingdom formula. _childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: I'm a huge fan of the Kingdoom series, i love its simple style and its hard learning curve. You get very little explanations of what's going on and have to try and error until you get it. I played Kingdom, New Lands, Two Crowns, Shogun and Deadlands. And i liked every one of them in their own way because their mechanics differed a bit though the core mechanics were always the same.And now we have Kingdom Eighties. I am a "child of the eighties" so this was a no-brainer for me. 80s, synthwave music and pixelart? I'm totally in.A STORY?The first big change here is the fact there is a real story with cutscenes. And I like it! It is well done, has a nice retro touch to it and just doesn't disturb at all. Plus, there is a real connection between the levels, not the standalone-feel of the islands as before. Sure, it's not a Nolan-esque story with plottwists and deep characters, but still it's a nice addition to the series.SAME MECHANICS?You still build archers, constructors and walls. And you still walk from left to right (or vice versa) to manage things. The rest is a bit different - no farming for example (but money isn't a problem), less units (and soldiers are pointless imo), more environment stuff but less things to build. Instead there is a "big goal" for every level to step on with the story. MORE EXPLANATIONS?What i liked the most about Kingdom was that there were no explanations (just a few at the beginning) and you had to figure out the rest on your own. This changes drastically with the Kingdom Eighties. You'll see a lot more help in form of little icons above the things you'll find and this made it a bit too easy for me.TOO EASY?Yep, Eighties is more a Kingdom light. You have a lot less building possibillities and you can't (and don't need to) go back to earlier levels. If you rush you could probably finish it in 2 hours or even less. I like some of the new mechanics, the movable trash container for example makes the game a lot more forgiving e. g. when you accidentally start building just before the night sets in. At the same time you can just rush through once you built the trash shield and the robot, they make it very easy to proceed. Even the big guys are no problem at all anymore. And because i read it in other comments: YOU CAN LET THE TRASH CONTAINER STAND ANYWHERE AND DON'T NEED TO TAKE IT WITH YOU TO THE OTHER END OF THE LEVEL. ;)STILL KINGDOM?Yes, BUT this one clearly has its focus on the single player story part, the pixelart and the soundtrack. There are lots of easter eggs of all the cool stuff we all liked in the 80s, that is some nice fanservice. The sound is brilliant as always, i absolutely adore the sound design, gets me every time. Sometimes the art is bit overkill, but always putting the eighties on screen - if you ever watched advertisements or outfits and hairstyles from the eighties... well... those times brought some really weird things to life XD. I personally really like the way the purple stuff adopts the plants and animals, that's much nicer than in every Kingdom before. And it is short, REALLY short.BUY IT?I'd say yes, even for 10 bucks. It is short, way too short, definitely yes. There is no coop-mode, another definitely yes. But still, it is a nice addition to the Kingdom series and personally i like the style. You can see it went a lot of work into the art stuff, there is a lot of love to find. The best scenario probably is you buy it if you are completely new to the Kingdom series as Eighties is a good entering part. Once you finished it you can step on to New Lands and then Two Crowns to get the real Kingdom with all its deep mechanics, coop-mode and replayability :)

_childDocuments_.review: Really short and not as fun as the original.The story is a very, very, very poor "Stranger Things" at home. I wonder what the 3 additional writers from the credits did, but it would have been cheaper and better to ask ChatGPT for a short 80s horrorstory in Stranger Things style. I guess people love references to the 80s so we got it in like every second pixel.. it felt more like: how many easy recognizable things from 80s pop culture can we put into every level? Also you can't skip the really boring completely unnecessary cut scenes. Yawn.Gameplay: You now have companions.. but just because. They are not helping the gameplay at all... they just had to be there because: Stranger Things vibe. The levels are beautiful pixel optic, they are just so cramped with stuff, that it is hard to see things you can interact with. Also all the bikes you can interact with, even if you dont want to because they are in the way.The new squad mechanic is kind of annoying, it looks fun at first but gets quite cumbersome later on.I really liked the original where you send out your squad and they do their thing while you help them by throwing money at them or just kill the stuff they encounter. Now you get a shield object in the front and a shooting tower that follows you where ever you go. Even when you need to collect money from the other side of the level.I really liked the soundtrack though.All in all I had not at all the fun I hoped I would get. I don't care for the lost money, but for the opportunity from the devs to make a really good game once again. Let's shoehorn every aspect of Stranger Things (besides the interesting characters and story) into a game just for the sake of it didn't work well on my end.
