_childDocuments_.review: Child Labour at its finest loljokes aside, the game is great, the ending couldve been more fleshed out, it kinda seems abrupt, thats the main thing it kinda lowers the rankings for this game, the whole game play is nice tho, its has nicer items you can use through the journey, but once you finish it theres zero replay value. still good tho, id give it 7.6/10The visuals are nice just wish it was longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, more story-oriented than the previous ones, and with great visuals, music and new gameplay additions.It also extends the lore of Kingdom, which is cool !If you are a veteran of Kingdom games, I suggest you start the game in Cursed mode if you want real challenge, because I started it in Hard and it was still a bit too easy for me, took me about 6 hours to finish it without real difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I have very mixed feelings on this game and am overall disappointed. Here is what I have experienced after playing it on the highest difficulty and on normal mode to see the differences.Pros-Amazing art detail. They have improved every time they make a new game for the visuals such as number of layers, color coordination and art designs.-Great music-Different when compared to other Kingdom games-Has more variety of enemies-The highest difficulty is actually a challenge. It feels thrilling and was actually probably one of the more challenging things I had to complete in the series.-Has an actual storyline, that is somewhat goodCons-Lack of content/replayability; overpriced for the amount you get-Over complicates on how to do things to the point where it can be frustrating-Does not have the satisfying progression, and feel rewarding for new items when compared to Kingdom Two Crowns-Lacks the mystery the previous games had, which helps keep the game interesting-Another point about the lack of mystery is that it tells you what side the big portal is on and what to destroy which removes the fun of exploring for it on your own-More basic in what you can do when compared to prior games as some mechanics have been removed entirely, and what they add is very bland, and limited-The lower difficulties helps you realise how empty the game feels-Cannot go back to previous levels if you missed any secretsThis feels like a broken down version of the previous Kingdom games. The devs definitely put in the effort but it takes more content away than it gives. If you have played any of the previous games, then you will enjoy this one because it is more kingdom and I would say give it a try, but if you are a new player, I do not think it is as good or as enjoyable as Kingdom Two Crowns, and therefore I would not recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Not a huge departure from the rest of the series, but it has great style and a cute story. Some mechanics have been removed, others added, but largely I'd say it's less-complicated than some other entries. Some nice quality-of-life changes that prevent you from ruining your campaign due to simple mistakes/unintended consequences.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best looking Kingdom game of them all but also the least replayable.What they've put into the visuals is amazing! Such detailed environments are simply breathtaking. All the 80s hommage is great, hidden "quests" as well.But it all comes to the expense of replayability. This time there is a story, but that means you cannot travel between "islands", or rather biomes. The story is also a bit short for my taste and I could finish it pretty quickly.Yes, I like the game, it reminds me of my childhood and is still a Kingdom game. However I am a bit disappointed... It's more about the art and aesthetic than gameplay.Do I recommend it? Absolutely.Is there a better Kingdom game? Two Crowns. Definitely.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about the game, but overall I'd recommend. _childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the addition of a story and some quality of life upgrades, but I feel like this game would be a bit better with a proper endless mode where you can choose the map and have all characters + structures on each one, and the little bit of delay between fulfilling an upgrade and being able to upgrade something else has caused many micro stutters / wrong coin drops from someone very used to the older timings. The new vehicles were also a nice touch.Overall, this game has a fun theme and neat story that makes for a solid addition to the franchise.

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: For those who played the previous ones, this one feels like a dumbed down version. Short, easier, few constructions and upgrades, portals very close to each other, obvious choices to make... you really don't have to think much. If you are new to the series though, it's a very good starting point. This one is way less punitive to wrong decisions like, say, New Lands. Also there's a good effort explaining what you need to do in order to unlock things and progress. I guess for the newcomers there will be a lot to take and understand, and then jumping into Two Crows will not feel that overwhelming. Anyway, I loved the 80s take, music, references, art style etc. So yeah, it was easy, short, and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: I love this franchise, I'm 200+ hours into Kingdom Two Crowns, but that version is a better experience than this. I beat this three times very quickly and I don't see myself playing it again. Ever. Maybe if there's a huge update and new areas added? BUT the new gameplay concepts and weapons on Kingdom Eighties are bad@$$. This game IS fun but it doesn't have the original games feeling of accomplishment, you just move forward until it's over (like an actual 80's videogame). I'd play a session of the original Kingdom for DAYS. This version is over in about 3 hours, even if you play on hard. The original Kingdom is much longer, because you have to backtrack to the previous islands to progress.    Sooooo.. if Steam used a 5-star rating system, I'd give this 3 stars. Kinda seems like a downgrade from the original. Cant give this a thumbs down though!
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the entire Kingdom series, I was really looking forward to this game.  I really love the beautiful artwork and 80's aesthetic and how they tied in game mechanics and made them work in interesting new ways.  However, it's not difficult (I beat it easily on hard), it's short and there really is only one way to play it and it actually becomes a little tedious.   The game also shows you what to do in a way that the original Kingdoms didn't, which is actually not good.  Part of what has always made this series cool is the cryptic nature of the instruction. Clues are there but it's rarely explicit.  It was always fun and rewarding discovering new mechanics that you didn't know about.  80's doesn't have that.  Also, the story is fairly tropey and the writing not actually that great.  They didn't even name the characters, they just gave them their roles as names (leader, champ, tinkerer, wiz).   I enjoyed the game but my takeaway is pretty mixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: This games improve alot on the kingdom stories and the story amazing while the may have similarity to kingdom two crowns campaign in the sense its not survival like kingdoms it makes up with interesting story i hope in the future they challenge or some form of survival highly recommend if your a fan of the series also look out for easter egg
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game in 7½h on difficulty 4/5, got 26/31 achievements, and had a good time.A lot of things have been streamlined and simplified.Only three 'classes' of minions, unemployed, workers and archers.Archers still hunt critters for coins, and defend the walls at night.Many locations where both Unemployed and Workers can generate money.Other noteworthy simplifications:'Archer towers' no longer tie up minions and work automagically.Permanent allies that follow you and help knock back enemies.You control the 'assault' when trying to destroy portals, no more 'send knights away and hope'.Can thus kite enemies when assaulting, pelting them with ranged attacks if overextended.Thus would definitely recommend this to someone new to the Kingdom series.As a 90's kid, all the various references made me smirk a few times as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Great installment in the series. The 80s theme is fun, the visuals & cutscenes are dope, and the different levels make it refreshing. This title is more story focused and it definitely benefits from that. Bicycles instead of horses make it a little more accessible since you no longer require grass to recharge your mount; each bicycle has a slight difference in usefulness too. In this title you team up with NPC companions, each with a different function in the grand scheme of things. There is no co-op at launch, but if you came here looking for a single-player 2D tower defense game then you absolutely will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just ok. I've been following the kingdom series for years, but frankly i'm just disappointed by this one. _childDocuments_.review: kingdom has always been fun. its a nice spin on the survival settlement builder. there is always something to plan for, resource and time management are needed for success. and anything can become a gamble. i highly recommend any kingdom game. Kingdom Eighties is the newest entry, and this time around we have a campaign. it's nothing special but it does the job of keeping you engaged for the campaign. took me about 5 hours to beat it on hard. but these games have always been about trying to see how long you can hold out.I do highly recommend it for the price. and to me its a perfect choice for the steam deck
_childDocuments_.name: Kingdom Eighties

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I loved it. I'll do a pros and cons below.Pros:- Music 10/10- Art 10/10- Combat is good- New towers, vehicles, ways to make income, etc- New enemy type- Tons of 80s references. ET, Fargo, Back to the future, Married with children, etc- Throwback to old kingdom games- Plot and story is really good. I loved the cut scenes.Cons:- Playtime is wayyyy too short. I beat it on hard in 5 hours.- Finding the "homeless" kids are difficult. It's hard to tell if I have recruited them or not.- Replay-ability isn't really an option.- Getting into the cave portal on the 4th chapter is a pain. This needs to be fixed asap.- Job system isn't really explained. But I believe normal kids are prioritized for jobs and if their isn't any then builder kids do them.Recommendations:- Needs more content. Either another story afterwards or an endless/wave survival gamemode. Game is just too short.- Needs more upgrades once content is expanded. Dumpster definitely needs upgrades. Like more health or what I say below, adding units into or onto the dumpster.- The knighted kids are basically useless. I literally never used them once during my play-through. It's just a waste of a kid. Some ideas I have; knights charge during defenses then retreat, knights hop into or onto the dumpster during portal assaults and swing their sword, or knights make money somehow like chasing down animals. Knights just need something, they are basically useless. You shouldn't be using knights to defend your retreat, your units already run wayyy before your wall falls. So your next defense should be close enough for knights not to be used.Overall, the game is a solid 9/10. I loved it. Just lacks from being so short. I recommend it but just know you will finish it within 5-8 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: And the saga continues..Thank you for the release!Edit: Ok, what's going on in the last level? In the cave it seems very pointless when the bag is full of money but the trashcan is destroyed. All the kids abruptly leave the scene with it and all you're left with is the agonizing slow death. It seems pretty conceptless to me....Once you've done it, you can always go back into the cave, but then you have (!) to finish it again +  watching the credits.On the other hand, there is many many pixel stuff that I found really good and appropriate. This also includes the pizza and burger store ;D. The parallax scrolling is not to be despised. Reading the daytime by the sun movement was better in Two Crowns.So the short playtime and the somewhat comical ending scratches the surface a bit, but overall it remains a nice game, though I'd rather go back to Kingdom: Two Crowns.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Fans of the series should definitely get this. As the game suggests, do start off on Hard if you're experienced.I might wish this game was a little longer, but on the whole, I think it makes an interesting and fun Kingdom variation.It took me around 5-10 minutes to really get my bearings on the look of each new level, such as what was going to be generating new "kids" (peasants) and how the various pieces were functioning, but after I did, I was able to fall back on previous experience.Some of the changes, other than simple '80's chrome and reference humor:Your companions provide a quite reasonable level of personal defense.Archers don't provide as much income.Recruited "peasants" (kids) will work money-making stations, like farmers.Engineers also take up money-making stations, meaning that the overall build should probably go more engineer-heavy.Towers, once they arrive in the game, don't require people at all to work!In all, a lot of fun to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, very short tho. Someone mentioned that knight are pretty much useless and that the unemployed kids look almost the same as the other ones and I agree. I also hate the fact that it lacks replayability and coop. From the start, it shows new things and unique tasks with each island which was very exciting but later its pretty much the same island but with different environment. The whole story felt like it was one big island from the previous games. The first episode felt like it was polished the most. _childDocuments_.review: i'll make it short.asthetically beautiful game, in my opinion the most beautiful and immersive yet. I enjoyed that part a lot since it also had many references to Stranger Things and the 80s as well, obviously haha.here are the shortcomings: story is simple and straightforward, you don't learn enough about the characters to really care, especially the main character (who looks at times kinda dead inside). the game is linear and you cannot go back after you finished a level. although there are more buildings, almost every single aspect of the games in the series has been simplified which takes depth off of it and thus meaning and progression.I would usually give this a thumbs down since the game is pretty short, not very demanding and quite broken down mechanically. However, I enjoyed it and I think it just should have been a DLC lol. For 10 € (on sale) it is definintely okaay for around 8h of fun, nostalgia, fun references, great music (!!!), beautifully handcrafted levels and cute cutscenes. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, if you have ANY kind of experience with the Kingdom series, DO NOT play on normal. The game will tell you this as well but I know many won't read that. Play on either hard (even that is pretty easy!) or higher for a better experience.Quite enjoyed my time with it. I was afraid it was going to be just a reskin but they do change it up by adding a story, cutscenes and making the game a bit more "linear". Based on some of the reviews I am reading here, you either find this a good thing or a bad thing.  For me, if I wanted something more like regular Kingdom..I would just play that instead.I was also a bit worried about the style, but I am pretty sure that this is something we never have to worry about anymore, graphics and music are amazing as always. 1 complaint is about the child units, it's sometimes hard to tell if I already recruited them or not, or if the yellow helmets were blonde hair etc. Doesn't break the game but could def use some work.The cutscenes we got were cool and new but I found the art style incredibly ugly compared to the amazing pixel art. It is a huge contrast, I also feel like it might have benefited from some voice acting. Also please make them skippable for repeat playthroughs. Story is a little lackluster either way.Overall more of the same, but honestly way easier. There is less to keep track off, way less upgrades and it's pretty short.I would rec this to beginner players of the Kingdom series, veterans will still enjoy this but might themselves disappointed by the dumbed down mechanics. Still giving it a thumbs up because it its core the Kingdom gameplay is fun and greatly addicting and the sounds, music and graphics are always mesmerizing. Personally I find the price quite reasonable too.

_childDocuments_.review: {Missed Opportunity}Context:The concept is fresh and offers a very wide range of possibilities especially when it comes to the original game and its supposed lore of "greeds being an ancient life form that render's a world's growth corrupted with malice.". Having this perspective of the lore seen through the games and dlcs that Kingdom New Lands offer where in the past, different cultures of humanities have fought against these greeds, thriving and progressing until they manage to neutralize the local greeds of their region then as years of peace passed by with the Kingdom Eighties bringing the same old conflict but bringing new additions to solve the problem through technologies that the eighties era offer.Why a Missed Opportunity?The game doesn't fully utilize all of the possibilities that the "Eighties Era" concept could possibly offer.Missed Opportunities and Problems in:[The Story], its lacking, it has the foundations but it was hurried, it was basically "Oh noes, whats  happening? greeds!" then "How Mysterious now im worried about my family" then "lets go save em" and thats basically the major key plots, the other characters werent given any background story at all, as if they didnt have a family themselves, and their characteristics were shallowly introduced. The Gameplay Mechanics doesnt blend well with the story too. Alot of Plotholes, like wheres the government? The military? The Adults?? The game doesnt take advantage of the realism that an Eighties Era can potentially bring and its unlike the original games (Kingdom New Lands and before) where you can really feel the direness and helplessness of the situation as a primitive civilization trying to survive and fight against magical monsters which adds a fun value to the game along with the mechanics. The story shouldve taken an approach which MAKES THE GREEDS PART OF THE SETTING and not as the obvious antagonist instead of it being the only conflict, many conflicts intertwined to one another would make the story more compelling having more depth. Bonus points if some conflicts tackle contemporary issues of the eighties til now (like problems of young teens trying to find who they are in a  massive world or more worldly problems like politics or humanitarian conflicts, war etc.), overall RawFury really missed alot of great opportunities with the concept.[The Game Content and Mechanics]The new additions were nice, but too little new mechanics and its like 80% copy pasted from the originals. Probably because the story was too shallow to add new mechanics that would blend with the story. An idea where new modes of transportations are made through technologies like trains, cars etc. make it possible to travel in different ways, like trains to travel to any train stations on the map immediately which not adds a new mechanic but also content where to make the train stations usable, youd have to clear it out of greeds, a potential epic fight scene where you fight inside the train too. The larger the scope of the story from regional to nationwide or the whole world, the larger the amount of content and the more mechanics there can be but even with the small scope that this game goes for, there were already alot of mechanics and content that couldve still been added without an expensive budget like new mechanics when handling the adult military as a kid where instead of outright command, you indirectly force them to move or do something. which in itself needs to build the game from scratch. or you could just have the protag also be a person of some authority so you dont have to start at a literal scratch. Anything is fine honestly... anything new that sticks to the game's theme. Overall, its still fun but fun in a tired way.  Some new things made it genuinely fun but only 20% of my time was. This isnt really the biggest issues, the story was since the game mechanics and content heavily relies on that.[The Arts: Sound and Graphics]The main art/graphics not including the cutscenes is Stunning, a marvelous masterpiece, honestly like the only(?) redeeming quality of the game, it blends well with the story and the mechanics of the game and it also sets the right mood in every situation, both the visuals and music is. Each music in varying scenarios differ yet blends with one another, a huge greed wave is coming? you'll feel the tension in both the visuals and the sound, the sense of dread that will shudder you in fear, oh its just a peaceful day/night? dam relaxing visuals and music that makes you feel like youre in that world immersed in a beautiful time enjoying the scenery in the background. Very well coordinated, harmonious, a shame that i do not have the vocabulary to concisely explain its beauty.SummaryMeh, i rate it 6/10 overall, was it worth its price? i'd say its worth 55% to 63% of its price, unless if they add more content which isnt paid.If you just want to have a great time on the side of relaxation and just viewing beautiful art while playing something interesting without wasting too much time in playing, this is for you, but for people craving lore and fun/enjoyment in pure gaming, then it aint for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little stand alone side game in the Kingdom series.  It features more story, and actual set characters.  Many of the mechanics are changed since Two Crowns and its DLC Norselands.  Many mechanics are simplified. We still have multiple levels of walls and bases, but once you get Wiz, they're responsible for building unmanned laser turrets that are similar to the ballista towers.  Champ covers the knight role when you go on the offensive, pushing a dumpster to defend the archers, and Wiz brings up the rear with a mobile laser turret. The tinker is left to knock back waves (on a cooldown), and repair the dumpster when the coast is clear. Once you start your offense, you can keep going, as if you were transporting a bomb in Two Crowns. In place of islands, we have multiple settings, which have specific goals to clear.  This is a linear affair, with no travel back to previous stages.  All unlocked mounts are available at bus stops in your current level. There are no more shrines, no hermits, no farms, no pikemen/ninja.  During blood moon events, All archers will automatically go to the besieged end of the camp. Knights are only useful in the event of a wall failure, to protect archers while they fall back.This is probably a good game to start with, if you've never played any of the Kingdom series of games.  It's definitely easier on normal than any of the other games. As for downsides?  It can be difficult to tell the difference between a recruited character and a "vagrant" child. But this really only applies if you haven't been stocking bows or hammers. There's no real benefit to having jobless recruits. It's a little busy, visually, but you should get used to it. It wasn't an issue for me, but your mileage may vary. Some might find it a little short. I didn't.  I wasn't in a rush, and I beat it in 4.2 hours, according to steam.  This is more than acceptable to me.  I would rather have fun playing a short game than be bored playing a long game that's been padded out and has had its pacing ruined in the name of "more hours is more better!"I haven't played any of the Kingdom series in co-op. This game does not have co-op, as is clearly marked. Not a deal breaker for me, obviously. This is a great game to sit down and play for one or two sittings. Well worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review:
Kingdom Eighties is a new and standalone title in the award-winning micro-strategy series, Kingdom. A love letter to the nostalgic days of bike riding, summer camps, and sitting around in your pajamas on a Saturday morning in front of the TV. 

You play as The Leader, a young camp counselor who'll have to protect their family and the entire town from the relentless attack of the mysterious Greed. The young neighbourhood kids will be at your side, and you'll also find some new friends along the way: The Champ, the Tinkerer, and the Wiz will lend you their skills and support in battle.

name: Fear the Spotlight
detailed_description: Fear the Spotlight is an atmospheric third-person horror adventure with a disturbing mystery to unravel. Sneak into school after hours with Vivian and Amy, survive a séance gone wrong, solve tactile puzzles, and, whatever you do, stay out of the spotlight… Sunnyside High has a dark history. When Vivian enters the deserted corridors for a seance with the rebellious Amy, she suddenly ends up alone, and at the mercy of the monster who wanders the halls. Vivian must avoid its gaze, find her friend, and uncover the disturbing, murderous truth of a decades old tragedy. Fear the Spotlight is a creepy love letter to classic 90s horror experiences with a focus of rich storytelling, puzzle solving, and a tense atmosphere. This is a perfect narrative horror game for those new to the genre. THE THRILLS   ESCAPE THE NIGHTMARE   The séance went terribly wrong. Amy has disappeared, and the school has transformed into a nightmarish version of its former self. Play as Vivian to uncover a dark hidden past while attempting to save both you and your friend  DELIGHTFULLY HORRIFYING GAMEPLAY   Sneak to avoid detection from an unknown entity in tense hand-crafted stealth moments as Vivian explores the ominous darkness of the school corridors  Solve highly tactile puzzles that pay homage to classic genre favorites while evolving gameplay to satisfy modern horror fans  Explore the eerie setting of a derelict Sunnyside High with a flashlight, screwdriver, wrench, and more to uncover a web of mysteries  1990s ATMOSPHERIC DREAD   Explore the hellish version of Sunnyside High as Vivian in this ode to classic 90’s teen horror. A retro art style, tense audio design, and a nostalgic setting will delight both veteran fans and those new to the horror genre  AN EXPANDED STORY   Dive even deeper into the dark world of Fear the Spotlight with an extensive additional storyline  Fear the Spotlight is the first title to be published by Blumhouse Games , a video games label within Blumhouse Productions focused on championing the most creative and unique takes on the horror genre.

Easy to become immersed in the game from the style, but the story is pretty weak. Pretty standard teen drama story that doesn't get into anything deep, though it really doesn't need to.At a quick playtime this is a perfect experience for a night of tension. _childDocuments_.review: After a game of oujia gone wrong, your friend gets abducted by unknown powers and you find yourself in the remains of the old schoolgrounds.Overall a fantastic game, it looks beautiful, hand crafted areas with many details. Good voice acting, unique puzzles. Even the chaser is something you havent really seen yet. Wish it would have been longer. I guess the story is rather mediocre, but I dont intend to spoil anything. Not that it matters though, because you cant buy the game.They removed the game off the store October 2023, because they want to add new content and plan console versions. There has been no news on this really. They also talk about improvements while the game sits at 98% positive reviews... what improvements. No one has anything bad to say, my experience was completely bug free, no translation problems or typos.What you do with your creation is your choice, but so is my opinion regarding this. Taking it off the store instead of just leaving it for other players to enjoy, is something I cant understand. You can very well work on a project while keeping it accessible and also make profit at the same time. This is one of the dumbest marketing decisions I have ever encountered on this platform. Cozy Game Pals, you guys are masters at botching your own sales.Today, 22nd of October 2024, they came crawling back and charge double the price from the original release. First you take away the option to purchase it, now you expect people to hand over twice as much money. Not even a relaunch discount included. I own the game, so why exactly should I care about any of this? Because it isnt about me and such practices are ♥♥♥♥♥♥, simple as. Im not sure how anyone with a good conscience can support this. Clown on me all you want.Dear dev, what kinda response is that? I know I get the update automatically, since I own the game. Also, that filler content or "B-Side" you added is in no way worth as much as the base game. Im sure you doubled the price to cope for the loss in revenue when it was off shelves. The fact that you dont even have an introductory offer reflects that. You partnered with a publisher in the hopes to get some sweet investors. Nothing wrong with that, but it just shows how much yall thirst for money now. Maybe dont sabotage your own sales next time?

_childDocuments_.review: Prepare to be transported back to the golden era of survival horror gaming with this remarkable indie gem! Crafted by a passionate duo, this game is an absolute triumph in capturing the essence of PS1-era horror titles. As soon as I fired it up, I was engulfed in a wave of nostalgia, thanks to its classic video game graphics and aesthetics.One of the standout features that immediately drew me in was the game's stellar voice acting. The characters truly come alive with performances that could easily rival those of big-budget productions. The emotional depth and authenticity of the characters served to immerse me even deeper into the gripping narrative.Unlike many contemporary horror games that rely on cheap jump scares, this title takes a different approach. It masterfully builds an eerie atmosphere and sustains spine-tingling tension throughout, leaving me genuinely on edge without resorting to gimmicks.The heart of this game lies in its captivating story. Unlike some horror titles that put gameplay before plot, this one strikes a perfect balance. The narrative unfolds in a way that's both engaging and meaningful, making it an experience you won't forget anytime soon.While it draws inspiration from classics like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, this game manages to forge its own unique identity. It channels the essence of those iconic titles while delivering a more manageable level of stress and anxiety. With a completion time of 2-3 hours, it's the perfect length for a satisfying, immersive gaming session.In summary, this PS1-era throwback is an absolute must-play for horror aficionados and fans of classic gaming. I'm eagerly anticipating what these talented developers have in store for the future. Don't miss out on this extraordinary journey into the heart of classic horror gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, it's back after a year of being delisted from Steam. Fear the Spotlight is a third-person horror puzzle game about Amy and Vivian, two high school students who break into their school, Sunnyside High, to perform a seance believing that it has a strong connection to the spirit world. During the seance, something happens and Amy vanishes, and it's up to Vivian to find and rescue her from the mysterious and dilapidated Sunnyside High.Completing Vivian's story unlocks Amy's chapter from her POV. The game consists of a few sections where you must solve puzzles to get pieces to solve more puzzles all while avoiding a monster shaped like a man but with the head of a spotlight beam. There are small story snippets giving the backstory between the students who perished during a fire that caused the school to close down. The story gradually becomes darker as you progress before the conclusion that led to the events is revealed.The game has a lot of interaction which seems to be common in modern horror demakes - twist to unscrew, move your mouse in circles to tighten, click items to operate them etc. I enjoyed the tactile nature of the game and liked finding a use for all my items; puzzles were relatively straightforward and easy - you don't need to think much to solve them. Vivian operates on a breath meter which is recovered through asthma puffers - which aren't in short supply. As soon as you use one, you're likely to find another one. The game also checkpoints through every door you enter, so it's quite forgiving. There's not much music in the game but it builds atmosphere quite well and the sound design and voice acting are all top notch. The voice acting felt natural for the characters and they were decently personified in the game. Amy's chapter reveals a lot more about the two girls and helps build them into more tangible characters. I found her chapter quite tragic and I really believed that Amy and Vivian relied on each other given the backstory of each. It's not a long game - it took me 2.6 hours to finish the first time, then replaying Vivian's chapter AND then playing Amy's only took me 3.5 hours. I fully believe this is worth playing and one of my favourite of the modern indie horror games that are coming out (that aren't too scary).

_childDocuments_.review: I’m not going to lie, I thought I would not like this game.I despise horror. _childDocuments_.review: Fear the Spotlight is basically a kid-friendly love letter to Silent Hill (or other PS1 era horror games) which is a perfect fit for younger gamers or people who love horror games but might want to have a less intense/stressful experience. Since the dev team is called “Cozy Game Pals”, the name checks out. But even if you do enjoy your hardcore horror games, this indie horror stealth & puzzle game is impressive because it has a clear vision and makes sure that all the details fit. The story is a high school murder mystery with a few creepy apparitions sprinkled in and it’s paced incredibly well and told through notes, cut scenes and a lot of small and big environmental details. The gameplay is reminiscent of PS1 games but controls a lot better, even the parts that annoyed me (our lovely protagonist is very slow even during stressful moments) seem deliberate to create tension. The stealth sections are designed well and therefore offer the adrenaline spike without the frustration. Admitted, stealth wizards might think it’s too easy but even then it might be interesting enough, since hardly any section is alike.The puzzles are also not breaking anyone’s spirit but are varied and quite fun, again, given that this game seems to be aimed at a younger audience as well, this is a fantastic entry game for kids and teens who want to dive into indie horror. I loved the controls and how intuitive everything feels. The voiceover is great, the writing is fun and moves the story along and the different chapters all feel well paced. Nothing overstays its welcome. This is not a long game but that’s an advantage since there is no confusing puzzle box mess in the storytelling, nor any repetitive stuffing to the gameplay. I really have no criticism because it’s so clear what this game wants to achieve and in my view, it does so with a cherry on top.

_childDocuments_.review: Fear The Spotlight is an early resident evil/silent hill inspired horror game taking place in a spooky school with a sordid past. It is one of those games that you just never want to end, nailing everything that it is aiming for.The setting and ambience is incredible. The level design, art style, visual effects, environments - all so engrossing. It feels like a real place. It could’ve been any of our public schools. The PS1 style graphics have some modern flourishes - it’s grainy, wobbly, gritty. The puzzles are so fun and creative. The story is so interesting (think Carrie but darker). The environmental storytelling and bits of lore were great.My only complaint is the length. It took me about 5 hours, but it was possibly my favorite gaming experience this year.If you love early resident evil or silent hill, give this one a go. It’s in my top 5 or so of modern takes on the genre (along with tormented souls and Signalis). I implore you to pick this one up!P.S. - this was my review of the original. The update includes a whole new story, while also being pretty dang short, was good as well. I think I prefer the original story and setting to the “side B”, but I enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: I remembered this game very fondly from the Haunted PS1 collection, so I was super happy when I received the notification of its release! I got it right away and decided to dive into it yesterday. If you're wondering how long does it take to complete, take my current timestamp (2.7 hrs) as an ideal benchmark.Really liked the visuals and overall mood, and as a professional sound designer I also enjoyed this side as well. The only sound I would personally go back to is the "sliding rope" one since it is quite clear it's duck tape (probably over some cardboard?) which found a bit distracting. Something I believe could use a bit work though are the overall animations of the stalking nemesis since they look quite "generic" and as a result were a bit detrimental to its overall scenic presence.However, it is time to just aknowledge the fact that this game is the result of the love of 2 developers who poured their heart in this and I do recommend giving Fear the Spotlight a try. There's plenty of other things I liked, such as the way you interact with items (quite reminiscent of the Wii version of Silent Hill: Shattered Memories). You might argue its length maybe doesn't have enough room to get all the narrative potential from the featured themes, but it has a proper beginning and an end which leaves nothing behind so there's not much else we could be wishing for. While I was playing this I got some Carrie (the film directed from De Palma) vibes too along something from The Missing (White Owl Studio), which I both loved.I wrote enough I guess, so my last words are going to be a big cheer to the devs and all my best wishes for a potential next project :)

_childDocuments_.review: [Spoilers!]+ The shadow-people child-ghosts that peek from around corners and watch you from the dark are hairraisingly spooky. Every moment with them is incredibly well done; they are not antagonistic, but boy do they up the tension and create the creepiest of atmospheres.- Mr. Spotlight, however, isn't the least bit scary, sadly. Encounters with him can be slightly tedious too, especially when he interrupts the puzzle solving.+ And that's because, while not the most challenging, the puzzles are fun to solve, engaging and make good use of the tactile elements. + Viv's final encounter with the Spotlight monster was pretty fun though and neatly uses the same tools you use to solve puzzles, which I found inspired.+ The reveal that you can play from Amy's PoV as well at the end of Viv's playthrough was a pleasant surprise.+ PSX-style graphics are very effective at building up the eerie atmosphere and give the game a great retro look.+ The Lady of the Black Waters that occasionally stalks Amy is way spookyer than the Spotlight monster. Makes for some tense moments and made me jump once.+ Story was fun to piece together across the two playthroughs, a budding romance between the two teens (with good voice-acting and well written dialogue) amongst conspiracies to hide a Phantom of the Opera inspired tragedy.+ Ran without issues on the Steam Deck

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this was an awesome short game. What I liked:- Strong silent Hill / Resident Evil vibes. This hit a lot more of the RE puzzle solving/inventory use notes than I was expecting, which was really cool- Interacting with puzzles and objects in the world felt really really cool. A lot of polish here on game feel in terms of opening latches, using items. There's a very specific puzzle in this game I won't spoil, but it uses alot of what the player is taught up to that point and it was just very cool and rewarding to fiddle with.- I see a lot of dithering used in horror games these days and I am a fan of it, but I really liked the implementation here that this game uses. Transitions between dark and light areas are where the dithering is most apparent, and the sensation of dithering accumulating into a void of nothingness adds so much more to the worlds atmosphere and tension.- Voice acting was great.- The story is interesting and has some really great turns/twists as it progresses. I was certainly hooked.- A story that can be enjoyed by all ages. This is a game my 10 year old can play. A lot of horror games these days are somewhat violent/gruesome for younger audiences. Overall a very solid, short but sweet horror game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played and reviewed the original release of this last year, but with this updated version, I felt compelled to update/revise my review as well:Fear the Spotlight is an extremely charming, carefully crafted and spooky little ghost story, made with genuine love and care. There's no visceral action or gore, the game is far more interested in atmosphere, slowly building dread and delightful spooks, with a focus on exploration, puzzles and avoiding danger. Simple, charming story, great PS1-ish aesthetics, and some very moody sound design. Well I say simple, but I more mean it doesn't try  you know. There's no awful melodrama, there's no crafting from 45 different types of scrap material, there's no single use lockpicks or defense items or QTEs. It knows exactly what it wants to be, and uses its dialogue, environmental storytelling, notes and letters to build a strong sense of place and history to the school and the characters involved, perfect for Halloween season.The original game (now dubbed "Vivian's Story") was relatively "short", but didn't overstay its welcome and felt all the more satisfying to go through because of it. With this enhanced release, the developers have added a second playable chapter, where you get to experience new events from Amy's point of view, instead of Vivian's. I wasn't sure what to think initially, but Amy's chapter proved to be an excellent companion piece to Viv's, adding detail and depth to the characters, providing some great spooky moments and satisfying puzzles. Much to my delight it also adds a bit more closure, making the ending even more satisfying, so both chapters are well worth playing even for previous owners.If you do play it, I recommend going in the graphics options and adjusting the polygon and camera wobble to about halfway each. With the retro framerate selected and TV filter at max, it looks wonderful.Just, what a delightful spooky time. The original was one of my favourite games last year, and with this update, the game feels more confident, more complete. If a horror game could be called cute, this game is cute. Endearing. Earnest. Delightful. One of the most charming games this year, as dark and sad as its story can get.The devs have every reason to be so proud of what they've achieved and I'm so happy for them, but also eagerly waiting to see what they will create next.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a tense game.It's a fairly short game, you could probably beat it in one sitting. But for what it's got -- the tense atmosphere making you feel unsafe the entire ride and fairly scary antagonists -- I'd say it's worth buying.For twenty bucks though? Not really sure, I'd say get it on sale when you have a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Fear the Spotlight

_childDocuments_.review: I finished it before reviewing. Took around 2h.It's the second game this year which pulled me based on it's PS1 graphics style and genre I like after Psudoregalia. However, while Pseudoregalia is my favorite game I played all year (not even kidding, it's fantastic) - this leaves a lot to be desired. Even devs low-key admit that the game isn't great in the credits sequence.Pretty boring, not very scary, not big on gameplay mechanics and with simplistic puzzles. Also disappointing story. Not worth full price.PS1 inspired horror puzzle game. It says it's also a stealth game or a survival-horror but it's nothing of the sort.You will mainly walk around areas, looking for key items, using them and reading notes. Sometimes a guy with a headlight for a head will appear in certain areas and you will have to avoid him to progress by staying behind or under obstacles like desks or tables. If he notices you - you get grabbed even from the other side of the room, pulled to him, and damaged. You can get hit 2 times, 3 is death and you go back to an autosave point. You can heal all injuries with inhalers which are sometimes awarded for completing puzzles or found lying around.I bit overtuned on the wobble (polygon precision), probably achieved with a vertex shader of some sort, but the areas are quite detailed and interesting to go through. I also liked lots of moving parts when solving puzzles.I had 1 puzzle where I had to stop and think about what clues I have and how to solve it, every other puzzle is straightforward and easy.Barely any mechanics to it. Hiding works janky in some situations. It's unclear whether you are hidden or not as it's not really based off visuals. The monster can shine his light straight at you, but if you are under table - you won't be seen. But then if you hide behind something and it looks in your direction - it can count as a hit.It's not a very difficult game though. I died once.Monster isn't scary. There's 1 scene taken from the original Silent Hill and it's still effective, but other than that the game feels very light.Boring love drama with teenagers. Then devolves into a love drama with long-dead teenagers. Ends with a sappy, overly positive note. With how little struggle or character development there was it felt out of place and undeserved.This game is looks only. It lacks the substance to hold it together as a videogame. It's still a solid try from just 2 developers (1 programmer, 1 artist). I'm sure if they had some more ambition they could have made a proper survival-horror game.But to Fear the Spotlight I'd give aIt's functional, but not very good. You won't be missing much by not playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fear the Spotlight

_childDocuments_.review: So good! I was impressed by how quickly I was invested in these characters and story. But, I was even more impressed by how well they delivered on a good horror experience, especially in the second half of the game. I hope we get more from this mighty team of two in the future, because they know how to write and develop a good game!Indie horror fans are eating good this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Fear the Spotlight

_childDocuments_.review: Just to preface, I never got to play the original so I'm not entirely sure what all was updated.  What I am sure of though is that this is a wonderful little passion project through and through.  The ambiance, sound design, voice acting, and gameplay turns this into an immersive experience that I thoroughly enjoyed.  At no point did I feel frustrated with a puzzle as they were always very logical and fun to solve.  I greatly appreciate the settings that allow you to scale down the visual effects such as the pixel shifting and screen wobble, they were set quite high at default and were making me feel dizzy.  I highly recommend this to anyone who likes smaller scale narrative driven indie projects, it's a great one!
_childDocuments_.name: Fear the Spotlight

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it!Decent spooky short story, charming and nostalgic feeling graphics, all characters are fully voiced, simple but fun puzzles, and yes there are enemies that can hurt/kill you, but they are easily avoidable and there is only a few encounters with them throughout the game.If the price of the game concerns you because the game is short, then wishlist it and pick it up on its first decent sale, you wont be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: Fear the Spotlight

_childDocuments_.review: Nice horror game, not very challenging but it has great ambience and a few legitimately  spooky and creepy moments.The puzzles are fun to solve and the stealth segments are well made and spaced out in a way that makes them tense rather than frustrating.I was suprised at how different the two campaigns were, they're both 2-3 hours long but there's no padding at all, everything feels important and relevant in some way. The first campaign focuses more on the disturbing mystery  of the characters' school while the second campaign is a more personal, introspective journey, Recommended for spookseekers everywhere !

_childDocuments_.review: Such a well-crafted and polished game for only having two devs! This is a genuinely enjoyable horror experience all the way through. _childDocuments_.review: A wonderful love letter to PS1 era horror adventure games. _childDocuments_.review: OMG this is SO GOOD!!! On the surface you might think it's just a PS1 horror throwback (which it is) but it's so much more than that! The story is engrossing and the characters are endearing. I enjoyed it so much I played it in one sitting because I started at night and wanted to finish at night to not break the atmosphere created by the game.The pacing is excellent with a nice mix of uncovering the story and solving puzzles. The puzzles are just the right difficulty to be fun, but to keep the game going without getting stuck and they all integrate into the setting in a believable fashion. Every moment, scene, and environment in the game feels like it's been given a lot of attention and love, without a single moment which feels like filler; it all feels very tight.Even though the art style is PS1 inspired, the art direction is also fantastic with beautiful dynamic lighting and shadows which make the feel of the game that much stronger. The voice acting is also top notch. I also really liked how you have to use the thumbsticks (or mouse) to physically drag things like locker doors, cranks, etc. It gives a great tactile feel to the game.This game punches WAY above its weight and for myriad reasons the ending is great. It's definitely spooky, but never so scary I felt like I couldn't continue (I'm not much for games like Amnesia O_O) PLAY THIS GAME!

_childDocuments_.review: when i got to the end of this and saw it was made by 2 people i was pretty blown away, this is a super polished game with great voice acting and (in my playthrough at least) not a single bug. if you've ever even tried to make a game you'll know that's a pretty amazing feat on it's own. it uses ps1 style vertex snapping to create a really appealing effect, but don't mistake the look for a shortcut. while "retro" can often times feel like a synonym for "low effort" in the world of indie horror, it's used to great effect here and i genuinely can't imagine it looking any other way which is really the goal of any designer. the ps1 style visuals coupled with modern effects like cloth simulation and shadows cast by your flashlight also add a lot to the presentation and stop if from feeling amateurish.that all said, i do think that the story is the most important part of this particular experience, especially given that the puzzles are incredibly easy (which was absolutely the right decision, it keeps the pacing super snappy). the story is where i feel like it sags the most though. the story itself doesn't really have any sort of major peaks. it definitely has a climax and a buildup, but if you were to graph it the angle would be maybe 10 degrees with a small 5 degree spike towards the end. i think a major problem is that the story primarily revolves around something that happened in the past and doesn't really pertain directly to either of our heroines. you find notes left by people you never meet about people you never meet relating to events you never see while your goal stays singular, direct and unchanging. they aren't distant relatives or past lives or anything like that. it's notes from people who just happened to go to the same school as the main character which is just not a strong enough relationship to make up for the lack of actual contact.this part is highly subjective but i do also feel like the monster's design is just incredibly lazy. a huge amount of work clearly went into this game so i hate to use that word, but i just can't think of another way to describe it. it's very boring. the way it functions is great and there are some really clever things done with it when it shows up and some of the set pieces involving him but the design itself, the visual representation of the character, just does not hit with me at all. i almost didn't get the game because of his design alone, but maybe that's just me.so in conclusion, i think it's important to note that both of my major gripes with this game pertain to 2 of the most subjective elements, that being the story and the design of the monster. with the story i got the distinct impression that it was not made for me and aimed more towards people the age of the characters in the game. for the monster, well you can make that decision for yourself based on the trailers and screenshots. i will say though, if you're at all interested based on the trailers, i absolutely still recommend checking it out despite my personal misgivings because you may find something to connect with in the story that i couldn't.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely stellar, spooky little game horror adventure game that focuses on exploration and puzzle solving, along with a fun story and enjoyable characters to boot. If you enjoyed more puzzle-oriented, old-school horror games, this will probably scratch the same itch for you that it did for me.While the game is tagged as survival horror, Resident Evil it is not - you won't find much in the way of resource management or challenging encounters, but in lieu of that, Fear the Spotlight goes hard on another common element of the genre: key item puzzles. A lot of the gameplay will see you exploring creepy environments and taking screwdrivers, batteries, spare change, and all other sorts of trinkets back and forth to progress through different puzzles. Though very few of them made me stop and think for very long, I found each new puzzle to be entertaining; it helps that many added a tactile dimension by having you move a cursor to open lids, twist screws, smash with hammers, and the like.A few more things of note about Fear the Spotlight:- Most of the game's difficulty comes from stealth-like segments where a particular monster is stalking you while you attempt to sneak around it, as well as a few environmental hazards you're asked to navigate around in similar fashion, but they never stay around in one scene long enough to become tiresome.- Regarding the aforementioned difficulty, I wouldn't consider it particularly hard - you might have a bit of trouble if this is your first non-action horror game, but I wouldn't worry about many people getting stuck on it.- It only took me a little shy of 5 hours to complete the story, but I also wasn't in much of a rush, so you could likely blaze through it in a couple of hours.- Nothing in the game is really scary enough to warrant a change of pants in my opinion, but it does maintain some tension with creepy environments and ambient sounds, as well as a few little scares and spooky sightings.- The story is fairly interesting for what it is. The first chunk of the game does a lot of exposition through notes, diaries, articles, and the like that you pick up, slowly getting into the history of a tragic event that happened at this school and some of the darker things that happened behind the scenes. Halfway into the game though, it pivots off of that story a bit and starts focusing on some more personal stuff, seeing some backstory for the characters in the form of voice mails, text messages, and exploring old haunts. They both get wrapped up in the end though and end on a high note, so really I have nothing to complain about, full marks in my book. It does also have some LGBTQ+ rep, so brownie points for that.- The game is at its weakest during the first half hour or so, but only because the introduction to the spooky scary version of the school feels like a bit of a slog - if you hit the part with the payphone, you've made it past what I think is the low point, so it only gets better from there.- There's a slew of fun little achievements, and only a few of them actually require being "good" at the game - most are for doing weird little things while you play, like solving puzzles in a particular manner or being thorough in your exploration.- In my opinion, the best part of the game comes up after you've "beaten" it for the first time - do yourself a favor and don't skip out on what Fear the Spotlight has to offer once the credits have rolled.Overall, Fear the Spotlight is a fun, spooky adventure game with some puzzles that feel good to do, a story that's interesting enough to keep you interested, and characters that are genuinely likeable. It does a great job of being spooky without being outright horrifying, though I will admit one or two encounters with the big bad monsters made me tense up. I never felt stuck or annoyed, and I really enjoyed my time playing the game. If you like games like Homebody or Silent Hill: Shattered Memories, you'll probably find a fair amount of enjoyment in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: the review below is for the old version! I'M SUPER EXCITED TO PLAY THE NEW ONE <3Amazing game! Completely recommend. To me, it has the perfect balance of difficulty throughout the entire game. Never too easy, but never too difficult. The puzzles were clear without being too obvious. Minimal backtracking. The problems this type of game usually has are not present here. It was the perfect amount of fun-stress without being overwhelming. I was always excited to continue to the next area.The only thing I'd like to see is possibly a more optimized way to use stuff like when unscrewing two screws, instead of unscrewing and selecting the screwdriver each time, possibly just selecting the screwdriver as the item you'd like to use and switching between them. I admit that the system has a great charm though. I'm not terribly nostalgic for this type of game as I didn't grow up playing survival horrors, but I still like the older charm of the UI. The visuals are also fantastic, I can tell there was a lot of love put into everything. As far as accessibility I'm so glad there's a setting to turn down the wobbles and TV static. Normally I would like difficulty settings in games, but I honestly don't think it's required here given how perfectly balanced it is. Can't overstate my love for that. Lastly, the story. I'm a big fan of the story! I was able to stay on track with the story beats and each puzzle piece fit together well to help me figure out what was going on. It was perfectly unsettling and had great metaphors. I think that it's especially scary to me as a girl, given the themes of .  But man, that ending! I really want to know what happens after! _childDocuments_.review: In the end credits, the devs say they hope I enjoyed this game even though it wasn't perfect. Guys, what are you talking about! For what it was, "Fear the Spotlight" was absolutely perfect, and I wouldn't change one thing about it. Short and mechanically simple, sure, but nevertheless perfect. Rather than a PS1 nostalgia trip, it's a fun and well-designed modern horror game that will appeal to pretty much anyone. The target audience would probably be teenage girls, but as a 30 year old white cis guy, I still enjoyed the hell out of this teen horror story/LGBT drama. That's the advantage "Fear the Spotlight" has over, say, Puppet Combo games; even though it wears its inspirations on its sleeve, it's an accessible game that explores some heavy subjects delicately and thoughtfully. If you are generally squeamish, this may be just about tame enough for you to stomach. If you are a genre veteran, you may not soil your pants in terror, but I'm sure you'll appreciate the aesthetic. And by the way, even though it's stylized after PS1 era, the graphics are actually pleasant to look at. Rather than highlight the crude blocky 3D models and texture wobbling, the devs do some amazing work with light and dark, and make good use of dithering effect. Not sure who did music and audio design for this game, but it's very effective; the main villain theme being particularly memorable. And on top of all this, the two main actresses do a good job with their dialogue. Their work made me forget I'm playing a low budget indie game. What can I say, I'd love these devs to continue in this direction while experimenting more in the gameplay department. Whatever they do next, they already have me hooked.P.S. If you're here for the nostalgia trip though, I'd say this game most strongly reminded me of "Silent Hill 1" and "Silent Hill: Shattered Memories". Not a fan of "Shattered Memories", but I felt "Fear the Spotlight" takes some elements from it and actually makes them better.

_childDocuments_.review: Fear the Spolight is a twee Silent Hill like. It's The Midnight Club compared to the darker and gorier Midnight Mass. Analogies aside, it's short and sweet and feels good to play, and looks fantastic if you're into that retro sort of thing. My only complaint really is the story. The implications of the story were far grislier than the protagonist seemed to acknowledge, and she was more focused with her *far* less important problems. Then again, they're teenagers. Maybe there's a certain amount of truth to that. I just feel like the story was leading us to a much more interesting place than where we ended up. Missing just one last revelation and then moment of catharsis. For what it is though--a retro indie horror game developed by a super small team-- it's really quite impressive and I had a great time playing it.

detailed_description: One day, a terrible calamity struck a peaceful kingdom. In the chaos that followed, the people began to deceive and backstab each other. Their King used his powerful magic to steal away people’s ability to speak and hurled himself into the Abyss. His daughter, the Princess, cried an endless flood of tears until they encased her in a giant crystal teardrop. Many years after these events faded to memory, seven rainbow-colored lights flew from the Abyss. These rays of hope appeared before the Princess manifesting themselves as seven heroes, ready to answer the Princess' call for help. Why did the King abandon his daughter and his people? And why did he steal their ability to speak? ◆Seven Heroes, Seven Unique Fighting Styles Choose from a motley crew of characters like the well-rounded Wanderer, long-range specialist Archer, or heavy-hitting Warrior to find whose skills suit your playstyle, and embrace new roles and abilities as you gain more experience. Use crystals found throughout the Abyss to switch characters or return to Base Camp. ◆A Home at the Edge of the World Find new recipes and materials and return to your Base Camp at the edge of The Abyss, where each character has a unique job. From alchemist to blacksmith to cook, each hero brings something different. ◆Engaging Exploration and Dungeon-Crawling Experience a new layout each time you enter the enigmatic Abyss, keeping you on your toes every moment you explore, and look out for Memory Rifts, where greater rewards -- and challenges -- await. ◆A Vibrant Storybook Aesthetic The Princess narrates each step of your journey, giving the feeling of a fairy tale come to life -- right down to the dark mysteries waiting to be uncovered in the visually stunning underworld.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Adding context because there seems to be confusion on my gear progression point and loot issue.This was one of the games that I was interested in from the previews at the Directs and other game shows. I love Marvelous because of Rune Factory and I loved how it was stated to draw elements from Rune Factory. It was portrayed as if Rune Factory meets roguelite dungeon crawler which had promise because of how complex Rune Factory is as an RPG/sim and making this a roguelite dungeon crawler was a fresh perspective. However, it fails to deliver, and the actual gameplay ends up feeling like a mobile game due to how restricted your skill sets were which was a huge red flag.1.	Art - is chibi style but not overly chibi. It's just cute enough and it works because of how it references other Marvelous titles.2.	Music - sounds good, fits the areas they were composed for. It helps maintain your immersion which is great.3.	RPG level progression - most roguelites don't have levels you keep so this game having that was a nice touch as it lessens the grind you would need if you wanted to play multiple different characters. This was the most prominent positive I could find as time is a very important topic that I'll go over in the following issues.3.	Gear progression - It's very linear and keeps itself simple which saves you a lot of time. No you don't need that one extremely rare material to make a legendary rarity weapon. They all share similar materials that you just need to farm which saves you headaches in the long run. Ex: The wood you find on floor X will be used for all equipment from floor X.1.	Story - To be perfectly transparent, I genuinely feel like the story was crap. From the way its narrated, to how it proceeds, it sounds like it was a story that was a WIP (work-in-progress) for another game, but was scrapped. The setting and introduction was very blunt and wasn't interesting at all. By the time you get to the second area, you can predict the rest of the story incredibly easily because there's no depth or complexity involved.2.	Maps - the floor maps start out basic, but quickly devolve to annoying. You have limited movement options outside of your dashes to the movement speed stat, so at least 50-70% of the maps are a literal walking simulator. The devs didn't think to condense the maps or make it function as different rooms like how you may see games like Hades does. Ultimately, watching yourself run around to grab things 24/7 ruins your immersion and eats up way too much time. Now, normally this wouldn't be an issue for a RPG game, but this is also a roguelite, meaning you will have multiple runs. Multiple runs means experiencing the same maps over and over if you see where I'm going with this.3.	Loot - the way gear upgrades work goes by both rank and rarity. You start at rank 1 which has the lowest scaling and stats, and the rarities go from common through to legendary. However, that being said, most of your loot becomes obsolete the second you advance to the next area. This means every material you farmed for, every piece of gear you crafted are now essentially trash. Combined with how expensive it is to level up gear later on, this makes for a toxic loop of grinding that shouldn't need to be in this game because you get forced to start from scratch. At least in a good chunk of other RPG's, they mix different materials you may have gotten at various points to craft something new. Personally, after getting the satisfaction of beating the boss of an area, finding out the gear I worked so hard to get is now going to be worth nothing feels incredibly disappointing.4.	Combat & Controls - you have three skill slots, one item slot, one dash, and normal attacks. Does this sound familiar at all? I hope it does because this is the same formula as a run-of-the-mill action mobile game. And yes, it is a "tried and true" formula, but this severely restricts your gameplay because when your skills are on cooldown (and they will be on cooldown), you just mash the normal attack mindlessly. And you'll do this for every run. Even if you choose to equip only low cooldown skills, you're still restricted to those three skills only and the only difference is that you have a shorter downtime in between rotations.5.	Combat & Enemy Scaling - I wanted to mention this separately, because this was what made me stop playing the game entirely. The combat is definitely fun once you find a character whose style works for you, but even that goes down the drain when the enemies grow progressively more annoying by having triple (or more) the HP from the previous map. For a frame of reference, by the time you reach the third area (after 5-6 hours of gameplay), you are fighting enemies that take half a minute to kill if you don't have certain specific setups for both your skills and weapon modifiers. To make matters worse, whenever you craft the next tier weapon, you only get a rough 20% damage boost which is nearly nothing compared to the massive HP pool the newer monsters have. So not only do your weapons feel like they have less value, you also have to spend more time mindlessly fighting regular mobs that sponge your attacks if you don't spam skills the second they're off cooldown. The cherry-on-top is that their damage reflects a similar scaling as well so you will likely die fast if you can't dodge every little thing or build tanky for some odd reason.The game gets stale very fast, the upgrades you obtain feel less impactful than other roguelite games, and they chose both the wrong elements and too few elements to pull from Rune Factory. If they incorporated Rune Factory's whole stat system where you can level up different facets of gameplay by simply performing the action, this game would be a lot more rewarding to play, but they didn't. For example, continuously crafting weapons to get you blacksmithing levels which gives a STR boost or something. Instead the only real Rune Factory references are the names and pictures of the materials and food. Everything else is a subpar, low-budget experience you could get from a $10 game elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all let me say that this game is NOT a roguelike nor a roguelite. I dont have any idea why would people called this game roguelike/lite. This game is a dungeon crawler RPG similar to diablo, torchlight, grim dawn or PoE. its got a hub and a few dungeons to explore with boss on the last level/floor but with chibi anime character and so much simpler gameplay/build.The game gives you 7 characters with diff classes (wanderer, warrior, fighter, rogue, archer, caster, and farmer) each class have 3 skills and each class have 2 advanced jobs that you can unlock so you have a total of 9 skills per characters but you can only equip 3 skills, you can freely reset your skill points without any penalty.The whole gameplay is so simple you start in the hub area where you could do a lot of stuff like crafting weapons and accessories, process raw materials like ore and wood, and farming yes farming but not really you just have to pick what you want to plant and it automatically planted after that you can harvest it after you comes back from dungeon, You will keep going to the dungeon for either farm exp, materials, or rune (kind of like recipe/blueprint for weapons and accessories) and after you completed the main game you will unlock a harder difficulty and some post game content.I honestly am not really into dungeon crawler game like diablo but i enjoy this game so much (just look at my playtime, also just 100% the game) because this game is so much simple like you dont really need a complicated build just pick a 3 skills out 9 and equipments with suitable traits to your build and thats it.I would really recomend this game if you enjoy anime rpg, but definitely not on full price, buy it when it goes on sale and believe me you dont need more than 1 hour to decide this is your game or not, if its not just refund it, thats easy (thank you steam for the refund feature).If i need to give this game a score i would give it like 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a gameplay loop similar to Phantasy Star Online series, Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles handheld series, etc, this can be the game to look into. This is a somewhat randomly generated dungeon crawler action rpg game. After you gone through all the dungeons, a higher difficulty unlocks which yields better drops and equipment going from Normal to Hard to Master difficulty.You have 7 heroes, each with their own playstyle and skills. Each character can learn up to 9 skills tied between 3 classes and can equip 3 at a time. The skills have a cooldown system oppose to a MP system. You can swap characters mid dungeon run and get additional buffs depending on the character you swap out. Along with skills, you can outfit your characters with 3 pieces of gear: 1 weapon and 2 armor pieces, each having upwards to 3 different perks on the pieces. You can also equip gems that alter your characters offensive and defensive elements. It's intended for you to have multiple characters worked on to ease progression. Swapping characters during the dungeon helps you cover elemental weakness. It is possible to go through the game with a single character but it will challenging.There's a simple and basic crafting and farming system.Obviously this is a very grindy game.Some cons and nitpicks:-No multiplayer, could really work considering other similar games usually have multiplayer-Even though the dungeons are randomized, there are very little variety to the room design and layout, you will run into the same design fair quickly and frequently-The bosses and enemies don't get new attacks or patterns in the higher difficulties, just a stat increase-There isn't much reason to do the lower dungeons once you get to the late game dungeon because the drops scales to dungeon progression. If like enemies and bosses having unique material and equipment drops, that would give some more incentive to farm them-Some of the late game dungeons a single floor runs really long which can grow tiring-There is an element in your base that is tied to the story that disappears after you finish a certain boss, which is like like the first 15-20% of the game, I wish there was an option to still have that thing considering you'll no longer have it for the bigger part of the game's grindIt's a fairly decent game if you're into this type of gameplay loop. I had a good time with it, just stuck at the endgame grind atm.

_childDocuments_.review: Not outright terrible, but horrifically overpriced for what it is.The gameplay loop itself is simple enough, and I have no problems with that.Enter dungeon, fight monsters, collect materials and blueprints, exit dungeon, craft and upgrade gear, rinse, repeat.The problem however is that for however simple the gameplay loop is, the actual gameplay itself is equally as simple.Just spam attack until things die, occasionally use a skill, dodge sometimes. Really it's just not satisfying to play.And to be clear, I'm really not being reductive about the gameplay itself.On top of the combat being just generally quite uninteresting and unsatisfying, it isn't helped by the fact that it's also a little bit clunky. Not horribly clunky, but just enough to detract from what precious little enjoyment there could have been in the first place. To give the game credit though, the combat  functional at least.The crafting is pretty lackluster as well. Not that crafting can really be super engaging to begin with, but particularly with regards to having to refine materials for creating new gear, it's just a bit redundant.The added step to refine materials feels entirely pointless and designed exclusively for the purpose of wasting a players time. It's not even as though these refined resources require various types of other resources. It's just a single resource getting condensed down into fewer 'refined' resources for no reason other than bloat. Which this wouldn't even be so bad if it didn't have an arbitrary time gate on it like it was some sort of mobile game.Then there's actual progression which started out okay but rapidly became more and more of a slough. In my relatively short time with the game, I only got down to the third 'world', the snow area. But in my short time I noticed a sharp decline in better gear. From the first area dropping legendaries left and right, to the third area barely even giving common gear. A distasteful pattern that I have no reason to believe won't carry on through the rest of the game. Suffice to say upgrading gear became more of a chore, if even at all possible.Without getting too into any of the other nitty gritty qualms I have with the game and its design, I think I've given this game enough time to tell that it's not something I plan to come back to any time soon.Bottom line is it's just not that fun and far to expensive for what little fun you could realistically have with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: While in the end I decided on a thumbs up, this is one of the harder recommends I've made when reviewing steam games, and I had to think about it. I got this game because it looked like cute, fun little roguelite RPG that reminded me of Dragalia Lost. I like the different characters and playstyles decently, as well as the core conceit of exploring deeper and deeper into a randomly generated abyss and then building up your base between expeditions. I can't call the game bad, and I ultimately did like it, but I had some problems.This game really doesn't have very much going on. It's very repetitive, without much meaningful variety or depth in terms of character abilities, enemy designs, or layouts. The different layer styles are essentially coats of paint, with very little to differentiate them. It takes a long time to get through it, and it seldom feels like you're really making progress. Things usually are easy enough that the real problem is zoning out and making mistakes, and difficulty only really comes in numbers, where you reach the point where you haven't done enough material farming and you do so little damage that enemies physically encircle you and stunlock you to death, or bosses kill you in two hits. The story and characterization are nothing to write home about either. I found myself looking at the clock constantly as I tried to push through it quickly so I could play other games.Despite all my negativity, for which I apologize, I do think it's ultimately an alright game. There's nothing technically wrong with it, and it's a pretty complete package. It's just barebones and not all that inspiring.
