_childDocuments_.review: Highlight of the game is the combat. The skills chain fluidly and combos are satisfying to pull off. The mage can cast a blackhole sucking in enemies and comboing with aoe spells. Fighter has a pull, uppercut, and fireball that is satisfying to combine.The rogue has her daggers, blade dance, and backstab reset on kill that makes you feel like a real assassin when you shred 15 enemies in a row. The warrior has her shout and spin to win movesSometimes you'll hit a wall and need to farm a few floors before you have the material to craft the gear to actually clear mobs, but it never feels like a big deal since the combat is so fun.Game has a decent amount of monster varietyLoot has a lot of rng aspects. It can roll with or without a socket. Besides general stat lines, it can have skill specific buffs leading to a lot of dead lines. You'll almost never find the perfect gear.Negatives:Boss encounters are a huge weakpoint of the game. Felt like they could've had more mechanics and been more engaging.The crafting menu has startup lag and defaults to "no" on everything when you want "yes" a large majority of the time.The whole crafting and time gated part of the game seems unnecessary and feels like the menuing of idle games.KBM controls are rts / action rpg style instead of WASD which will bother some people.

_childDocuments_.review: Of the 7 playable chars theres 3 classes for each character, but its not any sort of choice thing, its a linear straight line basically: 1st class -> 2nd class at lvl 15 -> 3rd class whenever the heck you hellgrind enough to clear i guess the "true" final boss long after clearing the actual main story, which makes it feel extremely pointless and redundant. To make it worse, each "class" only have 3 skills, and you're only allowed to take 3 skills with you on a run, so theres a very real possibility that you'll only take 1 or 2 of your next class' skills in the first place, and since you can see the 3rd class skills at any time, there's a very real chance that you won't even be interested in some or all of them.the story of the game feels almost completely non-existant, there is no RPG storytelling period, you get an occasionally narration about events briefly after every few floors of each dungeon stage, but it doesnt feel worth anything and doesn't add a single thing to the feel of the game, made worse by your tiny little hub Outpost thing outside the dungeon you stay at at all times.gear progression feels absolutely horrible, and while you can constantly craft resources and gear in the hub outpost, there is no actual way to choose to do something like, "craft Milk x 3 in all slots" or "max craft Obsidians" or something, so you will constantly have to fill up each slot one by one, over and over, until the tediousness of it all feels nauseating. The food buffs you can take with you also have pathetically low bonuses like, "you get an extra 3% hp" or "extra 1 % movement speed" .... ya nice stuffs... there simply is nowhere near enough content to justify the price tag, even at $20 it feels like its overreaching. the combat can be fun, but theres so many highly questionable design choices here, that i cannot recommend this game to anyone unless you just want a timekiller

_childDocuments_.review: Silent Hope? A Journey Through Silence! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)In the enigmatic world of Silent Hope, players embark on a quest shrouded in mystery, guided by the ethereal presence of the Princess. This rogue-lite dungeon crawler, developed by Marvelous, has stirred quite a bit of anticipation in the gaming community. With seven unique heroes, an immersive storybook aesthetic, and the promise of combining elements from beloved titles like Rune Factory, it's easy to see why Silent Hope generated high expectations. However, as we delve into this silent world, we discover both its alluring qualities and some noticeable shortcomings.One of the game's standout features is the diverse cast of seven heroes, each with a distinct fighting style. This diversity allows for different levels of customization as you navigate the Abyss. The RPG level progression adds depth to the gameplay, as you can keep and improve your character's abilities, providing an element of continuity between runs. The game's visual style, featuring a charming chibi aesthetic, is a nod to other Marvelous titles, and the music adds to the immersive experience, complementing the various game areas.Despite these positives, Silent Hope is not without its issues. The story, while an integral part of the game, feels underdeveloped and lacks depth. The predictable narrative fails to captivate players and make them emotionally invested in the characters' journeys. Additionally, the maps in the game start off as basic but quickly become tedious and monotonous to traverse. Limited movement options result in repetitive gameplay, which can be a significant drawback in a roguelite.Loot and gear progression pose another challenge in Silent Hope. While it initially seems like the game offers a linear and straightforward system, it becomes apparent that many materials and items quickly become obsolete as you progress. This leads to a frustrating cycle of grinding and crafting, making the rewards feel less impactful. Furthermore, the combat and controls leave something to be desired, with a limited set of skills and a noticeable lack of depth in the combat system.One aspect of Silent Hope that shines is the combat mechanics and the fluidity of skill chains. Each character has their own unique abilities, and executing combos is immensely satisfying. The variety of characters ensures that players can experiment with different fighting styles, and the encounters with hordes of enemies are where the game truly excels.However, the game falters in its boss encounters, which lack the depth and mechanics to make them truly engaging. The crafting system, while promising, has some issues, such as startup lag and a default setting that can be frustrating. Moreover, Silent Hope demands precise controls, and the decision to opt for RTS/action RPG-style controls instead of the traditional WASD may not sit well with some players, especially those accustomed to a different control scheme.In conclusion, Silent Hope presents a mixed bag of experiences. While it boasts a beautiful visual style and a compelling combat system, it falls short in terms of storytelling, map design, and loot progression. The repetitive nature of the game, combined with a high price tag, can be a turn-off for some players. Silent Hope offers a unique and visually appealing experience, but its limitations might leave some players yearning for a deeper and more engaging gameplay experience. As with any game, it's important to weigh the positives against the negatives and determine if Silent Hope aligns with your gaming preferences.Interested in discovering great Steam games? _childDocuments_.review: I've been kind of obsessed with this since seeing the reveal, and I can't really explain why beyond "I like it's vibe". After playing the demo a bunch, and jumping into the full game, I'm still enjoying the vibes but would mostly recommend the game to other people like me who watched the trailers, joined the livestreams, or visited the dedicated website and instantly fell for it.It's a very straightforward Rogue-lite dungeon crawler, with it's greatest strength in my opinion being the focus on switching characters in and out to stacks buffs and keep a run fresh, and jumping in and out of the Abyss being fairly quick and easy for short bursts of dungeon diving. It's biggest weakness is probably the tedium in both traversal and inventory management. The story... Exists.  You can dig into the monster encyclopedia or the website to get some flavor, but for the most part the focus is on just making your way through each level of the Abyss while collecting items and leveling up your favorite characters. I'm fine with it being that way since it mostly gives a framework without getting in the way. Except for maybe how much the Princess talks at your base camp, but you can go into the settings and turn that off.The charm is really what carries the experience. The art style and environments are comfy, and the characters manage to pack in a decent amount of personality despite not really talking or having names. I guess to oversimplify things: For better or worse, Silent Hope feels like a memory of Nintendo 3DS games.

_childDocuments_.review: GUYS THIS GAME IS PEAK EASILY GOTYAhem, honestly speaking, the game is really good and provides more than what you think. _childDocuments_.review: Fun game, but it is grindy. Combat is shallow and generally so is the story. I can really only recommend it between 50 to 75% discounted. I think this would be a fun game on a handheld on the steamdeck on the go. Budget-wise i think they spent too much on voice acting and on that opening anime music video. More money should have been invested in making the gameplay loop more robust. The game has a gimmick regarding character switching mid-dungeon. It allows you apply stat buffs based on the character class. This system forces you to play characters which you may have no interest in playing. You also need to level each character separately to make sure your swapping character can survive at least 1 dungeon floor. This feels intrusive to the gameplay.Combat is basic; you have 7 characters each with their own weapon type. You have your 1 string normal attack and you have 3 skills. Some moron should have told the combat designer to use the LT button on the controller to give you a second layer of skills. in total you have 9 skills (3 per class on a character) and you can only access 3. They wasted the RT button on item pick up which they could have used for a 3rd layer of skills. No option for automatic pick up of equipment loot. After you beat the main story you have a dungeon that appears to be an epilogue (true end), this is where the 3rd character classes are unlock, and then the game lets you replay all the dungeons again on a harder difficulty. You get stronger loot on these harder difficulties, but they appear to be rehashes of the weapon models on the normal difficulty. The equipment loot system is also very flawed, very RNG and legendary weapons can have RNG not to include an element slot.Overall the MSRP is overpriced. Do not buy any of the DLC, they are of the fast track start weapon variety you push you ahead; this is predatory and the developer should be ashamed of themselves. If you want to cheat just use cheat engine.

_childDocuments_.review: $32 and 5 hrs spent playing this game, and I honestly regret every cent. I hope I can get a refund because i never plan on touching it again. I am sorry devs but this ain't it. Let me be clear, the game isn't bad for technical reasons. The art is good, the princess's voice actor is one of my favorite. There are multiple play styles, and combat can be fun. Character level up and class changing is nice, but only unlocks when your in the hub world. I will say the abilities and level ups are probably one of the best features of this game but its made obsolete by the weapon stats that hold you back. The maps are basically the same, with you running around aimlessly killing monsters and collecting materials while trying to find the exit to the next floor which is the same. die and you lose some and get sent back to the start. but then it has the "looter-shooter" aspect where you keep getting recipe drops for older weapons with slight stat variations, so you can craft and then disassemble them for booster parts to then upgrade actual good weapons, which become obsolete after each world. The process of refining materials is annoying and almost feel like a mobile game. You set the materials you want to refine (2-3 at a time when some items require 10) and then you [bold] have[/bold] to do a dungeon run for them to process or spend a bunch of runes for instant upgrades (which isn't worth it). so then you boringly spend time milling away in the dungeon because you wanna build the new weapon and move on. Monster forms are basically repeated with slight changes. Floor maps get repetitive and annoying. I made it all the way to the 3rd floor on my first run and then upon returning realized i'd have to do two more runs just to get all the mats to upgrade my equipment and couldn't proceed. The story is also super generic. kingdom destroyed, defeat evil at the bottom of the pit and save a princess or something who cried herself into a crystal (its a 5 min prologue movie). I was not motivated by literally anything in this game to keep playing. The story didn't make me curious, and after the 4th repetitive world and combat just with even more floors i was annoyed. then add in the only way to progress was to keep grinding those floors cuz mats wouldn't process otherwise and its a perfect combination for a boring game.  Ultimately i'd say save your money. this isn't a $32 game. its more like a $5 mobile game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really have no interest in dungeon crawling or roguelites, and I only picked this up because I saw woolies in the trailer so I was interested in finding out what kind of game it was firsthand.My initial impressions were positive, it's cute, the music is nice, and the combat was challenging enough.At a certain point I hit what felt like a wall of progression. I was either going to need to grind or to git really gud to progress.So, I decided to interact with the game's selling point: switching characters mid-dungeon. It even provides buffs for doing it as much as possible, but there's a problem.All your characters need gear, and they can't even share items that aren't class restricted, like accessories. As gear is very important, this puts a big focus on the crafting. Sadly, the crafting is not only barebanes compared to Rune Factory, it's also gated by the main currency in the game.Faced with the wall of grind ahead of me, my feelings toward the game immediately cooled off. I might see how the game goes but I've already lost the initial spark.The game itself has no technical issues. It even supports Steam Input controller glyphs, as far as I can tell. There are 2 things I've noticed that irk me:- When you're going through the menus and crafting stuff, you can't input a dialog before it has fully transitioned into view. This means there's a small input delay between every action.- When you're going to quit the game from your main camp, there is no save button and it warns you of unsaved progress. Why can't it just save when you're quitting?I'm giving this a negative review for now. If the game really turns me around, I'll change it.

_childDocuments_.review: What the heck, this game is so cute and FUN! I had it on my wishlist for a while and was too busy to play it on release, but the reviews got me a little worried. I decided to take the plunge anyway now that I have more time and YES YES YES, what a fun ARPG dungeon crawler! It reminds me a bit of Harvestella somehow with the characters/classes and combat, another recommended gem of a game. You'll definitely want a controller for this one, though!Silent Hope hits so many on my checklist for games like this:- satisfying combat and controls (controller) where your skill is the limit, and no clunky-ness being a stick in the mud- great variety of playstyles with decent customization options and unlockables!- you can swap between the characters/classes practically on the fly at checkpoints in the dungeons or in the camp, useful for multiple loadouts or just wanting to try something else- loot out the wazoo! if you're a weirdo that hates random stats on gear then you might wanna look away, though it does not make or break combat necessarily, it's more there for people who enjoy the details like me, an old school Diablo 2 freak still to this day (it's much simpler, but I still love it)- the dungeons layouts are pretty straight forward but grow increasingly deep, with some extra challenges and options within- the enemy variety is pretty good and you'll find some good challenge trying to fight multiple types enemies and attacks of all different sizes and speeds simultaneously- in-game "challenges" you can do for extra and unique rewards, such as "craft 5 weapons," "kill X enemies with Y," etc.- a pleasant artstyle with variety and good visual clarity- Japanese voices are good (haven't heard English), music is decent, so far nothing crazy, but keeps the mood goingI'm sure there are a ton of other things I could compliment this game on. I actually don't have any glaring negatives to point out that take away from the experience except that you might want to either make the voiced camp interactions less frequent or even turn them off entirely because it feels a bit much.I'm someone who despises when people play games and essentially complain that they aren't something else entirely. I enjoy games for what they are and the vision that the developers had for them, and I point out criticisms where the existing systems feel lacking within that scope, not claim ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like "this game should have been such-and-such instead," or "it needs to be more like this other game (that I'm a fanboy of)," etc., it's just obnoxious and is nothing more than an affront to flavor and creativity.

_childDocuments_.review:
Seven heroes, seven fighting styles. Dive into the Abyss and explore their silent world. One day, a terrible calamity struck a peaceful kingdom. In the chaos that followed, the people began to deceive and backstab each other. Their King used his powerful magic to steal away people’s ability to speak and hurled himself into the Abyss. His daughter, the Princess, cried an endless flood of tears until they encased her in a giant crystal teardrop. 

Many years after these events faded to memory, seven rainbow-colored lights flew from the Abyss. These rays of hope appeared before the Princess manifesting themselves as seven heroes, ready to answer the Princess' call for help. Why did the King abandon his daughter and his people? And why did he steal their ability to speak? 

◆Seven Heroes, Seven Unique Fighting Styles
Choose from a motley crew of characters like the well-rounded Wanderer, long-range specialist Archer, or heavy-hitting Warrior to find whose skills suit your playstyle, and embrace new roles and abilities as you gain more experience. Use crystals found throughout the Abyss to switch characters or return to Base Camp.

◆A Home at the Edge of the World
Find new recipes and materials and return to your Base Camp at the edge of The Abyss, where each character has a unique job. From alchemist to blacksmith to cook, each hero brings something different.

◆Engaging Exploration and Dungeon-Crawling
Experience a new layout each time you enter the enigmatic Abyss, keeping you on your toes every moment you explore, and look out for Memory Rifts, where greater rewards -- and challenges -- await.

◆A Vibrant Storybook Aesthetic
The Princess narrates each step of your journey, giving the feeling of a fairy tale come to life -- right down to the dark mysteries waiting to be uncovered in the visually stunning underworld.

name: CHAOS;HEAD NOAH
detailed_description: Takumi Nishijo is a second-year high school student on the verge of becoming a shut-in. 'I have no interest in 3D.' He lives surrounded by his beautiful girl figures in his room. He lives in Shibuya, where there has been a series of bizarre serial murders known as 'New Generation Madness' (aka NewGen). The culprit has yet to be caught and has been causing unrest on the internet and television. One day, a gruesome image that seemed to predict the next NewGen killing was sent by a mysterious figure called 'Shogun.' The next day, on his way home from school, Takumi encounters a horrific crime scene, exactly as predicted. Before the corpse is a blood-soaked girl - Rimi Sakihata.

_childDocuments_.review: Chaos;Head Noah is a brilliant game, one that immerses you into the mind of its pathetic main character to tell a story only a VN can effectively do. It touches on a lot of interesting philosophical concepts regarding society, identity and desire, and explores lots of heavy subject matter through its phenomenal cast. It's a story around trauma, where it can take you, and what outgrowing it can entail. It's a story I think most people can find themselves in, and can mean different things to lots of different people. It's also incredibly accessible, being ambitious yet laser focused tale, with rarely a dull moment in sight. Even if you're not the type to regularly play VNs, or the type that have a hard time getting into them, you might just find yourself caught in its clutches.So, why am I recommending against it? Because this release does not reflect the quality of the original game. It has, frankly, one of the most embarrassing localisation works I've ever witnessed. Constant mistranslations, continuity errors, and stilted awkward phrasing that doesn't reflect the original script. Bugged effects and features that draw the reader out of the experience. It genuinely feels like an alpha build, and will ruin your experience of a stellar piece of fiction.As a fan whose primarily motivation to learn Japanese was to read this title, I genuinely would not wish on my worst enemy to read this version. It's a bad, unpolished mess. I would ask anyone who is interested in checking this game out to download the  by Committee of Zero. It retranslates the entire game, fixes many technical issues, and restores cut content to make this version actually playable. It is basically essential to actually enjoy the game, and the kind of quality that should be coming from the official sources.I wrote this review back when the game had just come out on Steam, and I saw the poor quality with my own eyes. Back then, the patch was an uncertain ways off, and it was important to tell people not to support this broken version of an otherwise great game. I've considered since then whether to change my review to a positive one when the patch drops, as I do wholeheartedly recommend this game if you do download said patch.I've decided against it, overall, as the base product is still absolutely unforgivable, and while we can keep trying to spread the word of the patch, there will still be a lot of people playing this game raw coming out with a bastardized understanding of Chaos;Head Noah's quality. Simply put, this is not a product that should be sitting on store shelves, and unless an actual fix happens officially (which I heavily doubt), I'll continue condemning the base product, as people should not need to mod their games to make them complete.

_childDocuments_.review: Chaos;Head Noah is an interesting game to talk about, given it's history of struggling to get an official English translation for so long. Hell, it's canon follow up, Chaos;Head: Love Chu Chu (yes, really), at time of writing, doesn't have an English version, let alone an official PC port. It's actually a miracle, in a way, that I'm even able to recommend people play this, given how long it took to actually reach us in an official capacity. I'm also in a semi-unique position, as I have experience with the original Chaos;Head via a fan-translation, so I can actually say what was changed with this release based on that version.Before I actively review the game: I want to make it VERY CLEAR that I am speaking as a person who experienced the game from start to finish with the Committee of Zero patch, as I think it is essential in a number of ways. As such, this is the only chance I'll get to mention it: if you want an experience truer to the original release of Noah from back in 2009, then you will need that patch, as this version of the game is based on a newer release that saw a degree of censorship via the removal of certain scenes. The Patch restores those scenes, and has a translation fix to boot. It's easy enough to find and install, so I recommend it if you choose to experience this title.Also, before I forget: The anime adaptation, while I don't think is as awful as many other do, is not that reflective of the overall experience of Chaos;Head's story, as it becomes a little more "anime original" by the end in how certain things unfold. It's an anime that is a poor reflection of the VN it's based on, so try to go into this title with an open mind if you are familiar with the lackluster anime.Now, onto the actual thing itself: I can safely say that this is a very different beast for those coming into this title to experience the origins of the Science Adventure games, especially if you're only familiar with Steins;Gate. This title's story deals with Delusions, and the protagonist is a paranoid otaku shut-in, so it goes into some interesting places. It's a lot more bloody and horror-ish than, say, Steins;Gate or Robotics;Notes. If you're at all sensitive to things like suicidal acts, murder, and other things of that ilk, I'd say steer clear, as it touches on that kind of stuff more the deeper you go. I'd go as far as to say that some of the ideas (like a specific flashback involving a baby... if you know, you know) boarder on being a bit excessive with how it describes things. Of course, this also comes with some really good, tension building in the writing. It's a solid "Denpa" story, if a bit clumsy in places.Takumi is a sort of unlikable tool of a protagonist, and you'll either learn to like him/tolerate him, or you'll be put off by him entirely. Given a big chunk of this VN's plot is his gradually deteriorating mental state, I think he works for the kind of story he's in. I can totally understand if one were to dislike him, as he does very little to be likeable. He's like Shinji Ikari in this respect.The other characters are mostly solid, and that's something you can thank Noah for. The original version of Chaos;Head, prior to the original release of Noah, lacked a lot of substance for the bulk of the female cast members outside of Rimi, but now they all have dedicated chapters via routes you can access through specific choices. Of course, the way you get there is a bit annoying, but we'll get to that in a minute. If I had to say anything, I think that Rimi still walks away as the best of the bunch, and Yua walks away with me not liking her due to the structure of her route. All of the other routes give you something to chew on, though some go into interesting directions that make me go "yeah, if this were in any other title, I would hate this" with how they end, but it works for Chaos;Head's overall tone.Keep in mind that when I say "Routes," it doesn't mean romance. While some routes have a bit of a romantic vibe to them in places, the story largely has no delusions (if you can pardon the pun) of being a dating sim with basically saying "Rimi is the love interest." These routes are more like branches off of the common route that end after a single chapter. This is fine. Accessing them is reliant entirely on one Delusion Trigger choice each (along with a few Yes/No questions afterwards), which is also fine.However, this is where a wrinkle occurs. See, in order to access these routes, you need to finish the Common Route, and get the First Ending. The game makes it a little easier after doing so, as you'll be able to jump to whichever chapter the choice needed is after doing so, but it's still an interesting choice. Hell, in order to get the True Ending, you have to experience a total of EIGHT other endings. The normal ending, the endings for each of the girls, and a "the villain wins" type of bad ending. THANK GOD for the skip button!Delusion Triggers are this game's primary mechanic. At certain points in the plot, a ring will appear on screen and obscure your view a bit, while applying a static filter. On the sides of the screen are a green button to the left, and a red button to the right. Green corresponds to "Positive" Delusions, which are generally, but aren't always, some kind of suggestive or romantic scene, leaning on Takumi's pervy otaku side. Red is the opposite, as they play more into the horror and paranoia of Takumi's personality, and tend to be where you'll see more of the potentially triggering content. You can also choose to ignore them, as that counts as a choice too. So long as you don't exit the time frame the ring occurs, you can swap freely between them by pressing the opposite button to cycle back to "normal" and then the button to the other type if you want.As a person who played the original Chaos;Head, I have to say I'm not a fan of the visual changes made to the Delusion Triggers, as I feel they are more intrusive from a UI standpoint. In the original, the buttons were on the top corners of the screen (as the top of the screen was home to a black bar all the time), and were represented by green and red heart rates, and a heart rate-esc echo-y beep noise. It was less in your face, and was more miss-able to a first timer, but I generally just think it's better, so I think the changes are a little stupid.As far as visuals are concerned, this version is less dated looking than the original, but that's not saying a lot. There's still a lot of dated 3D graphics in places, and there are certain choices for legally distinct things that make you raise an eyebrow. Namely, their Wikipedia stand-in, which I won't say here just because it's that questionable imho. The character sprites look crisp for the most part, but lack proper aspect ratio scaling, so can look jagged if you use the wrong resolution.Something of note is 100%ing this VN is a little bit of a chore. You'll likely get extremely annoyed if you try going for everything, as while you can get most of it in the playthroughs required to get the true end (which is made easier because, again, thank god for the skip button), but as there are no comprehensive guides for anything but how to get to specific endings, you'll kind of be pissing in the wind looking for most stuff if you miss it. Also: having to see all positive and negative delusions is a pain in the ass, even with the skip button. Would not recommend for anyone outside of the die hards like me.To wrap things up, I'd say Chaos;Head Noah is not necessarily as approachable as it's younger siblings Steins;Gate from a content perspective, for a number or reasons. You have to put in a lot more effort than said younger siblings to get the True End for the most part, and some of the writing is, again, a bit much in places, not to mention a bit clumsy in how it delivers certain ideas, but it's still a really solid start for the SciADV series. Here's to a (hopeful) English release for Love Chu Chu!

_childDocuments_.review: People do not like Takumi, the main protagonist. Because he is soft. Because he is crying. because he is weak and constantly seeks help. But, Takumi could also be a real person, the lonely male in the flat next to yours.It is hard to connect with Takumi and cheer for him if you are a normie. But if you are an Otaku, if society has pissed on you, if you are a kind soul deep down inside then occasionally you just retreat. You retreat to your 2 X 4 box and you live there. But because you need company since man is a social animal, you make up for the loss of normie human company by living in someone else's dream. You live in a delusional world, lost in your own thoughts; those being grandeur or victorious or self-defeating and catastrophizing. You talk to your waifu from your favourite anime who is always there for you, wakes you up in the morning calling you a dork with her chirpy helium moe voice. And you become a God in an online MMO where you make up for life's L's. But, isn't this why we all are in this platform chasing achievements?We are all Takumi now.Chaos;Head Noah is a mesmerising trip that mixes fantasy, psychology, drama, thriller elements with a sociology narrative creating a tale that sucks you in. There are some harem elements there and you can exploit them with the nine endings and your feel good delusional choices, but ultimately reality catches up with you.The dark, sick and twisted reality of filthy adults who wish to control the world for their own delusions and psychopathy. Just like what happens today in the real world. The Committee of 300 is probably a real thing.Chaos;Head Noah discusses mental health (in 2008) when mental health was not even a thing in the west. It is so ahead of its time, it is frightening in a way. How many times did i wonder whether Takumi (i as the reader) was watching a "real" event or was he (i) lost in my thoughts. What is real anyway in a world of possibilities?Chaos;Head Noah is above all a human story about our weaknesses. And it is a story to be read and read again.PS: having never read the original there are admittedly mistakes in the translation and I can see where this could have been done much better. But, I was waiting far too long to read this, so thank you Mages for this 2022 present.[An update will be posted when I reach the true ending; so close now.]

_childDocuments_.review: I have to give Chaos;Head Noah a thumbs down, unfortunately, despite being quite intrigued by it in the early goings. The best thing the game has going for it is its controversial protagonist. I've never read anything starring someone quite so unlikeable and unpleasant, but it works in the context of the story's unsettling vibe. Putting a character already suffering from paranoid delusions into an actual horror story is an inspired choice that works; at least for as long as Chaos;Head is a horror story. And that is ultimately the problem. About two thirds of the way through, the tone takes a dramatic shift into the realm of chuunibyou/power fantasy storytelling, to the extent that most of the rest of the game doesn't really matter anymore in the last few chapters. The murder mystery that was driving the earlier parts of the novel ultimately is completely irrelevant, to the extent that one of the alternate endings literally just exists to tie up its loose ends because of how thoroughly the main story drops it. There is an investigation by several side characters into a conspiracy that also ultimately doesn't matter at all. And the excellent disquieting and paranoid tone of the early chapters ultimately can't coexist along with all of the teenagers with magic swords that become the main focus by the end. The last chapter and subsequent routes in particular confuse extended descriptions of nauseating violence with actual horror--I felt physically ill a few times, I will certainly concede, but that isn't the same thing as horror, at least not to me. The game ultimately ends up as a paradox to me--a mystery story where the mystery doesn't matter, a conspiracy thriller where everything is exactly as it seems to be (there are no actually meaningful twists to the story after the first few chapters), and a horror story that loses steam long before the end. All that leaves is the teenagers fighting with magic swords. I am by no means above enjoying that sort of story, but unfortunately Chaos;Head Noah doesn't do chuunibyou/power fantasy that well either. The limits of people's powers are poorly defined, the cast outside of the main character is underdeveloped, and excluding one or two interesting uses of the delusion powers there isn't enough sense of fun, wonder, or craziness to sustain interest, at least in my case. I ultimately alternated between being bored with the monotone grimness and nauseated by the endless graphic scenes of torture as I powered through the last few routes, none of which contributed anything positive to my overall assessment of the main story. Despite my initial enjoyment of the story, ultimately I could feel my excitement draining right around Chapter 7, and it only continued to diminish the longer I read. A shame, because I really do like certain parts of Chaos;Head Noah quite a bit, even if I ultimately can't recommend it. Note: I used the Committee of Zero fan translation patch. While I can't speak to the accuracy of its translation, I thought it read wonderfully and would highly recommend it--for the bug fixes if nothing else.

_childDocuments_.review: The first entry in the beloved Science Adventure series, CHAOS;HEAD NOAH is about a male second year high school student named "Takumi Nishijo"  (or Taku for short) who has the unique ability to see his surroundings more positively and negatively - this is called a delusion. Throughout this game, you'll be able to decide whether the delusions Taku will see is sweet or sour. In Takumi's world, a series of murders have begun to occur called the NewGen murders. Taku is a shut in, introverted hardcore Otaku and gamer who just loves to fantasize about the world of 2D and video games all day, and because of his lifestyle and hobbies, he often joins chatrooms. In such chatrooms, he encounters users who send him images relating to the NewGen murders. One way or another, this causes Taku to get involved with the NewGen murders. At the same time, all of a sudden, someday, a suspicious girl enters Taku's life. Taku first meets her in front of a grusesome NewGen murder scene and then at school. Oddly, apparently Taku and the girl  were always best friends at school yet, Taku has no memory of her being his best friend...Lastly, throughout this story, Taku will often encounter an odd question that he doesn't understand as well as large swords held by some people that only he seems to notice .Will Taku uncover his relation to the NewGen murders, figure out who and why the suspicious girl that he has no memory of has entered his life and learn what's the deal with the weird question and the swords he's been noticing lately? Play to find out! Well, first off, I'd like to note that I had played using the  This includes more accurate translation. Anyways...Honestly, CHAOS;HEAD NOAH is an absolutely beautiful story. All confusion and questions the player may have in their mind begins to be answered at Chapter 9. Up until that point, I didn't really like Taku, probably because he stutters so much and I can't relate or connect to him  that well as he's somebody so introvertted, into 2D female figurines and enjoys genres of video games that I don't enjoy at all.  However, you have to fully play the game in order to begin to like CHAOS;HEAD NOAH and especially Taku in particular as a character.  Seeing the common ending - "Silent Sky", isn't really the most happiest way to end this story. Working to reach the "Blue Sky" ending should be your goal as I consider it to be the true ending of the story as well as one that makes the most sense for Rimi and Taku. The story has many twists  - I did not see all of it coming!  Ultimately though, I loved the Blue Sky ending, it made me smile and tear up. Amazing way to end the story. I do have a few painpoints to share.1. The lack of BGM, especially inside of Taku's container. The frequent lack of music at times can bore, fatigue and make the player sleepy. I know that Taku's container has some sort of static or raindropy noise running in the background, but it's just not enough to keep me awake and active while reading inside of the container and other places lacking noise. So, I wish there was more music playing throughout the story. 2. After obtaining the common ending, please, introduce the feature to let us skip entire chapters while doing another playthrough. It would be more faster and convenient than the "E" key (skip mode). This would have been really useful for obtaining other endings. 3. I am not the biggest fan of the sprite and animation quality. It's good but not good enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so, just to clarify, I'm about 75% of the way through the Switch release of the game, so obviously my playtime on Steam is not indicative of actual experience.This is a GREAT game, which is unfortunately marred by a flawed translation/localisation.  There is a "glossary" in game to explain certain things (just like Steins;Gate etc) and in some of the entries, the translator has written things along the line of "This is a cringe 2000s internet term that sounds uncool, so I haven't translated it", or "this wouldn't make sense in English, so I'm not going to try translating it".  Like, it's as if the translator has decided that the player might not like the cringe, so they've removed that agency entirely from the player - almost as another added layer of censorship.I have played through Chaos;Child previously, both unpatched and then with the Committee of Zero patch, and boy does it make a difference!  Things are normalised, all of the stupid internet/otaku slang is there, it's a great time. Overall, this game is definitely worth your time, even without the patch.  If you're used to playing poorly translated games like I am (*stares at Aksys and Idea Factory translated otome game library*), then you'll probably still enjoy this psychological thriller/murder mystery.  Its gore factor isn't quite as high as Chaos;Child (or I've just gotten a stronger stomach), and I'm honestly having a really hard time working out why it was initially refused by Steam when games like Kara no Shoujo and Song of Saya (Saya no Uta) got on here no problem with arguably more heinous content.I will be updating my review both when I finish my Switch copy, and then once I've played through the PC patched version.  In its current form, it's definitely still playable, but the glaring errors and laziness of the translator could be off-putting to newbies to the VN scene.

_childDocuments_.review: (I have already played NoAH elsewhere prior to this Steam release, hence the low playtime)An absolute masterpiece and one of the best visual novels out there. Chaos;Head NoAH is an amazing story with an incredible horror atmosphere and one of the most interesting main characters out there. That being said...The English translation here is of shockingly low quality, it's by far the worst the series has seen. To outline just a few basic issues with it:-The complete lack of quotation marks-Awkwardly phrased narration that's hard to follow-Inconsistent terminology with later games in the series-Flat and dry dialogue that removes a lot of the personality from the original game-Untranslated Japanese terminology (Ria-Ju, Chu-Ni, Mochitsuke, Hikikomori, ノツ, Chu - almost all of which are either straight up wrong, not used in the correct context, or have perfectly fine English equivalents), additionally several TIPS have been altered to have the translators say either "this has no English equivalent so we didn't even try to translate it" or "this DOES have an English equivalent but we decided to omit it because we thought it would have been cringeworthy" (I am not making this up)-Mistranslations galore-Odd bugs like missing sound effects and sprites, some of which affect pivotal moments-Censorship, resulting in large chunks of the game being cut out (admittedly this is no fault of the localization staff or Steam, as it affects recent Japanese releases as well, but still worth noting), and no I am not talking about the Seira DLC stuff, that's a stupid thing to be getting super annoyed over, the content that's cut here will majorly affect your understanding of the main plot-Bugs that prevent you from progressing at certain pointsSo yeah, until CoZ's patch is out around the end of the month, please hold off on playing this. Chaos;Head is an incredible game and it would be an awful shame to experience it through such a butchered release. I'm also aware that a lot of the problems here are probably not the fault of Spike Chunsoft, who have produced some pretty good translations in the past, the main problem was probably just a lack of time and money, like it was with Robotics;Notes' translation.Seriously though, please do better next time, MAGES.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I had the opportunity to play CHAOS;HEAD NOAH, and I'm grateful to the Committee of Zero for translating the game, fixing its technical issues, and restoring it to its fully uncut state. That said, it just doesn't stack up to the rest of the series.Most of the ostensible main cast don't even contribute much to the story. It's hard to avoid the impression that their primary role is to give Takumi cryptic hints to push his development along, given that once they've done so they tend to disappear as suddenly as they arrived.In the same vein, it's close to meaningless to speak of cast chemistry in this title, for the simple reason that they are rarely (or in some cases never) seen interacting with one another. The one common thread and central focus is Takumi, with everyone else as an afterthought. This is only somewhat alleviated by the character routes because all their backstories (minus Nanami) can be summarized with “I have experienced buckets of physical/psychological trauma,” and they’re not fleshed out much more than that. The story revolving almost solely around Takumi isn't an issue per se, but I just didn’t find his character development particularly captivating for some reason.Additionally, the amount of gore is at times excessive to the point of being eye-roll-inducing. CHAOS;CHILD had its moments, but in CHN it’s just over the top. As I mentioned earlier, I’m glad that the patch restored all cut content, but even so, the gore feels overdone.I don't normally feel the need to leave a review every time I play a middling VN because let's face it, most of them are manufactured by hacks checking off genre and fetish boxes. But I hold SciAdv to a high standard, and CHAOS;HEAD NOAH was disappointing enough that I thought it worthwhile to mention. You might still want to play it anyway for the sake of completion or getting a better understanding of some of the concepts and themes that recur throughout the series. Really, though, the biggest reason to play this is that you'll finally learn what the noids are.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the weird nerds review bombing this with negative reviews while complaining about translation (if you look, the people doing that don't even have any play time to judge the translation quality, it's all knee-jerk reactions).They're all brigading from the same place--a fan community for this game that's been around for a long time since long before an official English release was announced, and in general they do not like any translation that was not created by their community. The patch they're talking about is supposed to restore some cut content, and will give a translation that is more literal (to the original japanese) and consistent with their other fan translations, so I would still recommend it if only for the cut content. Though I find it really distasteful that they're review bombing in an attempt to advertise the patch.From playing myself for a few hours, the translation out of the box is good quality. If you don't want to wait for the patch, or don't want to get the patch at all, it's perfectly fine. The story makes sense and is true to the intent of the plot, and the english is fluent and reads well without spelling/grammar issues. It isn't a literal translation in some areas (though it does still use a good amount of Japanese slang), but professional translators will tell you that it's better to localize translations so that they make more sense rather than going literal (which can confuse readers who don't know japanese. Like for example, a literal translation of a japanese pun won't make any sense).Now all the translation shenanigans aside, I would highly recommend this if you're a fan of Steins;Gate and the other Sci Adventure Series. Chaos;Head of course was the first game that started the series (though it is more violent than Steins;Gate if that's your only exposure to the series), and I'm really excited to finally have an official release!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, that's a stupid joke, but not meant as an insult to the VN itself. I appreciate that this VN exists and for all the countless hours of hard work CoZ put into patching it. And from a moment to moment standpoint, I really enjoyed reading C;HN. It got me through being on bedrest and made the time pass very fast. Its pacing is great, the tension is held through most of the read time and it built up a  very interesting story with a pervasive sense of creeping dread.So why the thumbs down?Simply put, I have never been let down so much by any (good) thing I have ever read, before.The murder mystery, the strange broken world, the shadowy creepy villains, the existentialism, the denpa vibes, the masterminds behind it all and sadly even the  themes of a game in the Science Adventure series, don't matter. At all. There's nothing to piece together, nothing to figure out and nothing to ponder over. Everything about the world building, the atmosphere and intrigue turn out to be complete throw-away, to the point that even calling these elements "meaningless set dressing"  might be implying they matter more than they do.Everything boils down to "just because" with no real depth, and all the things that made me interested and kept me hooked in the setting and narrative had no pay off.So what I was left with in the end was a solely character driven narrative. The problem for me with this angle is that the characters themselves, while decent I suppose, just weren't interesting, deep or compelling enough to make the experience worthwhile; nor was there any real room for growth or character development during the short time frame the story spans. One thing I will praise here, is Takumi. Despite being the most unlikeable protagonist I have ever experienced, he's truly fascinating and his voice actor does a great job of bringing him to life. Takumi is the star of the show and while in all fairness this is  story, he's just not strong enough to hold up the entire rest of the novel's shortcomings by himself. When I finally reached the true end, I was left with this disappointed sensation of "that's it???" with every single thing I cared about being rendered pointless. I had no real emotional reaction to the resolution of the cast's struggles either and I tend to be a bit of a sap most of the time. Instead I felt exhausted when it was over and the end just fell so flat for me. That said, I've read many VNs with higher levels of cruelty, gore and traumatic events taking place but with all of them, there was a much greater reward for doing so. I'm not name dropping nor trying to say that every story must be held to X standard, but the reward for suffering through the awful scenes in C;HN just wasn't there for me at all. Its not a *bad* story per se. It's well written. But it didn't resonate with me one bit, left me feeling hollow when it was over and in the end, it was nothing but a very compelling bread crumb trail that ultimately lead to absolutely nowhere.Its hard to explain without spoiling, but if you're ever experienced a bait-and-switch VN where everything seems like a mundane high school slice of life until it hits you in the face with a harrowing and total mind**** reality, this story feels like the exact opposite of that, which it turns out is not nearly as interesting.Of course your milage may vary, but if you have the same interests in narratives that I do, I warn you: the mystery is so contrived, the science fiction is so soft and the intrigue shoved so far into the background they might as well not even exist. Even the mystical vibes the story delves into later are exceedingly shallow. Don't waste your time trying to figure things out, jotting down notes or making extra saves to review later.C;HN succeeds solely as a character study on Takumi, but fails in all other categories it presents to the reader. Whether or not that's enough to warrant the actual price, time cost and mental taxing of admission is definitely subjective. For me it did not, and I look forward to the day I completely forget certain scenes.But a lot of people really love C;HN and SciAdv as a whole is often recommended, so my opinion is obviously not the majority one. I wish I did have a more positive experience but I did not and I offer a different perspective. Instead of excitedly starting what I expected to be the beginning of a long trek through some of the highest rated VNs of all time, I am now hesitating to read anything else in the Science Adventure series because if they all boil down to these same issues, its really just not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: As one of the few, the proud who's 100% cleared Chaos;Head without any fan translation I can say- you really don't need to wait. The game is completely playable, understandable and entertainingly written, right now at this very moment. But everyone has to make their own choice.It's something of a miracle that the game was able to release on Steam after the earlier fiasco when it was announced, so I'd encourage any fan of the genre to pick it up and show their support.Chaos;Head is not one of my all time favorite VN's like Steins;Gate and Higurashi, but it's a good read and the Noah version makes it even better with a bunch of new routes that each add a couple hours to the game, as well as giving additional context and explanations for things we see in the original story. The protagonist, Takumi is a stereotypical otaku shut in, written intentionally to be very difficult to like and that doesn't change much throughout, but we do get a really good understanding of his thought processes, feel his terror and helplessness, his loneliness, and maybe even come to feel a little fond of the guy by the end. We've all had those moments where we internally scream, "Why me? Why is it always me?" and Takumi is the epitome of this. There are a number of different girls in the story and while there are sometimes romantic scenes, particularly in the extra routes where each girl gets a spotlight, this is not a romance at heart, it's a mystery with some strong science fiction/fantasy elements that sets the foundation for the entire Science Adventure series. Rather than a traditional choice system, you can choose to have either a negative delusion, a positive delusion, or none at all at a number of points throughout the game. Some of these are just for fun while some influence what will happen later on- it keeps things fresh but it an be a little tedious when you want to skip through to get to other routes, or hunt them all down for achievements.So play Chaos; Head when you can, and don't forget to check out the rest of the series on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me wish Steam allowed mixed reviews, honestly.It's simultaneously got the best elements of visual novels (gripping plotline, an interesting cast of characters, banger soundtrack that elevates the otherwise static visuals) and the worst (deeply unpleasant 'fanservice', tediously babysitting the skip function to see half of the content, wildly varying quality of writing across the different endings).Add on to that perhaps the most unlikable protagonist I've ever seen in a video game (yes, it's written that way on purpose, and yes, he does develop  by the end of the game, but OH BROTHER THIS GUY STINKS) and I find it really hard to give this game a glowing recommendation. There's a lot to like here, but plenty of moments that'll make you question what you're doing with your life too.Go play the Steins;Gate games first, and then if you really want to dive headfirst into the rest of the Science Adventure series, come back to this one later. You'll know pretty quickly if it's for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty close to stopping my playthrough of this within just the first few hours due to the protagonist. I knew nothing about the VN other than it was a part of the same series as Steins Gate. And just looking at the poster, I didn't expect to get a protagonist that would feel so unbearable at the beginning. The only other SciAdv VN I've played is Steins Gate and I like that quite a bit. Chaos Head barely resembles that story aside from some shared concepts and ideas. I started playing this on a whim with no real expectations but became invested by chapter 3. This is a VN I wish I could give a higher score because the things I like about it I REALLY like. But it has so many issues that stop it from truly being great.The main draw of Chaos Head is its wholly unique atmosphere, and frankly, it's the thing that kept me coming back every night for the first few chapters. And as I've mentioned, and I'm sure many others have mentioned, the protagonist is what throws people off from the VN. Takumi is inherently unbearable. Surprisingly, over time I started to find bits and pieces where I found him relatable. And parts where I started to really feel bad for him. It takes a while but he becomes someone you form a connection with because like 70% of the VN is trapped within his thoughts. Even when I'm calling him stupid for doing something or cringe at some terrible things he says and does, I still stick with him because of the moments when he feels real and human.I gave it my best to try and understand him. He's a creep, a loser, awkward, unable to communicate properly, has anger issues, is a coward, and relies on single hopes. But he's also fragile, confused, very mentally and emotionally unstable, and a kid in a mind-numbing situation. The best thing about his character is the unreliability of his narration, it adds a lot to the story. Another great thing about him is he does his best to avoid others, so when you do see him interact with someone you get a bit nervous too after a while. Cus u have no idea how he might react. The story has many ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up events that you hope are just delusions and this led to me averting my eyes from the truth along with Takumi. Hoping that it's just another delusion. And not knowing what actually happened.This suspense is Chaos Head's 2nd best feature and meshes very well with its atmosphere. Many scenes build up suspense expertly and the payoff tends to be cathartic. Paired with a cold yet familiar and isolating atmosphere it becomes Chaos Head's biggest triumph. The first half is better than the second half purely due to how much of a trip it is. It's confusing, weird, and chaotic. Despite Takumi's seemingly unbearable nature, it adds to the drug-fueled nightmare due to his confusion and worthlessness. Pair it with a good indica and it's genuinely an unforgettable experience. Unfortunately, it's held back by many issues. Like many of the twists sometimes bordering stupidity in how they were written and executed. Some of these terrible writing choices are forgiven because they lead to cool ideas and moments. But it easily could've been fixed by making different choices.As for the characters other than Takumi, they aren't around much but serve the story well for the most part. Out of the "heroines", Yua is probably the worst character but even then she has some great moments. Ayase just isn't all too interesting even though her route adds a lot to her. Nanami was brutalised way too often (it genuinely felt like she was the writer's punching bag) and underutilised. Her character arc feels the least satisfying which sucks cus she could've been one of the best characters in the story. Kozue has problems but many character moments with her are fascinating. Rimi and Sena are the best out of the "heroines" because their arcs feel the most fleshed out. The side characters are decent at best. I was interested in learning more about Ban but by the end of the VN, we didn't get much other than his personality. The main antagonist could've been better as well. He's a terrible, terrible person but outside of that, he doesn't have a character. He just enacts cruel torture and is used as a way to move the story forward and that's kinda it which is lame.In regards to the endings and routes, the common ending was pretty good and the bad ending was eh. Some parts of it were cool. Nanami's route was ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and also a little disappointing. Yua's route was easily the worst one and just straight up sucked. I hate twin character switches and think it's lazy writing, it being pretty obviously hinted at in the main story was already enough to make me like her character arc even less but this really made me dislike her the most. The only bit of ambiguity of her character is gone, it felt very unfinished, and the ending is terrible. Ayase's route was the first character route I played that felt like a route. It feels fleshed out and has its own story arc going on while keeping it interesting enough. Kozue's route was mostly just gore and murder but had some interesting moments in regards to Kozue here and there but also had the worst moment in the VN and it's related to Nanami. It felt incredibly unnecessary and jarring to include a story detail like that. The route's ending was haunting though and was my favourite ending out of the character arcs. Sena's route was probably my favourite out of the character routes. It did a good job fleshing out Sena and her dad's characters. It also had some cool moments related to the overarching story of the series. Rimi's route provided much more context related to what she was doing throughout the story and her thoughts. It felt like the most necessary route out of the bunch. The route's ending was pretty good. And finally, the true ending was nice. It added a bit more to the common ending and the prelude was cool but I also wish it had more to it.Finally, the other aspects of the VN like sound and art direction were great. The voice acting was solid and Takumi's was the clear stand out due to how hard I feel it is to pull off. The sound effects are good and the soundtrack is pretty good as well. It fits the different tones of the VN well for the most part. There were a couple of times when music played that didn't fit. But it chooses when to play music very well. All the ending songs are great and the opening is an amazing representation of the story. I like the overall art style of the VN but the character designs I have some issues with. Some of them feel very generic and look a lot like a copy-paste of a bunch of anime characters I've seen dozens of times. Especially from the 2000s. Ayase is probably the biggest offender when it comes to this but the other heroines aren't that much better. I'd like to defend these character designs if they were subversive in terms of character but they have the personalities and archetypes you'd expect them to have if you have prior knowledge of anime girl archetypes.Again, I wish I could give this VN a higher score purely because of how unforgettable many aspects of it are. However, it has many fatal flaws related to writing choices like its many twists, misused characters, and one-dimensional villains, as well as going too far in terms of cruelty making it feel jarring at times. Sometimes it felt like the scenes were padded out to the point of ridiculousness, which made the pacing of the VN much worse. But the story's atmosphere and suspense are something that I'll remember for many years. Interested in eventually getting around to Chaos Child.Played with the CoZ patch, thx to the team for their amazing work.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Writing the review in the middle of chapter 7, because I just can't bring myself to play it anymore. I read the bad reviews but they all seem to be focusing on the same aspects (insufferable protagonist), so I'll offer a slightly different perspective.For me, the first 4-5, even 6 chapters were enjoyable and I honestly don't mind the MC at all. Yes, he is pretty much (as one commenter perfectly said) a schizo incel, but I found myself being drawn to the fact that he was written so true-to-life, and I wanted to immerse myself into the character out of morbid curiosity. He's disgusting, pathetic, and weak, but I hoped that he would grow as a character and overcome his struggles, because he's a person that, ultimately, needs help (psychiatric). What really made me furious were the side characters, more specifically the harem that was forming around him, because they were all just the cringiest, blandest tropes that you could possibly create. Just imagine the most popular, boring, uninspired cliche harem love interests, and there you have it. They speak in cryptic, aphoristic sentences just to prolong screentime/playtime and seem deeper than they actually are. Some of them are downright infuriating, and for them I genuinely hoped that there was a setting not only to mute the character, but to just delete it from the game altogether. I'm generally open to cringe wish fulfillment and can stomach a lot of questionable fanservice (which is sometimes handled quite amusingly in C;H), but not when the characters are this boring and insufferable, especially because of the potential the plot and its themes have. S;G handled the harem aspect so masterfully that I had high expectations for this as well, and I ended up feeling so disappointed that it ruined the entire game for me. The game's length could've been cut in half if the characters actually said something of substance instead of cool one-liners, not to mention the constant redundancy of the dialogue that also did nothing for the plot, just inflated playtime. Example of the type of dialogues that are in the game (mainly when interacting with the female cast):girl: "... (obnoxious high pitched moany breath)"mc: hey, that girl has the same uniform as i do. now that i think about it, she is my classmate. she goes to the same class as me.girl: "umm..."mc: hey, did this classmate just speak to me? huh? no girl classmates ever speak to me!girl: "... (again the same obnoxious breathing)"mc: "..."girl: "i...i..."...and it goes on like that for 15 minutes without any relevance to the plot. By the way, "..." is pretty much the level of depth that you can expect from the female cast, because even after 7 chapters and 18 hours of playtime, I know nothing about any of the girls aside from the sporadically mentioned cool/edgy/appealing cliches that are supposed to be their personality/backstory. The detectives got more characterisation than the girls, for crying out loud. I'm disappointed because the game's premise, the characters, the plot, everything had so much potential, and it could've easily been a complete masterpiece, if the writers took their time fleshing out the characters besides the protagonist. The only reason why I still might try to finish the game is because I want to play C;C with full understanding of C;H, but from what I've read in other negative reviews, maybe I'm better off just reading the plot summary. This could've been a thriller-horror-murder mystery masterpiece, and instead got lost in a sea of boring, unnecessary scenes, unappealing characters, bad pacing etc.

_childDocuments_.review: The start of it all in the Science Adventure series. I never thought I'd give this title a shot after I watched the horrific anime adaptation years ago, but Chaos;Child really changed my mind. With the majority of what I watched forgotten about after I pushed it out of my memory, I went in to this as blind as could be after I had played Chaos;Child, and it was a great time. This visual novel is nowhere near perfect, but it's far from being bad. It's a good VN that suffers from some clunky story structure and literal game development problems, but it still delivers a satisfying journey to embark on with multiple interesting characters and events.The biggest problem is the protagonist, Takumi. He is weak in many regards, so he's not all that fun to follow at times in the story. But his weakness is everyone else's gain, as the story, events, and characters that surround Takumi become interesting and engaging. So I'd say it all balances out. Other than that, I'd say that there's one or two other characters that just don't end up having much of a purpose in the end, which really bummed me out. One of them just gets used as everyone's punching bag in almost every route, which really stinks. But other than that, I have no complaints with the characters. While some are quirky and weird, they're still very enjoyable.Similarly to Chaos;Child, this title has the same approach of having everything being confusing and hard to follow as you go through the story, up until when things get revealed at the end of the common route and in the character routes. It's fun trying to figure out what's happening even so many things seem extremely disjointed and not coherent whatsoever. At times I kinda just gave up and accepted that everything is just a chaotic mess, especially with the concept of delusions. But things do come together, and it's satisfying connecting the puzzle pieces at the end of the common route and in the following alternate/character routes.Finally, the most shared complaint is how clunky and messy this game is. This title was actually shipped out broken, where many reported that they couldn't even view the final route's ending sequences, which prevented them from finishing the game! Luckily this was fixed with an update, but there are also other problems. You have to cap the game to 60fps to avoid animations being too quick, having certain USB controllers plugged in will freak the game out in menus, the font is terrible, there's no quotations around spoken dialogue, etc. It's also unfortunate that there is cut content shipped with this game. It's super depressing for a title that many in the Science Adventure community looked forward to having all of these issues.There is a patch that fixes some of the problems I listed, however it changes the official translation to that of a fan translation. If you use this patch, you have to use the translation that a team of Science Adventure series fans put together, which is fine. There are names and such that have been changed for a variety of reasons as they expect you to always use their patches in all other Science Adventure titles. If you don't mind that, then you do get a better font, quotations on dialogue, and the return of cut content (specifically a collection of scenes that pop up in the alternate route after completing the common route, which isn't necessary to view, but preferred in my opinion). Either way, you can absolutely play the game with or without the patch, as both translations seem to be totally fine (they both tell the same story). I played the first ~6 chapters of the common route without the patch and the rest with it. It's quite obvious of there being some glaring changes in the fan translation, like the mentioned name changes, more cursing, more aggressiveness out of Takumi, and localized lines and more modern internet slang.In the end, I'd say this is a visual novel everyone who enjoys VNs should try out. This is a great introduction to the Science Adventure series, and also the obviously preferred one, but Steins;Gate still works as a good alternative introduction to the series. While it may not be the strongest in the series, Chaos;Head Noah is absolutely worth the time and effort to figuring out the big question of... Whose Eyes Are Those Eyes? And hey, if you went through Chaos;Child first, no worries! You didn't spoil too much and there's still a wild adventure to embark on. Plus, it'll open your eyes to some new stuff that'll make going through Chaos;Child again worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: While the atmosphere, mystery, and general sense of unease during the first few hours was enough to get me interested, Chaos Head never really capitalized on those elements in an interesting way. The mystery never actually goes anywhere, the tension in the atmosphere soon gives way to some sort of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ chuunibyou power fantasy, and none of the ideas or concepts at play ever get more than a surface level analysis (and most don't even end up mattering to the overall narrative).Very little of what Chaos Head does past its first 3-4 hours really felt worth experiencing. The delusions are painfully underdeveloped as a mechanic and just feel like a way the game can do whatever it needs to move the story forward, the side characters may have one or two interesting aspects about them but rarely contribute in a meaningful way outside of the one chapter where they play a role, and the main character's schtick of being a paranoid shut-in is interesting at first but quickly runs out of steam.But what brings this from mediocre to outright bad is just how badly Chaos Head manages to botch its pacing. The game has its two main routes (though one is essentially just ) as well as an additional route for each of its heroines. You need to get through all of these before you can unlock the true ending, effectively requiring 8 playthroughs. But the game makes doing this such a monumental pain because of how they are structured.The two main routes are simple enough. You just gotta get through the story and make specific choices each time. But what's especially annoying is the 6 character-specific routes since the point at which you 'enter' a route is near the very beginning of the game but everything is the same until quite late into the game, meaning (barring a small handful of extra scenes) you need to spend ~30 minutes per route just skipping through text you have already read. And this is made even worse by the fact that the skip function is very finnicky, stalling the game whenever it reaches a choice, often not skipping certain voice lines for unclear reasons thus slowing down the speed at which you can get through the game, and refusing to skip certain scenes entirely because one line changed even though 99% of the scene is exactly what you've seen before.Put that together and you're looking at around 15% of your total playtime being nothing but skipping scenes and a very large chunk of the rest of the story being very poorly paced for other reasons. Get through all of that and you can finally get to the true ending... which literally turns out to be . I genuinely feel like 15 hours of my time was wasted in the hopes that something towards the end might reignite the interesting stuff the game was doing at first. Some sort of twist or extra detail that might compensate for the game's other shortcomings. But that was not to be.So yeah... I wouldn't bother. The few areas that Chaos Head did well never really mattered while its flaws grow ever worse as the story goes on. I really can't think of a good reason why I might recommend this to somebody because even somebody who is interested in the premise and has low standards for everything else would still probably walk away disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Putting aside the rate at which this was translated by whatever team they got to do it. As it was pretty quick which is nice but perhaps too quickly. Translations take a long time for text heavy games, so combine a niche genre that also happens to be a huge money sink hole with likely little returns when translating and you get rushed pretty quickly. Happens pretty often. Heck, Steam almost not letting this ESRB rated game on it's platform is another example of why these things like this happen to VN games in particular, where it's a fight to even get the thing on the store at all.I'd differently use the fan translation patch as that has been in development for over 5 years by Committee of Zero and it comes out around after when this comes out as luck would have it. Besides the translation fixes, it also makes sure unique terms from the SCIADV universe are better understand which is part of the fun in things in a larger universe. One thing to note is the translations projects that take that long surprisingly are not even that uncommon in other text heavy games so while it did take a lot of time, it's hardly too odd of a thing.They also have patches for steins gate, chaos child, and robotics notes of which were all good.As i've been waiting for this game to be translated for literally years on end it feels like. It feels great that i'm able to buy it on an easy to access store at all. Not to mention it's pretty cheap for a VN. _childDocuments_.review: I went into this game with high expectations due to playing Steins;Gate and hearing about this game and Chaos;Child, and while it doesn't compare to Steins;Gate I genuinely enjoyed playing this. I feel like in most games especially visual novels there tends to be an issue with the protagonist lacking a personality, or embodying the same tropes over and over again. So to play as a guy who is so awkward and cowardly was refreshing. Some of the decisions Takumi makes despite being shameful, are extremely relatable. While I'm sure we all would love to be the hero, and to make the selfless choice every time, I'm sure if most of us were put in his shoes we'd also be running for the hills. While the main story was amazing, I felt like the girls routes didn't live up to that same hype. I was expecting while playing through the individual routes to be given more information, or lore pertaining to that main plot line, but that didn't seem to be the case. The routes strictly focus on the girls backstories, if you can even say that, with Sena's and Rimi's routes being the most rewarding in my opinion. There is a splash of romance implied in those individual endings, but it's not heavy, or directly stated. Despite those endings feeling like a drag to me, in the end it seemed worth it to watch the Blue Sky ending which felt so much more satisfying than the original endings. After finally receiving  100%, I think the only thing I was really left wanting for is more info on Nanami. But oh well.Overall I'd give it an 8/10 and I'd recommend even if just for the common route.

Takumi is kind of an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. A lot of the more disturbing scenes in the VN are ridiculously edgy and gory in their description. I honestly am not sure if they really needed to describe half of the stuff on display. The story can also drag at times, where I feel completely lost in overly-descriptive philosophical bs that takes me out of the entire scene to begin with. On purpose? I wouldn't doubt. This vn is made to just mess with you.Should you play/read this? I... really wanna say yes, but it's a special kind of "you should play this," ya know? Should this be your introduction to the Science Adventure series? No, that should be Steins;Gate. Should anyone play this? No, not unless you are aware how unlikable the main protag can be and the stuff that happens in here is very messed up. It's a good VN but it's not something I would recommend to just anyone. I have plenty of other suggestions before this one.Regardless, I still liked this, for the most part. It's a good vn to read and some of the ideas in this are kinda cool, if at times it can feel a bit confusing and murky to follow. I think Steins;Gate is a *much better product,* but this one? Yeah.
