_childDocuments_.review: Before anyone judges this review, it is my first one ever. I have played the trilogy of Utawarerumono and I have to say it is one of the greatest Visual Novels ever written bar none, however it was lackluster when it came to gameplay.In comes Monochrome Mobius and by God did they throw the ball out of the park with this one. Not only they still retained the same excellent writing, but they also improved on the gameplay by introducing Trailsesque JRPG elements. It became almost of a joke how I compared the gameplay to Trails but that is the charm of it as well: Aquaplus learning from other studios has to be a step in the right direction for them.The Story (may contain spoilers):The story is about our three Mask Holders from Mask of Deception BEFORE they became the Mask Holders we know about, however, with an additional character that came out of nowhere: Shunya. To say that this lady is a mystery behind an enigma is the understatement of the Utawarerumono series, especially with how the game ends which literally gives more questions than answers. Everyone I know hinted about a second game of this new Monochrome series coming to light and I have to say I 100% am hungry for more!The Gameplay:Any Trails gamer would LOVE this game, no questions asked. It has so many mechanics reminiscent of the Trails series (How to navigate the map, how to find treasures and monsters, how to evolve and improve your characters and their equipment, how to pre-emptive strike weaker enemies and so on). Was this radical change in gameplay welcome? Absolutely yes! We get to finally explore Yamato or some part of it, we get to know lore we didn't know about, we get to fight the fauna, the flora and whatever hidden in between, we get to grind (Grinding is something I love and is always welcome in any of my games! I am a grinder through and through). Suffice to say, whether you're a JRPG fan, a Trails fan or heck, even a regular Utawarerumono fan, this game is made for you.By the time I am writing this review, all I have seen is people complaining about the Text Bug. Rejoice: It has been fixed today. This shows the determination of the Dev Team to carry on caring about the Utawarerumono franchise. Not to say that the game is perfect by any means: Perfection is simply an unobtainable concept, it is however a gem in the rough that needs to be constantly polished in order to shine like its predecessors shone before it.

_childDocuments_.review: Monochrome Mobius: Rights and Wrongs Forgotten is a classic JRPG by AQUAPLUS set several years before Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception. If you have played the previous Utawarerumono games, you'll be in for a treat as it expands further into the world building and characters that you love. Story - 9/10The story expands further more on the world of Utawarerumono as well as the history of characters and how this affects the events that happen in Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth. There was never a moment I wasn't engaged with the story wanting to find out what happens next, not to mention just being able to explore the world that you saw background art in before was really cool. The ending of the game leaves you off with plenty of questions answered, but also some unanswered questions. Likely hinting at a sequel in future?The only part of the story that I disliked; the game was building up towards you heading back to Arva Shulan more than once, but that never happened. It also felt like you only got to see a small portion of it too, a Capital City was shown in background art but you never got to explore it. Characters - 9/10Oshtor as the main protagonist really shines in this game, you learn of his motivations and the will to never give up. You can see why he became so respected but also he's a guy who knows how to let loose and have fun. You can see how close he is with his family, friends and legacy, showing what it means to be a true warrior. Shunya as the main heroine is an innocent yet strong willed girl with a secret. She gives Oshtor the push he needs to keep going but is also fun, cheerful and loves adventure. Munechika is a woman gifted with a strong body who has been yearning to explore the land beyond since young. She has a maternal feel to her as well as a voice disorder. She loves cute things and can be easily embarrassed. Later on she unlocks her true calling and becomes the badass you know from Mask of Deception/Truth.Mikazuchi is a hot headed guy who strives to be the strongest warrior in the land, going so far as to challenge Oshtor when they just met. With his rivalry they really build each other up by one upping each other. Along the way he realises that he cannot rely solely on his strength alone to win but he has friends who he can back him up.Halu is a sentient robot doll that was found in the ruins of Arva Shulan, he seems to have the personality of his creator. He plays an important role of being the mascot and support of the team.Mayacowl is the main antagonist and there's not much that can be said about him really. He appears a insanely strong masked individual under the command of the Shantuuara the high priest of Arva Shulan.  Throughout the story he just remained as an obstacle for the party to overcome. I wish we learnt who was behind the mask and what his relationship was with Oshtor's father and Shunya. There are plenty more side characters like The Mikado, Honoka, Dikotoma, Raiko, Maroro, Dekopompopo and more that get a lot of characterisation in this game.Gameplay - 7/10Combat is a classic turn based combat system and can be quite addictive in its simplicity. There's your standard attack and defend options as well as skills. As your characters fight they build up Zeal which can be used to ascend up the ring and later on your characters are able to unlock an ultimate skill to use. Characters are able to ascend the ring by hitting a staggered enemy or building up zeal; this increases the characters speed. However during regular mob fights this rarely happens so you may struggle to ascend the ring. This means the difficulty of the game can be quite hard early on.One part of the combat which I felt was sorely lacking was the Enemy info. There's no indication of a HP bar or stagger meter or even elemental type.  Elements are poorly utilised here, rather than trying to counter elements in the combat, it was almost always better just to use the best damage dealing attacks. Whenever you would receive a buff or debuff, it would just flash your characters but wouldn't indicate what type of buff/debuff it was. Using Halu in combat was unsatisfying, because his AP bar never gets extended. His skills don't get a discount either. Building up his bar is a pain too unless you got lucky with him going super saiyan.The exploration in this game is amazing, there are many wide open areas to explore and it almost seems like an open rpg with the places you can go to. Being able to run around in such a big land on foot or on mount really sells that you're on an adventure. The big downside however is the Dash gauge, I honestly don't think the game should have had one as all it serves to do is to artificially slow down your progress. Plus the game doesn't allow you to toggle run in the settings. You would have to configure your controller in the steam settings in order to do this.This leads me to the settings, honestly its quite bare bones. There's not even any way to fine tune graphical settings other than setting it from low, medium or high. Not even V-Sync, I had to force V-Sync in my graphics control panel because of the screen tearing.The stat screen really needs more info, such as stagger meter, zeal bar, accuracy, dodge and critical rate. Many accessories just say increase one of these but you never know by how much. As you level you are able to increase your main stats with bonus points, these bonus points gradually increase as you level and you never have to worry about not maxing them all. There are issues with accessories too. We should have been allowed to equip more than one accessory. There are plenty of accessories in this game but you rarely used most of them. It would have been far better to be able to use two accessories to cover more stats and give the player more agency. In addition we should have been able to combine lower tier accessories to craft the higher tier versions.During the mid game, the materials you gathered from enemies and gathering points can be used to invest into shops or upgrade your general game play. This is a pretty neat feature as it gives you a reason to revisit areas around the map. Many of the side quests are your standard fetch/kill monster quest and are timed. However there's only 30 of them and its always worth doing for the rewards.Art - 7.5/10As you would expect from Misato Mitsumi and Tatsuki Amaduyu their art is iconic with the Utawarerumono series, the character designs and background art they provided here stands out. They definitely knew what they were drawing when they did the drunken men scene.The environments are quite pleasing to look at and there's plenty of variety, from deserts to ruins to caves and thriving cities. As you can't adjust any graphical settings there can be issues with frame rate in certain areas such as the Trials or dense forests with a lot of textures. The obvious downside is the NPC models, they are pretty bad. After a while you can get used to them and they will be patched later on but it would put off a lot of people when they first see it. The fight scenes however are quite dynamic and the character models move fluidly.Soundtrack - 10/10Overall the soundtrack is fantastic and it changes whenever you enter a new area. There's a dedicated desert theme, ruin theme and more. Plenty of upbeat, sad, emotional, atmospheric, techno, traditional themes. A banger in Harukanaru Tabiji. Emotional in Utsurou Omoi which uses the games leitmotif. Personal favourite is Shousei. As usual Suara does a great job on the opening and ending. The voice acting is fantastic too, honestly the Utawarerumono series has some of the best voice actors in the industry and it shows in their delivery.Overall - 8.5/10Monochrome Mobius: Rights and Wrongs Forgotten is a must play for fans of the Utawarerumono Series and those who are looking to get into a classic JRPG with a Stellar Story, turn based game play with a Fantastic OST.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a huge throw back to those who already played the Utawarerumono Trilogy [Mask of Deception/Mask of Truth/Prelude of the Fallen]. But to those seeing this game for the first time, this is a journey that is worth embarking.Do you have to play the previous games to play this one?? - No, you don't have to but I highly recommend you to do so if you want to experience the same feeling I have had when playing them.Monochrome Mobius is a lot more slower and at your pace in terms of story telling/character building to battle sequences but is executed in a timely manner compared to the other releases. The graphics compared to the Trilogy is mediocre in comparison but I personally don't care and loved this game regardless. I am playing on [Hard] on my first run and I can confidently say that it's still very enjoyable. Yes the battle system for Monochrome Mobius is a bit "In your face" at first but with a bit of time, you'll easily understand the fundamentals and will zoom with ease.There is a scene in Monochrome Mobius that made me tear up hard that veterans can only understand. If they have had Suara's voice/song in that very scene as that scene's bgm, I'd probably ugly cry to the max.Highly recommend playing Monochrome Mobius to it's fullest and if you have time please play the Utawarerumono Trilogy.

_childDocuments_.review: Monochrome Mobius is a great game featuring a battle system I don't believe any other franchise has attempted. After completing the game, I can consider it balanced and complex as it involves many features that isn't required to figure out (even I haven't figured all of it out), which is why I think that makes the game even better, the vagueness the game has to offer with its battle system that it explains is what makes it so great to experiment and figure things out on your own if you're just that kind of person. I found myself often excited at learning new things about the battle system simply by playing enough and realizing why certain things happen the way they do, (even though I could also just look it up in the codex the game has).There are apparent FPS issues due to high amounts of foliage existing in one place, which is the main reason for most of the negative reviews since the first of roughly four instances happens when you enter the overworld for the first time. While this can be fixed by lowering the graphics setting, its understandable that it's undesirable to do so. The graphic design I would describe as Unique and "PS3 Era" which is more than acceptable seeing as this isn't a AAA company and also the first time they've had a go at 3D environments that doesn't consist of a fixed overhead camera in their previous tactics installments.The story and writing the game has is on par with the previously made games of the franchise, but might not show to most until you obtain your full party, when the character interactions can properly play out. In the end I had alot of fun with the game, the later boss fight are all phenomenal with most showing off the importance of the battle system. The lowest marks I can give it is from the first impression of the overworld which both grew on me and improved after a certain point of the game until the end.Graphics: 6.5/10Gameplay: 10/10Writing: 9.5/10Overall: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Man.. they can't just end the game off like that!! (sequel perhaps?) First getting into it I was pretty hesitant in buying the game in the first place, but after 40 hours of living out the casts' journey I have to say it was absolutely worth it. I will admit the gameplay gets stale and bloated after awhile, but I still believe that it holds up till the end. The story itself is very worthy of being an Utwarerumono story, you get to see so many new faces of characters being explored and it's all so incredible. _childDocuments_.review: I was initially a bit disappointed when I learned the big Aquaplus 20th anniversary was more Utawarerumono instead of a new IP for Aquaplus, but little did I know, this game would revive my love for Utawarerumono tenfold and make it stronger than ever.Mobius really excells by getting you to get hands deep in Uta's world through its open world RPG game, it's crazy how much more immersed and excited I got with it by controlling the characters' adventure through WASD, and the story is truly stellar. While there are certainly links to Utawarerumono, this is *essentially* a fully new story separate to the trilogy, showing new angles to everything the world had to offer in ways we couldn't see before. Characters I already loved as side characters in the Utawarerumono games were given way more dimensions and elevated them so much more, I cannot underestate how much the time spent with them meant to me and how much stronger this game makes you feel for them.Probably the biggest critique (if you can call it one) is that it's obvious this Mobius is only one part, and this game NEEDS a sequel snice there are too many questions left unanswered and characters we haven't seen the deal of. But despite that, this story ends on a very satisfying stopping note that leaves me feel satisfied despite still wanting more. I feel like I properly completed a game, not half of one.I still don't know how I'd rank Monochrome Mobius with Uta's other entries, and I'm not sure if I want to, what I can say though is that this is 150% worth the play. Fans of Utawarerumono fans NEED to get on and explore this world the way the game lets you. Seeing these sides to this cast is just too valuable, and this story is so powerful, emotional, and too exciting to miss out on.

It is not the greatest game in the venerable franchise, but it is still a story worth experiencing.

_childDocuments_.review: I throroughly enjoyed the journey 'Monochrome Mobius: Rights and Wrongs Forgotten' offered and would strongly recommend it to anyone interested in story-based games. It's a worthy addition to the Utawarerumono family as a prequel to the 'Mask of' games, but also holds its own as a standalone game.To me this is the most important rating. The story and the characters are what the game is really about. The way small references in Utaware trilogy were expanded into compelling scenes and storylines was impressive. Seeing the younger versions of familiar characters and their development is a treat.While familiarity with Utaware helps appreciating the finer details, I believe MM does stand on its own for newcomers as well.It's not a perfect story by any means, but there are enough cool, intriguing, sad and funny moments to raise a very good story with a few flaws to a 10/10 experience for me. Since it leaves many questions unanswered for a possible sequel, some might disagree.I played on 'hard' difficulty and found the gameplay a little grindy, but still mostly enjoyable. The turn-based battle is interesting and varied enough to carry through most of the game. Battling lower level enemies does get too repetitive at times, since you don't even get/need to use most of the features, but boss battles remain positively challenging all the way.Running around in dungeons and forests isn't my favorite part, but having to take your time to get from point A to point B does often add to the immersion and feeling of achievement. Quick travel was much appreciated once the option was added. Field attacks to kill lower level enemies without a battle are oddly satisfying.I know the graphics are nothing special compared to bigger budget games, but mostly they serve the purpose well and at times the scenery and some of the creatures looked really impressive to me.I've read a lot of criticism about the NPC lacking faces (before the update), which didn't really bother me. What does however hinder some of the scenes are the very limited facial expressions of the main characters.The 2D images used in some of the visual novel parts are great. I just wish there were more.The soundtrack is a little more hit or miss compared to Utaware trilogy where the OST really shines throughout. Mostly it adds to the atmosphere and emotion, but a few of the tracks felt amateurish and poorly orchestrated.The voice acting for the most part is top notch as expected. It's a shame sidequests aren't voiced.It took me around 80 hours to complete the game. I let the scenes play out at a leisurely pace, completed most of the sidequests without going for every achievement, didn't rush through levels, and had to redo battles a couple of times because of mistakes. Now that saving is available anywhere and the need for grinding has been reduced, I would guess around 10 hours can easily be shaved off.

_childDocuments_.review: Monochrome Mobius was not really a game I was looking forward to play that much since the game did not look really appealing to me before it was released. But I still gave it a try since it's still Utawarerumono even if it's not mentionned in the title, since I was interested in how a prequel would work out.The result is that it's in my opinion a very bad RPG with a nice enough story (and a lore as good as the trilogy).I'll start with the good (since I have way more bad things to say than good) :- The plot is interesting, it start with something really classic (finding the truth about a disappeared father), it really feels like a journey since the game make you visit a lot of places of the universe (a lot of them are new even to the Utawarerumono fans). But very quickly, it takes this basic plot of finding your disappearing father to add a lot of elements to the lore, some of them are already known by the players since it was already spoked during the Mask duology, but it gives more details to it. I think any Utawarerumono fan would be at least satisfied by this.- The music is good, nothing breathtaking (especially compared to the original trilogy) but it's still nice to hear the composers working for a RPG this time. I'm a bit sad that the exploration OST are so few though.- The dynamic of the main party is good (mostly between Mikazuchi and Oshtor), it feels like a real group, with no one being out of place (something I can't even say for the original trilogy since some characters were mostly just there, not that it's a major flaw to me). It really helps that the game only has 4 playable characters (a bit like Trails of Zero). I don't really like her but Shunya is still a solid character, with enough development (part of it is pretty subtile, so it's nice).- The last scene of the game is really good, it tease some really interesting points for a sequel (if it's released, the game will probably flop, and the sales in the first week in Japan were really weak for a newly released game).For the bad (or the things I didn't enjoy) :- While the story is still interesting and the lore is rich, I really disliked how shonen the narrative structure was.Of course it make sense but for me, it was executed in a bland way, with a lot of tropes I've already seen in other JRPG/animes (the game has some scenes with similarities to Kimetsu no Yaiba, and it's not a compliment to me). I'm not against shonens at all (I'm a Xenoblade 2 fan after all) but I was a bit disappointed by it since the Mask duology had some shonen scenes/aspects but it was less invasive.- The game was honestly a pain to play, the gameplay is dull and balanced poorly, the game forces you to kill a lot of enemies (and there are a lot of them in the dungeons) and to complete a lot of (bland) sidequests to keep your characters at a decent level. I found myself being underleveled before the final boss even though I completed 20 sidequests, I don't think it was a good decision given how the fights are tedious in the long run for me.- The game is also quite ugly for me, it's their first JRPG so I could have forgiven, but for a game of 2022 it's really ugly, the characters models are lacking in charm, their facial expressions are bland, the graphics are really poor, and the map is also really bland. And frankly, the NPCs without a face are shameful, I've never seen that in a recent JRPG (some titles at least are more elegant about that), they didn't even try to mask it a little bit. It's not an issue for some people but I think immersion is something really important in a JRPG, and the towns of the game felt really hollow and lacking in life because of this. It was also annoying to see these NPCs during some cutscenes, it was hard to take the game seriously at times because of that. But it's not the only issue with the towns, they are quite empty with nothing to do, you just go there to start some (uninspired) sidequests and to buy equipement and items. There are also a lof of invisible walls, with part of the towns you can't even access, while the towns are already very small.- The exploration is not satisfying to me, there are some little secrets but they have nothing really worth to give to the player except nice items, sometimes it reward you with "viewpoints" but frankly it did not feel rewarding since the game has poor graphics and the art direction is lacking (even if sometimes it has nice ideas, like the final dungeon).- There are also some aspects of the characterization of Shunya and Munechika I really disliked, but it's hard to speak about it without spoiling for Shunya. Regarding Munechika, I really didn't like how tropey her character was and how they wrote her "feminine side", it felt a bit cringe and too clichey (even if it's probably a persona).- The cutscene direction was horrendous, the game really has poor animation and it's even more visible during the cutscenes, it was often hard for me to take the game seriously during the "hype scenes" since the characters feels really static, it was honestly worse than Cold Steel 3 and Cold Steel 3 was not good in this aspect (while being a game of 2017).- The main "antagonist" of the game is unique in some aspects (with a good design), but fails to be really compelling because of a lack of presence during the game, it's a shame since the motives of this character make a lot of sense given the the story/lore of the game. Regarding the other antagonists, one of them was okay, nothing really that interesting but at least his character was cohesive, but the other antagonists were just annoying and very clichey, it's a shame since the game point out that no camp is really evil, but the game still has some really cartoon evil characters. The antagonists were never the main strength of Utawarerumono but I was expecting them to improve a little bit regarding this aspect, but it did not happened.- The visual novel sections are really poor, with not enough sprites, all the characters have like 5 different sprites. I could have forgiven this if it was fully a JRPG but these sections are separated for the rest of the game, so it's hard for me to ignore. The rare CGs of the game at least are good, even if I think the chara design of the visual novel sections are way below the style of the Mask duology and Prelude of the Fallen.- The pacing of the game suffers because of the length of the dungeons, and I think the game is a bit too long for what it wants to tell, even if the story of the game is not really complete.TL;DR : I did not enjoy the game at all even if the plot was nice (with some underwhelming aspects in my eyes) but it was not enough for me to appreciate it since it's in my opinion a bad RPG, Aquaplus should have sticken to visual novels in my opinion, even if I can still respect their wish to release a RPG. I also had no real expectations as a RPG but it was worse than I thought it would be, and I thought the story would also be better. I would still recommand this game (it's a shame there's no neutral option instead of "I recommand" or "I don't recommand") to the Utawarerumono fans who have no issues with archaic JRPG since the story is kind of good and the lore of the game is really interesting. (Game finished in 54 hours, I was mainly playing offline)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm savoring this one!As a longtime admirer of the Utawarerumono trilogy, this is a real treat!I'm just four hours in as of this initial review note, but it's clear this is a work of respect and love, an homage to the trilogy.I feel that the Utawarerumono trilogy is almost uniquely distinguished among creative works in the new digital media, approaching literature in terms of characters, heart, and depth of feeling. There's a lot of heart here as well.If you're new to the story, it'd be my recommendation (at least, as of now) that you work through the trilogy first, to afford yourself the experiences of recognition, surprise, and delight that have characterized my brief time with Monochrome Mobius already. For those who've been through the trilogy and are wondering whether to dive into this as well: Yes, by all means, this is faithful to the original body of work, and you're in good hands.Editing to add one observation... You'll run into prompts early on saying, "Take your time".They're not kidding. That's the best advice I could offer. If you're enjoying the story and spending time with these characters, you can make it better by not hurrying. You'll get so much more out of this work by slowing down, walking not running, exploring the maps fully, engaging the monsters, finding the goods. There's no reason to hurry, and there's huge reward for NOT hurrying... Enjoy!I'll continue to update this as things progress, but if you're at all curious about them, this, and the trilogy which preceded it, are well worth your attention and time. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: As a Steam Curator and JRPG entusiast, I digest Turn-based RPGs for breakfast. I've been playing them since I have memories. I love them. After completing the game at 100% of all the achievements and content I can say Mobius Monochrome systems are extremely traditional and yet really fun, but the game has a big flaw: it's EXTREMELY easy, to the point that I am forced to NOT invest any points earned levelling up or I'll be able - and I'm not even joking - to oneshot bosses. I'm playing at Hard Mode, which is the hardest selectible one (easy and hard), and I just unlocked another system at chapter 5 which grants me even stronger weapons/armor and accessory if I have enough materials, which, of course, as I like to collect everything and finish my secondary missions before proceeding with the story, I had. Now I am also FORCED to not buy new equipment or I'll risk to break the game.I'm not entirely sure how this level of unbalancing is possible, and how easy it's preventable creating multiple levels of difficulty, but gameplay-wise, Mobius Monochrome makes me wish there were reasons to actually invest my time into understanding the systems of the game, and actually play the game, by the time of this review I'm sad to say this big flaws almost make me quit playing.Story wise isn't extraordinary but it's really anime-like and lightheaded, to my taste characters are its strongest card: they are likable, they have a development, they are multifaceted and most importantly interesting. There's an abundant amount of dialogue which is expect from a game like this but it's disheartening to notice lots of them are useless or even missplaced. Most games are diveded equally alternating dialogues to gameplay, in this case things don't really have a pattern, by the time you're reading useless stuff after half hour of dialogue one understand somethings doesn't add up. Same thing happen with exploration, the game is explained as a field exploration but there's so much vast of nothing with very little exploration, and, as the dialogue, when you think you have had enough before the next location, you're still at half the trail you're supposed to follow.I hope things are addressed in other patches, as for now, I'll leave a negative review because after chapter 5 I'm nearly dropping it and I feel extremely sad because the game has really good potential. TL;DR Decent story, likable characters, extremely easy and poorly balanced gameplay.[If you find my reviews interesting, follow me as a Steam Curator and join my group: I go by KureinInSight]

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is a solid, great first attempt on Aquaplus' part. I enjoyed it all the way through. Initially, I said this game was meant for those who had played the rest of the series, but for those that are new to the game, it's written in a way that references the other material, but you can still have a good grip of what's going on, generally speaking. If anything, playing/finishing this is incentive to play the other games. It's a bit of an odd case, because the game has more impact if you've played the series, but retrospectively changes how you look at the others. Regardless, there's plenty to be enjoyed here. The voice actor messages that you get upon completion were a really nice addition. I enjoyed hearing their perspectives on their works and the game. Now, onward to my walls of text that I'm too lazy to shorten.__________________________________________________________________________EDIT EDIT EDIT: As of 12/21, the NPC faces have been given detail. As I said, the developers have been very responsive to bugs and game issues. Several patches have been implemented since launch. Give it a shot. The game has been made easier since I finished it, but I imagine my points still stand generally speaking.EDIT EDIT: I finished the game. That final boss was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard, but I made it. Excellent game. I'm more than happy that this came out, and more so that I played it. Looking forward to what Aquaplus does next.EDIT: I have about half the achievements in this game, so I'm assuming I'm around halfway through. I have a much better understanding of the game, so I wanted to revise my review a bit. The game's battle system is not just a typical turn-based, and I question why so many reviewers had dismissed it as such(as though that would even be a bad thing). The action ring plays a major role in battle, as enemies will take advantage of it as well. This is more than apparent in boss fights, as a good number of them will steamroll you if you're not considerate of turn order and your available options. The further you get in the game, the more abilities, passive and active, you unlock, and it just gets more interesting from there. Also, for the love of god, do not forget to defend. Spending your time mashing the attack button, a la Final Fantasy, is going to get you in trouble. That being said, I think the difficulty in this game is very fair. It is usually the case that the game gives you enough resources to manage fights. I do tend to play somewhat conservatively with MP, but I will throw out items and abilities in a boss fight like it's nothing. I've not had one instance in which I felt the need to grind(thank goodness), but the game has provided a steady challenge throughout. Boss fights are pretty damn fun, and demand strategy. The level curve is pretty steady. Provided that you're relatively active with side quests(I just do them as they become available), it's unlikely you'll fall behind with levels to any major extent. I would recommend Hard mode for someone who is experienced with JRPGs in general. There's no shame in playing on normal, but I only have hard mode to reflect on. Those that would prefer easier story progression can play Normal. Make no mistake, though, this game is solid gameplay-wise. Story is the main focus, but there's plenty to do along the way. Storywise, well, it's Utawarerumono in all but name. You know what to expect. A world full of great characters of various backgrounds, mysterious secrets to unfold, and a mix of serious conflict and lightheartedness as well as touching moments between characters, tear-jerkers, knee-slappers, a little va va voom(looking at you, Murasame; your daughter got it from her mama), all that good stuff. Monochrome Mobius has actual cutscenes and sequences this time around, which help to progress the story. I think they're pretty well done. I especially like the sword fight sequences that pop up from time to time. I'm a sucker for that ♥♥♥♥. If you're ready to learn more about some of your beloved characters from the series and dive deeper into Yamato's history, you should play this. Some may prefer the VN format, but I can say I'm pleasantly surprised and greatly satisfied with what we got here. I don't know how the game ends yet, but if this is a hint of more to come, whether it be part of the Utawarerumono series or not, I'm looking forward to it.Shunya still a qt. I love that we get the chance to see Oshtor's backstory. Can't wait to finish this one. Also, if you run into a bug, don't get too frustrated, The developers have been very responsive in issuing patches.__________________________________________________________________________Previous Review:Of course I'm going to recommend this, but if you're even considering it, then you're probably familiar with the series. That being said, why even bother reading reviews? Get it for yourself.Anyway, I'm not going to say much because I haven't done much, but it ran without a hitch on Linux, Looks great, runs greats, sounds great, feels great. Imma keep playing. Returning characters make me giddy, and Shunya a qt. Looking forward to seeing how this develops. Oh, NPCs have no face. That was kind of a thing in the other games, but there's way more actual random NPCs, so it's more noticeable. I just chuckled and kept it moving.Obligatory "It works on Linux" statement. Proton Next seems to perform well for this game. Although depending on the version, cutscenes can freeze temporarily, which is annoying. Only happened to me in the ending sequences.. Thank you, Aquaplus. The transition from VN to 3D game is looking pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. I was concerned at first, but now I'm just happy to play it. Now, while you could play this game standalone, I think it's more than clear that you should be playing this after the 3 Utawarerumono games. There's all sorts of things to reference, even in the first 2 hours. Not to mention, you know, the identity of the main character.Enjoy. I know I will.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR with no detail spoilers-ishShould you play this if you are new to Utawarerumono? - NO, while things at the end of the story seem to connect to Mask of Deception, it still has its own storyline that doesn't seem quite done yet and perhaps we should expect a sequel to further explain it.Should you play this after playing the trilogy / if you've played the trilogy?- ONLY IF YOU WANT TO, the game is okay-ish while the story is so far alright. As I've mentioned previously, it hasn't tied up all ends in its own story yet and brought up more questions at the end of the game so *sequel maybe*. If not that, then maybe you just want to play anything related to Utawarerumono then go ahead as this game furthers the world building of the Utawarerumono universe giving us the coming of age stories' of Oshtor and the gang. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I must admit, I did not research deeply regarding this game. Only that I saw trailers and gameplay videos on YouTube thinking its a full 3D game. Which is why I was *slightly* disappointed that they went back to VN styles for certain cutscenes throughout the game. Like at the start for example, a cutscene in Oshtor's house. You can see the house fully modeled but then switch to CG's when you enter. Me expecting animated 3D cutscenes instead was a tid bit disappointed. For places we've been in MoD/MoT, you will see the same CG background art whatever you call it.The gameplay is different from the trilogy that we know going back to the traditional turn based gameplay. It tried putting its own spin by making it spin like a clock with a way to ascend as to rotate your turn faster but really, it just is a generic turn based mechanic that is re-skinned.Like every other JRPG, it is tiring to play as you'd have to grind out mobs to level out decently. And so, I'm not sure how well you could progress in this game if you just wanted to play for the story and avoid most monsters. Fortunately, I am used to grinding games although the hassle bit does remain and reached up to level 75-80 for the gang and had essentially no trouble going through the last part of the game. Except maybe for the last boss which took me some retries.If it does help ease the pain of grinding, getting much more powerful than certain monsters get you to instantly kill them when attempting to initiate a battle instead of you know, battling them. Overall, the gameplay is nothing special with a few mini puzzles along the way that are relatively easy to solve but perhaps a hassle for some (due to me being lazy to walk places in parts of the game). If anything, just remember I guess that you're here mainly for the story whether you like this type of JRPG or prefer the trilogy gameplay. As from the initial release of the game, the generic NPC's still do not have proper textures, although they've at the very least added faces now lol. They still look like they came straight out of a PS1 game. This could be a deal breaker for a small few but perhaps not the majority.Not gamebreaking but kind of ruins the immersion you have with the game as they've shown they can do it properly with the merchants having proper faces and textures day 1. Were they just lazy? Was this game rushed? Who knows.Fortunately or not, regional pricing has this product equal to about 30usd to me as I've heard it costs 60usd for others. Which is why I was able to let go of some issues I have with this game, especially during launch. But alas, it's a new venture for AQUAPLUS in trying out this JRPG style and let's see if they'll continue and improve upon it the next time or just be lazy again.

_childDocuments_.review: A PSA of sorts for those who plan on buying this:The 60FPS limiter in-game is misleading as there's still plenty of other in-game portions that feel like they're animating and updating at 30FPS. This is despite the TimeManager in the GlobalGameManagers file having a FixedUpdate rate of 16.67ms (60FPS). Also, despite the advertised keyboard and mouse support, the mouse doesn't work and most of the UI elements are navigated using the WASD keys. Attempting to use Special K or another external framerate limiter (like RTSS) to fix the frametimes is a futile effort from my time using them. I'm able to achieve rock solid frametimes, and I'm using a $700 graphics card before anyone wants to strawman me like a smartass about "buying better hardware".I'd consider investigating these issues, but BepInEx absolutely refuses to hook to the game, AND it's using IL2CPP on top of that (instead of using the plain Mono runtimes, which much to the dismay of certain types of individuals makes little difference in CPU utilization on PC, but also makes debugging these issues incredibly difficult).I'll at least give them props on having the option of PlayStation and Switch button prompts, alongside forcing KB/M or Xbox prompts if you are using a Steam Controller or a Razer analog keypad or something on those lines. That, and the fullscreen mode seems to work properly (in Windows at least) with proper letterboxing/pillarboxing being done (I'm unsure if the resolution options are being hardcoded though), so it's unlikely that you are going to experience a ton of resolution related jank like the previous Uta ports on PC if you have a non-16:9 display.As for Steam Deck/Proton support, I've had issues with the game crashing on the opening FMV cutscene with an up to date version of Fedora 37, but I've heard that Steam Deck users are able to play the game without said stability issues. So it's entirely possible it's another Persona 5 Royal situation where there's odd behavior going on.But for now, I'd advise waiting for a sale and patches (Which considering the track record of the other Utawarerumono games on PC, may never come in an official capacity). Unless you are fine using an external 30FPS limiter (As most Unity limiters are inaccurate) alongside some tweaks to lower input latency, I wouldn't recommend it in it's current state.

_childDocuments_.review: This was kind of a let down.  First, there are no English voices - which is understandable if they are on a budget. But the voice they use for the main character is somewhere between "Extremely angry Japanese newsman" and "Extremely angry Japanese gangster". It's like he's angrily shouting everything.  Combat was OK - It's turn based, but has this weird ring that show the character icons. Would have been better with no ring, or a linear layout.  The story takes a long time to really get going - some guy's sister pops out of a portal, and she keeps referring to their dad, etc - and he doesn't even put 2&2 together, and only realizes later. He must be the dumbest guy on the planet. The other thing I didn't like is that, while the main characters are fully modeled, the NPCs have no faces. That's right - they look like bargain basement department store mannequins - no eyes, no mouth. Just a bump where the nose is. This is a very strange design choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Monochrome Mobius is a game that I have extremely mixed opinions about. On one hand, the humor in this game was great! It had the classic great dynamics between the main cast that the Utawarerumono series always has. The story itself was also great in many points. Watching how Oshtor, Mikazuchi, and Munechika grew into the great characters they ended up becoming was also amazing. It really highlighted how nobody starts off as a super badass charasmatic leader and even the greatest among us start with infinite flaws. Seeing the backstory too of everything such as how Ukon and Sakon came to be and just the origin of their relationship was such a nice addition to the story too. The main plotline too I feel was also very intriguing and I was constantly on my toes about what was going to happen next on their journey together. There were also plenty of emotional moments too that brought a tear to my eyes watching certain things play out.However, I do have a long string of complaints for this game. First is the difficulty. I will say I played through this game on normal mode but seeing how hard mode only changed the stats by a small amount, I dont think much would have been changed but keep this in mind while i talk about this. So the very beginning was generally pretty simple as with all rpgs with the initial bosses being relatively easy. The early middle stages of the game were frustrating beyond belief though, Most bosses just had attacks that one shotted me over and over again and at some points i just gave up on healing cause chance are they were going to be one shot by them regardless, it made for a really frustrating experience where I couldn't really do much. I tried using defensive buffs, I tried using better gear but I just couldn't stop the one shotting. Part way through the game I finally decided to just sit down and grind for a bit and o boi after 45 minutes of grinding, the rest of the game became the easiest thing in the world. So this game has a special autokill system once you are 9 levels higher then the enemy but once i reached that level, maintaining the 9 level difference was simple so i never had to fight a regular mob again. In terms of bosses, because i got so overleveled so quickly, I never actually struggled with any bosses at all afterwards either so basically with 45 minutes of grinding, I had trivialized the gameplay part of the game.....The actual RPG aspect itself I feel like was also pretty dull, alot of the mechanics didn't feel like there was that many opportunities to interact with. For example the action ring mechanic, I never could use in some fights because bosses would stagger me so often and I'd lose the extra movement without getting much millage with it. With some bosses too they were basically resistant to stagger or had a huge ass stagger bar so i never really got a chance to stagger them before they just died. So long story short, alot of the "fancy" stuff was just fluff that didn't really add much to my gameplay in the end.Also one last qualm. I have to say idk why every JRPG does this but the final dungeon for this game was miserable. The puzzle itself wasn't so bad but the wait time where your not doing anything cause your waiting for animations to finish was one of the most miserable things I've experienced in a game in quite a while. I was half tempted to just not finish the game as just watch wth the ending was to give you an example of how much i hated waiting for the animations in the stupid dungeon.Overall, I feel like the best way to describe this game is that I feel this was a game I sort of wish was just a regular visual novel. This was a game where it felt like the gameplay didn't particularly add that much to my enjoyment of the title it just detracted from it and if it was a game that was just solely focused on the story I could have had a much better time because we also would have been able to have more development than what we had and the pacing would have been better from a more continuous story. If the game had a better system, then maybe I would feel differently but currently thats how I feel about this game. I Still do recommend although only for fans of the Utawarerumono series. If not, I recommend you just start with the original visual novel games. While this game can be played as a standalone, I do feel like it doesn't showcase the strength of the series anywhere close to as strongly as the original ones.TLDR: story was great, gameplay was super iffy

_childDocuments_.review: i hate to say that my feelings are mixed for this entry in the Utawarerumono series. i absolutely loved the trilogy proper, however, Monochrome Mobius did not give me the same experience. i'll list some likes/dislikes as well as a spoiler section which will highlight the primary reasons for my mixed feelings. that said, if you want more Utawarerumono lore/story then you definitely want to play this game. i don't recommend playing this game as your first exposure to Utawarerumono, definitely play the trilogy first. -more Utawarerumono. this is the primary reason of my recommendation. the series is just very enjoyable and to get another opportunity to experience it gets my recommendation-getting to see the journey of oshtor/munechika/mikazuchi to their current roles in MoD/MoT-the voice actors appeared to all be the same from the trilogy, and the voice acting in general is exceptional -much less visual novel storytelling. i would have liked them to stay more in line with the original trilogy. there was too much exploration/battles. the primary draw of Utawarerumono is storytelling. its fine if they wanted to try a JRPG format but it just wasnt as good of an experience for me-many of the 3d cutscenes seemed very stiff and janky to me-some of the achievements were really annoying and there are some missables, otherwise you can 100% it in one playthrough-the OST is not up to par, a big miss considering how exceptional the trilogy's is-the battle system is replaced by your typical turn based party combat, however i did not find it very engaging. it just didnt feel like a cohesive battle system

_childDocuments_.review: I am thoroughly enjoying my time with Monochrome Mobius, but I for sure can't give a blanket recommendation for this game. It's competent, with a few novel ideas like the Action Ring, being a fun twist on the visible turn order mechanics of other RPGs. This game is part of the greater Utawarerumono series, a trilogy of visual novels broken up by some very fun SRPG segments. While I wouldn't say that familiarity with that world and its characters is downright *required* to enjoy this game, the game doesn't make much effort to get you caught up, should you be unfamiliar. There's an in-game glossary, but I doubt that'd be enough for someone wholly unfamiliar with the IP.Game runs really well, and the characters look fantastic, but you can tell this game had a lower budget and knew where to spend it. Things like generic NPCs and some environment textures being almost laughably low resolution can absolutely bother some folks. It's amusing for me, but it might be a dealbreaker for you and make exploring the thoroughly-thought out world of the Utawarerumono franchise less enjoyable.It's also a bit on the simple side, which for me personally isn't a bad thing. Makes it more focused, comfy, and a bit easier to zoom through, but if you're looking for something with tons of side content or minigames that you can lose dozens of hours in, Monochrome Mobius is not that game.If those cons listed above don't deter you, I think you can really get into Monochrome Mobius and appreciate what this game has going for it, with the love and effort put in to expand the rich world that the Utawarerumono games had already established.Not for everyone, not even among JRPG diehards, but for me, this is what am wanting in a game right now.

_childDocuments_.review: The transition to a fully rendered world is overall a nice one for Utawarerumono. It's pretty rough, the graphics aren't great but they also aren't bad either. But the world does feel like it'srelatively expansive, the main highways of Yamato do feel pretty big. But then there's the capital, which is really small yet has a fast travel service NPC between 3 areas. In terms of the battles, it's interesting, but playing normal mode, it's really easy to get yourself overleveled so you can't really experience it to the fullest.In terms of story, there's a lot of additional development for the Mask of Deception/Truth cast, makes me appreciate them more. The new additions to the story are kept quite mysterious. Like once I got to the last stretch of the game it felt like new points were being dropped constantly without elaboration, only room for speculation (until a sequel perhaps). I don't dislike that, I actually think it's neat.

_childDocuments_.review: I first became familiar with Aquaplus by playing the unofficial translation of White Album 2. I enjoyed the writing and wanted more. This was how I came across Utawarerumono.  So how does Monochrome Mobius shape up? Writing wise, it's great. I had a lot of laughs and even tears during the approximately 30 hour adventure. That being said, it never reaches the peaks of Mask of Truth but fortunately doesn't fall as low as some of the valleys of Mask of Deception. Overall, very solid writing.Now as far as the gameplay goes. It's a very by the numbers JRPG. Nothing that jumps out at you. Just a vehicle to tell the story, not unlike the SRPG component of the original series.Production value is on the weaker side too. The faceless NPCs have been well documented. And if you were hoping to explore the Imperial Capital's busy streets and the training grounds of Ennakamuy like in the original games... you won't get that. You see a few rows of buildings with an equipment vendor and a consumables merchant. All of the cities are like that. Witcher 3 this is not.I still enjoy what I got out of the game and am glad I was able to revisit some old friends and can't wait for a Monochrome Mobius 2. But this was a clearly budgeted production that I felt might have done better as a straight visual novel. Get it if you're a fan of the franchise but you may want to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great masterpiece of Utawarerumono franchise brought by Aquaplus, but could be just for fans are already for the series. Most of the unpleasant experiences happened in my first 10 hours of play as many have mentioned, but after reaching the Yamato capital the 'flaws' in game play were mostly 'fixed' by the ABL, and then great story started to unfold. The story itself was like typical JRPGs, where you could figure out most of the story line at an early stage. For average players this may not make the Monochrome Mobius stand out, however for fans, there will be a lot of moments that are so resonating and nostalgic, flashing back memories from other titles of the franchise. Those moments were throughout my last 50 hours of play, and really made me feel I had avoided my mistake of giving up or negatively commenting the game too early. Everything in this game, the story, the music, the characters, are still very Utawarerumono. And thanks to the well made open world, even exploring the Yamato land became a new way of knowing this universe, especially when coming across landmarks from past titles. Some of the scenes were just purely beautiful to watch.I like the Utawarerumono series because of the fascinating background settings and touching stories, so battles were not my main focus, although I still enjoyed the 20-30 hours extra of getting characters to the appropriate level. This was in Normal mode, and I wish there could be a choice of Easy for players like me. Also, it would be better if players could replay the events after the endgame, which was doable in past titles.In the end, Aquaplus please keep up with your good work, and I look forward to the next episode of the Monochrome Mobius (also pc ports of Zan 1&2 if possible).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm of two minds when it comes to this game. On one hand, I've a few major/minor issues:The visual quality along with the fact that the game can still have instances of stuttering/slowdown in some areas. (Hopefully the recently announced updates will fix this.)Pretty bad item drop rates plus enemies that have the chance to not spawn at all when you go to the areas that they do spawn in.Somewhat forgettable overworld music. (Suara carries the vocal OST as usual, and has yet to disappoint me.)Slightly undercooked side missions and story presentation. (I give them a slight pass for this considering that this is the first time that they're doing a game in this style.)A translation team that is somehow as bad or worse than NISA, along with occasional errors with the text. (Some of those errors might have gotten fixed, but I doubt that the major issues I have will be changed at all).However, even among those issues, I still found myself enjoying the game. The tag line: "It's the story that brings an RPG to life." rings true with every mainline game in the series, and this is no exception, even if I personally felt like some instances felt somewhat inconsistent with the later stories. My issue with that will be completely null depending on how they decide to take the games following this one.Thus, based on what I've experienced, this is what I'd suggest Aquaplus does for the next installments:First and foremost, get a good translation team. I feel like all of their games have issues on this front no matter what.Edit: I take back what I said, drop Shiravune entirely from translating your games. Get a group that cares about actually translating without fiddling around too much with what's being said.Next, take some notes from other games or developers. In this case, I think that taking a look at Falcom's Eiyuu Densetsu series would do them well. If I'm completely honest, they were actually almost to that level in terms of that kind of presentation, but they fell short in a few aspects.Personally, I'd also say to take notes from Utawarerumono ZAN 2 in a few regards as well. I think that Tamsoft did pretty well with adapting what they did in those games.Obviously upping the visual quality is on the list, but it's not a 100% necessity for me. I'd just like the game to run at a consistent framerate.One extra thing I would add to that is having a slightly more extensive enemy glossary, both in the menu and one that you can do mid-battle to see the stats and type of enemy that you're fighting. Optionally, also a description. The mid-battle menu would could also possibly be optimized in a way akin to Persona 5 or Eiyuu Densetsu: Sen No Kiseki 3/4.I will hold my full thoughts on the story, as the ending seems like it will be leading directly into a follow up title, thus I'd like to see if any of my theories will be proven true, at least to some extent. Personally, I'm taking this as an alternate timeline to the mainline games with events that line up with the originals until the rest of the story unfolds. Still, it's a fun title going in for the story, just like the other games.I'm leaving a positive review in hopes that this is just a stepping stone for Aquaplus to keep doing what they're doing and improve on their shortcomings. I've seen what they can do before now, and knowing them, I hope that they'll take any criticism to heart and do better.Also please rerelease your older titles on Steam or an alternative platform. That would be nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial Review (~20h in):Great game for fans of the original Utawarerumono trilogy. Shunya is an excellent addition to the rest of the cast returning from the Mask games, and there are plenty of great moments with the ensemble cast. Some areas leave things to be desired though, especially the comically bad NPC models. Definitely worth picking up for fans of the Utawarerumono series.Revised Review (Story Completed):What I said above still holds true and for the first 10 chapters this is on balance a great game. However, a combination of factors led to my opinion flipping. Without spoiling any plot points, the final (11th) chapter opens countless questions and answers none of them, resulting in a thoroughly unsatisfying conclusion to the story so far. 'So far' because this is the most transparent hook in to a sequel I have ever seen. If you're likely to get invested in the story I'd suggest holding out on this until the likely sequel releases.My final impressions weren't helped by the complete lack of a new game+ mode. As a result if you're not careful you can effectively brick yourself from getting a complete set of achievements on a single save file quite easily, even if you're being careful to take care of new side-quests as they come up.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, where to start with this game? For starters, since it is this studio's first attempt at typical JRPG, I won't judge it too harshly on that front. However, I will criticize the story because it is the main selling point for this game. The story and characters were fairly good. There were comedic bits that honestly did bring a chuckle to me. Character interaction and their growth was done well I'd say, especially for Mikazuchi. Every character had something unique to bring to the table. Although the weakest link in the group would definitely be Oshtor. He does carry around the occasional snark but other than that, he seems like a typical upright MC that you could find in a multitude of other JRPGs. You could say that I expected a bit more from his character. The combat system was fairly simple to understand once you got the hang of it, but honestly I missed the old action rings. Learning the timings of the moves and pressing just at the right moment to make critical hits is something I wish this game could implement. Gameplay-wise, Shunya is both the weakest and the strongest. Her field attack being a projectile makes her supremely good for catching monsters off guard, but during combat most of her stronger skills are locked behind a wall which other characters don't have to go over. It's an interesting mechanic, but it needs to be thought over a little more. Game dungeons are linear and require little to no puzzle solving but I wish we were able to fast travel between checkpoints within the dungeons themselves. There's a lot of backtracking that can take place. The game UI is a little difficult to get used to. There's not really a great separator for consumables and most of the time you have to rely on rereading the effects to get an idea of what they can do and when they can be used. I do have to say though, a major HUGE gripe I had with this game was the localization. There were so many times where there was extra added lines and different meanings to multiple dialogues. The previous game had that issue as well, but they were not as abhorrent as the ones that occurred in this game. Adding lines to what it essentially just a single word changes who a character is. It brings about a contrast in a characters actions and their lines. Going down this road leads to context that gets cut out due to poor localization. Lines lose their meaning when translated one way only for it to appear different in another instance of the same line being used. It's especially bad when the localization team misses the point on certain lines entirely. Certain don't translate entirely well to English, but the attempts made here do a disservice to the actual lines said. I just wished the eased up on some of the localized lines and went for a more direct translation. With the oriental theme of this game, it makes sense for their to be sayings that an English-speaker wouldn't entirely get. But with enough repetition, the meanings become clearer.All in all, this is a decent attempt for the Utawarerumono series with a game outside their safe zone. If you're an Utawarerumono follower, you'll want to play this game just for the story. It ties in a lot of ideas that were brought up in the previous games. If this is your first look into the series, I suggest looking elsewhere. Don't get too disappointed that the game does not flow like usual JRPGs. I hope for more answers to the lore in future sequels.

_childDocuments_.review:
In the small province of Ennakamuy, on the frontiers of the great empire of Yamato, there lived a young man with his mother and sister. One day, at the local lord's behest, the young man was investigating a small irregularity when he encountered a girl he'd never met.

The words the girl spoke were what shocked him: She told the man that his father was still alive.

Seeing a trace of his father in her and resolving to learn the truth, the young man and the girl set out together towards the land of Arva Shulan - a country that doesn't appear on the map.

A new JRPG from veteran studio AQUAPLUS, commemorating 20 years of the multi-media Utawarerumono series. This is the story of a man who will be sung about in legends.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to reluctantly recommend this, but when I tried to list any coherent reasons why, I couldn't find any. This game is not for Valkyrie Profile fans.This game is not for JRPG fans.This game is arguably not even for action or slasher fans. And definitely not for people expecting a good story. This game is a proof of concept at best, using Valkyrie Profile as an asset box, borrowing the terms, setting and mechanics to re-imagine them poorly. Valkyrie Elysium reminds me of a "Yoko Taro tier" game without Yoko Taro. So basically a low budget, clunky, repetitive mess but without a bizarre story or fun characters. It feels hollow and having almost completed everything it has to offer - it unfortunately is. I hope it doesn't mean the death of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: The "Maybe This Will Be Cool And Unique" to "They should've just let tri-Ace make Valkyrie Profile 3..." PipelineThis story is not interesting. This combat has neither the depth of the turn-based Valkyrie games nor the fluidity and style of proper character-action games. It certainly doesn't approach the "best of both worlds" vibe that Scarlet Nexus and Tales of Arise do. It's just... neither this nor that. I think the most heartbreaking thing about Elysium is that unless you're just a very forgiving player or this happens to be 100% your jam, your most likely experience will be feeling just intrigued enough to keep playing, but just bored and frustrated enough that you'll regret it the entire time. It is so, so close to being good, at times it's even close to greatness. This game was phenomenal at making me believe that hey, maybe there's something here, maybe it'll get better, maybe if I keep giving it a chance, it'll impress me. 13 hours in, the unbelievably stiff and clunky combat never reached whatever heights this game hoped for when they chose to abandon the combat-system of earlier Valkyrie games. The story is so thin that it's nearly non-existent, and what little narrative does exist was for me, so excruciatingly boring, that I started mashing past all dialogue and skipping all cutscenes about five hours in, because I just could not bear it any more. This almost NEVER happens to me in games. Valkyrie Elysium has so many great ideas. The Elemental Break Gauge is really cool. The way different Einherjars are summoned and assist you feels like they almost got it right, and a lot of my Tales of Arise/Scarlet Nexus mental comparisons come from the inevitable reminder of those games' SAS/Boost systems that Einherjars give me. When you actually get to combo enemies in a way that feels satisfying, the impact of animations and spells does feel pretty decent. But none of that actually coalesces into a meaningful whole. It's just "God, I Wish This Was Good: The Videogame"I tried really hard to enjoy this game, I wanted to like it, I was excited for it and I waited for it to hit Steam. I'm sad.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is an interesting one. Big cult classic PS2/PS3 action game vibes, very divisive, certainly could have used more budget, some baffling decisions, but a genuinely very fun time for the right sort of player with the right expectations. Recommending it because there's a good game here, but you really need to know what you're getting into. Tl;dr: Fun, quite unconventional and obtuse character action game that takes more inspiration from Ninja Gaiden than say, Bayonetta, with a focus on technical play, several progressively harder difficulties from trivial to wtf. Nice ambient music from Motoi Sakuraba, an okay story that borrows from the older Valkyrie games as set dressing and you have to kinda go out of your way to find. Great bosses, a cool Vergil, and nice enemy designs/art style. Lackluster RPG elements like towns, side areas, etc. Lots of smaller QoL features that are missing and annoying. Hard to recommend at $60. $30-40 range much more worth it, especially as the game is on the shorter side, 15-25 hours depending on how much you do.Just want to expand on the gameplay since this is the game's biggest strength:Combat: Genuinely very good, but starts off feeling quite limited and shallow. As you progress you keep unlocking more and more abilities and weapon moves, and very quickly, within the first 3 levels or so it starts to feel a lot better. The devs are some of the ones who made the Itagaki-era Ninja Gaiden games (Black and 2), and you can feel it in the design philosophy. Large focus on numbers and waves of enemies, enemies dodge/block, counter, grab, can quickly stunlock you. Importance of crowd control. Restrictive animation cancelling, ninpo iframes, soft lock on, etc, even down to stuff like the Ultimate Techniques, obliteration techniques, flying swallow, are all in the game in spirit.As you go through the game you'll unlock several weapons and you can hotswap between 2 during combat. You'll also gain access to arts, which grant you a brief invuln, cancel animations, and can exploit enemy elemental weaknesses. You have a grappling hook, which can zip you to any enemy you can target, and acts as the building block of continued air combos and enables combo cancellation into weapon switching on the fly. You've got blocks/posture, perfect parries, perfect dodges, counterattacks, you've got the ability to sort of powerslide around enemies on your knees for extra mobility. There's a lot of really cool stuff here, not to mention the spirits you can summon for extra firepower (and that you can configure to autosummon when certain conditions are met, like perfect dodge etc.). I see some criticize the combat as either excessively shallow or too clunky for a character action game and I have to disagree. I think a lot of it comes down to how much the game does for you. When you play something like Nier Automata or DMCV or Bayo, it feels immediately fluid and has a low floor to being able to do fluid-feeling stuff. This game will let you do a lot of very fluid things, but you absolutely need to work for it, and figure out nuances that the game will give you no indication of, in terms of how it handles cancelling, priorities etc. It's sort of like how you might play Nioh as a slightly faster Dark Souls, but then you look at high level technical play and you have no clue how people make it look so sick. Same vibes. It's entirely possible the beat the game on lower difficulties by just pressing buttons or doing the same stuff over and over, but that's like almost every modern action game, and there's no fun in that. You can play it technically, but can also play it as a button masher.To that end, some tips for making things feel better:- You can't dodge cancel whenever, but you can dodge cancel the recovery animation of many swings. Afaik these aren't consistent across weapons, so you need to experiment.- Upgrading weapons unlocks more mobility features of those weapons. A big one is the slide. - You can guard to cancel recoveries which can let you combo faster or dodge faster.- Arts and grapple hook cancel basically everything (any recovery mostly) if you can use them. Arts grant iframes, grapple hook doesn't and leaves you exposed. Grapple hook lets you quickly switch weapons. In mid air then, you might keep your air combo varied between starting and various weapon combos, cancelling into grapple to maintain pressure while switching weapons, and evading other attacks with arts iframes back into grapple hook, stuff like that. You can absolutely lock down some bosses and enemies into infinite loops with the proper planning. Fun stuff.But the game absolutely wants you to experiment. It gives you an extensive dedicated training mode where you can configure many settings and fight any enemy, and while weapons will behave differently, and have different use cases, the move lists are generally similar in terms of inputs. Think Smash is to this game as SFV might be to Bayo or NG etc. So it's much more about learning how to piece your kit together and figuring out those nuances than learning how to do complicated inputs in a vacuum. Oh and there's a mini bloody palace and Vergil arcade mode when you beat the game.But yeah. Big PS2/PS3 vibes. Lots to love, lots to hate. Give it a shot on a modest to heavy sale. More than many games I've played this year this is the one I'd be most excited to see a sequel to, provided they give it a larger budget and sand down some of the rough edges. Feels like the best game the devs could make with a shoestring budget.

_childDocuments_.review: I ultimately can't recommend this game.I haven't played any of the previous entries from this IP so I'm coming in fresh here. I don't know how this is related to any of those games, nor how the style of gameplay differs. From what I’ve read only, this is a bit of a departure from the games that came before this one.1. FPS lock to 60 (can be fixed with Universal Unreal Engine 4 Unlocker thankfully)2. The story , until the middle of the game and then near the end of the game falls terribly flat.To expand on that some, I can tell there's an interesting story to be told, but they don't tell it effectively.2a. Most of the interesting tidbits about your Einherjars are stuck behind audio-only logs that show up in your inventory. Couple this with the fact that they could have done more here: having some simple animations, maybe a comic style something, or actual character model animations. This, honestly, was the most frustrating part of the game to me. I can’t tell if they ran into budget problems or what happened, but when asking for $60, I expect a lot more here. Just from a story delivery standpoint, this game should have cost $15 to $20 less.2b. The protagonist is very dry which can be excusable if there’s something else going on with that, but there's not enough to really take away from how boring her story is until you get about halfway through the game. Her lack of meaningful facial animations and her dull interactions with her Einherjar also isn't really helping. I understand how she came to be and of course she's going to be , but do something with that and have her be a sounding board for a more interesting character more often while she's running around.When listening to the protagonist throughout the course of the game, you see her become , but the problem is that it doesn’t feel natural. They basically must tell you, the player, that she’s becoming this way as she doesn’t have much for interactions with her Einherjars to have it feel natural.2c. In the event you're lucky enough and hear some chit-chat between characters, hopefully you don't hit a loading trigger and miss it. I guess you could just play through the level and get to that spot again, but that's kind of lame. Space this stuff out or design the level in such a way where that it can't happen.3. The combat feels bad, mostly early on. Everything is animation locked. It's like it wants to be an action game, but also not  much so the flow will feel bad until you get more abilities (which, incidentally, is also about halfway through the game). Unlocking skills shouldn’t take the game from feeling bad to acceptable. It should take it from feeling at least decent to great if you master it. For too long of the playthrough, I felt crippled by the stiff feeling of swinging/thrusting my weapons.4. Sometimes I found myself fighting either the camera or the particle effects. This happened more often with the former than the latter, mostly because if there were that many particle effects, chances are that I at least had i-frames. Instead of the camera moving out of the way, sometimes it would simply crunch up right next to the wall, making things hard to deal with especially if I happened to have an enemy or two next to me preventing me from repositioning.5. The price you get for the aforementioned doesn’t make sense. There’s a lack of quality here that $60 doesn’t justify. In a world where publishers and developers are starting to ask for $70 for games, we must start saying “no, this isn’t acceptable.” Luckily, I bought it discounted so my buyer’s remorse isn’t too bad.6. Minor: difficulty achievements that require multiple playthroughs even if you beat the game on the hardest difficulty. That’s just a minor gripe of mine, but one that will waste time for achievement hunters for no good reason. Cascade those, please.1. After unlocking enough skills and combos the combat starts to feel a little better. You can shoot off more magic and more often as well as have longer combo chains which helps distract you from the lack of animation-cancelling abilities.2. The ending was . There are multiple endings to find, and what I’ll consider the good ending is worth working towards.3. Seemingly nothing is missable. There’s a chapter select so you can always revisit a level if you missed something and there’s counters on the map screen that tell you certain things you missed (except for chests).------For $60 this is a pass. I recommend one of the following action RPGs instead just off the top of my head:- Tales of Arise (better feeling combat and story)- Ys IX (better feeling combat and story)- Asterigos: Curse of the Stars (better feeling combat and story)- Trials of Mana (better feeling combat)
