_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure if Soleil realizes it, but they've made a Drakengard game (Likeness more specifically to 3, but Valkyrie Elysium runs far better than that PS3 exclusive)The crux of this game involves:- Running and fighting through hallways - sometimes open spaces - while following an objective marker (go here, kill this, find that)- Fighting enemies alongside computer controlled party members that you can forget about (for the most part)- Being able to switch between two weapons (that you can assign/reassign at any time) on the fly, with their own unique movelist and depth (Of note: each weapon requiring upgrades to unlock more of their moveset, also akin to Drakengard)- Mission based story progression- Sidequests in the form of replaying/backtracking through previously played maps While technically there is more depth to combat than that (such as enemies having weapon weaknesses and/or elemental weaknesses, special moves/spells you can cast all with their own unique properties, a skill tree system where Valkyrie gains more moves and attributes)...The majority of your time with this game will very much feel like playing Drakengard. Lots of fighting, leveling up your weapons, with the occasional spectacle boss fight (or story cutscene) sprinkled inbetween. Everything minus the dragon combat, that is.If this style of hack'n'slash pacing is familiar to you, then Valkyrie Elyisum should be bearable enough.If you're a longtime fan of Valkyrie Profile (VP:Lenneth PSX/PSP, or VP:Silmeria PS2), consider buying this game only if it's on sale. For such a niche title, gameplay loop, AND style of presentation (hence the Drakengard comparison), it is hardly worth the full price that Valkyrie Elysium is asking of you, given how dated it is despite being a game that came out in 2022. I consider this unfortunate, as Soleil does deserve praise for what they have accomplished here: the game is solid, straightforward, simple, and delivers on its premise (a Valkyrie Profile reboot). However, it is definitely not worth the 60$ triple A price tag(That might be on Square Enix as publisher, but what do I know)

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure whether to buy this game or not, having seen the lukewarm reviews as a fan of the previous Valkyrie Profile games. In the end I did in a sale, and although not life-changing, I definitely feel it is worth the time I put into it. It was fun and great for winding down at the end of the day.Things I liked: - The story.- The exploration factor (finding the flowers which gave snippets of thoughts from the souls they belonged to, and the mysterious Verdant ones as well, which pay off if you get them all). The game rewards you for exploring, which I appreciated.- The art style. I see comments about the graininess in the background, but this further served my nostalgia, as it is reminiscent of the graphics in the older game(s). I liked the designs of the characters and their expressions.- The voice acting. The English dub is super.Things I didn't like:- I found some aspects of the battles a bit clunky, such as switching between the weapons in my quick slots being a bit slow, and needing to go into the menu mid battle to switch to more effective weapons against the particular monsters I was fighting.- Being unable to change difficulty after initially picking it at the beginning.- Repeating entire levels if I missed an item. _childDocuments_.review: The Good:- I'm just glad that the Valkyrie franchise isn't dead.  And hopefully this isn't the end of it.- I really like how they brought back the stories of the einherjar like the first game.  In the second and third, the einherjar had basically no backstory or plot, and was one the things I found most interesting about the original game.  The mechanic were you learn about them while you are searching for them is really cool.  I'm just kind of sad how few there are in the game.  But in the future, more of this.- Overall, combat was mostly enjoyable, there are some issues, which I cover in the bad, but for the most party, it's generally good.  A bit button mashy, as you aren't really using certain moves for certain scenarios, you just kind of throw out whatever seems to work.  But between that and spells with summons, it's a decent package.The Bad:- The game wouldn't play nice with my PS4 controller, and wouldn't even recognize the button inputs using generic numbers.  I had to pull out a busted 360 controller with a pretty heavy dead zone to even play the game.  Like I know it's 2022 and it's only a small developer like Square Enix, but I don't think it's too much to ask to have support for PS4 controllers lik 95% of the rest of the games on steam.- The constant and repetitive remarks during and after combat got old so quick.  Not to mention they weren't even appropriate at times.  I can't tell you how many times I've heard "A FEARSOME FOE" to a random group of trash mobs.- The camera would go nuts if you end up fighting someone against a wall or in a corner, and it happens a lot.-I hate that they use the combo meter from the past games, but filling it doesn't give you access to chain together super cool special moves.  In fact the combo meter does basically nothing at all in this game but count.  Nibelung Valesti just becomes a spell that costs far too much to cast at the end of the game.  Also, you can't swap weapons unless you are basically holding perfectly still.  In DMC, you can buffer the input, and the swap would happen between hits, but in this game, it just eats the input.  It became very annoying trying to swap weapons mid-combat.- Sometimes you have to be far too particular about how you interact with an object using L1.  Like, you can be standing right next to a save point or chest, but you'll only use your grappling move until you move the camera to a point it's happy with. The prompt will even be on screen and you'll still just throw out your grapple move.- The game had a lot of reused assets, like rooms that were just copy paste, and one part that really stuck out to me was when getting Cyper when everything was supposed to be frozen.  All the objects weren't encased in ice and it really just kind of stuck with stuff like green plants in this frozen world.  Or like, here's the same giant foutain for a 3rd time, broken exactly like the last two were.- For some stupid ass reason, all stat up items like max health, soul, and arts are not applied when you recieve them.  Instead they are added to your inventory and have to be used.  I didn't realize this until the final fight of the game.  I can not understand for the life of me why it is this way.  Truly baffling.- More time than I could count, attacks, even when locked on to enemies and right next to an enemy, will send you sailing past them as your flourish of attacks hit nothing.- When it comes to exploiting weaknesses, the autosummon mechanic (which should be one of the coolest features in the game) gets in the way of itself.  You generally want to summon the einherjar that the enemies are weak to, but also buffs your attacks with that same element.  But autosummon temporarily removes that element with the autosummon's.  So it's just constantly removing the buff that enemies are weak to.  Not to mention you still have to pay soul bar for autosummons.  I just eventually turned them all off.- The way drops work, everything thing in the tree is progress gated.  It's not like in other games this wants to be like, say Devil May Cry or God of War where you can just keep upgrading everything you want unil you are out of experience.  In this, you are hard-stopped in your trees till you get to a level that drops the new type of materials.  And insultingly, you will need thousands of each, but some can be found in chests in groups as low as 10, which isn't helpful in the least.  I particularly remember a dead end room with four waves of enemies that gave a chest with 20 silver. -_--Also what they call a "puzzle" is insulting.  Like there's a breakable wall that you need to break with one of your einherjar.  That's it.  It's the same as just opening up a new way in a metroidvania.  But to further the insult, it gives you the tutorial every time you approach a new one.  And even when one you've seen before, the person who can open it always says something out loud.  And a lot of the time locked doors will have their key in a chest just a few feet away.  Like, does this really pass as level design and puzzles these days?- Other nitpicks are: Can't dash through breakables. Can't pause cutscenes. Enemies and bosses breaking the target lock constantly with movement quickly or teleporting. No ranged options and situations where you really could use them. Glitches like einherjar stuck in walls, enemies stuck beyond the blocked off fighting area. There's a stat slotting system for the weapons, but you only ever get a single slot the whole game when it really looks like you're going to get more as you level the weapons.  You only get a second at max level.The Ugly:I see a lot of reviews saying not to compare this Valkyrie game with other Valkyrie game.  Which, first of all sounds ridiculous, but second of all, I don't know if all these people even played all three of the previous games, but they are ALL quite different from one another.  Hell, 3 was a tactical RPG.  Even before I bought the game, I was watching a streamer almost seemingly angry that people were reviewing the game poorly and basically talking down to them for expecting a Valkyrie title from... a Valkyrie game.  But even if it wasn't, there are still far too many issues to still find this game acceptable, specially with a $60 price tag.  It is perfectly fair to compare this to others in the franchise because it IS part of the franchise.  A franchise which I love.  And I know it can be better than this, and I hope in the future it'll have that opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: Valkyrie Elysium could have been one of the finest character action games in years. All the parts are there. An experienced team, strong fundamentals, good art, good enemy variety, good music, mostly good bosses, nice defensive and offensive options and variety...However it fumbled the last and most important 20%. The design is schizophrenic, Squeenix wanted an RPG but Soleil makes character action. So enemy HP is bloated because you have pointless stat upgrades for your weapons. Enemies all have elemental weaknesses that can apply 10 second stuns on break so all your magic is used only to secure those breaks and not for style or damage because the resource is too precious and the breaks too useful. Enemy HP is bloated even further to make sure they can outlast ten seconds of free combos with 2 or 3 summoned NPC allies also beating on them. The game lasts about twice as long as it should and the fights about three times as long as they should and by the end you are locked in dozens of tiny closets with giant HP sponge monsters that reduce a great combat system to an unpleasant mess. A bunch of talent wasted by stumbling over the parts of game design you cannot really afford to botch

_childDocuments_.review: The game is mediocre at best. Not worth full price and for what it is and wouldn't really pay sale price either. If you came for the IP then you won't enjoy the game. Most of the staples from the IP have been removed and the game has been turned into a action game with some minor RPG elements. What was once and intuitive RPG is now a Devil May Cry Reskin. Game is also incredibly short being able to finish causally within 20 hours.With the systems in place the game comes off much like the PS2 action RPG Chaos Legion. Where you run thru a linear map fighting bad guys as fast you can to get your letter grade at the end. The Letter grade based on skills, spells, items used, time elapsed, damage taken, and dodges made. There is no real level up system anymore just collect resources to enhance which is basically a staple in Action games.  Einherjiar are the only thing that make the story and plot some what enjoyable. Due to the Protag and "god" coming off as Machines in how they talk and look at the world. But in most cases the Einherjiar get pushed to the side story wise. There is no real Puzzles or Platforming either which was a staple in both previous games for dungeons. The closest thing you get is a "Barrier" that is opened by using one of the Einherjiar. Which is really sad considering they don't appear often and are really just a animation lock to keep moving down the linear path of the stage. Story as a whole is kind of wonky. With its plot twists just being dumped on you nearly immediately with no real build up.  There are far better action games that do what this game does better. The game trys to add some platforming and puzzles but they are very basic (Jump on the rafts to cross the river) or have little to no challenge (Use this Einherjiar to open the path). Again other games do it far better. Combat is a bit slow and clunky and if you played other action games you'll probably be upset with the slow/little response you get with the dodge and parry mechanics. This gets more fluid as you upgrade your "skills". This however is more of a demerit as it seems pointless to hide mechanics to help make the game more enjoyable. Like why is "Quick Perry" or "Quick Evade" a skill. I really is just a unlock able QoL for the combat which should be base kit. Another issue is the visual grain contrast between the world and characters. You'll notice character will appear more clear than the world as the walk thru it. So much so they leave a visual outline separating them from the world. Not sure if its an artistic choice and deliberate. But apparently there are mods out there to fix it too. So sadly if you came here due to it being an action game I wouldn't recommend it. If you came here for the IP, I can't recommend it. If you came for an RPG, Its not one so I can't recommend it. If your here for story it can't be recommended. If the lack of a local arcade is what you want I could recommend this as that is what it most feels like. A game thats decent enough to dump a couple quarters in. Not the price tag they have on it. *Personal opinion and Spoilers*On a personal note I'm not sure why Square is trying so hard to make all its IP's into a FF15 simulator. Its starting to feel like they want to be cheap and have the same system for all IP's just so they don't have to custom code for each IP's unique mechanics. Its great they are trying to use the older IPs but sad that they don't want to keep what made them special.  This one also had its original IP story basically ripped and summarized with very few/minor changes. I'm not sure why they didn't just create a whole new story. With all the directional and design changes this legit has nothing to do with the Original Franchise. It very much is a nostalgia cash grab from a once prestigious RPG company but much like the presidents constant letters about NFTs Square is slowly just showing it no different than many of the other cash grab companies. Willing to tug at heartstrings and memories to make a quick buck. A further note I have completed the game. My opinions still stand. Even the multiple endings of  this game are poor. The "True" ending which is simple to get if you  just keep an eye out for the little plants just lead to an ending that is super similar to the "Bad" Ending expect you run away leaving someone else in charge. You kill the beast who wanted to dethrone Odin, Then kill odin yourself and rather then fill the power vacuum and put the world on a path of rebuilding you leave the gods to pursue a life with your forgotten lover. Luckily all isn't lost cause your rival Valkyrie will take the helm while you indulge yourself. The True ending feels weird. I'm just overall Disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really, really wanted this game to be good. It's not. I kept thinking to myself that eventually if I played long enough, that something would change, that the plot would become interesting, that the gameplay would evolve, that the voice acting and music would get better, that the environments would become interesting. Nothing improves or really changes. It's the same throughout, from the tutorial (why are there two btw?) onwards. Everything about this game is bland, even without looking to the previous titles, it just feels like a bland amalgamation of modern RPGs- it's enjoyable enough, just utterly forgettable. And then you get to the post-game DLC. Hilde mode has you go through the game backwards, but with no dialog, plot or fun, until you eventually beat the final boss , and fly off into the sunset, without a single word. I suppose it's like Vegil mode in DMC, if Vegil was boring, unfun to play, and again, offered no new gameplay.Seraphic gate is... Bloody palace from DMC but worse. I was so hoping that this would introduce some fun elements to the gameplay, cool cameos, callbacks to previous games, or something interesting, but sadly not.I want to lie and say the game is good, so that there's a better chance of the older games getting ports, but I can't, it's just not a very good game. _childDocuments_.review: Valkyrie Elysium was truthfully my most anticipated game of the year. Being a huge fan of Medieval and Norse Mythology, I pre-ordered the game months before and rarely found myself as excited for Valkyrie Elysium. It was regrettably this same expectation that blinded me to the true premise of the game and robbed me a fair amount of enjoyment for the title.Final Fantasy has always been my favorite in the fantasy genre, and I wanted a return to roots of an immersive fantasy medieval open-world RPG with magic, angels, and divine beings. However, instead, what awaited me in Valkyrie Elysium was an instance-based dungeon system with repetitive gameplay loops. You start in a hub, interact with a globe to do quests, and finish whatever objectives you have before you return and repeat. The combat is fairly challenging, but I wasn't able to appreciate the Einjerhar system as it dampens the immersion. Einjerhar supposedly translates to "army of one" or "those who fight alone", but it's probably referring to the people you spam summon and not you.Progression is standard and the plot is predictable. The environment is okay with some stylized harsh toon shader outlines, but the character models themselves were quite disappointing, especially Valkyrie whose character model felt far from the tall and valiant beauty she was portrayed to be. There are several collectibles to be found throughout the game with some lore text, but personally I wished more effort was spent translating these bits and pieces into actual visual and auditory experiences instead.The voice acting was great and the combat was pretty fun. Apart from the starting cutscene and missing tutorial videos, the game runs flawlessly at a stable 30 fps with high settings on the Steam Deck. It was unfortunate that half the reasons I didn't enjoy the game were mostly due to unrealistic expectations, but it is undeniable that Square Enix seems to be involving themselves in more and more projects with the quality of individual titles spreading thinner and thinner. It's a decent title but not what I had hoped for.

_childDocuments_.review: The evolution of a signature battle system can be seen being refined from VALKYRIE PROFILE: LENNETH to , a signature tri-Ace game that released in 2010 in which the world does not move unless the player issues commands. VALKYRIE ELYSIUM attempts to  the series in the 3D space it concerns itself with by homogenizing yet another unique battle system. Logically, it should have attempted to build upon the strong foundation the prequel to Lenneth set in VALKYRIE PROFILE 2: SILMERIA as it has become synonymous with the gameplay of the mainline series. It has earned this association through vestigial commonalities with . However, bodies such as Soleil Ltd. would have had no such obligation. Instead, Soleil Ltd. implementing the simple ability to break enemy body parts for rewards as seen in Silmeria and  was struck in favor of a generic battle system without playable party members that inadvertently demeans the authorial attention to meticulousness in the original games by either its visible laziness or ineptitude in execution.  Otherwise, reluctant disparagements like these will arise—and they will be naught but In this era, some developers lack respect for source material  that it becomes evident upon consumption of their product that they may not have played or researched more than one entry in the series they have been charged with breathing life into. They ride on the shoulders of giants while failing to revere the very greatness of the ground their feet find themselves upon. The natural result of such mishandling will be soulless abominations like Elysium.Elysium attempts to associate itself with tri-Ace games through . Hold fast, for these are efforts to validate itself in order to gain your patronage. It  misappropriates story beats alongside other elements from Lenneth’s game and grafts them onto itself as afterthoughts while displaying a  understanding of the source material. Players are bombarded with farcical vignettes in a predictable and weak narrative. Listless combat is padded by rudimentary, reused and lifeless maps intended to artificially extend playtime. Arbitrary feature sliders betray bad designs that cannot be remedied by changing the targeted parameter. In short, there is no innovation or redemption to be found in Elysium’s decisions. It is hard to find justification for Elysium to simply exist. Therefore, its “callbacks” and “references” emerge as hollow and unwarranted. They amount closer to belittlement as Elysium’s entire presentation belies This leads to the plot that was lifted as a clear point of interest for players who have not played Lenneth; it is a lesser parallel of Lenneth’s narrative that will most likely fail to earn the dedicated intrigue of any new players, let alone fans of tri-Ace. If you have a genuine interest and curiosity for this series, then we implore you to explore the games of the not-so-distant past instead of this apathetic rehash of a cult classic. Not only is the entropy of storytelling apparent, but strong characters as well. The original Valkyrie Profile had 25 party members,  Valkyrie Profile 2 had 50 party members,  and even Covenant of the Plume, an isometric pixel game, had  controllable party members. To go beyond the VALKYRIE games, RADIATA STORIES, a beloved tri-Ace PS2 game with a lively fanbase, had . In juxtaposition,  has 3 main playable characters in a cast of 17. This contrast shows tri-Ace’s range in ability by contextualizing versatile, expertly-voiced and memorable characters in the face of the derivative stories that are seen today; its scale and magnitude towers over baser stories told by those without passion.A story is driven by characters and their ability to sow drama. Developing an original story  is a challenge that can produce a unique homage if done seriously. However, it should be obvious that it is hard to forge a signature in a pre-existing franchise without an enthusiastic, inspired attitude and resources. With Elysium, this feeling is present universally and many remain unimpressed with the benighted world and its characters. In order to have created a more worthy successor, the deciding power brokers would have had to gatekeep the privilege of creating "the latest title in the VALKYRIE series" as hard as how VALKYRIE PROFILE: LENNETH Unfortunately, the mobile game VALKYRIE ANATOMIA lasted for at least one year and three months, culminating into the eventual subversion seen today. There had not been a mainline VALKYRIE game for  years. Why even  using the likeness?It is  game that could have been made under an entirely new intellectual property—but was not. The property’s fate was handed to a Tencent-acquired company that had little-to-no understanding of the established, esoteric nature of the VALKYRIE series.  I pray that some talented souls will one day create a true spiritual successor to Lenneth. It is painful to watch such a uniquely beloved series be mishandled as such. Owing to the decision to unashamedly derive a multitude of elements from a game not forgotten and failing spectacularly in doing so, any praise and interest for Elysium will eventually shift towards the progenitor—VALKYRIE PROFILE: LENNETH. After all, they were bundled together to show the vast difference in sophistication.This is declared in rejection of such borrowed inheritance.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult one as not all is bad, I was 50/50 on wether I should recommend it or not but the overall package is simply to lacking for me to recommend it.As I said not all is bad, there is actually some great parts here.The voice acters are great,.The music is good.The character design is for the most part good.The characters feels like they have a background.Sadly the negatives outweigh the positives, and to list them.The game lacks in exploration to the point where as you are looking for something it is easy as you just follow the path.The visuals while not horrible is not good.Combat while entertaining for a few hours does wear on you and at the end of a rather short game I was tired of it. Combat also becomes way to flashy and busy visuals to the point that is was difficult to see what was going on.The variation of weapons are not good, sure the different spears and swords act different but overall.Calling on your companions is also nice but turns into a way to counter <insert color> enemy.The last boss is annoying, not difficult just annoying. It is however at a point that you can feel there is something great there, that there are things they missed on.What I mean by that is that while the characters have dept that is not explored, while they open the door for something deeper and interesting they just keep that door open but never ever do we go through. The story could have gone into such interesting places but it never does it just teases about it.The combat could also have been much better, more different weapons, more party members to switch between, more combos to unlock, more things to unlock.The maps could have been bigger and more open for exploration.It is just so annoying since there are good ideas there, they have great voice acters. _childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer, I'm reviewing the game after playing up to Chapter 7 in Valkyrie difficulty. TLDR: Do not recommend if you enjoy action games, you'll find a lot of flaws. 5/10 passing score.I've played a few action games such as Sekiro, DMC3, DMC4, DMC5 and this game just can't even compare to those games in terms of combat.Here are some downfalls to the game with what I've experienced so far.1. Lack of monster diversity. You're going to be fighting the same monsters with a twist, each monster will have several different elements which general doesn't change much of their mechanics. So far I've seen 11 monsters (excluding bosses) and they all have 3-4 different elements. By chapter 7 you'll notice a pattern where the game is just adding more numbers and you end up being zergged and dying to a combination my complains below, which are camera angles, lock on system and animation locking.2. The lock on system is trash. You have to toggle R3 (on controller) and then change targets using R3 directional. If your camera angle is in a bad position (next to he wall) you cannot change it unless you untarget the monster, then use R3 direction to move the camera. If you retarget the monster after readjusting the camera angle, there's a chance the camera moves back to the previous crappy angle you had resulting in you dying to something you can't see.3. You cannot dodge while in attack animation. This was a big gripe for me and it just defeats the whole purpose of an action game. You will be stuck in an attack animation and you see a monster charging an attack and you can't dodge. You can somewhat play around this with Divine Arts cancel which provides about 2 seconds of invincibility frames. But if you're out of your arts gauge, you're screwed.4. You cannot switch weapons mid combo. By Chapter 6 you'll have 5 weapons in your arsenal. You can only equip 2 at a time and can change the loadout during combat. However you cannot swap a weapon in mid combo until an attack animation is complete. This just feels like a bad design choice and limits the players choice of attacks and overall making the game feel terrible. An upside is that the animations look great so you have plenty of time admiring your attacks while a monster is about to hit you.5. The checkpoint system. If you die, which is fairly often in Valkyrie mode, you will spawn back in your previous checkpoint. If you upgraded your weapons or reconfigured your arts, there's a high chance that they were reset too. You will then have to do all the upgrades again and reconfigure your arts for the first encounter. There may be a way around this by walking a big circle in your explored areas and back into the checkpoint. I have not tested this but it worked a few times for me. They could have added an option to load from save.6. Menu menu menu. Constantly in the menu re-configuring your arts for element advantage. The game will change the element for each encounter which forces you to go into the menu and reconfigure your arts. This is just annoying in harder difficulties, because when you die often and you will have to go through the re-configuration process all over again from your previous checkpoint.7. Lack of characters?By chapter 6 you'll have 3 summons to choose from, and met a handful NPCs. The NPCs are Odin himself, Hilda, some child I do not remember the name of (apparently he is important from the logs page), a villager that provides a subquest and a few interactions with people in a house that you can't even get in. I get that the world is ending due to Ragnarok, but it hasn't ended yet, so why is there no one alive? The game feels like an arcade game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this as a person who loves VP that has played the original multiple times. I'd suggest just playing the original version on PS1, this game won't really make complete sense unless you've played the original (or give you the sense of nostalgia that it tries to sprinkle throughout). If you happen to enjoy the original, then you'd probably like this game. However, this game doesn't really hold up in terms of having relatable characters you can attach yourselves to, which is a huge selling point for the OG. There's a ton of flaws compared to the original. The things we loved about VP: the lovable characters, Valkyrie's character development, and just overall good story telling altogether; this game doesn't even hold a candle to that. I won't say I'm disappointed overall though, since I still think this game is a nice homage to the masterpiece we all know. Music is pretty reminiscent of the OG at times, sometimes I'd feel as if I'm walking back and forth through Artolia again lol. As a huge Street Fighter fan (fighting game fan in general), this game is really fun. The comboing system is right up my alley, which ultimately saves this game for me. If you enjoy fighting games and learning enemy battle mechanics, then this game can be right for you. Otherwise, there really isn't a reason you'd play this cause you'd probably be very upset with the uninspired story. I have yet to complete it, but with 16 hours in, I think I get the gist of what this game has to offer. This game had the potential to be good, but in all honesty, the lackluster storytelling makes the experience pretty dull. I will say that I'm still having an immense amount of fun though. It's not a bad game per se, just horrible execution story/world building wise. I started my first playthrough on Valkyrie (hardest) difficulty, so if anything, I'm enjoying the challenging battles at the very least.Still waiting on Nurse Joy's reappearance, let's hope there's a future for this franchise."Come to me dark warriors, battle awaits us!"

_childDocuments_.review: : I completed Valkyrie Elysium on the hardest difficulty 'Valkyrie', so my thoughts are based on how the game feels to play on that difficulty. It's possible you can get  enjoyment if you lower the difficulty, but I found the game to be either too easy or too hard.So with that said...I'm a sucker for action games with JRPG art design and when I heard this game had some Team Ninja people behind it, I wanted to atleast try it. Now onto my review...: The hard mode is too easy, the Valkyrie (hardest) mode is one of the most frustrating experiences I've ever had in gaming. The only way to beat this game on Valkyrie is by abusing the summon system and praying to the RNG gods that the enemies attack your summons and not you. Every enemy is a bullet sponge on steroids that can two-shot you at any moment. The amount of times I died because my character got knocked onto the ground or the camera obscured my vision was insane. The final boss is one of the most god-awful encounters I've come across in a game and as I was wiping to him repeatedly I was legitimately Googling if anyone had beat him on Valkyrie since there is a way to "finish" the game by talking to an NPC bypassing the boss.: There are two gamebreaking bugs I can't look past - both of which can and will result in softlocks. One is the checkpoint system is broken, meaning, if you kill an elite enemy and it drops health/soul gauge, and you die on the NEXT wave of enemies, if you load that checkpoint, it doesn't remember you picked up the health/soul gauge from before. This can be the difference between clearing a section and reaching the next save point or not. You also have to reopen every chest & break every box/barrel each time you die. The second bug is enemies get stuck on objects and you can't target them while the area is blocked off. This happened several times in my playthrough. If you're on Valkyrie difficulty, you're desperately trying to get to the next save point at all times, and the last thing you need in an unbalanced mode like this is the game fighting against you.: The story is some of the most uninspired schlop you'll come across up until the last chapter where it gets slightly interesting. By that point, it's too little too late.: It runs on an elemental stagger system which can be satisfying to stun a horde of enemies but the lack of animation cancelling kills the combat system. On the highest difficulty, you're committing suicide by trying full combos because you get locked into a long animation leaving yourself open to getting two-shot by any enemy. The hit detection is questionable at best, especially when you're fighting the oversized bosses. One more nitpick:  There are waves of enemies every 10 meters and there are so many times where I wanted the game to just let me walk around and explore the environment and catch my breath. By the end of the game I was so happy to be done with it.I cannot recommend this game, even if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: First off as a fairly casual hack and slash player, I am really liking this game so far. The combat is pretty intense and its definitely no face roll. The bosses and sub-bosses can be particularly nasty, till you figure out their vulnerabilities. Valkyrie reminds me of Vindictus when Vindi was good. The Mobs are dangerous as they should be, without being ridiculous and that is a huge plus for me. In chapter two you find your first "Einherjar" allly, the Soul of a dead warrior, who you can summon to aid you in battle. Believe me you will be happy to have him at your side soon enough.The game is very story driven, a big minus for me most of the time, but the story is pretty well written and the voice acting is very good, so in this particular game I find myself listening to all the dialog, and not skipping scenes.I do wish it were easier, smoother to change spells before a battle, as sometimes it is vital to have the right spells equipped, and the system is a bit awkward and counter intuitive; but there are limits to what one can do without a full keyboard. There is a good bit of map checking as well, if you just follow the beaten path you'll miss a lot of your power ups and you will want them later, so that rather breaks the game flow and the immersion. In the same vein, you will want to pick up your subquests.., "In most role-playing games, deviating from the story's main path may lead to optional content — sidequests — that can then be completed for a reward. It's not so much that Valkyrie Elysium rewrites the book on this approach; rather, it does them in a somewhat obtuse way that can trick first-time players into inadvertently skipping these sidequests entirely." ~ The  While it definately breaks the narrative flow of the game to stop between Chapters and do subquests, they are necessary to level your weapons, and Einherjar allies; again something that is more important than the game makes clear on it's own. I had to visit 3rd Party sites to figure out why my party seemed so underpowered. Now you know. The game art is pretty stylized, but I find I prefer it that way, "Realistic" game art looks old in just a few years, and IMHO Valk will still look good say 5 years from now.You may have trouble finding the main menu. If you are directed to the + button, but don't have one that is for an Xbox, on a PS Controller try the options button; that is where I found the menu. The Devs definately should have been more clear on this point; as I have found this question in several online forums, usually unanwsered. Valk, is a Play Station Port so you will want to use a controller. In my own experiance, controller support has been iffy, sometimes I have to toggle steam enabling 2 or 3 times before the game responds to my controller, but that is really the biggest bug I have encountered, and the gameplay has been so worth it. Ultimately even with a few warts, if you play games to fight Uglies, Valkyrie Elysium is well worth your time, and your dime.

_childDocuments_.review: Slow start, but it gets better eventually. If beautiful female protagonist is enough to keep you motivated until the game becomes good, I can highly recommend.The difficulties feel just right for me, but I don't like how the Valkyrie difficulty completion achievement doesn't count towards normal and hard completion achievements, which is usually the case for other games. So to get all the achievements it seems like a player needs to play through the game at least 3 times. From what I can gather, there's no NG+ where we start from the beginning and re-select the difficulty either. Combat is fun. In the early stage it feels quite limited what the character can do, but we do eventually unlock skills and actions and make it not clunky. Animations are beautiful. All of the weapons except one for me are all fun to use.Hilde's Vengeance lets us play as Hilde but we can never use her in the main game, which is a pity, as she is super fun to play.Seraphic's Gate mode is nice enough I guess. I prefer a smoother experience.The Japanese voice of this game is absolutely amazing. _childDocuments_.review: played on hard mode, did every side quest and collected every itemtl:dr - 4/10, not worth it without a good discount, even less so if you're a vp fanit tried to be a unique action rpg maintaining the originality of the older vp games, but ended up feeling generic as an action rpg, and like it abandoned too much of what made vp games funthings i like about the game-plenty of different spells to use, even if a lot of them are just different levels of the same spell-using a part of the original vp music in the fourth area, very nostalgic-chaining through fights can easily get the counter up to 999, which is always satisfying to see-has a hookshot mechanic that makes getting to enemies relatively easy-a handful of interesting character interactions, but definitely not enough-almost forgot, one kinda sorta trans characterthings i don't care about the game, but aren't really bad-only 6 weapons, wish there was one more that was sort of the ultimate weapon-skill tree is kinda bland and very linear-you'll go through some big fights just for a chest with a small amount of resources that you got a ton of from the fight itself-mouse/keyboard default controls have spells and summons both tied to the movement keys-einherjar have a limit to how strong they can get, which i hit really early on-only equipment is weapons and the runes, which aren't really that fun to use, as they're mostly offense/defense buffs which don't feel like they make any difference-the valkyrie's development goes from bland as a wet slice of bread, to a dry slice of bread, to a bit of a lightly toasted slice of bread. she's supposed to start bland, but i feel it didn't go into the development enough-enemy list is mostly reskins of like 10 monsters give or take. -it takes too long to get your first einherjar. the tutorial gives you 2, but it takes roughly 2 hours to get your first one afterwords.-summoning einherjar only lasts a set amount of time, between 15 to 60 seconds, but there's no timer for it-environmental puzzles feel very forced and in your face, nothing's really hidden-no arngrim :(things i really don't like about the game-all the weapons have the same stats. the staff that says it's good for magic has the same attack and magic as the heavy spear that's great for sweeping attacks. -keys are always around the corner, several locked doors and stuff will have the key just right next to them, sometimes no fights needed-no recovery from getting hit, you get knocked out of the air or smacked to the ground, it's so slow to get back up-only 4 einherjar, the game kinda vaguely puts things that make it seem like there would be more, but there aren't-earth elemental magic has one whole spell that nothing is actually weak to, it's just to gather enemies, while there's another spell that does the exact same thing-healing and items have a very limiting max for carrying, you get plenty early on but not much later on, especially smaller healing items, which could easily be fixed by having the one npc you meet offer to sell you items for the tons of gems you collect. he literally talks about collecting and delivering supplies and meds for people. just not you.-all the characters pose like they're idling npcs, standing around and not looking at one another during dialogue scenes, and the mouths never match what they're saying, even in the cutscenes-there's a lot of places early on to fall off the map which deals roughly 25% of your hp, and you sometimes keep your momentum and it sends you off again, might be a bug but i've died to this twice-second area is extremely laggy, had to go down to medium graphics settings and still had some choppy moments-big enemies will body you into a corner and beat down on you, and enemies can also combo you really easily. had several moments of going from full to dead without being able to do a single thing about it.-final boss(es) teleport way too much. one doing so almost constantly. also some fights have the enemy nearly always constantly ignoring your attacks with immunity frames. it's not fun when dark souls does it, it's not fun when this game does it, it's not fun when any game does it-the collection page is so barren, for most of the game you'll only have 1  person under important characters despite there being a whopping 4 (3 by the game's count). which is another issue, so-the game feels so empty. you'll find a handful of souls and flowers that tell you some thoughts from people in the past, but all the gods are also gone. valhalla is pretty big, but empty for most of the game. you get a couple people around, but even then they're only in a small part of the map.-lots of animation locks. when you cast magic, you're invincible for those frames, but not when you're summoning, or during most attackspersonal peeves as a vp fan-einherjar feel really bland to use, it's nice they're doing their own thing, but when the previous games all had them with soul crushes, really big, flashy, fun moves to use, it's disappointing when the final move you unlock for them is just a move you have, or just a really basic attack. especially when each one has their own thing they do during a specific set of side quests-seraphic gate feels like a super waste of time that doesn't introduce any new enemies, it's only reward is the final form of a move which is mostly just a trophy-odin is written like a toxic manager, he comes off as so lazy and obnoxious, which i get is sorta the point, but he doesn't act at all like the leader of the gods-it doesn't have any iconic valkyrie profile characters (or really any characters at all)-again, no arngrim

_childDocuments_.review: The story is not bad.Just one problem that it is unfinished, the whole game. It feels like they couldn't make it in time so they cut like 40% of it and slap on something presentable with a premium $60 price tag, the audacity square. $20 is already burglary. _childDocuments_.review: When this game was announced I was very happy as a JRPG fan who originally played Silmeria on PS2 and Lenneth on PSP.  I find myself enjoying the game so far; the music and atmosphere and the distinctive style of the Valkyries in this series has always allured me and this game has the same affect on me. The combat is a massive departure from the series' turn-based roots, although, some elements from the OG series remains, such as each face button initiating a party member's attack. As a fan of the Badass-Character-Action genre a la Bayonetta, DMC, Ninja Gaiden, etc, Ive enjoyed it so far.Though I am still in the midst of playing through the game, the story seems a bit vapid so far. I am hoping it will pick up as i play through more of it. Also, as a classic JRPG fan, this game has been leaving me wanting some more classic elements implemented like NPC-filled towns with bars, inns and shops (not that Valkyrie would use them, its just for the pageantry of it). But the reasoning for there being no one around so far is because of the world ending event, Ragnarok destroyed most of civilization. This makes sense, but again, I like the pageantry of having those classic JRPG elements. Instead the game has flowers called "Hollow Blossoms" scattered throughout levels, which when picked up, allows Valkyrie to interpret the thoughts of the past, which act like Resident Evil files and give more context to the games world. There is also something about the level design that, though i cant quite put my finger on yet, is kinda odd. I think part of it is that much of the combat takes place in towns instead of dungeons. Although the stages are designed well enough and give a good amount of freedom, they are also oddly restrictive. Certain ledges or a random toppled pillar youd think you would be able to jump on, instead have collision barriers preventing it. While you can actually jump atop building rooftops and over banisters. Its like the game is trying to keep the player from breaking its level by platforming somewhere you shouldnt be able to, but it is done in places that seem inconsequential. There are other times when the game jails you off from returning to previous sections of the map simply because the game wants the player to move forward, eventhough it seems like it would be harmless to allow it. Perhaps it is to avoid manipulating the one time healing a save points grants the player the first time its used. The game is designed by the team behind Ninja Gaiden, so the game has a cool sense of style to its attack animations, making Valkyrie look like a badass in battle and there are some neat game design choices shared between these two games as well. Such as enemies dropping blue orbs that fill Valkyrie's Soul meter (Ryu Hayabusa's health) and yellow orbs that are used as currency (same in both games). Valkyrie can even use the orbs to charge a "Soul Burst" up to 3 levels to unleash a hailstorm of savage, but oh-so-graceful strikes with her blade in the vain of Hayabusa's Ultimate Technique.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so messy.Structurally, it's similar to . From an overworld map, you choose a main quest. After completing the quest, you can go back to part of the area to do individual side quests.Combat wise, this game is full of "-isms." Valkyrie has an Izuna Drop, a Lunar Staff weapon, instant charging of an "ultimate technique" after absorbing souls, finishing moves, etc. As with every game these days, it also has -style parrying for some reason.However, combat is where the game is messiest. Recovery times are way too long. Attack animations can last way too long. When Valkyrie gets knocked down, it takes way too long to get back up.It's like if  didn't have nearly enough development time to tighten everything so player and enemy attack timings mesh well.Level design is better than I expected. There are a lot of alternate paths, secret areas, and optional combat encounters. Many more than SOP:FFO had.Character progression is fine, but too slow. But that's the Square RPG side intruding into the Soleil hack'n'slash side. Slower progression makes the game longer, but at the cost of the combat getting smoother by unlocking more combos and abilities.Story wise, I have no idea. It's fine but forgettable. None of the characters are very unique or full of personality. They seem to be the standard stoic, monotone, serious fantasy game characters.Music is great.The art style is... high resolution ? That's all I can compare it to. Textures are kind of cel-shaded, but in a more realistic way. The colors are also washed out overall. The game could use more vibrant colors.If you can put up with some messy -like combat, then the game is a slight recommend on sale. (The NG Master Collection is better, though.)I liked Soleil's other game, , much better than this one. That game has a lot of quirky personality that makes it a more unique experience than this.The game isn't bad. It's a more grounded hack'n'slash type of game. Its biggest sin is being $60 USD, but it's a decent experience on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok it's been 30 hours, feel like i can comment now.Story is as expected. Odin, Fenrir....i mean it's ragnarok. You know what you are getting into.There are elements that get left unanswered (why is there are dark valkyrie?) Side quests aren't too tedious which is a good thing. There isn't a crap ton of story in this, so since the maps are limited, side quests being tedious would have been very bad. They do a good job of providing you with proper leveling up and item collection, along with the side quest objective. Battle system..here is the meat of the game:So as others have said it's a bit um..Clunky for lack of a better term? I'm used to pressing buttons at my own pace (x, x, x, y), but this game makes it so that you need to wait a bit between presses for certain combos (think x..wait x...wait x..wait y). Not quite as slow as i typed it but if i'm comparing  to the combat style of oh....Nier, then it's much less your pace of button pressing and much more you adjust to the game's pace. Takes some getting used to. The camera during battles is wonky. You could easily end up in a corner and zoomed in on yourself, unable to see anything going on around you. Maybe there is an adjustment for it to not zoom in. Haven't looked at all the camera setting to see. What i'm talking about there is the default setting.The "dodge/Block" mechanic. Nice idea, poorly executed. Blocking is essentially pointless unless you are preforming the "perfect block-dodge" (a mechanic in which you block upon instant an attack hits you to perform counter movement or attack). I'll have to try a play-through in which i use that mechanic more than the perfect dodge mechanic to see how much better or worse it might be. As of writing this, the base price of the game is 59.99. Can't say i would recommend this game at that price. I purchased the deluxe version for half off. So about 32.00. Yeah, that's probably much more what this game is worth.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna start with the cons, as there are some. This game is NOT anything like Valkyrie Profile 2: Silmeria. I'm gonna be honest that's what I was hoping for but that's not what I got.Game takes a little over 20 hours to complete without DLC or NG+ counted. So if you're one of those people who wants 1 hour of gameplay per dollar spent don't buy this unless it's on sale.This game is poorly optimized for PC and a lot of people, myself included, had issues with game crashes. However it DOES run on the steam deck, contrary to what you may have heard. I managed to complete my playthrough on that system with no issues.Now the good: The combat is actually really fun and not terribly complicated. It's more of a hack n slash style game instead of a turn based system. It's actually enjoyable.The game maps are relatively straight and arrow, which given the time I played it is a welcome departure from open world games. They give you a mission, you do the mission, and find treasure hidden along the way. Subquests are also short and sweet, giving you new stuff like weapons, spells, or stat ups. Instead of the subquests being tedious fetch quests they're just going to specific locations to slay some monsters, straight to the action. The story and characters don't unfortunately get interesting until you're near the end but the ending is satisfying and climactic. The final boss fight is a decent challenge even on normal. I imagine it'd be a nightmare on hard. If you like hack and slash RPGs, wait for this to go on sale and buy it. It's not worth 60 bucks, but 40 or less and it's a fair price, which is what I paid for it. Taika is best girl and needs fanart ASAP

_childDocuments_.review: The problems with Valkyrie Elysium aren't immediately visible. I still enjoyed playing the game. It is generally polished, the lacking or unfinished elements are tidied up well enough, but by the time one reaches the end of the game it really feels as if half of the development is just missing. There isn't enough content, mechanical inconveniences. Hardly any investment into writing, cutscenes and dialogue animations. Oh the characters talk to each other, but for the most part it's just voice over everyone standing around as the camera wanders off. Side quests to find some spirit's lost ring or fight a couple of waves of enemies are set up to make you revisit a small segment of the mission area you already explored.Enemies have five possible elements. You can only have four spells on your hotkeys. You also can't easily pick the strength of the spell or whether you want to use the aoe version. You have a couple of utility spells and a spell that is actually a sixth element. It's just not put in the game anywhere else, but you have an earth spell. However you probably just want to keep those main elements because elemental advantage is the core of combat.You probably also want to make sure you summon the appropriate companion for whatever spell you cast, boosting it an extra level. It feels like you're meant to get more companions, that there would be more characters to interact with and develop bonds with. More stories to explore, and maybe switch out as poorly as you switch spells in any given situation, but you only get four. Note that does mean you have two elemental spells you cannot boost or gain as a buff on your melee attacks. There is an auto-summon feature for these friends, but as you can only have two out at a time this leads to the auto-summon unsummoning one you have already summoned deliberately, and given the range of elements on enemies, your auto-summons will be set to the wrong element 80% of the time.There is also weapon advantage against enemies; you do unlock a nice selection of weapons, but you can only have two equipped at a time. They also have rune slots so that if you do want to switch weapon for the damage boost, it's going to be a thirty second or minute pause every short battle.There is a great deal of potential in Elysium, but it seems Ragnarok came too early.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay at best. What the game has going for it is the battle system, but that is all. It lacks what makes Valkyrie Profile what it is around every end.1. The deep, complex, yet simple enough system to learn.--> VP series before this point had always had a system that is deep, simple to get into, but a bit difficult to master. Elysium lacks this.2. Story.--> VP series is known for its amazing story. This game is pretty bland, with some ideas that could have been expanded on. VP 1 and 2 did far more in 10 hours than what this one did in the same time.3. Evolution of Nibelung Valesti.--> The one thing out of everything, and they screwed it up. It looks like they missed the reason on why it is such a special ability. Version I is what you're supposed to start with but you don't. Version I represents loyalty to Odin in VP 1, and naivety in VP 2. Then version II, which is unlocked mid game in VP 1. It is around the time of conflict, doubt. In VP 2, it is more like independence and resolve. This was unlocked near the end game, but a good chunk of the game left. Version III, in VP 1. It represents the evolution of the Valkyrie to becoming Creator. In VP 2, it represents how souls are free, that they cannot be bound. These were shown in the last battle. Elysium? Nothing of the sort. Version I is unlocked right before the last section, and doesn't have meaning. Maybe at best doubt? But I think that is a stretch, since it was just handed at that point without any sort of relevance.Version II is a Side Quest, defeating the point of the Valkyrie's growth through the main story. And was more about lore, rather than the Valkyrie herself. Version III is the prize for the Seraphic Gate, which made it pointless.4. Seraphic Gate.--> Everything that made the End Game of the VP series fun is gone. It is just 20 floors in a row, you can't use your character or their skills. It is preset, making it pointless. There is no story, no usual bosses, etc. Nothing that makes the VP series what it is supposed to be.5. Dungeons.--> No dungeons.6. Exploration.--> No exploration.What it does have going for it though, would be how simple the endings are to get. The game does have a bit of a story, but nothing much. The characters aren't even given time to be expanded. In the least they could have showed a better progression of the Valkyrie and that would have made it passable.In the end, I can only recommend this game for the battle system which I do find good. Though, that is all. I know I am giving this a like, but there are a few points to it, not much though. One such point is that, the story is between Chapters 8 and 9, the last two. And this shows the gods who devours souls, Maria being turned into a Valkyrie. How she goes down her path, and ultimately what she chooses in the end. If this was built a lot better from the start, it would be a solid game.At best a 5/10.Compared to the rest of the series? 1/10 or 2/10.Since I can't paste a full on review of the whole series. You can read it on the forums.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, Valkyrie May Cry."Upon the scales to weigh, a choice that must be made."A new Valkyrie for a new era.Finally, an attractive looking female character. Pretty rare and precious in these times.Not gonna lie I first bought this because I thought it was a Val Kilmer game...Overall, this is a solid AA diamond in the rough. It also manages to stand alone as a Valkyrie game. It feels like its own thing with its own characters, and although it borrows a bit from VP1 in its story, it still has some new and interesting things with the gods and souls and the valkyrie that will feel fresh. Its callbacks to the original Valkyrie Profile games are also pretty neat and it's clear that Soleil put a lot of heart and effort into paying respect to the legacy.Combat is fast and fluid and easily the best part of the game. There’s tons of options, very visceral, and really great feeling of being a divine warrior who hacks her way through monsters in extremely cool manners. Think a better Scarlet Nexus with roots in Ninja Gaiden and Bayonetta. Once you start getting more options, you'll find yourself in a rhythm and realize how much fun you’re having zipping around like spiderman and getting massive combos. The animations are impressive. The different attacks and combos that the Valkyrie does are so incredible to look at, it's by far one of the best additions to the Valkyrie series in terms of action presentation. The spear and the rapier are insane to see in action. They did go overboard with all of the breakable objects though. Crate Smashing Simulator 2022.The levels are decently fun and have varied landscape. The graphics range from impressive to mediocre. The characters look beautiful in the right lighting conditions and some of the environment can be pretty neat to walk around in, especially Valhalla.The skill tree feels like it actually gives significant jumps of power to your valkyrie at times. Between leveling your weapon and the skill tree you'll feel stronger almost every level which is a good feeling.While the story itself is pretty predictable, it still felt like a production with an honest vision behind a competent team, just that it was a vision that no one asked for (no one was asking for a VP reboot). The story exists and is there. Don't expect a lot here and you wont be let down. It is clearly not the focus of the game.The sidequests are more like Nioh and Ninja Gaiden or Scarlet Nexus: Very barebones, mostly just focused on combat segments. Luckily the combat is super fun, so it's not that much of a problem. But the sidequests are not that impressive from a narrative point of view.It's also really nice to have a female protagonist again and the cast of characters is very enjoyable and diverse. I mean, it’s beautiful girls fighting monsters,  what’s not to like? Kudos for staying classy too and not overly sexualizing them. That is something I really appreciated.The length of the game at 9 chapters will be a positive or a negative to some people. It doesnt overstay its welcome and it’s enjoyable all the way through. Personally I couldn't had been happier to find out that a Square RPG is shorter (it's around 22 hours with all the subquests ). I usually play games while I’m working or taking care of a toddler, I don't have 88 hours to play a single damn game. 20-30 hours is my max. This may have even sold me on it.Overall it’s a very fun game and is highly enjoyable if you go in with the expectations that it’s a very solid if somewhat short action game. It's like a low budget Scarlet Nexus but better in certain areas (combat, level design) and worse in others (cutscenes, social links, production values).If you are a Valkyrie Profile fan, I definitely recommend the game. I know it's not the exact same game people played 22 years ago, but it's a good effort with enjoyable gameplay loop, nice characters, and cool action. It's only restricted by its budget and lower production values, but it's still a nice enjoyable experience. It's like your typical flawed AA PS2-era game, but with modern graphics technology if that makes sense.I'd say a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so hard to recommend. It has a beautiful world and the character designs are lovely with so much detail put into both. Taika anyone? The action combat is flashy and fun to look at and perform, but becomes insanely repetitive. This is my first intro to the Valkyrie franchise and I'm not going to make this game be the judge of the entire franchise. I'm a fan of ARPGs, but this one felt like a chore to play by the end game. There are tons of things to nitpick at also. First off, the game is not worth the current price tag and the bonus DLC should only be worth a dollar at best.The story is okay and has a semi beautiful ending on the true end route, I wasn't dissatisfied by the outcome and I kind of enjoyed it overall. There are collectible flowers to find while you play and give some side story, but these are generally uninteresting. The green verdant flowers are needed though if you want true ending.The enemy variants are only elemental based. By the end of chapter 5 or so, you will have seen all the enemy variants and at that point, it just swaps what they are weak against.Experienced no performance issues. No lag, stutter, or crashes.The combat... Flashy, fast paced, different combos to pull off, different weapons have different combo types, and a decent amount of Artes to use. But all packed into repetition. -The weapons all have different combos, but swapping between them means nothing. No weapon is more powerful then the other, even when maxed out. I went the entire game with the starting weapon and maxed it out with SSS proficiency. Sword, spear, staff... they are all the same and that is disappointing. Performing combos, puts you into animation lock and can ultimately screw you over, especially on boss fights. -The lock on system is piss poor and when locked on, you lose control of the camera, if you get backed into a wall and are then stun locked (which happens A TON) you wont be able to see anything but a wall. -You will have the help of 4 companions you can choose from with about 2 ever being able to be summoned at a time. Each has it's own element type which they provide a GREAT help on combat. They, however, can prove to be troublesome at times because the there is collision on them ( they are suppose to be spirits). So they can push you out of the way when attacking or trap you and the enemy in a corner while they try to help. Overall, this doesn't happen a whole lot, but it is annoying.I started the game on Normal difficulty, and the game had quite a challenge to it. Early game is a bit punishing and unforgiving, by late game, still the same but slightly worse. Items are a luxury. Bosses will stun and knock you around like no tomorrow. Mini bosses are just as deadly, and small enemy types can stun and combo you to death if they swarm you. By the end of the game, I had no health or Arte potions, which made teh boss fight(s) twice as hard. You can't buy any of these items, you could theoretically go and farm out items on missions, but you will need to fully complete the mission to have the items and weapon progress save. I can't even think how hard Valkyrie or even Hard mode difficulties play out. If you want a true challenge, play on Hard mode and when you complete the game, Valkyrie mode unlocks.The minor nitpicks of the game: Text in the subtitles are sometimes slightly unaligned, meaning the entire phrase is leveled, but a letter here and there is slightly lower then the rest, which is odd. The voice over, at least in English, is pretty good, but sometimes lacks emotion and it makes it worse since the animations are not all that great either. The characters lack emotion and have dead pan stares for the most part. In cut scenes, they are generally looking one direction while someone is speaking and have no reaction. Lip Sync is completely off like some bad dub.Overall, A fair price I feel this game should be half the value. It feels half baked and half done. It is fun and frustrating, provides a decent challenge with a mediocre story but plagued with many things that make the experience sour the longer you play it. Wait for a sale, and if you are a fan of the Valkyrie franchise, listen to the other reviews and come in with low expectations. They game is a decently low hack n slash ARPG, but doesn't set any standard of being among the greatest. The graphics truly do set a high standard on the store page that this game "looks" amazing, but that's all it is...looks.

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed everything, at least to the point of not going insane with getting S ranks, I would fully recommend this game to anyone looking for a action JRPG.  Keep in mind, this is coming from someone who's never played Valkyrie Profile.The story, while not the strongest in the series, is what you would expect from Square in general.  It's entertaining where it needs to be, emotional where it needs to be, but it won't blow your socks off by any means.  However, keep in mind there is multiple endings, and some of the endings are far worse than others, with the true ending being the only one I felt really was remotely satisfying.The combat is some of the best action combat I've seen in awhile.  Your swings have impact.  Striking an enemy makes it act like it's been hit.  Hitting big enemies with big attacks staggers them.  You can work elemental combos in to deal additional damage, including hitting them enough times to put them down to open up a window of scoring plenty of combos.  I don't play many action RPG's due to combat feeling you have no impact, but this one kept me fully entertained.  The bosses are enjoyable and unique, as well as having that special JRPG flavor to them you come to expect from classic turn based titles.Overall, I'd say the game is fully worth you're time if you're not going in expecting Valkyrie Profile, which to my understanding is wildly different than this title.  Expect at least 25-40 hours of content if you expect to do every side quest and get all the endings.

Gameplay-wise, it's in the vein of combo-centric Platinum-style  games, except there's no ability to cancel out of an attack to dodge (or at least, if there is, I haven't unlocked it yet).  For the level of effort on display in this title, $60 is waaaaay too much of an ask.

_childDocuments_.review: A great third person action game. It's fantastic to see a melee action game these days that isn't a Soulslike. It's also been ages (maybe since Devil May Cry 1?) since a game gives you health and magic power ups without breaking them into 3 pieces and expect you to ferret out every piece. _childDocuments_.review: Take my recommendation with a grain of salt, because I think this game deserves a Positive rating at the very least.The only redeeming feature about this game is it's combat, which is pretty complete, you have combos with light and heavy attacks, mid-air combos that let you juggle the enemy in the air, magic spells, executions, different weapons, dodges with i-frames, blocking that becomes a parry with the right timing, and summons that aid you in battle. In short sessions, this game is pretty fun time-killer and will not disappoint.Now that I'm done speaking about the good of this game, the rest goes from meh to pretty bad, starting with the level design: the chapters have maps that are very long and you will be able to explore to find collectibles, side-quests that give you new weapons, and items to use, however, the design of the levels is kinda bad, there's a lot of re-used assets that make all levels feel the same, and even the last chapter is just the previous one recycled.The characters are lame, Maria (the nameless main character) has some kind of brain damage that doesn't allow her to have a different face other than sleepy eyes and a frown, and she speaks about the same thing through most of the game, the Einherjar (your summons) are okay and much more likable but very plain, and the antagonists are just boring. Same goes to the story, it doesn't offer any kind of drama or any kind of engagement to the game, if you play this, I'd say skip the cutscenes.My rating for this game is that it's just "okay."At the end of the day, play it if you like the idea of being a strong valkyrie goddess and want a fun combat experience, but don't expect anything else out of this game. Once again, take my recommendation with a grain of salt, because if this game had more positive ratings, I would give it a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: In an attempt to save a world, Odin used his remaining power to create Valkyrie. Angel of death. Funny enough it's similar to Bleach's soul reaper. It's action packed with actions and cool cutscenes.  Ok so the story starts off well but takes a while to pick up with character development. Like roughly halfway. You awaken as a valkyrie with the power and knowledge Odin bestows you and task you with cleansing Midgard in an effort to help him regain his lost powers. She has a name i honestly don't remember lol... To be fair, everyone calls her Valkyrie. The main baddies were interesting but unfortunately not enough was done with them. The story cutscence kept me wanting to know what happens next but at some point it sort of derailed... Also a lot of stuff goes unanswered as a result. I get the feeling the story changed quite a few times. Some things made no sense. In short, starts great but ends up being meh. It's average. 5/10Gameplay is good along with its combat and everything is weak to a certain element. You can do cool ♥♥♥♥ with abilities and summon Einherjar to aid you in battle though you do not control them. They each have their own element type for their abilities like in many rpg games and doing so also add their element to Valkyries melee attacks. Unfortunately, a lot of map location feel empty and it's somewhat linear. And yeah i hear you guy in the back. That's the whole point.. I know. I'm saying instead of it just being empty for the sole purpose of have large empty area for enemies to spawn, they could have do more than just have more spawns over and over. In fact, it would feel even more empty if you remove all the destructible objects. There's i guess collectables flowers that you find but it just feels pointless once you find them. Doesn't add much. Combat is solid but guarding kind sucks which is strange. You have this grappling beam (hook) called Soul Chain that can be used to get around certain areas and is used also in combat. I love being able to block something that would harm me in style but here guarding against an attack is lame for a Valkyrie that's very proficient in swordsmanship combat and magic. You have two things this game uses for its combat. Divine Arts which are your abilities as Valkyrie which are swap-able and uses what i call the Art meter that are orange diamonds and your Soul meter which is a blue meter for your Einherjar summons. Occasionally you can use your Einherjar outside of combat for very specific purpose. 7/10So this game ran fine for the most part. The game will often drop frame when a lot of abilities or a lot is happening at once and in some cases can make it unplayable. Wonder how that plays like on console. Speaking of frames, this is capped to 60 fps for some reason. It's possible to unlock the cap but i imagine it will cause performance issues. Ran fine at 155hz for a while. No complains. The only thing is since it doesn't go much higher than 60 fps, you may just want to stick to vsync on. Have less heat being dumped in the room from the monitor. I had 1 hard crash literally when i beat the final boss. Literally.... Totally not mad a about it lol. Of course i had to redo it lmao. Smh. 5/10The artstyle this game uses is interesting from the world you explore and its character. Works well in cutscenes. The character designs look great. I really really like Taika's design. I also liked Kristoffer. They both have that FF aesthetic that i liked with their outfit and look. Oh yeah i played this at 1440p. Noice. I wish i could change the outfit of Valkyrie to something else i was telling myself at one point since i was using the dlc weapon from start to finish. Would have been cool. 7/10The sound had some good one especially during the boss fights and combat. But early on i found the same looping music to be boring and lack punch after listening it for hours. It needed something more like these during exploration at times.    I haven't listened to the full playlist for this game but i'm sure i'm missing some. 6/10Valkyrie Elysium is good game that i think you should eventually pickup on sale. Story is meh but enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: I'm roughly four hours into the game, and I'm genuinely shocked at how little press the game has gotten. It's an above average action game that feels as competent as your Devil May Cry or Bayonetta with flashy action and responsive controls (i.e., it's a great game), but what Square-Enix really nails, and Valkyrie Elysium is no different, is that fantasy aesthetic and mood. I really like the sort of "comic" filter they use as well.  Given how the einherjyar system is implemented (the game's "summons"), I have a feeling I'm in for some more poignant narrative moments as well. I love this kind of stuff. I also really want the sound track and kind of wish that was a bonus similar to Tactics Ogre.The game's visual options aren't as in-depth as something like Cyberpunk or Doom Eternal, but it DOES have super ultra-wide (32:9) support right out of the box, and that speaks to a refreshing (and surprising) attention to detail. Maybe the experience breaks down as the game goes on, but right now I'm having a blast..

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a decent action RPG, with a well-crafted combat system that is comparable to other AAA studio titles such as Ninja Gaiden and Devil May Cry. The game offers players a variety of options for combat, including the ability to use magic and melee weapons. The game's difficulty is also noteworthy, as it is challenging even on the highest difficulty level.However, the game is not without its flaws. The camera system is problematic, as it does not always provide a clear view of the action. The level design is also criticized, with a high number of enemies and a wide distribution that makes it difficult to navigate. Additionally, the knockback system is problematic, as it takes a long time to recover from, which can negatively impact the overall gameplay experience.The character design is also criticized, with the protagonist being portrayed as a young girl in a silly costume, rather than a believable Valkyrie warrior. Additionally, the story and world concept are not well-realized, with little connection to Nordic mythology.Overall, while the game offers a solid combat experience, it is overpriced for the quality offered. The game's potential is acknowledged, but it is recommended that the developers address the issues present in the game and improve the character design, story, and world concept.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that has played the original Valkyrie Profile back on the original PlayStation, this game doesn't even compare or feels like what the series should of been. The characters feel very bland and I'm not a fan of how the Einherjar are more like equipment and not actual characters and how they are limited to solving puzzles or time limited summons from 15 seconds to a minute, sure they get the job done in combat, but they don't really feel like partners to the Valkyrie.  I only made it to the 2nd Einherjar and just acquiring them felt like a chore and not rewarding.  So honestly, this game shouldn't be put into the same series as Valkyrie Profile, the game is too expensive for what it is worth, mediocre combat, bland characters and terrible story direction, I would only give this game a 3/10 at best.
