_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: Only recommending this if it is discountedAfter unlocking all 4 endings I ended up feeling like maaaan, it was not worth full price(60 USD) playing through this overall MID title. I was first interested in this title bc I thought the gameplay looked cool in the trailer and came in neutral w/ no knowledge of the Valkyrie Profile IP. And there are things I like, such as the character design of the main cast and their development( especially Taika ), the weapon variety that includes a familiarity level that encourage the player to stick and practice w/ each of them, the skill tree being simple and resource-capped(instead of level cap) that prevents the MC+weapons from reaching max level early and maintain a bit of challenge. And bc the skill tree is resource-capped, and the main chapters are big long linear missions, grinding is not necessary.What’s weird is that the game is treated like a Character Action game but the combat doesn’t fit the genre since there’s no dodge-offset(like Bayonetta) or anything that cancels an attack’s animation, and ALL of the enemies have posture, which prevents you from staggering+juggling them(Like DMC or any musou game). Like the movelist and tools are there, but it’s lacking the essence of making YOU feel like a badass while you’re building up the hit-count meter. Another annoying thing is how the way this game uses enemy typing feels bad, you can try to ignore it and stubbornly fight them but there’s no incentive to not open your menu( multiple times ) to switch your special moves and take advantage of their elemental weakness. This game also made me realized that I HATE teleporting enemy and I think devs needs to STOP making these kinds of enemies that messes w/ your lock-on.Other than that, I’m just glad that the conditions to unlock each ending is easy, even though the final chapter is a slog. The “Bad” Ending was hilarious. The subquests are mostly uninteresting but they’re better than replaying Main Chapters to farm resources. Even compared to other hardcore action games, it’s weird that this game doesn’t have an item shop for you to refill your already limited item inventory. And maybe if only they tweak some minor details, I would have enjoyed the game a lot moreOR  maybe I should’ve played it on easy/normal instead of hard.

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason I'm recommending this is that I enjoyed the combat system and because I got it on sale and not at full price, regardless, the combat has the same issues mentioned by the majority of the reviews here.-There are a lot of issues with Lock-on during combat.-The "Disable Input" delay between each action is a bit long, especially when using the dodge function.-There are a lot of collision issues, especially between characters, but also between characters and the surrounding environment.-I started having fun with the combat the moment I reached chapter 3.-The skills, the summons, and the elemental combinations make the combat more enjoyable, alas the "Lock-on" issue mentioned before ruins things.-If you missed an important item in a location and you want to get it, you have to replay the whole chapter, despite having the ability to return to the hub area from any manual save location.-A plus for the devs for how the elemental type of the summons coats your equipped weapon and gives you an advantage in combat. -I have nothing to say, it's beautiful and well done.(This includes the base mesh, hair, clothing, animations, and voice-acting)- (Good)-  (Good)- (Perfection and the top character in this whole game, the voice actress did a formidable job, kudos to them).- (Should have been designed differently)- (Bland, imperfect, and the voice acting is just robotic and annoying, even at the end of the game when things start changing).Perfectly done, especially for spatial environment sounds, but  I expected something more epic during the boss fights.-Weak, linear, and lacking. If you expect a story with the complexity and depth of any JRPG, you will be disappointed.This game's combat system might be far more enjoyable if it wasn't for the technical issues mentioned before, especially since the combat system itself is the only value I got from this game. (In my opinion only and I do not wish to offend anyone) Hilde's character design and English voice acting are far superior to the main playable character and should have been swapped.Overall, I did enjoy the game but I'm certain that I would have given a different review if I bought it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews with so few hours (if at all), but the mixed reviews cover up a series that I want to see more of (especially as I missed the wave due to a near non-existant middle/high school gaming budget).To explain the stiffness of the combat others have critiques, attacks *can* be animation canceled. Just not with the dodge or block. Moves can be jump, summon, and spell/"divine art" canceled. However, each has drawbacks. Jumps don't have i-frames (that I know of, but I'm a player who did not notice Devil May Cry's until it was pointed out to me). Summons/spells cost resources, but the dodge does provide the same "shield" animation effect that the dodge has. This includes the spells with slower cast time, except there are recover frames where you're vulnerable. So, you better hope your enemy doesn't use a meaty attack on your oki. Summons don't have any invulnerability, unfortunately, but they do draw enemy attention.Having loved games with more fluid combat like Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, Unsighted, and Sekiro, I wish the game devs gave more emphasis on blocking and dodging. However, I can respect the design decisions. Overall, I say the game is worth it on the discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Valkyrie Elysium’s strongest point is definitely the action RPG combat. Valkyrie has access to multiple different weapons and can equip two simultaneously. Each weapon plays a little bit differently and can exploit different enemy weaknesses.Valkyrie can summon up to Einherjar’s (partners) to assist during combat. Each Einherjar represents a different element and can be summoned to exploit an enemy weakness. You’ll constantly be changing primary weapons and the summoned Einherjars to make the most of the combat. This keeps it feeling fresh and engaging.The game is split up into chapters. Each chapter is a different stage. The stages play like an arcade stage, they feel like they’re designed to be replayed and you are scored upon completion. Each stage has collectables. It can be frustrating if these collectables are missed, you often cannot back track, forcing you to replay the entire stage.Side quests are present in the game but rarely offer much in terms of story. They usually just involve re-running stages and fighting your way through waves of enemies. They pad out the playtime but don’t offer much otherwise.Valkyrie Elysium’s premise is interesting. I found the delivery of the story to be lacking. The majority of the story is told in the opening and closing chapters of the game. The chapters in between don’t really push the story or characters forward. Fortunately, I found the combat fun enough to keep me playing through the middle section of the game.Valkyrie Elysium’s story has multiple endings. I liked the way that each ending felt like it could be considered a canon ending to the story - even the “bad” ending has value.Valkyrie Elysium has some stylistic choices that I didn’t personally like.The character models have a thick black outline around them, similar to a style you’d expect to see in a cell-shaded video game. This style looks jarring against the otherwise realistic looking model textures. The irremovable film grain effect also makes the game look worse. Fortunately, there are mods available to remove both of these effects and this makes the game look much better. I’d highly recommend installing these mods if you’re playing the game - they’re both available from Nexus Mods.The game has a super desaturated colour palette - it’s very grey. The colour palette makes sense with the somber tone of the game’s story, but it’s not something that I personally liked.I’d recommend picking Valkyrie Elysium up on sale. There is fun to be had, but it’s probably not worth paying full price for.

The story isn't anything stellar either, but wasn't expecting a blockbuster or anything in that area.Even the coolest mechanic you can use, the soul chain which allows you to grapple to an enemy and perform some special attacks after, seems to only work about half the time. The other half it just flings off towards your targeted enemy and then.....just does nothing. Same with some of the spells you can use. you cast them, watch them visually connect with the targeted enemy, then...just nothing happens. As if there is some unwritten range to your abilities that isn't described anywhere. The variety of weapons and spells is okay, each one semi-unique enough they have their own uses, but it doesn't help the poorly implemented systems at all. _childDocuments_.review: This game is all over the place and deserves mixed reviews. Here's the quick rundown for Valkyrie difficulty experience:Chapter 1-2: Pure suffering. You have no weapons, no spells, no simps (Einherjar) to summon. Combat is pure suffering. It's clunky, all over the place. You die, instead of choosing "respawn at checkpoint" you choose "return to title screen" because you manually saved the game so loading from a checkpoint would delete progress.Chapter 3-6: Peak of the game. You are unlocking weapons, skills, spells and simps. The combat is very enjoyable, you care about getting combos, using the right weapons and spells, controlling your simps. You do not yet see the problems with the combat system.Chapter 7-9: Absolutely tiresome. You unlock nothing new. There are no new enemies. There is only near-endless waves of the same enemies, again and again and again and again, infinite health enemies. Enemy design is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It's not difficult, just so, so insanely tiresome. You just want to kill the wave and move on, but the game throws a new wave, and a new wave, and a new wave. Never have I felt so beaten, not because the game is hard, but because it is just so tiresome. Same combos on the same enemies. Same vulnerabilities exploited. Same enemy. Kill two trees, next wave is two trees. It just keeps coming and does not stop. At no point are you at a risk of dying because:1) You can pause the game and use healing items Nier Automata style.2) Channeling spells, including Estus flask gives you invulnerability. You can break out of any situation by chugging, which is kinda funny. You generate enough Arts to keep yourself alive through everything.Bosses are the best parts of the game, not because they are difficult (they couldn't hit you even if they tried) but because they are not so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tiresome. It's just one enemy, you can use one weapon and one element. You don't need to pause the game swap weapons swap runes kill one enemy pause the game swap elements stun one enemy pause the game swap weapons swap runes kill unstunned enemy pause the game swap weapons swap runes...What makes this a lot worse is you never get a Darkness element simp, making Dark enemies a pain in the ass, and the game spams them like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The enemy design at this point is also horrible: Simple grunts who scream and try to grab attack you 24/7. Trees that spam AoE mist. Supportcuck wizards who use shields and heals, and for some reason are tanky as hell. Everything has so, so much health it is incredibly tiresome. Out of the 25 hours I probably spent 13 just attacking a stunned enemy again and again and again because it just refuses to die.Don't bother playing the game on Valkyrie difficulty, it's not one bit harder than Easy, just far longer. Beating Valkyrie doesn't give you achievements for beating Hard or Medium either by the way.The combat system is based on using the right weapon and the right element and the right simp. If you do so, the enemy is effectively perma-stunned. This makes combat against single enemies a joke, thus, you always fight huge packs. But there's a few problems:You have a weapon proficiency system so you'd rather just use a low proficiency weapon instead of the "right" one.You have 4 spell slots, and there are five elements + Estus flask. You have to constantly go to the menu and equip different spells. You do this 20 times in a single fight.You have two weapon slots and 7 weapons. If you want to use the right weapon, you have to pause the game and change weapons from the menu. You also have to un-equip runes from the old weapon and equip it on the new weapon. You do this 20 times in a single fight.You're supposed to summon your simps based on enemy weaknesses. But actually, your simps gain permanent strength with every summon, so the winning move is to spam them all on cooldown to snowball in strength.The score system punishes you for using items. This makes sense for healing potions, but does not make sense for temporary buff items. As such, the proper way to play is to not use items. This makes exploring the map worthless as the only thing you find is chests that tell you "You have the max amount of Small Mana Potion".You have an allowance for how many skills you can equip. This gives you the  choice between disabling your passive or active skills. What makes this extra retarded is that upgrading a skill deletes the earlier version of the skill. You upgraded Soul Burst to level 3, it now costs 40 more CP. Disable the skill or disable something else. No, you can't go back to Soul Burst 2.LOOK AT THIS ♥♥♥♥My god, does your heart not sing in the chaos, seeing this? That is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beautiful,  game design. Amazing. After you unlock the first half of the skills, you can just stop there. You will never enable the other half.You are an  Valkyrie working for Odin, who is sus. You fight  rebel-Valkyrie 5 times but of course she can never straight up tell you why Odin is sus.The big reveal is that Odin was sus. The story is actually told decently even if it's kind of mediocre. Your simps are good characters with good backstories. Solid 7/10 overall. There's a lot of anime voice actors.The baseline that is there is actually good. This is why the mid-game was actually worth playing. I saw the negative reviews but I sensed there is some value below it all, and I was right. But in the final third of the game it just becomes so, so, so painfully tiresome. You enter a room, the first wave of enemies gives you a 999x Combo. There are four waves. A solid 10-15 minutes of just smashing and smashing the same things again and again.Then you move on to the next room. It is true hell, never have I felt so tired. Fighting  rebel-Valkyrie for the fifth time and the final boss three times over (it's the same fight every time) felt like climbing Mount Doom. You've come so far, so godsdamned far. The end is in sight. It is so tiresome you become tired of being tired. Refined autism is the only thing keeping you going.This game is a trainwreck and a car crash crashing together. It is awful, but there's something beautiful in it too. At times Valkyrie Asylum feels like a 40€ Square Enix game and at times a 20€ Unity Engine game. It is truly bizarre how something can be great and awful at once. It's so all over the place I can't even describe it properly.At no point does it feel like a 60€ game, that price point is a joke.Somehow, I still enjoy this game. Maybe 60 minutes per day, before it becomes tiresome again, I can still feel the good side of it's combat system. During Chapter 9 I thought I'd rather kill myself than play any longer, but now I am actually considering 5-Starring every mission.Am I going to play the  rebel-Valkyrie storyline? Possibly.Do I recommend this game? Absolutely!  Games that make you  something will always beat games that don't. Positive, negative, it doesn't matter what. I hated this game, I loved this game, I despaired, I felt depths of tiredness I thought impossible. I don't care that I hated half of it, I'd rather play a game I hate than a game that makes me feel NOTHING.Yes, you could buy another boring Ubisoft engagement metric-designed game. You could say "I enjoyed this game". But you couldn't say you FELT the game. Valkyrie Asylum is a mess, but it's a mess that actually has an impact on you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game per se, but it's definitely a bad Valkyrie Profile game. The story is sparse at best and only becomes mildly interesting in the very end if you go for the best ending.Graphics are alright, but there are some illogical performance issues where the FPS rate drops significantly on character close-ups. I also noticed some crazy glitching/blinking hair at the beginning of the game. But at this level of graphics, the game should run smooth as butter on an RTX 3080 Ti which is often doesn't.The combat is fine. It's a bit simplistic as the only real effect/variety in battle is elemental alignment. After that the game doesn't really evolve battle and it feels the same for the next 15-20h. I haven't really noticed much difference in the attacks or weapons and it felt like I could just button mash anything and still do a good job.In general there's nothing major wrong with the battle EXCEPT one major glaring issue: There is no dodge-cancel. Each attack animation can easily take 1-2 seconds and if the enemy isn't staggered and starts a counter during your own attack, it's impossible to evade the attack (and/or perform a Perfect Evade maneuver reliably) just because the game doesn't actually let you. (I barely blocked so I don't know if this applies to blocking as well.) At least enemies don't hit too hard so the punishment isn't that big, but it's still frustrating to get interrupted so often. Targeting could be better, camera could be a lot better. I've especially had issues with aiming Niberlung Valesti as enemies move slightly to the side and I lose 6 Art charges for no good reason.It saddens me that the music is so subpar. A few ambient tracks sound similar to the original games, but apart from that, they all just blend together. I'm missing the over-the-top epicness of the original games in both music and overall presentation. When the game does try to be epic, it comes across as hollow and forced because there wasn't a good build-up to it.The extra mode Hilde's Vengeance was alright for the most part until you get to the final bosses where it kinda becomes major ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in terms of difficulty. After dying a few times quickly to Fenrir, I just gave up. It's just not fun when the game suddenly dumps Dark Souls level difficulty on you (dead in 2-3 hits and enemies with huge AOE attacks), but doesn't let you dodge-cancel. Surprisingly, I didn't have any major issues with Fenrir when playing the normal game. This is the main reason that I won't even bother with Seraphic Gate. It doesn't feel like the devs bothered to properly QA these extra parts of the game and adjust the difficulty properly.All in all I can still recommend the game. It's alright in terms of graphics and combat, albeit combat sometimes feels clumsy and sticky (I turned off the auto-targeting thingy in the options and it's still sticky). The upgrading system is fine, but as enemies scale rather quickly, you don't really feel the punch of the upgrades. Music is a bit bland and the audio mastering is weird (especially character dialog in some scenes, I couldn't hear anything the characters were saying in some scenes). The story is basic. The game itself is fun, but don't expect AAA quality. Unfortunately the full price does imply AAA quality so don't be fooled and get the game on a sale.But:- If you want a better character-action game, play DMC5.- If you want a better Valkyrie Profile game, play any of the the first 3 games. (The 3rd is weird and dark, but good in it's own way).

_childDocuments_.review: Overall - I think this game is a fantastic, simple game. Definitely worth it to pick up on sale. I'm not sure how long the game will end up being, but I'd consider spending full price so far!TLDR: fun, mostly fluid combat system with lots of possibilities. Simple, yet effect progression system (you don't need to remember 1000 different mechanics in game). Environments are awesome, graphics are good (except for 60fps lock), audio is great. Story is engaging and interesting. Characters are cool and fit within the story the game tells. Full review:Some of this review may contain spoilers. I tried to hide the elements of my review directly related to the story or specific game mechanics.Combat---------- Personally I think the combat is very fluid and feels great.   - I did not personally feel that the combat was particularly painful at the beginning of the game. Yes, as other reviews mentioned, combat definitely gets more varied as you unlock more, but even in its beginning form, I thought combat was fun.  - I do think I personally play this a little more as a button masher than a "technical" type combat, but as you play, you do learn what combinations of moves are most effective, so you naturally play a little more technically over time.  - As other reviews mentioned, you cannot cancel out of frames for a lot of moves - once you start the move, you are locked into it. But you CAN quickly recover after moves into other combos. There are tricks you can do to minimize the moments where you are left open to attack from enemies.  - There is some decent weapon variety to unlock - and I'm not even that far in yet.  - Graphics / Audio / Environments------------------------------------ The environments in this game are awesome! They remind me of Nier Replicant / Nier Automata, but in a mid-evil type setting mostly (big castle-like towns, smaller sprawling ocean towns, viking snowy wilderness).- Graphics are great - the game does appear to be locked to 60fps.- Audio is great as well - lots of cool soundtracks.This next section talks about a lot of specific game mechanics, so I wanted to hide it incase you want to experience it for yourself!Bugs------- So far, I only encountered one bug where I got stuck floating. Had to revert to quit and hadn't manually saved recently, but the game autosaved about 10 minutes of game time before I got stuck.Summary----------I put this game on my wishlist as soon as I saw it a LONG time ago. When it finally came out - I didn't want to buy it on my PS5 right away, so I waited until I saw it on Steam. When it released on Steam, I was kind of surprised by the mixed reviews. I personally think this is a really solid game that's definitely worth playing. I'd pick it up in a heartbeat on sale, and even at full price I don't think you'd be too disappointed. One of those times where I'm glad I took a chance even though the reviews were a little mixed.

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part, slapping on the title "Valkyrie" has just made this a cash grab, exploiting the nostalgia for most long time fans of the series.I personally don't mind the departure from the classic Valkyrie Profile gameplay style since modernization of most classic games almost always gravitates towards fast-paced action RPGs... but the way it's implemented on this game is just lazy and half assed. The combat has no nuance and just feels like a glorified hack and slash. The camera angles become atrocious at times. The character's attack animations are stiff af.But the most egregious issue I found with this game is the fact that you're stuck with just 4 Einherjar throughout the entire game. Like, what was even the point of having a list of Einherjar and being able to assign them to a hotkey when, at the end of the day, you don't really have a choice to begin with? One of the main draws of the old games was the abundance of Einherjar to choose from, which compliment your Valkyrie's play style. You can have your Valkyrie be the front line while having a team of mages and archers, for example. Or have your Valkyrie use a bow while you have a team of Einherjar forming a wall in front of you to defend and dish out melee damage. The possibilities were endless, back in the day. And, while we're on the subject of variety, the lack of weapons and weapon types was really sad for this game. Everything felt like it was super dumbed down and 10 steps backwards, especially considering the advancements in gaming ideas and technologies we've had since the last Valkyrie Profile game was released.And last thing I'd like to touch on is the atmosphere and stories the older games had that this one just doesn't really pull off. Probably still tied to the limitations on the Einherjar and other important characters, this entry to the franchise just misses the mark, for me. Even to this day, I still have recollections of some of the memorable stories of the Einherjar from the very first Valkyrie Profile game on the PS1... even the side characters that join you to become an Einherjar felt they had more fleshed out backstories than the ones this game offers.I played a few hours of this game and already knew that this wasn't the Valkyrie game that I wanted, nor did the entire fandom as a whole deserve. I just forced myself to power through 20+ hrs just so I can finish the game and make the most of the money I spent on it, even though it was not the best experience for me. So, in conclusion, I cannot, in good conscience, recommend this to anyone. For the long time fans of this series, we will continue to mourn the death of this franchise. For newcomers who wanted to check out what the Valkyrie Profile experience really was, I'd steer clear from this and check out Valkyrie Profile Lenneth (the OG remaster).

_childDocuments_.review: Valkyrie Profile is one of my all-time favorite JRPGs, but as a series it took a huge nosedive in quality in my eyes. The first game on the PS1 I absolutely adored and enjoyed thoroughly from beginning to end but I did not particularly like Silmeria, I absolutely hated Covenant of the Plume and I'm not gonna talk about the mobile game because I don't want to wake up in some Cambodian re-education camp.Generally I have zero expectations for this series anymore and this game being a spin-off by a third party developer I've never heard of made me go in with even less than that.And to my absolute surprise I ended up loving it. Now the game has some problems, but it's the most fun I've had with a Valkyrie Profile game since the original.I'm gonna get the two biggest problems out of the way right now before I talk about the actual game. Do not fall for Square's tricks. This is clearly a AA budget title and there's nothing wrong with that, BUT they are trying to sell as a full priced AAA release. It went -50% off very fast after it was released and I believe that is the real price. I got it for 30 bucks off the Christmas Sale and for that much I can thoroughly recommend it. But for 60 bucks? Yeah, nah, f*ck off.PS4/PS5 owners of the Deluxe Edition got a port of the original game for free (granted I'm not overly fond of the PSP version that the port was based off, but it's fine). On PC all we get is a an extra weapon that's essentially a reskin and is pretty much useless throughout 80% of the game. If this changes in the future and we do get Valkyrie Profile 1 for free with the Deluxe Edition then you can grab it but for now save your shekels.With that out of the way onto the actual game.The story is more or less a cut down and re-arranged version of the first game's story, but it takes place in an alternate universe and has no connections to previous games. If you've beaten Valkyrie Profile 1 you already know what will happen. It does have its moments though and I did enjoy it overall. There are four endings to unlock and thankfully they are fairly easy to get unlike the cryptic bullsh*t that was ending A of the original game.For a budget title (which is what this game really is) the visuals are fine. I was originally a bit put off by the cell shading effect, but it grew on me and I enjoyed checking out the different areas you visit (Valhalla looks glorious). The characters and enemy designs are pretty cool even if a good chunk of the enemies are reskins (I'm writing this off as a budget thing).My opinions on the actual games aside if there's one thing I've consistently loved throughout the entire series it's the music. My man Motoi "JRPG Jesus" Sakuraba is back at it again with another killer soundtrack. The style is quite different compared to the older games. It feels closer to his work in Tales of Arise mixed with a tiny bit of his Dark Souls days, but despite that it managed to subconsciously make me think of Valkyrie Profile the moment I started playing the game, so he's once again nailed it in my books.Unlike the previous games Valkyrie Elysium is an action rpg, though a few elements from the old games are present once more.I love the combat in the original Valkyrie Profile because it's fast and to the point, Silmeria and Covenant turned it into a tedious slog and completely ruined it for me. Thankfully this time around the combat is once again great and easily the highlight of the game. However it takes making a good bit of progress before it really starts to shine. You're very limited by what you can do in the beginning and it can give a terrible first impression to most people. Progression is very spaced out (you don't even get Nibelung Valesti until the last few chapters) and I feel like they should've given you more stuff earlier because you can really do a lot later on.There are only 4 Einherjar this time around and they function quite differently compared to the old games. Here they work as timed summons that you can call upon at will as long as you have enough soul energy. They will fight alongside you (you can unlock more moves for them by doing their respective side quests), but their most important function is changing your weapon's element.Enemies are weak to a particular element and weapon. Using the right weapon results in greater damage. Using the right element also fills up another bar that will stun them for a while when it reaches 100% (similar to how it works in modern Ys games). There are 6 different weapons you can find (7 with the deluxe edition), each with its own moveset. You unlock more moves by upgrading the weapon.You can upgrade the Valkyrie too which will give you stat bonuses and more abilities (a highlight is being able to auto summon Einherjar during certain actions). All upgrades cost a certain amount of CP to be active, but on normal difficulty you've got enough to have everything active simultaneously. On hard and above you'll have to mix and match. You have the ability to block, parry, dash and do perfect dodges, but one thing to keep in mind is that you can't cancel out of attacks and I'm pretty sure this is by design. You can probably button mash through the early chapters, but you'll end up getting heavily punished later on. There's a small bit of strategy involved during combat as you're meant to exploit elemental weakness and use your Einherjar to help you build up the stun bar as well as keep some enemies busy while you deal with others. Once you're a good bit into the game and have unlocked a good deal of divine arts and abilities the combat really opens up and it's an absolute blast to go through.The actual game is linear and mission structured, but said missions are fairly long. You pick where to go to from Valhalla whether it be a main mission or a side quest. On Valhalla itself there's also an Arena where you can practice fighting enemies you've faced before. Everything can be replayed as much as you want, so there aren't really any permanent missables. I do recommend doing all the side quests, because the rewards are worth it and all the extra combat will net you the materials you need to upgrade everything. Once you beat the game you unlock two extra modes. The Seraphic Gate returns as well as a new game mode that lets you play as Hilde.The game isn't particularly long and I had a nagging feeling throughout my playthrough that there was meant to be more to it, but the budget Square gave the devs didn't let them do everything they wanted. Even so, what's here is quite good and despite the slow start once it got going I had a blast playing through it.Given that this is a spin-off by a third party dev it's a perfectly solid and very enjoyable game that unfortunately takes a while before it really begins to shine, so it'll probably turn off some people. If you're expecting Valkyrie Profile 3 or something on par with the first game you'll be solely disappointed, but I admire your optimism nonetheless.  F*ck Square for trying to sell a budget title as a full priced game though. DON'T fall for their tricks. Wait for a sale, preferably 50% off or more. For 30 bucks this is a solid recommendation. Also avoid the Deluxe Edition like the plague unless Square updates it to include Valkyrie Profile 1 like on PS4/5.

They run with you in very tight circles. Enemies have a decent selection of moves. Maybe 3/4/5 moves a piece. Issue is when it comes to parrying, good luck. From slow, medium, to fast and in-between (start slow and instant swing or vice-versa). I love parrying, it is my go to. This game, I cannot zero in on it. Maybe if it is one on one, but when you're surrounded, too much to deal with. Fighting one enemy is impossible. Enemies can swing through one another. That includes throwing magic at you. To fight off one and then suddenly a water/fire ball comes flying through the chest of the enemy you're fighting and knocks you back. Garbage. Small bugs creep themselves into your fights and you'll see them. Again, not the biggest issue (getting stuck on a pebble), but on the harder difficulties, can be your death. Get stuck + get stun locked by enemy = death. The description does say, "For those who are okay dying". But I thought that would be for the punishment of getting hit, not the above mess. Like a LOT of Eastern games. Harder seems to mean beef up baddies and downgrade your character. Annoying. Also, once a difficulty is set, I see no way of lowering or increasing it. So if you pick too easy, your stuck. Too hard, your stuck. Choose wisely. Also, the games check point system overrides your manual saves. never have I seen this. Let me explain. You walk up to a save point. I, always, see about upgrading. Whether it is Valkyrie or her weapons. Typically both. I do all that and two fights later I die. OK. Happens. Reload. It loads the save BEFORE the upgrades. So YOU have to upgrade again, THEN, pick up all the notes / lore, all the chests again and again and again!!! I am loosing my mind with all the terrible decisions. No exaggeration, TWO tutorials (back to back). Not only that. There is something called "Concentration". If you're using a controller, right stick + left stick at the same time... Easy? I agree. However, Square believes you'll forget. So, anytime, and I mean ANYTIME the game deems concentration necessary, it'll be a reminder to the left of Valkrie... floating there. As a constant reminder. Rain, sleet or snow. Or in this case! Running, looting or fighting! And I mean it. (I do want to state this will most likely (hopefully) be patched out.. soon..er then later.. maybe. I don't know. I don't work for Square)This game came out on the Playstation like a month or so ago. You're telling me it is like this over there too!? Wow! Wait for 50% sale or do not buy. This is ridiculous. Square, it is 2022. I am no longer shocked they sold as many IPs as they did. If this is their future, I would liquidate while you can. It may come off acting like a bandit. But at least you get away with something. Because this, this ain't it chief.

_childDocuments_.review: Revised review 2022-11-19This is the most polarizing game I've played this year.Was this game rushed?Is this game a cash grab?Oh wait... I know another Norse mythology game released around this time. Maybe this game was trying to compete with it.SPOILER FREE REVIEWand of course everything is subject to my experience of this gameIn summary:1) Story: yep, there is a story... I guess...- not much to say, but the story was a failure, there is nothing memorable about the plot- only thing that was "good" was the side characters missions and getting them to join the main character- everything else that happens in the plot, left the implication "ok.... sooo? what?"2) very fun yet frustrating combat system.** you would expect a fast paced hack and slash ARPG, but nope, this game functions between a hack and slash and dark souls like game. You can complete the game by rushing down enemies but if you do so, you will most likely take lots of damage, or just die on higher difficulties.TLDR; very awkward game mechanics- spells are probably the best mechanic in the game, and is mostly why combat is fun at all- attack combos mostly feel fluid and are quite enjoyable against normal mobs- attacks have a slight input delay that can make the game clunky at times, especially during boss fights or large mob encounters- against mini bosses and major bosses, the game mechanics are very flawed, why?- when you attack you are stuck in that animation, so you cannot block or dodge and are completely vulnerable during attack animations- there are counterattack skills, but most are useless, because the majority of enemies "guard break" you- counterattack skills that work are "block or attack when enemy is about to hit you" skills, but for even those, block or attack animation must be complete.- cc or stuns are very punishing, once you get hit enemies are likely to chain hit or stun you.- it takes a while to get back up, so by time you get back up, enemies can sometimes be in animation to hit you again.3) all weapons except the first two swords you obtain are TRASH- unless your going to achievements that require maxing all weapons proficiency, there is no point in using the other weapons- the first two swords you obtain are VERY fast and can combo easily, not to mention the combos are straight up superior, there are MUCH more hits or attacks per second, meaning more damage overall. In addition the animations (at least to me) are much smoother and more visually appealing- other weapon animations are just too slow for the game, you will get destroyed by enemies because the animations take significantly longer, and trying to maintain combos is a nightmare because most of the attacks knock back the enemy too far away, which lets enemies recover by blocking, or dodging

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and I feel like it deserves more attention. I played and beat it in about 20 hours on hard mode (which I recommend everyone play it on) and I'll probably be playing it more.Pros:The combat system wasn't too complicated, the fights were all fun and involved, and the different weapons have unique movesets that can fit different playstyles. During my time playing it, I felt like there was always something I could do in a given situation thanks to the pretty wide range of actions I could take. Essentially, you're never left doing just nothing in combat.Admittedly, a lot of the early-game combat consists of the player just spamming the attack buttons (as you might expect for a hack-and-slash), but as you unlock more Arts (magic) and Einherjars (companions), the combat gets way more involved and interesting. Not to mention the dodge and parry systems, which reward you for timing them correctly. This game also has a scoring system to summarize your performance during a mission. Toward the end of the game, your screen will be full of half a dozen enemies getting torn apart by your, your magic, and your companions. The combat especially shined when you were fighting fellow humanoids who dodge, block, parry, and cast magic like you. It was during those fights you really had to utilize your kit properly.Even though all the maps are quite simple, the game does reward you for exploration in the form of items, gems (used to upgrade stuff), and magic. Since the game always has an objective marker and map, you always know which path is the side path.The story was an intriguing take on Norse Mythology. It was a bit jerky at times but overall it kept me interested. The pre-rendered cutscenes were always pretty, but the normal ones were kinda stiff. The voice acting was always good though. Oh, and all the characters are hot.Cons:Unfortunately the camera can be finicky, at least on controller. The right stick is what controls the camera and it also targets enemies/switches targets (so you can't turn the camera manually if you're targeting something). This can be disorienting as your character moves around in combat a lot, causing the camera to jerk around to stay on target. Additionally, some of the magics in the game are very intense and your companions use them as well, which can be blinding if the camera happens to be positioned poorly. The main reward for a good performance in the scoring system are yellow gems, which is an upgrade material used in almost all upgrades. However you will more than likely have more than enough of this gem just from the missions themselves, so the scoring system isn't really mechanically rewarding.In conclusion, I believe this game definitely earns the 8/10 a lot of reviewers have given it. The combat system is where it really shines.

_childDocuments_.review: This game would be a lot better if it wasn't so stiff. Your character is supposed to have the powers of a deity but is less responsive than a Fromsoft character. I don't even mind that it's a character action game instead of a JRPG, and I have played almost every game in this series. It's just frustrating being constantly stuck in animations. And before anyone asks, I'm aware of the guard cancel and it mitigates the problem at best. It shouldn't be such a huge ordeal for a character action game protagonist to not be glued to the ground and stuck in animations, yet here we are. There are multitude of defensive options that feel satisfying to pull off, but the lack of cancels just makes them feel not worth using.Optimization is rough, with the game stuttering and tanking in framerate when enemies or the player produce particle effects/magic, and that's something you do every few seconds in this game. The camera is also your worst enemy, but the stiff player character just makes things even more frustrating. Too often will you get full frontals of the enemy's private regions, and since you're likely stuck in an animation when this happens, sometimes it feels like damage you take isn't your fault.In terms of people disliking the game because it's not a JRPG, I think this game has potential even as a longtime fan of the series, but Squenix was never going to give this game more than a shoestring budget of $5 and expired cat food. This game has clear design flaws even as just a character action game with context-free combat rooms; I can't imagine what it would be like with this same budget being required to make a full-fledged JRPG. The Valkyrie Profile franchise has never  stuck to the same idea more than once, and even the first and second game are vastly different gameplay-wise. Having this be a character action game isn't unusual for this franchise, I just wish the stiff combat and camera didn't make it such a frustrating experience.There is almost no postgame content in this, which is a major flaw as the game opens up when you interact with its many progression systems. It is blasphemy for a character action game to have no NG+, as games like this don't really start until the end of the first playthrough. Between this and the port's arbitrary 60FPS cap and aforementioned issues, it's hard to recommend this at its base price. There are better character action games out there for much cheaper, with better balanced and more responsive combat. The patch that launched with this version does add some postgame content, but the Hilde mode is basically identical to the format of Vergil in the DMC special editions (being dumped into the campaign as a different character with no context, and STILL no NG+) and the Seraphic Gate is essentially a randomized Bloody Palace. The latter would be mostly enough for me if I enjoyed the core combat more, but it feels like I fight the unresponsive character and poor camera than the enemies themselves.Buy DMC5 and Assault Spy for cheaper than this game, and you'll likely have a much better experience. If someone mods more responsive cancels on dodging, blocking and weapon switch cancels, this game would be a better purchase. If anyone is up to do this for a commission, please hit me up in the comments!

_childDocuments_.review: Another solid showing from Soleil team. It's not without it's flaws (Levels can go on too long on higher difficulties, the tether can be finicky at times, you can be bursted incredibly easily when caught in a barrage of attacks unawares or without resources), but it's a successful ARPG framework, with combat and system interconnectivity that, once you get a bit further in, punches a bit above its weight. My particular favorite components are the Magic tether, which, despite the finickyness I mentioned before, serves as an incredibly useful ground and aerial gapcloser thatoffers gameplay benefits, such as a unique set of attacks that offer bonuses for pulling off, as well as some downsides to help balance out the massive utility gain.  I also greatly enjoyed the balancing of the magic system, which builds as you attack (or your einherjar / summons attack) and, upon use, offer you invincibility for the duration of the spellcast, allowing a moments reprieve as well as ensuring that your cast won't be interrupted, allowing you to utilize the system both defensively and offensively at the same time.The parry / Just guard / Just evade mechanics also work incredibly well and promote and encourage skilful use of your defensive options.The biggest flaw, gameplay wise, is the lack of sufficient enemy variety and what can feel like some cheap enemy types (particularly, the bulbous core enemies that emit smoke) that can easily catch you unaware with surprisingly quick attacks or abilities that obscure large areas. The different elemental variants of enemies do a little to switch things up here and there but, largely, you'll be facing similar enemies throughout the majority of the runtime which, despite my 38 hours shown at the time of this review, is thankfully not too long, most reports I've seen seeming to clock in around 12-15 hours max.One thing I'd like to point out is that, despite the game's obvious budget, I found the game to be rather appealing graphically (a somewhat bland color palette notwithstanding) and containing some surprisingly good cutscene camerawork at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, recommended, but don't expect much. Or at least, don't expect this game is on par with the Valkyrie Profile saga. Details below.The Good Parts:1.  GameplayThe core gameplay is quite fun, I enjoy these simplistic combat. It feels like playing a much easier DmC or Nier Automata.2. Visual2. Graphic is also nice. Vivid environment with a hint of art on the character model.Aside from these two good points, I noticed this game has a two major flaws:1. Story lineThe story line its so basic and predictable. Maybe its not easy to create action game with rich story, but game like DmC or Nier Automata can pull it off. So big name like SE should have no excuses to pull it off too! The character development here is nonexistent, saves for the Valkyrie with a teensy weensy character development at the end of the story.2. The Game DesignThis is what I feel like the most fatal flaw. Feels like the game is rushed so they did not give the design enough thought.Case 1: We do have SP to cap which skill we want to equip. But with all available skills equipped, the total matches with our SP cap that we have at the beginning. What is this for?Case 2: The items. Use of items are discouraged here, the game will penalized your score for using items. But almost all treasure chest contains items. Then they put an item limit in your inventory, if its full, you won't be able to pick up anymore item from treasure chest. So many of the treasure chest I found feels useless since I'm not using any items.Case 3: Equipment. Einherjar is ok, since you only have 4, you will always have quick access to them since you can equip them all. But how about weapons? 2 out of 4 of my quick slot is fixed on items that I'm discouraged to use by the game and it cannot be changed. Moreover for magic we only have 4 slots while we have lots of Magic types. I'm forced to pause the game and update my equipped Magic. Its not fun for an action game. Action game should aim to have a smooth uninterrupted action.Lastly, let me add one more bonus review that self explaining: ANIMATION LOCKSOverall, still enjoyable game to play, as long as you tone down your expectation to not expecting too much. Treat this as a separate game and not one of the Valkyrie Profile franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I've now played this game for about 7 hours in one day. I'd bought a bunch of new bits & I was giving them a quick look to see if there was any crap I should return - I VERY rarely do that. I certainly didn't think I would with this... the more I play it, the more I love it. It's all about perspective - I made a comment in my initial review that I look at this as a third person beat em up - it has more in common with that than it does a JRPG. I've come to the conclusion that this games strikes middle ground between Shredders Revenge & Elden Ring - it's certainly nowhere near the behemoth of gaming that is Elden Ring - but you know what - sometimes I really just can't be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ to play Elden Ring; I just want something that oferes instant gratification & less intense game play, and as for Shredder's Revenge... well... Im 42 years old, been there & done that 30 years ago. I really don't have time for the past, especially when games have only gotten better & the only nostalgia I ma interested in is my mum's shepherd's pie.The simplicity isn't a negative IMO; I play all sorts of games & I skip cut scenes frequently unless it's a VERY story driven game. I don't need deep character arcs & relationships in every game. I've been playing games for 37 years & this is back to basics with the lack of  full on story approach. The gameplay is just superb - the combat, although nothing as technical as a souls like, is absolutely fantastic - fast, fun & super satisfying. I'be paid $60 for games I  bought months ago & haven't played as much as this. For me, this game is objectively a 9/10 & it's absolutely one of the games of the year for me. A huge, huge surprise. My initial thoughts after 3h below.---Given it's in a sale for just less than half price, I am definitely giving this one thumbs up - but this is no a $60 game - but then again, what really is???I think this game needs to be looked at on face value. If you're a fan of the series, I can understand you want a new Valkyrie JRPG.For around $30 bucks, it's great fun! It's essentially a 3D, third person beat em up - I know people call these 'hack & slash', but the truth is it's essentially what you'd get if you took a game like TMNT : Shredders Revenge & made it 3D. I think the combat is far more satisfying than any such beat em up - it feels great, you can pull of some great combos mixing magic with your blade & you're constantly learning new skills/getting new magic abilities & you feel like a bit of a badass smashing all of the enemies up. Summoning squad members for certain parts is also fun... basically there are enough little new additions to keep you going. I really don't need a story for such a game, and it's pretty threadbare - and I really could not care less.Sometimes you just want something that is fun & does not require a ton of thought - this fills that gap very well indeed.Don't buy it for $60. Don't expect a life changing gaming experience - but do expect a damn good time.It's exactly what I wanted it to be based om gameplay footage I'd seen & from an objective standpoint, it nails it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hard to review. 5 hours in, I can confidently say that I'm in love with the game. I absolutely love Valkyrie Profile, it's one of my top-10 games of all time. No chance of this game ever sniffing the top 10 or anything close to it. I absolutely love modern action games. Bayonetta 2 is one of my top 10 games of all time, I absolutely love it. This game, again, not even close. This game feels only nominally connected to the Valkyrie Series. It's got the look right, it's got the vibes down. The music is able to evoke the classic the classic Motoi Sakuraba soundtrack, through clever bits of sampling and other tricks that I probably don't consciously notice,  without managing to sound anything like it, which is an interesting feat. The graphics are very good but make some interesting choices. The levels feel large and rewarding to explore. At first glance I assumed it was an open-world game like Nier Automata but it's more of a dungeon crawler with distinct missions and levels. It's level-up system has a little more thought put into it than XP+skill tree, but so far it doesn't feel like I'm locked into any specific "build" and I would anticipate that the endgame is probably pretty similar for everybody.The combat is the star of the show here, in true "Valkyrie" fashion. The original Tri-Ace Valkyrie Profile turned turned-based RPG combat into an exhilarating, almost arcade like action sequence that made every battle exciting and never tedious. This game is not so revolutionary, though likewise never boring. The action feels very "Platinum Studios" like but just seems to be lacking that certain something that makes Nier feel so amazing. The combat here is excellent, but at this early stage in the game, for me, feels like a tier below. That said, I've had this game for a few days now and I can't stop thinking about it. There is a "vibe" to this game that feels familiar yet unique and it feels good to immerse yourself and let it wash over you. It feels like it's a mod or 2 away from something amazing, I don't know anything about the developer nor their plans to continue to support, tweak, or create new content for this game but I hope they and Square-Enix haven't just "moved on". If you're craving more Nier, this is a good place to start. If you love the Valkyrie series, I think this is the best entry since the original, which was also divisive upon release and took years to gain a following. 6 hours in, I don't think Valkyrie Elysium is quite the game that Valkyrie Profile is, but it's still very fun and perhaps by the time I've played it like 20 hours I'll feel differently.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love the Valkyrie series, I must say I was mostly disappointed with this game. I'll try to give unbiased opinions here, and will not sugarcoat anything bad I've seen.I waited until I finished the game (no platinum, I'm not a ♥♥♥♥♥♥), but I saw that there is an ending I am yet to get, so I'll edit if it changes my opinion. I'll divide the review by topics.They are not new gen whatsoever, but who cares? Graphics don't define a game.It is... ok. Whilst action RPGs are so proeminent nowadays, the combo system is decent and the tag-team mechanics with the Einherjars is quite nice. However, the goods are good, but the lows are very low. The camera in this game is just like Dark Souls, and if you have played it, you know this is not a compliment AT ALL. The common enemies attacks, while not impossible to predict, are quite hard to parry or dodge due to no wind-up. Some of them are almost instant. Some enemies are obnoxious to fight (like the mandrakes), and the combat is so hectic sometimes that you get easily hit by stuff off-screen, or even by the enemy you're fighting due to the sheer amount of effects (like Taika's Ifrit Embrace). If you lock-on an enemy, good luck. The lock-on has no depth, as in, if you push the stick forward or backwards, it doesn't change the target, only swiping it sideways. The boss battles are also decent. They have their mechanics, but some of the attacks are either too fast or too delayed, so it's kinda hard to dodge or parry. Some enemies have multiple hitable limbs and the camera doesn't help at all.The effects, particles, everything are detailed enough to notice, and I give props to them for that.Magic is broken. Always use magic. But the enemies can dodge them, so use with care.I, for one, am not picky with things. But after playing all the other Valkyrie games... only 4 Einherjars? Where is the flexibility? This was one of the lowest lows, but I can understand why: all other Einherjars in the other games were mostly "fodder" since you'd use around 3 or 4 and give the rest to Valhalla and call a day. Why make so many new Einherjars if only 4 would appear in the story, after all?I really, really, really had good expectations for their stories as well. They could be developed so much, yet all we got were some lines of text being voiced. No images. No fighting. No seeing actual events. It was boring to say the least. I did hear all of them, and it would be so much better if we had a sidequest showing the past or something.Oh boy. I am not someone that is too fond about the story of most games, but I've always given some care to Valkyrie's. But this one... it's bad. Just... plain bad. The story is slow to develop, and once you think it is picking up the pace, it gives you a middle finger and tells you to wait. Valkyrie only starts to develop around 3/4 of the game, but at this point you probably just want to end the game and won't care about her story anymore. Her Einherjars play a decent role on her development, but it's just... too late. The game seems to have three endings and I've gotten two of them, one being so bland, abrupt and unexpected that I couldn't help but laugh through the credits. I am yet to get the third ending, and I plead to the gods that it is good.The story could develop in a neat mid-Ragnarok Norse fantasy, but the lack of development, even between the first two characters, makes it slow and boring.If you have played FFXIII, you'll know what I'm saying. Valkyrie Elysium has closed "corridor" maps and I can see it not pleasing everyone. The exploration is just some side routes you go for a chest or an item, sometimes (and I mean it) a puzzle. Sidequests are Nioh-esque, you just come back to a specific portion of the map, do something, sidequest ends. Einherjar "development" is through these, but as I said, no cutscenes or past showing. Just you killing some stuff and the Einherjar commenting on something. There's no open world, don't come expecting this.It feels somewhat fluid and you can get every upgrade in a single playthrough. Around the middle of the game you get super difficult sidequests (to the upgrade state you're in) and the damage might feel unbalanced, but by the end you'll steamroll through everything. Unfortunately the sheer amount of weapons from past games is gone, and we're stuck with just a few.Being frank, it could be a little more minimalistic, but the UI/HUD doesn't hinder you gameplay by any means and everything is well explained. The game has two tutorials, in fact, one being the actual tutorial and the second being all the pop-ins you get when you start getting stuff (like your first Einherjar puzzle). Most of the pop-ins should be just disabled because you've gone through the tutorial already.The enemy executions are in a weird place. I've tried both automatic and not automatic, but it feels the same, sometimes it work, sometimes it doesn't.Game has many languages, so that's nice too.It feels repetitive when you're walking around the map, changing when battles happen. Character themes and boss fights are super good: after all, it's the master Motoi Sakuraba (from Dark Souls) that we're talking about. But some tracks feel... empty because you probably won't give two cents about most of the characters. Overall, it's a good soundtrack and the final boss track (of the not-apparent true ending) S L A P S.Valkyrie Elysium came trying to embrace a new population of players, but it did a mediocre job at best. In my ratings, I have weighted "Combat" and "Story" with "Einherjar". Don't pay full price AT ALL.The game is mediocre and should be treated as a pastime.Now, I shall keep playing it, because Valkyrie's smile warms my heart. I hope you have enjoyed my insights.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't dislike the game, but it's really hard to find good things to highlight to prospective buyers.It's a bit short and any plot twists are very predictable, especially if you have played one of the  previous games.  It's not bad, but a lot of it almost feels spoiled by the previous games and you would be better served having never played them.The gameplay is fun, though it isn't particularly tight.  It has an elemental stagger mechanic which adds a bit of depth, but it doesn't feel particularly satisfying when you've triggered it.  Plenty of different weapons and spells, though the limit on your action bar of 4 spells might have you swap them in and out over the course of a level.Characters aren't very deep, which is a shame.  You spend a lot of the game with companions, but their characterisation amounts to a series of side quests that basically amount to "I've refocused myself".  I feels a bit underdeveloped and really feels like there was a real limit of budget that caused story and characters to suffer as a result.It's a good enough looking game with a bit of style, but it can sometimes look mismashy with the lightly cell-shaded/painterly character models with the mostly grey and brown blandness of the environment.Overall, it's just above a mediocre game, but it's still worth playing at the right price.  I would recommend it at a deep discount as there is at least 20 hours of game to be had here, plus some additional side story content.

_childDocuments_.review: Like most people, I got this game because of nostalgic feelings for the VP series of old. I wasn't expecting much from this game. Therefore, I wouldn't say that I was disappointed. The combat is actually quite fun, and your kit quickly expands as you progress. I was actually going to write my review after getting further into the game, but it suddenly hit me. What sets this game back for me is that the RPG (or rather XP and stats) aspect of it is entirely unnecessary. This game would be much better served by being a full-on AA action game because all of the RPG elements only amount to busywork. All upgrades being reduced to functional upgrades (no extra damage/defense, those could be confined to the runes system) would have made this a more streamlined and, IMO, fun experience. You would be free to experiment with every new weapon without a pointless power-up system that only serves to pad the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun so far and I will finish it, but as a long-time lover of the series, I was really expecting a lot more. For one thing I wish it was twice as long, and there's a lack of really amazing cut-scenes (having the opening be a static drawing and some narration was bad decision, and none of the endings have really impressed me so far, either). The lack of minimap and the inability to buy potions or farm without completing an entire level is also sloppy. I didn't mind the smaller cast of Einherjar, but I would have liked to have seen more of them. Their backstories are all given with voiceover narration, which was disappointing and not-fun to click through. And I had hope that the two aftergame modes might fill in some blanks or offer a new experience, but they are just clunkier versions of the regular game. The review isn't a hard no, it's not an awful game by any stretch. It just really doesn't live up to the first two at all.

_childDocuments_.review: First, a video reviewDon't forget to like it )The Will of the Allfather. Valkyrie Elysium ReviewThe spiritual successor to Valkyrie Profile in action-rpg incarnation.The story itself and the characters involved don't really catch on, and the arcs of the protagonist and her partner einherius are terribly banal. One has amnesia and the other has a mysterious past.The stories unfold weakly, and 99% of the clips and dialogues lack even minimal staging. The characters are barely moving mannequins, gesticulating sluggishly and saying the same thing over and over again. Your hand is drawn to the button to skip the boring dialogue. That said, the game has a whole encyclopedia of terms and descriptions: both monsters and heroes. It's a lot of reading, but there's a question of who might be interested in it. It looks like an attempt to cram into the text what did not have enough budget in the gameplay.For example, some of the "characters" are dedicated descriptions in the encyclopedia, but in the game you do not meet anything other than a couple of references to the name and a couple of sentences about the hero of the partner Valkyries.Although, fans of reading notes will definitely like this.Not everything is smooth with the story chapters, of which there are nine in the game. Yes, they are long, and passing 100% can easily take an hour of time. The locations are varied and the game regularly throws up new enemies.However, half of the chapters is a return to an already completed location, where you have to walk the path, for example, in the opposite direction. Of course, previously inaccessible parts of the level open up, but backtracking is still present and striking.The chapters themselves are linear and it is impossible to get lost, but the game still made a marker to the goal for some reason. And if really nemogogotu it is possible to open the map. Benefit from this is - it displays all the lore flowers and side quests.ResultIt's a strange situation. Valkyrie Elysium is not a bad game, but it's hard to call it good either. It is an optional fall release, which can be played, as they say, without a fish.It is not too long to get bored, but the plot is not able to captivate and give any emotions. The characters don't really catch on, and their stories are boring and sparse.Battles are interesting, but only until you start using the same effective combat strategy mentioned in the text above.In the end, it turns out that Valkyrie Elysium is a game for show. Created to plug the hole before Square Enix's next big release in the form of Forspoken.On the other hand, thanks for that as well. Fans have wanted a new game in the Valkyrie series for a long time and they got it.Albeit in a way that's far from a masterpiece.66 out of 100

_childDocuments_.review: Foreword: Sorry for any mistakes, but english is not my native language.Now for the review: This 'Valkyrie' game was the first (and probably) the last game I ever buyed from this series. I just gave it back shortly before finishing the first chapter, because I was reaching the 2 hour refund limit and I literally had nearly 0 fun.Graphics (4/10): Felt like they tried to bump up the last generation graphics for PS4. Not super bad, but not as good as you would expect from a brand new 'Square Enix' game with a well known franchise. The enemies at the begining are so similar, that they look like a re-textures of others of their kind. Maybe they are. The worst part (and point killer) is, that they kept the damn console rendering distances and FPS limits (60). Some objects (like flowers) literally spawn 5-10m before you out of thin air. And I had ever setting maxed out.Sound (5/10): Casual music that you would get to hear in any 'nordic' or 'medieval' game and a really plain and sometimes bored Valkyrie voice-over. To be fair: I just tested the english voice, since I hadn't more time before reaching the refund time limit.Gameplay (5/10): The developers liked the Dark Soul games and The Witcher 3. That's obvious. Attacking with combos, casting a spell, summon an 'Einherjar' - there is much to do. But when the game continues as it starts, then you don't need much tactics on the 'Normal' difficulty anyway. Dodge, hit and repeat. The skill system seems a bit weak and you have to use a limited amount of 'CP' to 'equip' learned skills, even when they are passive. Talking about 'old school'. Could not really test the upgrading system, but it allows you to broaden your attack repertoire, when equipping certain weapons.Levels / World (3/10): They obviously didn't want an open world game, but they created wasted, empty levels with only some enemies and way to much collectibles anyway. Do you like invisible borders at every corner, like they did in the good old gaming world? Here you will get them. Maybe the later level designs are better, but I highly doubt it. Oh and there are riddles... the tutorial tells you how to use your 'Einherjar' to solve them...Story (?/?): I didn't play long enough to say much about this topic. But the beginning was kind of 'casual' without much 'WOW!' moments. I personally didn't like a 'thin, blonde, curly haired' Odin.Overall (4/10): I would not recommend this game for this price. Maybe I'm just spoiled by Final Fantasy from the same publisher here.

Like many Japanese PC ports, there aren't very many graphical settings to tweak. The game shows its cards through the tutorial and doesn't improve much beyond that. It just feels very uninspired. Square brought back a cult series like this to try and make a quick buck while also putting in zero effort or giving it a decent budget. It just rubs me the wrong way and I can't really recommend this to anyone due to how expensive and mediocre it is. A budget game should be priced accordingly. _childDocuments_.review: I'm very torn on how to rate this game. I did the old "try it before you buy it" approach (that's why I have 8h on record, but my save is 22+ hours), and I like what I saw so much I actually bought the game and finished it. So I can't really give a negative review of a game I bothered finishing, but there are many flaws...The combat and the combat animations are the stars of the show...I liked that part a lot, but pretty much everything else is either mediocre or bad. Even the combat has a big problem holding it back, in the form of the absolutely TRASH camera and targeting system. Other then that....story is pure garbage, especially considering how easy it would be to have a good story about Norse mythology; music is generic; graphics are nice, but the performance is pretty bad; level design is bad (like most of these Japanese action-brawler type games). If this game had another year of just polishing everything up and maybe adding more interesting characters, it could have been a classic...but as it turned out, the 60% positive reviews are pretty much on point. For me  the combat carried it because I love these types of games, but I can totally understand people hating every bit of it, so just be aware of what you're getting into. Also, I only paid like half price for the game on sale, it is in NO WAY worth 60$, even 30 is a stretch.

_childDocuments_.review: A simple action RPG with a battle system taking cues from games like Devil May Cry and the like. Valkyrie Elysium has some rough spots, but has even more potential. The combat feels weighted but fast, something like one of the early God of War games. The story is standard fare with the genre, you're here to fight monsters, purify enemies and kill a god. The unique part is that unlike many JRPGs, you get to choose which god to kill, and you get different endings to choose from. The supporting cast seems shallow like the protagonist is at first, but their stories can be discovered through sidequests and unlockable audio dramas.This is a great action game, if you can tolerate some basic visual issues (or you use ReShade) - none of them are game breaking. I like the game. :)

_childDocuments_.review: This will only be a review of the port itself, since I've spent a decent amount of time messing around with it but haven't played much of the game yet.First off, it's capped at 60 fps. It runs fine but there is some minor stuttering that happens frequently. The framerate cap can be overriden by using Universal Unreal Engine 4 Unlocker but when I unlocked the framerate it introduced even more stuttering. I ended up just dealing with the default cap because the stuttering was much more bearable and I got used to it after a bit.Now the other issue.. upscaling is half-broken. I say half because it does work effectively, but only on "low" settings. I can confirm this being the case for DLSS and I've heard the other upscaling methods are broken in the same way but I can't confirm that. DLSS works perfectly fine on low though, and does improve framerate. Medium and high settings completely tank the framerate and I couldn't see any benefit. Normally I'd expect a patch to fix it but this is Square Enix we're talking about, so don't expect anything.Other than that, I'd say it's an acceptable port but not perfect. There's enough graphic settings to choose from so it's not bare bones and it runs well enough. It's just a little disappointing that there's some stuttering and broken DLSS support. But I guess it wouldn't be Square Enix if something wasn't broken

_childDocuments_.review: This is a 7/10 game, Valyrie Elysium is a solid AA experience sold at a AAA price, and published by a AAA publisher, go in expecting it to be ok, and you'll be fine. (sadly, I was expecting higher things from it).Now that I told you it's ok, let's get into the meat and potatoes on what the hell this game does to bother me.________________________________________________________________  Valkyrie Elysium is a game Square-Enix released as a 60 dollar game in 2022, Valkyrie Elysium is also a game that they sold at a 35% discount 2 months after it came out for the winter sale.  Valkyrie Elysium is a game that wants to be a character action game with dodges, parry's combo meters, and many moves and weapons to learn over your playthrough, but at the same time the game wants to be an action RPG, with branching skill trees, AoE magic, summons and many a resource bar. It tries to do both, and becomes a slog of a game to finish because of.   Valkyrie Elysium's combat hits a brick wall at the 11 hour mark (maybe sooner or later depending on how many sidequests you do as the become available). The enemy variety is very limited, usually only having 2 types of enemy fight you at a time (I beat this game on hard for my playthrough, and the game wasn't the least bit challenging outside of the lack of resources some fights give you, until the final boss fights).   Each enemy has a weakness you can abuse with your summons, and a weakness to one of the weapons you unlock during your playthrough, using both of these at once eliminates any challenge a mob of enemies can dish out due to every spell cast you make giving you invincibility frames (one of the only ways to have them in the entire game, actually) on top of that, once you pick a summon, if you use a spell with the same elemental type as it, the spell is empowered which lets you decimate mobs on enemy monsters even quicker.  There is a skill tree in this game, it uses multi-colored gems as the currency for it, each zone has certain gems that can drop, which means you get stuck unable to upgrade things a lot if you go for sidequests, you just run out of options you can purchase. I had an excess of 14,000 purple gems by the end of the game, and had to grind out rainbow gems for an hour because the last level (the only place you can get them) doesn't have sidequests, so I just had to play Chapter 8 3 times instead. You also use these gems to upgrade your weapons, which makes the 14,000 extra purples very sad, and the extra playthroughs of that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ swamp level all the more annoying.  This game uses each boss fight at least twice, (many of them are 3 time fights, like the Dark Valkyrie), and this is even more apparent when you fight the same boss for your accompanying Summon characters future side quests. The boss fights are largely just races to see if you can chain-stun them before they unintentionally dodge your spells and you run out of arts charges and have to wail a 40-hit combo onto them to refill it. Speaking of combo, I got a 999 hit combo and it literally does nothing but give resource generation, the kicker with this regeneration though, is that to get it you have to let the combo fall off, which means you have to not summon anything, and not hit the enemy, which forces you into up to 20 seconds of dodging projectiles in a game where the camera likes to ♥♥♥♥ with you.Short story long, this game is flawed. But it was personally worth it for me, I'm a sucker for RPG's that try new concepts, and this game was admittedly middle of the road in but production and execution. The combat was really fun until it stopped adding things into the mix, and the story wasn't anything special (it's Ragnarok, if you know what Ragnarok is you can figure it out pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ easily). The characters had fun quirks and little tidbits of personality, but never really went anywhere (it is the end of the world after all, not many places to go), I played with the JP dub and the voice acting was great in terms of voice range and general performance (I don't think the subtitles match up very well like usual, with these localization liberties)

_childDocuments_.review: An underrated jewel of game. I get the mixed feelings some have, but most of what I read is too high expectations. Some people come from Elden Ring, and this is not it. However, it's a great game with 30ish hours of fun, great story (explained through the game, items descriptions and a collection), great characters, superb combat and an interesting (somewhat secret) plot twist.Things I liked:- Everything is clearly explained and information can be accessed later in the collection.- Combat flow is great, you can do crazy combos but still have to pay attention to elemental/weapon weaknesses.- Weapon and character leveling is nice and not grindy.- Valkyrie is gorgeous. She also develops nicely as a character.- NPCs are amazing. Customization is great.- Story has heavy Nordic references with the typical embellishment of Square Enix games.- When you completely develop Valkyrie, she is a war machine, but isn't unstoppable. The challenge will always be there.- The game nicely offers you a clear game save just before branching into the various endings. You can easily reload and play a bit again to see the alternatives.Things I didn't like:- Camera tends to get stuck to the wall when finishing monsters, you lose vision of the field of battle.- The game has 7 elements but you can only quick assign 4. This forces you to go into the menus to switch spells mid-fight which completely breaks the flow.- Game is extremely lineal. Areas are big enough to explore here and there, but the general path to follow is always pointed to you.Bonus tip: Try to collect all the flowers. Specially the green ones.
