_childDocuments_.review: I got excited for this game after watching some content creators I know play and review it, all of who had pretty positive or even glowing things to say about it. I will say this now before I go any farther, if you're like me and thought the game looked cool based on the marketing or press, PLEASE read on.My absolute first impressions were "Oh wow, this feels...slow." Your attacks come out slow, you move around the stage pretty slow. It's not just that the game is slow, there is a run button and speed powerups can be purchased later, it's more that the game feels , a problem that is much harder to rectify. This is compounded further when you play as the boss characters who, while powerful, feel like pushing a bike through mud.But eventually, you push past it. You notice the game has pretty cool tag mechanics that let you interrupt almost anything, and that you can chain your special moves together if you're fast enough. After I experimented around enough, I found a sort of flow and yeah, when you get here, the game actually feels pretty fun. So fun, even, that you might ignore the red flags up until this point or just on the horizon.See, every level you beat, the others get longer and more difficult. Where the first one you tackle has 1 stage and pretty easy difficulty, the next will have 2 stages with the second being considerably longer and more challenging. The last 2 will have 3 stages each, and this is where I have to talk about the difficulty. While the first 2 stages aren't bad, with the second being a reasonable challenge, the 3rd starts feeling a bit unfair around when you fight the boss and the aggression levels and damage start ramping up. And then with the 4th and final stage, you smack headfirst into an unscalable mountain of difficulty.Late bosses have this habit of spawning goons, and they're all extremely aggressive. So aggressive that it's not uncommon to get stunlocked and killed from full health. You can tag as a defensive option though, which can get you out of those situations!...Except, tagging isn't invincible. In fact, pretty much nothing in this game is. If you tag, you will bring out your partner, but they're fully vulnerable as soon as they jump in. And to add insult to injury, the character you tagged with initially is ALSO not invincible, since they have to take their time jumping off the screen first. In that time, again, it's very common for them to be annihilated by the constant enemy onslaught. So the best defensive option you have turns into a prison that can cage you into losing  your characters rather than just one.So, inevitably, you die. But it's ok, the money you've built up to this point can be used as continues! Which you'll really be needing if you wanna see those credits. Oh uh, by the way, even . You read that right, the INSTANT your character is back on screen post continue, they can be hit. Leading to unavoidable damage as you fall helplessly into enemy fire below, losing 2/3rds of your health before being able to fight back.But hey, enough continues and some good fortune and you can beat the final stage. It's now that the game tries to sucker you into its bad ending; if you refuse, you go to the final stage, by far the most BS of all of them up until now. I have no idea whose practical joke this stage was, but I'll say in a game with permanent consequences to failure and limited continues, it felt like quite the kick to the unmentionables. Basically, it's a hallway gauntlet filled with a "who's who" of the most obnoxious enemies in the game. The guys with the twin uzi's win that particular "worst enemy" award, as their bullets not only cover full screen and an INSANE amount of vertical space, but they can fire while offscreen! This means that, before you even see anything, you can get gunned down for over half your health.This slog of a stage goes on for at least 5-10 minutes as well, as you plow through what feels like hundreds of these goons. Finally, you reach the big bad at the end, and the game devs have one more practical joke for you. Remember how I mentioned how unfair the bosses can feel? Well, what if we just...summoned them all back again and had you fight them  It's exactly as ridiculous as it sounds, and once again it's insanely easy to just be fully combo'd to death from any stray hit on a screen filled with attacks.Did I mention yet that your credits go up in price with every one you use? By now, after how unfair Level 4 and its boss were already, you're probably starting to feel that burning a hole through whatever pocket you've got left. And if you run out of credits, it's Game Over. You can use whatever tokens you've accumulated to fund a Continue, but once you're out of those...the run's over. Back to the title screen.Well, it WOULD be threatening, if you couldn't just quickly pause and choose "quit game" before the credit timer counts down. The game has autosave, so you'll be back at the start of the final stage, but you can in theory challenge it as many times as you'd like, though granted you'll be limited by the funds you came in there with. And without at LEAST one or two credits, your odds of beating it aren't terrific.So, say that you do beat getting jumped by every boss at once, congratulations! Now you can fight the silliest boss in the game, complete with a health pool over 2 times that of even the 4th stage boss, and moves capable of hitting for 3/4ths of your health in a single strike! He can also spam moves that hit fullscreen, and finding a moment to hit him isn't easy. If it was a 1 on 1 fight, it'd be annoying but doable. But that's just not this game's MO; instead, mobs constantly flood the screen! All the same extremely irritating enemies will swarm you nonstop, and killing them just makes more of them appear. Couple that with this ludicrous final boss, and you're left with an almost unintelligible screen to manage, filled with all different flavors of death.If you somehow,  navigate all of that and come out victorious, then congratulations! You've beaten the game. And that's when that red flag I mentioned earlier suddenly hits you...No other modes, no time attack or boss rush, no randomized mode that shuffles things around, no online. There is nothing but a threadbare story mode that, even with all the difficulty leaps and frustrating design, will take you just over 2 hours to complete. But there's the rub; once you're done and realize that, beyond unlocking other characters, you just experienced the entire game...it's too late. You've played for over 2 hours, rendering the game ineligible for refund.Now, yes, because of the "roguelite" nature of the game, if you only beat it once you are missing some content. Every level has its own 3 stages, so to see them all you'll need to play the game a minimum of 3 times (since the last 2 stages you pick always have all 3 stages in them). All told, that is maybe around 6 hours of content unless you REALLY want to play all the characters. And while they are kinda cool and have their own quirks, you'll still be taking them through the same exact content with little to no variation, barring whatever lite difference you can squeeze out of the powerup system at the end of stages.For $25, I think that's a very steep ask. I understand the devs put their all into this one, and I really do commend what they've done here. Make no mistake, there is a solid core underneath the issues and barren presentation. But I have to speak as a consumer for a review, and as a consumer my time playing was unfortunately wrought with frustration and emptiness. For everything I enjoyed, there were 2 things that held that enjoyment back.Please, if you've read this far, wait for a sale or a substantial update. That $25 can get you much more.

_childDocuments_.review: Another game from one of my favorite video game series of all time! Playing through Rise of the Dragons was a super fun time that left me wanting more. There are so many things that I think this game does right; variety of characters, customizable story mode runs, special abilities, cool unlockables, and multiple endings. There is a ton of variety when playing through story mode with you being able to pick from four characters right off the bat depending on your playstyle, and then you're given the option to choose in what order you want to take on the gangs. This game is even better playing with a friend in local co-op. The feature to have two endings was super cool and made playing through the game multiple times an even better experience. For all achievements, you’ll have to beat the game a minimum of four times to see all four gang’s full missions (the last one you face being the full mission). The gameplay mechanics are killer and the bosses are super unique. And of course, the Double Dragon soundtrack is phenomenal. If you like the “beat ‘em up” genre, this is definitely a must-have. Looking forward to the next installment in the franchise coming to steam hopefully later this year!Achievement Count: 20Time to 100%: ~7.5hrDifficulty: ★★✩✩✩Genre: Beat ‘em up, Side Scroller, 2DFun Rating: 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: You want to play something with your significant other?There are many fighting games in which we use punches and kicks to beat up the masses of oncoming opponents, but the really good ones are relatively few and far between. In recent years, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge or Streets of Rage 4 were pretty good, but my favourite was Mayhem Brawler. What all these games have in common is that they bring the spirit of the arcade games of the 90s back to the present day. The best way to play such brawlers is together with a friend, and that is of course also possible with Double Dragon Gaiden: Rise Of The Dragons.One of the special features of Rise Of The Dragons are the roguelite elements that appear in many new games today. This is supposed to increase the replay value, but is it really worth it if you have to play a level over and over again to be able to buy "tokens" with which you can unlock new characters and other content? The actual gameplay is good though - you play (at least initially) as brothers Billy and Jimmy Lee (assisted by Marian and Matin), who take on the crime syndicates to restore order in a New York dominated by four major gangs. The mayor is on your side, but pretty powerless. Enemies are dealt with in the usual manner, you simply keep hitting them until they run out of life energy and disintegrate. You can use a variety of punches and jumps to do this, each of the 13 characters in total (nine have to be unlocked first) has a different repertoire of punches. Objects can be picked up, furnishings smashed, boss opponents can withstand considerably more hits. Quite fun, at least as long as you are not getting hit by an opponent over and over without a way to get out of his attacks. All in all, it's a fun trip into the past, especially when you fight your way through the city together on the couch in local 2-player mode.

_childDocuments_.review: The GoodI really like this game and I recommend it for beat-em-up fans, though it plays more like Fight'N Rage than any Double Dragon game.  Very customize-able difficulty makes the game fun for all skill levels.  Being able to have four different final bosses based on the stage selection order is a fun and novel idea and it makes the first few replays very enjoyable.The BadIt doesn't support two controllers.  How can you release a split-screen coop game without working controller support in 2023?  Is this a joke?  Someone should be fired over this.  Manually remapping the 2nd controller to the keyboard with Steam Controller Configuration is tedious but your 2nd player won't work without it.  If you aren't comfortable making custom Steam controller configs, you will be stuck here.  Lots of people will probably refund at this point.The marketing is dishonest.  This is not a roguelike game.  For the one millionth time, RANDOMIZED POWER-UPS DO NOT MAKE A GAME ROGUELIKE.  The marketing says, "Experience endless playthrough possibilities with a dynamic mission select".  You have the choice from 4 levels, then 3, then 2, then 1.  That's 24 possibilities.  That's nice, that's not endless.  After beating all four versions of the final level, I can say there is no significant variation from run to run.  The levels do change based on the order you select them but they appear to always change in the same way.  This is not a roguelike, it's an arcade game, and its replay value will be relatively limited.The unlockable extras are mostly garbage.  Most of what you will be unlocking is concept art, background music, tips and hints that should have been free, and extra stages for versus/survival.  The only good unlockables are the playable characters which range from quite good to laughably bad.All of which brings us to the big problem:  the $25 price tag is much too high.  I think $10-15 is probably the right price point for this game considering the length and depth.  If this game was priced lower, it would probably be getting a thumbs up right now even despite the broken controller support.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember when some third person games first started to include 1 to 1 animation and movement syncing for added realism, directly tying controls to long-winded animations, resulting in sluggish controls? That similar feel is here. Whenever you initiate an action, you are stuck for about a second afterwards, unable to move. This includes things like landing from a jump and at the end of a combo, you have to wait before you can move again. The hold time is a bit excessive.That combined with pretty substantial lag in the inputs, which resembles them being queued up, makes the game feel stiff and slow to play.You're incentivised to bunch people close together then use your special move, dropping rewards in return. This just feels restrictive and slows the pace too much as you run around trying to herd everyone together and they move at turtle speed.There's also a focus on collecting coins which disrupts the flow. Lots of standing around and backtracking to pick them up.Liked the tag mechanic, allowing you to switch in and out characters mid fight to mix things up using different move sets.The bosses are a mixed bag and encounter design is not very good. Many times it throws a few guys at you which are all identical to each other, waits till you finish them, then sends in another group of the same guys. There's not enough attention given to having engaging synergies or timing things interestingly and the overall game flow in general is lacking.Would go for neutral if steam gave the option. It's alright but definitely been the least enjoyable of the newer beat 'em ups I've played. Can't really recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game to old-school brawler fans.  It's phenomenal.  The way they made combos and health and energy and coins and all that flow into one seamless resource... it's just elegant in a way I've not seen before.  I'm 50 and have played a lot of brawlers.  This one does a lot of things I wish had been implemented long ago.  For example... if you combo a big finishing move against 3 enemies at the same time (which means you got their health down to a dangerous level, positioned them, have the required energy for the special move and hit them all at the same time) you'll be rewarded with a small meal that boosts your health.  Catch 4, get a bigger meal.  I think 5 is the biggest.  They stay on the ground for you or your teammate (or your tag character) to eat as needed.  This allows them to throw in endless mooks during boss fights for you to setup as health banks while also focusing on beating down the boss.  This multi tasking adds a lot of excitement to what might otherwise be a repetitive experience once you'd memorized the boss' patterns.  You also have to maneuver around them while attacking the boss so you don't squander their health resources by killing them too early.The fact that an unskilled player can still play the game by mindlessly killing all the enemies in 1's and 2's and getting no benefits but that someone who takes care and plans can benefit greatly from their patience and skill makes for a 'play as you like' sort of experience.  As you raise the difficulty, the skill and planning becomes a necessity.  It's depth that most brawlers lack.There is also the level selection order mattering greatly, but I'll just say that of the 4 options, the first one you choose will last one of it's potentially 4 max levels.  The second 2, and so on to the last zone being the one you go all the way through to the final boss at it's maximum difficulty.  So you have a lot of replay just to see the entirety of all 4 zones.  If you really hate one, go their first.There are a ton of special characters to unlock with the coins you get from the combos.  Those coins also buy you character upgrades allowing you to focus on upgrading the moves and stats that appeal to your play style.  This becomes very handy in Survival mode, which is awesome.  I will say that my favorite character, Abobo, is beyond broken in SM.  You can get him to the point where he cannot lose and goes indefinitely.  I eventually just had to give up because he was never going to lose.  But still a lot of fun getting there.That's the thing.  On top of everything else, the gameplay is just a lot of fun all along.  Give it some time though.  At first I didn't know what the hell I was doing and it seemed awkward and confusing.  When it clicks, it all makes sense.

_childDocuments_.review: “The most in-depth beat ‘em up game that I have ever played” - GameGrinThese people have not played Streets of Rage 4, River City Ransom, Absolver, Sifu, Mother Russia Bleeds, and I'm probably missing a lot.Not a good beat em up, not a good roguelite, the "diverse roster of characters" is a joke, you basically unlock the bosses and mini bosses as playable characters, but - big surprise - they're not designed to be played against a horde of enemies : they're slow, have long wind up attacks, and are easily countered : which is normal ! _childDocuments_.review: For the full review:Double Dragon Gaiden: Rise of the Dragons is an appreciable attempt from a small team of devs who are well-versed in its legacy. Huge character variety, Tag system and the Roguelite elements are welcome additions to the long-stagnant IP, and it can be a genuinely fun game at times. However, it does not always hit the right notes. A criminally short campaign, the lack of additional gameplay modes and the TBA online co-op makes it a tough sell when SoR and TMNT have offer so much more at a cheaper price point. If I were you, I’d wait for some content updates before taking the plunge.

_childDocuments_.review: Literal hot garbage...It's the memberberry edition of Double Dragon... or should I say Devil's Dare? :/ If you hated Devil's Dare, you'll hate this game, plain and simple... The mechanics are absolute jank trash and even on the easiest settings, they will hinder you from enjoying the game. Everything is clunky in this... the jumping, the attacking, the hit recovery... you'll get infinite juggled by enemies and basically die. Without the use of cheat engine and hacking your cash, forget ever enjoying this game... You'll feel so defeated and frustrated the further you get when you wipe to cheap b.s. and have to start over, it only gets more unfair as you progress. You could spend the entire game saving up money and have it all get wiped away in a matter of seconds at the 95% mark of your play through.I didn't die at all until I had to do the 4th mission, then it was just cheap death after cheap death. I died about 6 times on the true final boss just from him attacking me once. If he lands any attack you're basically toast, this game is just a bunch of trash mechanic nonsense.I'll give this game props for remixing some cool tunes from Return of the Double Dragon/Super Double Dragon which is one of the best soundtracks in the franchise next to DD2. There was some Double Dragon III peppered in, very little Double Dragon II, which is a shame and a bunch of classic stuff from DD1. They pulled a lot of tracks from that dumpster fire that was Double Dragon IV which is unfortunate because that game's music was garbage.Either way, this game is absolute trash for a $30 price tag, it's just unfair garbage... This dev basically just threw a Double Dragon coat of paint on top of their garbage coding from Devil's Dare and that's about it. The roguelite elements really butcher subsequent playthroughs as well... You'll feel like you're going backwards when you start a new game up. Thankfully you only have to beat this game 4 times through tops and then it's over. I'm assuming they expected you to beat the true final boss with one of the cheap boss characters like Okada because Jesus H Christ, he's ridiculous if you get within melee range.I would say buy it on sale if you're a hardcore DD fan, like at least 50% off. In all honesty I wouldn't even pay $15 for this... it's a fairly piss poor Double Dragon entry. I just can't understand why every game made today has to play like absolute garbage... it's like these games are made for someone with Asperger syndrome... I don't even get it.If you MUST play this due to your own personal FOMO mental illness. Do yourself a favour and make sure you buy the blue lightning bolt to increase your characters speed immediately. If you don't get a speed increase, you'll be sorry by the end of this game... it's almost unbearable without it. Also the SP recharge skills are a must if you expect to tag in and out on the fly because the game is literally conditioned around you doing this... as soon as you get hit you basically have to tag out and play as your partner to save yourself from getting instant death combo juggled in the air.The art style is subjective, I think it looks OKAY for what it's trying to do which is be all chibi and super deformed, so there's that, if you hate it, you hate it. IMO I would have preferred a much more serious version of DD. A more realistic art style, less cartoonish, with a much darker plot... Also, good game play mechanics wouldn't hurt... just a thought. :/This game feels like you purposefully have to slow down your own reflexes because the recovery frames are so jank that you'll end up mashing buttons and your character will just sit there doing nothing. Don't expect much from this tripe and don't listen to people who say this is even remotely a good game, it's a pile of $hit, those people are just so used to mediocrity their option doesn't count. They didn't live through the silver and golden era of games when quality meant something. It's also just terrible for a DD game because behind the scenes it's Devil's Dare. If I had to measure it to another game in the franchise, this is on par with Double Dragon III for the NES... just absolute cancer.Double Dragon II still holds the torch for the best Double Dragon entry, plot wise and challenge wise. Super Double Dragon / Double Dragon Advance still both have the best game play mechanics in the entire franchise... they're just smooth and give the player so much freedom and control, this game feels like you have a ball and chain attached to your character at all times... it's just off and doesn't feel natural... also the running mechanics are fu<king garbage. You can run left and right, but the fact that you can't double tap the d-pad to run and require a dedicated button to do this is just bush league level programming... Long story short, this game is lazy AF in design.DD Gaiden is a step backwards and I can't help but feel this developer tried to re-invent the wheel but in reality they just copied bad code from a bad game to save on time and resources; Then went and slapped a brand name IP over it so they could jack the price up three times what their original failed project was worth... *sigh* This $hit is so depressing.EDIT: Upon further playing this mess, I managed to save up enough tokens to unlock Okada and The Mysterious Warrior and honestly, these two characters break the game entirely. Their special attacks legitimately allow you to ignore all of the garbage ass mechanics and just spam special attacks over and over. The Mysterious Warrior alone is just an unstoppable power house and Okada is a good long range back up character for cheesing boss fights at a distance.This still doesn't make me like this game, in fact, I hate it even more knowing that the two main characters Billy and Jimmy both suck ass and two of the hardest bosses in the game are the most broken characters to play as... pretty pathetic honestly. I came here to play a Double Dragon game, not some $hitty openbor fan game.

_childDocuments_.review: Plays almost nothing like the original Double Dragons, but neither did Neon. Unlike Neon, this is a solid, nuanced, relatively deep game. And unlike Neon, this game respects the Double Dragon setting, history, and characters... as much as westerners can as we never really got exposed to the story.It is only a roguelite so much as a pure arcade game, which is for the better.There is a lot of interesting ideas in this one. Your iframes are limited, but no boss or enemy has heavy armor against knockdown attacks, so with all the special moves thrown around, offense and defense takes a different flavor than what you are used to. The result is a clever, nuanced game with a good amount to learn. At the high end of play, I'd say there are balancing issues; the game is incredibly punishing and despite all your tools some bosses just have way too many tricks. And on the technical side there are way more softlocks than there should be. But, all the same, DDG is a great breath of fresh air that stands strong alongside the recent beat-em-up releases.

_childDocuments_.review: Double Dragon 2 was a game i played a lot as a kid, yet failed to finish even one level at the time. You didn't need to have 5h long tutorial to keep 4 years old playing back in my days. Just give them one frustratingly good game and have a total amount of a single number of game available to purchase !That being said, it kind of explains why DD kind of fell of my radar.. Until this one, which possess a surprisingly deep combat system. Normal move ? Yes.Unique attack ? Yes.Special attack ? Yes.Grab ? Yes.Dash cancel ? YesAssists ? YesOff the Ground (OTG) attacks ? YesWall Bounce ? YesCommand Grab ? Kinda, yes. Just cancel a normal into a grab. Or a special. Or an assist. Or a special into an assist. An assist into a special ? Yes. Combo ? Did you just read that cancel basicaly what you want ?My god, they made a fighting game. They made a freaking tag fighting game. Because yes, it's a tag game. And a coop one, or a versus one. Depending on which game mode you choose.  And you still both get to play 2 characters.There's also good old 3D beat'em up mechanic progression. Beat the living out of some rando, take half their money like any good 10y old on journey would do and chose an upgrade at the end of the stage. Which will reset at your next run. Which is nice, 'cause it ties down to the difficulty of the game. Will you consume like you're at wallmart on a saturday's afternoon for some powerup or will you save up to buy some token to permanently unlock new characters, art or music ? No microtransaction here, just good old play to unlock.Also, it's nice pixel art, and the music are good, and nostalgic when you boot up and hear the Double Dragon Theme again after 30 years.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Double Dragon IP, but unfortunately this game just isn't what I'm looking for in a Beat Em Up game.First off, this game has roguelike mechanics and it ruins the game. Roguelike mechanics have no place in a well designed Beat Em Up. Having randomized upgrades like this means you can't balance the game properly. There is even an upgrade that increases the "efficiency" of your basic attack combo. Why is that an upgrade? The basic attack combo is the staple of the Beat Em Up genre; you need your basic attacks to feel really good out of the gate, but in this game your basic attacks feel weak and very delayed/slow.The game is designed around abusing your special moves (moves that use the blue meter to perform). Every time you kill 3+ enemies with a super you get a health drop. Also you get bonuses for killing bosses with special moves. Enemies can't block your special moves. These are just way too many incentives to use special moves, and the game is more about spamming your specials than typical Beat Em Up game play.Miriam is a playable character and she is broken (overpowered). She is literally bringing a gun to a fist fight. She is the most overpowered character I have ever seen in a Beat Em Up game. She is a great example that this game just isn't designed to be a well balanced Beat Em Up.The game is very slow paced. Enemies are slow and not very aggressive. There is a massive recovery for even your Character's basic attacks (feels like up to a second to recover from a single basic attack). There is recovery from landing from a jump. I just feel like I'm doing more waiting for my character to recover than I am actually controlling them. This feels especially bad when all you are trying to do is break the destructible crap in the environment to collect money... There is just too much wind-up and recovery time to every single action.I need to make a special note for how worthless grabs are. Grabs are often a key mechanic in Beat Em Ups, but the grabs in this game are a death sentence. Grabs leave you vulnerable to attack. I don't understand why the game was designed this way.I hate the art design. I like pixel/sprite graphics but I just don't like the implementation here. A lot of the animations don't look very good. The game is so bright/light and I don't like it. Billy's weird smile on his character model especially bothers me.Although I didn't run into a ton of bugs, I did run into an issue where on the Asian level one of the ninja enemies clipped out of bounds and got stuck which resulted in a soft lock for me because I had to kill the enemy to continue but it was impossible for me to do so.There are some positives to the game though. I really like the idea of having a tag system in a Beat Em Up. I have personally not seen that before and now I want to see more it in more Beat Em Ups.Another massive criticism I have for the game is a lack of a scoring system and proper leader boards. There are leader boards but they are how many tokens+money you collect and not based on a proper scoring system for how you played. Scoring systems are a great way to add replay-ability to your game so people can keep trying for better scores; The Double Dragon franchise is in a bad place. Double Dragon Neon had issues with balancing due to it's horrible RPG mechanics. Double Dragon IV is a game I really enjoyed, but it didn't resonate with game reviewers and doesn't look like it will be getting a sequel anytime soon. We will likely never get PC ports of some of the important games in the franchise: Super Double Dragon, Double Dragon Advanced, the Nintendo ports of the original trilogy, and Battletoads and Double Dragon (although more of a Battletoads than Double Dragon). I want to see more out of the Double Dragon franchise but I want it to go back to basics and not try gimmicky roguelike crap.Here are some games on Steam I would recommend over Double Dragon Gaiden: Rise of the Dragons...- Double Dragon IV- Streets of Rage 4- Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge- Final Vendetta- The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors- Fight N Rage- The Takeover- Double Dragon Neon EDIT: The developer replied to my review. Thanks for the reply. :) As the developer has mentioned, they have been implementing updates to this game and all the updates so far seem like steps in the right direction. However, my negative review is still accurate at this time, and it would take a lot more updates/changes before I could personally recommend it. :( What I would really like to see is a game mode without roguelike elements with much,  faster paced combat and a proper scoring system & leader board. I will keep an eye on Double Dragon Gaiden: Rise of the Dragons, and hopefully they keep improving it. :)

_childDocuments_.review: The negative reviews don't make sense and all sound inexperienced.  I've played every Double Dragon, and love this one more than the originals.  My friends and I love chaining supers, scarfing burgers, and locking that cash away at the upgrade screens.  (Something you won't hear mentioned in the negative reviews.)  Basically many don't understand the dynamics of the combat system, or don't care to learn before they run back to "crashing castles, and bunga-ing cowas."  Get skilled and start banking that money instead of taking upgrades in between stages.This game plays more like a Street Fighter title than many of the other sidescroller brawlers.  (Including the original DD titles.) and heavily rewards understanding the unique combat styles of each character.I genuinely wonder if people giving it a bad review ever got to eat a burger, or even a hot dog.I say it's worth 20 bucks.  Anything more and you are paying for the DD name.  I do think that just calling it a double dragon game would be a bad Idea.  It's definitely different. "Double Dragon Gaiden."  It's written in the name what you can expect.  If you loved Ninja Gaiden and Double Dragon, and fancy playing a mix of the two, this is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited my review to a recommendation since my complaints were addressed. Full original negative review below since it highlights positives about the game too. Know that my issues have been addressed.I love the beat 'em up revival that we're experiencing right now but this game is a big step back. I love the pixel art, the music is good, and I was enjoying the gameplay at first. However, as the difficulty ramps up, the small frustrations become more apparent and more annoying. One of the worst is enemies that attack you from off screen. Please fix this! Enemies shouldn't attack as soon as they spawn off screen! Now, you might be thinking, well don't hang out near the edge and you won't get attacked and that's true but some of the enemies have long ranged attacks and just start shooting you from off screen. This is so infuriatingly annoying.The game really got on my nerves during the helicopter boss fight. The boss is immune to all attacks except jump kicks and if you make the mistake of jump kicking him near an edge, you have to deal with a long, slow sequence where he is immune again. The fight just takes way too long with many delays and sections where the boss is immune to damage or off screen. Very boring and frustrating. First time I died in the whole game too.The difficulty is fine for the most part but the end of the game starts to get to be too much. I've played all of the big beat 'em ups that have come out and loved them, so I don't think the problem is me. I think the game is salvageable but they need to think about the end game difficulty and also have enemies be less aggressive until they are visible on screen. I will revise my review if anything changes. Right now, this game deserves a "Mostly Positive" rating on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: The "Neutral Special Attack" and "Throws" don't have any invincibility frames, while enemies unfairly have TONS of invincibility during their special attacks.  The controls are great but the movements are just too painfully slow.  Also, the Crowd Control rewards disrupts the flow, especially if multi-players are involved.EDIT:  The Developer responded to my concerns, and addressed most of the issues I raised.  This is amazing and I really appreciate them for making improvements upon listening to customers' feedback.Even with a smoother game play, I still can't recommend this game for several reasons.  Its Rogue-Like style and mechanics might have worked for the one-off success like the "Streets of Red", but it just doesn't pack the same punch as any other "Double Dragon" beat-them-ups that have been consistently made across the industry.  IGN rated "Double Dragon Neon" a 3/10, but I would choose to play Neon over Gaiden any time.  This should really be a $5 mobile game for a Double-Dragon spin-off, instead of a $25 multi-platform game.  I had higher expectations from Arc System Works with its IP distribution.

_childDocuments_.review: Really well made game, lot of replayability and a great beat'em up.The gameplay is really simple, you get quick and special attacks that hinge on a special meter that grows over time, but the game has a ton of feedback to reward you for doing better, you can create crowd control moves by defeating multiple enemies at once that both feel great to perform, as well as reward you with food to give your health back; it's difficult to describe the visual effects that come into play to make this rewarding, but trust me, they make it work really well.The basic gist and gameplay loop of the game is that you get a modular difficulty selection in which you can customize things like: how aggresive enemies are, how many lives you have, how much health, how much it costs to revive, so on and so forth; the harder you make the game though, the more tokens you get out of cash, you obtain cash by defeating enemies and breaking stuff around the enviroment; this is a really good game design choice because it's satisfying to both get the cash to contribute to this tokens, as well as looking it fly out of enemies after defeating them.The game is composed of five levels which you can play in your chosen order, the tradeoff though, is that the levels get more difficult after you complete one, but they get difficult in really fun ways. Like completing a level can make it so there's minibosses in the next one, and you can even make them longer with more elaborate level layouts and more enemies. The levels also have challenges that are generated randomly as you progress, so after defeating a boss you can get a challenge that gives you a ton of cash for performing five crowd control attacks and the like.The token system is one that works after beating all bosses or loosing your run, you get to play as two characters alternating between them at anytime, although the tag mechanic only works by consuming your special meter, so you have to choose between an special attack or a tag, is a good system and it isn't as restrictive as it could be which helps in mantaining the pacing of the game.Once you get enough Tokens you can trade them for a number of things, new characters, tips, concept art, music, etc. It's a really nice system.I think though, what's really cool about the game is that the core gameplay aspect -which is the beat'em up part-, works really, really well, it's incredibly satisfying to go into a room and destroy enemies by using their own weapons against them at times, whilst in other cases you juggle them around; you can even do this in co-op as well if you like.Overall, I'm really happy with the game, there's some critiscisms here and there when it comes to the level layout a few times being a tad bit confusing -the trick is always knowing you're moving foward, never backtracking-, and there's also some issue with some upgrades that you get in your matches not being that significant. But overall? This is a really, really sweet game; I also quite like the aesthetic as well, and the music is pretty darn good too.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: In the past few years, we've seen a resurgence in the 2D Beat 'em Up Genre, with some incredible showings such as Streets of Rage 4, TMNT: Shredder's Revenge and more.  Double Dragon Gaiden keeps that positive vibe going by introducing several fun and fresh features that make it currently one of my favorite beat 'em ups of all time.The genre, originally meant to munch quarters from players in an arcade, became stagnant in the 90s due to a million (not exaggerating by much) soulless and bland clones that flooded the market in both arcades and home markets/consoles.  It was almost impossible in some of these games to NOT die and have to continue unless you had a good trick or exploit to use against the AI.  This lead to some monotonous gameplay over time and a lack of strategy.I feel the "new guard" of the genre including Double Dragon: Gaiden improve and fix these issues left dormant for over a decade.  Combat is very much skill based with player's choices and ability easily allowing you to avoid all damage if you're good enough.  There are a variety of difficulty modifiers to fit any gamer's playstyle for maximum challenge or a smooth sailing beat down of the bad guys.  Traditional arcade experience of 2 or 3 lives and infinite continues?  Set it up.  Want just one life for a roguelike experience and that's it?  Do it!  These difficulty modifiers, as you increase the 'heat' so to speak will give you more currency to spend after your game to unlock new characters and content (for 100% free).Speaking of free, the game now includes a free DLC that adds 3 new fun characters that are fully unlockable from the start for $0.00, which is a fantastic gesture in this modern age of game developer greed.As mentioned previously, gameplay is a far cry from the old days of mashing one button repeatedly and occasionally jumping.  You can look forward to combat using super manuevers (every character has 3 whole supers moves for variety/options), combos, dodge moves, double jumps and even a tagging system.  That's right, you choose 2 characters and will tag between the two each stage!Stages, you say?  Replayability is crazy here as.  You'll choose from 4 target gangs to clean up the city to start, but the order you choose will change the pathway entirely.  Segments will be added to stages, boss fights altered and more, all keeping things relatively fresh as you get to know the game and ultimately clean up the city!Overall, between the incredible fighting gameplay and optional rogue-like elements, Double Dragon: Gaiden has me hooked and is my current leader of the pack in the beat 'em up genre.  Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good beat 'em up that is oddly being advertised and listed as a roguelite.As a beat 'em up, this is fun! Characters play different from each other and you actually get to pick a 2 character tag-team per player with the ability to tag at any time as long as your auto-regenerating special meter is full. The combat is a little different than most beat 'em up in that this is deliberately designed around doing special moves to land special KO blows on crowds of enemies at once to get guaranteed health/money drops. When this happens a huge splash screen pops up with your a tiered health and money item drop at 3 KOs, 4 KOs, and 5+ KOs at once. It's fun but at stock difficulty this makes the game a bit too easy when you have guaranteed health drops so often. I actually one credit cleared this on my first playthrough so I would really recommend turning up the difficulty sliders if you're experienced with the genre.That said, calling this a roguelite feels like false advertising. This is a standard beat 'em up with a random single upgrade per character offered between stages. That's really all that you can loosely say that ties into the roguelite genre. Levels are not procedurally generated and there is no permanent upgrade system that is making your character stronger between "runs". Purchased upgrades also do not fundamentally changing how you play so there really is not the replay value and variety that you would expect to see when a game is listed as a roguelite. You also only can spend your awarded "tokens" upon completing a playthrough on things that are very standard to traditional beat 'em ups like unlocking alternate characters, music, and artwork.Skip it if you're looking for a roguelite but give it a shot if you're fine with a fairly traditional beat 'em up.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty clear that the reviews with less than an hour played or did one run were a little early on giving a thumbs down to this game. This game is actually super dope.- There are THIRTEEN characters in this game and they all feel different! All characters have different movesets and specials making mixing and matching really fun. Every character comes with a standard X and Y move, B for grappling and every character has 3 different specials to use. Some characters seem way better than others but it's all a matter of personal preference. I particularly like grappler dudes and Uncle Matin and Abobo feel so good to play especially when the enemies start getting into bigger groups as the difficulty rises and you take one dude and piledrive him into a group of his friends. Uncle Matin's Right Trigger move is especially my favorite because he can catch anything in the air and just yeet it at enemies, super fun to play volleyball with those pesky ninja dudes. But being able to actually play as Abobo is truly special haha.- The combo system is extremely fun in this game. This game isn't so much technical on the movesets like Streets of Rage 4 was but this game goes for a different approach, something more akin to Jitsu Squad (another tag team beat em up you should check out if you haven't). Everything is related to your combo bar and you can fill that bad boy way faster than you're used to in other beat em ups. The more enemies you kill on screen, the more you can just chain kill groups of enemies if you're utilizing the all the buttons on your controller or keyboard. You can combo a special into another special, combo a special into a tag team move, etc. The combo bar controls the specials but also when you can tag in and out but you can chain everything together as long as your bar is blue. It makes for some very fun moments when you kill tons of enemies at once. Enemies dying together with a special move is a fun mini game in its own right. The larger your combos, the better the food you get for heals. Food combos start at 3 for the smallest food heal and you get a 100 heal (or money if you're full on health) for killing 5, etc. and everyone big combo kill is greeted with a stamp of approval and a dude commending you along with a pic of the food item that's about to drop. I still don't know how I feel about that part but it is a nice break on my old thumbs. What also makes this system fun is that you can still get a "special kill" on enemies even when their HP bar is drained. As long as they don't disappear, and they will after the special kill, you can still combo the body. I think the game would feel a little too easy if you could just combo endless groups because they would just keep dropping food.- The game is pretty much controlled by in game currency. There's also some special objectives to complete per stage to get more money. Every enemy defeat has them popping out with coins and special meter orbs. When you beat a round, you get to a selection where you draft upgrades for both of the characters you're controlling. I don't feel like I can comment too much on the roguelite part but there are really fun ways to enhance your attacks and some attacks even change animation depending on what skill you bought. With all the characters in the game, I'm sure there is at least some build variety bound to happen.- There are 4 worlds and you choose the order to tackle them and you start by clearing out a world with a boss then the subsequent stages get longer by 1 with increased enemy stats and groups with a mini boss at the end of a stage and a boss at the end of the world.- Music is also pretty baller as well. I think for 25 bucks it's a large ask, just like any other beat em up doing the same, but this one I feel like at least has some replayability with how it's structured. Unfortunately there's no online co-op which is a huge bummer but it's apparently planned in a future update. There's also a level with these spear traps that is just really annoying since items can drop on the spears too. Overall though, I like the package as a whole!

_childDocuments_.review: For starters I am not going to bore you to death with how I am old enough to remember riding my bike to the yogurt shop to play the arcade version of the first Double Dragon back when it was new.  Or how the main characters were named Hammer and Spike back then. Or when I first learned to throw elbows out, which is still my preferred method of attacking. Or when it first came to NES and my buddies and i would crowd around the tv to see how far we could each get. Or beating...both versions.But I probably already did bore you with it. So lets move on...just know I am:1. old!2. a big fan of the series from when it started.Since then Double Dragon has been, well, not as fun as the first. Each release seems to get less and less play time with me. I enjoy playing them, but the magic just isn't there. So hearing about this one didn't really get me all that excited. Curious...but not jumping off the walls happy. (And this is probably a good thing...since I said I was old, all that jumping might not be good for my joints. And my physical therapist will want to have some not nice words with me...)Oh wow, did I not expect this to happen. I bought it thinking that I might not get much play out of it yet...but when my buddies come by, I would get more co-oping it. And that was so very wrong....I went in to test it both on my pc and my steam deck (which it plays right out of the box on the deck). Test means a few mins of play to make sure it appears to be working. That testing turned into almost an hour, including hitting 10 tokens on one play, and already unlocking Adobo, Chin, and Linda. I am freaking addicted to it already, and can't wait to try remote play. I haven't been this excited about a Double Dragon game since each time riding to the yogurt shop to play the arcade. I haven't been this excited about a brawler since I first touched the Turtles arcade game. This game plays fantastic!If you are an old school brawler like me that doesn't mind dying and starting over, then get this. Set permadeath and everything to high...score tokens...and then cash them out and start unlocking the characters. Doing the stages over on this one is not boring at all.And that is probably the most important thing that needs to be said about this or any other brawler: starting from stage one with no boosts does not make the game bad. It is still just as fun. And that is the most important aspect of any brawler. it has to be fun or it won't be played more than once.This game succeeds in that....easily.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game!Double Dragon Gaiden sits right atop the Steam beat em' up heap along with Fight N' Rage.The mechanical depth here is impressive. You've got a jump (and you can also double-jump), an attack into a combo, a "special" button that varies per character, and a special move button (which uses your special meter).You can tech-roll to recover from air juggles and also tag out to interrupt your character getting combo'd.When you start the campaign or survival, you pick two characters and can tag out at any time so long as your special gauge is full. Like in the old Marvel vs Capcom versus games, recoverable health of the character tagged out replenishes over time.This leads to a kind of meta-strategy as you are playing. You have to know when to tag in and out to keep both characters healed up.  Some characters are going to excel in certain situations more than other characters too.For instance, if you know you are going to be surrounded and need to take out a heap of enemies, a character like Abobo can either smash the ground or do a jumping piledriver that clears out all the enemies around you. But if you are trying to avoid lightning strikes from the sky, you'd want to switch to Billy or Jimmy for the faster move speed.On that note, all the characters have different move speeds, health pools, attack speeds, and other special properties.For example Jimmy Lee can do two of his special moves while in the air leading to extended air combos. The Lee brothers are also the only characters in the game, to my knowledge, who can pick up enemy melee weapons and use them. Their "special" button causes them to enter a simple grapple state, where they can bash or throw enemies.Meanwhile the ninja Yagyu Ranzou can't pick up weapons but has a dedicated katana, and his "special" button causes him to do a teleport attack that can hit grounded enemies. So you can do combos with him that lead to a grounded state and then pick enemies off the ground with his teleport attack.There's TONS of stuff like this, and I could go on and on.The harder you make the game, the more money you beat out of enemies, and you exchange money at the end of runs for "tokens" which you can use to unlock new characters, stages, and artwork.There are a lot of characters and what's super impressive is that none of them feel cut-and-pasted in. I assumed the boss characters would feel generic and stripped down, kinda like how it feels to play as Bebop & Rocksteady or Shredder in Shredder's Revenge.That's not the case. Each of them has their own fully fleshed out moveset and characteristics. I just finished a Survival session as Linda, who wields a dagger and a whip. She's got good move speed and her dagger is used for fast up-close attacks. All her whip attacks use her special meter and give you insane range and crowd control potential.If you get the game, make sure you head over to the gameplay options and disable the "Special KO" freeze and enable double-tap run. These features were evidently patched in and not present at launch, and I couldn't imagine playing this game without either feature.Not a super long game, but it's extremely fun to play and the Survival mode and extra characters give it legs. A great time-killer game... oh and did I mention the music is superb? It's at least as good as the Shedder's Revenge OST.Only downside I can really think of is a stage progression in the campaign where everything is dark except for your spotlighted character. Makes it hard to see which enemies are around you and is a bit brainless. But this is a small gripe.The value you and enjoyment you'll get as a beat em' up fan is huge.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a tight beat em up! Everything glues together wonderfully, every character has an unique toolkit and the tag mechanic teaches you to experiment with your options.I'm having a blast doing 1 credit, permadeath runs, and the roguelike elements keep things fresh! Every level you beat, you get to choose either passive perks, or MAKING ONE MOVE PERMANENTLY EX. Knockdown dudes with tools you couldn't before -- switching up things and broadening the depth even more!The crowd control system is also genius, a mechanic that is kind of opaque in beat em ups is now emphasized and thought out in such a cool way: you're gonna get food primarily from bunching up enemies together with quick stunning jabs, and then putting together a flashy combo that has to have one of your specials in it.If I could ask the devs, I'd just wish for that the characters had more air options -- Billy has four as far as I recall, so I always feel inclined to use him. Dude can do a neutral air special with the inertia from his run, he has a bouncing divekick and also a heavy, crowd controlling divekick, and a horizontal air kick, all with cheap meter cost. This allows for wonderful combos, but the rest of the cast has more limited options in that aspect, normally having only one air special. I'd love to see a DLC expanding on this! But the combat is already so juicy.And as for the art: charming as heck... There's clearly so much love and attention to detail put into the animations, it's a joy to see.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good. I've played this pure solo tag team mode and a few runs of the free roguelite mode, which got boring real fast. It does some clever things but it's also got some issues - it needs some more difficulty sliders to make things actually difficult, primarily, and a way to skip that intro cinematic where the gangs show up. I've been playing Double Dragon/River City stuff for years, played though pretty much every beat em up I've had access to (most of them), and installed OpenBOR, then played through all the finished stuff I could find there, too. Been around the block a few times, contextually. I usually describe Double Dragons as games of fundamentals; they're relentless, and you need to be precise with your angles to catch dudes without getting pummeled. Of the mainstream line, I generally like the GBA remake best, followed by Super Double Dragon. OpenBOR's Ultimate Double Dragon is pretty incredible, with an awesome free-flowing style change system, and tops the main games. THIS one, though... it's definitely my new favorite main-line, and just a cut below Ultimate DD. It's nowhere near the trash that was DD4, importantly. It's a lot easier than your typical Double Dragons, but it also makes sure you're rewarded for skill rather than just kicking you lives/not murdering you with a couple dudes in your back or whatever. There is exactly one major cardinal sin presented in this game: coins/energy need to bounce before you pick em up. This is an old PS2 era problem that was solved long ago, and doesn't make much sense these days. When coins release, let me grab em in the air. Waiting a couple seconds for a bounce just slows down the action. Also, on a minor note, hitboxes can get a bit squirrely at times, specifically the destructibles. Jimmy's staff style feels weird too, like the hurtbox is very, very narrow. With the long startup this can be dangerous, so I usually just throw it. Everything else is pretty brilliant. There are a lot of cool systems at work. I'll try to list em, and why they're good:- Money system: Earn money. Use it to upgrade, or save it for extra credits. Sort of a roguelike system. - Special multi-kill food items: You're invited to use your specials or weapons and get the most use out of them by finishing off 3+ dudes. Kill 3, get a 25 health hotdog, 4 gets a 50 health burger, 5 gets a 100 health turkey. You don't have to rely on crates, but skill, to earn more HP. - HP items give money: If you don't need them, HP items give you equivalent 25/50/100 money instead. This means more skill means more money. Wrecking a room, racking up Special multi-kills again and again gives you a fat wallet.- Roguelike level-ups: End of level/section you get a chance to purchase a skill upgrade for characters. You only get to pick one, and it's randomized... you may get a change to level your combo efficiency early, or maybe your jump attacks, or grab. Maybe you don't want this stuff and just take 500 extra bucks instead. This also prevents optimized jank; Marian with early upgraded rocket launcher and SP refill every crowd control is nutty (big blast, 60 damage that scales with most dudes until endgame), so you'll have to fight for it. - Special Bar Is Fast: Yeah. It's fast. If you connect and kill with many specials you get an instant recharge. It doesn't take long to get to a full meter, and several specials can be upgraded to be half cost. You can use them a lot, and as above, are rewarded for it. - No I-Frames: I haven't found a damaging move that's invincible yet at any point of the string. It's hunting/herding for openings, creating them with some basic attacks for the stun and confirming into a special to finish em off. Again... skill. No spamming, because your specials can get you killed if you do the wrong one on a dude in an armored animation. - Level Select: First level is one map, second is two, third and beyond is three. You fight minibosses or hulked up goons from level 2 and beyond, and the boss arenas are different for it. You wanna fight Willy on a rooftop, pick him third. You'll be dealing with extra gun goons too. Cool replay factor. - Mutators from the start: You can tweak all kinds of stuff when you start playing. It's how you control difficulty. Scaling up means you get more tokens to unlock stuff for less in-game cash (the same stuff you're buying upgrades and credits with). You start at 1000 gold per 1 token, but can go up if you make it easier and down for harder. I haven't beat it yet, but really, I kinda wish it could push further. At max aggression and max enemy stats I'm only seeing 7, 8 dudes on the map at a time and they aren't really that aggressive. - Dash Cancels: Rush down and juggle. Recovery of Jimmy's shoulder smash too long? Dash cancel. This is that whole "skill" thing again... timing is important to play best. Certain characters get really nasty if you cancel. MOST characters can't OTG reliably, so this is your way of extending combos and killing if you don't want to deal with the squirrely enemies getting up again. I do have a couple issues with the game, mostly related to no option to double-tap to run and no UI reminder of what your three specials are. After awhile you build muscle memory, but I've accidentally done a Jimmy power bomb a couple times when I meant to do a Raging Dragon flurry. The dashing is better on a button, really, because of how much you SHOULD be using it, but it would still be nice to have the option to double-tap.And, it's really, really easy. I came back when they released some new characters and hoped they added some new difficulty options. They didn't. The roguelite mode is stupid easy, with a lot of power-ups quickly and max level, no extra difficulty boost from around level 40 or something. You get a lot of coins if all you're doing is beating dudes up because the multiplier is maxed out (and wraps, making you think you lost everything around level 50). But it's the same thing over and over. The game itself, once you figure out that flow, feels pretty good... but after finishing it up at max difficulty (all bars set to their hardest) without much effort, you can see the cracks. The core system of making more enemies more aggressive is they bunch up, which means supers kill more or them, so you get more health and more money. I'm revisiting this review after awhile and have definitely shuffled a bit. Fight'n Rage is still the best beat-em up on Steam for my money, but SOR4 and Shredder's Revenge flipflop the number 2 and 3 spots because they both have a pretty good roguelite mode, and Shredder's Revenge on hard is decently balanced. I would probably slap this game around the #4 or 5 spot, swapping with Phantom Breaker Battlegrounds.

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: Brawlers is a genre I love, but which has gotten increasingly niche as it's a formula that was built around arcades and quick fun as opposed to longevity and depth. It's amazing to me that it's taken this long, but Secret Base has not only made what I think is the best Double Dragon game, but also has brought a ton of new ideas to the genre that modernizes it, adds a lot of replay value, and which I hope we see expanded in future indie brawlers.The core gameplay is still familiar, but a ton of systems have been added around that to make it something new. There are a number of different characters you can unlock, some of which are melee focused, others which use actual firearms, with their own advantages and disadvantages. You pick two characters for every run, which can be switched between and the one you aren't actively using will partially heal themselves when out of the fight. Score is measured in money, which you can use to buy upgrades for each character that enhance their run, or which you can horde and cash out at the end of your run for tokens, which unlock a variety of things, including more characters. You can also spend chunks of money on continues, and you can adjust the difficulty in a number of ways, which will reward more money if you choose to make it harder. Unlike other brawlers, where healing items are often in static locations you have to plan around, they're dished out here by executing combos of 3 or more finishing moves, making it much easier to change up your strategy.You can choose the order you play the levels in, but each level gets both longer and the enemies and bosses get tougher as well, meaning that your experience will change significantly depending on how you choose to order the levels. This isn't a "one and done" experience like many brawlers and in fact, is not intended to be. You're meant to play it multiple times to get different experiences. This formula is so refreshing and the kind of innovation this genre desperately needed to shake its reputation of being shallow. I really hope to see more developers innovate on this further.My main frustration is that co-op is local only. With Steam Remote Play, this can be overcome on PC, but I would have liked to see proper online made available for all platforms. Even if you want to solo though, there's still many hours of fun to be had.If you're a fan of brawlers, just get this and I don't think you'll be disappointed. If you're one of those who find the genre shallow and not very interesting, this might be worth a shot as the innovations it brings might sell you on it. I love this and am looking forward to what Secret Base brings next.

_childDocuments_.review: "The boys are back in town!"Having grown up on the Double Dragon franchise (I still regularly fire up DD2 on my Switch!), this game has plenty of heart and charm to carry it through to the finish line - which, 30 minutes in, seems admittedly short. However, the game's replayability factor lies in the level redesigns upon defeating one stage/boss - I am looking forward to exploring this mechanic further and am certain I'll have a blast at getting better with the unlockable characters.As far as game mechanics go, this go-around with the Lee twins feels somewhere between the original NES classics and its more recent reboot, Neon - admittedly, Neon was a little *too* deliberate in its controls and felt a hair sluggish for my personal taste, while the original games' controls felt snappier and more immediate (in comparison to Neon and to this newest iteration). That isn't to say that Rise of the Dragons doesn't feel responsive - on the contrary, the controls are tight and movement in general feels good. Rather, the combat mechanics demand that the player understands the toolset available to each character and practice better situational awareness (i.e. tagging in your partner when taking damage to interrupt the enemy). Button mashing isn't going to win you any coins or food!I am truly hoping that this game gets further support and balance updates down the road, even after the initial patches and MP online add-on - Secret Base appears to have treated this game as a genuine love letter for the Double Dragon franchise, and despite some occasional hiccups here and there, I would be more than happy to purchase some tangible DLC content and hope that some additional modes could find their way in this title!

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Despite the fact that my stats say I played this for less than an hour, I have finished it several times on my Steam Deck offline and that time is for some reason not reflected, which seems to be an issue with any game in general.I grew up loving Double Dragon I & II on the NES as well as the original Double Dragon arcade game, and I've always thought it was a shame that none of the sequels managed to live up to those original games. Something was missing.Well, this is the first game in the franchise that has felt as fun as the originals and, despite the visual design departure, it actually works pretty well and you get used to the new versions of the characters. I especially love that their move sets are not identical and that you can now play a Marian but, instead of a martial artist, she's a cop and all her moves involve weapons such as guns, batons, flashbangs and even bazookas. It reminded me of the weird '90's cyber-punkish Double Dragon comic book Marvel briefly printed where Marian was actually a cop and had zero issues shooting bad guys. Between this game and the two River City Girls games, the kid in me has been delighted to see characters like Jimmy, Billy, Marian and Abobo pop up in recent games. The most basic premise of the franchise in all it's 80's splendor.First of all: pixel art is gorgeous. Beautifully animated and fluent, with saturated colors that only make the characters stand out between all the chaos this games can reach so you barely will be lost in all the beating.Second: the gameplay is demanding as it should. Game is by no means slow since enemies will approach you from all angles and try to open you head with a metal pipe and, with movement animations being full commit you have to be aware of who is where doing what so you don't get overwhelmed. Gameplay is smooth in general and the small upgrades enemies recieve as you progress the stages will add a lot of replayability while not overstaying it's welcome.Third: music is just beautiful. Remixes of many DD stages all over the place (in a good way) with that arcade's  tune glory. I wouldn't be able to recommend this soundtrack enough.The only nitpick I could state is the lack of online co-op. A solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This one leans closer to the disappointment side of the coin. It's Double Dragon, but just barely. It uses a cutesy aesthetic which doesn't work great with the post apocalyptic setting and frankly, there's not much to this game. It's feels like something that's just a few steps above how a mobile game looks and feels. You're more focused on optimizing the collecting of coins to unlock a few characters and some temporary passive combat bonuses than really being tactical or playing a decent brawler- your only real concern amounts to grouping enemies up and then using your special move to keep unlocking food items and higher coin bonuses. That's it. Beyond that, there's some bland empty transitional areas and some jumping (yay, platforming in a DD title /s ...) and you're just repeating the same four levels over and over. They're only extended by a few stages based on the order you tackle them. Honestly, most of these levels are uninteresting in design and that's part of the biggest issue here.DD Gaiden is tedious. Just constant session grinds with some dull rogue elements for buying passives. The play loop is just boring. As a whole, this game badly needs more content. Everything about it is very shallow.As a further gripe, the hit detection is kind of irregular. While there's invincibility frames with certain moves, even bosses can't always figure out where to hit you on a Z axis while you're standing still (Okada and Killers bosses in particular). Combine this with the dash grab button being the same as the loot pick up and you're left with a guy who keeps tripping over himself because he doesn't contextually know if he's lunging or looting.This is... some other gimmicky game with Double Dragon branding. I don't know what it's supposed to be and while it can be fun in very short bursts, it's very tedious and limited in play. Get it on a very low sale if you must, but even half off wasn't enough. Definitely not recommended for any Double Dragon or brawler fans.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun take on the beat 'em up genre with a roguelike twist.The latest Double Dragon game has been developed by Secret Base who previously made Streets of Red. I haven't played it but Double Dragon Gaiden appears to be a spiritual successor to that game as it combines a beat 'em up with a roguelike.The way it works is that there are 4 missions to choose from (think Mega Man games where you choose which order to play the levels in) and each level will get increasingly more difficult but also will have more sections of the level open up depending on the order you play them in. So if you do multiple playthroughs of the game with a different mission order each time then you will have a different experience. For example the first mission you play will only have a single section, the second will have two sections, and the third and fourth missions will have three sections each. The bosses will also get progressively harder and by the fourth level you will battle the mission boss in their final form. Each section will also feature their own boss battle with the mission boss being fought at the end of the final section.  In addition to these expanding stages you get the option to purchase upgrades for your characters after completing each section of a mission. These can be damage upgrades for attacks, speed and recovery, health upgrades and many more. You get a choice of 4 random upgrades that you can buy or you can also opt for the 5th option to get cash. Choosing cash will not cost you anything and if you're good enough you could potentially opt to playthrough the whole game without any upgrades. You can also buy tokens which can be used to purchase items in the in-game shop like additional playable characters, artwork, music and tips or you can use them to purchase continues if you get a game over. There are adjustable settings that you can change whenever you start a new game to make the game easier or harder. Harder = more tokens you can earn.The combat seems quite simple at first. You have the standard melee combo, a jump attack and a dive attack, a character specific action and 3 special moves per character. You can also double-jump which is also useful for the few platforming sections in the game (although they are not as obnoxious as in DD Neon or IV for example). Special attacks are pulled off by pressing the special button or pressing it in combination with a direction like SOR4. Some attacks can OTG and some specials can be performed in the air. The ability to cancel into specials (even from other specials) and tagging your partner in and out opens up the combo possibilities and makes for a very satisfying combat experience once you come to grips with it.Now where Double Dragon Gaiden differs from most other beat 'em ups is in it's tag system. It works similarly to some fighting games or the recent Battletoads reboot. You select two playable characters at the start of the game that you can switch between during play. You have a blue meter under your life bar which will allow you to tag out and perform special moves. The bar must be full to start and then you can start combining special moves and attacks between you and your partner. For example you could do a forward + special with Jimmy and plough through a group of enemies but say one or two of them will survive the attack, you can tag to Marian who will appear in the air and then do her forward + special to fire her bazooka and finish them off. Different special moves use different amounts of meter but expect to be able to chain a few special moves together when tagging characters in and out. As well as being able to special cancel and tag cancel your moves you are also able to run cancel. For example with Okada do your basic combo and on the last hit immediately press run towards your opponent + attack to dash attack cancel the recovery frames and then immediately cancel that into forward + special. Understanding these principles are key to performing longer and more damaging combos and combat will start to feel very satisfying.Defeated enemies will drop cash which can be used to purchase upgrades for your run or can be used to buy lives if you die. If you finish enemies with a special move then you will get a special KO. Do this to a group of 3 or more simultaneously and you will get a crowd control bonus where they will drop food which will replenish your life bar. Any upgrades purchased for your character will only apply to that particular playthrough. If you complete the game or get a game over and cash out then you will lose them unlike in DD Neon.The backgrounds have a colourful 16-bit look to them but think more Turtles in Time than Super Double Dragon. The character sprites themselves have a chibi look to them which will be divisive to fans hoping for a modern SDD. I'm not personally a fan of the art style of the character pixel art but they do animate quite well. Also I should note that it's definitely a step up from their previous game, Streets of Red in my opinion. I'm not a big fan of the hit sound effects used. They're not bad per se, but they don't pack quite the same feel as some other beat 'em ups like Fight'N Rage or SOR4. There is some voiceover work for the various characters which I'm indifferent to. It's a nice touch but some players have complained that there is no option to disable them. As for the music, the soundtrack is fire! They've taken classic tracks from multiple games and remixed them for modern audiences. Series fans will instantly recognise the familiar tunes. Definitely my favourite part of the game.The unlockable bosses do feel unique but still complete and not half-baked like some might have expected. Like the soundtrack they have really delved into the previous games and brought back bosses from throughout the series history. I have to give the devs props for the amount of research they've put in to ensure that characters are true to their previous incarnations. For example Marian being a cop, Abobo getting bigger like the Neo Geo game etc.There are things that I wouldn't mind being changed like alternate colours so that you won't mix up a boss that you are playing as with the enemy boss (although apparently this was a restriction placed on them by Arc System Works), maybe some startup i-frames on some moves and after a revive so that you don't get knocked out of your special moves or lose two characters because of it and maybe a training or challenge mode to let you practice moves/combos. I'd also like them to give us some use for the tokens once you've unlocked everything. They could be used to randomise the upgrade options at the end of a stage if you are not happy with the ones available. Perhaps a stage practice option as well and a proper final form for Duke. Lastly I wish the game supported modding so that we could add our own skins/characters, custom colours etc.The game was local co-op only at launch but an update has now implemented online co-op, 3 new playable characters and Survival and Versus Modes. As it goes I have to say that this does not feel like any Double Dragon game (or beat 'em up for that matter) that I've ever played but it does feel fresh and is still very enjoyable. Don't let the roguelite element put you off either. It is still primarily a beat 'em up. Think of it a little like the alternate paths you get in some beat 'em ups in that you will still play some of the same levels but you will play other different areas too. It does feel slow compared to others in the genre but then Double Dragon has always been a slow, methodical beat 'em up. Do I prefer this roguelite/beat 'em up hybrid to great modern beat 'em ups like SOR4 or Fight 'N Rage? No. I personally prefer the depth of the combat and mechanics in those games but because of the uniqueness that this game brings, I will definitely be returning to it.Bring on the Battletoads crossover DLC!
