_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give this game a thumbs down given how awesome the artwork, sound design and music is but a thumbs-down it must be. Nostalgia & self-punishment does not automatically mean a good game.Controls are not just sluggish but locked into long animations which may or may not be cancelled by one of your character's special attacks (very inconsistent results), compounded by an absolute plethora of enemy iframes (on-demand invincibility for even the most basic NPCs), "overwhelm" number-based difficulty and stupidly punitive environmental hazards. Getting hit by anything often means getting hit by everything; even if you tag your character out before they get their entire life bar combo'd into oblivion, your partner character will be eating damage sandwiches before they've hit the floor. Counters, turnarounds and recoveries are clearly not intended by the designers.This makes for a gameplay experience which feels less like Double Dragon (a series I've been grinding for 37(!) years now), and more like a "INSANE DIFFICULTY" mod that just slows your attacks down and gives all the enemies iframes.And it really sucks to be refunding this game because a LOT of work has gone into it and I absolutely LOVE collect-a-thon games which hidden/secret/unlockable characters... But this is 2024, literal decades beyond the crappy sorts of design decisions and cheap punitive mechanics of the mid to late 80s.Maybe a fun buddy-up game while you're under the influence and looking to share some brainless frustration together, but far too mechanically annoying and intentionally punishing to count as a worthy addition to the franchise.Sorry Art & Music people, you did a fantastic job and deserve better gameplay for all the time and effort you put in.

_childDocuments_.review: The Double Dragon series has a lot of spin-offs. Gaiden is a spin-off/retelling of the first Double Dragon that also borrows a little story from part II and characters from the four numbered games.At the start, only the four heroes are available, but nine bosses and minibosses can be unlocked over time. Like Double Dragon IV, everyone gets unique special moves. Marian is a ranged character, and thus great for beginners, and Matin is a clunky grapple character. You unlock the bosses at the token shop. Tokens are gained from the unspent gold at the end of the game (and you can also cash out early). Other unlockables include concept art, music, and tips.- The variety of characters- Special move-focused gameplay that rewards players for defeating enemies with Special KOs- The level designs are creative and include verticality and non-linear elements- Boss fights are exciting.- The first 4 out of 5 levels can be played in any order. Each subsequent level gets longer and harder, encouraging players  play levels in a different order when revisiting the game.- The soundtrack is made up of catchy remixes of classic tunes from the series.- The tag team concept is cool, but tagging out consumes your Special meter, so you can't tag very frequently.- Billy's face is poorly drawn in the cinematics.- The Crowd Control animation that pop-ups up when you get 3+ special KOs at once can be annoying. If it bothers you, see the forums for a mod.Read my full review at  for lots of details and screenshots.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is FIRE 🔥🔥🔥Edited my review after binging it for 2 days straight. I've never written something this long on Steam so bear with me. I feel like a kid in a candy store playing this game so I'm just gonnasay there's a couple wants I have for this game now which are just ideas from Streets of Rage 4 and would only add to it's replayability but not necessary and some wants I'd have as a beat em up/fighting game fan. Just straight up copy these SoR4 things and it'll be perfect. I'll also include some minor things that could use some polish but aren't a big deal.1 Training mode2 Vs mode. Not like the SoR4 one where enemies are always there, make it toggleable like a full fledged mode where you can choose if you want random mobs or not. The choice of a couple small stages with no gimmicks and maybe a bigger stage or two. Nothing too crazy but enough to have some options and land some cool combos and juggles on. Hazards should be toggleable for this mode as well. Ex: falling rocks, holes in the floor, spike on the floor or walls poison gas etc go crazy with the options. Make it so we can either fight another person/cpu controlled character or the opponent with enemy mob(s) of our choice like on SoR4. Make the enemy cpu and mobs have adjustable strength and difficulty like Urban Reign or the story mode. It's already in the game so applying it here would probably be easy? I play fighting games pretty seriously so I'm just dropping stuff in from that perspective. Maybe people would buy the game just to play this mode if it was done right like I wrote. Oh yeah make the music choice an option too for this mode, it would make unlocking the tracks have more value. I mean there's already a great tag system in place why not take full advantage of it with a good vs mode?3 Some endless run mode seperate from the story mode like the SoR4 Mr.X's Nightmare mode. Go full roguelike here. We can get more upgrades in this mode too maybe?4 Add some I-frames to specials, we have to work for the resource to spend it so using a special should have the benefit of not being interrupted so easily. Some have armor like Abobo's neutral special so adding I-frames only makes sense to complete that aspect of combat. It would also make fighting bosses better because the stunlock situations you can end up in are really irritating and people have complained about that. 5 Maybe some more stages?6  A bunch of pallete swap options like in SoR4, it's a minor touch that would go a long way, make the characters colors customizable even because why not? It would be an edge DDG would have over it's competition even if it's a tiny thing, because people love customization.7 Make the crowd clear pop up a toggle between how it is now and a smaller pop up under the health bar that doesn't stop gameplay, make the smaller version the default and we're all good.8 Make the movelist button track which character you're on so you don't have to scroll. The music also resets when you leave that menu which is kind of annoying, flash games do that type of thing. I know minor nitpick but not a knock against the game.9 Boss rush mode, adjustable like everything else. Include any dlc or added bosses here too and their forms.I think adding the ability to jump in and out of a session should be added when the online update rolls out as well. It might affect difficulty but it would make things fun which is most important. One thing the game has gotten right overall is that it is very fun. A lot of the negative reviews are really just scrubs being mad that they suck and I even saw a preview that Game Informer did and one of the guys doesn't even like beat em ups and he was covering the game! WTF!? Not only that but they usually don't even understand the mechanics and are looking to nitpick and make this love letter to the series look worse than it is so make your own judgements. Alright, thanks for reading this. I hope the devs read this because I love this game and have been waiting for it to drop so I wrote this as a passionate fan.  I rate the game 5/5

_childDocuments_.review: Fun brawler with nice pixel art graphics, good, responsive controls and awesome Double Dragon music.Double Dragon fans get a good dose of their beloved old-school brawling and some new things. New players get a fun game at a fair price!This game balances duration and re-playability. You can do the entire campaign on a single session or play 20 minutes and return later. Difficulty can be customized (but I guess hardcore DD fans might feel default difficulty a tad easy).And, watch-out for Marion, this time she's up to protect the brothers! With some power ups, she gets quite OP!Gameplay is fairly simple but special moves, character swaps and even the power up system provide a good amount of variety.  You also get un-lockable characters by playing the game! No paywalls, gachas or other modern b.s...The game runs just fine and you don't require a top notch computer either... so, what else can we ask for?Seriously: this is a no brainer, just get it and have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant little game.When I saw this game had a ninja dlc allowing me to play a stereotypical action movie Ninja I decided to give it a try.And yes it's definitely worth trying if you like a beatemup.Much like the old Double Dragons from my arcade days as a little kid it's a sidescroller beatemup where you have a limited set of moves, positioning is key and you have to use pickups such as food and weapons.The ninja for example cannot use weapons but his powerset is definitely good enough to endure the handicap it seems.The levels are technically the same but the order you pick them changes how many sub-levels per boss you  face and how much stronger the bosses become. (for example the Yakuza leader dons an armor and fights you at the end of a 3 battle gauntlet instead of 2 sub-levels) There is a double ending with a possible extra level to play depending on your choice.Replay value is great though I suspect the game can use a few more levels and perhaps some more randomized subbosses or some extra events.The aesthetic is a bit cartoonish compared. It's pleasant though I'd have personally preferred a grittier spritework.The only thing I disliked were:- the stun mechanic of one boss. - the traps could sometimes be a bit tedious, slowing the game rhytm down a bit but all in all nothing too bad.I did experience a bug where at a boss fight on a rooftop my character fell off and respawned off screen, unable to rejoin the bossfight.My 2nd playthrough was fully problemfree though.Difficulty is heavily modifiable. Health, agression, etc. The harder you make it the more unlock tokens you'll get.Doesn't look like the grind is too bad. And I could unlock the ninja already after my first playthrough and the Yakuza Lady after my second. All in all... a recommend for fans of the genre and those who want to chill with a nice retro buttonmasher.Fight on!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I come from playing other Beat em ups that came out earlier and recently before, like Streets of Rage 4 and TMNT: Shredder's Revenge. I decided to buy Double Dragon Gaiden and give it a shot thinking it would be a similar experience to those games. All I have to say it...It's...different. Maybe "different" isn't the correct word, but rather "UNIQUE". They could have just played it safe and made a Double Dragon game in a very similar and more traditional style and spirit as Streets of Rage 4 and TMNT: SR did, but no. They added a whole lot of interesting features that made it feel so different and separate it from its peers. At first I felt a little turned off, or not turned off, more like confused. Not in a bad way by any means. I thought these new features like the level select that allows you to play the game in whatever order you want, rogue-like features such as power ups and upgrades does give this game a pretty unique flavor that I don't think any other arcade style beat em up has ever done before, at least not in the same way as this one did, a tag feature that allows you to switch between two characters on the fly as you play also add a unique dynamic. I have only played this game for like 30 minutes at the time of this review, and so far I'm still getting used to it. Getting used to the new features, getting used to the combat system, which again, feels very different from what I'm used to in other games, at first I had a bad feeling that this unique and changed up combat system was going to turn me off and make me want to turn off this game and go back to the others, but on the contrary, it has intrigued me. I want to get good at this game and I want to see what combos I can come up with and have a completely different feeling from what I'm used to from the other games I've played. In Summary, I am glad that Double Dragon went out of its way to try and do something very different and unique, rather than just playing it safe and just copying what SOR4 and TMNT got right and just making a straightforward, plain, and simple traditional arcade style side scrolling beat em up Double Dragon game.

_childDocuments_.review: This does the same thing that Cuphead does as a brawler, beat 'em up, rumble fighter (not duel fighter).  Cuphead will be considered, or reckoned, as better because it has more areas and money put into it.I love this new Double Dragon!  Good sound, looks, and feel!  It adds the tag-team element into the game and the special move meter from duel fighters like Art of Fighting and Wrestling games.  It also adds Technos' "direction input changes moves" style of moves making.  What it has done for us, Double Dragon Gaiden, is bring together all the beloved elements of the past Double Dragon, and even Kunio-Kun (Renegade), games into one product and add something new to do.  At first glace it will look like ANOTHER entry into a saturated marked that simply plays well or is fun, but this does something new: a "living gamespace".  You see, the missions change upon the player's choice of direction.  As you complete missions, the following missions will be further advanced in sector requirements!  This is proceeded with narrative explaining the bad guys are responding to the justice of our heroes by increasing their defenses.  You beat one level, and the next level has more area to fight through!  The bosses have more to bring to you!  This is new and fresh, and keeps an otherwise short game long.  However, if you find the game too short, increase the difficulty for even the hardest setting with "permadeath" is not to hard.I found the unlockables by token and platforming to be challenging and appropriate, not frustrating or cheap like I have seen other journalists or YouTubers purport.  It adds depth and character to the game.  What I would have wanted to see in this game are secret areas to fix the "less areas than Cuphead" thing.  Also, I like the implementation of what we now call rogue-like elements.If you are looking for the next entry into the new 2D electronic entertainment product since Cuphead  (that does fresh things all my beloved 2D copies/brews of 3D or past-gen games), you have found your game!  Simply take your expectations to a pleasure over wisdom place because it doesn't have as much as Cuphead, even though it has much to offer.Enjoy, and beat 'em up! (any KJV/Bers or AVers? "beat" means more than hurting people, lol)

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A quality reintroduction to the beat em genre, although simpler to others in the genre's revival, the presentation and care really make a nice, easy way to get into the genre as a whole. Only really lacking in terms of challenge (besides the last level if you go for the better ending) and feeling like it was meant to be a bit bigger.The gameplay is sick, but lacking in depth and difficulty compared to Fight n Rage and Streets of Rage 4. The Crowd Control and Tag mechanics are a simple but satisfying way to add a little depth to Double Dragon games, which, nostalgia aside, haven't aged as well as the SOR series. The graphics and animations are really well presented and nice and bright, it's a nice simplified pixel facelift. The character's feel pretty distinct and getting to choose two makes you consider what each character is better at handling. However, this is one of two things that make me feel the game could have been bigger, The enemy types are pretty good and varied, but the game doesn't really feel like it truly challenges you to be careful about your choice of tag team. The price point isn't too bad either, however the gameplay loop lends itself to a deeper game. Ultimately your runs encourage you to stash cash to convert into unlockable tokens, and while there's a decent roster to unlock, maybe adding a gallery of previous DD game artwork and concept art could have fleshed out the unlockable list. A process which is there for the music unlockables, but really only for tracks used in this game. Adding more classic gallery or music tracks from previous games could have made the loop feel a lot bigger and expansive, while also offering fans and nerds a more celebratory look at an old franchise.  My only real criticism isn't the amount of content for the price, it's that the gameplay loop does feel like there should be more. The core game is excellent, but feels like an expansion pack could really round it out, maybe add a leaderboard and an arcade mode or a survival mode for longevity.

I simply cannot stop playing this game and it is giving me the dopamine hit that I need right now.If you are in for some quick beat 'em up action with awesome tunes and precise controls that make you feel like the game is not cheating, then I highly recommend this. _childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant at first.  I was expecting more of the same, and more of it.  This is not that.  It's got a bit more depth to it.  Even the stages have depth to them.  The order you play them in tells you how long you'll be in them.  Each stage has sections, and each section has a bit of a challenge to it.  So if there's a stage or a boss you absolutely hate fighting, maybe take them on early so you only have a 1-1 or 1-2 for their stage.  You earn money doing everything.  The more people you take out in different ways, the better and the more money you'll get.  Every stage you get through, you can select power ups for each person in your tag team.  It is a roguelike, though, so if you get a game over, you lose those power ups.  Each thousand dollars (roughly, you can adjust it before starting) you earn translates to one token.  You can use tokens to earn characters, upgrades etc.    They did a pretty good job of explaining most things, but some things I had to learn on my own.  Such as the only one who can one shot breakables is Marian.  Punching breakables with anyone else (so far) takes a whole combo, but everyone has either a dash attack or some kind of attack that can do it in one hit.  This will save you a lot of time if you're collecting everything you can, if you might not have Marian on your team to just shoot it.  I haven't unlocked a single character yet, so I'm sure the synergy combos will grow as I do.

_childDocuments_.review: Double Dragon returns! It's a blast, great music, a highly varied roster (even the Lee brothers are distinct from each other). Some roguelike elements, lots of slider options, and the way the progression of the missions works means no two playthroughs are going to be anywhere near the same.If you are usually turned off by potential repetition in beat em ups, then I'd say try this one, it doesn't get old and it challenges you really well. The combat isn't as in-depth as say Streets of Rage 4 or TMNT Shredder's Revenge but it does it's own thing very well, that being the tag systems, roguelike elements and a big roster with simpler movesets but incredibly varied in what they do. Marian for instance is one of the only beat em up characters I know who is purely ranged. Gaiden is a full return to form for the Double Dragon brand, and I hope we get more Double Dragon's and even more beat em ups in this renaissance of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna be real, I was super skeptical going into this game. Watching gameplay looked slow and sluggish, and I have no nostalgic ties to the series... BUT I just couldn't stop playing!The Tag Team system honestly makes this game! Extending combos to properly crowd control by calling in your 2nd character is always satisfying. Managing your health between 2 characters also adds some additional improvisation to get through stages safely. And because there are a ton of characters to unlock, it is a great way to learn their strengths and weaknesses.Stage Select is also a welcome feature to the beat em up genre to specially tailor each run. Whichever stages you choose later on in the playthrough will be more difficult, longer in length, and eventually culminate into altering certain boss fights. IT'S NEAT!The currency of the game gives incentive to make smart decisions when it comes to risk vs reward. Spending money on perks after stages will make you more formidable, BUT saving up money will revive you upon death. OR you can quit to cash out, and use the remainder for unlocking characters and features.Music is solid and character voice lines for attacks and actions are easy on the ears.SO back to my initial worries, is the game slow? Yes, and I honestly wish the game had a 1.5x speed Turbo Mode. While you can run fast horizontally, traversing certain screens vertically feels like moving through mud with an anchor. BUT MOST OF THE TIME, getting better with the Tag Team system mitigates the speed, and honestly keeps me coming back for more! So overall, I do recommend the game, even when taking the lack of online play into consideration. There is enough here to keep you busy if you enjoy punching the bad dudes, whether it's by yourself or with friends!

_childDocuments_.review: Double Dragon Gaiden is a fun reimagine, simple to pick up and play while allowing you to push your limits. Double Dragon the Arcade Machine and Double Dragon II : The Revenge on NES are the Pinnacle of the series Gaiden stands close to them. It borrows from River City/ Kunio which inspired Scott Pilgrim with money acting as EXP to power up. The music remakes had me putting down the controller just to jam out or giving me the boost I needed to clear a wave.     The combat is fun, the lack of punch and kick buttons in favor of a grab button, a run button instead of double tapping the direction and special skill use is good for beginners but can feel gimped for veteran players who are used to executing specials manually.They did manage to make the skill ceiling high; learning to juggle, maintain multiple combos and getting special KOs is where it shines and allows both playstyles to merge into a cohesive experience for all players.My Gripes are the game length which is the oldschool formula, it can get repetitive even with new characters. I was in favor of the Double Dragon Neon approach giving us a little more story and stages. With no Damsel or Shadow clan the lack of urgency or desire for revenge made the story a bit dull much like Super Double Dragon, it has great combat and music but nothing behind it so it becomes a mindless beat em up when Double Dragon was always decently story driven.

_childDocuments_.review: (Full review follows below) is an action, arcade style, beat’em up game. It is part of the Double Dragon franchise. Trouble is brewing in the city as four gang factions are taking over the city. Billy and Jimmy Lee, along with several other supporting characters have to defeat the gang leaders and free the city of it’s evil entities…at any cost.  The game premise is like most other Beat-em Ups, with the twist at every level you can buy an upgrade to improve your characters.  Additionally the game has a grind feature to unlock additional characters, tips, art, and music.  It will take multiple runs in the game to get enough tokens to unlock everything. The game can feel complicated at times as the enemies can still hit you when you are mid animation or landing.  There are times just like the old NES days, that you will want to whip your controller to the wall (“Don’t do this!”). Play time for this game is ~1-2 hours to complete the main campaign once. It will take ~10-12 hours to complete all achievements. Lastly, expect to spend ~13-15 hours grinding out tokens to unlock everything. The game has a lot of replayability, and is probably worth playing after you have unlocked everything if you need a gaming break for an hour or so.  You can also take a break between boss fights making it acceptable to come back later from where you last battled.  I recommend this game to anyone that likes Beat’em Ups or is an achievement hunter.

_childDocuments_.review: This is perhaps by favorite Beat'em Up game. I loved these kinds of games as a kid. Golden Axe, Streets of Rage, but... my first multiplayer game was Double Dragon on NES. I've been really wanting a legitimate comeback of this genre. I enjoyed streets of rage remake and some of the other ones. But, as great as they are... it's just pretty much the same old game with new skin. Double Dragon Gaiden departs from that and modernizes your beatem up game.It's all about the combos, rogue lite progression and different level types depending on your choices. With two characters you can chain back to back to back(6x+ depending on your pickups)combos. This game really impressed me and have hope that we can get more games in the genre. Personally I would love a modernized golden axe, that's multiplayer online. Rogue lite mechanics, tons of heroes that keep getting added and online multiplayer.That's where the crime lies here. Double Dragon Gaiden is not Multiplayer Online. A slight crime to humanity... you can play over remote play, haven't tested it yet. But, this game would be enhanced SO MUCH if we had the ability to just join up randomly or host games online in the client.I would love to see a fully fledged step in this direction and I'm sure it's coming. Tons of characters, varying combos and builds, procedural levels, special enemy attributes/affixes, 4 player online coop should be a must. Of course this is DOUBLE Dragon so I get the 2 player here. Also I'm not sure how the multiplayer works yet.Here's me checking out the game: twitch/youtube inaliFTWTLDR Double Dragon impresses the hell out of me and is a really refreshing play.

_childDocuments_.review: Double Dragon Gaiden: Rise of the Dragons is the newest entry in the Double Dragon franchise. And, quite possibly, it’s best. By combining class arcade sensibilities, modern presentation, and a good bit of clever design to bridge the two, Double Dragon Gaiden: Rise of the Dragons is a triumph of retro revivals, and has already made it’s way to the top of my beat ’em up list.If you like Beat ‘Em Ups, you should get this game. If you haven’t really played them before (like I hadn’t, at least not for years), then you should get this game. Hell, even if you hate Beat ‘Em Ups, you still might want to consider it. It’s a tight, fun experience with fantastic replayability, smooth gameplay, top-tier aesthetics, and progression systems that most other games wish they had. While there are inevitably going to be some naysayers who will dislike where Double Dragon is going (after years of not living up as a “serious” title), anyone else interested is likely to love it. Near-perfect from start to finish, Double Dragon Gaiden is the polished example of just how much you can do with a retro property when you’re willing to innovate and modernize the rock-solid core. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Game is fun, Roguelite elements are light but well implemented. Here's my early impressions after one (failed) solo run.The game looks and sounds beautiful, and it ran fine on my PC (others are reporting FPS issues so your mileage may vary). The gameplay is definitely fun and an interesting breed of beat'em up and roguelite. There are four levels, five including the final, optional one. Each stage you beat makes the rest of the game harder, but also gives you the chance to upgrade your characters (you always have two characters that you can freely switch between during gameplay).These upgrades are mostly stat boosts however, so you shouldn't go into DDG:RotD expecting the next Binding of Isaac; the character building options don't drastically change how you play the game.At the core of the game is the Special K.O. mechanic, which rewards you with health and money whenever you kill enemies with a special move. Use a single special to kill multiple enemies and you get even more rewards. This part of the game is super fun, it makes the fights more strategic and forces you to familiarize yourself with your character's unique special moves.It's worth noting that the game's difficulty is highly customizable, and that harder difficulties reward you with more currency to buy additional content; i can't comment on how much extra content can be unlocked yet, but what's available when you start playing is already fun and makes you wanna keep playing.So far, i feel very positively about DDG:RotD. If you don't like beat'em ups, this is not the game that will change that, but everyone else will have a great time.

name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective
detailed_description: Solve your own murder in this quirky, puzzle-packed mystery classic, now in HD! BANG! A single bullet rings out in the dark city. But as one life ends, the story is just getting started... Sissel wakes up as a ghost and realises he has lost his memory along with his life. “Who am I? Who killed me? And why?” With only a few hours until sunrise — and oblivion — to uncover these answers, Sissel must solve the mystery of his own murder, starting with the detective who may have witnessed the crime... Using the powers of the dead, you can possess and manipulate objects and even rewind time as you work to solve brainteasing puzzles in a story chock-full of quirky humour and charming characters. This long-awaited HD remaster of Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective, the classic mystery puzzle game directed by Shu Takumi, creator of the Ace Attorney series, features upgraded visuals and sound. Enjoy new music arrangements by celebrated Great Ace Attorney composer Yasumasa Kitagawa which are fully synchronized with the original music so you can switch between them at any time during gameplay. There's also a new gallery of artwork and music. This is no trick: it’s the ultimate version of this puzzle-solving mystery adventure classic!

_childDocuments_.review: The 21st century can definitely be considered the golden age of Nintendo in the handheld console market. The release of the GBA in 2001, the NDS in 2004, the 3DS in 2011, and the NS in 2017, has had a profound impact on the entire video game industry. Among these, the NDS stands out for its unique dual-screen and touchscreen interactivity, fostering the creation of a series of highly innovative games. Takumi Shu, renowned for directing the highly acclaimed and bestselling “Ace Attorney” series during the GBA and NDS eras, launched a unique game for the NDS platform in 2010 – “Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective”. Despite widely acclaim by its player, the game saw modest sales, making it a long-overlooked gem. The remastered version, though lacking in new sincerity, offers a good option for those restricted by platform limitations or who resort to emulators.The game's mechanics are innovative and easy to grasp, allowing players to traverse the afterlife and the real world, intervening and altering the destinies of different characters. This unique setup is hard to find anywhere else, even today. In terms of narrative, the game excels in suspense, urgency, and immersion, with a well-paced story full of twists that pique players' curiosity. The numerous foreshadowings and tightly knit logic lead to revelations that make players marvel at the script's ingenuity. The game features a large and closely connected cast of characters, whose lively and exaggerated hand-drawn animations fully highlight their distinct personalities. The vibrant electronic soundtrack adds a lot of fun to the gameplay, and the preservation of the original score allows veteran players to relive the emotional impact from the past.“Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective” initially faced some criticism for its storyline upon release, and the remastered version doesn't introduce any substantial new story content. Instead, it features a remastered soundtrack, enhanced graphics, and the addition of dynamic sliding puzzles and concept art images, which might seem a bit perfunctory. The game's relatively short duration may not fully flesh out some main characters, potentially leaving players wanting more. The narrative climax is focused on the latter half of the game, and aside from a somewhat shallow storyline, the solutions to mysteries are relatively simple. The game relies more on clever twists and narrative techniques to build suspense, making spoilers devastating to the player's experience. In terms of puzzle design, the game emphasizes the player's observational skills and quick reactions over strict logic, with the butterfly effect and the interaction between different items being more critical, making it less suitable for hardcore mystery and puzzle solvers. Additionally, the game's save mechanism and the system for skipping previously read text are poorly designed, detracting from the overall player experience.For many veteran players, “Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective" may feel more like a work of nostalgia, but that doesn't mean its quality is in any way lacking. I was personally deeply moved by the game's storyline. Just like the characters in the game, this single night's incredible, magical, and heart-stirring journey is something I'll likely never forget in my lifetime. If you're someone who hasn't experienced the original NDS version, a fan of story-driven, casual, or indie games, this title is definitely worth trying. However, for those who have experienced the original, it's important to note that this version only offers graphical and musical enhancements, with no substantial new story content.

_childDocuments_.review: The original  release is one of those unfortunate games that received high critical acclaim but sold quite poorly. A mobile port of the game for iOS/Android came to be in 2011/2012 but  would not make its way over to PC or other consoles, seemingly forgotten by publisher Capcom. This changed in February of 2023, when Capcom suddenly revealed that a HD remaster of the game would be available on PC, PS4 and Xbox One – a rare second chance for a game like this.Thankfully,  hasn’t lost any of its charm and is still as appealing as ever, which hopefully results in better sales this time around. If you’re a fan of the  games (which share the same director as , Shu Takumi) or adventure games in general, give  a try – there’s a free demo available to download if you’re still on the fence after reading through this (& others) review.Let’s briefly go over the changes present in this HD edition before discussing the game itself. Graphically, it’s a fantastic upgrade over the DS version for the most part: Up to 4K resolution, 60fps and  instead of the 2D sprites featured in the Nintendo DS version. It looks great in motion, the beautiful animations are still like they should be, and above all else,  sounds fantastic too, as you can switch between the original soundtrack and a rearranged version.There is, however, one decision concerning the technical upgrades of the HD version that might be a bit controversial: The 4:3 aspect ratio of the original DS game remains unchanged. To still achieve a 16:9 image, big borders featuring (customizable) artwork are present to the left and right side of the “main game” itself - similar to retro collections like the  or . Additionally, information that used to be on the top screen of the DS (e.g. time remaining during puzzles) is displayed on those borders as well (or simply got incorporated into the “main game”)Personally, I feel that you tend not to notice these borders anymore once you focus on the “main game”, so I don’t think of them as a demerit. But as some players feel more strongly about these borders, be advised that this HD version is not a “real” 16:9 conversion of the original 4:3 game.The remaining additions of the  HD version are the usual stuff: art and music galleries, support for more languages (9 in total), achievements – and a minigame called “Ghost Puzzle” that was originally added with the iOS version of the game. Said minigame consists of just a few really basic sliding puzzles featuring scenes of the game however, so it’s hardly worth mentioning (or playing, really).Overall, this HD edition of  is exceptionally made, with great graphic upgrades that are still in line with the fantastic artwork of the original DS version, which makes this HD version probably the best way to experience the game today. It’s a bit disappointing though that no meaningful playable bonus content has been added, like an extra chapter or new puzzle solutions. The game is essentially the same as the DS version, which is great for those who never experienced it, but subsequently less interesting for those who already know the original by heart.To move on to the actual game, I’ll only be able to talk about the absolute basics, as the game is best experienced without knowing too much about it. Generally speaking,  is an adventure game that’s partially puzzles, partially reading through dialogue sequences. Your protagonist is a ghost who wakes up with no memories about his death – or even who he is. Trying to find the answers to these questions, he uses his newly obtained power of manipulating objects to explore a world after his death.Throughout the game, you’ll not only encounter a lot of memorable and unique characters, but also a lot of satisfying plot twists and turn around every corner. The game keeps up a great pacing, which allows the story to not overstay its welcome while simultaneously providing enough information to lead to a fulfilling ending.  also tells a story that feels entirely complete, with all mysteries fully explained and every character properly handled. It’s the rare adventure game that’s so satisfyingly concluded that you simultaneously want more of it but also feel like a sequel wouldn’t work.The only weak point of  might be its puzzles. As mentioned, as a ghost with the power to manipulate objects, you’ll use these powers to manipulate events in order to achieve a certain outcome. For example, you’ll manipulate a candle to burn brighter, which in turn sets a rope on fire, which you previously moved so it would lead to another candle, and so on. Each puzzle offers a variety of objects to possess/manipulate, so it’s all about finding out what to manipulate and when to do so.For the most part of the game, you’ll quickly know what to do and have fun setting off contraptions in order to achieve your goals. There’s also a hint system through speech bubbles, though it’s honestly a pretty hamfisted way to give your players additional tips. It’s also not helpful when it comes to the timing of certain manipulations: Each puzzle only features one solution, which means certain actions need to happen in a certain time frame. This can lead to some frustrating trial-and-error moments, especially since checkpoints are oddly spaced at times, which means you might’ve to rewatch certain scenes more often than you’d like to. A fast forward button could’ve helped but it’s only available when characters speak, not when they move/dance/etc.Again, most of the puzzles are nicely designed and fun to play through. But the occasional exception, mostly found in the later chapters, might be even more frustrating as a result – especially if you got the right order of manipulating figured out and are just stuck on the required timing. Again, the hint system usually doesn’t help in these situations either – so I’d advise just looking up guides online in case you’re stuck and want to move on.Concluding,  is an excellent adventure game with a satisfying story, great characters and a fantastic art style and soundtrack. This HD edition only adds to that, although more bonus content would’ve been great. Even if the puzzles could’ve been a bit better done, if you like adventure games,  is a must play and a cult classic for a reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick is laughably easy; its central gameplay mechanic is as deep as a puddle and it certainly won’t be winning any awards for presentation, yet it is one of the most compelling titles I’ve played in recent years. Any curious observer would question why this niche Capcom title is so vaunted. As much as I hate overused adages, it’s because Ghost Trick is greater than the sum of its parts. Shu Takumi delivered a masterful performance as the Holy Trinity on this title: being designer, writer and director. While such a task is lofty and demanding of hubris, Mr. Takumi created an experience with an addictive and engaging narrative, one of the best oddball casts in video game history, and perhaps the best dog in the entire medium. It’s  no wonder why Ghost Trick belongs in the upper echelons of detective fiction, it’s simply elementary, my dear.

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly one of the greatest game stories of all time. Intricately plotted, with a dozen plot threads going on all at once making it impossible not to get tangled between it all, by the end of the game several of my predictions were crushed, revived, then crushed again. Almost every single character and location comes back in a different context, causing you to rethink your initial assumptions. Only for everything to get wrapped up together in a satisfying little bow. When all the little plot puzzle pieces started fitting together, it was just WOW.The characters in this game are really really silly in a very charming way, which is funny since the plot is taken almost completely seriously (Ace Attorney vibes). The gameplay is entertaining at best and mildly annoying at worst, a lot of it is just messing around and trying different tricks until it works, but that can be pretty fun in and of itself. None of the puzzles outstay their welcome and I never found myself wanting to bang my head against the wall out of frustration. Excellent game, I would recommend this to anyone who doesn't mind reading a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective. Search this title online and you'll realise that somehow, no one has played it, but paradoxically, it's one of everyone's favourite games and you MUST play it. Capcom originally dropped a massive clanger marketing this game, so it attracted very few sales and wouldn't achieve its cult hit status for a good few years after release. I believe that the online clamour throwing this game in your face is really justified, and would recommend this to any gamer with the patience for visual-novel type games.For one night only, Sissel is experiencing one of the most desirable power fantasies I've ever seen. His life has already ended, but he can still physically influence the world (press "Ghost" to warp between possessable objects within range, and "Trick" to make your object do something), and even commune with some of the living. On top of that, if he finds a dead body, he can head back to before the death and interact with the past world. With these powers, he merrily defies the fate of several characters, without fear of any consequences, and if things don't work out he shrugs it off and tries again. His ultimate goal, and the source of the game's tension, is to obtain full closure on the circumstances of his death, and truly rest in peace.I thought the game encouraged patient, experiment-based gameplay but other reviews penalise a "trial-and-error" approach to puzzle solving. This description barely applies - in any situation, there are only a few Trick-able objects around, and object placement and optional character comments provide ample hints of what to do. Even if the solution isn't what you expected, you were still guided into making it happen. I got stuck and had to check a walkthrough twice - both times, I was already Tricking the right object; I just had to Trick it again. Enough room is given for your brain to do some work, while smoothly propelling the player forward so that even stupids like me can finish the game in about twelve hours. The exceptions are some rare occasions where you know the correct sequence of actions, but it's easy to flub the execution. These can prompt several restarts from a checkpoint, and cursing of the lack of a basic undo button.Each level is a 2D side-view cutscene, the progression of which is influenced by your Tricks. You'll mostly find yourself in the kinds of mundane-made-kooky environments familiar to players of this game's Ace Attorney predecessors, starting in questionably-decorated apartments before graduating to luxury prisons, pollocentric restaurants, weirdo-attracting parks and so on. The opening levels might feel inconsequential but they all tie back into the story later. The nature of getting between levels causes Sissel to take on what feel like side missions, putting together the stories of apparent side characters, but the game's cast is so well interconnected that every level is a step forward and a new tidbit of information. The plot is almost more twists than straight parts, so the number of mysteries blossoms quickly and is almost too much, but for a useful summarising monologue at the start and end of each chapter. All your questions are resolved at the end, and I can't think of any loose ends or plot holes. The conclusion is jaw-dropping in a really life-affirming way; a long way from the dark, moody gut-punch twists which are so fashionable now. As with the best-written mysteries I was kicking myself for not getting it sooner. Almost everything was in plain sight, begging me to find it, but some blend of practised sleight-of-hand and my own incompetence kept me guessing the whole time. Even if I never forget this game's story, I'll look forward to playing it again and noticing every time the answers were staring me in the face.I'll also look forward to revisiting the colourful pantomime of characters Ghost Trick treats you to, in which the Ace Attorney spirit is palpable. Most characters have a unique quirk to their writing, so given almost any text box, you can tell who said it. Just about everyone shares a friendly, optimistic nature, and whichever cast member reappears on screen, it's a little dopamine hit every time. Their distinctive designs are accompanied by charming, delightfully floppy CGI-rotoscoped animation. The background art is not so memorable but services the gameplay just fine. I would have preferred a clearer sense of depth, which would have helped me understand some puzzles more clearly. There's a cracking soundtrack with several very replayable pieces, though I thought it was a bit lightweight. There are ten minutes of sadly unused tracks in the game files, which are worth a listen online.Capcom's other HD remasters of Shu Takumi's back catalogue look great and are functional, but technically in need of some patches that never arrive. Ghost Trick's remaster is no exception. It's a delight to see the perfectly updated sprites, and even better is to hear the full richness of the soundtrack from decent speakers, and then, to hear it elevated by a new arrangement of every track. You can switch between original and arranged music freely. As you earn achievements you unlock wallpaper-size bits of artwork from the game, and unlock "Ghost Puzzles" - simple slider puzzles which are not at all worthy of the puzzles the main game gives you. I would have happily traded Ghost Puzzles away for more attention to the graphics and UI, for example fixing the messed-up intro animation of Inspector Cabanela or the fact that the Options menu has two "Controls" tabs.So yes, as the old saying goes, "Please play Ghost Trick". A consistent, exciting visual novel puzzler, working alongside original gameplay and beautiful characters, and one of the best narratives the DS era had to offer, now truly shining in a great HD remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick's gameplay isn't that spectacular. It's not bad by any means. It is actually quite good, but simple. _childDocuments_.review: I have been wanting to play Ghost Trick since it was first released in 2011. Unfortunately I didn't have a Nintendo DS at the time, so I missed out. Now that it has been released for the PC, I finally had the chance to play it- and boy, did it not disappoint.Ghost Trick is a single-player puzzle game in which you play as an amnesiac ghost. Your goal is to figure out the mystery behind your death, as well as to prevent other deaths from occurring. You have the power to witness what transpired in the last four minutes before a person's death, and then manipulate the events by moving objects to prevent it from happening. By doing this for multiple characters, you slowly unravel how they are interconnected while saving their lives.The controls were straightforward and easy to grasp, and I found the Ghost Trick mechanisms pretty clever. The puzzles increased in difficulty as the story progressed, and a few times I had to look up hints to see what I was missing. I didn't find the puzzles too tedious, even if I had to do them multiple times. In fact, it motivated me as I got closer to the solution with each try.Some parts of the story were gripping and had me sitting at the edge of my seat, waiting to find out what was going to happen next. Other parts were heartfelt- I teared up at certain points, but I am easily moved. The story does get pretty outrageous since it delves into the supernatural. And to match that enthusiasm, the characters are pretty outlandish. What really struck me as special though, is that each individual character has their own unique animations to match their personality and mannerisms. Even the minor characters!! The grunts all look different from each other and even their personalities are fleshed out a bit. It really adds a sense of variety and amusement to the interactions. You can tell there was a lot of love put into this little game.  The game itself is relatively short- there are 17 chapters, and each one takes about an hour or less to play through. I took longer on some puzzles, and also aimed for all the achievements, so I have closer to 30 hours. Some of it was spent sitting around just listening to the music though, it's super catchy and relaxing to listen to.The person behind the direction, writing, and game design is Shu Takumi, who is known for creating the Ace Attorney franchise. If you like that series, you will definitely like this game. It has similar narrative and puzzle-solving styles, wacky characters, hilarious animations, and a fun story to play through.I highly recommend this game if you like crime fiction, murder mysteries, solving puzzles, and fun characters!!

_childDocuments_.review: i played the original on the nintendo DS. i loved it, and i still do. its one of those games i come back to and replay just to re-experience. people who know me personally will tell you that i usually do not replay games. this is one of the handful of exceptions for me. i love the characters, the story, the puzzles, the gameplay, the dialogue for both the main story and if you decide to go off the beaten path. everything about this game just brings me joy.imagine how i felt hearing the game i played over and over again is getting remastered. i bought the japanese steam bundle at the risk of not being able to make rent. this game has stuck with me through thick and thin. its seen me at my lowest and my highest. its seen my friends, my family, and its seen me; the me that i show when im alone. i felt like i wouldve betrayed not only this game but myself if i didnt get at least physical copies of the OST.of course, this is not the DS version that i played all those years ago in middle school and after. i wouldve been surprised if they adapted the dual-screen onto a monitor somehow. in fact, i would not be surprised if they used the iOS version as building blocks. yet, despite not being the original i got blasted with nostalgia in HD. seeing the characters in this version was like when i put on glasses for the first time. it was , and i felt happy. if the third impact ever happens, i can only pray the last thing i see is the final image of this game before i become part of the primordial soup. the OST, remastered from their chains of age to glorious high fidelity  my ears. i would not be mad if i got tinnitus from this soundtrack.its not perfect, nothing ever is. mankind isnt perfect, so why should we expect those which has been created by man to be perfect too? but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if it isnt close to perfection. idk if i'll ever father a child, but if i do their birth could not compete to what i felt playing this. take my gripes like you would take a hipster who claims to have been a fan since day one. my main one is . oops sorry for the rant. my other gripe is mainly how they changed dual-screen cutscenes but i also understand that monitors have one screen and they did their best, which is still fantastic.the other changes they added though i love. challenges? hell yeah i wanna see if i can do them first try. slide-tile puzzles? another childhood memory, one not as lucky to be kept as fondly. concept art? why did they draw  like that lol. some poor parallel universe got cursed with that version. achievements? more chances to beat my record of 767 unlocked achievements in a year.yes, i play nsfw games on main. yes, lack of attention as a child and my parents' divorce not only gave me mommy and daddy issues but it also made me do streaming as a hobby. yes, i own a mannequin torso downstairs that was going to be thrown out but i salvaged it and regret not taking its three other siblings to dress-up in cosplay that i wouldve bought online. yes, i am self-destructive to the point i worry those close to me. despite my drawbacks, . hell, even if you buy this game at a discount i would be proud. this game is probably my oldest friend, and its one i am not afraid to share to others.

_childDocuments_.review: Brought to you by the creator of Ace Attorney, this is Takumi's masterpiece. From the first time I experienced it a decade earlier until today, its biggest tragedy is being overlooked. No better time to change that fate, ey? Ghost Trick achieves the seemingly impossible by welding its novel gameplay and story together into a formula where one is inseparable from the other, into a puzzling, galaxy-brain mystery with lovable characters and a dark atmosphere bursting with character and humor. And what a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ story it tells. Waking up next to his own cooling corpse, our protagonist's ghost must haunt his way through the night to discover the truth of his own murder and the bigger, more sinister picture at play.The art-style is a dashing enigma, contrasty color palettes setting the night of murder ablaze with some of the swankiest animation you'll see in a game. Set to the beat of a  groovy, emotional soundtrack, solidly remastered by Great Ace Attorney composer Kitagawa. All of which makes my umpteenth replay of the ghost game as joyful as the first playthrough. Finally, I get to play it on the couch with friends, blessing them with the same experience.To say anything more would be doing the game a disservice, as It's best experienced without any foreknowledge. I have yet to meet anybody who has walked away from Ghost Trick without a shade of wonder. Give it 4 minutes of your life and it's guaranteed to steal the night.

_childDocuments_.review: I write this as I just finished all the achievements in the game.Ghost Trick is one of my favourite games from my childhood. I love how the story makes a lot of things make sense once you beat the game. Heck, I've replayed my DS copy of Ghost Trick multiple times and constantly recommended it to my friends, but finding DS copies were near impossible and not all of my friends had an iPhone to buy it there either. Now I can bother them to play it on any of the platforms it re-released on and they have no excuse to miss out on my favourite single player story-driven game. Even if you have already played it, playing it again with all the knowledge you have from the first run can make you appreciate all the dialogue boxes and jokes even more. If you still aren't compelled to buy it, maybe the art gallery and the slider puzzle can convince you (granted, the art stuff is unlocked gradually throughout playing the game again and the slider puzzle is for completing the game once, but there's a setting option that helps to skip the dialogue faster if needed) It may have taken 13 years, but Ghost Trick is available on all current platforms, and it should be, as this is a story I hope everyone can experience.

_childDocuments_.review: You NEED to experience Ghost Trick. It's no stretch to say that it's Shu Takumi's (The Ace Attorney creator) best game. Honestly EVERYTHING is done so well in here. The animations are now more fluid than ever, and I really like the redone soundtrack too (though if you prefer the Original DS soundtrack, you can also turn that on through the game's options menu. It also has... Ghost  Puzzles after you beat the game which certainly... um... exist...If you've made it here, at least play the free demo and give it a chance! I loved my time with Ghost Trick and after playing it now I'm trying to get as many people as possible to play it  and my friends who gave it a shot have also loved it! It's absolutely worth the price tag and you NEED to play it for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: is a simple and light puzzle adventure game from , the creator and director of the original  trilogy and  series. This man not only knows how to make one hell of a narrative, but knows how to nail the execution.  is no exception. Be prepared for an unforgettable experience with insane twists and turns, a killer soundtrack, and explosive character motivations. was originally released on the Nintendo DS in 2010 and features incredibly detailed and nuanced animation of stylized flat-shaded characters who are bursting with idiosyncrasies and hilarious dialog. You possess inanimate objects as a spirit to further the narrative with a sort of pseudo-“Rube Goldberg” set of actions by drawing lines in-between objects you can interact with around your environment. Although the game is much more about character driven narrative than it is gameplay depth, don't let that fool you, as the game is always full of creative and engaging activities.If you asked me who I'd recommend it to, I'd say anyone and everyone:  And you should absolutely go in blind, or you'll defeat the purpose of playing.The game takes about 10-12 hours to complete and there isn't really any replay value after you finish it, but the 2023 version adds achievements to applicable platforms and promotes perfecting certain chapters and seeing ways to fail through the game as well as the insipid slide puzzles from the iOS version.All that said, this is yet another careless product by Capcom. It's not the Denuvo or the price that bother me. It's the quality of this, so called, remaster, and why I’m not recommending this 2023 version. This game deserved so much better.  deserve better.Even Shu Takumi tweeted about issues of this remaster on the day of release, and was displeased about the lack of the attention to detail.The assets look like they're rendered at far less than 1080p. The backgrounds and characters are filled with aliasing, ringing, compression artifacts, posterization, and an overall lack of definition and consistency needed for the game's distinct art style. It has oversights and missing graphical elements that were in the original game. Even if you don’t notice it, it shows how little attention was paid by those whose job it was to remaster it.The characters and inanimate objects you possess are very soft and blurry. On the very small low resolution screens of the Nintendo DS, everything is super clean and sharp at its native resolution; this version just looks like you have Vaseline on your eyeballs. They should have taken the original CGI data and translated them into real time models, if they still had those, or at least recreated the assets at a higher resolution.The game is rendered in 4:3 just like on the Nintendo DS and you can't turn the borders black, so you're always stuck with a rather busy windowboxing or one of a few colors. Why isn't it 16:9? It's possible the camera was very specifically located to keep certain elements framed, or perhaps it would show nothing. Either way, the attempts to improve this discrepancy is underwhelming. An attempt should have been made to bring the original dual screen framework over instead of slapping some crap on the sides. The remaster trailer is full of misleading and fake motion graphic flourishes that aren’t in the actual game, that look great and would have added to reinvigorating this new version.All I know is that in a world of 4K Ultra HD monitors, all of this under cooked presentation is unacceptable. They failed to translate the original artwork. Yes, I expect crisp, clean, artifact free visuals that are beholden to the essence of the original, which didn't have a single pixel out of place.The interface is poor. Text boxes and UI elements are massive, and no thought was given into translating it from the small screen. It's like staring at a Nintendo DS about 1mm away from the screen. The UX is convoluted and reeks of the typical inability for developers to understand basic UX for PC games. You use WASD to move the camera, Q, E, R, G, and C for various commands. They just remapped the console buttons onto various keys, which is really strange, because a mouse is analogous to the stylus/finger you would have used on the DS. You can use the mouse, but the overall controls and interface weren't refined for an intuitive PC experience. Other oddities are pressing C to go "Back" in menus. Please, use  like a normal person. If you play this game on a 16:10 screen like the Steam Deck, you’ll get small gray letterboxing bars on the top and bottom. If such an oversight is all it takes to get "Deck Verified" I don't even want to know what "Supported" looks like. I'm going to assume on 21:9 monitors you will also get gray bars.Camera judder and inconsistent presentation of animations round out the disappointment.There’s a Steam demo if you want get a taste of what this version is like and it features the first 2 chapters. Your save data will carry over, and you get a few bonuses for completing the demo before playing the full game, but at present time, using the same data from the demo prevents achievements from unlocking in the full game. The chances of Capcom fixing anything is 0%.I can't recommend this version if you have critical perception and care about quality. It disappoints me that people can't see such obvious issues in front of them, and I think you’d have to be freaking blind to not see them. What's worse, is anyone lining up to defend such poor standards and gulping down an inferior product at full price. For some reason consumers love to pay more for less. Capcom was more interested in spending $1 million to protect this travesty with Denuvo than spend it to improve the game they expect you to pay for.The original developers cared about their game's presentation. This, supposed remaster, just doesn't do justice to the sweat and blood the original team put into the Nintendo DS version to make sure everything was just right. They wanted their vision to be put in the best light possible. It’s called integrity, and it’s sorely lacking in the video game industry these days, unless you happen to like $70 bloated stutterfests.It's too bad the original game has become so expensive on the second hand market, because I think you'd get a much better experience in quality and execution. You suck, Capcom. Do better. The game looks poor and deserved respect. If Capcom had put the original DS game in untouched and correctly presented as a bonus, maybe I would have recommended it. I was looking forward to playing this again, and once again, greed and incompetence took it from me.How it’s suppose to work is the company spends resources on talented people to provide an improvement over what came before. In exchange I give them $30 to recoup that investment. Instead the company did the bare minimum in an attempt to maximize profits. Supporting crap means companies will put out more crap. Corporations are eager to defecate in your mouth and make you pay for it, and people are more than happy to line up and suckle on their sphincters. People love to put feces in their mouths. You know, the ones that leave Jester Awards on critical reviews because they'll never have an objective thought in their heads. Thanks for the free Steam Points though, I guess.For the discerning consumer, learn how to use a search engine for a superior experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I am entirely at a loss for words at this game masterpiece. I saw the gameplay of this Ghost Trick way back then but could not play it as I did not have a Nintendo DS, so I was very excited when I heard it coming to Steam soon! Shu Takumi proves yet again that his storytelling with the supernatural and mystery genre. The story, the puzzles, the music, the characters, and the game mechanics combine to create a satisfying experience. However, a few puzzles get confusing, and the controls on a keyboard regarding movement, in particular, could leave more to be desired! This remaster is a good portrayal of this game. The updated graphics and visuals all look beautiful on the PC port of this game. Unless you have a lingering affection for the pixelated touches, it's a general improvement visually for the game.With Ghost Trick, we are presented with a mystery for us to uncover, one that, no matter how hard you may try with the clues given to you, will still be left oblivious until the actual reveal. This is precisely how a mystery should be created, keeping the audience guessing and at the edge of their seat, trying to uncover the secrets in the dark. The story is well-written despite starting at a particularly unique moment, right after the main character's death. The game paints the story so that you get all the relevant details surrounding the main character without deferring to what a lot of other authors/game directors do with 'fillers.' the game is relatively short relative to Shu Takumi's other games, such as Ace Attorney, spanning around a 10-20 hour playtime. With that, it is the perfect duration for the conclusion of this game, with how the chapters are linked to the time. The story stays true to its theme and provides plot twists that make me gasp at the realization despite the facts being laid bare before my eyes. It contains an intriguing plot that can't help but make you feel like you have to finish this game in one sitting.The characters are all likable, each with motives for doing things, so it does not feel like they're just extra background characters. They are lively, breathing characters, all with their purposes in the plot besides being a bridge of relevancy. However, some characters should have been explored more in-depth. Still, this was avoided to reduce redundancy and keep the focus on the main character uncovering the mystery about themselves. The character designs are all beautiful and creative, with each character having a defining trait or feature about them, which the game uses to create comedic humor as they interact with each other. This is mixed even more with the visuals and flashy animations given to the characters to further represent their uniquely defining traits, and Ghost Trick ensures that their visuals please the greater audience with their creativity.The music is immersive, with tracks that are not only a treat to listen to but fit entirely the game's themes and the scenes they are attached to. I often find myself bobbing my head about this and feeling chills when the set gets good as the music plays. I always believe that a mystery should have the most fitting music accompanying it, as it helps to give a provocative reaction to the information being shown in the story, such as when time is being lowered for example, the music starts becoming fast-paced and chaotic, indicating you to hurry up without the use of words. Ghost Trick features a fantastic blend of music genres and outstanding music direction and production that will immerse you in its world. I've heard many beautiful tracks over time, and Ghost Trick's ways are sure to stand out even then. The puzzles were entertaining, despite my pondering my head on many of them with the time limit. The level designs were all very creative, and Ghost Trick maximizes the mechanics they've created to ensure that you use every item at your disposal. The game mechanics make use of timing, which can be difficult for some players to work out and, admittedly, can get confusing when it plays into a scene. Still, regardless of difficulty, the developers have found creative ways of implementing movement in that regard. A lot of the time, you may find yourself restarting the puzzle/chapter like me to figure out what to do and trust me, it is expected to have to retry multiple times as the developers have also made it relatively easy to restart. The game will also drop hints if you are stuck or missed your opportunity at a certain point. My only problem is that you should be able to skip or fast-forward some dialogue if a cutscene is not from a speech bubble.Ghost Trick is a fantastic experience for those interested in a different type of mystery. Shu Takumi excels in blending the supernatural with mystery to create a story that makes sense from almost entirely fantastical elements, making you think of how these abilities came to be and how they play a part in uncovering the mysteries in the first place. The game is imperfect, but its strengths overshadow many of its shortcomings, as the story provokes your mind to think more about discovering the unknown and overcoming obstacles. You will only have time to think about something else as each chapter presents you with a new mystery and a cliffhanger to worry about instead. I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a different mystical blend of mystery.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is a game that forces you to look at the world in a different way, and it does so by using mundane settings for creative, dynamic puzzles with a ticking clock. These puzzles would be excellent enough as their own reward, but they're also strung together with a captivating mystery full of twists and turns, to say nothing of memorable characters and witty writing. The incredibly slick presentation is the cherry on top of a fantastic adventure game.

_childDocuments_.review: A remaster of one the best DS games almost ten years after it came out? Sure, I'll take it.This is my 3rd or 4th time playing through the game and it does still hold up well. I had no technical issues with this port at all, which was a pleasant surprise.It's difficult to talk about the game without entering spoiler territory so all I'll say is you'll likely have a great time outside of a few annoying trial and error moments. The worst is probably an escort mission halfway through. This remaster even makes completing it without mistakes into an achievement...If you're looking to play the game, are turned off by the $30 price and happen to own an iOS device, the iOS port is still available to download for $10. It holds up perfectly fine despite running at 15 fps. Really, you get used to it quick. (Edit: Capcom announced on December 20, 2023 that the iOS port will be delisted on March 25, 2024, possibly to be replaced by a port of this remaster at some point. If it does happen, the price probably won't be very cheap)Though, if you already own the game, the price does become a bit hard to justify. As nice as the updated graphics and frame rate are, I don't mind the way the original game looks at all. Your brain can fill in the details. In fact, I'd argue being able to see the characters' faces so clearly can make them look a bit goofy at times. Then again, not much they could've done about that when you're remastering a game for larger displays.I'm a bit mixed on the newly rearranged music, most tracks are fine but there are a few where I prefer the originals. Thankfully, you're given the option to just switch to the original soundtrack, though the sound quality is of course still low.The main highlight of the port for me personally was the gallery where you can find a ton of art and storyboards. All the notes are still in Japanese and no translations are given, but it's still a cool bonus.What I didn't really care for is locking content up behind the pre-order and playing the demo version. It's possible the pre-order DLC will be offered for sale later but from what I can tell, that still isn't the case for Great Ace Attorney, where the same thing was done. It's just a dirty way to give people the fear of missing out and needing to buy the game for full price. (Edit: In a surprising move, the pre-order bonus content is now available for purchase as of September 21, 2023, no such luck for Great Ace Attorney)As for the demo, If you happened to purchase the full game before downloading it, the demo download won't work, so you will need to download it on another account or do some trickery with command line to get it. Not sure anything can be done about that but it's awkward currently.Overall, a good port of a great game. Definitely worth buying during a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite games of all time. Ever. I have replayed this game multiple times yet still get chills every. single. time. The story and mystery is intriguing, the characters are lovable, the puzzles are fun and the music suits the game amazingly well.I first discovered this game years ago as an Ace Attorney fan (most Ghost Trick fans are Ace Attorney fans). This game is written by the same guy - Shu Takumi (my hero, I love you Takumi) and the story will not disappoint. The game is around 10-12 hours long, quite fitting for a game where the story takes place all in one night. The puzzles are fun and challenging for first time players, but not frustratingly so (Chapter 9 can go suck it though, in my opinion).Like the Ace Attorney games, this is a story you will want to constantly revisit. This remaster is probably my fifth playthrough of this game; the characters NEVER get old and I cry at the end every time.  This game seriously needs more recognition. Maybe a streamer will pick it up and play? This game deserves more love. The length of the game compared to the price is quite steep; so definitely get this on sale. I was happy to pay full price however as I never regret buying a Shu Takumi game. Anyway, I've gushed about this game long enough. Hurry up and go play this masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original game on the DS, so I am happy I finally got the chance. Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is a game where you're a ghost trying to solve the mystery missing memory by using ghost tricks to manipulate your environment, helping people and changing fates along the way. The game is overall rather easy, but the illustrations are great, the story is fantastic, the characters are amazing (love Missile) and the music is a banger. You can't go wrong playing this absolute classic and I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm normally not one for more story heavy games and environmental puzzle games, but hands down this might be one of the best ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ games I've genuinely ever played. The story Is so incredibly well written and it wraps up very nicely, and the twists in this game hit like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bullet train and there are a ton of great twists throughout this game. The puzzles are also very good, there were a few i was left extremely confused on how to solve, but that might just be a me thing though. Nonetheless the puzzles are intuitive and are well made. My only gripe is that the way steam achievements are handled is a little buggy if you are offline; although I've beaten the game i don't have all of the story based achievements due to the fact i was playing this offline. Despite that I HIGHLY recommend that you play this game, you will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are 720p, which is fair enough, but they are blurry upscales with compression artefacts and presented in glorious 4:3. It feels like all the assets where blindly processed with a quick script and haphazardly inserted into a minimal effort game engine. For example, speech bubbles and similar UI elements are obviously designed to look good on a tiny DS screen, and just looks ridiculous scaled up on a 60" TV.And unless you have a proper controller you should forget about this game. The keyboard interface is just insane, every action has been assigned a completely random key with no logic or reason. You can almost hear the devs going "Yeah, whatever".Just to be sure, this is a great game, but the port is just horrendous. If capcom wants to charge full price for an old game they should also put a bare minimum of effort into the product, this is just embarrassing.

_childDocuments_.review: I had been wondering what kind of mysteries Shu Takumi might write if he wasn't constrained by the world and continuity of the Ace Attorney series. Honestly, the guy could be Kotaro Uchikoshi's long lost brother, because the plotline ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ he pulls off in Ghost Trick shares so much genes with Zero Escape, AI: Somnium series and other Kotaro's works.Gameplay mechanics aren't important here, the puzzles  engaging, but very simple. This is primarily a crime detective mystery visual novel featuring plot twists as ridiculous as they can possibly get.I am particularly impressed by the style and detail of character animations. I imagine they were originally designed to look clear and distinct on the DS's tiny 256x192 resolution. The remake appears to be reusing the original source content: on a modern resolution PC displays and framerates these animations look almost comically exaggerated, but I actually found their design charming and unique.

_childDocuments_.review: A *fantastic* little game! It's not super long (think around 10-14 hours to complete, depending on whether you're as bad at puzzles as me), but the story's a wild ride with twists aplenty and lovable characters, and the puzzles tie seamlessly into it while providing fun brain-teasers that even stumped me a few times.If the premise of a ghost trying to solve his own murder interests you at all, give the demo a shot - you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: Shu Takumi really can do no wrong. As a huge Ace Attorney fan, I played a bit of this on DS back when it first came out but didn't stick with it beyond the first few chapters. After completing it, I was pleasantly surprised by the length and depth of the narrative and the truly amazing variety of ways in which the simple core mechanics are used. Worth playing for the dog alone.
