_childDocuments_.review: I first played Ghost Trick a decade ago on iPod Touch, and I adored it. It stuck with me for years, and has always held the spot of my favorite puzzle game. Now, a decade later, I've replayed it on PC, and not only has it held up, it has surpassed my previous experience. The twists in the story got me all over again, and I couldn't help binging through the game because the story grabbed all my attention. The port is fantastically done, and is well worth getting, especially if you get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick is in my top two games of all time and it's not two. I first played Ghost Trick back in 2017 on the DS and I was blown away. I had heard that it was good but I couldn't imagine exactly how good it could possibly be. This is my third time playing it and I'm still blown away by how tightly written it is. There's so much that I had forgotten over the years but it holds up so well, and I wish I could talk about the story but it's so satisfying to watch it play out for yourself without knowing anything except the basis of "you're dead, you don't know who you are or why you died so you're trying to figure it out." I'll recommend this game until my dying breath, and even after I'm dead I'll have "play Ghost Trick" written on my gravestone. If you like mysteries, play this game. If you like puzzle games, play this game. If you like creating chaos and destruction, play this game. If you like fun, silly, well written and complex characters, play this game. If you like bright, unique and fun art styles, play this game. If you're into a solid soundtrack, play this game.  If you like dogs, play this game. If you like chicken, play this game. If you like ghosts, play this game.  If you like video games, just play Ghost Trick. I literally cannot recommend it enough. I've been going crazy with the knowledge that I have had after playing this game in 2017 and I literally cannot talk about it because it's all spoilers and if you want to feel that same rattling jar of thoughts about this game in your brain please play it, and then recommend it to your friends so maybe they'll play it too :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: If you're unfamiliar with Ghost Trick, this is a fine way to introduce yourself to it but it's pretty blatantly obvious that it's a touched up port of a DS/iOS game. UI elements are absolutely massive, character animations that used to run at ~24 FPS now run at 60 with some occasional notable jumps and hitches, and certain background elements don't even look like they were upscaled. If you already know the game inside and out, you get nice high-res graphics and the option of a remastered OST that is  really on-point, and can unlock full scene portraits and a music test by playing the game again -- although I can't tell, but two of the music tracks  have been locked behind preorder DLC?As for the game itself, it's known mostly as that cult classic DS game by the Ace Attorney studio trying their hand at a new property, and while it was a bit of a sales flop, is well-regarded for good reason. It's one of my favourite stories ever told, all of the characters are absolutely amazing, there's some masterful misdirection to keep you guessing at the biggest twists, and the moment-to-moment puzzle gameplay is at  on par with the Ace Attorney courtroom segments, without the constant retracing your steps and wondering where you missed a progression flag. I'd rather not say more than that, it's best experienced going in blind.And for the people complaining about the price, it costs as much now as it did when it was on the DS. Age has absolutely not devalued this game and it  a new port, so I don't see the problem.  Nevermind Denuvo, now Capcom's replaced it with some shady Russian DRM that may or may not be malware. Just get it on Switch unless Capcom unscrews their head from their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in time to fix this.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I played Ghost Trick when it originally came out on an em... ehm, on  borrowed Nintendo DS (yes I definitely had a girlfriend). Loved it back then. The PC re-release gave me an opportunity to offer penance and pay for the game myself. I was a tiny bit sceptical whether it would be worth it. Admittedly, it is a bit expensive if you know what you're doing, you can easily get through the game in about 15 hours. I think that's how long it took me. The remaining 30 hours was just me struggling with sliding puzzles (designed for elementary school children).As a huge fan of Shu Takumi, I can confidently say this is still in his top 3 best works. I dare say this game has  in all of video games (if you know you know). It gets a bit annoying in the prison section, before "The Great Escape" but after that it's a non stop edge-of-your-seat thriller combined with a slight dash of mystery and a big scoop of heartwarming.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: So as someone who has played the Ace Attorney series to the point of obsession, I admit it took me an embarrassingly long time to come around to this game. Probably partly due to the timing of its initial release and its subsequent languishment in relative obscurity on the DS, I never really gave this game much thought, even after learning of its connections with Shu Takumi and the AA series. I am very glad to say I've rectified that glaring oversight, and now I'm hoping to guide others to the same bliss I've recently experienced.This game is masterful, almost better than the gimmick it's built around should have allowed for. I played the game on a controller, so I cannot speak for how it plays on a mouse, but considering this game was ostensibly designed with a touch screen in mind, I wager it can't be too difficult. Either way, the gimmick itself is actually very fun to play around, but it would amount to little more than a passing curiosity, a , were it not for the frankly brilliant writing.Without giving too much away, Ghost Trick is, underneath all the silliness and style, essentially a very labyrinthine and turbulent mystery. Like all great mysteries, the less you know beforehand, the better the payoff, but the reveals are so stellar that I daresay this game honestly holds up better once you already know all of the secrets it has to reveal. This makes it a natural chaser to any AA game, and it's a damn crying shame that this is very likely to be a singular entry in the IP, a one-hit wonder. Please, if you have even the remotest interest in the AA series or mystery games in general, give this a try. It's not long, and it's one of the coolest experiences I've had in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: 10 years ago I bought a second hand copy of Ghost Trick for the DS and I loved it. _childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: JANUARY 2024 UPDATE:  Although it pains me to do so, I've changed my review to negative in response to Capcom changing the DRM of this game. When I bought Ghost Trick, I did so knowing it had Denuvo which is a familiar name at this point for better or worse. A recent update to this game changed the DRM to Enigma. Not only was this not disclosed but Enigma lives up to its name and I can't find much information about who creates it. Looking online only brought up some Russian company with the same name and a frankly quite sketchy looking website. I cannot in good conscience recommend you to install this game on your computer until we have more information on Enigma.===============================I first played Ghost Trick around 10 years ago. I remembered really enjoying the game and I remembered there being *something* special about the story-line but I couldn't really remember any of the details. Anyone who's familiar with the game will realise how funny that sounds, but it's the truth.When I saw the game had an HD remaster I decided to play it again and I'm really glad I did! If you enjoy puzzle games, Ghost Trick offers a pretty unique puzzle mechanic wrapped in a mysterious story featuring genuinely lovable characters. This all plays out to an amazing soundtrack to top it off.It's honestly incredible that with such an interesting puzzle mechanic, the part of the game that stands out the most is the story. Although it twists and turns in unbelievable directions, it comes together in a really satisfying way at the end.I won't say too much more to avoid spoiling anything but if you've never heard of Ghost Trick, maybe give the demo a try. This game made me laugh, this game made me cry, I'm so glad it's on PC now so more people can enjoy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Beat this game originally on the DS years ago so when the Steam pre-order first went up months ago not along after the Nintendo Direct announcement I had to get it again. Still need to get through this but I'm up to Chapter 3 and so far the remaster seems excellent; the graphics are much improved, the lack of the DS's dual screen is skillfully worked around with the new UI and controls, and the new remixed soundtrack is real nice too.Ghost Trick is one of my favorite games, Shu Takumi and the Ace Attorney team's magnum opus, and one of the greatest point and click adventure games of all time. The Rube Goldberg puzzles are fun, never getting too hard, but you still got to think on your feet a bit. The narrative is where the game truly shines the most though as its one of the best in the medium. The cast are all deeply endearing, the pacing is fantastic with some genuinely great twists and turns, and everything is tied up so satisfactorily and conclusively in the end. In an age of sequels and remakes, Ghost Trick is one of the greatest examples of a standalone game that didn't need a follow-up.Ghost Trick has been a cult classic game for years but hopefully now with this remaster it can be finally garner the success it always deserved. Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Immaculate game.Superb, endearing, heart-warming - I can't heap enough praise on it. I loved it when it first came out, and all these years later, it holds up. _childDocuments_.review: This game was probably one of the single most influential titles on me as a person. _childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Its a master piece, this game is Capcom at its absolute best. It rivals the writing of some of the best ace attorney games like Trials and Tributlations. It has a wholly unique gameplay loop that is actually really fun. Its EXTREMELY well paced, in around 12 hours you get a fully complete and deep story. Combine that with excellent music, stylish and fun visuals, an incredible port, and unforgettable characters and you end up with this miracle of a game. If you need to know if I recommend this game the answer is YES, go into it with as little information as possible and enjoy the ride. What follows from here is just me rambling about certain things that I noticed or that I want to write about.At the start of the game you wake up learning that you died, somehow you can manipulate physical objects around you and you have no idea who you are. Its up to you to learn who you are and what is happening in 1 night. This concept starts of fairly overwhelming. But the game does an extremely good job of introducing all these new characters, the rules of the world, and the eventual plot that it ends up feeling very digestible. That is in my opinion maybe its greatest strength, everything makes sense and everything always ends up feeling complete, there are so many times where other games leave the plot up to imagination or where nonsensical stuff just hangs in the background. Every relevant detail always gets explored and its always fun to see how it all fits into this massive puzzle of a story. It was always a massive joy when I made a discovery on my own and it ended up being true later, nothing is super obvious but at the same time every mystery feels solvable without the game shoving it in your face.My biggest complaint is that there is no short rewind function. There are so many things I wanted to experiment on, but in this game experimentation can quickly lead to a reset of the level. There are also moments where you make a small mistake and that also once again leads to a reset. And every time you reset you have to wait like a minute or 2 before being able to execute your plan again. I wish there was a way to rewind like 5 seconds back so I could try something again, I think that would have made for a smoother experience, but its not something that is even remotely a deal breaker. Every level is fairly short so any resetting never leads to big wastes of time.Usually this is the part where I gush about wanting a sequel, but this is maybe one of the first times I am satisfied with what I got and don't expect to want more. It feels like a complete product and that's what I love so much about this game. If you enjoy the wacky story telling of something like Danganronpa, ace attorney or if you enjoy the puzzle solving aspect of games like Limbo and Inside then you will probably end up loving this game. I think most people will end up enjoying this game and its totally worth its asking price of 30 euros. I give ghost trick my biggest recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so, listen. Hear me out:I've been a huge fan of this game since it's original DS release in the West. It is painfully, PAINFULLY underrated. It's getting more love now but it still deserves more love. Back during it's DS days? Oh man, very few people, even on the web, had played it. I was finding DS copies of this in the BARGAIN BINS at stores. Something that was a horrible crime to humanity and the universe. I remember seeing a trailer for it on the Wii back when you could see trailers for upcoming games on it.I think it may have been discovered late because secondhand copies of the original DS version went into the $100's later.Shu Tamaki's top works, Ace Attorney (the original trilogy) and Ghost Trick are absolute gems that came out on the DS in the mid 2000's and neither got the love they so rightfully deserved.I cannot tell you how much I adore this game. Shu Tamaki is one of the best writers of our time. (At least in video games) There are maybe four games that I will, without hesitation, purchase over and over and over again, no matter how many times it is re-released. (Ace Attorney being one of them, also Shu Tamaki's work, can't praise that trilogy enough) This is one of them and I was extremely happy to see it get the second chance it so rightly deserves. If you love visual novel puzzle games, buy it.If you hate visual novel puzzle games, buy it.If you don't care either way, buy it.Buy 10 copies. Make your friends buy a copy. Make your grandma buy a copy. I don't care. Everyone should experience this game at least once. I have three copies so far:The original DS copyA physical switch edition (Since Capcom U.S seems to hate giving us any physical copies)And now thisAnd I'm eyeing another version online as well1000/10 game. Shu Tamaki's writing is so good and clever I can only dream of being as great as he is. You are actually hurting yourself to not play this.If there is one thing I'd say, it's that I feel like the DS sprites had the tiniest little charm that the HD version doesn't have. Does that hurt the perfect score I'd give this game? Nope. The artwork is still amazing, the puzzles are clever and fun, the music is outstanding, the writing is top tier and the characters are well written and unforgettable.Just buy it. Play it. Love it.Pardon my passionate rant but I can't stress how much I love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I put this game off for so long man. Skipped it on DS, skipped it on iOS. For what it's worth, I probably couldn't appreciate the game as well then, as I do now. One of my buddies has been pinging me to play this game ever since, but I couldn't wrap my head around playing a game that's so distinctively outside of what I normally play.A puzzle game with heavy dialogue elements to where it's almost a visual novel, no voice-acting, and a slow start. It's antithetical to the games I generally play. Not to mention that with this port, it shoves the entire DS sized screen across my entire monitor, making one-page of dialog(ue?) now consume 500.Despite all of this, I fell in absolute love. The characters, the rising questions, the mechanics, that music tuned to important events occurring. For what the DS was limited on when this game first came out, and what little room they had to work with, it oozes style with grace.There isn't much to say about this game without spoiling things otherwise, but I'll leave it to that: I have a lot against the general gameplay/genre here, and I fell in love. If you feel like you might do the same, give it a shot.But also...

_childDocuments_.review: This game popped up out of nowhere from my perspective, when years ago my sister lent me her copy on the (3?)DS. I played it in one long night, and despite it not being my preferred genre (I've never been big on puzzle games), this game found itself in the dubious position of being my personal favorite title.My sister ended up giving me her copy because I enjoyed it so thoroughly, and while that went missing in one of many, many moves between then, the game's always held that spot in my heart. So of course I picked up the remaster (almost) as soon as it launched, and played it in one sitting yesterday.Game's still amazing. I wish I could play it again without remembering it all, but that I guess is the biggest downside.Remaster quality wise is fantastic, everything is incredibly sharp, animations are smooth all over, and while there are certain sprite foibles (paint stains on Jowd's hoodie 'flipping' location when he turns), I believe they have more been 'preserved' than forgotten. Intent instead of accident.Anyhow, if you haven't played this game before, do yourself a favor and just play it. It's a super interesting, smart, heartfelt story with killer style, fun (and funny) writing, and clever (but not too difficult) puzzles. Remaster adds some additional stuff in the vein of old DVD extra features, an image gallery, music player, and some nifty little slide puzzles that have moving backgrounds of in-game scenes.My biggest wish would've been to have the soundtrack included as an additional download, though. Either lemme pay extra for it, put it on Spotify, or put it in as a freebie, but it's a bummer that my options to listen to tracks are either boot up the game or find it on youtube.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that was amazing on the Nintendo DS, and is amazing now. This is an easy recommend for people who love Ace Attorney, as it has series creator Shu Takumi in peak storytelling form, but I would also wholeheartedly recommend it for anyone who loves a good mystery story, fun characters, incredible animations and top notch music. Also makes for a great experience playing together with a friend or loved one - Definitely a great "pseudo co-op" experience when you puzzle your way through the story together.It's not an incredibly long game but it never overstays its welcome, the narrative resolves extremely satisfyingly, and other than the very occasional moment of iffy puzzle design, you won't have too much trouble understanding the logic to progress after a few tries.Also, here is where you will find the best dog in videogames, and anything I could say to explain that would be a spoiler, so ... just play :D

I'd stay up late, under the covers circa 2010, puzzling away. Now I sit in my own home, reliving the memories.This game is a masterpiece. Wondering if you should play it? You should. _childDocuments_.review: I had already played this game about a year back, and it became one of my favorites. Great story, unforgettable characters, and intuitive puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a puzzle adventure that is similar to the classic Phoenix Wright games then Ghost Trick is for you.  Ghost Trick features great puzzles, a great story, and a great big mystery to solve. Jam out to some excellent music while wielding your ghost tricks to solve puzzles, protect people, and solve the mystery of your own death before dawn.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is a remake of a 13(!) year old game for the 3DS. The graphic improved alot and the controls are also mapped so it makes sense for either keyboard+mouse or plain old controler.But lets get to the meat of it all: The game.And here shines Ghost Trick the most. You play as a ghost that can interact with the environment to achieve certain goals (most of the time save other people from dying). You do that to figure out the mysterious circumstances of your own death before you vanish at the dawn of day. Due to limited options while interact with all objects the riddles are not really difficult, so please dont expect Outer Wild levels of complexity. But, as with Phoenix Wright, the riddles are nevertheless quite fun. And every character you meet (even the animals) have their own quirks and characteristics, so you wont forget any of them anytime soon.The sound track was also remastered and fits every scene really well.In addition there were so really helpful quality of life features added, like level select if you want to play a specific chapter again. And now you have the option to complete slider puzzels as a bonus as well.The story maybe starts slow but trust me when I say, it will get really juicy.So as a final review: The game is really good to scratch that capcom riddle itch for a short while and I really hope they continue this trend to bring classics to PC (looking at you Miles Edworth Investigations!).
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick is absolutely a game I would recommend that everyone play. It's really, truly well-written, it has great art and music, and you feel somewhat clever when figuring things out.The only weaknesses it has are being a bit too hand-holdy at times and... not really being made for repeat playthroughs, hence my 30 mins after having played it way back elsewhere, because it really is just the same thing again. There are no alternate solutions, hidden easter eggs or anything.It also suffers a bit from its "save" model which is checkpoints that, if you take a bit to figure out the right order of things can leave you redoing a lot of stuff and getting the same dialogue over and over, just because there's one thing you're having trouble nailing perfectly.Still, I would call it very minor stuff. _childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one for me. I have been wanting to play Ghost Trick for years now, so I was quite intrigued about the game coming to PC. After having finally played it, my feelings are mixed.The game itself is great. The core idea and game mechanics are intuitive and innovative. It has a unique and somewhat "indie" feel to it that I would really like to see more developers dig into. However, the story and characterizations felt somewhat flat for me. Coming from Ace Attorney, I was expecting a deep and emotional narrative with fleshed-out characters. For me, the game did not deliver here. I liked the story and the quirky personalities, but I felt like I did not really learn much about most of these people, nor about the world they live in. The protagonists felt very "game-y", if that makes sense. I could probably summarize each individual within two sentences, and I have no idea what their lives would look like outside of the game's narrative scope. Considering that this is in fact a narrative-driven game, this to me felt quite odd. What is there, is enjoyable, though.Most twists I saw coming from miles away, but maybe Ace Attorney has trained me too well in the way the game's author writes story arcs. Without spoiling anything: I was especially disappointed by the main antagonist, whose motivations and behavior felt very cartoonish, mundane, implausible and honestly somewhat stupid to me. Do you know TV series that build an intriguing mystery and then, when the reveal finally happens many hours later, some of the magic just vanishes into thin air and you are like "Oh, okay, that's all there was to it?" Yeah, I got a bit of this feeling here. It is not extremely bad in a way that lessens the game significantly for me. But it still felt a bit underwhelming -- like out of all possible solutions, they went with a rather boring one.The puzzles had a weird dichotomy to them where for the most part, they are extremely easy, but then sometimes, they get ludicrously convoluted and require a lot of try & error. Not quite a walk in the park. Easy puzzles are okay if they drive the narrative. Hard puzzles are okay as well, if they can be solved by logic. This often did neither. The easy ones played out mostly for themselves but often worked as breaks between story bits, whereas the harder ones were pretty much impossible to actually "solve" by logic. I think this is an innate issue with the concept of the ghost tricks, because they work as a chain of events that build upon one another. Each trick changes the puzzle in a way that opens up possible next steps, but these changes are for the most part unforeseeable and sometimes feel absolutely arbitrary. You  to try'n'error your way through until you make a mistake, rewind, try another option, and see what happens instead. This is interesting in its own way, it is not a bad mechanic. But what it  is that it greatly takes away from the perception of having "solved" a mystery.Generally, I would absolutely recommend the game for its uniqueness and innovativeness. However, the remake feels lackluster to me. The UI is atrocious and not at all adapted for PC play. Also, hopefully without overusing these comparisons: the game goes for the same asking price as, for example, the Great Ace Attorney Chronicles, which took me 115 hours to get through. Ghost Trick I played through in about 12 hours. It is definitely overpriced.To sum it up, Ghost Trick is a nice, creative, but very short and somewhat faulty gem. It feels to me like an extended proof of concept, and a very good one at that. If it goes on sale, you should absolutely try it out. For the full asking price, I cannot recommend you get it. If that is of no concern to you and you still do get it, though, you are in for a few very enjoyable hours with some hickups along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick holds a really special place in my heart. I first played it when I was a literal fetus with a DS. I could barely read English back then, and only understood enough of the story to get by. However, the bits I understood still blew my little baby brain out of my skull, and Ghost Trick was my first ever experience with a truly phenomenal video game story. I would then go on to discover Ace Attorney, Zero Escape, Bioshock, etc... Now, 14 years later, I've read a ♥♥♥♥ ton of crazy visuals novels, and played a ♥♥♥♥ ton of narrative-driven games. To this day, I still play video games for their unparalleled storytelling potential, and Ghost Trick truly was my gateway drug into a mad, mad world. You may ask, then, now that I'm revisiting this game in my manchild years, does it still hold up? Well,...Pros:+ Like any Shu Takumi game (the entire Ace Attorney franchise), the story of Ghost Trick is wonderfully weird and layered like an onion. The more you peel, the more you find. Each chapter gives you answers while piling on more and more mysteries until all the pieces fit together beautifully in an orgy of reveals towards the very end. For a story with so many moving pieces, Ghost Trick still manages to move briskly and stay concise in its runtime. It's a complex but very cleanly executed mystery story, and I respect it for that. A lot of mystery stories, in their never-ending quests to pile on plot twist after plot twist to appear more complex than they really are *cough* ISLAND *cough*, overstays their welcome and makes an absolute mess of things. Ghost Trick weaves a great mystery, gives you answers, then leaves. No bullsht. Play it and see for yourself. + For a relatively short game, Ghost Trick does a surprising amount with its characters. They all think, act,  and feel like people, with most of the main cast being sympathetic or interesting in some way. I didn't really dislike anyone in the story, and they all have their own character moments that make them memorable when the story is said and done. After making the first three Ace Attorney games, Shu Takumi has a very firm grasp on how to write strong characters, and it really shows in this game. + The artstyle is still timeless. This game is a prime example of artstyle being superior to graphical fidelity. If games like Ghost Trick went for a more realistic graphical style, they would have aged like milk left out in the Arizona desert. This game looks like it hasn't aged a day since 2010. The character portraits look crispier than ever on an HD screen. The 3D models, while a bit stiff at times, are still really stylized, vibrant, and full of character. This is a Shu Takumi game through and through - the characters' movements all have that signature over-the-top, cartoonish, and animated Ace Attorney energy to it.+ The soundtrack is great. Without being compressed to hell and back and played through tinny DS speakers, you can finally hear the music as it's meant to be sound, and damn does it sound good. It weaves suspense, mystery, tension, joy, sadness, and everything in between. Throughout my playthrough, I kept switching back and forth between the original and remastered soundtracks, and I gotta give this one to the remastered soundtrack. Not only does it keep the essence of all the original tracks, it also hones in on the things that are good about them and makes them even better. The catchy melodies pop out more, the beats have a stronger kick to them, and the background instruments are a lot clearer - that kinda thing. + There is absolutely nothing like Ghost Trick out there. It's been 14 years and the game's artstyle, gameplay mechanics, and story still have not been replicated. The only thing that can even be remotely like Ghost Trick would be Ghost Trick 2, which sadly, does not exist. Danganronpa, Ace Attorney, AI: The Somnium Files, Gnosia, Zero Escape, Ever17, and many, many, many more - take your pick. I can't recall any mystery game out there like Ghost Trick, and that's insane. I don't know how Shu Takumi even comes up with this ♥♥♥♥. Cons:- Some plot points are a bit contrived and require a degree of suspension of disbelief. However, I think this isn't too bad since Ghost Trick never set itself up to be this super-realistic, gritty murder mystery or anything. Right from the beginning it lets you know that it's a weird, over-the-top, and slightly cartoony mystery game. The contrived plot points that are there all serve to create a more coherent mystery, so if you can suspend your disbelief a bit, the rest of the story will unfold quite naturally around them, making them not too jarring when all is said and done.- The artstyle can be cartoonish and PG to the point of breaking immersion. I know I just said this is not an overly-realistic or gritty game, but the lack of blood is something that kept bothering me throughout. In a game where watching people die in horrific ways and then finding ways to save them is the main gameplay loop, a little bit of blood can really help to elevate the tension and make you take the situation a lot more seriously. People can get absolutely eviscerated in this game but there will never be any hint of damage on them whatsoever. I know it's an E-rated DS game so they couldn't exactly show that kind of stuff, but at least give me a little bit for immersion's sake, like in Ace Attorney or Danganronpa. I can't take deaths seriously when characters take point-blank shotgun shells to the chest and "die" but still look completely fine like they're in a Tom and Jerry episode. This takes a lot of tension away from the otherwise very serious and suspenseful story of this game.  - No fast-forward option. This was one of my biggest gripes with the original DS version, and I was looking forward to this quality of life improvement in the remastered version. Well, this remaster lets me fast forward dialogue, but not the actual in-game scenes, which are the actual time-consuming parts. Each time you mess up, you still have to watch the entire "case" unfold again until it finally reaches the part that you need to interact with. This can get really annoying later on as cases get more complex and there are a lot of moving pieces and windows of opportunities you need to look out for.- Like Ace Attorney, some logic puzzles can be a bit obtuse. Sometimes, you have to do some really wacky sh!t to get things to work out the exact way needed to solve the case. Luckily, the game regularly gives you hints on what to do because it realizes that if it didn't, no one would be able to figure some of this sh!t out without pure trial and error or looking up a walkthrough. It's THAT obtuse. TLDR: 8/10. While it's not a massive, sprawling mystery story for the ages or anything, for its uniqueness, ambition, and pristine execution, Ghost Trick will always remain an absolute gem of a mystery game. It is definitely up there as one of Shu Takumi's best games. Even when I revisit it as an adult with a more critical eye, it still manages to hold up extremely well. Save for a few quality of life hiccups, the core of the experience, which is to say the mystery, story, and characters, is rock solid, and I'd recommend anyone who is interested in a short, sweet, and very unique mystery game to give Ghost Trick a try. You will definitely not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: "Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective" is more than just a puzzle game—it's an emotional journey that keeps you guessing at every turn. This 2010 classic by Shu Takumi, the genius behind the "Ace Attorney" series, has been reimagined in a stunning Steam remaster. If you're looking for a game that will tug at your heartstrings, leave you in awe with its plot twists, and keep you guessing until the very end, this is it. Let's dive into why "Ghost Trick" is a storytelling masterpiece.At its core, "Ghost Trick" is a deeply moving story about identity, redemption, and the ties that bind us. You play as Sissel, a ghost with no memory of his past, who must navigate the afterlife to discover the truth about his death. What starts as a simple whodunit quickly spirals into an intricate web of interconnected characters and events. Every step you take reveals new layers of complexity, and the game masterfully intertwines narrative threads that seem unrelated but culminate in an awe-inspiring conclusion.The plot twists in "Ghost Trick" are nothing short of mind-blowing. Just when you think you have the story figured out, it flips on its head. These twists aren't just shocking for shock's sake; they are meticulously crafted, each one building on the last to create a tapestry of intrigue. The game keeps you on the edge of your seat, eagerly anticipating the next revelation, and the final twist will leave you gasping in disbelief.The characters in "Ghost Trick" are what make the story truly memorable. Each character has a unique personality, backstory, and motivation, and their development throughout the game is exceptional. From the endearing camaraderie between Sissel and his companions to the heartwarming tales of redemption and forgiveness, the characters bring depth and emotion to the narrative. It's rare to find a game where you care about every character, but "Ghost Trick" accomplishes this effortlessly.The emotional impact of "Ghost Trick" is profound. The game explores themes of love, loss, and sacrifice, and there are moments that will make you laugh, cry, and everything in between. Whether it's the poignant flashbacks that shed light on Sissel's past or the touching relationships that form between characters, the emotional resonance is palpable. The story builds to an unforgettable climax that will stay with you long after the credits roll.One of the reasons "Ghost Trick" is so effective is its impeccable pacing. The game balances moments of intense action with quieter, character-driven scenes, allowing players to truly connect with the story. The way the narrative unfolds, revealing just enough to keep you intrigued while holding back key information, is a testament to Shu Takumi's storytelling prowess. The Steam remaster enhances this experience with its improved visuals and sound, bringing the story to life in new and vibrant ways."Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective" is an emotional rollercoaster that takes you on a journey through mystery, redemption, and the power of human connection. With its brilliant plot twists, heartfelt characters, and a story that resonates on a deep level, this game is a must-play for anyone who appreciates exceptional storytelling. The Steam remaster breathes new life into this classic, offering a polished experience that captures the essence of the original while enhancing it for a modern audience. If you're ready for a game that will make you laugh, cry, and question everything you thought you knew, "Ghost Trick" is the perfect choice. Don't miss out on this unforgettable adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: I could start and finish this review by simply saying I truly think this is a perfect game but i think that would be a disservice to the 2 people that will read this review! This game achieves everything it wants to do with absolutely no mistakes - it tells a fantastic story, interlaced with incredible  characters, plot threads and twists without ever leaving the player frustrated or confused - You feel every time a question is answered at least one new one pops up, but you can still feel yourself getting closer to the end, meaning the plot is always progressing - a very tough balance to hit but this game nails it perfectly!The puzzles in this game come from a simple start to get you used to the mechanics but ramp up in complexity fairly quickly - initially i was frustrated by time sensitivity (i hate feeling under time pressure in games) and puzzles feeling very trial and error  heavy but i learned quickly that is by design - You are heavily encouraged both in story and gameplay to rewind and mess around with different objects to see how you can use them at different times to different effects and are never "punished" in lore or in gameplay as you can quickly get back to key points in the puzzles in less then 30 seconds once you know what you are doing, so don't let this put you off!Going into the final quarter of this game i remember thinking "There is still way too many plot points going into the finale of this game there is absolutely no way ANY writer could tie a neat bow on all of them" but unbelievably not only did they manage to, but they managed to do with finesse - so many games stumble at the final hurdle after hours of great setup but this game nails the landing perfectly with an emotional climax that will leave you thinking about and digesting the ending for days afterwardsA final note on characters - The game does an amazing job bringing out these characters personalities while leaving them all likeable even while their motivations and morality  remain unclear, sometimes with similar games i groan or get annoyed by characters but in Ghost trick i was invested in pretty much everyones storyUnlike this review there is no fat whatsoever in this game, it's a shame it did not do so well commercially and relies on word of mouth of passionate fans to spread the love for this underappreciated game, if even one person plays this game based on this review i have succeeded.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple but unique and intuitive mechanics, a story that remains constantly interesting and entertaining, and features vivid locations, expressive personality filled animations, and two of the best pets in the medium.A puzzle mystery game where you wake up with no memories after having recently been killed only to witness an assassin threatening a woman near your body and discovering that you have developed special powers. These "ghost tricks" allow you jump between and manipulate objects, travel through phone lines to other locations, and to travel back in time four minutes after a person has died to change their fate which also allows you to speak with them in the past and once they are safe in the present. In one night you attempt to keep your potential friends and allies safe from a group of assassins, discover the truth about your powers and others who have gained similar abilities, and learn of a decade old event that ties together your former life, the police, and foreign spies.Each stage has you using your ghost tricks to manipulate objects in a way that will effect the environment or people in the environment in a way that leads to you completing your goals. This can have you moving and manipulating objects to increase your reach allow you to jump into new things, manipulating lights or sounds to attract or distract people, leading a character through a dark room while avoiding assailants, or timing multiple interactions to create a particular sequence of events that will aid you. There are some new mechanics added over time but little gameplay wise changes over the course of the adventure. This can normally be a bad thing but each area is designed in a way where they are interesting and amusing to explore, the story that remains the highlight is allowed to progress quickly, and none of the events ever become overly cluttered, confusing, or tedious to deal with in a way that would detract from the enjoyment of the game and its strongest elements. The narrative over time explaining why certain thing can't or couldn't be done in a way that fits for the setting and often in ways that make more sense as more elements of the story reveal themselves.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: In , you play as Sissel, a man who finds a woman being attacked by a mysterious assassin, only to discover that he himself is already dead. Using his Ghost Tricks, Sissel is able to manipulate the environment to stop the assassin and save the damsel in distress.His relief is short lived as Sissel realizes that death not only robbed him of his body, but of all of his memories as well. Teaming up with the girl, Lynne, Sissel sets out to discover who he was and why he was killed. He has to hurry though: for his ghostly existence will be snuffed out by the next sunrise…The game’s main mechanic involves Sissel using his powers to manipulate objects in the environment to create a Rube Goldberg-esque chain reaction to save someone who is about to be murdered. Yes, just like , it is almost always murder, and just like Ace Attorney, it is very satisfying when you successfully figure out the game’s puzzles.If I had to give  a genre, I would call it an adventure/puzzle game. While figuring out the puzzles does take some amount of creativity, it also requires an equal amount of just messing around with objects to see what they do. If I told you that you would have to complete said puzzles while also under a time limit, you might think that’s unreasonable, but it’s actually .Since there’s no penalty for resetting the puzzle, and since the puzzles are all less than five minutes long, it creates a gameplay loop that rewards trial-and-error exploration. I even discovered, to my amusement/horror, two instances in the game where a specific series of actions will, instead of preventing the murder, make it even .The writing for the story, is of course, brilliant. If you’re familiar with Shu Takumi’s previous work in , you’ll feel right at home in a story about police detectives relentlessly seeking the truth against a series of escalating threats. There were multiple points where I audibly exclaimed “Wait, what??” in response to what I had witnessed. Sometimes ridiculous, sometimes heartwarming, always entertaining.The soundtrack is what the kids would call ‘a certified banger’.  fans will feel right at home as  OST emotional beats echo those found in the  games. The remastered version available on Steam have given the already solid soundtrack additional clarity.The graphics are…adequate. While the character’s text sprites are reasonably detailed, the overworld models are somewhat simplistic, though I never found it enough to distract from the game. I suspect that part of the issue is that I am playing a game originally designed for the much smaller screen of the 3DS, on the much larger PC monitor.If you are a fan of the  series, the idea of a ghost setting up elaborate Rube Goldberg devices, or just a fan of good writing, then  is will worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: originally came out on the DS in 2010 towards the end of the DS's lifespan, and as a result it had a rather poor reception in Japan. The game follows Sissel, a man who had just been shot and killed who is traveling across town trying to figure out who he is, while also preventing the unfortunate deaths of those he finds by rewinding the clock and going back . You're given a myriad of tools in order to save each person, and the puzzles themselves are a delight to complete. Each character is vibrant and a joy to interact with, you'll rarely (if ever) be bored by any conversation, as it'll either be fun and comedic or have fun story to dig into. The story itself is quite engaging as well, taking course over a single night of trying to figure out the truth of why you were killed, as well as why the people that are involved with your death also seem to be wanted dead. By the time you've gotten through the game, you'll be wishing that there were more chapters just so you can keep playing.The soundtrack in this game is phenomenal and this remaster comes with a jukebox so you can listen to your favorite tracks, which are unlocked as you complete chapters. Likewise, new illustrations and visuals are similarly unlocked, and you can easily view the information that your character "knows" so if you ever feel lost on who someone is, you'll be given an easy refresher. The game was remastered to perfection with stunning crystal clear graphics, which is certainly a pleasant surprise considering it was a DS (and later ported to phone) game originally. Furthermore, the gameplay feels clean and easy. For those who played on the DS, it can take a little time to adjust, but for new players it won't be difficult to get used to.The game respects the player's time, and there's no end of unique dialogue that you can find by exploring around between Chapters. The Achievements in this game are quite fun too and make for interesting and challenging plays of a given Chapter, they're not a chore to get for the 100%. Even the new slide puzzle section that was added as a bonus was a nice surprise that they didn't need to add.All in all, I would call this an amazing example of a remaster. It would have been nice to gain an extra epilogue Chapter in theory, for those who have already played the game before on the DS so they can have new additional puzzles, but otherwise I'd say everything else was perfect. For the pricetag, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: It's obvious that anyone who likes Ace Attorney should play Ghost Trick. So instead I'll discuss the less obvious: Why someone who doesn't care for Ace Attorney (or simply hasn't played it) should still play this game. Ace Attorney games often have filler cases that are barely related to the main plot. Even in the important cases, there are still parts that drag. Ghost Trick, on the hand, has very little fat. Pretty much every person or location is important in some way. Every chapter has some exciting reveal, or at least a memorable set-piece. It's a roller-coaster ride from beginning to end. This does come with the caveat that Ghost Trick is a lot shorter than the average Ace Attorney game (about a dozen hours for a first-time player). But quality over quantity, and all that. While Ace Attorney sets itself up as a logical - albeit quirky - legal drama, anyone who's played it can tell you that it rarely matches the actual law. And that's before the magic gets introduced. This can be frustrating both for the story, and when trying to solve the game's puzzles. Ghost trick avoids all this by mainly relying on it's own set of rules surrounding the ghost world. Time travelling ghosts may be an out-there concept, but it works because of the internally consistent logic. The basics are established early on, then expanded upon as the game goes. This also means that learning the how and why of ghost powers becomes a fun mystery in itself. As a visual novel, Ace Attorney's animation is charming, but limited. Anything beyond the most basic actions relies heavily on the player's imagination. Not in Ghost Trick. Everything is presented in a detailed side-on view, where characters constantly interact with the environment and each other. This isn't just for show, either: These interactions are often used in puzzles, too. But Ghost Trick isn't content with just functional animation: Every action is lovingly animated with as much personality as possible. From a dog's excited barking, to a novelist's furious typing, to Cabanela's... everything. The biggest selling point for the remaster is seeing all this great animation made even better with a higher resolution and frame rate.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute delight of a game, with great story, music, and a very unique gameplay gimmick that is a refreshing take on the puzzle genre. This is a remaster of an old DS game but the re-arranged soundtracks and updated visuals have shown that the style can stand the test of time, and being touch-screen focused it transitions SMOOTH to PC. If you missed this gem back in the DS days don't miss it this time, this game is an all time fav of mine.This game you play as "Sissel", a recently departed soul who's lost their memory, and is seeking to solve the mystery of who killed them and why. The gameplay gimmick is you move from item to item through the "Ghost World", and then manipulate them, all while the rest of the world plays out around you. This really gives you the feeling of being a poltergeist haunting the area, such as manipulating objects in a chain of events to simply navigate, or making a noise to alert a person to draw them in to investigate. An early puzzle has you turn on a fan and blender, all so the fan can blow a nearby flag rope into the blender which catches the rope and hoists the flag so you can ascend in the flag itself. It lends itself very well to environmental use.Because of this beautiful mix of having characters and events unfold in front of you and even react to the odd changes you present, this creates such fun interactions with the environment. Not only do you use items in some clever ways, but you use them to manipulate the people too.All of this becomes especially prevalent in the games 2nd gimmick; finding somebody else who's died and going back to a mere minutes before their tragic fate in an attempt to avert it. This will have you racing the clock, while trying to take advantage of routes in the environment that may only exist for a few moments, forcing you to plan your actions careful. They use this gimmick to the fullest, and each puzzle is just as refreshing as the last for it.This all might not stand out as much if it weren't for the very animated cast. What's really nice about this is that you have a primary cast where the mystery isn't paused by foolishness or stupidity, but where they're all actually reasonably smart and come to genuine conclusions. Very goofy, all with their charm, but also recognising the situation for what it is.Plus the story at large is a fun take on the murder mystery. The story has you questioning what's going on with your limited information, and challenges even the most basic assumptions from the get-go.If there's any complaints about this game, it's that it sometimes relies too much on trial-and-error where some interactions just won't make sense until you simply try it (at which point you may lose your 1 opportunity to progress in that attempt and have to restart the attempt). Similarily, there's a particular solution where you attempt to guide somebody and the area you gotta bring them to isn't the most obvious place imo (to put it simply, it doesn't look like they should be able to reach there, but they can) so it may leave some players stumped.But that's a minor gripe on an otherwise beautiful gem of the game. Don't pass up on it if you like puzzles, mysteries, or are a fan of games with similar casts like Phoenix Wright.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick is one of the very few games that I'd consider to be nigh perfect in all aspects of the genre and beyond. Its story, characters and narrative are so cleverly interwoven with one another and with the riveting and truly unique gameplay wrapping it all together, that I can't help but recommend it to anyone who's even mildly curious about it and/or interested in an incredibly fine, fun, captivating murder mystery thriller. Shu Takumi, best recognized as the creator of the Ace Attorney games, as well as this, truly gave it his all with this one, as well as his incredible team of artists and co. that helped shape this wonderful game, and it shows. This, to me, is Shu Takumi's finest work to date and it's no wonder he and Capcom decided to shine the spotlight upon it once again, after the rather criminally lackluster marketing for the original NDS version of the game had. Those that have experienced GT on the NDS will certainly have a fantastic time with this remake, as well. All of the tracks of the originals have had their music remixed and re-arranged to suit the newer hardware the game's now available on, including some new tracks as well, and I fell in love with the new renditions immediately and I feel many will feel the same way. The classic tracks are also available to switch to, should you prefer to hear them instead. If you're a fan of the Ace Attorney/Visual Novel games in any capacity, I do implore you to go and play Ghost Trick. The characters are just as likeable, fun and intriguing as the cast of the AA games. The puzzles are fun and intuitive and the narrative is absolutely brilliant from start to end and will likely make you want to re-experience it all over again once you're done. As with any good story, many of the plot's elements are foreshadowed and hinted at earlier on in the story, making for a very rewarding second playthrough ^^ An easy 10/10. Missile's best boi

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that came on Steam without much fanfare but in this day and age its importance cannot be understated. It is a single player, narrative-centric game with puzzle/adventure aspects that mainly thrives in exploring its colourful cast of characters and supernatural/absurd premise.Being a port of a 3DS game may turn away potential customers who know that port usually equals trash, but other than some minor control issues with the keyboard which one will quickly acclimate themselves with, it is damn near perfect. The story and characters are excellent, the music sublime and how enjoyable the game is on a Steam Deck should not be understated.So, if either: 1) You are nostalgic of an era when a game was a complete product without microtransactions that had a story with a beginning and an end you could actually finish,2) You are a fan of puzzle and adventure games with the illusion your actions influence the outcome of the story (and it IS an illusion, no real story changing stuff but really well-executed),3) You do not mind a cartoonish/absurd story with funny characters and eventsThen I 100% recommend to buy this game, even at full price. It is totally worth it. If you are sceptical about any of the above, keep it in mind for an eventual discount and try it at a later date. It is a slam dunk of a game to play during that odd winter weekend you are stuck at home due to the flu or something.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a port to a game that has flew under everyone's radar. I will begin with saying that this game is definitely a game to play. The average play time for this game is 12 hours but I managed to finished the game in about 102 hours (Not sure where the extra 2 hours is coming from). The OST is def one of the best parts of the game, very suave and detective like. Characters are very memorable, each one having their own quirk. The story is def another great part of the game, the plot twist being well worth the time it takes to get to it. In terms of the difficulty, I honestly did not find the game to be hard really. Due to the game's mechanics, there isn't much "variability" in what a player can do, I kinda figured things out pretty quickly because there isn't really that many "pieces" to work with, the environment essentially lays out what you need to do, and the dialogue will hold your hand and flat out tell you what to do. There is also not really any penalty for not solving things in time as you can easily just reset every puzzle (not sure if this applies to the deathless achievements but I feel if you reset at the last second then it would still count). For about 70% of the game, the mechanics don't change, they end up introducing another "ghost trick" to vary gameplay but I feel this would've been better earlier in the game. Overall I give this game an 8.5/10. Story, OST, unique game mechanics, and characters are all amazing. The difficulty brings it down a bit because of how easy it is to see what you need to do and dialogue flat out telling you. This is coming from a dev of Ace Attorney which is IMO one of the hardest story based logic games I have played so I had expected a bit more

_childDocuments_.review: I say this completely truly and genuinely after a 3rd playthrough after like a decade: This is one of the greatest games ever made.No spoilers here, mostly just me gushing. Skip to the end for a few criticisms, but from the graphics and art design, to the music (now wonderfully remastered!), and most importantly to the gameplay and story, Ghost Trick shines nearly flawlessly in every regard in a way very very few games can achieve.I really struggle to think of another game, particularly within the genre of puzzle games since that's about the closest place you can put this, that so expertly interweaves the story with the gameplay mechanics. To make up an analogue, imagine if Baba is You had a compelling mystery to explain and drive forward why you're doing the wacky nonsense that you are. Thankfully this game is not quite such a headscratcher: The puzzles can get tough, and at times it can take some trial and error of banging your head on a wall, but the game is pretty good at giving you hints on where to go and the number of moving parts in a given puzzle usually make it easy enough to isolate a solution over time even if you're stumped.A particular note of appreciation for this game's art style: It was cute and charming 13 years ago on a little DS screen, and now it's gorgeous and oozing style today in this top-notch remaster. 60 fps and strong crisp HD lines do amazingly well to enhance the already excellent visual design and lovingly animated characters.Okay, so two minor sticking points. Not deal breakers, but they're things I think worth knowing to set your expectations about the "nearly flawless" part of this game. One, some puzzles do get a *little* too obtuse. Just one or two, and we're not talking "Monkey Island" tier, but if you get stuck there is no shame in grabbing a spoiler free guide to help your first play through. And second, when you do get stuck, you'd best have a snack or something because the checkpointing is very hit or miss and you may be stuck rewatching some scene and fast forwarding through a bit of dialogue for your retry. Retries, more often than not.If you have any appreciation for strong puzzles and/or an excellent mystery story with fun characters, you HAVE to play Ghost Trick. Emphasis on "or", even if you think you don't like puzzle games do yourself a favor and just grab a spoiler free walk through to enjoy the story, because you're still in a for a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: From the creators of the Phoenix Wright series comes a remaster of one of the last great games of the Nintendo DS generation. Ghost Trick puts you in the shoes of someone who is newly deceased and is attempting to remember who he is and how he died. Using his new 'Ghost Tricks', he is able to help prevent the deaths of those he encounters while also trying to see how his fate is tied to theirs.This is a wonderful and digitally beautiful remake of the 2010 classic. The overly exaggerated animations and gorgeous 2D sprites show just how revolutionary this was for 2010 and is equally as impressive in 2024. I appreciate how they handled the transition from a duel screen setup to one that works with just one, however the character icon was often too big and covered a lot of the background image which would sometimes be an intense "someone is about to die" scene. This wasn't a huge deal but I do wish the character and dialogue boxes were a bit smaller.The 'Ghost Tricks' mentioned earlier are the standout mechanic of the game and will be your only line of defense at maneuvering from point a to point b and preventing deaths. Many levels will require you to watch the scene play out to see where you witness a death first hand just to gather information before manipulating the objects around you. It requires a lot of trial and error as many objects can serve as red herrings and will force you to restart the death sequence. It's not too difficult to where it becomes tedious and these sequences are only a minute or two long, so not much time is wasted - however, there is only  correct solution for each of these puzzles which limits creativity and free thinking. More often than not, the actual solutions are a bit illogical and almost defy my line of thinking which I wasn't a huge fan of.The story is a relatively dark one that centers around evil organizations and people who spread death in their path - these deaths can usually be prevented with our ghost tricks so it's not all that bad. The plot twists rival the greats such as Bioshock and Spec Ops: The Line. That being said, there is a LOT of dialogue in this 12-15 hour adventure and some of it can feel incredibly drawn out as each chapter focuses on a death or collecting evidence or intel. If you're visiting this game as an Ace Attorney fan though, this shouldn't come as a surprise or be too bothersome.Ghost Trick has a few missteps with it's story and lack of complete freedom in puzzle solving, but this was a beautiful and well cared for remaster of the original classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Nice visual novel puzzle game, with great music, an engaging story and characters with nice twists & turns. The storytelling & characters explanations make sense and has a lot of charm and character with a positive spin on what could have been a potentially darker story and characters. The story places you in the shoes of your character coming to realisation of being a ghost spirit who wakes up unable to remember what happened and why he is not alive anymore. The game starts with needing to save the life of the detective who the main character was meeting. Discovering now as a spirit can interact & able to manipulate non-living objects in a way that can set off a chain of events to change fates. Along with ghost trick powers of being able to rewind time to four minutes before a death and thus giving the opportunity to now save lives, & further change & rewrite events to continue the adventure of trying to find out and solve what happened, why & and how these supernatural powers were obtained and who our character is, puts the player on a fun journey of meeting lots of well designed puzzle location scenarios & interesting characters who are somehow interlinked.The character animations, environment detail and small attention to details are superb.The puzzles are clever and are not too difficult. Considering the game origin is from the portable DS hardware, unsurprisingly the game pacing is perfect and can be played per episode length and return later for the next chapter. The puzzles were clearly designed with stylus in mind but that does not detract from the gameplay as the powers of a ghost translates as normal to PC. Main negatives would be the final chapter has a lot of exposition dump to tie loose ends that were not sufficiently covered in previous chapters so there is more reading required than normal in one go, than experienced in the rest of the previous chapters. This maybe could have been alleviated with an extra chapter to match the pacing of the rest of the game. Lastly the game plays in a 4:3 aspect ratio with no widescreen is a disappointment for this HD remaster. Overall the game is fantastic and the music throughout deserves special mention for being especially excellent and elevates the whole vibe and experience of Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok the game runs fine. Now that concern is out of the way. Before this port, I have already played this game twice on IOS. The millisecond this port was announced I pounced on the preorder button. This is in my Top 5 Favorite Games of All Time, and I highly doubt it will ever leave the Top 5 in the foreseeable future. If this was Shu Takumi's only game, I would still consider him one of the greatest scenario writers to ever live. His ability to effortlessly write a narrative that both services the game play while maintaining an absorbing plot is mind blowing. The story may not be on the level of French Cinema or the Great American Novels. But like an iconic pop song or a finely crafted classic adventure film, Ghost Trick ignores pretension in favor of just being a perfectly fine tuned experience. There are very few pieces of media that guarantees enjoyment quite like Ghost Trick. I will recommend this game to literally everyone I can. It is without question one of the finest game play experiences you will ever have. If I could ride Shu Takumi's ♥♥♥♥, I bloody would.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Ghost Trick on a sale after seeing it's remaster and was always curious about it since the original release. For what I paid (just under 17 GBP) I think you can't go wrong, it's a really nice remaster of the game that looks great and plays smoothly on a PC. I do think it's worth the ~£25 but I think it's important to note that the game is about 12 hours long with not much replayability other than a few achievements about solving or failing the puzzles in a specific way. It doesn't waste your time but if you're looking to do a couple of puzzles for five minutes and then come back later this might not be the game for you - each chapter is about an hour. If you've played Ace Attorney, it is very similar in structure with the puzzles being part of the story. I never got stuck in this game, the in-game hint system of characters talking to each other helped enough without taking away the "aha!" moment for me, and you can ignore them completely. The challenge was a good one without being frustrating or too easy. I won't go into the story as I think it would spoil it, but I enjoyed it and it's about the same level as it's sibling series Ace Attorney - mostly logical with a couple of weird bits that fit the Shu Takumi vibe. I think Ace Attorney fans in general will get a kick from Ghost Trick, as well as fans of similar somewhat kooky, story driven puzzlers like Professor Layton.Overall I think if you've been eyeing Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective I think this is the time to pick it up. It's aged really well and translated well to PC despite being originally for the DS. If you're unsure I'd perhaps wait for a sale as Capcom seem to do them fairly often but even at it's original price it won't disappoint if you're looking for a weekend game. I played a few hours at a time over the course of a week which felt like a good pace.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick might have the best mystery story ever told in a video game. Shu Takumi's mysteries are always great, but this one maybe feels the most complete. And maaan, that ending gets me every time. I adore how Takumi writes his characters. They are all so unique and lovable, and the humor is as brilliant as ever. The incredibly stylish art style and animation give this game an incomparable charme. I really hope we'll see a new game from Takumi soon.Sadly, the remaster could have been better. The UI from the original DS version was not updated at all, which looks way too large on big screens. Animations, while a big step up from the iOS version, look kind of jittery at times (especially during walking animations). The background art is of inconsistent quality, often looking rather compressed. The rearranged soundtrack sounds fantastic for the most part, but lacks some polish in the mixing. Overall, I wish a little more effort could have gone into the remaster -- then again I'm overjoyed more people finally get to experience this masterpiece at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is a very charming and unique mystery game that will keep you guessing until the end, all the while cleverly foreshadowing a lot of its twists. Most of the puzzles in the game are more like fun brain teases that operate on videogame logic, so I doubt you will be stuck on most of them for too long. You play as a ghost that can possess objects to manipulate them and also go back in time to 4 minutes before a person's death to change how events unfold. What you can do with objects is very context-sensitive, and sometimes you might find yourself questioning why you can't interact with an object that's similar in nature to another one you can manipulate. This limitation is just something you just have to accept when playing this game. It didn't bother me too much personally, but I can see some people being distraught by it.The soundtrack can be quite catchy at times and sets the mood well.You can finish Ghost Trick in about 12-14 hours, which felt perfect to me.Since the game is very polished, I think it's worth buying it at full price.This game is not for you if you don't like reading at all, since it's for the most part a visual novel with fun animations and light puzzle solving.WARNING: You might feel the urge to adopt a pomeranian after playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: This is currently my absolute favorite game of all time. I played the original version of Ghost Trick on the DS and LOVED it. The gameplay is very unique and is unlike much that I have seen before. Shu Takumi wanted to make a game that involves you looking into the world, almost like a doll house. You get to see all the characters do their own thing and you are there to observe. Of course, being a ghost does allow you to do a little more than that. You know how ghosts are known for messing with lights and such? Yup, well, you get to do that now, with your little ghost tricks! All the puzzles in this game are a blast. The game somehow made moving around into a core element of puzzle solving and it's so much fun! You get to save people's lives by possessing objects and messing with them--doing a rube goldberg machine of events to get your goal. Seriously, the gameplay is fantastic!The narrative pulls you in fast and does not let go. Mysteries and twists are constantly thrown at you in the best kind of way. This game is a roller-coaster and you are in for a wild ride! This is one of those stories where you pick up on something new every time you play it again. There are so many small details and foreshadowing; it's all genius! I would know, I have played this game three times before and now on my fourth! (That's not an exaggeration, by the way.)The characters are all charming and are full of personality. That goes for the character designs, too. They were designed to have a distinct silhouette to stand out against the background and other characters. Each character has their own little thing going on and almost all of them are important to the plot and, more importantly, the mystery of you. The game knows this well and keeps track of all of the characters in a handy journal that you can access at any time.If you have not played this game before, PLEASE give it a shot. There is a FREE DEMO just sitting there! You get to play through the first two chapters of the game, which is more than enough content to let you know if this is the game for you. This is no time to be lolling around dead! Get to playing one of the best and most underrated games of all time!

_childDocuments_.review: There's probably some major spoilers, of this game and some ace attorney games, in my review for Ghost Trick. It's impossible to not spoil anything when talking about this game, and even the slightest spoiler would destroy one's experience with it, almost like how Outer Wilds should be played with no prior knowledge.So for a quick verdict, Ghost Trick is absolutely a fantastic game. And within the vast set of fantastic games it falls into the kind for which I want to poke a stick into my brain so I can forget about my playthrough and start fresh again. But you already knew that, and this much is the only thing one can say about ghost trick without spoiling it. What I want to comment on here is one of the not-so-subtle themes that goes across this game and some older games Shu Takumi directed, being that a challenge the the grim reality of Japan's legal system. All of this would be very likely my blue curtain, so take this read with a pinch of salt.For the background, we can refer to Human Rights Watch: . For those who played the Phoenix Wright trilogy, this should sound somewhat familiar. The very article further elaborates on the grim implications from this singular fact, that the justice system, quote, "holds you hostage until you give prosecutors what they want". Sounds even more familiar, right?The urge to convict and the lust for systematic justice is clearly one of the many things Shu Takumi's games argue against. We can see that from the Phoenix Wright trilogy, in which case after case getting proven false conviction by our favorite hedgehog lawyer. In a truly Japanese fantasy way, the games posts a underlying theme: desire for quick just would result in the horrible mistakes that only supernatural powers can amend. In exhausting and emotionally devastating court battles, parties on the case fight for a grim "truth", one whose retrieval would not bring anything but a slight, slight sense of comfort for the few who survived the horrors of an unjust justice system. That being said, this game is not Ace Attorney and it's not about hedgehogs. Ghost Trick, in some ways, is about actors in the scene of system justice with roles even smaller than attorneys: for the most part, they are just unfortunate bystanders in front of horrors of their life. In Ghost Trick, we witness the lives of front-line policemen, owner of a busted restaurant, or maybe stray cats who showed up in the crime scene. At the same time, however, we are seeing much more brutal scenes, animated, that Ace Attorney games seem to hide. Lots of blood and human bodies flying around almost all the puzzles in Ghost Trick. However, more important than the gore and violence portrayed, is the direct and almost cruel depiction of police brutality. Police brutality, being probably one crucial ingredient to a justice system optimized for efficiency, is what really kicked this whole game to its snowball-rolling start. Just like Jowd said in the game, even without the meteor shower, he would have fatally shot Yomiel. A series of tragedy would have happened at the fateful night ten years ago, regardless of the rock of god, giving its way to nothing but the resilience of Missile (absolutely good boy). If you have ever wondered what does it mean exactly when Edgeworth says he'd do anything to get a guilty conviction, look no further than what Ghost Trick showed us. It's an attack on a oppressing police state with much more power and resentment than our favorite courtroom drama. Peeling open the veil and showing its audience the unsettling reality of manufactured justice, however, is not all that Ghost Trick is about. In my opinion, it's also about redemption and hope. A wise lesbian once told me that a good happy ending is one that's purposeful and intentional, and I think it describes this this game very well. Ghost Trick has a very satisfying good ending where everyone got out from the whole lot of misery once brought about by the Temsik meteorite, while also paying for the mistakes they made prior to that. In some ways, the whole game is a means to the singular end of redemption - not just Yomiel, but also Jawd and Cabanela. Despite being twisted by hatred and ten years of lonely darkness, Yomiel's desire for revenge can, partially, be justified: in the end he's an innocent man pushed to the absolute limits by police brutality, by a justice system seeking resolution over truth. This is the same criticism shown in the Phoenix Wright trilogy and later reprised in Spirit of Justice. What's different, is the kind of agency the player has in Ghost Trick: this time, we get to actually revert time. With this much, much greater supernatural power, the story goes beyond the discovery of the past and finishes the loop by fixing it. Instead of leaving the players to feel the pain of permanent damage done to the broken souls, Ghost Trick gives us hope. Hope to redeem the sinned. Hope to dissolve hatred. Hope to correct the system's wrong. That is not to say, however, that such redemption comes free. The incredible powers players get to wield, combined with a series of reversion of death by the last second, creates a long and effortful road to the redemption and hope we strive for. It is also not to say that such hope comes only by the deus ex machina called main character. In fact none of the things player does would have made any difference if it's not Cabanela selling his soul to the devil called ambition, Lynne's insistence on her investigation, or Missile's resolve keeping him entering the 10-year loop again and again. What the story entails, is an eventual and inevitable good ending that comes from the combined effort of small actors in the bigger crisis. We are left with the hope that even though the ultimate wrong is from a powerful system, those whose fates intersect around the wrong can, and probably should, strive hard to make it right.
