_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving it a thumbs down in the hope it will help steer the rating towards the "mostly positive" I think it deserves to be. This game gets a 7 out of 10 from me. The 30€ price point seems too steep to me. I bought the game at 34% discount (so, a little less than 20€) and I think that's a better price point for this game.Let me also mention that, at the moment of writing this review, less than 50% of buyers have finished this game (according to the achievements). Not that this is fully representative of how good the game is (people can play offline without achievements and the game is a remaster, so people might have bought it for nostalgia's sake) but it still brings into question the current "overwhelmingly positive" review status it has.The game is episodic, with the ability to save between each episode. I'm playing an episode (sometimes 2) per day. I'm halfway (chapter 9 of 17) when writing this review.The tl;dr for the later paragraphs: This game is too much visual novel and too little exciting time-warping, puzzle detective gameplay, in my opinion. The dialogue takes up so much time only to sprinkle in a bit of gameplay every now and then. It's not that the dialogue is entirely unpleasant but It does dare to repeat itself occasionally, for when the sheer volume of text made you forget anything that was said earlier /s. Luckily, the game is pleasing to the eyes and ears.In the story, you play as the ghost of the main character who recently passed away. The ghost has no recollection of his death or even his own name, and wants to figure out what has happened. He learns he has all sorts of paranormal abilities as a ghost, like being able to possess and control certain inanimate objects and the ability to rewind time under certain conditions.Up until now the story steadily kept growing in narrative. All the characters presented seem to have a function in the larger story arc. Some plot twists have been revealed already. I'm excited to see if the game will be able to surprise me until the end. The only thing that bugs me sometimes is when chapters end with an exposition dump, just two characters talking sharing what they know. It's boring to experience even though the new info provides new insights.The gameplay and puzzle mechanics are kind of interesting. It's trial and error based, where you need to make events happen in a certain order. Some things you can deduce, simply by considering the options, while others you need to have played out once or twice to understand the consequences of the actions. There is a timer constraint but time only runs when the "real time" events are in motion. There's also a "ghost mode" that pauses time, in which your character can jump between objects (if they're within reach). While in "ghost mode" you can't interact with the objects. Sometimes you need to think about the correct use of motion in "real-time" to complete a puzzle, which isn't always that obvious at first glance. Puzzles haven't been excruciatingly difficult up until the half-way point, the logic has always made some sense to me. If it doesn't make sense, then there's always the speech bubbles the game throws your way during "real-time" that will help you steer in the direction the game wants you to take. These are optional but can provide some story flavor if you want more visual novel experience.What I believe the game excels at are the animations, character designs and music. They all have their unique quirks. For example, I really like the police chief who sits at his desk without shoes. He's got this grumpy look on his face and you can read his stress levels by the number of times he moves his feet around and twirls his toes. I also like how the game seems flat 2D but then an object movement happens and it reveals the 3D'ness of the environment. They seemed to have used live instruments for the music in the remaster and you can listen to the original digital versions of the songs in the extra's, making it easy to compare the two songs with a switch that toggles between the current listening position of both versions.

_childDocuments_.review: I've already played this twice on the DS, so I mostly just wanted to see what the port was like before making a recommendation. In general, I have no complaints; it allows you to use the gamepad controls and keyboard bindings if you want, but you can also play the whole thing with a mouse, which in my opinion is a far better option given the gameplay. The HD graphics all came out looking gorgeous, and while I do think the transition to high resolution occasionally reveals some imperfections that weren't as visible on the DS's low-res screen it's still a beautifully animated game. The only thing I could see people being mixed on is the letterboxing on the sides of the screens, but given how often the game uses the camera to obscure things or move the frame for dramatic effect I can see why they did this instead of just cropping or expanding the view.If you haven't played this before, you owe it to yourself to do so; everything Shu Takumi directs is gold, and Ghost Trick is maybe one of the best games he's done yet. It's an extremely well written mystery with really neat gameplay mechanics, and I couldn't be happier that it's finally free from the DS and iOS store.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and unique game, kind of a danganronpa feel to it.Unfortunately strapped to a vehicle with the ambition and subtlety of a particularly slow blues clues episode. I completely understand how this went overlooked. I felt punished every time I completed something too quickly, or dared to check in on the optional dialogue.Some of it can be fast forwarded (tho not very quickly) and everything else is an excruciatingly long series of animations and pauses I can only assume are meant for kindergarteners still overwhelmed by the sheer concept of the gameplay by level eight. The rewind function actually made me want to die. You watch the full event, along with every pause, every innocuous comment, and at least fifteen full seconds of admittedly nice animation in between.Then it replays after another two minutes of discussion on what should be done.Then you try to win the replay puzzle as quickly as possible.Most actions are reliant on timing, which means every replay happens in real time with no ability to skip ahead if you need to reset a level. Which is horrifying when actions can ALSO be game breaking, in which case you have no choice but to reset, often multiple times.The game encourages you to keep track of unskippable dialogue or thoughts as they might be clues, but it only took about three of each for me to understand they were the equivalent of Dora the explorer slowly and clearly enunciating a single question with plenty of repetition so that even the youngest kids understood in order to receive a “hint” that was was only helpful if you’d gotten up to go to the bathroom for twenty minutes and had only just returned.If they ever do go back to this property, all I can do is beg them to keep the gameplay and destroy every other element of this thing so that nobody spends twenty dollars on a puzzle game you might only find thrilling post botched lobotomy.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: A game that does not respect your time. I've played half of the chapters and do not intend to finish it. The "puzzles" in this game are narrow, single path solutions, which blissfully are generally heavily hinted, guiding you down the designers' single path to success. However, there are a number of occasions where you must intuit their intent, in conditions that are not particularly intuitive! This can entail watching the same hokey animations play, over and over, for minutes on end, only to advance to the next logjam, and repeating the cycle once more. The humor is thinly written, with some questionable character choices played for laughs - e.g., blue-skinned people who are vaguely sinister and characters with large or strangely shaped noses. I don't understand the positive reviews, but more power to those who enjoy this. I'd rather do literally anything else with my time. Zero stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: One of Shu Takumi's MANY masterpieces. Ghost Trick is another of the most phenomenal games in the Ace Attorney Franchise. It was one of, if not, the greatest puzzle games I have played. The art style, dialogue, character design, story, and puzzles were all a 10/10. The main character has such a unique look I fell in love immediately. The banter between each character separated it from any normal puzzle game, and each character (even the side ones who barely had a few minutes of game time) was genuinely likable in their ways. I genuinely believe this is a masterpiece, that despite being so old, still exceeds my gaming standards in 2024. My only complaint was this game was very short-lived, my play-through only being 15 hours long (and that seems to be long compared to others). I bought it on sale for 15$ so I have no issue with that, but if I had bought it for the normal 30$ I would be a little disappointed. In all a 10/10 game with very few issues. No outstanding plot holes, everything wrapped up nicely at the end, AND some very surprising twists!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game, it is a bread trail of clues as you try and solve your own murder. The trail is winding, and if it is your first time playing the game, it will take you time to figure out all the tricks. You may even get stuck. Or maybe you're clever enough to catch on the first time through. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best mystery games ever made. This is a port of the 2011 Nintendo DS game of the same name. The premise is simple, you play as an amnesiac ghost as you try to figure out who you are, who murdered you and why. Along the way you learn that by possessing the corpse of a recently deceased you can travel back in time to 4 minutes before that persons death. This is where the most of the puzzle solving happens. You manipulate small objects within your limited range in order to prevent said person's death and learn more about the mystery enveloping the night and your death. _childDocuments_.review: Spoiler-free review!Ghost Trick is a really nice remaster of a DS game. Its story holds a lot of mysteries that are solved over time with lots of death preventing puzzles. That, with a great soundtrack accompaning you all the way. I can definitely say I like this game.Ghost Trick is all about playing out a scenario in a certain way to attempt to save someone from their death. As you are a spirit, you jump from object to object in order to find an object that can be used to change fate, I'd like to describe it as a little puzzle with a time limit.You, the protagonist have recently died in a junkyard. You lost all your memories, and suddenly you see a girl being hunted by a hitman. Who is she? How did you die? And most importantly, who are you?For a DS game, they remastered this very well. The environments look detailed and high quality, characters have high res art and unique styles, and have neat but sometimes choppy looking animations. This game is far from demanding. Based on how well it ran ony Steam Deck with just a little bit of power, you can expect this game to run well as long as your PC isn't say, more than 15 years old.I love the music in this game. There's two versions. Original and arranged, since this was a DS game, you can choose to use the original DS soundtrack, or am entirely remastered ost that's filled with groovy songs. - The story- The characters - The graphics- The music- The performance - The file size of the game - The animations - Some puzzles may feel a bit repetitive - I really liked this game, so there's not much I'd change aside from some repetitive puzzles.I easily give this game an 8 out of 10. I enjoyed it, but wouldn't quite quickly put it in my favorites list. That's entirely on me though, maybe you'd enjoy it a lot too!

_childDocuments_.review: "Ah, a contest then! Which will stop first - my dancing, or the turning of the planet?!"From the mind of Shu Takumi, hot off the heels of the first Ace Attorney trilogy, we have Ghost Trick - a zany and immaculately-paced murder mystery visual novel with some novel point-and-click puzzles, a colorful and memorable cast of characters, a comic book visual style, and a fantastic synth-heavy soundtrack.GameplayThe puzzles in Ghost Trick are fairly simple point-and-click affairs, and thankfully the level of "adventure game logic" is fairly low - I never felt like I was flailing around in search of a solution. I could usually tell what I needed to do in order to progress, and it was a lot of fun to see what happened when I interacted with different objects. The latter third of the game dials up the difficulty a little bit by handing you a second set of mechanics to work with, though it remains very manageable. One small annoyance I had was, upon retrying a puzzle, knowing what actions I needed to do, but having to wait until the scene progressed to the proper point. All the scenes are only a couple minutes long, so it was never much of an issue, but I would liked to have liked a "fast-forward" button or something. Failing a puzzle was never frustrating, since the scenes were all very short, and there were checkpoints in many of them. Story & CharactersGhost Trick's story is a lot of fun, and helped greatly by the pacing, which is some of the best I've seen in a mystery story. The plot moves FAST, while never feeling rushed. Each chapter adds new layers to the mystery, expands on a character's arc, and provides clues to the solution to the overall story.There were a lot of twists and turns through the story, and it was a good balance of things I could predict and developments that caught me off guard. Given all these twists, I was surprised and pleased that nothing felt like an ass-pull, or overly contrived. I think the final couple set-pieces are very "out there" but they make sense within the context of the game's world, and lead into an extremely satisfying and cathartic ending.The entire cast of characters is charming and well-rounded. The main characters all have satisfying arcs over the course of the ~10 hours in which the game takes place. The side cast as well is a lot of fun - even characters that appear in only a few scenes have unique designs and memorable traits. Ghost Trick also has the rare honor of having a talking dog as a main character, and it is fantastic. We love and cherish Missile in this household.Visuals & SoundGhost Trick has a really striking comic book art style, and all the characters have great and distinct silhouettes. Reading about the development history of this game, it was done mostly for readability on the small DS screens, but it really looks great, and has a ton of style. Everything has thick outlines and a lot of pop colors, which gives the game a very appealing look. I like how the environments in the game don't really contain any strong cultural indicators, it's easy to imagine it taking place in a variety of different places (This is probably a conscious decision by the developers after how much of a nightmare Phoenix Wright was to localize).The environmental sounds used in Ghost Trick are serviceable, but nothing special. The soundtrack, however, is awesome. There's a lot of really invigorating tracks in the game, that make heavy use of synths to achieve a unique style, really heightening the mystery and emotions of each scene. It's definitely a soundtrack that I'll return to and listen to outside of the game.ConclusionI really loved my time with Ghost Trick. At around a dozen hours playtime, it doesn't last long but it makes that time count with a fast-moving and dynamic story that wastes no time moving from plot point to plot point, keeping you on your toes without leaving you feeling rushed and disoriented. The characters are great, with colorful and memorable designs, charming traits, and satisfying growth over the course of the game. I highly recommend you give it a try if you're at all a fan of mystery stories or visual novels.I'd love to see another game in the Ghost Trick universe, though it would likely need to focus on a mostly-new cast of characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I heard a lot about Ghost Trick when it was releasing WAAAY back (God the fact I have to use that for 2010 of all years got me all kinds of Matt Damon’d up) in 2010. Never had a chanced to play it until now. Really should have played it back then because this is a solid mystery/puzzle game!So the premise is fairly unique in that you start off flat out dead. Not someone soon to be dying like your typical Soulslike, or someone whose basically dead like...well your Soulslike (Hey, I’ve reviewed almost 10 of them, you’d have them on your brain too). You are flat out deceased. But hey, at least by the way your corpse dresses they were one cool cat when they were alive. Anyway, as a disembodied ghost, the only two people in your vicinity is a young woman, and a weird blue-skinned Mafia type. It looks like you’re going to have some company soon since he’s got quite a big gun trained on the lady. But you aren’t helpless! It seems like you have the power to possess objects and cause weird coincidences to happen like Death from the Final Destination movies finally  got some therapy. With your new found powers, you do what you can, but sometimes that’s just not good enough. The lady gets shot, and dies. So now there are 2 corpses...but perhaps not for long.Turns out, in addition to the ability to manipulate objects, you can also travel 4 minutes into the past from the point of a dead body. But you better make the most of it, because it turns out that come morning you’re going to be heading to the after life. Just who is the one who iced you in the first place? Was it the mafia bloke? Obviously yea. But what does he want with the girl? You’ve got less than half a day to answer these questions...Ghost Trick is a mystery puzzle game that originally released for the DS. The game design and presentation makes it quite apparent, but still the port still handles being played with the controller well so you wouldn’t miss much. It’s up to you to determine the best course of action to save peeps on your path to learn the truth of your death. I found the puzzles mostly straight forward, and only needed a guide on about 3 occasions, which besides 1 I would say I could have figured out on my own. This isn’t your Myst or your typical 90s Adventure game with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ logic. What is new to this version includes the original 3D models, where the initial release had released with rasterized sprites. Everything looks crisp and clean, and the original cartoony art look good even on my 1440P monitor. Music was a treat, filled with absolute bangers, with my favorite being Cabanelas, and the full main theme. Plot is just as wacky as you’d expect from them ind of Shu Takumi, the writer and director of the first 4 Ace Attorney games. The game is basically “tell me you were written by Shu Takumi without telling you were written by Shu Takumi. I enjoyed it and the mystery was decently interesting, but I should say it does go places. Let’s just say that a lot of loopholes and “exact words” are present.All in all a splendid adventure game with great art, characters, music, and puzzles. It’s an absolute crime that it flopped so hard back then, but perhaps we can give it a second life? I have a soft spot for the mystery VNs/Adventure games so I always try to pick up the ones that stick out.

_childDocuments_.review: ghost trick: phantom detective is a masterpiece. please please PLEASE, give this game a go. it's worth your time. i haven't simultaneously laughed and cried to a game like this in so long, and i finished the game wanting so much more. it was such a thrilling journey and adventure. not to mention the witty, funny dialogue, paired with banger soundtracks, all from the same writer and composer as the ace attorney series.a piece of advice, though: have a clear head before sitting down to play, because these puzzles might make your brain explode. don't be afraid to look up a guide if you need to, because damn, this game can make you feel stupid sometimes. but AVOID SPOILERS AT ALL COSTS, and prepare to be hit with twist after twist in this very cool and sleek mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: This is a puzzle game with a mystery plot -- by manipulating the circumstances immediately before a death, you can change the course of events and slowly untangle a complex and (to me) interesting story. The ultimate question of "Who am I? Why am I dead" is the main reason for you to chase characters around the town undoing their damages.There is a demo available - it gives representative gameplay but the text is patronizing and not representative of the normal amount of handholding. Oh, speaking of text, this is partly a visual novel. If you don't like reading a lot of dialog to understand a complex story/plot then give it a miss. It's by the author of the Ace Attorney series, but this one has much more emphasis on puzzle-solving.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: This game is oozing with personality and cleverness. _childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly wish I played this game so much sooner, this is one of the few games I could genuinely call a masterpiece, everything from the story, the music, the art, the gameplay and more excel's any expectations which were already quiet high as many people who worked on this game were also responsible for the Ace Attorney games.The game is a mystery and is a great one at that, it immediately makes you ask questions you want to seek answers to, it gives you enough to figure out aspects if you think hard enough but knows what to hold so you don't immediately figure the mystery out, and even if you can figure out the twists before the reveal you will still be left asking questions as even if you get answers, it will still bring up more questions to be answered.the game is a puzzle game with you interacting with objects to change the outcome of a situation to prevent a death, despite how repetitive it is it is never boring, how you go about preventing these deaths is different each time and has unique solutions, some aren't obvious first time round but that adds to the fun, the experimentation aspect and without spoiling more elements will be added that keeps the gameplay fresh and allows for further experimentation and keeps it fun.The art is another stand out aspect of the game, it has so much style and it alone is enough to make the game memorable, when I finished the game I immediately went to the gallery to look at everything from the character portraits, the environments and the concept stage of the characters designs, this isn't something I typically make note off but I just found it so interesting looking at how designs changed and seeing how game could've turned out, a lot of the original designs seemed a bit more "realistic" in certain aspects such as hair and you can see the more subtle shift towards the more exaggerate, stylistic designs we have now.and off course the environments are also fantastic, nothing feels out off place, everything feels like it naturally belongs unless off course it's deliberately not supposed to, it makes the puzzles even more impressive as you would need to take consideration of what objects would be in a set environment and how they could be used to prevent a death all the while telling the story.There's so much more I can go into, but I feel like I've made my point clear of just how great this game is, it easily places itself somewhere in my top 10 favourite games, if your considering getting this game even in the very slightly then go ahead and get it, I really do hope we can see more games in this series in the future but I won't complain if we don't as without spoiling the ending does tie things up in a very satisfying way.

_childDocuments_.review: Shortish game, beatable in a couple sessions. Cool modern take on point-and-click adventure puzzle games that works the plot into it’s own mechanics quite well.You play an amnesiac spirit waking up to their own murder and trying to remember who, how and why it happened in a night before they disappear. They end up traveling through-out the city finding other murders and mysteries that all ultimately tie into a long term unresolved conspiracy. You encounter other spirits of those caught up along the way but are able to relive their final moments and prevent their deaths.Basically a point-and-click where you can only get around through object possession in a very cartoonishly ‘Rube Goldberg-esque’ and ‘I Spy’ way (Or you know, paranormal Home Alone), essentially it all boils down to possessing objects in range and ‘triggering’ them to create the necessary chain of events to progress a scene and solve the puzzle. Some solutions can feel arbitrary as some puzzles often do, but because they’re mainly visual or signposted with story beats, it never feels too frustrating if ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game for the first time and it truly is one of the greatest games I have ever played. And nothing is left unanswered by the end, the game wraps everything up beautifully.I absolutely recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of visual novels, and for some challenging ghost trick puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a game that I did not expect to enjoy so much. Ghost Trick is a story driven game that makes the player focus on timing above all else; it utilizes each scenario to make the player think outside the box despite the simple gameplay. The story itself has many twists and turns where some were predictable and others completely surprising. Honestly don't know how Shu Takumi was able to think of a story like this, but it was great. A detective game where the main character searches for the mysteries of their identity is peak.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is a fairly linear puzzle game that you could absolutely beat in one sitting if you have the time.If that was all there was to this game, then it'd be an easy pass for some.Everything about this game, from its stunning artstyle, its innovative mechanics, and amazing soundtrack, was really a labor of love from Shu Takumi, better known for the Ace Attorney series. The story is so memorable and well-woven together that it still blows my mind despite playing this game on the DS several years ago.The praise that people give this game is not understated. It's absolutely worth your time, and if you don't think so, you can at least give the demo a shot. I almost guarantee that you'll be hooked by the end of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

But I also love that this is not a spin-off of that series but is its own type of puzzle game with clever and fun mechanics. The game keeps the puzzles fresh throughout, and has the characters provide in-game hints so the player doesn't get discouraged when they're stuck. Even better ,the game ties these excellent characters and fun puzzles together with a fantastic mystery story that will keep you guessing until the end. This game is so fun, quirky, and heartfelt, that I could enjoy playing it over and over. I would hugely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love, love, LOVE this game, from the brilliant mind that created the Ace Attorney series, Shu Takumi, comes a "brand new" (well, 2010 but I digress) where you control an amnesiac ghost who seeks to find the cause of his murder as well as his identity.I have waited for a PC port of this game for years, I played it on the original DS release and it is one of the few games that I have replayed over and over until I lost the cartridge one day.I'd recommend checking it out if you have have the time. (You can spare a couple afternoons, can't you?)Well written characters, great story, interesting puzzles (even if you normally dislike them), banging music, and an overarching mystery, the game's got it all.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Was amazing back then, still amazing now. It's truly a testament that after nearly a decade I STILL remember most of the puzzle solutions because they left that much of an impact on me. Great characters (with the bestest boi), story and gameplay. I WISH with this port they streamlined some of the dialogue so that it would not repeat when you replay certain scenarios, so it would just skip it all together, but that's the smallest blemish in otherwise a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: The story takes a bit to truly get going, and there are 2 chapters with genuinely obscure solutions, but it is overall a great experience. The largest issue in this game has is that in some chapters, execution is a massive problem. The time limits the game imposes are never that bad, as usually the puzzle is to figure out how to do what you want within the time allotted. However, there are a few actions that will not cause the desired effect unless done at the exact correct time. This has caused me to become stuck on 3 separate occasions simply because I did the right action at a slightly incorrect time. I suggest being willing to see a walkthough for this reason exclusively.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is a great game that over the course of it's events becomes an amazing game. Every part of it ends up feeling incredibly well thought out and just about every lead feels properly explored to the fullest extent reasonable. It's ending was absolutely perfect, and I can't praise the game highly enough. Missile is easily the best dog in all of video games, and I don't say that lightly, I'd recommend playing blind like our protagonist, because the twists and turns of the story hit like a truck if you don't know where they're going, and it really improves the experience a lot. Also it no longer has Denuvo in it, so there's basically no reason to pass this up now, get it and play it, you will definitely not regret it
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: A somewhat short game, but it has a strong, well paced story that is the perfect length. Not too short, not too long. Incredible OST, memorable characters and gamplay that isn't like any other game I have played. Everyone should give this game a shot, especially if you enjoyed the Phoenix Wright series. _childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the OG Ghost Trick  on launch week back on the DS, when it originally launched on IOS and even re-played it on an Android DS emulator years later while in University.  I've played this game countless times in various mediums already, and yet I was no less eager to dive into Ghost Trick one more time.While nostalgic bias is 100% a thing, same as with my previous playthroughs, I had a blast playing Ghost Trick this time too! - The pacing of the game's story is phenomenal; it's short, sweet and is actually something the average person could finish in a handful of sittings.- The writing is snappy, but expressive. It's not afraid to get goofy with the script and characters, but it can just as easily pull at your heartstrings. The writing is earnest and fun, and really pulls you in.  - The setting, story and presentation are top notch, and the expressive animation of the original translates super well to the remaster. - The music is FANTASTIC; catchy, fun, frenatic and magnificently atmospheric. The original composer 	Masakazu Sugimori and the arranger for this remaster Yasumasa Kitagawa did a fantastic job here. I could keep gushing... but I probably ought to leave it there. All in all, this gets my highest recommendation; Ghost Trick remains even all these years later one of my most memorable and most enjoyable gaming experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: +++ Insane story, lots of twists++ Amazing music++ Likable, interesting characters++ Charming artstyle/animations+ Unique gameplay* Some unskippable dialogue after restarts- Some confusing puzzles- Unskippable end credits (after the first ones)-This game was amazing to play through, with one of the best stories I've ever experienced with many mysteries and twists. The characters are very likable and getting to know their past and roles in the story was very interesting. The artstyle and animations are very charming, looking minimalistic, but funny and fitting at the same time. The music is amazing and the gameplay is pretty unique as well.My biggest problem is, that a few of the later puzzles are very confusing, with some nonsense solutions, nothing a quick Google-search can't fix though. Another smaller negative point was that there are two end credits: the first one was very interesting, the second one however was not, and was unskippable. The last negative point concernes a pretty big plot hole (for me), which killed my immersion a good bit, as the rest of the game was just written THAT WELL.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: The first time I saw Ghost Trick, I was still in primary school. Being a kid who loved gaming was always a little trying, since gaming was (and still is!) expensive. I was one of those kids who was allowed to buy maybe 1 or 2 games a year; I vividly remember having to choose between Ace Attorney, Professor Layton, and Ghost Trick. Ghost Trick lost out, over and over again. I didn't really get any spare money to buy games for myself until well into my 20s, and by then Ghost Trick was a distant memory.So I'm so glad they remastered it and brought it to Steam. I never would have been able to experience such a phenomenal game otherwise. Shu Takumi truly is a master of storytelling. Ghost Trick made me laugh, cry, it got my heart pounding when moments got tense- I'm so grateful I got to play something so fun and incredible; it really is a work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely phenomenal. The story gripped me from start to finish with the usual Shu Takumi twits and turns, some of the twists took me so off guard that i was so surprised the got me that good but they all made perfect sense. The characters were a true treat, the main character in particular is a joy to follow, he (and everyone else in this game) is a comedy riot and they had me rolling on multiple occasions. The gameplay is so fun and unique, the style lends itself some of the most interesting puzzle solving i've experienced! And my personal highlight, the music is absolutely amazing, every song in the OST slaps and the songs always fit the scene they're used in to an absolutely insane degree.all in all. Play this game. Shu Takumi is a genius.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 story, 6/10 game design, would recommend shouting "shut up and let me play" at the screen.Seriously though, this is a very nicely written visual novel with puzzles that slot very elegantly into the overal story.The only downsides I can think of are:- Characters tend to butt in and explain puzzles to you as you are solving them.- Some time-sensitive puzzles include pieces with long animations... Or even pieces that trigger dialogue as you get them into place.- Dialogue skipping is atrocious, and you can not skip character animations. Not a big problem, but can get annoying if you have to retry and watch someone twirl into the frame for the fifth time.Overall, if you like point-and-click adventures and visual novels, a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played Ghost Trick a fair while after it first released, buying the game secondhand and using a 3DS instead of the original DS. I enjoyed it enough the first time through that I played it again several years later, and a third time when this remaster released, and through each of these my thoughts on it remain the same. The music is fun, the stylized visuals are extremely funny and memorable, the puzzles are good with a great ability to get across tension without being stressful, and the story is far more amusing and interesting than I could have ever anticipated before playing. If you enjoy puzzles, goofy characters, good music, and a story with twists dotted throughout, I highly recommend buying this game or at least trying out the demo!

Some of the puzzles do feel like they're dipping into 90s-era Adventure Game logic, and there's one 'stealth' segment in the middle that's incredibly frustrating, but a fantastic game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, the great opportunity to finally follow up on all those "play ghost trick!!" calls.All in all, it's a nice game/story, but for me it probably could never have lived up to the hype.The story is very anime or rather japanese. So say if you are into stuff like Steins;Gate, DuRaRaRa, 999 or Death Note, where very paranormal or mysterious events get deconstructed into their tiniest convoluted components, this is for you. And as a bonus it definitily has great characters plus the overall Shu Takumi charme.As for the gameplay however I think they could have polished it a bit more, especially as part of the port/remaster. Something among the lines of a fast forward AND backwards to cut down on some of the more frustrating parts & encouraging more player experimentation. Also streamlining the controls to cut down on some button presses for many actions would have improved gameflow.But all in all, those are rather nitpicks.  It is definitely one of the greats, especially when you are talking about outstanding story telling in the medium of games! (I would actually look forward to Nolan addepting this for cinema~)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a LOT of fun with this game right now. I will say, if you are anything like me, the first hour or so of this game can be a bit slow, since the first chapter is just a giant tutorial and there's really not much to hook you at that point. But once you actually get into the game (past I think chapter 2 or 3), the plot REALLY opens up. Right now I'm halfway through the game and there are like ten separate plot threads that are all starting to intersect in really cool ways.  Edit: Now having beat the game, I can genuinely say that this is probably my favorite video game story ever. I was REALLY worried that they wouldn't be able to stick the landing,  but the ending elevates this story from a 8/10 to a 10/10. They wrapped up EVERY SINGLE PLOT POINT. I almost want to replay the whole game if I can catch all the clues. HOWEVER, a lot of the puzzles can feel pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at times, and the hint system is basically useless for a lot of them. You might have to look at walkthroughs from time to time to progress or else you'll just be doing trial and error a billion times until you find something that works. Regardless, the art, the music, and especially the writing elevates this to a MUST PLAY.

_childDocuments_.review: I have seen this game recommended to me for a long time as a top new mystery game, so I have been forward to this play-through for a while.  When I started the first couple of levels, which were dedicated to teaching the mechanics of the game, I got so invested in the puzzle aspect that I convinced myself that the game would be following along the storyline of some generic mystery story and that the mystery would be lacking.  As it turns out, it is possible to create a game that is not only a remarkable and unique puzzle game, but also follows an incredible story filled with twists, turns, and lots of foreshadowing.  The characters are rich and colorful while also capable of being emotionally complex and real.  I want to give absolutely none of this game away, so I simply give my full recommendation to this one and hope you'll decide to give it a go.  10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: My only experience with this game was hearing Gametrailers (RIP) constantly rave about this game on it's original release back in 2010. I never picked it up, seeing as I didn't have a DS at the time, and I slowly forgot about it. Thankfully, Capcom remastered it and released it on the Switch and Steam, giving me an opportunity to try it out.Guys, this game is an absolute bangerI expected fun puzzles and a good story, as that was what most of the praise centered around, but I certainly didn't expect the masterful degree to which the developers (led by Shu Takumi and Atsushi Maruyama) would execute those things. Everything here is worthy of praise. The puzzles are interesting and all have unique gimmicks that stack on top of each other, the characters range from likeable to best characters ever (Missile my beloved), and while the writing suffers from localization issues, the narrative Ghost Trick spins is some of the most compelling stuff I've ever seen in a video game. I was on the edge of my seat from Chapter 3 all the way to the end.I certainly wish this remaster had more modern production values, like voice acting, but I admire the level of restraint Capcom had when designing this version. It's not overdone or underbaked; it's just right. At the end of the day, it's an absolute travesty Ghost Trick was so overlooked on it's original DS release, but given it currently sits at a 97% approval rating with over 2,000 reviews on Steam, we might finally be able to bring justice to this incredible piece of software. If you were thinking of picking it up and trying it, you have my whole-hearted recommendation. Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is just as good as everyone says it is.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest games of all time from the Nintendo DS has been given new life on current gen consoles and most importantly, the PC.I wont go into too much detail on the story, which is great as always. Instead I'll talk about the improvements for those who had played the previous version.  If this is your first time, don't worry, no spoilers involved. Just know that this is Shu Takumi of Ace Attorney fame's masterpiece and it combines a wonderful story, his signature colorful characters, with a beautiful 2D time-based puzzle system.  Even if you're not great at puzzles, it shouldn't be too hard to figure out what you're supposed to do and complete them under the time limit.  You can restart as often as you like, so don't worry.Now for the improvements. This version is based on the mobile version, so the graphics are high res and crisp. You don't have to worry about blurry DS resolution here.  The backgrounds are lovely, the characters are sharper than ever and things really pop with the art style, unlike some slightly iffy updates on the Ace Attorney collection. The character animation is even more charming than it was on those tiny DS screens.  The game includes a remixed soundtrack as well as the original for absolute purists and plenty of extras to unlock including background artwork so you can appreciate every stage.  You also have the option to choose the border image for your screen, since the original was a square 4:3.This is where my one complaint with the game comes in. (Aside from not being able to play with the mouse and treat it like a stylus in the original) There is no option to choose just a black border for the screen, you have to choose one of the images.  Sure, you can mix and match various ones together but it is annoying if you just want black bars.  Do you have a monitor with a higher aspect ration than 16:9? Well things get even worse since the rest of the screen gets filled with light gray bars. And there's no option to change that either.  So we have gray on the side... then images blocking off the 16:9 aspect ration down to 4:3.Ultimate it's not a deal breaker, but I'm highly disappointed that Capcpom messed something in their games up again and never provided a fix for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is a masterpiece.an amazing story, fabulous visuals, an absolute banger of an OST, and, it goes without saying, ludicrously fun and interesting gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick was a game I played as a child many years ago- I recall playing a demo of the game on my iPod touch and being hooked by it- though I decided to play the game on the DS rather than continue with the mobile port. I remember really, REALLY enjoying the game, and was thoroughly excited when I heard that it was getting a port to modern consoles and PC.I remembered the plot from years back, so I was fully prepared for a solid experience replaying the game. However, having played through the game again now, for the first time in over 10 years, it still struck me how incredibly well-written and deep the plot in this game is, and how well everything ties back into itself and resolves over the course of the story; despite recalling the plot to a rough degree, as well as the ending, I found myself asking "How come that happened? Why didn't this happen?" and so on at several points in the plot. And yet, despite noting several things that I *thought* were plotholes as I was playing the game, by the ending explanations had been given that resolved those questions perfectly. In some ways, I was able to experience the story and twists anew as a result, despite remembering them from my first playthrough.This game is truly a masterpiece. Shu Takumi's work in the form of the Ace Attorney franchise was already phenomenal, with many top-tier narratives being told between and across cases within those games. And yet, I think Ghost Trick is his best work. The story being told is stellar, and there were no moments where I felt the game lost steam. It continues building up mystery, where resolved questions merely beget more, until the final acts in which the mysteries all begin to unravel. It is a polished gem of an experience from start to finish, and I cannot recommend it highly enough.The port itself is really well put together- it looks good, sounds good, and plays good. The controls aren't exactly complex, so they translate over from the DS touchpad to modern platforms well. The highly stylised art style translates well also; the game doesn't at all feel it's age.For the port-specific features- I like the new re-imagined OST. It remains faithful to the original DS version's tracks, yet adds a little more emphasis and fleshes out the tracks with a fuller, and higher fidelity sounds. I wasn't super keen on them initially, mind you, but they've grown on me significantly. If, however, you don't like the new arrangements, you have the option to switch to the original OST in settings, which is a lovely feature that I'm very glad they added, if only for nostalgia's sake.If there's one part of the port I'm to nitpick, it'd be the post-game sliding puzzles that unlock concept art. They're not bad, and I don't dislike the practice of adding extra content, but it felt very disjointed from the base game and wasn't at all engaging. It doesn't drag the experience down at all, being extra content you access from the main menu, but I was just very confused by their inclusion, almost as if they were included just for the sake of adding *something*.In conclusion, Ghost Trick is a game I am immeasurably happy got a modern remaster, as the improved accessibility means many, many more people will be able to play this masterpiece. If you haven't played it, do yourself a favour and do so. It's not a particularly long experience, but it is one that I have treasured since I first played this game many years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It's quirky, short, and fun to play. I completed it once on DS, and I remembered real-time sequences to be a pain, where I would wait for the moment I could do my thing. This time I didn't remember solutions to any of the puzzles, but I didn't find real-time waits to be a problem. It takes only few dozen seconds at most to get trough the most scenes to the point where you can do the thing. It's fine. Ghost Trick is fine!You're playing a role of recently departed man, who was most probably murdered. And you have only one night to find out who and why killed you. But wait, you're dead, so how will you solve the case? Fortunately for you... you're a ghost, and you can move trough some of the objects littered everywhere. And even move some of them. Now with your nearly non-existent powers you have to save this girl from an assasin. After she was already killed. This was written by a creator of Phoenix Wright, and you can feel it. The style is very Phoenix Wright-like, so if you liked those games this is a must play. The cast of characters is very interesting, as in every PW game. Here they also move around, often in very intricate manner. The animations are top notch, and ooze personality. Even if I didn't remember some characters after 13 years I did remember their quirky animations.The game is rather short, about 10 hours to beat. The story is pretty focused and self-contained. I liked the timey wimey stuff that happens, and all the conspiracies and big reveals. The game is very satisfying all around.That said, there are places that seem a bit undercooked. For example there's a character early on that can detect you, and threatens you. It builds up towards eventual confrontation where you would have to beat this character while hiding your presence... And it never happens, this character just disappears from the story. There are other situations like that, where it seems like either more was planned, or maybe sequel was expected. It doesn't deter much from the overall experience though.One thing I didn't like were monologues the main character would have at the end and beginning of every chapter. Those are too frequent and add little to the game (if anything), while killing the pacing. The game is divided in free roam moments, where you have to get to the next story point by solving environmental puzzles at your leisure, and into "4 minutes before death" sections, where you have 4 minutes to solve environmental puzzles. That said there's no stress, as you can rewind those 4 minutes to your liking. And once you solve half of the puzzle you get ability to start from the middle of the puzzle instead of the beginning. Including time component into the puzzles makes them pretty interesting, and different than what you see in most adventure games.That said, the most difficult puzzles are actually in first few chapters of the game, and second half is much easier. You get less items to interact with, and there are less time-limited moments where you have to be precise. At least that was my feeling, but maybe I just got too good with the kind of puzzles offered. That said the game is rather on easy side, and you shouldn't need to ever look into any guide to get trough it. I'd say it's on Phoenix Wright difficulty.There's a demo of first 2 chapters, and it can carry over save to the full game, so just go and try it if you're on the fence. It provides a decent into to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely easy to recommend this game, but difficult to discuss without directly addressing the story or its characters. Many characters are built with love and care for how they come off, how they develop advancing into the story and subverting your view of them, and making you fully understand how they came off that way from the beginning with flawless execution. It's a wonderful mystery that leaves plenty of hints and clues for reveals to come, but leaving said reveals so perfectly hidden that you can't immediately unveil what's what as you advance through the story. If anything, this is the perfect kind of game to go through on a second playthrough just to pick up on things that you might not have otherwise noticed or thought about.Others have also said it, but if you like Takumi's storytelling, characters, and themes in Ace Attorney, you'll just as easily love this. He is great at creating a wonderful setting that walks the thin line between goofy, cartoony ideas and scenarios, and the grim seriousness of real-life drama and subjects without compromising either or dumbing down words in order to fit a more "child-friendly" vibe. Subsequently, for those who love this game, check out Ace Attorney next; no other series has discussions about the grim ramifications of an innocent blamed for the senseless murder of another in cold blood with a gun, while at the same time having your deceased, big boobied mentor speak to you from beyond the grave through her spirit medium sister to help you in the case.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VN mystery game Capcom have made makes a surprising return thirteen long years after having only the DS and mobile version being the only official ways to purchase and play, with enhanced visuals and a remade ost breathes new air into this classic mystery visual novel. Fans of the Ace Attorney series style of writing should feel right at home when they play this game as it comes from game director Shu Takumi.The story of Ghost Trick takes place over the course of a single night that begins with your death and the mystery around who you were and why you were killed, as well as preventing the deaths that occur over duration of this night in order to unravel the mystery of who you are and why your fate appears to be connected with the colourful cast that will accompany you.The gameplay is very simple enter the ghost world and use your powers of the dead to manipulate objects that you possess, possess someones core after death in order to speak with and travel back 4 minutes prior to their own death, using these powers you will not only prevent death but navigate the area, or use your powers to just play around with different objects to see what happens. The ost is an arranged version composed by Yasumasa Kitagawa who also composed the ost for The great ace attorney chronicles, he created a remastered 1-to-1 soundtrack to accompany the games leap to the RE engine in which he did a fantastic job in doing so some tracks I prefer his version to the original but the original music is still here in case you prefer it to the new one.If you enjoy visual novels or mystery/puzzle games or perhaps you are just a fan of the Ace Attorney games than I would highly recommend giving this game a try as it might be just what you want in a game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played and arguably Shu Takumi's best work. I say this after having played most of the Ace Attorney games. Unlike AA, Ghost Trick is a lot more gameplay-heavy, with a pretty unique and creative puzzle mechanic. Don't think I've personally ever played or seen a game with something similar. At times I did get stuck for a while on one or two things inside a stage, but it's usually because I over-thought the solution when it wasn't that complicated to begin with.  Best to read the in-game hints if you get stuck and review all your options, BUT there are times where it's a bit hard to grasp the logic of the puzzle and figure out what you need to do, so requires a bit of trial and error (or use a guide, it's okay). A bit annoying to have to start over a stage if you mess up before certain save points though. The story is pretty exciting and well-paced and I definitely wasn't expecting the journey to get so emotional. Unlike AA, Ghost Trick has the advantage of having a lot more visual story telling with the character models and animated scenes so there isn't as much reading, which helps a lot in digesting the narrative. The characters are great and have very fun designs with even greater animation. I'm simply smitten with the art style! Lastly, Ghost Trick's soundtrack is so unnecessarily good?? MANY bangers. Capcom should like maybe release them on Spotify or something.P.S.  Missile is the best boy in the whole wide world <3

_childDocuments_.review: Contender for best DS game of all time, neck in neck with The World Ends With You, and easily one of my top 10 favorite games of all time. The puzzles are fun, every character exudes style and personality, the music is insanely catchy and memorable (and the remaster tracks do the OST a lot of justice), but most importantly the story, writing, and dialogue. This is some of the most well paced, enjoyable storytelling I've ever had the pleasure of reading. No character is unlikeable, and this coming from someone who usually LOATHES mascot characters akin to Missle, but here it's done perfectly. Every character has this positivity and confidence about them that makes you just love them and want to see more. No one waste your time restating the same BS or holding the story back by simply being dumb for plot convenience. Everyone has a purpose and fulfills it with flying colors. There chatter is kept to only what's needed, and only what adds to them as characters. Not one sentence feels like fluff or filler, it's impeccable. To any aspiring writers, you owe it to yourself to play this game, and to anyone who just appreciates good writing that knows what it is and what it wants to do, here ya go.10/10, mystery puzzle solving VNs don't get better than this. Adding this sentence for steam rewards chievo :^)

_childDocuments_.review: By far the most noteworthy mystery game I have ever played. A complete and utter masterpiece in every sense of the word. It flawlessly balances a gripping mystery with fresh and exciting gameplay. The puzzle-solving is definitely unique in its own way. Instead of investigating for clues to solve murders, like Ace Attorney or Danganronpa, your goal is to stop the murder itself from happening in the first place. Or, in other words, to change the fate of the deceased. This can be done with your Ghost Tricks, allowing you to interact with intimate objects around you. Moving from item to item, using various unique tricks in each chapter to change fate, felt satisfying and rewarding.  This reward comes from impeccable writing and how it makes you care about every character. Extensive effort was put into the dialogue and interactions to make each one feel distinct and likable in their own way. My favorite character was the brave little dog, Missile! In tandem with this, the simplified yet unique way Koki Kinoshita goes about character design made me fall in love with the world and its inhabitants even more than just the excellent writing. The uniquely designed silhouettes, outfits, and faces of the characters helped each one stand out. Not only this, but the scope of over-exaggerated animations for each character also breathed even more life into them. I loved watching Detective Cabanela waltz across crime scenes and the crazy way the guardian of the park shuffles across the ground.The background music suited every moment perfectly, too. Masakazu Sugimori's electronic, synth-heavy style blends seamlessly with the game, accentuating Ghost Trick's sleek and simplified noir style. The rearranged tracks in this game pay great homage to the original, using some of the same instrumentals used for the DS but with more modern accompaniments.There is a reason why this game has been a cult classic for years now, with an incredibly passionate and dedicated fandom. Please give it a chance!10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick is still the amazing and unique puzzle game that released on the DS. _childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: The short of it: A storytelling masterpiece with gameplay that fits it like a glove. It's perfect. Play it.The long of it: I don't think I've ever played a game that had me on the edge of my seat this often.Starting with the gameplay, I LOVE it, and I wish more games had mechanics like this one, or even at least had these mechanics this well-integrated with its story as this one. I seldom ever enjoy games with time limits, but Ghost Trick's "fate" time limits are not only a part of the story itself, but are thoroughly backed up by the fact that you're playing through events as they play out in real time. Even the mechanics themselves are very naturally integrated into the story. Everything makes sense and feels great to play, and it's complemented by wonderful world and puzzle design.Now, for the story. It's awesome. It's very engaging and entertaining - there's just never a dull moment, never a scene that doesn't ooze personality. Even with characters I didn't particularly like at first, I found myself later at least respecting them, if not admiring or outright adoring them. I found the interactions sometimes hilarious, sometimes heartwarming, sometimes heartbreaking, but never boring. The story itself, the events that take place both in the present and past leading up to the fateful night you play through... everything just fits together so well, and the twists left me floored every time. Even the little details you might not notice the first time around or may not remember at all often lead to a feeling of, "Ohhh, so  why!" when you replay it after knowing the full story. It's great.The fact that this game was so overlooked when it came out on the DS is absolutely criminal, and I wish I had known about this gem sooner.Try the demo out, and if you like it, absolutely get it! Do whatever you must to avoid spoilers like the plague and go in totally blind - you will not regret it.Note: Like other reviewers here, I really wish I could purchase the awesome soundtrack, both the arranged and original versions. Throwing my money at the screen doesn't really work, so... yeah.  :P
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to playing this game for a long time. Thank you Capcom for releasing it to modern platforms!What I liked: * The mechanics of the puzzles are unlike any I've encountered. You have to move a soul around and you can interact with things to alter the outcome of unfortunate events.* The vibe is very Ace Attorney with exubarant characters. Fun movements and great sound effects. * The story is fantastic, you start with the death of the main character and it all spirals up and down from there. The final reveal is a bit much, but I like it. It will certainly stick with me. * Missile. Best doggo. * Gameplay is switched up towards the end game which brings fun new mechanics. * The hints while solving puzzles never feel like handholding. They were very welcome and to the point, but still left the challenge to piece it all together. What I didn't like: * The music was a bit extreme especially during the puzzle segments. I had a hard time concentrating. * The dialogue moves a bit slow. There are only a few dialogue boxes every time, but it still (even with FF button) feels tedious to go back in time. I wish there was an instant-rewind when you make a silly mistake rather than replaying a section (even if it's only two minutes of work). Once again, happy I got to experience this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick is a marvel of an experience from start to finish. Smart, thought-provoking puzzle design, a beautiful story, sharp visual style, all wrapped up in a puzzle box of a package that leaves zero loose ends and maximizes the utility of everything you see. Truly, nothing goes to waste in this game - every character has a role to play, either in the story or in puzzle mechanics, every story element feeds into the climax of the story, hell, even the game mechanics are vital to the themes of the story. Gameplay-wise, it's straightforward - you can manipulate certain objects, with the goal of setting up a set of circumstances that changes the scenario playing out in front of you. These abilities will change a little bit over time, but what you get at the start of the game is pretty much your entire kit, and the variety comes from the incredibly inventive level design, and how the game takes the base components of the gameplay and reconfigures them in ways you wouldn't expect, pushing you to think differently in order to figure out the way forward. Story-wise, this game truly is best experienced knowing nothing going in, beyond maybe the initial premise that you have died, and you're trying to solve your own death. The twists and turns the story takes from that base premise are simply astounding, and I was delighted by every minute of it. Go in blind. It's worth it. The whole game is worth, it really - it's a beautiful, heartwarming experience, and I'm so, so glad it's widely available again.tl;dr you ghost, you trick, that's all there is to it

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game! If you're familiar with the Ace Attorney games, this game is by the same mastermind behind those games... Shu Takumi!That said, don't think this is going to be anything like Phoenix Wright. It's not. You play as a character that has recently passed away. He is now a ghost that has lost his memory from when he was alive. You notice a woman about to be murdered, and learn that you are able to "possess" and "manipulate" inanimate objects. From there, you use your powers to try to save the woman while learning that there are more supernatural powers or "ghost tricks" up your sleeve that you didn't know you had.The primary goal of the game is to figure out who you are and who killed you while also using your powers to protect certain people (and animals) of interest along the way. The story behind this game has a surprising amount of plot twists. Every time you think you have an idea as to what is really happening, you find out you were way off. As you continue playing you will find that you have more and more questions.  By the end you will get your answers... and they'll be surprising, satisfying, and it will all make sense.... typical of Shu Takumi's style.I highly recommend this game! if you're a fan of Ace Attorney, I highly recommend you give it a try. Even if you're not a fan of Ace Attorney, this game is different enough to where I would still recommend trying out the demo and see if it's something that would interest you.

_childDocuments_.review: About a decade ago, I had my first exposure to Ghost Trick via the Nintendo Channel on my Wii. They had several demos you could upload to a Nintendo DS for cool games like Rhythm Heaven, Picross 3D, and, of course, Ghost Trick. I liked checking them out, because after all, what better way to see what the DS had to offer?Without getting into the story, Ghost Trick is a game that leaves an immediate impression on you. From the highly stylized graphics to Masakazu Sugomori's signature compositions, to the vibrant characters and intriguing storyline, this is not a game you simply "check out."Having played the game from start to finish multiple times, and even considering playthroughs of it a reoccuring pilgrimage for me (I have 200%'d it on RetroAchievements just because I could, if that's any indication), I can safely attest that it's a timeless masterpiece well worth playing even today. Even tomorrow. Even in another decade!Alas, due to Capcom's infamously poor marketing campaign for Ghost Trick, it ended up selling poorly, and worse yet, falling under the radar, becoming a so-called hidden gem. For years, I simply couldn't find the game in any store near me. The iOS port existed, but I had no iOS device to play it... not to mention the port eventually became defunct with Apple's decision to remove support for 32-bit apps.I want to make it clear that I am by no means a "casual" fan of this game. It has shaped the way I look at video games, and I'd liken its existence to that of a very good book. Every aspect of its design, from the moment you start it up, to the moment you're returned to the title screen after beating it, is meticulously crafted in a way that no other game I've played has ever been. It does not need a sequel. It does not need a remake. Anyone who's beaten it knows it is already perfect.And yet, in my many years of knowing about the game, and indeed, shamelessly having played it in an emulator several times over (reminder: I didn't feel like buying a second phone just for one game), Capcom seemed to simply have forgotten about it.I poked my head into Capcom's many Twitter accounts on June 19, 2020. That was the 10th anniversary of the game's initial release. I expected them to finally announce, or at least acknowledge, anything related to Ghost Trick.Not even a single tweet was made to acknowledge its existence. As far as I could tell, the game was, ironically, a ghost.Its memory lingered in everyone who had played it, but with the only two versions either not being sold anymore, or not running on modern devices, it was as good as dead.I went on with my life, fully aware that Ghost Trick was never coming back. My hopes and dreams had been crushed by the deafening silence on that fateful day.Out of nowhere, Capcom announces Ghost Trick. "Yeah, we're bringing Ghost Trick back. It's in HD. Animations run at 60 FPS. We made an arranged soundtrack. It's on every modern platform. It's only $30."I'd say I was shocked, but truth be told I thought I was being messed with. A quick search led me to the website, and indeed, it was owned by Capcom. This was real. It was finally happening.I would've settled for a simple port. It would've been fine. Like I said, the game was already perfect. Just put the iOS version on Nintendo Switch and call it a day.Instead, I got everything I could've ever wanted and more. This remaster truly respects the source material in a way I never expected Capcom to even be capable of.It fills my soul with joy, having waited over a decade for the opportunity to finally buy this game on a platform of my choice, with all these additions and improvements present. It feels so cathartic to open social media and see people finally being able to play the game that I and so many others had the chance to experience all those years ago!Saying I'm grateful is an understatement. I'm never asking Capcom for anything ever again*.Look, if you're still reading this and don't know whether or not this is the game for you, do what I did a decade ago and download the demo. Launch the demo. Play it.Whether you enjoy it or not, whether you're going to buy the remaster or not, I can guarantee you, it's not an experience you'll ever forget. This game leaves an impression on you. If you're on the fence about it, take your time and maybe someday you'll be ready to give it a chance.I can't think of a more fitting way to end a review for my favorite game of all time than to repeat my unofficial catchphrase... This re-release is now as close to perfect as it could ever get. Thank you.It can be  (lossy audio, Japanese track titles) and bought  with English track titles and FLAC audio quality. They just , making the main executable drop from 380 MB to just 54 MB. If you were waiting to buy it when they remuvo Denuvo, now's your time.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games from the library of the massively successful Nintendo DS has finally been remastered to be played in HD and has been brought to multiple systems.Ghost Trick is  underrated. Most people see the title picture and shrug it off as something too silly for their taste. Or they hear that it's a "story-puzzle" game and immediately jump to the conclusion, "This game isn't for me." But I implore you to give it a try anyhow – I promise that it will totally surprise you. You'll be hooked in the first 10 minutes, guaranteed.Ghost Trick is full of fascinating characters, boasts an amazing unique art and animation style, and features hands-down some of the best music in the entire video game industry. This description is  an exaggeration. The level of quality and polish that went into this game is truly remarkable. It was overlooked by way too many people back on the Nintendo DS, making it fail in sales and thus it never received any sequels. But every single person who gave it a chance walked away completely loving it.Now we finally have a second chance for Ghost Trick to shine! Please do yourself a huge favour and give the free demo a try. I promise that you will be pleasantly surprised. And once you fall in love with the game, please tell all your friends about it. If this new HD remaster finally gets the attention that this wonderful gem of a game deserves, it might prompt Capcom to make more like it. What a dream-come-true that would be!I fell in love with Ghost Trick back in 2010 on Nintendo DS and have wished for an HD version ever since. Copies of the DS cartridge go for upwards of $300 USD even in 2023 due to how amazing the game is. Now that Ghost Trick is available on multiple platforms, I bought a digital copy on Steam and PlayStation, and I even tracked down a physical copy for Nintendo Switch. I want to ensure that I will always have full access to this game in the years and decades to come. Ghost Trick is truly a "desert island" game. A game I never want to be without.

This game is perfect - its game design is perfect, the story is perfect (which in the end, made me cry a bit), the music is perfect, the art is perfect! And at first I had doubts "is it really worth $29.99?" You know, I only tend to spend < $5-$10 on games that are on sale or are not as expensive before. _childDocuments_.review: Yes, it is a port of a Nintendo DS game they're charging $30 for that can be completed in ~10 hours,However,It's a very captivating 10 hours with a very fun gameplay mechanic that gets used to most of it's potential. However, it is very context sensitive and there's little to no story justification for why you can use certain ghost tricks on some objects but not others, but I was perfectly willing to suspend my disbelief on that while playing because everything about the game is oozing with charm and has some of the best story pacing I've ever seen in a game. Absolutely none of the plot points are unnecessary or added just for padding, and none of it feels rushed neither. Though it would have been nice for certain game elements to be more responsive and a more variable rewind button would have been nice when you only screw up one small thing about what you need to do (though I can see an argument for not having that feature as well). One unfortunate fact of this being a DS port is that it can sometimes be hard to link your spirit to the node you're after rather than one next to it on a controller, where this wouldn't have been a problem on hardware where you're using a touch screen.This was written by the same guy that wrote the Ace Attorney games, Shu Takumi. When compared to those games, the puzzles in Ghost Trick are simultaneously easier to solve while also being more involved and intricate so they don't feel easier, if that makes sense. They're easy by the simple fact that the amount of variables you can manipulate in the game is often very limited so even if you're lost on a puzzle, you can usually solve it by simple trial and error so I don't see many people ever needing to look up a solution if they're stuck. Like Ace Attorney, many of the characters have an odd quirk about them that makes all of them entertaining to experience.But hey, if you're not sure, there's a demo for the game so there's little reason to not at least try it out. I have a feeling it'll vibe with most people as long as you can handle a bit of goofiness.
