_childDocuments_.review: A detective adventure based around environmental puzzles and quirky characters.Ghost Trick sees you take control of a recently deceased person who reawakens as a ghost and is given one night to solve their own murder. As a ghost, you reside in objects, jumping between nearby ones in order to move around. You can also use "tricks" on these objects - causing them to move or activating electronics. Lastly, you're given the ability to speak to other dead people's ghosts - giving you the opportunity to find out more about the events surrounding your death and enabling you to jump back in time in order to prevent their death.Ghost Trick's main gameplay sees you solving puzzles by manipulating your environment in various ways in order to move through levels and alter events. The most common and most elaborate puzzles see going back in time and altering events in order to save another person related to the events surrounding your murder from dying. You'll have to figure out the functions of the various objects available to you, then combine them in the right order and with the right timing to cause chain-reactions benefitting you. These puzzles strike a good balance, being easy enough to figure out on your own while still posing a challenge which may require a couple of retries to fully figure out. They're also wonderfully integrated into the environments - with all objects feeling like they belong in their place and interactions making logical sense.Breaking up the puzzle sections are conversations, accessed either by talking to other deceased people or through listening in on the living. These dialogues are very well written, with a variety of quirky yet genuine feeling characters, well executed intrigue and a good sense of humour. They go on maybe a tad too long but are otherwise well paced, with the alternation between talking and puzzling feeling similarly well executed pacing-wise.Told through this gameplay is a compelling story, which starts out as a rather benign murder investigation, but soon expands into an extensive web of mysteries. More and more questions as to what happened in the night of your death as well as the time preceding it begin to pop up, with reveals often leaving you with a wholly new perspective on previous events and more questions than you had before. The way things are built up and resolved is wonderful and still makes it hard for me to put the game down even on repeat playthroughs.This version of Ghost Trick brings with it some notable upgrades to the original handheld release, most notably the high-resolution graphics. While not being quite as charming as the original pixilated style in my opinion, they certainly look great and retain the game's beautiful art style along with the slick, stylized animations. The soundtrack was also rearranged and sounds wonderful, with the memorable tracks helping to set a perfectly fitting atmosphere throughout the game. You can even switch back to the original versions of the tracks at any point.As you progress through the game, you'll unlock various artwork as well as music tracks (both their old and new versions) which you can access through the menu. You're also given a bunch of backgrounds to customize the area used to expand the game's 4 by 3 aspect ratio during gameplay, which I found to be a lovely touch. There are also some optional sliding puzzle mini games unlocked after beating the game, which are rather benign but are presented in quite a neat way, making for a nice addition nonetheless. I was also happy to see that the phone book notes detailing Sissel's thoughts on all the characters and location he encounters are made available through the menu after beating the game, letting you view all variations tied to story progress.I wholeheartedly recommend you buy Ghost Trick. It tells an amazing story, challenges you with fun puzzles and has been one of my favourite games ever since I played the original, which this port does justice.Note: I was very happy to find that Ghost Trick allows you to change the icons displayed when playing with a controller, allowing you to seamlessly use various controllers through Steam Input.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally released of the Nintendo DS, Ghost Trick is quite simply one of the greatest games of all time.Have you ever been so caught up in a story, a TV series or book, that you had to see how it ended "right now", and chose to push on through to the end rather than something more important like sleeping for the night?This game right here.You play as the ghost of someone recently deceased with no memory of who you are or why you were killed. You also have the power to rewind time on any other person recently deceased and try and prevent their demise.The game is structured in to various chapters where you save multiple people (or dogs) lives in this fashion, while trying to get to the bottom of your own mystery. To which you have to hurry, as when the sun rises the next morning, you will cease to exist.The story is fantastic and paced well. By the end I was in tears. Go in blind and enjoy the ride. _childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective is a triumphant story driven "point & click-esque" mystery game that keeps you playing through it's engaging story, well-written characters, and interesting puzzles. The story is the real star in Ghost Trick, as it becomes the main driver of why you play. Right off the jump, you are thrown into an intriguing scenario that leaves you with too many questions to stop playing. In the world of 50+ hour games, a concise story is a treat. The pacing is well done with twists and revelations thrown at you every chapter. Story events occur in the background which makes the plot more believable and adds a lot to the various characters through the game.  The roster of characters in Ghost Trick, like it's parent series Ace Attorney, give the game a distinct personality. The main cast all have layers which you peel back through events and dialog throughout the adventure. They all have their own objectives which make the story more interesting as more characters are added to the roster. The writing is genuinely fantastic. It's sharp, funny, and concise. Gameplay is a variation of the traditional "point & click" adventure with a few added restraints. As a ghost, you possess objects where you can perform designated actions. It all comes together when elements like timing, environments, and dialog are added to the scenes. Sometimes I've had to resort to a more trial and error approach as opposed to cleverly piecing together a logical puzzle. The connectivity between the gameplay and the story engaged me more than the puzzles themselves, but it isn't bad by any means. Clocking in at a 10-15 hour play-through, I highly recommend Ghost Trick to anyone who has an interest in the premise, loves mysteries, or is a fan of the point & click adventure genre.

I would have a hard time retelling this complex plot, but everything makes sense as you play it. You follow each new reveal slowly as you play and all the rules that apply to puzzles also apply to the mystery of this world you are trying to solve. One of the best examples I can think of intertwining game play and storytelling.I can not recommend this game enough. I played the original and had two DS copies just to borrow one to friends and always keep one.

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the best story ever told in a videogame. There are so many clever ways every character is interconnected. It's able to consistently keep you guessing about the truth behind it all and man of man that ending is too good. The gameplay itself is clever as well. A lot of puzzle games I've played have the unfortunate problem of having the puzzles kind of feel like they have no story around them or the puzzle feels hamfisted into a story that didn't need it. Ghost Trick manages to advert that problem by having a lot of the puzzles being about going back in time and preventing someone from dying. None of the puzzles themselves are too bad to solve. Once you understand how a room works you can build exactly how this rube Goldberg machine is gonna come together to prevent this death.An incredible game and now that its on more platforms you should absolutely check it out if you like good stories in games or are a fan of puzzle games.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first beat this game, I believed it to be on par with the original Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney. After replaying that game, I believed this game to be even better and on par with the third Ace Attorney game. After replaying both that and Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective I believe GT:PD to be better than every Ace Attorney game yet. This is Shu Takumi’s magnum opus as both a developer and a writer. The game’s plot wraps up so perfectly in a way I have only seen accomplished by Takumi himself (except maybe for Takeshi Yamazaki occasionally). Every character is delightfully goofy and brimming with personality and charm, and deep in emotion when the game turns to its more serious tones. Sissel and Lynne have become some of my favorite video game characters of all time, not to mention the villain probably being my favorite villain of all time. Each chapter leaves you in shock and awe from the games incredible story direction in a way that still remains cohesive and easy to follow, making this one of the easiest games to play through all at once on a first play through. The puzzles and gameplay are tense and complex thanks to both the incredible score and Takumi’s excellent direction. The art direction and animations are where this game really shows off with the beautiful and colorful sprites really stretching the Nintendo Ds to its limits. If you have the opportunity to pick up the remaster of this game when it releases this summer, please, PLEASE do it. I promise you will not regret buying this masterpieceScore: 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's been a HUGE fan of Ghost Trick since playing it for the first time a few years ago and having replayed it multiple times since, I can easily say the game still holds up incredibly well. It is just as tightly written as I remember it being, with even the smallest loose ends getting an explanation. A real feat, especially when it comes to stories that deal with time travel. The game has several plot twists throughout its duration, yet they never become overly convoluted or seem as if they are being piled on for no reason. The characters somehow seem even more charming, with Missile easily being one of my top 5 favorite characters of all time. The game-play is extraordinarily entertaining, with puzzles that give a good challenge without being so difficult to figure out that it sucks the fun out of playing the game. I'm not usually one for puzzles, so it surprised me how intuitive the game-play was. For a game that was originally released in 2011 and had gone largely unnoticed until now (save for building up a bit of a reputation as a cult classic), every aspect of Ghost Trick ties together to make it something so wonderful and memorable over a decade later. 100000000/10 thank you to Shu Takumi and everyone else involved in the production of both the original DS release and this new modern remaster. There are not enough words in the universe to describe how grateful and happy I am that Ghost Trick exists. Please play Ghost Trick, you will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, it's Ghost Trick! One of the best puzzle/ADV/vn style games ever made. And now you can get it without selling an organ.When this came out back in the day on DS a lot of people passed over it. Hopefully it gets a second lease on life with this new version. If you like Ace Attorney, Danganronpa, Zero Escape and the like, you'll probably enjoy this game. The game is very unique in that exploration and traversal is centered around manipulating everyday objects to create paths that you can traverse, sort of like setting up all sorts of Rube Goldberg machines. The premise is straight and to the point, the characters are quirky and likeable, the music is superb, and the visuals and animations are stunning considering it was a DS game.PC port is good, with a couple exceptions -- first the game forces pillarboxing on all displays, with borders. You can customize these borders but there's no plain black option. The dark blue is close enough and was fine. Further, if you're on a non 16:9 screen, the game will add grey letterboxing. I would suggest using borderlessgaming and playing in windowed mode (e.g. on Steam Deck) to get around this. Finally, in the conversion to 60fps, some of the animations seem to have been a bit borked. Nothing major, but some look like they're playing faster than they should, some have the odd small stutter, things like that. Really minor. Mouse and kb controls are fine, but could have been streamlined further. Additionally, game is capped to 60 fps -- so you'll need a 60Hz mode on your monitor/gpu to make things look right it seems (or 120hz with forced 1/2 rate vsync etc.)

_childDocuments_.review: Plenty of games get the title of "hidden gem". Does it still hold up after all these years, or was I just nostalgic? Would I spoil those old happy memories I had of Ghost Trick?Thankfully, there was nothing to fear. _childDocuments_.review: After finishing the work on the third and originally final entry in the Ace Attorney series, Shu Takumi, the creative lead behind those games, wanted to do something similar but fresh. Which ended up becoming Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective for Nintendo DS in 2010. Unlike the Ace Attorney games, this title was more of a puzzle focused adventure game, where you are a spirit, who can perform the titular “ghost tricks” when possessing different items on the screen to solve problems. And instead of unearthing or solving crime you were often focusing on preventing it by having an ability to possess a recently deceased person and go 4 minutes before their death to attempt and prevent it from happening in the first place.The game was very well received critically, but had poor sales, according to Capcom themselves, and soon after Shu Takumi returned to work on more Ace Attorney games. Luckily, the game wasn’t forgotten and we now have a new version of it adapted for modern platforms, running on RE Engine (as it’s now the main engine Capcom builds their projects on) and with a couple of neat improvements. And it’s great.As already described, the game works as a puzzle-centric adventure. You can play around possessing different items on the scene and exploring options and visit different non-mandatory locations to see some additional bits of the story, but in each of the game’s Chapters you have a certain problem that you must solve. And the solution of that problem is the puzzle for you to figure out, as there’s only one way to do it. When inside the 4 minute before death parts of the game, you are more limited in options and the game expects you to fail a few times, since some of the options you will try are dead ends, and some of those dead ends completely block the solution of the puzzle. To unblock, you can restart the whole segment from the beginning or, if you’ve progressed far in longer segments, from a checkpoint.And frankly, this is the only truly frustrating bit of the game. A lot of the solutions are meant to be trial and error and in a lot of the cases that doesn’t lead to a permanent block of the solution within a try. However, in the parts where it does block you entirely, you have to restart, then slowly fast forward through sections that can be fast forwarded (and not all of them are), then redo everything up until the block and try something else. And if that something else also fails, you have to repeat the process again. Which can be even more so frustrating in puzzles, where you need to just wait for an extended period of time before something happens to even attempt again. I really wish the game had a realtime rewind instead or at least a full skip of mini-cutscenes of “oh this could be useful” that trigger every time you replay the puzzle.Thankfully, the moments where this becomes infuriating are extremely rare, with only about 3 Chapters in the game being unpleasant to puzzle through, with the vast majority of the game being extremely fun and playful. Helped by the fact that the writing, the characters, the style, the scenarios and the music are all fantastic. It is ridiculous, as one would expect if you’ve ever played Ace Attorney, but unlike those titles, the characters in Ghost Trick are consistently likeable, even when they are “slow” or too much of a stereotype. They’re really good and their shtick manages to not get old through the course of the game.Speaking of music and visuals – the game looks and sounds great on modern hardware. Music has been updated and sounds richer, while retaining the mood of the original tracks (and you can use the old DS soundtrack as well if you wish). And visuals just look gorgeous and it’s often easy to forget what parts are supposed to be real time 3D, and what is just 2D background. The game does keep its original 4:3 aspect ratio, so instead you can use different borders from the Options. And since the original game utilized the dual screens of Nintendo DS only for very few cute transitions, you’re not even missing anything important in the transition to the one screen gameplay. One aspect that is notably worsened, though, is that travel cutscene, it being a loading screen, visibly lags horribly, whereas it was more smooth in the original version of the game. But it’s very minor and hardly affects the overall experience.I loved playing Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective, even if some parts of the game were frustrating. Which is highly contrasted to the original Ace Attorney trilogy (and my attempts at playing The Great Ace Attorney), where I was often bored or frustrated by its design. It’s a really fun and often funny experience that I could easily recommend to anyone who loves puzzle focused adventure games with a good (if over the top) story.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game back on the DS over a decade ago and it became one of my favorite games ever. I replayed it expecting it to be a nice trip down nostalgia lane, but instead the game's just as impactful as it was back then, despite my knowing all the game's mysteries. The game just foreshadows things wonderfully, I'm kind of astounded. Beyond that, the game's just a treat. The music, the animation, the characters, the story. Everyone should play this. The only downside is the small stealth section; I remember it really annoying on DS, and I still don't love it here, but at least it's short.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: My only complaint is that most of the UI elements are unchanged from the DS, which means the dialogue option boxes take up a third of the screen. This made sense on the small DS screen, but they're way too big for PC and consoleEdit to add: One complaint that may come up is the game's 4:3 aspect ratio. The game relies heavily on its staging, and its original stage was a 4:3 screen. If you change the aspect ratio, there are scenes you'd have to restage and rooms you'd have to redesign completely. This could lead to a whole host of unintended problems because the core gameplay loop depends on the layout of objects in each room. Keeping the game 4:3 is the cleanest and most elegant solution(I wish one of the backgrounds was a stage curtain framing the screen, which would play into the spotlight aesthetic, but I like the backgrounds we got)
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games on the DS, with an incredibly memorable plot and some great characters and animations. Unlike other DS ports (TWEWY, 999) Ghost Trick didn't rely on the features of the DS so heavily that it would suffer being ported off it, so this is a great way to play the game.(Don't let my low playtime fool you, I mostly played it with a friend on his account. Plus I beat it on the DS years ago as well.)
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick is one of, if not the, best visual novel games I have ever played. I've completed it multiple times on DS and when the remaster was announced I just knew I had to get it. It's packed full of charm, gorgeous graphics, lovable characters and what I think is one of the best stories in gaming. You owe it to yourself to experience it, play Ghost Trick.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent mystery puzzle game. This game didn't sell super well when it first released which is a pity. If you like mysteries, puzzles or good writing you should play this game, it's easily worth the price. Ghost Trick's writing is undeniably Capcom, and despite the grim subject and moonlit-night setting the environments are colorful and vibrant. The characters are fun and lively, and despite their comical idiosyncrasies they are able to carry a serious and at time touching narrative. The game does a good job at balancing silliness and seriousness and seldom feels like it has a clash of tone. While not every twist lands, the game does a good job at keeping you guessing and it has that wonderful quality that once something is revealed things that seemed meaningless suddenly make sense.The game has a lovely soundtrack, so the inclusion of a music player is a welcome edition. The remastering of the sound also helps greatly as it softens some of the harsher bleeps and bloops we got on the DS (although one or two tracks sound fairly different with the new mixing, so it's worth listening to the original OST as well). The puzzles are not too complicated or difficult but there are some really clever moments that tickle the brain. Some of the weaker puzzles can seem like trial and error, but most of them are short and contained enough that you won't feel like they become overlong slogs. Worst case scenario, if you're someone who likes really hard puzzles they're short enough that they won't waste your time or keep you from the narrative (the real meat and potatoes of the game as far as I'm concerned). Likewise if you're really bad at puzzles they're simple enough and come with enough hints that you won't be getting stuck often.The review ends here, the next part is a request.Do yourself, and me, a favor and play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: If you like visual novels, play this game. If you like puzzle games, play this game. If you like Shu Takumi's other works, play this game. If you like eargasmic music and a uniquely beautiful art-style, play this game. If you like good stories, play this game. Just play this masterpiece already. You won't regret it! Shu Takumi my beloved, i hope this time people will give your underrated gem the love it so rightfully deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Trick is a story of mystery and intrigue that blends fun logic puzzles with the world of the supernatural, making for an entirely new and unique experience in the handheld gaming space. Part adventure game, part puzzle game, Ghost Trick's gameplay will challenge player's brains while its distinct art elements and character designs will deliver the fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective

name: Railbound
detailed_description: Railbound is a comfy track-bending puzzle game about a pair of dogs on a train journey around the world. Connect and sever railways across the world to help everyone reach their homes and solve over 240 clever puzzles ranging from gentle slopes to twisted passageways. BEND RAILS TO MAKE THE TRAIN GO ‘CHOO-CHOO’ Place, remove and reroute connections so that carriages safely connect to the locomotive. But, be careful and don’t make them run into each other! 240+ PUZZLES TO COMPLETE Our main levels will take you through a variety of locations at a relaxed pace. Forks along the road will lead you to spicy brainteasers that’ll please even the most demanding players! TRAIN-INSPIRED MECHANICS Use tunnels to cover vast distances in an instant. Delay trains using well-timed railway barriers. Switch tracks to reroute cars in different directions. Pick up cute friends on the way and encounter even more challenges on your journey! ART AND MUSIC FULL OF WHOLESOME VIBES Across the game’s world enjoy our comic-book-inspired visuals and a relaxing original soundtrack by the team behind Golf Peaks and inbento.

_childDocuments_.review: Railbound does exactly what I like to see in a puzzle game:A simple set of rules are premised. They are expanded upon with different mechanics that force you to think up a different solution. Levels get increasingly difficult until the mechanics have been exhausted. Now solve puzzles with a combination of these mechanics. As a bonus, have some optional levels as real headscratchers. The minimalistic art style is perfect at conveying the clarity of different objects in a level. Thanks for the reset button and ability to see solutions to completed levels.This one goes in the long list of puzzle games I'll 100% in ~5 hours and will have enjoyed my time playing. Great job!
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: It's very cute, and there are many puzzles, but be warned that the puzzles here are quite difficult.  After the first few worlds, I find myself twiddling an extremely chaotic systems of switches to get the timing between your train cars *juuust* right to solve the puzzle.  Maybe if you are galaxy brained you can see all the way to the solution from the initial conditions, but for those of us who are mere mortals it is more a process of laying out some tracks and observing results, then flipping tracks here and there to hopefully, eventually get to the solution, which feels less satisfying than having an insight from the start and working through the details.I found that the developer's earlier puzzle game, Golf Peaks, which was somewhat easier, was more satisfying for me to actually solve, so maybe check that out first unless you are hard puzzle game superfan or really into the train theme.Despite my criticism, I can't bring myself to give the game a negative review, as there is clearly a lot of care and craft that went into this, though now you have been warned what you are getting yourself into.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Railbound was fun for an hour, but the core mechanic starts to break down pretty quickly. With the tiny solution space and limited resources, the game quickly devolves into guess-and-check because it's significantly easier to try out the only 4 possible solutions than it is to reason about some of the more advanced levels that have you looping back multiple times and criss-crossing in a way that few people are going to be able to solve in any meaningful manner. Once you get to guess-and-check territory, the game is no longer fun and worth playing, it simply becomes busy work. I think the developer restricted themselves too much with this game mechanic and should have expanded the problem space--both physically in terms of board size and conceptually in terms of extended mechanics--and allowed for puzzles which actually encouraged novel solutions. A puzzle game without thinking ceases to be a puzzle game at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: It is an adorable looking puzzle game where you are supposed to build rails so you can connect the train carts to the locomotive in a specific predefined order. There is 12 chapters most of which introduce new mechanics and over 240 levels to solve.I enjoyed it, but god does it make me feel really dumb :DWorks without any issues on Linux with Proton (8.0-2 and 9.0-2) as long as it is played in windowed mode.Edit: Updated amount of chapters (10->12) and levels (200->240) as the developers made a free update with more of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical of this game initially because it looked a lot like Cosmic Express, and I had huge issues with that game. It very quickly devolved into trial and error where the goal was just to finagle the tracks into the correct shape, and it would take ages, and it wouldn't involve any interesting new twists on the mechanics, but just cryptic busy work. I saw a review here that said that Railbound took the core ideas of Cosmic Express and fixed its problems, so it turned my curiosity right around and I decided to buy it. Unfortunately, I do not find I agree with that reviewer, and my experience has been riddled with annoying trial and error and very few a-ha moments.The problem with Railbound comes in the fact that you don't just have one trail cart, you have multiple. You have to guide the numbered train carts so they arrive in ascending order at the destination. What this means in practice is that there's a lot of race conditions. You can't have 2 carts reach a tile on the same moment or they'll crash. And you have to manage their paths to correctly sort their distance to the goal. This by itself is not too bad, but it gets to be a giant problem when switches are introduced. Some switches open and close gates, and some change the direction of the lane switching. So cart 1 may reach a lane switching tile and go left, hit the switch, and when cart 2 comes behind it, it will be routed to the right. This very quickly turns into chains of switches that create highly unpredictable paths. It's race conditions gone wild. It gets so complicated to simulate the path of the carts in your mind that you just stop trying. It's way faster to just try to figure out what path uses up exactly all the pieces you have available - The level design is extremely prone to this. And if that doesn't work, tweak the connections a bit and try again. Even when you land on the solution you rarely feel like it did anything new. It's like, that's it...? Hub 4 of this game is where these problems start to mount up, but I beat two more hubs after that - there's 8 in total - and I've found that it generally stays the same. It's a shame, I'm always hungry for the next puzzle game, and thought this looked promising from all the positive reviews, but it gave me more frustration than anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute presentation, but don't be deceived! These puzzles can be brutally hard! Many possible railtrack layouts but only one or a few possible solutions plus you need to get your head around multiple wagons, switches and many more mechanics at once make these puzzles difficult. Very recommended! If you like this you may also like Cosmic ExpressRailway Islands - PuzzlePlease Fix The RoadRoom To GrowJetstreamPuddle Knights
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: spectacular puzzle game. only thing i don't like is that if you get stuck on a puzzle you kinda just have to keep on trying and trying and you can feel really stuck. I think games like this need a level map where you don't have to do them all in order, but instead just need to beat a certain number of levels to move on to the next world.All in all, though, great puzzles, great game
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: A few years ago, I reviewed a little game called "Cosmic Express" and I gave it a pretty heavy-handed negative review that garnered a bit of "controversy". That game was conceptually very similar to Railbound - you lay down train tracks to get your train carts to the main train (or, in CE, the exit). When I played and reviewed Cosmic Express, I had a lot of gripes about how open-ended and thus "trial-and-errory" the game was. With so much open space and so many possible ways to lay down the tracks and pick up passengers as well as barely any limitations, it devolved quickly to blindly trying out everything until something works, which is the opposite of fun puzzling. Puzzling should be intuitive and you should be able to look at a puzzle and figure out the solution in your head, logically, without ever touching the mouse or controller if you want to.Enter Railbound, a game that does what I wished Cosmic Express did back then (again - just bringing up the game because it is very similar yet different in a few important key aspects, so the comparison is apt. Plus the game and it's problems stuck with me and felt like the antithesis of what puzzles should be). Mainly, it allows itself to set restrictions which lower the amount of trial-and-error to basically zero. The levels are smaller, the carts are numbered which means Cart "1" has to be coupled to the train first, then 2 and so on, the passengers themselves are numbered as well (in levels that have them) and - most important of all - you only have a limited number of train tracks you can lay down. All this means that the levels in Railbound are smaller, more focused, more guided and a lot more fun than in the previously mentioned game.Every mechanic is self-explanatory. There are still quite a lot of levels that involve heavy thinking, but I never feel like a level is unfair - if I can't solve it, it's just my fault for not being creative enough. It's an excellent puzzle game and I am very happy to finally see this concept brought to a satisfying, fair and challenging level. I hope for DLCs and/or a level editor for this charming little game!
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: I dont like this game.From technical perspective it is immaculate - nice graphics, smooth working without delays. Just focusing on the puzzles.But solving the puzzles in Railbound does not give me so much fun as in other games. Solving puzzles in BaBa is you, the Witness or The Talos Principle makes you feel smart. You noticed something, thought of something new, actually visualised the solution. Super rewarding.Later levels in Railbound  are the opposite. There is nothing ingenious about solving them. Just apply some rules to create a solution that maybe works, check if it does, if not rinse and repeat. You never know why exactly the solution worked, fixing "almost working" solutions hardly ever works. And in the end, instead of being rewarded of finding something genius, you are like "oh, this worked" and are completely unamazed.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND this game to anyone who looks for real challenge in puzzle games. I myself am a big fan of puzzle games, and I think Railbound is probably if not the most challenging one I've ever played. The game itself is made with quality, did not lack any element of a game due to its puzzle nature. There's fine graphic designs and music. Many aspects of the games are fairly admirable. The challenging nature was not the easiest to manage. Most of the levels are very well designed. Obstacles/limited resources given sometimes felt perfectly measured, giving me the "just if only" vibe, which further proved its success. On the other hand, there are poorly designed levels not to be ignored. There are a few levels that made me sick even after completion because it was simply complex, not smartly designed. There are also levels that feels like a waste due to the limited options we have, which encourages trial & error sort of approaches. I think at some point in the middle of all levels I felt like the monkey trying to type Shakespeare. Thankfully that did not last long. It took me roughly 24 hours to solve all the puzzles (record time is much higher because I often left the game on while IDLE) and I think that is quite a long time for a puzzle game. The fact that I did not seek any guide other than finding the final hidden level feels ultra satisfying. I'd recommend the same to those who wants the best experience out of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: I noticed a lot of the reviews for this game (particularly negative reviews) commented that it descends into trial and error. I would like to push back on that. It is true that you need to put pieces out on the board to solve the puzzles. Doing it your head would be a bit masochistic, to my mind, unless you're a champion chess player who's used to mapping out visual fields in your imagination. But putting pieces down on the board to see what happens isn't necessarily trial and error. Once the pieces are down, if you only change things randomly to see if you solve the puzzle, THAT is trial and error. But I am completing these puzzles not by randomly changing things but by tweaking elements of the puzzle after carefully observing what went wrong and devising a strategy to correct it, often by learning how certain shapes can be deployed to create certain types on movement. For instance, learning how to creatively place 4 track loops to reverse a train on its course travelling one way, while letting it pass directly over passing the other, is a key to many puzzles. That is not 'trial and error', that is iterative design.I am still only a quarter through the game, but I feel like I can see the rhythm of things, and I am passing all the A, B and C puzzles without trouble using this method. You don't seem to need to resort to trial and error, IMHO.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like all train games, just the *tiny* train games. This is a great tiny train game. I loved Train Valley, I loved Train Valley 2, and I love Railbound. Great tutorial sequence, and nice difficulty curve and when felt I got it all figured out, I went for optional levels and got my sad incompetent ass handed back to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: After two hours of playing i can say it's a great puzzle game. The game loop is classic however it does everything in a perfect manner. Easy to understand set of rules, good difficulty level increase, intuitive controls, beautiful and clear art style and a lot of levels make you get one more level syndrome.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Game is an absolute delight to play. Charming, simple enough to pick up and difficult enough (at least later) to make you think a bit. It does not suffer from clunkiness like many other rail sims do, and didn't lose it's way in telling a lighthearted story without words. Music was pleasant to listen to, and there were a few Easter eggs hidden, including a hidden level, achievements for doing things, and yes, petting the dogs. Your time will vary depending on how long you take to do everything. I believe the game is guided should you need help. Overall a solid recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Another overwhelmingly positive game that has only 30% players have played after the half of the game and the rest of them stop in the early sections.The rule is simple, place a rail on the area to let the train reach the goal with various gimmicks. The idea of the game is fine, but the dev adds too much preplaced rails and gives us limited rails that we can put on the area, which means we only can add our rails to fill the gap between preplaced rails then adjust the direction of each rails. After the few first sections I realized that you can't be creative to solve the puzzle instead should follow the process of the goal that the dev want, that's very boring and unsatisfying to solve the game especially a puzzle genre. Actually you can be creative in the very late section, but solving a hundred sections to reach the section wouldn't be worth and wasting your time.This game could've been better if each section has more space and rails that we can use, and reduce a number of preplaced rails to be more creative.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Steam Deck.Quality title even if it is less than half the price on mobile stores, not sure what that's about but the game is good! It plays great on the Steam Deck, with the controls being perfect out of the box and the audio sounding great. The music for each area is charming and the visuals are unique so the whole feel of the game more immersive than a normal minimalist puzzle game while still keeping the simple puzzle structure. The puzzles get a bit too convoluted towards the end and there is no hint system which highlights the non-progressive nature of each stage. There's nothing you can do to work towards a solution, if you don't get it you can't even figure out if you're on the right track (har har) or not. This is only an issue for some of the more obtuse puzzles and it does make it feel even better to finally get the solution!
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: all other negative reviews are talking about the same issue (trial and error), and they are rightyou see the map, so you place down rails right in front of each train, in front and behind each conjunction, and 90% of your rails are already gone, those rails that just got placed are basically definitely there, 0 braincells needed to figure that out, and nothing we can do about it (since puzzle usually only have 1 solution)now time to brute force the solution by placing down the remaining 10% of the rails, and keep tinkering with the rail directions until it just somehow worksif you ignore all the side A, B, C puzzles, and only focus on the main story stages, it is kinda fun i guessbut if you wanna attempt those side ABCs, theres just no point, virtually no one can do those puzzles by visualizing how the trains gonna go in their brain first, everyone just pull out the classic "random bs go" and cope that it passeswhen im playing other puzzle games, (take patrick's parabox or baba is you for example), at least i am sure that i can recreate the solution after beating it once, but for railbound, if you ask me to redo a stage that i legit just finished 2 seconds ago, i still wont be able to do it, cause i didnt learn ♥♥♥♥ from it other that brute forcing
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent puzzle game.This is a satisfying game to think about and watch. After solving a hard puzzle, I'd often just re-watch my solution a few times. The game looks good and made me feel clever. I thought it was funny how often I'd get frustrated, then take a break and almost immediately see the solution. Some of the puzzles get very tricky, and it's easy to get tunnel-visioned into incorrect set-ups. Taking breaks was a very valuable tool in completing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: This game... well, the graphics are super cute and right up my alley, the music is calming and chill, the controls are simple and straight-forward, but the puzzles... these were some of the hardest puzzles I've ever done. By World 3 or 4 I was pulling my hair out. If it weren't for my OCD and the game's hint system, I would have burned this game off my computer. I hated these puzzles. At some point I just stopped even trying to solve them and would just use the hint system until it was "solved."I would watch the cars move about towards the locomotive and be incensed at the solution because honestly I can't see how anyone but a computer could actually solve these puzzles, aside from just randomly laying tracks and sending the cars on their way, over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over... forever until you just stumble onto the solution. They weren't all so convoluted, but there were more than a few that were.I've been told that this is typical of puzzle games, but I've played puzzle games before and I've never before had such a hard time, or been as frustrated. If you play lots of puzzle games, well maybe you'll enjoy this game, but if puzzle games aren't 99% of what you play, stay far, far, far away from this game. The cuteness is deceptive; this game is pure torture.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like train games? Yes! Great, Do you like Puzzle games? Yes! Do you like stressing to see if your 1st cart will beat the 2nd cart, causing you stress? Yes again! Well then I have a game for you, Railbound is a simple train puzzle, or puzzle train game, in which you have to connect your train in the correct order, some of the levels are simple and easy, and some will make you questions your life and sanity (Haha just kidding), but some of the levels took me alot longer then I would like to admit! Overall the art style, music and puzzles and game are a real treat, though I am not going to lie, you might have to hit the internet for the harder puzzles! I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a good puzzle!
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: This puzzle game is very fun! For about the first 6 or 7 worlds or so. After that the puzzles aren't about puzzle solving anymore, but simply brute forcing your way through a level until you get to a solution that works.This is no Portal where you are sure you might've missed something or the solution is hidden in plain sight, because in this game, the solution is often hidden in your endurance
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: + charming art style+ chill music+ plenty of levels (240+)+ various accessibility settings+ great on the Steam Deck- heats up your cranium- not really relaxingA lovely logic game about building train tracks so your cart(s) can reach the locomotive. There are twelve areas and each of them adds a new gimmick (and new style) to change up the process of puzzle solving. From extra carts to switches, tunnels, passengers, barriers and semaphores. You tackle these with a limited supply of tracks, sometimes not even needing all of them. Then the last (13th) area throws a load of tracks at you and let's you choose how to build up the track. It is not really relaxing in the later stages as the difficulty ramps up a bit. But overall I had fun and enjoyed my time with it. Worth a mentions are accessibility settings - hints, colorblind mode, focus mode and unlocking all levels in case you get stuck on some (or don't like them. A sweet game worth a buy if you are into logic games!------------------------------------------------------------------
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: No pause, or increment (step-wise) or skip (anti-frustrate) buttons. No hints and no consistent difficulty gradient.But it's the lack of solution flexibility that bugs me most. The puzzle maps are so small, with so few track pieces that there is almost always only one solution - and if you can't figure out that one specific solution - the lack of of anti-frustration features means you can't enjoy any other puzzles until you either brute force it or google it. The game isn't building up a coherent mental model of its behaviour the way Mini Metro or SpaceChem does.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best puzzle games I ever played. The levels are pretty fun, I felt many emotions, from feeling stupid I don't know how to do some of the more complex puzzles to feeling very smart that I've managed to do some of the puzzles.The music is amazing, the graphics are great, and this is the perfect definition of a "chill & cute puzzle game". I fully recommend trying it. Without spoiling the experience, I can say that the mandatory levels have a difficulty curve from easy to moderate, and the bonus ones can get really difficult, yet very enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't allow you to make a creative solution, just forces you to find the only one possible solution by trial and error. Feels like a sudoku where only 1 solution is possible but in sudoku there are rules and strategies that allow you to solve the puzzle. Here you have only trial and error, nothing else.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: If you like puzzles, this is a fantastic example of the genre. The art is cute, the animation is slick (and also cute!), and the puzzles require some genuine thought once you get a little way in; when I first started the game I thought it was a bit boringly easy, but it does ramp up. Each 'world' introduces one new mechanic, which helps to keep it fresh and also gives your brain a slight break as the first couple of levels of each world are designed to teach you the new mechanic rather than challenge you.My only criticism is that sometimes, because the game gives you a set number of rail pieces (which is necessary for the way most of the puzzles work), you can kind of brute force a level by simply placing the pieces in the spots they must go because of the fixed pieces already in place. You usually still have to work out the direction of a connection or something, but it doesn't give you the same satisfaction as feeling like you actually 'solved' it. This is relatively rare and there are lots of levels.There are still some bonus levels in the worlds I've otherwise completed (I'm on world 6 of 8 currently) which I'm stumped by, so it's definitely a good workout for your brain overall. The overview from which you select a puzzle is also easy to navigate.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: I have read some negative reviews, and I must admit that there is some truth in them: game gets very complex at some stage. But isn't that the point of puzzle game - to be challenging? And if some problem is challenging, do we have to be able to imagine whole solution?But let's get back to the start for a moment.You can see at first glance, game is cute, big plus for simple, cozy graphic.Another big plus for teaching new mechanics by experience - first puzzles in stage are very simple just to teach you without any descriptions. That's the best way puzzle game can teach player without single word.Those are (almost) unquestionable strong sites of this game.And then comes complexity. Is it only trial and error? If you want, yes, it can be. But if you decide to think about that specific puzzle to recognise some must-be elements, to cross out what won't work, you might be able to find the answer. Of course, you will find it after couple/dozen/even more attempts, and yes, it might not be today... I played this game 27 hours, and I still don't have 4 achievements. But also I still feel challenged, not overwhelmed, by those puzzles I didn't solved yet. And I keep coming back.Retrying is not the problem for me, since I made changes due to educated guess.What might be repulsive is lack of feedback - you either made it or not. I get it, some people like to work toward the goal with small steps. Here you can only assume that if you connect your first cart (and didn't try to move others yet), that it will be part of whole solution.But again, it is complex game with specific structure - you can't say "those 3 rails are correctly connected".Some say there is no freedom, just recreating one correct solution made up by devs. But isn't that what most of puzzle games do? (Yes, they do). Funfact: just now, before writing this review, I have finished 11-8B in a way that devs didn't planned :P So there is some tiny level of freedom, I guess ;)It's not game for everyone, sure. As negative comments shows, it's not even for all puzzle lovers. I get that. But still I recommend it, because it is fun, and challenging, and sometimes forces you to ignore obvious moves to find out the correct one. So if thinking AND experimenting is what you like, or at least want to try, than go ahead! Even if not for everyone, it's a very good game.PS: it's not as hard as "Baba is you", for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Like the other two previous titles of Afterbrun (Golf Peaks, inbento), Railbound is a cosy and relaxing puzzle game, with exceptionally cute art and sound effects. The UI and control are simple but functional, with both keyboard and mouse control, undo and reset button. On top of that, Railbound has many accessibility features, such as colour-blind mode, focus mode, hint system, etc. The devs are great people too: they respond actively to user feedback and keep updating the game with QoL improvements and new contents.However, IMHO, puzzle design ventures into the terrain of trial and error far too deeply. The problem is that its mechanics (especially the switches), albeit interesting, cause great trouble for visualising the consequences of changing a tile of track. This  from Thinky Games and this  both put it very well; you should read them (and other negative reviews too) if you are concerned about the quality of the puzzles.On the other hand, the in-game hint system is self-contained and can guide you through any level. Despite being deterred by the puzzles, I find it weirdly satisfying to put down the tracks with the help of numerous hints, then watch the carriages run to their destination like a little animated show of a Rube Goldberg machine. It is really curious that so many complicated movements can take place within such a tiny space!In short, I give a neutral thumbs up. If you are into cosy and comfy little games, this may intrigue you.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: While puzzles start off as being mappable and solvable in your mind, it later becomes a matter of laying down tracks and making small adjustments to see what works via trial and error. Basically, it becomes more of a process of elimination as you progress through the game. This is not necessarily a bad thing, and I managed to get through half the game using this this method. ...but then I get to world 6, and the tracks get peppered with multiple switches that cause tracks to flip directions every time carts pass over them, and this becomes a major mind f*ck, so much so that it becomes less about puzzle solving, and more about taking wild stabs and hoping that I stumbled into a solution. Because of this, I kinda wished the puzzles had a bit more flexibility in the way they could be solved, instead of restricting solutions to only 1 or 2 possibilities. So even though there are 12 worlds to play through, expect to only really play through half of them on your own effort, unless you're some elite level chess player who can truly map out every sequence that takes place.Another slight complaint I have is that I wished the orientation could be adjustable, because I found myself either tilting my head or the handheld in order to better visualize the puzzles.Overall, Railbound is a great game to play for those short on time or simply looking for something chill. But make no mistake, the difficulty tag is definitely an understatement.PS: Review is mostly based off my Switch playthrough
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Great brain-teaser where we have to figure out how to place train tracks to connect all carts to the locomotive(s) in the correct order. As of now, there are 12 different levels, each one introducing a new mechanic added to the previous ones.There is not much of a story, but some puzzles are so tricky, that they will keep you up for a long time. There is lots of trials and error to do until finding a solution...I definitely recommend this game to any puzzle lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cute and the first 3 worlds do a great job of teaching you basics so that you need to think your way through problems. But starting in world 4 (4-5 specifically for me), the level design stops being fun.I attribute this to incremental progress: In the early levels, you can experiment and get closer and closer to the solution, fiddling with your tracks until you get it right. By world 4, you're dealing with enough complexity that you don't know if you're even on the right track to begin with. Perhaps you need to start over, perhaps you need to fiddle, you don't know, you never feel like you're inching closer to understanding the puzzle, the answer is either given to you entirely by the hint / looking it up, or you luck into the answer without understanding what your're doing. It IS cute, I love its aesthetic deeply, almost everything about it makes me want to sing its praises. But a puzzle game lives and dies by its puzzle design, and the sharp increase in difficulty for me just broke me from being able to recommend it. Others may sync with the puzzle design better than I did, I can't speak for everyone who plays this game, but I can say that I really love puzzle games; from baba is you, patrick's parabox, and recursed; to just any sudoku like and nonograms, I love puzzle games, and this just doesn't scratch the itch after world 3.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game in which you have to join the rail cars, in the right order (numbered), up to the locomotive by placing down rails. You start off with a tutorial of what to do in the first few levels. After that, it's up to you how you set it all up. Some levels are easy whereas others can be rather challenging. Overall, I enjoyed playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Railbound was an absolute joy to play. As someone who loves solving puzzles, I found its challenges both engaging and extremely satisfying. What really stood out to me, though, was the game’s charm - beautifully crafted with cozy visuals and a kindhearted story that gently unfolds as you progress. There’s something so calming about piecing together tracks while enjoying the cheerful soundtrack and whimsical art.For me, Railbound was the perfect escape: a relaxing yet rewarding experience that I didn’t want to end. If you love puzzles or just need a bit of joy in your day, I can’t recommend it enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Very much recommend this puzzle game for people that just want to sit down and play something for a couple minutes before moving on. Very excited to hear they've added more puzzle come to one year birthday of the games release and am excited to try them out soon

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a cute game!! I played it every day after waking up, to get my brain moving before work.The art/graphics are so pleasing to the eye and the mechanics are really smooth.You can change settings and turn Hints on and off, for when you completely block out of ideas. Also, the hints are not fully given all at once, they're given step by step to make sure you can get the best chance to enjoy the game!The achievements were also really fun to get ^^ I'm really hoping DLCs with extra levels are released in the future.

If you're still unsure whether you should buy this game or not, you can check out my full Let's play on  :D
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle game! The levels are very well designed with the main game levels being definitely doable and the bonus levels getting very tricky. The music, sound design and graphics all fit very well and enhance the game a lot.Only gripe is the controller support is a little bugged at the moment but the devs have said they're looking into it so hopefully fixed soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game! Nothing too fanciful but really solid mechanics and level design.I liked the difficulty progression, it starts off simple and relaxing, and the main puzzles are mostly quite manageable to complete. However, the bonus levels can get very challenging (and there's many I've yet to solve too!). Mechanics are really interesting too! Each world has a new set of mechanics with nice levels that'll surprise me with interesting ways to use them.I also really enjoy the mood, it's really calming and satisfying to watch the trains move.One warning though, a number of puzzles require quite a bit of trial and error to get to the solution, even if you do see the core idea. I don't see this as a bad thing, it's the nature of the game to be hard to visualize where the trains move at each point in time. Alot of the time the puzzles are placing the tracks in something that makes sense and hoping it works. Thankfully, most of the time it either works or it's easy to modify it until it works, but sometimes it's hard to tell if I'm on the right idea but just missing a detail or I'm completely off track. So yea if you don't like this kind of trial and error optimization/engineering this game might not be for you (but it could still be!)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful puzzle game. You're only able to place basic train tracks and make connections throughout the game and the set piece of puzzle tiles means that really is all you need. The concept is so simple.Some of the puzzles are fiendish. The bonus levels in particular. If you love trains and puzzles you'll enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Railbound is a gorgeous puzzle game about guiding trains to a locomotive in the right order. I love the introduction of new mechanics as the game progresses. Each idea is a great development on the main gameplay loop and very well executed. I adored every moment I spent playing Railbound. Overall, 9/10. Excellent puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Soothing puzzle game with a wholesome calming atmosphere. The puzzles start easy but work their ways up to complex with additional mechanics that the game teaches you how to approach through play rather than text boxes. If one gets overwhelmed or confused by a puzzle, the hint system allows for a way to incrementally nudge players in the correct direction rather than outright telling. Loved everything about this game. Looking forward to what the devs do next.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts out very simple because it will be just about drawing train tracks so that you can navigate the fixed environment so that the trains will arrive in their correct order. However, this quickly becomes more challenging as more mechanics are introduced in every world. Loops are a vital feature you will need to learn as all future worlds past 3 require loops to finish the level.This is a game where you need to plan out visually where something will go without seeing it all take place in front of your eyes. Sometimes you'll look at a level that just doesn't make sense to you, and then your next 3 levels afterwards, you will think this is a breeze because it logically makes sense. The progressive hint system is very helpful as it gives a faint line where some tracks should go, . The more times you press the hint system, the more the tracks will be revealed, but it will never 100% complete the track. This system is an excellent way of nudging the player in the right direction without losing the level's challenge.This is by far the reason I bought this game. The art style is adorable and relaxing, accompanied by the lofi music.A nice wholesome relaxing puzzle that you can finish within 3-4 hours. There's no time pressure to finish your railroad. You only need to be methodical in how you get to the end of your answers; if you get stuck, there's always the hint system to help you. I recommend it to players who love puzzles and are train otakus. However, the price may put off players at $19 AUD, but I think the art style and gameplay are worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to say that this game is really cute and also really mindboggling for sure. It may look easy but once you get to the harder levels, it really wraps your brain around that sometimes I keep getting on the wrong track *ba dum tss*. But in all honestly, the artwork is a delight and the music is really soothing. Props to the devs for making a really good puzzle game!
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Like all good puzzle games, this game makes me feel , but it does a really good job mitigating my frustration and anger at the fact that I suck with really cozy music and a good chill vibe that makes me feel like it's okay that I suck, an I'll figure it out eventually. I'm not 100% sure that's true, but this game does as good a job as any puzzle game I've played in years of trying to talk me into believing it.And to the game's credit, I'm figuring out the required puzzles pretty consistently, they're not that bad, but the optional puzzles are absolutely brutal.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: If you like solving puzzles in a cosy, light atmosphere, this game is for you. There is apparently a hint system if you get stuck. On the other hand, if you like the challenge, there are  bonus levels (sometimes really mind-bending!) along the way. Each chapter adds some new mechanic (like tunnels or barriers) so you won't get bored.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Railbound is a charming puzzle game with difficulty that can both decrease and increase your blood pressure, while producing a lovely art style and a pleasant environment to be in.The aim of the game is to move a number of rail carts from point A to B, making sure they arrive in chronological order. As you progress through the levels, the difficulty increases with the use of tunnels, switches, rogue trolleys and even passengers to pick up. I will admit I was completely stumped on a few of the later levels, but the game has a hint system to assist you, you just need to enable it as it’s (rightly) disabled by default.There are 8 “worlds”, each with their own themes from a holiday paradise to arctic plains and arid desert lands, each with their own musical themes. One issue I found is you start to notice how quickly the music loops in the later stages as you’re spending longer trying to complete the puzzles, so you may eventually need to mute the music and stream some lo-fi hip hop radio.I’ve managed to complete the main levels, and as you can see by my play time the game is fairly short. However for a majority of the levels, upon completion you unlock a variation of the puzzle, where rail carts, tiles, or the entire level is either rotated or displaced. These levels are a lot harder and I’m slowly going through them as I write this review. Overall, this game is a delightful brain teaser worth your money and that extra cup of coffee you’ll need to pour as you play. I’m all aboard this hype train.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a fantastic experience. Some puzzles had me stumped, yet i continued on my merry way to 100% completion. Something about engineering your own railroad layouts kept me engaged for all 8 worlds. I was sad when I completed all the levels, even though the game is adequately long. Good stuff!
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: Review by Unam This will be one of my shorter reviews, as Railbound is a small game that is worth picking up. I'm a sucker for puzzle games and hidden gems, and Railbound happens to be both of those. If I could use one word to describe the game it would be . It's all about connecting train tracks with given rails and structures. This never changes, and it doesn't need to. There are roughly 150 levels in the game and it surely won't take you long to complete, but some of these are hard puzzles and most will make you think thoroughly about them. Steam has a feature where if you play for under 2 hours you get a full refund, but I strongly recommend against this. You should take your time with it, enjoy the nice graphics, and just chill out. Plus, the game is not expensive and you should support the developers. At the end of the day, Railbound will not change your life, nor will it take you through a breathtaking experience, but it sure as hell is a pleasantly fun game.I give Railbound a...
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: After you pass the first very easy level, it comes to an abrupt cliff that you have to climb. Puzzles are looking easy, but there is always a missing piece that makes the puzzle hard. Some puzzles are strangely easy (done in 10s), where others can take hours to solve. I had to look into one solution as I was stuck several days.. But then when I saw the solution, I had this "ooooh that was so simple" moment. Take your time, do others puzzles while you can, then come back to the hard one. You will succeed. The only little issue is that there is ONLY ONE solution for each game, it could have been more open, with a competition based on the number of rails elements used. But here only ONE solution. Good luck!

The last few levels also felt "free for all" with how easily they were laid out. Overall super recommend if you enjoy mild difficulty puzzle games."Last" achievement hint:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a delightful puzzle experience that really shines with its charming design and clever mechanics. The railway-themed challenges are engaging, offering just the right balance of difficulty to keep you hooked. The soothing visuals and relaxing soundtrack make it a perfect choice for unwinding after a long day. If you enjoy thoughtful, visually appealing puzzles, this one is definitely worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Railbound

_childDocuments_.review: If you are familiar with the 94' game "The Lost Mind of Dr. Brain", you may remember one particular puzzle, the train of thought (with good ol' Rathbone slouched in a barrel, ah the memories). I had a lot of fun on this one, and I bought Railbound to scratch this specific train-puzzle itch that never left me. On that perspective, after 4 "regions" completed at the time of writing, I'm completely satisfied.  On the surface, Railbound turns out to have a lot of charm with its drawing-like graphics, lighthearted music/sound-design and cute characters. In terms of mechanics, it's a simple matter of setting a limited number of rail sections so that each train cars joins the locomotive in the right order. Whether it be the rail limit, the car order, the interface or your level progression, everything is perfectly clear and easily accessible. All the qol features I'd want in such a game, like going back any number of actions or resetting everything with one key stroke, are there. And I appreciate that each region takes its time to introduce the new mechanics so that you've fully grasped them before you get to the serious stuff.In addition, the nature of the game makes it ideal for very quick sessions, and you'll find your last puzzle exactly as you left it before exiting the game.The only con in this game that I can currently think of is that the speed of the train cannot be modified ahead of the train-cars launch, which isn't practical at times, but remains a minor bother. Other than that, Railbound is a cute and satisfying game, very pleasant to play to. I have no doubt that I'll be completely overwhelmed at later levels and potentially never finish the game, but I don't care; the game plainly does what I bought it for and has only brought me happy times so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Railbound is a cute puzzle game about trains and animals. Featuring 12 (+ 1 bonus) world, it employs a wide variety of mechanics from switches, semaphore signals, trolleys, and an entire other train. Whilst the difficulty in some places feels off, there are a lot of steam community guides to help you out. The artwork, music, and sound design is just perfect, and really shows the talent of the developers. While the game is no longer in development anymore and the developers have moved onto a new game, I wish that there was a community map maker. It would really help increase the replayability of the game instead of just the base, bonus, and hidden level.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game from Afterburn, looking forward to their next game! Would definitely recommend Railbound (and all of their other games) if cozy puzzle games with simple mechanics used in creative ways sounds interesting to you.Railbound has really cute visuals and sounds, withplenty of accessibility features as well to tweak these to your preferences/needs. Also has a LOT of levels which allow a smooth difficulty curve both across the whole game and as each new mechanic is introduced. Some negative reviews suggest that trial and error is the main way to progress through the game. While levels *can* be solved via trial and error, there is also some logic/key realization that every level is trying to get at. Besides the easier levels, I would say I used some kind of iterative problem solving for every level, keeping the game both challenging and satisfying to progress through. Trial and error definitely becomes less viable as you move into the more complex levels as well since some of the assumptions used in trial/error start to break down.

_childDocuments_.review: Railbound - A captivating puzzle gameOnce upon a time, somewhere around the Early Paleolithic, as a primary school student, I read “The Dog Who Rid the Railroad”. I admit that I shed a few tears at the time, because the book ends very sad. Now I spent a good few hours at the monitor just allowing two dogs to ride the railway. And I had a lot of fun.Although I will admit that once or twice I was close to tears again - but rather those caused by anger. Other than that, sometimes I puffed and sweated like a pig(*), straining my brain, cursing (increasingly louder), and sometimes, for a change, I squealed with joy like a small child. A lot of emotions, apparently - apparently! – a simple puzzle game created by a Polish studio, you will admit.(*) Fun fact: pigs don't sweat. They have no sweat glands at all.The story doesn't exist here. We just have to lay the tracks on the next boards - and there are as many as 150 of them, although some 1/3 of them are optional stages that we can skip - in eight different worlds to allow the train to pass to the next station. That's all. But as it turns out, a lot can be squeezed out of seemingly simple rules. Add to this very low system requirements, nice graphics and perfectly selected relaxing background music (I'm playing it while writing this text. It's a pity that this one song is playing all the time in the game), and we'll get something that can be defined as a "good trip".At the beginning, a slight disorientation - practically from the march we get to the first board. There, only in a scaled, very clear and minimalist menu, we can set various gameplay or graphics options. What to do next, you have to guess ... although it will not be difficult. We click the mouse to lay the tracks (we always have a top-down limit of "blocks", but we can recover those already laid), and when the route is ready, press the start icon. If we have done everything right, the car(s) join(s) the locomotive, it emits a brisk whistle and takes us to the next board.Because the first steps are so easy, at first I was genuinely offended that someone thought I was an idiot for giving me such trivial tasks. But don't worry, it's just a kind of tutorial and the difficulty level increases quickly. Each subsequent world introduces some complication to the game, such as tunnels or arriving wagons (there are as many as four at the end of the game), which we have to connect in a specific order. Barriers blocking the route appear (they can be lifted after passing through the appropriate button on the track), switches, turnouts, semaphores; there are stations where passengers boarding a specific car are waiting, on the route we are disturbed by draisines, etc.Combinations of all these elements are sometimes a really great challenge and can give a person nystagmus and rage quit when trying to grasp it. Believe me, if in the first world I was disgusted with the low level of difficulty, in the third one I started scratching my head, and around the fifth one I muttered under my breath more and more often what I would do to the author of the board if I got him/her. What I shouted at eight, better not to say.Fortunately, the game also has a well-thought-out hint system that does not put coffee on the table, but gently suggests the next step. And if we do it and we're still stuck, then we'll get a little more accurate advice - and so on until the end. Needless to say, I had to ask for help a few times. Because Railbound also has stages where a truly hardcore level of difficulty requires multiple attempts by trial and error before you finally manage to discover the correct track layout. You don't even know how frustrating it is to watch your last car, after making numerous maneuvers, suddenly turn in the wrong direction at the last junction or stop in front of a closed barrierBecause despite various frustrating moments, I had a great time with this game. On reflection, however, I decided that there is something about Railbound that makes the final rating need to be lowered a bit. And I don't pick on quite superficial flaws such as the not-stunning length of the game (it will take you four-six hours), one piece of music or minor problems with the construction of the tracks (the game itself places the appropriate "block" when we click on a field, but it doesn't always understand our intentions, so sometimes it takes a few tries before inserting the element that suits us). The problem I have with Railbound is - so to speak - much deeper, even fundamental. Maybe I'm being picky now, but...Well, in 2001 came out the brilliant Pontifex (I recommend it!), in which we built bridges. They were supposed to just work, and what they looked like, the game didn't care at all. As a result, I often constructed structures that were truly crazy and defying all the rules of engineering - all according to the principle "if it looks stupid, but it works, it's not stupid". Then I spent long hours trying to optimize these structures by eliminating unnecessary elements or creating their simplified versions. Or I was building a completely new and differently conceived bridge from scratch on the same board. It was a great creativity lesson!Meanwhile, here, although the puzzles turn out to be very ingenious (the creators of some of them should burn in hell!), the truth is that they can only be solved in one possible way - as the author invented. The construction of the board and the exorbitant limit of available "blocks" practically eliminate any alternative solutions. As a result, Railbound teaches not so much creativity as the ability to reproduce someone else's reasoning. There is no room for our invention here - we just have to guess "what the poet meant" and repeat it. I will say maliciously that this can be a valuable lesson for people who want to make a career in corporate - learning to meet the expectations of their superiors ...But just to be clear: it's still excellent - even appealing! – game, so I sincerely recommend it to you. Both for solo and family play. Just remember not to swear in front of your child. You can cry.
