She is the brawl and the brains in the team (is Frank a leader? lol)But, alas, nothing is ideal and there are some moments which I hope team will fix in near future: - Some annoying bugs:Almost all saves got file date 00:00 01/01/0001. Sometimes you can get sound lag while investigating and in cutscenes.- It takes some time to game to launch.- IDK what happened in team but [SPOILERS] why chapter 3 has too many locations and ‘find helluva items just like in several typical point-and-click games, we don’t care that much”. [/spoilers]- Some descriptions are very hard to read, they have got too small fonts.And some complains:- It’s been a year so where is the OST? I mean, yeah, maybe Burly Wood (which songs we can hear in the bar) is an underground rock band but, certainly, give guys more attention.- The ending is just ???? Like, is team going to make DLC or sequel? Put a bold full stop here will be a very bad decision. We need more information about the universe, about racing, about Frank, Gavin and Sally.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: There should be a Hardcore tag if the game is meant to be this challenging, or there should be at least a different difficulty choice. I didn't expect it to challenge me in EVERY mini game and combat, especially at the early stage of the game! The art and the voice acting, OST and perhaps the narrative became the drive that made me keep playing until now
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: I like the style - closest thing I can think of would be Disco Elysium or maybe Shadowrun. Innovative game-play, basically a point-and-click adventure with turn-based combat. Cons: I think the combat is a total slog. Having to use AP outside of combat actively discourages experimentation.Verdict: I think it's worth the low price tag, but I'm not sure that I'll play even halfway through the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the pros:- The art and the voice acting is pretty good;- The hybrid RPG/VN works quite well, and it's a fun game to play;- The setting and the story are captivating.Now the cons:- The game is easy as hell;- The combat as little variety in terms of both enemies and skills (although there are many skills, you'll only ever use a few); - The mini games are a tedious loss of time at best;- It's way too short (finished in 12hrs), the ending is underwhelming and there is no replayability.I would only recommend it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun great game to play until the final boss and I would have recomended it.The end boss hits like a truck, regularly attack multiple times, causes time pressure (that aggravates me to no end) and out damages any healing you can do.It's a dum dps race. Hoping you take hime out before he kills your team.I was overflowing with aggression after a few attempts on the boss.I can understand that the end boss should be a bid harder, bud this is just dum.Loved the story, characters. Had fun with most puzzles als long as the where logical.Could forgive that getting some puzzles solved was dum luck.Bud this end boss is a royal ♥♥♥♥♥♥ for me.To save me sanity and regain my composure, I'm just uninstalling
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game so much. The art work, the voice acting, the mystery of the world they're in, the battle mechanics; it's all amazing. I just CANNOT get past the hacking. I don't know if I'm just an idiot or what, but I've looked at guides, explainations, requested help from roommates, and I legit just don't understand it. It sucks because there is no alternative way to to get into some areas other than hacking so it hinders the story or makes it extremely difficult to move forward making it more frustrating than enjoyable. Hopefully in future updates they'll make this easier, but I'll have to put this in the backlog for now.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: The point n click + AP system was very unique and interesting. The AP unique to each character was engaging as well. Combat system was pretty middle down the road like 6/10. The loot pool felt very bland receiving duplicate items. But oh man not to spoil the story, but one part of the game left a bad taste in my mouth. Id only recommend for those bored, looking for something quick, and the game on sale. Otherwise, the game isn't worth its normal price.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun and original game that combines point-and-click puzzles and RPG combat in a cyberpunk London. The game has nice graphics, funny dialogue, and an engaging story, but it also has some issues with length, difficulty, and ending. I enjoyed the game, but it could use more polish and content to flesh out its better features. 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game with both point-and-click gameplay and turn-based RPG combat. The story is decent, but the voice acting really carries this game, as it is excellent. The only complaint I have is that there is a tedious bit of inventory management (this character has to move this individual item to their inventory to use it) and a few sequences where you have to repeat the same process multiple times. 7/10 so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: The production quality of this game is actually insane, I did not expect to to play a title with such a creative artistic direction.Sunday Gold experiments with mechanics and visuals i've never really seen in other games, and they work very well too, yes there is some minor frustration factors here and there but thats nothing compared to the good of this game.The fact that this game isn't that well known is kinda mind boggling, it is a super solid title and I wish more games of this quality existed on the market.Now I want to point out some of the good parts and frustration factors of Sunday Gold:--- The Characters ---The 3 main heroes (Gavin, Frank and Sally) are very well written and come with funny dialoge. The way how they just interact with eachother and enemies kinda gets you invested into their characters. Their voiceacting performance is also noteworthy.--- The Story ---The story is simple, streamlined and easy to follow. It has some unique things tied to it but overall nothing too expensive, but it works in the games favor. Whenever I progressed in the story, I never was surprised or shocked to the discoveries made, but it still gets you invested in it and wanting to solve/figure out whats up ahead.--- The Combat ---The combat's framework is turn based combat but with some big strings attached to it, I do like this system due to its uniqueness and options. Tying action points used for both combat and exploring is a different take on this genre and is done very well. There generally are a lot of cool mechanics unique to this game even outside of combat, its fun to explore these options.However this game has a weird learning curve that may lead to defeats if the player doesnt understand the potential and consequences of their actions. On the other hand, combat can also feel braindead and cheesy. There is the composure system, which can lose meaning due to the cheesy regenerative abilities that you have, I noticed in order to make this mechanic work, the game literally has to force your entire composure pool to 0 to make the player play around it. This is what I mean by "cheesy combat" since it feels like these mechanics are conflicting with eachother.Overall the combat is a mixed bag, it can feel awesome, frustrating or cheesy/braindead.--- Sound Design and Music ---Don't overlook this, the music and sound design for Sunday Gold is seriously outstanding. Pixel Audio worked on this, they are the best audio studio I know.--- The Puzzles ---I enjoyed them, the game forces you to figure them out on your own and think outside the box. They can get pretty though but still give you enough clues to work things out by yourself. This is subjective though, I could see why some players may not enjoy some of them.--- Artistic Direction / Visuals ---The visuals of Sunday Gold is another factor that I really do appreciate. It generally is just beautiful and nice to look at.Besides a comple of the frustration factors (which are subjective and can be played around), Sunday Gold is still a hidden gem and I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Sunday Gold is an underrated indie that's full of style, not only in it's unique artstyle that resembles Disco Elysium but also in it's well-developed characters that make a simple story come alive. A simple turn based combat system with an added Darkest Dungeon-esque stress mechanic makes it enticing and never repetitive. A shame this game is not given the due attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: This game had the potential to be awesome, but in general, it is just a good game. The characters are well-written, the music from the pub is very enjoyable, and the emphasis here is on the beautiful art style and the INCREDIBLE voice acting.However, it lacks in gameplay. The AP system doesn't make any sense from a "point and click" perspective. The puzzles are fun to solve and discover, but they annoyed me when I had to end the turn, enter a 10-minute combat just to move a box, or in a super important part of the story, enter a fight with random characters that disrupt the atmosphere of the scene. Besides, the boss fights are repetitive .
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: If you set your game in London would it kill you to hire British voice actors, or at the very least ones who can do a passable British accent?That aside, action economy also applying to out-of-combat interactions was an interesting idea but unfortunately it's let down by the tedious combat. Constantly managing action economy becomes a chore very quickly especially faced with the frustrating minigames for lockpicking etc and the fact that your combat action economy carries into the exploration round so half the time you are going straight back in for more combat before being able to do any of the interesting part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommend this game. Combat is fumbly at the start but absolutely smoothes out the further in the game you go. It’s not a perfect game, but reminds me of a combat-focused Disco Elysium. Absolutely amazing puzzles, I like the skills and the voice actors are amazing. Would recommend taking the plunge on this game to anyone on the fence about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know how to explain this to either crowd this game is trying to appease to. There's the point and click side, which functions well on it's own - and the (j)RPG side that also functions well on it's own. Combining the exploration of the world to a constant threat factor with the difficulty that the game imposes really kills my vibe to play this game anymore. I want to explore this world but every action has it's consequence and unfortunately in this game it's basically you either min/max your play through (impossible for first timers) or tough it out and hope for the best (luck). The story being told is fine, it's cyberpunk standard. The art style is great in both story telling and battle mode. I just really wish you could tone the difficulty down a bit, or at least add more indications of a major fight coming to save manually (having to do the server puzzle twice wasn't fun, even with the answer the second time). Idk not a bad game, but functional - probably done after the first chapter and won't touch it again. Check it out on discount, I say and check your mileage pre-2 hours before refunding.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: I love the point and click aspect of the game. The voice-overs and graphics are amazing. But running out of Action Points (AP) at the very beginning of the game and being unable to "end turn" or regenerate AP before I'd even finished exploring the opening interactive scene is a complete turn-off. The AP should have been limited to fight sequences only, in my opinion. The "turn based" and action points aspect completely ruined what could have been an enjoyable point and click adventure game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Story: 7/10 Art: 9/10 Game-play: Puzzles 9/10, Fighting 4/10 Overall score - a solid 7/10 The characters are fun and interesting enough but nothing too deep, same can be said for the story - the conversions are pretty quick and simple but give enough information and life to the situation so youll be interested enough in the plot, but i dont feel anything here thatll leave you unknowing what to do with your life after you finish the game. The Art is great, the comics-like stylization give it a unique look and for sure gets the attention it deserves, the cleaver uses of coloring and timely pop ups of text or imagines really make it shine. The game has 2 main gameplay aspects, the investigatory puzzle aspect that would remind you of the nancy drew series, piecing clues together and exploring the areas till everything just clicks together, the puzzles are fun and well done, require just enough thought to make it interesting. i have 2 grips with it tho: 1. When interacting with some puzzles you cant access the inventory to seek out the clue that you know solves it, i used snipping tool and put the clues on my seconds screen so i wont need to stop the interaction each time or alt tab. 2. Each character has it own minigame which is required to progress the game, theyre fun enough but towards the end of the game i did feel like theyre getting repetitive, some variation in each would have helped alot And now the sore thumb, the fighting. Ill start from the good, the item system is pretty fun, you can change your damage types and optimize for one of the weapons that each one gets, its not super complex but it gives you enough flexibility. The turned base aspect with the composure mechanic is a fun idea and the timer works well to make the fights feel urgent, but it falls short because of its downsides. So.. The bad - no one wants to be a tank heal bot but youll see that you cant really do without it, the fights in the begging are fine but the enemies become a HP slog towards the end and so the fights take way too long, especially if you dont have all the characters present which doesnt help that sometimes there are too many fights with the same type of enemies.But, the biggest downfall are the bosses. Between enemies that just get back thier full HP just because, multiple turns that the bosses take compared to 1 per turn of each of your characters, and the large damage they do that may force you into a healing cycle - pointlessly prolonging the fights yet again, it makes the fights that supposed to be epic feel like a chore. im usually fond of turned based fighting but really towards the end i longed to just get back to the puzzles and the story. OVERALL, i do recommend the game if you can look past its downside, on sale it easily clears the 1$/Hour mark and will give you 10-15 hours of a special game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Great aesthetic. There a lot of smaller mechanics that some people will find either interesting or tedious, such as the fact that it is a point and click game that requires some thinking and tedium, the minigames, managing composure, and the AP system affecting both combat and out of combat actions. At least with the minigames, you can tune them down in the options. The game also feels quite imbalanced with some of the encounter difficulties and certain abilities being completely overshadowed by others. The biggest issue is that if you run into a tough fight and did not prioritize certain abilities, the fight can be very difficult and potentially unbeatable for more casual players without restarting the chapter to skill differently. It takes some figuring out but once you fully unlock all the abilities, it is easier to figure out a working strategy. If you but I don't feel it takes away from the experience. Overall, it's not perfect but still very playable and enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, love the art style especially the character portraits which reminded me of Disco Elysium. Sharing Action Points between combat and performing actions within the locations with the increasing threat level from ending your turn forces you to make the most of your AP and be cautious or risk entering a fight with no AP putting you on the back foot. Mini games for hacking, lock picking and feats of strength are nothing unique but implemented well and why reinvent the wheel.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR in case you don't want to watch the video:1. This is no ordinary point & click adventure; there are turn based combat, stealth, and RPG mechanics layered on top of the usual point and click style of gameplay.2. The turn based stuff is pretty straight forward, and nothing really new - but when put together with the somewhat dated 'P&C' format, it made the experience a lot less frustrating and a lot more fun.3. Storytelling, writing, and voice acting are great - and while there may not be a ton of branching choices, there are a few choices that really matter. The world is also immersive, and many details about the character backgrounds and world setting, are also told through the environment and intertwined with the clues you need to solve puzzles and progress in your heists, which makes the process feel intuitive.4. Individually, the elements don't look like much - and there are some slightly annoying UI issues - but it is the sum of its parts that make Sunday Gold a fresh and enjoyable experience.I would recommend this to fans of point and click adventures, as well as turn based lovers who enjoy a good story.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Those fights are SO BORING. I hate everything about the fights. Random encounters, that stupid animations, those "hard" fights that lasts for hours without being hard.... Buggy music, no option to disable audio or animations in game. It could've been an entertaining game without those fights. They make you dizzy, too... Ugh!
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! At first it seems to be so easy but than you notice the strategic elements and that it can be really important at what moment you save or how you distribute the skillpoints. There are so many levels to it. And the art style is just marvellous, the colours, the weird faces and movements. Such a cool game!Thank you and I am really looking forward to see more like this in the future :)))
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches an itch I've had a long, long time.Despite its flaws, I had fun with this one. You feel like an adventurer. Your party isn't just all-combat or all-survival. Frustrated trying to solve a puzzle? Why not kill some guards to blow off steam. Want to use a help system? Go right ahead, but it might cost you in your next battle. Minigames can be hard or easy depending on how many combat-oriented stats you're willing to sacrifice for adventuring skill points.The art style was minimalist yet spot-on. The artists went all-out using their constraints to make semi-still frames come to life, and you're constantly wondering if you're in the 2070's or all the way back to the 1970's.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed the game, felt a little short and had a few issues, but I'll elaborate.The game has some interesting ideas, everything is turn based, the combat and explorations with an action point pool governing everything. An idea that felt imperfectly handled. It was interesting, thinking about where to put my characters while they ended a turn to regain points. No idea if there were roaming patrols or not, hope so. But after a while it didn't feel it was adding much. You could always get more points, and combat became easy enough that the slight risk of triggering another fight didn't mean much. If anything I ended up trying to regain points during the fight to use later. Although, when you've just hit next turn to regain points, triggering combat which may, easily reduce your action points, it feels it clashes a little.There is a composure system, which intrigued me, but felt underutilised. It appears almost like a clock, the characters lose composure when things are going wrong, like the guards discovering them, or a grisly scene. But you get enough items to medicate it away normally, there aren't many situations that really give it in large quantities. No enemies apart from bosses which impact it in a meaningful way. Making it so easy to avoid, it loses its use for tension. The final boss, has an ability however to instantly set your composure to zero for a couple turns, before it goes back up. Which might have been interesting, except the simple solution was just to defend till it went away, making it, again, not very impactful.I did enjoy the puzzles, the point and click exploring aspect felt pretty good, and the minigames were fun enough. The damage types and so on of the combat felt good, the characters felt distinct and likeable, lots of good in there. Lacked polish though. For example, an item I found to, boost my lockpicking pushed it above the highest limit, which seems to have effectively set my lockpicking back to 1 while wearing it, had a conversation or two where their lines didn't play correctly, out of order. Little things that slipped through the cracks, nothing gamebreaking though.Storywise, I'll try to avoid spoilers. The whole art style and world was interesting, if a little goofy as intended, but I can roll with its sense of humour. Reminds me of almost comic book style. There were a lot of little, links that were fun to find, overall found the story interesting. Only a couple of things that sort of nagged at me. There is a, resolution moment, sort of, with a character from your past which felt a bit weak, and the ending has... a twist. A silent ally whose motives, I think I understand but it's based almost purely on supposition. The ending felt, sudden and almost, unresolved. A lot of unanswered questions. My guess is this ally was, driven by something I didn't realise, guided by their history which is only hinted at. But that, motivation which made you their enemy, made them your ally in the end as they, sought to protect someone. But... again this is mostly blind guesswork done after the fact. In the moment it felt like it came out of nowhere to a degree that was, just confusing. I don't know whether I beat the boss too fast and they had more, dialogue to hint at something? I found the boss's power compared to my party to be so severe only the most, powerful if cheap strategy would work, which took them out in only so many attacks.All the same, I had fun, happy to support interesting ideas, not sure the best ones were, put to full use here though.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot better than I expected!The gameplay was nothing extraordinary. A typical point-and-click adventure with typical turn-based combat however the 'Composition' meter (more akin to a 'Sanity' meter) was a nice touch. Certain actions or attacks in combat would lower your composition to the point your character becomes a gibbering mess. It visually effects your UI inside and outside of combat and you're forced to complete your turns in combat in literal seconds or risk missing your turn, so you have to be quick on your feet!The games art-style really shines (Think Persona 5 mixed with Disco Elysium) and the voice acting which really sells the character chemistry is arguably the games biggest strength.Three nitpicks, firstly I HATE the hacking minigame. Oh my gosh do I LOATHE it. So much so that I dumped a bunch of skill points into 'Gavin' (The tech nerd of the group') just to circumvent ever having to attempt one of those awful puzzles and there are A LOT of them.Secondly, there should be an option to turn off battle-animations. As gorgeous as they are, any skill that you use beyond your basic attacks has an animation and it is tedious to have to watch them every time, especially for the longer fights that can go upwards of 30+ turns.Thirdly, the story was decent enough but without any spoilers, the final ending scene was soooo abrupt? Like they tried to cram a 10 minute conclusion about everything that happened in the game into 90 seconds which took a bit of shine off the experience as it just left a lot of unexplained questions you thought would be answered by the end!Overall I don't think there's enough in this game to escalate this to an all-time-great status but there was certainly enough there to warrant a 15 hour play through (And I'd happily play a sequel with this crew again!) Solid 7.5/10 for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: A cool mashup of adventure game and turn-based rpg with great art direction. Doesn't overstay it's welcome or pad things out. Short enough to finish in a weekend. Read reviews complaining about certain bosses taking too long to kill or full-healing, but that honestly happens once and should serve as a warning to change your strategy. Also, play around with the different abilities to figure out which ones are most effective or else you'll be doing chip damage. Don't let the whining reviewers put you off. It's only a $20 game and they clearly worked hard on it. We should encourage high-quality smaller games over bloated big budget games that pad their run time with fetch quests.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Stay away from this game. It looks charming at first and it might seem interesting... And it is. The exploration part of game, the graphic, music, dialogues. All is great. Problem is everything focused around combat. The games briefly and extremely quickly just spams you at the beggining with walls of text which are explaing the basics of the basics. That's it. After 2h of playing I soft-locked myself. Then I restarted the game and just add all into fighting skills. And I was trying to over use the Action Points mechanic. Seriosly, why AP are the same both for combat AND for exploration is beyond frustrating becuase sometimes you just end up in a loop-hole without PA. Especially in chapter 1. Some skills are seems to be extremely pointless [seriously? 4 turns to activate something? just why?] Just avoid. It's a shame as the game overall design is fantastic. But there were lots of bad choices around combat that just ruined the game. Especially NO DIFFICULTY BUTTON. And the game loves to punish gamer for lack of knowledge.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: I was and am pleasantly surprised on how much i enjoyed this little romp.In brief, on the rain soaked streets of future England some time in the future you and your tag tag trio go an adventure that looks more than a little like it was illustrated by the artist responsible of the design of the band GORRILAZ. Theres a lot to like.The game itself is almost like a combination of action point systems and a point and click during the exploration phase and a basic turn based rpg during the fight phase. There isent really a lot of room for experimentation in regards to character builds as each character has their class tree baked in and there really is a dominant strategy especially towards the end game.I enjoyed the journey and the britishness of it despite the fact that it appears the entire team that made the game were french which i find quietly disturbing....how do they know our secrets.My only real regret is that it feels like there could be about another 30 hours of game if they really wanted to/ had a bigger budget.get it at a slight discount if you dont want to pay full price but otherwise id say its worth it.8/10- " Shut up Gavin"
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend getting this game on sale.I think the game is about 15 hours of playtime.It's pretty difficult and the story and actors are very well done.Combat/Gameplay wise it's pretty unique but it can be pretty hard to beat from time to time!All in all I think the final boss is a big to much of a difficulty spike but I was still able to beat him in 2 tries.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Since the day I first played Dishonoured I always looked forward to seeing more of this oil painting styling in games and while devs at BKOM studios captured that impression successfully most times, they resorted to use primitive AI to animate characters' faces in certain occasions which resulted a lazily, badly done animation that drags players down into the depth of the uncanny valley. It all feels like a deliberate sabotage from that one techbro in the team and it's real unfortunate because the visual department nailed it in other parts.But enough about the looks, what about the gameplay department? Well, not ideal. They made a decision to tie both combat and out-of-combat gameplay by making most point and click actions cost action points forcing players to manage efficient use of their AP's or risk random encounters. This mechanic actively discourges players from exploring, getting straying from the set certain path and is a frustratingly bad design. Especially so because you don't get to have better weapons and enhancements to equip without consistently searching for them. A typical player may not realize this fact before facing the first boss which is the hardest in the whole game in my opinion, and at that point it may be too late for them. Fights come in the form of traditional JRPG turn based combat as you can see in the screenshots from the store page, which is a boring continuous loop of attack-heal-attack and it forces players to play defensively, skip a turn and charge characters' APs before ending the fight because of the reason specified above. Characters are very likeable, and arguably is equally interesting to the art direction part. They may be not the most fresh looking cast of chracters but their dialogues are well written, they get along with each other and most importantly, exceptionally well acted. Too bad they're wasted on a story that is so predictable and short. Game has your typical was that the end sort of abrupt ending so lower your expectations on the last chapter. You're bound to be disappointed.In general, for what it goes for on major sale(<$5) it is worth your time and money even if it's just to hear their banters.Is this game a hidden gem? It's more of a finely crafted fake acrylic gem that's pretty and cool looking enough to keep but has no actual value whatsoever. 6.5/10. Not a must play, but do pick up and try if you feel bored with your usual selections.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Taken from a perspective of a gamer who's not into point-and-click games much. I have to say, this game is a blast! Gritty graphics which underline the witty humour of the game blended with top notch voice acting which perfectly fits for the main characters. Only downside of this is story which sadly isn't anything special. Another great stuff about Sunday Gold are the RPG system, combat and turn/stamina mechanics, that gives new meaning and breath of fresh air to point-and-click games. Also you have plenty of weapons and gadgets to equip for your characters which gives different bonuses and could be said different play styles as well.At the end, I can't forget to mention puzzles...♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ how I hate puzzles. But somehow devs managed them to be done without fuzz, even for me...which is kinda miracle to be honest. And I salute them for it!So verdict is...Yeah, I recommend this game pretty much.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Game is  a little fun for most part with some interesting events. However for the price of the game and content, not worth it. I was expecting a little bit more of a feel for getting into the story and developing with each one. Not really, just kinda jump into it being criminals then goes down a basic employee revenge story where all enemies are identical.The investigation was a neat aspect, but combat seems more of a boring obstacle than anything else. You don't get any unique synergy with the characters, will repeat the same bland combat, and each character is very force handed that you just build it the way the game wants you to do. Style is amazing and that is the only thing the game has for it. I was expecting more difficult puzzles, wider options in combat. For how short this game is, it is just a money grab.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: The ambience reminds me a bit about the Shadowrun trilogy games. Wish someone would make more of those. You got a bit of futuristic cyberpunk theme, plotting your next job in the basement with your crew. Of course it is only some 3 missions, continuing on each other. And not in 2.5D isometric as Shadowruns.Instead, art style in Sunday Gold is very nice hand-drawn 2D comic style. Mostly based on still images, similar to traditional point-and-click gaming. Only you don't actually "move" around. Just jump from item in the scene to another.Some futuristic tech elements, along with old school knives and basic guns. Quite the macabre setting and depicting as some might have described it. Choices are not just about being nice and cuddly, but more realistic options for the crew as well. Game is a bit of a slow burn to start though.Music is fine. Story is nice, not too grandeur but more of a regular set of people. The strong female characters is actually strong and not making a number of it. The three main characters complement decently well the group and their strengths. Mostly likable and quite believable, strengths and weakness in person and skills.The combat gets a bit tedious after a while since it is quite basic and repeating. It is also annoying how enemies spawn all the time, and due to game mechanics getting action points requires you to rest all the time, causing more spawning, etc. Could use less of the chore, more focus on the interaction with the puzzles and items.There are minigames that are terrible at the start due to how hard it is to match the little pointers with fast moving elements and timeouts. Put 2 points to hacking skill tree and 3 to lockpick and strength to make it a much nicer experience and playable. Should have some setting to do this right away.It's a fine game as long as the price is not too high. Not too long to get overly tedious, even though changing some elements would make it more enjoyable. Mostly those are already discussed in all the other reviews too.. As usual, I pulled a walkthrough up to consult when stuck or wanting to check to not missing anything important. That helped.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Sunday Gold was a pretty rad game. It has a great aesthetic, interesting writing, decent puzzles and quality voice actors.Fairly standard turn based combat with an interesting panic system, minor adventure gaming where you spend the same resource as you use for in combat actions. The mini games for lock picking, hacking and strength are passable but not great.Overall I would be interested in a sequel that continues the story and has some minor quality of life updates.It took just under 12 hours to beat with almost 100% achievements (I could have gotten them all if that was super important to me, but probably won't replay to kill a few more enemies and do a quest differently)The final boss is a bit of a slog but that is to be expected for a JRPG fighting system.

You are no way to know the boss weakness type unless you fight him.Also for boss fight, if the boss weak to blunt and Sally is the only blunt type in your group, you're gonna have a hard time fighting since Sally is your tank/healer/taunter, but nothing beats bunch of bleed stacks lol.Second, the Art and VA. It's very well done, I'm having great time admiring the artstyle and UI cleverness, probably inspired by Persona 5, but I'm going to get hate for saying that.VA is amazing, plot is nothing special, very predictable but still enjoyable.my only nitpick for this game is the 3D models are not great, it's lowpoly and it's the art direction they are going for, but the model just look bad on Frank, while Sally and Gavin.It's a fun game, TLDR: art good, gameplay ok7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly thought Sunday Gold was fantastic. Three misfits are teaming up for a heist, but they are quickly getting involved in something bigger which plays out over the course of 3 acts.The voice acting is very well done and fits the characters perfectly, the soundtrack is great and the artstyle is very unique, and I mean that in the best sense of the word. It's a dirty, rough, almost menacing artstyle, perfectly fitting with the game's tone.The way the game plays is in turns; each turn, every character has a certain amount of AP they can use to undertake actions in the world, like opening doors or searching locations. Once your AP reach 0, you end the turn, which refills them, but also raises the alarm level by one and may start an encounter with enemies. In those encounters, which happen at the end of a turn or randomly after taking actions or entering rooms, you fight enemies in turn based battles - which are (mostly) fairly balanced and actually require quite a bit of strategy. All actions taking in battle also require AP; those are refilled in battle by guarding, so there is a kind of equilibrium between wanting to end battles by guarding so your AP remain high for overworld actions, but also launching strong attacks.Lastly I should mention the unique composure mechanic, which adds an additional layer of strategy. Characters can lose or gain composure after certain actions or through enemy / ally skills. The lower the composure, the faster you have to act in battle (you get a time limit) and certain actions also gain negative affects. Gavin especially has problems when getting low in composure, so he may randomly attack or berate your other teammates, but there are items / actions to help with that.The only small issue with the game are the boss battles. Bosses are huge damage sponges, especially in Act 1 and 2. In Act 3, however, I had a much easier time with the bosses, mostly because you got a strategy going and have very strong actions / equipment available. Because of this, I found the final boss(es) to be much easier than the first boss, for example. The battles require some strategy, so you can't just spam attacks, which I think some of the negative reviews don't take into account - and almost every skill in the game serves a purpose. The characters also level up after actions / battles, which gives points to put in skills / stats. Another small issue is that the game mostly only saves after taking turns, which can be annoying.Overall though, I think Sunday Gold is a fantastic and highly unique game that only drags a bit because of some lengthy battles, especially early on, but the overall story is short enough to never get boring, the battles are (mostly) strategic yet fair and the overall world vibe is very unique. A definite recommendation in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: A great idea of an elevated point and click adventure game meaning it has deeper gameplay than what you would expect from a game of this genre. The characters are kinda Guy Ritchiesque, the art direction is reminiscent of Disco Elysium slightly and I liked the whole dystopian UK setting with the weird brutal dog race activity or whatever that was, sadly they didn't really get into that part of the universe enough. Anyways the puzzles are decent and logical, some of the dialogue and interactions are funny and the game offers some variety in the approach towards combat. What this game lacks is content first and foremost, I think this game is in dire need of an expansion consisting of at least 2-3 additional chapters and a better ending because the one we've got here is so weirdly abrupt that at first I thought my game bugged out. The inclusion of a JRPG style combat was awesome and I thoroughly enjoyed it in the first chapter but it got very repetitive and needlessly drawn out afterwards due to boring sponge enemies. The bosses were alright but the rest of the combat was tedious at times and the challenge completely disappeared after the first chapter because I figured out what the best abilities were and I just leveled up my characters (unless you count trying not to fall asleep as a challenge). I think this game needs a bit more diversity in character builds, a couple more playable characters and bigger pool of enemies, because right now the combat, even though it is a great addition to this style of a game, it feels a tad bit superficial. Anyways, Sunday Gold feels and plays like a game which is a really nice idea but needs a little bit more work and content, more time in the oven as they say, so I think if the developers get enough support to work on a sequel, that could really turn out to be a unique and fun experience. Overall I am mixed about this game but still feeling positive and hopeful about what's to come from it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: An experimental blend of turn-based JRPG and point and click adventure. Sunday Gold is as its best when its systems intertwine to discourage typical adventure game habits of just clicking on everything until divine error forces the solution and encourages you to actually consider the environment before you commit to spending precious AP on a course of action. This unique style of adventure gaming is sandwiched between a wonderful visual style, likeable characters and serviceable but not outstanding combat to create a game that is experimental and original and I'd say gets more right than it doesn't with that experiment.The blend is not without problems, it's possible to get into loops of fights caused by exiting battles with low AP, whereas entering combat with low AP isn't anywhere near as much of a hinderance. The characters, while likeable, don't seem to have much personal stakes in the fairly predictable plot and the whole thing plays out with a lot of flash but you won't exactly be shocked by any twists. I like the characters, but the game struggles to get you *invested* in them, if that makes any sense.Still, I came away positive on my time with Sunday Gold and would very happily play a sequel that expands on the very evocative world or is more character driven. Experimental, but a successful experiment and one worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Game Gud, Get GameThis is a really groovy title. Like it's description says, it is a point-and-click, but with a comic book-esque artstyle and it's RPG base mechanics meld very well. I'm not sure how far in I'm in or how close to beating the game, but it has it's hooks in. The battle animations kind of remind me of Pokemon Stadium. There is basic equipment management, with new equipment, one-time-use items, and non-usable quest items being found during your point-and-click exploration. Challenging but fair puzzles are also present. The kicker; the unique aspect of this game is that there is an AP point system used in AND out of combat. On top of that, there is also a fear-type status bar (kind of like Darkest Dungeon, shown as a percentage 0-100) that make things fun/weird/creepy if it goes down, based on certain actions. I believe this to be different enough from other titles, and executed very well and worth a purchase. There is great writing, awesome English voive acting and dialog (almost all dialog is fully voiced), and streamlined fighting mechanics. I am glad I bought this game and would recommend the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others Video review: Rainy London serves as a backdrop to a dystopian future, where a trio of highly skilled criminals makes their streets a playground to put all their evil skills into practice. This is the premise of Sunday Gold, an RPG adventure title, with many puzzles and turn-based mechanics when it comes to combat.After an event that ended with the capture of one of the elements of the old trio, Sally and Frank, they find themselves without ideas and without money to approach the future. Here comes Gavin, the nerd on duty, with a clue that appears to be unattractive at first, but quickly proves to be quite peculiar and dangerous. Although they are a gang of thugs, the main characters have their convictions on the good side of the fence and this being a clue that promises to unravel the danger that is plaguing the city at the moment, they decide to join their forces even knowing little or nothing about this new team member. The mission will thus be to unravel the machiavellian plans of an evil megacorporation and the malevolent billionaire behind it.The adventure involves exploration and combat against enemies in a turn-based premise. Each action is necessarily associated with the use of "Action Points" which also automatically translates to combat against enemies. Each character has X number of "Action Points" at their disposal and it is possible to manage resources by spreading the actions among the different members. Although, for certain moments it is necessary to use the "key" character to complete the puzzle.Frank is the person responsible for opening places that are closed with a normal lock, as his finger dexterity is quite advanced and he treats each lock as if it were his friend. Sally, is living proof that muscles are not just for the eyes to see but to help in situations where strength is the real catchword. Finally, Gavin, the service mastermind who is capable of hacking everything that is electronic locks, or pc passwords. An interesting point is that each "special" action is associated with a specific minigame of the character. Get your brains ready because Frank's mini-games aren't sweet pears.There are key moments where combat against enemies is unavoidable, in a Boss Fight situation, which mainly follows the purpose of the story. The other moments of combat against enemies are mainly due to the need to change turns since you can no longer perform actions because you don't have "Action Points". In this sense, it is possible to pay attention to the "Alert Meter" present at the top of the screen.The confrontations themselves essentially translate into strategy mechanics where it is important to understand the different enemies that are faced. Each enemy has a weakness and an attack type it has protection against. In this sense, it is important either to change weapons that present the intended type of attack or to use the abilities related to that. While there isn't a huge repertoire of weapons, there are small nuances when it comes to the use of various weapons. Each character can only use one firearm and one weapon of melee damage and specific to her abilities. Although not very important, Frank is the only one who, for example, can use a heavier firearm, such as a shotgun or a riffle. On the other hand, Sally is unique in that she can use her fists to deliver punches that promise to deal a lot of damage.The RPG mechanics are translated into a skill tree, which, although not very extensive, makes it possible to define a skill plan for a better performance in your practice. As you would expect for each chapter completion, encounter against enemies or puzzle solving, a small percentage of experience is added to each character. I didn't find any efficient way to "grind" or in other words, to get more experience, nor did I feel the need to, except in a period of combat against Bosses that can become somewhat tedious.In a way, the combats against the enemies are the point that least interested me in the course of the action. Despite having an interesting graphic impact, I didn't feel great depth of mechanics, often ending up using only the most useful attack skills against enemies. It should be noted that there is a bar affecting the mental form that has a direct impact during periods of combat. Each character has 3 different levels of mental composure, and for each level less, it is possible to fall into a mental state of madness that will increase as the story progresses, or when faced with an enemy attack. To heal these less positive effects, it is necessary to either use skills or even certain items that allow you to regain composure. Also with the end of the chapter it is possible to recover all the negative states and of course, the life bar up to lost dateSunday Gold tells a somewhat interesting story, where each character presents exquisite voice acting, and interesting puzzles, but it owes some points to a somewhat monotonous combat mechanic and an "Action Points" system that can become tedious and that essentially lead to moments of some frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished I think I'm gonna settle on a review of 'I'd recommend it, but maybe on sale.'Sunday Gold is an odd game. Aesthetically it's a marvel - distinct graphics, strong soundtrack, and enough worldbuilding to get me sold on the setting. But as it is at the moment the gameplay itself feels oddly janky and takes away from that experience. There are some obnoxious bugs like the game not recording the time/date of save files properly, thus turning your list of saves into an unreadable mess. But for the most part the game still functions fine, with interesting enough puzzles and combat that doesn't overstay its welcome.Chapter 3, though, is where things really start to fall apart. Besides being a long dungeon with a lot of backtracking, it's here that things start to feel monotonous. You haven't gained any new skills for several levels, so combat becomes samey. There are only three exploration minigames and this is around the time they start getting old. The puzzles don't make sense and in one instance I had to resort to a video guide because I simply could not find a way to solve something. Most bizarre of all is . The rushed ending and lack of closure on several key points also leaves a bit of a sour taste in my mouth.That said, some initial issues have already been hotfixed, so it's possible that there'll be improvements on these points in the future. I don't regret my time playing Sunday Gold, but I do think the third act could use some real polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadowrunish world combined with Guy Ritchie. Super stylish, great voice acting, fun writing, and the turn-based combat gets very strategic by the first boss. Very much enjoying this!edit: Well, by chapter 3 I was kind of done with this. I love the art style, the character design, the voice acting, and the worldbuilding, but the game itself is just okay. The point-and-click adventure that uses the same AP currency that your combat uses is really interesting, but there's just not that many interesting choices to make. Extremely linear progression and even character builds don't really feel meaningful by the halfway mark.For me, the biggest sin is that the final battle just takes FOREVER and there's not really a lot of strategy to it nor is there a meaningful way to grind up for it to make it easier. The big bosses get 3 attacks each sometimes, you're whittling them down, healing and reviving, whittling, OOH BIG SURPRISE HE HEALED ALL THE WAY BACK UP, lather rinse repeat. I kind of zoned out, quit in the middle and watched the ending on youtube. The battle is a war of attrition in the most tedious way where if you screw up and wipe, you won't really have any alternate strats to try, you'll just be fighting the RNG and hopefully healing up a little smarter.This game is a flawed gem for me. I love about 80% of it and really disliked about 20% of it. I think it's a solid introduction to a REALLY cool world, I love the characters, I would be interested in a more balanced, more polished sequel for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I can already tell from the 20 minutes that I've played that the majority of the negative reviews I've read about this game are right. It's not that the game isn't fun, but it just feels wrong. It doesn't help that it doesn't run well (i.e crashing before the main menu screen the first time I launched it, constant stuttering, audio stuttering when clicking on stuff within the world). And it's a point and click game with really nothing to offer in terms of graphics. Sure, the art style is nice, but it isn't demanding to run. The combat isn't fun. Every enemy has a stupid amount of health, and if that reflects on the bosses that I've read about, count me out. The "Use AP when not fighting" mechanic is dumb and made me not want to investigate things because there's a chance that if you rest in the room where you just beat a group of enemies, they'll immediately respawn without you getting your AP back and then you'll just lose because you legit cannot fight without AP. The "paranoia" mechanic is broken. Your characters will lose confidence when doing absolutely nothing. Like, everything can go well, and they'll still have mental breakdowns. Some of the art (especially the character splash screens) look like it was made by the earliest generation of AI. When all your game has to offer is it's art and story, (because the combat is whack and exploration isn't really a huge thing with point and click games where you're just stuck in small rooms), it's a really weird choice to make your characters so fugly they're not pleasing to look at. It's really sad, because I love Point and click games as well as turn-based RPGS, so this should have been an easy win for someone like me. I also love the art style, but games are for fun, and if you're not having fun, why play it?
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique game that combines two genres that personally I've never seen done before. It combines point and click style adventure games (like Monkey Island) and JRPG and maybe even a bit of western RPGs. Its style and voice acting is amazing and invokes thoughts of Persona 3 in its battle system.Because of this, it is pretty mid in both genres and a bit awkward at times, but overall makes for a recommended playthrough, moreso if you're a fan of point and click adventure games than RPGs. It really is more like Monkey Island with RPG elements than the other way around.The game's puzzles and 100%'ing the achievements in this game are trivial to straightforward. It's a fairly short game and doesn't waste much of your time, which is why it's also recommended.The minigames get kind of old, even though they are fairly easy. There is also an accessibility option for them if you're having trouble. I wish they made the minigames more interesting, or at least made them all deductive ones like the hacking one. There are IMO weird places where there are realtime elements mixed in with what otherwise is a purely turn based game (e.g., composure panic).The weakest part of this game is its RPG elements and battle system. It's not horrible, but feels like they wanted to do a lot there and didn't really get it right. The battles as you'll find other reviews mention can be a grind. You'll find that you cannot wing some of them and have to reload and prep. You basically have to always keep your party healed (so much healing). Battles are more difficult in the beginning due to limited skills/items and get more exploitable in the end game. This is pretty common for games. E.g., frag grenade items seem to become incredibly OP with Gavin's abilities in the late game.Statuses/weakness/composure can mostly be ignored if you don't feel like diving into them. I pretty much just brute forced battle without much issue and didn't really bother to read status effects and weaknesses, which is why I think they tried to do a lot with this, but didn't work out. There are also way more abilities than you will need in the game. Some of them seem objectively better than others, or maybe I just didn't find the "correct/exploitable" use for the other ones. But then again there was no incentive/reason to do so.Composure is kind of silly in general and doesn't really do much except when forced upon you by the final boss. Otherwise there are usually plentiful healing items or infinite healing by just passing turns to gain AP to keep everybody's HP and comp healed. I do find it funny how Frank can motivate/appease himself.The AP system in the field is hit or miss. It's supposed to encourage you to plan, but you can just restore AP by ending your turn and maybe fighting an enemy that's generally pretty easy to kill anyways. The only time it might matter is when your party is split and you actually want to avoid fighting enemies. But it's also random/luck, so you can just save and reload. The same AP is used in the field and battle which also doesn't make much sense.I think this game suffers in challenge and diminishes the point of the AP system and minigames by letting you save everywhere/anywhere and reloading without any consequences. I don't think this was designed right. It should have only let you save at certain checkpoints or something.Storyline is mid, predictable. Lore is mid. Ending is sudden and a let down.But overall, just give it a playthrough, it won't change your life, but helps kill some time.

_childDocuments_.review: What a great lil game. It'll fun up about 15 hours or so, depending on how quickly you figure out some puzzles. The game is a big of a point and click adventure game, and turn based combat that uses action points that you can refresh by guarding, over any sort of mana system. You have your health points, action points and compose percentage, which can change depending on actions both in and out of combat. The lowest your composure, the harder combat can get, so watch out for it.The action points also carry over into exploration mode, where actions take up points, and only certain characters can do some actions, so it's good to try and finish a fight with high action points. If you run out of action points in exploration mode, you end your turn and risk getting into an encounter with some enemies. As turns pass, your suspicions guages can go up or down, with the higher it is meaning you're more likely to get into a fight. The style of the game was a big selling point for me. Very comic book-esque in how it deals with it's animation, which yes you could say does hide what might have been a restricted animation budget, but I think they pulled it off nicely. The vibe of the world is just spot on for a grungy future-dystopian London. The artists and character designers did a great job. It's nice to play a group of unlikely protagonists every once in a while. Frank, Sally and Gavin are rough around the edges, and I love them all the more for it; only bolstered up by some fantastic voice work. Gavin especially, was a highlight for me. And Sally's accent is just delightful. Get ready for some very heavy London accents and some slang. Living in the UK just made it all the more enjoyable, getting all the little jabs that someone from out of the country might miss,Combat is punchy, and the sounds design in it is great. I love the boss fight music especially. But battles (especially boss battles) can feel a tad slow paced, trying to whittle through armour, that sometimes feels like it regenerates too quickly and you can easily miss your windows for those big damage turns. Combat is where the animation might come across as cheaper feeling to some, but it didn't bother me at all. Overall, I recommend this to anyone that enjoys turn based combat games. I had fun with the characters and the narrative enough to do a second play through to get the achievements I missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: The levels are not fun. Once reaching your objective for the mission, there will be some arbitrary reason why you can't complete the objective, forcing you to go back through the level digging for whatever random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the game demands of you.On top of that, they made their characters intentionally hard to look at. Interesting art choice, I guess, but at the expense of ruining every dialogue scene between characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: While it lacks polish and the combat is kind of unbalanced, it does play with some interesting game mechanics, and the story and characters are well formed. I experienced an annoying save game bug, which gave all save games the same date, so they don't sort properly in the save game list, and even 'continue' just loads a random save. Other than that, I found the game enjoyable enough to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: A tight three-act adventure game with a super interesting take on integrating turn-based combat, a phenomenal aesthetic, some really cool setpiece moments, and a well-written and warmly acted trio of protagonists, all while unflinchingly wearing its budget production status on its sleeve. Do you miss when B-games used to (1) exist, and (2) be a little clunky in a charming way because they were actually doing something ambitious and unusual without the budget or dev time to nail the execution? Then you should play Sunday Gold.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: I agree with all the negatives (and the positives) below.I hit a brick wall because my characters are low hp and i keep losing the fights.When losing the fight i am sent back 2 rooms and I HAVE TO PICK UP EVERYTHING again, and to do the MINIGAMES again.I love the hacking, lockpicking is bugged and strength is mediocre.Artstyle, voice acting and music are 10/10.Basically i love everything about this game except ....the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to finish this game. Everything that the bad reviews here say I can see happening already. If chapter 3 is the worst then I'm definitely not interested. The minigames aren't fun - I'm sure the lockpicking one is glitched, because it fails when the blue rectangle is clearly in the right area sometimes. _childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: When I started playing it, I thought it could have been something more, even a second Disco Elysium, unfortunately it wasn't. There is a decent atmosphere, music and graphics. The combat seems cool, but from the middle it starts to get longer and longer, and less enjoyable and fascinating. The plot seems interesting, nothing special, but I was curious to see what would happen. Being honest, I have mixed feelings about this game, mainly because I gave it more than 10 hours (I even liked it), but at the end I got one of the most unsatisfying endings. A quick cutscene that is weird and opens the door to a sequel. Overall, I recommend giving it a try, but it is average at best.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. It combines really well the point and click aspect with the rpg combat with an interesting story and good characters and setting. Absolutely recommended. The bad part is that the ending is kind of abrupt and I wish it had some sort of epilogue to know what happened afterwards.I wish a sequel was in the works, but I don't see anything about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing authentic graphics style, good story and some interesting well-blend mechanics.Extremely recommended if you like puzzles, turn-based and/or management strategies.If you don't like any of these genres, the inventory and equipment management (which is a puzzle by itself) may be kind of annoying.Hope there will be a sequel game someday.

_childDocuments_.review: +Concept art (portraits, combat illustrations, character + env. art) is excellent+Characters and their missions are balanced+Puzzles and hacks are fun+ The story is original-Enemies have too much power compared to main characters-There is nothing surprising about the combats, once you memorize it, it becomes repetitive.-Lack of enemy variety, gets boring after a while
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game, plenty of style and atmosphere to go around! Combat works well, and the characters all bring something interesting to the table. _childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game! I'm always looking for unique games that I can play with a mouse, and this is such a unique blend of adventure and turn based strategy that I keep pushing other games aside and just playing this. _childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible! I'm confident if it had a bigger budget it would be a leader in its class. _childDocuments_.review: i love the characters , the voice acting , the freaking music ( i wish the OST is sold somewhere ) and the overall atmosphere is amazing.im really enoying it, so far lots of quirky weird characters and lovely locations. at the beginning i felt lots was introduced and was hard to digest everything at the same time but it grew on me in the end. the puzzles sometimes they get fun and sometimes they are nerv wrecking due to lack of game design clarity and guidance

_childDocuments_.review: I started Sunday Gold two nights ago. I've now got 15 hours in the game and have successfully beaten it and MAN what a ride. I love how much this runs like a TTRPG that you'd play with your friends with both combat elements and roleplaying elements. Sunday Gold is like a massive game of clue with turn-base, Persona-esque combat sprinkled in. The art style is like nothing I've seen before: it's a beautiful combination of comic-book art styles, backgrounds with vibrant colors and extreme detail, and 3D character models that just blend right into everything else. I am now patiently awaiting Sunday Gold DLC or even a sequel to get more of this. Truly fantastic work from the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I spent a lot of time with this game and had some fun with him, so I gave a thumbs up in appreciation for the developers, but I can't say that I really recommend this game. It's original, but at the end of the day, the battles are long and repetetive, take away the fun and just feel like a tedious task you need to finish to return to the game.So here's my pros and cons summary:Pros:- Interesting story- Excellent voice acting- The art style is kind on the eye in general- Longer than I thought it would be- Some puzzles are intelligent and challengingCons:- Annoying battles most of the time. _childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: It convinces with its interesting setting and artstyle, has an unusual mix of gameplay elements, but is not without issues. The combat gets very repetitive and enemies tend to be damage sponges. While it's a great idea to have actions cost AP to prevent you from mindlessly trying everything, there isn't much of a consequence ever for running out of said AP other than eventually having to fight, but that also grants you XP which is beneficial.There also is a tonal mismatch in the characters' behavior, dialogue and gameplay as the game cannot decide whether the protagonists are tough, cold blooded criminals or not and it becomes rather silly at certain points to see them be "mentally" affected as if harrassed by a horde of eldritch horrors even though they're actually doing pretty well, so that reduces the whole stress mechanic to a meaningless number you just have to keep high like a second health bar.At one point, the protagonists enter an  So some aspects of this game aren't all that well thought through, but it's still pretty fun and original, doesn't overstay its welcome and is overall worth your time if you want a point and click adventure spiced up with RPG mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Voice acting is good, game design and artwork are compelling. But the game mechanics are underwhelming. Puzzles become unfair in the later game and the fights feel very random. The final boss is painfully slow and boring. After which the ending is anything but satisfactory. Don't expect any surprises, neither for story nor gameplay. Do not recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Got it for $8 during the summer steam sale - this was worth every penny and then some. It's definitely *not* a $22 game, though.The artwork is great, the VA is pretty good (sometimes emphasis wasn't put when it was clearly indicated in the text), and the stoy is nice.However, the inventory system *sucks* - it is one of the worst parts of the game. The first act is amazing, the second act is good, and the third act is okay - the game just suddenly ends. No closure or anything, just beat the boss and the game's over. No closure on the rest of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Sunday Gold a lot, even if it had a lacking final act. Some people complained about the combat, but I liked it. There is an opportunity cost to optional actions you take in the world that will increase the chance of having more combat encounters. You can either choose to spend action points to get more loot to help you in combat, or breeze through levels to only play through mandatory encounters. The boss battles for the first two chapters felt great to beat.The last chapter felt weird, the writing and encounters felt much less coherent, and the ending was less than satisfying to say the least. There were so many loose ends you couldn't help but feel the story was condensed and was supposed to have another chapter, or at least better foreshadowing in the previous chapters. The last chapter left me thinking it was a step too far but also wishing there was more to the game. I would recommend getting it on sale. The art style and sound design is stellar, and it has some fun and novel elements worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: I am at the boss fight at the end of chapter 2 and I have no desire to continue past this point. The combat in this game is challenging but very fun with the notable exception of the boss fights. The game lets you know right off the bat that there are rules for the way combat works that are never broken throughout the first chapter until you get to the boss fight. the boss breaks these rules in a way that is completely unfair and unfun.  This repeats in chapter 2 as well, the entire chapter those rules are followed but they are again broken by the boss but even worse this time. My major criticism really comes down to a few very strange choices made by the devs in my opinion. The fact that AP mattes both in and out of combat makes is just annoying and doesn't add a sense of heightened precision that forces you to think about your actions like they wanted it to. instead its more of just a way for them o shoehorn in more combat, as without the RNG enemy spawning at the end of the turn system there would be maybe 3 fights per chapter lol. outside of these 2 major things though I would say the game is fine. The combat against non-bosses was pretty fun in my opinion and I really liked how you can give your characters skills upgrades so you can decide which attribute you want them to focus on. The loot system was great and whenever your character got equipped with more gear it felt great to see how much the extra time to loot payed off. I also really liked how in the point and click part of the game you were rewarded sometimes rather than punished for clicking on everything and anything because if you're anything like me your conscious will drive you insane if you miss even one loot item that would have made game play slightly easier. I haven't mentioned the art style yet but that is because there isn't much I can say about it that others haven't already covered. The style is beautiful being a very grimy futuristic version of the 1970's. The comic book style dialogue boxes also fit very well with the point and click adventure style game-play and I liked it a lot. Finally the voice acting was great. about 80ish percent of all dialog was voiced and it really helped with being able to immerse myself in the story and connect with the characters. Overall I would have to give it a 5/10 it was a pretty unique albeit slightly repetitive game that was completely ruined by a few unnecessary and bad game-play mechanics. I hope the devs make a sequel or another game in this style and refine it with the feedback that alot of people have shared because I believe the foundations for something truly special are there, but this one just aint it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Overall fun game. I am not good at puzzles so I used a guide but the story was interesting enough. The final boss fight can drag if you're ill-equipped. The main gripe everyone has is with the end of turn mechanic. All major actions in and out of combat cost action points(AP). The main way to refill them out of combat is by ending your turn. When you do that there is a chance you are forced into a fight so you can get stuck in a loop of needing AP to solve a puzzle but every time you end turn you get into a fight and aren't able to end it with high enough AP on your characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun. A bit of a different take on the mechanics what's mostly a Point & Click adventure with turn-based combat because the Action Points being limited for each "turn" + risk of combat you may or may not want as a cost of ending your turns does inject some strategy and weigh against the instinct to click and collect everything you possibly can. The art is lovely. The battles are fun and at times challenging if you're unprepared or still learning the ropes. The characters are enjoyable. Entertaining enough story, though nothing revolutionary, and that's mostly for the best. It's just trying to be a pretty fun game, and in that, it succeeds.

_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing artwork, voice acting, banter and compelling characters. Overall a really fun turn-based rpg where you are forced to utilise each member's talents wisely to solve problems in order to pull of a heist.Lots of different ways you can approach to solving a task.The only downside is the hacking Gavin has to do throughout the game - really wish there was an option to skip it. Not being able to guess the correct combination with the symbols (especially when he's going through his phases of crazy) really impedes the progress of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. Such a fun hybrid of ideas and genres. It’s so colorful. It’s got this  vibe. Big characters with even bigger flaws. Eccentric evildoers. Everything feels larger-than-life. And who doesn’t love a good heist setting anyway, right?There’s some really smart ideas behind the gameplay design here too. It’s basically merging a turn-based combat game with a point-and-click one, essentially giving some weight to every click, both inside and outside of combat. Every action you take spends time, pushing the story forward -- giving the scenario a sense of momentum. That’s rare in genres that traditionally feel very rigid. Meanwhile, in Sunday Gold, you’re constantly pushing your luck by going deeper. Checking one more drawer. Taking one more jab at picking that lock. Even when you know the risk is a heightened security detail. But it gives the game some actual urgency and  implications to the choices you make and how you spend your time.Sunday Gold is exactly the kind of game I love. It’s inventive. It looks amazing. And it feels like a fleshed out challenge where choices matter and every step is a brain-bender.I can’t produce enough thumbs up for this one. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent mix of adventure and JRPG mechanics. The game is constantly moving between problem solving, battle, story, and mini-games so you never get board. Story is unique and well told. The characters have a playful dynamic between them where they act real, and give each other ♥♥♥♥, but you can still see why they would want to work with each other.The adventure elements are intuitive and the only time I needed to look up an answer was because I opened a safe and forgot to loot it (a battle popped up and I forgot about searching the safe afterwards.)
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: 7 hours in I find the game great despite some minor problems.I like the exploration very much, and I love the fights, but the mechanics could be a bit more transparent, and the only boss I fought so far could be less of a bullet sponge. I think both parts fit each other and provide some necessary changes of pace.I love the setting a lot, And I love the characters (happens rarely), I love the voice acting sooooo much.To sum up: What a great twist on a point and click formula! I hope more people learn about this game and love it and that it leads to more corageous experiments in the somehow stale genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Sunday Gold

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a decent gameThe puzzles either line up nicely, or require a key item that doesn't seem to have much related to the puzzle at all.Action point system works out alright outside of combat, sometimes forces combat between turns which would be nice if the combat didn't get repetitive at times.Some reviews say the combat is difficult, it's not it just drags out the turns longer because you're spending at least 1/3 of the time healing with Heal Tank Sally and the other turns guarding for more APWhich also doesn't help when the AP after the battle is set to what you ended the battle with, so you may not be able to do much before you next end your turn, in turn potentially starting another battle (use adrenaline to avoid this).Story is alright, but lacks a satisfactory endingstill a decent game for it's drawbacks
