_childDocuments_.review: Some people will say that Octopath Traveler 2 is just like the first Octopath Traveler, but with a new coat of paint. Others will state that it is a vastly better experience.Both would be right.You don't need to have played the first Octopath Traveler to enjoy this game. But you need to like turn-based J-RPGs with a lot of story, and old-school pixel-art.If you do happen to have played the first game, then let's go down memory lane a bit...My opinion of the first game is mixed. Octopath Traveler's whole concept is : 8 separate stories, each with one among 8 characters as their main and sole protagonist. What brought them together? Not much, just the need to travel in a group in a dangerous world. And in the end, maybe, if you were tenacious enough to go through some optional sidequests, quite a lot of farming, and a gauntlet of 9 bosses with no saving point, the reveal that they were all more or less part of a bigger picture.Intriguing, interesting even, with a refined combat system and a world open right from the get-go...but very flawed, to say the least, to the point that I was skeptical of this very concept. After all, one of the things I personally enjoy the most in J-RPGs is how the characters feel as a group, the interactions between them. So a whole game where such interactions are mostly implicit, where there are 8 main characters and no support character...I could understand the aim, to have all 8 characters be developped equally, to present something of an anthology of 8 stories, and I enjoyed it...to a point.I could never finished the first game. Ultimatly, I think this is because it is very, very, very formulaïc, and thus predictible. 8 characters, 8 stories, each divided in 4 Chapters, each one consisting of town exploration, dungeon, boss. Rinse and repeat. Same for the world, 8 regions, each with 3 areas of increasing difficulty, each area with 1 town. Rinse and repeat. 8 classes, 4 secret classes, each garded by 1 boss. Rinse and repeat. And I already spoke of the infamous true ending.So, I won't lie, I was still skeptical when I started Octopath Traveler 2. How could such a flawed concept be improved upon? Well, turns out, you need a lot of changes, some big, but others surprisingly small. What I really want to point out is that, this game is truly the same concept as the first : 8 separate stories, each with one among 8 characters as their main and sole protagonist, brought together only by the need to travel in a group in a dangerous world, with an ending tying everything together.But now, it truly works.Because the common ending isn't secret now. Because it is better foreshadowed. Because there are more interactions between the Travelers. Because the whole structure of the game is more organic, some stories have branching paths, more or less than 4 chapters, some chapters don't have any Boss, some have several...Because each character truly plays differently now.No, it's not a perfect game. But it is special, to me at least. Here is what I have to say about Team Asano, the developpers of this game : it takes a very special mix between confidence and self-reflexion to keep a heavily criticized concept and repeat it while also listening to the critiques and improving it to such a degree, especially since said improvements are mostly small, but decisive by their sheer quality and number.I couldn't finish Octopath Traveler, despite its qualities. I 100%ed Octopath Traveler 2, despite its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's a really good JRPG, one that sets a new benchmark for the genre. 10/10If you liked the first, you will LOVE this second entry. This game stays firmly in the mould set by the original game, but improves it in every way possible. If you just like JRPGs in general, you will also find this a treat, because it's best in class.Once again, you will follow 8 characters in their own personal quests, but this time, there is greater foreshadowing of the sinister forces at work behind the scene. Character arcs are more nuanced. Though the plots are straightforward and direct, each scene has plenty of emotional kick. It's a great triumph of using the JRPG as a medium for storytellingThe art design is also the same, but improved: gorgeous 2D sprites in a 3D layered world. There are plenty of refinements: camera angles zoom in at climatic moments, shifts and tilts add suspense. The OST is good and atmospheric.Leveling progress is more streamlined compared to the first. There isn't much grinding, if you take your time and enjoy the journey, bosses are manageable even with different party members. Sidequests are aplenty and breathe colour into your adventures.It's a beautiful game with a beautiful message: life is not just a journey, it's a journey best filled with companions.

You go there knowing full well that you will love the crystal clear waters, the beautiful weather and be forced to deal with the sub par food.This game has the BEST music ever! Graphics are fantastic as well. Where it falls short is the story yet again. Don't get me wrong, it is much better than Octopath 1 but that's like saying you got the deluxe meal package at the resort. It's still basic and feels rushed. If I took out the magnificent musical score that comes in at the exact right moment to save the day, most of these stories would be pretty difficult to slug through.There are no annoying characters this time around (looking at you H'annit) so that's a plus and the crossed path stories do add a bit more cohesion but I am still annoyed with the basic story telling.How can you put such masterpiece scores of music with such banal and overplayed plot points?Would I recommend this game?Yes, yes I would, but Square Enix, please oh please fix the writing. These games can contend with the likes of Chrono Trigger and Final Fantasy 6 if you do.All the other ingredients are just right

_childDocuments_.review: Octopath Traveller came out in 2018, and really set a new standard for 2.5D JRPGS. In a world where they are increasingly vanishing with more JRPGS choosing to go a different direction, its nice to have other games that still offer this way of a JRPG experience.On that, I'm happy to report that Octopath Traveller 2 not only is a great title, but it prefects what Octopath Traveller already set in stone, and knocks it out the park. Everything that was in the first game is here, and is just expanded upon, exactly what a sequel should do.The characters, are more fleshed out, I dont think I found a single character boring or dull this time around, and they all have extremely interesting interactions to boot. Voiced perfectly by every actor/actress. The art style and presentation has been taken up a notch, and while im biased because I have thing for this sort of visual style, you'd be hard pressed to find many better looking 2D JRPGS nowadays.And the music? Go listen to the soundtrack, just do it. Overall, this game got me through a tough time personally this year, and will forever hold a special place in my heart. I urge you all to at least try it.GOTY contender, for sure.

If Final Fantasy 7, 8, 9, 10 & 12 are  9/10, this game is a  6.5/10.Characters mostly go through their own stories alone and they don't have a ton interactions with other characters.You have to visit Taverns to switch out your characters, and you can't remove the character that you started the game with from your party.Like... Why?And the 8 characters' stories are all over the place.I miss epic RPGs, where a groups of characters grow together, help pull each other out of their own personal turmoils and put their lives on the line to save the world from corrupt, evil governments. When are we gonna get another one of those again?Music is ok, but the older Final Fantasy games had more memorable music too.I don't recommend this game at such a high price. I got it 50% off and it still seems like too much. If I knew what I know now, I wouldn't have spent more than $20 on it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the original Octopath Traveller, you'll be head over heels for this entry in the series, as almost every element of the game play has been improved. It is quicker to list what hasn't changed first: mini-map is still a radar; you get 5 strikes for reputation in each town but no obvious indicator of it's level when you re-enter a town; the camera angle is fixed making it hard to find entrances to certain paths; the deity pantheon is still the same.Improvements: improved weapon selection, plus the weapon artwork changes to represent the equipped weapon when striking.more hidden entrances - dungeons & shrines might have an entry point that is not directly visible, requiring you to explore more.bodies of water (streams & open sea) - allow for more aquatic enemies and more complex paths to reach selected  locations.day/night cycle (~8 minutes between changes) - influences monster selection, which path action a character performs (they have 2 each) and which NPCs are available and where they are in some cases. Job skill sets have been re-vamped, some more than others; each hero can unlock 2 unique skills for their job ; up to 3 heroes may now have the same secondary job. Advanced jobs have been changed - 4 new skill sets, however not every one requires a drawn out boss fight to acquire it - first one can be stumbled upon in the first few hours if you select the right start location (east continent).Some path actions have been improved: captured monsters can become food, dancer & merchant hirelings can provide extra assistance. the warrior can learn extra skills from duels.Stories are now more diverse - it is no longer visit 4 dungeons in sequence and defeat the boss therein. Stories can have more than one route; some chapters will require both path actions to progress the story with the merchant's story requiring you to spend sizeable amounts of money.The only story I felt no connection with was the Dancer (Agnea) - wanting to be a star.
_childDocuments_.name: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts pretty slow, but it definitely picks up. Most of the characters are pretty interesting and bring something new to the combat to spice it up.Speaking of combat, it's pretty fun. It took me probably around 5 hours of playing to grasp the way combat flows and understanding the BP and breaking system. As you play through the game, combat only gets smoother as you get more characters and unlock the different secondary jobs. It has very impressive visuals and the music is absolutely stellar. Exploration is interesting, and I think they strike a decent balance between finding gear vs. consumables. My only complaint is about the writing/dialogue, which sometimes feels cringy or childish. If it were more mature and bit better in some instances, this would be a damn near perfect game. Overall a 9/10 game. I'm still playing through it, but I can't see my opinion of it changing by the time I complete it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is possibly the best JRPG I have played since Chrono Trigger. It all comes together so well that honestly it overshadows most JRPGs these days.

_childDocuments_.review: Octopath Traveler 2 is a stunning world of beauty, art, and sound. The music coupled with the dialog meshes so well you feel like you're watching an anime protagonist go toe to toe with their arch nemesis. Some of the story lines are extremely well written too. I particularly enjoyed Throne's with several "OH S***" moments. Some storylines were more straightforward like Hikari's and Partitio's, but they were very entertaining nonetheless. Personally I felt like Castii's story was the worst out of the 8 characters.Where this game really shines is the boss battles. It's a symphonic combination of strategy, art, music, and cooperation with your 4 chosen travelers. Some fights had me barely getting by, holding my breath as another massive attack was unleashed from the boss. You get the hang of combat after some trial and error, but I was happy with the overall difficulty. Only gripe I had was with the consumable item menu in combat. Over time, you gain SO many items, and many are extremely useful, meaning the difference between winning and losing difficult fights. This menu took forever to slowly scroll through in combat. So if i had to change one thing, it'd be this.Overall, if you like turn-based RPGs, I HIGHLY recommend checking this one out! P. S. : Partitio's theme song absolutely slaps, I put it on my workout playlist!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing JRPGs for over 20 years, and Octopath Traveler 2 is one of the finest that I've played. It is on the lengthier side of things, with it likely taking players 60 hours or more to 100% the game's story content, but I feel like my time was well spent.Mechanically, Octopath 2 carries over the already tried and true battle and customization systems from the first game, and then improves on them, adding new features and abilities that make each character worth using and ensuring that no character truly feels like another in battle.The individual character stories from the first game are back, but come along with more engaging writing, more memorable side characters, and a much better job at threading our eight protagonists together from a greater overarching plot. And there is a larger plot at play throughout the game. It makes its presence known very early on, without detracting from the individual character stories. Story and character elements are seeded throughout the game that end up having satisfying payoff. There are also opportunities for real, meaningful character interaction between our eight party members, which was completely lacking from the first game. It's not perfect here in Octopath 2, the eight travelers still don't have any impact on each other's stories outside of battle, but there are new stories to play through that see our heroes getting up to some stuff together, as well as all eight coming together for the game's overarching plot.In short, Octopath Traveler 2 takes everything from the already good first game and improves upon it all to make a truly great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Octopath Traveler 2 is a masterpiece that will leave you breathless, with its beautiful graphics, immersive storyline, and unforgettable characters. From the very first moments of the game, you will be swept away by the stunning visuals that are both nostalgic and fresh, with its retro-style graphics that feel both classic and modern.The game's narrative is equally captivating, as it takes you on a journey through the lives of eight unique characters, each with their own motivations, struggles, and triumphs. From the stoic and determined warrior, to the cunning and resourceful thief, to the compassionate and selfless healer, each character is expertly crafted and beautifully realized.But what truly sets Octopath Traveler 2 apart is its emotional depth. The game tackles complex themes such as love, loss, sacrifice, and redemption with an honesty and vulnerability that is truly rare in video games. As you travel through the world of Osterra, you will witness the characters' struggles and triumphs, feel their joys and sorrows, and experience their growth and transformation.The game's music is also a highlight, with its sweeping orchestral score that perfectly captures the epic scope of the adventure, as well as the intimate moments of the characters' lives. Whether you're battling a fierce boss or simply exploring a beautiful landscape, the music will draw you in and keep you engaged.In short, Octopath Traveler 2 is a tour de force that is not to be missed. It will take you on a journey through a rich and vibrant world, introduce you to unforgettable characters, and leave you with a profound sense of awe and wonder. Whether you're a longtime fan of JRPGs or simply looking for an immersive and emotional gaming experience, Octopath Traveler 2 is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh... yet another rage-quit from this franchise.  The devs seem hellbent on not learning anything from their sins.  "Recommended level: 45".  Head in with a level 70+ team... party wiped in two turns.  Sure, that sounds about right.  The problem with giving players "options" is that you need to make sure any of said "options" are viable ones.  When you have to double the recommended level to even have a chance of survival... just, why?  WTF is the point of this?  Is it that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard to actually, IDK, PLAYTEST a game for balance?  Some of the battles in this game are designed by people who are destined for hell, as only someone evil could devise them.  When the boss steals ALL of your magic, AND ALL of your BP, AND steals a character to fight on their behalf, ON TOP OF THEIR ATTACK... just, are you literally even playing a game at this point?  I'd strongly argue 'no'.It's just forcing an obscene amount of grind on people for little payoff; padding out the runtime with repetitive battles where the bosses are prone to one-shotting the party, and spamming attacks until you're down.  I'm not sure what people are twisted enough to misconstrue that as fun.And it sucks, because practically everything else about the game shines.  Too bad it's 'paywalled' behind pointless and often impossible battles that just make you feel like you wasted your time.  Is it too much to ask for a Story Mode for those of us who want to play games, without devoting our existence to meaningless grind?  Grind can be okay... provided there is an actual payoff besides unlocking the next impossible battle that requires even more grind to survive.This is the kind of game that should be perfect for me, but the combat just ruins it completely by being so sadistic in difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Octopath Traveler 2 was overall a very good game, but it wasn't without it's draw backs that I personally just didn't care for.  First the good things.  This game is absolutely beautiful.  OT2 takes this "new" 2.5 HD pixel art to new heights and it somehow manages to look even better than the first Octopath game did.  Definitely the current best looking game using that art style.  The music is also a big winner here.  There are so many great and memorable tracks found in this game and honestly might overall be my favorite single thing about it.  The combat also continues to be great, adding some new mechanics from the first game.  The turned based fight mechanics also continue to be one of the best selling points of this series and I'm looking forward to seeing what they can do from here.  Voice acting was also top notch and I found it to be better than the first Octopath was as well.  Finally the bosses for the most part are very well done and some can be very challenging to defeat as well.  There was just so many memorable boss fights in this game and it throws a whole ton of them at you too (which is great!)Now the stuff I didn't care for.  The single worst thing about this game IMO was I found it a bit too grindy for my taste.  Could be that I was playing it wrong, but I did have to spend a lot more time than I wanted to just grinding out levels at certain points in this game.  However, having said that, it's was nowhere near as grindy as the first game was.  So good on them there I guess.  While the individual character stories were all very well written and good separately, I still feel like this series has a long way to go in making the entire adventure feel more cohesive.  I just felt like the stories were too disjointed and I still don't like how only the current "main" character has any part of them, while the entire rest of the party is no where to be found.  One of my biggest peeves of this series is still that you cannot change out party members whenever you want and can only do this from a town 'bar'.  You also cannot remove your initial character choice from the party until you finish their individual story.  I found there to be absolutely no reason to still restrict the player like this at all.  The funny thing is, (minor Spoiler here)  In the final chapter of the game you finally CAN change out party members (when out of combat) whenever you want!  Please just do this from the start in Octopath Traveler 3.... there's no reason to restrict this, it's just an annoyance.While I found that the middle third of the game started to drag and became a bit of a slog.  The final third of the game when you start going up against all the final bosses becomes very engaging and was a joy to play through.  Overall, cannot recommend this game enough.

The game is very similar to Octopath 1 but there are enough new things to keep it fresh, i played Octopath 1 about 2 years ago but if you played it more recently you might find it too similar. There is a decent amount of "endgame" content but no new game plus. Overall great game but don't expect anything drastically different than Octopath 1, if you liked that game you will enjoy this game too.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely repetitive gameplay and storytelling. No interaction between characters whatsoever. Forced to play through multiple low level areas because of story reasons even though your party is almost end-game level. Side quests are obtuse as F and basically take you from one corner of the world to the other bringing crepes to sick girls without any guidance. Everytime you enter a new town you're "forced" to check every NPC in both a day and night cycle for items instead of naturally getting them through the story or exploration. Square Enix miss the target entirely with these 2DHD games time after time. Soundtrack continues to be the only high point.
_childDocuments_.name: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the first game, the sequel is just as awesome. Combat is still very fun as breaking and exploiting the weaknesses of enemies still have that nice addictive loop. One problem that is present here like in the first game is difficulty. The game is by no means hard and I'm saying that as someone who is not very good at strategy games. It is easy to overlevel yourself as there is still no difficulty slider. I would love it if the the third installment of this franchise allows for you to delevel yourself like you can do in Xenoblade Chronicles as being too strong sometimes take away the atmosphere of a boss battle. It is best to play the game using all of the 8 travelers to make sure that difficulty is controlled. Plus you get to learn the deeper mechanics of each character if you routinely swap them. Aside from that, the game has better interconnectedness compared to the first game as characters do have actual interactions with each through certain chapters. This is much better than the character banter as you do get to see the characters share a moment together. Overall, the game is just phenomenal. I myself have yet to even conclude the game myself, but I totally recommend people to play it. 9/10.Edit: Finishing the game with 200+ hours clocking in, this truly is one of the most fun experiences I've had the pleasure to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Over 60 hours in and I'm not even half way...and that's fantastic. Worth the money and more. I'll wait till I finish the game before saying for sure but as of right now I'm almost willing to put it above FF7 (original) and that's my #1 JRPG of all time currently. I can't praise this game enough. I've literally never felt the urge to leave a review on anything, really, but this game deserves it if it means somebody happens to read this and it's exactly the push they need to buy the game. I promise you this is everything you want from a turn based JRPG and MORE! The character abilities and the freakn combat is so satisfying. Not to mention the several quality of life features like item optimization for characters or the whole team, as well as insta-selecting the character with the least amount of health when selecting a healing spell or item. I didn't even mention the art style yet which is crazy because oh my damn is it so great. A PIXEL GAME AT 120FPS IS SO OVERKILL IT ROCKS! And the landscapes, shadows, small details in every area/bulding/room/ship/cave/everything...THIS GAME IS AWESOME. Top 5 of all time for me for sure. Stop wasting your time thinking about it and just do it. It is so worth the money if you like turn based JRPGs. 100/10  Overkill, Break, Untouched, Victory! and yes Throne is a babe I must admit.

_childDocuments_.review: Review in short:"Astonishing visuals and a good combat system crippled by a massive ludo-narrative dissonance, story inconsistencies and issues with enemies scaling."Intro info on how I played:* Played on PC with controller* Played in japanese sub engPro:+ Astonishing visuals+ Really good OSTs+ Stories with adult themes accessible for a younger audience, although sometimes said themes are treated with too much naivety+ Really good voice acting+ Interesting combat mechanics+ Visible turn order and how it changes with certain actions+ Not all chapters are battle-related+ Good visual hints for secrets+ Party banters+ Side-stories with character pairs (although it's only a small amount)+ Fast travel from everywhere+ Day/Night mechanics+ Possibility to remap controlsCons:- Save game is possible only at save points- No difficulty selection- Too many random encounters- Description of companions or summons abilities is not available in battle, only their name- No Flee confirmation- Cannot change the party in battle or in the over-world, but only at taverns- No party interactions or reactions to certain actions (such as stealing)- No dialogues log- Too much redundancy and overlapping in characters' out-of-combat abilities- Cannot remove from the party the character chosen to start the game, making them always over-leveled as only characters on the field gain exp- Severe issues with the management of enemy levels in areas and story chapters; too much disparity throughout the game.- No character influence or even just presence in each others' story chapters, even when it would make sense. But at the same time, in party banters characters talk about events as if they were there.- Only the party banters of the currently deployed characters can be seen during a story chapter, all others will appear only in the journal after finishing the chapter- Cannot change or remove equipment of a character not deployed in the party- To progress all stories at the same time, farming is required; and mid-game farming is pretty hellishMiscellaneous:* Random encounters* Minimap only shows general direction of next areas* Characters level up only if alive and deployed at the end of a fight* Enemies HPs are not displayed, but their name changes depending on the percentage of HPs left* Based on , the game lasts roughly 60 to 100 hours depending on the completionism levelVote: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Octopath Traveler II tells us that we don't need to be a superstar in order to bring hope to people. If you can make even just one person smile, you've accomplished something incredible and they will be a ray of happiness to you in return.It conveys the idea that anyone can lose their way if they let their own pain taint their actions, and that it can be difficult to get out of that state of mind without a helping hand. Being patient with such a person in a time of need may blossom into a lifelong bond. Saving someone from their inner turmoils and giving them a chance to get back on their feet is a worthwhile endeavor.It urges us to seek our own path, for we can never be truly free when adhering to someone else's expectations unwillingly. Sometimes, if your words fall on deaf ears, the only option left is to remove that person from your life.It encourages us to be good to people, with no ulterior motive, and not to be insecure when challenged by misguided individuals who perform irrefutably malevolent deeds. If you let yourself be swayed by someone who acts with hatred, resentment or jealousy in their heart, you can quickly become just as lost as they are. It also reminds of the importance of patient critical thinking over immediate emotional response.It even manages to tackle the topic of technological advancement and the need for wealth redistribution as new things get invented that improve the efficiency of production. After all, if knowledge exists to be shared with all, dough shouldn't just be hoarded either.It is a tale about enjoying the simple pleasures of life, and spreading warmth and happiness around us.~ ~ ~This game is more than everything I had hoped for in a sequel to the first game. Much of  I had for that game also applies here, so I won't repeat all of the things Octopath Traveler II took from the first game that didn't need to be fixed, but let's dive into the ways in which it improves upon the original.Improvements to the skills make it so there are much more ways to break enemies, and classes have been rebalanced in a way that feels like they all complement each other even better than before. The new Latent Power and EX Skills also make each character have a stronger identity in combat, and there is now a way to equip the same sub-class onto more than one character if you want to.This series continues to have best-in-class music. As catchy as it is epic, as comforting as it is melancholic. Most of it is new, but a couple of melodies from the first game made a return in remixed fashion, striking a chord of nostalgia within me while strengthening the continuity of the series. It gave me the sentiment that these eight new travelers were experiencing emotions that the characters from the first game had also felt on their journey, despite having completely different stories. This is just one example of Team Asano's masterful understanding of emotion. Emotions are not unique; if it's a real emotion, then anyone can relate to it, because we are all human. Hearing those melodies again made me feel those intended emotions twice as strongly, as I thought of my past adventures in the continent of Orsterra as well as my current ones in Solistia.Something I love about this series is how much the story feels like it ties into the gameplay and vice versa, and they went above and beyond this time to give us some jaw-dropping moments with the path actions at the end of each story. They somehow even managed to weave in the new day/night cycle mechanic into the plot.The world is even more fun to explore due to the addition of boats and the way the map is less predictable to navigate. I think there are also more bosses to defeat, or at least they are spread out better. I still recommend equipping the Evasive Maneuvers scholar skill to reduce the encounter rate, making it just right as you explore. The chapters are also less formulaic this time around, making it so you don't know for sure what to expect from a given chapter. The post-game is much expanded as well, with some fully voiced side-quests that let you see what happened to some important characters in the story.The Japanese voice acting performances are absolutely fantastic and full of life. One day, I will play through the whole game again with the English voices, but I can't comment on those yet.The new cross paths really help tie everything together. And when I say everything ties together in the end, I mean it. Also, in the first game, a lot of the camaraderie between your party members came from your own imagination and roleplay. I'm glad that aspect is still present throughout the game, but there's a lot more jerky around the bone this time around, if you will. The final segment of the game made everyone feel even closer than I imagined my party in the first game to be, boosting the affection I have for these characters even more.As the end approached, I didn't want to say goodbye. I'm grateful for this warm feeling... thank you for traveling with me.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly my journey with this game has come to an end and it is something I have not been looking forward to at all. I bought this game day 1 and I do not regret it one bit. _childDocuments_.review: Octopath 1 was a game that was fun to finish but not to complete. The stories, characters and especially the music have  all stuck in my mind in a good way since beating the OG game: heck, with some mods to help smooth the process over, I even would say I quite enjoyed the post-game content and final boss. However, trying to achieve all the trophies was headache-inducing. There were so many missables that complicated the process, and there wasn't any easy way to track your progress with said trophies unless you used a spreadsheet. I eventually lost momentum, and decided to call it quits. Octopath II however was a blast to 100%! All the goals the game gives you - both in game and in the trophy list- are really fun to shoot for. Level grinding is much easier than in the original.  No missables when it comes to trophies/, which is fantastic.  And the post-game challenges, while tough at points, were also rewarding.Between that and the stories, characters and music between as good or better than the original.... yeah, I'd say that Octopath II easily surpasses the original for me!  I'd still easily recommend the original though, if you be curious, since I'd say it still holds up.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly infantile story-lines, characters, dialogue, and flavor banter, all juxtaposed with depression-inducingly heavy themes like poverty, genocide, kidnapping, implicit s3x-trafficking, and murder-gr00ming of children. Like honestly, who is this game for? Literal toddler-level threads like the dancer pep-talking a carnival-troupe's leader about the power of friendship and the huntress-girl prancing around doing her silly Luffy-skits about meat jerky are interspersed with stories about how the thief's adoptive parents abused her as a child and coerced her into slitting people's throats when she was six while telling her that they use the blood of their victims as sandwich-spread, I mean what the hell? The game is also rife with signs that the story-production was rushed, with tons of internal discontinuities, like at one point the thief runs into an enslaved woman in chains in the trafficking-dungeon of a rival thief guild, whom she leaves sitting in chains for no justifiable reason, only to find that the girl has been spirited away when she returns for her, and this never comes up again in the rest of the game. She literally left a trafficking victim to get trafficked, and the game just goes yeah this is not a loose thread we need to deal with she was just a prop for showing how goal-oriented and badass the thief is, and then 3 minutes later a banter dialogue pops up with the thief and the huntress discussing perfume as if nothing happened.The combat is also incredibly boring. Normal attacks do next to no damage, the vast majority of skills are complete ass, and the majority of overdrives, jobs and passive perks are completely devoid of creativity. Random encounters with par-leveled enemies take up to four turns before your party can even start doing proper damage due to the stupidly designed vulnerability-system, and boss-fights, while incredibly easy, are enormous slogs that can last for the better part of an hour due to the stupidly high HP-pools and vulnerability-recoveries. In conclusion, worst purchase I ever made, and I am counting Cyberpunk 2077 into that equation. 3/10, regret not applying for refund while I had the chance.

_childDocuments_.review: I remembered that day, when the game was revealed on that direct. I remembered listening to the music, recognizing it and quickly going through a potential list of game it could be. I wasn't expecting it to be Octopath 2, and ever since that day I was absolutely excited for itWhen the game is close to release, I thought I might have hyped myself too much. Worried that I may have set such an unreasonably high expectation that is going to be impossible to be met by the game. But in the end, I stayed up to midnight just so I can buy the game the second it was out.I'm happy to say that not only did this game met my high expectations, but it absolutely blew it out of the waterThe music, the gameplay, the story, the graphics, almost everything you can name is significantly better than it was in the original. Thought the original was really good but needed a bit more polishing in certain areas, This game delivers that in spades.Is it a perfect game? No, I personally think some of the stories could be better, Like Throne's for example, I thought the final chapter of her story is just utterly ridiculous and dragged down the rest of her story. But overall, it is a massive improvement over the original, and I definitely consider this as one of the best JRPGs I have ever playedIf the jump of quality from Octopath 1 to 2 is this big. I can't wait to see how masterful Octopath 3 would be
_childDocuments_.name: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II

_childDocuments_.review: It takes everything that was good on the first game and improves further on it as well as fixing a lot of the negatives of the old game. The story and the way the characters' stories weave together is much better than the first game, the stories still feel somewhat disconnected at first and it requires you to pay attention to them to see how they slowly connect but even just this is tons better than the first game which had great individual stories and then suddenly shoved another story that affected everyone somewhat at the very end. In OT2 you can see how the big story slowly forms in front of your eyes. There is one exception though, one of the travelers doesn't have a story connected with anything and they are literally just shoved into the big story because they chose the wrong traveling companions.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 9/29/2023: Circled back to this when I had more time. Still cool. Finished four stories so far so I still need to finish the game. I will say that 1) you'll obviously connect with some stories more than others (Agnea's was... okay lol) and 2) some character class combinations can really trivialize some fights (Partitio Arcanist in particular). Still HIGHLY recommend this game if you like story and turn-based RPGs. It is a gem in a year plagued with live services and endless games.---I never played Octopath 1, so I can't really compare. So far, I'm having a great time with the game. Yes, it's going to feel like an anthology more than one coherent story. The characters acknowledge each other via combat callouts, travel banter, and crosspaths (which are a great feature not present in OT1 apparently). For me, that's enough, but it might turn away others. Each of the stories feel for the most part compelling. Agnea's is always going to be a bit divisive since it's so lighthearted in nature. Combat and music are also great IMO.I'll update more and add more detail as I play through the game, or finish it. For now, with 30+ hours at what feels like a halfway point, I think this is worthy of the price tag if you're into the old school turn-based RPG's and/or compelling short stories.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first game back when it was released on Nintendo Switch. And I was pretty much bored after around 10 hours of gameplay. Not with this one though. Where the first part had a bunch of uninteresting unconnected and mostly boring stories,  the 2nd game has deep and heart-warming stories that are rich and well written.  And yes: the stories are intertwined with each another, in  despite of what people are writing here. The battle system is pretty much the same as in the first game as far as I can tell but with more variety and tactical depth to it as you can get your second career skills much earlier in the game. Also, I love the soundtrack which will be added to my playlist ones it has been released.

_childDocuments_.review: The first Octopath Traveler was a masterpiece.  I have no idea how they have exceeded it in every way.  Do you like Chrono Trigger and Final Fantasy 6?  Well, here is your new crack addiction.  I've never seen a retro, traditional turn-based RPG with such depth and yet streamlined mechanics.  The production values of the scenery, music, and even camera movements are incredible.  The characters are all engaging, their individual stories are all bangers, and I am only bummed out that at 30 hours in I'm halfway done with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Octopath Traveler 2 feels like an extension of the first game, adding new story and content, while keeping the gameplay largely the same. I like Octopath's spin on the classical JRPG turn-based combat with the inclusion of weak points. Weak point greatly increase the strategic variety, particularly in tougher boss fights. Moreover, the secondary job system allows a wide variety of play styles. Overall, I liked the story, particularly towards the end, while the start of collecting all the travelers can be a bit slow. Also, while bosses stay interesting, the regular encounters definitely feel stale quite quickly

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most fulfilling games I have played. The storyline for some of the characters can be a bit redundant, uninteresting, or sometimes extremely cliche, but at once you reach that final fight with your 8 travelers, you can't help but feel like you are connected to them. Graphically, I wasn't expecting to love the 2.5D graphics as much as I did. It's whimsical, yet beautiful all at once, and adds its own bit of flair and uniqueness to an RPG model.Gameplay wise, the battle system is extremely fun. Methodical, and difficult at times, there are moments where you need to fall a few times before you understand what the best approach is for each boss. Different class set ups, techniques, abilities, and combos that can be woven together are always satisfying.The games audio/soundtrack is by far one of the best I have listened to in years. The song for each area is extremely beautiful, both day and night versions. Battle themes ramp up depending on the difficulty, and there is a great sense of energy when fighting bosses. I sometimes find myself listening to the title song on full volume before even entering the game. All in all, Octopath Traveler 2 is a wonderful game, and I am grateful that I got the chance to play it and go on the journey with these characters. A solid 8.5/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game. A lot of the shortcomings in the first game has been squashed or improved upon. Story is definitely a major improvement from the first game. Music is still as good as the first game but that is to be expected since its the same composer.  Much more voice acting this time round as well (Ochette best girl, Hikari best boy) Overall 9.5/10 for me.  Anyone looking to pick up a JRPG, this is definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II

_childDocuments_.review: If you like JRPGs and turn-based combat it is good. It is not super grindy. There is enough stuff to find around the map that it is fun to find stuff and not too much that it is a drag. There is a fun thing called travel banter that is fun. I do wish all eight characters could do it at any time even if they are not in your current party. If you don't like JRPGs and turn-based stuff though then I would say this is not the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II

_childDocuments_.review: Basically an improved version of the original Octopath Traveler.  Is it good? It's ok. The characters stories are better than the first game, but they still feel like a collection of side stories.  The lack of a main narrative tying everyone together still feels like a big miss.The combat is solid overall. The unique abilities for each character are a nice addition.  Still the combat overall can be a bit repetitive, and I used pretty much the same strategy the entire game.  Beef up Throne to do as much damage as possible, and let her explode everything after the rest of your party breaks their armor. The path actions and night and day cycle can also be a little tedious.  It feels weird to be able to steal from or knockout everyone in a town without repercussion.Overall, it's an ok game.  If there was a neutral rating I would give it that, but I'm rating it negative because there is no way this game should have an Overwhelmingly Positive rating as lacking as the story is.

_childDocuments_.review: If you add it all up there are 41 Chapters in this game. That's 8 individual stories and 4 duo stories and a final last story that ties everything together.Most of the stories are light hearted and there are a few darker stories.There is a very large enemy variety. The boss fights are very good.The music and the voice acting are very good.In terms of rating as far as new-gen RPGs, for me.. this one is up there with Chained echoes,  Xenoblade 3, and Tales of arise. Not quite Dragon Quest 11 Definitive edition but it is very close.

_childDocuments_.name: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II

_childDocuments_.review: Just an incredible experience. I previously had Octopath 1 in contention for favorite JRPG of all time (up there with Dragon Quest IX and XI, and Bravely Default 2) and Octopath 2 has blown the original out of the water. Everything from the character designs and voice acting, worldbuilding, overworld and enemy designs, and music culminates into a masterpiece and, as many have put it before me, "a love letter to classic JRPGs." Hell, I made it past the final boss with minimal grinding, as levels are not integral so long as you understand the ebb and flow of battle and the plethora of battle mechanics. If you enjoyed the previous title, play this game now. If you like JRPGs, play this game now. If you even *think* you might enjoy this game, play this game now.
_childDocuments_.name: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II

_childDocuments_.review: Octopath Traveler 2 masterfully builds upon the charm of the original, offering a beautifully crafted world filled with rich storytelling and engaging gameplay.  Each character’s journey is compelling, with intertwining stories that feel both personal and epic. The turn-based combat system remains satisfying, allowing for deep strategic play while maintaining a fast pace.  With its evocative music and thoughtful exploration of themes like redemption and destiny, Octopath Traveler 2 stands out as a captivating and immersive RPG. Octopath Traveler 2 improves on its predecessor by offering more cohesive storytelling, with deeper character interactions and intertwined narratives that enhance the sense of connection between the protagonists. However I would've loved to see character combine their skills like you can see in "Extra Battles" I do recognize that is probably the future game feature and thankful for the developers care put into the game.
_childDocuments_.name: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II

_childDocuments_.review:
This game is a brand-new entry in the OCTOPATH TRAVELER series, the first installment of which was initially released in 2018 and sold over 3 million copies worldwide. It takes the series’ HD-2D graphics, a fusion of retro pixel art and 3DCG, to even greater heights.
In the world of Solistia, eight new travelers venture forth into an exciting new era.
Where will you go? What will you do? Whose tale will you bring to life?
Every path is yours to take.
Embark on an adventure all your own.

1. Begin your adventure as one of eight new travelers, each with their own origins, motivations, and unique skills.

2. The series’ HD-2D graphics, a fusion of retro pixel art and 3DCG, have reached even greater heights.

3. The story takes place in Solistia, where diverse cultures thrive from east to west and the industries of the new era flourish. You can sail the seas and explore every corner of a world that changes from day to night.

4. Each traveler has a unique set of Path Actions they can use to battle townspeople, obtain items, take others along in their travels, and more. Where will you go? What will you do? Every path is yours to take.

5. Familiar mechanics from the original game have been preserved, like the freedom to develop your travelers’ jobs and skills, as well as the Break and Boost system that made battles so exhilarating. New mechanics have also been added.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: GORGEOUS artwork and noticeably more "likable" character subplots, but Mortal Kombat 11 is still active, its launch server issues got mostly fixed, its player count is aging a lot more gracefully, and there are a lot more things to do — still, I can't discount how much fun I had with this game's story and arcade ladders; pay only what you would if this game had no multiplayerBeautiful Backgrounds 1 is a game that's more fun to look at than to play, with spectacular stage artwork that in my opinion is the genre's gold standard.  The story, told in NetherRealm Studios' typical "cinematic" style across several chapters and playable characters, is probably the 'least' well written of those between Mortal Kombat 9 and now, but it's still pretty decent.  Despite this game marketing itself as a reboot, I wouldn't recommend its story to you if you are a series newcomer: everything that happens in the story, right down to most of the dialogue, feels like an alternate-history punch line that only makes sense if you not only grew up on the series but also played the PlayStation 2-era games because of this installment's unorthodox character-roster choices that reduce some of the most familiar faces to being Kameos if they appear at all.  "I'm ruler of Outworld!" is only going to have meaning for you if you know enough about thirty years' worth of stories to be able to say, "Wait, wrong realm."  That's a shame because the story — which contains quite a lot of remarkably poignant and inspiring development for a bunch of characters who used to be one-note personalities — is effectively now the game's only real selling point, as people are moving on to other games, or even back to Mortal Kombat 11, as I've done.I will say I liked the various characters' arcade-ladder endings a lot better than I generally did in the earlier 'modern timeline' installments, with far fewer needlessly depressing or bittersweet character endings.  Individual character tutorials took a huge step back and now just have a collection of flashy but impractically difficult combos to perform, instead of being a step-by-step description of a character's special moves and why each are important.  The lovely environments have a huge amount of concept art, but the characters' concept art, by comparison, is so limited that it makes the characters feel like background dressing in their own game.  Some characters' redesigns look much better artistically (Ashrah) than others do (Li Mei, despite her 'firework' aesthetic being inspired and complementing the festival setting very well).I eventually warmed to the game's Kameo system, which has a mostly separate roster of characters, each of whom has its own small selection of moves assigned to some combination of the Kameo button and an input direction.  The main use for this is extending combos, but in a game where the time-to-kill feels so short, consistently losing nearly half of your health because someone missed one block doesn't feel fun to play regardless of whether the burden falls on you or your opponent.  When Kitana in Mortal Kombat X was capable of removing 40% of her opponent's health bar without expending limited resources, this felt vaguely fair since she had fewer methods for circumventing an opponent's blocks than did other characters more suited for close-up combat.  Here, that level of damage is the norm, complete with a vastly increased emphasis on aerial combos, so instead of looking like exciting brawls, online ranked matches tend to be a game of "footsies," with both players being visibly scared to leave their characters vulnerable.I didn't dislike the controversial "Invasions" mode as much as a lot of people understandably did, since being able to explore the gorgeous environments helped remove most of the monotony for me.  Moving around node by node on a map that reminds me of "Hitman Go" is an intriguing concept, even as in practice it basically just feels like a nonlinear level select with seasonal boss fights, limited backtracking features, and an uninteresting ability to equip random-characteristic Relics and Talismans and assign stat points when you're usually just throwing everything into Attack power.  Invasion-mode characters having Pokémon-like elemental types, coupled with most fights generally having easy AI, means you're basically just meta-gaming which character's Element overpowers that of your opponent, which I vaguely preferred over previous games' high-difficulty Towers of Time throwing half a dozen environmental obstacles against you at once.  The bigger issue is that series staples such as end-of-match finishing moves are now locked behind excessively grindy experience bars, both for each of your playable characters and for their limited-use Kameo companions, most of whom don't tend to see practice in actual play.Massive spoiler for the very last level of the story, but this is too important not to mention.THIS IS THE COOLEST IDEA I'VE SEEN IN YEARS AND THE GAME DOES NOTHING WITH IT.  It's not in the rest of the story mode, the Arcade ladders, the few online modes, or the Invasions mode.Between the smaller character roster and no variation therein other than which Kameo you choose, pre-match decision-making feels very limited here.  Custom outfits are thankfully purely cosmetic and have none of Injustice 2's outsized balance issues (Mortal Kombat 11 split the difference by having these enhancements generally be single player-only), but most of the choices are color palettes, with far fewer true costume changes than in 11.  Character movesets can no longer be customized or split into variations from a menu.  Mortal Kombat 11 could have done a better job of explaining its custom variations and slowly integrating them into the story — this game, instead, often has you playing as characters who haven't discovered all of their tricks yet — but the depth was there and still feels rewarding and versatile to this day.  That's a problem when, here, many characters' play styles feel much more thought out than others, with several returning faces now having different stances to switch between during battle while some other characters have no such feature.  Johnny Cage even has a dedicated Hype meter that, when maxed out, vastly enhances his combo abilities.The game feels feature-stripped — no Mercies, Friendships, AI-vs-AI battles, or custom movesets — but I didn't hate the core mechanics despite battles feeling too short.  Many cosmetics and achievements are far too grindy, but the core mechanics felt solid even if poorly balanced.  But if this game ever gets a background-art book, just buy that instead, and you'd still have money left over to buy 11 Ultimate.

OVERALL:I feel like this game was made as a cash grab. It fails in comparison to all the details and work put into to 9, X, and 11. It feels rushed, the one player modes are not fun at all (I had more fun in the last 2 Krypts than i have in Invasion mode). The fatalities look kiddish and lack detail (no gore, just 3d model chunks breaking off with red ooze). I feel like they could have better spent their budgets and made more money back from expanding on 11 instead of rushing out this p.o.s. , this is a NO BUY FROM ME. - Disappointed MK Fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I would only recommend this game at full price if you enjoy the Mortal Kombat Franchise and fighting games in general.The offering outside of the competitive gameplay is barebones. Invasion and Tower mode add nothing really interesting in terms of single player content vs what they've released in the past.In terms of online modes - you still can't go into training mode while queued for matchmaking. Matchmaking is still barebones menu system. Netherrealm Studios could learn a lot from Arksys and Capcom in terms of Lobby systems and creating an environment where it's fun to play and keep playing against randoms online.All in all, I'd give this game a 6/10 for people who ARENT fighting game fans. but a 8 or 9/10 if you are.

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing to mention is that on PC this game currently is broken. There is a major problem with optimization, and everyone despite what system they have, have stutters and lag spikes all over the place. Developers already admitted the problem but how do you release a game for almost a 100$ that is completely broken. Didn’t you test it once on PC? Once again, we got bad PC port with 30 fps locks and in almost unplayable state. We received a patch before release now and NOTHING changed. I have 3090ti and core i9 12900k, and I still have fps drops and stutters in gameplay.For the second, this game feels like a downgrade from mk 11 in a lot of ways:1.	The ui, the menu etc, have very simple design and limited amount of information.2.	We have no crypt here, and for what reason? In mk 11 it was like another game inside it, and I really enjoyed it. To calm down a little and explore. We just have a simplified randomizer now for gold. So, you did less job with less content in the game but still charge the same price?3.	We lost a lot of customization. We have no variations and custom abilities now, like in mk 9. Characters have less customizable parts, only one item for each. That goes for other things too. It just feels like too simple and bland after mk 11.4.	The fighting system is broken with “new” cameo mechanic, which is just a 2x2 version like in mk 9. The real new part is that now every hero is like Cyrax back in the days with 50+ percent combos in game where braker costs THREE bars, and they don’t regenerate like in mk 11.5.	I can’t say much about story, I guess its fine but from the other part the same thing again, same villains, motivation and so on.So, we got a new game, with MUCH less content, less customization, simpler design in every way, broken fighting experience (even if you like it, the mechanic is old, nothing special here in cameos.), and most importantly, completely broken PC port which was not tested properly.Everything here feels like a rushed cash grab and I regret spending money on this.

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying that I am a life-long fan of MK, been playing since MK3, and have always supported the franchise. MK is in my blood (hehe).This game has an immense diamond-in-the-raw potential and I am (hoping) sure some of what I will describe below will be fixed down the road.The good:• The art style and design direction is insanely strong. Everything that you see in the game, from stages to character backstories to the smallest design choices, have an actual in-lore meaning and this is amazing. This goes for character design as well, it is very intentional and consistent.• The music. FINALLY I am able to praise the music in the mortal kombat game for the 1st time since I'd say MK:D. The Forge theme is a total throwback to MKII soundtrack and I am in love with it.• The roster. I know this is subjective but I am the biggest fan of almost every character in the base roster and I couldn't have asked for more.• Animations. The throws, the small slow-mo's, the cut-scenes, everything just oozes BEEF. Every hit is very impactful.• The invasions mode. This is a wobbly one, but I really do believe it has a potential. I like the introduction of the elemental chart purely cause it makes me fight as different characters that I usually wouldn't have selected and it makes the process a bit less stale and more fun, i.e. if given a chance, I would just fight 20 fights as Smoke and burn out, but the fact that I need to alter between 3-5 different ones depending on a fight helps keeping things interesting.The bad:• No intro dialogues on towers and invasion mode fights. I know that this is a beaten horse and one of the most common complaints, but there is a reason for this. I don't know whose idea this was, but this is a massive step back from the character/relationship development and simple pure fun from MK11 and simply a let down. I understand that with the current way the intro dialogues work (i.e. clash instead of a loading screen) this might be hard to implement, but I am sure that there are tons of great minds behind the dev team who can figure out how to use the dialogue intros in simple fights. PLEASE make this happen, you have no idea how much this adds and (in case you like that they are absent) how easy it is to skip them.• INSANE loading times on PC. Every. Single. Action. you take will either take you to a black screen aka Liu Kang's black hole of eternal wait or keep you staring at a beautiful background of a menu. Going into customization - wait. Every fight in invasions - wait. Go from any menu option to any menu option - WAIT a whole minute hachiko-style. I spent more time staring at Malevich's black square than kicking butts and this is very upsetting.• (this might be my own issue but I have to voice it) Terrible and very selective stutters in fights. Some stages, like Johnny Cage's mansion, run smooth like butter while doing a fatality at another stage will send you into a stutter fest. I cannot figure out what is the basis for these, cause I am running the game on a pretty decent PC that meets all requirements, but still end up with atrocious performance issues at some very selective moments.The ugly (aka bugs and complaints):• Terms agreement consent request appears EVERY SINGLE TIME I end up on a menu screen. I said yes to it more times than Jim Carrey in the movie "Yes Man".• Every time you come to a tower in the invasions mode the screen blurs making you feel like Peter Parker who forgot to take off his glasses.• Reptile face giggles in victory stances. I know his fingers twitch in the customization stance but I am sure his face looking tormented is not deliberate.• "New" notifications for customizations/kollection even though I already checked everything new. The bullets next to the options never go away, even if I have nothing new to check.• In the invasions mode character select/upgrade menu, you press X to bring up the elemental chart, but pressing O will take you out of the entire menu, and you know what that means - ONE WHOLE MINUTE OF A BLACK SCREEN. Pressing back should just close the chart, not the entire menu.• In store you cannot rotate characters to check out the outfits/gear you're about to buy. Why? It's exactly the same UI as in the customization mode, and you should be able to check out the item before buying it, but you can't cause you simply can't rotate the character. Same goes for the gear in the store.• You cannot see several characters' gear when you select it for buying in the store. What I mean is - they take a specific stance that makes it impossible to see their gear. Kitana has her fans closed in her stance, so how can you see what fans look like when buying them?! Same goes for Li Mei, as she has her hands behind her back, and khem-khem, you cannot rotate her to even attempt to see what they look like.• No map in invasions. This is insanely frustrating, especially beginning from the 1st real map in this mode that is quite expanded. I got towards the end of the map when I received Madam Bo's key, but how am I even supposed to remember where was that locked pathway when I already went through 60 fights and pathways?! I know I come from the time when we had to write down moves and notes in a notebook but do I really have to scribble that 47th turn left next to a bush leading to a shed is where I need to use Madam Bo's key? *Sigh*...• High quality textures are locked unless you have a high-end graphics card as I understood. I don't believe this is necessary. Even if I have a potato PC, I should still be able to try out every configuration to figure out the most optimal, and sometimes that combination may very well be "high quality textures & low/medium complimentary settings". And even if I cannot for the life of me run high textures in MK1, I will just try it, get 5 FPS and change it to low myself.• Last but totally not least - no combo/move highlighting in fights. Another essential and technically a very innocent feature that didn't get implemented for God knows what reason. I don't even need to explain why this is important.All in all, as I said - this game is oozing a very vibrant and strong character and atmosphere, the gameplay is fun and refreshing, the art direction and character designs are amazing, but it is full to the brim with these constant frustrations and technical issues and it just feels like you are being punished for something at all times with never ending loading screens of black doom and missing features. MK1 just feels like a very expensive and potentially delicious cake, perhaps the most delicious cake in the MK bakery yet, albeit severely underbaked. It is enjoyable but you will frequently find yourself choking and reconsidering eating it.I am giving this a negative review only because I have a feeling the bads and uglies will at some point outweigh the goods, unless they are mitigated. For now I will keep on playing.

_childDocuments_.review: As a hardcore MK fan I just have to comment on this.MK9 was the first 'competitive mk game' and also the best one. It had lots of issues when it came to balance, but it was the perfect start that just needed to be readjusted. Everything about the game is what u expected from an MK game, also the roster was incredible as were the fighting styles, the moves and combos made sense for the fighters and allowed you to be creative and had more ''expression'' than mk11 and mk1 as you could clearly see who put effort into the fighter to learn and do things that others that were not as good/creative simply could not. On top of that it was filled with content and like I said, its all you want. The tools for all fighters were also above average. Incredible game.MKX added even more player expression and creativity in the fighting styles, even too much you might argue because the core gameplay was rushdown 50/50s and armored launcher it is the scrubbiest game but oh boy was it fun! Now, MK11 stripped down all that creativity and setups that you could do in MK9 and MKX and made a very monotone boring gameplay, you could learn all the fighters in 10 min, not what u expect from MK because MK is supposed to be flashy and crazy. But............. MK11 had a ton of content at least, also its netcode was the best compared to the other MK's so far, but core gameplay fell short compared to MK9 and MKX imo.Now MK1? What can I say, theres is NO content, Invasion sucks, the pc port sucks, the netcode is a disgrace and the kameo system is just a lazy half assed mechanic that creates the illusion of it being ''in depth'' and allows ''player expression and creativity'' when in reality it does the exact OPPOSITE because most of the roster is so poorly designed because its designed with kameos in mind that need to make up for your ''fighters weakness'', if anything this is limiting more than ever. You see, the top tiers already are OP with the best kameos and the low tiers are barely playable with the best kameos. Most kameos arent even played because they add nothing. So the core gameplay is still like MK11 if not worse had there not been kameos? Because they are watered down design hoping that we use kameo to amp things up, lmao! Its funny because a lot of players are scared to approach when their kameo is on cooldown because theres nothing they can do without it without getting punished, laughable design.  When playing MK we want our fighters fully fleshed out and then we can play them in our own style because theres depth to it like I said above about MK9/MKX. But in this game everyone plays the same, everyone does the same because there is nothing else to it. Add this with all the issues I added above I Feel absolutely robbed/scammed however you wanna call it for spending 90 whole buckarinos on the premium edition. WHAT A JOKE!

_childDocuments_.review: A Bloody Good Time: Mortal Kombat 1 Revives the SeriesI'm thrilled to say that Mortal Kombat 1 has breathed new life into the series, offering a fresh and exciting take on the classic fighting game formula. As a fan of the series since its inception, I was skeptical about the reboot, but NetherRealm Studios has truly outdone themselves.The game's story mode is a masterclass in storytelling, expertly weaving together the complex narrative threads of the Mortal Kombat universe. The characters are well-developed, with nuanced personalities and motivations that add depth to the story. The cutscenes are stunning, with impressive visuals and voice acting that brings the characters to life.But it's not just the story that shines – the gameplay is also top-notch. The combat is fast-paced and brutal, with a focus on brutal finishing moves and a variety of combos that require skill and strategy to execute. The stages are also incredibly detailed, with interactive environments that add a new layer of depth to the fighting.One of the standout features of Mortal Kombat 1 is its roster of characters. The classic fighters are all back, along with some new additions that fit seamlessly into the series. The character designs are stunning, with intricate details and animations that bring each fighter to life.The game's graphics and sound design are also noteworthy. The visuals are stunning, with detailed environments and characters that look like they've been ripped straight from the pages of a comic book. The sound effects and music are equally impressive, with a pulsating soundtrack that perfectly captures the game's dark and gritty tone.Overall, I would highly recommend Mortal Kombat 1 to fans of the series and fighting games in general. It's a bloody good time, with a focus on storytelling, gameplay, and presentation that sets it apart from other games in the genre. If you're looking for a game that will keep you coming back for more, look no further than Mortal Kombat 1.

_childDocuments_.review: In its current state, I wouldn't exactly toss this game a bouquet of roses and recommend it for a grand night of gaming. Let's start with the good stuff, though - the graphics? Yeah, they're snazzy. The game runs like a well-oiled machine, and the music? it's the best groove we've felt since the Deadly Alliance era.But now, brace yourselves for the bad, and there's quite a laundry list. The single-player content, well, it's a bit of a joke. The story mode kicks off with some promise, but then it nosedives into the most absurd, asinine, recycled "writing" you'd swear was ripped straight from the newest Marvel movies. Invasion mode? it's like watching paint dry on a rainy day. Who in their right mind thought this was fun?Online play? Prepare for a lag-fest that'll make you wish you were back in the dial-up era. And as of my writing, there are no lobbies to be found. The place is crawling with toxic players who've apparently made a pact with the devil to spam the same three characters, throw in a dash of Cyrax, and unleash long, repetitive combos that'll make your eyes roll back in your head.In the end, it feels like NRS couldn't balance a game to save their lives. Nothing was confusing.  -  itself is pretty smooth, similar to MK11.  - Characters are   -  for some characters such as Liu Kang, Johnny Cage and Shang Tsung is really good  - Online is   - Decent amount of Here's what the game fails on, lots of things that MK11 did right but somehow went wrong in MK1:-  MK11 had 60fps menus and intros, whereas MK1 is locked at 30fps everywhere except fights (fatal blows are still 30fps, which causes stuttering going from 60fps to 30 in one combo). - . _childDocuments_.review: This is the most expensive video game I have ever purchased - and I am incredibly disappointed.Runs extremely badly on PC, as you can see from scrolling the reviews and discussions, a large portion of players are having issues with stuttering/dropped frames/freezing, etc.This kills a fighting game, needless to say. Good luck reacting to any mixups. Any overhead/low mixup character will have a f***ing field day with you.BTW, I've tried everything to fix it. Updated my drivers, adjusted some Windows 11 functionalities that could have caused issues, changed my display refresh rate to 60hz, and disabled my e-cores with Project Lasso. None of it has fixed the issue.Besides that, many players (including myself) are having continuous crashing and desyncs online.Even if the game is running as intended for you, it is still inexplicably locked to 30fps in everything but actual gameplay. Somehow, it nevertheless FAILS TO MAINTAIN a steady 30 in menus/cutscenes etc., it's a juddering mess. Maybe that sounds nitpicky, but you'll feel it. It wears on you, especially in Invasions mode.I personally cannot find a match under about 120-150 ping, whereas I played many low latency matches on MK11 - this leads me to believe that they have reduced server support to my region.Besides the omnipresent performance issues, let's talk about the game itself.STORY MODE is an entertaining diversion with some quality scenes but ultimately largely nonsensical plotline (par for the course with NRS). I had fun with it.I was hoping to see some further innovation in terms of actual gameplay, but it's still the same deal, each chapter gives you a new character to play, and you flail around for a bit with a few moves before moving on to the next chapter. Losing the ability to pin moves is actually a pretty big deal here.Standard towers are back also, I don't have much to say about them except that there's no boss this time around. Disappointing, although no boss is actually better than the Kronika fight in MK11 which was excruciatingly unfun. The endings are still a nice treat.INVASIONS is the new mode upon which essentially the entire experience hangs for non-competitive players. There's no Krypt or Towers of Time here (though it does incorporate some living towers as a bit of a compromise). This mode is intended to be the one-stop shop for single player content. I like the idea a lot, actually. But the actual play experience is not great.It's essentially towers of time/test your luck fights spread out into an RPG-lite format, but there's nothing fundamentally new here. More upsettingly, most of the combat modifiers are much more of a frustration than an interesting quirk.I don't know why the modifiers seem so focused on disabling the player in general. This should be the mode where you get to go wild with absurdly long combos and overpowered moves. Where is the fun in breaking every combo the player performs with offscreen attacks? Or blinding the player entirely? Or mixing up the controls? It just turns the whole affair into a nightmare of spamming buttons."Build variety" is essentially non-existent, you just want to boost your attack as high as possible while maintaining enough HP to take some hits.You will find dozens and dozens of talismans but they don't seem to do much, I'm not quite finished yet but I haven't bothered upgrading a talisman yet, or needed to use one for anything.So far it has been quite easy, but I will reserve judgement on that because I haven't closed out the season just yet. Also - I don't mind if it's easy, I'll play ranked if I want a challenge. I just wish it was fun.I am genuinely hoping they can address some of the feedback and turn this mode around in future seasons, because I think it could be great.KOMBAT LEAGUE is the de facto online mode, same as MK11. I won't go over it in great detail, as it's largely unchanged from the previous game. The downsides are still there, if you face a lower ranked player you still stand to lose a ton of points, despite KL rank having almost no bearing on player skill whatsoever. I really don't think this system needs to be quite so punitive as it is.Worth noting that matches are best of 5 now, so they take longer to complete than they did in MK11, extending the length of the grind.Also, we have skins tied to Elder God this time around, I have to assume the vast, vast majority of players will never achieve that. Whether you think that's a positive or negative I leave up to you.Also, KOTH seems to have been downgraded, not having any emotes or any chat functionality at all (unless I'm missing something?). There's basically no interactivity with other players at all now, which really seems like a shame.With the main modes of play covered, let's address the elephant in the room.CUSTOMIZATION - there's a lot less. It's not a huge deal for me, but I know a lot of players really loved the amount of items MK11 had. I think it kept a lot of people playing. If you are playing to unlock mountains of cool skins and gear, you're gonna be disappointed. It's just not there.I don't think every game needs to meet the previous in terms of content this way, that inevitably leads to excessive bloat. But there should be something else to replace the gap here, and there's just not. You can practically see a hole in this game where content should be.Now - most importantly....GAMEPLAY - it's really fun! If you like NRS fighting games you'll like this one too. If you didn't like previous titles, you probably won't like this one either. Notably, balance among the characters feels pretty good to me, almost everybody can do some wild s*** when they're in their zone. In general the game's a little more aggressive than MK11 was. Kameo balance feels more uneven, but it's really character dependent and too early to say.Kameos and air combos are perhaps the biggest new features and they both work well. You will encounter plenty of annoying meta pairings with Kameos if you go online, but that's unavoidable. I hope to see greater diversity with Kameo choice as players improve.Maybe you think it's strange I choose to talk about gameplay last, but that's exactly how it feels to play this game. It's a good fighting game buried under a mountain of bulls*** performance, frustrating design choices, and hampered by an overall lack of content.The fundamental thought I have while playing this game is "My god, this was not ready for release."I feel burned and disrespected by this game. Like they thought the consumer was too stupid to notice all the corners they cut. I won't pre-order another NRS title. F*** you, WB.
