_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Kombat 1, a fresh yet familiar reboot of the iconic fighting game series, brings both nostalgia and innovation to the table. Developed by NetherRealm Studios, this installment reimagines the origins of the franchise while incorporating contemporary gaming elements that cater to both long-time fans and newcomers.Gameplay and Mechanics:The core of Mortal Kombat 1 remains true to its roots, delivering the brutal, fast-paced combat that fans have come to love. The game introduces a refined fighting system with fluid animations and responsive controls, making each battle feel exhilarating and rewarding. The inclusion of new mechanics like Krushing Blows and Fatal Blows adds strategic depth, allowing players to turn the tide of battle with well-timed, devastating moves.Graphics and Design:Visually, Mortal Kombat 1 is stunning. The game leverages modern graphics technology to deliver detailed character models, dynamic environments, and jaw-dropping special effects. The attention to detail in each stage, from the eerie landscapes of the NetherRealm to the vibrant streets of Earthrealm, enhances the immersive experience. The iconic fatalities are more gruesome and spectacular than ever, pushing the boundaries of visual fidelity in fighting games.Story Mode:The story mode offers a compelling narrative that reboots the Mortal Kombat universe, providing fresh perspectives on beloved characters like Liu Kang, Scorpion, and Sub-Zero. The cinematic storytelling, interwoven with intense fights, keeps players engaged from start to finish. The plot balances nostalgia with new twists, making it accessible to new players while rewarding long-time fans with familiar yet reimagined lore.Multiplayer and Online Play:Mortal Kombat 1 shines in its multiplayer offerings. The online mode is robust, featuring ranked matches, casual play, and a variety of tournaments. The netcode is solid, ensuring smooth and fair matches, which is crucial for competitive play. The inclusion of cross-play broadens the player base, allowing for diverse and challenging opponents.Customization and Extras:The customization options in Mortal Kombat 1 are extensive. Players can personalize their fighters with different skins, gear, and abilities, adding a layer of personalization and strategy. The Krypt returns as an engaging mode to unlock rewards, filled with secrets and challenges that encourage exploration and replayability.Conclusion:Mortal Kombat 1 successfully reinvigorates the franchise, blending nostalgic elements with modern advancements to create a fighting game that feels both classic and fresh. Its polished gameplay, stunning visuals, and engaging story mode make it a must-play for fans of the series and fighting game enthusiasts alike. While there are minor issues, such as occasional balance tweaks needed for certain characters, the overall package is impressive and satisfying. Mortal Kombat 1 stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of the franchise, proving that after decades, it can still deliver a knockout punch.Pros:Engaging and fluid combat mechanicsStunning visuals and detailed environmentsCompelling story mode with a fresh take on classic charactersRobust multiplayer and online featuresExtensive customization optionsCons:Minor balance issues with certain charactersSome repetitive elements in the Krypt modeOverall, Mortal Kombat 1 is a triumphant return to the origins of the series, offering a nostalgic yet modern fighting experience that is sure to captivate players old and new.

Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is complete garbage. There is like 7 hours of worthwhile content before it becomes a complete slog. After you've beat the campaign and gone through invasions all you have left to do is play online or do daily/weekly towers. Daily and weekly towers are full of the worst gameplay decisions ever put into a video game. You will stand there blocking and when you try to attack, all you get to do is poke because the game will throw 10 modifiers at you that make it impossible to do anything. Thought you should be able to see the person you were fighting? Think again cause you're entire screen will essentially be blacked out while the game launches you into the air with fire, after that you'll try to get up only to be launched in to the air again while a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bat launches more fire at you. No one liked modifiers in towers of time MK11, and they've made them 10000x times worse in MK1. All you get is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fire modifiers EVERY DAY. EVERY WEEK. You sit there unable to do any combos and blocking till the time runs out. MK1 completely removed any enjoyable/rewarding single player content. You'd think going through daily towers of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ would reward you with a skin or something, but no. All you get is 100 useless coins that convert to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CONCEPT ART. YAY. They took all of the rewarding parts of MK11 and put those into a cash shop that refreshes weekly. You will never get anything interesting in this game without paying 5-10 extra dollars for it.The only place anyone can have any fun playing this game past the story is in local or online multiplayer. You're playing this game on PC presumably, so you'll probably never play local. Then, you're left with online play which is straight up never fun for the majority of players when it comes to fighting games.Overall, when you're simply just doing a 1v1 that doesn't involve modifiers, the game can be fun. Apart form that there is not a single part of this game that makes it worth the insane price of 70 dollars. I wouldn't even play invasions for free if that were a thing. Have fun playing what is a complete downgrade from MK11 in almost EVERY SINGLE WAY. Anyone saying this game is good needs to get their brain checked because this is an atrocious precedent to LET the devs think is okay. The game is 10% of what MK11 was.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to write this review, but currently I wouldn't recommend this game in its current state. I played MK quite a bit back in the PS2 era. Jumped back in for MK11, loved the story, had a lot of fun for the little grindathon that was unlocking the gear/cosmetics. Didn't do much PvP, but I overall found the systems and whatnot in MK11 to be very enjoyable.This is a $70 game, but it's already riddled with features of a free-to-play live service game. $10 for a skin in the premium shop, nothing like the krypt to unlock things (it's been replaced with essentially a gacha-style menu that drops rewards), the amount of cosmetic content for characters is very clearly left open for future content drops or premium skin shop updates.It hurts, because the core gameplay is great. I love the cast, the story was great (ending was weaker than the rest of the story but it was bombastic and fun and made up for it), and I still really enjoyed the PvE mode for what it is. There just isn't any longevity in its current state. MK11's Towers of Time felt like I could endlessly whittle away at and slowly get cosmetics for characters and enjoy the fights along the way. Currently basic towers reward you with little to nothing. There's one to two fights in the PvE mode that's new to the game that aren't really real fights, but they throw 3 NPCs that can be one-two shot and finishing it with a Brutality nets you with the most XP/coins for the rest of the game that are just grinded to no end to level things up. At least the Towers of Time felt like there was a game behind it, fights to be had, intros to be watched and enjoy the banter of, it was good. This game just... feels doughy at its core and like it needed some extra time to cook. Things like the lack of a proper loading screen so you don't know if the game crashed or if it's still loading really help that unpolished vibe. It really feels like they saw the model that Overwatch 2 took and went "Yeah that seems great, charge them $70 and ship the same thing."I'd love for everything I said here to be fixed and tweaked in the future because the spirit of what I wanted to be there is there, it's just shackled and smothered by... well... greed to rush a product out the door to make money off of.

_childDocuments_.review: MK1, This game rekindled my love of fighting games and I love it for that. The gameplay feels about as good as MK11 which was really enjoyable.The Kameo system is a great addition in my opinion, a system that makes for some new innovations when facing fighters. It's not as simple as learning their move sets and other players will always surprise you with something you've never seen before that consistent new tech, new combos it can refresh a meta and that's good for a game's lifespan.However NetherRealm being NetherRealm it's not perfect.Adding in Invasions mode for single player is a nice touch MK as an RPG? I'm all in favour! If it were like MK Deception and Konquest mode, but annoyingly it's made a challenge only by super armour cheese and messing with the game as a whole in terms of frame timing, rather than making it an actual challenge of skill.The hardest it gets is Test Your Might. That is not very fun. It would be much better if it rewarded the stuff that makes a difference in an actual match not relying on gimmicks. Now the elemental twist is nice but after a while stops being relevantOne mark off for the jittery PC cutscenes in story, that's pretty annoying AND exclusive to PC! (I'm on ultra settings on a high end PC with a 3080ti so I don't want to hear the 'inferior hardware' argument.)One mark off for Invasions requiring very little skill and relying on cheese albeit in typical MK fashion.One mark off for Micro-transactions, seriously. I get your game is a business but still, these things don't need to be omnipresent. What's wrong with DLC costumes over buying an in game virtual currency to buy them anyway?

_childDocuments_.review: I like when the funny man punches people's nutsBut seriously, it's a good game with some really frustrating things. For reference, I love Mortal Kombat but I'm a very casual player. I play with friends and bots, and that's about it. I've heard that the online experience is especially frustrating in this one. The following is based off of my experience, without online multiplayer.Positive:- Really smooth combat, actions feel like they flow together well.- Cool, weird story. It's a soft reboot that plays on your expectations of certain characters and still builds off of MK11's story.- Liu Kang is a god, I love to see it.- Kameo fighters are a cool system,- Creative fatalities that are just as fun and disgusting as you'd expect.Neutral:- Fighter variants and custom movesets are absent in this game, meaning every character has exactly one moveset that will not change. I'm not sure if this is a "going back to basics" type of thing or a step backwards for Mortal Kombat's gameplay.Negative:- Voice acting. It's terrible with some characters. Specifically, Nitara. I don't know who decided Megan Fox should try being a voice actress, but it's really, really bad.- Local/Offline battles and Story Mode do not contribute to your profile and character progression. You'll get a decent amount of customization to use from Story Mode (and the character Havik after beating it), but the Character Mastery will not change your profile level won't increase (which is required for unlocking more Kameo characters).- Quan Chi and Ermac are already in this game's story mode, but they're selling them as DLC characters? I sort of get doing that with Takeda, he's not in the game at all to my knowledge, but fighters that are already in the game should be free and available right now.- The title. I despise this naming convention of reusing titles from the past or calling a game "Franchise 1" or just "Franchise." Modern Warfare, Doom, Battlefield, Mortal Kombat (twice now, with the 2011 game "Mortal Kombat" and now this one) are just the ones off the top of my head.- My performance has been unusually bad sometimes with this game. I'd still consider my computer to be fairly high-end, but I struggle to hold a solid 60 frames without making the game looking like it was made 10 years ago.Overall, it's a good time with some issues. Hopefully they fix some of this in the future because they have a solid foundation for a really good game, but some issues stick out too much to ignore.

_childDocuments_.review: The worst MK in the modern era.  I wish I had not bought it or spent time thinking it would get better as time went.  Kameo system was a terrible idea, there is no originality.  The Kameo either works for the character you are playing or it doesn't really help in anyway for you character because they limit everything to stance kameo call ins when instead every Kameo call in should be an ambush which would open up endless possibilities.The DLC characters are half comic book characters who belong in the next Injustice.  How they thought they fit into MK is beyond me, they look terribly out of place and have no reason to be in the MK universe when NRS makes a super hero fighting game.The game is beyond whack, features still missing.  Had this game released in 2010 it might of been acceptable.No online lobbies or a date for when they will come, and at this point do you have any faith that they will actually be as good as the lobbies in SF6 or T8?  Surely they won't be.Crossplay took 6 months to be added and did nothing to increase the active fan base numbers, then it took a few months after that to get KOTH crossplay matches.Fatal Blows are still a thing... because if you're getting wrecked in a match and play terribly you should for some reason be rewarded with the ability at 30% health to push two buttons and get a mindless 35% damage off the worst handholding mechanic in modern fighting games.There are no real defensive options besides block and the new up-block, which is not nearly enough defensive abilities to get any pressure off you.  You have to build 3 bars to break a combo as the only other option than blocking.Instead of seeing the mountains of complaints from the fan base and addressing anything they say, WB continues to make the devs be quiet.  None of the issues since launch that the fanbase has been asking for have been acknowledged.Combos feel slower than ever, which creates the average match time to be longer than most.  The Ermac trailer had the fan base thinking that a speed increase and possibly a new defensive option were being teased.  Both of these have been pointed out as yet another misstep since launch day but NRS didn't hear any of the outcry as neither of those were introduced.Every patch the small ghost town that is the remaining online community thinks... This is it, here comes the changes.... and here we are 9 months after release with none of the major complaints being addressed.  It feels as tho every patch causes nothing but issues with online matches.  Online match seasons are 60-90 days, which is way too short.  There is no large ranking system to keep climbing for long periods of time, which makes the ranked seasons feel like a pointless grind if you don't want the rewards in the active season.  SF6 and T8 have large ranking systems that keep the players far more engaged for the long run.As a long time die hard Mortal Kombat fan there is no way to recommend this game to anyone.  It will never be fixed or become good.  The pulse left 2 months after release when the devs were forced to be silent by WB. The only way MK has a future is if Ed Boone gets them away from WB Games.

_childDocuments_.review: This acted as a wonderful reminder that MK is for a much more casual audience.The story is good as always (minus Nitara's poor performance, and a certain DLC character face)Invasion mode is not fun and a complete slog. The pacing is bad, and it is just a series of test your luck matches basically. of all the ways to pad the single player content, this may be the laziest MK option yet. I would of loved Kombat Kart, Puzzle Kombat, or even just a regular old Krypt.The entire online portion is feature incomplete; No lobbies, No online practice and  No way to skip matches if there is a bad connection. I can't go more than 5 matches without the game hanging on a black screen and having to force close it. Not to mention in the wake of SF6, for a AAA title, this netcode is not good enough. Wifi matches still feel like delay based wifi matches, and without the option to skip wifi players, Ranked is effectively useless.MK is probably great for your dad or uncle who loved MK as a kid and only has a few hours a week to mash buttons. But if you are looking for a quality fighting game that is feature complete, this ain't it. The combat is more fun than MK11, but everything else is under-cooked, incomplete, or a general downgrade from previous titles, and overall not worth the price tag of a AAA-Videogame. I was fortunate enough to be gifted, and thankful I was spared from wasting my money.If this was $40 and early access? maybe. but as it stands now? save your money and wait for the inevitable MK1 XL/Aftermath/Kompete version. maybe they will have get it together by then.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate doing this with a franchise, and a game, that I love. The game is fun. It is fast paced and it is challenging. I was hyped and hopeful for the first month about what was to come. In the second month, I became tentative and nervous. Now I find myself disheartened. They are selling a premium priced game that has all the micro-transactions of a FTP game. And it is going to get worse. The CEO of WB has stated they want more money for everything. He didn't hint about it, he didn't use some mixed message coding in his speech - he straight out said that they want more money for everything they add to the game. They are selling fatalities now! The hallmark - the trademark of MK is up for sale - $10 for a "holiday" fatality. It's a sad day when I have to leave a negative review on MK - I grew up playing the very first one in the arcade, and now it seems they killed it with the appropriately named MK1. It started at one and it has now ended at one as well. I cannot recommend anyone buy this game nor any other WB property going forward since they have said this is the direction they want to go with all of their major titles - MK, DC, Harry Potter and Game of Thrones. If they make them FTP and then have content that is purchased, that's fine, but don't charge me $70 and then charge me $10 for new announcer, $10 for an new skin and $10 for another fatality!!!

_childDocuments_.review: In other fighters, I am constantly thinking of all the options I have to win. In MK, my mental process is relegated entirely to "don't get hit". I don't mind blocking, I play Guile in SF6, blocking is what I do. What I do mind is when every fight is the same mental loop. Wait my turn, do my thing, wait again. I have extremely limited options to throw a wrench in that loop. If I'm out of meter, I'm just boned. I can't use my assists to break me out or do anything while I'm stuck getting juggled, and the other player can't do anything when I put them in the same spot.Invasions mode is a boring board game with a half-baked inventory system that isn't anywhere as enjoyable as just playing Towers or exploring the Krypt. Downtime between fights is immense. You will be looking at menus quite a lot. There isn't any way to just find matches while you are in training, which should be a genre standard at this point.Netcode seems to be having some real issues, with many fights sitting at a black screen for extended periods of time before anything happens. You'll drop combos due to the weird timing, and in a game all about taking turns, that is a huge issue.I used to adore the MK games, but at this point, I'm done. I'll play it some more to try to convince myself I'm having fun, but I suggest you don't put yourself in my situation. Avoid it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend getting the game, but I cannot.Let's start with the positives.  Graphically the game looks amazing, outside of any bugs, and the actual gameplay is amazing as well - there's is something satisfying when you are able to lab out a combo that uses all of your resources and you see that big number.Now though, the main criticisms and why I cannot recommend getting the game.  First, the actual gameplay loop is pretty lacklustre.  Invasions are not a fun mode to grind through, at all.  Having to fight through hordes of AI with bosses that have armour is not enjoyable enough.  Next, the missing features - there's still no PC crossplay at all so you are stuck with PC vs PC as things currently stand, there's no lobby system outside of KOTH and no online practice - both of which have been things since MKX.  If you want to play online, it's KOTH, Ranked or Casuals, no inbetween.  The last thing is the microtransactions - WB are just being insanely greedy at this point.  The infamous £10 Halloween fatality, £10 costumes even if you have the pass (MK11 this was not a thing, they did sell costumes yes but you also got costumes in the season passes as well), the sheer amount of Dragon Krystals you need to buy if you wanted everything is insane and it's compounded by, again, having to grind through invasions or online to get the Koins if you don't want to buy the Krystals.  This is ridiculous from a company of WB's size, yet also not surprising since everyone knows these companies just want more capital to go "LOOK AT OUR PROFITS GUYS!"Again I 100% wish I could recommend this because I do love MK1's core gameplay, yes there is busted things (Lao low hat, prepatch Baraka/Cyrax, Johnny Cage, etc) but the game at a 1v1 is fun, but everything else around it just brings it down.  Will I keep playing?  Yes because that's what I've chosen to do, but it's nowhere near the price at this moment in time.

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Kombat 1 Review: A Bold Return to the Roots with a New TwistMortal Kombat 1 brings the iconic franchise back to its roots while adding fresh and exciting elements to the formula. With its return to the beginning of the MK storyline, players experience a reimagined universe where beloved characters have new roles, alliances, and personalities. NetherRealm Studios has skillfully woven an alternate narrative that feels familiar yet refreshingly unpredictable, making it a must-play for fans and newcomers alike.Story and CharactersThe narrative reboot offers a fascinating reintroduction to iconic characters like Liu Kang, Raiden, Scorpion, and Sub-Zero, but with altered backgrounds and relationships. The plot is filled with twists that keep you engaged, with new alliances and rivalries changing the dynamics between these beloved characters. Liu Kang, now a god responsible for this new timeline, serves as a powerful central figure, guiding the player through a world that’s both nostalgic and unexpected.Gameplay and MechanicsThe gameplay in Mortal Kombat 1 has been streamlined but remains brutal and deeply satisfying. Familiar mechanics such as combos, Fatalities, and brutal finishers are still there, yet the game introduces the new “Kameo” system, which lets you summon iconic characters to assist in battle, adding a layer of strategy. Kameo assists add exciting possibilities for chaining combos and give players more control over the pacing of the fight.NetherRealm has also refined the controls to make moves feel smooth and responsive, making it approachable for new players while still offering depth for veterans. The game rewards skill, timing, and creativity with endless options for devastating combos and over-the-top special moves.Visuals and AudioVisually, Mortal Kombat 1 is stunning. The graphics are sharper than ever, with highly detailed character models, dynamic stages, and impressive lighting effects that bring the world to life. The gore and violence are still as intense as you’d expect, but the presentation is more polished, delivering one of the best-looking games in the franchise’s history.The soundtrack and sound design complement the visuals perfectly. Punches, kicks, and Fatalities sound visceral, enhancing the immersive feel of the combat. Voice acting also stands out, bringing personality and depth to each character and grounding the outlandish storylines in believable emotions and motivations.Modes and ReplayabilityMortal Kombat 1 offers multiple game modes to keep players engaged, from the story mode to online multiplayer and the classic Towers. The addition of the Kameo system and the variety of characters also give players a reason to keep experimenting with different combinations, adding a layer of replayability that keeps the experience fresh.The game does have a few minor setbacks, mainly in the online matchmaking, which could benefit from more robust options and faster load times. However, these issues don’t detract significantly from the overall experience.Final VerdictMortal Kombat 1 is a triumphant return for the franchise, delivering an exciting reboot with enough fresh content to feel innovative without straying too far from its roots. Whether you’re a die-hard fan or a newcomer, Mortal Kombat 1 delivers intense, cinematic, and brutally fun gameplay that will keep you coming back for more. NetherRealm has managed to honor the legacy of Mortal Kombat while successfully forging a new path, making this a title that’s worthy of the franchise’s legendary name.Rating: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Despite not liking the trailers i still bought the game thinking that you cannot properly judge a game you have not played. Also MK is one of my favourite franchises and the previous game is my most played game on steam. Unfortunatly my feeling was right, so far this is the worst money i spent on a game on steam (I bought the premium edition).Game Breaking bugThe game feature many bugs. The most impactful one is the bug affecting player two (on the right at the beginning of the fights) player two will have an objective disadvantage due to a bug on the hitboxes, this particularly affects long combos. You heard it right, in a competitive two players game one of the players will always have a competitive advantage. Other important bugs incorrect and missing frame data on multiple character, bugged inputs on some strings and special moves, bugged brutality inputs, bugged reward for daily and weekly rewards (you never get them), bugged premium shop that never started at 12 days from launch (for premium edition).Good things about the game:Some gameplay mechanics have been tweaked to permit a smoother gameplay, dash is way better than any other MK game, combo extension is easy but still need practice, you have more freedom in building combos, the breakaway from MK11 is absent and the combo breaker mechanic from MKX is back. I would have preferred a faster gameplay but so far the changes in the fighting department are for the better. The core of the game is good. The problem is everything elseBad things about the game:First of all, the grind is even more extreme than MK11, a game where everybody complained about the grind. The reward system is terrible, you need more than 40 hours of gameplay to unlock all the basic content for every fighter (skins, palettes, brutalities, fatalitie, gears etc). Multiply this for 23 characters in the base roster and add all the season cosmetics, you will have to play at least 1000 hours only to have all the basic content for the initial roster. The way you adquire the XP is through doing towers, invasion (wich is towers with extra steps) and online casual or ranked match. If you play local with another player or do a private match online you gain no xp.  If you play towers you have reduced XP (basically nothing). Also the rewards are way worst than the previous game. Skins are not that good and every character only have 3 skins (some have 4) and one gear to customize. The only things worth grinding for are the brutalities. Now in a game where you grind hard mostly for cosmetics you will think that you can show off your cosmetic collection right ? WRONG, you only have one loadout for every character. The previous game had 5 loadout and 3 gear to customize for every character. Pay more for less content seems to be the slogan for this game. In MK11 the initial price ws 60 € for 24 characters plus 1 if you placed a preorder. In Mk1 for the price of 70 € you get 22 characters plus 1 if you preorder (the characters locked behind a paywall is one of the main characters, he also have a chapter in story mode where you can play it while many other characters in the base roster do not). Also. many useful features from the previous games are absent.  Examples: tutorials for the characters, the possiblity to bind the combo strings to the screen to lab them, the wonderful intro and outro. Intro dialogues are now extremely short and only accesible in local or online fights, doing towers offline will not have them at all. The game feels extremely rushed and unfinished in almost any aspect. I cannot recomend it to anyone in the current state. If the game will be fixed i will probably adjust this review but i still feel swindled for buying a clearly incomplete product.

_childDocuments_.review: Y’all… I had a proper review going with some laudatory wordsmithing. Something clever. Something fun to read. I wanted to highlight what I thought were some legitimate strengths and weaknesses of this game. I had a lot to say, and I was taking a large chunk of my own time to say it right.Then they dropped a ten-dollar fatality and my 25+ year MK veteran ass said “Why bother? Why waste the time?” I’m so tired my brothers and sisters. I’m so done. Ultra condensed version of the review coming your way.I kinda love this game. I love the lore. I loved the story. It was better than most. I didn’t mind most of the changes. It was more fun than not. As a fan, I was very pleased.  I genuinely geeked out on the last chapter and played it over an over. I don’t play online. I’m that guy. I know that’s a decent chunk of the game, and I know I’m paying money to not use that feature. I’m fine with that. I look forward to the other things that give the game it’s replay value.In MK1, those other things are the Invasion Mode. And that Invasion Mode was built at the intersection of janky and broken. (I swear, I spent no extra time on that quip. It just came off the top of my head. That one’s free. Unlike most content in this game.) It’s passable. I play it. It’s still broken. It’s repetitive and things just don’t work. The last season’s tower had you grinding for an hour then getting nothing for your effort because you lost a Test Your Might at the top. Insulting and time wasting. This season is a new flavor of broken. Still. It’s passable and fixable.There's no Crypt at all. Just some boring ass shrine grinding out pallet swaps and concept art. Another victim of the monetization.And the monetization has gotten absolutely disgusting. I never wanted to be the guy that critiques a game on the company’s business practices rather than the game itself. But here we are. I can’t defend or ignore it anymore. I let “pay for EZ Fatalities” slide on X because I really didn’t care if people with more dollars than sense wanted to buy them. I didn’t mind DLC through MK11 because I thought it was reasonably priced for what genuinely felt like extra content.But 40 dollars for six characters? Two of which are in the story mode? And we’re gonna act like 5 Kameo characters make that worth it? I’m pretty sure the entire Aftermath DLC was cheaper than that. It was definitely larger on content. Maybe MK11s Kombat Packs cost that much. I don’t remember. But it feels jarring this time.And that 10-dollar Halloween themed fatality? No. Walk it back all you want, I’m done. People who want to defend it, do it on your own time, because mine is worth more than WB thinks it is. I legitimately like this game and I still wish I hadn’t bought it. I had to go into a media blackout bubble for weeks leading up to the release because of all the advanced copies they gave out and all the streams that already had the entire story mode and every Fatality, Brutality, and voice line on display. Little did I realize those streamers were doing me a favor. Next time I’m gonna do what I should have done this time. Watch the spoilers and skip the game, and the grind, until it reaches the 75% off mark a couple years later. There are so many more rewarding gaming experiences out there than this right now and my fandom is no longer enough to pull me through.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has beautiful detailed graphics, but in-game action feels less fluent/clean than MK11. Which is too bad because the game has great fight game-play potential, with an interesting move set. Environments look amazing. Sound is great, music scores are the best they have been in the series.Campaign was good, rich and fun, but don t expect stellar script or dialogue. It s just a game, not some Golden Globe winner series. There are noticeable stutters during campaign cinematics for PC.Training mode is very good and well explained, similar to its predecessor. Recommend completing it.The game as a whole looks quite Unpolished, though. Has obvious performance issues during fight and an outrageously amount of stuttering and disconnects/ errors in the menus, especially invasions. Quite a few noticeable graphical glitches with brutalities and navigation in invasions. I had expected a higher level of quality from NRS at release. Camera is very restrictive and buggy in the character view and during invasions navigation.The towers menu and navigation is an obvious downgrade from MK11, in my opinion, being limited by having to walk your character from one tower node to another with a crappy camera. Invasions sections have no map... Having all those nodes with no potential for overview is a great miss for QOL.Kustomization - You can only have one cosmetic variation now, and can t easily switch looks before a new set in Versus.Oh and characters only have one piece of gear.Oh, outside the Store, there s no way to tell what when and where one can unlock in terms of cosmetics.No plan, it s just a slot machine at the end of an encounter or ... gambling with the Shrine , 1000 gold at a time. If you have gathered 300k in gold coins, can t gamble all of it at the Shrine, 1000 at a time. Good night.Menus design generally is a downgrade from MK11. I could go into details, but it s on my time.I think the game is not finished, it seems that most of the game meta features and UI are bare-boned with little consideration for QOL. Maybe they did not have the time to finish before the madmen reigning the financials dpt were barking at the door for their quarterly revenue streams.Last but not least Megan Fox has some of the worst voice acting in the game dev industry. The intensity and immersion of her acting is at the level of obscure soap opera where the character is trying to decide what kind of coffee it should order alongside the dry croissant. Extremely noticeable in the Campaign. I don t think she cared and pretty sure nobody at NRS asked for Take 2.I regret pre-ordering just because it s too often now that big game studios deliver unpolished or unfinished games at release date. As a user I don t care about the deadlines, I care about the quality of my experience with the game. If they pushed the game 2 months, we d all been fine (minus a few vocal content creators, which are just media parasites).I m curious to know if it s as bad on PS5 or this is just a bad port.This still has the chance to be the greatest MK, if they fix their bugs, add some QOL for the meta and the team is careful with balancing the game-play. There s obviously a lot of effort and love put into the making of MK1 and I hope the ulterior patches will make things right.

_childDocuments_.review: Very Disappointed Mortal Kombat 1, the latest installment in the iconic fighting game series, sadly fails to live up to the high expectations set by its predecessors. One can't help but feel that this game is a significant step backward for the franchise, leaving me scratching my head in disappointment at the overall lack of features.One of the most glaring issues with Mortal Kombat 1 is the evident lack of innovation. While the core combat mechanics are undeniably smooth and the graphics are visually stunning, these elements alone can't mask the glaring absence of meaningful features that were present in previous Mortal Kombat titles. The game feels stripped down, devoid of the engaging features and customization options that fans have come to love and expect.The game modes, touted as the heart of any fighting game, turn out to be uninspired and painfully repetitive. It's disheartening to see that instead of introducing fresh and exciting gameplay experiences, Mortal Kombat 1 relies on mundane and unimaginative modes, making the overall gaming experience feel stale and uninspiring.Perhaps one of the most egregious offenses is the pricing strategy. $70, Bruh really... for a game that lacks essential features present in its predecessors is not only audacious but also downright insulting. Previous Mortal Kombat games, such as Mortal Kombat 11, demonstrated the potential for deep customization and engaging gameplay. Mortal Kombat 1, however, fails to deliver on these fronts.The attempt to extend the game's longevity through unlockable content feels forced and artificial. Locking away vital elements of gameplay, such as fatalities, behind a random chance system, where players must spend Gold at the shrine, is incredibly lazy rather than a thoughtful game design choice.Furthermore, the introduction of cameo characters feels lazy and uninspired. Instead of putting in the effort to develop these characters fully, Mortal Kombat 1 opts for a half-hearted approach, leaving me feeling cheated out of a genuine and immersive gaming experience by feeding off my nostalgia of old characters in the series.Lastly, the game's story mode, while short, has fun storytelling. Previous entries in the series might not have been groundbreaking in terms of narrative, but they compensated with sheer entertainment value. Mortal Kombat 1, despite its limited playtime the story is a blast.In summary, Mortal Kombat 1 is a lackluster addition to the franchise, marked by a sheer lack of innovation, uninspired game modes, questionable pricing, and a very short story mode. _childDocuments_.review: I played the campaign straight through in about 9 hours.  It's one of the best if not *the* best story mode for a fighting game I've played - like a popcorn blockbuster summer action movie you get to participate in.  Worthwhile just for the campaign.  I've yet to tap into the multiplayer but I'll update once I do.  The one downside for the campaign mode is that it puts you in the shoes of different fighters as the story progresses, and you play around 3 or 4 matches and just as you're starting to learn their nuances it shifts to a new character and you have to start again.  But I don't know how else they could've done it while giving you a taste of each character.  A worthwhile contribution to the lore of MK and it was fun getting a fresh take and playing a young Raiden while he's still a noob, for example.  If you're already an MK fan, solid buy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has tons of technical and performance issues; Yes, it's very pretty but, that's about it.It's heavily reliant on the game being installed on a very quick internal SSD or m.2 drive. It literally is unplayable if it's not installed on a fast drive. The loading times are otherwise unbearable and the inputs are incredibly delayed. I have no idea why the games performance is hindered based on the drive it's installed on. It's almost like the game engine is reading directly from the drive during gameplay and trying to stream the assets in during gameplay instead of them being loaded at the beggining of the fight. This is even noticeable on things like the character selection, where it could take several seconds for a character to load in if the game is installed on an external usb4-3 ssd.The games netcode is also pretty bad in relation to other fighters. There is tons of input delay and issues surrounding online play. The netcode pales in comparison to sf6 and other games like guilty gear strive.The actual combat is incredibly slow and spammy. The combos are cool but you can literally be in a combo for most of the round with barley any recourse to get out of it. Due to the input latency and netcode, it also makes it drastically harder to block or counteract things that a spammy character like Baraka does, where many of his attacks have 50/50sSome of the attack animations also don't visually match up with the kind of attack it is (low, mid, high, overhead). Some attacks can visually be a mid and hit low and some attacks even sweep vertically and hit high. There seems to be really poor thought into the animations and how they work visually with the mechanics of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, I feel so bad but I have to do this.Just a disclaimer, I can't say I did not have fun in this game because I for sure did. It is a good time but the cracks will start showing and will only deepen until you will realize this game has had mixed focus on its features but its replayability is lacking in many ways I will get into.I am a huge MK fan but I joined late in about 2013. My favorite to this day is MKX and still holds best and coolest combos. This MK1 introduces many ways to build combos which is quite awesome but sometimes these feel so drawn out and similar to MK11's gravity. Kameos are a great addition but is it really something new? I swear we had something similar in MK11 towers where we could use some character's help every now and then. Kameos bring new ways to play BUT they take fighters away. The kameos will almost never talk meaning they can put anyone in the role but I for one I am annoyed many of them are JUST kameo fighters and not normal fighters, with unique voicelines and more moves. As a Jax main, I miss punching the hell out of the opponents but I can only resort to some combo extenders foir others...Story is entertaining but it gets messy until its very end, just like MK11 but with more weird ♥♥♥♥. It is cool seeing all these returning characters, however I wish for some characters they had kept same voice actors. It is also inexcusable to have story characters as DLC...like Ermac & Quan Chi. Waiting for them will be pain...Invasions mode is such a weird RPG board game kinda thing that takes centuries to progress and its fights become annoying as hell with unblockable, uninterruptible characters & random effects that just makes you mad. You can tone the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ down with the syringes & upgrading your character as you level up.And one of my main points is the replayability: once you've gone through invasions & story you will realize you have such meaningless and similar looking gear & pallettes to choose from...these feel so lazy and barely noticeable sometimes. Very few are creative and cool but guess what...most of those are PAID SKINS! Skins that may cost even 10$??? In an already 100$ game? This is beyond greedy. Grinding this game is barely worth the hassle for now, they gotta do better.And for the really ugly: unfinished stuff. The story sometimes has insane lag & desync from subtitles, fades to black randomly despite me doing the shaders precompilation...Oh my god the menus take FOREVER...moving in invasions as well...I can't skip anything before & after a fight...just WHY?? Especially in singleplayer...Also training doesnt let me pin any moves, there is no crossplay, the brutalities have sometimes weird inputs to them but not as bad as MK11's. The character intros could have used 3 lines instead of 2 and make them less boring. There are no friendships(yet), but we got kameo fatalities which are cool I guess.There are so many more I'd like to point out but it's already getting long enough. Do I recommend this game? To a degree and a certain price drop, yes....but for 70 bucks I will definitely not. The game can be fun but has many many issues that could be fixed in time and IF they actually make the game better, I will then recommend the game and change my review. But for now, this game feels so much like early access & knowing some characters will NEVER be main characters, but just kameos kinda hurts, man. My man Tremor did not deserve that, as well as Jax, Sonya & Kano and all the others honestly. The gameplay can be quite awesome and addicting but your rewards are usually so meaningless and not much different. Hope they make better ones really...

Seriously, compare Peacemaker to Ed from SF6, and it's night and day. -Invasions is probably the worst mode I've ever played in a fighting game.-Even less consistency at character aesthetics and lore. Mileena for example went from Persian looking, to Chinese in MK11, to now Mongolian or something in MK1. Don't even get me started with people like Scorpion and Sub-zero. If you didn't tell me that Mileena is whom I'm looking at in a facial picture, I wouldn't have known who that is for example. NRS needs to disband and they need to get a new team to remake MK from scratch. MK lost its identity, and it has no legacy. So many God awful decisions made with every game it's insane. _childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★★★★☆☆ (8/10)As a die-hard Mortal Kombat fan with over a thousand hours logged into Mortal Kombat 11, I couldn't wait to dive into the latest installment of the franchise, Mortal Kombat 1. This game promised a fresh take on the iconic series with its new "kameo" system, and I was excited to see how it would shake up the classic formula.First off, let's talk about the gameplay. Mortal Kombat 1 offers a truly exhilarating experience that manages to feel distinct from its predecessor while retaining the series' signature brutality. The introduction of the kameo system is a game-changer. It forces you to constantly adapt your strategy in each match, keeping you on your toes and making every fight a unique challenge. This addition breathes new life into a franchise that has been entertaining us for decades, and it's a welcome change.Visually, Mortal Kombat 1 is a treat. The character models are incredibly detailed, and the environments are gorgeously rendered. Every punch, kick, and special move feels weighty and satisfying, immersing you in the brutal combat of the Mortal Kombat universe. The classic fatalities are as gruesome and satisfying as ever, and the new ones added for this installment are a joy to discover.However, the game is not without its flaws. The online matchmaking experience can be a bit frustrating at times. While it's essential to have a robust online multiplayer system in a fighting game, Mortal Kombat 1 occasionally suffers from matchmaking issues, including imbalanced matchups. These issues can lead to some less-than-enjoyable moments, especially if you're looking for a fair and competitive fight.One significant drawback is the occasional error that can occur during online play. These errors not only disrupt the flow of the game but also have the unfortunate side effect of reducing your matchmaking rating (MMR). This can be especially frustrating for dedicated players who are working hard to climb the ranks and improve their skills.In conclusion, Mortal Kombat 1 is a refreshing addition to the franchise, and the new kameo system adds a layer of strategy that keeps you hooked. The game's visuals and combat mechanics are top-notch, delivering the gore and excitement we've come to expect from Mortal Kombat. However, the online matchmaking issues and MMR reduction due to errors can be frustrating setbacks. Despite these flaws, Mortal Kombat 1 is a must-play for fans of the series, offering a unique and entertaining twist on the classic formula. Whether you're a long-time fan or a newcomer, there's plenty to enjoy in this latest installment of the iconic series.

You cannot access any modes outside of traditional towers and story, unlock any costumes and cannot progress through any characters mastery unless you are connected to the internet. The Invasions seasonal content is there to keep player retention and is designed to bait people into buying money on skins. To top it off, you cannot use PAID FOR DLC FIGHTERS IN OFFLINE MODE. I'm so glad I cannot use Shang Tsung, the fighter I paid extra money for, because the servers are down.I cannot recommend this game until this is rectified. Horrible practice and scummy to the highest degree.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is solid, it feels like a major downgrade from MK11.Performance is really really stupid beyond all human comprehension. For context, I have 144hz monitor.Some movies? 144 FPSActual gameplay? 60 FPSInvasion moving around? 30 FPSI understand that 60 FPS is necessary for frame data and whatnot. But why the actual hell don't you just set THE WHOLE GAME TO 60 AND CALL IT A DAY? The fact that FPS jumps back and forth, depending on what you do, makes me extremely nauseous.Not even gonna mention that it's 2023 (at the time of the reveiw) and the NR servers are still trash as usual. With extremely high speed internet, and good ping, you get 1-3 seconds delay vs some opponents, cuz they live somewhere in Antarctica and have 30kb/s internet. I am gonna get a handicap because someone else got trashy internet.I really dislike the new art style they went with for the majority of the characters. The biggest beef is how similar Raiden and Liu Kang faces actually look, despite the fact that, in previous games, they looked extremely different as an overall design.The story is quite crappy. I felt that MK11 was a "necessary" pain (with the whole time traveling crap) so that they could restart the timeline and try something new. I didn't necessarily expect it to be another huge part of this game, which makes it extremely annoying to keep track of everything. Not even gonna talk about the plethora of retcons that are "new timeline" things. Bleh.While the variety of characters is fairly decent, I'm not particularly joyful about the upcoming DLC characters and I'm very annoyed to see some of them not being back (I miss my boi, Fujin).Considering this is a purely opinionated review, I hate the Kameo system with all my being. They removed the variation system (which I understand was a pain to balance, but was extremely fun to play with and create something you could handle better, or felt better in your hands) and added this crappy Kameo system which makes it feel like some sort of team game right now (?). If I want to play a character, I want to play THAT character, not be forced to see actually important animations done more than 70% by some unimportant character I have to tag along with mandatorily.At least the new meter system is half decent.I'm starting to think this game needs a couple of years, to get some content in it, in order to actually be liked by more people.

_childDocuments_.review: Little summary of what I think are most asked questions...( with as little spoilers as possible )--How many modes ? : Story, Invasions, Towers ( normal, Daily, weekly, challenge), Practice, Training, Online, Kustomisation and Gallery mostly. What do you want more in a fighting game ?--How to unlock non-DLC chars and Kameos ? : Just play through story once, you should have most. --How about skins, palettes, gear and fatalities/brutalities ? : You unlock all those by playing your favorite char. Want to get all the gear and finishes for scorpion ? Play as him, any mode, and rank him up. Gear is only cosmetic. Chars have more than 1 Fatality/Brutality each. --No crypt ? : Nope, you unlock most through ranks and invasions, as for art and music, you pay 1000 coins at the shrine for a random reward.--Season rewards ? Does that mean battle pass ? : No battle pass, season rewards are coins you can spend in store for cosmetics, easily obtainable in invasions.--Length ? : Story is about 6-8 hours, Invasions is much longer with 200-300 fights to do ( more if you grind, or lose, or get secret fights ). Leveling a char to max rank takes a while, maxing them all ( + the kameos ) could take months depending on playtime.--DLC chars/Kameos not showing up ? : They are not out yet, i'm expecting 1 or 2 before X-mas.--Worth it ? : I would say yes. A few rough areas to iron out and please use a SSD or load times will be long, lolSolid 8.5/10 till I see if Kombat Pack 1 will make it a 9..

_childDocuments_.review: While there are some valid comparisons being made to preceding titles in the franchise, I think that MK1 offers the tightest gameplay in the franchise to date. Solo players will have at least 50 hours of gameplay within this first season (story campaign included), and that is a great start to a game that will no doubt receive many content updates. If MK11 is anything to go by, and some details within the story of MK1, there will be more campaign updates down the line in addition to kombat packs and QoL updates (which, currently, there are some QoL updates that need to happen; such as posting kombos to your screen in practice modes, skin selections in character select screens, no access to the game's settings during any game mode, etc). With all of that being said, my only real drawback from MK11 to MK1 is the limitation of having only one gear piece per character in this game. Raiden and Kung Lao have their hats, Lui Kang and Li Mei their arm guards, Geras his chest piece, etc, where as in MK11/Injustice 2 all characters had 4 pieces of customizable gear. Other grievances can be chalked up to my personal subjectivity, such as the removal of 3 line intro dialogue, as well as full victory sequences (though this seems to have been removed due to kameo fighter logistics). Overall, the presentation and gameplay are superb; Netherrealm Studios, led by none other than Ed Boon, have proven themselves time and time again to be not only competent fighting game developers, but leading ones. If you have enjoyed any of their previous games, or even if you are new to Mortal Kombat, this is a great title to pick up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review for the Khaos Reigns DLC. Even though I own it, I can't review the DLC on Steam. Spoiler warning: because the story is so bad I don't feel bad spoiling it. So, don't read if you think the story is worth it. (spoiler: it's not)I'll keep this short. The Khaos Reigns is like a story a 9 year old brat came up with to impress his 6 year old friend. The premise is that Titan Havik is super nasty and super into chaos. And he has henchmen helping him to do things. Basically he wants world domination. At no point did we get any glimpse into why his radical and edgy buddies are helping him. And, he relies on said buddies way too much to command any respect. He's all talk, basically.Khaos Reigns also introduced Noob Saibot. Unfortunately, he is also mainly all talk. You see, Havik turns Sub-Zero into Noob Saibot and gives him orders. What does Noob do? He talks. And because all he does is talk, the story ends up being incredibly boring.Havik creates Noob Saibot, Noob threatens everyone, Tanya takes him down. And then Liu Kang turns Noob "good" again with MK's mainstay story element: rays coming out of people's hands. After which Noob acts like a big baby and takes Havik down. So... why wasn't Tanya the main character? She seems to be more powerful than Havik and Noob.The writing is awkward, clumsy, and misses so many opportunities to actually shock the viewer. If NRS wanted to make Noob's story worthy, they shouldn't have let Rain (Tanya's husband in the story) die in the maze to trap. Instead, they could've had Noob kill Rain, That way Noob would've actually been a threat and cause conflict among the heroes.After Havik is beaten, the story abruptly ends. We don't get to know what happened to Tanya who basically was the star of the show. She's just gone. The writers of this story should be ashamed for being so incompetent. I'm angry for wasting 50 bucks on this. Since I don't care about the guest characters, I'd say this is actually worth 15 bucks. Maybe 20 because the three new DLC characters are all interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Another rushed release. I'm sorry to say, but technically this is the worst MK game I've played with in the last few years. The game is totally unoptimized for PC, and feels very strange to control. I'm playin on a high-end Legion gaming laptop with i9 13900HX, 32 GB RAM and RTX 4090 16 GB, but the game has huge input lags and major FPS drops which makes the fights rather unenjoyable. All cutscenes and in-game fatal-blow animatons are locked at 30 FPS, which is ridiculous. And what about this 60 FPS lock in-game in 2023??? Even the subtitles are not adjusted correctly to the videos. The whole game feels unfinished and unpolished. Not to mention that we don't have too many playable characters, there are quite a few choices on the palette that no one asked for. Characters that many people don't even enjoy playing with. (Especially if they are 'formed' by ZS-category actresses, we all know who I'm talking about). I'm sure that the game will become much better soon, I will give another try after a few months, but for now, I have to say that this game feels wrong to play on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: This port is awful. The cons heavily outweigh the pros.Pros:  + Solid gameplay (movement, combo system and neutral)  + Kameo system is fun and adds diversity, much how variations did in MKX Cons:  - Netcode feels awful 9/10 matches. Either choppy rollbacks or brutal delay  - Cutscenes, menus, single-player board game type mode and Fatalities are locked to 30fps  - Online lobbies are a hassle to set up, as you can't return to a menu AT ANY POINT once the matches have started. It just loops indefinitely unless you quit the lobby and start a new one. Can't invite new players in the middle.  - HEAPS of bugs in the port. Had crashes and instability issues mid-match, player 2 bug where your moves didn't connect properly, and many more.The gameplay is fun, but if you're intending on playing online do not buy this right now. Wait until they fix it, if they ever do. Shame on NRS for letting a port of this quality happen.

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Kombat 1 is yet another soft reboot for the series, and after the ending of Mortal Kombat 11 (the previous entry) a reboot was the obvious way forward.The visuals in this game are fantastic. The characters have never looked more detailed and the environments have never looked more gorgeous. The music is as good as you'd expect, but nothing too memorable. The voice acting is also very good aside from maybe one character...2011's Mortal Kombat popularized the cinematic story mode in the fighting game genre and further improved it in the later sequels. Mortal Kombat 1 sticks with the formula and once again Netherrealm have outdone themselves. Since this is a soft reboot, everyone's storylines start from scratch, but various past events are still taken into consideration. Many of our long-time favorite characters have had some drastic changes to their personalities and character arcs. Mileena, Reptile, Baraka, and Sub-Zero are all here but not exactly how we know and love them. This was a very risky approach for Netherrealm to take, because even slightly botching a major character could spark an outrage from the fans, but thankfully they hit it out of the park. All the characters look and feel familiar but still have a level of unpredictability to them. Then there are some characters in this game who have returned from the 3D era of Mortal Kombat who I thought we would never see again, such as Ashrah, Havik and Reiko. I am glad that they are being given a second chance. The cinematography and the fight choreography in this story mode blew my mind. It felt like I was watching a fantasy adventure movie. Throughout my time with Story mode I kept telling myself that I wish they made an HBO Mortal Kombat series that's similar to the games. Mortal Kombat has so much lore that it could really rival something like Star Wars and Lord of the Rings, but was just never fully taken advantage of. The Story starts out innocently enough but towards the end becomes completely absurd, and I wouldn't expect anything less from a Mortal Kombat story. The final chapter will have long time Mortal Kombat fans screaming with joy.As much as I am a life-long Mortal Kombat fan, I've never really gotten into the fighting genre. I'm not exactly a button masher but I'm pretty terrible at it. When I play Mortal Kombat I learn a combo or two, some special moves, and then I just try my best. It gets me through the main single player game modes, but when it comes to multiplayer I'm basically useless. Because of this, its hard for me to rate the gameplay. I would say that the gameplay is basically a slightly faster version of Mortal Kombat 11. There is a new kameo system during which your tag team partner can hop into the fight every few seconds to get a couple hits which essentially helps you build longer combos. There are almost an infinite amount of possibilities since you can pair any fighter with any kameo. My only big complaint about the kameos is that the fighter roster and the kameo roster are separate from each other. For example, Liu Kang and Smoke are only fighters. Sektor and Jax are only Kameos. Some characters such as Scorpion and Kung Lao have a version of both. I wish that all the kameos were available as fighters and all the fighters were available as kameos. I don't imagine that would be too difficult to implement, but I don't know.The other major mode in the game is called Invasions. This mode is pitched as a table top RPG, which sounds intriguing, but its honestly pretty underwhelming. Your character moves around from spot to spot as if they are on a table top game board, but there aren't really any gameplay elements to the movement. You literally just walk from one spot to the next and there's nothing else to it. You don't roll a dice, you don't earn points, or anything like that. Navigation is a very annoying problem in this mode. There is no map of any kind. Granted, these worlds are not very complicated, but it can often be very disorienting about where you've been and where you need to go because the camera twists and turns on its own nearly every time you move to a new spot on the map. You also move very slowly around the map. So if you spend a few minutes walking in one direction, only to realize that you've been going the wrong way, be ready to face a lot of frustration. The whole walking around the map element just feels completely tedious and unnecessary. The RPG element is also pretty minor. If you've played Mortal Kombat 11 then you remember all the consumables, talismans, and other stuff like that. MK1 brings back the consumables and now your characters can level up. As they level up you can assign points to certain attributes such as strength and HP. Each character also has an elemental type like in Pokemon so a fire character will do more damage against a grass character. The idea is that you switch your character for every fight to get a type advantage over the computer. After a couple fights you realize that none of this really matters, especially if you want to level up your favorite character as fast as possible.Every time your character gains a level you unlock something for that specific character. It can be a new costume or a colorway of an already existing costume. This game no longer has a Krypt, the vast majority of items are now unlocked in this Invasions mode. Each fighter can reach up to level 35 and each Kameo can reach up to level 15, so if you want to unlock everything for your favorite characters be ready to spend hours upon hours grinding the same exact fights in Invasion mode, as this is pretty much the only way to unlock anything for them... There is a Shrine in which you can spend 1000 coins at a time to get something random, but again, the animation for every unlock is unnecessarily long and you can waste thousands of coins (and many minutes) on pointless concept art instead of something useful. After grinding for hours and spending nearly 100,000 coins however, I did unlock a few pretty cool costumes for characters that I've yet to use, so sometimes you can get lucky and get something nice for your favorite characters in the Shrine. On its own Mortal Kombat 1 is a great game. As a sequel to Mortal Kombat 11 it feels like a slight step back. The gameplay, which many would argue is the most important part, is an improvement. The story may not please everyone, but the quality of it cannot be denied. The roster is always debatable, but I like it. However it does feel like Mortal Kombat 1 is lacking something and I think that it comes down to the lack of modes and overall content, at least at launch.

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Kombat 1 Review: A Disappointing Experience⭐️☆☆☆☆ (1/5)I went into Mortal Kombat 1 with high hopes, but I was sorely disappointed. Let me be blunt: this game is a mess.ControlsFirst off, the controls are a nightmare. They're unresponsive and sluggish, which is a cardinal sin for a fighting game that relies on quick reflexes. If you've played previous Mortal Kombat games, don't expect the same level of responsiveness here.Online ModeThe online mode is another letdown. Even with a 1000 Mbits fibre optic connection, the lag and jitter make it nearly unplayable. It's frustrating to lose a match not because of skill, but because of technical issues.Bugs and GlitchesThe game is riddled with bugs and mistakes. From graphical glitches to gameplay inconsistencies, it feels like the game was rushed out the door without proper testing.GraphicsVisually, the game is a step back. It looks outdated and lacks the polish that you'd expect from a title in the Mortal Kombat series.Final ThoughtsAll in all, Mortal Kombat 1 feels like a cheap knockoff of its predecessors. I regret spending 70 euros on this poorly executed game. Save your money and time; there are better fighting games out there.

BUTPlethora of issues with the game though, most of which are highlighted online, very clearly it was rushed out based on a decision by the publisher not the developer. NRS likely did the best they could to get a "playable" game on the shelf. The game is missing SEVERAL quality of life features that would normally be included with a launched title. Especially compared to what MK11 launched with. It's a shame, the best description of the game I've heard is that it is a party game at best in this state.Just a shame really, potentially a great game but just needed more time in the oven overall. NOT worth full price to play a 4 hour story mode and an incomplete online experience.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let's talk graphics. I mean, did the developers even try? The characters look like they're made out of Lego blocks, and the backgrounds? Don't even get me started. It's like someone spilled paint on a canvas and called it a day.Now, onto the gameplay. Ever tried to control a tank? That's what it feels like trying to maneuver these characters. It's like they're stuck in molasses or something. And don't even get me started on the special moves. Half the time, I have no idea how I pulled them off or if I even did.And what's the deal with those Fatalities? They're supposed to be the highlight, right? Well, let me tell you, they're about as intimidating as a puppy trying to bark. The pixelated mess that passes for gore is more likely to make you giggle than cringe.As for the sound, it's like they recorded it in a tin can. The music is forgettable, and the sound effects are more annoying than anything else. And let's not even talk about the voice acting. I'm pretty sure my cat could do a better job.Replay value? What replay value? Once you've seen Sub-Zero rip someone's head off for the hundredth time, you start to wonder why you're even bothering.In conclusion, Mortal Kombat 1 is like that old toy you find in the attic. It might've been cool back in the day, but now it's just gathering dust. Save your quarters for something worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: So, firstly, I will preface this with this will be an in-depth review of this game from someone who doesn't play it competitively. I'm a very casual player and only play online if it's with someone I'm already friends with. I really only play the single player Invasions mode. Speaking of, I've been playing the Invasions mode since season 2 and it has most definitely come a long way since then. They've improved upon it, trying to create new mini-games that are now optional which is fantastic. I'm not too big on all of them but thankfully you don't have to do them! I will say, when it comes to come of the mini-games, my game will just straight up crash. Sometimes I'll be able to play it once but if I try to retry if I fail it, I'll crash. That sucks and deters me from trying some of them, even when I'm interested in trying to complete it. Besides that, I really like the little type system for the characters. It's cute, but sometimes I wish there were more playable counters for some of the cast; it's not that big of deal, though. I'm really happy the developers made the decision to cut down on weaker color palette skins and made less skins that are really cool looking. Overall, Invasions is a lot better than how it used to be, but it could still get better.The reason why I played this game in the first place is because of how good the game looked. As an artist, I absolutely adore all the work put into this game. The lighting and graphics of this game are unbelievable. Some of the shots or frames of characters just straight up look real. The art team did a phenomenal job with this game and I can tell the people working on it do care about it. Genuinely, all the artists involved with this game are so talented its insane. I have a camera mod because I love to go through the fatalities or character screens to get better closeups and the detail is insane. So much of this game is rendered and I can fully appreciate it with the camera mod. I can't get over the way the team was able to animate WRINKLES!!! How did they get the character models to squeeze and stretch like actual human skin?!?! UUUUGGH this game is so beautiful. With the mod, I'm able to look through each map environment and the detail makes me want to explode. I LOVE how pretty this game is I even love collecting the art work in this game and looking through the gallery here because it's all such great work. The story itself is fun but it feels a bit rushed towards the end, though that didn't really stop me from having a good time. Honestly, I could go on and on about how gorgeous this game is to me.I feel like it's important to bring up the microtransactions this game suffers from. Now, I may be biased considering I was, unfortunately, hyperfixated on Overwatch and this game saved me from spending any more money on that godawful game. The microtransactions are not fun but they could by all means be worse. 5 dollars on a skin that comes with 5 other recolors doesn't sound that bad compared to 20 dollars for a skin on games like Overwatch or Fortnite or Valorant. The fact Shang Tsung has to be bought separately if you didn't preorder the game is scummy though. You even play as him in the story mode and he's treated as if he's not a DLC character, getting skins per season and having the same 35 levels as base game characters do. Also, 40 dollars for the DLC was crazy. Like, at first I hated it, but then I played through it and got a ton of cool skins (WWII Johnny <3<3<3) and the new character pack came with it so I didn't mind it as much. It's just......damn... my wallet...To sum it up, I think the game is fun and very beautiful and I'm in love with Johnny Cage

_childDocuments_.review: OK Look, we all already know the PC port is trash so let's skip the formalities. There will be two sections of the review the long part and the short part.Long PartOffline Content: Story mode is beneficial: By far the best story they've done when it wasn't as completely confusing as Mk11, so it's like a blank slate, so to speak. Apart from the long-ass invasion mode, which is fun, the offline experience is lacking because the gameplay, despite the beautiful graphics, falls short. There is also an arcade mode and a survival mode, but functions like Invasion aren't particularly compelling.Gameplay: The neutral in this game is retarded. Anyone who thought D1 should be the bread and butter of this game's core strategy should jump into Liu Kang's Black Hole Fatality: The balancing is equally bad. Kameos does not make a significant contribution besides extending combos or zoning and really adds anything significant other than a boring mechanic that functions like Tag in MK11. Online: The online works perfectly. Those who have a good PC should be able to run it without issue. However, the game's competition is poor, even worse than in its previous installment. In most cases, it comes down to a game of rock, paper, scissors. When fighting, there is no room for expressions except when performing combos. Aside from that pattern-heavy, no-contrast game, it doesn't get any deeper than spamming the same buttons and throwing. It quickly becomes stale and monotonous, but landing combos is at least somewhat satisfying.Conclusion: If you're terrible at fighting games, this is the game for you. There is no need to worry about frames because everything is plus a million on hit literally a generic jab gives you so much advantage it's not even funny how good it is and how stupid the competition truly is in this game. If you want to play a true fighter, try Tekken, Street Fighter, or Guilty Gear.Short PartConclusion: It's trash.
