_childDocuments_.review: I'm leaving this on positive but it's a soft one, kinda wish there was a mixed review because there's a lot of good and bad in this game. As a general quick summary MK1 does the core aspects of the game better than it's predecessor, however it also does a lot of things wrong (or not at all).- The actual combat is amazing, it's basically what MK11 should have been. It feels roughly the same except you have tons more options and there's actual combos in the game. Everyone also seems to deal more damage which really makes the gameplay more intense. I won't comment on the gameplay much further in this review as I don't think I've played enough to know the specific pros/cons fully.- The Story is most definitely a step up from MK11... for the most part. I'd say around 70% of it is the best storymode we've had since MK9 but they made some really bad narrative decisions near the end. What I will say though is that they executed those bad plot points in the best way possible so it was still somewhat enjoyable, just not as enjoyable as it could have been if they went a different route. Overall still lands on my positive list.- The graphics are amazing, I don't think anyone was expecting otherwise. There definitely isn't as big of a jump between this and MK11 compared to previous entries and you could definitely make the argument that MK11 looks better in certain instances but MK1 certainly isn't a downgrade. The stage design is phenomenal.- Roster of characters, splitting this up into two sections as the other part lands on the negative list but onto the positive! The roster itself is most definitely the best we've had since MK9. Almost every single character included is either a fan favourite, a character we haven't seen in ages which everyone has wanted back or a staple. I'd argue there's one or two duds but even they were made much more interesting in this release so I'm not mad.- The character design/aesthetic feels like it's gone back to it's mortal kombat roots, everyones appearance has a very fantasy/whimsical/majestic/ninja sort of feel which is exactly what mortal kombat always should've been visually. No more overly futuristic armour, special forces or injustice looking creatures that don't look like they belong in the mk universe (I'm looking at you Cetrion).- Roster size. There is 22 characters to choose from, 23 if you include Shang Tsung but he shouldn't be counted as he is dlc. This roster size does not feel small but it is smaller than previous releases which is always going to be a downgrade. It's made even worse by the fact Quan Chi and Ermac were clearly intended to be base roster, only to be moved to DLC at some point during development. So not only are we getting a smaller base roster, we're going to be paying for content we were intended to already have. Big negative.- Customisation. Initially I wasn't too mad at the fewer gear slots as MK11 felt overly tedious with the amount of gear it had when most of it made little visual difference when actually fighting. However, the customisation in MK1 is VERY underwhelming. There is only 1 gear slot per character along with the base costume, and there's currently not a satisfying amount of unique pieces available. I'm not entirely sure on the exact amount of skins/gear in the game but it does seem like far fewer than MK11 and MK11 had 3x the gear anyways. Custom intro/outro animations are also completely missing.- Intro Dialogues. They've been cut from a 3-way interaction to just 2 so they're less entertaining. Not only that but they do not appear in towers, invasions or most other modes.- Kameos. Before playing I loved the the idea of them and initially I did find them fun but they very quickly turned boring/frustrating. To start with there's not many of them, you'd think we'd get at least the same amount of Kameos as base roster characters considering in MK11 we had a huge selection of additional moves for custom variations ...but nope, there's only 15 so there's not as much variation gameplay-wise as there really should be. Then there's how kameos actually function, there's just 4 very basic moves which you can use in kombos which is fun but the vast majority of the time theyre just used for some really cheesy strats/spam which is not engaging gameplay.- Invasions. This has to be one of the worst, if not THE worst mode in any MK game since the reboot. They basically took MK11's towers of time (which I already disliked) + krypt, smashed them together, then dumbed it down and removed any incentive to play. You literally just do fight after fight with dumb modifiers (and armour?) which takes all strategy out of the game and what's worse is 99% of the time you get nothing worthwhile for winning fights or even completing the towers. I was initially excited to at least traverse the maps as it seemed like a lot of fun exploring but there's zero interactivity to it, you just press a direction and wait for your character to walk to the next fight. It's literally just a worse version of towers of time pretending to be something else; I would take the MK11 krypt over this any day.- Lack of basic features. Biggest one for me is pinning move inputs onto the screen when practising but I know there's many others missing too which I've seen people complain about.- Shrine. SO MUCH CONCEPT ART AHHHHHH.- The store. Not sure if there's store exclusive skins which can't be earned in game yet without the premium currency but it certainly is looking that way... which ew.- Characters usage in the story. I've already touched upon the pros/negatives of the story itself but there is one additional drawback which is how many of the characters were under-utilised. Some were brainless jobbers as per netherrealm tradition but others really felt like they were missing a chapter or could have easily joined another character for a duo chapter. This does happen in every MK storymode though so I wasn't expecting any different.- 30fps menu/fatalities etc.- Minor performance issues.- Megan Foxs voice acting.Overall I would recommend this game to any competitive player looking for a well-made fighting game for online matches or casual players who are looking for some short-term fun. I would not recommend this for players who want a super engaging experience with a ton of content to keep you interested outside of online for a long time, it's simply not there.Update: After playing online/invasions a ton I can say the combat is almost flawless. Kameos definitely still are an issue which I find take away from the gameplay rather than add but they certainly don't ruin it completely. Throwing is also kind of silly as it's far too hard to predict the throw direction and combo breaking costing 3 bars is way too harsh considering how easy it is to land high damaging combos. Invasions sucks far harder than I previously thought, it gets more and more tedious & frustrating the more you play because of enemy health, braindead modifiers and CONSTANT "secret" fights or ambushes that serve no meaningful purpose.Update 2: Changing my review to negative now that we know that there's store exclusive skins with an insane price tag. This isn't a free to play game so it's extremely scummy.

_childDocuments_.review: [Insert "I've been playing Mortal Kombat since 1992 here"] I really would like to love this game, it's quite an improvement compared to MK9, MKX and MK 11. I don't even mind the grind (I've been grinding here a lot more than in all of the Tony Hawk's Pro Skater games combined) or the ridiculous kameo system which doesn't really feel like Mortal Kombat. But what really kills this game for me are the unskippale animations. Starting with the shrine which takes ages to unlock something after the koins have been spent. You always have to endure the whole sequence. After ten unlocks, you're sick of it and don't even want to have any more skins or things like that, it's just not worth the time this animation lasts.The worst though are the unskippable fatal blows... About 10 till 15 seconds where you just sit there and watch the whole animation over and over again. It wasnt that bad in MK9 with the X-Rays or the fatal blows in later installments, but in MK1, it just sucks. The animations take so long that I once walked into kitchen, grabbed a drink and went back to my PC to see the end of the fatal blow. If I want to see animations, I watch a movie, but fighting games are supposed to be action ridden.About 37 hours into the game because I can finally play a non-sucking Smoke again since MK9. And since MK9 I'm still waiting for Smoke's anthroppmorphic half-brother Flare.2/10, no recommendation.Edit: After spending another 50 hours with the game I have to take back my opinion about the grind... I DO mind it now. Almost 90 hours of playtime and I have only 2 1/2 masteries finished with the kameo characters. Since I'm only two achievements away from completion, I'd really like to get the most time consuming one. But I need 5 kameo masteries for that, so it would be another 90 hours and I don't know if I'm up to that. NRS really should fix the xp system.Another thing is the invasions mode. Sadly it's absolutely boring and repetitive, not to mention the frustrating survive levels. I've played all three seasons completely so far (except for the titan battles which suspiciously pop up when I don't have time to play) and I only got enough seasonal koins to unlock about a third of the season unlockables.Online match making is another thing. _childDocuments_.review: My first MK was MK3 that released in 1995 and I've played them all since. The campaign was a 10/10 for me, watching all the characters stories unfold into how they came to be was amazing in most areas and with the lengthy cinematic's felt like I was watching a movie at the same time, spoiler free the last cinematic was the best thing ever and brought back a flood of memories. I will admit that the design of some characters let me down (Quan Chi & Reptile for example) however, this is only an opinion and this did not change my thoughts or feelings towards the game. My 2 let downs with the game itself were playable characters and the krypt changes. Some characters that I was looking forward to playing (Jax, Goro, Kano etc) are only available as Kameos and not playable characters ( so far from what i can see anyway) However with this being a remake I understand they probably prioritised what they deemed the most important characters to set their stories which leads me to ask the question of why Sonya wasn't a playable character as she was one of the originals. My other let down that I loved in all of the recent games was the interactive krypt. Earning in game gold and going to the krypt after to unlock tombstones of my own choice, unlocking different areas and being attacked by wolves, spiders and everything grave yard like was fun and it's style is what separates it from other games that instead have an in game store which mk1 has seemed to introduce. In mk1 there is no interactive krypt just a dragon statue that burns gold and gives you a random drop, it doesn't feel as rewarding to want to replay the campaign like previous games, regardless of adding the invasion mode, I feel as though the krypt should have stayed as it would of been 1 less game that didn't have a cash grab store, I also didn't find the final battle as challenging as previous games have been and yes I played on a higher difficulty. I could go on with the list but I felt like the important ones from my perspective are covered, once again, everything stated above is just my opinion. I thoroughly enjoyed this game and I'm looking forward to seeing where the game goes from here and hope some of the mentioned changes will be made as I know I'm not the only one that feels this way.

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay, the series' bread and butter, feels like a slight step back. While the new mechanics like "Kameo Fighters" add variety, the combat system itself lacks the depth and complexity found in MK11. The transition from MK11's robust combo system to a slightly simpler one might leave veteran players yearning for more intricate juggles and special move cancels.Also a major disappointment lies in the execution of Brutalities.  Landing these gory finishing moves was a badge of honor in MK11, requiring precise timing and complex combos. In MK11, it felt like a true reward for mastering a character. Here in MK1, Brutalities are significantly easier to pull off, making them feel less like a hard-earned feat and more like a button-mashing afterthought.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this game a review that's neutral, or half-good, half-bad, but that somehow feels both too fair and too harsh at the same time. So while my review is ultimately positive, it's meant to be taken with a grain of salt. This game, like Mortal Kombat 11 before it, is unfortunately more of the same; a mostly very good game that's almost ruined by a few big, ugly flaws. I don't regret getting it and playing it, and I'm sure I'll enjoy revisiting it in the future, but I really hope NRS makes some big changes when they make Mortal Kombat 13; it's going to need some big promises they'll absolutely deliver on right out of the gate to be a day one purchase for me. Otherwise, I might just wait for when all the DLC is out and it's on sale. But, anyways, back to this game specifically.Pros:- Kameo fighter feature is fun- JCVD skin and voice for Johnny Cage- Story mode is mostly pretty good all things considered- Invasions is interesting- More single player content- Finally bringing back more of the better 3D era characters after not using them at all for almost 20 years (Nitara, Ashrah, Havik, etc.)- A lot of the fatalities are pretty cool, violent, creative, and funny- Sindel is nice again- Interesting new interpretations of several characters- Slated to have John Cena as Peacemaker- Slated to have JK Simmons as Omni-Man- Easy to get invested in most of the characters- Generally fun gameplayCons:- As cool as the Kameo fighter system is, why not just bring back tag team fighting from MK9?- Like MK11, too much content locked behind microtransations/grinding/paywall/DLC; so ridiculous- Very scummy of them to have the slated DLC MK characters be enemies you can fight in story mode right now- Two of the slated DLC guest characters are just slightly different versions of Evil Superman- They made Sub-Zero a jerk- Would've been better if they brought back more of the debut characters from MKX and MK11, especially the Kombat Kids- Story can't decide whether it wants to be a reboot, sequel, multiverse or time travel story, and buckles under the weight of the ambition of trying to juggle them allI may update this review when I've played it more and/or when all the DLC is out.If you're a die hard Mortal Kombat fan and you're sure you'll enjoy it, absolutely go ahead and get it.If you're more of a casual Mortal Kombat fan, I highly recommend getting Mortal Kombat X instead ($20 for the base game, $30 with all the DLC, and that's when it's not on sale); it's still a much better game than this one or MK11. In that case I would also recommend getting MK11 and this game when they're on sale, and for this game, when all the DLC is out.I'm glad that NRS still has enough good quality elements in their games to make them worthwhile, but I'm also still disappointed that the flaws almost make them not worth it. I really hope things improve more with Mortal Kombat 13.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Gameplay is solid. Kameo system and other gameplay mechanics are unique and cool (IMO). Rest of the game is lackluster and lacking severely compared to similar games in the genre.  Strongly recommend not purchasing or at least waiting for it to go on sale for a very reduced price.Yeah so..... Game released unfinished and took over a year to make the game an actual product worth purchasing. Please keep this in mind when reading the review. This is a product they offered for upwards of $110 USD at launch, which literally was just a pre-order of the DLC and a Jean Claude Van Damme skin for Johnny . That in an of itself is reason enough to recommend not purchasing, but there is actually so much more to discuss.PROS:- Gameplay:  The gameplay is actually really solid. I really appreciated NRS going back to their old meter system, where you earn you meter throughout the match and brought back the breaker system, while keeping the flawless block mechanic, while also introducing new mechanics like the 'up block' and 'uppercut jump cancel'. The Kameo system (IMO) is actually pretty cool. Although its not perfect, I still like how kameos add a unique way to approach certain match ups and offers different tech and setups for the main fighters.CONS:- Lack of single player content:  Story mode, Towers, or Invasions (which is Towers, BUT DIFFERENT!). That is your MK 1 single player experience. Story mode can be finished in like 2-3 sessions. First half of story was promising but second half was utter trash. It read like they consulted ChatGPT on how to finish the script.  Towers is, well, towers and Invasions... *SIGH* If you know, you know.- Lack of customization: I'm not big on customizing characters or whatever. But for people who do value it, it is a big step down from what you had in MK 11. Most of the content has to be earned by grinding invasions for hours and hours (ew) or is hidden behind micro transactions.  MK 1 is the Overwatch 2 of fighting games. But even OW 2 is free to play.- Lack of online features:  There are two subcategories here. 1) Features that were missing at launch and have since been added (at least in some part), and 2) Features that are still not available that reasonably should be. 1) Cross-play between PC and Console, a way to deny playing against wireless players in ranked, a way to pin moves from the movelist in training mode.2) An *actual* matchmaking filter system for both ranked and player matches, KOTH room matchmaking, Player room matchmaking, online training mode, an ability to choose a KOTH lobby.All the features above are present in ALL other big name fighting game titles. I recently purchased Under Night In-Birth 2, which is a small anime fighter produced from a significantly smaller company with way less resources and even that game has more comprehensive matchmaking features than MK1.- Constant bugs and connectivity issues:  Matchmaking in this game was absolutely horrible on PC only until very recently. There was a period of time (MONTHS of time) where basically every other ranked set you played ended in desynchronization and forced players back into the online main menu, which meant the matches you just played didn't count. During this time you'd be lucky to get one complete set every five/six sets played. The game also launched with 'Player 1 advantage', which basically meant certain combos could only be performed on player 1 side. This advantage hasn't occurred since MK 9. Even in current day, the overall online experience is underwhelming. Even in games that are listed at >50ms, I still run into lag spikes and latency issues, almost every single game. I run wired 700ms down / 50ms up consistently. For a game that runs a funded series for competitive players, they sure seem to be lacking the resources to add sufficient servers for online play (which is where 99.9% of the players actually play).CONCLUSION:  Although the game play is a huge step up from MK 11 and is fun to play most of the time, the rest of the game is just lacking in so many ways. I've run the cycle of: Uninstall because game is uninteresting atm --> see new DLC and update announced --> reinstall and play for about 3 days --> get bored and repeat step 1. Given NRS's recent track record with MK 11 and now MK 1, its safe to say I would not recommend buying the base game nor buying the upcoming expansion DLC ($50 USD, LMAO). I would recommend you try another fighting game instead or just purchase any of the other previous NRS titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Kombat 1 is the worst game of NetherRealm Studios and the least enjoyable one in the franchise in my opinion. I only recommend it to players who like to spam attacks and abuse mechanics or mazochists who likes to be at the receiving end of it.The single player content is lacking. The cinematic Story is good, nothing extraordinary we haven't seen yet but it does its job. Towers have absolutely nothing new, only the usual ones. Invasions is absolutly the worst thing I've ever encountered with in a fighting game. A dull, boring grind fighting the same characters over and over again. Roster characters have stupid nicknames, you fight Chilly Brother and Snowy Brother and Winter Master Sub-Zeros to cover the fact that you fight the same character 10 times in a single Mesa and you have to complete 6 of them. And you achieve nothing but unlock slightly modified skins with different color palettes or reskinned gear pieces. Customization is nowhere near what it was in MK11, let alone Tekken 8. You can recolor your character and change one gear piece and that's it.Any kind of unique skin is locked into Premium Shop that require Dragon Crystals. You can earn some ingame for leveling up but apart from that you're forced to buy them for additional money or you can't unlock Premium content. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's an ok MK game, but a step back from MK11 on almost every front. Overall it's a fun game, but clearly was rushed and simply isn't able to match the focus and quality they've managed to reach with 11. I was hoping that this game would build on the success of MK11 and essentially be MK11+, however NRS decided to take a different route and completely changed how the game plays. Where MK11 was more deliberate, focused more on tactics and mind games, MK1 prioritizes memorizing long combo strings and just whacking away at your opponent. Often a round comes down to just landing 2-3 combos. The customization is also a massive step back, you have only one gear piece + one skin slot (with multiple color palettes), it just feels rushed and unfinished. One thing I absolutely love is the addition of so many 3D era characters to the roster, they fit right in and feel like a breath of fresh air. However the character designs are a mixed bag in general:- Some are really cool! Smoke and Li Mei for example look amazing! - Others are downright ugly and not in a good way, I don't even know what they were thinking with those. - There are some that look ok but have weirdly similar faces to the point that it's hard to tell them apart in closeup shots. I suspect NRS decided to cut corners by only using a few mocap actors for the whole roster and had to make the faces similar so they'll be compatible with mocap data. Variations are gone now, instead we have kameo characters, essentially extra moves and combo extenders you can equip in form of classic MK characters who just run into the screen punch your opponent and run away. It looks as goofy as it sounds and adds a lot of unnecessary visual clutter. With Kenshi's ability to summon a ghost you theoretically can have a situation where you have as many as six characters on screen at the same time.The towers of time and the krypt are also gone, replaced with the new Invasions mode that is just an absolute drag. It's essentially a board game style map where you move your character from point to point and have single round fights in hopes of unlocking something decent. Animations are both a step forward and backward at the same time, overall animations are a lot more polished and smooth than in 11, however... - All the cutscenes, fatalities, fatal blows are locked to 30fps. - There's this weird anime style slowdown and yellow flash on the final hit, very obnoxious and out of place. - Hitboxes are weird, with a lot of stuff connecting when it obviously shouldn't. - There's also some recycled animations from 11, not a deal breaker but for someone who played a lot of 11 it can be jarring to see Havik use Baraka moves for example. - The three line intro dialogues from 11 have been replaced with two lines and buried so deep that it's outside of an average player's gameplay loop. Really sad about this, these were hilarious and amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Chinese Chow Mein RecipeIngredientsFor the Chow Mein:8 ounces chow mein noodles (or thin egg noodles)2 tablespoons vegetable oil1 onion, thinly sliced2 garlic cloves, minced1 bell pepper, thinly sliced2 carrots, julienned2 cups cabbage, shredded1 cup bean sprouts1/2 cup snow peas (optional)1 cup cooked chicken, beef, shrimp, or tofu (optional)2 green onions, choppedFor the Sauce:1/4 cup soy sauce2 tablespoons oyster sauce1 tablespoon hoisin sauce1 tablespoon sesame oil1 teaspoon sugar1/4 teaspoon white pepper1/4 cup chicken broth (or water)Instructions1. Prepare the Noodles:Cook the chow mein noodles according to the package instructions. Drain and set aside.If using fresh chow mein noodles, blanch them in boiling water for 2-3 minutes until they are al dente. Drain and set aside.2. Prepare the Sauce:In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, oyster sauce, hoisin sauce, sesame oil, sugar, white pepper, and chicken broth. Set aside.3. Stir-Fry the Vegetables:Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.Add the onion and garlic, and stir-fry for about 1 minute until fragrant.Add the bell pepper, carrots, cabbage, and snow peas (if using). Stir-fry for about 3-4 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.4. Add the Noodles and Protein:Push the vegetables to the sides of the wok and add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil in the center.Add the cooked noodles and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, mixing them with the vegetables.Add the cooked chicken, beef, shrimp, or tofu (if using), and mix well.5. Add the Sauce:Pour the sauce over the noodles and vegetables.Stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes until everything is well coated with the sauce and heated through.6. Add Bean Sprouts and Green Onions:Add the bean sprouts and green onions to the wok.Stir-fry for an additional 1 minute.7. Serve:Remove from heat and transfer the chow mein to a serving platter.Serve hot and enjoy your homemade Chinese chow mein!This recipe can be customized with your favorite vegetables and proteins. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: This is not Mortal Kombat. Well, it's definitely not the Mortal Kombat I've known and loved. It resembles nothing to the originals or classics or just other iterations. The story is literally laughable at times. Such as when Madam Bo gets beat up. That scene made me burst out laughing. Same with the ice cube scene at the bar table. I guess you could say that's a good thing in a sense. But in other areas or aspects the story is just laughable and makes no sense. I'm not even that far and I'm already disliking the story and it's timeline. The voice acting is 50/50. Sometimes it's good. Sometimes it's not, depending on the actor or actress. Compared to previous titles the acting is obviously way better but since when was Mortal Kombat ever really taken seriously for their story? I miss the old MK9 voice actors. Let's move on to the designs. They're bad. Every female character is basically ugly. Are they females? I can't even tell. The only exception here is Nitara and Sindel. The costumes don't even take damage. The female costumes are not aesthetically pleasing to the eye. Since when did Mortal Kombat care about censorship? What happened to the old costumes for the females that made Mortal Kombat, Mortal Kombat? NRS and WB's last two iterations of this game has ruined this franchise in more ways than just the costumes. The last good Mortal Kombat in terms of female costume designs is MK9. The only good thing about the costume designs now is that there are variations and pallettes, that's about it.  Performance? Atrocious. Did they even bother to try this out? I highly doubt it. It's obviously a console port and it clearly shows. Terrible performance all around. 30 and 60 fps locks during certain animations such as x-rays. The game has terrible micro stuttering issues. Even when disabling E cores in the BIOS the game still micro stutters. Sure it helped a bit but wow. I can't believe anyone is actually praising this faulty product and it's horrible performance. Like they have the audacity to charge us 10 extra dollars for this. Why? Where's the justification? It's clearly not in terms of performance and or quality. Just browsing through the main menu is bad and stutters. Going from movie cut-scenes to actual game play looks horrible and stutters as well. Even the big fire dragon logo during invasions stutters. I'm so glad I didn't pay for this and received this as a gift. Gameplay? Repetitive. The controls seem wonky and broken at times. Command inputs seem to be delayed or not registering at times. It's been like this in every Mortal Kombat game. Input delay and commands feel sluggish and broken and this is offline. It could also be the fact that I'm not use to it and haven't played MK in a long time. Sure the combat mechanics resemble the best Mortal Kombat game ever created which is 9 but this game is far from that masterpiece. Some characters seem lackluster compared to previous titles and some are just overpowered like Kenshi and Ashrah. I do however like the idea of Invasions. It's a nice new feature that I do seem to be enjoying. Online is still a joke and seems to have so much lag and delay in terms of inputs and during the character selection screen. Game doesn't even have an anti cheat and macro users exist. Where's cross play? Where are the rooms? Why did this get taken away? Is it because in every half baked console port you throw out on this platform, it's been broken? Why is there even a store? Way to try and squeeze every dime possible out of your fans. I'm slightly disappointed.It also seems that QLOC can't port a game to save their lives. Considering every Mortal Kombat launched on this platform has been horrible.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're only interested in multiplayer then you can buy it, although I don't know if it's worth it at full price (quite small base roster for such an expensive game). Future dlc's will not be cheap, and the developers/publishers are very greedy. The game also currently does not have a cross-platform feature, and it is unknown if this will be implemented on PC.If you're interested in singleplayer modes, story and MK lore then wait for big sales because it's not worth it.My impressions:--- Corporate greed. Horribly expensive game with tons of dlc and ingame paid items store. Even for additional fatalities you have to pay extra. Wish they were so willing to make free content, QoL and balance changes (which don't come out too often).--- The final 25% of the story effectively cured me of the desire to play this mode in future games of the series. My hype was brutally murdered. Marvel comics garbage tier story.--- Too many single-player features require an Internet connection. (There are also situations for example you're in the 9th battle in the arcade tower, and you lose your connections, and you are forced to go back to the main menu.) Terrible treatment of single-player gamers.--- Updates are very rare, and this game badly needs them. The developers are more focused on releasing expensive skins.-- Netcode is more unstable than in 11. Frequent termination of ranked sets due to connection problems. At the same time the game has longer ranked sets than before (3 wins needed). Great job developers.-- Important characters from story mode will be released in a paid dlc, in the future!-- Wasted cameo potential in story mode. Instead of roster characters it's some elementals and other nonsense. If cameo roster characters like Darrius appear they are mute.-- 30fps in menu, cutscenes etc. I hate that!-- Roster is too small.-- The awful appearance of some of the characters, especially some of the women (AND Ermac). Quite a few are too old, especially Tanya looks terrible (I miss the design from MK10 or 4). Sindel and Li-Mei look like they are sisters. Kitana's lips are stuffed with botox. The best looking is Sonia, who is just a cameo! Even Cage's ex-wife from story mode, who appears for about 30 seconds, looks prettier than most of the women in this game! WTF!- Megan Fox's voice acting is atrocious. She ruined my immersion during the story mode. Even Ronda Rousey in MK 11 was better than this "professional actor".- Smoke in story mode was a jobber and didn't even have his own chapter. What a joke!- Lots of unclimatic and mismatched character costumes (just like MK11).- Single-player modes are again focused on boring grind. It's more of a chore than entertainment. The challenge tower from MK9 was much more entertaining than that.- Rain is less fun than the classic 2D or from MK9.- There is no pre-fight talk in arcade mode. What a joke.- Cameos didn't even get endings in arcade mode.- Using Shrine is horribly slow. What kind of moron came up with the idea that you can only spend 1000 coins at a time and have to look at a very long animation every time?* I've heard a lot of bad things about the state of the PC port, but personally I haven't had any problems on mid tier hardware. I have 60fps on max settings. Apparently, it's a very individual thing, and the game sometimes runs better on an average computer than on the high-end.++ Aerial combat. I liked it in MK7, and here it is much better done. Probably the biggest plus of gameplay in this game for me.+ Gameplay is noticeably better than in 11 but still similar (unfortunately). I prefer MK10 and 9.+ Before marvel garbage started, the story mode was good (definitely better than MK11 and 10).+ Some of the easter eggs and references to older games were cool.+ A lot of people complain about the length of the story mode, but I have the impression that it is longer than in previous games. + It's cool that Repitle and Baraka weren't such jobbers as usual and they were easy to like in the storymode. I like also the human part of the Reptile design, he looks cool!+ Longer and more enjoyable combos than in 11. Although I would prefer a longer combos without cameos.+ The return of many characters from the 3D era. + I'm also glad to see Motaro's presence (better cameo than nothing).+ No Kombat Kids and Special Forces for this time. Thank the gods!

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, the only thing holding me back from recommending this game is the steam version run so poorly still as of this day. I have the latest and greatest available in gaming GPU and Processor, and no matter what in-game or external graphical and CPU tweaks I can make, the current version still has constant micro-stutters and frame drops across all combat modes offline and online. It just doesn't get a smooth frame rate, regardless if you trying to get 60fps or 30 fps, low or ultra high settings, no change at all in the games performance. At least in my experience.Excluding that key detriment, MK1 has enough of what i'd expect in a fighting game to say it's a good game. The recent MK series inclusion of a cinematic single player story mode is a great enjoyment for myself. Is MK1's story the best written thing out there, not at all, but is it still enjoyable, Of course. If i move away from writing a review and just giving a personal opinion MK story really needs a big bad guy/threat, that feels like a big bad guy/threat. Kronika from MK11 didn't really have the sauce, but it was someone new. MK1's story kind is just a vehicle to ret-con the ret-con, but it's a story none the less, which is enough to tickle my fancy, and the cinematic's look fantastic. The realism of the character models blows my smooth brain.MK1 being an Assist fighter isn't my most favorite thing in the world, but fighting games change mechanics from game to game all the time. It adds a small bit of variety when fooling around with your favorite characters, and doesn't really hurt the game, other that an individuals own idea on what MK should be, which is everyone's own personal flavor. Excluding talks of balancing and effects on the "meta" may vary your experience with the assist mechanic, but I'm not going to EVO anytime soon, so it doesn't factor to much into my experience. I would love to get back to dedicated single character fighting, with a larger roster of MK characters, less special guest from the VHS's of my youth, but I can always dream of a better future and still enjoy the effort put into the MK1 we have.The only real bad part of the gameplay loops for me, excluding performance, is the Invasion mode, which is the single player live service model. For myself, the board game variant of a tower of time that is Invasion just does nothing for me. As someone who would play any mode to get a breather from getting my butt whooped in online versus, Invasion actively deters me from wanting to play it. Why that is, i couldn't tell you, this is a fighting game, and you fight in Invasion just like you would any other CPU mode, but something about it immediately makes me want to play another game. Even though it feels like such a drag to go through an Invasion season's content, in reality in only take a couple of hours to do the entire seasons content, then you have a month or more of waiting for the next season. I assume it was an active choice for Invasions to just feel bad to play, to where as you only want to spend 8-10 minutes a session doing Invasions, and which point you would have a "seasons" worth of content, as you torture your way through it lol. As of today I have completed 1 invasion season of the however many have been available since release, solely due to it's hard to convince yourself you're having fun while doing it. It may not rub you the same way it did me, but it is by far the worst alternative game mode of modern MK titles. I'm sure it's no small feat trying to construct alternative game modes to a fighting game but Invasion's, for me, seems like the bottom of the barrel of ideas that got floated around the office.Hopefully future optimization's for the PC port fix the actual performance of the game, at which point I say "buy MK1, you'll have a good time" but as of today i spend more time tweaking and benchmarking hoping to get a smooth consistent 60 fps than i do actually getting to enjoy the game. As my 4090 and 9950X can't seem to get that with the current version of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Back in the day, I used to play a lot of Mortal Kombat on the classic arcade machines (along with  and ), so I feel really lucky to have seen how this series has evolved throughout the years. Developed once again by NetherRealm Studios, guided by the legendary Ed Boon, Mortal Kombat 1 is a brand new reboot that follows the events of  and improves the core structures of the gameplay without reinventing the wheel. Old and new fans can find a completely new story mode that is very intriguing and extremely curated, featuring classic cinematic cutscenes and deadly QTEs. Without going into massive spoilers (in case you haven’t played the Aftermath expansion yet), the plot starts with one of the main characters taking control of time and resetting the timeline, creating a new universe where everyone has different roles. The story is divided into 15 chapters, and each one focused on a specific character, allowing you to discover their origins while also learning their different moves. Actually, the story mode is a really good place for new players who want to learn and practice combat while having fun. There is, of course, a separate detailed tutorial mode, but the story mode should probably be the first step for many players. Compared to the story mode of the previous games, which was essentially built as a way to present all the characters in the fastest way possible, the narration in MK1 is much slower, with longer cutscenes and well-written dialogues, jokes and twists.The game also introduces the new Invasion mode, which is basically a single-player board game with very soft RPG mechanics. You pick up a character and a companion (known as kameo) and you progress through different tiles in a semi-open world. Each tile has different fights, mini-games, challenges and of course rewards waiting to be unlocked. The latter can be specific for the Invasion Mode but also apply to other modes, like in the case of cosmetics (gear, skins, fatalities, color palettes etc.). You can also level up your character with different stats as well upgrade your talismans and purchase consumables. The Invasion mode is clearly meant to be end-game content, but also works as a live service format. Every six weeks there will be a new seasonal update, featuring different storylines and scenarios. While it certainly looks like a clever way to keep players engaged for a long time, I found this mode to be rather repetitive and too simple with its RPG mechanics. It also feels a bit grindy that you can only unlock everything either by paying (through microtransactions) or by spending a lot of time with each character in order to unlock all they have, including their fatalities. In comparison, the recent  mode works much better, perfectly tying together story, characters and live service content. There are other modes in MK1, such as the classic offline PvE towers with various difficulties, and online PvP modes (ranked and casual), which don’t include any surprises.The MK1 roster includes many historic characters from the series, such as Scorpion, Sub-Zero, Johnny Cage, Raiden, Kitana, Baraka and others. This time, they are assisted by Kameo fighters who can be summoned during fights to unleash their special attacks. These allies can be selected through a different list that also includes iconic characters such as Sonya, Stryker, Cyrax and Motaro, who come with their own fatalities and cosmetics to unlock. While the Kameo addition is certainly refreshing and fun (especially if used to chain combos), I felt a bit disappointed that none of these fighters are playable, because I used to play with many of them (especially Motaro in ). That said, combat hasn’t changed much from the previous title, being always brutal and gory, with spectacular fatalities closing each fight. Perhaps movements feel a bit slower this time, which improves coordination for less skilled players. Overall, it’s an easy-to-learn-hard-to-master kind of combat system, in which longer combos require good practice and skill.Graphically speaking, the game is simply gorgeous, especially the character models which look better than the previous game and more realistic. It’s so beautiful that transitioning from cutscenes to fights during story mode feels truly smooth and immersive. The performance is generally good, though I experienced a few sudden frame drops in some scenarios. I also ran into an annoying bug, a black screen randomly appearing while moving through the main menu. I couldn’t find any solution for this, so my only option was to constantly restart the game each time it happened. Story and gameplay-wise, Mortal Kombat 1 is a successful reboot. It’s intriguing, gory and beautifully detailed. Like every new beginning, it needs time to get used to, but the DNA is still the same. NetherRealm Studios didn’t reinvent the wheel and perhaps was too afraid of making drastic changes (like Capcom did with ), but at least they built a valid starting point for a new universe. Most importantly, the combat still delivers a brutal and satisfying experience that fans of fighting games will definitely enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: This latest instalment in the franchise has something special for every Mortal Kombat enthusiast. It not only breathes new life into cherished fan favorites but also resurrects characters from the 3D era, infusing each one with rich, multi-layered backstories that add depth to their motivations, rivalries, and loyalties.What's really cool about this game is how it manages to straddle the line between catering to die-hard fans with nods to the past and delivering a brand-new experience. If you're new to the series, don't sweat it – you can jump right in without needing a history lesson on previous games. Everything is explained, No reservations needed!Now, let's talk gameplay. It's like a well-choreographed dance – smooth, fast, and super responsive. They've cranked up the tempo from Mortal Kombat 11, which some folks (me included) found a bit slower compared to the earlier games, notably MKX. I found the Kameo system to be a little weird, I much prefer the 1 to 1 kombat or tag-team modes but Kameos left something to be desired, at least for me.I have to also say, I REALLY MISS THE KRYPT!!!!!!!!!!!!The graphics are mind-blowing. NetherRealm has always been a visual powerhouse, and this time, they've outdone themselves. I'm talking every muscle twitch, every wrinkle, and even the gory details of the fatalities – it's all there. Watching the story mode feels like you're at the movies, but it's way more intense. I played it on my PC, it looked stunning.Speaking of the story, it's my personal favourite in a while. It's got a gripping plot that's easy to follow – no more head-scratching over weird twists like in some of the earlier games.And the voice acting? Top-notch, except for Nitara (Megan Fox, really?) Nitara has a flat performance that sounds like she's reading off a sheet instead of embodying a character. These other actors however, nail their roles and performances and really bring the characters to life in a relatable way.In a nutshell, this game is a whole new level of awesome. It's now my go-to way to experience Mortal Kombat, whether they're building on the old or tearing it down for a fresh start. It's like Mortal Kombat on steroids, and I'm loving every minute of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin... This game is over priced, under developed, poorly optimized and likely the worst MK title to date. I say that with a heavy heart as I have been a fan for over 30 years. I will say that the story actually wasn't bad in my opinion, and that not everything is bad in the game(for the most part it is tho). The main concern here is how horribly the game runs and the clear lack of passion that went into the project. MK11 may in fact be the last decent MK game to ever be made. I am baffled that they thought that this game was worth full price. I personally feel cheated, as there was never a MK release that could have prepared fans for this travesty. Mk11 ran better (this game has frame issues when playing solo and MK11 never did). Mk11 had more cosmetic customization, more characters (even on launch),  and the online play was much more stable, although that may have a lot to do with the fact that the game only runs at 30 frames because making money is now more important than putting out a good product. I wish I had pirated the game so that I could rob them the way that they robbed their fan base. This may seem a bit dramatic, but as a professional in the tech industry, I would be ashamed to have my name in the credits for a game that blatantly was put out before it was actually finished. At best, it feels like the game is still in Alpha. The developers should do the right thing and pull the product until it is done. side note - who ever approved Megan Fox's voice lines needs to find a new job. If you are going to use voice actors, make sure they are good. She isn't even that good at acting. Adding her to the game made the release feel even cheaper somehow.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, I like this game. It's a blast when it works, it has a surprising amount of depth when you consider both characters and kameos, and it's incredibly fun to play and figure things out. But, it has too many issues at the current moment for me to actually recommend the game. It's unpolished and it shows, with a multitude of online issues (frame drops, constant crashes, freezes) alongside a bunch of bugs that make the experience of playing worse. For example, many of the brutality inputs are broken, and a large amount of the displayed frame data is just flat out wrong. While those issues don't severely impact the gameplay itself, it still demonstrates the fact that the game probably could've used another month in development. The larger issues however are the crashes and freezes mentioned earlier. These are pretty frequent, and about half the online matches that I play either crash at the beginning or end, or just randomly disconnect throughout. And you can tell that it isn't the opponent disconnecting themselves, because there's an ingame function where the opponent is supposed to literally explode if they manually disconnect. Additionally, the online play itself seems very limited, with the player search area being quite small and the connection/delay itself being mediocre when compared to other fighting games released recently (Guilty Gear Strive, Street Fighter 6, etc). There are also a few issues, which I'm not sure may just be on my end, where the loading screens seem to take way too long (like when clicking kustomize on the main menu), but that might be my hardware (although the fact that you have to reload the stage, which can take up to 30 seconds, every single time when completing character trials seems redundant to me). Again, I want to reiterate that the game is fun, and when it works I forget about the issues very easily. However, with the frequent crashes and such I can't recommend buying the game in it's current state if you want to primarily play online. Maybe in time the majority of the issues will be fixed, but as of now my experience when playing the game is severely hindered.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 55.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you NetherRealm Studios.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin...? I'm an MK fan, but I gotta admit, NRS fumbled the bag real badly with this one. I enjoyed MK11 a lot and I think it was a worthy successor of the franchise. I know a lot of people hated it, thinking it was bland and more restricted compared to MKX, but at least it had good online play, tons of content, loads of customization, and a variety of game modes. MK1 brings nothing new to the table, or does it? Okay, let's talk about the elephant in the room... Kameos. This is one of the dumbest ideas I've seen in a fighting game, ruining the essence of MK's nature - 1v1 Kombat to this weird hybrid of tag team. Instead of 2v2, it's still 1v1, but both players use a main character and a side character? A very bizarre choice, but the mechanic is badly implemented too. Moves that are unsafe can now become safe on block when you cancel into a kameo, and it's insanely boring to play against or even use. It definitely feels a bit spammy as well. Special moves or combo strings that are unsafe have a reason for it - maybe it's a launcher, maybe it resets the opponent, maybe it extends the combo for more damage. This means the high risk - high reward is thrown out the window with this new kameo system. This mechanic is so bland and flawed that it turns laughable at some point.As for the base gameplay itself, I genuinely like it. They got rid of the bad things from MK11 and fixed them in this one. No more krushing blows (I still liked some of them, but the requirements were frustrating and unbalanced, especially the 50/50 failed grab ones). No more breakaway. Fatal Blows now start an animation before the hit, meaning players can predict better and punish more effectively, making it less spammy. Lastly, characters in this game don't need offensive meter to begin combos. I see all of this as a plus for me. I enjoy a more rushed-down aggressive playstyle as opposed to the more strategic, zoning, and slow pace from MK11.You only have pretty much 3 game modes as I write this review: Story, Invasions, and lastly Towers. The Towers are the same old classic arcade ladder. Story works exactly the same since MK9 - each character has their own chapter and the fight ends, cinematic begins, etc. Lastly, THE new game mode: Invasions. It's so awful, how do I even describe this? It's a Map fighter with some elements of RPG, and you go ahead and fight against CPU opponents with modifiers that mostly came from MK11. Whose idea was this? It's insanely boring, and it gets old pretty quickly. At some point, I need to take a break and stop playing Invasions because of how boring it is. Now let's talk about the problems with the PC Port. How can we in 2024 have companies that launch games at 30fps, but oh, "the 30fps create a cinematic feel". It's stupid and very out of touch with today's standards of technology. If Tekken 8 can run at 60fps on every platform, absolutely MK1 can run at 60fps on PC (and consoles). This is laziness at its peak. And with all of that, there you go, that's MK1 - people pay 70€ (or more if you want DLCs) to have this unfinished and broken game. I genuinely think the MK franchise will die once more like Armageddon unless NRS makes a drastic move and changes the game entirely. Maybe add more game modes? Create a second versus mode with Kameos disabled? Mini-games? Even the Krypt is missing, for F*** sakes. Also, why can't Test Your Might be played by 2 players like in MKX? This is such a waste of opportunity. I want nothing but success for this franchise, but I really have to put this game's review as negative. MK9, MKX and MK11 are 100% superior games to play as opposed to MK1.At the moment, I'm cutting off completely with this franchise...

_childDocuments_.review: So smooth and beautiful, tons of stuff to do even if you prefer offline play and a well thought out and intersting roster with lots of smart changes and reboots of attacks and characters. If you never played a fighting game before you gotta try this one, if you already played a ton of fighting games and love them like i do, this game to me personally is the best fighting game ever made. Highly recommended for literally everyone.The roster changed a lot since MK 11, if you played 11's story mode you'll immediately know why it all changed if you don't it's fine since it's a completely new start in itself. The new versions of the well known characters and also the new characters are all worth the reboot. If you liked the crazy story of MK 11, this game goes even deeper and fleshes out every one of the main roster in a thrilling almost movie-like manner which gives the characters a ton of personality thanks to the insanely talented actors and writers behind it. And if you miss the old character designs, you can still select a lot of them as a Kameo character - which is an assist character on cooldown jumping in for you on a button and direction press.The fighting game mechanics themselves go all out, more than MK 11 did. You can do massive damage with combos, the game moves faster than 11 did and thanks to all this the rounds are over a lot quicker while still providing enough room for people to play very elaborately and aren't forced into a speed rush. A huge plus in my book.But the biggest and best change for me personally is the game's style. Mortal Kombat always was top notch when it came to graphic fidelity in fighting games and character design but MK1 takes the cake. Everyone looks cool and interesting and could be a comic book hero or villain for themselves, none of the fighters look like they don't belong or aren't up to the standards of everyone else and as a first for Mortal Kombat everything is a lot more colorful. There's still dark and gritty character skins, stages and moments, but color definately is more present than it ever was before in a Mortal Kombat game.And the classic towers are back, together with them counting as their own little story modes per character. The seasonal and "spiced up" content from MK 11's towers, that breaks away from the competitive online nature, went to a new mode called "Invasions", which also inlcudes the former crypt's puzzles and chests, which thanks to this is now an actual loot system in a more RPG style experience with elemental damage, character stats you can level up yourself, gear with stats and armor moves which can only be broken by using certain attacks in a certain timing, boss enemies and what ever else you expect from a RPG where the combat consists of solid fighting game mechanics is found in "Invasions".As i said, this is now my favorite fighting game, i hope it becomes yours too. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Mortal Kombat has been a staple in the fighting game community for over three decades, often praised for its innovative mechanics and iconic characters. However, the latest installment, Mortal Kombat 1, while ambitious, falls short of the series’ legacy.The introduction of the Kameo system, intended to add depth and variety, instead introduces a layer of complexity that detracts from the core experience. The system allows characters to break the traditional rules of the game, leading to unpredictable and often unbalanced gameplay. This unpredictability can be frustrating for players who prefer a more controlled and strategic fighting environment.Moreover, the removal of character variations, wake-up attacks, and rolls simplifies the game to its detriment, stripping away layers of strategy that players have come to appreciate in previous titles. The decision to eliminate krushing blows also removes a dynamic aspect of combat that added excitement to matches.The single meter for enhanced moves and the changes to fatal blows, while intended to streamline combat, instead make it feel less impactful. The new air combo system, although it allows for more damage without spending meter, often leads to repetitive and unengaging fights.Graphically, the game is a mixed bag. While some character models and environments are beautifully rendered, others seem rushed and lack the polish expected from a AAA title. The story mode, usually a highlight of Mortal Kombat games, is drawn-out and grindy, failing to captivate with its narrative.The online experience, a crucial component of any modern fighting game, feels outdated. The lack of robust online modes and features is a significant step back from previous entries, which offered a more comprehensive online suite.In conclusion, Mortal Kombat 1’s attempt to innovate results in a game that feels unrefined and unbalanced. The Kameo system, while novel, adds unnecessary complexity, and the removal of established mechanics simplifies the game too much. With an underwhelming story and an online mode that fails to meet current standards, Mortal Kombat 1 is a title I cannot recommend to fans of the series or newcomers looking for a solid fighting game experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to start... Huge disappointment. Unfortunately, MK1 is a step back in so many ways.Story:The story starts off promising, but quickly gets ruined by the series' classic time-traveling and alternate realities gimmick. Instead of a new and interesting boss, we get four versions of each character from different dimensions. What was the point of the reboot if we're back to square one, mixing up timelines until it's nauseating?Customization:I was expecting the ideas from MK11 to be expanded upon, but unfortunately, customization here is much more simplified and feels forced.Gameplay:The gameplay is simplified compared to previous installments, with no arena interactions, Kameo characters having only three moves each, and quickly becoming annoying. The combat system has deteriorated rather than evolved. Unfortunately, it's hard to take this game seriously. Weak character balance, Kameo, and a comically low number of moves you can execute.Censorship:With each new installment, the female characters (and now male characters too) are dressed more modestly. Once, the female fighters in the series were attractive and scantily clad - that started to change from MKX, and here we see the consequences. The game has lost all its edginess, and spark. There aren't even any Johnny romances. If it weren't for the gory fatalities (exceptionally weak in this installment), the game could have a 13+ rating.Atmosphere:It's sad to say, but the game doesn't resemble Mortal Kombat. The entire dark, gritty atmosphere has been replaced by colorful locations, shallow characters, and artificial politeness that oozes from every dialogue.Graphics:Gorgeous, meticulously detailed graphics. Beautiful lighting, character geometry, and arena detail. But what's the point when there are serious performance issues all the time, not just during gameplay but even during cutscenes? It effectively kills the joy of playing.Candy-coated, censored Mortal Kombat. Who would have thought that we would live to see such sad times?

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, Mortal Kombat 1, where the blood is as thick as the plot and the characters have more depth than my last attempt at a paddling pool. This game is a classic, a digital dojo where you can settle your differences without having to explain to the police why your neighbor is suddenly afraid of the color red.First off, let’s address the elephant in the room – and no, I’m not talking about Goro, though he could probably bench press an elephant. This game is the reason half of us got grounded in the 90s. "Too violent," they said. "It'll warp your mind," they claimed. Joke's on them, I turned out perfectly fine, and my therapist agrees...mostly.Now, onto the dad jokes, because nothing says "I'm going to rip your spine out" quite like a good pun:    Why did Sub-Zero refuse to go to the barbecue? He couldn’t stand the heat!    What do you call it when Scorpion wins a match? A Flawless Victory!Okay, now that you're groaning, let's sweep kick into the...Top Reasons to Play Mortal Kombat 1:    Nostalgia Trip: Take a trip down memory lane, where the graphics were as pixelated as your childhood photos. It's like a fine wine, it gets blockier with age.    Simple Pleasures: In a world where game controllers have more buttons than a NASA control panel, MK1's simple gameplay reminds us of simpler times, when all you needed for fun was a joystick and a dream.    Character Building: Literally. From Johnny Cage's ego to Raiden's god complex, each character is a PhD thesis in personality disorders. Plus, who doesn’t want to play as a ninja who can freeze stuff? That’s like the ultimate party trick.    Educational Value: Believe it or not, Mortal Kombat teaches valuable life lessons. For instance, always finish what you started...especially if it ends in an uppercut.    Because Friendship: Sure, you can rip your opponent’s heart out, but you can also choose to be a good sport with a Friendship. Who says you can't make friends while violently battling in a deathmatch?In conclusion, Mortal Kombat 1 is more than a game. It's a cultural icon, a digital rite of passage, and a testament to the timeless appeal of flying uppercuts and questionable fashion choices (looking at you, Liu Kang). So, dust off that old console, practice your button-mashing, and remember – no matter how old you get, you're never too old to yell "Get over here!" at inanimate objects. Just make sure the neighbors aren't watching.

_childDocuments_.review: The Story mode is probably the best part as it still has a solid story, but don't expect The Last of US 1 or anything its a 7/10. The problem is everything else, there is a lack of game modes, there are less characters than MK 9, 10 and 11, the customization is also lesser. I don't particularly like the addition of cameo characters, they do add another layer of depth for the game play but for most people I have spoken with they not a great addition, maybe at the higher levels of play people might like them but casuals either forget they exist of just use them as combo extenders. The long combos are still here but the tools at your disposal for defense are terrible compared to the systems in other fighting games right now. I dislike that the only way to brake out of a combo is to use your partner and that uses all of the special power, leaving you defenseless if you fall into another combo in the match. they made the grab counter a 50/50 chance for whether to press XY or AB. The point is that in this game offence is way more favored than defense which makes it feel very casual. it is less of a back and forward fight between two characters and more of "Its my turn to do my combo" than "Now it's my turn" most of your skill comes from your ability to start the combo, after that it is mostly memorization. If you like the MK franchise you will probably like this game as well, as a fan I would give this an 8/10 due to the lack of game modes and the predatory monetization with meaningless rewards. As a casual gamer I would say that its more of a 7/10 because the meat of the game is much less than in the last few games, I still think that MK10 felt better to play. MK1 is at its most enjoyable if you stick with it for a long time and master it, but then again I just think that there are a lot of other games that are more fun to master. Worth buying for $30 or less.

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could give a mixed review.The gameplay in MK1 is pretty great as far as NRS games go, and if that's genuinely all you want, I would cautiously recommend it. There’s a couple of clear winners in the roster, though, and if you want to enjoy your time with this one, you may find yourself stuck to fighters with the safest moveset. Nothing wrong with that, of course. It's a lot of fun to dust your opponents for a few hours.However, a lot of the content we've come to expect isn't here, and it's a bit strange seeing as MK11 felt like a much better -- and cheaper -- deal with how much content you got at full price.There's no Krypt this time, nor are there any *substantial* towers of time (they exist, but they're lame now, granting you nothing for completion) and the only thing to fill that void is Invasion.Invasion sucks. It's a kind of board game where you go from point-to-point (in glorious 30 FPS, I might add) to do a fight that will let you proceed and do more fights. On the way to fights, you can get ambushed with another fight, and sometimes you'll get lucky and get a Secret Fight after completing another fight, letting you do another fight. The problem is that these fights don't give you anything and there's zero variation, aside from the occasional Survive (stand still and win anyway) or Test Your Might (fill a bar by mashing buttons and then hit the trigger when the bar lowers into the right zone). There's very little to be gained here at all in terms of cosmetics, too. It pales in comparison to the 300 tier challenge tower of MK9, or the aforementioned Towers of Time from MK11, which mixed up the formula.I've also just realised I forgot to mention Talismans in Invasion, and that's because they're irritating and pointless.And to circle back to the subject of cosmetics... You can't see all the available cosmetics this time around, and the more cynical part of me suspects that's because there are no cosmetics to show us. The game feels empty because outside of the fighting there is really nothing to do, and the only use of Koins (one of many currencies in the game) is to play a slot machine. I wouldn't hate the Shrine if it actually had some interesting stuff in it, but it's padded with concept art and takes like 20 seconds a pop as you watch the same animation over and over again.(Though, watching the same animation over and over is essentially what this game is in a nutshell. Lengthy throws, lengthier Fatal Blows, lengthier-er Fatalities; it all feels much more padded this time around because sometimes you can just step away to make a coffee and come back to find you're still kicking someone's face out through their bum.)In MK11, the Krypt was a full adventure mode with secrets and puzzles that rewarded you for essentially everything you did. Here, you're not rewarded for doing anything, and that's even worse once you realise there's nothing to do anyway. There's no gameplay loop this time around, and I fear it'll hurt the longevity of this one.Most of the content comes from multiplayer now, which is all well and good, but I do miss when Mortal Kombat offered a genuinely solid single-player experience, and you just won't find that here beyond the Story Mode.The PC port is also lacking, once again. It's *fine* in places, but lacks the support, attention and communication it needs to actually be *good.*, which likely means that this game won't establish anything close to a PC playerbase, and thus your online experience will be tied to fighting the same people over and over again, before everyone leaves to play something more interesting.This game has a lifespan, like all games, but with the lack of substantial content and the shaky PC port, that lifespan will be short.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, having sunk a good deal of time into MK1 and various NetherRealm studios titles I really wish the passion that they have for their game, the art, the design, the writing, the world building, the storytelling was found even in some small part in the actual gameplay. I knew when I got the game that I was trading the experience of everything else they did with this game for the actual gameplay, because never has a game that feels this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad to play been so good... every other fighting game in existence, from Street Fighter to MVC to SNK to Guilty Gear to KOF to Skull Girls to Them's Fight'n Herds to you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ name it ALL feel so fluid and good to play, but their stories and world building are so shallow but you have fun playing them because they are designed TRULY WELL, then you have MK and the occasional Injustice title and its like man this game is pretty, so there's that...It feels like every other fighting game looked at the world of various martial arts and NetherRealm reduced the fighting experience to Rock'em Sock'em Robots, and like not even like a good one, like a busted, rusty, you gotta hit the button a few times to get a punch kinda one.It just feels like a mountain of wasted potential, I'm going to beat the game in the next few hours and then ill likely not play it very much after because to endure their controls and gameplay is akin driving a car with booted tiresI think the game can be endured for the story, but its definitely worth waiting for a sale.If NetherRealm could bring on some talent from other fighting game devs and actually consider breaking the mold that was made in 47 BC and break away from the sluggish frame data and for the love of god 4 directional inputs I mean guys 8 directional inputs are just strictly better, do you understand how much more fluid and intuitive a qcf+P for a fireball is over this [<, >, P]? Its archaic design like this that makes MK so frustrating to play in a world where your 2d fighting game experience translates from any title in the genre to any other title in the genre save for anything developed by NetherRealm. The single player mode leaves a lot to be desired, and feels like it's a truncated version of what we actually could have.It feels like WB pushed this out the door before it was truly ready. I feel like Netherrealm won't admit this, but I can't help but feel bad for them in this respect. With Zaslav at the helm of WB and the recent decisions he's been making about the direction of the company in general, a lot feels up in the air, but I hope that Netherrealm doesn't suffer the fate of other games studios, where they're gutted and their IP hoarded, but it's hard to not think that this could be the fate of a franchise like Mortal Kombat, which was along with Tekken my entry into fighting games.Verdict: Don't buy it unless you absolutely love MK.

_childDocuments_.review: Campaign: My first Mortal Kombat Campaign Playthrough and I thought that it was okay. There is not much to complain about nor much to complement besides the graphics. It does its job.Multiplayer: Aspect I spent the least time in, I can envision how this can be fun to learn the ins and outs to truly master the combat system but as a causal player this fighting game does not seem geared towards a newer player and that is perfectly fine. You get what you put into it and I am fine with not being catered to. The tutorials offered in the game are extensive but honestly I think I would learn more and get better and have more at fighting by playing a simplified fighting game and then coming back.Invasions: My least favorite part of this game and the main reason I put it towards not recommending, the issue I have is the difficulty in the game. Most of the events in Invasions are so easy that it numbs the mind of any fun and only adds dopamine in the hopes of XP gain for Kameos and Kharacters. Then comes an Invader or a mini boss of the season that causes you to engage back into the game, focus on how to best counter and fight it, use the systems of the game to stack the numbers in your favor and then it is over. Not even all the Invaders are like this but it is even more jarring when you see systems of the game used and adding fun dynamics to the game to only be thrown out once the next fight comes around. In my case, I used Omni-Man, Peacemaker, and Sub-Zero during my time and I would say maybe two or three times during my hundreds of fights in invasions did I need to worry about elemental damage what so ever, most of the time I could power through and could barely tell when I had an elemental advantage versus disadvantage. I only wish that the systems of the game were brought to their fullest potential but for what this is if you want to pour more time into this game that is not getting your face kicked in for multiplayer this is a decent way to play for your first time, I do not recommend playing more than one season. Side Note: The monetization of this game is quite odd and clearly here to make the most amount of money possible. I bought the Extra Special "give me your money" edition and I still do not have access to Shang Tsung because he was a pre-order bonus and now costs $7.99 USD for one character. I do not believe this value proposition is for the consumers benefit.I do not think I will play another new Mortal Kombat for a long time but I do appreciate the time I had with this learning to enjoy why fighting games can be so much fun. I believe that it is best to either wait for a large discount for this game or buy another game. There is always something else to play.

_childDocuments_.review: [NO SPOILERS](Written on the 18th of September, 15:51) I love this game, but the story-mode ending KINDA sucks. The first three acts do an excellent job setting up story-lines and building tension, with a plethora of exciting call-backs, twists, and set-ups. However, the final chapter only really resolves ONE of these story-lines, and it is a story-line that only really burned in the background of others. The ending felt extremely rushed, almost as if they regretted making the game a reboot, and were too impatient to wait two or three instalments down the line for their "epic finale", resulting in an unjustified ending that seems somehow to be too dramatic and astoundingly anti-climactic.It seems in the last quarter that NRS decided to switch their direction to a more Marvel-esque "multiverse-launcher" approach; but with only one game releasing every four years, I fail to understand how they expect our interest to hold for that long and maintain hype.I feel bad about being overly negative as I find the actual game-play to be fun enough, NRS brought back a lot of fun concepts from the klassic era, and I enjoy what they did with most of the characters; MK1 has taken characters that I previously cared very little for and made me like and root for them - that is very cool!But I do think that they should have spent more time on this one. I was getting so pumped up for everything they seemed to be setting up, but then was kind of sucker-punched by a rushed, below mediocre ending for the story. Additionally, as of writing this, the game has not officially released yet, I have just over 10 hours, and I have already beaten the story at 100%, and earned over half the achievements. As a game with significantly fewer unlockables than it's predecessors, I genuinely wonder how they are expecting to hold my interest for much longer.To conclude this, would I recommend purchasing MK1? Kinda. There is a whole lot to like about this game, especially if you are are fan of the klassic instalments; however, if you loved MK11 (specifically for it's story and unlockables), maybe sit this one out.
