_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot to say about this incredible game. The game is a beautiful combination of engaging exploration and interesting missions combined with educational information. I had no idea what I was getting into. I saw its initial announcement trailer and immediately knew I wanted the game. I went on a blackout from any and all information about the game and was very surprised to see it was nothing like what I originally thought it would be. I expected an underwater Firewatch style game with possibly some underwater horror or Lovecraftian elements. To compare it to Firewatch would be a disservice to Under the Waves. It is an entirely unique linear narrative experience with lots of freedom for exploration at all times. It has looting, crafting, and resource management elements, but the game does a tremendous job at making sure none of that is tedious. Exploration is rewarding from a collectible standpoint, and to obtain non-necessary blueprint upgrades. Resources are overly abundant and never something you're worrying about. The game does indeed have horror elements and dare I say a small amount of Lovecraftian as well, however, it is never scary. It may be eerie at times, but it never becomes scary, and I very much enjoyed the tone the game set throughout. Diving deeper into how Under the Waves excels at some of its elements, first I want to discuss exploration. Exploration is wonderful - seeing new marine life, exploring caves, seeing UniTrench installations and the pollution they've caused, it's all very mesmerizing. On top of that, there's an educational aspect to almost everything you find, through commentary or logs. If you're someone sympathetic to climate change or environmental pollution then you'll find this game will do some very interesting things incorporating real-world issues into its narrative and gameplay. Under the Waves features some fantastic music, especially after the big story moments. It has phenomenal voice acting that make the voices you hear through calls feel like real people that you know. The story is very well done. It's a slow-burn that escalates with each passing day you play as Stanley. The game doesn't hold back its punches when you get to the finale and it does some very special things to ensure this is a story you will remember.What is the gameplay of Under the Waves like? The best description I can provide is cathartic. It is a no-stress environment. Crafting and looting is based on cleaning up the ocean by picking up plastic and metal debris which feels genuinely good to perform. I had an overabundance of materials I didn't need because every time I saw a plastic water bottle I felt the urge to pick it up. Exploring the ocean, seeing wildlife, following squids into caves, and interacting with your animal companions (I love J0) makes for a fantastically cozy time. This is a game you should play slow - take your time with it and just enjoy it. Take in the beauty of the scenery. Don't be in a rush to get everywhere.If this has sold you on the game - great! That leads me finally to a few recommendations I have for anyone just starting.-Test out the graphics settings. The developers took a risk with the film grain and whatnot and personally I enjoy the graphics much more with them turned off, and luckily the developers allow you to adjust them to your preferences. The game is beautiful and in my opinion, best experienced without the camera effects.-Frequently go to the surface with the moon vehicle and just look around. There's nothing special to be gained out of it but it looks cool and you see the world around you change as the game progresses. It's a small detail that has a big impact.-This game is meant to be experienced, not rushed. Explore. Go into caves. Enjoy the scenery and the fauna.-Turn your HUD off when outside of the moon vehicle. It's so much more immersive and generally not needed when in just your diving suit.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m not going to sit here and tell you that I know trauma and pain better than anybody else. I don’t. But, like most people on Earth, I’ve experienced my fair share, and some events from that time of my life are a complete blur, and yet others I can close my eyes and see as vividly as the day they occurred. Grief is a deeply personal thing, and I want to say very clearly at the beginning of this review that I don’t believe there’s only one way to experience grief, to deal with grief, and to talk about it.All that said,  story about that troubling emotion didn’t resonate with me virtually at all. It didn’t reflect how I’ve deal with, or how I’ve seen others in my life deal with, trauma in really any recognizable way. And that made connecting with the story a challenge at  times.Stanley, the protagonist, is a wickedly bad communicator. That’s not a super uncommon trait among people but he’s  bad. Probably around half of what Stanley says are unfinished sentences and incomplete thoughts. You rarely hear Stanley say more than 3 words without a big pause. The occasional usage of this way of speaking serves to tell the player Stanley’s mind is jumbled, and he’s unsure, but the  usage of this is draining. At several points in the game, other characters finish his sentences, and it was like  A good comedic review of this point can be seen  by Sh4nkst4r.I can sympathize with this being a personal thing, but there are other aspects of the dialogue which are done without care, setting personal style aside.When characters are speaking with one another, the pauses between them are too lengthy, almost throughout the entire game. For normal conversations this is not a problem. But in instances of: warnings, arguments, emotional rants, interruptions, etc. one character  the conversation, but actually speaking after a 2 second delay when the other character stopped, is a jarring thing, and it completely removes you from the seriousness of the conversation.Other problems are the little comments Stanley makes when you pick up materials around the ocean. Stanley and Tim will be having a dark and difficult conversation about something depressing, and then suddenly you will pick up a piece of plastic and Stanley will say,  This kind of thing causes whiplash! I don’t know how the developers didn’t feel this way.And to be honest, besides these little comments from Stanley, this game pretty much never lets up. Nearly everything in this game is bleak. There are virtually no moments of emotional reprieve. It’s.. hard to play this game for an extended period of time because it is just immensely saddening at how lost and broken the protagonist is.Most of the gameplay is mindless, not in a negative sense, but there are a few small puzzles that are interesting. The twisting wheels/unlocking hatches feels way too slow and demanding, but the movement actually feels very nice, even for an underwater game! The dream sequences are relatively poor, until the end of the game where they finally become interesting. But that’s not because they become any more fun to play, but they became more mystifying and cerebral. Those were very nice.I feel that some aspects of the world are not explained. UniTrench is a massive oil conglomerate, but also incredibly bad at building efficient and well working systems? Unitrench is extremely powerful, but also does not seem to pose a threat when Stanley and Tim decide to go rogue, essentially.Also, not going to spoiler this, but it’s very cheap for . That felt very cheap to me, and also felt like a strange decision considering the very nature of the plot! I will also say that intended emotional moments lack impact without proper buildup, and the developers should have known one of their best moments was a fraction as good as it could’ve been had they incorporated another character far more into the required narrative.While this game looks pretty damn nice, and even controls well, too, which is hard to come by for underwater games sometimes, the critically important parts of this game (the narrative, the writing, and the vocal delivery) are just unsatisfying at best and frustrating at worst.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm two and a half hours in and LOVING this game! Beautiful & serene imagery, nice music, and quirky dialogue. Had to adjust some starting settings (inverting some controls & changing key binds to something that made a little more sense given other games I've played). There's some lip-sync issues with main character audio, and I'm not sure if it's a bug or if they just didn't care about lips matching words, but this is a super minor gripe. If you loved Subnautica, you'll probably get a real kick out of this game, too! I did have one major error that caused my game to crash, but this literally JUST launched, so a few bugs and errors are all par for the course on a fresh release. Overall, super stoked to continue playing this game! We've been starved of a good underwater game since Subnautica: Below Zero and I'd say this fills the void pretty darn well.

Although, there isn't much tension due to the lack of threats for all but a few segments in the game and the facial animation is bad. Overall, I enjoyed my time with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Sigh. I got a lot out of this game, so I can't in good conscience give it a thumbs down. But it's in many ways frustrating and bad. First, the good things are very good. I've never played an underwater game that gave me such an immersive sense of presence. You can feel the weight of the water, the loneliness, and even the cold. And some panic as well as your oxygen ticks away (there's always more close by). The story, too, is beautiful as a whole. Grief. Clinging to it. Letting go. And something about saving the environment, I guess. That part wasn't as well developed. But the gameplay is not good. Controls are finicky and inconsistent, often slow to respond. The camera constantly works against you. Traversing the world and collecting resources is plodding and awkward. Even the dialog is halting and tiresome, working against the engaging story rather than in its service. I finished the game without all the collectibles and am very fine with that.And the game designers seem to never have heard of affordances. The simplest missions become frustrating because nothing is properly indicated. Where to go, what to do, and even how to do it: all of these become irrelevant "puzzles" for you to solve. I had to look up "solutions" online quite a few times. And there is one maze-like level that serves no purpose except to highlight how bad the controls and camera are. I did not enjoy that one at all. is the opposite of fun.Of course, the subject matter doesn't demand fun. But it isn't helped by annoyance.I don't know how to end this review. If the idea of the game calls to you, then maybe you should play it. But come in with lots of patience and leave your gamer rage behind.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big indie games fan and I can forgive games from indie developers a lot. There's only one thing I really deeply hate and that's stretched gameplay and I can promise you... this game is full of it. Especially towards the end, there are many passages where you as the player are left completely alone and given no clues as to where to go next.What really annoyed me is that there are waypoints in the game. The developers just made a conscious decision to remove them at certain moments in the game, just to extend the game length. This is an absolute no go for me. Whenever I notice a developer deliberately wasting my time, I completely lose interest in the product. Other than that, the game is mediocre at best. After just 30 minutes, you know what the main protagonist is up against. The inner struggle with Stan's demons is repeatedly mixed with the moral club of environmental pollution. Both themes on their own are extremely exciting and very important. However, the developers don't manage to separate the two and thus create a predictable story that, at least for me, triggered absolutely no emotion. This is the first game from these developers, so they can still learn a lot from their mistakes. I just hope they learn from it.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game.  There's the bones of a game that I could somewhere inside of this mess, but they're too far hidden to subject another person to this game's failings.First things first: this game is jank.  Stan nevers quite moves the way you want him to or the way you expect him to.  Which makes everything else in the game a chore.Secondly, the story is...overbearing.  Oppressive.  I'm fine with everything not being sunshine and rainbows, but this game throws you onto the mat from the go and never lets up.  There are so many moments in this game where a story beat occurs and I went, "Jesus.  Again?"  I'd go so far as to call this game misery porn.Finally, the game is a technical disaster.  The UI constantly disappears - the cutscenes cause it to fade out and then they it doesn't bring it back - so I was constantly having to manually bring the UI back up again after cutscenes.  Then there's the accessibility options: two of them simply don't work.  There's an option to disable the camera sway while piloting the Moon that simply doesn't do what it says on the tin, the camera will still slowly swing from side to side while you're doing so.  The other is the option to disable controller vibration.  Again, it just doesn't work.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Stuck between a lot of Firewatch and a little bit of Subnautica.(+++) Jo might be the best companion in any game ever (but I love Bioshock Infinite too much to admit it).(++) The overall experience of the game delivers on the key premise - life in solitude deep under the sea.(+) The main activities revolve around your job of being on duty as a serviceman of under-water systems which justifies the fetchy nature of the quests and spills over naturally into exploration.(+) Looks good(~) The movement is pretty enjoyable (for all modes: walking, swimming and the sub controls) but very unintuitive due to the inconsistencies between the modes. (Forward key is sometimes 'forward', sometimes 'up', sometimes 'down', and sometimes you wish the devs just made up their mind finally)(~) The exploration of the sea bed is interesting at first but you quickly learn it's a lot of the same.(---) The game design is a huge, bland letdown in every activity you're forced to do. Characters are a bunch of hollow phrases. Story is just a chain of uncomfortably empty sentence exchanges.(--) The lipsync is broken. The facial animations come a good second+ after the audio plays and it breaks the experience a lot more than you'd think.(-) The crafting is absolutely redundant, just a tacked-on afterthought.(-) The dialogues can't be skipped.(-) Wish the events of the last day happened at day 3 as that's the first time the story actually develops further and interesting dilemmas are finally introduced.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Can't lie, I was completely underwhelmed by this game. It's probably my fault as somehow I had it in my head that it was like Subnautica but it's nothing like it. It's an 8hr story game and it's very easy. The game holds your hand the entire way through, there's no challenges and no creatures to threaten you and the crafting seems pointless as going through the game you're given everything you need to complete the game. I ended the game with 30 oxygen's, 27 fuels, 19 mines and 8 repair kits all unused.The game has two endings and you can't go back and see the second ending once you make your decision without playing the entire game through again.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm quite enjoying it. I love that nothing can hurt me (so far), just peacefully exploring and cleaning up plastic bottles from the ocean floor. I will say that other reviewer's mentions of the bad cutscene animations are correct in terms of the main character's face, if that matters to you. The voice actor does a great job, but the character's mouth just kind of... flaps? Think old-school RPG cutscene where the words don't match what the mouth is doing. Really not a big deal but some people don't like that.There is a bit of screen tearing present during the initial cutscene but I haven't seen it since.Otherwise it's very immersive and beautiful, peaceful and interesting. I'm going to finish this one.Play this if you like other walking sims or games where the story is revealed in bits and pieces i.e. Edith Finch or In Sound Mind.UPDATE: I beat the game.I have a few more criticisms mainly regarding the pacing of the plot and the attempts to make the player affected emotionally. The back story of the protagonist is revealed to us through radio calls with an old friend on the surface, calls to the protag's estranged wife, his own ramblings to himself, and his dreams.I found that mechanically the game did not keep up with the story in terms of pacing or punch. There were certain reveals and obvious "you should be sad now" moments in the game that just ended up being "oh OK, well anyways back to driving Moon around" moments. I am giving this one a 7.25/10 in the end. I enjoyed most of my time with it, I think they did a fine job with what they accomplished but you can definitely see the hard limits of the finished product in terms of technical power and story.Buy full-price if you want a not-scary underwater narrative game and know you enjoy slower-paced games.Buy on sale if you're just curious and think it looks neat.Do yourself a favour and listen to the game when it tells you to use a controller, your fingertips will thank you for it (no autodrive, must hold down W).
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:- Game crashes from time to time which causes you to lose progress. - There are also black screen freezes which do the same.- Missable achievements: You have to do multiple runs, if you missed any of them. There is no chapter select. - Story is very predictable. There is a lot of implying and "it"-calling instead of saying what is meant.- Gameplay and story are slow. Cutscenes are unskippable (which is very annoying in the second playthrough that becomes necessary if you missed any achievements the first time...). Nothing can be sped up. Walking is slow etc.- Character are all one-dimensional and therefore boring. ("Big oil bad, hm-kay?")- Story and gameplay are on rails. You have no choices throughout the story.- Not scary enough to be a horror game. Not interesting enough to have a compelling story.- Quick-time-events.- Underwater-walking-simulator, but not much else.Pros:+ Environment and looks of the game are oriented to look realistic.+ Beautiful world.+ Exploration is kind of the only thing that keeps this game afloat in the first playthrough.Conclusion:It is an okay, first attempt for a new developer, but overall it needs more polishing. I don't recommend it as of now. Patches and updates might fix some of the most glaring issues, but that is pure speculation at the moment.

The sense of being underwater is spot on.Played the whole thing on a Steamdeck OLED.10/10 definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Really can't recommend. The game has a very strong environmental message that I'm fully behind, but it's struggling to sell it outside of saying how bad things are bad. The gameplay is slow and dull. The controls are poor and objectives feel like a big, slow chore. Conversations feel frustrating and contrived. _childDocuments_.review: The game is not light fare and is not suitable for everyone. The main storyline deals with industrial pollution and exploitation of the earth. In addition, the playable main-character finds himself in a difficult private situation. There will certainly be emotional experiences in the course of the game. However, if you are aware of this, you can enjoy the storyline. It will make you think about things.It is not an action-game. Movement in this underwater-world is sluggish, slow and can be choppy. This can be exhausting in narrow underwater caves and wrecks. The use of a controller is highly recommended. Take your time. Don't rush through the story. Explore the water world at your own pace. You have to enjoy the many beautiful facets of the game, because the plot is hard enough.Otherwise: The graphics are great. Please note, however, that this is not a "life-is-beautiful-underwater-simulator". This is about environmental pollution, the tenor is rather depressing. The crafting system is unfortunately unnecessary. You can find everything you need directly in the sea - that could have been done better. The mini-games are fun side games. The localization is appropriate (played in german language). Achievement-hunters will also have fun with the game. In addition to the main storyline, you can explore and search for collectibles and points-of-interest as required, but don't expect a huge open-world adventure. It took me about 16 hours of gameplay, including playing all side-missions and collecting all achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: A Deep-Sea Journey Through GriefReview: Under the Waves is an emotionally charged adventure game, unfolding in the depths of a deep-sea open world.You assume the role of Stan, a seasoned deep-sea diver grappling with the overwhelming grief of losing his daughter, leading him to seek solace in self-imposed isolation at the bottom of the North Sea. As you immerse yourself in this captivating narrative, you'll traverse the expansive seabed full of beautiful marine life, delving into caves, and exploring wrecks. Along the way, you'll encounter challenges that require some problem-solving, urging you to gather materials and craft essential equipment to aid Stan on his poignant journey of self-discovery.Under the Waves captivates players with its gripping storytelling, cinematic visuals, and an enchanting soundtrack. Through Stan's trials, the game delves into profound human emotions, offering a reflective experience on isolation and the anguish of grief. In this brief yet mesmerising expedition, you'll plunge into the depths of both the North Sea and Stan's tormented psyche.Skip to the end: Under the Waves is a captivating deep-sea adventure game that follows Stan, a grieving diver, as he explores the North Sea, facing emotional trials and self-discovery amidst stunning visuals and a moving soundtrack.Score: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Under the Waves is an emotionally charged narrative-driven game that dives deep into complex themes of loss, grief, and self-discovery. The storytelling is captivating, drawing players into the protagonist's journey with a mix of poignant moments and introspective dialogues. While the plot can be somewhat predictable, the emotional depth and character development more than make up for it.The underwater environment is beautifully rendered, with stunning graphics that bring the ocean's mysteries to life. The physics of moving underwater are impressively realistic, enhancing the immersive experience. However, for those with submechanophobia (a fear of underwater man-made objects), the game can induce some genuine shivers with its eerie and detailed depictions of sunken structures and machinery.One major downside is the grotesque lip-syncing, which is shocking for a modern game. Characters' mouth movements just move random and don't match the dialogue, which can be distracting and break immersion during otherwise impactful scenes.Despite this flaw, Under the Waves stands out as a remarkable game that offers both visual beauty and a deeply moving story. It's a journey worth embarking on for any player who appreciates a game with emotional weight and stunning underwater exploration.TL;DR: Under the Waves is a visually stunning and emotionally resonant game that explores deep themes of loss and self-discovery. Despite a predictable plot and poor lip-syncing, its storytelling and underwater graphics make it a must-play.Pros:Deep and emotional storytellingBeautiful underwater graphicsRealistic underwater physicsEngaging character developmentCons:Predictable plotPoor lip-syncing

_childDocuments_.review: This seems to be the sobbing simulator :( I was hoping of a nice underwater adventure. What I got was a very limited story, which could take place in outer space or the desert as well, as long as the main character is in a deserted and lonely position. The story is switching between the game story and permanent sobbing of the main character due to some personal loss. This will result in loads of playable dream sequences, which will make the very slow gameplay even more tedious. There is a single choice for the player to make, the story is completly linear and offers no variations. Controls are really bad if you don't want to play with a controller - you get warned though that you shouldn't. Instead of implementing a warning, adding a propper mouse & keyboard control would have been better. After all, wouldn't recommend this game unless you like to see people suffering.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimatelly this is an okay/decent game but its the downsides overweight... Well, it doesn't actually have many upsides besides just being relatively competently made. I know, it's a pretty low bar. But it is really not "bad", it is just... bland- This is a walking simulator- This is a Firewatch under the water - a sob story, a tons of self-pity from MC and a melodrama at the core- The story is incoherent - the mix of "retro, science-fiction, and fantasy" basically means "we make up things and never explain anything"- There are a few bugs although nothing really serious- The design - of levels and puzzles - and overall narattive execution is sloppy. Especially closer to the endMostly the game relies on the cheap melodrama and the sob story to carry it through while actively working on sabotaging those with pointless activities, unrelated narratives and a whole bunch of subplots that are never resolved and exist just a distractionIt probably originally was a different game with a sort of sci-fi investigation/mystery story that was maybe metaphorically related to ecological problems Then they probably got a grant from the eco-activist foundation (which is prominently present and promoted in the game) and turned the game into the current incoherent mess of story by replacing _some_ parts of it with grant-mandated narrative. The old assets and elements of the narrative were kept around as a "mystery" - but that "mystery" is as fake as "crafting" or "upgrades". Yeah, sure, it is there but ultimatelly it's just a gimmick that leads nowhere - that story never resolves itself. Well, it's either that or whoever wrote the story was writing it while playing Firewatch on one monitor, Alan Wake on another all while also watching some Miyazaki anime on TVThe game is well is illustrated by it's graphics settings menu. It's barebones - does not allow you do select anything but presets. It selects the largest preset your hardware can support by default - to show off. And it has an "eco-friendly" mode (it's called that) to set settings to low "to save energy" because eco-activism - which is off by default, of course. And this is a walking simulator that heavily relies on computationally expensive visuals and effects (that are uncontrollable and to-the-max by default, remember) instead of potentially more "eco-friendly" gameplay. I.e. it is one of the least eco-friendly genres. This is kind of what the game is - a flashy facade with a sloppy execution that has a whole load of front-loaded blunt and forced narrative that probably no one on the team really cared aboutIt simply lacks a spark

_childDocuments_.review: Under The Waves Walkthrough And Full Gameplay No Commentary: Overall, "Under the Waves" is a visually nice and immersive underwater adventure that successfully transports players to the depths of the ocean. Although there are areas where the gameplay could be more varied and replayability could be improved.It tells a powerful and touching story about ocean and protagonist personal life plus some mysteries to uncover. Yes it's slow gameplay with some exploration which might not be for everyone but I think as a whole package this game worth experiencing.Graphics and Visuals (4/5):I really liked the game visuals and overall art style, although not very happy with heavy film grain and other effects that they added and there is no options to disable them. Animations are really nice and well done, except the facial animation of the protagonist and lip movements when he talks, they are not really great. Ocean is well designed and you really feel it when you are exploring it. Gameplay and Mechanics (3/5):The core gameplay of this game is about exploration and doing some basic tasks that have been assigned to you. There is some aspect of inventory management, crafting, upgrading your stuff and finding hidden objects but I never really felt the need to find items to craft or upgrade. Yes there are some missions that you need to find but in general you can finish the game without crafting. Necessary items are all around the objective areas. I feel the studio had great ideas and plans for these but probably ran out of time or budget to implement many of them. Another example is the AI that you have in your life module, it doesn't really do anything for you, just saying couple of repetitive stuff. The missions themselves are also very basic, there is no puzzle like missions, just simple basic tasks. I think they could've done a better job in this category too since most of them get repetitive after a while, but overall interaction with the world I think is very well done and satisfying. One other thing to mention is the controlling of the character and his submarine, I used M/KB and it was not a great experience specially controlling the sub, but game tells you in the beginning that it is best to play with controller which I am not a controller user. It wasn't game breaking but not great.Storyline and Immersion (4/5): This is where the game shines I think, it has a very touching story which covers personal and professional life of the protagonist of the game. There are so much information about the ocean life that was really interesting to me. On the lore side the game does a good job of unveiling the secrets of what happened in that area and keeps you engaged most of the time. There are conversations happening most of the time between you and the other person which again make it very alive and interesting. Sound and Music (3/5): Overall I think sound and music is good, but I had many issues with music specifically, first it is so loud. Try to reduce music sound in settings since most of the time when it plays you can't properly hear other stuff. Second issue for me was constant playing and stopping music when you enter a new area. It was annoying to me. Music itself is really nice but the implementation of it was not good. Performance and Bugs (3/5):Performance is good although game doesn't provide many graphical options but overall had good performance with 3090, 12900K at 1440p resolution.Unfortunately game has bugs, sometimes you can't interact with objects which stops you from progressing. One major bug was when i wanted to see alternate ending but after loading last save I couldn't progress since I wasn't able to interact with glowing jellyfish.Replayability (2/5): I personally don't think replay this game, there are some exploration you can do but it's not something that made me to go back to game and find secret stuff, most of them were basic items with a short story which really didn't add a lot to my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Swimming around in a beautiful ocean? Awesome.Everything else is a slog. Nonsense plot. Miserable protagonist who literally loses his mind after just two weeks of isolation. Countless lines of unskippable monotone dialogue delivered in a near-whisper. Meaningless icon hunting tasks. Meaningless crafting. Meaningless pollution clean up. Long segments of labyrinthine interior exploration with low visibility, an uncooperative camera and only occasional waypoints. Mysteries that never even approach any kind of resolution. A submarine that has no ascend/descend controls.Games can tell great and inventive personal stories like Firewatch or Edith Finch. This one wants to do that so badly that it ruins everything that could have made it a good (even great) game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game would have had a neutral review if the option existed. I was waiting for this game for two years and honestly I was more disapointed than satisfied. I like the concept of the game. An engineer working underwater to maintain equipment of the oil corporation in the ocean. You have to swim and explore the world using the small submarine for larger distances and scuba for more thorough examination of the environment. As a person who tries not to miss any games about underwater life I was really hoping that `Under the waves` would be a game about the ocean. I was wrong. You will spend most of the time wandering through long simplistic underwater corridors filled with heavy machinery and aglae. Your interaction with the world is reduced almost entirely to pressing `B` button, watching the same animations of the guy pulling the lever or rotating the wheel. And you will be collecting plastic bottles and other crap you absolutely don`t need in this game with the same button. The controls are really frustrating, I adjusted maybe only in the second half of the game. The mission where you have to find the seal and are squeezing through the tubes in a submarine is just painful. If you have such sloppy controls you have to have space for a maneuver. I just crashed the vehicle multiple times, I am not even mentioning that the camera lives it`s own life in this mission. And when you finally complete it, angry and irritated, on the top of it all the seal you where strugling to find is dead. I was extremely frustrated with all of it. The narrative. It`s a simple story about the guy who lost his daughter, needed to hide and went to strugle with his pain alone under the water, leaving his wife on the surface. Didn`t like the writing, too manipulative, too tearful. All this fortepiano music and convincing me he is deeply damaged is just too sloppy. I had the feeling that it lacks depth. There are also too many banalities like `It`s the circle of life...life...and death...`. Just `no` on this. But nevertheless, I liked the bad ending (there are two of them). Although it`s a narrative game, narrative feels secondary in it. Also really didn`t like the actress who played the wife. Overall the game is pretty dark and depressing. Not about the wonders of the ocean, it`s about the loss of this guy and about an evil oil company. From the good stuff. I liked exploring underwater. The base feels cozy, it`s a slow game, with this small activities like drinking coffee. Liked doing the small tasks, liked the first half of the game, liked photographing the sharks and whales, liked the fauna and exploring the nature. Some of the musical tracks where cool too. I actually think this game may be interesting for people who like underwater theme, but for others it would be just dissapointing. Thumb up for the concept, the work done and for the oceanic environments.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this game hit me right in the feels. I spent 7 solid hours getting lost in its story and world, and I mean that in the best way possible. But just when I was all in, it was over. I didn't rush, trust me. Sure, I didn't comb through every inch of that vast ocean, but every second spent in the underwater beauty was a total vibe. And yeah, I wish it had lasted longer.The story? It's linear, no doubt, but it's deep—emotionally charged, almost like "Life is Strange," if you've ever dipped your toes in that. It doesn’t shy away from the heavy stuff, and it just fits the setting like a glove. As a real-life scuba diver myself, I soaked in the scenery with pure joy. Yeah, there’s some physics that doesn’t add up if you wanna get picky, but who cares? This ain’t no dive simulator; it’s a work of art, a narrative journey.If you’re down for getting into the head of a character going through one of the most complex, psychological rides of his life, then this game is gonna pull you in hard. Just be ready for it to end quicker than you’d like. You’re left wanting more, and that’s how you know it’s a damn good experience.

_childDocuments_.review: If Steam had a neutral review option this would probably be it, but I slightly tend towards negative.Slight spoilers included, but the biggest ones are hidden.I'm a little sad about this honestly, usually I'm really into exploration/narrative driven games, but this did not really click with me or form any kind of emotional bond. It remained quite flat throughout.The only thing I was emotionally slightly sad about was , but instead of dwelling on that fact and using it to drive home the environmental message, our protagonist immediately turns it into a plot point for his own sad story, pretty much nullifying the impact.More on the protagonist story below.I'll just list my main points in a list.Alternatively this review is also pretty much spot-on:  Especially the part about the main protagonist (Stan) being nothing more than a "sad man at the bottom of the ocean losing his mind and talking like a scatterbrained sleeping pill".- Quite nice graphics/shaders underwater,- OK music, but nothing really memorable except maybe the "normal" background track while diving/driving around.- Voice acting is good, IF the dialogue of the protagonist wasn't so contrived and tedious. (more on that in the cons below)- The environmental message of the game is important and good and I fully support it and great projects to clean up the oceans, BUT in this game's story it's a little too exaggerated/forced IMHO. (see cons)- Map marker bugs where some chests stay after being found, also the collectible in  is always displayed as 0/1 found even after finding it.- Crafting system feels tacked on an unnecessary, there is not much point in crafting any consumables, I've had nearly 100 oxygen capsules by the end and everything else is given to you in enough quantities too.- Entering/leaving the submarine again and again just to collect and do stuff felt annoying- I didn't really need or care about the engine boost of the submarine, feels slightly unnecessary. The basic movement was just right. The fuel system was a complete non-issue, I didn't use a single fuel consumable and never went below ~75% of capacity.- The game takes itself pretty seriously and also has references to real-life stats and organizations, so I think the setting should also be at least somewhat realistic., so at the risk of sounding a little too critical: The story with UniTrench (the ruthless oil company) is extremely predictable, Mild TL;DR: everything goes to ♥♥♥♥ because greed for money.The worldbuilding for this company is not very believeable, their operation is in such a dysfunctional state that I'm not really sure why they are still in business in the game universe.Also, who thought it was a good idea to build such extensive infrastructure underwater such as  where the salt water will damage it all over time and all repairs are 100x more tedious and expensive?Also wild that the protagonist - Some plot elements near the end  were not explained at all ()- Story about Pearl was riddled with slow tedious dialogues and IMHO irrational behavior by the main insufferable protagonist. I couldn't relate or connect with him or any other character at all.- Ending was an absolute WTF - Game crashed once in the middle of the ending sequence.

_childDocuments_.review: Developers really don't want to understand that players don't like to be preached straight in the face throughout videogames.While this game offers apparently mediocre graphics, it actually also offers some stunning visuals and will allow the player to dive around a sandbox where you can find collectibles, big objects, consumables, etc...The idea is quite good and IMHO definitely less claustrophobic than Subnautica, since even a talassophobic like me can play this game.The main character and most fishes/mammals however look quite neglected graphically speaking (check that blue whale out, it almost looks like they're smiling to you).The gameplay is ok, surely repetitive but it works fine most of the times.What I actually disliked is the protagonist and his bigotism about people/companies polluting water: while he's of course correct on the matter, he tends to be annoying when every now and then he will indirectly try to make morals to the player and repeteadly show us how sh**ty polluted water is, albeit a few times it will be hard to say, since some areas are clearly pitch black, but our hero sees through the dark and sometimes he will be able to warn us in advance about the invisible damage only he can see.The protagonist is often victim of nightmares: each time he goes to sleep, he will have one.These nightmares are all very abstract, slow-mo-ish and boring, despite being quite short.The game tries to tell a touching story about regret and depression, and it mostly works well, it shows however that much more could have been done in terms of gameplay and partially for graphics.Luckily both of these matters are not really a bother, the game is enjoyable enough, the plot is fine, nothing out there will try to silently kill us from behind (thank you again Subnautica), and the achievements are also quite easy to get. Finally, the soundtrack is spot-on, thanks to Ambient music mixed with some Alternative Rock pieces.Overall, a simple game. Sometimes too simple, other times needlessly cryptic.Recommended, but please bear with the protagonist, he will constantly whine about how bad is to pollute water and will be everybody's favourite pain in the *** with that low, whiny, compliant, monotonous voice of his, not to mention that go**amned coffee the game forces you to drink each morning as if you're actually down there with Stan.Wanna go for a mission straight away? NO, you must drink that ******* empty coffee first, yes, because the cup is empty when he drinks.

_childDocuments_.review: Game doesn't really know what it wants to be, the story jumps from one agenda to another, as if 3-4 people wrote different parts of it, as a result it doesn't feel cohesive.You have the environmental agenda which does not make sense with plot-holes that could fit an entire oil tanker inside (things don't have to make sense but at least make them somewhat within reason: if you turn off a server, the data cannot be retrieved.)Game is full of mini-games and fluff that is not necessary and some of it is not even intractable, crafting system can be completely dropped and it does not change anything of the game, same with the mini-games.A lot of forced action where you don't have a choice in a linear story, and the very end game has an A-B outcome.To me it feels like there was a story about struggling to overcome a life-changing event, then some different agendas came in, and the game got shifted to cover those.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: If you like narrative "walking" sims this is another must play.Ran in to a couple of bugs so far nothing game breaking some minor graphic bugs during 1 cut scene and some weird facial animations where it looks out of sync. Game play wise though the game is solid and incredibly enjoyable a nice quiet night in kinda game.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting game, it has a beautiful art style, relaxing music and vibe and a dialogue and story similar to something like Firewatch. If you like chill games with a mellow tone then this is a good option, it lasted longer then expected and I didn't feel a need to complete all achievements as by the end I did feel done. The game isn't perfect, the story isn't told as well as fire watch and the VO whilst totally fine is also not to the standard of that game. There are some tedious elements especially relating to traversal, for example navigating the moon sub through tunnels is not very enjoyable but overall it was a positive experience and an interesting little game with a preachy if totally valid environmental protection vibe and a story about coping and living with loss.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Under the Waves tries to do many things in one package: First, tell the story of Stan, someone who just suffered loss in his life and is in the middle of going through grief. Second, send a message about the importance of taking care of the oceans and life itself, and show us why and what is happening.Third, build a game around the first two, with game stuff to do... game mechanics, deep sea exploration, quick time events, tons of collectibles, upgrades, resources and craft gigs. The first one, the story of grief, the story of Stan.... it has a point to share, and shared it is, many times, during the whole game. Until the last breath. The problem is, it doesn't go anywhere until, perhaps, the end. Stan is a slow one note character, who is telling the same thing over and over until something happens. Maybe that's what the people at parallel studios wanted to make about loss. I wouldn't know.I played games before who touched similar themes in many different and effective ways, sometimes deeply touching. Grief is a complex subject, with many angles, you can go as high or low as you want, but in this case the story of Stan left me cold, disconnected. I didn't care about him or the other characters.Second, the message about the oceans, was at times interesting. The closest this game got to doing something really well, and probably, the reason why I wanted to play it in the first place. The graphics while not highly detailed are nevertheless successful in setting an atmosphere, and also showing you how beautiful the oceans (our world) can be. So, in that sense, the message was sent, but at the same time there was all this documentation about everything related, the oceans, the flora and fauna, the organization working towards helping and the ones who aren't. That's all great, but it didn't feel as much part of the main experience as something you would see on a web page. Stan was also telling us about some terrible things his organization does, but it felt last second, and probably too much adding to his own grief. He also showed some care and affection for the ocean and life. But it was mostly used for making us feel worse when something bad happens. I would've like to see more of the beautiful things the ocean has.Third, the game, and this is important because it’s not just coincidence it comes in third (last) place. Under the waves could be mainly a narrative experience and that would be alright (if the narrative would be done right!) but in this case, there is a full exploration map, with tons of collectibles, main and optional objectives and... it really doesn't work that well. The main game mechanic which is the transportation aboard the "Moon" submarine is very clunky and it shows noticeable problems in later parts of the game when navigating in close spaces with the camera going crazy on you. It's not difficult, just annoying. Swimming outside the vehicle is not that great either.The collectibles, which are mostly not related to the story (except perhaps a couple of upgrades which need to be crafted with resources) are mostly random objects, except perhaps something you find relating to ocean life, but mostly accessories with no meaning and collecting them was busy task at best and annoying at worst when exploration got slow and mind numbing. I can only say that while I'm no stranger to grief and can find value in a game built around the subject, there was nothing for me to feel here. But I also understand that every life in this planet feels different, and so this game may reach someone else in ways that just didn't happen with me.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: I give a Thumbs Up, but you need to know what you're getting into.This is not an Action Game in the lines of Tomb Raiders and Uncharteds, nor is it a pure Horror Game in the line of the Dark Pictures Series or recently Still wakes the Deep (from what I heard).This is a game which is about Grief and handling Loss which is then weaved into a very nice and thankfully not too large Open World. There is also Environmentalism added to the mix, but I don't mind awareness, even if it is on the nose. A Comparison would be Sea of Solitude, though that was way more linear, had less gameplay and was sadly a bit too much on the nose for my taste. Under the waves handles the topics it wants to convey better.We definitely have enough gameplay not to end up as a walking Simulator, but you will do a lot of walking. But also swimming and submarining and I did enjoy the traversal in general.TL:DR: Be ready for a slowburn "dealing with feelings" kind of Story. If you can't get into that mindset, this will bore and or annoy you, if you can you get exactly what you think this will be.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: I was very much looking forward to playing this game, And the game started well and was intriguing. However about 2 hrs in my upbeat mood towards this game faded. What started out as a captivating story turned into a slow, shallow, very predictable and largely unoriginal mess. There is never any jeopardy or danger in the game, you just feel like your going through the motions with each task. And then we get onto the fact that the lip-sync is totally out, the crafting system is redundant and really pointless and most importantly the whole underworld environment is lacklustre and uninspiring.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Dealing with grief is difficult, we all do so in our own way. Sometime, when you need it most, a game like Firewatch or Under the Waves comes along and helps you deal with your own. Something you can dive into, just to forget about your own pain, while feeling the catharsis of another; it helps, somehow...This is very much like Firewatch, and it is exceptional. Don't expect any rpg elements or the danger/suspense of Subnautica. You do not need to engage with crafting at all (outside a few story/plot points).. This is a story, and you just follow along. But as anyone that watches tv/movies knows, good stories are worth a watch. The audioscape and soundtrack are fantastic. While the controller is recommended, I found it too clunky/jarring and much preferred mouse and keyboard controls. I'm not sure why that recommendation exists, unless it was by someone that has never used a keyboard/mouse to control a game before. Voice acting is great. However, I find Stan's "random" outbursts while picking things up to be more annoying than  anything, especially when they over ride the audio(closed captions) of the interesting lore/story/easteregg/etc content that you can only click once, then it's gone forever... just a minor annoyance. Missing features (Fov, film grain, chromatic aberration, bloom[dear god the bloom}, etc) I mean, how hard is it to just let the player choose.... I get that they(the devs) have a "aesthetic" that they're trying to convey, but quite frankly, I don't care. My comfort and enjoyment are more important than "aesthetic". I would give the game a 6.5/10Audio: 9.5/10Graphics: 5/10 (would be higher if I had options...)Voice Acting: 8/10Animations (Main character): 4/10 (why his face look like that? I mean... really?)Animations (Moon): 10/10 would submarine again!It's quite good if you like "play" a story (Again, think Firewatch, if you liked that, you would probably like this)if you need to deal with griefif you just need something simple/easy to play while the kids are doing homework (every menu pauses everything, including O2 use so you're never really in any danger if you pull up a menu to deal with your son pouring milk on your daughter's favorite barbie because she threw a rock at him)
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Read the full review here: Produced and published by Quantic Dream, the French house behind acclaimed interactive drama Heavy Rain, Beyond: Two Souls, Detroit: Become Human.Developed by Parallel Studio, the indipendent studio lead by Ronan Coiffec; he is the artistic director of White Night (2015), the beautiful tribute to early survival horror game Alone in the Dark (1992). I really like the artistic direction by Ronan, already in my list of great gaming artists; with UTW, he confirms to be one of the best and committed artists in the industry; Quantic Dream invested their money well!In a few words, UTW is Firewatch meets Subnautica! For the longer version, add something of Dear Esther and Abzu. It’s a serious narrative-focused interactive experience aimed at mature audience. The protagonist, Stan, suffers from the recent loss of his child daughter and takes refuge under the ocean waves, alone with his pain, far from the world and from his wife who still loves him. He works for a big company in an underwater facility for offshore oil extraction. Here it comes the main theme of the story, a meaningful ecological parable that blames offshore oil extractions, the cause of immeasurable environmental disasters. Not by chance the game is sponsored by real Surfrider Foundation  devoted to support ocean preservation; they provided scientific advices for the ocean set. The game is able to put the personal drama of Stan together with the ecological crisis with great expressive outcomes. You can feel the thrill of underwater exploration while driving your little submarine, together with the joy of taking photos of sea-life. Your main job is the maintenance of the facility; it will take you to explore the oceanic depths, to solve deep mystery and to have strange encounters that will put your rationality to the test. At the same time you can talk through radio with your boss and your wife, in the Firewatch style.UTW comes with a lot of interactivity and mechanics, variety of locations and relics to explore, many dialogues, lot of items to collect, an important choice to take. Graphics is very good, I just turned off the chromatic aberration and the noise effect, it depends on your taste, settings let you customize your experience. Animations and mechanics are very good for an indie production; don’t make the mistake to think it’s a big budget game just because produced by Quantic Dream; it’s an indie production with low/medium budget, don’t compare to AAA titles.My experience was too long, it took too time to come to an end for this kind of narrative-focused game. I went through a few missions that are not so different each other. I played for 12 hours, and I didn’t manage to explore and collect everything; maybe 10 hours were enough. Maybe I made it wrong, it’s better to stay focused on story events and not to take it longer with repetitive secondary missions that add nothing to the story. Developers are aware of this, so they tell you what are the primary missions related to the story and what are the secondary missions.  I suggest you to play only the primary missions and play the secondary ones after the ending credits.Frequent crashes were the biggest defects of my experience. Usually they happened at the end or at the beginning of a few chapters (maybe it happened 5-6 times). Weird, developers  managed to solve the issue just yesterday with a new patch, two months after the release. However it didn’t affect experience and the overall quality of the game, it was just annoying, that’s all.  In conclusion, this is one of the most mature games I ever played, something very far from  mainstream; we need tons of those games. Let me thank Quantic Dream for believing and investing in such marvellous project from a skilled indie studio committed to expressive video games. And again let me congratulate with art director Ronan Coiffec for this precious gem. Don’t trust negative Steam reviews, UTW deserves your attention, it’s a very meaningful interactive experience shifting the gaming medium towards narrative and artistic expression and commitment. Oh yes, it’s very melanchonic, sad, it’s an ecological and intimate drama, it’s not a game for fun, it’s a game for the thinkers. But, let me understand, do you watch movies or read novels and comics just to have fun? So you don’t watch movies like Oppenheimer or Killers of the Flower Moon, just because they are not for fun? So you don’t like movie directors like Bergman or Bresson just because they are demanding for the audience? You never read comics from Gipi or Marjane Satrapi? Oh my! Nevertheless, I think gaming medium is growing adult and mature, even if at slow rate, step after step, year after year. This is a very good year for serious, narrative and expressive gaming, not only because of UTW;  many interesting titles are coming or have just released, see The Invincible, Fort Solis, Indika, Still Wakes the Deep, Aftermath, This Bed We Made, Torn Away, We Stay Behind, American Arcadia, Open Roads, Closer The Distance, Arctic Awakening, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: The year 2023 was generous with good games. It's not easy to summarise, but one is simply worth it.I've always loved the game Subnautica. It's one of my all-time favourite games. But it has some annoying issues that are understandable from a gameplay balancing perspective, but still bad from a gameplay perspective.For example, Subnautica has very little oxygen for an underwater world game. No, I still understand a minute or two, but the oxygen tank reserve for 20 seconds is ridiculous. Or, for example, the stupid limit on inventory and the inability to stack items.Or fauna, for example. In Subnautica the fauna is fictional, but still, no marine animal from the point of view of palaeontology and evolution can do any tangible damage to modern technology. Unless by accident. But attacking? Come on!Also, the thing that always pissed me off about Subnautica is that the game is very cramped. I mean, bloody hell, you make a game about the world's oceans, why do I constantly feel confined when I should be thalassophobic? Why is everything so small, close, and skimpy?And then, finally, a game came out that fixed ABSOLUTELY ALL of Subnautica's problems, and in doing so, set a new bar for the genre. Both gameplay-wise and story-wise.An absolutely gorgeous piece of work that plunges you into the abyss from the first few minutes. Absolutely everything in the game is beautiful and perfect. Except that you can't build a base. This is a serious disadvantage, but everything else overlaps it more than enough.There are not so many good games about the underwater in this world, and at the moment Under The Waves is the best of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play this game because I loved Endless Ocean on the Wii, and I'm a big fan of anything Quantic Dream related. The story-line was heart wrenching but relatable. I loved seeing and hearing the whales and orcas. The controls/game-play and map were a bit frustrating for me. I was using my PS5 controller, and of course it only shows XBox buttons/controller mode. The map was fairly useless when in a facility as it never indicates where you are, so you're left guessing and just swimming around aimlessly. Swimming could have been made easier as well. Overall, I enjoyed it but there's multiple things I think could be improved upon. I got this during a sale so I don't feel like I wasted money. The soundtrack is amazing and I will be purchasing that in the future as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere in this game is great initially, but nothing story-wise is really consistent or even remotely interesting. We have no reason to be emotionally attached to any characters; the whole push is just "pollution bad, people bad," and that seems to be the best the game has to offer. Mechanics are not interesting either; gameplay revolves around going to a place and pushing Y to interact with an object. It gets repetitive super quickly."Day 15" is the 5th in-game day, and I want to refund. Also I'm donating 10 USD to Shell for every animal that died to oil spills in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this was a great game and my only real gripe is I wish it was longer!!! For a game in early access it's incredibly well put together, enjoyable to play and stunningly beautiful to look at. I will briefly note for lovers of Subnautica looking for more, this will be enjoyable but its much shorter, the story is linear and narrated, and the crafting was hardly ever necessary as the things you'll need tend to be readily available. Still a great game just don't go into it with the Subnautica mindset.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: In good consciousness I cannot recommend this game. This game made me understand how much I took basic controls for granted. Moving around underwater, whether in a submersible or diving suit, became a chore. The controls are unintuitive and make diving and ascending far more complicated then they need to be. It is a shame because the game is beautiful, which is why I bought it. I just didn't expect terrible controls to take away so much from the exceptional visuals and compelling environmental message. Look to Abzu to see how a game like this should be done.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Well, me like most of you were somewhat duped into thinking this game was going to be something it's not. Lots of comments saying it seemed like it was going to be like Subnautica, and i agree with you. This is a narrative story about the character joining a shady oil company after the loss of a child. The game does give you freedom to explore the rather small map, but nothing really harms you except for 1 enemy and 2 stationary objects. So there is zero need to worry about all the sharks and giant squids seen in the game. They wont attack you, hell they wont even acknowledge you. Besides what's stated above, I wouldn't bother with this game. Frequent crashes (even after the patch) and broken achievements. Various graphical glitches, and audio bugs too. Essentially this game is a 2-3 hour long picking up garbage simulator in the ocean, with a character going through loss. Nothing more, nothing less.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: I have some mixed feelings about this game. I appreciate the beautiful visuals, the music, sound design and the setting. I'm a sucker for story driven games in any deep sea or extreme isolating environment. This game has a lot of heart and soul, but it's dragged down by painfully dull game design. It's not particularly challenging or engaging to play and is plagued by repetitive tasks. The story can really hit you in the feels, if you let it but it's paced so poorly, the sense of boredom can get overwhelming. It barely gets a positive rating from me because it feels like the developers were genuinely passionate about the story they wanted to tell and the game can occasionally have a really ominous atmosphere, but I desperately wanted this game to be more fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Close to a negative review, partly because of the technical state of this game. Numerous crashes (4/5 for 8 hours of playtime), other gamebreaking bugs (such as glitching into walls, forcing a restart).But other issues arised, such as absolutly terrible facial animations and lip syncing (a shame, as the game is well acted otherwise), a sometimes frustrating protagonist, and polarizing dialogue that might feel annoying to some players.however, the game has a good art direction, a great sense of atmosphere, a good set of supporting characters, excellent musical score, decent story telling, and the overarching plot about capitalism and its environmental effects was interesting to follow. less could be said about the more personal side of the story. the exploration during your free time was enjoyable as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Under the Waves is an underwater exploration/puzzle game with a strong narrative focus.  It's like a more game-y version of Firewatch, right down to being alone with your only communication being with someone over the radio.  However, the narrative portion of the game just isn't very interesting and the gameplay gets worse as the game goes on.The first few in-game days are the strongest: you're assigned routine tasks and get to explore the map in your little submarine.  You'll collect materials for crafting, find wrecks, and do some simple puzzles to fix equipment.  You get some background on your guy, collect stuff to decorate your pod, and see some nice underwater scenery.  This part of the game is thumbs up.However, after a small in-game time jump, the game shows that it has nothing else to offer.  The narrative never really evolves beyond what we know at the start except to get super-aggressive with the environmental messaging.  It makes its point, then starts screaming "Did you see it?  The POINT WE MADE?  I'M GOING TO SAY IT AGAIN FOUR MORE TIMES!  SUBTEXT IS FOR COWARDS!"  The emotional journey of the main character is pretty stagnant, and the facial animations during dramatic moments makes them comical.  There's just not any new information or depth to the story to keep the player engaged past the first few hours.The gameplay moves from exploration to linear puzzle solving in cramped spaces where the controls and camera show their weaknesses.  The crafting is never really needed for anything, so you'll likely end up with a huge pile of resources you collected while exploring for no reason.  The map isn't that big, and there's not too much new to see asyou scoot back and forth for missions.  Most of the gameplay mechanics are just there, rather than contributing to a fully fleshed out system or being closely tied to the story being told.Overall, I can't recommend this game.  While I enjoyed the first few hours, the rest were considerably less engaging from both the story and gameplay angles.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: A very wonderful, slow paced somber underwater story, tense and yet relaxing at times. This is very much a story game, don't expect crazy puzzles, jump scares, crafter/builder style play. Controls are a bit of a struggle at times, and I tried both controller and keyboard, ultimately playing mostly on keyboard. Overall quite enjoyed it as a weekend play through for a story.PS. Do the side missions before the main mission or you may bug out and miss a completion trophy.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: It is a thoughtful adventure with an underwater theme. Feelings of isolation and emotion carry through. The game is slow moving at times, but it kept me interested during my play-through with the open exploration. Some of the best content in the game is just swimming around in the ocean with the wildlife.There are some limited collectibles and upgrades to do, but I only took them so far. I missed a lot of things by just blasting through the story, but I'm not sure I would play it any other way.If you like underwater exploration and heavy emotional themes, then pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: is a beautiful, but tragic, emotional journey with the sights and sounds of the sea as a backdrop. This is first and foremost a story-driven game with everything else being very much secondary, which feels appropriate given the subject matter. Follow Stanley as he tries to reconcile an unfathomable loss while fighting the injustices of the company he works for in the only way he knows how to.Games like this feel few and far between especially in recent years, so I am thankful studios are still willing to put the time and care into creating something that does not have the broadest mainstream appeal but perhaps equally as importantly publishers like Quantic Dream enabling them to pursue such endeavours. In an industry where it feels like we are increasingly served shovelware this carefully and thoughtfully crafted gem is a rarity.The only thing that lets this game down, and I do really mean only, are the frequent crashes. Despite some patches this is very much an on-going problem, so likely won't ever be fully resolved. I wish the save system was a bit more robust to alleviate the frustration as it can set you back quite some progress depending on what you were doing and as a result this issue ultimately prevented me from wanting to pursue a completionist run.Despite the aforementioned, studios like this are more than deserving of supporting and hopefully with a bit of luck we will continue to see games like this made.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Under the Waves is a really fun game and so far the story is great. Ive had the game crash on me twice, but due to the frequent quick saves I didnt lose much progress. I would say that the controls are not the best in the game, but its not a deal breaker either. I think the game was worth the price tag and really great storyline that pulls on your heart strings in dealing with loss.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Despite whatever everybody has said about this on the grainy look and the words don't match the lips in the talking regardless it's new it has some bugs but if the dev fix the little stuff this game would be really amazing and it is it's just the few little bugs.  Other than that great story and amazing on the looks.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself features an outstanding story with depth. The atmosphere is intriguing and the story is told through interactions between Stan and his supervisor as well as his dreams. The game loop feels repetitive at times but the discovery aspect of the game is challenging and great at the same time. I only once looked up a solution on youtube.I also encountered a bug when searching for Jo where the game was on a black screen, not sure if steam deck related or just a general bug. I restarted the game on my steam deck and then it worked.The environment, especially graphics and uboot physics is just great. What the game lacks in realism, it makes up with story, score and soundscape.Would totally recommend this game, especially for the adventurous divers and explorers.# steam deck remarkWorks on steam deck with lowest video settings. Once the battery goes into power saving this game always crashed my deck in a way that I thought all is lost. First game went super slow, deck UI very very slow. Then a forced reboot - wouldn't reboot. Did lots of forced reboots, got the deck working again.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta be one of my favorite singleplayer experiences out there. The visuals are stunning, the story is a little bit predictable but still pretty good, gameplay might seem slow to some but I don't think it detracted from the experience at all. Tense moments can really get your heart rate going and the calm moments of exploring the area are truly special. 100% worth a play, I enjoyed every moment of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this first entry into Quantics new Indie series. Beat it in under 10 hours, which was a tad shorter than expected and for that price tag. Heartfelt story, if a bit heavy-handed with the environmental messaging (which I didn't mind all that much). The graphics and atmosphere were excellent. Felt sort of like Subnautica meets SOMA meets Deliver Us The Moon. The only real grumbles I had were the incredibly wonky facial animations, the playtime for the price ($20 is more reasonable), and the constant dialogue from the player character (which sometimes made sense due to him being along and going a little nuts. All-in-all, great indie and glad I played. I would just suggest waiting for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: With a wife as toxic as that, no wonder the guy went stark mad.This is a flawed one, but may be worthwhile for the solemn underwater walking sim vibe.The writing (especially towards the rushed ending) and the lack of actual puzzles left such a bad taste in the mouth that I almost gave it a negative review, but honestly, it's a simple cute little chill exploration game with a cool vibe, marred by some pretense in the story department and weak direction.First, they get a few things right - the atmosphere and the environment (although smallish) is quite well done, interesting to explore and feels expansive enough. And the whole down-to-earth retro sci-fi setting's alright. The music plays in quite nicely into that too (when it's not randomly cut off to silence by a common bug).It also handles decently enough on mouse and keyboard, and makes the environment interesting to traverse. I notice in other reviews some complaints about the controls though, and can't attest to how it'd work with a controller, but, it being a 3D game, I'd imagine it's as horrid as any 3D title played with one.There's the crashing issue - the thing wouldn't stay stable with an unlocked framerate. Capped at 60, I could get anywhere between 20 mins and 2h of uninterrupted gameplay on a 1080Ti. Gladly the game's not that long and not captivating enough to spend much more than that per sitting anyway.And there's a few anachronistic design issues, e.g., the way it constantly wrests control from the player with the incessant cutscenes of the main character just looking around, is really clueless - you'd think modern games would have it figured out by now that that's not good design.You can tell they ran out of time too, as there's some assets that were clearly meant to be used, but never were. Which results in an even stronger non-puzzle game walking sim thing gameplaywise.But the big deal breaker, considering it's barely more than a walking sim, is that the story is weak and the characters aren't written well enough to make you care, and none of it is fleshed out enough to do so even if it were decently written.So if you're into the vibe and care to have a bit of a walk through it's pretty underwater environment for its own sake, go ahead and get it when it's on sale at a decent discount - that part it gets right. Ymmv, but I'd probably not recommend it if you want anything more than a cute little underwater walk.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely amazing.to keep it short, the game focuses on story and character depth, these elements are absolutely executed perfectly.the graphics are decent, but not the focus...still i think they fit very very well.gameplay is nice, controls can be a little janky but launch does have a few bugs.Launch bugs: a few crash issues(the game autosaves very often so mostly not a problem), a few lag spikes making panning the camera around funky, otherwise i cant think of any bugs, everything worked as expected.
_childDocuments_.name: Under The Waves

_childDocuments_.review: you know how some games grow on you? this is the opposite of it.First few days it's incredibly charming, main character looks like he's from the long dark, set in subnautica with firewatch tone to the story. the exploring is fun, the collecting is fun, taking photos of animals is wonderful (not enough shots allowed tho).It has some on the nose enviromental topics and mystery regarding your family that intrigues. Few days in you really start noticing how annoying the enciromental messaging is with every item pickup, every entry log. Mystery family is less family. Nightmare section was fun the first time, not so much the 5th time.Day 15, your personality is "oil bad and wife sad". Polution bad, gonna fix. Wife sad, not gonna fix. Anyway another nightmare. Few days in after some interesting quest (with stretched out gameplay) we reach a "find -something/someone-" quest that I cared for so much and ended up losing all my nerves in. Your little submarine controls like ass and it makes you go through a dark tight maze without the option to leave it. Suffering through it for a very obvious outcome.Did you know that pollution bad? It's so mean and careless to just pollute! Can't belive big companies would just polute like that, anyway I wish any of my or my buddy's theories about what's gonna happen next were true cause I think our creative thoughts made it more enjoyable than this cozily packaged "preaching to the choir" ended up being. Also I'm so over these child storylines, we're full of parental grief storylines like this. TLDR: The nightmare repetition was unreal bad, the main character was insufferable, kid scenes youve seen hundred times before, the writing and beats were amateurish, the gameplay was padded and clunky, the fish were cute.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had potential to be trully stellar and enjoyable, had it only focused on it's strong sides and a singlular plot line. You would think that the success of Subnautica would set a golden standard on how to make a great underwater exploration game and how giving a player a little room for thought to make their own judgement can make all the difference. For a game about exploring "loneliness" one might expect that being thrown few hundred meters deep underwater would mean your only lifeline to the surface, would be a single phone line in the hab module, and the game seems to present it that way at the start.Instead the protagonist rambles endlessly about every piece of plastic you pick up, and there is a constant chatter over the radio. Granted, Tim's actor does a good job, but it doesn't help immersion at all.But the most insulting thing for me is that the game doesn't go about letting any explanation about all the actually cool things, like all the varied scattered wrecks, how did they get there, Why are the sectors look like they do, who and why built  the walls the size of the mountains around them, what the strange oil actually is.
