_childDocuments_.review: Going to go ahead and give devs a thumbs up here. It's a great game and the devs are some real standup folks. As am sure most know by now, they gave this game out free to owners of their first game which was insanely generous and just goes to show the level of respect they have for their fanbase. (Thanks devs)In a nutshell, this game is identical to the OG Desktop Dungeons save a few things like some much needed balance changes and supporting newer GPU's/monitors. Game is so much easier on the eyes if you own a large monitor compared to the old game and now we can even zoom in very close to our little heroes which just helps this aspect further. It really looks and plays well on newer hardware without losing the original charm of the first game. Overall the game is a solid remaster and am very happy with it. I do have a couple minor complaints however. The biggest offender here is the lack of a Codex. The Codex carried all sorts of valuable information and stats to keep track of your playtime, what you've unlocked, information on monsters and all sorts of great stuff. All of which is absent in this game and that really kills the enjoyment I could have with this game as I love pouring over stats. I would call myself a stats junky and so not having any is pretty painful. Devs did say if things turn out well, they will devote a bunch of time to adding the Codex for this game too. So I really hope this game gets the attention it deserves so they can do just that because it's a good game and I'd love to see some more content/updates! The only other issue I have aside from the missing Codex is some bugs. I've encountered a couple in my short time, one was a 'infinite' saving bug where it just was 'saving' forever preventing me from closing the game and another was a main quest bug that had me redo the same quest multiple times. Other than those issues, this game is truly awesome. I love the new look and feel and being able to see everything on my monitor without straining my eyes. It feels a lot more fluid too and just dungeon crawling is a lot more fun this time around in general. All the silly humor and unique art direction from the original is here, just with a modernized look and feel. The only things missing are like I said, a Codex and maybe some touchpad/controller support so we can play this on TV's/tablets. Definitely a keeper if you enjoy puzzle roguelikes with lots of replay value and unlocks. For $20 full price (currently on sale) it's a steal considering how much playtime you can get out of it. Easy thumbs up. Great devs and even better game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of THOSE remasters. You know the one. The head-scratcher. The unnecessary one. The "What were they thinking??".Desktop Dungeons is a magnificent game. A puzzle roguelike for coffee breaks with simple yet smart game rules paired with clear visual design. Brilliant. The original game that is. This remaster on the other hand is a mystery. How can a team that created the original forgo charming and CLEAR visuals for a Hearthstone like cookie-cutter graphic style and an anti player UI? The monsters and items are small, the camera angled for some reason and all crucial information is scattered all over the screen seemingly at will. For a game that needs CLEAR information this re-imagining gets everything wrong. Just skim over a few other reviews (positive or negative) and you will see a common theme of UI issues. Fast and fun play sessions are turned into slow grinds against the interface.And the developer knew about the game's quality and still went through with it. They even gave away this game for free to people that owned the original in an attempt to fish for positive reviews. Don't be fooled.Rewind turned a beautiful game into an awful mess. Thankfully you can still play the original (for free!) instead of paying 20$ (lol!?) for this inferior "remaster".

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on a whim expecting pretty much nothing.  What I got was a very addictive and engrossing experience with a lot of charm and wit. _childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful remastering of one of the great hidden gems of PC gaming. While it inevitably draws comparisons to the roguelikes from which it draws inspiration, I would consider it to be far closer to the Dark Souls of puzzle gaming. It is uncompromising and challenging, but ultimately perfectly fair. No information is hidden, you always know what the outcome of a decision will be, but you always find yourself learning new tips and tricks to push the game a little bit further.Best of all, each session is 10-15 minutes, tops, so it's the perfect pallet cleanser on break at work or between gaming sessions at home.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this for free, as I owned the original.This is pretty much a step down in every way except graphically, where it's debatable whether the isometric 3d is an improvement or not. Character portraits and some of the art definitely seems worse, or at least inconsistent with the overall design.The game is surprisingly buggy, considering it's a straight remake. I've had challenge runs (fixed maps, where nothing in random) fail because certain mechanics didn't work correctly.Despite having the opportunity on remaking the game to tidy up some of the atmosphere and the humor, the only changes seem to have been to pare down on a few features. For $20, you're getting a worse version of a game from years and years ago. While it's a fun little puzzle dungeon crawler, and I enjoyed the original quite a bit, $20 is the same price window as Stardew Valley or Darkest Dungeon.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I do not recommend this game I will continue to play it. I played a number of hours on the original version of the game and basically landed on "this is a good game but it's too challenging and it could use a difficulty slider"... well this game has a difficulty slider and it's it's still overly challenging.It absolutely benefits from a graphical overhaul, the new graphics are gorgeous however the graphics of the original were never an issue. The new difficulty slider is appreciated. The new rewind function is fine but honestly I'd rather just randomize the level on a restart than going back to a random previous point in a mission; I can understand what they were going for but the fact that you have no control over the rewind ability that only happens once upon your first death makes it burdensome. Ultimately I wouldn't recommend this game unless it had fine-tuned rewind controls at-will to undo actions, or much more aggressive difficulty controls. I'm a pretty avid rogue player but the punishing expectation of this game to make you do math and planning order-of-operations with an incomplete understanding is just PUNISHING. I like the game, I'll play it for a few years, but if you're looking for rogues there are more accessible games in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind.It's an... alright game.Not great, not horrible, just alright.The game play itself is the same  puzzle RPG mechanics from the original game presented in 3D. It feels pretty good & seems to be mostly bug free. The update to graphics, such as the 3D & wide screen support & general supporting of a modern Windows system is done well.The main thing that makes the game play a bit annoying is the forced tutorial type stuff that keeps popping up.Maybe it's because it's been some time since I started a new game in the original product but Rewind feels like it has more of the tutorial/forced moves & that said mechanics take more clicking to get through.Over all it's a small thing to the game play & is eventually over leading to the ability to play nice short dungeons almost infinitely.However what drags the game down is its lack of accessibility & 'quality of life' options. For instance there's no colour blind settings, no key binding options or even a key list, no pausing the game on focus loss,  no GUI/UX options, etc.For instance... 'E' does something but I'm not sure what yet.. I suspect it's the last spell used but I randomly hit 'E" while playing to  get my only spell's 'spell ready' prompt.It's sure be nice to see what keys the game accepts instead of randomly hitting something & have the game act on it.Another example is inability to to change how the camera is operating; I prefer to have the PC in the upper right hand corner & will initiate actions while already 'scouting ahead' on the map... only for the camera to put the PC centre screen & no option to change this behaviour.Over all I don't feel the game deserves a 'great' or a 'horrible'; I feel the game is 'alright' but Steam's review system is either a 'yes' or a 'no' thumbs up or down system. And then there's the 'owners of the original game get Rewind for free'.That's a good move by the developers/publishers & a rare 'players matter' move... but it also feels very much like they're trying to 'buy votes'.Now... do I need to mark my review as 'received for free' as I own the original game? I don't know & am unclear on Valve's rules on such things.So I'm going for what I hope is the more reasonable road... I'm down voting the game despite thinking it's alright because I'm intending it as an attempt to even out all the positive votes to make the  a more neutral rating.I'm also not marking my review as 'received for free' as I did, at one time, spend $ on the game... I bought the original at full price several years ago.Update Edit: Small update to state of the game: the game appears to have shipped as 'complete' with no further content coming. This is not a surprise from this game developer. After receiving a few patches to squash several bugs the developer seems to have gone fairly quiet... while there's still bugs the most notable ones are ones that affect quests of which there's still several. Support in the first few weeks was great; now it's minimal.'Mostly Positive' is about what I would say the game deserves.Edit: Nominated for 'sit back & relax' as it's the only game I own that's eligible  & has basically no game play; I'd nominate just about any of my other puzzle games if they were eligible.

_childDocuments_.review: First, it's absolutely awesome that the developers gave this away to owners of the original game. Second, this is more than just a visual remaster (definitely for the better). I've been quite impressed at the visual, UI, balancing, and QOL improvements they've made.For those that didn't play the original, there's a lot to like here:* Individual runs are just the right (short) length* Meta-progressing is well paced and interesting* The components of a run (class, race, starting gear, etc.) are meaningful decisions* There's surprising depth to the game, far more than I originally thought ("hit each other" and "uncovering fog of war restores health")This game is a puzzle game at its heart, and you get access to more pieces as you go. While there are explicit puzzle modes, even the standard dungeon runs can start to feel like you're solving the same puzzle with different pieces after a while. Still, it's been fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons is a fun puzzle RPG played over small grid-based dungeons with trips back to town in between to refresh and plan the next adventure - think Darkest Dungeon. But instead of a consistent roster of characters making progress over many dungeon runs, each run begins with a Level 1 newb of a chosen Kin/Class combination.The map starts out mostly hidden, with a mix of walls, monsters, and loot scattered throughout. Using your chosen character's unique skill combination, your goal is to navigate the semi-open floor plan dungeon in search of the boss monster. Monsters are static in nature - they stand in one spot and don't attack you unless you attack them, so you get to pick and choose the timing of your combats to maximize your experience. And maximize you will, as enemies are not bags of loot, but bags of precious experience needed to level up and reach a high enough level to face the boss monster in combat.Sounds like a pretty standard RPG, so why is it a puzzle RPG? To start with there's basically never enough monsters in the map to attain maximum level just fighting fair. Monsters are worth more XP if they're above your level when you kill them, so you're incentivized to fight them early. But then you're also taking more damage as you go and there's limited healing items, so you're planning to hit those precious full-heal level ups as you go. Fortunately, every new map space you uncover grants you health and mana back. So you could punch the monster, then uncover some map to gain back health and mana ... but they'll get a chance to heal up too, so your attacks were less useful. Oh wait, but you could hit them a couple times, kill a really weak monster that pushes you over into a new level, get the full-heal, and THEN come back for round 2 with the big monster! Assuming you remembered to leave some weak monsters around - you did start planning which monsters you would prioritize killing first, right? Oh, and of course there's all this great treasure lying on the floor to make you stronger - but that means exploring into the fog, which will burn your precious chances to heal up later.Ooo, wait, this spell I found turns a monster to stone so I don't get XP for it, but then it makes the next monster worth 50% more exp. So if I turn a Level 1 monster to stone and kill something big, I'll get more bonus exp for killing the big monster than I would get for killing them separately. And it'll also create a barrier that I can throw this other monster into for damage. And ...Now you're really playing Desktop Dungeons.Also - as a long-time owner of the original Desktop Dungeons, they sent this to me free of charge!

_childDocuments_.review: Disregard some of the negative reviews you see here; there has been a misinformation campaign pushed that the devs did not agree to nor advertise. Otherwise... IDK what to tell you.Speaking of reddit. Just because reddit says it's so does not make it so.. _childDocuments_.review: Received for free because I own Desktop Dungeons Enhanced Edition, like many of the other reviews. That's a really cool thing for the devs to do!I'm a bit sad about that because I still think Enhanced Edition was the best version of Desktop Dungeons. DD is an excellent game I'd recommend to a lot of people, but the gameplay changes in Rewind are very minor and the loss of theme and character in the art is really significant. From a usability perspective I think the new 3D graphics are worse as well; the inability to easily see the whole map at once without zooming out is a problem and bloodstains are much less visible in this version compared to Enhanced Edition.The rewind feature giving you a partial do-over if you die is nice, but I don't think it's very significant. Something approximating an undo feature would be useful in the game - I've misclicked a loss in winnable dungeons more times than I'd like to admit - but the ability to essentially savescum dodges would be both optimal and boring. The rewind feature is obviously an attempt to solve that issue and it definitely doesn't harm gameplay like an explicit undo would, but i don't think it solves the misclick problem either.The balance changes are very minor. It's difficult to tell what's been improved in the combat prediction but you still end up having to do maths a bunch anyway; there's definitely room for UI improvements here but I think they'd need to actually involve user interfacing; you want to be able to ask questions like "If I cast fireball twice and then attack do I kill the monster?" without having to add up numbers yourself.Using "kin" instead of "race" and the art being less exclusively white are both nice changes, but I really wish they'd been made in the older engine.

The graphics are decent, but the visual clarity of the original is now lost and you have to zoom in just to see the various objects in the level. You used to be able to see the entire level all at once, but now the game defaults to a really zoomed in setting. Zooming out just means you can barely make out what's happening or what you're looking at and not to mention the UI is blocking part of the level as well. I can't stress enough how bad the UI is in this one - it's like it was made for mobile devices. There's less information available and the placement is horrible. I wish they kept a similar interface as the original while still upgrading the art. Overall, this remake isn't worth it when the original is still so much better. I hope they update this with a better interface and more visual clarity.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a visual redesign for the masterful puzzle game Desktop Dungeons. An excellent soundtrack and clever witty dialogue parades you through dungeon dive upon dungeon dive as you take on bite-sized puzzle dungeons in order to bring back valuable trophies to sell and grow your kingdom.The complexity grows as you unlock up to 15 (+6 bonus monster) classes who can mix and match with 7 potential races worshiping a pantheon of 9 different gods wielding combinations of 13 different spells and juggling countless items against dozens upon dozens of unique creatures in ever more difficult dungeons which approach nigh impossible.I adored the free original desktop dungeons alpha for its incredibly clever design and breadth of challenges, and the standalone game built on it in every way. This Rewind version is a perfect opportunity for puzzle lovers who've never tried it to dig their teeth into a quick to play, yet incredibly meaty, charming puzzle-venture.While I prefer the visual design of the original for gameplay, I prefer this version for looks.

_childDocuments_.review: I hecking LOVE Desktop Dungeons.I think I've actually been playing this game since its inception, I was probably in middleschool when I found this game. I remember when this game looked absolutely horrible and I still played it many weekends as a kid. It's been pretty neat watching the game evolve over the years. I wonder if I found it on gamemaker studios or just from googling roguelike rpgs.But this is a pretty good roguelike puzzle rpg. It starts off fairly simple, but very quickly the game starts to get very difficult and you have to start to learn how to push every mechanic at your disposal to its absolute limit. Sometimes you might find a very powerful combo or exact counter to a level instead. You'll even start this game thinking a few race class combos are best but then you'll come across a mechanic that requires completely different types of builds. It stays fresh pretty well and there's a lot of challenge to try to overcome.You can play a single game very quickly, if you have a lunch break you can play a round of this and move on easily.

_childDocuments_.review: First off: Huge props to the devs for making this free to owners of the original.I can't recommend the game in its current state.The default camera view, which is extremely zoomed-in, makes the game borderline unplayable. Every time I start a new dungeon I have to scroll allll the way out to see the whole screen. This effect can look okay if you're on a smaller dungeon screen, but normally I can't think of a single situation where I'd want the viewport to be more zoomed than it was in the original game. Maybe to take cool looking screenshots? Or maybe because:Much of the new graphics make objects in the game look muddier, smaller, or otherwise more difficult to differentiate than they were in the original game. Even all the way zoomed in, I can have trouble visually parsing some of the character models at certain angles. I actually stared at a staircase for about 10 seconds wondering if it was some sort of graphical glitch before clicking on it and realizing what it was.Enemy health bars are represented by an arc that is extremely close to the character model, and when zoomed all the way out, the enemy's level number can almost completely block the bottom third/half of the health bar. Overhangs from the 3D wall models can also block parts of tiles. For some weird reason, the player's health bar (next to the character on the map) has been completely removed?? The new UI almost looks like it was designed for phones, and it's much harder to tell what's going on at a glance.Overall, it feels to me like the game was designed to be played 100% zoomed in, and zooming in is one of the last things I would ever want to do in a game like Desktop Dungeons.  The aesthetic ("League of Legends circa 2013 on low settings"-core?) isn't my favorite, but I think it's salvageable. The UX/UI really needs some work, as it was great in the original game.These might sound like minor nitpicks, and maybe they are. They would also be relatively easy to fix. I'm hoping the devs take some of feedback to heart, because the core game is great and I'm glad to see so much effort being put into a reboot/remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks for the free game. The original DD is one of my most-played Steam games.You guys messed this one up, though. Here's what needs to change to have a chance at a positive review:- Allow me to see the entire map on one screen. I don't like zooming and panning around for my "coffee-break game," I want to see everything at once so I can make quick, informed strategic decisions.- Allow me to turn off the animations. I don't need to see the characters and enemies fight each other, I want to watch numbers subtract from each other so I can move on to the next set of numbers as quickly as possible.- Fix the GOD AWFUL UI. It takes double the time to make out anything in this mess of information, including the frigging character select screen. Labels would be nice -- I don't want to mouse over a dwarf to see that it's a dwarf. Why are all their heads brown with no distinguishing characteristics? WTF? Why do I have to click the challenge flags to see what they are? The information on the game map all blends in to the background.You did so much with so little space in the original. Now you have fullscreen real estate, and somehow I have LESS information to work with? Is this because you designed for mobile? You should have had DD non-veterans playtest this UI on PC. The only reason I got through was that I had most of this stuff memorized.- There's nothing wrong with the word "race," why did you change it? I'm more put off by the gore and violence you added to this previously accessible game. The opening title shows someone being murdered and spilling blood across the screen. One of your trailers shows an African adventurer's bloody, dismembered head falling to the ground, followed by a beschnozzed banker planting his foot victoriously. Yes, there were little blood pools in the original, but that's nothing compared to this. Guess I won't be playing this game with my kids -- the word "race" is far less objectionable.This remaster focuses on all the wrong things. I won't be playing again until I see an update addressing this.

_childDocuments_.review: You will either love of hate this game. This is one of those games where you "do the best of what you get from the RNG". You might go into every run with an overall strategy, but depending on what items, gods and spells you find you must be quick to adapt new tactics or rethink your entire strategy. NOTE. The game is 100% designed to be very grindy, unlocking new stuff can easily take 10 full runs, so the sense of progression is VERY sluggish. How often you complete runs is depending on your wits and the RNG gods. The ratio of your wits:RNG depends on the difficulty of the dungeons. The easy ones you'll quickly get a  100% win rate on when you get to understand the basics of the classes you play, while the really difficult ones you need a god like RNG to complete, some levels are just stupidly difficult - even if you have a super AI calculating every move perfectly you'll still be very reliant on the RNG.Overall, this game is PERFECT for a quick 5-10 minute run just for a quick break, game loads fast and takes close to 0 system resources.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: A 3D Unity-made update of Desktop Dungeons. Just as charming, just as devious. The Rewind edition adds several minor tweaks and the new rewind feature. Mess up and you may have another crack at the dungeon by warping back into time. Be warned though: this game remains extremely though! A puzzler, dressed up as a dungeon crawler DD asks you to count every tile explored on your conquest to get rid of all that stands in your way and defeat the dungeon boss. Its colourful heroes and monsters hide an elegant depth that only shows its wickedness after many hours. Pick classes as the debuff immune crusader, the evasive rogue or the potion juggling chemist and prepare them with swords, wands or a teddy bear. Or crash the party with a half-dragon. Hunt for more gold, spells and additional treasures in the depths and their many sub dungeons. Only the strongest will survive, but those that do surely will bring money and fame with them. That's a good thing though as your village desperately needs the income to prepare for the worst. And the worst... has yet to come.Recommended, but HARD. The teddy bear rocks though.Rating: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Literally the same as the normal Desktop Dungeons, just in 3D. At least the devs had the good sense not to call it "Desktop Dungeons 2". With that said, if you haven't played either, you might just buy this so if someone sees your screen, they'll think you're playing some weird turn-based hack-n-slash Diablolike instead of a roguelite puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, this is just a remaster, the original game dressed up in fancy new clothes. There'll always be someone out there who'd prefer the original and all, but ultimately for those who have purchased in the past, this was a completely free upgrade. I won't look a gift horse in the mouth, so thank you for that, and I'll happily be enjoying many hours on this.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay is very innovative, clever, and leads to lots of interesting variations for ongoing enjoyment. The core idea is that you have to "solve" the dungeon full of monsters of various levels. You always start at the lowest level and need to work your way up by choosing which monsters to fight in which order, using spells and items found in the dungeon. The way the healing/mana regeneration system is tied to exploration and leveling up makes it an interesting challenge to solve, and there are many ways the game varies the conditions of play that meaningfully lead to different problem spaces for you to solve. Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice of the developers to give purchasers of the original game the upgrade for free. The basic gameplay is great, I highly recommend playing Desktop Dungeons.Having said that I now understand the complaints about the new version. Like many, I prefer the original interface. The new interface adds nothing and I find it confusing to use. What I was really looking for rather than an interface change and the rewind feature is new content. So far it doesn't seem we are getting that. I would happily pay what I paid a significant amount for new content.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: I've been delving square by square through Desktop Dungeons since the alpha back in 2010, and it's never gotten old for me. The core puzzle is just endlessly intriguing in all the ways it can shake out, and the world and writing are almost always charming. This has been a game I've come back to over and over again for more than a decade, and Rewind is a really great update that I'm looking forward to having another ten years with. Lovely lovely stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original a lot, and it's cool that this one has updated visuals, but I really really hate how hard it is to tell whether a tile is ordinary ground or if it has something on it. I've walked past god altars, shops, and more because I thought they were either ordinary ground or ordinary wall. For example, I just failed a quest to "purchase from every shop on the level", probably because there was a shop that I walked past without seeing it even though I fully cleared the level.The spinning camera when zooming in is also weird. It works ok if you zoom out as far as it goes.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Desktop Dungeons off and on since the really compelling Alpha build over 10 years ago, and the Rewind game just appeared in my Steam library. Still a fun puzzle game. Still Desktop Dungeons. I wish I could lock the screen into a standard north-south aligned grid instead of zooming in with an isometric camera shift, but otherwise 10/10. Definitely worth the price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of so-so reviews of this game which seems unfair to me. Most seem to be comparing it to the original but even these say it is great just not the original. I never played the original but I have to say that this game is absolutely awesome! Runs are quick and fun and I love the puzzle nature.Don't let the OGs reviews keep you away from this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to make a more comprehensive and complete review for this game (in video form!) but need to support the game with a text review so here goes:I'd recommend this game, it has a lot of the same mechanics of the previous one with some improvements and an artstyle change (dare I say overhaul due to the change to 3D). Both styles being good, but this one is more likely translatable to the new 3D engine.It's got a very funny sense of humor, the challenge scales up just quick enough for you to keep up and you'll have enough close-calls that every victory feels earned and every defeat feels like you were just. that. close. to winning.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Desktop Dungeons since the Alpha days and what always struck me is how  it is for a  game.  is a refreshing take on what made the original game so good. The new graphics paired with the great soundtrack really puts you in the dungeon. Veteran players might feel estranged from the new UI, but after some hours of play I find that I prefer the new look better than the old one. Other than that, the QOL additions and balance changes also made the game a better experience for all players.There is something in the game for everyone, from casual runs taking 10 to 15 minutes to more involved dungeoneering that can take more than an hour requiring a lot of planning and strategy. For those who are interested there is also a competitive side in the form of Daily Dungeons.It is easily a 10/10 game for me and I recommend it to anyone who enjoys roguelites/puzzle/strategy genres.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: I have played for many hours the original game, and this game is still the same, a bite-size roguelike. Exploring small levels, gathering loot and unlocking new classes and races, makes for a very engaging and fast loop. Runs are short, and help the game from getting stale. The game has a bit of a puzzle feel to it, as each class and race combination works better with a certain way of solving the dungeon. As a disclaimer, I have received this game for free, as I owned the previous one, but I would have bought it nevertheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game and gets my full recommendation.The devs were nice enough to give players of the original the new "Rewind" version. This is just awesome and very uncharacteristic if you look at the recent trend of remasters. Certainly wasn't expecting it. I have high hopes this new version finds a bigger audience so the devs can recoup their investment. Make no mistake, this version, even though it's mostly 1:1 to the original version has seen a lot of work to bring the new version into the 3d realm. All monsters were recreated very faithfully from the old pixelated monsters. I think they have done a good job although I'm not the biggest fan of the art style, it's very readable, clean and not distracting which could easily happen with a more detailed art style. I think the devs made the right decision.So, if you played the old one, the new graphics need some time to get used to.The biggest flaws I can find, and they are pretty minor are the overlapping UI in the top/left corner and the odd angle when you zoom in. First thing I do with a new dungeon is zoom out so the 30-45 degree angle is gone. I find this game next to impossible to play zoomed in as you really need to see the whole dungeon to make good decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons is the only good video game. The original design is as perfect as game mechanics can be. The new art style keeps the goofy charm of the first retail release while being easier to scale to higher resolutions. Every other attempt to fuse puzzle games and roguelikes over the years cannot measure up to how good and dense with options this game is. A must buy. Five bags of popcorn. Run, don't walk.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: This is an odd one. So far I prefer the older, 2D version of the game. But that doesn't make this one bad. It's still a good game. I guess just consider which art style you prefer. There are a few mechanical differences between the two but I honestly don't think it's enough to make a decision based on that alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: I played to death Desktop dungeon Alpha (when it was not called alpha yet), and previous version of DD, and really loved it !The challenges are great and ingenious, and I really loved piecing together the lore hidden among the sub dungeons, puzzles and other bits of text.So if you are new to the franchise and the orginal graphics make your eyes bleed, DD Rewind is probably really worth a try.But beware : it is not any easy challenge to tackle. And you'll have to think a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: it's Desktop Dungeons with a few new features and balance changes, along with a new aesthetic that is kind of just whatever to me. i'm not entirely sure i'd call significant enough to warrant buying it again, but the devs were epic and gave it to all owners of the previous version for free and you can even import your old save and i've already put tons of time into it so i guess It's Good.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Unnecessary remake of a great game.While this remake does a few small balance tweaks that I think improve things, the vibrant sprite art of the original has been replaced with blander 3d assets. So I'd get that one first unless you really prefer 3d imagesI was provided a free copy of the game as an owner of the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Sunk hundreds of hours into the original to get a nearly totally complete save file. I *could* port it over, but it's been long enough that the game feels fresh again and I'm enjoying playing through everything. This game demands you think about every action, both short term and long term, and how the playing field and all of the systems affect each other. I enjoy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind is a close remake of the Desktop Dungeons released in 2013. There are a few balance changes, but the main thing are the significantly improved graphics. The remake even allows you to import your save from the original game as well as export it back! Whether you go for the original or the Rewind the game is pretty much the same - but in both cases worth more than the full price tag.As for the gameplay itself, Desktop Dungeon is a coffeebreak turn-based puzzle roguelite - typical run will take you 10-15min on average, and it will challenge you to optimize your resource usage to be able to defeat the boss of the dungeon... and later on even multiple bosses. The optimization aspect of the game is the center of what makes it fun - your resources are not only your hitpoints and mana, but also the fog of war (discovering it restores your hp and mp, as well as allows mosnters to regenerate) and the enemies themselves (setting up your exp to level up mid battle for a full heal). Hell, even non-consumable items are a resource in themselves, since you can destroy them for additional bonuses, such as permanent increase to your attack, hp or mp stats. While the initai dungeons are simple, they still provide a decent, yet not insurmountable challenge for new players - there are many things to learn to fully utilize the tools given you by the game. Even though the metaprogression aspect of the game with unlocks and pre-run preparations is strong, the game is still about you making skillful decisions on utilizing your tools and working around the quirks and special challenges of the various dungeons. There is more than enough content in the game to last you for several hundred hours of playtime at the very least, and each run will lead to your skill improving.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I can tell, this is pretty much the same as the original DD, but with updated graphics. The gameplay is still broadly the same and still enjoyable.I'm not a big fan of all the additional dialogue boxes in the village screen, but it detracts only a little from the game, which is as solid as ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Really liked the initial incarnation of Desktop Dungeon and bought it twice, for PC and mobile, bought it again on Steam for a promotion to get a free copy of Rewind. Not much has changed gameplay wise, there is updated graphics and a option to redo/rewind once if you die as far as i can tell.  I would recommend either version tbh, it's probably down to personal preference which version people will prefer but i do feel the price point here is perhaps a bit to high for an older game with a face lift and an optional safety net.Either way though, it's definitely better than a poke in the eye with a sharp spoon! the game is good and it's worth picking up one of the versions if you don't yet own it and like games of these genres.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: One of the hidden treasures of the last decade gets a superb overhaul. Highly addictive, great humor, and the new graphics are perfect. I did receive for free because the dev gave it to those who bought the original. Having said that, I would have easily shelled out some more bucks for this regardless. So I do thank the developer's generosity. If you you like the genre, I have a hard time believing you won't enjoy this game. Buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: An upgrade to the original excellent Desktop dungeons.Each dungeon is a bite-sized (10-50 mins) piece of deep tactics, with rouge-like generation and a huge roster of characters, items and boons to keep it fresh.  Each dungeon is a novel challenge to solve.I find myself coming back to desktop dungeons when I want to scratch that strategy and tactics itch but don't want to throw many hours into a run of RTS/city-builder/etc...The upgrades to the UI enhance the original fast deep tactics promise of Desktop Dungeons.  Mental maths that was formerly required for high-level play and tricks is now displayed on screen (hits to kill, your damage calculation) so you can use them in you tactical decisions without having to work them out for each enemy.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game, though I'm not sure if I'd recommend it over the original. If you're interested in the graphical update, that's mostly what you're getting in this one over the original. One downside is that Rewind won't run on a potato computer. The save files can be transferred between the games, so if you start in one, you can carry over. The main drawback is that only the original has access to the overhaul mod "Desktop Dungeons: Extreme Edition" This mod essentially doubles the amount of content in the game, and adds many more hours of things to do. There are also some slight balance changes in Rewind, but these are also included in the Extreme Edition mod, so I wouldn't use this as the deciding factor on which version to buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons Rewind is a fun and addictive roguelike game that lets you explore randomly generated dungeons, fight monsters, collect loot and level up your character. The rewind feature allows you to undo your last move if you make a mistake or get into a tight spot. This adds a layer of strategy and challenge to the game, as you have to think carefully before you act. The game also has a lot of replay value, as you can unlock different classes, races and quests. If you are looking for a quick and satisfying dungeon crawler, Desktop Dungeons Rewind is a great choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: I have been enjoying playing the game again and doing the unlocks but make no mistake - the original is superior in just about every way.   The missing codex as well as less ease of readability with the UI make the game quite a bit more of a chore to play once you get beyond the early stages.  This is too bad because there has also been some balancing in a handful of missions as well as class/kin related stuff that I think was great - if only if was retroactive for the original version too.Even with those qualms, the bones are just far too good to give a negative review.  Desktop dungeons is worth your time in either form.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the original Desktop Dungeons, it feels great to dive back in with a brand new art style, quality of life features, dynamic music, and God knows what else. It's been a while so I can't really compare too much between the two versions, but needless to say, if you haven't played the original, yeah you're missing out, but pick up Rewind. It's gorgeous and fun and challenging!: The game runs A-ok on Steam Deck. Full framerate, resolution, no glaring errors to speak of. That said, it's not fully optimized for controller, so you'll have to use the trackpad or touchscreen for a lot of what you need. Takes a little getting used to but isn't too bad overall. _childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: The guys who made this great game, the same the gave it away for free for the previous owners, where the one that had the previous game cloned and they revenue chunked.Please do the right thing:Buy a great game, become part of a great community and do a nice thing to great people.Also, there are a lot of goats and some new content under the surface in respect to the first one which was already a big satisfying experience.I already said goats?
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the 2D desktop dungeons, this is literally 1:1 but with a new rewind mechanic (edit: and some minor nearly inconsequential edits to certain classes etc.). So, you will like it exactly as much as you did the previous one (I loved the first one, so i'm loving this)Will say the rewind mechanic is not anything necessary at all though- if you die, it warps you back to a seemingly random point about 40-60% of the way through your run. it's actually something I usually don't even use, because it's too confusing to remember where you are now. _childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: I was originally lukewarm to the updated style, but with adjustments to the ability to zoom, manipulate the map, and some updates on visibility, this is a fun way to revisit the original desktop dungeons, which was already a lovely way to whittle away half an hour or more. _childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: The original Desktop Dungeons was one of my all time favorite quasi-roguelikes. The art, the humor, the surprising amount of depth really made it my go-to solution for coffee break games for a long time. DD had a slight problem, though, one that I think long time players were not impacted greatly by but was certainly preventing the game from drawing in new players or offering the devs much breathing room for future work on a wonderful game: the UI, as gorgeous as it was, was pretty limiting and showing its age pretty severely. Rewind at first seems like all it does is bring the original DD forward in terms of presentation -- a fresh new visual look with art just as charming as the original, maps that actually fit most monitors these days, new writing, and an admittedly (currently, as of the week of its release) somewhat divisive new UI that ultimately allows for more flexibility in builds and I imagine future development -- but look a little deeper and you'll find that they've also made some changes to some classes and kin to help bring less-used combinations into the spotlight as well as the new Rewind mechanic allowing you a chance to save an otherwise botched run with ~neat time travel animations~ It really feels like more than a fresh coat of paint, it feels like DD for the modern era and I hope it draws in new people and leads to even more stuff for a game I honestly never imagined would be given this kind of chance. If you've never played DD before, absolutely give it a chance, you'll love it. It's a bit like a roguelike and it's a bit like a puzzle game. It's got permadeath, but it's really quick and death isn't very painful. There are permanent upgrades to your kingdom in between runs which include things like new kin and classes to play as as well as new items and other goodies to bring into runs with you. Individual runs all take place on a single dungeon level of your choosing prior to departure where you'll start at level 1 and climb as high as level 10 or so by strategically taking down enemies and being clever. Enemies, in contrast with most other roguelikes or roguelites, do not move around or follow you. They exist only on the tile you discover them on, so you get FULL control over how you interact with them but that means you have to really think about how you go about fighting them so that you can best leverage your abilities to gain the most experience and waste the fewest amount of resources to eventually take on the level boss. In addition to a whole bunch of kin and classes to choose from, there are a ton of items you'll progressively unlock and see showing up in your dungeons as well as a pantheon of gods a la Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup who really make runs go in wild directions sometimes. Overall, tldr: Get this wonderful game and change your LIFE (as far as your coffee/smoke/siesta breaks are concerned)
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a modernized reboot of the original Desktop Dungeons with a few small changes. Which is fine, because the original game was already an incredible gane.Desktop Dungeons is basically a dungeon crawl themed puzzle game where a fresh level 1 character is dropped into a dungeon and you have to carefully manage your resources to fight enemies and defeat the bosses at the end of the level. For instance, regeneration occurs when you uncover new parts of the map, so it's important to explore at a measured pace to avoid running out of health. You'll also need to keep track of items, glyphs and the whims of the various Gods within the game.Lots of varied dungeons together with many different class and kin combinations leads to a lot of replayability. There are also a lot of puzzles and challenges that can really test your knowledge of the game systems, and a daily dungeon with a leaderboard.One thing I'm not crazy about is that the new graphics make it a little harder to see what's going on with everything at a glance. However there are some interesting balance changes and some quality of life improvements that I can appreciate.Anyway, it's a great game and you should play it, or at least check out the original Desktop Dungeons.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Fresh coat of paint and some really great new art. It handles a lot differently than the OG version but is still the same excellent game.Pros: - Same game- Kingdom's from OG game are compatible- Looks great- Some of the quality of life changes are excellent- Changes to class traits are great- Same bomb ass soundtrackCons- A couple QoL decisions sterilized style- Slower paced across the board- No codex T_TNow the long wait for DD2....
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons provides great bite sized puzzles in dungeon form.The daily keeps me coming back and I quite enjoy the stiff competition on the leaderboards :)The campaign starts off easy but there are many tough challenges as you progress.This new iteration isn't perfect, but it's still a well made remaster.The core is still the same great formula and well worth the asking price.Good luck new Administrators!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Owning the original DD netted me this game for free.I liked the original; it's basically more of that here with different or better GFX.Desktop Dungeons: Rewind, like its predecessor, is like a puzzle game in a way. You have to throw yourself, gear, and your glyphs (magic) at the right enemies for your level in the right order to kill without dying, regen by exploring fog of war squares, then do the same to the next enemy until you !SPROING! level up and auto-fill hp/mp making yourself stronger and able to more easily tackle enemies.Each run is a procedurally generated map and, if you win or escape with your life, you gain some money. You use that to upgrade your village which gets you new classes like Fighter, Wizard, etc, or species/races like Human, Elf, Dwarf, etc. and a couple other things.There's also a selection of premade puzzle maps to tackle.I have no reason to believe the rest of the game won't be more of the same, so I'll drop a casual positive review, keeping in mind it was free to me so price is not part of this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Got it free because I had the original game, but I didn't even realize this was a remaster at first. Great game before, even better now. If you like turn-based strategy game, please give it a go.Also, please have a sequel soon!Oh and I realized I could pay a tip as a DLC and did just now.  Thanks for the great experience and keep it coming please.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty neat re-imagining of the original Desktop Dungeon game. I'm glad they ditched the old artstyle for a little something more cartoony and whimsical, and the new features and balance changes are a welcome sight.Overall a pretty neat rework of an older title, with a little extra to justify the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons is a great and unique game. I'm less sure whether this version is worth playing over the original. This version has a few notable improvements - like dungeons aspect ratios being much better for contemporary screen resolutions; and better combat predictions so there's less (or no?) risk of dying in combat for a reason you don't necessarily understand, which happened occasionally in the original (e.g. maybe some status effect was applied mid-combat); and the rewind feature which revives you by rewinding time upon your first death in a level. There's also been some very slight rebalancing; the number of such changes can be counted with one hand, which is fine in what's essentially a remastered game.I also appreciated that I was able to port my save files from the original over to the remastered version.The overall new presentation and UI is more of a mixed bag. Top-down is just a better perspective for a turn-based puzzle game than this isometric perspective, where one must occasionally scroll to see all enemies. And I just don't understand why the health UI has player stats in the top left and enemy stats in the top right: the single most important thing in the game is to be able to tell at a glance whether you can kill a monster or not, and this is not possible here; instead you must constantly glance into either corner to compare what will happen to both you and the monster.A remaster is the perfect opportunity for genuine UI innovation, and the actual UI falls far short of its potential. Here it sometimes feels more like you're fighting the UI, rather than benefiting from it.With all that being said, the game is still Desktop Dungeons, so it's still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks so much for rebooting this wonderful game. It's hard to play this game, even when you lose, without a smile on your face. _childDocuments_.review: Between the demo and the original steam release, I have over 25 hours in this game already. It's incredibly well deisgned. It's brutal and unforgiving and it forces you to think hard about your moves and learn smart strategies, but very few games are so rewarding to learn. Not for the faint of heart or those expecting an easygoing experience.This new version has the benefit of looking really good, unlike the old version. The UI is different, and I don't like some of the changes, but it improves some things too. Overall the game trades off a small amount of readability for a massive improvement in visuals.It's a very good game, and both versions have their merits.

_childDocuments_.review: I HAVE NOT PLAYED THE ORIGINAL.This game is very good even for newcomers. There's an extensive (and optional) tutorial. There is also a whole section of "puzzles" they are unlocked which in these kinds of games act like advanced tutorials. Basically giving you a set scenario and teaching you to use features you may have overlooked or misunderstood.The games balancing seems perfect,  the damage calculations are clear and extremely quick to use.I'm a huge fan of older tile based dungeon crawlers, as well as the mystery dungeon genre and this game seriously scratches that itch.There's also a rogueLITE element to the game, as seen in the trailer and game description. You'll unlock new jobs and races, items, shops etc as you play and even more dungeons. Keeping you constantly progressing even when you die or escape a dungeon run.The games not mindless, the strategy and difficulty is there but it feels fair and rewarding. Being a rogueLITE the are times when you might need to escape a dungeon instead of clearing it but I've always at least gotten to the boss before bailing.There's a lot here, I can tell I'll be on this game for a while and I appreciate it.

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons starts off you very simply. You click on squares you want to move to, click on enemies to attack them, click on glyphs to use them, enemies attack you only when you attack them, and explore to regenerate health and mana. Your ultimate goal is defeat the boss of each dungeon and the dungeons are relatively short. Just thirty minutes max for a dungeon if you take your time on some the harder ones. All this may deceive you into thinking Desktop Dungeons is a simple game. It is not. The difficulty curve in Desktop Dungeons is wonderfully done. At first the only mechanics you need to master are the ones I listed above. Then classes, kin, and various enemies are introduced that force you tackle them in a variety of ways. Some classes rely on glyphs to win and others struggle to use glyphs forcing you find alternative ways to win. Some enemies are nigh impervious to regular attacks and others attack back when you use magical attacks on them. The semi random nature of the game will force you into situations where you cannot use optimal combos to win. Sometimes you're playing a class that struggles to use magic against enemies that you need to attack with magic to kill. So after you master the basics of the game you then have to learn how to use the various classes optimally and what to do when you can't use them optimally. You get a feel for what enemies are easy in what situations and hard in others. You advance further into the game and suddenly you find dungeons and enemies where previous strategies don't work. Those enemies you could kill a few levels higher than you suddenly can't be killed that way anymore. You have to find out ever better ways of leveraging your bonuses. Finding ways to deal just a little more damage or take a little less so you can kill tougher enemies. You have to manage your resources even better. For someone brand new to the game each hurdle the game places in front of you can seem insurmountable at first glance. But the game does a fantastic job of pushing the player to be better without having them give up. All the simple systems in the game get combined in a wonderfully complex way that never feels impossible to understand because of how the game eases you into them. For people interested in the game but have never played it: make no mistake, this is very much a strategy/puzzle game. The later levels will require you to really sit down and use your brain to solve them. The game never goes so far as to require you to calculate stuff out in advance to win but it will require a fair amount of foresight instead of blindly doing whatever actions seem best at the time. For people who played or know about the original are checking out the remaster: there a great deal of small gameplay changes that all make the game better in my opinion. You can see if tiles have potions on them from the glow on adjacent tiles, the fighter class had a number of changes, and you can see enemies in the fog if you get close enough. These are just a few changes they made. The rewind feature is really nice. If the new perspective annoys you there is a button in the bottom left corner that gives you a full overview like in the original game. My only complaint is that the old artstyle is gone. The new 3d stuff is good but I adored the original art. Some last remarks for those who have read this far. The writing is very good and the humor in the game is very much in the same style as Terry Pratchet. The music is also great and very fitting for the feel of the game. My favorite track is Troll in A Minor if you want to look it up and give it a listen before buying the game. I should also mention that the devs were kind enough to give the remaster to everyone who bought the original game for free. A completely unnecessary gesture given how much work has gone into the remaster more than justifies the price. Although my opinion doesn't amount to much, I would like to finish by saying I think Desktop Dungeons is in the top 100 games ever made. I put it so low only because of how many amazing games have been made throughout history and not to say that Desktop Dungeons isn't THAT good. Every single part of the game is amazing well executed and the game's relative obscurity is mostly due to the genre's lack of popularity and not because the game has been found lacking.

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeon is a phenomenal puzzle dungeon crawler that truly tests your strategic thinking skills. The game's retro-style graphics are charming and give a nod to classic dungeon crawler games of the past, but the gameplay is anything but old-fashioned.The game offers a unique blend of RPG-style mechanics and puzzle elements that requires you to carefully plan out each move, considering the strengths and weaknesses of your character and the enemies you're facing. As you progress through the game, you'll unlock new characters, items, and abilities that add even more depth to the gameplay.One of the standout features of Desktop Dungeon is its accessibility. The game is designed to be played in short, bite-sized sessions, which makes it perfect for busy gamers who don't have a lot of time to sink into lengthy gaming sessions. Plus, the game's intuitive interface and helpful tutorial make it easy for players of all experience levels to jump right in and start playing.Overall, I highly recommend Desktop Dungeon to any puzzle or RPG fan. It's a challenging, addictive game that will keep you coming back for more. Give it a try – you won't be disappointed!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid remaster of the Desktop Dungeons. There is some roughness in UI here and there by now, but core game mechanics are polished and balanced. The devs removed all the  'I'll wait until it is  done with autoexloring' thing of classic roguelikes, so no more grinding and searching for weaker enemies. You'll search for stronger enemies instead. The game leans more towards chess/puzzle side of the genre and it is a big fat plus. There is a little bit of luck involved, but one won't find any of the famous Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup Casino dice rolls (which are not bad, but sometimes quite irritating). The game's fighting system is intricated and every turn matters here. Your brain cells matter too, so keep them fit by playing it. Absolutely recomended for roguelike / puzzle fans. I hope devs will continue update the game with new content.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Desktop Dungeons for about thirteen years now. I poured hours into the free beta in 2010, picked up the Enhanced Edition in 2013 (and mostly played on my tablet). I always wondered what QCF was up to after Enhanced came out and then I saw this pop up during one of the Steam Next fests. I was not expecting to get this for free, but if you owned the Desktop Dungeons Enhanced Edition before today, you should already have this in your Steam Library. I was extremely excited by the prospect of more Desktop Dungeons. I wasn't expecting that my original Enhanced Edition save would transfer over to the new game. That's some real dedication. Desktop Dungeons is one of the first coffee break/puzzle roguelikes I ever played. Its charming and simple art style hides a pretty nefarious and deep system once you start digging into it. I don't have the time to dig into the details right now (and honestly, it's more fun to figure out how to get some bonus XP by killing monsters that are higher level than you are on your own). The different class and character combinations can yield some really fun gameplay, but the real fun is when you start experimenting with worshipping different gods and finding out how to play to their strengths.Desktop Dungeons Enhanced Edition is free on Steam if you want to check the game out for yourself. Rewind adds some quality of life changes and 3D graphics (among other things). If you like things like Golden Krone Hotel or Tactical Nexus, I bet you'll have a great time with Desktop Dungeons.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Supporter from the OG game. I think i bought it way before the steam release... i can absolutely recommend this little gem. You can try out the OG for FREE now.Nice concept, fast paced, easy to learn, hard to master.Mind you, i´m not good at this game... but i am always enjoying my time with it.I loved it 10 years ago - still do!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons: Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: Got it for free for supporting the original Desktop Dungeons! Same amazing gameplay, graphics modernized! What a wonderful excuse to get back into the game and play some more!!!Highly recommend! :)--- Edit after a couple hours of play!I'm back to enjoying this game, which is wonderful! It feels balanced, and fun, and as always allows you to really think through each combat and experiment.I am a little sad that the graphical art style for the models and the dungeons is a lot harder to read than in the original. It's nice to have graphical fidelity, but for games that can be this thinky and strategic, sometimes the ability to read the situation at a glance can feel more importance, so it fails a bit there.I also generally find the map-selection/quest selection UX to be confusing (you can go to the map, but also to a map's quests or something?), but maybe that's just me :)

_childDocuments_.review:
Founding a new kingdom isn't easy: it takes cunning, manpower, and lots and lots of gold. How will you pay for the outrageously overpriced taverns and banks? Better descend into the dungeons and steal riches from the deadly inhabitants any way you can.

Desktop Dungeons: Rewind bestows bites of tactical roguelike action, which will quickly fester into a deep, lingering, and strategic obsession. Bargain with gods, equip your spoon and pick your battles, before retreating into the healing darkness. But beware... there are still many monsters to face!

Desktop Dungeons: Rewind is a modern remastering of the award-winning, bite-sized, tactical dungeon crawler.

name: Anger Foot
detailed_description: Anger Foot is a lightning fast hard bass blast of kicking doors and kicking ass. Crash through the caffeine-fuelled fever dream of Shit City, putting the boot to a menacing menagerie of merciless gangsters. Unleash the world's deadliest feet on a colourful cast of anthropomorphic enemies. Clearing out slums, sewers, and skyscrapers as you grab new weapons, unlock new sneakers, and upgrade your powers in absurd and wonderful ways. Kick and shoot your way to the exit as you leave behind a smouldering trail of shattered doors, broken bones, and crumpled energy drinks. Fast-Paced Ass Kicking Action Shit City is a disease and your foot is the cure. Lace up a capricious collection of formidable footwear to fight through a diverse series of deranged city districts. Vibrant Visuals, Relentless Beats Enjoy a concussive, bass-thumping soundtrack as you stampede through a feverish criminal underworld. An assault on all your senses. Including common sense. Run. Kick. Repeat Are you the god of style, speed or power? Discover secrets and unlocks that encourage replayability - and learn to tackle levels in new creative, ridiculous and devastating ways. Master The Foot Become one with the toes and be quick on the trigger. Your skills must surpass human comprehension if you are to prevail and learn the secret of the Anger Foot.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty cool game. It has a Hotline Miami feel that only Devolver Digital could dream up. I have no arms, so I felt this game was meant for me, as the main character does so many actions with his feet. The ending legit made me tear up, as it felt personal in the way the main character uses his feet. I have done the exact same thing in real life, and it just felt really cool to be represented.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Video Review: It takes genuine talent to create a game as stupid as Anger Foot, and Anger Foot is better for it.StoryAnger Foot DOES have a story, but it doesn't take itself too seriously. The writing in this game is hilarious. I found myself actively going out of my way to talk to every npc possible to see what unhinged things they would say.GraphicsWhile not as advanced as other games, it has an art style that fits the tone of the game. It is exactly what Anger Foot needed. That said, there was clear effort put into the visuals. There are 5 different distinct locations and you can instantly tell enemies apart from each other. This is VERY important for how fast this game is.GameplayYou kick down doors, you kill enemies. There's a lot of these games. Hell, just a few months ago we got Mullet Madjack but Anger Foot manages to stick out. Enemies die fast but so do you. You can restart levels instantly. It never felt too challenging or too easy. There's a large enemy roster and decent variety of weapons, but the main source of variety are the shoes. As you play through the game you will unlock shoes that alter the game. One shoe give you a second life on death. Another shoe gives you ammo back if you kick enemies. ANOTHER SHOE TURNS EVERY GUN INTO A SHOTGUN. This even means the grenade launcher turns into a cluster bomb and the crossbow shoots multiple arrows.Roughly 7 hours to beat the campaign and many more to 100% it.This game is absurd, it's hilarious, it's stupid, it's every thing it needed to be. Easily one of the best games of the year so far. HIGHLY recommend.Full video review:

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever wonder what would have been John Wick if he were a very angry hoodlum, and instead of people messing with his dog, his sneakers had been stolen? Me neither, really—not until Anger Foot came along. With a very distinctive humor, cartoonish visuals, and unbridled gameplay, the title published by Devolver Digital is presented to us as a first-person kicking game (patent pending on my part), very funny and quirkily violent.The story follows our protagonist, Anger Foot, a criminal who has finally managed to get his hands on the last set of sneakers needed to complete his collection. Unfortunately, one of the four gangs that rule the city, the Gang of Violence, commits the worst decision of their careers by stealing his much-coveted footwear. With rage coursing through his veiny legs, Anger Foot sets out to get back what’s his in a revenge odyssey where he kicks everything in his path.It’s a comical plot from start to finish, sprinkled with action, that makes it clear what the adventure has in store for us. It's a very particular kind of humor, and maybe it won’t quite fit for some people, but truth be told, I love this style of comedy. Even so, it is not as if it were the central axis of the title, but an enjoyable addition.The gameplay is where Anger Foot shines, and it's no surprise. We'll be traveling through different areas, each belonging to one of the four gangs in the city, and we'll advance through levels until we reach the boss of the zone. As we advance, we'll be presented with new enemies, weapons, and some other mechanics linked or not to the terrain; such as explosive barrels, or toxic water that drains our health. The design of the maps is fairly linear for the most part, but some hide secrets, shortcuts, or slightly secondary paths that make navigation more entertaining. In addition, each level will award us up to three stars; one for passing the level, and the other two for meeting specific objectives. For example, sometimes we'll be challenged to go barefoot, or to eliminate a certain number of enemies with a particular weapon.The replayability becomes notorious when the challenges contradict each other, since sometimes the same level will ask us to use only our feet, and also to not use the kick on the entire level; that is to say, we must play the map at least twice if we want to fully complete it.While we can ignore these secondary goals and get one star at a time, it will be up to each player to decide if they want to get new skills faster or not. Every five stars will unlock a new pair of shoes, each with its own bonus. It’s worth noting that while some additional stars will be needed overall, it’s not strictly necessary to do absolutely everything, as I ignored several challenges and was able to get all the sneakers by the end.Regarding the abilities of said shoes, each one fulfills its own function. For example: one of the sneakers recharges our bullets when we kick enemies; another one makes the heads of the rivals comically huge and enables easier headshots; and another one gives us the mythical double jump. Among these Anger Foot footwear, there is one set in particular that can only be obtained by defeating bosses, a viable alternative for those who don't want to focus so much on performing challenges and collecting stars, plus they are some of the most interesting. The boss fights are very well thought out, having several combat phases with their own mechanics, which provides some more variety from map to map.As a final note, I have to say that I didn’t even touch some of the shoes, because I felt that they pale in comparison to others; however, perhaps more skilled or experienced players will put them to good use. I must say that Anger Foot was everything I expected, and more. I don't usually play this type of genre, arcade style and so on, but this title hooked me easily. What I'm looking forward to is seeing the speedrunner community play it, to witness the unholy runs that will emerge!Anger Foot is a game full of humor; and its frenetic gameplay invites us to a good time of crazy action. Its visuals are accompanied by a lively soundtrack that does nothing but motivate you to throw kicks through the air–-just don't aim them at the monitor if an enemy kills you and starts dancing on your corpse! Without further ado, I invite you to lace up your sneakers and enter the world of Anger Foot; it's time to kick some hoodlums!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty wild that this game and Mullet Madjack came out within months of each other. Candy colored neon styles for miles, fast paced FPSes that use a really similar "the foot is mightier than the gun" mechanic as an alternative to just blasting your way through, in series of small rooms that make up the games' levels. I mean, what are the odds? They're not the same people. Do they know each other? Are they buds? Do they go to the same dispensary? And you can buy them together in a bundle, too. If you buy anything during these upcoming holiday sales, BUY THAT BUNDLE.Anyway, this game is just brimming with new ideas to the FPS genre, genuinely funny humor, and a kind of pothead dirtbag vibe that makes it feel like underground rock. It's fast, but it's also strategic. It can be damn tough, but you can also tinker with settings and ease the load a bit. Many levels to beat, each with their own different qualifications to 3-star them, secrets to find, and hilarious conversations to be had. Some of the levels also lean more towards platforming, especially the one that sees you leaping though the air from building to building. Level of the year, if there was such a thing.One of those games you leave perma-installed and blast away at a few levels at a time when you need a hit. Just terrific. 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Anger Foot

_childDocuments_.review: Anger Foot is a competent arcade FPS that will be the ideal jam session for some gamers. Its core kick mechanic is satisfying, even though not many of the shoe unlocks are great. The level design is a bit of a letdown, due to the maze structures and forgettable designs. Difficulty spikes intend for players to replay levels, a bit like Hotline Miami, although it is not a hard game overall. Visually it is colorful and interesting, with contrast that works well for the rapid action. The bass-heavy dance music is fine for a while, but even it starts to grate. And so the game becomes tiresome to play over longer sessions, although it offers enough to hold interest over its six-hour campaign. While some may think Anger Foot is a snug arcade shooter, this is not a case of one size fits all.
