_childDocuments_.review: ((Babe, wake up, the Genital Jousting people made a weird foot fetish game))So, I stream on Twitch, and normally I don't think thats particularly relevant information, but it is for this review. I started my stream today playing Anger Foot, I spent a little over 3 hours having an absolute blast, and then I ran a poll while I took a short break to see if people wanted me to keep going with this or swap over to the Elden Ring DLC I haven't finished yet. Elden Ring's DLC won, and I went and played that. The entire time that I was playing the award winning DLC for one of the most award winning-est(?) games of the last 20 years, I couldn't stop thinking "damn I wanna go play Anger Foot"If that alone isn't enough to demonstrate how enjoyable this game is, I'll explain a bit about what I've seen so far. Assuming that there isn't some secret 5th level set (it wouldn't surprise me in the slightest), I am through 2 of the 4 main level sets and bosses at the time of reviewing. Lets hit the big points. FASTAnger foot is, I would argue, more entwined with the music than a similar game (that you can get this in a bundle with) Mullet Mad Jack. There's this almost blown out quality to it, like someone's playing it through a stereo at a party and that stereos been played so loud for so long that the music coming out doesn't always sound right, but that is far from a bad thing. It fits, because the bass never f*cking stops, its the heartbeat of this game and its going at 400BPM to egg you on to stick your foot into that dude's face and ram his head into the concrete. The enemies are dancing, you're dancing in your seat playing it, the rats are dancing, and when you get killed the goons will continue twerking right over your corpse. There's "fast" games and theres games that just play quickly. I think this is the latter, in a good way. You can most definitely go as fast as you want, or you can turn off the speedrun timer and just move through the levels at a normal pace. Both ways are fun, both ways provide challenge. FEETAnger Foot has a lot of feet in it. Gross, gnarly feet. The game is just kinda gross and gnarly. Its set in Sh*t City, where Crime is the #1 enterprise. Thats not a joke, or at least the seriousness of that statement is the joke. An honest living in Sh*t City is stealing stuff, being in a gang, polluting. Being awful is the good way to live and Anger Foot might be fighting the local gangs but it isn't for some honorable purpose. They stole his shoes and he wants them back, thats the whole reason you massacre so many goons. Mechanically this may play as a boomer shooter, but the wiggle room for you to weave in foot smashes and the special boss-shoes that let you do dumb moves or just the normal shoes that add stuff like making everyone's head massive or making your kick into an absurd uppercut. This is definitely a feet game, and at risk of sounding like a weirdo, its better off for it. FUNNY AS F*CKAnger Foot has its odd premise, its speedy gameplay, its art that just oozes with all kinds of pus and piss and any other bodily secretion you can imagine, but its also extraordinarily funny. There's rooms that hold no purpose beyond posing goons in a funny manner, there's skeletons taking sh*ts, when you arent ramming your foot through every door and take a second to look around, there's a ton of tiny details that speedrunners are never going to look at twice, and that attention to the tiny things isnt just present in the level design. The dialogue is funny, the characters are funny, the motivations of some characters is funny, what they're doing is funny, how they look is funny, their names are all punny and its all wrapped in a neat little bow that your gimp-suit wearing girlfriend (who is absurdly thicc) spit on before she gave it to you. This is a weirdo game for weirdos, but its also an excessively enjoyable game for people that just like good games. I have a habit of breaking Devolver published games (see Pepper Grinder/Cult of the Lamb) but aside from two tiny areas of a noticeable but tolerable performance dip this game has run and played flawlessly. Anger Foot is probably going to be one of my favorite games this entire year, and even beyond. I'm gonna go finish the game, but pick it up for yourself and see what I'm talking about. Thanks for reading. edit: Finished the base game (not the challenges) and my opinion only improved by the time the credits were over. One note worth an edit, though, there is one REALLY bad performance sequence where there's so many bodies on screen that the game just crawls to a halt. If they get that sequence and the few other performance dip sections (mostly outside areas or where they load multiple insides of buildings it seems) this is an easy top 10 of 2024 for me. They already fixed the jumps between buildings being too tight, so I imagine some performance hotfixes for those parts are coming down the pipe too. Great game from a great team that always delivers.

_childDocuments_.review: Anger Foot is quite literally an “Angry Foot Murder Simulator” and level based FPS speed shooter developed by Free Lives; a studio based in Cape Town, South Africa who had previously developed games such as Broforce (and its expansion Expendabros) and Genital Jousting. This game was born in a 7 Day Itch.io game jam according to the Wikipedia page, though I had to break out the Wayback Machine (link below) to see what that’s about. Regardless, it was a hit from what I saw and was later released on Robbie Fraser’s Itch.io page where I originally saw it many years ago. I had heard of this game from a buddy of mine named Nick, who had watched it from a Youtuber named Vinesauce? Now I don’t know anything about that but I know that he recommended it to me and as such, I believe I recommended it to a buddy of mine named Bad Ghosts to check out. Check it out he did and he made a mini-review of it (link below) along with three others (two of them I recommended or had played as well). Afterwards it dropped off the planet in my world for a long while until it was released straight out about a month ago. Having wishlisted it as soon as I saw the page and putting it on the top, I decided to grab it out the gate and go to town, playing it over the course of the last month and generally having a frantically violent fun time with it. Like a lot of games with simple murder loops ala Hotline Miami, the plot for Anger Foot is simple. You play as Anger Foot himself, coming home to watch something with his girlfriend during Movie Night when all the sudden some a s sholes barge in and steal a collection of his rare sneakers. He doesn’t do this so he follows the perpetrators (the leader of the Violence Gang) and kills everyone, only to learn that they didn’t have it and it moved to the next gang. This rinses and repeats but I’ll give some small context: Anger Foot lives in S h i t City, a city whose main export is literally crime in an on the nose and satirical way. The city is controlled by four gangs: The Violence Gang, the Pollution Gang, the Business Gang and the Debauchery Gang; all of them keep moving Anger Foot’s collection of sneakers around. Anger Foot’s gameplay can be summarized with this: it’s f u c king difficult but it’s a lot of fun. Comparing it to the obvious inspiration, Hotline Miami, let’s start with the basic gist. You go from one end of the map to the other (4-5 world maps overall) while killing as many goons as possible, opening doors, using weapons from your environment or kicking people to death and finding collectibles along the way. With each mission you beat (and replay doing certain objectives), you unlock stars which go to unlock certain shoes which have certain effects (like each kick/kill refills a single bullet, enemies have big heads or maybe a slide kick) and as such adds a different variety to the gameplay. You also have levels where you do nothing except talk to people and interact with the area around you, taking a bit of a break and maybe unlocking some optional achievements on the way. The enemies you face for the most part can go down easily but vary in its level of challenge: some are tiny rats who swarm you with his buddies and try to stab, some are just small goons with pipes who act generic, guys with plungers will be strategically placed to pull you in and have you dropped into danger and much more. This essentially requires you to adapt instantly to your situation or else die, and if you die then you restart from the beginning. You’ll have weapons like pistols, shotguns, miniguns, AKs, revolvers, plunger guns and more but most importantly: your feet. Your main form of attack is to kill with your feet, kicking down doors to move forward and to open up switches to unlock other areas. Having this while being swarmed with strategically placed enemies gives you a challenging but rewarding experience, ducking and dodging enemies while adapting to the enemies thrown at you. The boss battles for the most part are pretty solid, with some bosses being pretty dope (like the Violence Gang and the Debauchery Gang) while some are okay iffy to me personally but all of them feel like they could be in an FPS arena shooter so for the most part it’s fine. For the most part, the game is a near flawless experience in this part due to its simplicity, however there are some parts of it that get annoying. For example, sometimes the levels run on for a LOT longer than it should, which makes restarting certain stages to be frustrating to no end. There were also a couple of times where I would encounter glitches like phasing through a door, then kicking it from the other side to have a dead enemy flying out (tying enemies to doors to ensure some cool kills I guess) and the like but honest to god, the most frustrating part is the optimization. Almost every review I see that’s negative gives the game hell for its optimization (along with things like the challenges sucking, which I agree with but asides) and the truth is they’re right. You’ll encounter a lot of freeze frames and slow performances in the more intense areas and to me, that’s strange considering the smaller scale of the game but budget I guess. For the most part it’s doable, but there were a couple of times where I died DUE to this or would have to make an even snappier reaction so that I would anticipate the next move so I don’t die. There was only once or twice where I had a crash but I never lost progress anyways so that was fine. Other iffies I’ve seen are level design being a s s (kinda true sometimes) and the gameplay being shallow but honestly, I was satisfied enough that I wasn’t bothered with that. That’s about it though for gameplay that I felt. Art Style/Sound Design/Wrap-Up here:  Links:

_childDocuments_.review: I have a friend who is a sneakerhead, and I don't get him at all. For me, shoes are mere necessary, everyday objects, and I hate buying new ones. The thing is, I have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ leg: I can't stand for too long in one place, my tarsal bones are big, my heel is really sensitive, and I have flat feet. For me, buying a new shoe is a chore, and I hate it, and I never even owned a sneaker in my life. But, when I do find a cheaper, nameless-branded shoe in the nearby mall, which happens to be perfect, I use that shoe for years, and I am the happiest person ever. Well, this game is kinda similar to this personal story. If you want to be short, yes, this is Hotline Miami in FPS, and instead of synthwave, it was inspired by rave and gabber culture. But when I first tried the demo, I immediately felt it was something else too and had its own identity. I threw 5.5 hours into the demo and borderline started speedrunning it because the gameplay is simply THAT good. In fact, it was one of my most anticipated games in recent years, and I couldn't be happier when it was finally released. I was at a concert, and I downloaded the Steam app to my phone so I could buy it immediately. This is how hyped I was. I already wasted 4.7 hours writing this, and I cannot be happier with the final product. I only completed the first map, but except for one star, I completed all challenges and even popped some achievements out. A lot of criticism is about the length of the game, but I cannot disagree more. There is a lot of content, especially if you want to 100% the game (I see there are multiple maps, so I think at least I'm going to double or even triple the already-spent amount of time), and even if you find it short, the game is so addictive I'm just going to play it again and again. The gameplay is like me trying shoes on, a pure trial-and-error method. You will mess up a ton of times, you have to restart a lot, and certain times you might be even annoyed, but when you find the perfect formula, you recognize the enemy patterns and how to read the stage and enemies, and the game becomes a really slick, fluid, and enjoyable experience. Kick doors in, rush the enemy down with kicking and shooting, jump through the window, grab a new gun, slide down the rooftop, and bam, you have completed the stage. And then there are the challenges, which can be trickier sometimes, but overall there's nothing impossible, and with the right kit (or shoe), you can complete stages within seconds, making you forget the dozens of deaths and replays when you first tried it. The game is also really well designed. I love the colors, the funny posters and flyers paying homage to rave culture, the weird and uncanny-looking enemies, and the complete nonsense story about gangs stealing shoes in a crime-filled slum. There are even some filler stages, which serve the purpose of world-building and breathing some fresh air between the frantic stages. This game is unique in the sense that it's well-thought out and well-designed, and everything is in its right place. I really, really love this game, and I simply love playing it because it's pure fun. If you have doubts, don't. 25 EUR might sound like a lot, but for that amount of money you get a well-polsidhed game that runs well even on my potato PC, a game you'll have hours and hours of fun with, and even endless replayability if you can vibe with it's crazy and colorful world. Shoes mad, I guess?

I will keep this spoiler free.The goods:- It does an incredible job introducing new enemies, mechanics and various things that will become an obstacle over time.- Fast, fun and clean.- Enjoyable artstyle that isn't hard to look at.- Music is a bop, keeps you wanting to going on.- Nothing complex about the story that allows you to do whatever.The bads:- Can be overwhelming at times, with the quick pace and difficulty spikes.- Not for the completely casual, as it has no difficulty slider.- Sometimes can be a bit laggy.There's not much I can really say I disliked about this game, but I can see it having some flaws for some people. I suck a lot at quick paced shooters, specifically multiplayer ones. A singleplayer one that is built like this is a wonderful thing for me, and maybe you too. I would really suggest giving this game a go and playing it for the time you can.

_childDocuments_.review: Anger Foot is like an M-rated Nickelodeon shooter. You've got a bright and vibrant color palette, toilet humor, slapstick, and plenty of green slime. It's a fever dream of a game, a fast-paced FPS with a hardbass soundtrack that's built like a 3D Hotline Miami. It's unforgiving, over-the-top, and an absolute blast to play. Its gameplay is simple at first, but it has plenty of depth, and most of its challenges are creative enough to avoid being frustrating. In short, it's a work of mad genius you rarely see in games, and I loved it.Anger Foot puts you in the shoes of the titular sneakerhead in ♥♥♥♥ City, a cartoonish cesspool of a city where crime is the law. Just as Anger Foot completes his collection of premium sneakers, his apartment is robbed and his shoes divided up among the 4 major gangs of the city. Not one to take this lying down, Anger Foot and his girlfriend embark on a city-wide manhunt for the shoes, kicking his way through each gang's turf to take back his primo sneakers.Most levels have one objective: get to the exit as quickly as possible. In your way will be plenty of doors, gangsters, and other hazards to overcome. You can only survive a couple of bullets before dying, but you regenerate health after a short wait, keeping the gameplay exciting and active. You can restart almost immediately after dying, which encourages you to try a level again with the knowledge of what enemies will be waiting behind certain doors.Enemy variety is deep and impressive, with each enemy type having a distinct design so you can immediately tell what kind of threat you're facing. The melee-only crocodiles in varsity jackets will be a mainstay of most levels, while the minigun-wielding bears in riot armor will only appear in the last two gangs' territories. You'll be seeing new enemies pop up as far as the final gang's levels! Not every enemy design fits the individual gangs' themes, but it's a small price to pay for easy recognition and consistency among enemies. Each gang territory ends with an absurd boss battle with 3 phases, where the "minivan carrying a flail" is somehow the  ridiculous threat you face.Your main attack in Anger Foot is to kick, which blasts doors off their frames and kills most enemies instantly. You can also find a variety of guns to use, from a simple but accurate pistol to a crossbow you can charge for longer-distance shots. You can't reload guns, but you can throw empty weapons to stun enemies and buy yourself time to find another one. Combat is a mix of melee fights and gun battles, with plenty of room for mixing up strategies and trying new options for clearing rooms. The shoes you unlock as you play the game also grant you abilities, like a charging attack or a kick that turns enemies into delayed explosives.You unlock shoes by earning stars from levels. Each level has 3 stars: 1 for beating the level, and 2 for completing challenges. They can range from finishing a level in a certain time, killing a certain number of enemies in unique ways, or winning with a specific pair of shoes. Some can be really fun and can encourage you to try alternate playstyles, like the challenges involving environmental hazard kills. Others are downright frustrating and tedious, like the pacifist run challenges. You'll feel satisfied when you finish each challenge, but some just aren't worth the struggle due to how stacked they are against you. Anger Foot's soundtrack is a major highlight. It's a brutal collection of original hardbass tracks that accommodate the game's tempo. The more you're pushing into enemy territory, kicking doors and punting enemies across the room, the harder it's going to play. When the combat has died down and things are calm, it will be quieter and more relaxed. If you die, it'll be muffled and slow-paced so you can appreciate the enemies now dancing over your corpse. The sheer adrenaline created by the mix of music and intense gameplay can be enough to drive you forward, smashing into unfamiliar levels and reacting to threats as the bass pounds in the background. Even when you die, , you'll smash the restart button and dive back into the fight just for another hit of that dopamine-fueled action.I have plenty of good things to say about Anger Foot. Its overall length is good, and it has high replayability with challenges and shoe abilities. Its gameplay loop is fun and addicting, and its difficulty is challenging but rewarding. Its sense of humor is great, and the 2-3 hub levels that each gang gets sell the bizarre crapsack world of the game. Its art style stands out in a good way, its balance is pretty well-handled, and its soundtrack is stellar. It also has some difficulty settings to fine-tune your experience, like turning on aim assist or removing highlights on fallen weapons.A few issues to note: Anger Foot can be demanding for a PC. It runs well in most levels, but later ones with lots of enemies and physics objects can hit your frames per second, especially the final level's enemy onslaught. Some unfair elements exist with enemy design, like how the "hothead" bombers can still detonate if you kick or shoot around them even after killing them. The repetition of dying repeatedly to learn a level's threats can be enjoyable to some, but it might be too frustrating to other players. As I mentioned before, some challenges are just not fun to work toward completing, particularly the pacifist ones. I would easily recommend Anger Foot to fans of fast-paced shooters, Hotline Miami, and players interested in bizarre and unique game worlds. Honestly, it's worth the full price. You can easily get lost in the chaotic action and goofy humor for hours. Most challenges are a blast to figure out, which encouraged me to return even after finishing the game. Free Lives made a fantastic game that lived up to the hype of its 2022 demo.

_childDocuments_.review: Anger Foot is kind distilled FPS. Difficulty level is high, but levels are mostly short, maybe two to six minutes depending on how aggressively you play.For people who have good reflexes, the game might be easier as you can adapt to surprises quicker. Rest really feel that character is a glass cannon.When you can predict where enemies are and how to best deal with them, the game starts to feel like action movie. At later levels you even get chain gun, so can really start leveling enemies and destructible parts of the level. Ammo is limited though, so might have to use few gun types during the level.You mostly replay the levels quite many times, either because you haven't figured out how to complete it, or you're doing some challenge in order to unlock more sneakers.Speaking of sneakers, they unlock all kinds of different powers. Some of them are more funny than useful, though there are few that either help out with levels or challenges. Each boss is different puzzle, though with some of them there's lot of waiting to get your turn to damage the boss. Bosses give the most useful sneakers, so beating them is worth it instead of grinding for the regular sneakers. As side note, one of the bosses really look like it might have came from Genital Jousting. Speaking of that, the worldbuilding is quite wacky and there are some levels where you just get to explore and talk with people. Storyline actually explains why you might see some of the old enemies also in new gangs. If you are on the fence if you would actually would like game like this, the demo gives good idea how the game plays. It misses lot of the wackier stuff in the later levels, but can't really shoehorn everything into a demo.So as summary, frustratingly difficult FPS, but still gameplay is addictive enough so I played it all the way through. Which is something I rarely do with games.

The game boils down to going through dozens of obstacle courses that all share one singular goal, get from point A to Point B. But this simple goal is fine-tuned to peak crisp levels with fantastic audio, a unique and endearing artystyle & the interesting gimmick of kicking.Shockingly enough, that kicking gimmick remains fun and fresh up to the end-credits, thanks to earnable shoes that augment your kicks. Sadly a lot of the shoes are completely irrelevant outside of challenges. More on that here:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun.This game also mostly consists of running through extremely simple environments, a lot of the time its rooms with a couple of low poly models sprinkled about. All the levels so far have been about a minute long, then you return to a results screen.It drops to 30FPS on an RTX 4080. I genuinely cant comprehend how they even managed to make this game run as bad as it does. (this is with the beta patch released august 16)This game features a lot of dynamic music, when you enter an area or kick a door or whatever the music tends to pick up- which is great BUT the tracks hardly ever transition properly. They stutter or theyre not synced correctly so it completely breaks the trance that the game tries to induce. Wouldnt be a problem in most other games, but this game is all about that trance, all about the music.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: great game, but be a bit wary if you're impatient like meGreat music, great artsyle, and great game feel. Only downside I'd say is that the levels sometimes boil down to trial-and-error, and the only way to beat them is to replay the level dozens of times to learn the enemy placements and hazards. You can counter this by playing slower and taking more time to observe your surroundings but I feel that runs counter to the game vision. In essence your options are this: play the level quickly, as is most fun and clearly intended, and die a lot to learn it over time, or play it much slower and methodical (which is clearly not the intended playstyle) and then run it again using the knowledge you gained. I myself am not a patient person and ended up closing the game after getting tired of running the same mission time and time again. Though, I'm stubborn and insisted on playing the game fast because I like to speedrun and had to deal with running a mission tons of times over. The dancing enemies did help alleviate the pain, though.Overall, still a great experience and the music is an earworm that stays with me long past closing the game. So many things are great, I think it would be a bit better if there were some audio queues warning you of what to expect in the next room (like a ticking sound for bombers, or a distinct sound for a sniper) to warn you of an incoming threat so you can rely on your instincts more and get an edge if you're dialed in.8/10 great game

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to understate how much love and effort was made into this game. A great unique visual style and use of hard pumping music. You can tell that the developers wanted to make something special and push the game play style of games like Hotline Miami. But, after a couple of chapters the core of the game get's tiring. One of the most tiring aspects is the 3 challenges that accompany all of the levels. They range from super easy to challenges that can take you hours to master to some challenges that are straight up impossible until you unlock particular abilities later on. This leads you to leave some behind and loose the momentum. This disconnect of challenges can really affect the flow of the game which I think is an integral part of this games genre. The flaws of the challenges are also similar to the flaws of the shoes. The shoes are gained from doing said challenges and most of the time are horribly useless or completely game breaking. And strangely, most of the late game footwear are all jokes which can ruin any want to progress though the challenges. This game is difficult. There is nothing inherently wrong with difficulty in games but when you have to play a single mission again and again it can be very easy to scrutinize the tiniest details. A game with such a unique and clean visual style it's partly ruined by it's many bugs I encountered. I would often fall through floors or die in ways that are indescribable. Outside of bugs, some of the levels feel that they lack thought-out design in general. To up the difficulty in later chapters it seems that they went with putting more and more enemies on screen which can feel like a weakness of the design seeping though.The last point I want to cover are the moments around the heart pumping action. The menus feel clunky and slow which is a shame because they are beautifully designed. It requires 4 to 5 clicks to change your shoes between missions which just compounds the issues of the UI when you find yourself using it extensively. The next issue I need to stress. THE DRINKS TAKE TOO LONG TO DRINK. You pick up a drink and then you are stuck in a 5 second+ animation that can completely ruin the momentum of levels. To compound on top of that your character violently throws the drink when finishing. This wouldn't be an issue but when you need 2 or 3 drinks to get drunk and your looking at a pile of drinks it can explode the terrain and you have to restart the drinking challenges over this clunky design.All of that said, this game is still fun. And they even added difficulty settings if you just want to enjoy the world and progress through it's beautiful levels. I hope the developers learn from this game and leave the next one in the oven so we can fully enjoy the blood sweat and tears they put in games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen some other reviews comparing Anger Foot to Hotline Miami, which is close but I think there's a better point of reference: Anger Foot is dirty Neon White.Where Neon White has clean levels and minimal graphics, Anger Foot has levels full of chunky geometry, visual gags, and ragdolls flying across the screen. Where Neon White has a buttoned up anime-style story, Anger Foot has ♥♥♥♥ City. They both have fast paced, movement-centric combat, meaningful challenges, and amazing soundtracks. They both clearly love their artistic inspiration, from Neon White's PS2 import game to Anger Foot's blood-and-guts adult swim cartoon.I keep being impressed by Anger Foot the more I play it. Just playing the game feels good, the core movement, kicking, and shooting is feels good to do. Levels are constantly exploding and changing and being torn apart. I've not played a game where destructible environments have felt as good and meaningful to be inside of in a long time. It's also funny in ways I keep not expecting. Not the writing, which is middling, but the visual gags continually get me. This is a game that, in a fast-paced level, is not afraid to force you to walk through a joke to get to the next part. In an office I saw the top of an enemy's head, then walked around the desk to see he was sitting on a toilet instead of a chair. It made me laugh!The star-challenge system is also tuned extremely well. If you play this game you should absolutely try to get every star. They have a real range of purposes. Sometimes it's a speed run challenge that requires you to find a secret or some trick in a level to finish it. Sometimes it's a shoe-restriction that requires you to play the level in a totally different way. You're always solving some kind of puzzle. Okay, I need to kill 10 enemies with one explosion, how do I get 10 enemies to clump together? Or, I need to kill 15 enemies while drunk, I need to figure out where all the beer bottles are so I can stay drunk throughout this whole level. Sometimes it's as fundamental as, in this level I can't kick, how do I open doors? In very few games I've played have the "optional" challenges required thinking about levels in as many different ways as Anger Foot's do.A great example of a game that knows what it wants to do and does it.

_childDocuments_.review: Action-packed, hilarious as all hell, absolutely ridiculous and over the top in the best way possible. Someone said it's Hotline Miami if it was a FPS and that is pretty dang accurate. Think Hotline Miami mixed with Doom mixed with My Friend Pedro mixed with something outlandish and silly like Rick and Morty. I feel like I'm playing a video game version of the movie Hardcore Henry. This game goes so hard in the paint. Invites varying play-styles to overcome various challenges in the game and due to the conflicting nature of some of the challenges (melee only vs actually using a gun) there's plenty of replayability of the levels. You can play as fast or as slow as you like (unless you want to complete all challenges of course) but in order to progress, all you have to do is get through the level in any way you can and as slow or as fast as you want to pace it, though completing the challenges to earn 3 stars on a level is the quickest way to earn "new shoes" that give you different powerups and invite further different playstyles. If you like fast-paced shooters, get this game and style on some fools. Most fun I have had in quite some time with a video game. Load times are super fast (nearly instantaneous) and the gunplay and usage of melee feels very fluid and intuitive. This game is an absolute gem.

I've been impressed and inspired by the simplicity, dynamic gameplay and art style, but the full version surprised me even more. Thank you for delivering such a high quality product and for being my inspiration. I love the breath of fresh air that you bring into the scene! PEACE!

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game!- The crazy fast gameplay + short levels combo really works well and is fun to replay.- The challenges for the first world have been fun so far and have helped me learn more about the game's mechanics.- The death sequence watching the enemies dance to the beat is hilarious though I do notice the absence of the twerking animation from the demo. Maybe a licensing problem?- The world is so absurd and dark while still feeling light-hearted and colorful- The variety in shoe unlocks mix up the gameplay drastically and can be helpful for completing various challenges. - The mechanics offer a lot of flexibility: You can slow things down and play tactically to minimize damage, or run in gun through it like a trigger-happy fool.- Runs well and feels overall very good on the steamdeck- The difficulty jumps up and down, especially with challenges- Each level looks distinct- It's a nearly perfect game to pick up, play a few levels, try a few challenges then come back to it later

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Kicking stuff feels great in this game-Competent animation-Funny low-brow level design and world in general-Banger blood-pumping music-Challenging and rewarding gameplay (It's what Hotline Miami would probably be in 3D)-Cool three-stage bosses, I've been a fan of those since I completed the goocopkopter while playing the demo. When I first finished him, I beat him again in new shoes just for fun, because I felt very powerful doing that faster.-The challenge system is very engaging, I unlocked all non-boss-reward shoes by chapter 3 (out of 4.5)Cons:-It's a little bit buggy. Yeah, it's release-ready alright, but chargers often got me out of bounds, ruining a run. It's also a pro in a way, I skipped a segment in the penultimate level thanks to... I don't know what, I clipped through the ceiling while using the minigun shotgun and ended up in the end of the level. You can also sometimes clip through mesh walls or other objects that are supposed to be solid, I was able to cheese the CEO by getting out of the building and letting her blow herself up.-Chapter 5 is a bit underbaked. It had the most bugs per cubic meter, just a handful of levels, and the final boss... Is not exactly rewarding. I expected him to be as bombastic and insane as the other four, especially because Crime Tower is so short. I expected a final boss, I really did.

_childDocuments_.review: Anger Foot is wild. The gameplay is like Dark Messiah mashed up with Hotline Miami, with visual style of Sludge Life and an absolute banger of a soundtrack. Each level lasts like 1-2 minutes and has three completion goals. One is always simply beating the level but the other two goals will vary. Beat the level only kicking, take no damage, beat the level under a specific amount of time, etc. Completing these goals gives you stars, 3 per level, 5 will unlock a new pair of sneakers. Sneakers provide all sorts of modifiers, kicking returns ammo, enemies have big heads, kicked doors now explode, you can do a charged flying kick, like old school Goldeneye cheats. It all adds replay value, you can't complete every goal in one playthrough, but you want to complete every goal to get more shoes to get more gameplay modifiers.It's simple, lean, and fun as hell. You can't even be mad when you fail and die because your enemies dance over your corpse with the smoothest of moves.Took me about 11 hours to complete the game, I've got about 50% of the achievements, I could see it taking another 10+ hours to get the remaining ones. Overall it was really fun but there are some pretty noticable performance hitches in the later stages. For the most part the game ran at 144fps, but some levels were large, had a lot of persistent physics objects (dead bodies, broken environmental objects) and the framerate would dive hard, really chug in a few levels. I'm talking that Skyrim house full of stolen cheese wheels bad. This is on a 3080, 5800x3D, 32gb of ram.Overall Anger Foot runs well, but there's a couple of instances where when it was bad, it was really bad. Game was fun as hell from start to finish though.
_childDocuments_.name: Anger Foot

_childDocuments_.review: After about 3 years this game is finally here. The gameplay along with the music keeps the action flowing, with nonstop carnage with rest areas you can take as long as you want at sprinkled in between. This is the kind of game where you want to speedrun or do different challenges over and over again, so the replayability is there. The artstyle is instantly iconic, with all the designs being well done. My only issues are the story at times is too intrusive, and the game does not feel as optimized as it should be, especially compared to the beta. All in all a 8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Anger Foot

_childDocuments_.review: Fast-paced game with foot. Awesome. Very nice. Love the lightning-fast combat scenarios and feels like a 3D Hotline Miami in a way (sure everyone has been saying that). Performance and optimization in certain levels and scenarios definitely needs to improve. The last level in the game tanked my system and I can tell it was pushing the limit of the engine itself. This games does have plenty of levels, power ups, and decent weapon/enemy/level variety. Decent amount of achievements to get to add on top of that, so it adds some replayability. However, it does get a bit repetitive after a while and some levels even seem pretty short. Understand this is coming from an indie dev, but keep it mind that this   means the game can be beaten in just a few hours. You can also go back and do challenges or do challenges on the fly to add to replayability again (some challenges are not that satisfying in my opinion), but also it helps unlock additional sneakers that can change up play style and help with star challenges in each level. 25$ seems slightly too steep for the amount that you're getting, especially if you plan on moving on after beating the game. However, I knows there's a huge amount of love and work put into the game, and I can understand why it would be that much in a sense. The art style and the music are also great and matches what the chaotic gameplay portrays. Something like a steam workshop would really benefit this game if such a thing could be added in the future as well. The formula is simple, and I can see how that simplicity will wear off in no time, but if this isn't a problem, then i would highly recommend the game.Edit (10/18/24): Performance has been fully fixed and a lot of bugs fixed. Would say the game is pretty polished by now. Content is still a little shallow and price is steep. However, I'm mostly hoping for a content update or workshop in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly good game. I've gotten 16.7 hours out of this game (about 3 of my steam hours were from idling), and for a price of $25 isn't all that good, but I am not upset with my experience. Big fan of the art style and music, and the fast-paced gameplay can feel very clean at times, given you have good enough aim. Some of the challenges really do suck, though. My most hated ones are the pacifist, no hit, and do x to enemies challenges. Some times the ai clips onto some of the broken bits of furniture and just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dies, making the "do x to enemies" challenges be significantly harder, and usually forcing a restart. So in other words, even if you play well, you will still fail the challenge. This could be fixed by making broken furniture not deal damage to enemies. Also, there is this one where you have to suck 10 enemies into lava with a plunger, and that made me go insane having to deal with the constant self-killing broken ai.The pacifist challenge kinda goes against the whole game, I feel. Usually they aren't too hard, but that is the problem. On most levels with this challenge, it is just bashing your head into the wall until it works. Not fun. Not getting hit seems simple, but not always. It is always going to be slow. In a game were completing a level quickly would take a minute or less, doing a no hit takes like 3 minutes. Sounds short, but it doesn't feel like it. The enemies have near-perfect aim at almost all ranges, so there is a lot of jiggle peaking and prefiring angles. There have been a few times where enemies have shot me clean through walls as well, making this even more annoying.I really do with there was a more in-depth kicking system. Like maybe a grapple that tosses bodies or a wall climb. The sneaker abilities kind of help, but there are really only a few that are even worth using.Even with these flaws, i'd still recommend the game. There are a lot of funny gags and good gameplay in here. Keep in mind that if you don't do the challenges, the game is only really 3-5 hours (about the same as hotline miami), so you may want to wait for a sale first.

_childDocuments_.review: Anger Foot is a very fun game... for the first three or four levels. The experience gets boring very quickly. _childDocuments_.review: Devolver Digital REALLY likes this gameplay formula. It's Hotline Miami and Katana Zero. Again. But in first person and with a foot fetish. A fast paced action game wherein you and the enemies die very easily. But you don't even need to kill everyone in this one; just make it to the end of the level and go for optional challenges if you care to. The game plays well enough, and the gameplay itself is immensely satisfying. All of the guns feel and sound powerful as they one shot every enemy, kicks kill as many enemies as they hit, and making it to the end of a tough level is a great feeling. However, the game is held back by a few gripes that hamper the overall fun factor.The game runs like trash. A cartoony game that mostly takes place in cramped and confined spaces should not run this poorly, dropping into the low 20fps range on some levels. I get better performance in Elden Ring. The level design in some places feels very half-baked and unfair. Enemies with guns have perfect accuracy as long as they have you in their sights, and the amount of rooms that are just like "♥♥♥♥ you, here's 6 handgun guys in a group behind a door with no cover." is a bit too high for it to be an accident. Hotline Miami and Katana Zero work because they're top down and side scrolling, meaning that you can see enemies coming and react to them before they have the chance to kill you. But in Anger Foot if you can see an enemy, they can see you and are already shooting you (and in the case of shotgun guys, you're already dead.) There's one level in particular that has a switch to open a door at the bottom of a stairwell with shotgun guys on every flight, meaning that you just have to pray that you won't get one shot every time you turn a corner...4 times in a row, and it sucks.The boss fights are all bad, ranging from frustrating and annoying to braindead easy. None of them feel like tests of skill, just obnoxious obstructions or barely inconveniencing speedbumps.A lot of the unlockable shoes just aren't very good. A lot of them are either gimmicks to earn certain level stars or exceedingly weak compared to others. Once you unlock the first pair of boss shoes, they'll basically carry you to the end of the game, leaving me to wonder what most of them are really for. And I know it's low hanging fruit, but the game is WAY less funny than it thinks it is. It feels like an early Adultswim show, but stripped of the edginess and soul. If you're the kind of person that thinks Family Guy is high art (a.k.a 14 years old) you'll probably be pissing yourself laughing at the jokes, but I barely cracked so much as a smile for the vast majority.It's funny because sex.It's funny because drugs.It's funny because disgusting.It's funny because random.That's it. I laugh more times in a 30 second clip of Xavier Renegade Angel or Boondocks than I did in my entire 8 hour playthrough.In the end, I can't recommend this game for any price above a massive discount. It could have been a lot better designed and a lot better optimised, and by the end I was just waiting for it to be over.

_childDocuments_.review: Anger Foot was a day-one purchase for me almost by accident - I remember playing the demo during one of Steam Next fests, really liking it, and adding the game to my wishlist. Come July 11, I stumbled upon a notification that the game was getting released that day, and figured "Why not?"So, what is Anger Foot? From initial impressions, Anger Foot looks a lot like a first-person Miami Hotline. While there are some superficial similarities in graphics and gameplay, the games are vastly different in terms of quality and execution.The story of Anger Foot is simple and quite fitting for a stripped-down shooter: You are Anger Foot, the only independent criminal in… uhm… "Poop" City. One night, right before you're about to sit down and watch a movie with your lady love, a helicopter bursts through the wall of your apartment and absconds with your rare sneaker collection.Like any self-respecting sneakerhead, you immediately start a rampage of vengeance to get your kicks back, killing half the criminals and dismantling every major gang in the process. But seriously, those were some pretty sweet sneakers.After this brief introduction, you get into the meat of the game - four stages comprised of about 15 linear shooter missions, each with a boss fight at the end. The goal of each mission is to get to the exit in one piece, which may or may not include killing all the enemies in your way. To this end, you'll use any gun you can scrounge off of dead enemies, and of course, your trusty kick.Each level comes with optional objectives you can complete to earn stars, which in turn unlock new sneakers you can equip for various passive bonuses. There are also short intermissions between some levels, letting you wind down and take in the vibe of the game.The art style is best described as "intentionally ugly". The models are simple but effective (especially when it comes to enemy shapes) and the whole game is bathed in a stylish neon color palette. It reminds me of the illustrations done by Bob Živković, a reference that is almost guaranteed to mean nothing to anyone who didn't grow up in the Ex-Yu region during the 90s.The driving beat of the music works great with the overall frenetic pace of the gameplay, and only gets more intense as the action starts. The weapon sounds are serviceable, if not great, and the environment objects give off a satisfying crunch as you kick them into pieces.Unfortunately, this is about everything positive I can say about the game.The writing is typically not that important for games like Anger Foot - the story is simply there as a loose framework to justify why you're wiping out hordes of crooks with your deadly feet - but even then, what we got is really disappointing. As I've said in several reviews by now, I understand that humor is highly subjective, but relying on juvenile jokes and references that will be outdated in six months just doesn't do it for me.The gameplay takes a cue from Hotline Miami in that you have to complete an entire level in one go, and if you die, a restart is only a button press away. The problem is, Anger Foot rarely, if ever, manages to capture that flow state from Hotline Miami, when you're cruising through a level on pure intuition and reflexes. Instead, you'll frequently die because a random enemy shot you from somewhere off-screen or you got swarmed by a horde you didn't know was there until you opened a door.This is further compounded by the fact that the levels tend to be pretty long. I actually gave up on the game at one point because I kept dying to some random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at the very end of one of the longer levels. Ultimately, I decided to come back and try to roll credits - a decision I would come to regret.Anger Foot presents a very interesting conundrum, one that in all my years of gaming, I've never seen before - all the best parts of the game are actually in the demo.When I played the demo back when it first became available, I assumed (and I would argue, rightfully) that what I was seeing was the first segment of the game. In reality, the demo combines the best levels from the first two segments of the game and adds the interactive cutscene from the very end. This way, it creates an illusion of a full narrative section that the completed game will expand upon.Instead, the finished game adds a bunch of mostly subpar levels with some mildly to moderately interesting boss fights. There are a few more interesting and unique levels thrown in the mix that weren't a part of the demo, but not nearly enough to make the finished product anything but disappointing.In fact, if you're a moderately skilled FPS veteran just trying to complete the story and not caring too much about the side objectives, I figure you'll be done with the whole thing in about 2 to 3 hours. For me, that's not nearly enough to justify the asking price of 25€, especially when you take the questionable approach to the demo into account.The only way I can recommend you buy Anger Foot is at a steep discount. In fact, I would recommend you simply play the demo, since it already has all the best bits of the game (EDIT: if, like me, you were wondering where the demo button went, it's now on the right-hand side, discreetly tucked between related games and tags). Personally, I find it hard to escape the feeling I've somehow been bamboozled, so do with that what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: wears thin incredibly quickly. doesn't feel like theres much of substance here beyond the slickly edited trailers. progression structure is tied to replaying levels and satisfying dull challenges like "only use melee" or "get 20 headshots" the core gameplay loop isnt satisfying enough to make this feel worthwhile or like an interesting twist on one's playstyle. ideally said challenges would feel like a reward for engaging with the game more deeply or incentivize tactics that the average player might not arrive at. instead, the challenges feel like vapid contrivances intended to pad out the run time. this game is clearly inspired by hotline miami but makes a pretty critical misstep in attempting to replicate its violent nirvana. namely, the soundtrack will fade out in between combat encounters as you move from room to room. similarly the tracks start from the beginning upon restarting the level. im honestly baffled by the decision to sell this game on its high intensity soundtrack and then design the game to neuter said soundtrack so thoroughly.incredibly disappointing. this game doesn't feel like it had much consideration put into it beyond Booter Shooter as a punchline and $25 usd is a steep asking price for a joke that gets old after the first trailer ends

_childDocuments_.review: It's very cool. Delicious visual style, excellent music.Fun concept..Enemies feel lazy, slow, and extremely unpredictable in their timing - they might shoot you instantly, or they might miss. They might shoot you after two seconds of staring at you, and hit. You might race through a hail of bullets from five enemies all firing loosely at nearby walls, and kick each one individually without getting hurt, or you might die instantly upon entering the room, with no sense of a structure, a system, a pattern to why.The sense of sheer randomness is discouraging. It's boring. Every run you attempt, after a few levels, begins to feel like a coin-toss, having nothing to do with your choices or your skill. They'll either shoot you very quickly, or they.. Won't. They'll either hit you, not fire at all, or miss wildly.The only reliable early-game technique to avoid getting shot is to not even breach; just kick the door and wait outside for the enemy AI to very slowly wiggle over to you so you can kick them before they can fire. It's very, very dull and mismatched with the music, not something I'd recommend anyone actually do - but it does work, and it really shouldn't, from a design perspective.The game feels like a really compelling art gallery, and even has genuinely funny writing - but to my surprise the game just isn't very fun. Not £21 fun, when I could buy several other games for that price that offer as much style, and a lot more depth.Maybe one day I'll pick it up again - but I'm not sure I'll ever manage to turn off my brain enough to find the repetition + cointoss on survival entertaining. It could have been a sort of 3d Hotline Miami, as many say - but Hotline Miami was a tightly designed machine, for all its simplicity, compared to Anger Foot. Here, I don't feel like I know why I died - sometimes they shoot you, sometimes they just stare at you then run in a random direction, and shoot at a wall several metres to the side of you..

_childDocuments_.review: To the point=====================A silly, fast-paced, vibrant and extremely chaotic FPS. A great purchase for fans of BoomShoots, Speedrunning and Hotline MiamiGood Stuff====================- The game has some excellent controls. Whether it's the gunplay or the titular kicking, everything feels great and responsive. Foot-punching through hordes of gangbangers is a ton of fun.- The designs of Sh*t city, its denizens and gangs, are all extremely unique. The game does a nice job of pacing out new visuals, even in the same hubs, to keep things visually interesting.- Each zone and sometimes individual levels, helps to introduce new mechanics and you won't see them being grossly overused. This can lead to you running in to new and fun ways to interact with the world the further into your playtime.- The soundtrack is incredibly fitting and matches the action perfectly. I personally do not like *WUB* WUB* style dance music but it works so well here I can't help but enjoy it.- There's a nice variety to the weapons and the enemies that use them. I feel like I was being given new gear and facing new opponents right up until the final map. While some of these are just different ways of using the same enemies ( like standard enemies who hang from ceiling tiles) it really helps breaking up the monotony.- There was another game recently, Mullet Mad Jack, that was a speed running game but I really disliked it since you can't stop and smell the roses in a level. This game promotes speed running ( and indeed it's when I had the most fun with Angerfoot) but it's not required so you can appreciate the whole world aesthetic.- The challenges, 3 per level, really help to increase the run time. From simply speed running, to not using gun, the using a specific sneaker, promote a ton of replayability.Bad Stuff=================- Boss 4. For the record, he's not difficult, but absolutely one of the least fun bosses with massive periods of immunity and, for some reason, random attack patterns where he can go for minutes without revealing a weak point.- The shoes, while interesting, never really struck me as critical. Sure it's Angerfoot's reason for living, but I did the vast majority of the game barefoot and enjoyed the hell out of it. There are a lot of sneakers but none of them really changed the gameplay in such a way that I wanted to use them regularly.- It would be nice if you could restart a map and equip a new shoe without having to exit a level and go back to the map. Small quality of life thing but it would be appreciated.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only halfway done, and already it feels like my 2024 game of the year. First, the visuals and character design are outstanding. It's feels very original and unlike anything I've personally seen. Kudos for the sound design. Not only a great soundtrack, but each thwack, boom, shot, and other noises just feels so good. Good variety of weapons, great use of kicking too. Many games include a decent kick, but here, the kick is the star, but the loadout offered feels good and progresses through out the game. Keeping things fresh. You can even throw guns at enemies to stun them when you're all out of ammo. Can't think of many games that'll let you do that. Another unsung hero is the amount of damage you can do. It's not quite "break walls" down like Red Faction, but the game offers plenty of destructible furniture. You're gonna want to sometimes just stop and appreciate the destruction and havoc you create. The way a broken chair piece lies on a enemies body just so.Story is very fun, and humorous. They built a really interesting would to enjoy, and I do feel like it could be explored further via spin-offs and potential sequels. I'd love to see an open world game in Crime City personally. I can only imagine a solid 16 player deathmatch would be chaos.Overall, the game slaps. _childDocuments_.review: Anger Foot starts off as a thrilling, chaotic ride, and I enjoyed my time unlocking challenges and progressing through the levels.However, the experience took a downturn when I reached the 3rd act. Playing on the Steam Deck, despite the verified badge, became increasingly frustrating due to severe performance issues. The last boss and subsequent levels were particularly cumbersome, with frame rates dropping to as low as 15 FPS even with all the graphic settings turned down to their lowest.It’s a shame because the core gameplay experience is fantastic. It’s a die-and-retry where you never feel too powerful, requiring strategy to master each level. The challenges add another layer of fun, but some became nearly impossible to complete due to the performance issues.The game’s universe is brilliantly crafted—insane, detailed, and smartly designed with shortcuts that let you exploit the levels. Causing chaos in Crime City to recover my beloved sneakers was incredibly satisfying.Speaking of, one of the best mechanics is the variety of sneakers, each with unique abilities that are fun to experiment with. The preemo pairs are especially great as you unlock them after each boss. However, I was a bit disappointed with the final pair, as its power felt underwhelming at that stage.Ultimately, if the performance issues were resolved, I’d be eager to come back and 100% the levels. It’s a fun and challenging experience with a banger soundtrack that deserves a smoother finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Pure, unadulterated ludokino. This game is a masterpiece.When people say something is "video game-ey," they usually mean that in a way that relates to older, 8-bit titles. Lives, floating pickups etc. Anger Foot is a newer kind of "video game-ey": less inspired by older console titles than multiplayer FPSs. The characters do fortnite dances when you die, most of the AI is meant to be comedically stupid, and the humor tends to be very "haha ragdoll funeee" (though the writing itself is not without some considerable wit: e.g. "The Crime Minister" is a fantastic name for a primary antagonist).The only flaws I can think of in this otherwise perfect game are on the technical side. I've heard others complain about Anger Foot's performance (despite cartoony graphics that one would expect to be easy on the processor). I haven't encountered these issues myself, but I can believe them, because I HAVE encountered some rather noticeable glitches. Now it's worth mentioning that some of these glitches were likely left in on purpose because they were funny. Puncturing multiple enemies with the same crossbow bolt, for instance, can cause their ragdoll physics-object bodies to flop around hilariously. But I've also seen some glitches where certain enemies can become incapable of attacking, or even invincible. For example: there's this ram enemy later in the game that can only be killed after doing this charge-attack. Unfortunately, there are times when it can get stuck in the charge's "ramping up" animation cycle, which leaves it completely invulnerable. This fortunately means it won't be able to harm you either, so you can just walk away. But it's still obviously  annoying for anyone trying to kill every enemy in a given level.Aside from that, though, this game is absolutely wonderful. Don't let any of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I mentioned above distract you (unless your machine might have trouble with Unreal Engine 5). I really only mentioned them so that the developers would see them and patch the bugs. Otherwise, I'd recommend this game to literally anyone who's ever loved first-person shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: A hyperviolent, crudely juvenile, psychadelic game about kicking doors into people. I kinda love it. Hotline Miami with a foot fetish. Truly, the angriest foot-based game ever.Pros:- Crunchy, fast-paced, addictive combat. Every time you kick a door in, it feels amazing. You can literally kick everyone in the game.- New weapons and enemy types regularly introduced, forcing you to adapt- Exactly as long as it needs to be- Some very challenging encounters that combine spawn knowledge with twitch reflexes to win, a good balance- Funny, bizarro story and world, everyone is a little freak straight out of an Ed "Big Daddy" Roth cartoon. Design and character work are phenomenal. ♥♥♥♥ City is such a great place, I'd love a Mirror's Edge style parkour game in this world.Cons:- Soundtrack can get a little repetitive. There's only so much DUN DUN DUN DUN DUN DUN DUDADADA DUN DUN DUN you can really tolerate- Slide shoe mechanic should just be part of your moveset, best shoes in the game- Enemies can be easily cheesed with doors- A few levels feel pasted on, I would have preferred less levels with more ideas. Some level challenges are just annoying and not fun (headshot kills and ignites stink)- Last boss fight is kind of a letdown

_childDocuments_.review: Anger Foot is a case in point of "this could have been an email, but I don't mind it"; what could have been a simple gimmick-based title that lasts for 2 hours of fun and then ends without leaving much of an impression is instead elevated into a surprisingly coherent, engaging, full-blown shooter. And a damn clever one at that.The game just keeps on expanding, reinventing itself, non stop throwing new tricks at you until the very end. Scripted sequences, new and surprising environments, toilet jokes, narrative interludes, gameplay-altering perks, inventive bossfights, vehicle sections, supreme selection of designer footwear, this and much more.Somewhere along the way you realize the story that's a joke is actually fun and engaging and somehow kinda' moody, and you start to get "into it", with the hectic action, awful but lovable cast of characters, dark, vulgar but somehow witty humour, all along to an insane gabber soundtrack pulsing at the forefront, you just feel the *vibe* this game has going for it. Loud, obnoxious and purposeful, Anger Foot is probably one of the most fleshed out and *atmospheric* first person shooters I've played since years.It's like urinating in a public toilet and sharing a joke with the guy taking a piss next urinal over and fifteen minutes of pissing later you're discussing your favourite 70's slasher movies and obscure death metal bands and you realize you've just met an insanely cool guy.That's what Anger Foot is all about. Taking a long, satisfying piss and enjoying every second of it. That, and the gabber techno.And drugs.Game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: Developed by Free Lives, Anger Foot is an adrenaline-pumping, lightning-fast action FPS that blends frenetic gameplay with intense, bass-thumping beats. Set in the chaotic and colorful ♥♥♥♥ City, this game lets players unleash their inner fury through the deadliest feet imaginable. While the music may get a bit repetitive over time, Anger Foot still delivers a thrilling experience that keeps you on the edge of your seat.Anger Foot excels in its fast-paced, high-energy gameplay. The primary mechanic revolves around using your feet to kick doors and enemies with brutal force, creating a satisfying rhythm of destruction. Each level is a caffeine-fueled fever dream, where quick reflexes and precise movements are essential. The variety of weapons and upgrades you can find along the way adds layers of strategy and excitement to the gameplay, keeping each run fresh and engaging.The game's vibrant visuals are a feast for the eyes. ♥♥♥♥ City is a beautifully chaotic urban jungle filled with slums, sewers, and skyscrapers, each area more colorful and outrageous than the last. The anthropomorphic enemies you encounter are both menacing and whimsically designed, adding to the game's unique charm. The visual style perfectly complements the game's frenetic pace, making every moment a visual spectacle.One of Anger Foot's standout features is its high replayability. The game encourages players to tackle levels in new, creative ways, offering various secrets and unlockables that keep you coming back for more. Whether you're mastering the art of speed, power, or style, there's always a new challenge waiting. The diverse collection of formidable footwear you can unlock adds a fun twist to the gameplay, allowing you to customize your approach and keep things interesting.The concussive, bass-thumping soundtrack is a central part of the Anger Foot experience. The relentless beats perfectly match the game's high-octane action, driving you forward with every stomp and kick. However, it's worth noting that the music can become repetitive over time, with limited variation in tracks. While the beats are undoubtedly hard-hitting and energizing, a bit more diversity in the soundtrack would have added to the overall immersion and excitement.Anger Foot by Free Lives is a wild, exhilarating ride that stands out for its unique blend of fast-paced action and vibrant visuals. Despite the repetitive nature of the music, the game's core mechanics, replayability, and chaotic charm make it a must-play for fans of high-energy FPS games. If you're looking for a game that combines frenetic foot-stomping action with an assault on all your senses, "Anger Foot" is sure to deliver a kick-ass experience that you won't soon forget. So lace up your shoes, crank up the volume, and get ready to kick some serious ass in the feverish underworld of ♥♥♥♥ City!

_childDocuments_.review: Impossibly addictive. Free Lives outdid themselves here, and I'm saying this as a guy who owns Broforce on three different platforms. A genius, frantic murder frenzy that can be compared to Hotline Miami, but paced and executed very, very differently. Absolutely different vibes. Hotline Miami works really, really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard to make you uncomfortable while playing. It's like a low-fi snuff film. Regardless of whether you think it achieves it, it's going for A Message. Anger Foot doesn't have a message because it's too busy being it's own sick thing, and I love that. Everything in the game feels great and tactile. Kicking a door down, roundhouse kicking a grenade back at the poor mook who threw it at you, annihilating a subway train full of dudes with a smg that feels like it might explode in your hand, the incredible soundtrack and weight the game has puts you in The Foot Zone immediately. The game continues to introduce shoes (think Hotline Miami's masks), weapons, enemies, and special mechanics right up until the very end, which is a hard act to pull off. My only real gripe, beyond some optimization issues (there are A Lot of physics objects in every single room and stuff gets frantic, but I'm pretty sure the devs know this given that there's an achievement based around tanking the frame rate) is that reloading after dying takes like .05 seconds longer than you want in this kind of game but that's not that much of a problem when dying treats you to the visual of an alligator man in a letterman jacket throwing it back with enough enthusiasm to make Juvenile weep tears of joy.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Performance issues in this game can be mitigated completely by disabling Hyperthreading (SMT) in the BIOS. That said, this sort of change shouldn't be necessary in order to get a new game to run optimally.Here's hoping an update fixes it. In the meantime, update to the beta patch and if you're still experiencing performance issues, try disabling Hyperthreading. --Review:All the stuff that makes the first series of levels charming (floaty physics; chaotic enemy behavior; hit-or-miss hit detection; borderline hit-scan enemy accuracy, etc.) works against the fun factor when you reach the sewers.The game was a little buggy before the sewer levels, but the plunger weapons--which are basically Scorpion's harpoon--clip through everything. You end up being pulled into the geometry or else being sidelined by a plunger clipping through a wall. Or else you try to pull enemies into the toxic waste for a mission objective and the enemy gets stuck inside the geometry instead. Throw in unnecessary hazards and tedious platforming and, man, I just don't know about this one...Anyway, I love Free Lives. I bought Broforce in Early Access and still play it to this day. Genital Jousting is a magnificent party game. GORN is godlike. Yojimbrawl is good dumb fun. Anger Foot was a great demo. They should've left it at that.

_childDocuments_.review: The story of your lad, one Mr. Anger Foot, who has all his prized footwear stolen by the city's most notorious criminal gangs & goes on a rampage through the entire city to get them back. Violence, toilets and feet ensue.Had a ton of fun with this game; huge fan of the aesthetic choices; a gross, grimy yet colourful world bursting with as much character as it has crime, punctuated by a well-pitched soundtrack comprising hip-hop beats and thumping jumpstyle rhythms. Gameplay is fast paced & energising, level design is generally clear and linear, albeit with plenty of hidden side areas & opportunities for shortcuts. The boss fights are fun for the most part; one of them late in the game I found to be a major sticking point, though the option to freely turn assists on and off, up to and including invincibility, is a welcome addition that allowed me to press on with the game.Story is straightforward, not too in-depth but it never needs to be. Interstitial "breather" levels offer opportunities to speak to the denizens of the city, who offer silly dialogue & amusing situations which add to the flavour of the game's world & themes. The world is vulgar, crass, and frequently rude, & I relished it.Finally, big fan of the design of Anger Foot himself; one of my new favourite video game lads. A lean, green kicking machine who looks as intimidating as he is, with a unique fashion style comprising mismatched colours & clothing, which serve to make his upper body look bulkier, while also accentuating and showing off his defining features, i.e. his legs, and his big stompy feet for stomping on you with. Love him.Overall, brilliant little game, heartily recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game ever since I played the demo what feels like a million years ago. People have already described it as a first-person Hotline Miami and the comparison is apt.The gameplay loop mirrors that of Hotline Miami; bust into a room, murder everyone, move on. You'll absolutely die in a few hits and start over, and the game-over-to-restart time is pretty short. Some of the levels do drag on a bit, which can make the deaths start to feel grating rather than annoying. But that might be just me and my lack of patience.What really infuses the game, however, is the hardbass music playing throughout, that ramps up when you're engaging enemies and ramps back down in lulls between combat. I'm not one that likes hardbass but the music in this is excellent and greatly enhances the gameplay to keep you going.This isn't no kiddie game though; it's very unforgiving and you'll die a lot. But, there's plenty of levels and shoes you unlock have different powers to keep the gameplay from going stale for a while.For an indie game, you'll be hard-pressed to find a game just like this, and for that alone I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: A mixture of booting, shooting, and speedrunning that hits all the right notes. Levels are tight and well-conceived, the pacing (both with intermissions and enemy roster appearances) is  just right, the challenges are fun to figure out, the unlockable mutators ("shoes") are cool, and the humor hits a sweet spot of mild-but-committed-to-the-bit.The boss fights are jarringly boring, since they're so divorced from the blitz of the regular levels. The final level seems like it should've been the template; a big crazy fight to test how good your CC, movement, and output are. But, they're just a speedbump on an otherwise great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun chaotic game with a lot of style, character, and refreshing gameplay, cannot recommend it enough.All the character designs and sounds make me laugh and smile (especially the fat wobbly flies hovering around). The animations, destruction, and physics are so satisfying when you are flying through rooms and chaos is erupting all around you. The dynamic soundtrack is also really unique and appreciated. The game also does a great job of easing you into the mechanics and helping you manifest your inner Anger Foot.You complete levels across a map and get stars based on completion and other objectives for the level. You can replay levels to collect more stars to unlock shoes that have unique effects. For example one that causes the doors you kick to explode on impact, another that causes everyone you kick to go zero-gravity.I can write a lot more but it simply won't do it justice, just go play the game, you will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: You are foot man, you go from apartment to apartment searching for new shoes. the only problem is your massive chad like feet can only find solace inside the colons of other people. Thus it is your curse to wander the city searching for the perfect ass to shove your foot up.For real though Anger foot is a fun, fast paced, bass thumping romp through the worst city to ever have a surprisingly robust infastructure.The Story is straightforward. Bad dudes have stolen your kicks. are you a bad enough dude to get them back?Gameplay is tight. Way tighter than i expected the final result to be from the beta i played several years back. You're expected to move quickly through rooms dispatching your enemies with feet, guns and at times other enemies, if it exists you can kick it, usually at someone elses face. Nothing to kick? throw your gun at their face (or shoot them lol) Nothing in your hands? hopefully you've got one of the special shoes equipped that give you somthing like a slide or charge kick.Theres a star reward system for unlocking more shoes, you get 1 star every level but can get at least 2 more by beating their (sometimes obsurdly hard) challenges. Things that range from "no jumping" to "use only your feet" to "beat the level in 30 seconds with no survivors."They run from "might do it on accident" to "Get your south korean gamer buddy to do it for you."The world is quite silly and entertaining. ♥♥♥♥ City looks like Sesame Street if the zoomers ran it. The cartoony almost muppet style of the art design stays really consistent throughout making the entire experience feel really fun.Completionists will find this game to be their next deep bag of crack but those who are here for the ride should still find a fun time too given the asking price.TLDR: Muppets with guns steal your shoes. Are you a angry enough dude to get them back?
_childDocuments_.name: Anger Foot

_childDocuments_.review: I swear, this game is like someone modded the Mighty Foot in Duke 3D, gave it extreme knockback, and decided to base an entire game around that concept and the results are amazing. This is one of the most fun FPS games I've played. Relentlessly fast paced and wacky, it offers no pretenses.Anger Foot is a refreshing parody of a vigilante man kicking and shooting his way through a crime infested city, everything is taken to wonderfully cartoonish levels of creative silliness all while set to some really awesome, addicting beats. Everything is geared towards the fast paced action, right down to the fact I don't have to waste time reloading guns. Instead, I chuck the empty gun, stun two enemies like I threw a boomerang, run in to kick them down, and just take their guns instead. Way more entertaining than laborously tedious reload animations.The narrative is a throwback to silly, simple, excuse plots. Straightforward and funny, while giving the game its charm. Some nice breather areas between levels help set the stage and provide some laughs. Enemy variety - both visually and gameplay wise - are simple, yet creative and do the job well. Level design is simpler and less exploratory than older FPS games, but it plays into the fast pace while providing interesting challenge areas, making it more fun than just hallway - cutscene - repeat.The difficulty can be a tad unforgiving. Even the most basic enemy can take you down in one hit and they're not that sluggish on the draw. Coupled with devious encounter areas in later levels, this can make for some great fights. Though if it gets frustrating, the game is thoughtful enough to provide some assist options to adjust things to your liking. I definitely appreciate this commitment to making sure the game is fun, first and foremost, for as many people as possible and not just cater to elitists who complain everything is "too easy."All in all, great game. If you like fast paced run and gun action and enjoy craziness that doesn't take itself seriously, you'll probably enjoy this too.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is spot on and simple, the fighting is fluent and fits right in place, the enemies are distinctive and funny, and I still have laughs with my friends about a literal pigeon in riot gear. Anger Foot Is the best game inspired by Hotline Miami, Devolver along with Free Lives have done it in the best way possible and i still can't believe that i got an ORIGINAL GAME for the money that was given to buy this. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, if you like what you see in the trailer/demo and plan to do additional challenges outside of the main story, the game is worth it. It's an absolute blast! If you're going to rush through all the levels, wait until it goes on sale.------------What you see in the trailer is what you get, with the levels getting more challenging, more enemies, get added and more weapons/abilities are unlocked. Going for the fastest times on each level has been really fun. The music is always bumping and the NPC dialogue always cracks me up.Since I've seen people on the fence about the game due to concerns with length and performance for the price I wanted to weigh in with my experience now that I've finished the game. Length-wise, 100%ing the content at launch took me 18 hours.Performance-wise, my higher end build has been 144fps/1440p, on max settings for a vast majority of my playtime, but the larger levels or levels with a ton of enemies (especially later in the game) do suffer from frame drops. It was never unplayable, but did feel rough at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this one! As promised, there's plenty of anger and lots of kicking.
