Also I said performance was mostly fine, I did suffer a few frame rate drops at times and I'm running a 4090. Those moments were rare, though. Now I want more of this world. It took me about 6 hours to get through the game, but there's tons of replayability thanks to the brutal challenges for each stage. Plus, there are even more sneakers to unlock!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; its a good game, go get, you wont regret it.My not so TLDR:The music is kickass, but I wish it were a bit stronger. I'm only at chapter two, so maybe it gets better—who knows.I played the demo, and I don't know what happened after it, but besides some extra decals, the differences I noticed included an immense FPS drop. I'm not the slightest bit interested; it's done very barebones. _childDocuments_.review: Hotline Miami, but with a foot fetish in a weirdly fun way. Overall, it's a rock solid corridor shooter with an emphasis on speedrunning and precision. The game doesn't overstay it's welcome and it has some funny moments. Each level has two unique challenges to spice up how you approach levels. I found these challenges to range from "very fun" to "not even going to attempt because I'll hate the level afterwards". You have to replay missions quite a bit to get all the challenge stars which encourages replayability and it will certainly appeal to some people. I lost interest pretty quick in "completing" each level once the challenges started getting less fun. You use challenge stars to unlock new shoes which provide new abilities. To be honest, 90% of the shoes are worthless and not useful whatsoever outside of specific challenges which was disappointing. Bosses were mostly fun although I wasn't a big fan of the pig boss due to the wonky controlling of the boat in it's final phase. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game in spite of a few bugs or minor gripes here and there. The devs really need to fix the game's performance though. It's worth playing if you enjoy boomer shooters, Hotline Miami, and/or toilet jokes.

Freelives the studio behind this gem is based out of Cape Town South Africa.  Before release there were lots of vlogs about the development of the game.  They were vocal about making a world that in a way mirrored their own reality with a heavy does of satire and flat out childish humor.  ♥♥♥♥ City is a crime ridden version of Johannesburg that makes for a memorable locale.  The writing is hilarious, between some levels there are areas with non hostile NPCS you can talk to and I go out of my way to interact with every one.  The game play is a mix of John Wick meets Hotline Miami.  Where you go kicking doors and mowing down baddies left and right.  The game is no slouch either.  The levels are challenging, but the extra unlock-able stars to get shoes which modify the run with buffs are what makes it so compelling.  All this coupled with a BANGIN' original soundtrack from Jay Booty makes for a fantastic experience.  I can't wait to jump back in.  Now what are you waiting for?GET ANGRY

name: SAND LAND
detailed_description: Deluxe Edition The Deluxe Edition includes: • Full game • My Room Furniture Set: Army Base • My Room Furniture Set: Hideout • Speed Demon Pack • Beelzebub Decal Set About the Game Dive into a desert world where both humans and demons suffer from an extreme water shortage - SAND LAND. Meet the Fiend Prince Beelzebub, his chaperone Thief, and the fearless Sheriff Rao, and follow the team on an extraordinary adventure in search of the Legendary Spring hidden in the desert, and much more. The end is only the beginning, as beyond this arid ground lies a mysterious new realm to explore - Forest Land. This action-RPG is a nostalgic and heartwarming world created by Akira Toriyama, where you will become the main character, Beelzebub. Learn how to control his powers and lead your company of heroic misfits, exploring the legendary world of SAND LAND and the brand-new Forest Land. But beware of the many dangers that populate them: between bandits, fierce wildlife, and ruthless Army Generals, reaching the spring and saving the world won’t be easy! Use your tact and imagination to develop tanks and other vehicles that will help you navigate these vast resourceful lands, using a wide array of part combinations. Build up your base of operations into a thriving city, with the help of the people you meet along the way in this desert. RIDE VEHICLES FROM BEYOND YOUR IMAGINATION Unlock vehicles that can be leveled-up with various mechanic parts including weapons, engines, and suspensions. Design and operate a large variety of mechas including Battle Tanks with powerful cannons, Motorbikes that speed through deserts, and Jump-Bots that bounce over rivers to explore every corner of the continent. UPGRADE AND CUSTOMIZE YOUR EXPERIENCE Become Beelzebub, master his demonic powers and develop his fighting abilities to match your playstyle. Rao and Thief, your loyal acolytes, also have access to specific attacks, so that the team is never defeated, but always stronger. Your vehicles can be built and customized as well, to fit your taste, including paint options and decals! Save Sand Land and defy Forest Land Heaven your way and in style! EXPLORE BEYOND THE DUNES Take off on a bumpy adventure and discover two marvelous worlds. Explore SAND LAND and its canyons, unveil its secret, overcome fierce foes, and pave the way to the Legendary Spring! In Forest Land, discover a brand-new world in which awaits lush trees, reddish sunsets, verdant lands...and long-awaited waters sources! BECOME THE SAVIOR THE WORLD NEEDS Develop a basecamp in the city of Spino as you build relationships with its inhabitants. Watch the town and its capabilities grow as you bring back exiled people of the desert to Spino. Listen to their requests and wishes, and unlock useful materials and city features that will help you make SAND LAND thrive again!

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't super hyped about SAND LAND when I first learned about it. I love Akira Toriyama and his creations but, it just didn't look super exciting to me. The only thing that interested was the the art style. I looooove Toriyama's character design and vehicle design but that's all that drew me to this game. Well, today a streamer I like got a free code and gave it a go and suddenly I was immersed in the lore of the world and by the goofy characters. I was hooked. So I bought the game immediately a few hours before it came out. When I got back home the game had just released and I downloaded it and played up until the point I stopped watching the stream. And I'll say, it is FUN.The art style, character design, vehicle design, lore and characters are ALL great so far. The gameplay is actually tons of fun both in character combat and vehicle combat. This surprised me greatly and it's awesome! When not in a vehicle it's your typical new form of JRPG where there isn't any stopped time to attack or use items, it's all in the moment. Nothing too special about it, but it's fun and that's all you need! The vehicle combat is where the game shines right now to me. Not only is it super fun to roll around the desert in a tank and fight, but it has tons of upgrades and customization! So far I've only upgraded a few of the weapons but I can tell it's going to get crazy from here on! I also learned right before I stopped my play through for the day that there are other vehicles you will be getting throughout the game for different types of combat and maneuverability. Looking forward to that!However, so far the only bad thing I can say about this game is the stuttering. Once in awhile the game stutters and drops frames a bit. It's not that bad and you can easily play through it while it only lasts a few seconds. I hear this is an Unreal Engine 5 problem from a few others and that streamer I was talking about earlier. It won't stop me from playing the game but I felt I had to share this info!I will update this review as I progress through the game so stay tuned!If you're on the fence about getting this game I highly recommend it so far, even if JRPG/RPG's aren't your usual game because the story and characters are just fun!R.I.P. Akira Toriyama!
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I've been really enjoying this game. It hits just the right check-boxes of a fun-to-play, nostalgia filled, JRPG; so much so that I'm taken back in time a bit to being a kid and enjoying a long weekend just nerding out.But there's some glaring issues and I think its because they wanted to rush the game out, after Akira Toriyama's untimely death (rest in peace man, you're iconic and missed) and I desperately hope they patch these problems out.Here's what I like:1. Iconic art style that beats a nice blend of cel-shading, hatchy, hand-drawn goodness in Toriyama's style2. At least when I looked through comments, no one was talking about how amazing the music in this game is, like...seriously. I will leave it paused in the background when I step away to do dishes just for the ambiance.3. The fact you can build and customize a bunch of vehicles to explore a pretty huge map, and more and more becomes available to explore as you do, kinda keeps you going back to old places to look for things4. Not sure how others feel about this, but the segmented map + tower map unlock a'la Breath of the wild/Tears of the Kingdom is a plus for me. It's a good system5. All in all, it's been enjoyable to play and the characters seem relatable enough to want to keep playing.Now what I don't like...1. If you cannot fix the constantly-repeating field audio clips involving character banter, please add an audio option to mute character audio in the field.  I'm happy to hear the voice acting in important scenes, and story related moments, but without proper delay and a trigger that says "This audio clip has played already", well, it's the worst and most egregious thing ruining a game that is otherwise pretty solid. "Hmm, I'll keep it. This might prove to be useful later on" played no fewer than 529 times in a span of about 2 hours. We counted. WE COUNTED. Please patch it. Please? 2. Not all of the settings options actually seem to work, like anti-aliasing, at least not on my install, and there were some other weird resolution issues and limitations, not sure why. 3. Some of the character dialogue in english seems...contrarian? Like the guy outside of the junker city, speaks and acts like you're not allowed in and to leave...and I had a moment of like "Is...is this story, or" and then walked right in like the entire conversation never took place. But, basically, the annoyances are not mild, but are limited in scope so far. Put another way, Hmm, I'll keep it. This might prove to be useful later on.Updating 5/12/2024 with new somewhat gamebreaking issues:1. Cannot use crawl points in ruins, Belz leans down to crawl then immediately stands back up, no matter which side you're crawling from, this happens on all crawl points, only worked on 2-3 early game, thought it was intentional at first, but just tried both sides of a crawl point and it fails2. Cannot use zip lines on edges, character clips edge and falls (usually taking a lot of damage) Happens on spiral mountain, the place you chase the swimmers up a cliff, and a few other places3. Motorcycle and Buggy cannot make jumps you're intended to make with them, they fall short. Regardless of where you hit the nitro, success is about 1 in 12 tries on my gameAnyone know if they're going to try and patch-fix any of this?  Through the magic of japes you can finagle around some of the problems, but others...not so much

_childDocuments_.review: This game reaches into the folds of my brain and scratches a very particular itch (more like 2 or 3 itches), and it's kind of amazing that it exists considering how specific my interests are for a game like this. First off, I love my some big clunky mechs/tanks. I love the way it feels to pilot these things and I love the combat. Secondly, I love desert settings. My favorite area in most games is the desert, like in Breath of the Wild, I always rush right to it and spend as much time as I can there. There is just something incredibly enchanting to me about the vastness and the mystery. And this game captures that feeling of awe and scale not just in the desert but in other ways as well that I won't spoil. The third and final itch is that diversity for our cast of main characters. This is a Japanese game, so obviously there aren't any LGBT characters or anything, but having TWO old guys as main party members is really unique, and I am always glad to have characters in my JRPGs that aren't just teenagers. The main character is also somewhat of a kid, and he is very likable and endearing. I like Ann as well, though she is not a "main" party member. I want to point out a couple things that might make other peoples experience for this game more enjoyable. First, switch the tank controls. I don't know why they default them to where camera is facing and not where vehicle is facing. Maybe because it's more "mainstream," but if you want a good tanky experience, switch the controls. Second, I find the dub to be PRETTY dang weak. Where as the Japanese voice actors are all killing it. RIP Akira Toriyama. _childDocuments_.review: SAND LAND is an open-world adventure game adaptation of the 2000 comic series of the same name and undoubtedly one of Akira Toriyama's final works. But does the game do the artist and the series justice, or is this just another anime game left in the dust?You take on the role of Beelzebub, the Fiend Prince, on a journey across the drought-ridden, scorching Sand Land to find the legendary spring and bring peace to the savage land.But journeys are rarely so simple as the King has plans for the legendary water source and is making a fortune on keeping it as a commodity and will do everything in his power to keep it under control.You must fight against the army, bandits and even nature itself on the quest to pry the water supply from the government's grasp, but does the story end there? You will have to dive right in to find out.SAND LAND delivers a well-designed and intriguing plot despite having some moderate pacing concerns throughout the campaign. With a fascinating cast of characters to fill the few empty moments with entertainment, so you will never be bored. With that said, the open-world dialogue is incredibly repetitive and becomes tedious to listen to after some time, with no way to turn down the frequency or off entirely.A substantial part of the game is exploring its sizable open-world environment, which takes place across the entire campaign as new areas continuously open up to you.Exploration will be your primary way of unlocking and upgrading items for your vehicles because some of the best items in the game are hidden in out-of-the-way places, and resources scattered across the world, such as ore and wood, are used to upgrade them. Unfortunately, however, the map is pretty subpar in this regard, only really helping you navigate the world and not showing you where to obtain certain resources which makes attaining some mid to late game upgrades substantially more difficult than it should be.Which brings us to the robust customisation options available to you, SAND LAND has an enormous catalogue of parts, upgrades, decals and paints for you to truly make your bot your own, and some of the upgrades can truly alter the function of your bot in surprising ways.Fighting and killing enemies around Sand Land will also net you significant rewards in the form of resources used to upgrade vehicle parts or sell for money.Combat is the other significant aspect of the game, and you will spend a large part of it upgrading your vehicles or skills for this very purpose.Combat can be split into two categories: melee, which is your ground combat outside of vehicles and vehicular combat, which takes place in numerous types of bots you will unlock during the campaign.Melee combat is essentially fighting on the ground with your fists, and you will gain abilities throughout the story that will vastly change the flow of combat. You will also be able to invest skill points into a tree that bolsters your damage, health and the effects of your combat abilities.Vehicular combat is a little more complex as you will need to constantly upgrade your vehicles to stay relevant against the enemies of the world. You will use the items and resources you find in the world or on enemies to upgrade individual parts and increase your overall output potential.The average enemies scale with your level, but bosses are level-capped, so it is simple to out-level the story content. The boss battles usually take place in moderately sized arenas, allowing you some flexibility on what bot you want to use to defeat them. They are not incredibly diverse or complex to combat but can provide varying difficulty depending on your level.SAND LAND is near-literally bursting at the seams with side quests to complete as you progress through the story. All of the side quests give you some insight into the world and what has led to the events that are taking place and provide you with some significant upgrades if you complete them all.On top of the plethora of side activities the game has for you to complete you also are given the option to build and design a home for your character. Decorating the house does not provide you with any bonuses whatsoever but is a fun and creative minor activity to do between missions to give you some time to reflect.This game has not been designed for realism, but it still delivers a stunning visual experience that will continuously catch your attention with beautiful open vistas and seamless environments. The cell-shading art style enhances the visual experience by delivering a fresh perspective to the series.The audio doesn't quite hit the same standard. While the music in the game is captivating and fits every situation perfectly, harmoniously blending in levels of nostalgia for fans of Toriyama’s works, the general audio is pretty repetitive and monotonous for the most part, recycling most of the sounds for the entire game.While running SAND LAND on max settings at 2560 x 1440, the game ran buttery smooth the entire time with very few minor graphical or performance issues to report.RAM: 32GB 3200GHz G-Skill (DDR4)CPU: i9 10900KA 3.70GHzGPU: MSI Ventus RTX 3080Note: I have decided to remove the performance usages as they are only relevant to my build and not the general user base.SAND LAND does an impressive job of creating a vibrant open-world experience filled with diverse characters, environments, enemies, and customisations all wrapped in a captivating well-written story, making it one of the most outstanding anime games that I have ever played. With that said, Some foundational design flaws hold it back from being top-tier, and you may only find yourself captivated if you are already a fan of Toriyama's work. If it sounds like something that may interest you, I’d recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. I think I've reached the end of what I want to experience with . Just to offer a quick synopsis of my thoughts about this game before getting into a bit more detail, I think this would be a wonderful anime season, and the cutscenes are a lot of fun to watch. The game itself is as mid as it gets however. In fact, I struggled with wanting to even fire this game back up, which for me means it will be retired unfinished. Will I watch the 'movie' on YT though? Definitely. I know  was excited to see his vision in game form and believed this would be something people would truly enjoy. And perhaps he was correct, but while I think the devs honored him with the writing, they did not honor him with the actual gameplay. And, that $59.99 price tag? No. Just no. At most, this should have been priced at around $30 retail. On top of that, the DLC is just embarrassing. Remind me why you'd pay for vehicle colors.With that out of the way, the first thing I want to talk about is the sort of cel-shading used for the graphics. That was a good design choice in my opinion. The characters in the game and some of the environments really looked great. Unfortunately, there are vast expanses of areas that look incredibly boring and blah with assets being used over and over and over. Such as the desert, the inside of the ship wreckage, and so on. Interesting mix of real care, love and attention to detail balanced by plenty of phoned in artwork.The voice over work is top notch. The voice actors really did the characters in this game justice. And the dialogue is pretty hilarious on top of all that. Our protagonist constantly trying to convince people and demons that he is evil despite helping everyone who needs help struck me as being particularly funny and heartwarming lol. It is real easy to get sucked into the story as a result of how well the voice actors portrayed everybody in this game, and there is a lot of dialogue with quite a large number of characters.The gameplay...well, it's not good. It's not bad either. It's just a rehash of every other game you've played, and feels like every other mid example of cartoons and anime being turned into video games. It starts out kind of fun, but after a few hours, the melee and tank combat just gets boring AF. The upgrade system is pretty basic and requires a LOT of fetch questing. Movement is pretty seamless as is tank combat. Melee feels very janky. And, there are sections where the game switches to 2.5D side scrolling platformer for some reason. Those sections are universally annoying. Stealth is super basic. Nothing really stands out as good, with the sole exception of being able to summon your tanks/mechs pretty much whenever you want. That specific aspect of the game was a nice touch and something a little different.You (Beelzebub) and two of your companions (Rao and Thief) earn XP that can be used to buy some upgrades, and some of those are actually useful, such as Rao being able to also use a tank in combat. A lot of them seem more like an afterthought. Ann can't be upgraded but she does operate a shop which can upgrade your vehicles (tank, mechs, etc...).There is a lot of exploration available in the game. Unfortunately, that amounts to finding same-y caves with some loot/crafting materials, temples with some loot/crafting materials, and creatures that drop...some loot/crafting materials lol. You obviously will also find some points of interest that are story related, and there are plenty of side quests, bounty missions, and so on to keep you occupied. It's filler content for the most part and I did not find myself really wanting to do most of that. You will find some NPCs that can be convinced to move to the town you use as your homebase though, and that helps build up said town, which is in and of itself another side quest that has you running fetch quests and battle quests to get each NPC to be willing to join up. And the fetch quests....this game loves its fetch quests.I thought the melee combat was not well suited to a gamepad, but everything else handled just fine played with a controller. I used an Xbox X controller, personally.IDK. It's not all bad for sure, but Sand Land isn't particularly good at all taken as a game. But, if you are enamored of the manga and one anime season that was released, this could offer you another season's worth of content, and so taken as an anime season, it is excellent, albeit waaaayyyyy overpriced. Akira Toriyama did not live to see this game released, and I think he would have adored the story enough to overlook the meh gameplay, but me personally, I found it difficult to do so. I ended up becoming very bored with this game by the time hour eight rolled by. I'm giving this a positive rating, but with significant addendums to that rating. My advice would be to wait for a hefty discount before diving into this game. But, if you are so much a fan of Dragon Ball and Sand Land that you can overlook mid gameplay, then maybe it'll hold value for you at full price. YMMV. And a special thanks to my friend who gifted this game to me. Despite my criticism, I appreciated the opportunity to give this game a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Having beaten the campaign and explored every nook and cranny of the map, I can atest that this is an overall solid open world game. It might be best described as existing inbetween 2015's Mad Max and Far Cry: New Dawn as you basically go around the map doing missions and building/upgrading your mechs (which range from a tank to a hoverbike). Although the game doesn't really expect or even want you to go around collecting all the chests and completing all side activities (maybe except the arena), this is absolutely not the game for people going through an "open world fatigue" phase. If you are in the mood for some map objective clearing and don't feel like giving Ubisoft another cent (good on you), this is very much the next best thing.The mechs are undeniably the focus of this game. Although on-foot combat is still very prevalent and has its own progression, all the rewards and resources and parts you collect are in service of improving and customizing your fleet. There is a surprising variety of different kinds of mechs you find and each one of them can be customized in order to better fit the role you want of them. This, of course, doesn't cover the more cosmetic side of things with the also neat addition of a painting/decal editor that really lets you add that personal touch.The other main aspect of the game is building up Spino, a run-down town you encounter early in the game and get to slowly improve throughout. It's not really something you get to directly control, but instead it works as a kind of visual indicator of your progress, as some missions bring someone new to the town that adds a shop or, at the very least, makes a dusty corner of it look like new. I really appreciate how it's done, but I would be lying if I didn't say I would have liked to have more interesting ways to engage with this place that is very much your home base. The game does drop some hidden chests on each newly-renovated area, but beyond that there isn't really anything to do except darting between shops and the mechanic's workshop.Well, there isn't anything except a neat little Animal Crossing-style house furnishing feature. You get furnishings by either going to the respective shop or by finding some in chests spread around the world. You get three areas of different sizes and you are able to decorate them as you see fit (at least once you bought the access to them). I didn't get much mileage out of it, as this sort of criative feature isn't much my style, but I reckon many others might find this very appealing and fun to spend hours doing.Despite not doing anything revolutionary, this game still feels very ambitious with all that it is throwing on this 60€ package. It's not nearly perfect, of course. The stealth-enforcing Army Base objectives, for example, feel like a not-so-pleasant throwback to more annoying times even if the game has the decency of throwing in plenty of checkpoints so you don't keep losing progress because you had the misfortune of turning a corner and finding yourself face-to-face with a patrolling enemy soldier. It also had some performace issues, likely shader-related stuff as there was a lot of noticeable stuttering on my initial hours with this but subsided later on. With this said, I think it is a very solid package. 60€ on PC for this might be a stretch, but this is very much a "one-and-done" game that came out perfectly functional on day one and that you can just play on your terms. That sure is something that's oddly uncommon these days and I think people don't appreciate it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Sand Land is a bold and ambitious Action-RPG brimming with mechanical systems and diverse activities, set in a heartwarming yet post-apocalyptic open world created by the legendary Akira Toriyama. While it offers a wide range of features, it sometimes feels like a jack of all trades, mastering none. This range can detract from a more focused and polished core experience—however, the charm lies in its engaging story, stunning visuals, and enjoyable vehicular gameplay. Fans of Toriyama's work will especially appreciate the vibrant world and its delightful narrative. In a post-apocalyptic world, where water has become a rare commodity, the once-flowing river that sustained the land dried up. The king now monopolizes the remaining water supply. Sheriff Rao, frustrated by the king's greed, seeks help from the demons of Sand Land to find the rumored source of water. Demon prince Beelzebub and his friend Thief join Rao on this quest, which enrages the king, who mobilizes his forces to try to stop them.The story has an undeniable charm, infusing their journey with a sense of fun despite the dire circumstances. The characters are well-written, the journey is delightful, and the world is unique. This adaptation expands on the original manga with exciting new content that fans of the series will appreciate the added details and references. Sand Land ambitiously attempts to blend various genres to offer a diverse and engaging experience. Still, it fails to stick the landing due to stretching itself too thin and broad. The combat system is incredibly simplistic, whether inside or outside your vehicle. When on foot, you have four actions: a light, a strong, and a special attack, plus a dodge move, that's it. This limited set of options makes the combat on foot feel like a chore. As you level up, you unlock traits that allow different special attacks or stat boosts, as well as those of your companions.Fortunately, most of your time is spent in your vehicle, where combat is more engaging and varied. The different vehicle types and weaponry offer a broader range of strategies, making vehicular combat far more enjoyable and polished. The gameplay loop remains easy and repetitive, as enemies never adapt and always aim for your last given position. Simply running around them ensures they miss. Changing the difficulty only increases their damage and health without altering their behavior, which doesn't help the problem.Bosses look visually fantastic but function the same mechanically, making them dull to fight. However, despite everything, I found vehicular combat enjoyable enough to satisfy my playthrough. Sand Land's open-world design is immersive, with breathtaking aesthetics and stunning visuals. Navigating the vast desert avoids being tedious, thanks to various transportation methods and quick travel. The landscape has multiple activities such as stealth, side quests, challenges, ruins, hostile creatures, and bosses in remote camps. However, much of this feels more like a half-assed grind due to the mechanics needing to be fleshed out more. It is only worth it to experience the expanded world, but not for the gameplay alone. There is a surprising amount of customization, both cosmetically and mechanically. Vehicle upgrades, including weapons and parts, refresh the experience with each significant upgrade but require the tedious gathering of materials without clear guidance on where to find them or even if you can. The cumbersome UI makes it worse, as you must memorize needed items, locate the right shop, and buy materials individually (as bulk buying or selling isn't an option) before returning to craft upgrades. Cosmetic changes are extensive, but navigating the clunky menus is a hassle, and housing customizations, though cozy, serve no functional purpose, which is a missed opportunity and a bit pointless, unlike how by doing side-content you can slowly re-build Spino, which feels rewarding.  The visuals are simply stunning, perfectly capturing the essence of Toriyama's iconic style. The thick cell-shaded lines, vibrant colors, and detailed hatching and dotted shading create a gorgeous interpretation of his distinctive artistry. Deserts typically lack variety and visual appeal, but Sand Land makes its dunes aesthetically pleasing through clever-level design. The desolate environment is invigorated by its diverse inhabitants and thoughtfully placed structures. Although the architecture is sparse, it possesses a unique style that makes life in the wasteland not entirely bleak. The vibrant greens and lush, watery areas also offer a striking contrast and further showcase the game's impressive visual diversity despite the setting.Not to mention the incredible variety of vehicles and creature designs, which serve as the core centerpiece of Sand Land. These designs, combined with the world, seamlessly blend everything together, epitomizing Toriyama's distinctive style.The cast of VAs excellently breathes life into each character, from the main protagonists to the smallest of side characters, making the game world feel rich and authentic. While random one-liners might become repetitive, the dialogue remains engaging and enjoyable. Each character's words are delivered with depth and emotion, drawing you deeper into the narrative. Moreover, the sound effects are top-notch, providing the right impact during combat sequences and while traversing Sand Land. Every clang of metal and gust of wind adds to the game's immersive atmosphere.The OST brilliantly captures the shifting tones and moods, whether during intense battles, while exploring ruins, or simply wandering the vast desert. With standout tracks that elevate serene and adrenaline-pumping moments, it significantly enriches the game's post-apocalyptic atmosphere and emotional depth.

_childDocuments_.review: When the Japanese comic magazine Shonen Jump first reached US shores, I was in high school. It was a long time ago and the first issues had the very beginnings of Naruto and One Piece, but also had another series I'd never heard of. A short-lived series by Akira Toriyama of Dragon Ball fame called "Sand Land." It was a fun little series, didn't last more than around a dozen issues, but it was a neat idea and had some decent humor and action.If you'd told me back then that it would eventually be made into a video game, I'd have assumed you meant a quickie mobile cash-in of some sort.If you'd have told me it would become a really damn good open world adventure game I'd have called you insane. I'd have imagined that they would have done it for one of his longer-running series like Dr. Slump or, of course, Dragon Ball...But... here we are. The iconic tank of the series of course, but also various mecha, cars, and motorbikes. All of these you can fully customize the weapons, engine, and whatever moves them (treads, tires, legs, what have you) and even repaint and add decals and such. This really does look like the old comic book came to life, and thats a real treat for someone like me who re-read it a lot as a teenager because I didn't have a lot of money and stuff like Crunchyroll and Kindle didn't exist yet. Those of you who remember the old comic like I do will find that the end of that comic is actually just the end of part one of the story! There's a whole additional game beyond it involving a whole other country from Sand Land, an invading force, and new villains to fight.In the story you'll find a small village thats nearing the end of it's rope. Its mostly in ruins and people are drifting away from it. However, the vast majority of sidequests will end with you telling travellers, merchants, and the like about the village and sending them it's way. This has a direct impact on it by adding new shops, expanding the stock of existing ones, and making the village larger and much more vibrant. Its a real neat thing to see it go from a bunch of scrap metal to a proper desert city!You travel Sand Land as the adventuring party of the Fiend Prince Beelzebub, his demon companion Thief, and a human known as Sheriff Rao. As you travel, they will add commentary about the local landscape, tips on exploring, or just tidbits of desert survival... a lot. Constantly really. Bandai Namco would have been well served by giving us the option to either toggle how frequently they do this, or the option to turn it off completely.A bit of advice. If you see a random animal out and about in the desert: kill it dead. Every chance you get. Conservationism be damned. You NEED those bits to upgrade your vehicles! Desert Croc Steel, Petrodon Rubber, Scorpion Oil, the works! Do NOT spare the ammo with these things! If it moves, BLOW IT UP AND HARVEST IT FOR BITS! I can't count how many times I had to head back out into the desert when I found my latest upgrade needed steel made from the scales of those damn crocodiles out there...Its got some flaws, but I had a heck of a fun time with this one. If you're not sure you can try the demo, or just wait for a sale, but I'm enjoying myself.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really tough game to not recommend. There's a lot of stuff I really adore about it. Vehicle customization is absolutely wonderful, as is the wonderful variation in vehicle types. The game's artstyle is fantastic and really captures Toriyama's vibe and energy really well. I also did end up enjoying the town hub you build up over the course of the game, with it very effectively hearkening back to some Digimon World 1 nostalgia that's pretty dear to me.But ultimately, the game is at the end of the day, insanely repetitive. It offers decent enough rewards for exploration, but never any truly interesting sense of discovery since nearly all dungeons and caves and ruins you happen upon look extremely similar to one another and have really boring internal layouts. And the main story dungeons contain some of the worst, padded out, and downright boring level design I've ever encountered. You'll just follow your navigation marker through identical rooms for 45-75 minutes with some cutscenes peppered throughout.There's nice moments in the story, and it has some sweet enough things to say, but I really think you have to have a deep love for Toriyama and his vehicle design to get much outta this game. Absolutely not worth full price even for the die hard fans. Definitely wait for a 50% off sale minimum if you wanna jump in. And it is a lot better than the demo! Runs great on Steam Deck. Was able to tweak settings to get a mostly solid 40fps with pretty great visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, this game has blown through all the leeway I'm willing to give it, and I'm not going to endure another 30 hours of boredom to just complete it. I have a very high tolerance for the open world genre, but this is easily one of the most tedious and least interesting games I've played in recent memory. To start with the positives, the game does look great. The late Akira Toriyama's character designs are excellent and even the vehicles have a nice amount of character baked into them. The game has a similar visual style to Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot, where the characters are cell shaded while the world is slightly higher fidelity. It works well and if nothing else everything here is appealing to look at. However, this game suffers heavily from the dreaded Unreal Engine shader compilation stutter. I experienced this issue on two different machines, the ROG Ally as well as an RTX 3090 desktop. While performance was generally great on both devices, stuttering would crop up whenever a new asset or effect was loaded into the game world. If you play long enough these instances become less noticeable with time, but it is still frustrating that this known issue with the engine continues to crop up in games when it is not particularly difficult for the developers to fix. The biggest issue with this game overall is the incredibly boring and unsatisfying exploration. To start with, the majority of your vehicles are way too slow, topping out at around 50-60 mph. The world is overly large, with vast expanses of absolute nothingness between points of interest. When I started playing I didn't understand why this game needed an autopilot option, but after an hour I got it. You will spend so much time just holding the stick down as you slowly lurch towards your next objective that being able to just tap the autopilot button was a mercy. Not that there is much of interest waiting for you when you reach your destination. The majority of these are either small caves or climbable rock formations that take less than a minute to work through and reward you with a few treasure chests containing nothing but extremely common crafting materials you probably already have hundreds of. The world is absolutely brimming with this kind of cookie cutter, copy-paste map trash that most players will only bother to complete just to 'check it off the list'. All of this might be tolerable if it fed into interesting and rewarding progression systems. Unfortunately, Sand Land has some of the most aggressive level scaling I have ever seen. Every time you level up, the entire world levels up with you, meaning you are never going to encounter enemies out in the world who are beneath your level. What's worse is that there is a fundamental disconnect between leveling and your vehicles, given that only your characters level up through experience, while vehicles require crafting materials to progress further. Effectively, leveling up is a punishment, as your vehicles don't get any stronger from it, while all the enemies do. Crafting materials are also restricted by the regions available to you and the story progress, so it's very possible to out level your vehicles, causing you to lose ground against the enemies until you progress the story further. None of this is to say the game is particularly difficult. In fact, you will likely be hard pressed to die even once to most encounters on normal difficulty, as basic circle strafing is enough to defeat the AI of almost every enemy in the game. All of this results in a lifelessly flat difficulty curve, compounding the boredom and tedium of exploration. One negative I didn't expect came from the world building and story, which is all over the place. This game tries to juggle Toriyama brand goofiness with Fist of the North Star style post apocalyptic grittiness, and it doesn't really work. The game actually reminds me of Arkham Knight, in how you will mow people down with machine gun fire, run them over with your 2 ton death tank, only to have a character in a cutscene explain how nobody actually died and you non-lethally disabled everyone. Like, what? Really? Alright, so this is a light hearted adventure without any serious consequences. That's how it seemed anyway until I made a wrong choice in a side quest and a bandit straight up murdered an innocent girl right in front of the party. Why? Ohh, and by the way, you can't chase the bandit down and bring him to justice, because revenge is...LE BAD! This whole sequence of events was so off-putting yet asinine it just about killed any interest I had in seeing the story through to the conclusion.I really wish there were similar games I could unconditionally recommend over this one, but most post-apocalytpic open world games all have similar issues. I can say that I have personally enjoyed both Mad Max and Metal Max Xeno a lot more than this one, and though neither of those are perfect games, I would easily recommend either of them over this one. Maybe watch the Anime version instead if you can, otherwise avoid Sand Land altogether.

_childDocuments_.review: I just made my 5th and 6th vehicles in this game. I was gonna come here and make a review after I first got to the Legendary Spring from episode 5 or 6 of the anime by the same name and based on the same IP as this game is. This has quickly become one of my favorite anime games. The vehicle combat and using them to explore the world and dungeons is so much fun. Customizing them with various primary and secondary weapons, engines, and legs or suspensions depending on the kind of vehicle not only changes how the vehicle looks and what weapons it's bringing into combat, but how it moves in and out of combat and how much defense it has. Maybe you want a bit slower, but tougher legs/suspension. Maybe you want an incendiary grenade launcher instead of a regular one so you can leave sweet trails of fire around where you're Jump Bot is tossing grenades. Switching between vehicles in and out of combat is pretty seamless, and with you being able to make multiples of any of the kinds of vehicles you have unlocked so long as you have the parts and money required, you can fill your 5 capsule slots for vehicles with either an array of different vehicles for different situations you might run into on your journey-or up to 5 different versions of the same kind of vehicle if you wanted to do that for some reason. Although you can't swap out the Battle Tank you get near the start of the game until you complete the main story, so if you wanted all Jump Bots, or Hoppers, or Dune Buggies, you'd have to keep at least one slot for the tank.I'm probably biased from having watched half the anime that was coming out leading up to this game's release and that made me wanna check out the game, but I've been liking the story so far. Reaching the Legendary Spring is around where I left off in the anime as it felt like a good pausing point in the story to wait until I had played thru the game to see the rest of the story there and then come back to the anime and finish watching that later. A world where most of the water's gone and what's left is seemingly being completely controlled by a greedy King and his Royal Army so the protagonist and friends set off to find a Legendary Spring and restore water to the people suffering under the King's crazy prices for water and severe rationing of it. Fun enough story and of course things happen along the way to reveal more about the world and history of it. I did feel like the opening took a little too long for my liking to get into actually opening up and letting you really explore and play the game at your own pace like any good open world RPG should. I think it was 2 or 3 hours before I got to the town of Spino you'll be slowly building up over the course of the game and unlocked the garage there to start customizing my tank and other vehicles. I wish you were able to get there sooner, but having watched the anime, I get why it takes a while. It's following the story of the anime and at least that far into their journey, nothing much had really happened yet. They'd have to skip all that and jump straight to getting the tank in order to let you start playing around with it right away in the game and that would have definitely negatively impacted the story.Anyway, the story is probably at best only half the reason you would play a game like this. The real reason to play is the vehicle combat and obliterating enemies and exploring the world to find more parts to swap out or upgrade on your vehicles. It feels like the Armored Core game I played, but with only 2 weapons to choose from and different kinds of robots to pilot and fight with. The Jump Bot, Battle Tank, Motorcycle, and Car all maneuver very differently from each other to say nothing of how different their weapons are or can be. They all serve their own purpose, too-just the same as the various weapons you can put on them do. For example, missiles are fun and do heavy damage, but they generally can't shoot down enemy missiles coming at you-machine guns can, though. The Jump Bot can literally jump over some attacks from enemies and the Motorcycle is perfect for getting out of danger quickly. Each vehicle has it's own health bar so don't worry about swapping to a different one with less armor and getting obliterated on accident. I think they slowly repair themselves when not in use, too, but I don't know for sure. The weapons and other vehicles parts plus the vehicles themselves all can not only be leveled up, but you are encouraged do so. You need a level version of some weapon parts to upgrade to the blue tier of that weapon for example. I couldn't equip that incendiary grenade launcher on my Jump Bot until it was level 8 as another example. The quality of the base parts you put into a vehicle when building it will also seemingly determine it's starting level when crafted, too. I used better parts in my Hopper and it came out a higher level than the Dune Buggy I made right after it with just the basic parts I could craft. I really like customizing and upgrading my vehicles in this game and can see myself spending a decent amount of time on that over the course of playing thru this game. Speaking of playing thru it, I'm not even to Forest Land from the trailers, yet. I think I've seen about half of Sand Land so far and only have those 6 different vehicle types unlocked. I don't have any of the hover vehicles yet or the Battle Armor yet. It's a pretty big game just judging from what I've seen so far and also referencing to some degree how big the world map and locations themselves are. There's a location you learn about early on to get the Jump Bot frame needed to start making Jump Bots called the Lisab Battleship. I've been there twice now and still only seen about half of it as well. There was a spot the 2nd time I went back that needed the Battle Armor to move a block so I know there's going to be a reason to come back a 3rd time. Don't let the very bad demo of this game or the seemingly pretty empty wasteland at the start of the game throw you off. There's a lot to this game.I haven't even gotten to talking about the main character Beelzebub and his allies Rao and Thief that I've been leveling up and unlocking various passive or active skills for in their basic skill tree. It's nothing you haven't seen before in games with leveling systems and it's nice to get new abilities for Beelzebub to use in and out of combat, but I also don't think it's particularly needed. I don't find myself needing to use anyone's active abilities to help out in combat cause the main character or the vehicles he's using have always been enough so far. That may change as I get further into the game or it may be because I'm just playing on the normal difficulty and that's something you'd see more use in hard mode, but I don't say any of that to detract from the game. I don't think it hurts the game in any way by being there, I just don't wanna get anyone's hopes up if they thought the Beelzebub combat was going to be on par with or maybe even better than the vehicle combat. Nope. It's just ok. It's not bad, but not great either. He doesn't feel as fun to use as the vehicles in combat and he's only useful for reaching small spaces the vehicles can't fit into during exploration, so I find myself in the vehicles as often as possible. I like him as a character and he's not bad to use, he's just being outshined by how much better the vehicles are, I think. That could also again be my personal bias. I like robots and machines and vehicular combat.If you like robots, or the Sand Land anime or manga or the IP in general, you probably will like this game. You might get bored for the first hour or 2, though and that would suck if so, but if you get past that to Spino and start upgrading/customizing your tank, it opens up so much more for you to do and really starts to shine as a game.

_childDocuments_.review: A cute & cozy open world action RPG while also being a big throwback to the 90's in both aesthetics, gameplay & feeling! Sandland is a post-apocalyptic, Mad Max-ian experience imagined by the great Akira Toriyama and this game delivers exactly that, in a respectful while caring way. The cell-shades visuals & animations are beyond eye-pleasing, controls are solid, easy & enjoyable and the story pacing is interesting & fast without dragging things much! The game is a careful re-imagining & expansure of the same titled manga that was release at the start of 2000.From dialogues to camera angles, it pays amazing homage to the manga while adding upon it.In a vast land that's been hit continuously by natural disasters, resulting in water & general supplies shortage & monopolizing the remains of those by the human's monarch King, you play as Beelzebub, the fiend prince & son of Demon King Dabura (identical to Dabura from the DragonBall Z~ Majin Buu Saga!).At Bub's village you encounter a human sheriff named Rao, who's sick of the king's greed & is looking for aid from the demons to seek & find the legendary spring . Beelze & his trusty companion Thief decides to join Rao & thus the journey begins!The gameplay is that of a typical open world RPG with hefty vehicular exploration & combat, such as fighting to gain XP & items, leveling your party, upgrading skills & traits,collecting items & parts to craft/customize/upgrade your vehicles (which are plenty and all have different properties to help you embark on your quests)& all those accompanied with some stealth segments! The cast is above likeable & the voice acting (at least the JP which i experienced) is spot on, with interesting & non-draggy dialogues. There are a few niches & cliches here & there but they re just few & minor.While the majority of the game will be within some vehicle, you still traverse area's of interests, villages & secret areas on foot as well as bare fist fighting in between since our prince is a powerful demon after all. Add a few gigantic monsters & boss fights next to those & the fact that all vehicles could be eastern eggs to the ones existing the in Dragon Ball Universe, making it extra spicy for the fans of it.At the bottom line, Sandland scratches a few inches in the right directions & it's a fun ride,if you either a 80/90's kid, a Toriyama fan or simply looking for a short but enjoyable anime action RPG, this one's for you.
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: In a landscape filled with garbage licensed arena fighters that poorly tell the original story Sand Land manages to deliver a game that both faithfully honors the original manga and ties it all together with a competent modern open world game.Without the license this game would be a straight 7/10, but it really fits into a slightly underrepresented niche of happy go lucky Saturday morning cartoon style open world games that I think lets it punch way above its weight.The game does the story and characters, and the world really fits the style of game terrifically. The world has a fantastic aesthetic.  I'd actually go out on a limb and say this is the best most fully realized version of the Sand Land world across the manga, movie, and game.The gameplay is just competent enough to be fun and engaging with the standout positive being a pretty engaging vehicle customization system backed by a surprisingly well tuned in game economy.  The large spraeling dungeons and some more intricately designed open world areas are also surprise positives for me.On the flip side the melee combat is pretty bare bones and not very engaging, but luckily you very rarely need to fall back on it.The big glaring flaw is the incessant repeated dialog while exploring. This is honestly the most egregious repetition I've ever seen with extended back and forth conversations repeating ad nauseum. The conversations aren't even bad!  They're just repeated so frequently. For me personally I can stomach them by switching VO to Japanese which both sounds more dynamic and helps me tune it out.Overall I recommend this if you're an Akira Toriyama fan and can get it on sale for a decent price.
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: A cute open world game about beating up bad guys and driving quirky vehicles across a desert world.Basically Mad Max through the eyes of Akira Toriyama.The plot and the characters are simple, but not in a bad way and, aside from the too often repeating banter who gets old after a couple of minutes, they are defined, lovable (especially Beelzebub) and well designed.The cell shaded graphics are clean and while not "impressive" in any sense, they're pleasing to the eye. Akira Toriyama's design is simply perfect and in this game it shines. The game verges on the easy side of difficulty, but a couple of fights are interesting and not too shallow, just don't expect to be challenged at any moment.Exploration is fine, although Sand Land's map tends to get predictably repetitive after a while. Crafting is also present, although not particularly tedious, it is not particularly interesting either.Later in the game there will also be a small base to manage and rebuild, and it serves both as a hub and as an excuse to return to areas already visited by the player (in the original story the group of heroes is constantly on the move).Ultimately it is a worthy testament to the art of the late Akira Toriyama and a lovely parting gift from an artist I grew up with.
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Sand Land is pretty but doesn't know what it wants to be.The number of reviews on this game with less than two hours played talking about how fun this game is blows my mind when it took me almost three hours just to get through the long introduction of the game to the point where I could actually customize my first tank.The game tries to be a lot of things all at once and doesn't do any of them very well or in a way I found fun.It has walk-around standard fare RPG combat of light combos and a heavy attack.Then it has these really long and unnecessary MGS stealth portions that add absolutely nothing to the game except being tediously slow and breaking up the pacing.Then it has the meat-and-potatoes mech combat which does nothing that a thousand games before it haven't already done.Even on the hardest difficulty the game is boringly easy, with multiple seemingly unfailable segments that just serve to slow down pacing even further.Characters are interesting but the game pushes a ton of unneeded dialog that doesn't build on the characters or setting, just very standard RPG chatter. I wanted to immerse myself but quickly found myself skipping all dialog that was skippable because they would constantly point out the most obvious things and talk about just random environmental things that weren't important.The first real boss (Water plane... thing...) on hard difficulty, the game explains all these mechanics about hiding behind terrain, following behind it where it can't see you, staying out of line of sight, reloading in safety, etc... But I just shot it like four times and killed it while they were still explaining mechanics that weren't useful or needed for the fight.It is like the fight was originally way harder during development and they cut the boss's hp by 90%.The default controls for keyboard and mouse are abysmal. Another game designed for controllers with K&M as an afterthought.PC performance was mid, some mild stuttering but fine.The art is absolutely beautiful if you enjoy Akira Toriyama's work, but the best art in the world can't do anything for mediocre gameplay.EDIT: My refund was denied because I played this game for more than two hours.You cannot even see a single tank in this game before the two hour mark, much less get to the point where you can change anything about the very first tank.So if you want to do three hours of stealth BS and unloseable combat with two buttons on the off chance you will enjoy this game, I highly recommend waiting for a sale or watching some mid-to-late game gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is obviously geared more towards a younger audience (i.e. you don't really kill anybody, villains feel a little one-dimensional, etc) it doesn't take away from the charm or gameplay experience, unless corny anime dialogue makes your eyes roll outta your skull.The combat is very engaging, fluid, but somewhat repetitive. The various bounty style missions break this up for a bit, and some dungeon-specific traversal mechanics keep things fresh as the story progresses. Keep your eyes out for your crafting and gear drops; there are some really unique pieces of gear out there. For example, I got a piece of equipment that allowed my tank to lock in place and fire off a volley of 9 heavy cannon shots very quickly that made some of my bounty fights give me the giggleshits.Having mentioned the story, I'm almost 24 hours in and I've only made it through the first two acts because, while the story is interesting, if not straight-forward, the exploration is superb and your various options for navigating the aforementioned treacherous dungeons as well as cave systems, and other things that I don't want to spoil.The voice acting is really good, though some of the exchanges you hear as you travel get tedious and very repetitive ("RAO HOW WOULD YOU FIGHT BOTS?!", "PRINCE, IT SOMETIMES HELPS TO GO OFF THE BEATEN PATH.").TLDR: I am thoroughly enjoying this game, despite some repetition and a pretty straight-foward (dry) storyline because of some fantastic exploration and customization and rewarding combat. 8/10 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the manga from Akira Toriyama (which was recently made into a new anime), Sand Land is an action RPG that tells the story of Prince Beelzebub who lives in a world that is now turned into a wasteland after numerous wars and natural calamities. The King of these lands has gathered all the sources of water for himself, while Beelzebub and his demonic friends try to survive by stealing the water shipments for their village. Things change when an old sheriff called Rao reveals that he is looking for a Legendary Spring that can offer unlimited water to the whole land. Beelzebub and his friend Thief join him in the search and along the journey they also meet Ann, a mechanic who helps them steal a tank and fight against the Royal Army. While this partially sounds like the story of Mad Max Fury Road, the atmosphere here is much more relaxed. I was never able to read the manga (or watch the anime), so I can’t really say if the story is 100% faithful to the original material, but I definitely enjoyed the story, with its mix of dramatic and comedy moments. Prince Beelzebub is a very likeable protagonist (it reminded me of child Goku fighting against the Red Ribbon) and his companions aren’t bad either (some are better than others, of course). The game keeps the iconic character design from Toriyama, which makes each character very distinctive. Unlike the manga, the story includes a new arc that has never been showed before, which should be enough to attract players who have read the manga but wants to see more.Developer ILCA already showed their talent through Dragon Quest XI and One Piece Odyssey, but Sand Land is a much different game due to the depth and attention to vehicle combat. Vehicles are used not only to traverse the big open world and explore multiple locations, but also to fight enemies and solve environmental puzzles. This is a big part of the gameplay and probably the most engaging, especially during boss fights. Combat is also supported by many crafting and customization options, with every vehicle showing a great level of detail, variety and a different feeling when controlled. The fun thing is that you can summon vehicles instantly (like in Dragon Ball) and you will likely switch a lot during battles. The vehicle design is one of the aspects that I really loved, but unfortunately the experience outside of them isn’t equally satisfying. Beelzebub and his team can use meele combat and despite the presence of a classic skill tree (also for your companions), the combat itself becomes quite shallow and repetitive over time. During certain moments, the game will force you to use melee combat by disabling the ability to summon vehicles. There will also be some forced stealth sections that are poorly designed, but luckily most of the stealth is optional (can be used to infiltrate bases).An important aspect for the gameplay progression is the village of Spino, which is basically the player’s main hub that needs to be expanded in order to welcome new residents, unlock new shops, vehicles and upgrades. This is all optional, but it’s a great opportunity to dedicate some time in side quests, bounties and other activities, exploring new locations and receiving useful rewards. Not all activities are worth your time unfortunately and you can easily spot fetch quests and other repetitive tasks, but it’s hard to get bored unless you are a true completionist. Some side quests are actually really well-crafted and will make you more invested in the world of Sand Land and its characters.Despite having three difficulties to choose from, the game is very easy, even at its max difficulty. This has been a recurrent problem with these types of action RPGs, which are primarily aimed at kids and young teenagers, leaving all the grown-up and bearded adults very unsatisfied. This is also visible during simple exploration, unfortunately. There is a lot of useless dialogue coming from your companions; for example, after six hours they can remind you of things you have already read during the tutorial, or they can give you tips so you don’t get lost. It gets quite annoying and you will probably end up hoping for a mute button just to enjoy the silence of the desert.Graphically speaking, Sand Land looks quite impressive compared to other games that use the cell-shading aesthetic. It really feels like being inside Akira Toriyama’s colorful world filled with distinctive characters, beautiful lighting and special effects. It’s hard to turn 2D into 3D but once again ILCA managed to create a fantastic visual adaptation. The PC version also seems incredibly well polished and I didn’t notice any bugs or glitches. After spending quite some time in the beautiful world of Akira Toriyama, I realized what was keeping me playing despite the complete lack of difficulty and some repetitive, but optional, side quests. The first reason is the quality of the story, which for me was something new (as I haven’t read the manga) and very intriguing, also thanks to the wonderful protagonist and the general world building. The second reason is vehicle combat, which is always fun and engaging, with a great level of detail and variety that constantly encourages you to look out for more parts, upgrades and vehicles. I think that if you enjoyed the One Piece Odyssey quality of adaptation, you will likely enjoy this one too (even if you don’t know the story, like me), but you must also appreciate vehicle combat more than melee combat because that’s the main part of the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Sand Land is definitely a labour of love by Akira Toriyama, the ILCA Inc. Dev team and anyone else who might have worked on Sand Land as an IP with Toriyama.The combat is pretty straight forward beat-em-up combat, it might change a bit later but at the time of review I’m only 10 hours in. The vehicle combat is also fairly simple , especially since you get to customize your vehicles equipment which can change up how they perform in combat. Again, I’m only about 10 hours into the game and I’m sure with more vehicles, upgrades and types of enemies you fight it will add more depth to the vehicle combat. I also do like that you can swap vehicles on the fly in combat, meaning you can really mix and match to your heart’s desire. The music is pretty good when it plays but most of the time it’s more of a atmospheric dull tone.Very minimal performance issues as well. I do have two complaints:All in all, if you love the Toriyama style, I think you’ll like this game. The stuttering mentioned above got really worse during a few of the later segments to where it was causing me to struggle in a combat section. Again though, it didn’t seem to happen for a good chunk of the game so that’s not terrible.The vehicle combat is still fairly simple but once you get more vehicles, being able to smoothly swap between 5 in combat is very nice.There’s extra vehicles you can unlock that aren’t part of the story but at a certain point it feels like you need to grind a bit too much for materials to be able to craft and upgrade these non-story vehicles. To go with the material grind and upgrading vehicles, I constantly felt material starved to the point where I was having to go out and farm enemies for materials to upgrade stuff, at the end of the day I really only kept 3 vehicles updated and the rest more or less sat due to my personal impatience with farming materials.Some of the vehicles you get, it feels like you almost get them too late in the game when they’re used to progress extra areas of some temples/dungeons from much much earlier in the game. Quite a bit of back tracking to do those.What I thought was the midpoint of the game was actually the final quarter or final third of the game and that section went by fairly fast, even with me doing the majority of the side content available. All in all though, still a fairly fun game and I think worth a buy if you like exploration beat’em up vehicle combat gameplay with a decent story and a great art style.

_childDocuments_.review: been having a lot of fun with it so far!the visuals for this game look like they jumped right out of the manga, and toriyama's vehicle designs are fantastic.the combat, in and out of vehicle, is a little bare. there is generally no reason to ever do combat outside of your vehicle unless the game forces you to, so a lot of the upgrading you do for beelzebub feels a bit wasted.  vehicle combat is also very basic, and most things that aren't a boss will die in one or two hits. ammo management is not a worry at all if you swap between your weapons. i've rarely found myself using the ally abilities, aside from the one that summons rao's tank. sand and forest land are largely generic, there's not many landmarks outside of the battleships to make the maps stand out, which is pretty detrimental when exploring is largely encouraged. you won't find much outside of small grottos, spires which you need to jump up, and ruins that are all largely the same. it's very largely repetitive, but it lends itself to being a very laid back game to run around in.as you go through the game, you'll upgrade your little town of spino. this is what's been driving me to play more so far. seeing what was a junk heap grow into a desert paradise is really satisfying and is pretty much necessary for making your vehicles stronger. the side quests which you do to bring in new residents are all very basic- grab this, kill that, maybe do a race- they're very simple.vehicle customization isn't as deep as i expected it to be.  the weapons you choose will not largely change _childDocuments_.review: ---- Part 1 - The only part worth reading-----I'm writing this review at 70 hours played with all side quests and main quest completed.Sand Land is a solid 6/10 game for most people, for me personally I'd bump that up to a 7/10.The studio delivered a competent game and it's their best title yet, a 6/10 score is mostly due to my gripes with the pacing of the game as it is very dialogue heavy and the lack of challenge mostly because it's aimed at a much younger audience than me, and I'd say the price point of the game did factor into my score (£50 at time of review)The main story line follows the anime very tightly and is an easy to understand story told in a simple way that conveys it's events easily to the intended age group which I'm guessing is kid's age 8-12.---- Part 2 - Me Rambling----The Graphics, specifically the character design and rendering is great, Akira Toriyama's style is in every part of the game and I don't believe I've played a game that looked so authentic to the manga and the new 3d sand land anime.A lot of care went into including vehicle designs from Toriyama's other works like Dragon Ball and Dragon Ball Z, and this game was the perfect place to use those.I saw only a handful of "hitches" on my RTX 3070 in DX12 mode.The Voice acting was excellent, all of the main cast are voiced by the same actors as the anime and they all did a great job.Beelzebub, Lucifer and Ann were the real standout actors for me but they were all great.All of the side quests in the game are fully voiced.The sound design was better than average.The game-play is fairly simplistic, there isn't really an awful lot in terms for challenge even in hard mode, though I have found that at max level (level 30).Bosses lack any real depth to them, they each have easy to dodge moves that even when seen for the first time are telegraphed so blatantly you won't get hit by them.None of the fights featured any kind of standard video game mechanic you'd expect such as weak spots or anything which I found lacking. Most fights you can just circle strafe the boss and use your big moves when they're available, on the plus side the game pausing to allow the use of items and being so easy does make it very accessible for a wide audience.That being said the vehicles all feel fun to use and handle as you'd expect them to, bulky ones are clunky and the tanks especially handle perfectly.I almost forgot to mention that the melee combat when playing as Beelzebub is the biggest let down, it's very slow and clunky, it feels under developed but luckily it's barely used save for a few specific sections.The stealth sections are slow but they aren't frustrating or broken, there's also some nods to other stealth games, but they do feel very shallow, luckily there are only 2-3 small stealth sections in the main story.in the post game it does become challenging enough to feel a little more engaging than the main game, this is because the enemy level scales with your level, meaning at level 25 you will fight level 25 enemies no matter where you are on the world map, for the main story though you aren't going to feel any challenge if you've played any action adventure games.Here are some of the bad things, but I'd say none of them are deal breakers, just little issues that even a small studio like this one could easily rectify, the game itself is stable and solid with no erorrs/problems, it's most just quality of life things that could be improved upon with more development time that at for a full price £50 game should be there.There isn't really any puzzle solving or depth to the side quests, they're all very straight forward and the quest log does a good enough job at guiding you to the objectives, one quest early on called "A Jump-Bot?! Gimmie!" caused me to spend an hour searching for vehicle parts all over the map.The IGN guide says as much as they wrote that the menus are "a tad confusing" for this quest.The quality of life in terms of the menus and various vendors could use some work,You can't sort parts in the Sell menu's, this is annoying as the Parts menu quickly fills up with 100-500 items, you also have to sell parts individually which is time consuming.The only time you can compare weapons/vehicle parts is in the "Vehicle customisation menu", which means that you can't even compare parts while browsing the garages craftable part list or in shops when buying new parts.The part names are often called very similar things like "9mm Machine Gun","9mm Burst Machine Gun" and "9mm Machine Gun+", which is confusing especially with no way to directly compare the new part you want to make with the existing part on the vehicle in this menu.  Spino's Workshop where you craft materials is always missing materials during the main game, even if you do all of the related side quests, this isn't conveyed well to the player and could confuse people, essentially all of the Junker markets and the Trikke camp have the ability to craft more materials than the Spino workshop which is very strange considering it's so difficult to remember where the Junkers are in the Market, they just kind of stand around and look like everyone else.I almost forgot to mention this, because it's an open world game the characters will often interact with one another while driving around, this gets tiring quickly as they often repeat the same phrases over and over, what's worse is that if they're interrupted by combat or something, they'll start from the beginning of the conversation.I found myself stopping the car so that they could finish their dialogue before driving further just in case they were interrupted and had to repeat it all again, I hope this gets patched because 40 hours in having Rao,Thief and Ann have a back and forth about checking the map, or using a jump bot to reach high places is frustrating. The frequency of these conversations needs to be dialled waaay down, and they should be on a LONG cooldown once they've been said once.I had a situation where within 30 minutesthey'd said the map conversation 4 times and the "check your inventory for new parts" conversation 3 times, I was going insane.This isn't really part of the review but it's worth mentioning that there's an achievement named " Concerned Fellow Citizen " for delivering 45 lost property , these items do not appear on the map or unlockable treasure maps, are fairly out of the way in most cases and are part of untracked cryptic mini "quests" with no actual in game reward for completing them, It's very out of place in a game that holds the players hand through everything else, i don't really know what to make of that one, it's very strange, as with all other quest these lost property cut scenes are fully voice acted! a lot of effort for something few people will see (based on steam achievement percentage and current sales figures, around 100 people have completed this achievement)
