_childDocuments_.review: Hearing how this is one of the last works of Akira Toriyama I had to check this out. It's a slow burn but absolutely worth it. Fantastic story, wonderfully realized and written characters, a plot that just keeps expanding further and further across Sandland and beyond. Beautiful art style capturing the original manga's design down to an exact science. How they manage to do this so gracefully with full 3D render models still baffles me. Real artists at work. That ending too. That wholesome beautiful kind of ending that gives you pure joy and sadness all wrapped up into a warm fuzzy blanket. You're happy, comfortable, but also eager and hoping for more. There's some issues though, tiny ones but they sting at you. Crafting items and materials, sucks. It just sucks. You'll collect one material to upgrade a part. Good example a raptor scale. Simple right? No...it's not. See a raptor scale can only be used for so much, eventually you'll need to combine that with various other materials for a "Polished" Raptor scale to upgrade equipment. Leading to farming twice as many materials to combine into "Hybrid" materials just to add a nice cannon to your tank. Couple that with the stealth, my god the stealth. The Stealth of this game is a tacked on disaster. I've never seen anything like it. You tiptoe around guards, some of them having various detection ranges from within ten feet of spotting you to ten miles in a sandstorm. You alert one, watch the same cutscene of the base at full alert. Revert back, all and all a time waster not a total mess. What ruins it is "Stealth Takedown" It's adorable at first, Beez tapping a guard behind the shoulder, then hopping up to pull off a scary face in front of them to knock them out from sheer shock. Perfect,  ador...I mean downright fiendish!Issue is if you're in the middle of a watching that animation play out (which takes a good three seconds mind you) and another guard sees it...base on high alert, guards reset in position, start again. I've had this happen so many times. Still recall audibly catching myself shouting at my screen at one particular warehouse with guards in it. Those of you that have played this game I'm sure you know the one. The side mission with the jumper parts. That stupid segment. Oh and it's just that one stealth takedown animation, cute at first, then annoying, then "Please no more stealth..." Combat, fun, engaging, some enemies can be fairly spongy but the late game weapon upgrades chew through most of them. Bosses...okay. The first boss for some reason the game has the moral obligation to tell you how to beat it, literally taking control AWAY from you to show you. Despite it being painfully obvious to any age group. Dialogue, I've heard the same canned dialogue from these characters so many times. I can quote most of it verbatim. "If only we had a vehicle that could jump!" WE DO, I'M USING IT. AS...YOU...SPEAK... These are good voice actors, but the game never gives you the opportunity just to breathe and take things in. It's always halted by the SAME DIALOGUE. Don't make me hate Rao! But I can't take his constant "BE AWARE OF YOUR SURROUNDINGS" or "GET THE HIGH GROUND ON YOUR ENEMIES" speeches. "HUMANS ARE APPROXIMATELY 60% WATER." How does he even know that in this setting?Last issue, animations. The animations are beautiful but there's no segment where you can cancel an animation. Picture being in a jump bot, going full sprint, leaping across platforms. Sometimes the game will continue running the jump bot past the platform into the even expanding sand abyss below despite you jamming the jump button at mach speed. Lots of tiny things like that. One of the major issues with the stealth segment too.Despite all that, still HIGH recommendation from me. Story alone is incredible. Might top Dragon Ball Z for me. I know still shocks me saying that, let alone thinking that, I love Dragon Ball Z. Now I find myself loving SandLand too. RIP Akira Toriyama, you fiendishly wonderful person. The world got a bit dimmer after your passing. A big thank you too the studio behind this, I think you've done him proud.
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: I will tell you, the reader, right now that I was already biased to this game because of Akira's passing and I wanted to play it if only to celebrate his life work and all of the great memories that he has given us all. All that said, I do recommend this game even without my bias, it is a fun action/adventure game that has a hopeful and lighthearted tone to it. The combat is simple enough to grasp, the story is certainly a political commentary on how dumb us humans are towards each other and the characters are all very easy to like right off the bat. It is not a perfect game, but it is a game that deserves consideration for any fans of single player action adventure games, and most certainly fans of Akira Toriyama's work.RIP Akira and thank you for all the characters you introduced us to in your lifetime.

_childDocuments_.review: Was expecting an OK vehicle based game with some light story, was hoping for more of the story and world from way back in 2001. What I got? The combat is fun (albeit a little easy, but difficulty slider can fix that). the vehicle handling is good, and it's not just about the vehicles, it's actually still an RPG with fighting, stealth, and side quests (none of which involve vehicles) and the vehicles are GREAT and the customisation factor is so fun. I am SO happy with this game. 5/5 stars, would definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: mixed bag but a very comfy one.i should start by saying i'm a fan of the original old manga, not the anime, the physical old manga which was localized to my country by conrad back in the day, i was pleasantly surprised how i was enjoying this game, there are some new characters, but its not like i was expecting a 1-1 of the game, the story followed enough, stretched on some parts to make it long enough, but the tank part was absolutelly solid, when it comes to the tank combat, its simple yet effective, its very fun, few on the market can pull that well, fighting with the tank is the best part of this game, sure the dungeons were ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and the missions were padding, but i was getting near the end, fought not one but many insect men (this is a issue, will come back to it soon) and the story was done, the music was great through and through, it closed bealtifully, but then it happeneda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ act 2...i was open minded about it, sure, lets hear what these writes have to add to this story, and i got disappointed, and disappointed, for starters, they now wanted to add to the lore that sandland is not the state which humanity left the world due to its hubris, no, there was also an old conflict with, i kid you not, Forest Land.to this act 2 there is a brand new family conflict which we find forest land has an issue with its king and princess, so now we gotta join the rebellion against.... An Evil Angel..and this is exactly what i fear in these adaptations, they know this is all some fan fic BS, but they try to compensate, How ? the original story had one insect man which was said to be as strong as the demon prince and is a threat to the whole world ? well now you find 10, 50, as many as the spawn rate can give you to fight.the original story state that the aquanium explosion was so devastating that it scarred the whole planet and proceeded to hide one of the biggest plot twist in the original ? well in forest land they cranked those explosions up, now we had around 4 new ones.there is a whole bunch of new issues that were never present in the original, somehow the princess i kid you not is half demon (does anyone has a Fan Fic trope bingo around ? i should start checking squares by this point).its not like the new map is any fun at all, sand land has a personality to it, the desert feels alive, forest land feels like a bunch of stretched mountains glued together and sprowed some grass and trees to make it foresty, it is not enjoyable to drive around it at all, everything the original story does, this somewhat pseudo sequel adaptation tries to compensate for lack of competence by sheer number increase and it becomes so jarring.a story about some old people making up for the past and trying to build a future agains't hypercapitalism becomes a GRANDIOSE BATTLE WITH FAMILY CONFLICTS that was always that deep guys trust me, sand land world was ALWAYS this big and dense with... whatever they wanna add, oh also demon racism and people learning to treat them nicely, despite this happening in the original story back in act 1, the entire premise of act 2 is a playable contradiction, there are even events that contradict themselves, a group of bandits at one point back in sand land ask the protagonist that when he finds water, if he will allow them to swim on it, since they never were able to swim in abundant amounts of water, this happens in the original manga too, you know what forest land does ? it says that these same group of bandits were natives to forest land this entire time, forest land mind you, has water EVERYWHERE.i feel like nuance is a lost skill.but, its not all the worst thing ever, the ending almost makes me give a extra point due to how charming everything is, the characters grew on me, actually they were the only reason i even finished this or got past act 2, i love rao and wish he was my grandpa.i also can see this being a great game for kids to enjoy, but beware that this commits the worst sin of a dungeon rpg, repeated dungeons, it repeats the same dungeon 5 times the whole game with no difference aside from this one is blue and this one is yellow.with all that said, if anyone knows a cool open world tank game, HMU

_childDocuments_.review: interesting scenario and characters are a given looking back at the source materiali got my first "taste" of Belz back when (in my country, germany) mangas weren't realy a thing. didn't understand much of it (was japenese), but loved the art-style.it is an open world action-rpg at it's core.you kill stuff, get exp, level up, spend skill points, find chests/loot, etc. . but that is were the "normal" stuff ends. there is the without-vehicle layer which is a very basic melee-combat system, that gets better later on when you unlock more stuff. but it is never realy great. its servicable at best. the range of standart attacks is very short, there ain't no block or counter, there is no weapon(s). thankfully the meat of the game is vehicle driven. and it is fantastic. tanks, mechs, bikes, everything comes upgradable, everything comes with tons of options, beeing it the engine or actual weapons (or option(s) like additional mirv-launchers, point defense, armor, etc.), everything comes with great controls and most vehicles also serve as a kinda metroid-vania-aspect: the tank gun destroys rock-blockades, the mech can jump, the bike (trying to avoid spoilers) can get across quicksand, etc. . you can slot each vehicle to a ring-menu and switch around nearly all the time, beeing it mid dungeon or mid combat. where the on-foot-melee is kinda iffy, everything vehicle is just fun. the open world got what you would expect: random quests appearing on the map, caves to loot, ruins to explore, towns and camp-spots, wandering merchants and lots of critters or "bandits" to kill'n loot. it kinda starts out little and grows even 10 hours in by adding new elements.many a main- or sidequest is also very well done. often offering side-scroll like jump'n run areas, enviromental puzzles, lots of narration and unique locations.what ain't not so great are the stealth-missions. optional and sometimes quest-related you can/will stealth your way through "military bases". it is very basic stealth mechanics, without checkpoints and insta gibs/failure states. thankfully these parts are very rare. but when they appear they are at best a welcome diversion, but most of the time kinda annyoin.during your adventure you will also kinda rebuild a town, like you would your base in Suikoden or Eiyuden Chronicles. find side-quest, and get new citizens, which will make the town visualy grow and often offer new shops, crafters or other knick'knacks. what makes the game realy standout is the audio-visual design. it is very pretty to look at. probably the best "comic" adaptation i've yet seen. almost looks like the manga came to live in HD and very modern grafics. even in the depths of the desert there is detail around every corner or little locations you are gonna remember. even the passive skill tree has been done with great care. your companions got their own skill trees: once you unlock the looter function for Thief, working like a passive loot bonus, you will see Thief actualy run around and look for stuff...which is just one example. beeing it the skybox (day'n night) or the npc everything looks superb and just like it belongs. the animation quality is also top notch. during drifts small doodads on your bike kinda lean into the intertia, etc. . even more standout is the amazing OST. it is bold. often beeing kinda electonic mixed with more classical compositions. there is some Borderlands vibes here, but also very athmospheric almost etheral tracks during night time, or kinda Final Fantasy like tracks, the very melancholic ones, during dungeon exploration or standout moments. it is  always an amazing OST, but often enough it just blows you away with.VO is also very competent and there is a) a lot of VO and b) very little misseson a 3070, i5, SSD and 32 GB i played in 1080p and 1440p with everything possible maxed, having a constant 60 fps (locked manualy) and little to no loading times. 0 technical issues: no crashes, no slowdowns, no texture flickering.on the negative side of things is definitly the stealth segments and the melee combat. the later gets better the longer you play, the former thankfully doesn't happen very often.but the real standout negative and which many other people mentioned (and they weren't lying) is the repeating banter and action-voice lines. it is downright insane. we are talking full on conversations (banter) getting repeated over and over and over and over and over and over again. yes, the more you progress the main plot the more possible banter gets unlocked, but it is still gonna repeat to an insane degree. the moment a banter-conversation is over another one starts. someone in the core design team must realy hate silence or think everyone playing solo-games is lonely. nevermind Belz repeating (especialy early on) the same lines, like when you pick something up, but the conversations between Belz, Shiva and whoever is around aswell will drive you nuts. you can lower/turn off the voice volume which i would strongly recommend if you are just driving around to level or collect stuff. either the interval between the banter needs to be DRASTICALY increased or each banter only triggers onceduring 24h ingame times or whatever. but the way it works now does feel kinda broken.the constant auto-repeat-banter aside it is a fantastic game with some rough edges (stealth and melee), but over all a game i'd recommend to any and everyone liking action-rpgs, vehicular combat or open world adventrues (or the source material: definitly the best adaptation around).

_childDocuments_.review: Game is mid. The art style is great. Love the shading lines on everything. Cut scenes and story are pretty good(Really enjoyed the source material). The game is hindered by bad combat as Beelzebub (needs a lock on when on foot). Paired with simplistic vehicle combat which is never more then a simple pattern that you generally circle strafe around and shoot with your tank. There seems to be too many vehicles. You just use whichever is the fastest, the tank for the majority of fights and then whichever vehicle solves your immediate puzzle. Seems like they could have had a few vehicles do double duty here by giving multiple abilities to a single vehicle and then improving the vehicle combat with fewer vehicles. Stealth sections are so tedious, the camera jumps around and will hide soldiers on you in spots. It is fairly forgiving and will reload recently. Though there were a few spots so far where you had to complete a long chain of jumps to get to a specific chest and the game likes to not register your jump when you are very close to an edge moving forward with the camera behind you it seems. The controls feels loose too, nothing feels quite right. Also it will go into an overhead camera on roof sections sometimes but will be too close to see all the enemies on the roof so it actually makes your view worse. The exploration is boring there is nothing to look at and you spend all your time going between the few fast travel points (radio towers and points of interest should just be fast travel points) to go to a rock to climb with your jumper to open three chests with basic items. Every now and then you will get an item for vehicles you probably won't use. Also while exploring there are invisible walls all over the rocks to prevent you from climbing over them with a bot and most the time they feel pretty bad because you are trying to go between areas you could get to anyways. The game is alright but I can't recommend it to anyone but die hard Toriyama fans. If you know who Ackman is pick this up on sale but for everyone else just go read Sand Land or watch the the show that just came out.

_childDocuments_.review: Items are generic shallow looter shooter junk system. You upgrade vehicles, weapon, character, change parts and see the number go up, but literally nothing else changes. The only way to change anything is switching vehicles to use a different weapon. weapons on any given vehicle behave mostly the same (giving you little reason to swap)  RPG stats don't change ANYTHING about that. There's also dynamic level scaling which keeps you killing at roughly the same speed.Character progression unlocks stuff that you will never use, because using your character instead of vehicle feels awful in this game.I'd go lower than 6/10 on the RPG side, BUT they added a fair vehicle variety. They handle differently enough and despite overall small variety, it's more than some games do.It's a generic formulaic open world. The world offers nothing unique by itself and this game lacks the reward structure to support so much bloat of bland objectives. There's like 300 caves, 200 rock formations, 30 ruins. They are identical to each other, get marked on map before you see them and offer generic common materials as rewards. This world would be far more interesting with only 10% of those copy-pasted locations, if I had to find those locations myself and each one had something worth finding (unique equipment, rare material, a paint job).Vehicles offers unique ways to travel and transverse terrain, but developers decided to block all the creative ways to reach new locations. Even when looking for ways to enter a generic area (not story related), just like the one you're in, you might bump into an invisible wall. They effectively force you to take the 1 intended path. To clarify the locations areIt's not all bad as there are few locations you will want to reach for one reason or another, and it can take a bit of exploration to find a path. THIS is what the entire open world could have been. There doesn't have to be 400 locations. 30 would be enough if they were interesting.I'd rate the world lower for being so bland, BUT devs were self aware enough not to bloat these chores to Ubisoft levels and unlike ubisoft titles there's a little thought (really not much) put into terrain.Combat using the main character outright sucks. Combat overall have the responsiveness of an older MMO. It doesn't work in action combat very well. Devs clearly knew that because there's lots of non optional stealth and vehicle combat, but only like 2 fights you have to fight using Beelzebub.Luckily, you have the option to spend almost all of your time in vehicles. Vehicles control nicely and many of them behave differently too. The shooting despite sometimes feeling clunky fit the theme of the world.I won't rate it, but I will say that due to smaller world bloat, and somewhat limited fetchquets the story flow feels a lot better than in most games. You might side track, but it's never a 40 hour side tracking journey before you go back to saving your best friend who has a gun pointed at them.It's a hard sell due to crappy open world and many of the mechanics being so shallow, but at least this one has unique vehicular combat to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: I have made it to the end of part 1 of the story, where your starting mission has been completed. I don't think that I will continue with the rest of the game, and instead leave with a “relatively okay” taste in my mouth. This story and art can only cover the lack of depth to the vehicle combat so much. Progression is so story-focused that it incentivizes rushing to the next story objective instead of exploring the world, which seems antithetical to the open world premise of the game. The story and the art direction are the highlights of this game. If you are a fan of Toriyama's style (in both art and storytelling), you will probably love this game. There is a mixture of anime artwork in the characters and vehicles that meshes pretty well with the more realistic environment lighting and terrain. The game makes use of both Unreal lighting and crosshatching on the character models to bring out shadows in a way that mostly works. I like the English dub of the game, and the story moments that needed to hit ended up hitting for me. The music is also stellar. I found myself sitting in the towns or in rest areas just to listen to the music. The same cannot be said for the combat, traversal, and progression of this game, which seems to lack that same care. I don't know if this is an issue with anime games published by Bandai in general, but the same issues that I had with DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT's moment to moment gameplay are present here. There are two combat systems: vehicle and on foot combat. The on foot system becomes mostly irrelevant once you acquire your first weaponized vehicle (aside from its forced use in a bandit base). It borrows from hack and slashes, with a light and heavy attack and a dodge roll to evade. Combo finishers are determined by whenever you use your heavy, with the best being either on LLLH or LLLLH IMO. Small enemies will almost always be defeated with a single light combo, and larger enemies will take maybe 3. Larger enemies have super armor on certain attacks, forcing you to dodge. There is also a super meter, which allows you to perform certain super attacks once it is full (super attacks are locked behind story progression). It is basic, but definitely more engaging than the vehicle combat.Vehicles come in different flavors oriented primarily towards either combat or traversal, but you can fight with all of them except the intro one. They all have a primary and secondary weapon: the primary is vehicle specific; the secondary is some form of machine gun in all cases. One hit from any weapon will annihilate small enemies, with larger enemies typically going down in 3 hits from a primary weapon. Your significantly increased rate of attack and your increased health pool in a vehicle makes it so that clearing out mobs is tedious on foot in comparison. Moreover, there are certain enemies (minibosses and other vehicles) that require you to use the vehicle in order to stand a chance. Having a preferred fighting system wouldn't be that much of an issue if there was some depth to the vehicle combat, but there isn't really. Anything that doesn't go down in a few shots (i.e. only the minibosses) can be circled around and pelted with 50 shots from your primary until it goes down. Most fights take place in areas with little to no cover and a vast area to move around in, meaning that constantly strafing is really the only strategy. Combat itself isn't rewarding in the progression sense either. Just about every single defeated enemy awards 1-3 experience points, with minibosses awarding somewhere like 15-25. Completing a story mission in contrast will award hundreds of XP. Given that level requirements are in the 500-700 range, you will probably only get your level up after a story beat. Sidequests and bounty missions also don't award XP, focusing on either items or money instead. This really hinders the incentive to explore outside of needing materials for a specific quest or upgrade. Moreover, enemies “scale” to your level, and by that, I mean that their displayed level goes up. Their XP and item drops are still the same, and they will still be defeated in the same number of hits. This combination makes it feel like the only time you are making actual progress is when you complete a story quest; everything else feels like shallow filler that exists to pad the runtime.Later, you unlock the ability to change out your weapons, add specific boosts to certain systems (e.g. speed, decreased reload time) or have vehicle-specific overdrives (similar to active combat skills) that provide a limited time boost. Strafe and shoot is still the best strategy so most of these weapons feel either irrelevant or redundant. Being able to temporarily disable an enemy vehicle sounds useful, but I can't stress enough that the enemies that don't go down in 1-3 hits are easily defeated by the strafe and shoot strategy. Being able to burst fire, shoot a stronger shot less often, or have an additional status effect on your shot doesn't do anything to change up this strategy. Upgrading outside of required story progression (e.g. needing a new bot to cross over into an area, or needing a specific weapon to break down an obstruction) is wholly unnecessary, and only cuts down on the time you will spend strafing and shooting on the mini bosses. To put it bluntly, the progression in this game is boring. The vehicle combat (after the allure of shooting a giant gun wears off) is boring. It is wild to me that Thief's whole skill tree exists to cut down on the tedium of non-story combat and resource gathering. Here is a skill that will mine every drop in your local area. Here is a skill that increases the number of drops from enemies so you have to do less tedious grinding to get your preferred weapon. Oh, you have reached a spot in your progression where you have 0 of multiple items? Guess you better get on with the story so that you can get the quest that will allow you to craft that item. You have now leveled up! Here is a skill point for Beelzebub for his on-foot combat that is almost completely useless, and here is one for either of your allies!This review is long enough, so I will try to keep this brief

_childDocuments_.review: It's been quite a while since I'd first heard wind about this game, several months, or maybe a year or two, it's difficult to remember. I kept my eye on it for some time, my interest growing consistently. Not much word seemed to get out about it, up until we were nearing a few months before it's release, and I started seeing some hype for it, speculation and interest, people sharing the manga, and other Akira Toriyama content. I decided early on from them, I was getting this game. I wasn't hyped for it, or overly expectant of it, I was simply intrigued, because something about this game not only pulled on old memories, but it gave me an impression that was very much removed from what I've been getting about games from recent years.Frankly, what Sand Land is, the "soul" that built it, and the impression that it gives, is difficult to describe. What the game is though, is certainly not something that exists trying to out class or out perform every other game on the market. The marketing felt... restrained, and purposeful. Like, yes they are trying to make money, everyone who releases a product needs to profit. No, the impression that I got from this games marketing is the same impression I get from playing it; Old memories of game ads and demos from developers who really, truly invested their souls into what they've made. Sand Land is only what it was intended to be, no more and no less.I saw a lot of reviews for this game drop in articles, many with several complaints, much of which came down to "boredom" and complaints that the game wasn't outclassing other available games. That's true, because Sand Land doesn't have to. It's a well crafted experience; it's a lovingly told story crafted out of the world that Akira Toriyama built, and it's a distilled and refined game designed with sincere intent and well realized goals. There are complaints people are sharing, mostly boiling down to personal preference, about things like the dialogue or the combat, but many great games have annoying factors, and not every game is for everyone. My advice is... forget modern gaming. Forget the expectations. Forget what you think you know about what makes a great game. Sand Land doesn't need any of that, because it's not trying to compete with that.Sand Land is well worth playing, and well worth owning. It exists purely in that special memory of when games developers truly loved and cared for what they were creating, or at least those games that felt that way. In that era where every ounce of your gaming experience bleeds passion and happiness, where every moment has a deeper impact internally to your mind and heart. Sand Land isn't nostalgia for nostalgia's sake, and it's not out to win all the awards and to be filled with bombastic content. Sand Land was purely and simply made to bring happiness, pull you into a damned good story, and draw you into it's world.If it's not for you, then it's not for you. If you need that adrenaline drip feed of modern gaming's high stress uber-competitive need for profit and success, that's perfectly fine. Me, I don't need Sand Land to be anything more than what it was made to be, because it's damned good at being just what it is, and that's plenty enough for me. Akira... may you forever rest well, may your creations and your soul live on forever in the hearts and minds of those who loved it all. So long, our friend.

_childDocuments_.review: I ultimately feel very neutral about this game. The world is absolutely enormous and stunning to look at. It feels like it should be full of all sorts of awesome stuff to discover, and that ultimately kept me playing for way longer than I expected, but the reality is there's barely anything actually in this world and you will move through it very, very slowly.The combat mostly takes place from vehicles that you can customize and upgrade, which sounds great, and would be great if the AI wasn't incredibly basic and everything didn't die in the first half second of every encounter. There are a few higher powered enemies to be encountered, but they somehow end up still being boring and slightly more tedious due to a lack of depth. There is some hand to hand combat as well, but everything still dies in just a few hits leaving you feeling very unfulfilled.Hands down though, the absolute worst part of this game is the character chatter. Every 15 seconds the characters feel compelled to talk among themselves, but they only know how to have like 6 conversations so you hear the same exact thing over, and over, sometimes back to back. 30 hours into the game and they're still saying things that make it seem like we just started our adventure. If I hadn't paid so much for the game this would have ruined it in the first 30 minutes.This world and these characters could be something really great, and I kept hoping this game would become what my brain was dreaming it could be, but it just doesn't ever get there.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible, massive expansion to the original story of the Sand Land manga. Compared to its source material, many new characters were introduced, many assumed or untold events were fleshed out, and the world became massive.Sand Land's world will suck you in and not stop succin, enticing you with an adventurous soundtrack and beautiful, ambient nighttime synths.The fact is that Sand Land has many little problems: unclear invisible walls, weak non-vehicular combat, and obvious yellow signposting to name a few. Don't let that dissuade you from giving a try. There are some fantastic experiences to be had in this desert.This game's greatest strength is in its presentation. It's clear that the director's approach to Sand Land was through the eyes of the fiend you play, Beelzebub. Intriguing locations and mysterious encounters emulate that sense of wonder that you got as a kid. The deliberate use of camera perspective, sound, and character expression make exploring the world of Sand Land truly feel like an adventure.Sand Land challenges what I considered to be "good" or "high" quality design. There is so much to this game that enraptured me, yet at the same time there are many little things that have me muttering, "damn why'd they do this?" Those are little issues that would normally pull me out of the game and, well, they didn't this time. There's something to that, something in Sand Land's design that I find myself unable to qualify, but something all the same.Fantastic treatment of a little-known story written by a legendary artist over 20 years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun vehicular action game with RPG mechanics and tons of lovable characters. It's a very comfy game, and has a very beautiful art-style.Much respect and care has been given to preserve Akira Toriyama's signature art-style.The mechs and other vehicles are fun to control and customize. They have a very unique playful aesthetic style that you won't find in most games.The animators definitely worked their butts off bringing the  various creatures and characters to life. The story is light-hearted enough that you can play this with your kids, but deals with serious topics like war, famine, and death in a tasteful way that won't traumatize children but also will get them thinking about the costs of war, the pitfalls of human greed, and of course the folly of judging people by their initial appearances. You grow attached to certain characters, that you'll actually want to go out of your way to help them out and give them a second chance at life.As for the main cast: They each have their own unique personalities. Thief is more cautious and wary; concerned with keeping the prince safe and gives insights to the player as to how the demons view humanity. The fiend prince at first comes off as arrogant and reckless, but shows his true colors through his actions and deeds. Though he is proud, and tries to acts like a fierce powerful warrior, you can see he is a still a child at heart.  Rao is the father figure and voice of morality; imparting his wisdom and survival tactics on the prince, and guiding him towards making the right choices in an harsh world. Despite his age, Rao is humble enough to admit that even he still has much to learn about the world and stands to learn alot from his companions. It's a great game, and I recommend checking it out if you're a fan of Akira Toriyama's work, or are looking for a fun laid back story-based game with cute characters and fun vehicles.

_childDocuments_.review: Before release I took time to look at early reviews for this game and saw many underwhelming pieces written. While it's true that games based on manga and anime rarely hit home or deliver anything out of the norm, Sand Land finds a way to mix a tried and true open world experience with enough crafting and exploration to break up the monotonous fetch quest grind. The vehicle crafting and customization is varied and spread out enough that there's always something new to get, build or find after a lengthy main quest. The fun and diverse approach to battles depends on what you would like to use to fight them as opposed to solely relying on level scaling. The desert wasteland of a world is beautiful and expansive, drawing me from using fast travel in an effort to explore, spelunk and fight looking for precious resources and engage in humorous side quests. Movement in physical combat is fluid and vehicles feel as smooth or as clunky as they would realistically feel to drive. The characters are dynamic and the unraveling story is so fantastic that I will be looking for the manga series to complement my collection.Don't believe the middling reviews. Sand Land is truly a great man's greatest work and this game reflects the love he put into this series.RIP Akira Toriyama

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed parts of the game and think that it holds promise, as it currently is I cannot recommend buying it at its price as of writing of $60. Based off a manga series of the same name, Sandland mixes elements of Dragon Ball Z, Mad Max, and World of Tanks in a semi-post-apocalyptic landscape. Decades before the game's events, a massive war devastated much of the world and at least where we start out most of what's left is controlled by the nation's corrupt and ineffectual monarchy. It is also a world of powerful demons and lost alien technology, and we play as one demon who agrees to help a traveling human find a legendary spring and ease the water shortage.The game's biggest strength is its ability to combine ubiquitous tropes from other genres into an idiosyncratic package in a genre less accustomed to those tropes. The game's art is beautiful, capturing the style of a manga seemlessly in a vivid 3d setting. The vehicle building and combat are advanced enough to give the feeling of really customizing your own tank, but simple enough that someone unfamiliar with tanks can still grasp the mechanics pretty well. The moment you get your first tank, you can begin tinkering with it to best suit your style of blasting apart bandits or blowing petrasaurs out of the sky.However, as the story progresses, you will really start to hit the game's limitations and shortcomings. While multiple styles of combat are supported and encouraged, some only receive minimal attention. For example, most weapons do not specify range. This is fine for the relatively close quarters vehicular fights the devs seem to encourage, but if you prefer long range fights, you have to use trial and error to figure out what will even reach the enemy. More importantly, the game was originally released for game consoles, and even with a decent keybinding system, this leaves many controls feeling awkward for a PC user. For example, the default fire option is leftclick, but instead of being able to fire secondary weapons with by right-clicking, you need a third input to swap weapons. It gets even worse with some of the more advanced vehicles, until you reach the point with the so-called battle armor whose secondary machine gun is all but unusable if you only have a laptop touchpad. Finally, while the first half of the plot is amazing and gripping despite its reliance on old tropes, the second half is not only more hamfisted and predictable, but creates jarring disconnects with the first half.It was a fun game, and I'm even going to try and see if there is anything left to do. But I only bought it because it was on sale, and I'm not entirely sure it was worth the sale price.
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game but simply can't.Pros:1. The soundtrack is amazing. I thoroughly enjoyed the BGM in the game.2. Building up the town of Spino is very fun and rewarding, though there is no point in customising your personal room. It doesn't enhance the gameplay at all.3. I like the bots and their surrounding mechanics.4. The time trials were pretty fun and actually very well balanced. I had to retry quite a few times to get some instead of just steamrolling them as I would have expected.5. The achievements are pretty easy to get. I will be perfecting the game and don't expect it to take me any longer than 60, maybe 65 hours total.Cons:1. The game is incredibly easy, even on hard difficulty.2. Bot fighting is so fun it makes fighting outside of a bot a painful chore when it's forced on you in some boss fights and the battle arena.3. The story sucks. Pretty much every quest outside of one or two per arc is you winning the fight but losing in the cutscene. The only female character in the main cast is a professional kidnapping victim. All of the main characters are professionals at watching the bad guys do the bad thing as they stare dumbly during the cutscenes. The writing is so bad. I don't know if this follows the original manga or what, but sheesh, nothing in gaming sucks more than to kick the boss's ass no sweat only to fail your goal because the story demands it in a cutscene.4. _childDocuments_.review: I'm far from having finished the game (about fifteen hours of play so far, I think I've done 1 third of the campaign), but I'm really pleased.The game is really pretty, it runs really well, and the atmosphere is really nice. I knew the paper manga and I've really rediscovered the charm of the book and Toriyama's great designs. The customization of the vehicles is really cool and the numerous quests are often well written (they're a bit like FEDEX quests, but the NPCs who propose them have “real” reasons and fit in well with the game's lore).However, not everything is perfect: the game is very talkative, especially in the first few hours, and you're often interrupted by a cut-scene (not always exciting, as it's very static), dialogues and information that isn't very useful. In short, a kind of tutorial that drags on a bit, adding lore and explanations and justifications when you'd sometimes just like to be able to play for more than 5 minutes without being cut off. But as I say, it's really only at the start of the game, after which the pace is more pleasant and you're freer to explore.Another point, the menu interface is sometimes grooooosly lacking in QOL, typically the merchants' menu for selling equipment offers NO sorting system, and even worse, the same equipment (like a 5mm machine gun for the tank) that you own 3 times, will be present 3 times in the list of items for sale. And this is clearly a bug, because in this menu, one of the columns indicates the number of items you own, except that all double or triple (or more) items are “x1” but several times in the list.The result is a long list of items that are not sorted in alphabetical order, nor by type of equipment, or vehicle, or level, or rarity... it's just an appalling mess, and selling them is an abominable chore.Similarly, the menu for upgrading/making/equipping equipment on the various vehicles is impractical, with few options for comparing currently equipped equipment with equipment you want to make, or equipment already in your inventory.This is a real shame, as a large part of the game is about customizing and upgrading our vehicles, but the menus are at best passable and sometimes downright lame. But it's still a great game, I just hope a patch will fix the menu problems (at least the item resale menu bug where items don't stack).I'll update my review when I've finished the game (and when it's patched). As it is, it's a great AA, and all the more likely to please you if you like Akira Toriyama's universe and design.

_childDocuments_.review: Sand Land is a game that explores a lot of themes, in fact they almost cram too many themes into this package. Themes like prejudice, environmentalism, racism, religion and spirituality, politics, friendship and family relations, war and poverty - and more. This game is immensely complex if you look past the surface level, which is true of most Akira Toriyama works. But it is also comfortable to anyone who enjoys Toriyama's works. The 'tailed boy who likes challenge and adventure goes on an epic quest' journey to the west, coming of age trope that Toriyama adores in almost everything he does is still here. It's basically 'Dragon Ball' if Dragon Ball was set in a Post Apocalyptic Mad Max world, a strange - but familiar - alternate reality telling of that story. To some, the fact that it's exploring yet another trope might be 'samey' and 'boring'. To stupid fanboys like me, we never get tired of the nuances and differences. This game is as awesome as the manga and it's a shame there won't be more.10/10 Would let blonde dreads Bulma fix my tank again

_childDocuments_.review: Final Rating: BThis one had some potential, but ends up being middling at best.  SandLand won't win any awards; it's a product that's just "fine".  That said, it's not worth $60, but I say most people will probably find the game does enough that even a full price purchase isn't regretted.SandLand needed a little more time to develop.  The ground/melee combat is uninspired and uninteresting, the entire adventure is devoid of any challenge whatsoever (even on Hard), the character animations are a bit wonky and robotic at times (outside of the cutscenes where they are great), and some of the options don't work (resolution issues in text, anti-aliasing issues, and control schemes across vehicles aren't separated even though the game says they are). As for the story, it's a bit disjointed.  For those that read the manga, it'll be obvious where the game followed the original content and where they introduced "new content". Each side could have been more tactfully woven together to create an enhanced version of the original story.  Instead you get two halves of a goofy, "bruh-moment" Toriyama story sewed together.  And that's ok, because it still makes you grin and entertains.The part that is good is the vehicles - the real highlight of the game.  Combat with them is a bit stiff and simplistic, absolutely no Armored Core or anything, but the numbers and the equipment still make for a pleasurable time.  There's a small lootfest aspect where stuff can be found in the overworld or built in the shops; as your arsenal grows in strength and rarity, so too does your potential to just humiliate the opposition.  I had a great time fighting enemies of all levels and evolving my builds as I was able to utilize higher-tier weapons.I like this game.  I wish they'd have given it more time to bake, especially to develop that melee combat, but it is what it is.  What's here is a passable and decent JRPG adventure full of side quests, town building, friendship, serving up fresh knuckle sandwiches, and causing explosions in a tank.  That was Toriyama's original inspiration for the manga, and the game is our tributary to experience that adventure again in a more engaging way.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished Part 1. Taking a bit of a break before continuing the Journey. The game perfectly captures the anime and expands so much on the world that Akira Toriyama has dreamed up. Most NPCs are voiced and they even got the VAs from the Anime to do the voices here. The side quests are very meaty and provide a huge sense of progression, especially when you see the results of your actions slowly build up the main hub of the game.  The sandy environments are very distinct despite seeing vast swaths of land covered in the same *sand*. Each region has different fauna and geographical features that spice up things. Piloting a vehicle is very fun. Each vehicle has its own purpose and the variants of the main vehicles provide a different flavor from the base vehicles. Modifying the vehicles are very satisfying and they give you plenty of options on how to play each vehicle. Your allies will also be able to provide support here by way of active abilities that are subject to cooldowns.Other than exploring the overworld, there are two kinds of levels where you have to play as Beelz:I've just finished the dam arc as of the time of writing this review, so there's still plenty for me to see. The game takes a while to open up, a bit like the length of part 1 for Days Gone. This is definitely a relaxed experience moving the main quest forwards but still provides quite a challenge when you want to do everything there is to do in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: THERE'S NO TANKS IN THIS DOJOI am 3 hours in at the time of writing this, this is my initial thoughts of Sand LandStoryLittle Daemon Prince Beelzabub, his minion Thief, an old soldier Rou and a mechanic Ann, embark on a perilous journey to bring water back to the Sand Land, Standing in their way is the corrupt and powerful Royal Army.So far it is kitch and funny,  Like a 90's kids show. The humour and banter never lets up but the characters are pretty stock standard. I am enjoying it so far, but don't go into this expecting anything deep or unexpected.GameplaySo far I have spent about 10% of my time running around punching things as the little fiend Beelzebub, the combat is a little stiff, with only a few moves to choose from (so far).90% of the game has been in the Tank that you steal earlier on. That is fun. You roam around the desert annihilating everything you roll past, which as fun as it is, does unfortunately have the potential of getting old. I would recommend setting the difficulty to hard, because normal and easy are just moving you through the story without any real challenge.There is diversity in gameplay, a couple of stealth sections, some platforming and a fun crafting element with your tank and subsequent vehicles.There are little 'side quests' you find in the world that offer very little value and it takes you a while before any of the 'loot' even matters.The combat progression does feel poorly planned. I got the tank and spent about an hour rolling around learning the ins and outs, winning every battle I came across, only to reach a mini-boss and have a number of 'this is how you shoot', 'this is how you aim' lectures thrown at me, leaving me with a 'um, duh I know' feeling.The good news is the combat is smooth and kind of addictive for now, it's fun lining up shots and seeing your team hanging off the side of the tank, chatting away while you machine gun down a Velociraptor. GraphicsGorgeous. Toriyama's work in it's best video game incarnation. Makes me wish for a remaster of Blue Dragon and other games in this style.Definitely a highlight is cruising along admiring the beautifully animated vehicles, the sandy dunes, the mountains in the distance and the enormous Royal base over the horizon.SoundVoice acting is good with the characters being brought to life with very good performances. As I said earlier, it's like playing through a 90's Saturday morning cartoon.The Music is very meh. I would have loved a more Japanese inspired trumpet and violin ensemble like the original Dragonball score, the music in Sand Lands is serviceable,  but nothing will stay with you after playing Final Verdict3 Hours in, I haven't wanted to get a refund. I'm past the time to do that now, but that for me is a big deal with new, full priced games. I hope the game gets more difficult and there is more to do than drive around shooting at things, but we will see. If you are on the fence, maybe wait a bit, it's not going anywhere. Otherwise give it a go and have fun, because it is fun and that's whats important.7/10 (So Far)

_childDocuments_.review: Anime games can be really fun but they tend to have a fairly stale 'style' to them. Arena fighters and horde fighters tend to dominate the scene, and while those have some great games in them an open world exploration focused game is an absolute treat to find.Sand Land is kinda a deep cut for Toriyama's works but it's very clear this is as much a 'Toriyama IP' as Dragon Ball. Bright and vibrant styles, big characters, action focused conflicts. The story is a bit 'basic' but that basic nature lets the writers explore the characters deeper and they do a great job making everyone feel unique and distinct in their reasons for working with the strange little group of 'heroes' assembled.The game isn't perfect, the map bothers me a lot because it seems there's no marker for when the many caves and exploration areas are 'completed', so the completion player in me is bugged, and the menus can be a little clunky to use mid fight at times, but all in all the game feels very smooth and the vibe of this weird high fantasy Mad Max world is distinct and clear.The vehicles are all distinct and fun feeling, each having their own niche and role, and they're used for both exploration and combat to make them feel even more like a part of the party just as much as the characters proper. I've barely scraped the surface of customization so far and can already see how each of them I've unlocked have their own different 'builds' to go with and all that will make experimenting fun.All in all even if there wasn't the obvious emotional connection of this being one of the last projects Toriyama worked on I'd be giving this a big thumbs up, but it is fitting that one of the last things we'll see with his name on it is a genuine breath of fresh air in the genre and a unique and entertaining experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on this game for a while and obviously with Akira Toriyama's death was so recent, I knew I was going to get it. I was sent this game for free as a birthday gift so to me, as a person who put £0 into this game, I think its a very fun game.Is it worth the £49.99 that its asking for? Watch some videos, read some reviews, and wait for a discount that is worth what you believe it is worth. I am only putting this review as a recommend because I do recommend this game The is a lot of good to this game but also its share of bad. The art style is great, if you love Toriyama's art style and the way he designs his characters and the things in his world, you'll like this.The vehicular combat is the games key focus but its not without its issues. For example, The game is expecting you to switch between the vehicles depending on your situation but once you've levelled up the tank enough you wont be using much else as it has the most armour and does the most damage. The battle bot is probably also going to find itself in your rotation as its very fun to use. There are a couple of other vehicles you will use also such as the Bike as its the fastest available vehicle to traverse the open world. The vehicle customisation is also fun, changing up my tank every time i got a new piece of gear and finding the play style that sat right with me was enjoyable.The story is good, its not very long though. I estimate that the story is about 15 hours long but there is a lot of side quests to do to pad out your play hours. Some of these missions are fetch quest though which when you're trying to do everything in the game can get annoying. There is a hand to hand fighting system in the game but its not utilised all that often over the vehicular combat. Its your standard JRPG fighting system of "light attack, heavy attack" until you build up your special meter enough to do a special attack for the big damage.There are stealth sections of the game which can be fun IF you like stealth games. They can sometimes be a bit rough there is a specific route you have to take but the game doesn't make it obvious to you and there isn't much going on in those sections. You're not Sam Fisher and crawling on the rooftops or hiding in the shadows, there was one instance in the second stealth mission where you have to walk across some wires but that's been in so far. You are simple just trying to get from A to B without being caught and waiting for an enemy to loop there walk path so you can run past them. There is a way to "takedown" the enemies so if you need to back peddle you can do so without being caught. The dungeon crawling does get fairly same-y with a lot of repeating rooms and repeated enemy fights that don't really break up from the dungeon crawling and instead feel more like a roadblock. There isn't a lot of enemies in the dungeons either, you could go like 10 minutes without an enemy that like 5 easily killable enemies turn up which just brings you to a halt, rinse repeat.There is a lot of repeating overworld dialogue. Going past a rock that you need a jump bot for, there's a dialogue for that (every time). Go past an enemy, there's a dialogue for that, go past a radio tower, dialogue, you get the picture. For me, my brain was able to just filter it out most of the time and I feel like its just there as a reminder which can be seen as a positive and a negative.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Game is hella fun, looks great and handles well, but there are a few annoyances that drag it down a bit.  Good for a discount (maybe not full price) but definitely worth checking out!!!This is definitely an "under the radar" game that takes quirky Dragon Ball, Dragon Quest, Dragon Ball, Blue ... Dragon (HOLY CRAP THIS ART STYLE IS ALL ABOUT THE DRAGONS!) styled art and gives us an open world to explore as an Adventure .. ARPG?  I think ARPG gets tossed around too much, I'd say it's an Adventure game with RPG elements.  Combat can be had either on foot using your firsts or in a variety of vehicles that you can build (after finding the parts/frames for) throughout the game such as a Tank, Jump Bot, Car, Motor Cycle and more.  Plenty of options.  It's a fun and engaging game with an animation and voice acting style that any fans of the Dragon series content listed above would be intimately familiar with!  The game runs very smooth and performs well with the occasional stutter here and there.  Criticisms:  Voice lines throughout the exploration phase of the game are repetitious, happen way too often, not enough variety .. and it does absolutely NOTHING to better the game.  Downright annoying, but I don't want to turn voice off cause it does so for all of the voice lines.Exploration is fun, but heavily gated by the main quest and side quests.  Way too often you'll find things that you can't get past and then long forget even how to get there when it's time to go back .. or... forget they even exist.  Map is not very intuitive.. sure it shows locations, but ... with the verticality present in the game, it's often very difficult to figure out how to get to some locations, only to find out it's gated behind some other requirement.  Vehicle upgrades are another example of gating, components required to upgrade your vehicles are often only available after you've progressed through a certain point in the story (or even side quests) so as with many RPGs, people like to grind and then be an absolute CHAD when you're ready to do the story... yeah... you won't be able to do that.Combat is often repetitious and you can just as easily just drive around in a circle to beat most enemies.  yaaaaayyy.  Variety in the bots/vehicles you obtain can add a little flair here and there, but it's not enough to keep it fresh.  One such mini boss bounty that was sitting in a cave, didn't even move... i just shot it from outside using ballistic incendiary missiles from my car.  Sooooo ... yeah.  Only thing that killing open world monsters is useful for is getting materials.  Experience to level up is not really something you get enough of outside of quest completions.What's good about the game:  Love the art style and quirky animations!  That's what pulled me into the game.  The voice acting is really well done and makes me feel like I'm watching an anime.  I love that.  Some of the voice lines are humorous as well and I love their reactions to certain situations.  Vehicle upgrades and building is fun, but also limited through gating.  Early on you'll find weapons that have a level requirement you're not going to be able to reach any time soon, so you're sitting on better loot for a long time before you can use it.  Story keeps me going and the idea that i"m going to find more loot.  I love loot.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is awesome, and it closely follows the show. You can remap all of the controls, and it even side by sides the keyboard and mouse controls with the controller controls. It also lets you customize all the controls separate for on foot versus in vehicle, etc. It lets you toggle sneak and run, and even change if the turret moves independently of the tanks tracks or if the tracks turn with the turret. Some of the negative reviews you might see mention the game being too specific i.e. "We need this to fix this or to do this." Pay close attention to those reviews, because if they are less than 3 or 4 hours into the game they are probably still in the tutorial. I don't even have the first 7 achievements and its still kind of like being in the tutorial as it introduces new things. The tutorial is not called a tutorial, but its pretty long with the game introducing new things then explaining them very specific, maybe even at time a little too specific. The game does deviate a little bit from the cartoon, but it is awesome. I think its a great game. I do not regret spending 60 bucks on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Though the game is fun for what it is, it is also a tad too easy.  Which is typical of Bandai Namco games, other than their Tales of series.  For whatever reason, any game Bandai Namco puts out that isnt a Tales of game, tends to be on the easy side, even at the hardest difficulty. Is it fun regardless?  Well yes, it can be.  However due to pacing, and just how easy it is, you are never really pushed, to doing side content, much less explore.  Enemy Bosses also tend to be high predictable, to a point where I would just screw around in a weaker vehicle to fight them instead of using the usual Tank, Hopper or Battle Armor intended for those boss fights.  Their is also a nasty bug that, never corrected itself and made me stop playing until it is fixed.  The Quest if I remember its name right, Lifeless to Lush, at the final part of it where I bring the items to the farmer, he never came to Spino, the quest tracker keeps pointing to the entrance of Spino whether I am in it or out of it.  This may have happened because after I spoke with him to then come to Spino, I saved and stopped for the night.  When I came back on, he was not there, but now, he is nowhere in the gameworld.  Thus I cant get that farm advancement for Spino, and possibly other things as well.  Still seen no update to the game as of yet, if they can add a harder difficulty, and fix that bug, I may reverse my review.   Its painful to do a negative review on this, since this is one of three final games of Akira Toriyama, the other one being on its way, and the biggest one *at least in Japan* is still in the dark due to a development hell issue.  But I cant let things slide like that.  Ill consider changing it if things are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly just boring and uninspired; empty and pointless feeling.   No passion to be felt. They didn't even get a good AI to do the writing, as it is some of the worst, inhuman and robotic "conversations" or statements I've ever heard.  The "B-roll" lines that play between characters while traveling etc are also repeated over and over  again, so you really get a chance to appreciate this.  Even if the english VA weren't abysmal (which they are) it would still be trash because the writing is so flat.  It also seems the demographic is that of young children/teens.  Majority of the treasure chests are filler generic parts used to upgrade (Spring A, Bolt B, etc) making them much less thrilling to seek out.  There ARE unique-reward chests, which are thankfully larger and easy to recognize, but these were few and I never got anything from one that got me excited.The combat both on and off vehicles is , and mowing down infantry with tank shells IS satisfying.  The game world looks alright.  I think there is one single music track that I remember hearing in my entire playtime so I hope you enjoy it.I originally threw $60 at this with the allure of "Dragon Quest with tanks" as another reviewer put it, and the thought of a motorcycle with rocket launchers on it sounded so super enjoyable.  Unfortunately that other reviewer couldn't be more off base, as this is nowhere near Dragon Quest, and is honestly insulting to that IP to even mention it in the same breath.  Everything here feels "tacked on".The game stuttered really badly at launch but forcing DX11 from the launcher solved this for myself.I ultimately never even found out if motorcycles with rocket launchers are even possible because I just became bored, or worse yet, flat out annoyed.  Lifeless. [5/10]

_childDocuments_.review: Sand Land is a great game. On foot, combat and explorations are fine. In your vehicule, it's even better.There's a lot of vehicules to craft and customize. They have unique features for both combat and exploration. (A bike to jump over crevasses, A tank to destroy obstacles, a bipedal vehicule to jump, hover vehicules (cars and bikes) to float above water and sand, etc.) The open world is nice and the game is much bigger than I expected when I first started. Sand Land is only Half of the game. The story is satisfying and well animated.
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, good story, good characters, good gameplay and nice music....Big map, lots to explore, but there is a little bit of learning on how to play... it's not super heavy on farming and crafting but it's enough... and you have to really look and find a way to many areas... think of this game as a mixture of recore, nier automata, with tiny bit of mad max and far cry...now i do have a few nitpicks: when human enemy is attacking my character, and wild life joins the fight, they both team up on me.... thats stupid.... when the enemy ai shoots its own teammates, nothing happens.... that's stupid... when i descend off a cliff and not do a full jump by using bots fuel booster glide, and barely land, damage counts as a full jump, that's stupid.... selling items is a pain because it is mixed altogether, so you have to either memorize what you have equipped or write it down... (unless i cant see the equipped sign)....other than that it is a good game....
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: RIP Akira Toriyama, you are one of the greats! I recommend first watching Sand Land: The Series on Disney+ to know what this game is about. It's good! and the perfect companion to this game. The game has you wandering around the Sand Land driving the tank and other vehicles, and uses simplistic melee fighting for the main character.I'm not really sure why they made this game, or why you should play it. Besides loving Sand Land, the game play isn't satisfying. It an action game, but not a real RPG. Yet, the game looks great!!! You should check it out. The developers could add other gameplay modes to make better use of core game mechanics. I'd like to see more survival skills modes to make use of the wasteland. It may be too late for survival modes, however, as the vehicle and melee combat  have already taken over the core game loop.
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game is great, it’s semi steam deck compatible. Game play works fine, however. Halfway through the game, most of the cutscenes will cause the deck to crash. Pros:   Sand Land is probably one of the best titles I’ve played in the past five years. Haven’t been able to put it down since I got it. Controls are smooth, story is decent, the world is beautiful. Game constantly delivers, even in the post game. A lot of games tend to drop the ball for post game content, Sand Land doesn’t. Cons:      Pretty sure the devs started getting rushed near the end of development. A lot of the late game dungeons are just two rooms, not much exploring needs to be done.    Steam deck. It will run normal gameplay, fine, however. Half way through the game, the deck will crash during most cutscenes. The work around is to play those parts on, pc.     All and all Sand Land has kept me entertained, and is still continuing to keep me entertained even though I’m close to reaching one hundred percent completion. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: You get to control mecha that feel like they were made by Toriyama himself, as a mecha fan I approve. These are probably the best looking machines I've seen since Lost Planet.The quests are pretty basic but the main combat is incredibly fun, at the end game the quests end and it becomes a strange looter shooter, not only that there's new vehicles and weapons to play with, but without knowledge of where enemies spawn it feels incredibly aimless.Belz, Rao, Theif and Ann are all great characters but they talk A LOT, dont know if there's a way to make them pipe down, this can be a deal breaker.

_childDocuments_.review: As mentioned by other reviewers,  shares a lot of the strength and weaknesses of , despite being quite different in tone. Driving around and customizing your vehicles is fun. Combat is passable, albeit a bit clunky. Quests and loot, however, could've used more variety. What holds this game up are the quirky characters that are so characteristic for Toriyama's early works.There were a few things I didn't like, though. The battleships for instance. Large 3D mazes just aren't my thing, and these ones were particularly bad, because you had to backtrack out of them instead of being able to fast-travel out. Which is quite baffling to me, since fast-travel is quite decent everywhere else in the game. I also disliked how the rebuild of Shino kept dragging on and on and on after the end credits.Still, all in all a good game. Recommended particularly if you like , early , and of course the one-shot this game is based on.Rating: ★★★★☆

_childDocuments_.review: This game constatly surprises me with something great. I played through most of it on Steam Deck and it runs great there, most of the time hitting 40 fps with some dips to 30 fps (on medium / high settings). When playing it on PC, it supports 21:9 out of the box, which for japanese games is not that common. These are just the technical aspects......when it comes to the story and world building, it really IS fantastic. Sense of humor, exploration, character design, all top notch as expected for a game based on manga by Akira Toriyama (RIP). Gameplay is also very solid. Vehicles provide many ways of playing the game and in places where you could assume certain vehicle serves their role for good, it turns out there are further alternatives and additional vehicles serving similar role, yet they all play very differently.This is definitely a contender to game of the year so far and I cannot recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: For all fans of robot fights with customisation. _childDocuments_.review: there's just something about this game that's surprising and unique. The soundtrack feels Jesper Kyd inspired, and I'm often in awe at some of the ambient score. It's a shame I can't find any of it online.The combat is ridiculously simple and honestly not very well thought out. They want me to fist fight some dudes but you can literally just take out your tank and kill them instantly in a way that doesn't quite feel intentional. But the story is great and I love that the side quests are worth doing. Watching the town grow and come back together is a relaxing feedback loop. Honestly, a simple little game that is great to pick up and play especially on steam deck.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is solid but basic at it's core. The most similar comparison to another game I can make is interestingly enough is the underrated(imo) Madmax game that came out in 2015. All though the vehicle and on foot combat in that game was superior. It's ultimately the same formula of driving around and pimping your ride to accomplish various objectives. One issue I had was challenge, even on the hardest setting. Not every game needs to be super difficult, but It's more fun when you actually have a reason to use the various abilities, power ups, and builds. They give you all these options and abilities but 99% of the time you'll just open up with the tank and the fight will be over before its started.  The enemies aren't particularly aggressive or threatening. The bigger creatures can be a bit bullet spongy but are all easy enough to circle strafe. They do add some slightly more challenging small fast enemies later in the game but by that point their firepower wasn't really a threat to me and it was just slightly more time consuming to pin them down for the kill. The on foot combat is also fairly weak and uninteresting for most the game, it get's better, but not great. But thankfully you can almost entirely ignore it most the time as outside specific story points they do let you throw down your vehicle almost anywhere. Even in cramped areas where the game wants to consistently remind you that it is in fact cramped and you should go on foot. Sorry Thief/Rao, screw that, I'm mowing down those snakes with my Hoppers MG. Of course this also contributes to the games lack of challenge as non vehicle/giant enemies all die to a short burst from any of your rides secondary weapons. Another note of interest is the game has an old school design where it breaks up the game play with sections that are mechanically different from the core game play. Platforming sections, Stealth, even a few little side scroller areas. It also has an entirely irrelevant and ignorable bit of animal crossing style room design. I personally don't mind this type of design but I can see how it might be annoying to others so I'll just say that it's all brief enough that if you find any particular part distasteful you'll not be stuck on it for long/often enough to really matter. So far I've only really given criticism, so don't get me wrong, I still think it's a good game worth playing. It just has a lot more potential. For instance I love how your little hub town evolves and grows as you play, always enjoyed that mechanic. But considering they added an entire room design mini game locked away in a backroom it would have been more interesting if you could of added different decorations to customize our town as it's by far the place you'll end up staring at the most as you come and go.Exploration also could use some work. Ruins are mostly just copy paste assets with the same few enemies and the rewards are unexciting common crafting materials and coins that buy treasure maps that seem almost functionally useless as you practically have to be top of said treasure before it pings on your minimap. If you're on the fence about it I'd say the determining factor is twofold. 1) Do you have a particular love of the niche type of game that revolves around open world vehicle customization and want to play something besides the Madmax game? 2) Do you love Akira Toriyama(Dragonball guy) style characters, art, and stories? Because the world itself is fantastic if that's your thing(it is for me) and it really helps carry the game.If those two things are true you should absolutely love the game despite the flaws. If you care about neither you're probably wasting your time/money and can find more bang for your buck elsewhere.P.S. As of writing this the random dialogue in the game repeats the same lines constantly and it becomes real annoying real fast. Trust me when I say people are not overstating this, but I imagine this is something they'll patch out soon enough. Till then, pro tip, when they start talking shoot a random enemy as you're driving by to stop the dialogue.

_childDocuments_.review: Sand Land caught my eye back in some Summer Games Fest or whatever and, I recall, my thoughts were 'oh, dude! sweet! another game to satisfy my vehicle autism, but this time it's got the Akira Toriyama style on top of it!' This has rung true having finished the game itself - there's plenty of neat little vehicles and weapons to play with, and a whole heck of a lot of stuff for completionists to futz with. Gameplay's not very offensive, it's simple to-be-expected vehicle combat with some rather shoddy on-foot combat, and the general loop is what you can expect from an average JRPG. If you focus on the main quest exclusively, you can likely finish the game in a weekend. Me, I like vehicles too damn much, and wanna see *all* the possibilities. As far as the story goes, I liked it. It has a charm all its own, nothing CRAZY but it was still fine.All in all, if you want a vehicle-focused JRPG in the Toriyama art style...you're not going to find another one, but look no further than this game. It's a neat little treat and does what it does just fine for my tastes.7/10
