_childDocuments_.review: After 99 hours I dabbled and sunk into this game, it is time to review my experience with it. TLDR: a recommend ONLY when available for a budget price and for people who enjoy "non-story stories" and have the patience to overcome the story-locked (and therefore time-locked) access to enjoyable end-game-gear.Long review (English is not my first language, sorry for any mis-spelling):The game overall is a nice and long time killer. It is easy to learn, not overly difficult, and gives you some variety to choose how you solve some things. It has a nice looking and very nice performing world, lower hardware spec recommendation and is optimized very well. It did not receive a patch withing my 99 hour 100% playthrough (plus some part grinding, but stopped due to nothing to gain with that), though bug-wise and/or performance-wise it went OK with most users, apart from microstutters on some systems, that mostly could be circumvented when using DX11 mode. The story is linear and leaves no room for interpretation. It is mostly kid-friendly, even violence is just tapping on enemies which then run away, get unconcious or just vanish. Autoaim is very much a thing, but works not too obvious and in the background, and well. Autosaves are fair and in most cases not overly far back from the point you failed. The GUI is nice and easy to understand, also well placed. You can access loot from within the vehicles and the autoloot feature from mob drops is fair. At story's end you can access the whole map exept one region. Even some missions are still there after the main story's end. The guns and upgrades feel good and finding your own playstyle is easy and rewarding.Now the bad. The controls are awful on PC, with mouse and keyboard. I can just immagine, that it is eve worse on gamepad. I did not test it with gamepad, due to its "shooter style" gameplay. Sometimes it (resets and) locks your mouse movement for 2 seconds after changing a vehicle - which could lead to unfortunate and unnecessary, frustrating deaths. Sometimes you get tapped from enemies, and then also get a (about) two second timeout, not due to any stun-effects or anything that would be displayed, just have to "try again and again" to move by repeating mouse and keyboard movement. This is probably a bug and most definitely not a feature. And it leads to unnecessary deaths. Also jumping and climbing without a vehicle is very, very inconsistent and random. The game also has difficulties recognizing double jumps and badly relies on glitchy momentum. Jump bot's are affected by this as well, which makes jump races a chore. This leads to a lot of frustrating, forced retries. Hover vehicles often hang or get stuck on ground level, which sometimes lead you to get kicked out of your vehicle (one-seater hovers only). Some control schemes will definitely lead you to not prefer some vehicles, like the hopper e.g. It is also noteworthy, that on any tyre vehicle, if you have some momentum or pressed <accellerate> a short while ago, it will take every turning command as an accelleration command as well (who thought that up?). Some other vehicles are pointless due to their speed, and you just drag them around to move boxes when needed. Access to most vehicles is story driven, so you will see the better and more fun vehicles late game only. In the end you most probably will use the main tank only to open some "hard rock" barriers. Fight with the battlebot and hover scooter, travel with the hover scooter and two boost chips, and traverse from water to some higher rock edges with the mono-hover-cycle. That fact makes every other vehicle and every other part drops very, very redundand. Also the fact, that in most cases you will prefer small vehicles, because of limited manover space. What I am saying is, that these vehicles are locked in late-game, and until then you have to opt in with arkward and slow moving stuff you don't want to, but have to. This forceful pushing of the player also counts for the forced stealth sections. If you don't like them, well tough luck. Yes, there is always an "easier way" to do stealth sections, but you will miss out most of the loot there if you choose that way.One ingame feature is as necessary as an apendix: putting stuff in 3 rooms in your "apartment" style garage? Why? I found absolutely ZERO reasons for touching that gameplay element for more than 2 minutes and even advertizing that would be like commenting the brightness of the sun, after looking at it with the naked eye for some time.Now to the story. And here I just know that I will make people angry because that is a fan - or no fan issue. I am not a fan. And if you are enjoying the story, in my opinion, you must be either still growing your brains, must have a mental deficiency or you are just very simple minded. I apologize for my opinion about that to all and everyone who enjoy the story. And I recommend trying out something called a "good book" to experience a challenging huge difference. Especially the changes between power-fantasies and getting kicked in the rear by a tease, is someting of a narratively low grab I do not, and cannot enjoy in any way. You destroy a whole army ingame, kick the bosses rear and then the story wants to make you believe that someone can stop you with a finger? Year, nice... So engaging. That lead me to press "f + left mouse + right mouse" or just ESC+f every "story" element after my tormented brain could take it no more. A shame, because the developer put a lot of time and effort in something I would call "uneccesary and unconvincing trash". The voice acting e.g., which probably cost a fortune. (Sorry if my age shows there.)I also set the voice overs to zero percent very soon, because the repetition is just brain-wrecking. Especially when entering some regions or your NPC's falsely "detect" or randomly choose to comment anything I do. I could not make it stop by a feature option ingame, so I had to set the voice-over to zero. And therefore silenced every story section, which is also a negative point. A shame really. Wasted potential. All in all a enjoyable time killer, if you skip the unconvincing story cutscenes (thank the universe that they are skippable!) and can find a workaround for the badly-working and/or too slow vehicles. But not worth the asking price of 60€. I got a cheaper key for 45€, and considering I sank 90 hours in the 100% (plus some uneccesary part grinding) at a slow pace, I would say paying 0,50€ per hour of entertainment is OK. But considering that the story is trash (in my opinion, I know I will make people angry with that), wait for a sale before considering a buy.I apologize again to all people that enjoy the narrative and story of mangas, animes like that. But quality lies in the eye of the beholder. And this is my review and opinions after all. You don't have to agree to anything I wrote about how I felt playing this game. I am I, you be you!

No new game plus (so i am loading an old save and leveling up without doing any quests so i can have a maxed save with quests to play) and the APDS ammo dissappears at short range but the railgun doesn't

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 10/10 for me, going to start routing a speed run. Good drive and shoot, great exploration, and superb style.I love this game, the vehicles are brilliant and the art design of the late and great legend Akira Toriyama is to die for. The vehicle play is basic yet very refined and exploration is top teir and movement however is where it's at. This game is a speed runners heaven so far, what I mean by that is there is massive potential for sequence breaks and I have found quite a bit myself. No story skips but massive progression skips. Myself I have been able to explore all of Sand Land itself except for half of the maphin region before unlocking the motorcycle. I was able to get a hover tank chassis (what I think is a late game vehicle, idk haven't made it to it in the story so far) and grind out drops for all the parts to make one as my 4th vehicle just after unlocking the jumping bot. All of this done by making very precise jumps with the car and clever maneuvering with the jump bot.Note: I have not made the hover tank yet, the engine and suspension specifically drop at level 24 and up as far as I've seen and if anyone knows a drop for level 19 parts then you could make the hover tank as early as your 4th vehicle and be unstoppable.10/10 going to start routing soon

_childDocuments_.review: Running through this and the anime and manga at the same time is kinda fun, catching the same scene in all three. There's been changes for the sake of game mechanics, nothing world breaking. The over world is a fun place to explore, and is soo good looking, along with the vehicles, I agree with the statement I read about Toriyama's passion really being the vehicles vs the people, it's nice to have an actual open world game that figured out how to have vehicles without ruining the exploration factor, and exploration is absolutely something you want to do here. The characters are all well done, Beelzebub is the main one you play as, who gets a point per level, Thief and Rao have to share a point, and get used for their own little quests, such as Thief donning the Santa outfit to go stealing supplies, Ann was brought in early for vehicle maintenance, but doesn't get treated as really a party member, even when she joins you on your trips. It is a very good game, especially when so many open world rpgs lately have been disappointments in the open world exploration parts. I hope this does well, I'd love to see Bandai keep on this path for the anime based games.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who wasn't familiar with Sandland and Toriyama i did not purchase this out of fandom. I was more curious about the weird art style and gameplay and wow, i'm having fun with this title. Vehicle combat+brawler+a bit of ubisoft formula and quirky likeable characters. It fits well together. Exploring the desert is not like Elden Ring, this isn't a AAA game at all but it doesn't habe to be. It's nice to lean back and just have fun from time to time. Especially on the Steam Deck. Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not too far into the game and I'll update the review if my opinion changes, but so far I'm very happy with the game.The demo demonstrated the vehicular combat but it really didn't do the game any justice. The setting is like a Toriyama version of Metal Max. Despite being all desert, the locations are beautifully crafted and have a unique design but still exude that charm you know from Toriyama's other works. The characters are likable and I enjoy the surprising amount of story told through dialogues and cutscenes.With a huge pile of shame I'm particular these days about playing games, and I was worried this would be one of those games that you try to like but ultimately give up on playing because the gameplay is tedious or the story doesn't interest you enough. No such thing so far. The gameplay is smooth and enjoyable and the story motivates me to keep going. This is a genuine surprise hit for me.
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: Such a cool game, 10/10. Playing on steam deck, standard settings getting around 60fps with some dips. Game runs super well and looks stunning.Realy reminds me of stuff from the PS2 era. Straightforward and doesn't waste your time like a lot of super bloated JRPGs theses days. Awesome character designs and a fitting game to remember Akira  Toriyama R.I.P
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really impressed by the smooth graphics, highly optimized, very easy vehicular and manual combat controls. It's very fluid and the game plays like a movie with plenty of story cutscenes and chonky dragonballlz universe art style to eye candy for as you're enjoying the cutscenes. Plenty of humor also! I've only played a couple hours but it's so much more refined than the demo when i played it. I would say it's really worth the price. You will enjoy it so much!
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: I plan to come back and leave a more detailed review once I have more play time under my belt. As far as first impressions go, the game's pretty fun. Performance is solid, haven't had a single frame drop, the vehicle combat is a blast, the writing is jovial but not to the point of being plain cheesy, the characters are fun and their interactions are enjoyable even if they do tend to talk often.My only moderate gripe thus far would be on keyboard the dedicated "back" key is backspace. Leaving menus requires you to either take your hand off your mouse or move your other hand across the keyboard. It's a bit irritating that it isn't able to be re-bound to another key.
_childDocuments_.name: SAND LAND

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game with a decent amount of variety in gameplay so far.  I enjoy the vehicles; there just aren't enough games that do vehicle combat.  Not familiar with the source material, but the story/setting is interesting albeit seemingly aimed towards a younger audience.Stutters from demo seem gone and overall impression of the game is much better than I initially thought.  Still, the 70-ish Metacritic is likely valid.

_childDocuments_.review:
Dive into a desert world where both humans and demons suffer from an extreme water shortage - SAND LAND. Meet the Fiend Prince Beelzebub, his chaperone Thief, and the fearless Sheriff Rao, and follow the team on an extraordinary adventure in search of the Legendary Spring hidden in the desert. The end is only the beginning, as beyond this arid ground lies a new realm to explore.

In this action-RPG, players will find a nostalgic and heartwarming world created by Akira Toriyama, where you will become the main character Beelzebub. Learn how to control his powers and lead your company of heroic misfits exploring the legendary world of SAND LAND. Beware of the many dangers that populate it: between bandits, fierce wildlife, and the Royal Army, reaching the spring won’t be easy! Use your tact and imagination to develop tanks and other vehicles that will help you navigate this vast land, using a wide array of part combinations.

VEHICLES FROM BEYOND YOUR IMAGINATION
Unlock vehicles that can be leveled-up with various mechanic parts including weapons, engines, and suspensions. Design and operate a large variety of vehicles including Battle Tanks with powerful cannons, Motorbikes that speed through deserts, and Jump-bots that bounce over rivers to explore every corner of the continent.

BECOME THE SAVIOR THE WORLD NEEDS
Develop your basecamp in the city of Spino, as you build relationships with its inhabitants. As you bring the exiled people of the desert to Spino, watch the town and its capabilities grow. Listen to their requests and wishes, and unlock useful materials and city features.

ADVENTURE BEYOND THE DUNES
Travel through SAND LAND and its canyons, unveil its secrets, overcome all obstacles, and find the entrance to an unknown world.

name: Land of the Vikings
detailed_description: Manage your Hoard Chop down trees, plant and grow crops, hunt wildlife, mine for ore, and fish from the surrounding seas and fjords. Manage your resources carefully to ensure you can outlast the harsh winters, and expand your settlement from season to season. Know your Vikings Each of your villagers is a unique character in their own right. With 20+ characteristics, your villagers might be powerfully built strong men and women or silver-tongued thespians. Pay attention to skills and abilities when assigning tasks to your people. Not all Vikings are alike, nor are they equally good at all jobs! As your settlement grows, more Vikings will seek to join. You can choose to welcome them or turn them away. Over time, your Vikings will begin new families and give birth to new generations, extending their lineage and strengthening your settlement. Survive Fierce Weather and Events The land will bring many challenges to your settlement, from earthquakes to fire-starting lightning from Asgard. Unite your Vikings to withstand these disasters as best you can. The seasons bring their own challenges, as do events and disasters. Be ready for storms, blizzards, or the long, deadly cold of the winter season. Prepare firewood and food stores to keep your Vikings warm and well-fed! Trade with Neighbors Your neighbors are an excellent resource for goods and gold. Once you build a Trade Dock, ships will visit you with various cargos. You can also send out your own trade missions, as long as you have enough villagers to crew the vessel - and enough beer to fuel the crew! Raid and Plunder Any good Jarl will tell you that brute force is the best path to glory. Gather your Vikings and raid foreign villages to plunder their gold and silver, and gain Fame points. Train and strengthen your Vikings, and command them through the all-new battle system to ensure your victory, while defending your settlement from other villages! As your settlement flourishes, Viking heroes will want to pledge their valor to your cause. These heroes will lead your troops into battle, inspiring confidence and providing other bonuses along the way. Celebrate and Decorate No grids allowed! You can build wherever you want, designing your settlement as you see fit, and to increase your Vikings’ happiness. Construct monuments to Odin or Freya and customize the look of your Viking ships. You can even modify the look of houses with the Building Editor. This powerful in-game editor will allow you to build and personalize an unlimited number of buildings and decorations! Yggdrasil, the Tech Tree of Life Unlock new buildings and bonuses by spending Fame points in the Tree of Life. Discover beer brewing and build a Tavern for your villagers to relax in. Invest in goat farming to gather wool and weave fabric for better clothes. As you create better quality living and resources, your Vikings will become healthier and happier, and your settlement will flourish!

short_description: Land of the Vikings is a survival colony sim game. Build and lead your village, and expand it into a thriving city. A wise Jarl must manage resources, survive harsh conditions, and guide their fellow Vikings to work together through social conflict. Skál!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot more of this and have identified a lot of the issues so here's an update;You're going to experience one of several spirals but they're all inevitable.The most egregious is the need to constantly be expanding; if you're anything like me once you reach the endgame, you like to just watch. Anno, Cities Skyline, Frostpunk, there's something about looking at your hard work and just watching it run that is incredibly satisfying. Even in a cold sweat game like Frostpunk there reaches a point where you're left to just watch what's happening in between the panic.This game is not going to be one you can currently sit back and relax in, there's a reason - you MUST always be expanding. At all times. The larger the population the more you simply must just go ham on building more and more till something will either slip past your notice (which is incredibly likely as you can't track statistics, yes you read that right) or you'll inevitably be unable to keep up with the higher and higher requirement of any given resource.Now the fact that you can't track stats is a deal breaker to me Early Access or no but here's something that I have never experienced in a city builder before and it requires some explanation if you want to hop off here. I'd say check back later and hold onto your money. The positives are that is has a cool premise, unique theme, and an interesting foundation to work from - even if the UI and a lot of basic features are screaming for help.So, if you're still with me let me describe the actual worst thing ever, collaborated by other people in the discussions.Houses are not multi-generational and people age WAY too quickly, the parents ‘own’ the home and their children will reside in the home. Once the parents die the children stay in the home and not establish a new family… because they don’t have a new home to move to. If you’re seeing the issue here it gets so much worse.This creates a perpetual cycle where you’re trying to maintain a balancing act where you’re unable to maintain a population because eventually you’re going to experience entire households dying off without creating new families and ‘newcomers’ to your city can’t really be relied on to replenish because you have houses of people who are aging and the household isn’t freed up to accommodate new people so houses are required to be built to and… yeah. It needs some help. How? Well I don’t know I’m not a developer but this is going to be the ceiling a lot of people who are intent on reaching the end game are going to smack their face into. I hope they can wrangle the system into something that works because as it stands the tuning is off key.
_childDocuments_.name: Land of the Vikings

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard review to write - and I hope the dev reads this and is able to right the ship. At the point of this writing, I am nearly 40 hours in and on year 9 of my second settlement. At this time, only 8% of players have made it successfully into year 9 in their cities. Look, this is a good game. But here's the deal- many of the functions of this game are only there to slow down progression, and extend playtime. If you were to play the game with the hope of refunding it, you would have experienced barely anything by the Steam refund time. For example, I have created two cities (more about that in a bit) in 40 hours. In that time, I am probably about 50% down the tech tree. It would take me another 50 hours like to get the rest of the tech, and honestly that leftover tech is useless. The game is just a ramshackle of rough, unfleshed out ideas and a lot of "let's throw it on the wall and see if it sticks." On it's merits, it's a Banished clone, but a very light version. Resources are effectively unlimited, which is fine, but spread so far out at times that it can take a year or two to eventually reach iron and/or coal, and stone quarries. Food is also very simple - you have 5 resources (red meat, white meat, foraged foods and bread).  Vegetables are mentioned, but they do not appear to be in game. Also, you can make barley to create beer, which is listed as a "food," but isnt actually used unless you send ships to trade/explore/raid, or in the tavern. All three  of these are way down the tech tree - so there is virtually no reason to even plant barley until you have the requisit buildings.Let's talk about combat. About 6 hours into the game, roughly 2-3 game years, you will have a choice: trade or combat. You can't do both unless you have massive tech points, so what ever you choose will lock you for a while. This choice also stalls out your city progression for a while as you will not have enough points to move "up" the tech tree towards city upgrades. So, you pick combat - you can now make light infantry and archers. They both need leather and iron for armor, iron and coal for weapons, and iron and leather for shields. Making one soldier early on is time consuming and requires a massive industry - even though you can get through the game with only two tailors and one smithy. Once you have your equipment, you have to train your people. Takes about half a season. Meanwhile, they are getting older and quickly approaching a natural death (which is a debuff to city happiness, not that it matters much). Your soldiers are effectively worthless until you can build a drakkar warship, and even then they'll still mostly be worthless since you can only fit 10 on a ship at a time, and still, they need a hero to lead them. In my first playthrough, my hero got stuck inside a house and wouldnt come out. Dev said he couldnt fix it, so I had to restart. So let's say you finally get enough resources for to raid other settlements, what's next? Well your soldiers have no idea where the enemy is. So you send them on 3, 6 or 9 day scouting missions to find villages. They apparently sale randomly around Europe, sometimes discovering both Wales and Holland in the same trip,  but missing everything else in between. Even once these places are discovered, you have no idea of the strength or how rich the town is. So you keep sending scouting parties. This alone takes another two or so years to flesh out. Finally you are ready for a raid. One ship is never enough. You're party needs to be mixed - too many light infantry and they get slaughtered. Archers are only semi-useful sometimes. Heavy Infantry hits harder, but they also appear to die much easier - which seems odd. I never did unlock the other units. Combat is card based, with each card having a % chance at success. You never get anything that tells you how to influence these cards, so it's always just a blind role. Usually, most cards give you a 70+% chance. Every battle is basically the same. Pick how you enter the village, pick what your first attack is, pick how you respond to the defenders attack, then pillage the city/church/surrounding area before reinforcements show up. So maybe you you made it this far in the review and say to yourself, "Huh, that sounds like a lot of fun, but rewarding!" Well here is the rub. By the time you can finally muster enough resources for a raid fleet and army, you effectively do not need any of the items from the raid. Plus, your losses are either too much to recover from, or your economy is so strong that you can keep stamping out units. But to what end? By year 9 my warehouses were overfull, and my people spend most of their time just milling about. Trade is the same way. There is literally a tech that allows you to research trade, but locks you another year or so from being able to trade because the trade ship is in another tech. Also, you can't trade anything of substance. Maybe you focuses on food and leather and want to trade that for weapons and armor? Nope. Gotta trade for iron and coal, then build the stuff when you get home. Don't have an iron smith yet? Too bad. Maybe you have to sell off your massive stockpile of beer you made that you cannot use. Nope. Beer is not a trade item. Oh, hey, maybe I can see off some of my excess armor and weapons? Nope. Not a trade item. This literally makes 0 sense.Okay, one final rant before I put down some pros and suggestions. There is an event system in the game. Its bland, repetitive and serves no purpose other than to slow your roll. There are literally only a handful. There is an event where one of your villagers basically starts screaming in the town center. Everyone hates him and beats him up. You can banish him, which makes the family hate you, or you can pay him 25 silver and he gets a debuff for life. It happens, like clockwork, nearly ever season. If you dump them, be prepared to have nearly every family hate you at some point. If you dont, then expect to pay a 25 silver idiot tax every quarter. There is also a thief mission, where someone steals food. You can choose to do nothing (everyone mad), pay silver to create a pose to find the thief (you lose more money and in some rare events, you may catch the crook) or you can beef up security (which requires you have soldiers unlocked, and city defenses....which is wayyyy down the tech tree). Sometimes Freya will bless your fields. No idea how or why, it just happens. On one map, every year my animals got a disease and I had to kill them. This slows down your progress again as you do not get to keep the resources. Sigh. There are only like 2 more events, but you get the idea. So pros - It's slow. Maybe that's not a pro for you, but it's a fun little pick up and play simulation. The problem is that I will often put it on, run it at 2x or even 12x, and go fold clothes. Trust me, nothing will happen while you are gone. Another pro is the decorations system. It is still not fleshed out well, but each house and *some* buildings can be upgraded by using decorations. This removes the stagnant look of the cities, by adding your own customization. Even better, there are a bunch of assets on the workshop.It also has a asset editor. I havent played with it, and honestly probably wont, but the editor allows you to create new versions of existing assets, like new houses, decorations, etc. More games need this honestly, and I wish the dev put as much attention into the game as he did the editor.That said, and dev I hope you are reading this, here are some suggestions:- Vikings were known for drinking mead, not beer. Consider adding an apiary asset that is harvestable spring and summer, and a meadery. - There needs to be more early tech buildings before iron. Consider adding a wood craftsman and a bone/horn/antler craftsman. These crafters could make primitive tools and trade goods, and would be a good late-game resource sinkChar limit reached. Oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems stupid as I really like this game, but cannot recommend it at present as I feel it's not ready even for Early AccessLots of mechanics in the game are not explained, and for some that are they simply do not work. It states almost everywhere that you can use coal for heating houses, but you actually cannot and don't find that out until you either google it or wonder why you have warehouses backed up with coal and everyone is in their houses freezing.Once you arrive at the mid game there is no way to keep up with the stone production, and you cannot fill your village with good houses due to the bottleneck in stone. On the first scenario you can only build one stone pit which isn't enough to sustain your village once you get to around 500 population and the game is literally a struggle.It's far too easy compared to similar games (like Frostpunk) and I have like 3 achievements left to get from my first playthrough in around 40 hours of playtime (which quite a lot of it I admit I was AFK and checking in every so often). The progress in the game is so slow it's painful, you can see what you want to do but the game won't let you achieve it and you spend most of your time with the game on maximum speed waiting for things to happen.UI is simply horrible. You can have a max of 2 windows open. If you move your mouse outside of the menu UIs (e.g. assigning things by quantity, like food for raids) it disappears, so it can take 5 attempts to actually do something. Resources would be much better if you had an arrow below the pane at the top of the window and the full resources dropped down, or was configurable depending on your stage of the game. I feel you have to go through too many clicks to get the information you require. The encyclopedia has about 7 things in it so you are mostly left with no guidance and even with google it can be difficult to find information on what you need. Usually you find out that it's either an issue with a bug or bad design. I'm not even sure defance is a word and sure it should say defence...Once you complete all the basic objectives you are left to go native and pretty much there isn't really anything to aim for anymore except for the steam achievements. Even the raids feel pointless mostly, as most of the time I lose more than I gain by raiding, and the raid is basically just a short video that looks like it was made on playstation 1 with an outcome shown at the end. And yea, I'm sending enough attack power and not just sending my troops to die.As I write this review my village got raided, we failed to defend and I got another popup saying the villagers are unhappy which is stuck over the top of the raid results and therefore cannot close any window. It appears to be a game breaking bug. Hoping I can reload the game before the raid, but if not then I will just quit it for now.As I now own it I will check in again at a later date, for now it's a shame because some silly little things really let down what is otherwise shaping up to be a really good game and the early game experience is great, it's just very buggy and makes little sense later down the line. If they fixed the stone issue, game breaking UI and coal for heating I'd probably change my review to recommended, as if it worked then for the price it isn't bad value. I am reviewing this as an early access user but feel it's way less finished than most other early access titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I'm enjoying the game and will continue to play but so far it hasn't offered anything majorly unique to the genre to stand out. There are a few small differences as follows:-Ease of making money, usually you only really make money in games like this through trade/raid but in this game you can get a steady income from your market. (While in some games the market supplies a bit of coin  it's usually insufficient to actually do anything with or unreliable.) -Field placement, I enjoy that in this game you place field fences, stretch them out and join them up to form fields rather than the standard square/rectangle blocks.-Animal pen placement, when placing them you can stretch out the enclosure for smaller or larger size pens-House styles, there are three standard styles of house that cost the same resource wise but look different. It's nice to be able to choose the style of house I want to build instead of it being random or uniform.I haven't included personalities in this list since game play wise I haven't actually seen any way that personalities affect anything. I may be missing something so correct me if I'm wrong, but I really wanted to see a bit more social chaos going on based around different personalities since it is mentioned in the trailer. I also think that as a feature it would give this game the standout edge but without it, it's just a pretty viking themed addition to the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Land of the Vikings

_childDocuments_.review: I play all the colony sims.Land of the Vikings is gorgeous but there are a few things about it that are absolute deal killers for me.1) Forestry: you are discouraged from clearcutting because the trees grow faster and supply more wood if you don't kill the saplings, but wood is ALWAYS in short supply, you can't just set up some forester minions who are smart enough to chop the best trees, so you spend the ENTIRE game scanning the constantly for the biggest tallest trees. BORING, TEDIOUS.2) Deaths: you rarely notice when someone dies leaving your key industries unmanned so you are constantly having to monitor jobs to see if the number of gatherers dropped and you have to remember if you have 3 or 5 gather stations because you only see "5 gatherers" not 5/6 or 5/10, meaning you don't know how many employees short you are unless you are holding in memory a lot of information. That's fine if you started the game this morning, but if you come back to a game or get interrupted a lot this game becomes super tedious just tracking jobs are filled. Apparently there is a future tech that autofills jobs but ... "play longer so it gets less annoying" isn't a selling point.3) Gather/Hunting ranges: you have to plant your gather/hunt buildings out in the middle of nothing to get best coverage (a la banished), but once they are built you never know if your future actions are reducing their efficacy because clicking on them never shows you the range or percentage again. The games with moveable gather ranges are a better mechanic these days 4) Disasters: what stops a fire from burning down your village? Wells? Don't know. No tool tip mentions wells for anything but farming. Why does a thunderstorm last a month? Don't know, but it always destroys a bunch of homes and building is SO SLOW and wood is so slow that you've nearly always got pissed off homeless families.And so on.I want to enjoy this game but I cannot right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Land of the Vikings

_childDocuments_.review: This game is set to release in early October, but I definitely wouldn't buy it anytime soon. It's not ready. It's full of weird little errors, the mechanics and UI are clunky as hell, there's a lot of information you really need but don't get, the "events" are incredibly repetitive, half the time the wording is so bad you're left confused what's actually happening, even the basics aren't there- random capitalization, no consistency from panel to panel or objective to objective... This game needs another 6 months in EA.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm currently neutral on this game.  It has a lot of promise, but still plays like an Early Access game.  It's effectively Banished with vikings, which could be great, but just ins't polished enough yet to really be  engaging.  When you perform a basic action (like building a farm in a settlement game) and are given a giant warning pop-up that farms are still in the testing phase and may have serious issues then it's hard to believe this is a completed project.

_childDocuments_.review: overall recommend but with some things i didnt enjoy.Things I like:Graphics are pretty good! The world is nice looking and the sound and music is good too! Gameplay is easy to grasp if you ever played any of these types of games and things generally work together well. The events that happen with the villagers add some cool elements and choices to gameplay. Roads are great and glad its not a grid only game like other games.Things I do not like:-Trees get in the way and grow back a little too fast. If you want to build something where a tree was then you gotta do it immediately after cutting. need a way to clear an area and keep it clear.-Building anything is insanely slow. It's not fun and just frustrating. It's basically impossible to build everything you need before winter and feels like you're always playing catch up with the seasons.- I wish they would have more info when you click a building. For example, the hunting lodge has a productivity rating that you can see when you're building it, but if you cut down trees around it, that rating goes down but you cant see the rating anywhere after you build the hut. - TUTORIAL is not complete. They miss key things you need to build and you wont know that till things are going bad in your village.
_childDocuments_.name: Land of the Vikings

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, so early on and this game is simply addicting. If you like games like banished this is for you.[PROS]- True Sandbox Experience- Incredible amount of promise- Active community and developer team- Communicative development team- Many hours of challenging or casual gameplay both feeling rewarding- Excellent Art- Interesting quests and spontaneous events that make it much more engaging and immersive- TONS (And I mean TONS) to do. I have yet to have really any true idle time.[CONS] (Please note, this may not be relevant at the time of reading, please check post date).- Definitely early access, a lot of content coming but not there quite yet- Can become overwhelming when you reach a certain citizen limit, even on lower difficulty maps- Natural disasters are currently pretty horrendous, though they don't happen often, you can expect one every year at least with no way to combat it other than sitting through it.- Stone should be much more accessible and take less of a migratory effort to move your population toward a stone quarry- Animal Husbandry can be janky at times.- Lack of quality of life mechanics such as allowing the automatic filling of roles (refer to when I say it can get overwhelming)- Lack of life outside village, In Bannerlord they added cutscenes to depict certain events occuring. I think it would be nice to include some for trading and raiding to make it appear like it actually happened rather than just having a message saying it did.- Does not have an extensive tutorial.[WORTH NOTING]- The Soundtrack is excellent but repetitive. It would be excellent to be able to hear a wider variety of music, maybe seasonally 3 different songs on loop.- The ability to customize the houses more and create custom builds (sort of like in planet zoo) would take this game to a whole new level.- PETS THAT ARE USEFUL, so many games add useless pets, and while they do add to the life of the world, they miss all the potential in expanding their gameplay. Allow us to have dogs we can pair with our warriors to increase damage, or herders to increase yield, or hunters to increase efficiency. That would be sweet.- Terrain alteration would make this game worth twice what it is currently listed as ... I will only accept this as fact, not opinion.- Adding more into the religious side and populace interaction would make the game feel more alive. Let us host meetings, let us host rituals for new borns, let me log on and feel like a viking, not just a puppeteer, but rather, in the city, with the people.- Lack of customization in general- Gridless... but not COMPLETELY. I feel very restricted by the environment. Referring back to the terrain alteration suggestion, maybe even creating some sort of random map generation would be a good addition, making sure all of them are fairly mold-able.- No burial sites or rituals yet, your followers just poof away.[CONCLUSION]Is it worth the money? Yes.Do I recognize this game is early access and a lot of what I listed may be added anyways? Yes.Am I about to play this game right after typing this? Yes.Hope you got what you needed from this.

_childDocuments_.review: Viking City Builder.In the vein of Banished, but the failure deathcycle is a lot less easy to fall into.  It's got a really good amount of little touches that add up to a fairly unusual take on the genre.Decorations are pretty normal, but these have a wide variety of impacts on your town.  Shields and weapon racks add defensive strength.  Totems and banners make things purdy.  Lighting makes your people feel safer at night.  So forth and so on.  The default gameplay is gridless, which has its own issues, but most of those are easy to overcome.The farm fields are wonderfully customizable, as opposed to plain old squares, or painted areas, so common in these types of games.There are a LOT of minor changes that should be added, mostly UI and QOL, but since this is Early Access and the devs are wonderfully responsive... there's no reason to be negative about them (if they're there on full release I'll update this review).I started over 3 times as part of the learning process and I filled out the tech tree (Yggdrasil's trunk and branches) in about 15 hours in my last playthru, so it's DEFINITELY a "play a few times in EA then put it aside until next update (or possibly release)" in my book.  When comparing the early-game content w/ the late-game content, and the remaining branches on Yggdrasil, it's clear that they have a lot of content planned out.  Kudos.No crashes.Feels quite balanced.Plus... IT HAS A BUILDING EDITOR.All for 20 bucks US (i.e. low-tier indie price).IF it's your type of game... I highly recommend either watching a stream or two... or just buying it.I'm yonderyonder on twitch!

_childDocuments_.review: A very typical game of its type.  In fact it is the same as virtually everything like it but has less content.  After the 17 hours I spent on it I found nothing to do and I mainly strung it out to see what would happen. I initially thought, well it might not be out for a year so there is probably a lot more to come but then I read it is out in a week for general release.  That really surprised me as there is not much of a game here at all.  I should have got a refund while the option was still available. This becomes a theme as it is a weaker, less developed version of many other games like it in almost every respect. The UI and control system is pretty solid.  No odd mechanics but the way information is presented to give you feedback on the status of your town is not great.  You will spend much time just clicking buildings and adding a replacement for dead peasants.  Or, clicking fields to tell the to plant or harvest.  At the end of the game it feels like a repetitive mobile game and it is one of the weakest games of the genre I have played recently in terms of gameplay for this reason. Progression and technological unlocks is virtually the same as most other games but perhaps slightly less rewarding and it just feels a built underwhelming.Graphics - Runs fine, looks ok and you can zoom right in to the level of individual villagers and areas and it looks ok.  This does help a little with experience.Sound - Pretty good. Atmospheric sounds are well done.Overall a light version of many more accomplished city builder games.  It does a bit of what other games do but has less of everything.Trading - Ultimately feels like it was put in to tick a box.  Badly implemented.Technology Tree - Underwhelming and not very rewarding.Variety and depth of gameplay - Just not there.Maps - relatively small and pretty boring.  For example, you will see 1 place for a strone pit which must go in that one place and it is more or less the same for Iron and gold.Overall, the resources in general are limited and follows the same shallow theme.  A pretty poor effort.  Very shallow with little depth or longevity.   The least accomplished of all the many recent survival and town building games like it.  This is a mobile game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game for a few years. Land of the Vikings excels in its immersive portrayal of the Viking world. From the rugged landscapes to the authentic Norse mythology-inspired lore, the game transports players to a rich and engaging setting filled with adventure and exploration. The game offers deep role-playing elements that allow players to create and customize their own Viking characters. From choosing their appearance and skills to making impactful decisions that shape the story, players have a high level of agency in shaping their Viking saga. Land of the Vikings features a variety of epic quests and adventures for players to embark on. Whether it's raiding enemy settlements, exploring mysterious ruins, or engaging in epic battles against mythical creatures, the game offers a diverse range of exciting challenges to conquer. The game's world feels dynamic and alive, with various factions vying for power and influence. Players can interact with these factions, form alliances or rivalries, and influence the course of events through their actions, adding depth and re-playability to the experience. Land of the Vikings boasts stunning visuals that bring the Viking world to life in vivid detail. From lush forests to snowy mountains, the game's environments are beautifully rendered, immersing players in the rugged beauty of the Norse landscape. Despite its visual prowess, Land of the Vikings suffers from technical issues such as bugs, glitches, and performance issues. These issues can detract from the overall experience and lead to frustration for players, especially during intense combat or exploration sequences. The game has a steep learning curve, especially for players new to the role-playing genre. The sheer depth and complexity of the game's mechanics and systems can be overwhelming at times, requiring patience and persistence to fully grasp and master. While the game offers some degree of character customization, it is relatively limited compared to other role-playing games. Players may find themselves wishing for more options to personalize their Viking characters and make them truly unique. Despite its strong core gameplay and compelling setting, Land of the Vikings lacks the polish and refinement of other AAA titles. From awkward animations to clunky UI design, the game feels rough around the edges in certain areas, detracting from the overall immersion and enjoyment.Land of the Vikings is a standout title that excels in its immersive setting, deep role-playing elements, and epic quests and adventures. Its visually stunning presentation and dynamic world further elevate the experience, making it a must-play for fans of the Viking genre and role-playing games in general.However, the game is not without its flaws. Technical issues, a steep learning curve, and limited character customization may detract from the overall experience for some players. Despite these shortcomings, Land of the Vikings remains a highly enjoyable and engaging experience that earns it a solid rating of 7 out of 10.Thank you for taking the time to read my review.

_childDocuments_.review: A good solid basis for a game. There are absolutely things that need to change but there is enough here to make it a fun experience. It also just looks really pleasant. The sight of your village slowly expanding very organically against the mountain back drop is truly enjoyable.Now for the criticism. Most of this has to do with insane busy work.1: Logistics system. Currently warehouses are broken. Their stockpile is way too small and there is no way to move items around or to designate specific warehouses for specific goods. You can select warehouses to collect from specific production buildings but there is no way to set limits. So if you don't make warehouses for specific items they will fill up with a secondary item. Example: Warehouse for blacksmiths needs both coal and iron. Coal is also used for fuel for houses. Meaning Warehouse gets full of iron and accepts no more coal as coal is always depleting. You now need 2 warehouses instead of just limiting iron to 100 units max.2: Training of soldiers. Soldiers are trained in batches. You select X number of citizens to train as soldiers and then that batch is trained. You cannot cue another batch of soldiers until the first is finished. Soldiers can die in training. Soldiers can die whilst gathering their items to go on a raid before they even go on the raid. Soldiers can die on the way to the town to be raided. Soldiers die waiting for the previous batch of soldiers to finish training. This is stupid. Soldiers should be trained same way as other jobs. You set the upper limit of desired soldiers and the game auto-trains soldiers until they reach the maximum. Each soldier should get a training timer and this allows for WAY smoother recruitment.3: Maintenance and production of ships. Again you have to one by one build ships. There is no cue. There is no minimum number of a certain ship. Shipyards should have the ability to set a minimum numbers of ships so they automatically maintain for example 10 fishing boats and 6 drakar ships. It makes no sense for the player to CONSTANTLY have to order extra boats ONE by ONE!4: Jobs management. WHY IS AUTOMATIC JOB FULFILMENT AN UNLOCK!!! This is INSANE!!! 90% of the early game is just spamming the jobs roster so that all the people that die from old age get replaced! This should be done AUTOMATICALLY ALREADY!!!! This is stupid! This wastes so much time for NOTHING! And when you unlock automatic management you have to go through EACH AND EVERY building and turn it ON! WHY?! Do the exact opposite! Automatic management is unlocked from the start and you can turn it OFF! That's WAY better for the player instead of stupid tedious micro!5: Raids are pointless. 15 bread, 30 fruit, 20 leather and 30 silver? Are you serious? I raided Paris! I RAIDED PARIS! I got less money from raiding Paris than selling wool with my trade ship! I literally lost 20 soldiers! The cost to train these soldiers is 400 silver! Why would I EVER go on a raid?! It's completely useless as a mechanic because the investment is just a drain on resources with nothing but losses.6: I would like a map for trading and raiding. This is not a criticism of the game but something I think would give more flavor to the raiding and trading mechanic. Choosing which town to go to on a map, Looking at what is locally produced and sold. Can even make a mechanic where you can plot a raid/trade route on the map.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. It's too repetitive.  The only draw to this is the Viking flavour.  If you've played any other colony-building/town-management game, you've played this one.  Town creation is engaging enough, but the penalties for failure are absolutely unforgiving.  Every single thing contributes to citizen approval or dislike, and the negatives outweigh the positives.  If you get into a negative spiral, it's hard to recover.  The biggest drawback that I can't seem to overcome is homelessness.  As soon as a citizen indicates they are homeless, I build a few houses.  However, these are instantly populated, increasing the population but seemingly not providing a home to the homeless person.  If your villagers leave, you lose Fame and quickly lose the game.  People die, whether through war, natural causes, illness, or injury, but their houses remain occupied as long as there's one family member there, including even a single infant (this happened... baby living by itself).  On top of that you have incoming travelers or refugees or newcomers, whatever you want to call them.  If you reject them, you lose Fame, which is what drives your Tree of Life points that you need to improve your society/technology.  If you accept them, you need a lot more houses.  This would better benefit from some sort of prompt to build that specific homeless person a home, and lock it to that individual and their family, if any.  Having some sort of barracks for unmarried troops would be a decent idea as well, to help handle housing issues.  The other issue with housing is that there's only so much space on a map.  Having 500 houses for 500 citizens/families occupies a massive chunk of real estate.  Combat in this game is relegated to what amounts to choose-your-own-adventure cards, where you get a series of cards presenting an option (recon, wait, go in at night) and a chance for success. Press a button, random number gods decide if you succeed or fail.  I don't believe the percentages, either--I've had 35% chance of success be wildly successful, and 89% chance of success fail miserably.  That is how combat goes, you don't manage the fighting any other way unlike other RPG/RTS titles.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re someone who loves survival colony sim games like City Skylines or just management games similar to RimWorld, you will love Land of Vikings. Put yourself in a leadership position in a village where you will manage resources, survive harsh conditions, and guide your villagers to work together through conflict.I really enjoyed playing , the graphics are absolutely beautiful, and there are little to no graphics or frame rate issues. You will easily lose track of time, and you will become addicted in a heartbeat if you like this style/genre of game. The soundtrack and ambiance sounds are excellent and very fitting to the environment, but I feel like after 10 hours of playing, it will start to feel repetitive hearing the same songs on loop.With the developers' current progress,  has a lot of potential. The community and development team are very active and excellent at communicating what they are working on, which is a huge plus in today's games. There is always something to do in Land of Vikings; you won’t have a lot of moments where you have nothing to do. They implemented a skill tree called "Tree of Life," with ‘buffs’ for different jobs and unlockable buildings, i.e., mills, farms, taverns, tailors, blacksmiths, etc. You earn perk points by completing these objectives that will be given to you while you play. They’re kind of like quests or goals in a way. You will be given ‘fame’ in exchange for completing objectives. Fame will be converted into tech points for this skill tree.Throughout the game, you must prepare for the fierce and harsh winter and some more terrifying events. With some events, such as thunderstorms, the player cannot do much to mitigate the damage that they will cause to some homes. So you’re kind of stuck waiting there until it’s over. You also can’t speed up time during these weather events. It kind of just feels like you’re helpless the whole time during these severe weather events. I wish you could do things to help combat it, like maybe strengthening the homes with timber!You are able to raid foreign villages for goods and gold, but I never got this far in my current playthrough. You can also decorate your village to your heart's content. There aren’t *too* many decorative items, but I’m sure they are adding more as time goes on. I do wish there were more than two types of homes— but again, I’m sure they will add more in the future. There are currently three types of "poor homes" and two types of "good homes." But the developers have stated that you will be able to modify the look of houses in the future! So, that is some exciting news!There are some things that I would love to see added, and these are: the option to choose who your villagers will marry, and a burial site or some sort of mourning site for when villagers die. I want to know who died, instead of my villagers just poofing away :(In conclusion, Land of Vikings is pretty fun, and I would say that it is worth the price for all the content that it has to offer and it still being in early access. The community and developers being assiduous make the game look more attractive, in my opinion. There are so many developers that just release a game, drop development, and don’t really do many updates after release. This is not one of those games. You will heavily enjoy this game, and I suggest you give it a chance!Rating: 8/10

Yes there are occacional blessings of the gods, but they are so minute that you never really notice them making any impact.The lack of early "Replace worker automatically" is a royal pain in your rear and at the point where you finally get it, you have been micromanaging so much that even people who usually like it are fed up. Not to mention that the ones you sign up regularly seem to vanish and in case of one worker buildings, like the chicken farm you suddenly have random shortagesWhat could be done to improve this game?Early access to automatic worker replacement. The current one should be "Replace with workers that have at least X in this skill" unless going straight to the second option is preferred.More information: How much bonus do I actually get for "luck 2.5" and so on. Or if it's in the game I have yet to stumble over it. What do different things do? Do the gods hate me or not? Does it make sense to build street type decoration outside of house areas and so on.More events. MUCH more events. Currently they are so repetitive it's frustrating to have them at all.Some type of priest type+ location. You should have a rough idea if the gods like or hate you, More boons and curses depending on how much you praise or ignore specific ones. And if you think "We don't wanna make the religion too unrealistic... think about how many earthquakes there are in Scandinavia... or repetitive freak lightning strikes.Tl;Dr :The game is enjoyable, but it still has many issues that would be more forgivable if it was still early access and not a 1.0 release

_childDocuments_.review: This game is half cooked, even for the price, I would not recommend a purchase. This should not have left beta. The game has potential, so I will check back, but it is not ready for release.Note: while this review shows 42.6 hours of gameplay, it is more like 30. I left the game running on the title screen overnight and into the next day once.Good Things:- chill- looks decent- fun concept- potentialBad Things:- bug city-- quests disappear-- major pathing issues-- lighting issues-- decorations you cannot delete-- roads can be built for free-- engine crashes-- game caused my entire PC to crash twice (I cannot remember the last time this happened)- many concepts are not fleshed out-- example, you can decorate houses to increase villager happiness, which is cool for the first dozen houses, but when you need to decorate 200+ houses... not so much.-- example, there are like 5 events in the game and you get them over and over, I have had enough of the guy that lost his knife and blames the newcomer for stealing it- many concepts not explained-- example, there are signs you can put down that "increase villager movement speed", but the bonus is not explained in terms of range nor amount nor whether they stack, -- example, in the combat section, odds are given for the actions you can take and odds of success are given, however, it is not explained why the odds are what they are, and I also believe they are wrong after loosing 3, 90% chance events in a row [1 in 1000 odds])-- example, you can make "iron tools" that just disappear after you make them (assume equipped to a villager) but there is no way to see what they do, who has them, or what percent of villagers have them. Same is true for clothing, winter cloths just seem to disappear, whilst the improved clothing can be seen on the villager.- shallow-- the progress you make in this game is done in the first year or two of the game, then all you do is build houses, and more of the existing buildings. -- there is little in terms of improving the villager work flow nor making complicated work flows. The most complicated thing you make takes 3 ingredients, and the most complicated chain of crafting is 3 deep (raw ingredients, armor, soldier)-- there is no way to micromanage villagers to improve efficiency, for example, while there might be a wood storage and firewood station right beside a house, a villager will walk to the other side of the map to get existing firewood, or villagers will start taking coal to heat their homes while you want to use it for crafting armor/weapons-- no strategic purpose to defensive buildings as they just increase a number that is your defence (battles are just dice rolls on a screen you interact with)- disasters can be extremely punishing but at the same time are very boring-- I had an earthquake break the warehouse where I stored my weapons and armor as well as my warehouse that stores what I mined... basically all my progress-- there seem to only be two disasters, rain and earthquakes. The former is just wind noise, and the later is just your screen shaking. All they do is break your buildings.- beautifying your city (which seems to be the core of this game) is a chore-- placing a house forgets the rotation between placements making it difficult to build large numbers of houses aligned together-- once placed, some decorations cannot be deleted-- you cannot have a road become the same size as an existing road-- roads do not remember the size of the last placed road-- there aren't really a lot of decorations or house types/styles (5)-- there are only like 8 maps to play onOverall.Originally, I was going to say, this game is fine for the price, and you get decent entertainment value, even with the shallow game play. I stopped playing though when my town that took about 20 hours of game play to build, was completely crippled as all my villagers ran into a path finding issue and all got stuck on a cliff. This kind of ruined the last hope I had for this game. Up until this point I was thinking that the game, though shallow, was worth the money. This bug killed that as it left me feeling my time spent playing this game was wasted, and I do not want to play again (because of the shallow game play).Overall, with the shallow game play, the lack of micromanagement, and then game breaking bugs, I felt frustrated with my time on this game. There is potential here, but it isn't done. This game needs to cook. Right now it feels like a demo or a minimum viable product then a complete game. It should have not left beta.

_childDocuments_.review: Some good basics here, acceptable graphics; all in all not bad.   But does this have anything over, say, Banished?  Besides the viking theme, I would have to say...no.    The concept of having each villager have their own strengths and weaknesses is intriguing, a la games like Rimworld, but  ultimately the execution fails to deliver on that.  The only real result is that there is extra micromanagement needed to play the game, and few convenient or intuitive ways to get an overview of what job assignments were recently vacated by deceased workers.   This level of micromanagement seems to be something the developers actually *wanted* when building the game.  There is an option, in the game settings, to enable a mechanic allowing a very limited auto-assigment feature for labor.  As far as I can see, it only works for farms.  And the setting is off by default.   Enabling it grants you an achievement, called "Lazy".   There are other areas of *completely* unecessary micromanagement as well; such as fields; not only do you have to click a "plant" button before they start planting the crop, you also need to keep an eye on it and hit a *harvest* button later on, before the crops rot in the fields.   What an exciting, engaging, and thrilling gameplay feature!   This is one of several ways that the mechanics of the game really fail to respect the player's time, with no really good gameplay justification other than "we needed some way for the player to keep busy while things happen".   Ultimately a conept that was worth exploring.  In practice, it does not seem to pan out in execution.  It falls flat, you don't really feel any connection to your people.  Their lives are much too short for that.   I see a few very similar games like this on the horizon that will be released on steam;  I'm hoping one of those scratches the viking-themed city builder itch; because I really don't think this one is it.

_childDocuments_.review: What a chill and fun game.  I loved Banished and similar games and this is very much a game in the same vein except with a good deal of graphical improvements over most of them.   The game ran flawless on my i5-7400 @ 3Ghz, with 16GB of RAM, running on SSD, with a 1060 GTX 3GB Video card.  I did not see any graphical bugs nor did I have any crashes to desktop or any other bugs to speak of.   I do not usually play with in game music so I can't rate it.I give the graphics a good 8/10The AI seems pretty strong, I didn't notice any crazy pathing issues but to be honest I only spent a little over an hour so far so I wasn't paying a lot of close detail.The learning curve is very easy, the tutorial is very helpful, but if you have played a similar game you should be able to quickly figure things out.I will come back after I have spent more time with the game and give a more detailed review, but I highly recommend the game for the asking price.  I so far only played far enough to start building the shipyards.  I have had a nice influx of population, and I like how the game throws you moral issues to work around, such as someone has something stolen, do you instantly believe one of the original villagers, or a newcomer, or do you investigate deeper sort of thing.  It's a nice add to the game that while isn't required, give the game a nice, living world feel.Over all while it is still in Early Access I believe the game is worth the asking price and am very hopeful that the developers continue to put out a good number of updates and have a clear goal set in mind.   As is now I highly recommend the game if you aren't afraid of early access titles.  Luckily the game has a low price tag which goes a long way to help make the easy of deciding that much more easy in my mind.

_childDocuments_.review: As a released game, Land of the Vikings totally sucks. This game is acceptable for Early Access, but not at all close to what would be considered released. _childDocuments_.review: Well, it's a bit like every other city builder, with some twists. That is, you need fame to be able to progress through the science tree (the Tree of Life), which comes from what you do and how big your settlement is. Also your people age, not sure if one year per day or 10 per season, but somewhere there. That means your freshly trained warriors are dead about two years later, which is certainly annoying. Then there's disasters, PLENTY of them. Every year there'll be a thunderstorm, crashing some of your buildings, and an earthquake (same), and diseased animals, which kills off around 10-30% of your lifestock. Lateron there'll be raids too, and no matter how many warriors you have, it never seems enough to completely fend off those raiders. Oh, you may build palisades, archer towers and so on on strategically important points, moving your more valuable buildings behind walls of defenses - don't bother. Raids burn down random buildings in your village, like all other disasters, and kill off quite some warriors and citizens. Oh, you won? Well, you lost some ressources either way, tough luck. It almost seems like the devs want to make your life miserable. Speaking of miserable - there's quite some bugs. Now every family has one house, where father and mother are the heads thereof. If one dies, it seems like the remainder might just marry anew. Can't really say, because the devs don't follow norse naming schemes, so Ragnar Odinsson and Freja Thorsdottir have randomly named kids like Thorin Admusson, Fjala Pertodottir etc. What's worse is when both parents die in quick succession, rendering the house occupied only by gravestones and thus will never be inherited by anyone, not even their children. You can't evict them, so destroy and rebuild is your only option. Rebuilding - or building in quick succession, is achieved like with every other game, pressing SHIFT, but after you've painstakingly rotated the house to your liking and want to place a second exactly next to it - tough luck, the rotation gets reset - every - single - friggin - time. Some items you research also don't do any good, at least not after saving and reloading (like "Granaries have 10% more storage space"), quests don't count properly sometimes, parts of the map cant host buildings (or fields, which you only find out after placing them and having your farmers stop tending to it at some point, glitching about). Goat ranches have some collision issues, sometimes builders get stuck in a loop not reaching the construction site, being teleported back to the main house and then go straight to their beloved construction site again, ignoring buildings/roads etc. just to be teleported back again until death or destruction of said site does them part. Furthermore with a bigger settlement problems pile up: People complain about being patients (when being ill), but are not cured by the healer buildings any more, complain about cold homes despite having a stocked firewood storage/woodcutter nearby, the automatic people replacement sometimes just kicks people from slots for unknown reasons (despite them living 30 m away and being the best on the job for miles). Oh, and I've had 100 people vanish into thin air in one reload at some point, and don't know why. Sooo, prepare for bugs, but then, it's EA. Visual glitches also sometimes occur (e.g. figurines on customized drakkars displaced).Why do I recommend after I roasted almost every bug until it was charcoal? Because I like those games, hope the errors get fixed and that at some point thoughtful walls and archer towers actually make sense, because I really hate to have my storages with important goods just burned down despite them being in a safe zone behind three walls.So, if you're able to work around all this, and like a game that oftentimes just tries to annoy the living s**t out of you, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Land Of The Vikings is for me one of the better medieval colony simulators as it isn't heavily obsessed on one survival aspect like a lot of other similar games are, as well as having more to it than "what you see is all that happens".Sadly the game doesn't have enough gimmicks or enough depth to them to keep things interesting.In my opinion, the best system is the sea warfrare aka raiding as it brings another element to the survival aspect But with raids only being a statistics page on how battles went, the entire excitement buildt up through preperation dissapears with a big dissapointment instead of something that should have be a great climax.The game has a lot of potential for an early access title... of which it's not.This is an unfinished game that needs at least another year of development which it's luckily getting, but unluckily the biggest roadmap development of the last 6 months (Thralls) was released as a paid dlc while making the players think it would be a part of the full game.The thrall system is a much needed update to the game as it expands upon multiple areas including ocean warfare and more late-game content. But as a paid dlc, it shows how the devs doesn't care about the community, and the future of the game which is clearly dead outside of paid dlcs. Unless the devs changes their minds (which probably won't happen) you should stay away from this game unless it's at least 50% off and you're fine with bugs, missing content and no future content.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game.  What's there not to like when it's a settlement management simulator with a Viking theme?  I mean, the whole concept is BAD@$$.....but falls short, in my opinion.LotV has your typical settlement management.  Cut down trees to make logs, have carpenters make planks for you.  Mine stone, grow crops like wheat and barley, hunt for game, forage for berries, build docks and boats for fishing.  Get ores from mines.  Pretty simple.But in all this is some really questionable game design by the developer(s).  Aside from setting aside builders that do the work for putting up yoru structures, days are REALLY short in-game.  I don't know what the span is, but it seems like you have 5 minutes to do stuff when the sun is out, and another 5 minutes when it's dark.  Yes, you can build at night, but MAN.  It can take in-game days to put buildings up.  And they consume a LOT of resources just to put up.  Like you might need 20 logs 10 planks and 30 stone for something.  NPCs carry stuff to your build site, but they drudge along, drop stuff off to the site, then go off to do some other task.Trees grow back in time, but at some point you'd better consider getting some mines set up to get stone, because you're gonna mine all the stone around you pretty quickly.  That is, if you are willing to spend a game week or more waiting for your NPCs to haul stuff to the construction site.It gets old.  Fast.And you'd better build your basic structures before your first winter.  You'll need firewood building up so your people won't freeze by then.  You should have already a hang of how slow your people are in building, but you should have some extra houses up to house new settlers if you choose to take them in, or to make room for families that grow and have children.  You should have several food types by your first winter, but if you don't, you'll see the devastation wrought by the incompetence or work overload of your NPCs as they struggle bringing resources bit by bit to your construction sites.There is a cool tech tree, LITERALLY a tree.  You have a small handful of points that you can put into the main branch (or is it trunk?) that gives you various buildings, or side branches that may increase worker speed or like 1% extra villager happiness.The colors in this game are....bland IMO.  Nothing really to wow at.  It's dull, all of it.  Or maybe I'm jaded.IN SHORT, I DO NOT RECOMMEND this game, not at this time.  I'd give it about a year for the developers to patch it because the day-night cycle is too short.  It takes too many resources to build structures, takes too long to build.  I find it more unpleasant and unplayable in this current state, but don't take my word for it.  I think there's a demo.  Try it for yourself, or go for broke and get the game.  You might do better than I did, and maybe your game is more up to date with patches than mine is.  I've uninstalled mine and probably won't look back after awhile.  No, I'm NOT butthurt, I do like this game.  Just not enough to be investing my time in it so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Best way to describe this game is a Banished survival city builder in a viking theme.  So far I'm greatly enjoying it as it scratches that certain viking itch.Pros:  Graphics are very nice.  Background environments capture the era.  Winter effect is nice as you can see when it starts snowing, the snow will slowly build up and create mounds.  Decent size research tech tree to progress through and unlock more things to build.  Trading and military missions are in the game.  Random events keep things interesting.  Much slower gameplay than in other similar games.  Have not run into any game-breaking bugs yet.  Some minor glitches here and there.  Managing population is key.Cons:  Micromanagement hell during late stages of the game.  Micromanaging all the tasks such as cutting trees, planting and harvesting farms, slaughtering livestock, assigning workers to replace the ones that passed on.  Natural disasters like earthquakes and lightning storms destroying too much stuff.  It feels like you forgot to sacrifice something to Odin and now he mad.All in all, I think the game is on a solid foundation and plays very well.  I'm hoping for some automation in the future update to lower the amount of micromanagement and give us ability to scale down the natural disasters.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend the game, but with reservations.I hadn't played a construction/colony sim game in years and wanted to try a recent title. I love this type of strategy. As a game for beginners or returning players to this genre, the game is decent. The atmosphere is nice, it's not off-puttingly difficult, there's some variety in the gameplay, but that's about it for the pros.The cons are that it's too monotonous overall. The repetition with the bickering between the villagers, the mysterious plant discovered, the annoying natural disasters and the raids are just one after another from one point in the game onwards. Trade is boring, it takes 10 hours or less to build all the buildings and it becomes tedious to maintain every house that collapses from lightning, earthquake or fire. Speaking of houses... There's a bug where a family that moves into a house has children, the old generation dies, and the new generation doesn't create another generation because... they live in their dead parents' house! So the player has to expand non-stop, building new and new houses to have some younger generation, but his village is doomed to age anyway, and with that the maintenance of social functions becomes tedious and almost impossible. At some point from now on you will spend more time recruiting younger people into the jobs of dead old ones and building new homes... nice, heh?I would recommend that the price for this game be lowered because there is too much to finish on it and let any prospective buyer read some reviews before giving their money for 10 hours of gameplay that ends in nothing because the player is bored and sees no point in continuing...
