_childDocuments_.review: As far as city builders go, LotV is not a bad one. The lack of a traditional grid makes it a refreshing change of pace, requiring the player to be creative when laying out their houses/industries. Interestingly, the usage of decorations also has a gameplay impact, aside from being eye candy. For example, placing decorative carts or crates next to Warehouses or Markets increases their storage capacity. Or placing shields, etc boosts the settlement's defences. It's not a game mechanic I've encountered in other games.On the flip side, LotV is perhaps not as fleshed out as it can be. The lack of a map editor (as of this review's writing) is the biggest drawback for a city-builder, although the developer Laps Games should be credited for allowing players to make their own custom structures & decorations. Likewise, when playing Immersive Mode, the frequency of disasters which destroy your structures is perhaps a bit overenthusiastic. It makes having to rebuild a chore more than anything.So, as a typical game of its genre, LotV is not bad. Not something I'd get at full price, but if it's on sale, then why not? I suppose I got my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good Banished clone. At the time of this review, I only played for 3 years and reached 600 populations; but except for a single crash, I found the game to be in reasonably good shape. All resources are sustainable (i.e. endless), although getting stone pit and mines can be tricky once nearby stone deposits are used up / replaced by housing depending on your map selection. The food production is A LOT easier than Banished, i.e. starvation is highly unlikely. But it has the same issue as Banished as in that if you stop growing, then your city is starting to die. It is like riding a bicycle, not so easy when you try to balance the death of your elder citizens with the birth of newborn babies unless you keep building new houses ad infinitum (limited by your map size and your computer ability to simulate thousands of citizens).The plus side is the Viking raids (both defending against raids and sending missions to raid), the setting (which is quite popular for those who likes the Viking TV shows), making a hundred Freya idol stones so your people keep breeding like rabbits etc. It has its own Viking charm and it is very beautifully rendered.But in the end, like Banished, it is a "survival" city builder - so it attracts certain kind of people who likes to play around with the supply chain and the replayability is quite limited. Anyway, we are  not short on good banished clone and this is certainly one of the good ones.

But what does that mean? Do they move faster if they are within a certain range of one of these decorations? Do they apply a movement speed buff, which lasts for some time, when you get close? And/or is the default pathfinding poor per design so that it can be improved with these?I do not know the answer to any of these questions.

_childDocuments_.review: After 9 years in the game and 100% achievement completion, figured it was time to write a review.TLDR: This game is not perfect, but I enjoyed it. Worth the money for the time spent (I got it on a sale).Pros: Lots of decorations! You can create a beautiful village, and it really feels alive and interactive. I enjoyed the production chain and city management aspects. You can speed up time (and will) as needed, but still enjoy a slow pace if you wish. Feels like a sweet spot of grinding/building.Cons: I had to turn disasters off. Some people might count this a pro, but the constant RNG of buildings getting destroyed annoyed the crap out of me.  Thank god we can turn them off.INFORMATION: the biggest con, there is so little to no info!! I had to learn what some buildings did by pure experimentation, and you have NO idea what bonus amount decorations give other than storage numbers. I could list a hundred different things and they all come down to simple lack of information.The research tree takes nearly 10 years to fully unlock, and you HAVE to go into raids/war in order to get the fame... and thats with ZERO of the 'relics' (which I found around year 8 lol didnt even know they were there). It takes so long that it feels useless to go for, simply unlock major buildings and forget it. Youll never really get to enjoy fully unlocked trading and war both and still go for auto-employ feature, you got to choose one of the three... and you better pick war, because its the only qood way to get more fame! #rantoverInfo for people interested: You can do all achievements on one map/playthrough, they are all very simple and easy. It took me 12 hours to get a city to 9 years, but i didnt have time sped up all the time and i spent a lot decorating/designing for fun. As for replayability? I hope they add more content, otherwise I cant see myself doing more than the occasional city. There are a limited amount of maps and once youve done them once, it feels 'over' for me, you know where everything is and they will always be the same place. Raiding is just a mini-game, not actual fighting, same for invasions, so walls/towers etc feel useless and pure numbers-game not strategy.

_childDocuments_.review: Tries to be everything, fails to be anything.Trailers looked great, but there is a very obvious lack of polish. From the settings using default buttons & font to the music being louder in the intro than the speaker, even at 70% music volume. The camera is a giant cube in the sky; they made sure to turn off the shadow for it but not the reflection in the water. The wood chop and stone cut SFX is the same single sound repeatedly spammed, rotate is on Z for whatever reason, buildings show multiple entry points but roads can only connect to a single one, automatic road generation is annoying, manual road generation is annoying, your screen is littered with icons, by default your camera pans and zooms to everything you click on(seriously why?), decorations cost silver and can just be spammed anywhere instantly? The environment is bland and uninspiring; especially the starting area.The intro dialogue & "story" is laughable, as if written by a highschooler; just stupid lazy and generic. Some weird old guy has a giant popup that tells you all these corny things "youre the youngest and strongest and have to lead us!" ok dude im just a floating cube camera. With proper direction and polish this game could be promising, the trailers certainly make it seem so but instead its just another misleading throwaway colony sim that fails to hit every mark and was most certainly released too early.

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoy the game and the direction it could be going in its early access state. Its simplistic approach is helpful to having fun and the random story elements add a level of liveliness to make it feel like your actually managing a Viking Village. There are currently some game play aspects and engine upgrades needed such as map scrolling speed, an immediate attention alert and perhaps a noob friendly map that gives a much more in depth description of certain aspects such as military and food management for seasonal changes. Its rather good as a city builder and I look forward to its development further. Keep up the good work.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 17 hours into the game, and its been a lot of fun - especially considering the price. Pros and Cons list to follow:***Note:  The Cons list may seem long, but this game has a TON of potential - its already incredibly fun, as is...  It can just be better.  I'm really just listing some of my negative observations (along w/ suggestions) in the cons section.Pros:  1) its about vikings; 2) beautiful graphics 3) runs smoothly (for the most part); 4) a lot of promise w/ raiding and trading (I'll explain further in the cons section); 5) a good amount of building diversity, considering its still in early stages; 6) keeps you on your toes (village raids, natural disasters, etc.); 7) the editor is an AWESOME and easy to use tool; 7) game play is easy to learn and very intuitiveCons / Suggestions:  1) the game has crashed and frozen up on me a few times - fortunately, it auto saves often; 2) needs more content - @ 17 hours in, I feel like I've already done every single thing the game has to offer (at least as of 04.24.2023); 3) very little return on investment for raiding / trading - really isn't worth it, unless role playing; 4) needs more troop / building / ship diversity, as the game ages; 5) disappointing that there is zero troop interaction at the moment - I want to fight some battles, not be told if I won or lost after choosing from a small list of attack strategies... 6) the same events (w/ different character names) happen over, and over, and over, and over, and over; 7) wish there was more control / knowledge of what the Gods are feeling about you - would also like to see more scenarios that can piss the Gods off or make them happy; 8) while extremely fun, the game just needs more content, diversity (buildings, troops, events, disasters, etc.), and control / interaction (mainly over troops)Overall, the devs are on the right path.  Tons of potential here, and well worth it - especially, for the price.  Thanks!Grant

_childDocuments_.review: This is playable game and there are a lot of objectives to achieve including population growth and building. The weather patterns and landscape are nice. The structures are realistic and have lots of good detail. I have to say it does need a lot of fine tuning and detailing. Some of the choices seem to have little to no consequence. For example, the same civilian issues always pop up with the same two or three options. Smaller issues do occur including the occasional bug  such as civilians disappearing while dropping off supplies, and other common glitches - for example production equipment not producing enough processed goods despite overwhelming raw resources. Some features seem to only slow down the game including the fame point system. Ultimately it's not a difficult game to figure out once you know the rules but there are lot of features that seem out of date such as the fact that you have to read through the entire raid and battle sequences. The growth of the town is very satisfying to see, and the passage of time helps to ground your development throughout. The next updates could be more detailed oriented in getting rid of the more awkward bugs and ai issues. Overall it could use a some TLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly sad to not recommend this game, as I do enjoy a lot of elements of it. The houses, the setting, the battles... but there's just not enough game to make it interesting. Tree management is not great, so you're constantly struggling for lumber. Aside from that, limited mine space makes it impossible to keep up with demands with no upgrades .The main issue, though, is once you reach a certain point, you're just sitting and waiting on high speed to earn points to unlock new things, and occasionally tossing in new houses as the population continues to grow. I play farrrrrr too many city builders and colony Sims and all of them have end game grind issues, but this one really provided nothing to look forward to aside from winning harder raids, but even then, what's the point when you already have all resources anyway? I would love to see it grow and evolve to have more content, more to do, better menus for management, but seeing as there's DLC already (that shows in the base game but just isn't usable if you didn't pay for it - I hate that), I highly doubt the core game will get much more love. Disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Although available in early access, Land of the Vikings already provides a glimpse of what could become a standard-setting game for the Viking city-builder genre. The attention to detail in the generated maps, the terrain, the landscaping, the climate, and the audio effects are clearly differentiating and soothing to see and hear and can become immersive. There is tremendous potential for further development on the themes of farming, trading, raiding, and exploration that could set this game apart as the player traverses the "Tree of Life" and settlement survival and growth challenges even though some basics are available now. I look forward to seeing where the developers take this as the game matures. While not without, nor expected to be without, content gaps and balancing issues as an early release product, one can only imagine what could ultimately be created and the totality of the immersive experience that is possible with that vision in mind to truly become something special.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sneaked up on me.   Like a Viking, silently raiding my house.  I thought at first it was too basic.  That the supply chains weren't fully fleshed out.  But as the game progressed, I began to see the beauty of it.  Logistics issues became real.  Placement of buildings became important.   The good stuff in village simulation games.  Now, there's still some issues.  Manually hiring villagers to replace each person that dies can become pretty tiring toward the end of the game.  There's an option to have the game do this automatically, but you have to research it, and it's way down a tree that you may not get to for a while... and it's expensive to get there.  Oh, and please modify the villagers stats as they age.  When I search for my faster villager, it's concerning that my faster runner in my villager is 89 years old.But most other items are pretty minor in the game.  Overall, it's a good value, especially on sale.  I'd expect to get 100 or more hours out of it.  It doesn't have the depth of Farthest Frontier yet, but it has some more interesting combat systems and is really fun to play.I've only been raided twice.  The first was like 8 guys and a bucket.  The second time was nearly 10 years later, and I was lucky to survive.  Quite the ramp up.

_childDocuments_.review: As a passionate building strategist, I have to say that this game is really not well thought out, it feels like half of it is missing - balancing of resources is questionable (iron, coal and stone), resource management is practically non-existent, the only food storage is the marketplace, but here only resources from nearby are collected, if there is a closer marketplace to the resource that is full, production is simply stopped because the goods are not picked up. Visually, it is not THE EXPERIENCE par excellence. The weather events shoot away random buildings - either by lightning or because the earth is shaking, which is NOT the highlight I've always been waiting for in building games. The "events" such as disagreements between the Viking families are super repetitive and the constant killing of traitors doesn't really have any impact on the game. Good idea but the implementation is not successful. It's a shame, the Viking setting would be interesting, but it all seems a bit ill-conceived and like it's still in alpha/beta status.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 10 hours in and having a ton of fun with this so far. It's on a much larger scale than most colony sims like Rimworld or Going Medieval, so it leans more into the City-Builder genre, but still has the fundamentals of a colony sim such as villager skills/stats and jobs/task delegation. And since it's on such a larger scale population wise, there's isn't as much customization in regards to building. Building without a grid is fun so far, because it helps you create unique and organically shaped towns. It's possible I have a bias for Viking themed games, but so far, this is a game I can see myself putting a lot of hours into.

_childDocuments_.review: Land of the Vikings is visually appealing, atmospheric, and has great respect for the culture being represented, but lacks key gameplay mechanics and quality of life features that will neuter your enjoyment of it.Micromanagement and random events cripple the game's already slow progression. Resource harvesting must be manually queued, and no automatic harvesting of wood is ever available, even via the game's limited tech tree, despite it being easily the most important, and trees that you don't manually harvest will block the construction of buildings. The tech tree itself is dependent on "fame," which is earned through a combination of population and random events, which feels very arbitrary and contrived, especially since many of the random events also lose fame, sometimes because you're missing a key tech. Villagers holding a job who die must be manually replaced, and the game only bothers to tell you this if the building is empty, so you will frequently have buildings working at half or less efficiency because of missing people. Automatic villager replacement can be unlocked, but is at the very top of the tech tree, branched away from critical techs like military and trade. Storage buildings are laughably small and the only means of increasing their size is via spamming decorations, which cost money earned exclusively through the sale of food, which again feels very arbitrary and contrived.Ultimately this is a game that frequently gets in its own way and will prevent you from enjoying it in spite of itself. There is nothing in this game that hasn't been done better by multiple other colony sims over the last 10 years.

_childDocuments_.review: Land of the Vikings 100% steam achievement 27/05/2023 Solid choice for its genre but so clearly in early access as there isnt really any sort of goal currently. Objectives and events are limited and repetitive, prone to bugs and become uninteresting fast. The embedded feedback is really good and easy to use however so there should be ample feedback coming in. To start I like the use of mythology and norse words throughout and the tree progession is nicely thought out and well timed so its always something you want to strive towards. There are still issues with placing fields, deleting farms and making roads connect in construction stages but none of the bugs are game altering; just immersion breaking. I ended up turning the disasters off for my second playthrough as I couldnt handle playing on 1x speed just waiting for the disaster to end. I also wish there was a way of mitigating the losses for things such as fire - have a well close by or something? It took a while to work out what was actually happening with the fire too. I feel like it needs a notification or side bar alert like you get with winter. Trading is frustrating because its not guaranteed to sell everything making the trip not worthwhile and it isnt clear what effect having different crew amounts makes. I dont see the point in raiding at all. The amount of input vs the return is unbalanced also I can produce everything I need, including enough fame, within my own city. Even if its a city you attack it states you won/lost to a village. There's a grammar issue in english for when you earn money through trading/raiding. I enjoyed working through the steam achievements and there's scope for more easily. I do however want an easy way of finding out just how many places I had explored and further clarification on what explored actually means (just discovered, or newly discovered from exploration?) Also the military overview showing how many of each unit doesnt keep up when you have a lot of different unit types in training and a little box to show the total military size would be beneficial. My absolute grump is with the decoration. Now compared to other games I really enjoy the free and unlimited placement with no fighting to make something fit. I do however resent needed to place an endless amount of flags all over the same place just to make people happy. It's not really decoration when it's ugly and you only really need to use the same thing. It was just flags, archery targets, training dummies and weapon racks x1000. Also it was unclear where light needed to be and i seemed to place the lanterns everywhere and couldnt get rid of 'the village is too dark at night.' Also, I want vegetables already. Whilst I have focused on bugs and areas of improvement for this game it does have the basis to be very strong for the genre if feedback is taken into account and the game continues to expand and be developed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remake of Banished with different theme? The overal feeling of the game is a bit flawed and amateurish. The viking architecture is cartoon-like, the assets are modeled by people who don't have much knowledge of either vikings or buildings, which isn't a great combination. The ocean sounds like someone is pouring water from a hose. That's not what ocean sounds like. The scale issues are present, the nature would've been very cool to actually look like some viking area'ish nature. Now it looks like just Unreal Engine game with generic assets. This adds to the feeling of it being amateurish.The tutorial helps a lot to realize what's going on, but as a player you kind of don't FEEL the problems and the issues and the situation. It's hard to describe. Also something that is hard: it's hard to imagine people play this with normal speed? Like it's so slow? Then you have to accelerate it, and then it's really fast, and there's sort of nothing in between; in fast acceleration, the little atmosphericity the game had, disappears, and you grow even more distance to your village - which is also an issue; I kind of have to stay zoomed out all the time to see the entire settlement, but all you hear up there is wind. If you  come closer, you start to hear the village sounds, which is ok, but you're so zoomed in that it makes no sense. Forest disappear and reappear really fast. The sound world is a bit weird, if you've accelerated the game speed at all, the hacking sounds of mining stones and wood is like rattatatatatatata if you accidentally have your camera over the sites.Idk, I kind of expected something more pictoresque, atmospheric, chill vibes, but the cartoonish style and bad nature assets and the ocean that sounds like someone opened a water tap, just doesn't work for me. What are those mountains even. Gosh.Not gonna refund it, that's not my style - but I'll play it every now and then when I'm bored!

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment, I just can't recommend... I'm a huge city builder/colony sim player and I'm just not sure where this game fits in. There's a lot of immersion missing from resource collection/stockpiling. For instance, you tell a villager to chop a tree, it falls and a few seconds later, you see your wood count go up... Then there's QoL features that get put behind research... not very far but why? The free build is nice but in comparison to other games that have it, its missing a lot of features. Key binding, building rotating behavior also doesn't line up with industry norms. It feels like this game took a lot of the most basic features and did it different just to be different but just makes the game feel unpolished or clunky to play. There's quite a few of these 3D Rimworld type games out there that provide a unique gameplay but never seem to expand much past that which hurts replayability. Time will tell with this one.  I figured I'd write this review VS refunding and wait and see if this game goes anywhere.

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed playing through the campaign and this game has significant promise, it is apparent it is not complete. I would not currently recommend this game, but with some quality of life improvement and retooling I could see myself coming back and really enjoying it later. My main concerns are the following:- There is next to no explanation of how the game actually works, so you will be playing by trial and error and hopefully figuring out the mechanics along the way. Even after beating the game, I still feel like I have no idea what I'm doing.- Most of the game is quite repetitive, all the way from selecting trees to cut (and re-selecting and re-selecting, and re-selecting) to raiding. Each mechanic is fun the first couple times, but loses it luster quickly.- There could be better progression...or story...or something to make it feel like there is a goal to strive toward. In 19 hours of play I've beaten the campaign and gotten every achievement, and while that's not everything and freeplay can be fun I wish there was a bit more direction to give us a goal. Here are the main things I think this game is missing, and if they were added I would come back in a heartbeat and reverse this post:- Fill out the notes on how the game works in-game, all the way down to the math if you're ok sharing it. We LOVE having the ability to optimize layouts.- Add some quality of life improvements to make leading more forward-thinking, rather than having to select the same trees to cut down every few minutes.- The "objectives" system is great, but I would like it to be a bit more dynamic and maybe include tasks like exploration or raiding.- Rework the "decorations" system to allow fewer but more expensive items, maybe even upgrades or add-ons to structures. I found myself spamming items hundreds of times in the same spot to get the effects I wanted.- Rework the raiding system. The minigame is not very dynamic, and gets boring after a couple once you've seen all the options.- Add more long-term objectives and dynamic events to make the player feel like they're responding to an ever-changing world. Not a perfect comparison, but in games like Civ VI you can play hundreds of times and need to use a slightly different strategy every time to win even against the computer.

_childDocuments_.review: We come from the land of the ice and snow from the midnight sun where the hot springs flow.For those who like all things Viking, the city-builder survival sim Land of the Vikings might be right up your alley.Do you enjoy games like Frozenheim, and Dawn of Man , with events like Frostpunk, but with Vikings, however if you ask me, it also has a bit of a Banished vibe to it, and that’s a good thing. in Land of the Vikings, you are the Jarl of a new Viking village who must manage resources and survive harsh conditions, and enemy raids. You must do this while also guiding your fellow Vikings to work together through social conflict.You will need to expand your village by turning it into a thriving city, and help will come from Norse gods which will aid you with various rewards in return for their worship.You will need to chop trees, plant and grow crops, hunt wildlife, mine, and fish. Be sure to manage your resources carefully to ensure you survive the winter, and expand your settlement from season to season.Each of your villagers is a character in their own right with more than 20 characteristics. Pay attention to skills and abilities when assigning your people to a task because not all Vikings are alike, nor are they good at all jobs.As your settlement grows, more Vikings will ask to join it. You can welcome them or turn them away if you don't have room to spare. Your settlement will expand with or without them though, as your folks will start families and give birth to new generations.While this sounds like an idyllic existence, it may not be smooth sailing at all times. Mother Nature can throw earthquakes and lightning your way, and the seasons bring their own challenges, events and disasters. So expect blizzards, plenty of cold, and storms to contend with.If you find you are running out of things, you can always trade with neighbors after building a Trade Dock. Once you have, ships will visit you with different cargo and you can also send out your own trade missions with a crew. You can also raid foreign villages for silver and gold, and Fame points.In order to raid, you will need to train your Vikings to be either normal warriors, archers, berserkers, or shield maiden elites.One of the cool things about the game is it's gridless. This means you can build wherever you want, design your village however you like, and increase your Vikings’ happiness. Monuments to Odin or Freya can be constructed, and you can customize the look of your Viking ships. You will even be able to modify the look of houses with the Building Editor.As you go about the game, you can unlock new buildings and bonuses by spending Fame points at Yggdrasil, the Tree of Life. Discover beer brewing and build a Tavern for your villagers to relax in, invest in goat farming to gather wool, and as you create better quality living standards and resources, your Vikings will become healthier and happier, and your settlement will flourish.Land of The Vikings is far more polished than I was expecting.It offers an extremely polished experience with enough content to satiate your city-building real-time strategy needs. Sure, there are some inconsistencies here and there, but for the most part, Land of The Vikings is a shining example of how to take an overburdened genre and breathe new life into it.This is a genuinely brilliant strategy game with a lot to offer, and one I cannot recommend enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Super hard pass on this one.It's a pretty game, with an interesting premise, but it is just not fun.Natural Disasters and Events are a joke. I've had to cull my herds 3 or 4 times a year, every year since starting due to 'disease'.Earthquakes and Storms can put you back years, but that's okay... surely if I build the good robust housing I'll be okay? Yeah.. nah. The rebuild button is a nice touch, but 50% of the time it doesn't appear and you are left guessing what building was supposed to be at the end of that road stub.Holding Shift, X and then left clicking to place a structure, only to find that a tree has started to grow, so you have to exit, clear it using the forestry tool, just to start again is poor game design. Let us place it and have a worker clear the area prior to building... just like every other game on the planet with any sort of quality of life features.UI feedback is terrible. Want to know if you've planted enough food to get your through the winter? Tough. Just plonk down as many fields as you can before you run out of terrain that isn't 'too bumpy' - maybe you'll get lucky and manage to micromanage your way through the harvesting stages. Between micromanaging the replacement of dead workers, and field rotation this will be your game play from now on, because you will have little time for anything elseWant to know why you aren't making any dressed stone, despite having 1000 stone, two working stone cutters and 30 idle labourers to transport the stone? Nah. Just cross your fingers a save/reload works.Want to assign housing to villagers near where they are working? Nah. Just get punished by travel time.At least you can go raiding right? Assuming that half your army hasn't died of old age before the rest has been trained, or that you knew they needed beer. Don't worry if you didn't. You'll just have to start again after you've set up a whole Barley/Beer production chain.. because they'll all be dead. I'm guessing they were buried with the armour and weapons I spend months making.Very frustrated by the game as it looked promising. This isn't a colony management/raiding game set in the viking era like I had hoped, its a tedious colony micro-management game.

_childDocuments_.review: if you need a time-killer, this is sweet for you, I'll start with some pros:- Good concept- relatively simple to grasp.Negatives;Repetitive, Theres not a lot of buildings to choose from, you essentially spend an hour or so surviving your first winter, then its 'build houses, build food production, repeat.' the other options for the houses have no real benefits either, for example the 'best' poor house is only a few logs & stones more expensive than the 'worst', so no incentive to build the worse houses except cosmetic.Life-spans, People die too quick and you don't unlock auto-replace until much later in the game. so you spend most of your game replacing (manually) dead employees.Disasters, I don't know if the Devs have ever seen a thunderstorm... but I am yet to see one that demolishes >10-15 buildings at a time, Also the disasters are FAR too frequent; an earthquake a year, and a thunderstorm or two, then a blizzard meaning you can't rebuild your destroyed buildings.Food, Your vikings are always hungry and the food production is unupgrade-able, ie with 500 ish citizens, I had 20-25 fields (wheat) 10 (barley) 15 Windmills, Cattle Farms a plenty, Coops & Goat farms; and marketplaces every ten or so houses and people were STILL hungry, especially annoying when you looked at the top bar and had 350+ saved food.Automatic features, VERY poor; Auto repair in the shipyard as an example doesn't work, nothing else to say.Combat mechanics, Turn based and hard to follow; makes walls and towers basically cosmetic.UI, UI is very basic, Mines are especially its hard to know what you're mining for until you've played a while. No upgrades; Once the basics are unlocked theres no way to improve and most of the production buildings cannot keep up.In short; this game has a lot of potential. But I cannot recommend it quite yet, Come back in six months and check on completion of a few updates.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... okay right now. Cons below:As best I can tell, there isn't a random map generation, which is going to very quickly kill replay value. Disasters, if turned on, slow the game down to the slowest speed and you can't speed up until they complete (you can see why this would be annoying). You can't do anything to prevent them as best I can tell, you're just forced to wait slowly through them.The skill tree of life has branches for passive bonuses. Problem is, not just beelining for the new upgrade buildings will cripple your progression and potentially make it impossible to complete some timed objectives that appear. The game doesn't communicate very well when people die, and since auto-replacing workers for every single building type is an unlock in the tree (see previous problem) you may have buildings operating with just a single worker for some unknown amount of time. I have no idea how to tell if I'm going to have enough food in the winter since pretty much all production stops the instant it hits. Some buildings need trees around them to have a higher productivity. Once you place the building, you can't check what that productivity was, so you can't risk touching anything in the area. That said, it feels a lot like Banished, and I've never played a builder better than Banished. It's simple with enough complexity to some areas without being overwhelming. I lost 4 hours of my night very quickly and definitely plan on losing my entire Saturday to it.

_childDocuments_.review: It is pretty half decent for it's early stages. I love the non-grid layout and how unique your town looks. Despite there being some bugs I have found like the Tavern is not collecting beer (and beer is taking up most of the space in the warehouses) and the Blacksmith is not getting leather despite having tons of it, it is great. It is so detailed and designed to the nail and is a deadset beaut of a game. The tree of life is a nice way of 'leveling' up and better than tech trees or population milestones IMO. The seasons bring a challenge to the game, your year's worth of food and production better be a match for winter. - survival is good, and winter will test you, some you'll breeze through, others I lost 100 people due to famine and no herbs for the doctors. Gets you thinking how to survive the next one.- The details and how everything looks amazing, how every action that the computer does is animated good. Did you know that they sometimes climb tall trees and to chop them?, the level of work in the small animations and details of buildings is amazing. - Trees grow back relatively quickly.- Chickens are an infinite food source, they breed like crazy, Cows are the worse, Its been stuck on 8 forever. Utilise fishing, lifesaver during winter- Good trade mechanics. I had so much coal that i didn't know what to do with it and was making $500 each trip.- Natural disasters, storms destroy too many buildings, Earthquakes are annoying and Good houses are affected the same, shouldn't good houses be more resistant to that type of stuff? they don't seem to worth it at the moment. They still use wood for heating and they will get destroyed by a lightning strike i don't see a reason for these houses tbh. Or at least add a slider for disaster intensity or something.- once you get a large enough population, everything gets so tedious, assigning jobs was fun at first but when people keep dying and looking for the best fit is so tedious. I loved the micromanagement for the early stages but there should be more automation in job reassigning (like Jobs goes to their children would be cool and each family could slowly build there strength in their occupations) and bloomin' farming is annoying. - Festivals are not worth it, bought one and yadada and i was hoping for a party in the longhouse but it was just a happiness and production boost. - after a certain point (400/500+) you are just building houses and farms and more hunter/gatherer huts to feed your people. It gets repetitive. - more interactions with the open world, it'd be cool to get the option to rebirth yourself in a new colony in England, idk the trade system kinda falls flat. and the option to raid monasteries in England while in England if we ever get to that point.- more food for farming, veggies when? - more occupations, like a sears hut that could increase your tree of life points could be cool. -  A Mercenary addition, buy mercs to be in your army.- a more diversity of maps- when your first merchant ship comes in, there could be a plague aspect like a 1% chance of a plague hitting your settlement if you accept the ship, there is not disease mechanic in the game and since it is focused on realism, trade ports typically spawned plagues and infections.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I was going to like this game because I like city builders and Viking stuff, but this just isn't good. It feels like poor copy of Banished (which I adored). The controls are off (don't know how many items I accidentally placed items, losing silver). The UI is confusing and not intuitive. The tutorial missions are inconsistent in explaining mechanics and in general many of the mechanics just don't make sense. Goats make wool? You can only get wool from sheep. Which leads to my biggest gripe about this game: it's aesthetic choices. It takes "Viking" and uses imagery that you would find on the logo of a Viking inspired biker group or in a cheap Scandinavian shop rather than something more authentic and based in history. You can play Banished and it is more "Viking accurate" than Land of the Vikings. Over all I felt like this was not a game that entertained me or one that I felt like I could connect with which is disappointing because it had the potential to be something I would like. Maybe it will change in time and I can give it another go then but for now, I am not impressed with the game's direction.

_childDocuments_.review: This one wasn't for me.  I like city/colony builders, but for ones that present in this style, I prefer to just be able to build up the settlement and learn the economic expansion chains.  There is an option to turn disasters off in the settings.  I turned disasters off.  And then I had 2 earthquakes.  Honesty, the damage from them wasn't even that bad, but it forced the time down to 1x and shook my screen for about a minute.By itself, I probably would have continued on.  But there were already some weird UI interactions that were somewhat irritating.  Space doesn't always pause.  It normally does, but sometimes if you've clicked on something it doesn't.  Same for resuming whatever speed you were on.  Sometimes my camera would get stuck panning in a direction for no apparent reason.There was also the research locked micromanagement opt-out.  It seemed like a strange choice to force the player to micro every building and field in the beginning, and eventually let them research enough to not do that.  I know some people love to micro everything, but for those that don't I think it will be a turn off.I maybe didn't understand what I was seeing with the well placement UI, but it was looking to me like I wanted my buildings to be covered in the radius of the wells, but the radius of the wells cannot overlap, and they are circles.  Meaning that there will be uncovered diamonds throughout my city.  Also, I can't see where they are except when placing a well.  In fairness, maybe there's a view that showed me, but I didn't find it.I do think the decorating system is very good.  I like that the decorations actually give some kind of benefit, so you have a reason to place them beyond just beautifying the town.  I think that this will help towns look more vibrant even for folks who are just trying to optimize.

_childDocuments_.review: People like to compare city builders, and honestly, in my opinion, that's how you lose enjoyment out of them. You overlook the cool things you can do for features other games have. So here's some of the cool ♥♥♥♥ I got out of Land of the Vikings.- After speedrunning the War Dock and Training Camp, I was left with a big underdeveloped group of houses. Lots of homeless vikings. It was winter, and we had no meals left in the market, but I had enough silver saved up after stupidly training a bunch of warriors over planting fields, to either send a trade ship or a raiding vessel. Viking time, b*tches. Sent out my first raiding vessel, and by night they had success- bringing back enough food to get us through the winter. And- when our vikings returned home, they were no longer homeless. I'd built them a new village, a small ring to themselves beside the training camp- AND WITH THE NEW UPDATE I WALLED THAT SH*T IN IT LOOKS SO DOPE- I placed homes near the watchtowers, and I'm able to select THAT specific viking and his sons and train them as Archers,. Sick as f*ck.- My first ever Beserker lead a team of Heavy Warriors on a raid into a large city, and was killed when the raid failed. I erected a totem of Tyr in his honor outside his house, and trained his son to be a Beserker. His son led the next raid on the same city, this time with the ability to attack during church- and came back the new Thane of Ryngfjord.Overall, this game's not as polished as others. It's got some kinks, it's not got all the features, but the developers LISTEN to the community and they add features we ask for all the time, like auto-assignment and field harvesting. They even extended the length of an in-game day to adjust the timescale because the COMMUNITY said it was too short. If you want a game with active developers and a stable foundation while we all wait for Manor Lords, this is it. Great game.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I really love this game, it is like Banished leveled up. It draws me in and has a relaxed gameplay without being too easy or boring. It is stable; haven't encountered any crashes or bugs yet. I love it that your villagers are real individuals with individual traits but I don't like that they age so quickly. I love that the decorations you can place affect your town and I hope many more will be added. The little stories that require you to make descisions concerning the people involved are a lovely thing but sadly quite repetetive. A little more variety would have been nice. The thing I like least about the game is being spammed with disasters once you're up and running. Seriously, I cannot imagine any people staying in a place that torments them with 2 earthquakes, a blaze, and several lightning storms a year. Disasters themselves can add a lot but for now that part of the game feels really unbalanced. For an early access game this is very promising though, and I am really enjoying myself till thusfar.*Update*The latest patch changed the disasters to be more balanced, and now you can also switch them off. The people also live a bit longer now. Nice improvements, it is great to see the dev's responding to feedback with good changes!

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to start off by saying, I absolutely loved Land of the Vikings, by developer Laps Games and publisher Iceberg Interactive, and can’t wait until it’s out of Early Access. When I say I loved this game, I mean even my friends noticed I was playing this game more than my usual ones. It reminds me a lot of the game SimCity BuildIt that I would play in middle school.There are quite a few reasons I love this game, but one of the biggest ones has to be Laps Games’ attention to detail. Let’s start with the first one I noticed: births and deaths. Obviously in a game like this, you should be able to see your population at any point in time – and you can – but the added aspect of telling you who specifically died and who was born really surprised me. I mean especially if you’re keeping up with families (I wasn’t though). However, I’d see the message of someone dying and then suddenly my hunter’s hut didn’t have a worker – and that would happen multiple times over the course of my gameplay. Apart from that, if you zoom in, basically on anything, you can see and hear everything that’s going. I will admit that it does jumpscare me.After I had just built my carpenter’s building and they had gotten to work, my ears got blown out. Easy solution – just lower ambient sounds. Did I ever do that? No. Did I get jumpscared every single time I zoomed in near the carpenter’s building? Yes. Yes, I did. The reason I didn’t lower the volume is because I like hearing the wood sounds when I zoom on the builders. It’s surprisingly very calming to me (also pretty satisfying seeing the progress of the building – which I will get to later). There are a lot more ambient sounds too – cutting down trees, mining stone, environmental sounds, and probably some more I am forgetting at the time of writing this. Another cool detail I noticed was the ability to change your villagers’ name – first names, last names, baby names, all the names. I would definitely say if you want to change names you should try and be on top of it because one moment I was sitting at 30 villagers and the next I had 160.Speaking of villagers and increasing populations, you get newcomer dialogue quite often. It’s basically phrased as if only good can come of inviting new people in because if you turn them away you lose fame (which I still don’t know what that does just yet). However, the homeless people in your game pile up really quick, especially during the winter.Granted in this screenshot, there were only 4 homeless people, but the larger my village became the more of them there were. One could say it mimics life. Similarly, the happiness of the villagers plummets significantly in the winter – just like real life. I definitely feel as though my village was in the trenches, especially during the winter. I obviously couldn’t plant anything; my hunts were significantly less fruitful, as well as my gathering; and for some reason I could never keep up with the demand for firewood. Although, I will say I always had plenty of coal, but for some reason it was never used. I am most likely missing something I’m supposed to do with it, but yeah winters were no bueno.At one point, my herbalist building was full of patients. Yet another detail the developers added is that you can see every villager’s needs and their status. You can see their age, strengths and weaknesses, job, family, even where they live just by clicking on them. They even had little blurb for their strengths and weaknesses which I thought was a cute little detail. I definitely don’t think a majority of players will notice something like that, but I find it fun once in a while to just click on their stats and connect the families to dialogues/events that pop up.While I happen to be on the topic of events, there are quite a few of them, ranging from the aforementioned newcomer events to literal natural disasters (again mimicking life, they are cumbersome to deal with). I know I said earlier it’s phrased as though only good can come from it. Well, I lied. I think literally only conflict arises. Either someone’s getting bullied, washing their clothes in the wrong places, or just straight up homeless and squatting in places. And sometimes, you don’t even really win in the conflicts. For example, in the bullied event, the best solution is donation and the victim becoming disabled. The way this game mimics the consequences of life is perhaps more realistic than I thought (aside from the fact that you can’t just fast forward life).However, that is an aspect of this game that I absolutely adore. I can literally just sit there and play without having to wait extremely long times for things to finish. This wait time – which is meant to encourage players to log on every day – weens me off games similar to this one. In middle school, I ended up deleting SimCity because I couldn’t stand waiting days for things to finish or having to pay literal money to speed up the process. While I understand that mobile version of SimCity at its core is a free-to-play game and Land of Vikings is $20 up front, I think just being able to fast forward helps loads. When I first started playing, I thought there would be a time barrier to getting my buildings. But nope, as long as I have the workers and materials, it will get done – I can literally see it actively being built (touching on the point I mentioned earlier). It also helps with the other technical stuff like gathering materials or waiting for a trade ship. You can basically fast forward through everything; there’s no real set time barrier in the game that isn’t based on in-game time. To rephrase that, you don’t have to wait 3 real life days for your trade ship to come back or for anything.Now that I have hyped up this game (that I am genuinely excited for), I do feel like there is some room for improvement, mostly regarding the building part of the game. I really wish there was a grid system for building. My village is incredibly crooked, despite my best in making things straight. They do have an align feature, but it snaps objects to only one place, so there’s still room for player error. I also wish that I could move buildings after I place them. So, I could essentially pause the game and rearrange my entire village. In a sense, the lack of this feature mimics life once again, but I do think it’d be nice to give players the option. Another thing that was a pet peeve to me are the regrowing trees in relation to building. Sometimes I would chop down an entire area of trees, however, they’d “regrow”. By regrow I mean, they’d basically be bushes. Like if I highlighted so my laborers could cut them down, they would just disappear. Despite that, everytime I tried to place a building on it, the game would tell me it’s colliding with something. It’s just pointless extra steps I feel to place a building – especially if the tree isn’t even really a tree yet. The last thing I think would be great is having a help section in the Tree of Life, explaining some not-so-clear things. They do a good job in the beginning – even having video tutorials – but after that, players kind of have to figure things out of their own. Sometimes these things aren’t always self-explanatory. For example, I had unlocked trading in the Tree of Life, but I couldn’t build a trade ship and had no idea why. So, I kind of just shot an arrow in the dark and kept expanding the trade section on the tree until it was like “you can build a trade ship!”All this to say, I really enjoy the game and am looking forward to updates/improvements in the future. I also suggest joining their Discord (as I did) so you can see other players’ suggestions, feedback, and villages.

_childDocuments_.review: New Update as of 7/2/2024The in-game system talked about releasing Thralls in a future release. Instead of implementing the new system, these developers created a new DLC and are CHARGING people to buy it. Are you kidding me? The game is in early access and you're selling DLC for more money? These developers should be ashamed of themselves and kicked off Steam. --------------------Reviewed: 10/10/2023This Viking-themed game promises epic adventures and battles, and it indeed delivers on the fun factor. However, it also has the uncanny ability to force-quit on you at the most inopportune moments, leaving you both entertained and infuriated. If you're thinking about diving into this virtual Viking world, my advice is simple: save early, save often.The first thing that draws you into "Land of the Vikings" is its captivating world. The game's immersive landscapes, Nordic music, and the whole Viking aesthetic create an atmosphere that will make you feel like you've just stepped out of your longboat. It's not often you get to live out your Viking fantasies, right? Well, that's where this game shines - it's brimming with potential for epic Viking escapades.But here's where things get a bit wonky. The game's coding is like a ship with a hole in its hull; it's just not seaworthy. "Land of the Vikings" is notorious for its random force-quits. You'll be in the middle of an epic battle, hacking and slashing your way through foes, and suddenly, bam! The game shuts down faster than you can say "Thor's hammer!" It's like the digital equivalent of your longboat suddenly sprouting wings and taking off to Valhalla. Frustration galore.But wait, don't let the game's temperamental coding scare you away just yet. The good news is that when it's not busy rage-quitting, it's an absolute blast to play. The build system is both engaging and satisfying - until the inevitable crash, of course.So, what's the workaround for this Viking adventure? You guessed it - save early, save often. In "Land of the Vikings," saving your progress should become a reflex, like sharpening your axe before a battle. It might be a bit annoying, but it's a necessary habit to keep your sanity and ensure that your epic Viking exploits are not lost to the digital abyss.It's a rollercoaster of fun and frustration, thanks to its poorly coded stability. If you're ready to endure a few unexpected ejections from Valhalla and keep your fingers poised over that save button, you'll find a Viking adventure that's well worth the journey. Just remember: save early, save often, and enjoy the ride to a virtual Valhalla!

_childDocuments_.review: Land of the Vikings was supposed to be a decent Banished cloning.It's not.First, the game is clearly unfinished, and most probably it won't be finished ever. From placeholders to not working mechanics and even occurrences where the game is bluntly saying "this mechanic is to be implemented completely in the full release?" it's obvious that LotV is not ready. There are also a lot of bugs- not really game breaking, but visible enough to leave a lasting bad taste.Let's say that one day the developers provide the needed attention and actually finish the game - this will lead to the second major issue. Land of the Vikings is really really bare bone game, with really limited content and options (for everything you can think off - events, resources or even missing basic things like map or map generator). Add to that really unbalanced economy and difficulty (for instance, your people can live almost endlessly without food) and the end result is...meh

_childDocuments_.review: Menus are a bit glitched, but manageable. Also saw a deer sliding around on it's side and fire still burning where torches were removed...Other then that it's still a fun game. If you like games like Anno, Dawn Of Man, Age of Empires and WarZone 2100, you should like this game. Import to note that the combat isn't animated with troop micro management (RTS), it becomes turn based and you choose what to do based on chances with percentages of success. However normal play is pretty much a Sim City or City Skylines style of building your settlement but with ancient Vikings technology and Engineering. You need to place decorations to increase the defense rating and happiness rating of the village. Train your warriors young to defend your village from raids and send the old with the hero warrior out to raid others. Good luck with the frequent disasters such as lightning strikes, earth quakes and random fires destroying buildings, keep a good supply chain of materials to quickly rebuild after a disaster.1.0 version score9/10

_childDocuments_.review: First of all - you have done well for a small team! This is, overall, a solid game and I'm glad to be able to experience the early access phase.My accomplishments: I have put 45 hours into the game so far, reaching year 20 and a population of 900+ villagers.  I have also reached a food level of over 900 once, but I couldn’t tell you where it went.  More on that later.First, I love the UI. Intuitive and easy. Thank you.Here are some issues I would like to point out:1. Chicken coop is fully manned, but chicken man will not slaughter the five birds I told him to, nor will the population grow or decline. This non-progression sometimes goes on for hours of real time.2. The building priority system doesn't seem to work: For example, the poor, earthquake ravaged house with no build priority gets built when the prioritized warehouse next door sits unloved. 3. Overall lack of desire to support the build process: After a natural disaster, say, I've got several buildings that just sit and wait on resources. In the meantime, I've got plenty of resources and plenty of laborers - doing nothing. 4. Tavern: It's staffed, and there's plenty of beer on the map, but there's no sign of activity or any desire to get the beer. Maybe there's a happiness threshold that starts the taps flowing? I never saw anything happen in there.5. Destroyed houses can't be built on the same spot: I swear I hit the 'rebuild' button on every collapsed or burned house but sometimes there's an empty lot (with driveway) left behind that I cannot build in. Any new building I try to put up keeps getting stuck "on something" that's not visible or removable. I have several empty and useless lots now.6. Why can't we sell to incoming traders?  I would love to unload some surplus materials!7. Resource movement needs serious attention. When I have a blacksmith or a tailor, for example, who needs materials to create something, they can’t seem to get those materials, even when they’re right across the street.  Something is wrong there.8. Firewood choppers wait until late in the year to start chopping and they inevitably can’t keep up with larger populations. If we could assign workers to the woodsheds, like we can almost everywhere else, then we can start them chopping earlier and our poor villagers won’t freeze.9. The Trade Docks can’t seem to pull food for the crew, even though I can see it in the village’s inventory. Where do they get the food for the trade journeys?10. Over all there is a feeling that the villagers want to do nothing but eat.  Sometimes the food level is great for the winter, then it catastrophically sinks to nothing and people start to die of starvation.  It doesn’t “feel” right, like there is some hidden drain on the food supply.11. There is also a feeling that these villagers just won’t work.  You assign lots of laborers, lots of builders, etc., but nobody is DOING anything. A little disconnected.That’s it.  I’ll be watching and waiting for some updates before I jump back in.Again, good first cut that this game.  It has potential!

_childDocuments_.review: The problems of the game with optimization and synchronization, the processor warms up a lot, the game is lagging, a bunch of bugs! After playing for 20 hours, other problems turned out. Two problems with the warehouse, your resources sometimes disappear, disappear. And sometimes it happens that they get clogged and no one takes them away. You can put 10 farms (wheat, barley), but no one really works on these farms, despite the fact that you have hired more than 30 people, they don't really grow anything - there will be no food, it disappears, disappears. You may have more than 10 cattle farms, but your farms are empty because there are no animals. 5 cows may appear once a year, if you are lucky. The hunting grounds on the island do not really get the skin, because all the animals are extinct. They work almost in vain. Having about 5 lands, you can get at most 10 skins a year and then if you are lucky. You can put 3 fishing ports with 4 boats in each, but fishermen do not fish, they will work in vain. There is a constant problem with food, there is almost no food on the island. After living for 3 years and 5 months, my population of 600 people began to die of hunger and exhaustion! And you will not find food anywhere, this problem is not solved by any farms or other food industries. This is the biggest bug in the game, that after it you can stupidly delete the game. You will not advance further in the missions. I am surprised by the developers of this game, how it was possible to disrespect the players so much that they could sell such a bogged-down game. Many people have these problems, but they didn't even hesitate and didn't fix these errors and bugs out of respect for those players who have already bought this crappy game, which you can't even call a game! So much time has passed since the release of the game, but nothing has been fixed! And it is no longer possible to return this game, since these bugs have become clear with the passage of time, and the refund period has expired! I advise YOU NOT TO BUY this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I have logged almost 300 hours into this game, so I feel it is safe to say that it is a game I enjoy playing. Yes, there are bugs. The aging rate seems a bit off, I've had times where my carpenter is out in the woods chopping down trees instead of making planks when I have none and builds going that require them. All small things to be expected from an early release game, and usually are fixed by a simple save and reload.My problem, however, is that I recently got very engaged in the building editor. I became focused on building my own unique village, complete with many decorations, buildings, houses, custom roads, etc.. to make my Viking village my own. The building editor is, okay at best. The controls are not easy to work with, as you cannot move an object and move your screen at the same time. But the biggest thing is the 90 degree snap seems to only work 50% of the time, causing builds to take twice as long and be extremely frustrating. I joined the discord page linked to the game menu, reported the bug and waited for days for a reply, but got zero. Instead, another member who reported a tree in the new map not being able to be chopped and got a reply almost immediately.I was very excited about this game, and extremely excited about the content of this new update. But I would like to finish my builds before I restart my map, and the lack of response to my issue turned me off, so I am considering uninstalling the game. To me, with this issue, it is boring and unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: The worst city builder I have played in recent memory. There is no distinction between day and night on screen, other than the "clock" at the top of the UI. The environment looks like it is always in night time, even when it is day. The graphics look terrible and they look like a low budget game from the mid 2000's. Character models look atrocious and the water effects look hideous. The UI also feels very clunky, and after about 10 minutes, I got tired of hearing the same stale and uninspired BGM, over and over. The villagers also feel very robotic and soulless compared to other games in this genre I've played. The kicker for me though, was the Path of Exile inspired "research system", where you spend forever to acquire lots of "points" you spend in meaningless nodes, such as a whopping +5 percent movement speed or field working rate. This system was annoying when POE attempted it, and it was annoying now. I could'nt bring myself to make it to the combat section of this game, but if it's anything like the rest of it, it's probably bad.This is probably just meant to be a low budget game. Fine. I guess I just went into it with higher expectations. If this sort of game looks interesting to you, and at this price point, wait for a major Steam sale and just pick up Tropico or something. This game would have benefited with more time in the oven. I would have been willing to pay more money for it if it were of higher quality. Hopefully the developers are able to make some money off of this, make a better concept for a sequel, and line up a publisher or something for it, and make a better game in a few years.

_childDocuments_.review: So 19 hours in- I feel like I will get my money's worth. It has an interesting take on a colony builder, though I did feel after a while there could have been more mechanics or production chains or event types (especially event types). I got my first non-demo colony to about 600 people and a decent military force, filled the tech tree almost completely out, and will probably play a bit more in time. It is not my favorite 'Banished-like' but it scratched the itch when I just wanted a change from my usuals in aesthetic and some mechanics. I may be done playing it for this weekend, but I will definitely play it again in my game rotation.Mechanic I hate most: Fishing boat repair is micro management annoyance, I wish that I could unlock some kind of auto-repair or to auto build new boats if I just let 'em wear out.Mechanic I like the most: I am one of the apparently rare reviewers who LIKES the turn based tactical 'card' combat system! And I like it a lot, as it does give a threat to the town or way to pillage resources but is faster than a true RTS and combat is always my least favorite part of a game where my personal focus is on building the colony or city and surviving/thriving. Basically if I want to play a military RTS I will play a miilitary RTS but when I want a Banished-like I really prefer that to be a backseat issue, and I think that Land of the Vikings really handled that well for me. A game about vikings with no combat would've been a bit weird perhaps, and I find their system a good compromise.

_childDocuments_.review: The inclusion of the workshop and building editor really make this shine. I like how certain props contribute to building storage/villager speed/visibility/decoration/etc.  You can also get a large variety of buildings going with the workshop content. The lighting system also brings the cities to life in a way I haven't really experienced in a city builder before. With all the options for building, even down to the widths of the roads.. you can really make some dense and unique viking themed cities with several maps to choose from. The cycle of seasons and nice weather effects are also an excellent inclusion. Pretty cool the way snow was done.I appreciate the addition of the of how the combat loop works. With exploring other settlements and attacking/defending.  There's no real time combat, only simulated. However, I was fine with that. I like the small details of being able to see the warriors man the ships and set out. And all of this gives you a reason to build an economy that can produce all the things necessary for building ships and training soldiers. I ran into minor bugs. One was kind of major, but the dev said they will address it. The game performs surprisingly well for me even up to getting 500 population with high settings. My system is a bit dated, with an i7 7700k and gtx 1080ti. I also play at 3440x1440 or 2560 depending on if I need more frames.All in all, I caught it on sale for 16$ and was extremely pleased as someone who loves city builders. This one is slow paced, and even has a tech tree of sorts to move through with accumulated fame points. Which you gain through random events/raiding/and other ways.It scratched the itch for sure...  I'm just ready for Manor Lords to finally come out

_childDocuments_.review: Land of the Vikings is an engaging city-builder set in the world of vikings. The pace is relaxed, and the player can issue orders with the game paused. Later on you can build up a force of viking warriors and ships and go off raiding and looting your neighbors. All good fun.The one area of the game I found disappointing was the trading system. Trading ships from elsewhere will visit your settlement, and will have only minimal quantities of a few basic items for same, and will not buy anything. The player can build trading ships and send missions with goods to sell, but most of the time they return home without selling anything.

_childDocuments_.review: ● Overall opinion: Don't buy it. The idear behind this game is something I really like! I am kinda waiting for a game like this. But this game isn't properly made and I guess the ressources to really finish it was empty and they delivered a game that was 95% finished.I really want this game to be as good. I like this type of game; slow city builder pre-industrial tech. This game can be compared to Life is Feudal Forest Village; I am talking about atmosphere, feeling and speed. I like this atmosphere. I really want this game to be good.Annoying things:● I can't destroy resources. A Hunter gathers Meat and Leather. The Meat goes to the Market, but if the Markets are full, the Hunting Lodge has a problem: their stock can also become full. Meaning: eventually they also can't gather any leather, becouse their building is stocked with Meat. But at some point you need the more Leather! So the game punishes me for overproducing?! (later in the game you can trade goods, but not in early game and even than I should be able to destroy goods)● You can't cancel an order to chop trees. If you accidently mark a tree far away for chopping, you can't undo this.● I've made and bought (Trading) quite some High Quality clothes and Winter Clothes, but if I click around at villagers, I only see them use 'Poor Clothes'.● Building 'Wooden Walls' and 'Wooden Wall Gates' is clunky and buggy. Hard to describe, but believe me.And: You can't connect a wall to natural obstacles like stone hills?! Why not...? So you have to build a closed circle wall around your village. Meaning you can't include some of the buildings like mines and fishing buildings in the protected area.A road can go through a Wooden Wall Gate. Placing that road through the Gate is clunky and weird, but ok. But you can't place a Wooden Wall Gate on top of a road :') You have to remove the road first and than place it again after placing the gate. Some villagers refuse to walk through the fast route through the Wall Gate and take a short but longer detour. Other villagers are fine with walking through the Wall Gate.● From time to time there are pop-up messages that let you make choices. Not much variety in them. I've got about a dozen messages about a new found plant/herb and the Healer wanted to try it. I always choose 'let's try it' (or whatever the choice was called) but never got any feedback about my choice.● If people become homeless, that obviously effects their wellbeing in a negative way. If you keep providing homes for everyone, they become pregnant and your population grows. So your village will expand forever when you don't accept homeless people, I assume. So you HAVE to keep growing indevinately or face unhappy homeless people? I don't like this.● Like many games, they show some information in the loading screen. In this case I always see the same line of text, about the lack of distinction between warships and tradeships. Not an issue, but it shows the not-being-really-finished state of the game.● You can place a lot of different kind of decorations around buildings that improve those buildings. Way to much small stuff to my taste, but that's personal. But this game let you decorate your village visually to your liking. That's nice! BUT: people who like this will also appreciate that things like road paths between a house and the main road looks nice. But that is clunky and annoying, becouse the game auto-connects a house with a small road to the main road is you leave some distance. But this auto-connection is hardly ever a nice placed direction :( Clunky and annoying to make it the way you like.● I haver a very good pc, but even if I lower the graphics a lot and set the game to just 30 fps, I ALWAYS see a horizontal blurry line when I move the camera around. Even in Paused mode...

_childDocuments_.review: Land of the Vikings has a lot to show for it self. I can mention very good graphics, well thought out enviroment and much more that works really well. It it complex but not complicated so initially it have most of what is needed for success.The first hours I was quite impressed and as I for the first period started and restarted quite a few games to improve flow and efficiency I did nod really notice the most serious bumps in the road.But now after about 75 hours I have decided that it is time to take a brake and wait for updates.What grinds down my patience are mainly the following:1 Uncontrollable population growth - This makes it almost impossible to systematically plan and build for the future. You end up desperatly building new "poor" houses all over the place just to keep up. It also makes it impossible to have a controlled development of industry, agriculture and fishing to keep the population fed and occupied. You can argue that you can deny newcomers and/or kick out surplus homeless but that will cost fame resulting in a stalling of tecnnology development.2 No forestry building with foresters -  Timber is a key resource and it is not fun to mark out each and every three that are to be cut again and again and again....... I do not believe that anyone think this level of micromanagment is fun.3 Impossible challenges - You typically get events like the thefts where you can investigate if you have enough money, increase security or do nothing. Generally the best choice is to incvestigate but you do not always have the coins needed. If you do nothing people get unhappy. So you would probably choose to increase security. But what you soon will see is that you cannot increase security because needed tech is not unlocked and will not be for a very long time. You will then fail and people get unhappy and/ or your fame will decrease and it will be even loger before that particular tech can be unlocked.4 Unclear or illogical progression - I have not found a way to boost fame so that new tech and buildings can be unlocked. When you play without tutorial active the progression seem to be agonisingly slow and you also get very few free funds which is important early in the game. With the tutorial active you get goals to reach and these increase your fame and funds up to a certain level. But soon you get to a point where next goals rely on techs not already unlocked and then your progression  almost grinds to a halt.5 Storage - The very low storage capacity is intentional as you can boost it with certain "decorations". A good idea but it does not really work well. Very low step by step increase combined with very limited funds force you to build an untold number of markets and warehouses that feel very unnatural.Of these five points it is really  1 and 2 that does the most damage.Despite my complaints I still recommend the game as I belive that the developer will be interested in fixing this type of hickups, and then it will be a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome, this is extremely well done and clearly has a lot of thought put into the details.The developers are interested in what their audience has to say and capable of implementing feedback and fixes in a timely fashion. Also the early access amount of things to do ended up boring even this very relaxed player. _childDocuments_.review: Land of the Vikings has me hooked.... I thought "Banished" was good until I ran across this gem.  This game has plenty to build upon to become better and yet it's developed enough to be loads of fun as is.  Mind you this is a city builder micro management game that requires patience and skill to grow a proper village into a bustling town.  Yet at 20 hours I am impressed with the level of detail put into this early release title. The good-*Easy early game with good tutorial.*Random Events that require player decision input such as discovering a grave while building. *Ease of making silver to spend on much needed decorations.*Detailed individual worker/villager stats and abilities.*Detailed tech tree "Yggdrasil" which allows further development of your city. *Seasons that change the dynamic of the game... winter is coming =PThe Bad-*Lack of use of visual aids like a bar graph or pie chart to better track your resources, workers, beer flow... etc.  I would love to see a bar graph that shows whats going out and whats coming in to inventory.*Overall, years last 30 days which seems to be quite short to put all the seasons in but that might just be me.*Few starting options for maps.*MORE WEATHER!!... need dense fog.... and more weather options and effects even when disasters are turned off.Last word-Overall the game plays well and delivers a robust viking city building experience!

I'm looking forward to more challenges as the game develops. Now that I know how to play as it is, it's simple and fun.  More difficulty and maybe some fighting would be nice in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good-- nothing about it is particularly special in any real way as far as city builders go. In fact, it's lacking a lot of things imo, but it is in early access. It is BEAUTIFUL to look at, but the feeling of investment in your city gradually drops away as it becomes harder and harder to keep track of your citizens and assigning jobs becomes a constant chore. I think the early game and limited survival mechanics are fun to engage with, and the raids later, though all off-screen, do give it a unique flavor. I think with some time and polish this will become a really great city builder, but for now it's just okay. Get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I've changed my review. I'll leave the original below (because I'm lazy) but the original issue is fixed. I can and have played the game.The UI is a little strange, and functionality is a bit off (no clear way to repeat build, lining things up is a bit awkward, minor mispellings and grammar mistakes, no tooltips for some stuff like villager stats) but... other than that, the game is relaxing and works. It isn't incredibly deep, but just building a city and expanding it has a certain addictive quality and this game captures that really well.Graphics are pretty good. Villager pathing mostly works (though sometimes it doesn't, and fences which are meant to keep villagers contained don't work at all). Laying down roads is functional, but it's a bit nitpicky trying to get things to line up or not be a curve when you want a straight road.I'm glad I finally got to play it, and I don't regret buying it at this point. I do wish I had been able to play it much sooner, but what the hell; patience pays off.<<Original Review Below>>I left a review a few months ago, and it basically said "Doesn't work on Windows 7. Game looks nice though."Now, having upgraded finally to windows 10, I am trying to play it again, because the game still looks nice.... and I still can't play it.
