_childDocuments_.review: Aside from some bugs which are to be expected in early access, and some features that require balance, i would recommend this game to anyone that likes city builders and managers. it does get a bit frustrating that you cant ever really seem to get things balanced out between food, housing and population. i had 8 cattle farms, most max size, 8 coops, 5 goat farms, half a dozen hunters huts at 100% efficiency, 8 gather huts from 75-100% efficiency, 6 fishing docks all with 4 boats, and 8 max size wheat farms. often id have over 150 meals in stock, and people were still unhappy due to hunger. despite having at least 8 woodsheds scattered around the village and maxing the capacity to 600, and 3 coal mines, every winter 80% of homes were unhappy because they were cold, and people stopped buying food even though it was available. so every winter i was faced with my now city threatening to disband and just barely getting to spring just to start the cycle of frustration over again. i don't know if this was a flaw in my city design, or a game flaw. i'll have to test that out, but either way it points to a lack of information, which is my only other gripe, there's no information other than the in-game tutorial and vague tool tips. Aside from these minor (and i do consider them minor) irritations i enjoyed my first play through and will try again doing things a little different to see if that changes my results. and i would say give it a try. hopefully it goes in the right direction moving forward.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent city builder/resource sim.  Fairly easy to pickup but a few areas for opportunity in my opinion:1. Give us the ability to place a building for wood production.  Having to manually mark trees every couple minutes all around the island becomes tedious.2. Winters/Raids should be far more detrimental.  When you start approaching the 10 year mark, you have such a surplus of $ and resources that neither of these things seem impacting. I don't think at any point I dropped below 60 or 65 happiness in the entire game.3. Raiding should be provide a bit more clarity.  As it stands today, when choosing an area to raid, it'll provide you a Defense rating of that area.  Logic would dictate that if your defense score is higher than their defense score, you should be successful in the raid - but that's not what happens.  Often times your success rate is < 30% when your defense score is higher than theirs.4. The Tree of Life mechanic is great - I'd love to see the ability to have this broken down in the UI to give you a "heads up" as to what each branch takes you to without having to buy into it first to discover it so you can plan accordingly for early game objectives.  ie: Military, Production, etc.5. Why in the world are my villagers freezing but I have hundreds and hundreds of coal just sitting it my warehouse.  The tooltip even says, "No firewood or coal" so where is the disconnect here?Overall there's a really decent foundation of a game here.  I think this is worth picking up on sale if its your kind of genre - but as it stands today for the current price point, it's a bit lacking.
_childDocuments_.name: Land of the Vikings

_childDocuments_.review: After 16 hours I have essentially completed all the content in the game, I have fully unlocked the yggdrasil and constructed several of every building. At the current standing of this game at its price point I would recommend it for a friend for a small city builder that appears to take place between the years 800-900. The game starts you off with a very small viking haven and has you expand onto it with development of farmlands, fishery and hunting/gathering huts as sources of income and makes you cut down trees and mine rocks for the development of wood planks and stone bricks to construct houses that allow your haven to expand in population. About midway through the game you can unlock either the War path or the Trade path that allows your haven to expand into naval expenditures, The trade menu is something that can be improved on as it can be confusing if you're buying or selling your items. The raiding menu is very straight forward allowing you to choose which ship and which warriors you send on the raid to what city and its defenses if you've scouted it out enough. The game also has a system in place that allows you to deal with individual issues that happen within your haven. At times managing the individual people and workers of the haven can be a hassle to keep track of, the game has an auto select feature to select the best workers for that building type based on stats, however the auto replace of workers that die from old age / other reasons is locked until the very end of the tree of life. As time progresses throughout the years the seasons change and bring on additional struggles for your haven, as snow begins to fall your people will need warm clothes and firewood to keep them alive. In conclusion if you're into the whole time period of the viking age and city builders, this game does a great job of incorporating a lot of elements of norse mythology such as allowing you to pick several runic inscriptions to use as your havens banner/shield and the progression tree being based off of the yggdrasil along with in game events that happen, At 20$ I would say this game is very worth the price, The graphics are nice and clean, The landscape is vast and beautiful and it captures the nordic lands greatlyIf I were to rate this game I would give it a 8.5 out of 10 with its current standing, there are a few bugs but nothing too game breaking. “It is better to stand and fight. If you run, you'll only die tired.”

_childDocuments_.review: Solid city builder which needs improvements. I didn't want to give a thumbs down to this game as the basic gameplay is quite satisfying and it definitely has that "5 more minutes" quality.The graphics are good, if not excellent (for example, the tilt of the map shows different amounts of trees and some animations are a little clunky).The gameplay consists of the usual "find wood, mine stone, build stuff" and it is done well. There are occasional pop ups about "dilemmas" which, for me, don't really present enough of trade off one way or the other to be interesting. There are some real problems with the gameplay, however:- You can't find the "range" of buildings like the marketplace, so there is no real way of knowing if you are satisfying needs for villagers. I can't see how many villagers I have trained as archers or whatever, or even why I have trained them.- The well shows a range when being placed, but as far as I can tell, this can't be seen once placed. It is also circular and cannot intersect with another well's range, so this leaves large parts of your village outside of a well range. I have no idea if this has any impact on anything and the game doesn't let you know.- There is no way of knowing how some things interact; what do goats produce? What benefit is there to having cows instead of goats, is there a benefit to having chickens? What exactly do decorations do, besides a very vague description?- Lots of needs aren't obvious and there are bugs where , for example, you can have lots of leather stored but your tailor or blacksmith will be showing as having no leather. There doesn't seem to be any way to fix this.- The farming of fields, for example, is fairly haphazard as you can only nominate the number of farmers. When available the "auto plant and harvest" seems to work sometimes, but not others.Anyway, there are lots of little things which leave you scratching your head and wishing the villagers would do what you want them to and lots of things which aren't explained at all. Another example: placing the hunters hut gives a percentage efficiency at that time, but there seems no way of assessing if building near to it changes this.So:I think it's not worth the money at the moment, but I am tempted to put it aside for 6 months in the hope the devs fix the minor annoyances and bugs.Edit: 12 hours in and I feel I have reached the end of the fun to be had and I don't feel a new start would be worthwhile. There are some fundamental problems which need fixing, such as not being able to see the tech tree, there being no benefit to increasing defence of your village and point for tech unlocks taking too long to accumulate. There's a good game there at the core, but bear in mind 12 hours will probably be it for now.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game. I like it, really interesting. But I thought there is a problem with this game. The problem is about the raiding, there is no reason for players to try this function in this game.Firstly, the raiding needs too much food, or we say, the raiding takes so few things for the players` village. If I wish to send three full warships to attack a heavily armored rich city, I need almost 200 food or even more, many bottles of beer. Meanwhile, I also need to prepare 30 warriors for this task. That is a lot of expense especially when you send a group of Shield-maidens or Berserkers to loot other cities. But in fact, the treasure they take back is very few. This is a loss-making transaction most time. Also, the raid point appears too late on the Tree. The Viking village needs to have a completed industrial system and then can go out to raid other people. But if  I can produce almost all the things by myself, why do I need to go out to raid? I have had more than 3000 silvers, I do not need 156 bloody silvers, my warriors should not die for so little money and goods.The same problem exists in trading too.So in my opinion, if players can get some high-value things in raiding or trading that they can not produce by themselves, that will promotes players to go out but not stay at home. In addition, the raiding and training warriors options should be able to learn a little earlier than the current version, or players have no ambitions to loot others.That is all. It is a game with potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game - takes a lot of thought to balance out the needs and the actual quantity of resources needed to advance. I have been playing this game since it was released and would only be for those who are interested in a sandbox city building kind of game. A great plus is that your buildings and roads are not dictated by grids, which really adds character as you can create your village with more 'flow'. My main dislike for the game currently, which I am sure will be expanded on, is a certain lack of resources. Mainly THE most important one, wood. Once your village has reached a decent size, the wood use is extremely high, both for burning winter logs and future building. Using up land to expand also then limits availability for gatherers, which provide you with herbs so your villagers don't die from illness. There is limited availability on how much your trade ships can carry or what can be traded.Therefore, to the developers, my biggest request would be more building space not limited by so many mountains, as well as a form of a sustainable forestry mode. Even the ability to trade 'raw' resources would be extremely helpful. If I can trade food and coal, why not wood? I have stopped playing now as my wood supply vs game play is no longer balance and cannot develop my village any further. All in all, a pretty cool game which has a bright future

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it, but it needs a bit more automation to keep me playing. I don't like having to click each field twice, several times every year, once to plant and once to harvest. I'm also less than enthusiastic about not being able to automate repairs on fishing boats, so that I have to check the boatyard constantly in the hope that I'll be able to identify one which needs repair, then again two clicks to start the repair process. The issue most desperate for a bit of automation though is population allocation. You might allocate 12 people to your mines, but come back in 3 minutes and there'll only be 9, with the other three just vanishing for no particular reason *and not being replaced* even though you have plenty of surplus population.I'd say that about 75% of the time I played this game I was refilling population manually where every other similar game would simply keep the buildings topped up to the level I'd set (unless a population shortage occurred).However, it's good to look at, I like the trading system, the tree of life tech system is well-though-out, and I think the combat/raiding system has a lot of potential, although it's hard to focus on that when you're constantly having to manually reappoint a chicken farmer because the previous one simply vanished.

Villagers will not do anything for them selves, not the simplest of things which is fun at the beginning of the game but as i said as the village starts getting to a large size its uncontrollable and very tricky to keep on top of.I am by no means putting the game down as i do enjoy it but with all the micro management that has to be done in large villages it becomes less enjoyable as its all spent whizzing the camera round looks for red icons for buildings not working due to the staff dying. which can cause issues for collecting food or buildings going half finishedi know its early access which is why i am clicking lots of feedback in game. so jut like this patch which has solved a few things which i actually submitted i look forward to future updates to address other things :)So yes i do recommend the game as its still a fun game, could do with more varied events etc as the same ones keep coming up about someone being bullied then for someone reason if you dont exile him he is automatically crippled?  way way further down the line it would be nice to have a little bit more detailed textures and the text in boxes maybe larger or sharper as certain things when your sat away from the screen like on a sofa( even with the UI up-scaled to max) can still be a little small and squashed up. maybe some buildings which are slightly more identifiable from each other. when sitting get larger and your looking for something in particular, it can look awfully similar with all the wood lol * yes i now where its set and i do like it. is just my opinion :)ALSO... there are silly things such as so much bumpy ground when you are trying to place buildings that there there are so many areas that look flat around your village that you just cant build on lol. Then on top of that you have to place water wells which have a radius that are circles, nothing new there right? WELL these circles cannot overlap! which means there are so many gaps and so many buildings that are not covered by water.  the game physically wont let you build any more wells either because they will over lap?!?  This game has been around for a while now and has so many simple over sights like this that i cannot be bothered to note them due to i dont want to waste any more time on this review. Started off with so much potential and it has had alot added to it... but its as if the game play and things like this have been missed and forgotten about as extra buildings etc have been focused on. Its becoming too frustrating to play now. needs more updates which i cant see happening as i have given up providing feedback within game now as i feel nothing is ever listened to unless u are asking for more buildings or what ever.it is getting left behind and even the graphics dont seem quite right. i cant put my finger on it.probably why there hasn't been the most positive reviews recently coming in for it.i still hold hope but i think i will leave it for abit longer till more updates have come out and there is something note worthy on the patch notes instead of just more buildings being added with no thought on radius things.Like how can they get water wrong? lolIf you like banished or Ostriv then you will like this, its as simple as that. but i would say ostriv is more fleshed out as the updates are starting to make more of a impact on game play, i find banished a much more difficult game, so ostriv seems to be ahead at this point.stop focusing on battles  for one minute and get village building right surely ?anyway thats it from me for now... till the next big update :)

_childDocuments_.review: Good start for EA. I don't regret buying it. Needs more content and some improvements, but a really good start! It is definitely a thumbs up, keeping in mind the EA state. I'll wright about problems mostly, but it is not bad at all. A nice-looking city builder with few unique mechanics and it looks and feels different from others. This alone is a recommendation to look at it more closely! It has a good atmosphere, very nice too look how your little Vikings move through the snow, and the decorations mechanic makes your village look very cool. Villagers have 4 stats and more or less efficient with their tasks, also people live in their house with their family and don't immediately swap houses with someone to be closer to mine or tavern where they work =)- Stats are a good idea, but don't really work as for now. If you had 10 people maybe. But you have 100+ after the first year so you'll always have someone near with a good relevant stat.- Distance is working. You need to place houses near mines, a market to keep them fed, etc. Village grows naturally. And there could be a tradeoff to put someone with lower stat living near or with higher stat living far away. Micromanagement and lack of automatization and notifications. It is QOL mostly, and I hope devs will add it later.- People die all the time and there is a notification above the building that no one left to work. Most buildings have multiple workers and you must check them periodically if some vacancy "opened". There should be an option to automate this - I always check the nearest guy with the most stats. There is no choice here. Maybe build more houses near, that's all.- Chopping trees. It is stupid =) Every minute or so (not exaggerating) you zoom out and mark all trees in walking radius for chopping. Every Minute. Wood is needed in huge quantities and trees grow very fast. And the problem has an easy solution: we need Forester.- Research is boring. New buildings are cool, but villagers are faster by 1%? Really? Decoration has meaning and it is awesome.- There are a few different types of decorations for different purposes. It looks good and diverse =)- Decorations buffs buildings. Happiness for villagers, speed for roads, production speed for some buildings. So, you have a mechanical purpose to make your village look nice. More events needed- For now, you have one social event, and one disaster per year. Sometimes two.- Disasters are the same, just different visuals. Storm looks much cooler than the earthquake. Maybe add some form of defense against them? Not entirely but maybe for some buildings. It gets repetitive to repair the same house every year.- Social disasters are the same. You can get disabled guy or banish someone or family. Of course, I'll banish them, I have about 200 people, less mouths to feed.- There are "consequences", but they are irrelevant as for now. If something collapsed click rebuild, and if someone is upset.. They'll forget in a few months and be happy again, as long you don't choose permanent debuffs. Shure, that guy had a name, but I don't really know who he was.. there are literally hundreds of villagers, how do I know or why should I care who Sigvald is?

name: Wanted: Dead
detailed_description: Wanted: Dead is a new hybrid slasher/shooter from Ninja Gaiden and Dead or Alive authors. The game follows a week in the life of the Zombie Unit, an elite Hong Kong police squad on a mission to uncover a major corporate conspiracy. Play as Lt. Hannah Stone, a hardboiled Hong Kong cop, and plow through mercenaries, gang members, and private military contractors in a spectacular cyberpunk adventure. The game is best experienced with a controller for fluid combos and intuitive combat. Hack-n-slash melee combat: Unleash a wide array of deadly moves and unique finishers to slice and dice. Third-person shooter: Engage in intense battles using a handpicked assortment of projectile weapons, including assault rifles, SMGs, LMGs, and grenade launchers. Brutal finishers: Over 50 unique finishing moves. Cyberpunk setting: Experience a wild fusion of high-tech weaponry and retro 90s futurism. Gripping storyline: Join the Zombie Unit as they unravel a massive corporate conspiracy in a dystopian version of Hong Kong. Truly hardcore experience: The fights will be challenging. Steel your resolve and use everything around you as you battle through hordes of mercenaries, synthetics, and private security forces. Old school beat 'em up: Take down enemies to progress further and revive the nostalgia in a modern twist on the established genre. A love letter to the sixth generation of consoles.

_childDocuments_.review: Magnificently Mediocre. Those two words explain it best. If you followed the game pre-release, you saw so much effort in the design, music, aesthetic. everything the game had seemed bursting with personality, and it seems like it was gonna be fun. Sadly it falls short. Gameplay - Wonky/Janky. Melee is somewhat fleshed out but barely passes the bar overall. Gunplay is odd as well. It seems half-baked and partially unoptimized. Apparently K&M support seems to be abyssmal as well.Aesthetics/Visuals - Rocking. It's a beauty to look at despite it's seemingly 8th generation graphics. It's a beautiful Cyberpunk world. Characters look unique and are interesting to look at... for the most part. Animations are, again, wonky. To the point that it sometimes looks like a character isn't actually saying what you are hearing.Audio Design -Why include audio design of all things in a review? because it's disgustingly bad. It's downright atrocious and the biggest reason I refunded, among these other things. Voice actors seem so lifeless when speaking, and sometimes background audio will be so loud you can't even hear important dialogue.Story -the first level and introductory phase seem to be 1:30 hours long, and throughout it, I never ceased to be utterly confused. Its seemingly just going to be another generic cyberpunk story.Tl;dr Do I buy this game? For $60? absolutely not. For $30 and below? Absolutely. It can definitely be enjoyed and I'm just going to wait for a sale to pick it up again.

_childDocuments_.review: If you played "WET" for the PS3/Xbox360, fondly remember it as 'a janky masterpiece of style,' and wish something like it existed for the PC, this game might be up your alley! I'm about 4 hours in, have been *loving* it, and not dying *particularly* often - especially after I got a feel for the run and pistol-stun-n-slice combo flow of combat.Pro-tip: You'll have a much better time with this game if you unlock the 'guard strength' power (so you can just hold 'block' to stop the first sword hit, then parry follow up hits from enemies), along with the running & sliding attack unlocks ASAP. Combat will feel less clunky after this.The plot feels like a translated-to-Engrish dubbed bootleg DVD, and I am freaking *here* for it. Know what you're getting into, and this game could be *exactly* what you'r!e looking for.----------edit: The April 10, 2024 combat overhaul update got me to fire up the game again. Combat definitely still feels great once you get into the flow, but it feels like it maybe becomes a bit more fluid a bit earlier into the game now, and the quality of life changes (making some areas feel less like ironman endurance challenges) are pretty nice.Definitely still recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of the most enjoyable surprises in gaming I've come across in years. Is it jank? Yes. Is its story barely cohesive? Yes. Is it hard as nails at times? Yup. Does it weave all of that into a fascinating whole that features genuinely intricate and well-thought out (though not exactly well explained) combat? Hell yes.This game is certainly not perfect by any means (minigames, I'm looking at you), but if you're looking for a videogame-as-hell videogame that's simply out to have a good time while also challenging you to learn its systems (and make no mistake, there is thought behind most everything in this game, it just doesn't scream explanations at you), go for this gem.(Unless you'd prefer the industry follow the homogenized, uncreative lowest-common-denominator guidelines the IGN crowd apparently wants it to, I suppose.)

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead isn't a terrible game, but it's far from a good one. The basic hacking and slashing can be pretty fun, especially with properly timed parries and dodges, but there's very little to see here. For the most part, you have two basic melee combos, a rifle, and a pistol. The pistol can't be aimed manually and is really only used for taking potshots at melee-range foes or for reversing unblockable attacks. The combos themselves also feel somewhat rigid, but they're manageable. The shooting, on the other hand, is quite poor and the main rifle just isn't much fun to use. For the most part there are also only five enemy types that the game spams for its duration and the melee enemies block almost everything all the time, which can get fairly annoying, especially when their blocking capabilities are vastly superior to our protagonist's. By default, getting hit a single time while blocking will break your guard. You can pick up other guns to use as long as they have ammo but there just isn't much reason to not fight at melee range. The most common enemies here are just regular dudes with guns that die in a single sword combo, which is what you'll be doing for most of the game. There are five missions broken up by out-of-place Yakuza-style minigames and running around the game's police station. The cutscenes are entertaining enough but the story makes very little sense and the voice acting is often laughably bad. The game likes to toot its own horn about how difficult it is and that's not really true. There are a few sections that are kind of infuriating but the rest of the game is mostly just easily cutting down weak dudes as they ineptly shoot at you. At least the finishers are rad and there are a ton of them. You have a four-person squad but they're mostly useless, save for Doc, who can revive you once per checkpoint.The bosses mostly aren't hard at all either. A couple are surprisingly easy. Even the final boss is mostly a pushover. The only "hard" boss battle here is only difficult because it's badly designed and requires you to fight a horde of regular enemies while he shoots grenades at you. It's one of the worst parts in the game. There just isn't really much going on here. Mastering the gameplay is easy since the main character doesn't get new main weapons or learn new combos for them aside from getting an additional hit here or there. Once you beat the game there's a new game plus that only lets you keep your abilities and gun mods and nothing else, so don't expect tougher enemy encounters. There's also a harder difficulty that removes the ability to recover health from landing attacks and using finishers, but it's not that much harder than the normal mode. I kind of like Wanted: Dead but mostly because I have a fondness for janky, badly conceived games. If that's up your alley you might want to try it out but it is NOT GOOD so don't expect anything on even remotely the same level of quality or challenge as Ninja Gaiden.

_childDocuments_.review: In the first couple hours you'll be exposed to horrible audio mixing, combat that waffles between "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that was sick" and "why do I keep dying", anime references, gritty social commentary, bizarre disconnected dialogue, literal anime cutscenes, a crane game, a rhythm game ramen eating contest and a lot of cats.  It's weird, it's imperfect, and I love it.You should play this.  It's firmly in the "they don't make em' like this anymore" razor's edge of AA jank that rides the line between polished and completely unpolished, but was clearly made with passionate badness. It feels like a PS3/360 game from 2008 that someone forgot to release until last year, and I mean that as definite compliment.  You're not wrong if you don't vibe with the game or aren't the kind of person who digs this specific kind of experience. It's a bit like having a taste for B-movies and preferring the honest exuberance that comes from a team wanting to make something cool and not quite getting it right.  If you are that kind of person though - yes, you should play this.

_childDocuments_.review: :  is basically a mix of melee sword combat, third-person gunplay, limb-severing finishers, various minigames and anime-style storytelling, and it was developed by the talent behind the Ninja Gaiden and Dead or Alive series. Unfortunately, the game has so many flaws and it didn't live up to expectations. ✔️ Gory combat with satisfying finishers ✔️ Great soundtrack with famous 80s songs (which for some reason you rarely get to hear in-game) ❌ One of the worst storylines I have ever seen in a video game❌ Awful voice-acting, terrible writing, lifeless characters, and pointless cutscenes❌ Janky combat that sometimes doesn’t make sense, while having to unlock “abilities” that you should’ve had at the very beginning.❌ PS3 graphics and subpar level design.❌ An unoptimized game with too many bugs. You play as Hannah Stone, a captain of an elite police squad that takes place in future Hong Kong, where body augmentations and sword fighting is the new trend, and that's all you need to know. The game’s story is a complete mess; to my understanding, there was no real plot to speak of, just a series of events and missions that have no relation with one another, they just happened without any real coherence or purpose. I'll give you more examples; after the first mission there will be a cutscene where you are introduced to a businesswoman who wants to chat with Hannah after she reads her “report”, except that it's the last time you’ll ever see her. In the middle of the game, you’ll see another random cutscene where Hannah saves a boy from an abusive father, and it doesn't tie in with the game whatsoever. Also, there are a few cutscenes where the cutscenes become animated, but they show a completely different story, making them completely pointless.On top of all that, the voice acting, especially Hannah, is absolutely horrendous. The writing is awful, the jokes are cringe and the characters are just lifeless. It was as if the game's developers had thrown a bunch of random ideas together without bothering to make sure they made sense or had any real impact on the player. If you're looking for a game with interesting characters and a complete plot, I would recommend looking elsewhere.It is a mix between melee sword combat and cover-based shooter; you can either take cover behind a wall/object and shoot down enemies using your assault rifle that you can modify with different attachments, or go up close and personal using your trusty blade to parry attacks, perform gory finishers and carve up enemies. In addition, you are equipped with a pistol, which has infinite ammo that is mostly used to stun enemies at close range, as it does little damage and has a slow firing rate. You can also equip various weapons that are dropped from fallen enemies (grenade launcher, SMG, shotgun and so on), but you can’t modify those.Sadly, the gameplay is held back by poor design decisions and numerous bugs; there isn’t enough ammo for your rifle, you are pretty much defenseless against bullets as blocking doesn’t do much against them, enemies can stun-lock you with no way of escaping, the AI of the enemies and allies were flawed that they sometimes wander around aimlessly, and squadmates offer little to no help during fights (except for the doctor maybe, as he can revive you every once in a while). There’s also a skill tree where you can use your skill points to unlock underwhelming abilities that you should’ve had from the start (such as unlocking grenades, finishers, dodging and longer sword combos). I played the game on hard difficulty, and once you unlock some of those skills and master the parrying, it becomes a cakewalk. There aren't a lot of enemy types, and they consistently use the same scream sound effect after you defeat them. There are 5 bosses in total, and they all feel flat, with only two of them providing any real challenge. The game also includes a variety of minigames, such as karaoke, a ramen-eating contest, arcade games, and claw machines. While some of these are enjoyable, others suffer from bugs or just feel boring. I understand the appeal of including minigames in a large game like Yakuza or Persona, but in this case, they feel unnecessary, as the entire story, including some of its minigames, can be completed in under 5 hours (less than 4 if you skip the cutscenes).While the visuals in Wanted: Dead are passable for a PS3-era game, the level design leaves much to be desired.; the five long and linear levels lack variety and fail to create any memorable moments. You can find collectibles in the world, but they add little to the story or gameplay. The police station serves as your hub, until a certain point, and it is pointlessly large and mostly filled with empty rooms, it serves no purpose but to play the minigames (which you can access from the menu anyways), chat with random police officers and your dull squadmates.In addition, the checkpoints are so far apart that you will find yourself fighting multiple enemies in different areas for a long time, and that's where the real difficulty lies. This becomes frustrating when you get killed due to a bug or get stun-locked, and you have and then fight the same waves of enemies from the beginning. I also love how they tried to make the food physics realistic, but it comes out as awkward and bland. The game was pretty unoptimized; I experienced FPS drops and random crashes during missions. furthermore, there was a sheer number of bugs, such as enemies popping up out of nowhere, characters repeating the same lines over and over again, getting stuck in the same place (as well as enemies), dreadful keyboard controls that change every time you exit the game, the cover system that doesn’t work properly (enemies can still shoot you and your grenades sometimes hit the cover), camera shaking uncontrollably when playing one of the minigames, music sometimes stops during missions, and animation glitches. The songs are pretty good, as the soundtrack features famous 80s pop/rock songs, such as Maniac and 99 luftballons, but other than listening to them from the police station's jukebox, you can only get to hear a few of them during missions and minigames for some reason. Overall, I was extremely disappointed with this game; the storyline is lackluster, and the bugs make the gameplay frustrating. Visually, the game feels outdated, and the optimization is severely lacking. To make matters worse, they're charging a full $60 price tag for a game that only offers 5-6 hours of mediocre gameplay. While the soundtrack may be enjoyable, it's not good enough to justify purchasing the entire game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have had my eye on Wanted: Dead for a while but decided to wait for a discount because of the mixed reviews. Playing it has confirmed what I strongly suspected all along--this game is criminally underrated.Remember the days when every single third person action game wasn't an open-world borefest, a "choices matter" action RPG, a Soulslike, or some combination thereof? Wanted: Dead drops you in linear levels full of enemies and expects you to kill everything from beginning to end. In other words, everything is as it should be. The combat system is tons of fun with numerous ways to dispatch your enemies, blending hack-and-slash gameplay with the ability to aim down the gun sights FPS-style at any time, backed up with copious canned-animation melee fatalities.Everything is coated with PS2-era jank, and I suspect this is why zoomers have downrated the game. Wanted: Dead is not like Bayonetta or God of War in that those games allow you to look awesome and beat the whole game just mashing random buttons. Instead, Wanted: Dead will feel decidedly un-smooth to a buttonmasher, but amazingly fluid once one understands the combat system, with a fairly high skill ceiling. The graphics are nice and clean, but not cutting-edge. The story and voice acting don't have the highest production values, but are pretty entertaining in a Deadly Premonition type of way.Overall, Wanted: Dead feels quite a bit like a spiritual successor to Dead 2 Rights, which is a very good thing. You have the quick transitions between melee and shooting action, the cool canned fatalities, assists from NPC allies, and a similar cover system. The cover system could use more polish, but overall Wanted: Dead is a great pickup for anyone who misses the way games used to be made.  8.3 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Wanted: Dead

_childDocuments_.review: If it isn't clear, Wanted:Dead is one odd package. Its filled with weird cutscenes. Sometimes characters say things and I don't know what they mean. Stephanie Joosten is a character, "Tom Cruise" a boss, and its a shooter and slasher that seems to disorient fans of both. It also has a reception ranging from "frustrating mess", "doesn't know what it wants to be" to "just what I've been wanting".The most direct comparison is also an unfairly loaded one. To compare Wanted:Dead to the Wii U exclusive "Devil's Third" might as well be a kiss of death if you ask many, but the comparison is unavoidable: They have the same DNA, even as they take two different but similar paths. They also have the same frantic, punishing angle to action that seems to be Itagaki's style which it likewise shares with Ninja Gaiden, if nothing else. Whether a comparison to Devil's Third should be a red flag is something I question, but with that formula and no less jank than before, it's not hard to see why this title has people so split down the middle. At the same time, I don't know if I can adequately explain why I played through it several times and thought about it so much.Wanted's flaws are really upfront and trivial to expose. Wanted struggles with aiming that can behave strange and levels designs that don't always favor the cover gameplay. The blend of melee and shooting results in each compromising for the other, like cover that doesn't quite stick when you want, aiming that occasionally snaps off center and awkward movement in melee combat. Worse is enemy AI that can go spastic, darting from cover spots at jet-speed to pop in and out at rapid intervals to tease out missed headshots that matter not just for your precious ammo pool, but skill points. Swordplay offers no crutch either, as enemies block and punish sloppy button-mashing where death comes quick and a poorly timed parry can lay you flat without a chance to use  heals. While this feels (usually) fair on its own, sparse checkpoints can make these missteps lead to lengthy setbacks, as Hannah (unlike Ivan) doesn't have the modern-game kit of rejuvenating health and frequent checkpoints.During portions of the game, you can be left questioning if you've even been playing right at all when some segments feel off-balanced and solutions you carve out often feeling in-spite of the presented gameplay. Its not until later that you realize how disregarding certain mechanics set you on a road from mindless fun to frustration. You may find yourself trying to avoid the dangerous melee, but HardMode starves you of enough ammo for the more durable foes, forcing you into perilous sword fights that feel like erratic difficulty spikes. Most of these complaints dissolve once you get into the whole loop. Enemies don't feel so spongey when you learn to parry. Reviewers who just wanted to get through the game struggle when they realize you can't always ignore the melee for the shooting. If you do, Wanted feels turbulent when in actuality, it's just not being met on its terms. For one, the parry and counter windows couldn't be any more generous.When Wanted gets it right, it has moments of bliss. The (many) melee finishers fall within a sweet spot between brief and spectacular, and never disrupt the player's camera either, aiding an open feel between melee and shooting. When a segment spills enemies at you, both melee and ranged, it can be frantic and engaging going between the two, showing Wanted's combat really does have something going on.There's no puzzle solving, escorts, venturing off the main path or any deviating from an arcade-y base. I see why some called Wanted's combat repetitive, but instead I appreciated it not wasting time outside what it does well. You only get variety in the waves of enemies and areas you fight them in with few gimmicks. In its defense, if it needs it, there are minigames and a surprising amount of attention given to weaved them into the story. One is a full in-universe arcade shmup.The minigames make up about half the heap of bonus content stuffed in, like a number of (pretty damn great) cover songs, a whole albums worth of Stefanie Joosten tracks I didn't expect to like as much as I did, other collectibles, and the in-universe cooking show. The carefree flexibility allowed in the story is here, and the appeal is definitely not lost on me. Not everyone will appreciate it all, but I couldn't call the package bare.Wanted's story is frankly amazing. With a basket of cyberpunk narrative tropes, it doesn't attempt to remain coherent, not because of scope, but of sheer creative choice it seems. There's what feels like light mimicry of blockbuster films: A scenes where the police chief throws things and yells at your brash team, sure, and then it goes off in its own and you're in a ramen eating minigame. Why? To show that your sniper Herzog has deep knowledge of ramen, I think.When a story tries to be quirky (as a plea to humor), its pretty apparent. With Wanted it's hard to know which parts, if any, are meant to be tongue-in-cheek with its air of sincerity. Everything out-of-place is in-place. It's a mood you can't force or imitate and a big part of what makes the story so enjoyable. That's no small part due to the cast, as I can't quite say enough how I love this cast of characters. I really grew to like Zombie Unit by the end, and Hannah as a protagonist. She's written more like a heroine of an indie comic than a game character from Japan, whose personal story has some jarring implications and her voice, delivered slightly clumsy, makes her something special. I only wish we got to spend a bit more time with her. Wanted's story has the feeling of being rushed; Cinematics are cut strange. They still blind-side you in wonderful and unexpected ways, but they do leave gaps in the flow that feel unintentional. It leaves me curious why, but when I find myself hoping I'll get to see these characters in a future game somehow, I think they made something really special with these guys.So I'm surprised more people aren't talking about Wanted: Dead. Between the strange cuts, violence, the characters and even Joosten, it obtains its odd personality so effortlessly. Add in a craving for the kind of action games that often graced seventh gen and its authentically what many are wanting.At the same time, it's clearly not appealing to the every-gamer, but that's on them. If what makes a game good is polish and the parts all fitting nearly, its an easy job to rip into. But often the criticism just doesn't fit, exposing weird misunderstandings. Some reviews were bewildered to find Hannah's not a godlike Bayonetta or Dante in ability. It's an echo of when major gaming outlets heedlessly slung criticism at Devil's Third in such exaggerated fashion, reasonable takes were drown out. Wanted's thankfully been given more slack, likely owing to presentation that better communicates it as a throwback (so the tone didn't fly over the average reviewer's head).Still, no one can pretend Wanted isn't a very flawed game. There's a constant roughness and the technical issues glare. I wish it spent more time in the oven, because there's so much good here that just needed to go down smoother, and the story given an extra chapter. Do I think Wanted is a gem among flawed games or cult hit? I think so, but its price asks you to overlook many flaws.It may not be apparent unless reading between the lines here, but I really freakin' love this game. Not for the era it represents. Not ironically. It could be a number of things, but Wanted has lots of heart, enough to makes me want more and I think they really cared about what they were making, even as they needed to cut back and make compromises. At the end of a third playthrough, I was left thinking "I hope there's a sequel someday". Maybe I'm crazy but I really do wish that.

_childDocuments_.review: Like that episode of Pokemon featuring Porygon, Nintendo wants everyone to forget that Devil’s Third ever existed. This infamous Wii U game attempted to combine third person shooting with the swordplay that characterised the Ninja Gaiden series. Why am I bringing up this critical and commercial failure? It turns out the studio that gave birth to Devil’s Third, Valhalla Games Studio, had a sister company called Soleli. Not only did they acquire the assets of Valhalla but has recently created a spiritual successor of sorts. Entered Wanted Dead, the latest attempt from ex-Team Ninja employees to make a game like Ninja Gaiden but with guns. Is this the game that every man wants to be gifted on Valentine’s Day? Or is it simply dead-on arrival.Wanted Dead takes place in an alternative version of modern-day Hong Kong, where fashion and music from the 1980s is now in vogue for some reason. Amongst this bending of the space time continuum lies an ex-prisoner, turned cop called Hannah Stone. Who fights crime by moonlight and sings karaoke by daytime. The game features a tonne of cutscenes that are lengthy yet berthed of any substance. There are some genuinely funny scenes that put a smile on my face. But when the game attempts to tell a serious story, the flat acting and robotic animations doesn’t do the narrative any favours. Not to mention, the glaring use of low quality, BIK files to present parts of the game’s story. Which stick out like a sore thumb when compared to the real time cutscenes running in 4K. For those that are curious, the shower scenes are rendered in real-time. I’m sure David Cage will be pleased by this news.Thankfully the gameplay makes up for the spotty story telling with white knuckle action delivered straight to your address with extra blood. Like Devil’s Third, Wanted Dead tries to mesh swashbuckling with pew pew action. Think Ninja Gaiden meets Vanquish and you’re on the right track. The biggest problem with Devil’s Third was the poor balancing that meant almost every scenario favoured guns over swords. Which wasn’t great given the guns had the impact of a cashew. Fortunately the tables have been turned with Wanted Dead as the sword is by far the most useful item in your arsenal.Slicing and dicing enemies is super satisfying with blood flowing like cheap red wine. Hannah doesn’t feel as light as Ryu in Ninja Gaiden and controls like someone whose diet consists purely of Four N Twenty Meat pies. But the frantic nature of the fights with enemies coming from every corner is enough to keep the blood flowing. Unfortunately, the firearms in this game don’t have the same impact as the sword. The massive dead zone and poor feedback makes using any ballistic weapon a real chore. But except for a few hard-to-reach targets, you can take down the entire opposition with your trusty sword and forget the guns exist. To the game’s credit, this is probably the most action focused action game I’ve played in a long time. No quick time events or forced walking sequences. Pure, unadulterated carnage from start to finish.Hannah is joined by three other members in the appropriately named zombie squad. Doc stays true to his namesake by offering the ability to revive the player after their health is fully depleted. But you’re only good for one revival between each checkpoint. Cortex can stagger enemies, allowing Hannah to take them down with a finishing strike. The final person in your crew is Herzog, who will occasionally take out foot soldiers with a single bullet to the head.In between each mission, you’ll find yourself at the police station where you can talk to NPCs and play various minigames. Your fellow co-workers have the personality of mud that pales in comparison to the character building exhibited in the likes of Astral Chain. The minigames also feel undercooked with a ramen and karaoke minigame that both play like a poor man’s Taiko Drum Master. There’s also a Skill Tester where you unlock additional goodies and figurines. I do appreciate the figurines showing up on Hannah’s desk as you acquire each one. It’s little details like this that I enjoy seeing in video games. Rounding off the mini games is a vertical shooter called Space Runaway. Which I couldn’t play since the game wouldn’t stop shaking. I don’t know if this is an intentional design or a bug with the PC build of the game.Completing the game will take around 8-10 hours. You can play through the game again on a harder difficulty or mess around with any minigames you’ve unlocked. You can rewatch any cutscenes on the memories page, including multiple episodes of a cooking show parody called Vivienne’s Late-Night Chow. Which are generally funny and look like something ripped out of RobocopLike many modern games, Wanted Dead is powered by Unreal Engine 4. While the texture work and geometry detail is solid enough. The sloppy animation and flat lighting are a notch against the presentation. As for which version I played, I opted to play through the game on my PC equipped with a Ryzen 3700X and Nivida RTX 3070. My first impressions of the PC port were quite positive. Loading times were almost non-existence when using an NVME drive and HDR is on the table for once. Both FSR and DLSS upscaling algorithms are included. But like many Unreal Engine 4 games, Wanted Dead doesn’t perform a pre-compilation of shaders on the main menu. In other words, the shader compilation happens during gameplay. A process that causes a drop in framerate and affects the fluidity of the game. But even with the shaders compiled, performance will randomly drop like a stone regardless of the visual quality or upscaling technique being employed. The game also crashed on multiple occasions and a bug caused the skill tree to disappear, forcing me to start the game again from scratch.It's obvious that most of the game’s budget went towards producing the game’s terrific soundtrack. The developers of this game somehow managed to secure legendary music producer Giorgio Moroder. Best known for his work in films like Midnight Express, Flashdance and Scarface. The soundtrack is peppered with iconic 80s songs such as 99 Luftballoons and Manic. But there’s also a great selection of original songs sung by various guest singers and a fantastic score composed by Keiichi Sugiyama. Even if you don’t plan on playing the game, I insist that you check out the soundtrack on Spotify. It’s that good.Wanted Dead is at its finest when you’re slicing enemies like the onions in a favourite infomercial while rocking to the game’s brilliant soundtrack. The writing is woeful at best, but it still managed to get a few chuckles out of me. But everything else in this game feels underdeveloped and could have used a few extra hours in the oven. However, despite its many warts, I can still picture Wanted Dead developing a cult following amongst a small group of weirdos that miss the era of middle-ground games that were commonplace during the days of the PS2. Games with a clear beginning, middle and end without the chaff that plagues modern, open world games. If that sounds appealing to you, I think you might get a kick out of Wanted Dead. Although I would avoid the PC version like the plague as it’s not currently fit for service.

_childDocuments_.review: $20 well spent at sale price, picked it up just after the Dec '23 patch and it runs great. It's really exactly what I was hoping it would be - an early 2000's 3D action throwback. The story and cut scenes are nucking futz, the voice acting "so bad it's good," and the game-play for the weirdly specific vibe they're going for actually nails it. Similar to Dead to Rights in art direction and tone, but more like Oni, The Matrix: Path of Neo, or Ninja Gaiden in terms of how it actually plays. All in all, it's a lovely homage to (and pastiche of) an era of gaming that a particular audience is especially nostalgic for.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is a mess, but it's a mess with character. My time with the game was mostly spent questioning a series of baffling but entertaining design choices. Why does the main character have an almost incomprehensible Swiss accent? Why do parts of the story just seem to be sort of missing? Why does the Karaoke rhythm game have only one song while the Ramen eating mini-game has ten of them? Why did I unlock a video where Stephanie Joosten teaches me how to make a Lasanga? All of these decisions make the game an experience to play through. Not necessarily a *good* experience, but an entertaining one. The biggest negative in the game is probably the gameplay itself. Wanted Dead takes inspiration from a whole host of PS2/360 era action games. This was a great time for games, and we're seeing more and more games take inspiration from that era. The reality is that in 2023 no one really wants to play a B-game from a bygone era-  you want to play the idea of what a B-Game was like in your head with a bunch of modern conventions that make it play better. Wanted Dead's messy gameplay is more memorable of the poor designs of that time than it is the good ones.Despite all of this I'd still be willing to give the game a positive recommendation for the experience of how weird it was and how much I enjoyed the whole vibe it's trying to pull off but in the end it's really hard to justify it at a $60 price point. At full price this is a pretty easy pass but if you're down for a gonzo throwback experience it's a recommendation once it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The Yngwie Malmsteen of video games.It's kind of audacious just how much this game is trying to do. The whole experience is ridiculously entertaining.Have you ever liked [insert literally any action game]?Well, this game does it.Do you likeThis game does all of it, all at once, with wildly varying degrees of success.Did you like the Spider Tank boss from Ninja Gaiden 3? Of course not, no one liked that. Well, it's back in Wanted: Dead.The Wanted: Dead logo is like a stylized, upside-down, horizontally-flipped version of the Metallica logo.For some reason, the keyboard settings bind sword swings and firing the assault rifle to the left mouse button. This has to be changed every time I start the game. Every other setting I changed is remembered other than that one. If I forget to change it, I either can't shoot or can't use the sword.The in-game loading screen.Lieutenant Stone wears a necklace with two crosses, because one isn't enough.The amount of blood on Stone's face in-game and in cutscenes is ridiculous. Hilariously distracting.Exiting the game from the menu doesn't always stop the game in the background. At 1.8 hours, I exited the game to get lunch and think about it. Came back a while later and Steam said I was at 4.7 hours.The twelve cats at the police station. The cat tree. The cat on the cat tree.There are no Asian people in Hong Kong at all.I usually hate "games as movies" with long cutscenes, but the long cutscenes in this game are so absurdly compelling, I haven't skipped a single one.There are a ton of enemies in Level 3 with the exact same voice actor, all calmly taunting you as you carve them into pieces. They speak over each other in a cacaphony of violence and absurdity.Somehow, after everything it does wrong (which is almost everything), the game is still a lot of fun.It shouldn't work. It doesn't work. But it all comes together in one of the most memorable video games I can remember playing.The combat is great. Maybe the best combat since NG3:RE (which had excellent combat but a slew of other issues).I love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is advertised as a janky 2000's action game and I have no problem with that. You either get it or you don't and that's where the you love it or you hate it comes from. It's pretty much a Soulslike meets Ninja Gaiden with some John Wick looking glory kills sprinkled in and personally I love it. The moment to moment gameplay is simple but you can make it as complex as you want and that'll be the reason I'll keep replaying this for a long time. The game does need a bit of polish because it's rough around the edges and it could do with more content that's for sure. It's unique and if you're a fan of that era of action games I'd recommend it at full price otherwise wait for it to be on sale. I get this ain't everyone's cup of tea but I hope we see more of this in the future whether that's more content for this game, a sequel or even a completely different game from another developer. Hack and slash games are getting rarer I love the genre and would hate to see it disappear.

_childDocuments_.review: This day and age, just about everybody is a critic, too dramatic, and takes life way too seriously. This is the time for heart in games to return in my opinion, with all the depressing news on media. Not every game has to be photo realistic, The Last of Us acting, has the same mechanics as every other super-sized reskinned game out there. Play games because you want to and enjoy a game because it's meant to be just that: a fun and entertaining game. And this is what Wanted Dead is. Did the developers have to throw anime cutscenes in? Have elaborated cutscenes with parts that didn't need to be in it? A huge Police station to explore? Did the characters have to look as good as they do? NO. But the developers loved what they were creating and it shows with the budget they had. The more you master the game, the more the game keeps getting better. I'm on my third playthrough of the highest Japanese Difficulty. I like Detective Stone, her Swiss accent, and all of her comrades. The game doesn't rely on waypoints and distractions like most AAA games but on its core mechanics: combat and gunplay. They'll remind you throughout the campaign, that there's AAA talent behind the works, now and again by showing some great cutscenes, addictive gameplay, and world-building. If you're a true moderate/hardcore gamer who loves stylish action and fun sword and gunplay then you'll most likely love this game. It's that simple. But if you're a gamer who wants to clap at pretty fireworks and prefers the experience over learning/having a difficult challenge and enjoying something refreshingly quirky/different then this may not be for you. And that's okay, play something else.The real faults are that the game sometimes crashes and 2 cutscenes stutter very badly. But making sure that no other graphic card-eating software is opened helped improve the experience.This is far from a bad game, and glad I ignored some of the bad reviews. This is a jewel for me and others who played games from at least the PS1 era onwards.
_childDocuments_.name: Wanted: Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I can only recommend this game for people who get it via redeemable key for 5 bucks like me.There is a lot to unpack here as this is a really mixed bag. I will start with the good parts.The game follows agent Stone of and her notorious zombie squad who seems to be swiss judging by the accent.The zombie squad and the police headquarter have a cool vibe. The graphics and the character design rocks. Especially from the female protagonist. Likewise the title and loading screen really embody this cool touch.When the combat works, it is actually fun. The parries with the katana feel nice. The finisher come with lots of cool killing animations and on top of that a lot of severing of limbs regularly happens. There even is a chainsaw called beavertooth for some really gory gameplay.The skill trees are decent and reward the player with worthwile upgrades to both melee fighting, utility and defense.Apart from the fighting, the police HQ functions as the overworld hub. One can engage in minigames here like the shooting range, playing a crane game, karaoke, an arcade and one can play a rhythm based ramen slurping game.Additionally, the game included a lot of collectibles which in turn give xp for the skill trees and contribute to the lore, further adding to the replayability apart from score attack etc.Last but not least there is a jukebox with decent vocalized music songs in the HQ to play around with.Now the bad...The game has frequent fps drops and is too short with its few levels.Unfortunately the combat, while it can be action-packed. often feels quite janky. It feels as if this was patched together during development without sufficient QA resulting in an uncohesive mess of only 3 combos.This is further exacerbated by the fact that the enemies are friggin bullet sponges. The idea of a hybrid katana-bullet fighting game loop may be a thrill in theory, but the tankyness of the NPCs counteract the mechanics. Even with katanahits it takes way too long to kill an enemey or get a finisher in. This terrible balancing makes the battles a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ drag sometimes.And given how many enemies are coming at you at once and how quickly the HP of the player flatlines, making the the enemies so spongy is an incredibly bad design choice voiding most redeemable aspects of the somewhat decent mechanics. Even having a. revival once per checkpoint does not rectify this as the checkpoints are quite punishing leading to a lot of loss of progress and replaying mundane passages of the levels. How infuriating...The scarcity of ammunition in the game makes this quite problematic.Now the dialogue and cutscenes...oh boyOverall negative remark is that the volume is mixed inconsistently showing a lack of quality control.The game does not take itself to seriously which is a good thing in this case.However, the direction of dialogue is bizarrely comical at best and painfully cringe at worst. One joke in the elevator made by one of the squad members was along the lines "dad I woke up with four balls" ending on the punchline "you are getting ♥♥♥♥♥♥, son". Profanity fits the setting of the zombie squad but some of the dialogue is just painfully cringe like when talking to the gunsmith for instance.At least the game is bizarrely funny by this hodgepodge of weird design choices and certainly makes you chuckle.Then I encountered a bug at in the spider mech bossfight. The boss got stuck in a doorway and became somewhat untargetable and ultimately unkillable leading to me reloading the checkpoint.The game deserves all the negative reviews overall and I understand why it averages a mixed review score on steam. However most reviews only amount to one or two sentences and I thought to be fair and at least give this beautiful mess a comprehensive review.A lot of players who are unsure about whether they want to buy this will have a negative experience due to stun lock when taking damage and the challenging placements of checkpoints. Overall a diffiicult game with quirky voice acting.I wish this game was as good as cool the character design of the protagonist Stone is.But this game looks significantly better than it indeed is.You’ll doubt the sanity of the development team, but the they tried and it is somewhat enjoyable.At least Detective Stone's backstory is shown in nice anime cutscenes.5/10 rating.It sucks for full price but I love it!

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is really a unique game and how I like my action games, hectic, chaotic and combines two fantastic genres in 1 game: shooters and slashers, add some bloody scenes in the shooting and slashing and you already get a nice view of the gameplay.Speaking of gameplay, feel free to check out a snippet here: The story is spread over a total of five different levels, but in between you can walk around the police station and you will be presented with minigames or cutscenes.You fight enemies with your katana or with weapons, but the deadliest option is a mix of both. You have an assault rifle with which you can kill enemies at a distance, but you also have a pistol with which you can perform combos together with the katana, which also provide great finishers where even the body parts fly around.After a while you will learn how the different combos work and which weapons work when.In other words: get good.The game also has good support for playing at ultra-wide resolutions, you can see a vb at 3840*1080 here: I must admit that I did not dare to test the “hard difficulty” mode, I leave that to you.What I do know is that each level has several old school checkpoints and fortunately, the levels can quickly run up to an hour per level, and you will occasionally have to deal with difficult boss fights throughout the level. No, I'm not lying, in these boss fights you will have to master your deadly maneuvers.You can upgrade your weapons with better parts that increase its strength, but you can also strengthen Stone itself with new skills that affect her attack or defense. This costs you pennies that you earn throughout the game. Her team can also provide you with upgrades, because you always take them with you at the different levels and they provide support.Wanted: Dead also works perfectly on the steam deck:

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game... The trailers and gameplay looks absolutely fantastic.. that is until you get your hands onto it.. it is very janky. The attacks are not smooth at all. In the tutorial it shows you a combo by mixing your pistol attack and your melee attack and it ends up coming out as, swing, akward pause shot, awkward pause, then wonky swing. The story from my experience is kind of all over the place. The random minigames that you cant skip and are too long are unneeded and to me quite annoying. Its like they tried to put too much into this and it ended up coming out as a big mess of things.  It is definitely an awesome concept, but needs to be polished heavily. Hopefully the gameplay gets worked on a bit and smoothed out. I'm going to trek my way through the rest of the story to see if it gets any better, but as of right now the main killer for me is the gameplay... oh and gotta add.. the constant ear ringing from the enemy spamming grenandes.. i can deal with the same scream because its quick and done as soon as you move onto the next, but that damn grenade ringing.. ugh

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a massively underrated gem that will have a cult following in the future, mark my words.The off-kilter energy of the storytelling and unconventionally delivered voice-acting hide an actually interesting plot, and the strange sense of humour the game carries had me grinning and laughing pretty hard. I ended up getting more attached to the characters than I expected and the overall strangeness was worth the price of admission alone for me.Combat wise, which makes up the bulk of the game barring some appreciated downtime exploring a police station where everyone hates you and singing 99 Luftballons down at the Karaoke, while it initially seems a little basic, having now beaten the game on 'Japanese Hard' there is a lot of hidden mechanical depth here that helped me a lot, like guard cancelling and implementing third person shooting into combos. The combat flows beautifully and has some of the most brutally awesome animation I have seen in this genre. I have never seen a game combine third person cover shooting and 'character action' combat so seamlessly, and it never failed to get me pumped doing so.The amount of heart put into this production is clear in every aspect, even if it's a little rough around the edges with some minor bugs, like for example having to switch to fullscreen every time I start the game because the settings wouldn't save, but it's all forgivable when this thing is such a joy to behold and not something I'm going to forget anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a deeply flawed, eccentric action game with incredible personality. The script often feels like it was written by aliens but the most of the characters are endearing and fully realized. Parts of it feel like a game that they couldn't finish so they scrambled together whatever they could, but then there are numerous scenes--often depicting something hilarious mundane--that are filled with the kind of little details that most games overlook entirely. Wanted: Dead is a strange one, perhaps this generation's Deadly Premonition, and I the more I think about it, the more I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those "I wish there was a middle option on steam reviews" moments because while I do recommend Wanted:Dead I do so both with the warning that I don't recommend it at full price (£50 as of writing) and that it's honestly not that good of a game... kind of.... Wanted:Dead is weird in a lot of ways xDI guess the best way to describe it is as one of those weird Xbox 360/PS3 cult classics that everyone kind of forgot about at the time but then years later some people who played it when they were younger have some fond memories about it so occasionally bring it up in conversation again but then they never really go back to replaying it so all their memories of why it's good are a bit rose-tinted and sanded down after like 15 years... You know the kind of thing I'm talking about right?It's not very well optimised, the gameplay is jank, the acting is really awkward and poorly sound balanced, the story is both really simple and yet told in a way that is often just unclear and confusing. It's often got frustrating checkpoint placements, not very good boss fights, a weird karaoke minigame that lets you play "99 Luftballons" and nothing else; the game is meant to be a hybrid hack 'n' slash and 3rd person shooter but the sword-fighting sometime makes the camera go insane and then the aim assist occasionally aims to the right of the target and doesn't let you move it left... This game is sometimes genuinely terrible.And yet it's oddly nostalgic and charming; those moments where it works are really satisfying, the cutscenes are so weird that they're just fun to watch and laugh at with mates, and then out of nowhere there's like 2 or 3 moments where the quality of the storytelling skyrockets and does something really interesting before immediately crashing down again (nightclub cutscene, I'm looking at you!), without spoiling it I'll just say if you stick around for the post-credits scene it genuinely makes the story way more interesting than it has any right to be and I wish they went with that angle of the story way more than they do. Wanted:Dead is so weird but it's also something that isn't devoid of good ideas; it often feels like the product of something more ambitious being cut down in many ways (some of the adverts for the game give far more details and story to the world than the entire game does...Not joking, if you go on the "110 Industries" channel and watch the "game world overview trailer", "Vivienne's Late Night Chow", and "She works hard for the money" you will know more about the world and some of the characters than the game itself will ever tell you, it's genuinely bizarre). But I can't deny that the moments where this game gets it together for 10 seconds to show you some absolutely crazy finisher animation or giving you a level with enough cover in it that you can actually avoid gunfire consistently to eliminate individual targets with your sword is kind of awesome; there's a world out there where this game was amazing, we don't live in that world but... I honestly hope the devs try again, I genuinely want a sequel because there is absolutely something here that you only get to see glimpses of while playing.Wanted:Dead is not a great game...But I found my time playing it ultimately a net positive, it is not a strong recommendation, but for all of its problems, I think there are others out there who will find some odd nostalgic charm in this thing, not despite the flaws but instead because of them, and for those like me who'll have that experience, just know that you are about to hear Herzog shout "grenade!" a lot.... Enjoy :)
_childDocuments_.name: Wanted: Dead

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun ive had with a game in a long time. I humbly ask you to give it a shot as well. Here's why:Wanted: Dead is very traditional when it comes to character action games which is a good thing, it's also to be expected since the developer team consists of a lot of the prior Ninja Gaiden & Dead or Alive devs.You shouldn't expect any modern Bayonetta or DMC type aspects, no no no, you gotta get very technical and lab your moveset out like in a fighting game. (It has a literal training mode just for that.) After that the game will open up for you. You need to learn to use the guard cancel for your advantage so you are positive on block. Always move around, use spacing to your advantage. Run, dash, slash. The gunplay combined with the melee, guard cancels and dodge rolls will all come together if you are willing to learn it.The game offers a nice variety of enemy types which all have their respected movesets. These enemies are no joke either, they are insanely aggressive and will push you out of any cover you are trying to take. It's no Ninja Gaiden but it's quite high up there.Playing the game on Japanese hard mode with the whole skill tree unlocked, that's where it's at.The game flies off the handle with the story, characters, voice acting, mini-games etc. It's really refreshing to see.GOTY 2023!

_childDocuments_.review: Being a ninja cop was a lot of fun! It can be a difficult game but if I was stuck on an enemy or boss battle. I just needed to parry a bit better.It has the Dialog similar to The Room and Deadly Premonition, enough mini games to rival Yakuza game, and combo based combat that strings many of your finishers together which is all a fun time!That being said, if you do not parry the game can be very difficult to a frustrating degree and I think I had 3 crashes during my playtime. If you can look past the jank you have here a very entertaining B movie like game to run through on a weekend!
_childDocuments_.name: Wanted: Dead

_childDocuments_.review: You know when you're watching one of those films that's so bad it's actually brilliant? Well, that’s Wanted: Dead for you. Bloody hell.The voice acting... oh my God, the voice acting. It's like they grabbed random people off the street and said, "Here's your line, just say it like you're ordering a coffee while having an existential crisis." There's this protagonist, Hannah, right? She delivers her lines like she's simultaneously trying to save the world and figure out what she had for breakfast. Brilliant.And then there's the story... I mean, one minute you're in this gritty cyberpunk shootout, proper serious business, and the next you're in a bloody ramen-eating contest. It's like someone took The Matrix, Blade Runner, and a Japanese game show, threw them in a blender, and said "That'll do."But here's the thing, right? It's actually... good? Like, properly good in that "what the hell am I playing and why can't I stop" kind of way. The combat's this mental mix of shooting and slashing that somehow works despite having no right to. It's like if John Wick went to anime school and forgot half the lessons.You've got these cutscenes that look like they were animated by different studios who never spoke to each other. One minute it's all realistic, next minute it's full anime, then suddenly you're watching what looks like a cooking show. It's like channel-surfing while having a fever dream.And you know what? This game is exactly what we need right now. In an era where everything's so polished and focus-grouped to death, here comes this absolutely bonkers title that feels like it was made by people who just thought, "Sod it, let's put everything in." It's the gaming equivalent of ordering everything on the menu because you can't decide what you want.So yeah, should you play it? Absolutely. Just don't expect it to make sense. It's like watching a B-movie marathon while playing Dark Souls and eating sushi - it shouldn't work, but somehow it does. And if anyone tells you they fully understand what's going on, they're lying. They're absolutely lying.Science is still trying to figure out how something this gloriously stupid can be this bloody good. And you know what? I hope they never do. Sometimes the best things in life are the ones that make absolutely no sense whatsoever.
