_childDocuments_.review: I got sent a key for this game from the devs, so be aware of that as it might color my review a bit as biased towards them. /sThe review: This game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks.Seriously, I cannot remember a time where I legitimately rage quit a game before this. This is coming from the guy that sat through to the credits of Balan Wonderworld in one sitting. I play most of the things that developers send me and only quit for 2 reasons, the game is either unfinished or unfun. This game is both of those things.As far as being unfinished, I cannot legitimately think of something quite so confused as to what it wants to be as this one. This game is like Deadly Premonition levels of whiplash as far as whats going on and what people are saying and doing. The story makes zero sense. The characters are genuinely some of the worst voiced I've ever heard in a game, especially considering the budget size of this game. There's a lot of really weird tone issues too. The game is supposed to be set in Hong Kong, but everyone speaks English and there are English words written all over, the main character is Russian (I think) and the officers in the police station all have British accents. Its wildly confusing. On the topic of voices, beyond the voice acting being bad you also hear the same voice lines 10,000 times. Its Xenoblade Chronicles 2 levels of bad.The biggest issue I have also ended up being one of the more entertaining parts. The dialogue in this game had to be written by AI. You cannot convince me otherwise. I streamed this game and the amount of times both myself and people in my chat just sat there going "WTF" was absurd. It was so weird that I genuinely don't think I can describe it to you accurately. Go spend 5 minutes in someones stream watching this game and you'll see what I mean, unless they are in one of the combat missions, in which case you will see the second part of the twofold reason I quit on this game.Unfun. See, when you market your game as "the makers behind Ninja Gaiden and Dead or Alive" expectations are set. What the marketing did not say is that this specific developer team has only made essentially 3 games now. A ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Naruto game (its ♥♥♥♥♥♥ FOR a Naruto game, which is saying something), Valkyrie Elysium which is probably the most universally ♥♥♥♥ on Square Enix game from last year, and now Wanted Dead. All 3 of these games are disappointing and things seem to be getting worse with time. The combat in general can feel okay sometimes when it flows as intended, but 99% of the time its just frustrating. The goal, I think, is that you don't focus your attention on any one enemy, instead dashing around and using your pistol and guns to stun enemies out of attacking you while your back is turned then go back to slashing. The reality is that your sword is basically a pool noodle and you are shooting Nerf guns. I played on the normal difficulty, and I could not believe how many shots these things took. 31 with the pistol, 22 with the AR, yes I counted. The enemies are such damage sponges that you can't really play the way I think they wanted you to, and they do far too much damage to you as well. Stun locks on the player happen very frequently. The final straw for me was when I got stuck in an alley in a fire. The animation for being damaged in a fire lasts so long, that if you are still in the fire (you will be, the animation doesnt move you back at all) you get stun locked into burning to death. You cant heal, you cant dodge out, you just die. And thanks to the godawful and just straight up annoying checkpoint system (you go back to the start of the level almost regardless) you just end up doing the whole thing over and over again. As I burnt to death by stunlock and was about to ALT-F4, the game did it for me! It crashed, for the 5th time in 4 hours. Forgot to mention it before but yeah I can confirm even on my high end 2 pc streamer rig the game runs like ♥♥♥♥.I'm genuinely really disappointed in this one. I think there was a really fun idea here that just got executed on so, so poorly. I legitimately spent an hour playing the crane game and ramen rhythm game rather than the main story because I was dreading the combat that much. Its not hard, its just poorly made and frustrating. I'd like to say I'll go back another time and finish this, but barring a major update that fixes the big issues, I won't be reinstalling Wanted: Dead. I got this game for free and still feel a little scammed. For any prospective buyers, consider yourself warned. Wanted: Dead will quickly turn into Wanted: Refund for you.If you made it this far, I normally review games only after completing them, the last couple I've done though I've stopped a bit short, but I do my best to give a good overview of what a game is, and following my curator page helps. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat system is very good and deep as it forces you to experiment and find your own style that works for you. You can mix katana strikes and block and parry and dodge with handgun counter and general handgun and other weapons shots. Finishing moves that you can perform are probably the best part of the combat because they look nice and feel satisfying. It is a very rich and interesting system that requires you to get better at it if you want to defeat more difficult enemies while not really requiring almost anything from you when you fight the general weak enemies. Like killing basic soldiers in stage 1 or android workers in stage 2 or bouncers in stage 3 is easy as all it takes is a few shots or few katana hits.But killing ninja enemies that also have katanas or big exoskeleton enemies that carry heavy machine guns is much harder as you have to get really good at parring their attacks in order to win because they are fast moving bullet sponges that will do their best to dodge your shots and get close to you and it will be easier and faster to kill them with katana than it is with guns. But thankfully you can also cheese ninjas with fire grenades because if they will start to burn they won’t dodge any of the bullets making them easy to kill with guns or you can use fire grenades to separate one ninja from the other so you can fight 1 vs 1 making the fight easier. Because your handgun is the only weapon in the world that has unlimited ammo you can even cheese ninjas by just shooting them a few times and dodging away till they are dead. I also find it funny how the brown ninja will die from a propane tank explosion but it will take 2-3 grenade launcher shots to kill him.Enemies wearing exoskeleton are the hardest enemies and the biggest problem in the game if you try to use things like guns or grenades against them. Thankfully they are not intelligent at all so despite having all that armor and heavy machine gun and infinite amount of grenades that they can use to destroy you from a distance they prefer to charge you and fight with you in melee trying to hit you with their heavy machine gun. Thanks to them being just stupid the best way to kill them is to parry their hits and do gun counters and slash them with a katana. The funny thing is I tested them and they will survive 3 whole magazines from your assault rifle or 12 shots from grenade launcher without problems but 12 combos from a katana will kill them. I guess they are just coded in a way to be a bullet sponge of the worst kind where katana deals more damage to them than anything else that exists in the game. Funny thing is that 12 shots from grenade launcher is enough to destroy stage 1 boss and that boss is a tank but they are not enough to kill a guy in exoskeleton. I guess the only reason tanks are produced in this world is because they actually use their weapons to shoot at enemies instead of trying to fight them in melee like the exoskeleton guys. Thankfully these exoskeleton guys can be killed with one hit from a chainsaw just like any enemy in the game.Sadly your squad attacks mean nothing and deal almost no damage. I think their guns should fire paintballs at enemies for added realism of how useful they are. It feels like the teammates that are with you exist only to be a distraction so you won’t get swarmed than any real help in combat. I think the most important skill they have is screaming “grenade” when enemies throw one at you and that the Doc will heal you once when you are down. Thankfully there are skill trees and in that skill trees there are even skills to make your squad a little better but these will probably be the skills that you will pick last as after seeing your squad in action you will just focus on improving your own skills to kill faster and survive longer. Oh where to start… The voice acting of our main hero Hannah Stone is the worst. It shows no emotion and it sounds like someone did just read a script and after googling it out I was surprised that it was made by a real living person and not just a computer reading the text. But the voices of everyone else are not at all much better. And the whole way anyone speaks or moves or gestures in the cutscenes is just bad. Thankfully when we see Hannah Stone remembering her past life it is done as anime and these animations are much better. I think all cutscenes should be done by the same person that did these animations because they are the only good looking cutscenes in the whole game. Thankfully cooking videos that you can find in claw machine are also funny.And the claw machines and the shooting range are the only good mini-games that this game has. Eating ramen is ok – I admit I’m bad at rhythm games but still I can see that this mini-game is just ok as it is about mashing 8 different buttons but at least you can find additional tracks to play in the claw machine. The karaoke mini-game is just bad. It is just the copy of ramen mini-game somehow made to be worse. Not only it has only one song and that song is 99 Luftballons but there are no other songs to collect anywhere in the game. I can’t imagine why they created this mini-game in the first place just for one song. The last mini-game is the side-scrolling shooter called Space Runaway and sadly it is bugged. I saw other people on youtube that were able to play it how it was intended but mine was set in a way that I saw only about 50% of the screen and my mech and enemies were huge.And the bug with Space Runaway was not the only bug I had and I think it was connected with graphic settings bugs. Each time I did exit the game the graphic settings were resetting so I had to set them again to my liking changing from 60 to 144 fps and changing the blur to 0 and forcing the game to be launched in full screen mode and not just in a window. Sometimes grenades bounce back to me and the grenade launcher shots explodes in the front of my face because they are hitting some invisible wall in the air. The worst bug was with the unique weapon that you can win from shooting range – not only it is weaker than your own assault rifle – it is even hard to swap this weapon out for your normal assault rifle at checkpoints. When I was testing that weapon there were many times where I had to try 5 or more times to swap back to my normal assault rifle at checkpoints for the game to even recognize that I don’t want to use it anymore.The worst part of the game is the story. Parts about Hannah Stone make sense but there are multiple holes in the rest of the story and many things that never get addressed. Why enemies in stage 1 did steal money if it can’t be used in this part of the world? How losing that money that can’t be used makes the most famous company go bankrupt over night? Why the police force that is famous for killing all suspects all the time would be send to stop a protest and why they would start by just killing protesters with a sniper rifle from a helicopter? And why a few days later after murdering more than 100+ of such protesters their leader would be ok with helping us? There are many holes in the story like that. Also many cut-scenes add additional informations that are never addressed again.The whole game is just 5 stages connected by a story that makes little to no sense in the end. It looks like the story is only there to push the player from stage to stage. This game would be much better with no story at all – just fighting stages and nothing in between them. Good combat and bad everything else combined with 40$ price.Rating: 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is a game that makes me angry and to be honest games are not really something that I get angry at very often.It made me angry not because of its clunky gameplay, bizarre difficulty curve, or clumsy mechanics; it made be angry because of a strange sense of betrayal.Like many I had been lured in and colored intrigued by the many trailers and gameplay teasers leading up to the games release. The aesthetic looked fantastic, the premise of shooting and carving your way through swathes of enemies as a cyborg taskforce was tantalizing. The 80s style anime trailer, featuring Donna Summer's "She works hard for the money", was just the icing on the cake. I couldn't wait to get my hands on this game. Really I have no one to blame but myself for my disappointment. In life we learn to temper our expectations and even more so in the video game sphere. Launch day bugs, performance/optimization issues and unfinished games are unfortunately all too common.However in the case of Wanted: dead, I allowed myself to get caught up in the hype, only to be firmly regrounded and thoroughly disappointed.Created by 110 industries and Tokyo based Soleil, on paper the game has excellent pedigree. Soleil are responsible for some decent output including: Ninjala, Valkyrie Elysium and Naruto. Most notably Ninja Gaiden which, if the marketing is to be believed, carries its DNA into this game. The premise sees you take on the role of protagonist Lt. Hannah Stone the leader of a special task force called 'zombie unit', hacking, slashing and shooting your way through a dystopian, cyberpunk vision of Hong Kong.Graphically the game does look really nice, but that's really where any praise I can honestly give the game ends.It's a clumsy mix of cover shooter and close quarter hack and slash, however it does neither of these elements well and is a complete chore to play.The shooting feels cumbersome on a controller. Compounded by the fact that more often than not, your view will be obscured by your own characters head or body making it doubly difficult to aim. If you do manage to aim correctly, you will find that ordinary rank and file soldiers, will take upwards of 10 shots to dispatch. That's getting on for half a magazine and ammo is particularly scarce in this game.Low availability of ammunition, along with the seemingly infinite supply of grenades that the enemy has, seems to force you out of cover and into close combat. It seems as though this is the way the game wants you to play and I would be perfectly fine with that if it were fun ....which it is not.The game is being pushed as a difficult, almost souls like experience and it has souls like melee controls to match. But this is where all similarities end.Melee combat feels just as clunky and awkward as the cover shooting. The AI for both enemies and your team seems almost placeholder in its stupidity.The whole time you are engaged in close quarter combat, there are still a plethora of bullet sponges shooting at you and tossing grenades from behind cover.... Seriously where are they getting all of these grenades from? Soulslike games are always very difficult but at the same time very fair, learning patterns, repetitions along with well-timed parries and Dodges will soon earn victory.Wanted: Dead just throws seemingly mindless enemies at you until you die.Going back to a checkpoint isn't so much part of the learning curve as it is simply frustrating because very rarely will you ever feel that your last death was justified. There is a 'limb sever' mechanic and slow motion chained kills, which both look very cool but only the first few times. It's just gimmick and very quickly wears out it's welcome. Paper over the cracks. In summary Wanted: Dead is a deeply frustrating and very unpleasant experience.An awkward 'frankensteins monster' of a game, with different genres stitched together with no real cohesion.The core gameplay and ai is so flawed that even pretty graphics and some genuinely 'genius level' marketing can't carry it.Avoid at all costs, one of, if not THE worst game I've played this year.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 3 hours in and... wow. This feels like an early Xbox 360 game from an alternate dimension where Swery decided to make straight up action games instead of... weird mystery adventure games. This is Premium Trash, and honestly? I'm here for it.I understand the mixed reviews - those first two boss fights were ROUGH, and I'm sure they don't get much better. The combat is strange too, with an uneven mix of mediocre 3rd person shooting and surprisingly competent, albeit jank feeling hack and slash action. The first hour of the game absolutely felt like a slog until I understood what the game actually wanted from me, and after a few unlocks in the (rather small) skill tree, thankfully things did start to feel decent, with plenty of combo kills and dismemberment to reward my patience.The writing is... uh... it is very clear that the writers knew exactly what tone they were going for, and while I'm not sure what that tone IS, I'm sure they're nailing it. It can be VERY funny, though rarely intentionally, and many of the line reads and choices of subject matter will have you scratching your head. It's not good writing, but it IS interesting, in its own way.Also, because I have to mention them - the minigames. There are... so many. Karaoke, claw machines, arcade games... They're taking a page out of Yakuza here, and I can really appreciate that the developers opted to have a little fun with this weird thing they've created. Again, this probably deserves the mixed reviews - it's not for everyone, and while I'm generally having a good time wondering what the hell the game will throw at me next, I could see many folks getting super frustrated with some of the choices made here.Ultimately, I think if you're curious and can appreciate weird, jank video games, this is worth a (discounted) buy. It is so uniquely itself in every moment, and that's kind of awesome to see. At the very least, Wanted: Dead has kept me guessing, and in a sea of ultra-predictable, depressingly samey experiences, I'm thankful for it.

_childDocuments_.review: This games reception is absolutely criminal. Its fantastic. One of the best character action games of this generation. Cyberpunk style with 80-90's cop film tropes. Cool synthwave music, lots of cheese and terrible voice acting, in a good way. Think the original resident evil to those ends. Hard as nails, and if you play harder difficulties, unless you master the combat system, you will get beat down repeatedly. The combat is hard to explain. It flows like devil may cry or ninja gaiden, with the stiffness of a souls game. Which is actually to its advantage, as if you dig, theres depth here, with block cancelling, parrying, dash loops and whatnot. The sword does the most damage at first glance, but if you learn the unexplained mechanics, certain attacks are good to block cancel, into ads headshots with your rifle, which actually combo. Just trust me, learn to mix the shooting with the sword as intended, and the depth reveals itself.  Dont just play the first level, run out of ammo in the first room, decide the shooting sucks, then start using your sword on rooms of armed soldiers just to get killed repeatedly and decide the game sucks. Theres the occasional bug, but it hardly detracts from the experience. You dont play this for the story, you play this for the combat. And the combat is awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: I  wanted to like this game.  Hack n slash shooting with a cyberpunk setting and goofy rhythm-like mini games that plays like a ps3/xbox 360 game sounds perfect for me on paper.Unfortunately the game is too clunky.  Enemies zoom past your screen when trying to aim with your gun and block every sword attack making it so you have to slow the game down and wait for them so you can parry.  I'll be waiting for Enemy 1 to melee so I can parry, meanwhile Enemy 2 is shooting full auto at me from 30 feet away.  Which would be fine if the damage taken wasn't so ridiculous.  You can die in 2 seconds from an enemies' 3 hit combo and the checkpoints can be pretty far apart.I can deal with bad voice acting but my god, it makes me think I could make a living being a voice actor without any training.Really what killed it for me was the game crashing though.  Multiple times I would defeat a boss or enter a new area (after dying over and over), and then receive a FATAL ERROR which closes the program.  Boot the game back up, and now I have to redo the last 15-20 minutes since the checkpoints are so spread out.  I had just under 2 hours of gameplay and had to make a decision on whether or not to refund the game, which I did unfortunately.I will definitely give this game another shot in the future if they patch the game or it releases on game pass or something.  But for now, it's not even worth the $20 I spent on it.

_childDocuments_.review: It physically pains me to have to write a negative review for this game. There is a lot to love in Wanted: Dead: Its fast paced combat, John Woo action scenes and fun and unique blend of melee and ranged warfare.But the bottom of the line is: there is even more to dislike.For a game that is trying to brutally hard: why do none of its systems to keep you out of harms way work reliably?Cover system? Doesn't work reliably, you'll find yourself out of cover when you want your character to be in cover. Have fun eating lead when you should be in cover.Parrying? Doesn't work reliablyAttacking? Shame but again, doesn't work reliablyStopping an unblockable move? Doesn't work reliablyYou want to do one of those cool finishing moves that the game has to offer?Well tough luck, it doesn't stop you from receiving damage, you'll catch a torrent of grenades being flung at you and just die the instant the animation is done playing. Quit having fun!It's just frustrating in the end: this is a game I really want to like, but it's far from ready and is already being sold at $60.It's a crying shame but I look forward to returning to this game one day and having all of its giant issues be at least adressed.

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you combine interesting gameplay, stellar game design, well-judged humor and taut writing in one of the most refreshing and memorable character action game in years?A "Mixed" overall on Steam.The sheer amount of hate this game is getting is upright disappointing but not surprising. Gaming Industry as a whole has been oversaturated with infinite slop that resembles anything but a video game. Biased journalists & gamers alike are in shambles in the mere presence of Wanted: Dead, they can't get themselves together, they are absolutely infuriated and feel completely insulted at the thought of a game being an actual game, playing like an actual game, and challenges the player... like an actual game. Wanted: Dead wears its influences on its sleeve and stays true to its roots, with a difficulty option literally called the "Japanese Hard Mode" telling you all you need to know about its direction. It is by no means an easy game, and it knows that. The fluidity of combat, which most haters here cite as "janky" is nothing but a spark of genius by reintroducing traditional game design to the modern age, each enemy encounter feels unique and requires the player to adapt to different strategies in order to succeed to different stages. Speaking of stages, one of the complaints most people have here is the length, its short but its meant to be short. Level design is very reminiscent of the old Arcade, SNES and Genesis titles where you have multiple parts to a single stage, just like the original Ninja Gaidens or Shinobi games, having checkpoints scattered around each stage fulfills that very exact purpose. Overall with the learning curve of the game and its mechanics, including the side content, took me about 14 hours to complete in Hard Mode, and I'm definitely going for multiple playthroughs afterwards because of the addictive, visceral combat it offers. At any point, it never gets stale when you get the flow going, the controls are very responsive to the players inputs which is a huge plus that many recent action games ignore unfortunately. Besides all the hate its getting, lets focus on the love it was given by the developer team. With the sheer amount of extra advertisement put out for the marketing, you can't do anything but smile from the sheer love that was put into for all of them for the sake of building the lovely world of the game and expanding on its colorful cast, more notably featuring Stefanie Joosten of MGS V fame putting her best in the game's advertisements:Including putting out some bangers along the way as well!You can just tell she had one hell of a good time.Overall, I believe all the recent hate the game is getting will get overshadowed and receive a cult classic status like any other game with a rough critical start, like Ninja Gaiden II or Deadly Premonition (which the game resembles very heavily, including the acting department)Approach cautiously with an open mind. As Wanted: Dead does not forgive with its difficulty, but once mastered, will truly hook the player right into its core.

_childDocuments_.review: (Ignore my playtime for this game as Steam did not record my playtime offline.)I had a ridiculously fun time with this game; the combat was refreshing as I alternated between third-person shooter and hack-and-slash. The inherent charm that came from this game for me was that the game didn't take itself seriously. I would go from a gritty cinematic to playing a rhythm game and singing karaoke.Story (Spoilers)War criminals turned cops work to quell an uprising caused by a labor force of human-looking robots gone rogue.(I wish they had done more with this story line, instead of getting bogged down with the common cliches of if robots had souls and what differentiates a person from a machine, the corporation was evil all along, etc.)However, it wasn't the story that made this game for me but rather the characters that populated it. Despite the voice acting each character adds an interesting dynamic to the team which makes for great scenes.CombatHaving a hard time making the perfect parry during a sword fight? It's nothing your assault rifle and a pack of incendiary grenades can't fix. All encounters, except for one boss fight, can be approached as a third-person shooter or hack-and-slash game. Find the approach that you enjoy the most and level up that skill tree, it's as simple as that. I went into this game optimizing my rifle and combat skills for faster more fluid game play.The only two bad spots for me when playing this game for me were the godawful Ramen eating rhythm game and the final boss fight. The Ramen Rhythm game:The Ramen eating rhythm game is an unskippable mini game that does everything wrong you could do with a rhythm game. The visual was boring, the music used was the equivalent of what you'd hear in an elevator, and the game play was irritating due to button commands and no discernible rhythmic beat. What astounded me was that the Karaoke mini game was so well done and enjoyable that I got immediate whiplash.The Final Boss Fight (Spoilers):Let me put this simply the boss fight was the equivalent of rubbing sandpaper between you're palms. It's mildly annoying at first until it becomes an unbearably painful experience. Everything I loved about the games combat was immediately forsaken and opted for you to parry each attack perfectly in an uneven sword fight. The boss does not take damage from your grenades or guns, so the only option is to attack him with your sword. In most cases, this would be fine except that he can begin his player-killing combo at any time reducing your health in mere moments if you haven't been parrying his strikes. If that wasn't bad enough at his final stages he will run off to heal himself and you have to attack him with your sword to stop him from undoing all of your progress. During those moments it was equally frustrating because you needed to hit him once and constantly dodge before he immediately begins his combo. Honestly, I wish the boss fight on the rooftop had been the final boss fight, it was my favorite fight combining both gunplay and swordplay. The fight pushes the player to think outside the box for how best to uncover the location of the invisible assassin before they appeared for a lethal blow.ConclusionIn conclusion, despite those two rough patches, the game was a wildly enjoyable ride with characters I couldn't help but enjoy. The combat was a refreshing change of pace due to its combination of third-person shooter and hack-and-slash. So, pick up this game if the goofy dialogue or the combat looks interesting to you. I will return to this game soon to try out the game's combat at higher difficulty levels.

_childDocuments_.review: What makes a game a cult hit?  Ask fans of games like Deadly Premonition and Shadows of the Damned.  Far-fetched ideas and head-scratching plots melded together with shoddy but lovable gameplay and enough charm and humor to overlook the flaws that pepper the title.  The game may not be good, and critics may have panned it across the internet, but ♥♥♥♥ it: you like it, and that’s what matters!  But cult hits aren’t manufactured, they’re taken in by a select few that embrace it for what it is.  So, if all the above is true, what happens when you try to make a game a cult hit?  To do everything “average” on purpose to garner the love of the select few and be a nugget of enjoyment for the ones willing to see through the flaws?As a self-proclaimed “love letter to the sixth generation of consoles,” it feels like Wanted:Dead wanted to see how far down the road nostalgia could take them.  Playing as Lieutenant Hannah Stone, a cop with a rapsheet longer than a CVS receipt brought in to serve the toughest streets of Hong Kong, runs the equally heinous Zombie Squad: think The Suicide Squad but 480p.  This ragtag group is on the cusp of unearthing a major corporate conspiracy that will unravel the futuristic city of its devilish details within the darkened alleys and backdoor deals that decide who runs who in the underground.Wanted:Dead hails itself as a hybrid of third-person shooting and hack-n-slash melee combat.  Enemies will pounce you into having to use both as a mixture of melee-based swordsman and assault rifle wielding sharpshooters work together to mow you down.  Stone is tooled with a main rifle and secondary pistol and grenades, the former two customizable in several aspects to cater towards different aspects like being harder hitting or more precise at long ranges.  Secondary weapons can be picked up from fallen enemies, like SMGs, LMGs, and Grenade Launchers.  Melee is done with combos, dodges, and block/parrying.  Enemies will attack you with normal attacks and the occasional unguardable that can be interrupted with your pistol to keep them on their toes.  Melee damage can revive small portions of HP recently lost ala Bloodborne, so it’s sometimes worth the risk to run in swinging to get back lost health.The enemy placement does well to mix up both aspects of combat, but the whole experience feels one-note and stale.  Gunplay is mapped to cover-based shooting, but Stone doesn’t have a dedicated cover button and just morphs to cover when close.  This will inadvertently have you eat some bullets waiting for the game to catch up.  Shooting is snappy and the customization of your weapons feels good, but it all boils down to “wait until person pops their head out, shoot at head, repeat ‘til dead.”  Melee offers a little more variety but the enemies attacks don’t vary enough to pose much of a challenge so it comes down to recognizing their one pattern of attack and abusing it until the combat is over.But for the love of God, don’t let anything hit you.  Looking to amp up the difficulty, every enemy hits like a damn MAC truck, especially the melee enemies.  It’s common for melee fights to remove near 80% of your HP with one failed parry and eating a 3-hit combo, thus forcing a heal and making sure you don’t goof again.  It’s a tough lesson to learn in the early game as the first level’s first fight is 3-4 melee fighters and 3-4 shooters at one time, and they will throw you around until you understand the rules of this world.  After dying a few times, I wondered how the checkpoint system would be set up, if there even was one at all: thank you Gunsmith for providing a flying drone to refill my weapons, med kits, grenades, and a one-stop shop to customize my guns with new fittings.  These drones were like a gift from God, in which you feel eternally grateful for their contributions and they are never around to help you when needed the most.  You’ll feel this squeeze later on in the game where drones are separated by multiple fights and mini-bosses and dying at these scenes can net you back almost 30 minutes of game time, which was incredibly deflating.When you beat a level, Wanted:Dead takes this time to inject more plot and scenes to better relate you with Stone and the Zombie Squad; what you receive is some of the hardest pacing whiplash you’ll get this year.  Time at the Police HQ will give an opportunity to grab some of the game's many collectibles which range from enemy dossiers to reports of past crimes and newspaper reports of current events.  Starting your next mission will hit off a series of cutscenes, showing off the grisly details of what was learned last mission and what you’ll be settling into going forward.  Scenes will have an intense aura of them, no nonsense attitude conversations and what they hoped to be gripping police drama, and with one singular loading screen you’ll be thrown into a buddy-buddy scenario doing a rhythm mini-game on how much Ramen you can eat.    This happens again in the game with a hard-pressed interrogation scene with a cybernetic fugitive going into the ethics of pseudo robotic slavery and the free will of mechanically thinking beings that feels straight ripped from I, Robot, followed immediately by a fully anime-esque animated cutscene straight into a karaoke singing mini-game with Stone and Gunsmith covering 99 Luftballoons.This whiplash is exasperated even more so with the barmy script, direction, and voice acting.  I don’t want to dog on the voice actors working with what they were given but there was a distinct lack of direction with the scene’s emotion so lines are delivered as flat as week-old soda.  Enemy lines are re-used frequently where one level has multiple androids with the same voice actor spamming the same 3 lines to the point of head-shaking hilarity.  For a game running this caliber of a team with as much man hours put into it, the quality of this portion of this game is inexcusable and releases any tension in the game with scene delivery as poor as this.But in the back of my head I’m thinking to myself, “...this feels almost purposely done?”  No cult game plays perfectly.  It runs that dumb charm to the grave and banks on it like a 00 on the roulette board.  But Wanted:Dead doesn’t even commit to the silly, off-brand humor bit throughout its paltry 5 mission campaign.  It plays like something you’d buy at GameStop for $7 with the generic Sharpie-scribbled title packet and forces you to live in its crazy multi-dimensional world, and then scraps the whole damn idea on Mission 4!  You play 40% of the game in absolute serious connotations and this game just cannot do that!  These last two missions are by far the worst parts of the game by implementing crushing lengths between checkpoints, where getting through the amount of enemies becomes a war of attrition and your biggest enemy was running out of ammo and resorting to your blade.  Multiple failures would add hours to your game time.  These missions re-hash an earlier boss, which is unacceptable given there were only 5 slots for main bosses, and the final boss has a one-hit kill, because of course they do.But that’s the problem with cult hits: you either love them, or you don’t.  Some may read between the lines and see the light-hearted enjoyment of just making a game as ridiculous as you want, packing in whatever is felt necessary and utilizing your characters to do what they want outside of the hard-nosed job that they’re practically forced to do.  But all the ideas in Wanted:Dead don’t feel fleshed out nearly enough to cover the ridiculousness of the full package.  Stale combat, ludicrous pacing, poor design decisions, and a complete lack of direction show why trying to make a cult hit never works.  You just create a lacking experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game recommended and gifted from a friend. And sure I was in for a roller coaster ride.At first I wasn't super impressed and the game doesn't do the best of keeping you hooked from the get go. You start of with rather few "skills" and the game isn't the best of telling you to do your upgrades (which you can do whenever you want). Voice acting is hilarious bad/good but quite charming, difficulty spikes is just weird (but rather nice). Controls felt rough and I feel the devs could put way more polish and care into that and the connecting hits of when you attack. Not the biggest fan of the cover shooter aspects but none the less it's refreshing. I encountered several weird visual glitches (especially for the mini games). Some enemies are just BS and boring to fight against. Story is well, unique to put it so (but engageable enough). Bosses are really a hit or miss in terms of fun.But somehow the game grows on you really fast if you give it enough time and a chance. The somewhat wonky gameplay loop of doing combos with your handgun and katana felt rather dull, until it didn't. It suddenly clicked and I was in for a very satisfying hack and slash game that felt impactful with every hit you did. The handgun mixes up some rather unique combos but I wished there was slightly more variations of the combo and maybe some more area wise combo to hit multiple enemies. I really like the challenging gameplay and it took me back to times of playing Ninja Gaiden. I played on hard difficulty and sure I got stuck on some parts in the beginning, and you should expect the game to not be easy on you. You'll be actively tested if you understand the core mechanics and I love that. The game will let you now when it doesn't want you to hide behind cover. That's when you pull your katana, rush against the enemies with no fear. The game actively let you explore by yourself on how to approach each situation and enemy. A game that doesn't hold your hand and I love it.Not gonna say that I won't overlook all the down things of the game, but the game deserves way more praise and attention than the steam reviews gives it of.Overall, a surprise of a fun game, a diamond in the rough and rather quite enjoyable game.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: A scrappy, unpolished B-movie style game with some bizarre budget allocation decisions. The swordplay is relatively constrained in options compared to, say, Ninja Gaiden, but being able to switch to guns and grenades rounds it out nicely, along with being able to parry not just melee attacks but any red-flashing powerful attack with a one-button pistol shot. There's also Ninja Gaiden 2 style obliterations (one-input execution of enemies missing a limb), but that's about where the comparison stops.Even though combat has a wooden quality to it, there's also a flow to it. It very much slants towards the defensive side, with the parry ripostes often leading to an enemy being in a state vulnerable to instant execution.The later third of the about 10 hour experience on normal difficulty turns into a slog, with about 2 or 3 hard encounters per checkpoint. On the one hand, I really resented having to replay these so much just to die to the last encounter before the next checkpoint again. On the other, it really forced me to engage with the game's mechanics and exploit them to my advantage.- Oh, I don't feel like fighting the melee guys, so I'll just unload into their faces with a machine gun before they get close.- Cool, you can parry the hulking heavy machine gunners' melee hits too.- You can draw this beefy guy past an exploding barrel and shoot it.- These ninjas spend some time flailing if they're hit with a fire grenade- If I parry and then riposte these hits, their followup hit still hits me, so I need to dodge insteadAnd so on. The end section was pretty grueling but it made me play better/dirtier, and the feeling of beating it was better for it, despite the frustration.The minigames are so-so and entirely avoidable except the first go it forces you to do, but they're still weird and entirely out of place (you literally do some karaoke after committing a massacre), so I appreciate them being there.Ultimately the game is a rollercoaster of janky but compelling action, baffling choices on where to spend its development efforts, and a grueling difficulty ramp near the end. If it looks in any respect appealing to you, go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the most soulful video games ever, I don't think I've been charmed by a game like this in ages. Wanted: Dead can go from being totally nuts with over the top, unbelievably satisfying action gameplay with gore and awesome body dismemberment to a cozy moment where the crew is sitting at their favorite diner just chilling and chatting to a shockingly hard rhythm minigame to an anime flashback cutscene without an explanation or a reason. Minor spoilers aheadNow Wanted: Dead can feel a bit janky for a few reasons: no enemy lock-on, the camera has some collision issues, music with poor looping, tough gameplay on a mechanical level, a rushed final two chapters, and a story that's a bit confusing and obtuse, but I feel the love in it even in some of the bad. The lack of lock-on may seem odd at first but it makes sense with the way the levels are structured and designed makes it work. The camera may have some collision issues but tends to stay in a good spot and they've got some sick angles for the finishers (which are brutal and satisfying to do) plus it's really snappy when you're aiming your gun. The music may loop poorly at times but the OST slaps and is catchy and memorable. The game's tough but it's really rewarding once it clicks, with skills/abilities that synergize, personalization of your guns' stats, different partner combinations in the missions, and a good variety of tools for any situation (I think the sole skill I never made use of was the Charge Attack, and even still thinking back I could have effectively used it in several encounters)I think the only things that I can't find much positive about are the lack of enemy variety and the final two chapters. While I think the core combat is really fun and satisfying and the overall combat encounters are well designed, there's a only like a dozen enemy types in the whole game (not counting bosses). They're all relatively simple and don't use much strategy to fight you. Melee enemies walk at you and attack with simple combos, gun enemies duck behind cover, ninja enemies slash at you and get distance after being hit to throw their kunai, big guys charge and shoot at you while throwing grenades. I think this isn't a *major* issue with the game since it's so short, but I still would have loved to see more enemy types in this cyberpunk world. The bosses are overall really solid though, they keep with the game's combat mantra of being punishing but you always have the tools to take care of them so none of them feel unfairNow the final two levels, they're designed with way more enemies and combat encounters with less story to them and it's kind of obvious the budget was dwindling, leading to a clumsy rush to the end. The few present cutscenes feel very rigid and mechanical, the voice acting is generally somehow worse (with the third to last boss has some of the worst voice acting I have ever heard) and the second to last boss is just the very first one (but you fight two so it's somewhat different I guess). Even still, the game still wraps the plot up (unlike another charming, mis-maligned game D4) so there's still resolution for what main plot there is upon getting to the end. The story's definitely wishy-washy, the anime flashbacks can come out of nowhere, the final pre-credits cutscene comes out of nowhere, and there's rarely more than a sentence that explains what you'll be doing next, but I feel it's completely feasible to make all the connections required to understand what's being toldBesides the silly tone and the fun action, the minigames are another major strength to this game. I really like how they change the tone at the drop of the hat, plus they aren't just shoved in with barely any effort put into them. Target practice lets you feel how good the gunplay is on a precise level. Seeing all the various models in the crane game is really silly and it's nice to get new music for the jukebox or the noodles minigame. Karaoke, despite having a single song, has some great animation work, a high difficulty floor, and a very obvious joy put into it by the actors. The random history of noodles before the minigame had me cackling and they do a good job at adjusting it so it's different from karaoke in how it plays. The Space Harrier homage plays shockingly well and feels like it was made with a lot of care. They all feel completely random but I'm glad every single one of them is presentI think one of this game's strengths that I haven't seen talked about much is the game's ability to slow things down and show you the world. The character interactions and moments between chapters are bizarre, lengthy, and don't serve a major plot purpose and yet they stood out to me. Not for those reasons, but because they're very intimate and make the world feel more lived in. Games don't do this very often, even in ones with character-driven plots (which this one doesn't have, I couldn't even tell you what really drives the story). I feel like all of these nonsensical choices were incredibly deliberate and exactly what the developers and writers wanted even at the expense of other aspects of the gameWanted: Dead is anything but boring. It feels like a lost PS3 game with an uncompromised vision and no corporate mismanagement. I can't say anything about the game at launch (I heard there were a ton of performance issues and people thought it was too hard) but I think the current post-patch reception is far too negative. This game is silly, extravagant, unrefined, satisfying, bizarre, and has no quality through-line and I absolutely adore it.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was an option to give a game a neutral review, that's what Wanted: Dead would have gotten from me, unfortunately, there's not.I was pretty positive seeing videos about Wanted: Dead and excited to sink a few hours into it. A few good things about Wanted: Dead:-An interesting, weird setting;-Detailed, varied characters;-Serviceable combat system with gory effects and executions...-...which are really nicely animated and often context-triggered;-Pretty (even though only a few and short) anime cutscenes;-A handful of minigames which can be pretty challenging-Each boss fight has unique mechanics that you often have to figure out by yourself in trial and error manner.On the other hand:-The story feels like it was written by a not-very-talented teenager;-The dialogues are pretty bad;-The game is pretty short, even though fully corridor-based...-...and due to that some of the stages spike in difficulty as the checkpoints are far apart; -The progression system is mediocre and doesn't make you feel like you become more powerful throughout the story;-The weapon customisation system is pretty useless;-Optimisation is a bit botched in some places;-The voice acting is atrocious.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I ENJOYED this game. Played it on hard first then replayed it on 'japanese hard' because I found the glint that makes it fun. But for the majority of people they would not enjoy it since I'm assuming that most people don't think about nuances of games. Right off the bat the audio engineering is pretty bad, dubbing is bad, story is nonsensical and not cohesive, graphics look like generic unreal engine assets, just overall it would not be appealing to the mainstream. But for those that persevered through the gameplay, and the people that gave it a recommend, know that there's something in the gameplay: it's fun and exhilarating... once you understand what kind of game it is.So at first the game plays like a third person shooter, but the guns are pretty weak and they're only mainly used for ranged infantry/grunts because the meat of the game is on melee combat. Once you encounter a melee opponent they can take you out with just 2-4 hits and that should be an indicator of 'wow, melee does a LOT of damage. I should try switching to melee combat whenever those guys are around'. However it's not much conveyed and the majority of people will just scratch their heads and wonder 'why does the enemy melee do so much damage?' never switching to melee combat.And there are a lot of good things in the melee combat:+ parry system is good(can even extend the parry window if you have skill points)+ the gun kata/gun fu is great, there's a distinction of when to use your pistol and when to use your sword   * sword combo is normally a 3-hit combo and using your pistol then doing a sword combo reveals another set of sword combos which lets you have a longer string of melee combos   * sword parries melee(early on) and gun parries unblockable attacksThere are much more bad things about the game that others have touched upon but on the gameplay side these are what I noticed:+ the game's camera switches to a cinematic camera when doing melee combat, which is ok for the most part, and it does look cool...- but when there are a lot of enemies sometimes you can't see enemies that will attack you off-screen...- and adjusting the camera is annoying because sometimes it fights you...- and in the later parts of the game there are a lot of claustrophobic areas and tight spaces which the camera doesn't handle well because it shows bad angles of the fight+ unblockable attacks have a distinct sound so you can react to their attack...- but since the game has bad audio engineering and the game doesn't shut up, it gets drowned outMuch like this game my thoughts are just jumbled because there's really something to this game. The game ends on a cliffhanger ending so if they do decide to make a sequel then I will probably keep my eye on it. On the sequel I hope that it won't lean towards meme culture and will actually be a more cohesive story.Overall it really is the most 5/10 game. But you can also see that it's a budget game that they still try to do something creative with it... if you can see it. Also side note, apparently this was by makers of Ninja Gaiden games? The caliber doesn't show. Feels more like Devil's Third than Ninja Gaiden honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: A fine title for connoisseurs and old school games enjoyers. 👌Wanted: Dead is not for everyone, it does have a lot of flaws but it's still a fun game with satisfying combat !The game got review bombed at launch because apparently there was one version available for purchase in the store which was packed with corrupted files leading to people experiencing constant crashes.Some people had to refund and re buy the game but unfortunately for them the price was increased shortly after release.No matter what this will be a divisive game for sure, don't expect to see very positive ratings on steam anytime soon.Some people will love it and the majority might find it pretty bad and clunky.It was the same scenario with Gungrave G.O.R.E, another niche misunderstood game.Right now at least I can already say that Wanted: Dead is way better than Gungrave G.O.R.E.I haven't played much so far but would still recommend if you can tolerate some jank and enjoy mid tier old school games.The soundtrack is great, graphics looks nice and the combat is damn fun.Be warned the game is quite hard, not as hard as Sekiro or Dark Souls but still quite challenging.There is a lot of irritating things like the enemies spamming grenades and the grenade launcher AOE, some poorly balanced bosses are to be expected here as well.But these things should not be a hindrance for too long if you have experience with these types of games.Just a quick review to counter the review bomb, will edit later.Wanted: Dead is far from perfect and there is a lot of issues here but it's still well worth playing IMHO.Probably going to be a 6/10 in my book and a buy on sale recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy the 2nd option, there seems to be a lot of issues coming from that version. Outside of that, minimal issues from my playthrough. Fairly straightforward story with cutscenes that don't exceed over 2 minutes most of the time. The gameplay is good. Started off on hard mode and probably died about 50 times because melee enemy types can kill you within a single combo if you're sloppy. This game is definitely challenging and doesn't hold your hand the whole way through. The combat isn't too deep, but does take a while to master. The pistol is your best friend when customized to add more stun. Plus it helps to extend combos with the katana. Gunplay is fine, not terrible, but not amazing. Melee combat will challenge you the most. You just gotta learn the enemy's attacks and know when to dodge/counter/parry if you want to have a good time. Parry is really good, it will leave the enemy vulnerable for any attack for a few seconds. Highly recommended when fighting tougher enemies because you can simply pull out your rifle or secondary and dwindle down their health fairly quickly. Bullet time is a life savor, but it seems like a lot of people don't know how to properly use it. You can target up to 5 enemies within about a 8m radius. Weaker enemies are put into a stunned state for quick takedowns. Tougher enemies will only be stunned for several seconds, which is great to pull out your rifle to kill them off quickly. Besides that, make sure not to be too close to any enemy when using it. The attack will mostly likely only affect that enemy, so be sure to watch out for that. Besides that, don't fight melee enemies on stairs. You're at a huge disadvantage when attacking or defending. So don't think you're Obi Wan when you have the high ground.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've been waiting for this game to release and here's what I think - I see what everyone says when the movement can be a bit clunky, it's not as bad as most say, for me once I learned how to combo my gun with sword attacks further than what the tutorial will show, it became even more fun. Upgrading on the skill tree helps you in combat as well as expected. It can make things easier once you start putting it all together or learn to chain attacks. Overall, it is great but could have used just a bit more work to make it smoother- The enemies can overwhelm you IF, you allow them to do so such as rushing into combat and not taking note of how many enemies are around you. You have limited amount of health packs so this is important to note. It's like some of the classics from the early 2000s. You have a limited amount recovery items until you get to the next area. - As far as the customization of the weapons(Guns), nothing that'll make you lose your s***. Skins, barrels,  stocks,  clips, sights. That's it. It does make a difference in combat though and that's what you want. How much of a difference? No COD type of difference when upgrading weapons but upgrading does help in areas of your combat- Voice acting is ok, could have used some work in this area too. Not horrible because I've heard worse, but not great neither. Right in the middle.-The minigames were pretty fun for me. Reminds me of the yakuza minigames sort of.I think overall for me I'd give the game a 7.5/10 because there's some things that could have been better, hopefully a patch in the future will update some of these. If you're looking for a game to kill some time, have fun with for a few hours and a challenge if you play on hard or "Japanese hard" once you unlock it which I myself am looking forward to, I think you should give it a try. You can see the Ninja Gaiden influence(some of the devs from Ninja Gaiden helped on this game), the Devil May Cry influence or hack & slash theme in some ways although its not there 100%. If you're a fan of those series it might be worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly interesting game, but it's definitely going to taste your patience at times. I think it's worth trying if you liked the Xbox/360 era Ninja Gaiden games and if you enjoy Deadly Premonition. This is not Devil May Cry, and if you go into it expecting something like that or a cover shooter, you're going to probably be pretty annoyed. It's a game that you have to kind of accept for what it is, which feels like a forgotten game from the early PS3 era when stuff like Heavenly Sword was around and while character action games were still trying to figure out exactly what they were. There's a lot of quirkiness and dialogue that makes this really enjoyable, and the combat is great when it works and you figure it out, and there's also some pretty entertaining, if random, mini games. I personally think it's worth the full $29.99, but if you can get it on sale, go for it. Just be warned - you need a high tolerance for difficulty, questionable checkpoints, and maybe even a few glitches, but this feels like it's destined to be a cult classic right up there with Deadly Premonition and Devil's Third. This isn't for everybody, but the people it hits with are really going to enjoy their time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is an amalgamation of the kinds of third person action games to be found during the PS2/Xbox and early PS3/360 days. If you enjoy Devil May Cry or Ninja Gaiden, and you're willing to trade immaculate design for charm and enthusiasm, Wanted: Dead is worth a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted; Dead is clearly made for a very specific and niche audience.If you enjoyed  the era of third person games Army of Two, Max Payne, Lollipop Chainsaw, Vanquish, Wet, maybe with a  tiny splash of hack/slash elements from MGS Rising or DMC, this game might be for you. Just remember alongside all those elements, it's packaged with all the shovelware copycat games of that era, despite a vibrant and well marketed world.NARRATIVEThe narrative premise is simple, but unfortunately goes nowhere. You are a war criminal turned enforcer for the HK Police, working for a company mainly known for creating synthetic android factory workers. And from there, a bunch of different and definitely not connecting plot threads are made chapter by chapter, but go nowhere. Apparently there is some corporate conspiracy, but let’s just say the story is not important at all. All of this is presented in full anime style cutscenes, and in game engine ones. The medium switch is interesting, but doesn’t help its writing and awful voice acting. GAMEPLAYWanted; Dead revels in itself being bad like an older era gaming. If that was its intention it did it in spades. Looped enemy dialogue, bullet sponges, bad enemy AI, and extremely punishing checkpointing system. I cannot remember the amount of times I were to die and be sent so far back in the level, just to go through the same mob waves all over again.Trust me, the majority of the more casual player base of this game might not even be able to finish Wanted; Dead. It’s very punishing, and not until later in the game when you unlock more of what feel like key skills from the skill tree to open up the game, does it all start to come together.And that's about all that Wanted; Dead has merit wise. A somewhat fun but tough gameplay loop of gun-kata, with emphasis on the melee aspect, despite it being very limiting even with all unlocks. I enjoyed doing flashy executions, cutting through a crowd of enemies, and it did what it set out to do; emulate that era of gaming, riddled with third person shooters with minor melee elements. For better or worse, like I mentioned before, it takes with it all the same frustrating problems. PC OPTIMIZATION I played this on PC, and let’s just say the controls take a lot of time getting used to and rebinding, and a key element of perfect parrying melee attacks often feels like I’m getting punished for doing so. And the enemy AI and teammate’s AI are both horrendous. To put it simply, Wanted is an epitome of jank in 2023 for a game like this. BOSS FIGHTSInsult to injury, the first boss you fight, you fight again later on, except guess what, it’s two of them. Two Spider tanks.. Every boss fight is a bullet sponge minus the last one, where the devs kinda tell you, “Ayo you cheesed every fight with infinite pistol ammo? This guys will dodge every shot, gotta finally put those melee combat practice in”  SETTING Another thing that irked me is that it’s set in an alternate present dayish Hong Kong. As a Hong Kong native, this game literally has nothing to do with Hong Kong. There is a single character that is Chinese, and the rest of the world beyond random Chinese signs, has nothing to do with HK.  Mind you the police station which is in inbetween level base  is riddled with non-Chinese NPC’s with thick British accents, despite the game just introducing itself as post handover HK. It’s very strange, and near the end of the game you literally run through an equivalent of a North American Chinatown rather than Hong Kong. There are a few little nods to Hong Kong like a parody of Watson’s,  the metal fence apartment doors, and one single public transit Xiao Ba. everything else just screams “I’ve never been to Hong Kong, but sounds Cybeprunk.”  Even if this is supposed to be a 80’s version of HK, nah man. This could have been anywhere but HK.ANYTHING GOOD?Despite all this, I can’t help but be charmed by a lot of the little things. Be it the awkward rhythm games of eating ramen at  a street vendor japanese ramen shop (out of place for HK) and karaoke (not so out of place), the crane machines, the fully made bullet hell arcade game, the very dumb interactions between the characters of the  main Zombie Unit that you are part of, the fact when you go afk, each character has their own full idle animations. In addition, the very 80’s and fun soundtrack strums my die hard synth heart. It’s all nice touches, and very Yakuza-esque with a touch of Cyberpunk. It’s a shame cause, when I saw the perfectly put together holiday trailer, I was very excited and looking forward to its release. Both being from HK, a big fan of these types of games in my PS3 days, I was quite disappointed in the end result. Someone told me they felt like this game was a “Uncharted game without any soul, set pieces and polish” and it definitely felt like that. Wanted; Dead tried to shove so many different third person game elements together without any compromises, and it shows. It really felt like given a bit more time, the game could have been something more. There are very few elements of it screaming “Ninja Gaiden” Or Dead or Alive, beyond maybe the same sound bite from the ninja enemies.At the end of it all, I cannot recommend this game at  60 bucks, especially with something as good as Hi-Fi-Rush at 30. Maybe if it came out in 2011 in a bargain bin, it wouldn’t be so bad. But with a play time of 8-12 hours, and if you wanted to, subsequent playthroughs on ‘Japanese Hard’ of the same game, with its mediocre package, I’d recommend waiting for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been writing reviews for a long time, and once in a while, a game emerges to really show me how things have changed. It's 2023, and I'm in my early 30's. If  were to come out 12 years ago, at the highest of the seventh generation of consoles (Xbox 360, PS3), it would have been a pure hit. But like I said, it's 2023. presents the player with the Zombie Unit, a team composed by ex-military personal serving a life sentence. On contrary to the A-Team, this unit does have an official second chance, as long as they manage to keep themselves on the line, while handing-over the harsh and cruel justice to the enemies of Democracy.The game is not to take it seriously, in fact, as soon as you jump in, you'll start to notice the huge amount of references, comedic dialogues, and even memes here and there. Imagine if a festival of hipsters was transported into Cyberpunk, while inside an Avant-Garde dream. I'm probably not still close enough, but you get the idea. It's really funny and smart how Sergei Kolobashkin wrote  to be fun, while being modern and sometimes, even brave.As soon as I started , I got a huge nostalgic feeling from another game I deeply love, called WET. Both featuring a female hero with guns and swordplay mixed with intense action combos. Other games like Sekiro and Ninja Gaiden may be used as a reference, but ultimately,  is a product of its own. It's solid enough to be unique, that much the game deserves.Unfortunately, many games from the Xbox 360 / PS3 times are considerably better mechanically, and that is the first biggest issue with this latest product from . I feel it could have been further polished, or perhaps further tested. This truly hurts me, because I really do miss a pure action title with no intermediary compromises, and zero stalling, while having a profound respect for players time. Unfortunately, this isn't it. has a lot of features in its gameplay, and focuses mostly in a deadly combination of swordplay and guns. The mechanics go much deeper than a simple button smash hack and slash. In fact, if you're button smashing, you'll have a hard time here. A lot of thought went behind the conception of the game, and on paper it's flawless. Once playing, though, things change a bit.The character moves very fluidly, but I immediately noticed we could have all benefit from the ability to lock-on-target. Not that I don't enjoy a free flow movement, in fact, since Hannah can't block attacks unless she is facing them, the free camera helps. However, it's the same camera that sometimes becomes too much loose and conflicts with your intended target.The parry ability was a fantastic addition, and when it works, it's impressive. Relies entirely on blocking attacks at the right time. Enemy attacks may be single, or multiple, with all sorts of weapons. It's not very consistent, and you'll easily miss them, especially with the camera being inconsistent. It's an obligatory skill, as without understanding it, you won't go far in the campaign. passes the message of being a freestyle action game, but the truth is, as a shooter, it's terrible. You're forced to memorize the parry timings of the bosses and their animations. Hannah does use her handgun to interrupt enemy actions, which is handy, but as Riffles and Shotguns go, they will leave you open to damage with no reward for taking the risky approach.Understanding that swordplay is the key to success, we come across another issue, the I-frames. Hannah is truly only having I-frames when using her Finishing Movies, which are dedicated animations to kill enemies with style, once they are almost dead. Every other animation is susceptible to damage you can't control, including grenades from your team mates.There are a lot of little details that separate the top games from the ones with, well, Mixed reviews on Steam. It's the little things that make a difference. Unfortunately, many of such details are lacking in , making the gameplay frustrating, and many times, messy. One disgraceful detail, is the simple fact Hannah cannot stop a weapon reload. There's no cancelation option, unless you replace that animation with something else. Imagine the fun of reloading a 12 shell Shotgun in a middle of a fight.Most actions reward you with XP, which can be used to unlock new skills in the Skill Tree. Many of those skills add impressive abilities, and even a few for your teammates. You'll have plenty XP to unlock them in a single playthrough. New Game+ is available, but you cannot carry those unlocked goodies into a new difficulty. Clearly, the game wants you to give it all on harder difficulties. I found many of the unlocked skills highly important and even essential.It hurts me to realize it, but  truly does have mediocre gameplay, even when compared to titles release 10 years ago. Unfortunately, that alone isn't the reason why so many negative reviews are present around the web. The optimization could, and should have been improved, especially when dealing with the PC market. A market that, rightfully so, is very demanding of PC functionalities. is unfortunately archaic in its methods, starting with the very limited support for keyboard and mouse. That alone destroys the hopes of many, as you can't rebind extra mouse keys, such as, Mouse 4. The keyboard scheme itself is obnoxious and feels extremely counter-intuitive, even when compared to older action games. used DX11 as the API! You know what this means for AMD users? A nightmare. My GPU (RX 6700 XT) spikes in mini-games which is ridiculous, constant frame loss in busy areas, and a horrendous performance across the whole game, with as low as 17 frames per second! I tried to use DXVK, which fixed the performance in open spaces, but didn't do much for closed areas.That's where it came to me, I have forgotten just how good games felt in the mid 2010s. All the memories and passion I once had holding my Xbox 360 controller, came rushing through me.  reminded me how much I love these games, and it's exactly what you'd expect from that seventh generation era. It's painful to see such a fantastic title unpolished and not given the love it deserved.The campaign may hold you up to just 12 hours, containing a valuable replayability, with skills to unlock, add-ons for your weaponry, mini-games to clear and complete, rewarding you with all sorts of nice little extras, with a phenomenal OST. To top it off, the pleasant gameplay growth, as you adapt and become a powerful killing machine. Would be pretty good to unlock different costumes for Hannah, or at least a variety of skins. Whoever is brave enough to overlook the controls will find himself beholding a masterclass of an action game. Even more so, if you can ignore its awful performance on AMD, accept there aren't and there will never be any future update, and realize this is a straight-up console game that could benefit from a few extra months in development.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember how this game came out earlier this past year and was honestly curious about it. I saw the reviews kinda panned it, mixed on steam. However, I still wishlisted it and held out. After seeing some gameplay I knew I was interested when it was on a steep sale. So it finally came at 20 USD and I am personally cool with that and I am glad I did.A lot of people just sh*tpost on steam reviews so I want to try to illustrate a better picture of what this game actually is. I could best describe it as a game that is trying to mimic aspects of an arcade game. It's a short game, probably 4-5 hours first time and then on subsequent playthroughs it's about 2-3. It is a game that lets you try to figure out and devise ways to effectively take out enemies in certain sections of the game along with exploiting your moveset to the best of your ability (AKA an arcade game). When you think of the game like this you get a bit of a clearer picture of what it is.The combat is a lot of fun when you take the time and effort to actually learn it. Using guard cancels, rolls, pistol shots etc to cancel into other things makes the game make a lot more sense opposed to how it is on the surface level which makes you feel extremely clunky and slow. You definitely can feel your improvement as you play from the speed you are killing enemies. Not many games really deliver that and I appreciate it for existing. The game has guns and cover, however it's not ALL about the shooting. Guns are like 40% of the gameplay where you use it to dump damage on staggered enemies and pick off distant targets from time to time. Plus, it being so short you can just say well I feel like playing this today and allow it. I would highly recommend looking up a “how to play this game” before getting it unless you want to do the discovery process yourself because there are a lot of interesting attributes to it.Now for the negatives and criticism for this game.First, the price. I stated at the beginning of this review how I was waiting on a price drop for this game. I knew it was short and it would be 40 dollars. This game is for such a specific niche within a niche. This is for people who enjoy action games, but then REALLY enjoy them to the point of breaking the game for repeated playthroughs. The average player is going to play the game, say “this sucks” and refund or go play something else. With that, the game should of sold for 30 at least for launch. Then maybe it wouldn’t have so much negativity for normal individuals EVEN THOUGH I do feel the enjoyment from subsequent playthroughs does amp up the cost being worthwhile. I'm not a studio or a publisher but if the launch price could have gone down it would have honestly won more people over. Maybe.With that price, you also expect a bit of polish. Story and presentation I don’t want to harp on because honestly this game has a Deadly Premonition vibe to it which I love which is always a happy accident. But the game should work. On my very first playthrough I had enemies stuck on a cliff in the first 20 minutes of play and I wondered why I could not progress. Executions where enemies will get frozen and take no damage until I damage them after the fact. Enemies will get stuck in doorways spinning like mad. Enemies running away from the fight with the will that they HAVE TO LEAVE even though they get shot at and dont even turn around to fight back. Music fails to play or 2 music tracks play on top of one another. Dialogue lines in Stage 3 that all play at the same time from the same voice actor that are absurdly hilarious. Granted, these things could be polished through patches and maybe they will. But honestly I don't have that much faith in it considering it's been 11 months since launch.For gameplay choices I primarily have 2 major gripes. 1, there is no health regen on attacks on Japanese Hard (Yes it's seriously called that). So melee strikes I get because you can parry, but gunshots you can’t. Most of the time when you enter combat for some reason the AI is in agreement to let you duel them but you will sometimes get shot. I feel like shot damage throughout the game should always be able to regen from executing enemies. It just makes sense because of its borderline unavoidable damage. 2nd gripe, not an even harder mode. After my first playthrough on Normal I had a good grasp on the mechanics and was honestly underwhelmed by Japanese Hard and wished for a greater challenge. I could self impose handicaps but it still felt mostly the same.Last critique overall is after you beat the game. There is basically nothing after that. For something marketing the gameplay design of legacy console generations, where is the unlockable outfits? We know you have different color shirts for Hannah and when she's in the police station she has a different getup. Where are more weapon skins? Where is a god mode katana or something? No bloody palace or a challenge tower? No speedrun mode to skip all the annoying minigames? How about a point rush mode where you can have a score along with keeping track of your time? This system is already in the game from its training missions. Just simply add it to the entire game so I could play a score attack mode of some sort. No level select? Checkpoint select?There are so many things that could have been in this game to cater to the niche audience which they didn't capitalize on.I don’t know, so many questionable things are forgotten but maybe down the road they will add it who knows.To wrap up, this game is sick. It made me laugh at times and I enjoyed the combat quite a bit. Just don’t go into this game expecting Devil May Cry or Ninja Gaiden.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is fun. The gameplay objectively isn't "good" but it isn't "bad" either. I actually think, to my tastes, it does a lot of things right. The game is hard, and bordering on super unfair at times, but it's all doable. The game is VERY campy, and I love it for that.The combat is, in my honest opinion, quite good. There are some very tanky enemies, but the majority of fights feel frantic, and satisfying. Enemies are brutal, even a grunt can knock off half your healthbar if you mess up, and it makes the game feel quite tense. Not to mention, the parries, and gun counters are very satisfying to pull off. I did feel like I learned a ton of how to play the game, and aside from longer parry windows, you mostly have to just learn how to fight on the game's terms, and by the end, you feel powerful as you wallop an enemy who destroyed you before, through sheer skill. Early on, you have to fight a bunch of goons with a chainsaw at your disposal, you can get hit during the chainsaw animation, so you lose a ton of health. Right after you have to fight a really tough melee enemy, followed by 4 shield enemies, all of which I had trouble with, so instead of using the chainsaw to fight the first wave of easy enemies, I didn't, I just killed them with my normal equipment, saved the chainsaw, and one shotted the mini-boss. I think that's kinda cool, as a problem to solve. The game doesn't really have a ton of this, but it's cool that it was something that was possible. The level design actually isn't bad. I think the levels flow quite well without being too distinctly 'video game' level-y. It's a generally, good experience. The encounters can feel very unfair when you're tasked with defeating 3 minibosses between checkpoints and dozens of goons, but I also felt more tension than I have in a while with action games. I wish there was more gun customization, because the gun combat is actually kinda fun too. It's nothing special, it's just a serviceable cover based shooter layered into a very fun hack and slash game. As for the writing. Wow, I don't know why this game was made, but I want to thank them. It's so full of heart, with bad voice acting and just some beautiful moments. It's also dotted with like, ACTUALLY good cutscenes with real emotion. I don't know why this game is capable of doing this, but it's wholly unique in it's way of bounding between "The Room" and actual melodrama. But... more on the side of "The Room"If you want a fun action game with a lot of camp and strangeness, and you're up for a challenge. Give this game a shot. It's most definitely a one-of-a-kind experience.
