_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: If the devs could drop some profile customisation content, that would be great.  Give me a background for the Atomic Heart diner, or the Deaf Panther Club, or both.  I know you have the means lolFull disclosure: my roommate and I played this with a Switch controller and turned all the sensitivity settings up to 75, with the graphics slightly reduced.  I've been reading that people found some of the keyboard controls problematic, so maybe use a controller instead of the keyboard & mouse.As a fan of old-school Capcom games like Resident Evil and Devil May Cry, we LOVED this.  It's stressful at times due to some instability in the game registering inputs (and because of Cortez throwing grenades into small hallways with propane tanks in the last chapter), but it was still a great time.  Having a nonverbal character was a pretty cool change, as was including Stone's lactose intolerance.  The more you watch Herzog's behaviour, the more your realize that he is the sweetest, most overprotective older brother type and he's charming as hell once you get used to him.  Doc is kind of annoying for reasons unbeknownst to us, but I guess it's good to have a medic in the party.  I don't think the other reviewers even know what bad voice acting sounds like, because it's perfectly fine and actually sounds MORE like natural speech to us than most games.  (For reference, Sonic Adventure & the original Resident Evil are ACTUAL examples of bad voice acting.  Hell, even the original Devil May Cry was oddly disjointed in comparison).  We suspect people just aren't used to whatever brand of Scandinavian Stone's VA was lolMy only real gripes with the game is that cutscenes will spontaneously decide to mute everything but sound effects & playing music unlocked in the crane minigame from the menu completely breaks the sound engine and forces a restart to fix it.  The parry system leaves a bit to be desired, but it's not a deal-breaker.  There's also a small input delay in the ramen minigame, but we weren't here for minigames.Overall, the game seems to have a bit of an issue knowing what it wants to be, but it's still fun af.  I feel a little let down story-wise, but I'm pretty used to tings being cut from games to get them out by their release date (Soul Reaver, anyone?) so it's probably more of a failure of the development schedule than the game itself.  This game absorbed several weeks of mine and my roommate's lives, but we have no regrets.(Also, they render food really well.  This game made us buy ramen TWICE.)

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is a solid albeit unpolished action game. It has a simple, satisfying, and fairly punishing combat system; the moment to moment gameplay is straight forward and doesn't waste any time throwing in anything unnecessary, focusing entirely on ripping through swathes of enemies. However, everything surrounding that core game is some of the most bewildering and unhinged content I've ever seen. Everything is poorly written and poorly performed, but there are glimpses of interesting world building or a more interesting story that never get explored or followed up on. There are several mini games that are far more involved than one would expect and feel like tonal whiplash when they happen. There is an unlockable cooking show for some reason. Every second I spent with this game led to being struck by a new kind of confusion. Wanted: Dead tries to do so many things that, when looking at the product as a whole, it becomes disjointed and completely all over the place; any time that isn't spent slicing people in half feels like a fever dream. I don't know who this is for, maybe the developers made a game purely for themselves, but I love it and would never recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like, but overall this game is a big disappointment.Everyone has already talked about the bugs, the poor M+K support, the janky combat etc...All these things are there, sure, but I could've overlooked them if the rest of the game delivered.Unfortunately, it does not.The style and aesthetic is there, but there's no substance. The side characters had potential to really make a solid team but none of them get time to flesh out their characters or stories in any meaningful way... you never feel like you know them despite the captain saying you're all basically one big family. The writing is bad, and the voice acting too, even though I found Hannah's VA endearing in a way.The villains are garbage, cliche, poorly written and you never understand their motivations properly.The plot is the biggest let down. The story, which only takes about 5-6 hours to complete in its entirety, is convoluted, poorly executed and makes very little sense. There's so much going on, and none of it fits together in a cohesive way. I was confused about what was going on and who and why I was fighting for 90% of the game.The melee combat is the best thing about the gameplay, and even that gets boring after the halfway mark when you fully unlock the skill tree. There's not enough depth to the combos and the movements don't flow well from one combo to the next.The difficulty ceiling is insane too. As someone who doesn't normally play these kinds of games, normal difficulty felt like slow torture and I couldn't even get through the first mission without dropping the difficulty to easy (which you can't do at the beginning, the game only presents it as an option if you really suck). Even on easy difficulty, some of the enemies are so tanky and the combat janky enough that you'll just randomly die and then have to redo half the level again.On the positive though, the finisher animations are amazing.The minigames are cool.The anime cutscenes are stylish as hell.Stefanie Joosten is amazing, although her character is criminally underutilized and she gets barely any screentime.The game looks pretty good, and you can clearly tell a lot of effort was put into creating the setting and everything in it.It's a real shame that something with such potential was wasted like this.TLDR:Really wish this game was better, but after paying $60 for a 6 hour game that was confusing and frustrating to play, I'm  very disappointed. I'd gladly pay $20-30 for something of this quality, but $60 is mad.

_childDocuments_.review: "Wanted: Dead" is a fascinating gem in the world of gaming, and while it may have its rough edges, it's an experience I've grown to love. As a fan of titles like Ninja Gaiden, this game immediately piqued my interest. It's described as a hybrid slasher and shooter, hailing from the creators of Ninja Gaiden, and I must admit, it's not without its quirks. Prepare to die numerous times, often uttering "What on earth is this?" in disbelief, yet the game's peculiar charm makes it all worth it.One of the standout features has to be the voice acting, which falls into the category of 'so bad, it's good.' During certain cutscenes, I found myself half-expecting Tommy Wiseau to make a cameo, perhaps delivering an impromptu "Oh, hi Mark." The game's setting is intriguing, casting you as a member of the Zombie Unit police in the vibrant city of Hong Kong. While the story presentation may occasionally fall flat, the gameplay more than makes up for it."Wanted: Dead" offers a challenging and adrenaline-pumping experience. Don't be discouraged by the initial difficulty; mastering parrying is key to overcoming the many formidable enemies you'll encounter. The satisfaction of executing flawless finishers is second to none, and it's a testament to the game's combat system.Beyond the relatively short campaign, the game offers a range of entertaining mini-games that I found surprisingly enjoyable. These side activities add a layer of depth and fun to the overall experience.In conclusion, I wholeheartedly recommend "Wanted: Dead," although perhaps not at its full price. Keep an eye out for a sale, and you'll find yourself with an engaging and strangely endearing game that's sure to provide hours of entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is a modern day masterpiece! The developers have cooked up something special here and I can quite easily see this game having a cult following in a few years time. The game is designed to feel outdated. Taking a lot of inspiration from 90's games while adding its own unique flare. The voice acting and cutscene's along with its simplistic level design really do a good job selling this and add a lot of charm.The combat is hard, but feels fluid, requiring a lot of skill to get through each section. This requires a bit of practice , luckily there are quite a few training levels you can re-play to get accustom with the controls and combos. Pretty soon you will be doing chained take downs like a pro! This becomes easier over time as you unlock new weapons and abilities.Each mission feels unique and has cut scenes and mini games to lead you into the next section. This keeps the game feeling fresh and stops things getting stale like a lot of other games in the genre. The characters are hilarious and Iv had quite a few laugh out loud moments. I just cant quite seem to get enough of this game which is very rare for me. If you have ever said to yourself. "Man, these new games suck! Take me back to the good old days". Then this game is for you!If your on the fence about buying this do not listen to the likes of IGN or the millenials in the negative review section. You will be totally missing out. _childDocuments_.review: If a few months or years ago you told me I’d one day be playing a game that’s essentially a mix of John Wick, Metal Gear Rising, Yakuza and Deadly Premonition, I would’ve probably looked at you all funny, but here we are. Wanted: Dead is an absolute wild ride of a third-person shooter/hack & slash hybrid that proudly wears its goofiness on its sleeve and is not ashamed to be itself, nor does it take itself too seriously. And I kind of love it for that. Yes, it’s rough around the edges. Yes, it’s got some jank. The controls may put people off and the main character’s voice acting might not be everyone’s cup of tea. For some, the game might be a bit too unhinged or its difficulty too unforgiving. But if you embrace its high-octane combat, its general silliness and the fact that it plays and feels like a long-lost classic from the PlayStation 2’s library, you’re going to have an amazingly good time with it.For more honest indie game reviews, check out our Curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't been able to stop thinking about this game since I first started it. There are a lot of things about this game that are certainly not for everyone, but I came into it having greatly enjoyed this studios past work, as well as being a huge fan of 6th and 7th console generation games that aimed higher than the publishers budget would allow, and this game attempts to intentionally emulate that style of experience and by my reckoning succeeds with flying colours.The combat is unquestionably tough and divisive. If you're not in the flow with it and don't play by its rules it is stiff and frustrating, but when you lean into its strengths and learn how to best utilise the systems the flow becomes immaculate and it feels like you're playing some amazing hidden gem from 2007.The game also features elements that aren't combat, containing an assortment of minigames that are experienced over the course of the story and become available from the main menu once you've tried them for the first time.I had some serious technical issues with the retro space shooter minigame (but it is optional so that didn't hurt my experience too badly) and things like the shooting gallery and crane game are entertaining little breaks from the action and ways to hone your skills and obtain collectables respectively, but the two remaining minigames are Rhythm games, one being a wacky abstraction of a ramen eating contest and the other a painfully realistic karaoke rendition of "99 Luftballons" and as a huge fan of rhythm games I must commend Soleil for their beat mapping, controls and charting for these modes, as not rhythm game I have played in the past has so effectively provided me a challenging but reliable experience when played with a standard controller!The story and presentation are a mixed bag with this game. The main character's model looks fantastic and the game oozes style and charm but many of the assets are distractingly lower in quality and the games flair can stray badly into "style over substance" territory. The game also deserves credit for marvellously utilising a mix of original music tracks with some fun choices of licensed music used sparingly and appropriately.The narrative is hard to explain without spoiling it's biggest moments, because it's a story with a big difference between "what is it about" and "what happens".The events of the story are a series of strung together and fairly uninspired cyberpunk police oriented action setpieces and character beats that will leave the vast majority of players unsatisfied by the time they see it end, but the storyline going on under the surface and the themes therein I found extremely compelling and had an interesting spin on the idea's of the stories this game was clearly inspired by, so if you pay attention to the world and subtext here you're definitely rewarded for it.The biggest thing holding this game back, and the thing that makes it much harder than I wish it was to recommend it is the disparity in price and content.My first playthrough took me about 7 hours and at least an hour, maybe more of that were spent indulging in the minigames, but aside from said minigames the game severely lacks optional content, and as replayable as I find it, and as much as I personally feel I got my money's worth purely from the charm of the experience, that's not an easy sell for everyone and if you don't love this game like it's your child by the time the credits roll, you'll likely feel a bit ripped off having paid almost $90AUD for such a short and comparatively unpolished product.Nevertheless I had an extraordinary time with Wanted: Dead and if you long for the days of classic, no holds barred 2000s console game charm then this is one not to miss, at least on a good sale.Final Verdict: 6.5/10Feels Like: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted Dead is still a game in progress, but it's progressing in a positive direction. It wears many of it's hollywood, anime and sci-fi influences on it's sleeve and while not a deep meditation on the cyber punk genre by any means, Wanted Dead still offers something that you can't quite find anywhere else.The game is challenging, and fans of difficult action games like Sekiro, Souls, Ninja Gaiden, DMC and others will generally find something to sink their teeth into on the gameplay front and fans of quirky auteur style games like those of Swery65, Suda51, and Hideo Kojima will similarly find little flourishes that will scratch that itch for a game with a unique voice.

_childDocuments_.review: I was disappointed when  was released (February 2023). But it's because I set the wrong expectations; I didn't give it an honest chance. I was approaching this believing it would be something comparable to what has been released in the past few years. I thought that's what I was craving - I was wrong.Wanted: Dead is arcade gameplay comfort food. It's something other than what you play for story completion or optimal graphics. You play it because it's fun.I appreciate Wanted: Dead so much more now as, although incredibly imperfect, it only covers a little of what makes modern-day game design unbearable. Yes, it's janky, but AAA games these days are so optimized that they have become dull with .Remnant 2 is a prime example of a game receiving plenty of praise from reviewers and players. Still, I refunded it because although it is universally praised, it suffers from this  mentality that runs rampant with game design. Modern-day games feel bloated and full of filler that puts me to sleep. And although Wanted: Dead has some silly cutscenes and useless but fun mini-games, it trims a lot of the fat and just lets the player dive right in.Several negative reviews highlight the game's length, but it is perfect when you approach it like an arcade game. Each level feels distinct from the others and has end-level bosses. There's a lot of variety in approaching situations - you don't have to parry everything. This is a mistake I made when I first started playing. There isn't a scoring system, but I still want to re-run levels. An additional "Japanese Difficulty" is an admittedly cool name, too.After giving this a second chance,

_childDocuments_.review: It's trying to be Metal Gear Rising, or Devil May Cry, God of War with a mix of Max Payne, or maybe Resident Evil 5, but combat feels so stiff and lacks impact.Enemies are bullet sponges, you have little ammo and they keep running around. You can empty entire clips on certain enemies, all headshots, and they don't die! So as a shooter, it's annoying.Melee enemies have fast and high damaging attacks, even on the first level. You have very few attacks, and other than cool animations for finishers, it gets repetitive before you even finish level one.  Transitioning from melee into sprint feels unresponsive.But the absolute deal breaker is the checkpoints! I'm a 80s gamer, when they said the checkpoints were bad i scoffed. But no, they're AWFUL and get worse the further you get in the game. For example: There is one area in the mid-game that makes you fight 4 shield SQUADS (without grenades they're tedious af), then 7 waves of generic samurai and soldier enemies, then a ninja (which is basically a mini boss) and to top it off TWO Heavies (which are also like mini-bosses). You have to beat all that with 4 health packs and 1 revive, mind you even a single samurai unit can insta-kill you if you fail the parry. This is Dark Souls on steroids, imagine having to beat dark souls but you MUST kill every single enemy with 4 Estus flasks while shooters slowly drain your health with nothing you can do about it but try to kill them faster. Even Ninja Gaiden wasn't this obnoxious!It's not a terrible game, it just has some very odd design choices and poor balancing. Call it "old style of game" if you want, but games like Devil May Cry and even WET weren't this bad.If enemies took more damage and staggered, while melee combat being more like classic prince persia duels. This could be a fun game. Unfortunately there isn't such a mod.I dunno, maybe the devs thought it was too easy and instead of making smarter AI they just increased the difficulty with more health pools and tanky enemies.Looks pretty though and has cool designs.Do NOT get this game. Buy Sleeping Dogs, Sifu or something!

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly positive reviews paint this game as one of those 'so bad it's good' games.  I personally couldn't get through the first level without getting bored.  Voice acting actually felt AI Generated because of the lack of emotion and quality.Details that I didn't pick up from other reviews (Played on Normal):-Keyboard controls are a bit jank because they tried to do melee and ranged at once while still letting you hip fire.  But the only sort of annoying thing is you can only back out of certain menus with backspace.-No regenerating health with limited heals.  Checkpoints are frequent and you get a little health back from melee stuff, but it's one of those 'grey health only' sorts of heals.  This is not told to you in the tutorial-Adding onto the last point, enemies are very accurate and cover only works sometimes.  There is no warning you're about to be shot at except for heavy ranged attacks like shotguns, so you're constantly taking chip damage.-If you get hit in melee, you take most of your health in damage and if you get stuck in a combo because your handgun parry hit someone different, you usually die.  -Very little ammo supply so you're encouraged to go into melee and get it back from fallen guns.-The first miniboss is mostly melee but also has a damaging ranged attack that isn't telegraphed and he likes to use it point blank, and if you aren't expecting him, he can just instantly kill you.My main issue is that even when I figured out how the game wants you to play, it just wasn't really all that fun.  Sprint in, stab someone, occasionally shoot, occasionally parry or block.There are probably actual enemy variants later on that change up the gameplay but as far as I got it was just the same enemys over and over again and you didn't need to ever change your playstyle to deal with them.

_childDocuments_.review: Sooooo, it's going to be probably one of my weirdest reviews. I don't recommend Wanted: Dead not because it's bad, but to give a word of caution. I enjoyed what the game had to offer, but I can't broadly recommend it. It's NOT for everyone.One of the best ways to sum it up was a Polygon review I saw comparing this game to the French New Wave in cinema and ... it's not an absurd comparison. Wanted: Dead is an experimental game oozing with passion for the videogame medium, but it's an acquired taste. Most people won't get past the jankiest combat system of the 2020s, or the random tonal shifts, or the non-sensical retro-futurist setting, or the "plot".It's an acquired taste. It's something you'll have trouble to find interest in if you were not playing obscure AA titles during the PS2/Gamecube/Xbox and the PS3/X360 era. Games as random as Soldier of Fortune, Project: Snowblind, Binary Domain, No More Heroes 1 & 2 or WET. If you can think of one feature from that era, chances are Wanted: Dead tried to have it in, including drawbacks you didn't think you could still find nowadays, such as the camera consistently being lost and getting you blindsided by enemies like it's 2002.It's a game trying to do everything at once and failing at most of what it tries to accomplish.That being said and despite the jankiness, Wanted: Dead is the only game cramming a shooter/beat 'em all hybrid with John Wick-finishing moves, Cyborg Ninjas AND Samurais, a soundtrack featuring Quiet from MGSV singing 80s inspired pop, a Yakuza-style karaoke game in German, a Taiko no Tatsujin spoof based on slurping ramen, Tarantino-diner scenes, a *complete* Gradius clone with gorgeous pixel art and anime flashbacks in one package.And it's a clear work of passion that, despite being not that great, left a greater impression on me than most videogames I played this year.So, to sum it up, if you're a casual gamer looking for a safe choice to pass a few hours, you will probably regret spending money on this game.If you come prepared, you will probably enjoy it. And you'll definitely have a reason to be a snob to those From Software plebs who think they know what Old-School Hardcore Games are ! (Too far ?.. Too far.)

_childDocuments_.review: Hits that gaming itch like I expected. Even though simplistic the combat formula/timing is difficult which was an immediate hook for me. The dialogue is goofy and intentionally bad reminiscent of Suda51 games, Hideki Kamiya's God Hand, and Swery65's Deadly Premonition. Much like the games aforementioned the whole package feels gamey/fun which is why I would recommend it.The jank is definitely present. You will see enemies spinning in circles/facing walls and you'll find yourself aiming/shooting through walls, but the flow of the combat is a lot of fun once you unlock new abilities from the skill tree. My only major complaint is that the abilities you unlock are things you should have from the get go. For example: the ability to follow up with a pistol shot after a pistol parry feels like second nature, but the game restricts you from the follow up attack until you unlock it. Once you start unlocking abilities Wanted: Dead's combat flow becomes a lot more interesting and that along with the quirky story make for an enjoyable game.All aspects of the game feel like something reminiscent of the seventh era of games (PS3/360) which isn't very common these days, and I'm here for the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like the year 2008 somehow manifested itself as a video game. Do you remember those small-to-medium sized games that were pumped out by random studios, offering interesting ideas and somewhat solid gameplay under unpolished, janky, lackluster packages? Stuff like the Altered Beast reboot, Wet, John Woo's Stranglehold, 50 Cent: Blood on the Sand, Nanobreaker, between many others.This is exactly it, but somehow released now.The voice acting is horrible. Cutscenes are buggy, have weird animations, pop-in. unsynced dialogue and the weirdest writing that feels as if it was written using Google Translate. The gameplay is glitchy, enemies will sometimes go invisible, weapons will clip through geometry...... but even then, this game is filled with charm. The core gameplay itself is fun, challenging and hard to master-- exactly what you'd expect from the people behind Ninja Gaiden. Parrying, comboing with the sword and mixing TPS shooting with slashing feels very fun and addicting. The replayable nature of the game and the enemy variety allows for players to sink in a lot of time into the game.It's not for everyone and it's not a great game, but what's there to be enjoyed is pretty good under the right circumstances and eyes. It's that charming PS2/Xbox 360 era jank that has a A LOT of heart put into it and can entertain those with the right mindset for it.Stefanie Joosten is in it, too.7/10P.S.: Wanted: Dead has the worst grenade launcher I have ever seen in a videogame. Ever.

_childDocuments_.review: —a game shrouded in criticism for its so-called "jank." But let me ask you, pathetic humans, what do you even mean by "jank"? Is it clunky controls? Unpolished mechanics? Or is it simply that your feeble minds can’t handle a game that dares to be a bit different? As a seasoned warrior of Cybertron, I find this kind of nitpicking weak.First, let's be clear: Wanted: Dead  The combat feels fluid, responsive, and most importantly, satisfying. Melee and gunplay blend seamlessly, offering a visceral experience that pulls you in with every brutal execution and well-timed parry. There’s a rhythm to the chaos, much like a well-orchestrated Decepticon invasion, and once you get into the groove, it’s a blast.Yes, it’s not perfect, but that's what gives it character. If "jank" means moments where the game’s rough edges show, I call that charm—something even the most polished titles often lack. For all those critics crying about it, maybe they just don't know how to handle a bit of unpredictability.What’s more, the game's environments and character designs, while not revolutionary, fit the gritty, neon-lit dystopia it presents. It’s a place where chaos reigns, and if you ask me, it's quite fitting for someone like me—ruthless, sharp, and unforgiving.The story? Serviceable. It won't win awards, but it's enough to push you through the action. But let’s be real here, nobody’s playing Wanted: Dead for its narrative complexity. You’re here for the combat, the challenge, and maybe a little bit of that so-called "jank" that gives the game its unique flavor.In short, I find Wanted: Dead to be an underrated gem. If you’re a Decepticon—or just someone tired of perfectly polished, soulless games—give it a try. I give it a 7/10So, before you dismiss it based on what others say, take up your weapons and dive in. You might just find that its rough edges are what make it shine.—Starscream, Ruler of Off-Topic and Commander of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is pure action, difficulty, and frenetic gameplay, which I've been longing for since Ninja Gaiden. The absurdity of the world, characters, and tight pacing will make this title a cult classic.I'm surprised (and glad) a game like this can still be developed. It's even more surprising that it has been received relatively positively by some mainstream critics (or more so it's being recognized for its attempt at subverting modern gaming tropes), especially in this rigid Soulsbourne zeitgeist that nearly all action/RPG games are now evaluated under (which a overhaul of that style is long overdue).Playing a game like Wanted: Dead will make one realize how homogeneous AA and AAA games have been in this decade. There is a crisis among the contemporary gaming community that AAAs are uninspired, designed to maximize capital returns at all costs, and just flat-out boring. And playing this game makes one realize style, irony, camp, and creativity aren't video game virtues that they once were. The indie scene has been pushing these boundaries, but major publishers and developers are no where to be seen.I can't think of an AA or AAA game in the last five to ten years that had this much fun with itself, and rejected the self-serious, pretentious tone that too many have these days. There's room for those games, but there is a crater of empty space where games that are just simply fun to play are supposed to be.TLDR: it's an absurd postmodern masterpiece that very few major-publisher titles have attempted before. Most agree this game will only receive more and more recognition as time goes on -- but I hope it does even more: revitalize the emphasis on creativity and fun (and subsequently deemphasize narrative games that feel like they're trying to get nominated for an Oscar).

_childDocuments_.review: is a gory and challenging action game with fast-paced, unforgiving combat. You take the role of Hannah Stone, a lieutenant of the Hong Kong police and member of a four-person squad infamous for wanton destruction. They are tasked to uncover a corporate conspiracy involving one of the major producers of synthetic humanoids on the market. The game is split into five lengthy missions of multiple stages.The combat is a mix of third person shooter and slasher, with Lt. Stone and her team making their way through hordes of enemies. Baddies are primarily dispatched using katana and pistol combos, which routinely comes with a loss of limbs on their end, and there are some twenty-odd finisher attacks (which don’t quite approach the Mortal Kombat gore level). The window for parrying enemy attacks is very tight and once you’re hit, it’s very difficult to prevent further hits. There is a short window to recover some of the lost health by dishing out more damage. There is a skill tree in which you progress at a pleasant pace, but only because the game is rather short.The combat has a number of janky aspects. Oftentimes when you are fighting enemies up close, the too-close camera position makes it hard to see enemies to your sides and behind you. Compared to other parry-reliant titles this is unnecessarily bothersome. Further harming your spatial awareness are two other issues: your teammates are too difficult to distinguish from enemies in the heat of battle, especially on dark levels, and it is too hard to keep track of which enemies are still alive and thus dangers you have to be aware of. Since you can partially dismember many of your opponents without fully incapacitating them, just seeing gore isn’t a clear indicator. The only clear ways to know is a tiny visual indicator showing XP gain, and the very repetitive death scream you hear from most enemy types. With a less close camera, teammate icons, and perhaps outlines for living enemies, you could be spared some deaths that are frustrating only because the game does not provide you enough clarity.Other glitchy or just unpolished bits that are less of a bother are that snap-aiming on enemies sprinting at you often just doesn’t work and instead puts your crosshair far to the side, and that weapons you intended to leave on the ground for later or were using when you got downed like to despawn. Notably, the powerful chainsaw is just gone from the game if you die holding it, and it can feel more efficient to die again to retry from the last checkpoint to get it back.The systems design of  regularly bites off much more than it should be trying to chew. There’s a cover system that doesn’t make all that much sense in this game, as you have to constantly keep moving and attacking. Shooting in general is not very effective, with an enemy requiring many bullets to kill, and many of the available weapons suffer both from a lack of accuracy and a lack of available ammunition. Besides a weapon slot for guns you take from enemies or the environment, you have an assault rifle that you can customize at checkpoints, min-/maxing its stats using the gradually increasing amount of available parts. None of these mechanics really had to be in the game.While her teammates are close by in most of the fights, the player can’t control them, and they typically do not kill too many enemies on their own. Only Doc has the less cosmetic purpose of providing the player one revive per checkpoint. The only other healing is through injecting stimpacks that some stronger enemies can drop on the lower difficulty modes.You can’t talk about  without touching on how it’s both way too little game for the $40 asking price, yet in other areas there’s inexplicably much content. There are only five missions for a eight to ten hour duration, which goes down to around four hours for an experienced player on a lower difficulty level. At the same time, it has as many wacky minigames as you would expect in a Yakuza title. A collectible might just play a lengthy character backstory flashback. Shortly after the first mission, a memory is played out as an anime. There even are several minutes-long live-action cooking videos!This discrepancy leads to the matter of who should and who shouldn’t be recommended the game:There are so many largely-intentional idiosyncrasies in . This starts with the main character being a war criminal released from prison, pressed into police service, but with a wholesome work environment and an active dating life. The game can’t even decide if she’s a police  or  – the terms are just used interchangeably. Despite her English/American last name of Stone, she is supposedly Swiss, and speaks with a thick German accent (this admittedly is addressed by the end of the game). Meanwhile, her Russian teammate Doc has the least Russian voice ever.There’s a full shoot ’em up created by Japanese developer PiXEL that is also available as a . Characters have cybernetic implants, there are parody soft drink companies, and random references to our pop culture that don’t exactly make sense in a post-nuclear-war future. So many intentionally goofy things made it into this release, in a way it’s truly "art for art’s sake".The game’s  mode was initially hidden behind a cheat code and only unlocked for everyone a year after the release. The Steam comment section of that patch is chock-full of complaints that there shouldn’t be an easy mode to begin with, and complaining about other beginner-focused QoL improvements of adding an extra checkpoint and a health bar to the first difficult mini-boss.If you value challenge more than polish, this title might just be what you’re looking for. An adequate new game plus lets you hone your skills over and over. is very much aimed at hardcore players, who don’t get frustrated from repeatedly dying and repeating a fight as often as needed. The enemies are tough as nails and the damage received can feel massive, even when playing on  difficulty mode. The recently-unlocked  mode is far less challenging, but does not feel like the intended gameplay experience.Getting all the achievements not only requires completing the game on the three non-easy difficulty modes, but also flawlessly hitting some 800 key presses in a rhythm mini game. Unless you mastered several Dark Souls titles, this is unlikely to be a game you can get all the achievements in.Fortunately, collectible and achievement progress accumulate across your different save games, so it’s not necessary to find all items in the same run, or to complete tasks like performing 100 handgun counters to unblockable attacks on the same save. is recommendable to players belonging to two particular niches: the "git gud" difficulty fanatics will be pleased that the game is quite hard on  mode, after which there’s  and the appropriately-named . 1980s B-movie connoisseurs. The other group will appreciate the game for being , from the retro-cyber-futuristic world building all the way to the many intentionally odd and unfortunately-janky parts of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted Dead is a brilliant action game. If you like Ninja Gaiden Sigma, you will love it. A higher difficulty is more fun in this game since you really need to be strategic about the choice to attack (shooting, two grenades, and melee) and defense. Through the gameplay, you would find and establish your favorite strategies/skills like guard canceling, sliding/jumping attacks with a hand-gan combo, or grenades after incendiary grenades, which are not expressed in the training mode explicitly. The best parts: - Well-thought-out combat with shooting, grenades, and melee. - Excellent character design: I love all team members and bosses. Especially, Stone is a unique, stylish female protagonist with tenderness, calmness, and cruelty. - Not-too-complicated game system. You can play this game without learning too many rules in the game system. You focus on learning game strategy/play itself. The parts that could be better: - Storytelling: The developer could put more information on the story. The story looks exciting, but it is impossible to understand clearly.- Voice acting. It is actually bad...- Police station: This is basically a fascinating idea. But if the developer spent more effort to create a vibrant atmosphere so that the player can feel and live the everyday life of people in this police station, the later event would be more impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: Lieutenant Hannah Stone is an ex-convict relocated to the Zombie Unit, an elite squad of Hong Kong police on a mission to uncover a major corporate conspiracy. Her methods are unorthodox, but the results are always unquestionable.Developed by former Team Ninja employees, it's a hack & slash (only with katana) and 3rd person shooter with covers, which forces you to use all available mechanics, something that encourages strategic gameplay but feels uphill at first contact. At the controls, the sensations are similar to those hack & slash more unknown PS2, as Nanobreaker, Devil Kings or Nightshade. Sometimes bordering on the B series, especially with dub and narrative (somewhat rough) loaded with clichés of crime movies of the 80s/90s. The difficulty as a trademark of the house is felt from the first stage with a melee combat that, without being as precise as other exponents of the genre, is demanding in the dodge and parry of a special attack with a very short reaction window (can be improved).Since it's not a long game, I recommend a first run in "Neko-chan" mode to get used to the mechanics and enjoy Hannah with these badass kawaii cat ears.Although the core of the game is based on shootouts and sword duels, between stages we can go through the police station where we can collect documents that expand the lore of the game and participate in minigames such as karaoke, UFO-Catcher, eating ramen or playing some shmup.Cons?~ It has a lot of cinematics (some cool anime style) and yet the plot is unintelligible as heck~ Poorly balanced difficulty modes (same experience as Left Alive by S-E)~ Checkpoints too far apart on the last stage~ No NG+And despite the above tweet I recommend it (at the right price, of course). It's a lighthearted game that offers pure challenge and fun without hijacking you for hundreds of hours, that didn't deserve the treatment it received from much of the press.

_childDocuments_.review: I plan to write a piece for my Website/Youtube, but for those curious about the game, I'll give you a mini review.Wanted: Dead is a very fun game, BUT it isn't for everyone AND the game TAKES SOME GETTING USED TO.  Allow me to explain.I first tried this game, thought it was incredibly clunky, unfun, the enemies had too much healthy and the damage was punishing for no reason.  The gameplay was a lot of Jank.  However, the game gets more fun the more you understand the flow of combat and unlock skills which aid in the experience.Learning how to utilize the parry system, the skill upgrade which allows you to do finishes on dismembered opponents, and a few of the defensive upgrades (damage taken decreased) will help out tremendously.  But also learning to use cover, patterns of discouraging enemies, and in later levels, keeping the Light Machine Gun on you.The game in and of itself has its own charm, and the Jank and characters leave a very unique experience.  The biggest issue with this game is that they use old school "Play and figure it out" in place of holding the players hand and giving them enough support early-on to make the flow of the game more digestible.  It's not very palatable initially and turns into an all-you-can-eat later, which makes you want more.I plan on trying it out on the "Japanese Hard" mode, but one play through with the game is honestly enough.  It's very memorable and should've did better, but it makes a very bad first impressions but makes up for it the longer you stick with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not for everyone. The dialogues are weird, the action is interpolated with minigames such as karaoke and ramen eating, and the checkpoints can be pretty brutal. But this is a really, really good action game. The animations are superb and the combat flows in a very satisfying way after you understand it. It's one of those games that asks you to use and understand every mechanic available, and if you do try to really *get* how the combat works it's hard to imagine you being unhappy with it. It really is quite great.And while the dialogues *are* weird and the story feels unfinished, it's also all very charming. You'll find it bad if your reference for "good videogame narrative" is God of War or The Last of Us, but fans of offbeat Japanese creators like myself (think SWERY, Suda51, etc) will eat it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Is the game objectively good? No.But I really love it. It's kinda like watching a toddler try to do something and fail miserably, but you still like it because it was cute.The premise of the game is that you lead a squad made up of war criminals on dangerous missions. Your squad is effective but leaves way too much collateral. That's it.On one hand, the writing is very confusing — I could tell you some of the things that happen in the game, but not how they connect into a coherent narrative. By the end we kinda get most of the context for the main character's backstory, but not for the game's story in present day. It really feels like the story was trying to emulate a Kojima game, but didn't have the means to do that and it just ended up being a confusing mess.On the other, you have one of your squadmates cracking a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ joke and the protagonist repeatedly yelling at him to shut the **** up. The cutscenes are riddled with stiff animations and nonexistent lip syncing,  but then you get high effort ones when the main character tries to eat the cafeteria lunch and fails because the food is as solid as concrete. Also, you get really high effort anime cutscenes that just pop out outta nowhere.The combat is fun, albeit simplistic. You have melee combat that generally involves your katana and handgun, and ranged which involves your assault rifle and whatever you can pick up from fallen enemies. Ranged combat is serviceable at best, melee is where it's at. It can be a bit button mashy, but stunning the enemy with your handgun and proceeding to combo them with your katana is pretty fun. Takedowns are also cool and varied and can be chained together.Voice acting is atrocious aside from exactly one character - Gunsmith, played by Stefanie Joosten (voice of Quiet in MGSV), who also lends her face to the character. Voice actors for most characters, including the protagonist, very noticeably aren't native English speakers. This might have been done on purpose, as the story implies they are there as immigrants and are in danger of being deported if they screw up. It's a bit overkill though — the voice actress for the main character has a very thick German accent and a lot of time it feels like she doesn't know what the lines she's saying even mean, and is only pronouncing them the way she thinks they should sound. This results in a lot of sentences with completely wrong intonation and pronunciation, that end up not fitting into the dialogue at all.One area the game excels at is the soundtrack. There are covers of popular 80s songs, half of which are sang by the previously mention Stefanie Joosten, and the other half by a band named Bella and the Switchblades. I recommend you listen to the cover of "She works hard for the money", it has a really well made anime music video on YouTube.There are also several mini games like you'd find in a Yakuza game. Karaoke of course, is there. But there's a catch — the only song you can sing is 99 red balloons, in German. This might be some sort of meta commentary on the state of German karaoke bars, but the dev team is part Canadian, part Japanese, so I don't see why that would be the case.All in all, if you can find the game at a steep discount and go in with tempered expectations, there's a janky and charming game waiting to be played.

_childDocuments_.review: Expect to die a lot. This game doesn't hold your hand. You will "Git Gud" the more you play. As you unlock more skills the flow of combat becomes a lot more fluid too. You'll become a parry master in no time and be pulling off multiple finishers on groups of enemies if you take the effort to feel how the game flows. Wanted: Dead is deliberately made to feel like an old school action game from the ps2/ps3 era. There is no Health Regen. You will have to rely on your limited health items. When you reach checkpoints you will get resupplied with ammo and healing items. The end of each stage has Boss Fights.Between stages you can explore the Police HQ floors and play some amusing mini games. The voice acting is very...bad but in a good bad way.  The game did crash a few times thought that didn't stop my enjoyment or finishing the game. I hope Soleil does roll out a patch for that. Overall it was a fun ride and had a lot of fun. If you like old school action games I say buy whenever. If not my more unbiased opinion would be to wait for a price drop.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead was, from what I played of it, a very fun 3D action game, though the PC port is marred by performance issues.  If you wanted a game where you play as a militarized police unit, with an aesthetic similar to Deadly Premonition, then Wanted: Dead is definitely your game.  Ideologically, Wanted: Dead presents a cyberpunk, dystopian setting.  Given the present political situation here in the states, with the recent killing of a protester and environmental activist by a similar, but real militarized police force, just take note that you're playing the game from the perspective of these folks being "good, well-meaning folks."  Just something to note, I feel.That said, the action is relatively straight forward and eschews the combo/juggling approach modern action games take in lieu of snappy finishers and dismemberment.  The game is very much like a spiritual successor to Ninja Gaiden 2, for better or worse.  I even got into a fight where I was eating munitions fire while fighting an homage to the tank from the ending of Ghost in the Shell.I didn't have enough time to really gauge where the game is going, but there remains one issue that prevents me from recommending this game which is its very poor optimization and performance.  The game has a quirky sense of humor, intentional or otherwise.  Once on sale, and with some fixes, I plan on giving it another shot.  For now, I consider what I did to be a demo where I paid collateral to experience. Works great on console comparatively, though I still ran into some bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, challenging third-person hack-and-slash/shooter with lots of silly comedy and fun characters. The cutscenes add a unique style to the story-telling with the way Stone's flashbacks are depicted in anime style and the campy voice-over only further adds to the charm of the characters. The music is great too, with a mix of instrumental tracks and Stefanie Joosten's foray into music serving to liven things up with disco beats and 80s pop.On top of the main story, there are a multitude of mini-games that offer collectibles and unlockables throughout the game's main story - figurines that are displayed in your office, music that you can play as well as new tracks for the rhythm game (a minigame where you eat ramen to the beat of the music!) all giving the game plenty of variety and some much-needed downtime inbetween missions.All in all, there's a lot of content here and the game has a fun atmosphere that few games ever manage to capture. Easily worth the asking price at 30 bucks!

_childDocuments_.review: Duration: Steam says 6.9 hours (nice) but at least one of those hours was me tabbing out to try and process what I was playingScore: 2/10Advertised as a throwback to the sixth generation of consoles and a love letter to the 'uber-difficult action games' of the PS2 era, Wanted: Dead would really love for you to believe that its problems are intentional. After playing through it myself in a fever dream of a week, however, I'm not convinced of this claim. I can say with confidence that this is the worst game I've ever bothered to finish, and in the interest of an honest review, I feel compelled to explore why. Taking place in an alternative 2022 where a war between the East and West allowed super-corps to take over, Wanted: Dead has all the window dressing of a compelling cyberpunk setting and there's errant threads of a story attempting to be told about worker's rights, but it's buried under what can only be described as a love letter to police brutality. A death row convict placed in command of similarly condemned elites that make up a Suicide Squad-style 'Zombie Unit', protagonist Hannah Stone sleepwalks her way through a disconnected intrigue when she's not busy abruptly passing out to trigger a random cutscene or having the history of ramen noodles narrated to her in a one-off joke that's as insipid as it is abrupt.Onto my usual summary of the pluses and minuses, dropped abruptly into the middle of this review to better reflect the random tonal shifts and one-off scenes of the subject at hand.+Hannah's design is cool, and she's mostly likeable, voice acting aside.+The finishers are a weird highlight; there's a lot of them, they're flashy, and they look cool+It only crashed once, I guess.-Presentation is awful. Graphics, music, voice acting, all just bottom of the barrel-Combat is still and overly simplistic, substituting punishing enemies to try and mask a tiny moveset and simple, predictable patterns/enemy type-The story is disjointed and incoherent, gleefully jumping between random scenes and sabotaging any interesting ideas it has-Infrequent checkpoints and endless corridors grind repetition into the player regardless of difficulty level-Damage sponge bosses with predictable patterns make for dull fights-The entire cast outside of the protagonist are unlikeable, one note, and for the most part, aggressively awful people-Undercuts what little it has to say-Somehow feels padded and profanely inefficient even with a 5-6 hour runtime-The third person shooting element is bolted-on and doesn't work wellOn paper, I should have been the target audience for this game. I famously love jank. Creative but rough-edged videogames are among my favorites, and I even played some of the incredibly weird Zeno Clash II alongside Wanted: Dead just to make sure my 'clumsy creativity' censor wasn't broken. But despite the stiff combat, terrible voice acting, repetitive gameplay, and incoherent plot, jank isn't actually my problem with Wanted: Dead. It's a lack of ambition; it's the game being so obsessed with mimicking the B-movie nostalgia of mid-budget 2005 games that it forgets to actually stand on its own in any way, and it doesn't even have the courtesy to be an entertaining ripoff of better trash. It's got the jank but not the creativity, all too content to tread tired police squad stereotypes, needlessly infrequent checkpoints, and repetitive 'skill-based' gameplay that just amounts to button-mashing until you have to perform a timed parry pattern. What little the game had to say that hasn't been done in other, better games is abandoned for the next hallway of faceless goons and wooden acting.In trying to ape the charm of a supposedly bygone era of gaming, Wanted: Dead instead accidentally drops its mask and reveals itself to lack inspiration and focus. It desperately wants to convince you that it's not like other modern games, but it doesn't actually put the effort in, substituting random vignettes for genuine charm and odious stereotypes for witty characters. I walked away genuinely angry at the game, not for being bad, but for trying to take a bite of a too-small mindshare in gaming, wearing 'old-school quirkiness' like a hat without actually doing anything to earn it. If you really miss cool middle-budget games inspired by the early 2000s, respect your own time and play one of the good ones; they're not as rare as Wanted: Dead would like you to think. Space Marine II just came out and it's pretty cool. Try a cool indie title like Katana Zero; give a difficult-but-creative game like Arboria your time. Hell, just reinstall Metal Gear Rising again, since this seems so obsessed with trying to be it in the second half. But don't believe Wanted: Dead's lies. It doesn't give a ♥♥♥♥ about the games it's trying to mimic.I don't think it even likes them.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: C+This is, hands down, the best C+ game I have ever played. Before getting too far I need to emphasize that on a purely technical front, the game is thoroughly mediocre. Its two major combat styles, third-person shooter, and brawler, are stapled together with the elegance of a back-alley surgeon. Switching between the two styles during combat never felt unnatural and stiff. Especially by the end, the combat wore very thin. Long hordes of enemies with very little variety who only get spongier as the game continues. The core combat system also lacks the depth of its contemporaries which leads to repetitive, tedious encounters.  Yet, I still love this game. The characters are poorly acted and the plot has three different threads running simultaneously and concludes none of them. But it has heart. This game constantly makes baffling, unorthodox decisions which only come from a group of people working on their passion project. Why make eating ramen an insanely difficult rhythm game? Why have karaoke with only one song? Why make a full (pretty decent) shmup? So many questions and the game refuses them all.  At the same time, there are moments of legitimate, no qualifiers excellence. A couple scenes in particular, (about halfway through and the after-credits scene) are wonderfully done and show a real understanding of narrative and visual storytelling. On the other end, there are scenes which routinely made me laugh, actually laugh out-loud at the line delivery or the script or the visuals. The charm is palpable, even if the skill isn’t always. But peculiarities like these make me feel the people behind the game. This is a piece of art, however flawed, made by real human hands who aspired to make something great. And, in a way, they accomplished just that. I will think about this game far more than “objectively” better titles because of the soul, passion, and sheer absurdity. While a deeply flawed title, I will hold it close to my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a solid "B-movie" game. It has flows, but it is not like there are tonnes of gun-fu games with lots of juicy blood and dismemberment. I'd totally love to get other games like this, hopefully more polished.I've bought it on a discount and finished it after anniversary patch on normal.Technical state was fine for me: no drops, stutters, major bugs etc. Visually it looks fine to me, combat animations were good, I liked the design of the heroine.Voice acting (eng) sounded specially amateur to me, but it's fine, adds to that B-movie vibe.Story was whatever, it doesn't really have ending. You might think the main focus was about corpo power struggle, but the ending is to the absolutely another story line you didn't really know existed until that point. Anyway, the main reason to play this game is the combat. It consists of two parts. The first part is sword and handgun Sekiro-like melee combat. You hit, block and parry with a sword, you stugger to come closer and to extend sword-strings with a handgun, and you parry some special attacks with a handgun. And you have "rage"-meter and finishing moves. When you cap your meter, you press it to stagger up to the whole room of regular enemies and finish them all with a single smooth finishing move. All of it looks pretty awesome,  you may cut a limb, cut them in half, there a great variety of finishing moves and they are quick and satisfying. The blood stays on you, so to the end of a mission you're fully covered in it. Absolutely love it!The second part is your average third person cover shooter with rifles and grenades. Nothing to wright home about. Kinda clunky with a gamepad.You want to play meele all the time, it is a lot more engaging and satisfying system, but closer to the end you kinda forced to switch to cover shooter time to time. The segments between checkpoints getting longer, the amount and dunger of enemies grow and potions are very scarce.  And while ranged damage is mostly a joke to you, and you are totally able to run on a 5 gunners with just a sword, their cheap dmg adds up. So instead of running in sword blasing you have to play lame and methodical. I mean, it's not that bad, but it is a bit of "you gave me this new awesome toy, and now you want me to play tetris for a few minutes" situation.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the common fatal crashes, janky ai interacting w/ the environment at times and few bugs, its a solid 7 or 7.5 game. The core gameplay and mechanics are quite good. Melee combos flow well. Attacks can be guard canceled, or canceled into shooting. It has good hit stun, satisfying gory finishers. Having melee (and a pistol), 2 firearms, 2 grenade types, parries, and dodges gives the players options to deal w/ the various combo of enemies thrown at you. One would think that it would be weird to combine action game mechanics w/ a third person shooter but it actually works. Some would say its a bit short but its honestly nice to able to finish a playthru in a few hours rather than several, it also means you can do more play thrus on harder difficulties. The only thing I don't like is the mandatory mini-games in the middle of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's certainly not for everyone but so far all the negatives in this can also be considered positives if you just don't take the game that seriously and have a laugh over it.-The voice acting is terrible in an amazing way, for some reason I still felt for the characters and I don't want it any different.-The game's story is everywhere yet it feels like it's at least getting somewhere at the same time.-It has such randomness while also having serious moments (or at least tried to) which makes me wonder what the hell they were going for, but in a good way.-There's so many unnecessary minigames thrown at you but I can't even be mad at them because they're an absolute blast to play through. Multiple times I almost laughed myself to death in the karaoke.-It switches to an anime art style at random times for no particular reason but it somehow fits in as well.-It has a supahotfire loading screen reference sometimes.-Stefanie Joosten did a portion of the soundtrack and even got a role in the game. I love to be dutch.-The game feels short and thus can quite come over as a lot of things just quickly thrown together and happening way too quick but at the same time it feels like it's just enough, especially if you want to do a second playthrough. Although I certainly have been wanting more.-The combat feels great and clunky at the same time, but never felt..Too unfair at times? Sure it has some moments where I had to take a break but it wasn't too bad. The end where it's just one big hallway shooter with loads of bullet sponges thrown at you wasn't very fun though not gonna lie.This game is FAR from perfect but I definitely believe it will gather a cult following as it's not even a terrible game. It's really not for everyone but I absolutely love it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself has a few flaws that need to be addressed. The main character Lt. Stone couldve been the nextgen kill bill movie style waifu but instead we got dead line emotionless line delivery Voice Actress. Not trying to disrespect her work but this type game requires a different delivery and personality. Think of the crisis remaster with new zack VA except less cringey but even less emotion. The camera is your enemy as its hard to focus properly with controls and you need to work on the sensitivity asap. 3rd person camera also is sort of fixed over the right shoulder style which is awkward for some. Especially when its too close to you and you're trying to pan for enemies and youre view is severely limited.Its a awkward mix of 3rd person shooter and sword melee but fails to implement both in a meaningful manner and the camera adds to the ughhh factor. Ammo is hard to find and you can unload your entire supply almosy entirely on two enemies. Then you need to melee but if you go swords blazing you get dropped by enemies have to fall back to cover shooting. It wants to be dmc style action but is reduced to awkward cover shooter with enemies that move around ALOT. Combine these quirks with bad camera work and the ehh cgi movie cutscenes and the dead delivery of the va lines and youre left with a game that you wish had more time in the oven to cook.The best part of this game is the trailers and the game art screenshots which sold me but wow i feel burned. The actual end product however is really rough janky double A lost-in-time of a previous era game. At least its not forspoken levels of dialogue

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely underrated. There’s a lot of depth to the combat and charm to the story and characters. I think a lot of people went into this thinking that it would be like every other character action game. Instead, the game’s combat focuses on controlling the battlefield and using everything in your toolkit effectively and efficiently. Figuring out when to shoot, when to throw a grenade, and when to go in for melee takedowns are all essential to your success here. It’s a very difficult game, but one that’s extremely rewarding when the combat clicks for you.Also, don’t depend too much on parties. This isn’t Sekiro. There are multiple ways to take down enemies and the challenge is deciding which method to use.
_childDocuments_.name: Wanted: Dead

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing it on Hard and Japanese Hard, I have to say that it's the most fun I've had with a game in a pretty long while. It's a short game and everything around it screams AA, so having that in mind helps to appreciate what's there - great absurdist humor, combat system that equally combines shooting and melee and stylish level design that makes you feel like you are playing a cyberpunk John Wick. Having trouble with the cyberninjas? You can combo&parry them, or you can set them on fire with a grenade and shoot them in the face. Resource management is tight, and the spacing between checkpoints in the final level is perfect for maximum tension. The plot is confusing to represent the protagonist's jumbled memories, but I honestly think it's one of the most relevant plots in recent cyberpunk.There are problems - camera bugs out quite often, minigames other than the shmup are sorta broken(but entirely skippeable), the game doesn't really explain too well how to get the maximum enjoyment out of itself, they should have included the cool marketing material like the cooking show into the game itself.I legit don't get why people complain about the voice acting - the characters sound like expats speaking in foreign language, and that's exactly who they are supposed to be. Overall, I really missed this kind of game from the times of The Punisher on ps2, Manhunt 2, BloodRayne, Enter the Matrix.. When games weren't trying to be perfect, didn't all play the same and didn't waste collossal amounts of my time with useless progression systems and empty open worlds filled with copy/pasted content.
_childDocuments_.name: Wanted: Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I did a play-through of this game right when it came out. I would describe this game as: advanced.What do I mean by that?This is not a game created/designed by a committee. Not made from focus testing. Someone had a vision and it was insane. Distilled insanity. Some of the decisions for the storytelling, voice acting, and pacing feel like dream logic. This is exactly why I love it though. Terrible/fascinating delivery of dialogue. Extremely odd minigames between missions. Full transitions into 2D anime artwork that looks like Interstella 5555. Chainsawing someone and a -CENSOR- graphic pops over their body. The artwork. The OST. Fantastic.Gameplay? Above average. Derivative. BUT.I think that's intentional? I DON'T KNOW. That's why it's so fascinating. I love the style. I love the uniqueness. Buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd easily consider this one of the most misunderstood titles in the last few years. Beyond all the silly dialogue and various slice of life cutscenes/minigames.. what you will find at the heart of the game is an excellent combat system, meshing third person shoot and cover mechanics with visceral hack and slash melee combos, all wrapped up in a short and sweet campaign spanning about 12-15 hours. The difficulty is high and you will find yourself dying and retrying sections over and over to progress. I have only played the game as of the most recent holiday 1.11 patch and on my system it feels very stable, albeit a few kinks to still work out. This game is a love letter to many games of older generations.. most notably the Ninja Gaiden series, Gears of War, Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance and Vanquish in terms of combat and style.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a type of 6/10 game that is going to be very divisive, for the people that like it its quite fun and special. But there are definitely some shortcomings. Combat is very stylish and fun, this is the highlight of the game. It has you performing melee attacks, using the pistol to interrupt incoming melee enemies, 2 types of counters with a melee parry and a gun counter against red attacks, an adrenaline guage attack that lets you do a finisher on every enemy it hits which is super cool. And some cover shooting thrown in. In a sense, it reminds me of Oni in that guns are more of a special resource than an integral part of the combat. You can use guns to eliminate problem enemies like the brown ninjas later on. The humor and general B style camp is a plus for me, its an odd game that just feels like a fever dream at times. The whole thing feels like some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ 80's straight to VHS anime ova. Both in setting and the clash of hyperviolence with off kilter humor. The main issues for me were, while the story has some actually interesting pieces to it. The delivery of the story is so clumsily done and some story elements seem to be introduced then just dropped, they leave room for a sequel at the end which.... is likely not going to happen looking at sales numbers so its all a bit of a mess. But more of a tragic mess because there really are some interesting bits, and I like the characters. Just some bad writing and directing getting in the way of it all. On the gameplay front, there are some wild difficulty curves. I played on hard mode and this was generally enjoyable but some serious inconsistency. Some later missions were easier than earlier ones, one of the bosses near the middle ended up being the hardest one for me. And at least 2 checkpoint stretches were absolutely brutal to try and get through, they could have used another checkpoint in between them. Or have the stimpack drop rates tweaked to give some sustain. What mainly sucked about these parts was I felt I had to play super cautiously (aka, in a boring fashion) so that I could have enough health and supplies for the home stretch before the next checkpoint which was normally when they threw the toughest enemies at you. Stimpack drops are very rare in my experience so you are stuck with 4 (if you got the perk) which is not much since on hardmode many enemies can straight up kill you in a combo or put you close to death. They have a bloodborne-esque rally system for the health but its pretty minor and in most cases wont change the threshold of needing to use a stimpack. And there are no skills you can buy in the skill tree to recover health either. Some other oddities: on the club level, the enemies kept repeating and layering voicelines in battle in a way that just seemed broken, and they mostly stood around too making me think the ai was broken. On the last stage it loops this music that seems fitting for like.... the literal last moment of the game, as if you were climbing a staircase up to the final showdown or something. But it plays in the entire stage. I ended up turning the music off for this part it felt so out of place and annoying. They have some odd mini games that would fit right in with Yakuza, but without the Yakuza world/ mission format this just feels out of place and im not sure the game really benefited from it. There are also no outfit unlocks or much of anything to boost replayability. If that sounds like a lot of negatives, it sort of is, but I still enjoyed the game quite a bit despite all that. Combat was great, bosses (other than that 1) were great with the last boss feeling very Sekiro. I love the character designs and general vibe of the game. Its more sad and disappointing that the game didnt live up to the potential I feel it has. Some more time in the oven and some better direction/ directing could have done wonders for it. For the price I think most people are going to enjoy this better on sale and can only recommend full price to people who really like the vibe of the game and are hoping for some thin hope that voting with your dollars may lead to some more ( and hopefully better realized ) games in the future from the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: The game-play is not smooth. It has some cool cut-scenes and some high adrenaline combat. However the gun-play is ridiculous being shot no matter how much you dodge and try to shoot without getting shot back. The melee combat however is fluid and when mixed with gun-play creates  some interesting combos. On top of that add the finishers and you have a pretty rounded action game. The graphics are good and the game runs fluid on my setup. As you complete levels you have a skill tree in which you can unlock some extra ability's and perks.It also has a really good soundtrack.The graphics are actually nice and well put together to give you that Ghost in the shell feel. Frame-rates were tight for me giving me above 70 fps with no drops.The skills you unlock are like ability's to throw grenades and dash etc there is a mix of offensive/ defensive/ and i think passive.I think if they did more work on the Gun-Play and and added Co-op there would be hours of fun to have.Also to increase the drop rate for shotgun ammo as i found you can get the gun but only use it with 3 ammo shells.I also found the cover system to be somewhat finickyI give this a 4/5Its pretty but still rough around some edges.A definite "Buy On Sale"

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly if you can get in the flow of the combat, it is hella fun! There are things that need some cleaning up and the Devs said they were looking to patch the game, which I'm already looking forward to. Music fits perfect in my opinion. Hard rock with that cyberpunk mixture. I truly believe if they can clean up the combat a bit (smooth it out some), add some more finishers (why not), maybe a lock on and clean up the story (based on other reviews), I believe we MAY have a cult classic here. However, to be fair, the patch is coming post was stated back in Feb 2023, three months ago. In case I'm not being clear, that is now a quarter of a year ago already. What softens the blow a bit, I waited for the first sale and I think what I paid is so far worth it ($38). Just to note, during a heavy fight, standing in the middle of said fight, trying to do a finisher, the game crashed (only one so far). With the two hour refund you can experience the combat (fun if you get into the flow), story (Interesting enough) and acting (pretty bad imo) to make a good decision. P.S.Just so you're aware, there IS a chainsaw you can use.. however, what it does is censored. No joke (as in I do not find it funny) a big red CENSORED pops up as you use the chainsaw on an enemy. I find this counter-intuitive. Chainsaw VS katana.. Chainsaw is censored for some odd reason. I am just going to opt not to use it, but it would also be nice if the censored was removed. I think there is enough of that in the world as is.  Second Boss Fight. August. While playing on the hardest difficulty. This needs a MASSIVE overhaul. I truly feel soft locked right now. The rate this boss shoots at you (no way to deflect bullets), runs up on you (hitting you out of cover), follows you everywhere and has an insta-roll (even during your combos) which can lead into August melee or shooting. Typically the latter. I do not mind the RNG of his attacks, I DO highly mind the irritation this causes though. I cannot beat him. He just shoots which melts my health. I even tried hugging / staying near cover but so far that's pointless. The rate I chip his health down VS mine isn't even close. I am 99.9% sure Solelli didn't play test this fight / difficulty because this is evident within seconds. I am going to have to rate this unfair. The rate he rolls, pulls and shoots, you're going to get hit. I understand the main protag cannot deflect bullets, but this needs to be tweaked for sure. The rate August gets hit, rolls out and shoots is faster than your ability to hit, miss and get into cover. Driving me crazy honestly. (Still giving thumbs up because most do not play on the hardest difficulty and I am hard headed and won't turn it down). UPDATEI finally beat the boss. In this time I have grown to really dislike Sollei. Truly, I believe Guardians of the Galaxy couldn't inform you of a more inadequate dev team. Their rhythm games are WAY off rhythm. Their design choices are perplexing to say the least. Their control scheme SCREAMS someone forgot to program it and went in with five minutes left on the clock. Need an example? To swap grenades, you have to hold RB to prompt the throw, THEN press left on D pad to swap it. To swap your firearm, left and right on the D pad at all times. Question. Why not left D pad for grenade and right for firearm (or vice versa)? Want another example? Some enemies (Tank enemy) are very annoying. Ignoring the whole team except Stone (you). It is 2023. This doesn't pull anyone out of it? Doesn't hurt immersion? Not only that but the tank comes with a one hitter quitter shoulder tackle that charges within a step. Meaning if you're in front of him and he decides to shoulder you, one step for full force / kill. ANOTHER example? When parrying, there is the typical *ding* sound and time slows. However! That does NOT mean it is your turn to attack (like most games). Oh no! Time slows just for the enemy to attack again and usually one more time after that. However, the August boss fight doesn't slow mo after every parry. Only after the LAST attack (sometimes). Point is, assume there will another attack coming.  Sollei, in my opinion, have the *DING* sound when you successfully parry, however, only slow mo when it is time to attack. Notifying the player to go. Otherwise you trade hits and on hard that can be game over or the enemy is faster than you and you just lose out right. To be fair, this is MASSIVELY bugged. You could get the ding and slow mo, or maybe just the ding, or maybe you hear the ding, but the game doesn't count it and you take full damage. I've had it all. Look. I cannot deny this game has charm for me (thumbs up). I would like to believe with more money they could achieve more.  I like cyberpunk. I like melee. I like pew pew sticks. I like John Wick take downs. So you have something here. But man. I cannot deny. Wanted: Dead 2 (if such a thing), I would be low key more excited to hear Sollei sold the rights to some other dev team. It is like Sollei is trying to be the next Ryu Ga studio (Yakuza / Judgement series). Except Sollei comes with zero rhythm mini games, 80% more controller issues, 90% more bugs, 95% more design issues and 100% worse acting.Hope this helps. Here is to hoping for a great patch soon(er)!UPDATE Crazy SOB actually patched the game quite a bit. I mean, a year later, but I get it. We're not all AAA. Kudos.
