_childDocuments_.review: Very rough around the edges but enjoyable if you like hack and slash games.Pros:The combat becomes quite enjoyable after you get a few level ups under your belt. It has an arcade kind of feel where you are quickly running between enemies, hitting combos, and killing things quickly.The art style and character design are pretty unique as is the world the devs created.New game plus mode for those who want to replay or speed run.The kill animations are very well done and have a gun fu type of feel. You’ll always look and feel badass when dispatching enemies.Challenging but fair difficulty.Cons:The voice acting ranges from flat to terrible.The story itself is nonsensical, lacks direction, and has no satisfying conclusion. Enemy variety is pretty bad with many re-skinned enemies. You basically just have standard grunts with guns, ninja’s with swords, a big guy with a mini-gun, a melee focused grunt, and three different bosses. That’s it.Performance issues. I frequently got framerate dips especially when entering combat.Not a big fan of the mini-games sections although thankfully they aren’t forced upon you after a brief introduction to each one.I think some of the checkpoints are a little unfair.Fire grenades stagger you which wouldn’t be a big deal but if you’re standing next to a wall you will get stun locked until the fire goes out which will most likely get you killed.Final thoughts:I had a surprising amount of fun with this game despite it’s many flaws. Challenging games like this don’t really exist anymore and once you get a handle on the mechanics of the game it’s quite enjoyable. That said only a specific kind of person will like this game. You have to be OK with games that are primarily gameplay oriented and that don’t hold your hand at all. You have to be OK with some jank and overall Japanese weirdness. Think of older mid-tier games from the ps3 era like Neverdead or Killer is Dead where the biggest draw is that the game is attempting something new and wacky to distinguish itself from the crowd. If you’re one those people who like experiences like that then I’d recommend Wanted: Dead to you.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews but I felt compelled to this time because this game seems to be getting a lot of undeserved hate. Wanted Dead is a perfectly good game, It's not great, but it's also not terrible. Wanted Dead is a love letter to cyberpunk anime from the 80's and 90's. With it's premise lifted directly from Cyber City Oedo, and a couple of boss fights stolen from Ghost in the shell. The story is fairly derivative, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. While the cast is small everyone has their distinct personalities, even if most of them lean on established tropes.The game play is divided into action segments which are the meat of the game punctuated by segments where you can freely explore the police station looking for collectibles that help flesh out the story, and play mini-games. In total there are 5 missions. You are given a limited tool set to complete them, but each item in your tool set is essential. This isn't a game where you can just get by by mashing the x-button, especially in the 2nd to last level where you have to go through a couple of long gantlets of tough enemies you have to manage your resources, and take each enemy's weaknesses and pasterns into account. While the game can be tough, if you play it wisely it's not nearly as difficult as some of the reviews make out. The hardest part for me was the karaoke mini-game, but that's not mandatory to beat. Also one more thing to note even though it gives you a gun, and you can enter FPS mode to shoot that's usually not the best strategy, the gun-play is a supplement to the sword play and not the other way around. All in all if you like cyberpunk, and you like action games this game is for you. My major criticism is the length what's here is good, I just wish there was more of it. The regular price is $59 given the length I feel that's a little steep, but I bought it on sale for a little less than $40 which I think is a fair deal for what I got.

_childDocuments_.review: This game achieves what it sets out to do. Expectation management is critical to enjoy this game.If you go into it expecting Ninja Gaiden or Bayonetta levels of gameplay and polish then you are in for a rude awakening.If you go in expecting something akin to WET, Oni, or Devil's Third in both gameplay and jankiness then this game might suffice or maybe even slightly surpass them.Only thing that I can agree about the criticisms is the price for what we are getting, though funnily it is priced at the equivalent of 30 USD in my country, so I myself have no complaints. _childDocuments_.review: First impressions: It's freaking awesome! It's a combination of shooter and slasher I've always dreamed of. Performance: I'm not much of a setting diddler, but it runs smoothly at 4k 60FPS DLSS-Performance with RTX 2070. But I think HDR option doesn't work correctly atm.UPDATE after beating the game:If you liked Lollipop Chainsaw, Killer is Dead, Wet and the like back in the day, then this game will probably be your jam. There's also a few small things that reminded me of Deadly Premonition, humor wise. The combat is highlight of this game, it's stylish and responsive, transitioning between shooting and slashing is smooth and fast. Took me around 15-17 hours to beat it on hard, but it doesn't seem to be a particularly long game. Music is great, but graphics are subpar which is usually the case with these budgety titles that target specific niche. Story is a bit wobbly, but there is something to piece together on you own. Overall, had a great time with it and recommended it, if you are not afraid of a bit of a challenge and learning curve.

_childDocuments_.review: + good graphics+ good effects+ good detail in BG and Visuals+ gun and sword fights+ literally in some fights pretty hard (one-hit kill)+ nice slice and dice (reminds me of Kill Bill somehow)+ I love Human screams in the Morning :D+ game has cats+ I take my Knife to a gunfight :D+ really hard sometimes+ great effort making minigames (should have gone more into polishing and balancing gameplay)+ parry and dodgebased fighting- OST seems at times a bit weird- english voices are not fitting (would prefer japanese)- character models look a bit weird- wanky camera without a possibility to fix targets- audio bugs (some encounter music: missing, not, missing, not etc.)- visual bugs- some stuttering- checkpoints are pretty nasty to reach in some points- camera is your biggest enemy (no fix function, often decides to face different way, depends on walls or obstacles, very annoying)- screenshot functions is pretty much off and stutters the client while taking one- some weird after effects (blurring) while in some conversations- I dont really like the switch between anime scenes and CG...too inconsistent- the client is pretty much instable (crashing, bug, fps drop in certain areas or fights for a few seconds)- story is a bit weird at times- game feels like 60% done. but then rush rush rush....Conclusion:This game could be very good, but its lacking serious technical and gameplay problems, which occur at random and in the most crucial times. As this game has a high difficulty level, so all in all to execute the system and not dying in 1-2 hit it should run nearly flawless. Well it should, it doesn't. In some cases client crashes randomly in fights. Sounds and music are glitching which can breeak the concentration. If you parry or roll you can end in situations were you dont see enemies because the camera flips around (while doing nothing with the camera button) or loosing your enemy focus, because the game thinks you target another one (like the "target the nearest enemy"-effect, but without even targeting, because you can't do it here), which all can result in dying very fast. Movement are not consistent and some hits go through the enemy, which is really bad, cause you build your hit and successful kill on hitting enemies (of course). Enemies sometimes hit you while behind a wall or an obstacle (not while aiming), which is also very bad for surviving against certain enemies (Boss fights are a little bit easier because you can focus at least after some time on the enemy). But surviving there is also a struggle with the already mentioned fps drops, bugs and some glitches. The basic fundemental things are here which I already mentioned, but the devs kinda abandoned some critical things which can break your fight in seconds. Many ppl quit because of the difficulty of this game. Which is in my opinion not that hard. The crucual things are the technical ones. Some other ppl tried again again and won, after struggle against all odds. As for me I can#t play a game where i can die through: 20% crash, 20% camera turn around, 20% getting hit through walls, 20% hit box things, 19% certain bugs such as suddenly vanishing enemies and then respawning to the point 30 minutes before. For me it was a fun game until the problems began before the Second Booss Fight (). When you wanna try this game go ahead. I already stated the positive and negative things. For me I will set this game aside until the bugs are fixed, which i presume....will never happen. Sadly this a game which could be a Sekiro-DMC-Batman cross, fails mainly at the technical aspects, which can kill you very fast.Score:4913/10 some very fat cats- 13/10 the voices will hunt me in my nightmares

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead feels like a mesh between the early 00s console games and the late 00s console games. One of the late 00s games that comes to mind is WET, but it is only vaguely like that, on the surface. Another game that I was reminded of is Dead to Rights. This is a difficult game - which I'd describe as just classic video game difficulty. Up until the final boss, it is hard but fair. The final boss goes a touch beyond. It might be this, that it seems to be made like a video game rather than a modern interactive movie holding your hand, that makes me like it.It has a charm in this, and with its story ---However, the game and its story feels somewhat gutted. Like there is a lot of content, context, and character development that was taken out. Whether this is due to development time or what, I don't know. But something feels missing, that there was something more expansive that has been left bare. The skill tree and the weapons could have also been expanded on. There could have been more guns and more ways to upgrade or modify them. But remember the core of the combat is your blade. The pistol is important for countering attacks and the assault rifles and shotguns are there for when you can get behind cover to take on multiple enemies. It's definitely not a perfect game and there is something that could have been much bigger here. But I would like this game to do well enough that they can expand on it and create and even better sequel with all of the elements that they have at hand. If this game did come out in the early 00s, it would be something that wouldn't automatically come to mind but would probably be remembered fondly by a lot of people. Like the game Dead to Rights, for example.Bottom line, I am not comfortable blanket recommending this game to anyone - especially for full release price. But at a lower price, if you are interested in a challenge and do like games such as Ninja Gaiden, Dead to Rights, Shinobi, or WET, look into it.

The combat is pretty fun, especially once you get a few upgrades, and there are multiple goofy rhythm games sprinkled in between missions which I quite enjoyed.If I had to sum up the whole experience into a single word it would be: bizarre. _childDocuments_.review: “Wanted: Dead is a new hybrid slasher/shooter from the makers of Ninja Gaiden and Dead or Alive”, according to the store page.I’ve never played those games, but “hybrid slasher/shooter” seems interesting. Well, the protagonist looks cool despite her weirdly massive hands, and I enjoyed the strong Xbox360/PS3 era vibe through characters, atmosphere, environment, and overall aesthetic. Unfortunately, these are the only highlights, everything else falls short.The slasher mechanics borrow elements from souls-like games, including dodge, block, parry, but replace traditional light/heavy attacks with normal attack (slash) and handgun counter. There are three simple combos, some alternative moves such as charged and dash attack, finishers (all triggered the same way) and a power burst mode called bullet time that doesn’t really slow down time and feels underwhelming. That’s about it – the slasher gameplay doesn’t have much depth. There are no alternative melee weapons, flashy combos or special tricks to keep the gameplay engaging and less repetitive, as most of the time it was just button-smashed normal attack since it is like the most efficient way to fight. To make it worse, combos don’t feel very connected and slashing doesn’t feel very good as most enemies are overly spongey. Additionally, the narrow design in the final level often causes the camera to put main character and enemies out of screen, adding frustration. The shooter gameplay is designed to be a cover shooter, but covers are rarely useful due to the poor placements and the extra inconvenience of having to interact with a cover to enter. Shooting feels decent on controller, thanks to controller rumble, but with a mouse, it feels light and lacks impactful feedback. Keyboard and mouse players also face the hassle of excessive key bindings, as functions like finisher that combine two existing keys on controller to trigger, require dedicated new keys on keyboard.Mechanically, you have a main rifle that cannot be swapped out, a handgun acting as a melee weapon due to the short range, a secondary gun picked up during combat, and two types of throwables. The rifle and handgun are customizable, but it doesn’t make much difference in gameplay, and the difference between recoil handling stat and accuracy stat is hard to comprehend. Throwables are underwhelming - enemies can dodge hand grenades easily and the long detonation time reduces the usefulness; incendiary grenades explode instantly, but the weak damage makes it more of a stun weapon for small enemies. However, the burning effect greatly obstructs the vision to aim, with an added risk of burning yourself.The secondary gun includes SMG, shotgun, LMG, grenade launcher, chainsaw and rocket (exclusive to endgame), but only LMG is consistently reliable: SMG depletes ammo in three to four kills because of the fast firing rate and weak damage; shotgun is only effective at very close range with headshots; grenade launcher has erratic hit detection that goes straight through elites and farther enemies (and many foes can dodge it like a champ), with the possibility to self-harm; chainsaw is a one-hit-kill melee weapon, but leaves you vulnerable during its long animation. Therefore, despite the variety, you don’t actually have many good options. Overall, it is a generic third person shooter, with many aspects desired to be improved.Both slasher and shooter gameplay are lackluster, and the “hybrid” makes them feel awkward and disjointed. It feels like playing two completely different games in one, as two types of gameplay don’t enhance each other and lack integration, resulting in an incohesive experience. At first, I thought the gameplay would naturally alternate between shooting when enemies have guns and slashing when out of ammo (happens too frequently) or facing melee enemies. However, I soon realized you can do either at any time because the game doesn’t have a clear direction to follow. While some may argue this gives players freedom, this lack of guidance leaves players unsure of whether to slash or shoot, and to me it makes the game feel aimless and confused, like the game never finds its footing and the game dev never envisioned what the game is supposed to play like.Outside of gameplay, Wanted Dead is a bigger mess. Not sure if it is cultural difference, lost in translation or simply poor writing, the story is indecipherable. It is also incomplete and ends abruptly, leaving many points unresolved, like it never fully explains how the protagonist becomes a war criminal.What’s worse, characters are weird and unlikeable because of bizarre characterization. Voice acting doesn’t help either, as voice actors sound mentally checked out in recording. There are also some jarring anime cutscenes in flashbacks that clash with the overall style.Wanted Dead feels like a rushed product that lacks serious polish in gameplay and story. I don’t think there is a good reason to play it given its poor quality. The ending implies a sequel, but it probably won’t happen as this game flopped so hard.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR It's crazy that this exists.  Great soundtrack.  Okay game play.  Strange choices by the devs.This game is weird.  I want to love it.  I want to hate it.  I want to say it's so bad it's good.  I want to say it's secretly brilliant and subversive.  If you make it to the end you will have said out loud, "What the F is this game?" several times.  The moment to moment game play is pretty solid although can get repetitive.  The difficulty spike at bosses and minibosses defy explanation.  The story is... present at best.  The voice acting so baffling most of the time.But I can't help but be charmed by how crazy it all is.  It's dripping with style.  The soundtrack is all killer no filler.  The absurdity of it all makes me laugh.  And executing a sick combo on multiple enemies feels rewarding and well earned.There's a lot of bad, though.  And I can't help but see the potential left on the table.  It feels more like a vertical slice than a complete product.  There's a great game that someone will make that is inspired by this one.  But this is not it.On the other hand Stefanie Joosten voices a character modeled after her and sings on many of the songs in the soundtrack.  Because of that 10/10.  Must buy

_childDocuments_.review: Jank. But a lovely one. Remember the moment when Nier Automata threw you with different kinds of gameplay in first few minutes of the game, from top-down shooter, to 3rd-person shooter, to side-scrolling platformer and then to beat-em-up? Yeah, thats not happening here. But what is here you will either love or hate. Combat system might make me frustrated sometimes. But when everything I planned aligns in execution it makes my brain go happy. And thats addictive. Cutscenes range from serious themes of "bad evil guys plotting bad evil things or are they bad at all who knows" to everyday co-workers being everyday co-workers where punchlines are left hanging in the air sometimes. The last one is what happens daily in most people's lives I think, so I find these charming. This one has minigames too. They are fun and introduced though the story in a lovely weird way, I liked it too. But from what I saw, there is only one song in karaoke and ramen-eating game is also the same if you retry it. Arcade shoot-em-up is what it is. They are here to make you smile, not more, not less. In my case they succeeded. To anyone who likes weird PS2-PS3 titles (and not so obscure, like Yakuza and Godhand), give it a try. You have 2 hours to refund anyway and you will find out if its your cup of yakisoba or not in less than that.

_childDocuments_.review: The nonsenical story, the weird but very lovable characters, the accents, Herzog's 24/7 no context ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the desynced cutscenes, the odd music choices and the general awkwardness of this game give it so much character and charm that I can't help but love this game to bits.Hannah's voice actor is either the most or the least talented VA in the history of video games, and every line that character says is so weird, so genuine, and so imperfect in such a human way that she truly feels "lifelike" in a way.And her facial animations are much the same.Herzog is also super underappreciated and one of my new favourite "lovable idiot".Play this for the atmosphere and the often times surprisingly solid soundtrack, for the cutscenes, or to scratch that Godhand itch, not for the story or the gameplay.The combat flow  It kinda breaks a bit too often, guns are practically useless but the melee combat? _childDocuments_.review: I like the CQC here, but it seems to get really repetative (I still need to play around with the skill upgrades). The shooting so far is... meh. I especially like finishing animations. The difficulty spikes were unexpected. The level design sucks, it sometimes just closes you with enemies who don't get how to behave in a tight space and neither does this work for ranged combat. The enemies spawning all over the place doesn't help it either as you sometimes just go back and forth through the room and lose your direction to some extent - a more conscious enemy placement a la Hotline Miami would be a much better decision. The main character is adorable, though I still need to get used to her subpar voice acting.I'm running this on a sub-optimal hardware and it works buttery smooth and looks crisp, albeit it's not a game about modern graphics. I didn't have audio issues. It's nothing like Ninja Gaiden apart from the edgy dismemberment. It's basically an improved Devil's Third done better and on a capable hardware. There's still a long way to go in terms of game design, but I love what I see so far. I'll update the review as soon as I have more to say.As for the price, seeing this going for the same value as, say, Hogwarts Legacy might confuse some, but it all comes down to your own perspective. I personally don't think that a 60$ full-price should be a monopoly of AAA industry giants. Wanted: Dead has a nice combat flow and keeps me invested every minute while some hyped western AAA-blockbusters with next-gen graphics just make me want to sleep, and for me that's the main argument. Although it could also cost somewhat less (40$ would be optimal) I'd rather vote with my wallet for more games like this to exist and evolve into something great.

_childDocuments_.review: Has a lot of problems, and I mean A LOT of problems. But it runs well enough. I experienced a few crashes but that may be related to some fixes I put in place for the broken HDR. Overall It ran very fast in stable. Which was hilarious for me to see at a time when games like 'Redfall' and 'Star Wars' are getting dragged all over the net for their poor PC performance. The characters and story (for what there is) are likable and kind of funny. Even the actress who plays Stone. For as much crap as people gave her by comparing her to Tommy Wiseau, shes actually not too bad and I'd like to see her in other things, same with Stephanie Joosten who has some legitimately funny moments in this game. Combats pretty good too. Fast and punchy with a little bit of jank to keep you on your toes. Really hearkens back to Ninja Gaiden even if its not nearly the same rhythm.  Held back by the abysmal skill tree, that feels like its locking out essential parts of the combat flow for the sake of filling empty slots.  I wish Steam had a "buy it on sale" button tho cause this definitely isn't worth full price; sorry Soleil, it just ain't. Maybe add some karaoke songs in there. Don't think I didn't see the licensed song credits you straight up didn't use! But it was a really good time. If the stars ever aligned and a sequel came out, I would buy that one too.

_childDocuments_.review: So the gameplay itself is fun. It's a mixture of hack n slash and shooting mechanics. Both are not as advance as other games but it's passable. The combat can be challenging, sometimes in an almost cheap way. But it's still satisfying when you get past a section that was giving you trouble. This game does have that late 2000's/early 2010's Xbox 360/PS3 era feel to it that's nostalgic to me personally. My biggest gripes with the game are the laughably bad voice acting, and how short the game is. If you master the combat quickly and dont die much then you could possibly complete the game on normal in 4 hours, maybe less. Also it feels like there are cutscenes missing because after about halfway through I had no idea what was going on or what the plot going forward was. Nothing made any sense and it felt like they just gave up on anything resembling a story and just had you going from area to area slashing through waves of enemies. Even with all these shortcomings I enjoyed what I played. It's mindless fun but I would deff wait for a sale. It's deff not worth $60. I would say $30 max for how low budget it feels and how short it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played about 2 hours of this game and I really like it so far. It's difficult but if you take the time to learn it's systems it's actually pretty cool. If you like late 2000s/early 2010s AA games you'll adore this. It's got a lot of heart and the jank is there but it's honestly not bad. Just keep a few things in mind, this isn't Ninja Gaiden or DMC. It's a very different kind of action game though it's hard to describe. I find the best way to play is to fire long ranged weapons while closing gaps to get to your melee range or just pick off the odd straggler. Most actions require commitment so keep it in mind if you swing willy nilly you'll get bodied. Use your sword for heavy damage and your hand gun to keep the enemies off balance. Also don't neglect the skill tree. If all else fails if you die enough times you'll be offered and easy mode, kinda like the chicken hat in Phantom Pain, they even give you a set of cat ears. Parry when you can too since follow up attacks can put enemies into a state where they can be finished off. If multiple enemies are in this stunned state you'll finish them all at the same time. One last note is the game has a rally system similar to Bloodborne. As you take damage a portion of it will be purple on the health bar. Deal damage to refill. This means while engaging in a melee combat you'll be fine if you take a few hits from gunfire. Finishers fully restore the rally bar too.Overall I'm having a lot of fun. Is it worth the price? To me yes. This game nicely fills a very specific niche for me of that fun shlocky AA action game you'd buy on a whim and love. To most people though I'd advise you wait for a sale. This game isn't for everyone and that's okay. Try it when it's cheaper if you're on the fence but if you have a soft spot for those weird but memorable AA games from the PS2, Xbox, PS3 and 360 you could do a lot worse!
_childDocuments_.name: Wanted: Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I love some solid jank. A great 7/10 action game if there ever was one. Didn't expect it to be as difficult as it is. I do not think its unfairly hard (most of the time), I think it respects the player to become skilled enough in its mechanics to win. Combat is where most of the jank comes in for this one though. Movement and switching between targets feels clunky sometimes, you stick to cover when you don't mean to, you have to juggle small crowds of enemies who do move and try to attack you, sometimes all at once. But the parts of combat that work? Once you find the parry timings (which took me longer than I'd like to admit) melee feels amazing. I really like how the guns feel to use and that I have just enough ammo to thin out the crowd before I go in for the flashy kills with my sword. Grenades suck, you just kinda lazily drop them at your own feet and enemies dead sprint out of range long before it ever explodes. The incendiaries can trivialize bossfights if you get them out just right. I really like the third levels bossfight. Very MGS2 ass boss.On Normal difficulty enemies don't feel like bullet sponges (save for like, the second level, which I will kinda forgive because it makes narrative sense and also you can unlock a skill that solves that problem pretty quick if you bother to read through all the skills).  Sometimes it feels like the game just conspired to make you die but its arcadey enough that I don't really mind having to do sections over again.The minigames are minigames, thats for sure. I really like the ones that aren't rhythm games. The claw machine and ShMup are neat. The Ramen and Karaoke minigames make me suffer. I am not good enough, it is a skill issue that I can't multitask two tracks of key prompts that span the whole controller. I am bad - that is the only reason I won't be able to 100% this one.The voice actors are phoning it in. My current belief is that is part of the artistic vision the devs had for this homage to the finest the PS2 had to offer. Through this passable vocal performance we get a story I think is neat and fits perfectly into the vibe of those PS1 and 2 games like TRAG or Metal Wolf Chaos where you are a police officer who is doing action stuff in place because reason. Add in the twist that you are a notoriously lethal squad of War Criminals who have been inexplicably released from their life sentences to be Law Enforcement, and we have the kind of schlock I'm looking for.tl;dr Sometimes you just need a junk food action movie that knows you're not here to have your world changed, you're just here for a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: I've heard  called "The Best Bad Game of 2023". I'd say that's an apt description. The awful part is, it didn't HAVE to be bad.  is a great  for a game. On a design document level, all the fundamentals are sound. But every good idea is undermined by bad execution.The story feels like it should be compelling; the setting's interesting, and the plot does two or three things I really liked. But the writing is just bad. The dialogue is intended to be witty and meme-y, but it comes off as laughably try-hard. Actual snippet from a cutscene: "What happens when she finds out the truth?" "What is the truth?" "There is no truth." The voice cast does their best with subpar material, and occasionally a bit of wit shines through. But an additional problem is that they're mostly playing off the main character, who sucks. The character has a thick accent of some kind (she's from Zurich, in canon), so I won't call the actress bad, because she's clearly struggling. But the end result is the same: wooden delivery that undermines moments that are supposed to be humorous and dramatic. And any potential that might have been in the storyline is squandered because the third act is missing; the game ends abruptly shortly after things have gone to hell, with no resolution to any ongoing plot threads. It's a clear sign that the project had production troubles of some kind.It's not the only sign either. There are hints that the game was intended as a  style game, with an open world full of oddball characters, weird sidequests, and goofy minigames. But if this was the intent, it was massively scaled back. All you have now is a home base full of expositionary collectibles and NPCs with nothing important to say. The minigames remain, but are... well, bad. There's karaoke, but only a single song, and awfully designed, using ten keys that appear in unintuitive places on two different tracks. There's a ramen-eating minigame, which is karaoke without the performance. There's a -style arcade shooter, which is okay but nothing remarkable, and a crane game that's as frustrating as they usually are. At least you can kick the crane machine until it breaks. That's a feature I always wanted in .The actual meat of the gameplay, the combat, is the best part. It's nothing revolutionary, but cutting through swarms of enemies with a katana and a handgun is genuinely appealing, and the brutal finishing moves- another element taken from - never get old. But even here there are missteps. There was no reason at all for the game to have guns. The handgun works because it's part of the melee system, but the rifles put you into an alternate cover-based third-person shooter mode. You can't mix melee combat and cover-based shooting like that, because they require completely different designs. Melee requires enemies that rush at you, or else you rush at them. Whereas shooting from cover requires those enemies stay relatively stationary and form a nice little shooting gallery. And no, run-and-gun is not the best of both worlds, especially not when you're plagued with clunky controls and strict ammo limits. Even if you can get it to work, the results from gunplay are pathetic compared to slice-and-dice. I'm convinced that the BFG grenade launcher . And ranged and melee alike are both bound to an experience-based skill tree that is completely unnecessary, locking off moves that really should be standard. I played after the April 2024 rework, and from comments it used to be much worse, with things like invincibility frames tied to the skill tree. Even post-update, we have enemies with invincible riot shields that require one of about 4 techniques to disarm, all of which are on the skill tree. Bet somebody's gotten softlocked because of that.It's all a great shame, because there's a lot of potential here. At some point, the devs had an ambitious, genre-making design planned out, but it never came together. They must have been lacking in some vital resource. Time? Money? Talent? Who knows. As released,  was a disappointing experience, but I still want to play the game in that original plan. Or at least hear the story of how production went wrong, because I have a feeling it's a good one.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a slashing and shooting game, get Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance instead.I get that this game is supposed to be difficult, but even the normal difficulty which is how it is "supposed to be played" is kind of a joke and a mean punch to anyone who genuinely just wants to play. I even joked about LOTR: Gollum having a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ writing but this game offers the worst of both worlds. If you are advertising the game having a "gripping" story, I should feel immersed. The main character not even sounding like a main character is turning me away from this game, even more so than the mechanics...Well, the mechanics is nothing to brag about and bring home to your mother and show her how awesome this game is, cause it is anything but that. Not only do you tickle the enemies with your swords, but the grunts and low tier enemies you are killing don't really feel like low tier enemies. It is incredibly frustrating and the controls are janky.Yes, I only have 0.9 hours on record and I should "play more" to get the "optimal experience", but there is just so many negatives about this game. I was looking forward to it, I REALLY wanted to love this game and thought this would be one of the few hack and slash games that would make me feel captivated in a story, but it feels like a half cooked pasta that nobody really wants to eat.If there is a future update that fixes all of these problems it would be a game worthwhile picking up, but I would not even recommend getting it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awful game.It's not a hidden gem; it's just an unfinished, unpolished, and broken piece of code.The authors claim it references the golden era of PS2-PS3 games, but it's closer in design and overall quality to the PS1 era.The combat mechanics are simple - you can hit enemies with a sword or shoot them with a gun or rifle. It sounds promising, but it just doesn't work. You can't parry enemy attacks because the timings are unclear, there are a lot of overpowered enemies, and there is no joy in killing enemies.The upgrading system is stupid - you upgrade to finish enemies without legs and buy abilitiy to throw grenades.The game is full of bugs.The cutscenes are disconnected, and the storyline is inconsistent. _childDocuments_.review: Not as bad as some people are saying.It's kind of a mix between Nioh and Ninja Gaiden (It is made by the guys who made Ninja Gaiden) it has plenty of blood and dismemberments, for the guys like me who like that kind of stuff.Is it perfect? No but then again we've all paid more for worse games than this (I'm looking at God of War Ragnarok, you'll all see when it comes to PC at least I hope you will) this is a game that keeps you in the action and I like it for that.Is the voice acting the best? No but it isn't the worst either. It's obvious they hired some cheap actors, My only issue here is the poor audio balancing for the voices, sometimes they're just too low you can barely hear them. Subtitles recommended.The graphics are pretty decent, easily better than GOW Ragnarok, the effects and the screen space reflections were very well used and you can destroy things in the environment. I know I wrecked all the the sliding paper doors.Music is pretty good so far, fits in nicely with the action.Combat works well though using the rifle will require more skill than some people have since guys rush you a lot. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game and I will recommend it if and only if you watch footage and it looks EXACTLY up your alley. If it doesn't, I do think this game will have a hard time winning you over.It just feels like a classic game. Leaning into arcade roots while still sprucing up the animations to make it feel like you are playing john wick. And the game oozes style that makes you want to keep playing and learning its systems.I really like the pistol as a combo extender vs a traditional third person shooter weapon. It works really well as a parry mix up mechanic that feels so rewarding to get rolling with.For the negatives: the gunplay doesn't feel strong enough to compete with melee. Even if the screen is loaded with ranged opponents, it is still usually a better play to sprint around like a maniac. I've come to terms with it but I hope for a patch that both strengthens ranged combat (maybe either adding ammo or making the enemy smg's less terrible) and increases the intimidation of being outnumbered by ranged opponents. The game could benefit from full lock on autoaim similar to red dead to make switching styles quicker as the game is definitely a melee game at heart (which is why the pistol mechanic works so well)The other big negative: The game starts out obnoxiously difficult even on regular in my opinion. I'm sure it will be easier on a replay, but I don't think lack of skill is the prime reason it's difficult. The skills you unlock are so important to your kit and once you get to the second level you'll wonder how you played without them. All the way through the first boss I was really having a hard time finding any rhythm. Once I unlocked a few more skills though the game all the sudden felt way different and like I had enough tools to simply turn it into a melee only game and it did get more fun, but the lack of good gun mechanics and balance stuck out more.That sounds like a lot of negative but those two things are really it. The gameplay (when you start focusing on melee) really comes into it's own and is a ton of fun to start chaining wonderfully animated executions with. On top of the great sense of style (even with seamless anime cuts and great music) it just feels good.I did want to call special attention to the negatives as I don't think this game is for everyone and knowing those two things and balancing your impressions of the pre release footage I think will help inform your decision.
_childDocuments_.name: Wanted: Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Some cool ideas, but far from worth anything. A camera boss that you fight the whole time, but gets very repetitive. Not much enemy variation, no animation cancelling (in an action game? really?) and a very bad checkpoint system that sends you very far back if you fail anywhere, leading to many headaches. Technically, it was fine. Only had any frame drop in one place and no crashes. Story was everywhere, in a bad way, not like a Yakuza at all, which has nods to it all over the place. Random anime scenes inserted to muck up the story even more and make you even wonder wtf is happening more every scene. Weird pacing. Do a level and then eat 10-30 minutes of cutscenes, almost making you forget how to even play the game by the time a gameplay segment returns.Bosses were a cake-walk compared to the level they came from, and also were very boring. They had no real flair or abilities that made them different from enemies within their levels, and had no real gimmicks that set them apart, aside from the last boss who just tries to steal elements from the final boss of Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance (go play that instead).Overall, this is a $15 indie game masquerading as a full-price, AAA experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Wanted: Dead

_childDocuments_.review: It is clunky, lacks polish; but little touches like stealing the entire ramen appreciation dialogue from the film Tampopo, and its interpretation of Western memes through a Japanese lens, gives it a quirky b-film charm.It really wants to capture the limited lives side scrolling/beat-em up arcade era of yesteryear, but given strange control design choices makes it more frustrating than fun occasionally. With time, and getting gud - replay may be more enjoyable. If you make it to the KOLCHAK boss fight and understand countering and standing toe to toe by then, maybe you'll enjoy it.Stefanie "Quiet" Joosten's return here is mixed. Great to see her do more video game voice acting, but some of the lines feels like she slept in the booth or dialed it in. This isn't for everyone - more for players that love quirky titles like Killer 7 and Killer is dead (aka Suda51/Kadokawa Games/Grasshopper Manufacture games) with their occasionally intentionally frustrating controls and gameplay uniqueness.Honestly, the difficulty level is forced by bullet sponge bs and inability to lock on. Your NPC buddies are worthless even with upgrades. You get in a groove, think you've progressed only to go back several battles due to an asinine checkpoint system. It is archaic by intent, but that doesn't make it less frustrating.I literally haven't been triggered to break a controller like this since SF2 on the SNES when I was a child over 3 decades ago...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually pretty fun. The combat and mini games at least are decent, and the shmup minigame is actually awesome. The story is nonsense, the characters are weird and unlikeable, and the voice acting is an atrocity, but I DID enjoy my time with the game overall (enough to 100% some of the mini games at least, but not enough to complete NG+)....but hell naw it aint getting a thumbs up from me. It doesn't deserve it. Idk what happened during development that resulted in this half finished mess getting shipped, but it clearly came out too early. Every part of this game feels like it was made by people who actually wanted to make a good game, but didn't have time to finish it. If this was early access, it would be fine, but it's not. If it ever goes on sale for $5, then I'd say it's worth it. Otherwise, just play something else.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: When I first booted up Wanted: Dead there was a problem with my installation and all the floors and walls of the first level were missing, and the game was broken and unplayable. I then fixed the install issue and realized that unfortunately playing wanted dead while it's broken is about the same amount of fun as playing it when it's working properly, which is to say, not very. The thing with wanted dead is that there are parts of it that one can enjoy, like the cutscenes or the weird minigames, bits where the game reaches "so bad it's good" or genuinely fun, but the majority is a boring and incredibly predictable slogWanted: Dead is trying to be a throwback slash em up but also a cover shooter which in gameplay terms is weird and muddy, the cover mechanics are pretty bad and the game really wants you to kill the melee enemies with your sword please, so their health has been inflated like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bouncy house. The parrying mechanics are bad and feel bad. Timing on them is weird, there's no real feeling of reward or skill like when you're playing a better game. Attacking enemies with your sword is also bad, and also feels bad. It might as well be a foam toy for all the weight that it has, and this game's idea of difficulty as mentioned previously is enemies that can take a stupid number of hits without so much as scraping their knees. The enemy ai is dumb, and your squad ai is similarly dumb but their guns are clearly firing airsoft pellets for all the good they do against your enemies, so you kind of end up forgetting that they exist. Overall the combat is trying to be difficult but it also wants to be a fun casual sort of game, so both end up cancelling out. The combat in the game isn't really "difficult" in any meaningful skill based way, you just end up dying a lot and have to repeat large sections over and over again which wore down at my will to play the game. If I want to play a rewarding and difficult game I'll boot up sekiro, if I want to play something light and fast I'll boot up something like the force unleashed. I won't turn to Wanted: Dead.The game isn't even very fun to look at in combat, the finisher moves you can do are trying to be really cool and failing pretty hard, the only time a finisher made me feel anything was when I killed a protester with one because it was so stupidly over the top that it made me laugh in shock. The game also lacks any sort of choice, your character's skill trees are all pretty generic and it's not even hard to max them out. The levels are all linear to the max and as previously mentioned the game's combat really wants you to deal with enemies in set, specific ways. In general the game lacks polish and is not very good. The bad voice acting, cutscenes, and weird minigames are a plus, but they're few and far between the rest of the content. In fact the one thing that Wanted Dead did right is have such bold voice acting choices, the way Herzog says "Grenade!" when an enemy throws one sends me into laughing fits. I played this with my friends on stream and we'd constantly go from "oh that's funny or cool" to "this game is horrid" whenever I got into combat. I would watch a playthrough if I wanted to experience the wackier moments, playing the game is an exercise in misery. Also, this goes without saying, but this game is NOT worth $60. This game isn't even worth $30 which is the price I bought it for. If anything I should have been paid $30 for deciding to play this game. 4/10 not worth

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted Dead has all the makings of a fantastic gaming experience, offering a unique concept and engaging gameplay that promises excitement at every turn. However, as it stands, the game is unfortunately plagued by a plethora of bugs, glitches, and a tendency to crash, significantly detracting from its potential.The concept behind Wanted Dead is nothing short of brilliant – a wild-west adventure filled with bounty hunting, duels, and an immersive open-world. The game's foundation is solid, and the potential for an unforgettable experience is evident. The mechanics, when they work, offer a glimpse into the thrilling world the developers intended to create.However, the frequent bugs and glitches act as persistent roadblocks on this wild ride. From NPCs getting stuck in peculiar places to missions failing to trigger correctly, the overall experience is hindered by these technical issues. The promise of a seamless open-world experience is shattered when the game crashes at crucial moments, leaving players frustrated and, unfortunately, wanting more than the game can currently deliver.That said, it's crucial to acknowledge the potential that lies within Wanted Dead. The core gameplay mechanics, when functioning properly, showcase moments of exhilarating gunfights and intense showdowns. The graphics and atmosphere capture the essence of the Wild West beautifully, immersing players in a world that has the potential to be truly captivating.While I genuinely enjoyed the concept and moments of Wanted Dead, I can't ignore the technical hurdles that currently mar the experience. With dedicated efforts to address the bugs, glitches, and stability issues, Wanted Dead could evolve into the standout title it aspires to be. As it stands, however, I recommend keeping an eye on future updates and patches before fully committing to the journey this game promises.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I gave this a chance as I've been looking for this exact sort of game: a straight to the point, instant reflex, action title that puts its all into focusing on the core combat.I'm mostly indifferent to the characters, licensed music, mini games, and themes. However, it's satisfying to complete increasingly efficient mission runs... learning how to not only get past--but eventually crush the game's many challenges.That said, I probably wouldn't recommend this game to any of my friends. The difficulty is merciless and each new enemy type requires a sizable investment of time and patience before you can finally feel proficient. Insta-deaths are frequent and the game's mechanics aren't immediately apparent. But I never felt that the difficulty was cheap. Even at 40fps, on a handheld, I was able to complete this on hard mode. Performance wasn't great, but things were still playable--if not pretty.If you belong to that subset of action game enthusiasts that enjoys mastering a punishing and deliberate combat system, you might give this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: It breaks my heart to give this game a negative recommendation, but those last 2 levels are such a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring slog that I feel like I'd have to apologize to anybody I talked into buying this. It's a damn shame, because the first 3 levels are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic. I was having a great time with this game early on and loving the pacing. Combat, story beats, character moments, minigames and random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ all happening at a pace that kept a smile on my face and my interest high. I kept playing the crane game to unlock new collectibles and minigame tracks, so I could then play those. I beat all the high scores in the shooting gallery and was running around trying to find all the collectibles. I was genuinely confused about all the negative reviews, because Wanted: Dead seemed like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome videogame to me. Also, it needs to be said: I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love the characters in this game. Hannah is a sexy tall woman with violent tendencies, Herzog is a stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the likeable way, the Captain is 100% intentionally a stereotypical hard-ass police chief and I'm surprised he doesn't call you a loose cannon, Gunsmith is adorable, Cinnamon is 10/10 character design and I loved the pointless diner and ramen shop discussions/impromptu ramen history lesson. The karaoke was dumb and charming and heartwarming as Hannah and Vivienne awkwardly sing and dance while the boys are losing their minds.Then all that ended when the police station level started. Room after room after room after room after room of waves of enemies. So many of those huge damage sponges that take a while to kill no matter how you fight them. I thought to myself:"This must be the low point of the game, so I'll power through." How wrong I was. After the police station, you get to the Kowloon streets and slums. My brother in Christ, it feels like that M.C. Escher painting of people walking up and down stairs in a circle without ever getting anywhere. Endless! ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ endless rooms of fighting the same enemy types over and over! It becomes so unbelievably ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring.When I started this game, I was so hyped that I wanted to 100% it. I was gonna play through it on every difficulty, find everything, maybe write a Collectibles guide and try to convince people to give it a shot. By the end, I realized I don't even wanna touch it anymore after the first time. At most, I might reinstall it years from now, start a Hard mode run and just stop after I beat the night club. What an astonishing dropping of the ball in those last 2 levels and this game legit needed to be about 20% shorter.

_childDocuments_.review: Developed by some of the creators of Ninja Gaiden, Wanted: Dead is 3rd person action shooter primarily aimed at players who feel particularly nostalgic of the golden era of linear action games. The game is set in a dystopian future where the Hong Kong police department is formed by mercenaries and war criminals who for some reason have been converted to police officers. As Lieutenant Hannah Stone, you will lead the Zombie Unit in a set of missions with the aim of uncovering a major conspiracy filled with corrupted corporations, androids, giant robots and other cyberpunk stereotypes. Unfortunately, the plot is nothing amazing and most players will quickly get bored by it. It has a bit of charm, mainly because of some unexpected nonsense moments and the design of some characters, but it’s nothing you have already seen, especially if you are used to more weird Japanese games (like the ones from creator Suda51). Characters are introduced very quickly with not enough description, but the worst aspect is their voice acting, which is awful (you can immediately hear it through the protagonist’s voice). Mediocre dialogues and wooden facial animations also don’t help characters to express themselves in a good way. Despite being a Japanese game, English is the only language available for voice overs and that probably makes it worse. Stefanie Joosten is in the game playing a recurrent side character (she was Quiet in ) but this clearly isn’t her best performance. For some reason, there are also some cheap anime cutscenes that don’t really mix well with the super realistic graphics and will only make things more confusing.The focus of Wanted: Dead is obviously the gameplay. Developers tried to combine fast-paced melee combat with cover-based gunplay. Essentially, a mix of  and . Stone’s basic weapons are a katana, a rifle and a pistol, each one tied to specific buttons. The game wants you to take cover when being surrounded by enemies and slice through them when you don’t have enough ammo or when they get close enough. Still, there is no reason to prefer guns over melee combat. The gunplay is terrible and it’s easier to run, roll and slash enemies with your sword or combine it with your pistol (like John Wick) to quickly chain combos. When an enemy has very low health you can also perform a bloody and spectacular finishing move. After playing a couple of hours though, you will realize that this is all the gameplay has to offer. Sure, there is a simple ability tree from which you can unlock more skills (like grenades), but it’s not enough to make combat engaging in the long run. Movements also feel very janky, so you don’t get much satisfaction by using your sword either. Due to the lack of diversity in the enemy types, the gameplay can become monotonous after just a couple of hours, with the only exception being bosses who require parries and counters, making fights somewhat enjoyable despite all the combat issues. You will always fight with your Unit alongside you, but they are only good to distract the enemy and you will do most of the work by yourself.The PC version is greatly optimized and runs flawlessly even at max settings, but the graphics aren’t really much impressive, especially compared to other modern action-shooter games). Not only levels are linear, but they also lack details and feel too similar one to the other. The most bothering issue though is the low quality of facial animations, which basically ruins every single cutscene.Wanted: Dead is a game that can only attract players nostalgic of old linear games, particularly those who enjoy weird action games like  or . It’s ridiculous on purpose, but also involuntary, and you won’t feel involved in the story no matter what. Its mechanics are enough to make the game playable and you will probably enjoy slicing enemies with your katana, but there isn’t enough progression and the low variety of enemies will quickly make combat monotonous.

_childDocuments_.review: (Lower the price and this review will change to reccomended) Wanted dead is a bit of an oddball. Many feel it's trash and a core fanbase really value its janky weirdness. What is certain is that the asking price is almost double What it should be and I think it would be hard to argue otherwise.Wanted dead, is a simple to learn but punishing third person shooter, action game that can take some time to masterSo what does wanted dead do well?Well, setting up chain executions is a lot of fun. Watching Hannah go John wick on a crowd of goons never really gets old for me. I wouldn't say wanted dead is funny but the dialogue and direction is always "what the hell?" one minute they might be talking about guns and the next minute you're in a karaoke minigame. (this is either a pro or con depending on your tastes) Speaking of mini games, the rhythm games, claw machines, and bullet hell arcade game are all fun diversions that helped pad out the game.What wanted dead doesn't do well. Levels, there's 5 levels, and they are functional but generally bland and lacking detail. Check points can be sparse and add to player frustration. Voice acting, delivery and pacing is all over the place, again either a pro or a con depending on where you're coming from.Wanted dead looks dated in appearance any way you slice it.Wanted dead doesn't offer a lot in terms of player choice, you have your katana, your primary assault rifle and one weapon that is pickup dependant.The game as a whole has a janky look to it. Partly due to the graphics and lack of detail and partly because some of the animations don't blend well. (though looks less dorky than jedi survivor imo) Wanted dead has the opportunity to explore complex issues but squanders most of it. On paper Wanted Dead sounds like a bad game, it should be a bad game, but I also can't deny that I had a lot of fun and I was never bored.Gun to my head, Wanted Dead gets a 6/10  (4/10  price tag included) If Wanted Dead had taken a safer and less weird approach it would easily have been 4/10. It has a charm that is hard to describe but you either get it or you don't.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, I was excited to play it because it brings brutal swordsmanship and third-person shooter together. So, I finally played it and it was disappointing. It could be a cool game, but there are too many cons. Combat is fun, you can parry, combine katana strikes with handgun shots, you can unlock skills to learn various combos, and there are nice finishers, but shooting with long weapons is not good because enemies feel like bullet sponges. Also, weapons sounds, and overall all sounds, are not good. I felt like I travelled a few years back, and the person who is responsible for keyboard keybindings never tried to play it, or they are a strange person. Ctrl is a sprint, shift is parry, Esc doesn't open (press Tab instead) etc. So, probably you will have to rebind them to enjoy it on the keyboard.The story is not great, not terrible, but the voice acting is horrifying. The characters sound like the actors were just reading lines from paper with very little emotion, if any. Maybe it's a problem of budget or bad recording conditions, but this game is an example of how not to do it.The game is divided into five levels connected by two types of cutscenes: in the visual of the game and anime style. The second mentioned will tell you more about your character Lt. Hannah Stone. She is the commander of Zombie Units, no you are not fighting zombies, but you are protecting the people of Hong Kong as a special police force that makes a lot of mess when it's deployed. At your disposal are three more members: Doc – a handy doctor, Sgt. Arnold Herzog – ramen lover and mute Sgt. Manolo Cortez. Also, there are more characters at the police station. The most iconic is gunsmith – Vivienne Niemantsverdriet. She loves cats and owns twelve that you can find roaming around. So, everyone that you will meet is unique, but that bad voice acting ruins immersion.Levels are short and they can be completed in about 40 minutes to one hour each. It depends on your skills. Each has a few checkpoints that refill Stimpacks (healing items), health, grenades and munition. Also, you can customise your main assault rifle and pistol there. During fights, you gain experience points that you can spend any time on various skills that make you stronger and give you more combos.The AI of your squad is not artificial intelligence, but stupidity. Many times, I saw them just running around or hiding somewhere back. During fights, it looks like they are here as placeholders rather than real help, except Doc because he can revive you.After completing the story, you can start New Game Plus, but for some weird reason, you can’t change the difficulty there. So, what is the purpose of NG+? Just for collectibles, I guess.Besides the story, the game offers some mini-games: shooting range, crane game, eating Ramen soup, karaoke with 99 Luftballons song and old-school space shooter. They are a fun addition to the game and If you want to test your reactions, you can try to complete achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally like it and I have footage showing how often I had been killed in the first 30 minutes -- It gives the impression that its a hack and slash game like Devil may cry, but it really does play like a tactical, over the shoulder third person shooter. If you approach the game that way, and manage your resources (ammo and health packs) you can pick the enemy NPC's from a distance. The tank type NPCs that like to charge at you, well, its obvious that they are the priority. I completely ignored the finishing moves - the NPCs will glow in a dim white light, that's your que to deliver the final blow. you'll finish the fight faster that way. All of this is explained in a tutorial, but I guess a lot of people skip it. The slashing part of the game does feel stiff; there are quality of life changes or functions that a lot of players are used, and this game doesn't have them. No regenerative health, ammo is scarce and you cant control your team mates. They just go about doing their thing. With the new patches, the game does save at checkpoints and the checkpoints are now reasonable. There are times that it feels like when you die, you get sent all the way to the beginning of the game. I suggest that people buy on a sale. Its a PS4 era game that needed more polish, but I guess it needed to meet a deadline. The story: I like it. I am used to watching Masamune Shirow anime like Tank police: Dominion. Or Ghost in the shell. This game lives in a similar universe. Weird characters set in a cyberpunk world. I give it 3 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew what I was getting into when I purchased this and I was still shocked by just how clunky and amateurish it was. I heard about Wanted:Dead from a YouTube reviewer who praised the surprising depth of the combat and how satisfying higher difficulties were. The actual gameplay is indeed pretty good, despite the jank permeating every element of the game, but there's one thing really holding me back from "getting good" at this: the terrible checkpoint system. Growing up with arcade games, games with password save systems, and even full length games with no save system at all, having checkpoints 10 or more minutes apart is still unacceptable in 2023. The low enemy variety, combined with being forced to clear several rooms again after a death, would make this tediously unplayable if it wasn't for the sheer absurd spectacle of this game.Wanted:Dead feels like a 12 year old somehow got their hands on a big budget and ran wild. The MC is clearly someone's DeviantArt OC and the game seems built around her. The police station base has multiple mini-game rooms and lounges for her to hang out in and they include substance-less cutscenes of her showering and changing her outfit into a different set of clothes after every mission. The rest of the cutscenes are boring, poorly directed, and poorly shot, and add to the amateurish feel of the whole game. Almost all of the voice actors sound like they're not native English speakers, but she stands out the worst, sounding like an eastern European who is just reading words off a page. The only passable VA is Doc, who sounds like Harrison Ford from Fiverr. The rest of the audio is pretty bad too with the OST sounding like one minute loops of royalty-free tracks and all of the sound effects sounding cheap and repetitive with no variation or modulation.The graphics overall are okay but a lot of it still feels like a first pass. Small details that most people take for granted in other games stand out jarringly here: for example, character's eyes are too matte and their eyelashes are too short. The MC has comically large irises (like the live action Battle Angel Alita) that clash with the semi-realistic art style of the game, and Gunsmith (modeled after Stefanie Joosten, known for MGS5) has a poorly rigged face that is rigid like a mask. Explosions look cheap and cause environmental "damage" like papers exploding or glass shattering but the effects are simplistic and without variation. The environments look okay early on but degrade in quality over time, with the last level looking like reused assets from a PS3 Yakuza game.When the game actually lets you engage in combat and isn't pushing you through bad cutscenes or ridiculous mini-game tutorials, it's still better than expected. However, this game exists in a weird alternate reality where games like DMC3 and MGR were never made and feels 15 years too late. There's no lock-on, the gunplay is terrible, parrying is strictly directional, and the parry window is shorter than expected. Even with all of these issues, I loved the absurdity and jankiness of it all, but I still can't recommend it. This is a guilty pleasure, something that is better experienced by watching someone else play it, and something that I wouldn't admit to liking in conversation.

_childDocuments_.review: 🟩 Pros: + Pre mission weapon customisation + Dismemberment and finishing strikes never get old + Three skill trees (offense, defence, utility) offering fast paced and unique gameplay🟥 Cons:- Linear level design makes it feel like an on rails shooter- Cannot change to pistol despite being in the pre mission loadout?- Audio is heavily repeated throughout the game e.g. comrade dialogue or enemy death cries Wanted: Dead (WD) is described as a hybrid slasher/shooter, and ultimately, that’s exactly how it plays. From the very beginning up until the first boss, it was a non-stop action-packed thrill ride. Execution however leaves a lot to be desired. On paper, WD appears reads like an amazing game, I mean who wouldn’t love exhilarating combo filled melee combat crossed with intense gunplay? In action, it plays similarly to Devil May Cry, although much less polished. Ultimately, it feels like a game made for consoles past (think PS3/360) opposed to a 2023 title.However, my playtime was unfortunately cut short, and I stopped playing prematurely. Bugs, jank, and questionable game design decisions hold it back. While I personally don’t consider it a good game, it’s because it’s not made for gamers like me.WD opens with a short cutscene, and this is where my first problem with the game exists - The accents and voice acting are awful. It’s as if Tommy Wiseau was tasked with finding the voice actors. Words cannot explain how awkward and uncomfortable the characters sound.The first mission feels like a rail shooter with melee combat sprinkled throughout, which highlights further problems with the game – Linearity, a poor checkpoint system and questionable game design. Some may enjoy this style of gameplay, but for me, it’s a big no.A prime example of these problems is a ninja fight which occurs relatively early on. While different enemy types are introduced before this point, none prepare you for the mechanics of this fight (questionable design). When you inevitably die to the ninja's onslaught of abilities, you’ll have to battle through four waves of enemies again before you can reattempt the fight (poor checkpoints).

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game to anyone although there are cool things about it. Wanted: Dead absolutely drips with the style and flash of Japanese action games like Vanquish and Binary Domain, but, unlike those gems, Wanted: Dead never feels good to play. The combat is a jerky mess that feels like a constant fight against input latency more than your opponent. This problem gets mitigated slightly as you unlock longer combo strings, but you soon start fighting enemies that outclass your ability to deal damage so much that you are stuck in a routine of dodge-and-poke with the longer combos left unused as recipes for getting stun-locked by any mook with a sword. All of this would be fine if not for checkpoints that occasionally just don't exist regardless of traveling between areas or triggering cut-scenes. If you get this on a steep discount, it could be worth seeing some of the goofy cut-scenes, but maybe find something better to burn cash on?

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to review this game. I have a love hate relationship with it. Maybe more hate. But the game was better than I expected.First, I will say I'll just give Wanted: Dead a 5/10 simply because Steam has no proper rating system. In all honestly the game has fun value but it was too hard for me to master and I got stuck only 1 hour into the game. Unless I find a mod or something to make the game much more easy I find I wasted my money. I understood most of how to do things but did not understand how to string them all together for success and that is the main thing that hung me up. And also that I feel the game got too hard too fast. I'll say what others may have said. I got stuck on the first major ninja. Not the minor knife wielders. No matter what I did if it hit me I died. Grenades did nothing. Bullets did nothing. I had to go in fighting and I was just not good at going one on one with them. Plus, usually by the time I got to them I had already lost one life so if they killed me I had to start the level over again and again and again. I hate that. Rinse and repeat annoys me to no end.Throwing grenades was easy but targeting was not great when taking cover.Leveling skills could have been a bit faster too in the early levels.Blocking didn't seem like it was effective enough. Dodging which I could do easily also didn't seem to be as effective as it could have been.No clear tutorial on how stringed attacks happen. Even in the practice I could not get past the two enemy part without dying fast. For me, I just wanted to get to the next level and continue enjoying the game. _childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead ReviewWhen I heard that Soleil was going to be making a game that utilized their pedigree in gaming from their past works such as Dead or Alive, Ninja Gaiden, and Devil’s Third, I was immediately on board with what they were making. From the trailers and sneak peeks that I got to see of Wanted: Dead, I was immediately excited and couldn’t wait to get my hands on it. You see, gaming in the modern era is very formulaic with little to no innovations with developers either sticking to a winning formula or remaking a game from the decades past. Experimentation is not a common thing in today’s gaming landscape save for the indie-devs and the few times AAA companies allow their devs to make something original (Hi-Fi- Rush I’m looking at you), so for me I was all in on something new that would disrupt the genre again. And here we are with Wanted: Dead from Soleil. Does it live up to the pedigree of the studios previous works and blaze a new trail, or does it stumble out the gate and land with only the hardcore of gamers that miss the 2000’s era of gaming? Let’s find out!Wanted: Dead is set in a cyberpunk dystopian 2022 in the shoes of Hannah Stone who is a formular war criminal turned police officer and head of Hong Kong’s Zombie Squad comprised of ex-cons serving life sentences. Hannah and the Zombie Squad are tasked with stopping any threats deemed too dangerous for normal police work and are therefore given freedom to eliminate whatever threat appears, Hannah and company will have to come to terms with their new roles as well as the dangerous bullet laden future that awaits and ultimately wants them…..dead. The gameplay of Wanted: Dead is essentially a third-person action hack-n-slash with cover-based third-person shooter mixed in it. You’ll run into mostly empty arenas and fight wave after wave of enemy before you can proceed further which is a gameplay formula that was at it’s peak in the late 2000’s. The best way to describe this game is Devil’s Third 2 or Devil’s Third Remake, which is accurate when you consider that the team at Soleil also made Devil’s Third and some of the Ninja Gaiden games. As someone who is used to this genre of gaming, after some trial and error, I got my bearings with the combat loop that you find yourself in. Hannah has access to a Katana, pistol, and various semi-automatic rifles. With the katana, Hannah is able to do a multitude of sword combos that she’s able to intermix with her pistol which can help guard break enemies who end up blocking too much. You can also just fire off rounds of the pistol by pressing the Y button on the controller which will automatically aim at the closet enemy near Hannah. The third-person shooter part of the game plays similar to Gears of War with you being able to run up to objects in the environment and get into cover. From there you can do blind fire as well as ADS or Aim Down Sights and shoot from an over the shoulder perspective which you would think would be good dealing with enemies, until you realize that the gunplay for the most part is entirely ineffective for the majority of enemies that are nothing more than bullet sponges. You will constantly run out of ammo and will need to rely on the katana to dish out the pain although that also comes with its disadvantages. The prime culprit is the fact that once Hannah is in a sword swing animation, you are fully committed to seeing that animation play out and if you want to dodge or parry, then you are SOL and will be taking damage. Borrowing the parry mechanic from Ninja Gaiden and Devil’s Third, Hannah is able to parry an incoming attack right before it lands by pressing block which will open up the enemy to being punished. If you see the enemy glimmer red, then immediately press Y to fire your pistol of which will parry the unblockable attack and leave the enemy open for either a meaty combo or if they get into a stunned state and are flashing white, then you can press Y and B together and grab the enemy and do one of numerous brutal executions.You’ll need to find a good flow between the sword and gun combat, as I find it is best to soften up the enemies with a few pistol shots followed by some sword swings, and if you get the opportunity to parry an incoming attack or counter an unblocking heavy attack, then do as it will allow you to mow down the increasingly difficult enemies. The other guns I find to not be worth the time as even if you line up a headshot, enemies will soak up bullets. That’s not to say don’t ever use the other guns as there are moments when you will be pinned down by gun fire, and trying to rush up on the enemy Rambo style will get you quickly killed, so use the cover mechanic and try to shoot the explosive barrels in the environment and take out some enemies with the gun. There is a gauge that builds up as you hit enemies that once filled will allow you to activate bullet time which will slowdown time and have Hannah fire off a bunch of shots that will put most enemies in a stunned state and allow you to do a chain of instant kills if enough enemies are in proximity and when used on bosses and sub-bosses, then Hannah will inflict tons of damage on them.You can carry up to 2 rifles, shotguns, or grenade launchers and can freely swap between them. Some weapons even give you the option to switch the firing rate at the press of a button. You can also use grenades which come in a variety flavors which really come in handy when surrounded by enemies. There is a skill tree system that allows you to gain new abilities such as being able to do follow up attacks after a parry, do a charged up katana swing, extend your basic combos, and even gain additional stat buffs and bonuses. Every defeated enemy gives you experience points that you can use to gain new skills that will help you in battle.At every check point you come across, the gunsmith will send their drone of which will allow you to customize your guns from the stock, barrel, ammo clip, scope, and even the camo skin. Each change that you make will change the stats of your rifle and pistol such as increased or decreased accuracy, recoil, damage and stopping power, ammo, and more. Its best to try and evenly balance out your rifle while with the pistol I find it best to focus on its damage potential and stopping power.Lastly, when not in missions, you’ll find yourself at the police station with you able to roam around and talk to various officers as well as play various mini games in the louche area.Graphically, Wanted: Dead is ROUGH looking. It is very much a game with visuals from the Xbox 360/PS3 era that rarely ever looks like a modern era game. This isn’t necessarily a bad thing but when you look at the fact that modern games look generations better than that era, it makes this one a hard one to say that it’s a modern game and not just some indie low-budget title especially when you consider that this is a full price game. Hannah and her squad all animate almost robotically and have the most stilted of facial features I’ve seen in years. The amount of detail in the character models and the lip syncing is all indie-rific and that’s all I have to say about it. Environments aren’t anything to write home about either and are mainly open areas with set pieces to take cover behind.So, with all the Jank and undercooked and half-baked ideas; is Wanted: Dead worth buying? Yes and No. I say no because this game as it is should not be a full priced game with how much jank is in it, however I say yes because I find the jank to be appealing as I am a fan of the developers of this game and miss this genre that has gone on to merely generate God of War 2018 clones. This game was willing to take some risks, reutilize ideas the team had from Devil’s Third and Ninja Gaiden, and make a game that I honestly had a lot of fun with. Is it for everyone? No, but it’s a game that will have me coming back to it over and over. If you’re looking for a game with a game
