_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is an enjoyable, but tough game to get into. I don't just mean the difficulty; don't get me wrong, it is difficult (especially in the Police HQ and Kowloon Street stages, seriously screw those stages), but I mean the gameplay is janky and takes a while to get into. Still, I was able to enjoy it after I overcame some of the most challenging parts of the game. The game definitely gives off niche mid to late 2000s to early 2010s Japanese game vibes, which is fine by me, but just know what you are getting into.  If Steam has a mixed rating option for recommending games, I would classify this game as that.Pros:- Charming & stylish artstyle and gameplay- Game is short and sweet- Decent mechanics- Skill tree is not very big- Fine boss fights- Likable characters- No censorship (I know there's a crude censored bar when you use the chainsaw) and politically correct woke nonsense- Hannah Stone is the good kind of strong female character, unlike Abby from The Last Of Us Part 2- Satisfying gore factor and execution animations- Somewhat enjoyable mini-games to break up the pace- Pure action- Not filled to the brim with cutscenes and isn't a glorified interactive movieCons:- Game play is janky- Gunplay is awkward- Checkpoints are too far apart- Technical problems like framerate stuttering and freezing- Game crashed on me at times- No borderless option- Parrying and guarding are less forgiving in this game than others- Game can be very difficult at times, but not in the fun and rewarding kind of difficult (please farm out skill points and buy 75-80% of skills from the skill tree before the Police HQ stage, you won't regret it)- You can't change difficulties on the flyDespite all of the problems this game has (at worst I'll give a 6.5 or 7 out of 10), I still enjoyed this game even though it was janky and got stupid hard at times. I recommend this game if you can get it on sale and enjoy niche, pure action games. It's not surprising that this game is difficult and the enemies take no prisoners since some of the people who worked on Ninja Gaiden also worked on this game. This game is really for a specific audience and just like I said, know what you are getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is the new epitome of ‘old-school’, it feels like a game that you’d expect to play from back on the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 generation. It’s silly, messy, frustrating at times and most importantly, it’s pure focus on gameplay makes it a fun title.The story revolves around the main heroine, Lt. Hannah Stone, as she leads an elite team known as the “Zombie Squad” in cyberpunk Hong Kong. Imprisoned as one of the losing combatants in a global war, Lt. Hannah Stone is given one final chance to escape her imprisonment, along with the other members of her squad. After a job goes awry, Zombie Squad and the department that keeps tabs on them are at risk of loosing their immunity to a company called Dauer Synthetics.As Zombie Squad continues their investigation into a sudden Synthetic uprising, they soon find themselves involved with Dauer and a world of underhanded dealings and politics. A mysterious set of mercenaries soon start to take aim at the team and begins to haunt them down.That may sound interesting now, but Wanted: Dead’s story isn’t going to stick with you, the writing feels muddled or even Frankensteined together. One moment you’re walking through the police headquarters and then, wham, a sudden 2D animated cutscene that dwells into Hannah’s past, then you go back just to be treated to another Hannah flashback, only this time using the in-game models.The characters themselves are enjoyable, but it’s too bad the game doesn’t focus enough on them, I wanted to know more about Doc and his way of thinking. Unfortunately, the game settles for a hidden character file that the player could miss if they aren’t running around the entire headquarters looking for secrets.Graphically Wanted: Dead is a relic, as mentioned before the game looks like a seventh-generation title, character models are serviceable, and the animation is ok. Levels don’t have anything too memorable or unique about them, even the enemies outside of the bosses are cookie-cutter masked soldiers and small variants of synthetics, the coolest looking minions are the sword wielding ninjas.The biggest draw for Wanted: Dead is the hybrid combat that consist of Hannah’s katana and her pistol, with a small selection of secondary weapons to spice things up, this is both a bright spot and a blemish. Balancing melee with a shooter goes against what many shooter fans know, stay in cover, and pick your shot wisely, unfortunately Wanted: Dead ignores that message and demands the player to continuously move around away from cover while facing a room of assault rifle wielding goons.The game wants its cake and eat it too, for some strange reason melee attacks to more damage than a shotgun to the face, even when it comes to the enemy ai. Sometimes they will get shots on me while I was doing a combo and the damage was nearly unnoticeable, but then other times those same shots would absolutely drain Hannah’s health as if she was getting hit with rounds from a gatling gun, these unbalanced moments happen far too often and becomes frustrating when you’re trying to get to the next room and you’re out of ammo.Speaking of ammo, the game really doesn’t want players to play it as a shooter, because ammo is so ridiculously limited that you won’t grow an attachment to any one weapon and the enemy ai is just raining ungodly amounts of rounds. The idea that players should run towards the grenade launching enemy while battling a spider mech firing silo rockets with just a sword sounds cool, but the execution just isn’t there.Although the execution animations are awesome and are one the most rewarding aspect of the game’s combat, by cutting off limbs there’s a chance that an enemy will become stunned, once this happens Hannah can go into an animation where she will pull of stylish kills depending on where she and the enemy are. She’ll push an enemy towards a wall to slice their throat with her Katana or spin and execute a headshot, my personal favorite is the John Wick-esq body roll to headshot, there are over 50 finishers and it’s worth trying to trigger them all.When it comes to available weapons don’t expect a wide array of choices, Hannah has a rifle, a pistol and a sword that can’t be changed out between missions. Throughout the game there will be an ally drone that will resupply the team and serve as a checkpoint, at these moments players will be able to change out certain pieces of Hannah’s rifle and pistol. The rifle can change out the sight, stock, magazine and the barrel, while the pistol is limited to a sight, barrel and the grip.The pieces player chooses will have small affects on the weapons’ overall performance, for example, changing the rifle’s barrel will heighten or lower the gun’s accuracy or recoil. Meanwhile, changing the sight on the pistol can affect stopping power and damage, they feel like small changes but can help serve a purpose when chaining together combos.Weapons can be picked up from fallen enemies including an LMG, a grenade launcher, a shotgun, an SMG, and the worst chainsaw in videogame history. As a friendly warning, stay away from the shotgun, it’s more likely to get Hannah killed rather than kill the enemies with it’s extremely low range and ammo count. And for the love of everything that’s good, avoid the aforementioned chainsaw, it’s a trap and basically gives enemies free shots at Hannah.As the game goes along, Hannah can acquire new skills and squad abilities to help her survive the onslaught of swords and bullets, some abilities will only work if you have a certain teammate with you, but you can’t choose who goes on a mission, the game does it automatically depending on the story.Skills are set into three categories: offense, defense, and utility. Utility allows Hannah to carry extra grenades and grants allies special finishers or the ability to give Hannah an extra health pack after reviving her if she dies while in battle.Even these features feel kind of half baked as the only ally ability that actually has an affect in the field is Doc’s revive ability, and that’s the last ability that can be unlocked which means you will have upgrade the first two allies before you can unlock the actual useful ability. The allies that fights alongside Hannah make for great distractions and cannon fodder as players don’t have to worry about any of them dying or bleeding out, they have unlimited health and will shoot well enough to eventually kill an enemy, but they won’t be around during boss fights and Hannah will have to go solo for that.Boss battles are challenging as each boss has their own gimmick and forces the player to slow down and pay attention to their attack patterns, from an enemy that can turn invisible to a duo that will attack with one of them using a blade to get close to Hannah while the other uses a gun to fire from afar, these are actually the most annoying part of the game because a couple of the bosses have a cool look to them but feels like Soleil stopped at the design phase. The bosses have no characterization to them as they serve little purpose to the story and are just an excuse to pit the players against an idea of a cool character.When players aren’t out on missions they can play some mini-games, from basic fun games like a surprisingly addictive claw machine, to karaoke and ramen eating. These mini games are a great break from the main game and will help de-stress some of the frustrations you may attain from the story.A game like Wanted: Dead is something I would recommend to friends like me, players who crave a single player game that doesn’t muck around with season passes, live service or loot boxes, what you see is what you get. Sadly, I wouldn’t recommend the game at the full $60 price tag, but definitely something worth picking up during a sell at $40.

Dumb..EDIT: Changed it to a negative review because 110 industries and all other devs that charge top $ for mediocre work and then after over 4 months, no patch. well they can all go pound sand and then some. Just bs false promises and lies about one being worked on with no eta. At this point it would not matter if they came out with a patch, or a sequel or anything. Done supporting corrupt, lizard people who produce hot garbage. Next time, don't take months for a patch or maybe find a new career. Game is trash and so are the sales. Shameful.EDIT: After putting 20 more hours into the game I can confidently say I stand by this review. I am now much better at combat and I am still not tired of watching the different ways I can execute people. My only things I would like to see implemented is cloud saving, steam deck verified and not being able to change difficulty when doing new game+ mode while having all abilities saving just makes it feels pointless. I do hope some DLC or a sequel are possible. _________________________________I have never played Ninja Gaiden. I was pretty young when that game was being talked about a lot. I watched a friend play it and watching him redo the same part of a mission for hours, just to do the exact same thing minutes later and to just rinse and repeat the process not only seemed tedious and boring but absolutely asinine. I would wonder how people enjoyed games like that. I'm an eye candy, Micheal Bay, Grand Theft Auto V kinda guy...You're probably wondering. "okay, this moron accidentally left a positive instead of a negative review". The thing is. The market now is filled with remasters, remakes, sequels, trilogies, spin off, etc. That is has become not only redundant, stale, and boring but out right disgusting. The industry has become a breeding ground for game passes, loot crates, microtransactions, season passes and whatever else and it's not entirely these devs/publishers fault because we keep buying it and saying thank you. With all that said. This. Is. A. Good. Game.I knew nothing about this game other than seeing it pop up in the steam market place last night. I watched the trailer and was immediately drawn in. The characters, the gore, the combat, the cringe dialog, off the wall story, the Japanese style mini games, the aesthetics, everything. Everything screamed this is my type of game. So when I looked up the reviews I was completely thrown off by what I was reading. It wasn't just performance. People are bashing on this game in every way possible. With a price tag of $60 I was obviously concerned but thanks to Steams generous refund system I figured I would try it and all I can say is I am glad I did. I thought this game was going to be your typical hack and slash game but I was far wrong. I was immediately thrown back to the days of watching my friend play Ninja Gaiden as that is identically what this game is. Rather than feeling thrown off like I did when I was a kid, I found a sense of accomplishment after finally beating a segment in the game by learning when to parry, dodge, block, shoot, run, heal, etc.. Even the checkpoint system people are complaining about is not that big a deal to me. It's not as frequent as most games now a days but I see it as more practice. Right now, I am not happy with my current abilities as I am still trying to get used to the controls and do more than just use my hand gun, dodge and attack. Until I am able to pull off some of these crazy combos I've seen others do, I don't mind 10-20 minutes between checkpoints. Performance for me is fine. I get 60 FPS on a 6 year old computer. If you were a fan of those mid/late 2000 games like WET, Velvet Assassin, Wanted: Weapons of Fate and you like the challenges and difficulty that Ninja Gaiden and Souls games bring than I would definitely recommend this game, Even at $60 there is so much replay value here. 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The cutscenes are terrible, the voice acting is terrible. Everything else is pretty terrible, too. I figured on going in not expecting much and just have fun with it for what it is, even if the story was kind of crap. That's not really possible because it plays like crap, too. Beware the people telling you it's the good kind of bad, because it's not. It's just bad. It looks and plays like a cheap remaster of a forgotten 50 cent Walmart bargain bin game from 2005. I'd be on board for laughing at cheesy story beats between missions, but the gameplay is so bad I don't even want to bother.    All of this is *after* they overhauled combat? ...How bad was it before this??? Simple things like taking and leaving cover are so clunky and unresponsive that they're difficult to do. Enemies are damage sponges. You die very easily.      I've bought some bad games, and even like some really bad games. This game is a serious contender for being one of the worst games I have ever played. The best thing I can say about is that it didn't crash when I booted it up to play it, but I kind of wish it had. It was dirt cheap on the Steam sale and the game is so bad that it feels like I got scammed. I'm honestly stunned that this was ever released at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead, a quirky third person shooter / hackedy slashy type action game (and most insufferably dumb use of a colon in a title I've seen in a good long while) is a game that broke me in only 4+ hours. It starts off with an obnoxiously long opening cut-scene, which I was given the option to skip since even the developer thinks it's utter ♥♥♥♥♥. Then, I entered a building and proceeded to take on enemies using a combination of third person shooting and katana shenanigans, which was simple enough until the game asked you to fight a melee enemy. Using standard melee, a melee enemy won't go down quickly unless you parry or counter, and then finish them off with your overly long finishing move. You can expedite this by getting the skill that let's you finish enemies who you've dismembered with standard melee attacks (and yes, this game has skill trees because it wasn't annoying enough without them) which made things pretty tolerable and cathartic at times, even with the camera that actively hated me and the enemy AI that makes me want to apologize to Bethesda.Once I was halfway through the first level, I encountered a mini boss that proceeded to kill me multiple times until I figured out you just have to parry everything he throws at you (sometimes literally) which wouldn't be so bad if the checkpoint system didn't force me to clear out the room he was in every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time which is annoying since one of his attacks can one-shot you. It's like going to a mini golf course with a 700 yard par 6 on the 9th hole.Afterwords, the rest of the level played out pretty normally (the second ninja mini-boss was a LOT easier to take care of after I "got gud") and I faced and defeated the final boss who proved annoying to fight, yet exponentially easier than Difficulty McSpikerton, the ninja. After more obnoxiously long, nonsensical cut-scenes (like, a lot of them) and an annoying mini-game or two, I hit level two and encountered enemies with incendiary bombs that killed me twice by locking me in place and slowly draining my health with fire (seriously, ♥♥♥♥ whoever designed those). No ninjas here (which was a relief, but also confounding in a way), but there was a boss fight that proved equally as annoying and it was at this point I decided to just quit and uninstall. I could have "git gud" and figured out the mysteries of this insufferable ♥♥♥♥, but then I though to myself, why? Why should I bother? So I can deal with more underwhelming gunplay? Enemies that take forever to attack so I can parry and/or counter them the same way over and over again? A camera that's entirely at odds with the unbelievably claustrophobic environments? More and more asinine cut-scenes with "we put out an ad on Craigslist" tier voice acting? Sudden spikes in difficulty that you'd expect from a group of complete amateurs (apparently the guys who made this worked on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ NINJA GAIDEN ARE YOU KIDDING ME)? Enemies that will zip past you at mach speed to attack your semi-competent teammates? Quirky rhythm mini-games? Chest high walls you can vault next to knee high ones you can't? Yeah, no, which is a shame because for all it's faults, the game is oozing with the charm of something you'd find from an auteur like Suda 51 or SWERY, but without any of the technical competency (which is already a pretty low bar). Basically, it's a shy nerd who spent all summer buying better clothes, working out, and improving his hair and skin, only to sit alone in the corner at lunch because he forgot to deal with his crippling social anxiety and inability to talk about anything not related to hentai or Magic: The Gathering.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat system is very good and deep as it forces you to experiment and find your own style that works for you. You can mix katana strikes and block and parry and dodge with handgun counter and general handgun and other weapons shots. Finishing moves that you can perform are probably the best part of the combat because they look nice and feel satisfying. It is a very rich and interesting system that requires you to get better at it if you want to defeat more difficult enemies while not really requiring almost anything from you when you fight the general weak enemies. Like killing basic soldiers in stage 1 or android workers in stage 2 or bouncers in stage 3 is easy as all it takes is a few shots or few katana hits.But killing ninja enemies that also have katanas or big exoskeleton enemies that carry heavy machine guns is much harder as you have to get really good at parring their attacks in order to win because they are fast moving bullet sponges that will do their best to dodge your shots and get close to you and it will be easier and faster to kill them with katana than it is with guns. But thankfully you can also cheese ninjas with fire grenades because if they will start to burn they won’t dodge any of the bullets making them easy to kill with guns or you can use fire grenades to separate one ninja from the other so you can fight 1 vs 1 making the fight easier. Because your handgun is the only weapon in the world that has unlimited ammo you can even cheese ninjas by just shooting them a few times and dodging away till they are dead. I also find it funny how the brown ninja will die from a propane tank explosion but it will take 2-3 grenade launcher shots to kill him.Enemies wearing exoskeleton are the hardest enemies and the biggest problem in the game if you try to use things like guns or grenades against them. Thankfully they are not intelligent at all so despite having all that armor and heavy machine gun and infinite amount of grenades that they can use to destroy you from a distance they prefer to charge you and fight with you in melee trying to hit you with their heavy machine gun. Thanks to them being just stupid the best way to kill them is to parry their hits and do gun counters and slash them with a katana. The funny thing is I tested them and they will survive 3 whole magazines from your assault rifle or 12 shots from grenade launcher without problems but 12 combos from a katana will kill them. I guess they are just coded in a way to be a bullet sponge of the worst kind where katana deals more damage to them than anything else that exists in the game. Funny thing is that 12 shots from grenade launcher is enough to destroy stage 1 boss and that boss is a tank but they are not enough to kill a guy in exoskeleton. I guess the only reason tanks are produced in this world is because they actually use their weapons to shoot at enemies instead of trying to fight them in melee like the exoskeleton guys. Thankfully these exoskeleton guys can be killed with one hit from a chainsaw just like any enemy in the game.Sadly your squad attacks mean nothing and deal almost no damage. I think their guns should fire paintballs at enemies for added realism of how useful they are. It feels like the teammates that are with you exist only to be a distraction so you won’t get swarmed than any real help in combat. I think the most important skill they have is screaming “grenade” when enemies throw one at you and that the Doc will heal you once when you are down. Thankfully there are skill trees and in that skill trees there are even skills to make your squad a little better but these will probably be the skills that you will pick last as after seeing your squad in action you will just focus on improving your own skills to kill faster and survive longer. Oh where to start… The voice acting of our main hero Hannah Stone is the worst. It shows no emotion and it sounds like someone did just read a script and after googling it out I was surprised that it was made by a real living person and not just a computer reading the text. But the voices of everyone else are not at all much better. And the whole way anyone speaks or moves or gestures in the cutscenes is just bad. Thankfully when we see Hannah Stone remembering her past life it is done as anime and these animations are much better. I think all cutscenes should be done by the same person that did these animations because they are the only good looking cutscenes in the whole game. Thankfully cooking videos that you can find in claw machine are also funny.And the claw machines and the shooting range are the only good mini-games that this game has. Eating ramen is ok – I admit I’m bad at rhythm games but still I can see that this mini-game is just ok as it is about mashing 8 different buttons but at least you can find additional tracks to play in the claw machine. The karaoke mini-game is just bad. It is just the copy of ramen mini-game somehow made to be worse. Not only it has only one song and that song is 99 Luftballons but there are no other songs to collect anywhere in the game. I can’t imagine why they created this mini-game in the first place just for one song. The last mini-game is the side-scrolling shooter called Space Runaway and sadly it is bugged. I saw other people on youtube that were able to play it how it was intended but mine was set in a way that I saw only about 50% of the screen and my mech and enemies were huge.And the bug with Space Runaway was not the only bug I had and I think it was connected with graphic settings bugs. Each time I did exit the game the graphic settings were resetting so I had to set them again to my liking changing from 60 to 144 fps and changing the blur to 0 and forcing the game to be launched in full screen mode and not just in a window. Sometimes grenades bounce back to me and the grenade launcher shots explodes in the front of my face because they are hitting some invisible wall in the air. The worst bug was with the unique weapon that you can win from shooting range – not only it is weaker than your own assault rifle – it is even hard to swap this weapon out for your normal assault rifle at checkpoints. When I was testing that weapon there were many times where I had to try 5 or more times to swap back to my normal assault rifle at checkpoints for the game to even recognize that I don’t want to use it anymore.The worst part of the game is the story. Parts about Hannah Stone make sense but there are multiple holes in the rest of the story and many things that never get addressed. Why enemies in stage 1 did steal money if it can’t be used in this part of the world? How losing that money that can’t be used makes the most famous company go bankrupt over night? Why the police force that is famous for killing all suspects all the time would be send to stop a protest and why they would start by just killing protesters with a sniper rifle from a helicopter? And why a few days later after murdering more than 100+ of such protesters their leader would be ok with helping us? There are many holes in the story like that. Also many cut-scenes add additional informations that are never addressed again.The whole game is just 5 stages connected by a story that makes little to no sense in the end. It looks like the story is only there to push the player from stage to stage. This game would be much better with no story at all – just fighting stages and nothing in between them. Good combat and bad everything else combined with 40$ price.Overall score 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Skip this oneThe story and presentation is pretty interesting and wacky and has me interested but the game play is nothing mixed with barely functionalIt's not a matter of polish, there's just nothing hereMelee enemy hit frames are not synced with the weapon and you'll be hit immediately on startup, meaning you have to basically understand the enemy's tempo instead of ever trying to react to anything"Aim Assist" seems to do the weakest amount of magnetism to demonstrate it exists, but when quick aiming in melee it just aims to the left of targetsSecondary guns are barely usable, and you don't get enough ammo to use them as they're designed, and the grenade launchers don't even one shot melee enemies on direct hitThere are instant flame grenade tosses on you so that you cannot react to them in any wayHealing is both weak (50% health by default) and you cannot use it while doing literally anything, and is so slow that you're almost guaranteed to get hit while using it in combatYou're then given this really confusing sense of that the game is really forgiving and you'll be picked up off the ground if you go down, but sometimes not, and then never on bosses, which is the place where it'd matter the mostBosses have multiple phases but can potentially kill you in two hits, but they are not as fragile, so you end doing souls like grinds on bosses for success but without the same systems to do so, without estus openings, without meaningful amount of estus, just so you can learn parry timings so you can participate in the fightAnd, to top it off, the bosses are the only interesting thing about the gameplayThere's nothing happening in the stages, it's just kill the same enemies over and over until checkpoint, repeat until boss

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is fascinating and weird. If you can look past a bit of jank there's a very captivating and interesting game here that's worth a couple of hours just to experience it.I bought and first played this before the Combat Overhaul update and i gotta be honest i really struggled with it. Since i am not really used to playing these sorts of games i struggled a lot and kept dying over and over again and it took me a good 2 hours to get past the first mission and i ultimately quit the game. Now after the overhaul (and the ability to chose easy mode) i gave this game another try and it has been a fascinating ride where i can't seem to stop playing because i want to know what happens next. While the level design struggles at times with jankyness, the combat is quite servicable and has some really cool and well animated and varied takedown animations. So if that turned you off in the past, you should really give it another try.But the real hook about this game is the absolute insanity that's unfolding in front of you in a narrative sense. I don't recall any game I've played where i'd loudly say to myself "Why would you do it like this?". The amount of tonal whiplash from scene to scene in terms of line delivery, background music and subject matter is unlike anything I've seen before. And it kept me enthralled to see what would jump at me next. It's a game that makes me keep playing because i was genuinely interested in what it will happen next, not because of some soulless grind or manipulative design.I want to be clear here, this is not some soulless slop. There is a clear amount of effort and passion that went into this beautiful mess that is visible in many places, with love and attention to detail and the sort of charm you get from someone who really wants to make something special but keeps stumbling over his own feet.

_childDocuments_.review: Euro jank 3PS with Transporter (2002) and Bad Boys 2 (2003) vibes.Fun characters and hilarious voice acting.Very cinematic and immersive experience.Has a few mini games which seem to be designed to mock mini games in general :DBizarre key binds out of the box, but easily re-configured.Bugs out in the upgrade menu. Bad QA.Each linear level is broken up into sections with checkpoints in-between for ammo reload and saving.Be prepared to juggle gun and swords constantly against waves of tanky, bullet-sponge mobs.Pro-tip 1: Upgrade pistol with highest stopping power and spam it repeatedly to stun lock your attackers to finish them with katana.Pro-tip 2: Limit your primary AR to burst fire headshot groupings only. Ammo is a scarcity until the next checkpoint.Insanely hard when it comes to boss fights which are complete A$$.If you miss the brief stun-state finisher opportunity on the long arduous boss fights, it's game over and back to square one.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from the Humble Heroines Bundle for 15 bucks. Given that I recommend this game on sale, but at full price it is a tough recommendation. I played this game on hard, and steam says 9 1/2 hours but in game it says 10 1/2. Imagine a 10 hour Yakuza game with all the minigames with added jank and not nearly as high quality.Essentially this game is a throw back to 90s style action detective. Think Die Hard, but with a kick ass female cyborg league. The biggest strength of the game is this charm.  The dialogue sounds like a B tier translation and the people speak as if their 10 year olds trying to talk like characters from an R rated movie; I am not sure if this is intentional or not. Either way it leads to equal number of absolute hilarious moments and absolute exhaustive moments. The characters you play with are stereotypical personalities for the most part, but I liked them all. The story though is interesting, but man its execution is not good. The main flaws of the game: The game is janky and while people say its intentional and supposed to emulate the 360/ps2 era... I hated it. I feel like it was exaggerated and I definitely found it frustrating in an unfun way.  Mainly due to the damn camera that even when unlocked in settings still fling about. Plus towards the end you fight the same enemies over. and over. and over. and over. Its like they took the worse aspects of the jank and little of the charm from those eras.  For some that will be fun, but for me I had to push past the two missions... out of 5. The gunplay and melee is very spammy, and it overall feels okay. The game overall has so many ideas that are thrown in and while it keeps things interesting. NONE of them are fleshed out to its maximum potential. Overall Wanted Dead was a game I had my eye on for a while, and glad I played. It has style and playing melee gun combat is fun enough. Personally probably won't come back to it, but an expanded sequel with less jank would catch my interest.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good action game (no surprise considering it's from the Ninja Gaiden people). _childDocuments_.review: Don't get fooled by the bad reviews as most of them are just blatant cases of skill issues. The real problem is that the game doesn't hold your hand and doesn't give you any real details about how the different combat systems work and will expect you to dig a bit by yourself to uncover the substance. Oh, and the camera is free, no lock-on or auto-targeting nonsense here. You'll have to learn to love that right stick.Once you understand that the different moves and combos can be canceled and linked between each other, it will open a new layer of gameplay that is very satisfying. Grenade a room, roll into cover to pop some baddies, vault over the tables, send some limbs flying in the air after sliding in their faces with your katana to finish them off in slo-mo john woo style. The team ninja legacy is strong with this one.The story is... let's just say weird. It's a tough cop b-movie set in a cyberpunkish Hong-Kong and of course you fight in Kowloon. All the tropes are there with the hardasses, the black chief of police that screams all the time and the uncanny delivery of the voice actors that often seem out of place. If you're a fan of 80-90's videoclub flicks, you'll be right at home.The game also has some mini-games... They suck. But at least you can karaoke 99 luftbaloons, which is something.The game is not without its flaws, the difficulty is all over the place with some rough spikes that will end up in cheap and frustrating deaths, coupled with the fact that some of the most difficult segments are also the ones where the checkpoints are spaced the furthest apart. Half of the secondary guns feel underwhelming and the grande targetting will have a few surprises in store for you. Finally, since there is no auto targeting you will need to learn that camera handling and if it's fine in most places, it can get difficult in more constrained rooms.All in all, one of the most fun I've had with an action game in recent years that doesn't take itself seriously and doesn't try to be something else. It's not a souls-like, it's not bayonetta and it's definitely the best PS2 game of this era.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of charm. It's got a lot of oddball humor, interesting minigames, and the combat is ""mostly"" enjoyable. But some enemies are just absurdly tanky, are nearly impossible to stagger and chase you relentlessly. This is fine in moderation but by the end you will fight multiples of them in narrow corridors with zero room to maneuver. That just exacerbates the sudden, camera freakouts and takes this immediately from challenging to just plain annoying. I initially enjoyed this game and wanted to leave a positive review, but after that utter garbage final stage I just can't bring myself to recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've sat on reviewing this game since I played it right at release and I had fun with the game even with some of the bugs that were present I saw the game as what it was a homage to games I used to see everywhere. Wanted Dead has a commitment to its style that I appreciate and more than that it is important to note the developers didn't abandon anything with this game there has been updates to address bugs tweaks to fights to even add more checkpoints and other small QOL adjustments.Gameplay wise this is an old school third person action game with a lot of speed and fluidity to combat once you really get through the skill tree and you can become a walking death march which a ton of fun. The cast of characters are ripped from the cheese of B action movie and there are mini games that you can just sink time into (so much in fact that the shump got a standalone release to indulge in)In the end I do recommend this game I had fun with it but I am the target auidence as well but a huge deal for me is the continued communication from the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead is genuinely the most SOVLful game of this awful console generation so far. The fact that IGN gave it a 4 (and most other professional critics seemed to echo those sentiments) is a testament to its bold, arcade-inspired game design that spits in the face of nearly two decades of focus-tested and normie-approved AAA slop. It's hard, but in a way that feels fair, making every death deserved and every victory earned. Protip if you're dying a lot: learn to guard cancel and never look back. It is the secret sauce of the game's combat and grants you a ton of options from your admittedly slow and cooldown-heavy melee attacks. Not a huge fan of the game's reliance on skill trees to upgrade your character (mostly because I feel that they're progression for progression's sake and only give the illusion of choice since you'll likely fill all of them out by the end of the game anyway), but the sheer fun and visceral insanity of the combat more than made up for it. I also think checkpoint placement and autosaves are just a little sparse- mostly because whenever I died after buying a bunch of skill tree upgrades, I'd have to go through the laborious task of buying them all again before I could get back into the action.The story and voice acting are definitely seated firmly in the PS2 bargain bin basement, but I was still entertained by the awkward-yet-endearing banter between Hannah and her squadmates. By the time I got to the Yakuza-style karaoke minigame set to 99 Luftballoons of all things, I was grinning from ear to ear and knew that this game was special. You can definitely tell that for whatever shortcomings Wanted: Dead has, it's made by a passionate team of devs who love and respect video games as a medium and aren't afraid of making something that's fun for fun's sake- I find that refreshing in this era of ultra-serious, Sony-produced, walkie-talkie dad simulators.Get it on sale if you don't like short games and/or don't plan on replaying it constantly to climb the difficulty ladder, but for everyone else, Wanted: Dead comes highly recommended. Also, play Ninja Gaiden Black and Ninja Gaiden II. Then, when you're done, have an oatmeal cookie and give thanks to our lord and savior, Tomonobu Itagaki.

_childDocuments_.review: Weird game. The first mission is a real hurdle and during it I was prepared to give the thumbs down before I even finished it. Then as the game turned into a cheezy B-movie with the worst voice acting ever with strange mini-games, I sort of started to dig it. It was charming in a bad way. Then during the second mission the increases in both my own skills and the skill tree started to make the game almost fun. And then the game just completely made a vindaloo with weiss bier and ice-cream mess all over itself, the bed, it's wife, the cats and the dog with the second boss fight. All that which may have at some point been joy turned into utter disappointment and disbelief. You had a rough start when you got on stage but then you somehow charmed the audience with your quirky personality and midly funny jokes only to end up dropping inappropritate F-bombs and bullying a sweet old lady in the front row. Would not recommend for gameplay. Would recommend as a study in insanity.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful mess of passion and stylish action. It is a PS3/360 game in the modern day in the best and worst ways. The combat is hysterical, the fighting locations are incredibly varied visually but just open areas and hallways. Auto-chaining executions because your grenade de-limbed an entire group of people never gets old.The story tries to make sense but I don't know if it has, or if it will. This game is a crazy aesthetic and unhinged transitions from telling people to shut the ♥♥♥♥ up at a diner to suddenly going to a karaoke bar singing 99 luftballoons.  Buy it, experience a game that feels incredibly, wonderfully, horribly dated: A video game first, damn everything else.I hope they make a second one.

_childDocuments_.review: Constantly surprised me.Normally I'd say this game had tone problems, but the way they repeatedly switch between action, emotion & complete nonsense like the ramen scene can only be deliberate.In fact, every issue I have with the story, dialogue & difficulty has me constantly second guessing whether it was deliberate, because I definitely did get something out of the story only feeling half done & the difficulty being all over the place.In the end, I did care about the characters & I did work out the difficult enemies.And it left me with an experience I'll think about for a long time, for good & bad reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible in the way that terrible B movies are worth watching over and over. Despite the short length of the main campaign, I didn't end up noticing due to the amount of time I spent on the side activities. The soundtrack and aesthetics are absolutely amazing.Gameplay: The combat in this game is satisfying and rewarding, but challenging at the same time. I believe some of the difficulty can be attributed to jank, but once I got the hang of things, the combat loop was very satisfying. Executing enemies with the various finishing moves was fun to watch every time (additionally it gives you a moment to breathe.)Side activities I would describe as Yakuza-esque. Two of them can be boiled down to charming rhythm games (amazing soundtrack mentioned below) and the claw machine was a fun time-sink offering in game collectibles. Boss fights (despite one feeling like it did not fit with the combat tools you have available  were incredibly fun, particularly the ones that engage you in sword combat. (I may have added difficulty trying to approach the fights in a cinematic way lol) The gameplay experience overall reminds me of Ninja Gaiden meets Yakuza in a cyberpunk environment.Graphics: Solid. No complaints. I was not expecting era-defining, graphics card melting, realism here. I found Wanted Dead to be very stylized and quite beautiful at times especially when the use of rain, puddles, and neon lights were present.Soundtrack/Aesthetic: Neons, blood, and synth. If you like the 80's, Cyberpunk, and or Kill Bill - I can bet you will enjoy the atmosphere this game offers. I added the tracks from this game to my regular rotation before even finishing it.Voice work: This is the area that will throw most off I believe, the voice acting in this game is...interesting... Not in the way that the old Resident Evil/House of the Dead games are, but in a way that seems like English was not the primary language of the cast (with a few exceptions) Thus, the vocal inflections in some of the readings sound incorrect or strange. It almost feels like the voice work was directed by David Lynch.Overall, I had a wonderful time with Wanted Dead and I think if the above sounds interesting you will as well. It is charming, satisfying, and absolutely wild. I would recommend that if you aren't in love with this game from the trailers alone, wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely  "so bad it's good". It's just bad.Combat is the only passable aspect of the game, but even this gets annoying, especially when dealing with the tankier enemies. Unless you're getting headshots reliably, guns are basically pea-shooters. Even the generic enemies can eat a whole magazine, which you only get 3 or 4 of. The melee combat is functional, but also nothing special. Again, dealing with tankier enemies get's annoying really fast.Everything else is just terrible. The story (if you can even call it that) is barely coherent, some cutscenes are random as hell, and barely anything makes sense or feels natural in any way. This game also having no charm whatsoever, certainly doesn't make it easier to sit through.The voice-acting, especially for the main character, is absolutely atrocious. I bet even I could deliver a better performance, and I've never voice-acted a day in my life. There's also some AI speech thrown in there for the no-name NPCs. They also didn't put a lot of effort into the mixing, because the audio levels are all over the place sometimes.The minigames (inspired by the Yakuza series) are pretty basic, and come completely out of nowhere. There's also no point in doing them, so you can just fail immediately and move on.And the OST was... alright, I guess. A lot of licensed songs, though the originals are completely forgettable.Fortunately, the game is pretty short. Took me 7 hours to complete, and I was taking my time (looking for collectibles). You can probably finish this game in 3-4 hours, if you just focus on getting through the story, which I'd recommend. Or better yet, don't bother with this game to begin with. Even on sale, it's hardly worth the money. I'd say 5 bucks is fair, 10 at the absolute most, but any more than that is a rip-off. Boy, am I glad I got it through a Humble Bundle deal. Charging 30 bucks, and even worse, 60 at release is downright criminal. I feel for anyone who paid that much, and can't get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kinda like a joke, in a very good way.Even the loading screen is a meme reference (or would be without an SSD, as you can barely see it if you have a high-end PC). And yes, the voice acting is also a part of this madness, as it is "bad for a reason". The story is kinda mediocre, but if you can lay back and see it as a parody, then it can provide you with a few hours of fun time during your playthrough.You can expect John Wick type of combat but not seriousness. The gameplay is hella fun, but could have been a little bit more fluid, especially at later levels as you have to hit some enemy types way too many times to be able to kill them with your melee attack spam mixing up with some ranged combos. Or you could just use bullet time for the head which might ruin the fun. But the soundtrack and visuals compensate for it in the long term.Performance was 99% fine. There was a time during my ~4th replay when there were quite huge fps drops for some reason upon reloading a checkpoint multiple times to farm the 1k kills. But it was also gone after a few seconds and never experienced it again or before.Currently, there are minor issues with the achievements as the final one 'Wanted: Dead' might not pop up upon completion. It is probably due to an updated version of 'Ramen World Legend' as previously you had to obtain a full combo as per the description, but with the latest patch, the devs reduced it to 250. I already obtained this achievement after the patch, yet I had to reach 250 combos again to get my 'platina' trophy.All in all, this is a quite fun and rare gem that can be replayed from time to time due to its awesome combat and humour.

_childDocuments_.review: Just started this game and there are some glaring issues right off the bat. I rarely post reviews for games is they aren't terrible, and so immediately after playing them, and despite the fact this game has potential to be solid, don't waste your money. For context I paid less than £4 for this game and it's just a frustrating experience. The animators clearly know what's up, there's some great visual elements to the game, but the combat just plays poorly. It's like it has tried to marry up the elements of a cover shooter that aren't fun with a hack and slash which makes no sense for the most part because cover shooters are designed to have very little toe to toe combat thereby leaving you exposed. Level design is linear, but that's fine, it's actually what I was looking for, but the repetitive nature of certain areas and the lack of variety even within the first level leaves me cold. The reason I'm even bothering with a review this early into a game is because one of the first 'boss' scenarios in the game is just silly and highlights the worst issues within a game trying to have hack and slash elements that are implemented poorly. The game has melee combat which seemingly doesn't function correctly and is broken for a few reasons, mainly the feedback and I frames within the game for both you and the enemy just aren't clear. This leads to dying needlessly and a frustrating experience because it is inconsistent when the game wants to to block, attack, parry or counter. Aside from the big red visual for counters that essentially one-shot you, an annoying mechanic in itself, the other combos of even the basic enemies can kill you immediately with virtually no feedback.Needless mini cut scenes and things like that get in the way of pacing, opening doors and being revived, go on for too long. Somehow the exposition of the game is both slow and somehow still lacking in any meaningful information, so you end up watching what may be visually well crafted but lacks any reason other than to build characterisation that falls flat because none of the characters have any depth. The voice acting for the protagonist is also terrible sadly which is bizarre. A strange experience so far, I'll probably give it a few more hours and then move on to something that isn't just a low-tier game made by people who seem like they've been pulled from pillar to post with the direction of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's description isn't lying, this really IS a love letter to the 360/PS3 era of gaming. The incredibly linear level design coupled with some simple but very fun gameplay make for a great time if you're someone like me who grew up in that generation. The structure of the game is so just essentially following what other linear games that era did that it helped keep my expectations in check for the rest of the game.The overall flow of the game can pretty much be boiled down to:Level with hack'n'slash gameplay -> Level ends -> Start in hub area to walk around/talk to NPC's -> Interact with something to start next level -> Repeat step 1 till game endsSprinkle in some cutscenes and some minigames in between those phases and you've got Wanted: Dead. The quality of both of these are quite serviceable, given how the rest of the game feels. Cutscenes are animated pretty decently, but the voice acting in them... no, the whole game rather, can be a turn off for some people with awkward and stilted line delivery that most of the time won't match the scene. I personally loved it for these exact reasons, especially the protagonist's VA, but I can definitely why people wouldn't like it.Minigames on the other hand are neat little break from the usual gameplay, they're nothing special but are there if you want something else to do. There's a crane game, rhythm game, and a very fun SHMUP with some beautiful spritework. Play through them once, and you can play them again in the hub area. While these are the glowing positives from me, there are definitely a few downsides. The game's visual style can be good sometimes but it has that whole cheap Unreal look to it, where the assets don't exactly match each other and lighting can be very basic at times. Performance was decent but can definitely be better with less stutters in some levels, like the police station and club levels. I know the game was updated recently to have shader caching but I still experienced a few of them here and there. To add one more, the options for the upscalers (TSR, FSR) are not updating the quality level names properly when you select them, and TSR straight up didn't work for me. FSR's quality levels were also reversed for some reason, where Quality was actually Performance, and vice versa. Overall, I'd say these are somewhat minor issues in the whole picture. As someone who picked this up for a meager $7.50 some time after launch, (RM36.00 in my currency, thank you for the generous regional pricing!) it's definitely worth a try at a discount if you want something reminiscent of the 360/PS3 days. Something that's been repeated ad nauseam, I know.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played. A seasoned gamer like myself plays the first playthrough of Witcher 3 on the hardest difficulty, which was ok. I thought this too would be a piece of cake - not so. Extremely steep learning curve, which probably is the reason most people give up on this undiscovered gem. However, once you've - through pain, suffering and grueling traing - reach the point where the game makes sense, it's hard to let it go.I love how it doesn't take itself too seriously, it's really weird at times and for some unexplained reason takes me back to when we as kids played Commodore 64, maybe it's the feeling of not quite knowing what to expect from the game because because back then every game was different, but it was almost always synonymous with a good time.Gameplay is really - unforgiving - is the word. However it's all the more rewarding once you start to master the intricacies of it. It really does give you sence of that "earned" mastery - not the one you get through ingame "XP points" - although there is some unlocking of skills to do as well, but from your training as a player. It rewards you for putting time into it. I love that it has 3 weapon systems integrated into a unified style, leaving you to have some options in terms of killing enemies. It's like a true combat simulator, making you consider the tools you want to use to dispatch enemies who can easily kill you - and make no mistake - every enemy in this game can kill you, so you feel the preasure to do it to them pre-emptively out of a sense of self preservation. I understand that this game is not for everyone. It's for the masters. The connoisseurs. It's for the people who are more into going to the restaurant rather than eating at McDonalds every time they're hungry.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry. I just can't recommend this game to anyone as much as I really wanted to.I really love what this game is really good at. Starting from the design to the mix of gunplay and swordplay. They are fun when they are working.You probably noticed already how I kept on speaking in a double manner. It's because while there are so many things I love about this game, there are also parts that, even if I manage to stomach through, I don't think other people should due to many negative elements such as difficulty spikes without a damn reason, poor story pacing and telling, and worst of all, enemy balance.I can't count how many times I have had to repeat a certain checkpoint over and over because of how messed up the enemy placement and mix-ups are in this game. At one point, you feel like you can breeze through like a slick ninja, then at another, you are struggling with even the most mundane type of enemies piling on you.Conclusion? _childDocuments_.review: At its core, Wanted: Dead is a decent mix of high-speed sword fighting and third-person shooting. It's got some jank, but not enough to ruin the fun.But everything else about the game is either poorly executed, strangely silly, or both. Playing Wanted: Dead is like watching a cross between a self-aware B-movie and a "so bad it's good" movie like The Room (the main character even sounds a bit like Tommy Wiseau), with a solid action game between the moments of unintentional hilarity. I have no idea what the story was about. I cared about none of the characters. The gameplay is admittedly repetitive and occasionally buggy. But somehow, it felt like more than the sum of its parts, and I had a great time.Recommended on sale if you like action games from the PS2 generation and love laughing at bad movies.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted: Dead has garnered its fair share of negative reviews, but personally, I consider the game to be a hidden gem. Once I immersed myself in its flow, the combination of shooting and melee combat proved to be a successful hybrid, offering a satisfying gameplay experience. Hannah's character and the abundance of goofy moments added to the game's charm.What sets Wanted: Dead apart is the inclusion of unique minigames like shmup, claw machine, and karaoke, which contribute an extra layer of enjoyment. In a gaming landscape where such diversions are rare, these additions were a welcome surprise and enhanced the overall experience.However, it's important to note that the game isn't without its quirks. The tone shifts in an unusual manner, the premise and writing exhibit an eccentric quality, and the voice acting is undeniably peculiar. Despite these idiosyncrasies, the exceptional gameplay shines through, serving as a heartfelt homage to the challenging PS2 era games.If you appreciate the nostalgia of old-school challenges and can overlook the game's peculiarities, Wanted: Dead is undoubtedly tailored for you

_childDocuments_.review: I love this piece of ♥♥♥♥ game. To be more specific: this game was clearly not finished so don't buy it at full price, but what it does in its limited time it does better than what most AAA games do in over 50 hours. The writing tries very hard to be cool and it fails miserably. However, it still is funny which makes it charming because of how bad it is, The graphics are like a low detail version of a PS4 game, but never sickening to look at. You can turn off anti aliasing completely and you should because you will almost certainly be able to run it at your monitor's resolution. The music is actually enjoyable, not incredible but fun when it doesn't glitch out.I actually am fine with where the story was going. It doesn't go anywhere meaningful because the game ends before then. But it could have been a decent cyberpunk story; and an actual cyberpunk story that deals with cyberpunk themes instead of just having neon and robots. Ultimately, what this game does incredibly is the action gameplay. It's kind of a culster♥♥♥♥, but it manages to be a really fun cluster♥♥♥♥. And not messy fun; you can actually be good at the game and strategize. Which you will need to do because it is quite hard even on the lowest difficulty. There are parts where they stage will throw 30 enemies at you and it is just really fun and fulfilling to use your mechanics to beat everyone there. It feels insanely hectic but it never feels like noise. It does do the bs where very useful mechanics are locked behind the skill tree but the game loads you up on skill points. They clearly planned for the game to be longer and when the deadline came they decided to just blast skill points at your face. None of the 4 levels felt awful so I assume they scrapped the least complete levels and focused on making the few that were far along good. The one thing that doesn't work is the third-person shooting. It obviously feels like ass on a controller but it is somehow worse on mouse. The aiming on mouse feels like it is snapping to pixels on a very low resolution screen. It's baffling. Thankfully the shooting is kinda pointless. In conclusion, I genuinely want more. I want more stages and more types of enemies and more combos and more weapons and more time with the hilariously bad characters. I hope this gets a sequel and the sequel is decently long.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted Dead is a single player linear action game. If you enjoy games like Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and Metal Gear Rising Revengence you will probably enjoy Wanted Dead.While there are guns you can shoot from the third person perspective, you will likely spend most of your time hacking and slashing with your sword. There is no jump button, so all of the combat is ground-based. There is a basic attack combo, a parry, a dodge, a block (and a timed block), a grenade throw, a finisher move (like Ninja Gaiden II's finishers on dismembers foes), a few extra combos & attacks if you do things like attack after pistol shooting or attack while running, and the guns as mentioned.Wanted Dead is a relatively short game, but it has a lot of replay value, and it has multiple difficulties. So expect to be playing the game multiple times. There are very generous checkpoints throughout the game, so dying won't set you back much.Wanted Dead also has multiple mini-games like timed button presses during ramen eating or karaoke, a shoot-em up arcade game, and a crane game.Positives:- Wanted Dead has skip-able cut-scenes.- Most actions are relatively fast and responsive as you would expect out of an action game. There is potential for animation canceling, but you don't have to use animation canceling to clear Normal mode at least.- I like the main character including the English voice acting. It is that cheesy kind of voice acting we used to see a lot of in games from the early 2000's. I just find Hannah Stone appealing as a protagonist. I do hope we get a Wanted Dead 2 sequel someday.- You get all your healing items and ammo back at each checkpoint.Negatives:- I wish there were more enemy types. You will fight a lot of the same enemies throughout the game.- I wish there wasn't weapon customization or a skill tree and you just had everything unlocked form the start of the game. We don't need unlocks in every single game.- I feel like a few of the animations could have been sped up a bit. Particularly the pistol then sword attack combo feels a bit sluggish, but that might have been intentionally balanced that way.- Some of the guns like the grenade launcher can be hard to use because you can damage yourself and the bullets can easily clip various objects on the map like railing.- Although I like the art style of the game and the character designs, I couldn't really get into the story much. I felt the story was rather weak or at least poorly told.- Most of the maps are indoors and include relatively small hallways and/or a lot of obstructions. This can lead to some jank or annoyance like trying to run kick an enemy but the hitbox/hurtbox doesn't register because the game thinks the enemy is behind something when you just clipped a corner of a pillar by a few inches (your kick should have still landed).All in all, I really like Wanted Dead. It is just fun. Is it the best action game of all time? No. Is it a must play? Probably not. But it is a solid action game.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first started this game it was right after playing Ninja Gaiden 1&2. I thought it was janky as hell. It is janky as hell. The camera easily is the worst part of the game as it constantly got stuck on things causing me to get hit hard with enemy melee which deals a good deal of damage. But…. But….. it’s so dang fun once you get used to it. Your character feels floaty and stiff at the same time which is weird. But dude, shooting guys hitting other guys with a pistol, building that adrenaline meter to do that handgun stun into a chain of executions and parrying those ninjas and killing them back to back feels so satisfying and good to overcome. Now on to the story they literally almost shove everything into the last two levels. Anything of real value builds the last two levels and then the final scene leaves you going what? And wanting to know what is happening. Then it ends. It cliffhangers you. I think for twenty this was a great purchase. I had a ton of fun playing hard mode. I can recommend it if you’re a fan of bizarre action games and amazingly awkward cutscenes and dialogue like Deadly Premonition. I really think this game was slept on for twenty. At twenty dollars it’s easily a 7. Will check out sequel if one is made because with the foundation laid I think a sequel could be much much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Man this game in terms of its design and the world off it are so cool however there is a lot to fix as well in my opinion.I didn't look into this game at all and just bought it during the sale and went for it. Didn't read the description or any reviews. Boy was I surprised to get chopped up during the first level while playing at the normal difficulty. This game is hard and part of that is super fun. The boss fights are insane and take several attempts from me at the least. However part of it feeling hard is also because its a bit janky. For example sometimes you press the attack button and it randomly attacks another character than what was the one in front of you and closest to you which makes it a bit hit an miss from time to time. Sometimes the enemies spam so many grenades that it just becomes annoying because it feels to easy for them to just lob grenades all the time. However despite my gripes with some part of the combat the overall experience is amazing. I freaking love the melee combat and slashing through enemies doesn't grow stale.The gun play is good but nothing special. The gun customization makes no sense whatsoever. For example putting on a longer barrel increases damage but reduces armour penetration... that makes no sense whatsoever. Gun grips/sights also modify gun damage which makes no sense at all. Ignoring the weird customization the shooting is still fun and feels really good.The perks you unlock aren't that major in terms of gameplay but they are okay.The story is good nothing mind blowing but good enough. The characters are okay and the voice acting could use some work but then again I played it in English which isn't its native language. Some of the names of characters are really funny for example the gunsmiths who is Dutch is called: "Vivienne Niemantzverdriet". The last name translates to nobody's sadness and the Z should have been an S but hey pretty cool to see them do a reasonable attempt at foreign names with a splash of humor.  The anime style cutscenes are cool and well made.The mini games in my opinion are fun but I wish they were optional during the story. It must be a cultural thing but within the main story I find them distracting and weird but I get that perhaps in japanese culture these things make more sense.The save system could use some work in my opinion. Outside of combat (so at the main HQ) I wish I could save manually or that it autosaves when you pickup collectibles because currently if you pick up the collectibles and then close the game they have to be obtained again.Some other minor improvement could be to add a delay to what an NPC companion can say during combat because outside from useful stuff like screaming "grenade" they often say the same thing and this becomes a bit annoying.I would love to have more graphics settings options because its a bit lackluster.All in all its a good game and a fun experience and I highly recommend giving it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was HARD sheesh. I consider myself a fairly competent GAMER and I still found the combat tough as nails. But honestly it's so much fun once you get the hang of it, and it's not a super long game so it doesn't really out stay its welcome. And the action is stylish and ludicrously over the top, but on the budget they had clearly limited a lot of technical areas and design - not a huge amount of locales and they aren't that detailed. But that said the art direction in my opinion is really distinct, with so much style that you don't see in Western made games especially. I love Hannah's design especially, her wonky accent, her tattoos, seeing her slice and dice and execute goons and bosses alike was enthralling honestly.There were lots of probably unintentionally comedic moments as well from weird dialogue combined with questionable voice work and animation, a lot of story scenes (and most of the plot) make barely any sense if any at all. But at the end of the day, it's a lot of fun, and you can tell there's a lot of heart put into making this game. All the influences and inspiration you can see the game wear on its sleeve. Oh, and the music throughout absolutely slaps, the nightclub scene especially - wow.Not forgetting this game any time soon.

_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating trainwreck of a game where you can tell the passion is there, but the final result leaves a lot to be desired. That's not to say it isn't a lot of fun though - the combat is a blast, with infrequent checkpoints being the primary frustration point for me, but it never overstayed its welcome and I loved how flashy it was. The story and cutscenes are a incoherent mess, but the direction and flair put into these exudes love and care, even when it's absolutely not firing on all cylinders. It's a game that's honestly hard to hate, but will definitely not be a game many can stand. It's a really irritating game at times to play, but honestly, you can tell it was in some way a deliberate choice, and I'm for it. It's a strange oddity - and we don't get these kind of games very often!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh what a shame! Such a nice combat setup with a great feel at times. A real John Wick gun-fu vibe running through this game that really should be taken into a better game. The balance is all over just a bit off, I'd like some off camera indications for unseen approaching enemies for a start with a game that wants you to get in and personal.  Boss strategies feel like more luck than judgement at times even if there is a clear strategy for beating them.  Overall the build just feels like ps3 / 360 era like pretty much everyone has said but it does have an odd charm that makes me want to like this game.  I bought it for half price in sale and don't feel aggrieved but would find it hard to recommend to anyone as its 50 percent good vs 50 percent annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: A hack n slash 3P shooter hybrid in the veins of Xbox + PS2 era games like Ninja Gaiden and DMC3. I have an affinity for this style game given my time with such games. So even though I didn't know about this game's until after it's release, I found myself oddly drawn to it. The game is clunky, unpolished, rough around the edges, the voice acting sounds like a bad foreign film dub from the early 2000s. But all that mixed with fairly smooth, intuitive and pretty satisfying gameplay makes for a oddly charming game. You play as Hanna Stone, a Hong Kong detective with a obscured past. You play through various stages cutting and shooting down waves of opposing soldiers, gangsters, androids, ninjas. You are accompanied by three AI controlled teammates all with their own abilities who assist Hanna in combat. There is also a fair bit more here than what I expected in the form of a hub area and a handful of minigames. I suppose one of the things missing (at least that I have yet to see) is chapter select and alternate outfits, which you would usually get in games like this for completing the game's campaign on various difficulties. Wanted Dead unfortunately crashes fairly often and is a game that requires a particular taste from the player to be enjoyed. The base price is high for what it is, but at 30% off, its pretty fair for whats on offer.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game. It makes you hate it enough initially to eventually make you fall for it, so mushy right, the game, however, is anything but. I hated August in May, but now it feels like spring as I gear up to start my JH mode run; this game has mini-games, it has quirkiness that is unique only to Japanese games but it has courage and it is the first time in a long time that I feel like upping the difficulty progressively and growing into the game over time than all at once,

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying objectively this game is a hard C. Not C- not C+, just a C. I personally love it, but It could very easily become a B with some quality of life improvements and basic staples of other games of its type:-The biggest thing holding this game back is the lack of a dedicated lock-on for melee combat and the forced snapping to enemies during combat.  This change alone would make it a C+.-Guns feel kinda useless because the enemies drink up bullets like they're trying to cure an iron deficiency, and they just don't stagger when shot.-Checkpoint system and restart locations need to get worked on as well, nothing more annoying than spending 5-7 mins clearing through an area only to get one-shotted and have to start that 5-7 minute section all over again.Past these not-so-minor frustrations lies an interesting hack and slash/3rd person shooter with some pretty bad-ass finishing animations and a fast-paced combat system that looks a bit like Sekiro had a baby with MGS5 and Killer is Dead. I would recommend this game to Suda-51 fans and old-school hack and slash fans, but if you're looking for a Triple-A game of the year experience, keep on pushing, you'll find happiness someday.

name: Blanc
detailed_description: Experience the poetic tale of a wolf cub and a fawn in the spectacular world of Blanc. Lost in a sudden snowstorm, they will have to lean on each other in order to follow the footprints their families left behind in the snow. Immerse yourself in the stunningly beautiful black-and-white world of Blanc – completely hand-drawn on paper in 2D before coming to life in 3D. Blanc focuses on the journey and experience of the animals with text-free gameplay and storytelling, allowing players to dive completely into its wondrous world. Each animal has their own unique strengths that complements the other, which you’ll need to make use of to navigate through the snowy landscapes. Using only two buttons and movement, this simple gameplay allows for anyone to play and follow their journey home. Two players take control of either the wolf cub or the fawn. Guide them through the environment, unforgiving weather, and obstacles that you must face together. Build a relationship together locally on the same screen or from far away with online play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential. The atmosphere is great, the graphics have style, and the sound design is phenomenal. I like the character design, the animals look really cute. Congrats on that. My issue is the gameplay is severely lacking. There's no "Puzzles". It's not like you have to figure anything out. It's literally just look where to do the next animation to continue. The story wasn't exactly a story. The goose escort gameplay was tedious, the "The goats are just like you" isn't new gameplay, it's just mirroring your gameplay in a more clunky way, then that gimmick comes up again directly after that same section. The sliding is very fun, the highlight of the game was the sliding section. My issue with it tho is there's almost no obstacles, it's not challenging in ANY way. This game is basically a walking sim with a subpar story. It's dripping in atmosphere though. I will be looking forward to another game by this dev if it looks more dynamic with more things to do. Please keep making games tho, this has so much potential and I don't want to see a good creative get discouraged. The game just needs more to do.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a very pleasant surprise for me. A warning first: The game is very short, in my case it was 3 hours for the first playthrough. Still it was a wonderful experience as a game and as a bonding session with my kid. This is a cooperative game. I played it with my 6 year old daughter, who only played a few touch screen based games before. She was able to use a gamepad to play through the whole game with me, without too much trouble. We used local multiplayer and I haven't tried the online functionality.You control two unlikely companions on their journey to reunite with their families. That's about it for the story, but the game does a wonderful job presenting you with real looking places, realistic problems, character development, unexpected encounters and more. It fully utilizes the "show, don't tell" storytelling approach. Almost all of it is done strictly with sound and visuals. The protagonists are wonderfully animated. There are lots of tiny animations that make the characters lifelike and also convey the emotions they are feeling at any given time. The characters also interact with each other and with the environment.I was very impressed with the game design. The visual cues and the well paced introductions of new mechanics made sure, that we always knew what to do next. We only got stuck for a little while in one of the final scenes of the game, your results may vary of course. My daughter was playing the wolf, which I would recommend for the first playthrough, because the wolf often needs help from the deer to be able to continue and it could save some potential frustration, when waiting for the deer to get to the right place. There are also some puzzles that require help from the wolf for the deer to proceed, but those are much more rare.The sound design is great. Next to realistic soundscapes, the sound cues and from time to time utilized musical pieces fit the mood of each scene perfectly. You only ever encounter animals in this game and they all sound realistic and at times delightful.We didn't encounter any technical problems., except it initially wanted to be played with the steering wheel that was connected when I first started the game. That was easily solved by disconnecting the steering wheel, even though there might be more elegant solutions. The game run smoothly and looked great otherwise. The only real critique I have for this game is the camera. While it is very impressive in its ability to keep both characters on the screen at all times, sometimes it fails at doing that. There are a few big setpieces and also some cases, where the camera turns to present the scene from a different angle at a certain point. There we had a few occasions where one of the characters ended up either being off screen or hidden behind the scenery (you can see its silouette still). When it happened it wasn't immediately clear, how to get both of us back into view. Just a side effect of a game that lets both characters move pretty far away from each other at any given time.In conclusion, this is a short, but very beautiful game. Get it if you want a heartfelt story, some light puzzles and an opportunity to bond with whomever you play this with.

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute and adorable game! _childDocuments_.review: I wish I could check a middle ground for the rating. I received this as a gift to play along side my wife, but dear god... I could use my teeth to bite through obstacles and he could jump so high and even helped me get to high places! We saw many beautiful and dangerous things on our way and had fun and sad encounters. But we never gave up hope. We knew our families were out there, somewhere. We knew we would find our way home.
