_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like Blanc, but unfortunately, there were too many technical issues to fully enjoy it. The 3D characters, environments and general art direction are all beautiful, and the out-of-the-box ultrawide support and unlocked frame rate allowed me to fully appreciate it, the character animations are great, but have some severe technical flaws, with characters frequently jittering between animations and moving though solid matter. I played the game with an friend online and the game doesn't have a very good lag-smoothing system, which is okay for a small budget game, but it contributed a lot to the clipping and animation issues.The game didn't have very many hard-thinking puzzles, but there were lots of interesting scenarios that kept things fresh. Blanc keeps it short, which is a good approach for a multiplayer game! I never got bored while playing since there was always something new to see. Unfortunately, The game's story was a little uninteresting, and the ending was I also quite liked the music in the game. It's dynamic and reacts to situations and progress, which is amazing to see! Unfortunately, at one point, there were multiple different tracks playing at the same time, at clashing tempos, which sounded... horrible.I think Blanc could be a cute, short little game if all of these issues are patched out, and it seems the developers feel the same, they've been slowly patching major bugs and crashes. Maybe in the future, this'll be a perfect, short little experience to share with a friend. At least, I hope so.

_childDocuments_.review: Like everyone else is saying... Game is pretty and the idea is cute but the controls and the bugs are just frustrating to no end. Maybe it needed more time and testing. We thought it was cute otherwise. I would recommend it to someone if it was cheaper
_childDocuments_.name: Blanc

_childDocuments_.review: In summary a cute game with nice art style but lacks the depth I was expecting and was buggy at times.PROS : Enjoyable coop with an easy to understand premise. Approachable for all levels of gamer which makes it a perfect game for couples. The art style, despite some criticism, is very well done when the detail and effort is put in, and definitely a selling point to those who enjoy artistic games. I did find myself very worried about one of the animals which does speak to the games ability to attach you emotionally to characters in a simple and quick manner.CONS : At times the art style was lacking. There were wide open spaces of white made it hard to navigate. I noticed this particularly in the second half of the game. I was open to interpretation as a method of story telling but it seemed to clash with the story tbh. The camera would also clip through the environment and was very awkwardly placed at times. I found at times there were bugs I think that originated from playing online coop. Sometimes characters would get stuck when there were four on the screen. Despite having good connection my coop partners character's movement was not always smooth and it was particularly bad during interactions. I also did find the second half to be repetitive, doing the same things over. The emotional tug of a character in peril was also an exact copy and made both times seem cheap.Overall, it's 50/50 if you like this game. If you are looking for a simple and fun puzzle game with cutesy art style then look no further. But if you want a longer coop game that offers a more polished experience there are better options out there at a similar price point.I can't recommend because I did refund and I don't feel that this game was what I was looking for at this price.

_childDocuments_.review: Here is my personal experience of this game!--------------------------Bugs:There are many game breaking bugs that occurred that caused us to have to reset numerous times such as game mechanics not working when it came to movement, the screen freezing on one end but not the other, etc. Whenever we would reset the game, we had trouble reconnecting again because of the invite system being janky. Invitations had to be spammed over and over for +5 minutes until one 'lucky' invite allowed us to reconnect.Gameplay:The movement for this game feels off because of the camera angles being awfully placed, even during dramatic scenes.If you wanted to change to WASD controls instead of the default arrow keys, (and it said that the controls had been applied) it would still be stuck at arrow key controls. For the game play itself, there was an incredibly tedious and slow escort mission.The area box to escort said creature was small and hard to control added on with the bad camera angles.There was also an "AI mirrors your move" mission and the AI wouldn't mirror you/move at all most of the time despite being in range of it. Music and Art: The soundtrack is great! It really adds to the vibe of every scene that plays out and the orchestral music is really beautiful!The art is the reason why we originally decided to get this game and the use of the monotone color palettes were done incredibly well. The scenery is drawn perfectly and the character animations were adorable.Story/lore:The story is very simple, very short, and wholesome! Nothing more and nothing less. --------------------------Conclusion:I enjoyed the game but I really do not think that it's worth the price it's at currently.The story is good, yes, and it was a generally wholesome experience, but it's not really worth it because of how short and buggy the game currently is. Even if the bugs were fixed along with the very off-putting camera angles and the inability to change your controls, I'd still say it's only worth if it was on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. If I paid full price (15€) for this game I would be extremely mad, because you can play through the game in less than 2 hours. It is NO WHERE stated on the store page OR ANYWHERE else that you need to install Epic Online Services in order to play the game online with your friend. I don't want this third party garbage on my PC. 3. Epic Online Services is extremely primitive with it's online play, you often see your partner stuttering, rubber banding all over the place or disconnecting from the game which is extremely annoying.4. The movement mechanics are extremely janky and primitive, often the game does mid game not recognize your controller or keyboard and you have to restart the game in order to fix it.5. _childDocuments_.review: Full Review: Blanc is a beautiful game with a wonderful heartwarming story. I played it alone, since my co-op partner was not available. But with controller this worked pretty well. The price might be a bit high for a game with roughly 2 hours of playtime, but if you can get it on sale it's definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Blanc is a unique and captivating game that tells its story through the actions of two animals that you control. Despite the game's black and white color scheme and lack of dialogue, it manages to convey a powerful emotional narrative that is sure to leave a lasting impression on you.The puzzles in Blanc are cleverly designed, and while they are a bit too easy for the most part, they are well-integrated into the story. You control the two animals, using their abilities to solve puzzles and progress through the game. The controls are intuitive and easy to learn, allowing you to focus on the puzzles and the story.One of the most impressive aspects of Blanc is the way it manages to convey emotion through its minimalist art style. The animations are incredibly expressive, and the sound design is excellent. There are sad moments in the game when other animals are in danger, and these moments are particularly heart-wrenching. I found myself feeling genuinely concerned for the animals and invested in their fate.Despite the game's easy puzzles, the experience of playing Blanc is still incredibly satisfying. The game's unique art style and emotionally impactful narrative make it a standout experience that is well worth playing. If you're looking for a game that will leave you with a sense of wonder and a strong emotional connection, Blanc is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Blanc

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cute. Not very difficult,  not very long, but charming. I like the visuals! If you like animals, you might like this game. It's a little journey with two animals. You help each other so you can travel together and maybe find your own kin?We played offline with two controllers. We had no issues, the game worked perfectly
_childDocuments_.name: Blanc

_childDocuments_.review: Blanc is a very cute, minimalist art style game about a Wolf pup and a Fawn becoming unlikely friends to help each other reach their respective families they've become separated from following a big storm.The style is extremely cute and the sound design was really good. Unfortunately, Blanc suffers from a few big glaring issues that make me not want to recommend the game at full price.The game is short. Very, very short. It takes less than 2 hrs to beat he game. 4 if you want to go for all achievements (as one requires you to play through the game twice). The puzzles are virtually non-existent, it's mostly just following the logical path forwards with the 2 abilities you have as each character, jump and grab.The duckling section really puts a hamper on the game if you're playing online co-op. The smallest desync would cause the mechanics for the section to be very difficult to navigate.The Goat section is also pretty janky, in that they don't always do exactly what you do, or they do it to a fault and it kinda breaks a little.Overall, the game is really cute and fun, but for $15 it's a bit of a high asking price. Pick the game up on sale for $5 and you'll not regret it. Just give them a bit of time to polish up the few bugs and you've got a fun little couples game to play.Full disclosure I was gifted the game by a friend for us to play together.

_childDocuments_.review: How did this game get made. did no one play this as they were developing it? at what point did they realise they forgot to put anything fun in here and go ''♥♥♥♥ it lets ship it anyways''.Blanc is a game that prioritises style over substance, but to such an extent that all it has is style and there is literally no substance. first off the game is an hour and a half long, so not worth the money in the slightest if you're considering entertainment to cost ratio, there's also no reason to replay the game with the characters swapped, they play exactly the same except one can jump slightly higher (which doesn't matter because you can just give the shorter fella a leg up). so already this game is a bad time investment.is it fun to play? nope nopety nope nope, all the puzzles last about 2 seconds and feel like they are designed with lobotomised toddlers in mind. not to mention the art style is so muddy and platforms so close to each other you are just blindly spamming jump through half the puzzles, and it works. are the characters at least fun to control? also nope, some of the worst feeling movement in a video game.is the music good... nope, but its not bad, its very serviceable, but in a game where all it has going for it is the atmosphere they should've done a lot better.How in the world did they manage to make an hour and a half feel like 5 hours, i legit thought i played for like 5 hours. its booooring.Why doesn't the wolf eat the deer? that's a pretty important question i think. why doesn't the wolf eat the ducklings or the goats, idfk.This game has so little going for it, i wouldn't have played it for free knowing what i know now. i have played so many co-op games with my partner, this torpedoed its way straight down to the bottom of that list. this is a puzzle game with no puzzles, a story game with a very bare and artificial story, an atmospheric game with a mediocre soundtrack and art style, why does it exist? seriously why?

_childDocuments_.review: Blanc is a cooperative adventure game developed by Casus Ludi and published by Gearbox Publishing. Released in early 2023, Blanc takes the unique approach to co-operative gameplay where it is required all the time and there is no single-player component.TL;DR - Short and sweet cooperative experience teeming with monochromatic atmosphere and emotion.Story (4/5) - Blanc tells the tale of a young wolf cub and fawn as the unlikely duo work together to find their way back after being separated from their respective packs.Gameplay (4/5) - Together with your co-op partner, you will be solving increasingly complex puzzles along this roughly 2 hour journey.Controls (3/5) - With support for controllers or keyboard and mouse, the game's controls are intuitive albeit not as sharp and snappy as I would normally like. Graphics (4/5) - Blanc has a unique monochromatic cel-shaded visual style that evokes a hand-drawn comic book style that's a real treat for the eyes.Audio (4/5) - Strong art isn't let down by equally strong audio which really helps to enhance the atmosphere of Blanc's snowstorm.Optimisation/Bugs - No noteworthy bugs or crashes. Net code works well for online co-operative play.Overall (4/5) - A short and lovely indie title that is as much about its visual presentation then its storytelling. A wonderful delight that's worth finding a buddy to enjoy it with.

_childDocuments_.review: Blanc is a short but cute game, something that is definitely worth playing through with your partner or loved one.The entirety of Blanc centers around two characters, a white Fawn and a black wolf pup, who are trying to reunite with their respective families and help each other along the way to that goal.This paired along with some nice sound design, an appealing art-style and some gorgeous level designs make this a nice addition to your Steam LibraryBlanc is an overall low requirement game stemming from it's size and graphics/ art.This doesn't however mean that Blanc doesn't have it's problems.Blanc offers from specific framerate limitations, not in terms of overall performance but more towards your partner playing with you. Blanc will lower the framerate of characters be it player or NPC alike when it thinks you are not looking at their model. This is a widely used technique to lower the processing power needed for your game, many refer to this as a form of Culling.The problem however is that more often than not the game will lower this animation framerate despite the player/ NPC being in full view of the camera resulting in your partner looking rather choppy, This isn't some gamebreaking performance and they will resume proper framerate when coming closer to the character but it can be rather disorienting in some locations.Blanc makes use of a very limited art-style. This gives it a distinct feeling of being drawn or painted but does fail to do this from time to time.I'm not sure if Casus Ludi meant to make some parts look highly Three Dimensional or if it's a limit of the game/ shader itself but it loses it's intended look sometimes in close ups or in some particle heavy locations.Overall however Blanc looks appealing and the characters look as cute as they can be.The story of Blanc isn't all that big.Lose your family, try to get back to your family and meet some friends along the way.This is however by no means meant to be a criticism of the game's story itself, some other games I enjoy just as much use the same no talking and explain the minimum required story.It is very similar to something like Journey for example These games make great use of a minimalist style of storytelling to make you look around the levels itself and get the full enjoyment out of themThe sound design of Blanc is rather basic but gets the point across.The music however is beautifully crafted and tailored to everything to the T.Blanc's gameplay is basic but functional, it doesn't do anything super nuanced but it does work well enough to get you through the game without much issue.There is however still an issue, jumping is rather precise. Not in the sense of needing to perfectly point your character somewhere or your jump to your doom, Blanc uses a pointing system much like Stray does where your character will look at where they can jump and a small indicator will pop up on the obstacle you will jump on. This selecting however is rather precise, I have jumped down from something while I was trying to jump up to something more than I can count.This won't hinder your play too much but it can get rather annoying in some locations.Blanc was a game well worth the money for it's charm, enjoyment and overall cuteness.With a fitting soundtrack, a pleasing art-style and enjoyable gameplay Blanc will give you a nice experience to add to your Steam Library and playtime together.Enjoy

_childDocuments_.review: Blanc is an interesting game that just came out on Windows and Nintendo Switch. Play as both a baby wolf and baby deer as they find their ways back home and become friends along the way. Gameplay wise you can either play this by yourself, or with a friend. The game recommends you play with a controller and I also recommend you play with one too, as the keyboard controls are pretty poor, they can be changed but it's not an easy task to do so. There is also an online play mode, but that is only to play with a friend online. You need to have a friend on your friend list who owns the game in order to invite them to your match. You cannot pair up with random players it looks like. So I was left with only one option and that was to play it on my own. So this first impression is from that perspective. In order to play this on my own on the controller I just had to pick the 1 controller option before beginning the game. Once you begin the game the left joystick and the left button and trigger would control the wolf, and the right joystick and right button and trigger would control the deer. This was, for the most part not that hard to control, though I did get things muddled up a few times. But I found if you just took turns in certain situations with the left and right side of the controller, it wasn't too hard to navigate the game. The puzzles are pretty light on the difficulty, and as is expected of a 2 player co-op experience, the 2 animals are meant to help one another to solve them. Some situations will require the deer and others the wolf, and sometimes both of them combined. There is no dialogue in this game, but the story is still well told through the actions of the game and the interactions between the deer and wolf during the short cinematics. The game is absolutely adorable though it is a shame it is quite short. According to the steam reviews, people are able to complete the game in under 2 hours, which for a game that costs 14.99USD is a bit underwhelming if you ask me. It could have been a bit cheaper for a game that can be completed in under 2 hours play time. Visually the game is very unique. Going for this 3D artistic book sketch style of visual art work that really was very gorgeous. It was simple and yet still able to portray a gorgeous snowy environment. The game runs really well, and I was always in the 200fps+ area while playing it. While it's not the most demanding visual game I've played, it's definitely one of the more unique ones, that's for sure. Overall I'd say that Blanc is a fantastic co-op 2 player game that can be played on your own, but if you want the maximum as intended experience, you should definitely try to play this with a friend. While the 14.99USD price tag may be a bit steep for a 2 hour game, it's still a pretty great game to play if you have someone to play with. I wouldn't recommend playing it on your own like I did though, it really ruins the experience if you ask me. So if you have a friend who loves to play games and would like to play a great 2 player game, I highly recommend this one to you both. And, better make sure you both have a controller to play with. Because I do NOT recommend playing this on keyboard.TL:DR: Fun but short game, but make sure you have a CONTROLLER and a FRIEND who has a CONTROLLER too. Don't Play this on keyboard.

It's not so horrible that you will truly regret the 2.5 hours you spend on it.There's the emotional side (honestly, I only felt any emotion at credits, but I guess that's because I already knew about the cheap "he's dead but not really" garbage). We had to restart the game twice (in 2.5 hours, remember). I played the deer, and trying to push things was awful - until the end I could not figure out how exactly I was supposed to press it (game never explains).I would say to get it for your kid, except some "puzzles" are too convoluted (e.g. you have a few things to interact with, but the actual thing you need to do is to just go left to the edge of the map) and the controls are quite bad.Not the worst idea in the world, bad execution, not for adults, not for kids, just get something else.PS. The soundtrack is "your first piano lesson". Just playing some notes. I am sure they thought it was "light and non-intrusive, perfectly completing the masterful work of art that is the game".

_childDocuments_.review: My wife and I love a good co-op game, we try to finish everyone we start. After finishing Blanc, we both can safely say the only reason we are recommending it is because we got it on sale!We went against the games suggestions and played on keyboard, so it was safe to say the controls were odd and clunky. The story was told mostly through a lot of jumping, walking, pushing, or biting stuff. It's emotional in the same way a sparkling water is  fruity. The camera angles are weird and its laggy at times.On the plus side, it's short and simple to play, with just six buttons to learn. The music is lovely and pairs well with the mood of each chapter. Honestly, it's just a really chill, cute, linear puzzle game. It just seems like it promises more than it delivers. If you have 8 bucks to spend when the game is on sale, go for it!

_childDocuments_.name: Blanc

_childDocuments_.review: After playing games like A way out, Portal 2, all of We were here, It takes Two and stuff like this with my wife, this game feels a bit unfinished. Let me say it like this: art style is fabulous, both of us are artists and seeing the hand crafted world drawn by pencil was fantastic. BUT it had no real story, chapters felt insignificant (like out of 10 chapters 3 of them had small plot-wist which was fun) and the camera was very confusing and not enjoyable. Maybe a split screen with more freedom would feel way much better. Also probably our biggest mistake was playing it with keyboard. This game was meant to be played with controller (it also says that when you launch the game). We played it on PC and controls were 50% of my frustration with this game. But still, it is a nice game for two and if it is on sale, we recommend :)PS: We would love to see more development into the game like hidden activities across the map, collectibles, silly encounters, work on the camera movement etc.. It has a big potential to be a "close to heart" game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blanc

_childDocuments_.review: Blanc is a visually captivating game, despite its monochrome palette. The black and white aesthetic is surprisingly beautiful and adds a unique, immersive ambiance to the gameplay experience.The game is designed to be played by two people, offering a wonderful opportunity to spend quality time with a friend or partner. Cooperation is at the heart of Blanc, and its simple gameplay means there's no need to get frustrated if one player is less skilled.It isn't very complicated, making it accessible to players of all skill levels. However, achieving all the in-game achievements can be slightly more challenging but is doable and relatively quick for those looking to complete everything.We encountered a few bugs while playing, requiring us to restart the game several times. Despite these interruptions, the game remained fun and enjoyable. These technical issues didn't manage to ruin our overall experience.It would be great if the game offered a solo play option for those who prefer to play alone or don't always have a gaming partner available. This could broaden the game's appeal to a wider audience.
_childDocuments_.name: Blanc

_childDocuments_.review: (I would recommend purchasing this game when it's on sale as I do not think it would be worth it at it's regular pricing) I loved this game, I thought it was so fun getting to play with my friend in a game where you must work hand in hand with another player. You'll spend anywhere from 1-2 hours to complete the game, you're met with multiple minor challenges, you get small cut scenes showing the story line (these can be skipped) and it has you not only interacting with the other player but NPC's in the game as well. If you're looking for a small, cute, cozy game to play with a friend this is a good one. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Some quick pros and cons about this game.Pro: Beautiful artstyle and music, cute character designs and great atmospheric environmenets. There is also some meta sound design, where the music will swell up, when you get into a snow storm.Cons:Lot's of recurring bugs and crashes, which force you to go back to the main menu and restart the game session or even the game. You also need to install some Epic Game Store software, because apparently this game doesn't run peer to peer, but from some poorly running Epic Server (see the bugs and crashes mentioned above).Also as other mentioned the game is rather short.I give this one, for the sake of the developers, a thumbs up, but please  patch the game and test your next game at least a bit more before putting it on a store.I'd recommend one person buying this game and then play it locally via steam remote-play-together to avoid the server issues mentioned above.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so beautiful! _childDocuments_.name: Blanc

_childDocuments_.review: Blanc is a slow and cute game with great potential. However, in its current release, it's not much more than a tech demo/concept that would need an awful lot of polishing to make it worthwhile playing. The art and animations are great and are a class above the rest of the game. Looks can be deceiving sadly though...The game is let down by the pacing of the story (shows no evidence of thoughtful targeting/capture of audience) as well as frustrating level design (What is an object that the player can interact with? Where's the edge of the map? Which way is "forwards", etc.), sub-standard jump/action mechanics and physics and other subtly annoying bugs (camera auto-management).Lastly, the game is very, very short (I'm more than half way "done" and am giving up...) and is not worth its current price, not even on a sale.I believe that there is great potential here for a sequel or a re-release and I'm very much looking forward to playing the future games of the developers. A near-miss.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend if you want something emotional that can be completed in a single sitting. It took me and my friend about 2 hours to complete, maybe a little less. The graphics are simple and clean but look deliberately designed, I believe the textures were created by hand and painted into the environment. The puzzles are appropriately challenging for this style of game. Our favorite chapter was 6, and I won't say why because no spoilers, but it's the cutest little mechanic in the game. The game overall does a great job of teaching you how to gradually use and build on the different abilities of the two characters to solve the puzzles and I think the responsibilities for each player are balanced. The only downside was that there were some issues with button remapping and playing online coop, some server issues that caused disconnections. Not sure if that is a localized issue between me and my friend since we live in different parts of the US, but it didn't hinder our progress too terribly and we were able to overcome it by restarting the game. I would also warn that the camera angle can get a little funky if you try to stray to far from each other, so be cautious of that.Overall, 9/10 game, absolutely loved experiencing this!

_childDocuments_.review: Blanc is a beautifully drawn story with a 'The Fox and The Hound' foundation.While the game is graphically and musically beautifully however it falters in it's speed, puzzles, camera and price.Pro's:-The visual world is beautiful consisting of only black and white and the ability to identify what everything is distinct so you very rarely get confused as to what you're looking at.-The story is heart meltingly sweet despite the fact there is no dialogue, text or even narration. You can fully understand what is happening through the use of the body language and visual cues.-The music is my favourite part of this game. Every song feels purposeful and delivers a beautiful nuance to what you are seeing on the screen.Con's:-The puzzles did not feel like puzzle but instead where do I go to next or what is the game showing I should do so you very rarely have to think.-The camera can be difficult to work with, you have on control over the camera and if the characters are seperated you will easily be able to take control of one character while the other has more guesswork which can be frustrating.-The pacing of the game is quick, spanning only ten chapters like with each chapter lasting approx. 10 minutes long.-The price is very expensive for the quantity of work, while the quality feels as though it far exceeds my inital expectations, the game being less than 2 hours had me a little disappointed.-Playing this game in multiplayer online requires you to purchase the game twice which makes the pricing even worse with no remote play support (however using a programme like Parsec moves around this problem)Ultimately, I do wish to give this game the thumbs up despite my cons outweighing my pros as I wish the company can make a beautiful game like this again taking all of this advice in stride and hopefully improving where I believe they have failed.

name: Dungeons of Hinterberg
detailed_description: New Game + is now available! You can play through the game from the start, while keeping your last playthrough's inventory, player stats, and most of the perks that you received from relationship level-ups! In addition, you can choose to either keep your past relationship progress or to reset it. Welcome to Hinterberg, a new tourist hotspot in the idyllic Austrian Alps! You play as Luisa, a burnt-out law trainee taking a break from her fast-paced corporate life to conquer the Dungeons of Hinterberg. There are plenty of dungeons to find and adventures to be had in Hinterberg – will Luisa be sent packing on her first day, or remain to become a Master Slayer? Only one way to find out… Snowboard down a glacier, zipline through the forest, climb a mountain, or have a coffee by the lake... There’s no shortage of places to discover while you’re out looking for your next dungeon! Monsters lurk around every corner in Hinterberg, and your sword and magic skills are essential for keeping them at bay. Harness the wind, conjure a snowboard out of thin air, or freeze your enemies in a jelly block! Braving a dungeon requires more than just cutting-edge sports gear and a good sword arm: Hinterberg’s dungeons are full of puzzles that will surprise and challenge you. Use your head, your magic skills, and every trick in the book to solve them! Spend your nights forging friendships with the locals and other adventurers! Some of them will help you get stronger or teach you new tricks, others are just here for excitement and selfies... But good relationships don't just make your stay more memorable - they're the key to becoming a better slayer!

_childDocuments_.review: Really early on, I thought this wouldn't be fun. I was worried that the social interactions would be stupidly trivial and wasn't sure I could cope with the art style. Fairly quickly I fell into the groove and found the game cozy, comforting, and refreshing. I fell in love with the art style. And I discovered that, as the social interactions advanced, most player dialog got meaningful - struggling with real life issues (sometimes in humorous ways). Especially the inner monologue of the main character, working through her issues. The dungeons are grouped into four separate areas with different geography, season, and feel. It felt like you were visiting four different places in the world. The thing I found interesting was that each area had its own set of two magic spells you could use, unique to that area and only functional in that area. The spells were useful in both combat and puzzle solving. Each area's different terrain showed up in the dungeons there. These things (different area feel, different dungeon terrain, and different spells) kept things from being boring or repetitive as you work through all the dungeons.The dungeon mechanics seemed to be an actual 50/50 balance between combat and puzzles. And, when set on Vacation (easy) mode, was well tuned to me. (I like a little combat but nothing that actually costs me something or causes my frequent death. I prefer story, exploration, and puzzles.) I found the puzzles frequently challenging but almost always something I could figure out. (I think I only Googled an explanation once.) I'm not a serious gamer (combat or puzzles), so perhaps this game will feel trivial for others. But I'd hope that the cozy, comforting-ness of it would still shine for those who value that. Bottom line is I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: Going on a vacation to slay monsters and solve puzzles in dungeons, never was that much fun! I <3 this game! It has some missable achievements. However, if you're aware of them it is easy to make sure you don't miss them. ~25h to completion. 25 hours 2/10 1 I wrote  and . I wish I had also kept track of where I found the coins but I didn't :(  No Yes, the coin in the beginner's dungeon is missable, finishing a new dungeon while being tired and you can't go back into the dungeons after you finished the last one when only using autosave. so make a manual save before attempting/finishing the last dungeon.  No No No No No No you can play on easy and still unlock every achievement NoSometimes you just fall in love at the beginning of a game just with the concept alone already, this game did that for me. Before starting to play Dungeons of Hinterberg I liked the idea and wasn't blown away by the artwork while I enjoy that it is a different style than we see a lot. However, after the first dungeon, I was already head over heels in love while that dungeon was short, straightforward, and easy. I could see already the potential and how smooth the controls of the game were. How good it felt and a peek into the people you'll meet during this journey. And the artwork grew on me while playing through the story. It includes so many details and is so well made.In Dungeons of Hinterberg, you're on holiday in Hinterberg. Where in other small towns/villages in Austria it might be normal to have winter sports activities while on vacation, Hinterberg is special... in Hinterberg you learn how to use magic and complete dungeons during your vacation. However, it still is a vacation so you can also just take the day off and enjoy a scenic spot and during the evenings you'll meet with all kinds of different people. And all those things will help you out with getting stronger. Yes, even taking the day off helps you out! This game reminds me of the "Persona" series combined with "Phantasy Star Online Episode I & II". The interactions and hangouts you have with the people feel like the social part of the Persona games. With bonus points for not having X amount of in-game time before the world gets destroyed. You can keep going as long as you don't finish the last dungeon. And the style of the dungeons reminded me somehow of Phantasy Star Online. In Dungeons of Hinterberg, there are 16 "people" you can get to know better and hang out with. Increasing your friendship level will get you rewards, but the people were so well-written that it was fun as well. I didn't like everyone, but when getting to know them better I understood where they came from. And it is awesome that there is such a range of personalities. The quiet ones, the social butterflies, the loud ones, the cheesy ones. You will find so many different people in Hinterberg, but all with a story attached to them. For the achievements you don't have to max out their friendships, which would mean that normally I wouldn't even go for that. However, I finished almost all of them just to get to know them. I think I spent around 5 extra hours, just to finish most of the friendship levels. There are 26 Dungeons in Dungeons of Hinterberg. What I enjoyed so much about them is that they weren't too long, you'll not spend hours going through the same dungeon, while also being different from each other. The dungeons are scattered over 4 areas in the game and in each area you get 2 skills and only those 2 skills. This made sure that the dungeons weren't too complex. It has puzzles but you also know that the solution has to be done with one or both of those skills. The first time I got new skills it took a bit of time to get used to them, but it works so well and you always know that one of them has something to do with range. Another nice thing is everything you do will improve your stats, even relaxing at the spa will in the end help you get stronger so you can get through the dungeons. This way you don't feel like spending useless time doing something and you can just strategize what is more important to go for at the moment. The rewards from leveling up your friendship levels are so nice as well. I love how many quality of Life features Dungeons of Hinterberg has. Think about having teleport spots all over the map, so you never have to walk that far after you explore the place the first time. Also seeing chests on the map you found but couldn't open because not having the key yet is awesome, so you don't forget them as long as you have interacted with the chest. Another welcome feature is that you can speed up the animation of entering a zone or the switch between afternoon to evening, evening to night ect. And last but not least as it is huge, the game warns you of so many things. "Do you want to spend time with this person, that will take the whole evening" aka "Have you done your shopping before you chose this option" and other warnings like that. After finishing the story you get the chance to say goodbye to everybody, and this was such a nice feature. I cried so hard during this because it felt really like saying goodbye to them as you learn to know them quite a lot. It was so bittersweet as I was glad happy with the ending and happy to play through this game, but that also meant saying goodbye. They did a great job with how to even include that in your Slaycation. However, there were possible hints as to where the story could go next... so hopefully at some point, we will join up with the main character and go on slaycation in another city! I give Dungeons of Hinterberg 5 out of 5 stars. Yes, I'm in love with this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons of Hinterberg is a fresh and addictive take on dungeon crawling with a healthy dose of puzzles and combat broken up with a carefree romp around the beautiful village of Hinterberg making friends and alliances which will help you with your slaying. The game loop is pretty much the same over and over but somehow, I didn't feel like it was repetitive because there are tactical decisions you need to make and the narrative kicks in once in a while to stir things up and pique your interest once more. By the end of the game, I was desperate to see how it all ended and I wasn't disappointed. During the day Luisa chooses one of the twenty-five dungeons to complete, and in the evenings, Luisa mingles with the inhabitants of the village. She learns of their lives and reasons for being in Hinterberg and helps them solve quests in exchange for perks and items which will upskill her and let her take on more dangerous dungeons.The story was surprisingly well done and gradually revealed itself in-between doses of dungeon crawling. It was a welcome break from the cycle of dungeon crawling then socializing, which happened every day, and it lifted you up when needed and encouraged you to continue. There are also new story elements produced from talking to the twelve or so characters you will meet and their lives are entwined into the story too.Getting to know these characters was a lot of fun and I wasn't expecting the game to have such good character development and well-structured narratives. I felt I was growing alongside the characters and becoming part of the village community and it was one of the most entertaining parts of the game actually.The core game play element is completing all of the twenty-five dungeons. Dungeons are ranked by difficulty level, from one to nine, and initially you will only be allowed to tackle the lower difficulty dungeons until you are skilled enough to tackle more advanced ones. Your skill level is determined by your physical attack score and your magical defense score which in turn is determined by what equipment you have equipped. In the morning you pick one of the five areas to visit, each with a number of different levelled dungeons. There is quite a bit of exploration to do in these areas, including finding and opening chests full of booty, and picking up monster parts that you can sell for money.  The environments all have a different feel to them from snowy mountain tops where you ski around on a hoverboard, to water logged swamplands where you paddle around the various islands in a kayak, and within each area there is the ability to learn two new skills which you will use when solving puzzles in the dungeon or even using whilst fighting monsters. Once you have found a dungeon or a place of interest, it gets marked on your map and then becomes instantly accessible through fast travel. The dungeons obviously get longer and harder as you try higher levelled ones, but the difficulty of the dungeon is well signposted and does correlate with your skill level derived from the equipment and upgrades you possess. I would say, after completing the game, that I felt a little over-powered towards the end, especially on the combat front, because once you have bought the most expensive equipment and are fully upgraded, it is quite easy to accumulate a lot of money which you can spend on health and magic potions, and also you will have been able to acquire charms and special powers that will annihilate most enemies, so I did think ironically that the later dungeons were easier. Combat is a lot of fun but it does come across as a little repetitive, mainly because you are always thrown into a small arena to fight the same monsters which you will recognize from other areas and dungeons. I think there could have been a few more different types of enemies to make it feel less repetitive and the arena itself could have been more diverse, rather than a circle each time. The enemies range from those that fire projectiles at you, to enemies that may have shields you need to break down, or may have powers like your own that you need to dodge, like a shower of meteorites, or traps that they leave on the floor. Towards the latter stages of the game, you will encounter bosses (there are about five I think) that require strategy to beat, and they look and feel great to fight against, but apart from a couple, they are mostly easy to beat once you work out how to destroy them. Your attack consists of a low powered and swift strike of the sword, or a slower meatier swipe which does more damage. You have up to three conduits which unleash special powers like missile strikes or tactical elements like destroying enemy shields. There are about ten different conduits you can collect which all do different jobs and you can equip and unequip conduits whenever you like so you can even tailor the conduits to the battle if you are finding it difficult to win.In the evenings, after you have completed a dungeon or have had enough of exploring, you return to the village where you can shop for items, such as health or magic potions, or pick one of the characters to spend the evening with. Each character has a certain skill set which spending time with will reveal and you can use these skills to upgrade your character. There are four characteristics which make up your personality called renown, amusement, familiarity, and relaxation. Spending time with certain characters will improve your score on some of these characteristics and other characters won't even speak to you unless you have reached a certain score in one of these areas. There are other ways to improve your scores like spending time at some of the attractions like the spa or cinema, or rowing on the lake. There are even options to find beauty spots and skip the dungeon that day altogether. The four characteristics introduce a tactical feel to the game and you will often be looking at your diary to see which skills characters can offer you and planning your socializing accordingly. Probably the most difficult element to the dungeon crawling was the puzzles and they had me scratching my head many times. Each area has two skills which you will utilize during puzzles and they were well crafted and were enjoyable to solve. For example, a jelly cube which lets you reach higher ground, or a whirlwind which you can ride over dangerous terrain. I really enjoyed the puzzles in the dungeons but if they do stump you there is the option to leave the dungeon and try another one.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons of Hinterberg is the suprise of the year for me so far. Playing as a lovely young woman, you arrive in an alpine village where 25 magical dungeons appeared, filled with monsters, puzzles and other challenges. These dungeons are located in several different regions that you can explore freely. Each region gives you unique magical powers, which you can use to defeat monsters, solve puzzles and to discover new paths and loot. The design of the dungeons is truly excellent, with lots of variation and clever ideas. Both the combat and puzzles are never frustrating, making this game a blast to play on a lazy summer evening.But there's more: each night you visit Hinterberg, where you can meet the locals and other monster slayers. By helping htem with their personal problems, you gain their friendship which is rewarded with new abilities, upgrades and skills. If you don't feel like socializing, you can go to the cinema or relax in the local welness facilities to imrpove some of your stats. And there are plenty of shops to buy potions, weapons and armor, gifts for your friends, enchant your equipment and so much more.It's incredible how a small team can make such an extensive game with so many lovely details. I enjoyed every minute of it and can't recommend it enough. Well done Microbird Games!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a good time, but can be tedious toward the final hours.The art style and puzzle mechanics shine the most, but some balance issues and monotony make combat feel like a real chore. Don't go into this expecting a Zelda-like; the skills gained to help with traversal and puzzles are basically limited to each major region, and combat skills ("conduits") can be swapped out at just about any time (and are a bit frustrating in their own way).The social and loot aspects are generally pretty light, but play into character progression nicely.Props to the dev team for the dungeon puzzles and mind-bendy perspective/gravity shifts -- the dungeons themselves all felt varied enough to be enjoyable.The story certainly leaves room for a sequel, and it would be great to see some of these mechanics fleshed out even more!

_childDocuments_.review: An Ocarina of Time for the modern day - and with its own totally unique twist.Seriously though, this is the first time I've had a game make me want to play another game (LoZ OoT obvi) AND scratch the itch to play that game all at the same time. I'm normally a shop-your-wishlist kinda girl, but I randomly stumbled upon this while looking for  to catch my interest because I was SO BORED and figured "eh, sure."SUCH a good call. I just finished my first run through and I'll definitely be back for seconds! While I can't help but draw comparisons to OoT, Dungeons of Hinterberg stands entirely on its own merits. The art style is engaging and playful but doesn't overwhelm, and the gameplay is fun and engaging. I played through on normal mode, which was perfect for me, but I appreciate that there's an easy and a hard mode (which I  might try on my next playthrough). The music was fun too (though I admit it was a bit weird to be walking through town after beating the last dungeon and having the normal evening music play).What I really appreciated as (I hate to admit it) an  was the pacing. The game is sort of broken out like a text-based adventure game, where days are broken into morning, noon, evening, and night chunks. Each chunk has its own actions to perform (ordering breakfast in the morning, open-world style adventuring + dungeons in the noon chunk, shopping & socializing in the evening, and recapping, lounging, and going to sleep at night). When a chunk ends, time passes, but by and large you can spend infinite real time between the start and end of a chunk. It always gave me good stopping places to put the game down and get ready to go to bed. Which, despite being in my late 30s, is a skill I have yet to master without such boundaries.I also really liked the puzzles - and they're probably why I am reminded so viscerally of OoT. I consider myself a pretty good puzzle-solver, but there were more than a handful that gave me trouble and two where I had to just put my Deck down and walk away until the next day. I LOVED it. Though I'm pretty sure there was at least one or two that I solved in a way that the game did not intend... Oh well.My only real complaint was that some of the location bosses were surprisingly easy, including the final game boss... or maybe I was just grossly overpowered by the time I ended my game, which is entirely possible lolI paid full price for this game and was happy to do so - it's well worth the cost. I'll definitely go back to it at least once more, and I'm already planning on gifting it to someone for an upcoming birthday. I'll be nominating it for all the awards I can come Steam Award Nomination season too. I strongly recommend this gorgeous game - it's a joy from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons of Hinterberg is a wonderful game on many levels:1. the artstyle is unique, reminiscent of Moebius at times, but impresses with variety in the different areas and mostly looks beautiful.2. the soundtrack is wonderful, sometimes very much in the background but always fitting and perfectly adapted to the atmosphere.3. the story is nice - but the real highlight here is the cozy Austrian mountain village and its inhabitants and visitors. There are no long, endless dialogs, but you always learn something interesting or the story develops a little further. 4. the gameplay was just right for me. It's uncomplicated, but offers some customization and combination options in the combat system. All in all, I played through the game in one go during my Covid quarantine on Steam Deck and can only recommend it. Actually, I just wish there was more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but dropped it hard after 6 hours of play. I saw maybe 1/4 of the dungeons in this time. The combat is a boring hack and slash fest, without the extended hack and slash fun, due to the way encounters are structured.The dungeons are mostly boring. Only one level in that time was interesting, with some Super Mario Galaxy vibes, although even that one didn't really have the gameplay to support the level design. The way the character controls is also pretty poorly done, even for an indie title.The idea of a cozy game where you get to know the other townspeople seems interesting, and the characters had a little bit of interesting flavor, but the interactions had no depth. The social aspect falls apart when your dialogue choices don't really mean anything, and there's no real interesting plot to note either.I like the sound, the vibe, and the looks, but it lacks anything interesting enough to engage the player deeply. Every aspect is shallow, and so I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but it is a hack and slash game (similar to Raji: An Ancient Epic, for example) with an never before seen story and an unusual graphical style (cel shading like in XIII).This is how you react to climate change! A typical little tourist town in the Austrian Alps switched from hiking/skiing to monster slaying. This is what happened to Hinterberg - when suddenly monsters and dungeons appeared near the town, they turned into a holiday village for monster slaying tourists. Instead of selling you new mountain equipment or clothing, the shops are now called Premium Weapons or Spellbound Smithy. There is still a run-of-the-mill supermarket, spa, gift shop or apothecary, though. Everything seems to work fine, the village is full of happy tourists and business is good.We play a young woman from the capital who booked four weeks holiday here to slay some monsters and escape her stessful job in the law firm... working the same job in the same town I can somehow relate to that. So, you do the usual things - check in at your hotel, go outside to drink a cocktail, meet the locals or other tourists, learn how to ski with an instructor... but the skiing/hiking instructor! I mean, they are here to teach young ladies how to ski, but in reality they also teach you something else, at least if you are pretty. What will my instructor - now dungeon trainer - teach me? Well, I will not spoil what good-looking, muscular (former) alpinist Klaus taught me - but he wanted to be nice and slow. Anyway, the first dungeon did not work out as planned. What happened was certainly NOT advertised in the tourist flyers.The actual gameplay is similar to the usual hack and slash monster slayer - kill creatures with physical attacks (slow/fast), use magic to fry monsters, dodge, watch your stamina, refill your hitpoints and magic points, lock on enemies, collect loot, jump and climb, solve little (but varied) puzzles. You improve your character, learn a few new spells, find some gear, and the aim is to get through a dungeon (alive) and have your dungeon book stamped. That's like the stamps you get on remote huts in the Alps to fill your climbing book. You get this stamp next to every dungeon exit - if you come that far. They are all protected by boss monsters. The difficulty is quite moderate, though - if you die, you are resurrected at the last autosave, which is most of the time a few seconds back. There are 25 dungeons to complete. You have an automap, inventory and quest log, a status page shows your stats. You can save any time - except when inside a dungeon. The game starts on day 1 of your holiday, when you enter a dungeon, hang out with someone in town or sleep during the night the time advances. When you meet with people, your relationship with them might improve if you treated them righ in the multiple choice conversations. Improving relationships earns you perks and might raise your social stats. Small charms you carry around also improve your stats.Little isometric single player hack n slay action game with some dungeons and a little village as game hub. Calling it a simplified version of Zelda meets Persona might not be that wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried the demo during Next Fest and adored it, excited to properly dive into the full game! The art style is thoroughly charming and helps create an almost serene, otherworldly atmosphere that lends itself well to the story and Persona-like life sim aspects between the dungeons, which themselves seem well designed and fairly intriguing from what I've played so far. The combat is nothing special, but functions well enough and provides just enough of a challenge on Normal to be engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: 2 hours in and I've done 5 dungeons, absolute 10/10 for me.I grew up playing Ocarina of Time, and these dungeons are like bite size versions of those!I've played my fair share of Stardew/My Time at X and the social aspect of this game hits the nail on the head!If you like puzzles, advanced combat mechanics, dungeons, bosses, gathering, NPC relationships or even just sitting on a bench, then this game is for you. How ever you want to play, the game will accommodate YOUR vision of Luisa, and its exactly what this genre has been dying for.I struggle to find a way to fault this game honestly. I could knit pick about character customisation or "same one outfit". But I don't feel like those criticisms are very fair when the game really focuses on Luisa as a person, in one of the best single player narratives since sliced bread!The only personal complaint so far is my lack of understanding when it comes to Austrian pronunciations LOL but that is more of a ME thing than the game :P
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: A very ambitious indie game. The designers tried to integrate elements from a lot of different games (Legend of Zelda, Okami, and Persona being the most obvious), and, while it doesn't all come together into a perfect product, I really enjoyed my time with this game. Long story short, if this is what Microbird is capable of as (what I believe to be) their first game, I hope they keep working together, because I cannot wait to see what they make next.I recommend watching some game play footage to see if it's your thing. If it catches your interest, go in with tempered expectations and an open mind. I think you'll have a good time!
