_childDocuments_.review: In a year stacked with amazingly excellent releases, this might be one of my favorites.On the surface, it's an action-adventure game with light combat, Zelda-esque dungeons, and a Persona-lite structure where you get to go hiking and (maybe) dungeonning during the day, then spend the evening shopping and socializing. Each of the different parts feed into the others and create a satisfying overall loop where every action echoes through the rest, and choices are significant and their consequences well telegraphed.The game itself is about taking a vacation away from relatable concerns of modern active life. The whole game reinforces this chill attitude, encouraging taking time off and using the days to rest, meditate and take stock. Far from a management hell sim, this is a laid back descontruction of productivist tropes, and while the game does require the player to complete all dungeons, there is no strict time limit given and it's perfectly possible to see everything and go everywhere at one's own pace.This breezy ambiance is magnified through a brilliant comic inspired aesthetic, with bold thick outlines, confident half tones and drop-dead gorgeous colorization (absolutely play on OLED if you can). The game offers a fantasy window over the real world, taking place in a credible Alpine setting coated with magic. The  character's heavy, weighty basic moveset is progressively counterbalanced through the unlocked magical abilities, giving us an increasing lighter feel and feeding into the escapist fantasy.While every individual part can be "light" with fairly simple and non-threatening combat and puzzles, the game is very much more than the sum of them and manages to evoke a unique melancholy ambiance, an escape from the real world that we sadly know we have to bring to an end - it's up to us to make it last just a little longer.At a glance, the game could be about existentialist musings under late stage capitalism and the environmental impact of commoditizing every aspect of our daily lives, but it's also (and probably moreso than) about taking the time to enjoy our surroundings off the rat race, earnestly engage with people and media, and maybe live slightly more magical lives ourselves by appreciating the uniqueness of the mundane.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, almost cozy game that isn't particularly challenging. The puzzles are nice and not too difficult. Combat is systematic and not really flashy, where the flashiest things you can do are quite overpowered. There's a bit of a persona-style-time system when your days are split into two major time slots: one for doing dungeons and the other for in-town activities. The weakest aspect in this game is the unbalance between these two. To be clear: there are a LOT more town-activities than there are dungeons to do, almost double. I could've beaten the game around day 30, but I keep skipping dungeon time to go do town activities until almost day 69. It's not that skipping dungeons to relax is a bad thing, but even with all the non-dungeon activities you can do - whether it is a quest, relaxing, etc -> you will finish all of it and still not be done with all in-town activities. This flaw isn't that big of a deal and the game's quality in all other aspects is quite good.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: It's incredible. An absolute love letter to so many genres it blends together flawlessly. Dungeons of Hinterberg really feels like a game the developers care about and put a ton of effort to make a fun, replayable experience. If you're a fan of action RPGs, get this game. If you're a fan of Sixth gen action adventure games, get this game. If you're a fan of life simulation (Persona) type games, get this game. It blends all of these together effortlessly and feels like a brand new experience. Easily one of the best games of 2024,
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This is a not recommend for me. By far the best thing about the game is the world design. The base town and the areas I saw outside of the dungeons were beautiful IMO. Unfortunately that is about the only thing I found to be really good.My biggest issue with the game is while they try to make the world feel large you are very limited to where you can go and you are essentially ushered to and through each location. There is no real sense of exploration. I also really disliked the massive amount of handholding the game does - there is no figuring out things on your own. Those 2 things were both massive turnoffs for me.The combat is serviceable, but does not bring anything new to the table and can be a bit clunky and not exactly challenging. As a level 2 I was able to bring down a level 7 "strong" mob and it's minions though it took a little time even on the harder difficulty level.I did not experience any crashes or any real bugs.I think the devs have a decent base game but it needs some work and some major changes for me to want to continue playing and recommend it. I'll keep an eye on the game for any updates that might address my problems and try it out again if it seems like they have. Sorry devs, I hate leaving negative reviews for indie devs but just want to be honest in my review.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's a pleasant game that is pretty upfront about what it is. It doesn't have particularly complex mechanics, but it's a pretty nice package of simple but good enough systems that culminate into a good game. It has some minor bugs, and there were occasional performance issues, but these usually happened in non-combat areas.The combat is a pretty standard attack-dodge system that really shows its flaws once you start encountering large amount of enemies at once, though mana skills and attack skills are a fix to this. There's also a charm that you get right at the start that helps with this, though I haven't been using it. But, the combat system isn't the focus here, and it's good enough. I mostly enjoyed it.I enjoyed the progression system in this game. You have a couple of different upgrade systems that are distinct and simple. Nothing complex, but it's good enough and doesn't feel annoying to interact with.However, it's kind of easy to skip portions of the progression since you might do a dungeon of a higher level than the game expects you to do and consequently pick up equipment that is a fair bit stronger than what you originally had and what the shops currently are selling. *I did go out of my way to chase dungeons that were a higher level than me, and the game does have equipment that has soft stat requirements.The writing feels pretty fine to me. I haven't yet completed the game, so I can't say anything about the ending, but the characters and plot haven't felt particularly oppressive. I generally don't care for writing or characters in games that don't fit a specific niche, so the fact that the story/characters haven't annoyed me so far and has been pleasant is a big plus in my book.The game is upfront about what benefits you get from spending time with a particular character.The puzzles so far have been mostly simple and relatively short. (Well, there might be a large puzzle that is composed of relatively simple and short sub-puzzles). Nothing brain-teasing, but it's "good enough" and I enjoyed them as minor obstacles.The visuals are very good. The graphics and design are up to the eye of the beholder, but I really like the camera-work. In some areas, the camera changes around and freshens the perspective up. It's a bit janky sometimes since your movement inputs won't be in the directions that you expect, but it's minor and hasn't popped up in a combat area so far.There's also some nice QoL. You can fast travel from anywhere, and the transitions were pretty quick. Conversations and most cutscenes have a fast-forward button.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: i really wanted to like this game. I think it has some excellent dungeon puzzling. The combat started off feeling pretty good but does not change a bit from hour 1 to hour 21. After the first couple of dungeons you'll have seen basically every enemy in the game. The difficulty feels very gear-based as later enemies are just the same as earlier enemies with much more HP and higher damage. There's some boss fights.. they're just bad. Tedious, repetitive.Someone else described this a "gen z vegan dungeon crawler" which is an apt description of the narrative vibe. The game ostensibly tries to present itself as an anti-capitalist story but all the NPCs are plucky small business owners and the antagonist is the government.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably for someone, but it's not for me. It'd likely be a good introduction for someone who doesn't play a lot of games into something Soulsy but not very punishing and very casual, but I found all the safety barriers and handholding to be extremely aggravating from the word go.You introduce me to the Austrian alps, you show me that there's an expansive mountainscape and cozy town just behind me, and almost an hour into the game you haven't allowed me to go poke around it without a leash yet. Every single area is crammed full of undiegetic "GEE WHIZ I SHOULDN'T GO THERE YET"-popups as the PC is unwilling to step around a cow or over a fence until game progress permits it.The first boss battle made me hope that boss battles would be interesting in the sense of being somewhat puzzle-y, but there's none of that either, by the second one they've already become pretty generic slashfests(complete with obligatory phase where all you can really do is dodge projectiles), and combat against normal enemies feels a bit lacking because they're all in nice, open, fenced-off arenas that make sure nothing gets too complex.NPC dialogue takes too long and is enforced too regularly. Apparently social interactions also give me mechanical advantages which means that if I don't care about the NPC's(I don't), I can't just skip them and go on my way. I need to participate, which annoys me when these characters are extremely blandly written."Climbing" could be an interesting mechanic, but it's literally just pressing the A button until you reach where you want to go. Conan Exiles showed us that climbing could be a fun minigame with just a stamina bar and requiring you to use your brain a little to spot ledges you could recover on.Just let me off the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ leash and let me go take some risks that might paste me in the Ultra Dungeon even though I'm level 1. Yes, put up all the warning signs, I'll suffer, but it'll be my own damn choice.Lastly, why the hell is the FOV slider a % slider instead of an FOV number? I usually roll with 110 FOV, so what's 0% FOV? 50%? 100%? Oh and having multiple unskippable logos so that I spend almost 20 seconds waiting for the game to actually drop me in the main menu should also be punishable by waterboarding for the entire dev team.This does not spark joy.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so great! I went in blind and I loved it. The art is beautiful, the music is good. Combat, although not very complex, is satisfying. I played on "Hard" mode and had no real issues.The puzzles, apart from a few, are not hard. If it were in the context of another game, I would have felt disappointed at how "easy" most of them are. But in this game, as the main character is just a normal person, I actually felt like it fit logically. It was like taking the puzzles of Zelda's dungeons and just distilling them to be short romps focused on each region's mechanics.I was surprised by some negative comments + reviews about the story of the game. I actually really liked it. The game does such a wonderful job of making you really feel like Luisa, taking a break from our real life. I felt like I very naturally slipped into the game and the mindset. I enjoyed the story start to finish. I would say the game is not replayable, but not every game needs to be. This was seriously a pleasure to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games like Persona, but want much more simple social mechanics and way shorter dungeons, then I think you may like Dungeons of Hinterberg. The game is loop is to go explore dungeons, then go shopping in the town, then spend your nights socializing with the locals. It's a fun intro take on the dungeon RPG. One of the best parts were the stories with the people you meet. This was better than the main narrative, which was also good, but not as good as the NPCs stories. Another positive was the art style. Especially on the ski lodge area. Every dungeon in that region felt unique and grand. Other regions as well, but this one was the best. Also the way each area has it's own type of magic ability that helped with puzzles and combat. I played entirely on the Steam Deck and it ran fairly smooth 60fps medium settings with minor dips to the high 40s at time. The dips were mostly during some traversal in an area with lots of water and rain effects. Never an issue during combat. The only negatives I really had was the games economy. It felt like shops were very expensive, but if you just wait you can find better stuff within the dungeons anyway. They almost didn't feel like they had a point to them.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game. The graphics in the screenshots and trailers are honest, the music fits the setting and doesn't get in the way, the day sequence plays like a version of Persona while being different enough, and the dungeons feel Zelda-like enough while being unique. The magic system keeps the four different zones feeling different enough as well as makes the controls not too hard to learn.The game does drag a bit near the end but it isn't too bad. The itemization is boring and how you play doesn't change much throughout the game. The power curve is a bit exponential, so expect to breeze through the end of the game compared to the beginning and middle. If you're looking for a pretty good game that you can play in bite sized pieces for a week or two (or looking to finish a game all the way in a weekend), I fully recommend Dungeons of Hinterberg.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I took my sweet time, but I've finally completed the game and had a great time doing it.No swearing and no gore, with a bright vibrant world meant I was happy for my 6 year old son watching me play. He even helped me with the dialogue options and was keen to see where the story was going to go. If you want a quick hack and slash game, this could be for you as all dialogue can be skipped. Me though? I liked chatting to everyone and hearing each of the unique character's stories. Personally I found the main story to be quite deep. The central character is a hot shot lawyer who seems to have lost her way in life. Having a successful career and a house doesn't automatically make you happy. Who do you talk to in this game to find your way? The guy with the big sword? Or maybe sit down and spend some time with a dog, or some outcast teenagers? I just loved the message of this game. Each person should not be underestimated and seems to have words of wisdom and in turn you can help them in their lives too.In short, this game is not about fame, fortune and grinding for success. It's about evolving yourself. The simple act of picking up litter, the decision not to tackle a dungeon that day, but to take a rest by a beauty spot will actually boost your character. A task that in another game would be a slog, in this game can be relaxing.A beautiful world, story, music, combat, collectables, optional costumes, customisable spells and swords, new game plus and of course dungeons! This game has it all
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: 3 hours in and i love this game a lot; I'm sure there'll be a lot of stuff in the future, but just the amusment park-esque method of exploring dungeons, all of which so far have felt so unique, with a pretty clear progression system that makes it easier to just play the game and not try and minmax everything to do endgame content at lvl 1 just makes it a nice slow burn that really makes you want to actually explore and talk to people, try to solve little hidden puzzles and stuff to get that little edge that slowly pushes you forward. The sound design and bgm is just really well done- it makes combat feel that much more satisfying. My one nitpick is that the walking/running animation feels clunky. This is literally the most nitpicky thing ever but getting from point A to B just feels kinda awkward watching the character move, everything feels really satisfying overall- but just *walking* feels weird
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is stiff and doesn't evolve much, so I don't think that will win anybody over, but the creativity and the absolutely inspired design of the game should.Dungeons of Hinterberg is such a unique premise for an ARPG and it does justice to all the other games it took inspiration from. The setting, style, and writing are all refreshing and stand out among any other bog-standard fantasy adventures. The dungeons themselves all play with the tools you have and don't overstay their welcome. Also, they all try to stand out from each other with unique visuals, gimmicks, layouts, and camera angles.If you can get over the clunky and repetitive combat, you will be pleasantly surprised by the imaginativeness this game brings to the table. (Also, it's not too long: 18 hours to 100% the game and it's achievements!)
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my GoTY and the fact that I'm writing my first ever review about this game hopefully expresses the level of my enjoyment with it.A really charming RPG with 4 main areas to visit, each with their own theme and spell sets unique to them. Each area is vastly different from the last and provides their own challenges to overcome. Simplistic but fun melee combat with opportunity to spec more into magic or skills to mix it up if you choose. Very pretty art style and fitting to the themes of the game. Relationship opportunities which were a really interesting aspect, as there were levels unique to each person, each with their own rewards. So you could omega-focus one person to try and see what their final reward was, or go wide to see what options you have available (the logbook you keep shows the next upcoming reward for each person). Or you could just hang with whoever you liked the vibe of the most. Characters I thought I would hate ended up surprising me by having some really rich backgrounds and ended up being some of my favourites by the end.The charms: These were a form of buffing you character throughout the game and allowed once again, to spec into your kind of build. Want a spell build? You can stack charms for magic damage or mana gain. Tanky/bruiser build? There's charms for resistances or damage reflection even. Sword build ones obviously. And then you can get some funky ones that you can build your whole character around. My build was knockdown based, where I had a better chance to knockdown and dealt more damage to enemies that were knocked. There's a bunch more but I'll avoid so anyone thinking of buying the game can find them for themselves.Dungeons: The dungeons are obviously the main focus of the game and it shows how much work was put into them to make each one feel unique and special. The general ambience would match the area it's in, but that doesn't limit what to expect. There are never 2 dungeons alike, as they each have a theme they are going for exclusive to them. The tools you are given to solve the puzzles within these dungeons can be used in numerous ways that you wouldn't expect when you first claim them.Speaking of Puzzles: These are a staple of each dungeon and in some cases even the overworlds which you find them. I don't think you will ever feel like they are unsolvable if you take 2 seconds to look at all the 'moving parts'. Sure some are definitely harder than others but each one feels rewarding and leaves you excited for the next one. Also, the dev's did a great job on introducing these puzzles, they basically start each dungeon with an example of how you may want to use your spells to solve the puzzles further in as they begin to get more complex. This is really handy if you've been traversing different areas day to day and forget some of the nuances of your spells if you haven't been to the area in a bit.Story (I'll try to keep it spoiler free): The story was surprisingly rich. You would expect that you just come to this village and slay monsters and clear all the dungeons, go home and fin. But as you talk to more of the NPC's after your days slaying you learn the impact that dungeons have had on this area, how the tourism has raised money, how some locals feel alienated, whether what your doing is right or wrong? It's a really interesting narrative and I enjoyed the themes it explored greatly. Overall, I think this game is fantastic. It took me 36 hours to beat, but I'm a no-lifer who played on the harder difficulty and wanted to max all my relationships and find all the collectables before finishing, so I reckon it could be finished a lot quicker. I would truly recommend this gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most underrated game of 2024. I had a blast with this vibey little RPG.PROS:-Vibrant graphics. I'm a sucker for cell-shaded games and this is one of the best looking cell-shaded games I've ever played. -Creative Dungeon design. Every dungeon legitimately feels like a new adventure. I don't want to spoil anything, but it's really impressive how much each dungeon shakes up the gameplay. -The game allows you to take your own pace. You can take days off and chill out as much as you want. -Plenty of content. There's about 20 hours and that's without New Game+-Whilst it's not an epic story, I do enjoy the novelty of the premise. The idea of going on holiday to play real life 'Dungeons and Dragons' is rather amusing. NEUTRAL:-The game seems to trigger the 'it's woke' crybabies. Dunno why but at least it gives us rational people something to point and laugh at.-Controller is recommended, but I didn't have much of an issue with M+KB. CONS:-I haven't played New Game+ yet, but the game is pretty easy on Hard mode. I don't think that's a huge negative as this is a pretty casual game, but it's worth noting for those looking for a challenge. -Combat is a bit repetitive as you're often fighting the same enemies and using the same abilities. Fights are only ever made hard because you're 'lower level' than enemies. Whilst you do gain different abilities, weapons and armor are just 'better numbers' more than anything else. It would've been nice to see some variety (for example, a heavy axe or dual wielded fast swords).
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: There really not anything wrong with this game, it's just really not for me. I'll go through the major issues, but it's all just preference honestly.In summation, if the art style appeals to you and the gameplay looks good, you may disagree and like this game. The biggest issue at that point would be if you would like the aforementioned story/writing/characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the best games I have played in a very, very long time. It's charming, well-polished, and frankly something you will want to take your time enjoying. I've read some people saying the playtime is about 20 hours, sure. That's possible. But if you take your time, enjoy the holiday, get to know the other characters and casually go about the game, you can really stretch out the content. I'm 21 hours in and only about 70% through the game. It's absolutely worth it, get this game, gift it to your friends, just do it. My personal game of the year 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I suppose the game is all about atmosphere and style (If you're into this kind of visual presentation), because, IMHO, the gameplay does not do very well: the fighting lacks momentum and inertia, the acrobatics are quite tedious, the camera moves all over the place (at least when using mouse), and the battles are both scarce and beyond easy. Maybe it would get better later on, but for some reason my eyes really tire of this game specifically, which is a reason enough for me not to try "Dungeons of Hinterberg" out further.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent RPG with an authentic feel clearly rooted in the makers homeland. I'm 6 hours in with 5 or 6  of 35 dungeons down and the game is still gradually expanding on systems so this is looking like great value for money. Combat is fluid and feels good. Dungeons, so far seem to lean a bit more puzzly than combat focused. I find that a plus but that could change as dungeon difficulty goes up.Graphic style feels a bit messy at times but is over all pleasing. It may be because I'm on lowest ettings on a steam deck stretched to a TV. Sound manages to be pleasant and despute not having a massive number of tracks so somewhat repetitive is never grating or annoying. Sound effects are virtually always satisfying.Game runs great on steam deck, only one non-breaking bug I've noticed.Over all a fantastic package, a fun game, and I'd say it's worth your time and dollars.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty solid game. It's an action game where you have a light & heavy attack plus 3 ability based attacks and 1 ranged attack. You traverse 4 different realms filled with a total of 25 dungeons and has things to collect throughout them. The developers achieve a pretty good balance between making an action game that has some difficulty but is pretty casual with pretty low stakes. The dungeons have some cool inspirations and work well, but they are fairly simple. These dungeons shift between action arenas and puzzle labyrinths. That said, the game is a little clunky at times, possibly overstays its welcome, heavily forces its narrative at the end, and the gem slotting upgrade system is arguably useless.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! The mix of genres is fantastic and something I'd love to see more of. The fighting is fun and challenging, the cast of characters and social aspects add so much charm. Exploring this world has been a blast. The art style is stunning - some levels are absolutely gorgeous! Although there are a few minor hiccups here and there, the game is incredibly well-polished, and the team should be really proud of their work!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: first, id like to say i enjoy the game, for the most part. i plan on finishing it. however, i have to give it a bad note because it literally makes me sick. normally i can handle third person games just fine, but after playing the glacier galaxy dungeon and having to throw up from motion sickness, i just wanted to leave this review. the next dungeon, minecart something also made me sick from the mine cart racing thing. maybe if there was an option to slow it down, it might help, but as it stands, its a quick path to a headache/vomit.TL;DR dont play if you get motion sickness unless you have some dramamine on standby.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty cool. The story is decent and the gameplay is basic but serviceable. The reason why I can't recommend it is that the game makes me motion sick to play it. I don't really have this problem with games in general but about 50% of the time playing this game has made me feel ill. I know they've added some options for this but at this point I'm tired of feeling bad playing this game.Folks should definitely consider getting the game but if you're prone to motion sickness, make sure you've assessed whether you want to continue playing past the 2 hour refund window.

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice puzzle platformer. Just the right length where you get to use most mechanics a decent amount but not so long you get bored of the gameplay.Had a great time that was relaxing and no annoying achievements.Just remember, you are never in a hurry no matter what the story indicate so take your time and relax at the spots and do the relationships because if you do a dungeon a day then you are going to miss out on stuff.The game got a bit jittery by the end of the game but no real problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: 25 dungeons with puzzles, basic combat, with an incredibly chill vibe. Recommend.To me, this is a distilled zelda-like where any frustrating parts have been removed. The game also is based on days like a Persona game but *you can do everything at your own pace*. You are not worried about missing out on anything, which is just one example of how this game respects you as a player and is the opposite of stress-inducing. There are also social-skill unlocks ala persona, but again, you can do whatever you want with no time constraint!The general story of the game speaks to escape from the daily grind, and you end up *feeling* it as you play the game. I'm at dungeon 15/25, day 25 or so, and have thoroughly enjoyed the game so far usually doing a dungeon each evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: It's a dash of a 3d Zelda mixed with some Persona social link stuff. It's more than that really, a story of finding yourself, of taking a break and enjoying life. The level variety is pretty good, from Mario Galaxy-esque zones, to M. C. Escher style puzzle areas, to just snow boarding on rails. Worth picking up and spending a few days with.

_childDocuments_.review: this is i guess a half-recommend? it's visually charming as hell with great vibes and everything but the actual gameplay is a bit mid tbh. heavy focus on the same exact puzzles everyone's been doing since literally 1998 (some are just ripped straight out of Wind Waker for instance), and unfortunately the combat isn't great either, though part of that's just down to the weird inventory/skill controls that make assigning a fromsoft control scheme impossible, so you gotta switch between right stick and face buttons all the time like it's 2001 smh. it's not terrible (though it also swipes Okami's awful block-off-the-level-until-you-beat-these-mobs mechanic) but every combat encounter ends up feeling just a tad jankspeaking of that era it frequently ALMOST reminds me of megaman legends, but worse in almost every way (thankfully, this game doesn't have MML's terrible 90s-anime-dub voices, so that's a point for Hinterberg). that's not a criticism, "Megaman Legends but worse" is a game i would pay $70 for day 1, no questions asked. this ain't quite there, the dungeons might be visually more interesting but they're mechanically stale and it feels more linear overall. also zero weapon variety and cooldown-based (yuck) special attacks, and the world and characters are nowhere near as quirky/offbeat/fun, but i really shouldn't fault them for not being as good as a game that great. like, it's also worse than Ocarina of Time (definitely a bigger inspiration) but if it wasn't that would be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wildalso big kudos for adding fashion features in the latest patch, even if it's sadly halfbaked with only a total reskin rather than proper individual clothing selectionoverall i think it's worthwhile if you want a cozy-ish zelda-like, but it doesn't really live up to the aesthetics and kinda ends up feeling like a missed opportunity, at least so far. i'm having fun with it but its influences are just too good for it to measure up. less plagiaristic puzzles, better combat and controls, and/or more Megaman Legends and less Ocarina of Time would all be very welcome in a sequel

_childDocuments_.review: Some people visit Austria to trakk on the alps, paraglide, or simply to relax. But we are here to slay in style or die trying!Play as Luisa Dorfer, a former lawyer looking for a change of pace in her life. Hinterberg is a tourist attraction due to its phenomenon of magic and dungeon portals. People known as slayers are trying to conquer them and you are now one of them. You can explore the village and four semi open world maps, with each of them having their distinctive biome and magic skills. There are many characters around Hinterberg you can meet and spend time with, relationships give you benefits in the form of perks and upgrades, or even special gear. Dungeons are very reminiscent of Zelda, lots of environmental puzzles mixed with combat and a boss for each biome. Some of the dungeons have very interesting and unconventional designs, similar to what you find in Super Mario Galaxy. Visuals and soundtrack are simply amazing, exploration feels great and is always rewarding.Theres a lot of customization going on. Many outfits to purchase, stat boost gems to be added to your weapon, a big variety of charms that give you passive effects or stat boosts and skill attacks that can be mixed and matched however you like. I recommend buying the increased monster loot charm at Hannahs store as soon as possible.Not too many complaints here. The plot is very generic, evil money hungry Mayor, yadda yadda. She hid one of the dungeons so magic will never disappear and she can profit off it forever. However, there are in fact four dungeons that are hidden and can only be discovered by specific means. The Tower of Trials dungeon was extremely laggy for me, I was almost unable to beat the level because Luisa refused to climb ladders or fell down. Even lowering all the settings didnt do anything to help. Some minor things that broke immersion for me was that the swords always kind of clipped through the shaft when walking and the dungeon Desolate Castle had a huge bed, park bench, swords and spinning wheels, indicating this may have been a giants castle until you notice that the whole castle is for some reason normal human sized. Why include all these huge props when the castle itself isnt adequate to their size?Sometimes I feel really bad purchasing cheap retail keys instead of waiting for a sale, or simply buying at full price, because Hinterberg deservers every cent it charges. Im kind of a cheapskate with limited funds and too much freetime, what can I say. I shall repent by buying the Supporter Bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I personally feel this game is getting far too much of a pass because it looks cute. After doing the first dungeon, I uninstalled - the combat isn't particularly rewarding, the narrator and her story isn't particularly compelling, and the wink wink meta narrative just feels a little overdone.Those comparing it to Zelda - Zelda, since Skyward Sword, has had a jump button. Jumping feels like it should be a big part of this game, but surprise - no jump button. This informs you very early on that YOU ARE ON RAILS (at times literally) and you aren't going off them at any point.It's beautiful and the art style is peak. Not much game there worth playing if you aren't a huge fan of "platformers," and I use that loosely with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: By the end of it, I didn't want to say goodbye.Only played this for a few hours around the time of release but came back months later and really got sucked into it. I loved exploring dungeons by day and hanging out with the wonderful characters in the evening. It was a gameplay loop that I really enjoyed and there was just so much variety in the dungeons and the characters you come across. I didn't max out the relationships with every possible person because I was always torn who to hang out with each day due to a mix of everyone being interesting and the wide variety of rewards you could get for connecting with each person.The dungeons were a joy to play, with each one feeling unique, offering a great amount of variety between them individually and the regions you find them in. I really enjoyed the whole game visually too, there's so much to love in all of the locations mixed in with the great music to really tie the experience together.I loved everything about this game and I was very invested in the story so if there is any plans for a sequel then I'll be all over it, for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: A satisfying adventure that's hard to put down. I keep finding more and more things to love about Dungeons of Hinterberg. Whether it be the gorgeous views from the mountaintops or the charming fellow slayers you can befriend, Dungeons of Hinterberg has it all. The protagonist is extremely relatable as someone who also seeks to escape from work stress, and Dungeons of Hinterberg provides a great way to relax, unwind, and slaaaaay. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I was honestly and quite gladly taken by surprise by this gameNot what I expected, but it really grew on me.... combat is well done, the different upgrade systems go well in hand with each other for a healthy growth.... and the story is quite niceThe only thing that could be improved is the balance towards the end of the game, aiming for maxing social and doing everything, kinda ends up disjointed from the main game.... at first it seems to go well hand in hand, specially if using resting points (so not really advancing the story at full throttle)..... but it requires so many evenings that the rest of the game just doesn't keep up.....  it's still fine since you can skip and allOverall a really good game and now that it has new game plus, with added replay value

_childDocuments_.review: After an extremely stressful past couple of weeks, playing this game set in the beautiful Austrian Alps was a breath of fresh air.Dungeons of Hinterberg explores Luisa, a burnt-out law student who comes to the titular town for the ultimate vacation. During the afternoon, she can travel to four unique areas of Hinterberg and either complete a dungeon or sit at a Scenic Spot; in the evening, she can take some more time to herself at the cinema, spa, or rowboats, or hang out with the locals and frequent visitors to gain access to unique perks, charms, and special attacks.What makes Dungeons of Hinterberg special is that it encourages the player to take things slow and relax in between dungeon crawling and slaying. Sitting at Scenic Spots and doing solo evening activities increases Luisa's stats, making her stronger as the dungeons get more challenging. In addition, hanging out with the NPCs allows Luisa (and the player) to see value in Hinterberg beyond a tourist destination; it's also a community, one that Luisa can choose to be a cherished part of. If you want an RPG that's has a good balance between being a cosy game and an action game, or if you want something reminiscent of Zelda, this a good game to pick up. I'm glad I did at any rate.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed spending time in Hinterberg. The dungeons are unique and the puzzles were interesting and fun. Combat got stale but once I started unlocking the attack conduits I was able to add substance to the combat instead of spamming sword attacks. Most games haven't been captivating my attention as of late and I gave this a chance on a whim and I am glad I did. Reminded me what gaming is all about and I hope Microbird makes a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons of Hinterberg is an incredibly fun genre mashup. The main draw is the Zelda-style puzzle dungeons, but the combat is compelling, too! And the social sim elements are well integrated, while being less stressful than something like Persona. The total package is phenomenal. It is no AAA game, and has a few stiff animations and awkward interactions. But the colorful graphics and art style are very well executed. Not to mention it's a complete and polished experience. At release! I didn't know they did that anymore.Anyway, highly recommended. Get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game rocks. Very cozy in vibes, half persona-like life sim and half tiny dungeon explorer. The social side and the dungeon side feed into each other, with perks from relationships making you stronger or even unlocking new features. Combat is simple but engaging, the real star here is the level design in the dungeons. The puzzles are super well tuned, requiring just a little creative thinking and knowledge of your region specific magic spells to get through. The game starts out quite humble visually early on but the spectacle and scale of dungeons ramps up across the game. By the time I got to the SNOWBOARDING IN OUTER SPACE DUNGEON I was completely hooked, it's so fun. The writing is also smart and well done, all the magic and monsters is dressing for a very real feeling story about a small resort town grappling with way too much success way too fast, and every character lives through it in a different way and offers other perspectives. Game also looks great, peep that art! Love it so far, exciting to finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: enjoyed this one for sure. great game to jump in and out of. if you like puzzles and exploring dungeons, you'll have a good time with this. also the magic abilities are pretty cool in each zone and add a little something. combat and armor/weapons are a little lackluster, its basically equipping the best set for your stats and moving forward, although it does get a little better when you unlock buffs and upgrades for them. combat does not change after the tutorial for the most part, so it can get a bit stale, though to be fair the attack conduits can help if you rotate them every so often. overall though, definitely recommend this one. had a great time checking off all the dungeons, exploring new areas, and unlocking new perks.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Zelda clone I've played since the actual Zelda games got their head too far up their own ass.  No Balsa-Wood Weapon Durability here.  The dungeons are the perfect length and the gimmicks don't overstay their welcome.  Each dungeon is designed around just two spells and you can't use the ones that aren't needed for that world. It's a smart design choice that cuts out a lot of trial and error.  You aren't swapping through every tool to figure out which one does the thing.  The dungeon level scaling could use some work though.  There's a difficulty cliff if you start doing dungeons above your level, though.Game usually runs well on Steam Deck, but the Hinterwald area has some notable frame drops.  I think the falling leaves effect seems to be messing things up- the dungeons are fine but the field is inconsistent.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This is certainly one of my favorite games - a beautifully crafted Austrian Zelda-like experience. I was already looking forward to this game for such a long time and it did not disappoint and has quickly become one of my absolute favorites. It combines really interesting game mechanics reminiscent of Zelda, smart puzzles, polished fights with interesting in-game villains and all it set in a uniquely Austrian context.The graphics are truly special—extremely polished, with smooth game play that makes every moment feel seamless.What I especially love about this game is the focus on the Austrian theme. The game is filled with so many clever Austrian insiders, with a fascinating story line that maybe pokes at little at tourism. It weaves in tons of Austrian culture, themes, and even mythical Austrian creatures in such a thoughtful and creative way.To summarize, it is humorous and interesting story, charming graphics, polished game play,.. just beautiful, and for me just an all-around perfect package.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an exact 7/10. When it does something well, it's incredibly fun. I love every vehicle related thing, and think the glacier zone could be a premise for a game all on it's own. Actually, if this game was just slightly surreal fast-paced dungeons like the minecarts and snowboards this was be a 10/10. On the flipside when it does something less than well, it's always tedious and annoying. The characters have great visual design, but are narratively rather bland despite being clearly intended to be diverse. They're not bad per se, they're just kinda boring. The main character usually also has three dialogues which are "be very polite", "say something polite but vaguely anti-capitalist", and my favourite "...". Honestly I wish every dialogue in the game had a "...".

_childDocuments_.review: A fun dungeon exploration game that has some really strong narrative points. I found myself really enthralled by the main characters monologues, seeking only the safe route in life and wanting more of the magic there is in the world.The Good:Fun combat and unique bosses.The dungeons felt unique and the puzzles were cool.The style and comic style overlays are awesome.The magic was uniqueThe upgrade systems, charms, enchantments, and conduits made me stay the few extra days to grind the materials to stuff as many charms as I could into my pockets.The upgrades you get for companions made the need to interact with them feel rewardingThe BadThe pacing of the game feels a little off.. The morning you choose a location you're going to spend the day in, you then go there and run a dungeon of meditate at a vista. Then you're left to the evening to interact with a person. But if you complete dungeons it quickly pushes quests and dialog on you.The NPCs had their own fun stories most of which kinda wrap around your own as the main character. However The gift system didn't feel at all meaningful and you have to interact with each NPC  at least 4 times. Which game-play loop-wise feels a little tedious at points.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good surprise.Pro - - The dungeons are well thought with a pretty good diversity in the puzzles. You need to think for a while, but it's never enough to get you stuck.- The fights are quite enjoyable, some mobs are more annoying than others but in the end, even in tough mode, it's challenging without being difficult.Con -The auto-jump. That feature is a pain. You can't decide when to jump, so your char will jump each time there's an edge, even if 1 meter away there's a huge cliff, I think I died more by Luisa jumping to her doom than killed by some mobs.- The shoping only in the evening. Some times, due to the scenario, you can't do your shopping on an evening, and since you are not allowed to do your shopping the next morning for some weird reason, you immediatly have to go back dungeoning without having been able to upgrade/augment the stuff looted the previous day. So either you have to relax just to go back in town, or you go in a dungeon with stuff that is lower that what could have been. Weird choice.But overall, the game is really pleasant, and at this price, it's really a nice experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This little game punches well above its weight. Effectively combines the Persona calendar/social link system, 3D Zelda puzzle dungeons, and a story that starts about the importance of taking a break from the monotony of daily working life and morphs into a statement on the tourism industry as leadership attempts to capitalize on Hinterberg's unique features at the expense of its citizens.It's a bit janky, especially the camera and combat (which makes the combat dungeons easily the worst). It's really only a way to gate and pace out progress. But I genuinely looked forward to playing a day or two in game whenever I had some spare time.If you're interested, it's worth checking out. Great for steam deck.

_childDocuments_.review: Requested a game key without having any ideia what this game was all about."I will just do my typical 1/2 hour livestream and just uninstall it after".Except, I didn't uninstall it.This game is half Persona, half Zelda, and it's a little bit jack of all trades master of none, but still a very very good Jack of all trades, I was very hooked at the ending to be honest.From the persona side, We have the social links, the relationships with the caracters, at first I was feeling a little bit too much of that DEI inclusion going in, but didn't last long, some characters are not very memorable and their personal issues and motivations could have been presented better with much more diverse actions in the social links events, and not only show them talking in the same places, also what was suppose to be our best friend was annoying as hell, didn't related to her.There are a lot of social links here, and some of them are much more elaborated and relatable than others, as well as their importance to the game.We also have the same time of day of Persona.Every start of day, we get to talk to some characters and we are immediatly forced to choose to what map are going we going to go (you can choose in between 4 of them), at the evening we get back to the village (hinterberg) and are able to explore, buy stuff that we need, improve social links etc.At night you are stuck in your room (pretty much like persona) and you can either sleep, read or watch TV, both watching tv and reading gives you stats but you will lose 25% HP next day.There are way more stuff into this which I'm not elaborating.As for Zelda part, the zelda part is mostly the dungeons and the open world part of each map mostly.Dungeons are great, we have 4 different environments, each environment have a certain ammount of dungeons, you will have a total of 25 dungeons to complete (probably more heh heh) and the basic objective is that, but just like persona, improving social links will improve your skills too, oh and you can have a lot of skills.Since Attack conduits which is special attacks you can use as well as magical attacks and meelee.Talking about magical attacks, each one of the 4 environments you will have 2 different magical attacks/powers, and during those enviroments and dungeons, you not only will use those magical attacks to kills mobs, but also to solve puzzles scattered through out the game.The pacing of the game was a little bit disappointing, at first if it wasn't my interest into the game, I would probably leave it behind, it starts slow, generic and boring, but it starts to pick up the pace in the story and caracthers and motivations also starts to improve a lot at mid game and that's where I've started to become more addicted into it.Unfortunaly the only thing that pissed me off is that it's easy to get to the last dungeons and you will have a lot of social links to improve and quests to do which require grinding which is the opposite compared to Persona 4 Golden.I've grinded a bit but ended up being tired about it and just proceded to the last dungeon to end it all (which was today)Fortunaly recently the game added a new game + which allows you to keep your quests progress, attacks, inventory and social links so it's an "easier way" to replay the game and finish the stuff with more interesting stuff to do than just blindly grind.Completed the game in the though difficulty, it was easy enough except some later dungeons or special monsters in the open world area, dying just teleports you back to the last auto-save, and oh boy this game auto-saves way to often.The last dungeonts did required me to go prepared with dozens of potions to keep me alive though.Performance wise the game is very lightweight, I was able to play max settings 1080P at 60 FPS locked with a 1650 Super, there were some very selected moments where it did drop in some enviroment, but only to 50-55 FPS and very very VERY RARELY.I've played most of the game in linux mint 22, performance is surprisingly on par with windows given we are playing over proton on linux which is a compatibility layer (it was suppose to loose perforamnce) so if you intend to play on the Steam Deck it will probably work without issues and with surprising performance.Cheers

_childDocuments_.review: Did you like the relationship-building stat boosting of the Persona series? Did you like the Jet Set Radio comic book visual style? Did you like the gated progression and lightweight, archetypal fable story structure and control scheme of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time?You're gonna love this. This is a game for Old People like me ... and kids.Yeah, ignore the fake controversy about this game being "woke" from the usual forum cockroaches. The only thing remotely "woke" about this game is the day/night sleep cycle. There's a bit of social coding here and there if you are REALLY searching for it. If there is a message here, it's a conservative one about preserving local culture and community under the constant crush of tourism and consumerist media saturation as well as the economic surge that comes with it.But what you are here for is the excellent visuals, unique art style, fun-but-not-hard puzzles, light story, and all the wild roller coaster rail sequences.The quality of everything that made it into the game is very high, but there are signs of cost/time controls everywhere. No open world, just four hub areas and a town to explore. Again, old people will feel right at home with this Playstation 2-era design, and it won't confuse the kiddies. Textures and models are re-used constantly, sometimes with creative results, and all of the characters use the same walk animation that makes them look like surly apes.The story can feel a bit disjointed on the first playthrough, if you don't choose to hang out with the characters that the game nudges you toward. I ignored a lot of their plot lines in favor of the Influencer character, who will validate all of your geezer predispositions toward YouTubers. Very Amusing. I wanted the game to make the antagonistic characters more sympathetic, but it feels like they didn't have time to develop that. The whole thing becomes "hero vs blind megalomanics" by the end.The cost cutting is most evident in the combat. There's a lot of it, but it's not varied, and it happens exclusively in makeshift arenas safely separated from the dungeon puzzles, much like Kena: Bridge of Spirits. Much like Kena, you will spend almost as much time fighting the camera as you will enemies. The half dozen or so enemy types just soak up more and more damage as the game progresses. The bosses are the Zelda use-the-new-weapon puzzle type. Fun for the first time, but not difficult at all on normal mode.For all of its limitations, this is the first game I've played in years that caused me to search for upcoming DLC, right after I finished the main campaign. There are hints in the game of other locations that might serve as sequel/DLC fodder, and I'm here for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed playing this game a lot. The aesthetic and the pacing give off a very relaxing vibe that makes you not want to play in a hurry. My time in Hinterberg has been an enjoyable one, I've caught myself amazed at some of the level design and the wonderful vistas. The friendship mechanic has made me care for some of the NPC. However the game can become repetitve, the dungeons are varied but after doing 15 or so it really feels as more of the same. Also, not a fan of the encounters taking place in a limited circular area.Despite it's flaws I really recommend this game,
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons of Hinterberg is a really cute game with an absolutely gorgeous art style. Its combination of fighting/exploration and social sim is heavily inspired by games like Persona, but the devs gave it their own spin and weren't afraid to deviate from the formula where necessary or beneficial. I also really enjoyed the story that contained some twists that worked well for me, although I wished it would have leaned heavier into some negative aspects .  The characters within the social sim are great too and believably grow over the course of the game. The persona-like relationship progression seems a bit de-synced from the main story tho and hanging out with characters later in the story than the devs expected can lead to awkward moments.The world and its dungeons are fun to explore and filled with interesting looking enemies and creative puzzles. I would've wished for a wider variety of enemies tho and while the fights are pretty easy even on the highest difficulty, they can be really frustrating at times because the controls feel the tiniest bit shaky and the telegraphing of attacks is too ambiguous for my taste.Overall a great game tho and definitely gets a recommendation from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: First, this game is absolutely BEAUTIFUL! The art style is so fun and captivating. It's refreshing to see this kind of cartoon pop-art style. It's also just refreshing to get some nice little German lore and scenery.Second, the gameplay is extremely addictive and fun! If you love puzzles and some fun fighting, then this is definitely for you. I was addicted to this game. And even still am. I'm ready to play through AGAIN. The story line is very cute, you get to make your own decisions on how you want to play. And Honestly, the environments are so NEAT!You're not just stuck to walking/running everywhere. There's so many different ways to get around in all the areas. There's always something good hiding around the corner. You get rewarded for taking the extra look-see. It's honestly the coziest little fighting/puzzle game I've played in a long time!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so in love with this game.What I like most playing this game is that the protagonist is totally relatable. Wanting to escape the matrix, yada yada. The protagonist's realizations during the cut scenes when relaxing in the dungeon are very uplifting.Every side characters story are interesting (it feels like watching animated shows with real life learning).Main story like has studio ghibli-ish touch in it.Gameplay mechanics are great if you love cozy game.The only negative I can think of is that the dungeon puzzles are so easy.Overall 9.5/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I should've taken the hint from the art style and character design but this game is definitely not for me. It looks neat in screenshots but in motion I can't say it feels satisfying to play, I choose Hard mode, completed the first day, chatted to the first side character and decided that I didn't really want to go any further. There's a lot of talking in 'that' kind of style that you can see in the social gameplay video which I thought would've been avoidable. The basic combat loop doesn't have good feedback, the basic enemies didn't really react to being stuck and just ran away when triggered to low health and the first boss is a puzzle boss which was damage the environmental structures that you've already been doing for the last 5 minutes.I'm not going to play through more to find out that the magic is the same while being limited.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. Kinda chill and really easy to pick up. The game doesn't hold your hand, but is really good at showing you opportunities to discover new mechanics. There is no deadline to get stuff done, so you're free to do whatever in any order. Would recommend mixing things up, rather than pushing through.
