_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons of Hinterberg turned out to be a surprise hit of this summer for me. I had no idea how this game plays, I just thought "nice visual style", added it to wishlist and bought it during the slow summer season. Didn't expect it to completely take over my time in the last few days.Its an interesting mix of genres, gameplay feels evenly split between building up relationships with people met in Hinterberg, fighting monsters and solving puzzles. Each of these elements is solid and while it doesn't set any new heights, all of it is very enjoyable. All characters we meet are likeable or at least interesting and some of them reveal surprising depth over time. Many will give you extra side quests, once they get to know you better. Leveling up relationships works kinda like a perk system and improving your standing with characters will unlock game changing set of abilities and upgrades.Combat, while entertaining is a bit of weak link. Its serviceable, but a little simplistic. It boils down to slashing enemies with your sword, rolling out of the way of attacks, casting limited number of spells (two per region) and using powerful skills on cooldown. There are no real combos, parrying, shields or other weapon types. I recommend playing on 'Tough' difficulty if you want combat to be more engaging and make equipment progression actually meaningful. Spells in this game are quite interesting, but more as tools to be used in puzzles and exploration. Each region, of which there are four, has its own two spells. I don't want to spoil some surprising mechanics, so let me just say that you'll be snowboarding, riding tornadoes and summoning gigantic jello cubes among other things. Every spell has its uses in combat as well, but they are the most fun in puzzles.Puzzles themselves are the main attraction of Dungeons of Hinterberg. While not super complex, they are fun brain teasers. Spells are used in surprising ways and game never spoils exactly how you should use them. I was never stuck too long on any puzzle and they were a nice change of pace between combat.Each region in Dungeons of Hinterberg is very distinct from one another, both visually and mechanically. Your progression through each region will be dictated by your character level and story progress. Locations will slowly open up and offer more challenging dungeons and better rewards. Typically going up against enemies that are even one level higher than you is difficult as they can one shot you easily. It isn't as restrictive as it sounds, since progression is well designed and you always have something to do in one of the regions or in village of Hinterberg itself.One thing that I was missing was the character customization. I really wish we could customize clothing of our character, unfortunately changing gear doesn't affect how Luisa looks. She looks good, but the game is long enough that I got a bit bored with her style.Visually its a fantastic game, color palette is well matched with each region and entire thing has this striking comic book style. Village of Hinterberg and surrounding areas look nice and cozy, but once you enter any dungeon it turns surreal, with levitating structures, unreal geometry and physics defying pathways. Personally I enjoyed the swamp dungeons the most, they look as if you are exploring ruins at the bottom of the ocean.Overall I highly recommend Dungeons of Hinterberg, its a fantastic breath of fresh air and a perfect summer game. Its also decently long, especially at that price. At the time of writing I put 19 hours into it and I still have a few of the most difficult dungens to go through and haven't seen the story finale. I think a lot of players will have fun with this one as it appeals to such a wide variety of people. Definitely give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Quite enjoyed it.  The combat is fun and the puzzles are satisfying.  Neither are particularly difficult, but it was enjoyable throughout.  The different magic in different regions kept the gameplay fresh, and prompted me to vary my combat styles more than I usually would in a game like this - which is probably a good thing.The length of the game felt just right; although maxing out all the social links was a bit of a grind (and unnecessary for beating the game/100%ing achievements).  Overall, definitely a 'recommend'.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: A nice comfy looking action adventure game. I really enjoyed the graphical style and tones of each region and dungeon, every dungeon distinguishing itself from others enough to feel uniquely different. The puzzle aspects of the game while not being very challenging making use of only two powers per region is surprisingly excellent, players won't be using the powers exactly the same way shows that Microbird made those powers with intent and creativity. Combat is probably my only real gripe about the game, which is probably some personal bias towards character action games but it is serviceable and at least quickly becomes less simple as the game progresses. If I could add anything it would be blocking and maybe giving Luisa some super armor on specific animations so she doesn't get staggered by chip damage. The bosses (excluding the final boss which was a little disappointing) are pretty good too, making good use of the powers in each area.I didn't 100% the socials of every character in the game but it's a nice way to break up dungeon diving, although the multiple choice dialog options on plot relevant choices bizarrely felt to have right/wrong selections. Possibly it would work better being able to respond with more than one choice while having a [CONTINUE CONVERSATION] option? Not sure.Overall I give it a solid/10, definitely recommend and eager for more from the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I've gone through 3 dungeons so far.  They scratch that Zelda dungeon itch in bite size pieces.  Unfortunately, some of the camera work gives me motion sickness, like when you're on a moving platform, and especially during some mine cart sections. They added an optional overlay setting to ease the motion sickness but WHY does it have to be buried at the bottom of the settings menu. I just want to flip it on during minecart sections.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like if A Short Hike, Zelda and Persona had a baby... but this baby is Sweet Baby Inc lol. Anyway, I enjoy it a lot so far, very nice gameplay and chill vibes.UPD: just finished the game and had a blast while playing every hour of it! One of the best games of the year I've played so far, highly recommend! My only 2 concerns are that I wish there were more fights cuz I really enjoyed combat and skills and also performance on Steam Deck is a bit unstable, especially in the last biome... Otherwise, a solid 9/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a lovely, lovely, delightful game. Dungeons of Hinterberg is a breezy, funny, charming take on dungeon crawling and adventure, with cozy austrian mountain town vibes, several endearing characters to befriend and spend time with, and numerous fun, imaginative dungeons to explore and conquer in between. It takes a while to get going, but once you've learned the systems, the story starts to pick up, you meet more and more likeable characters, and you get into the rhythm of the game and plan out your days like you were on holiday. It looks great, the skills are fun, the dungeons are fairly breezy, all in keeping with the more relaxed, holiday like experience and atmosphere. If you're looking for more tougher challenges, this might not quite scratch that itch, but I suppose you can also balance it by tackling tougher dungeons earlier.Story was surprisingly engaging once it starts moving, the characters are very charming and relatable, and the dialogue can get surprisingly heartfelt, introspective, thoughtful, touching on things like mental wellbeing, human connections, the effects of tourism and commercialization on nature etc. It's all just great stuff, and since there's no time limit, the day structure is never too stressful, if you don't see a character you wanted to spend time with one evening, you just do something else and talk to them the next evening instead.I also greatly appreciate any game with a range of equippable, upgradeable leggings.All in all, I'm really glad I played this and would love to see what the team will do next. This is one of the most charming and heartfelt games all year and you would do well not to miss out on the adventure.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons of Hinterberg is an excellent indie game and a mixture between Persona, Zelda and Après Ski. During the day, you get to slay monsters based on Austrian lore and solve puzzles. If you feel like just taking in the lovely views, that's also perfectly fine. In the evening, you get to spend some time with the (mostly) lovely inhabitants of Hinterberg and get to know them better. At night, you stay up way too late to watch TV because your amusement score is lagging behind. I loved the puzzles, they never felt too easy or too hard. The combat is not very difficult, but the different attack options bring some spice to it. Overall, I had a lovely time.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pleased that the game is rated 6+... because that's exactly what it is. A game for six-year-olds.The graphics have hardly been optimized. It's not like high-resolution textures are used here, etc... but it eats up too much performance.With all the praise and reviews, I thought there was a bit more to it than that and wasn't put off... Unfortunately.You don't even have to jump yourself... Just keep running and you jump automatically...As I said, it's a game for six-year-olds. Should really be emphasized a bit better...I recommend it... for six-year-olds... everyone else should think carefully about what they want to buy and the developers should perhaps learn some optimization... there's still a lot of work to be done.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: You come for the pretty visuals, and you stay for the puzzles <3This game has sooo much character! So vibrant and full of color, and Austrian cultural references everywhere. Where this game truly shines though, is - surprise - the dungeons. Each area is focused on a specific skill or ability, very similar to Zelda dungeons. This makes it never feel old as there's always something to explore. I really loved the puzzles, they made me feel smart and required a proper amount of trying solutions to solve. Bosses have a decent challenge too, not just in terms of skill but also in you figuring out the trick to beat them.Game feel is very smooth and the ice world is truly my favorite. I mean, who doesn't want to snowboard in the Alps?
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game! This isn't a deep or complicated title, but that's part of the point, I think.Each of the dungeons offer something unique and so they stay fresh for the entirety of the game, plus none of them are so long that they overstay their welcome. The developers of this game really found the sweet spot here and I was excited to jump into the next dungeon each time I sat down to play.The story and characters are wholesome and fun to get to know. The game encourages you to take your time, there's no rush. Get to know everyone, go to the movies, stay up late watching TV. It's a very introspective game, and a well written one at that.Overall, this is a real gem of a game. I was pretty sad when I finished it because I enjoyed it so much. Though, it did kind of make me feel like I need one of these "step away from everything" vacations...Kudos, Microbird Games! This was a lot of fun and I hope you revisit this in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice game with a gorgeous art style but not what I was expecting. Doesn't really scratch that Zelda itch - there is no adventure and exploration to be found here, it's more like the dungeons in cosy farming games. There is no overworld; you just wake up in the morning and warp to a region. Finish a dungeon and you're magically back at your hotel. The town is small but still segmented into even smaller chunks. Almost no buildings can be entered - pressing A on a shop door just pops up a menu interface. There doesn't seem to be any stakes or story, although I admit I am still near the beginning of the game. Everywhere you go you are walled in; having no jump button was definitely taken advantage of by the level designers - waist-high fences and rocks abound to keep you inside the small regions.I guess in the end I just don't really like cosy social games where you have to give gifts and choose who to spend your evening with etc. Not sure if there is a set number of days that you can spend on this "holiday" but it feels like there is, and the FOMO of not being able to talk to everyone and do everything is a real turn-off.But if it's your thing, this is a really slick and gorgeous game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.  Granted, I'm biased: I was a foreign service kid who was lucky enough to grow up in Switzerland and experience the Alps but I've always held it as one of the most beautiful parts of the world I've been able to experience.  This game captures the Alpine culture so well and does it with style.  It's built on such a cool premise and set in such a great location and pulls it all off exquisitely.  You can keep your post-apocalyptic worlds of various shades of gray and brown, I'll take a bright, beautiful world like this any day.  Since I can't take a vacation to Austria just yet, this game will fill the void quite nicely.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, just enough action to keep you engaged but not very challenging. Graphics are cartoon-like and pleasant, characters are likeable, the atmosphere is mostly relaxed and music keeps you focused. Recommended if you want to have a good time instead of a gruelling experience in a souls-like game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: what a criminally overlooked game. this may just be my favorite "zeldavania". at first glance it looks like a pretty simple dungeon crawler but i was not expecting this game to have such a great story along with a social features. and the dungeon themselves, each one has it's own theme and is all hand crafted with great scenery and puzzles. the combat itself is simple enough, light/heavy attacks along with specials and magic abilities.  and also the vibes, this is just the perfect game to chill to. not too hard, but not mundane either. seriously considering purchasing the soundtrack too.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I am about halfway through and thoroughly enjoying this adventure. If you're looking for 3D Zelda-like puzzle dungeons that won't have you tearing your hair out, and a souls-lite combat system with a surprising amount of customization, this is well worth your time.The gameplay loop has you dungeon delving during the day, then shopping and hanging out with NPCs in the evening to improve your relationship with them, which in turn provides stat boosts or even unlocks entire new mechanics. The art style is charming and, halfway through, the plot is good enough to keep me going. The dungeons and vibes alone are enough to keep playing, anyway. Challenge-wise, you're not looking at Dark Souls, but there's still plenty of room to adapt and grow into the game. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: A good game, if you want a better witcher combat, persona's relationship system, and zelda/botw's inspired dungeons; look no farther.Dungeoneering is the main focus. Most dungeons take about 15 to 45 minutes to complete and the puzzles are isolated enough that you won't bang your head against the wall too long. And this is one of the few games where 5-10 minor mobs are more likely to kill you than any boss encounters.The story doesn't start till the 2nd third, and it's not fancy but it works for the world they wanted. In this game there are 4 exploration areas, and each will give you a different magic combo. It helps the dungeons flow better as they are now built with you only able to use A & B skills, and the devs don't have to worry about you have X & Y instead. But naturally, everyone has they favorite layout, and while it's kinda nice they're made so there's not a huge preference, there will be an area I feel most players will be glade to get through; simply because those spells are lacking by comparasion.I can see how they will slot future DLC, either by adding local areas, or allowing you to go to other vacation spots.Overall, the dungeons are great and every other system is built to better serve that pillar. I can see this as a good example for play testing from a dev point of view for combat, and how they can expand on this. I'm eager to see how they will rework these system based off feedback for 'hinterberg 2'.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely lovely game. The amount of effort and love the team put in really shows on each corner.Up to the point as I was writing this review I played about 5 hours - the initial demo and a bit of the release version which shows a lot of tiny improvements to the demo.If you want to have a cozy vacation flair and you're a fan of Zeldalike 3D dungeon you will be very happy with Dungeons of Hinterberg.In terms of content there are 30 dungeons in the game, the ones i played took half an hour to an hour.There also is a cast of memorable characters you will interact and socialize with between your dungeon runs and those interactions mix up the game on multiple playthroughs.The game oozes holiday vibes, it also perfectly captures Austrian aesthetics, so if you want an adventure with an unusual setting, which is still grounded in a realistic place this is perfect.It's not a very hard game, although a very enjoyable one. Some puzzles definitely make you think. A few Qol things will feel a bit rough when directly compared to AAA games from first party developers and bigger studios, but also it's a cheaper title by a new team. The price is justified for the amount of high quality content you get. This is the studios first game and for that the amount of stuff which is done right far outweighs the few little rough edges. If next to a really solid game you also want to additionally feel good to support a smaller studio who put a lot of dedication in their game you can't go wrong with Dungeons of Hinterberg.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Love the pacing of the game. Battles are just challenging enough, everything feels fluid, and the puzzles make you think. Made it through three dungeons so far and i can't wait to play more. During the day you focus on dungeons or exploring and in the evening you explore the town and hang out with the locals. I thought that part would be boring, but the getting to know the npc's are fun and you have unlocks to work towards with npc. Overall, super fun and satisfying
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons of Hinterberg is exactly the kind of game I've wanted to play recently. Very chill vibe, fun systems that aren't overly complex, and great aesthetics. It's a perfect balance of exploration, combat, puzzle-solving, and socializing. The various systems combine seamlessly to provide the incentive to keep playing and avoid being frustrating by giving you different options to progress.While dungeoneering and socializing are the main mechanisms for moving the game along, you can always take a break from them and still get some benefit. Don't want to clear a dungeon? Find a lookout spot to hang out at and get a stat boost! Don't want to deal with the townsfolk? Go watch a movie or relax at the spa and get a stat boost! Nothing feels like a waste of time.I also found the characters to be quite relatable and actually grew rather found of a few of them. Luisa's feelings about her life's direction hit close to home, as I imagine they will for many people, so it was cathartic to help her out of her rut. And it would have been totally fine if the entire plot was just "clear all the dungeons," but there's a little bit of intrigue thrown in there, as well.I can definitely see myself returning to this game again in the future, and/or playing a sequel, should that be in the cards for Mircrobird. Either way, I will be keeping a lookout for whatever these devs produce in the future. Great game, easy recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Much like the theme, this game feels like an escape from, not only the mundane, but from other games. It takes elements from Breath of the Wild and Persona games but leaves behind the sometimes intimidating weight they carry. If you're looking for challenging puzzles, you won't find many here, but I never felt like my time was wasted. The game plays as more of a therapeutic experience, which is a welcome reprieve during a time when burnout is all too prevalent.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit that I wasn't a fan of this game's visuals at first, which almost led to ignoring it for good. I'm glad I gave it a try in the end, because the gameplay loop and overall design is engaging and FUN! I'm loving the mix of exploration, rpg elements and puzzle solving and I can't wait to fill my book with more stamps!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game!From the start, you can tell this game has had some love poured into it. The music, art, environment, characters, everything is stylized and polished to make an incredible package. Yes its fairly short, with 100% only taking me around 18 hours of playtime, but I do not regret the purchase!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute and cozy slayer where dungeons can be played in bite sized chunks, or a weekend can knock out dungeon after dungeon.  It's a perfect romp to spend your weekend, and has a fair bit of length as well.  I couldn't stop coming back to this for a bit.  The journey to Hintenberg was quite enjoyable!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game hits all the itches, you want to relax, relax. you want to slay, slay. you want to run around and do nothing all day thats awesome too. This dungeon crawler has a little bit of everything, without making it feel like its giving you too much.  Theres so much to this game and I feel like I have only scratched the surface. Its cozy where it needs to be cozy, the battles are well placed, and the puzzles are a blast to solve. over all mechanics of the game is fairly easy to learn as well. Please at least try this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start? What a great game! Style was straight out of a comic. Vibes were amazing, visuals and sounds as well. Gameplay is so simple and straightforward. Would really recommend to anyone who just want to vibe and fight quirky and challenging dungeons. Only downside is the concept of choice. It's great that they included dialouge options between characters to further the story and unlocking perks but there isn't any choice when it comes to tackling a dungeon. It would be great if there's an option to decline to explore the dungeons. Other than that amazing game! Truly! Kudos to the creators and hopefully we can have a DLC or an expansion or a sequel to this game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Over all it is a pretty good game. The dungeon gameplay is really fun and there are some extremely creative dungeons and bossfights, especially towards the end of the game.The game has two major problems though: The movement sucks and all the socializing and dialogues also sucks.The movement for any sort of platforming is absoluetly awful. There is no jump button - the game will automatically jump/climb upon ledges when it feels like it, whether you like it or not. This produces a lot of infuriating moments in which simply decending from a platform becomes an unnecessarily tedious task.The game has, somewhat unexpectedly, a huge focus on the story and socializing with NPCs and interacting with them. There are four different social stats which you can improve by spending time with different NPCs. Leveling up your relationship with an NPCs sometimes also unlocks other useful stats or tools. This in itself is fine, however, there is way too much dialogue that you have to click through. Somewhat often you are prompted with three different replies you can choose from. It does not matter which option you click on. The dialogue is completely pointless, nothing really matters. The NPCs themselves are mostly exaggerations of a single cliche character trait. All of this would be fine if it wasn't such a huge part of the game. Every minute you have to sit through some garbage dialogue, all you can think of is the dungeons you are currently missing out on.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Mhh, I don't know. I've played about halfway through now and while I like the unique setting and the whimsical art style, ultimately the game is pretty boring, a bit frustrating and anticlimatic.What makes it boring:- Collectibles are always in the same spots, which invites to always take the same routes over and over again- Not a lot of enemy variety- Very easy puzzles- Pretty rigid gameplay routines (aka gameplay loop)What makes it frustrating:- Mainly how it feels to control the player character. Which is to say: stiff. This applies to both the movement while exploring, but especially to the combat.- The timings between landing consecutive hits is so tightly paced, that it practically requires button mashing to land combos. There's no real rhythm to it.- Small things like the targeting system, which seems to pick a target at random, even when an enemy is standing right in front of me.What makes it anticlimatic:- No bosses?? What kind of dungeons are these?- Dare I say, the music. It rarely contributed to the atmosphere.Can't really understand all the Ocarina of Time comparisons. Aside from enviromental puzzles, (semi-)kooky characters and the ability to automatically jump from ledges I don't see much in common. This is coming from a major Zelda fan.On the plus side:- I like the art style a lot (maybe what drew me in in the first place)- The dialogue is nicely written, very contemporary and authentic imo.- Some cool mechanic ideas (charm shrinking for example)- Just a really original idea for a settingIn the end, I think, if it were more fluid and fun to actually control the character, I would have been more forgiving, that's really the biggest flaw.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game... I don't know...It is a good game, but it could be so much better.There are many things to do. like befriending people, collecting monster parts, visiting scenic points, collecting trash and so on.All with the goal to become stronger. None of it is necessary.Because the game is easy. Way too easy.The puzzles are easy, the hidden items are easy to find. Combat is more of an annoyance then a challenge and feels as if it is there only to prolong the playtime. It can be fun though the first few times you fight a new kind of monster.The bosses are... you can guess it... way too easy but with interesting mechanics.You can stay up late at night, watching TV or reading a Book to boost stats that do basically nothing. As a drawback you start the next day with -25% HP. The game suggests that you are too weak for a dungeon and should spend the next day with with a relaxing activity (like visiting the cinema, the spa or a scenic point) to boost your stats even more.It is just not necessary. You could do the next dungeon even with -90% HP. So many interesting ideas and concepts. But sadly you need none of them. I ended up befriending 3 people for the achievement and more or less ignored the rest. Collected some monster parts, not for the power boost... for the achievement.The story is not too bad but nothing to phone home about. Also it suffers from general unnecessary "wokeness" but I guess that is pretty normal these days and may be forced by the Austrian government. So why recommended?It is an interesting concept with cool monsters taken from Austrian folk tales. It has lot of potential, with its elements from Zelda, Persona and so on. Could be as good as them if not so much potential was wasted.But the price is fair for what you get. It is fun for the first 15-20h (a playthrough with all achievements takes about 30h) and interesting enough to finish it. For a 1st time game of a little Indi studio from a country that isn't exactly popular for making good games (or games at all) it is really good. Give them some budget and time and there could be great games.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: For a story based on you becoming a "slayer," the combat is very clunky and doesn't feel good. The games art style and world building is beautiful, but it just fell flat for me on the game-play aspect. I see other reviews comparing this game to Zelda, calling it "The Zelda that PC Needed," and I feel that's incredibly far-fetched.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons of Hinterberg is definitely recommended for people who enjoyed the Zelda games from previous console generations and PS2-era adventure games that have tight but semi-open environments.I really enjoyed the mix of cozy game, adventure game, and Persona-like social connections. The team put together the balance of the game well and gave it just the right amount of depth without making it tedious or having it overstay its welcome.The puzzles are basic and can be somewhat challenging but you figure them out pretty quickly if you've played games with similar puzzles in the past. The dungeons and areas are varied enough to provide a good change of pace when you've enjoyed the scenery of one area long enough. I really enjoyed the variety of the magic skills and how they're tied to each area - juggling too many magic skills becomes a hassle in other games and DoH avoided that pitfall. Some may say it's too simple but I believe that's part of the charm of the game - simple, cozy, straight-forward, and enjoyable.The characters were enjoyable to get to know and none of the characters felt like they wouldn't exist in real life. Even the character that starts off the worst gets fleshed-out and you begin to understand them. There were a number of characters that were bundles of love and joy and that was delightful. Some characters didn't receive as much love as others but were still enjoyable to get to know. While I didn't max links with every character I did enjoy the time I spent with them.There were a couple of things that have room for improvement of course. The simpleness is good, but I would have enjoyed being able to upgrade my conduits and enchantments. I was also surprised by the lack of elements on weapons as they're somewhat present in combat but I don't think it took much away from the game as the combat wasn't supposed to be too in-depth and I don't believe the lack of elements took away from the gameplay nor do I believe it would have added that much. I played on hard difficulty and had minimal trouble completing combat encounters when appropriately leveled. A few more small critiques of the combat system: at the higher difficulty the enemies sometimes felt like damage sponges and, near the end of the game, 3-4 waves of enemies became less exciting as you would sometimes have to dodge multiple projectiles continuously.The forced perspective moments in the game were the only truly jarring thing in this game. Many areas would switch to static or forced perspectives that diminished my enjoyment of the dungeon in that moment but overall did not ruin the entire experience. I would have just preferred they weren't there. I'm looking forward to what this team can do next. A direct sequel would be more than welcome in my book but I would also enjoy if they had a different protagonist for the next game. I'm glad I paid full price to support a developer with this much potential.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s always a good thing when you go to bed excited to wake up and play a game the next day. That’s a pretty good way to know whether someone recommends a game or not, and in case the big blue thumb didn’t give it away, I do recommend  as a fun, cozy-adjacent action game with neat puzzle dungeons. This is a game that has a setting I liked from the start, and I appreciate that it’s realistic in the way that weird things would be if we saw them happen around us. 25 magical dungeons pop up in modern times, which would cause a huge uproar and be international news within seconds, probably causing loads of panic and chaos in the process. In this game, people get over it and learn to live with the magical dungeons being in their backyards, and then the most realistic thing ever happens when people decide to monetize the dungeons by turning the town of Hinterberg into a tourist trap. The main character, Luisa, shows up for that reason. Looking for an escape from her unsatisfying life as a junior lawyer in Vienna, she recalls how she felt like every new place she went to growing up was like an adventure, so she comes to Hinterberg to challenge the dungeons to get a little adventure back in her life. She took classes back home to prepare, and when she shows up, she gets a beginner course in tackling these little magical dimensions around everywhere. Something as wild and dangerous as fighting magic monsters ends up being so normal that it becomes a major relaxation activity to do on vacation with beginner trials and training.That sort of idea is one thing I liked about  in particular. In that game, the unique shine of the supernatural and abnormal quickly wears off and everything becomes normal for the people who live in the direct orbit of what used to be wild and unnatural. At the risk of getting too real over a video game, this is one of the most human reactions someone can have. If you just give it enough time and live with it long enough, what’s weird and hard to understand becomes normal, and in this game, becomes a flourishing backbone for a small town’s economy, attracting a bunch of people. And the people are, as one might expect, the heartbeat and soul of the game and story. There’s a cast of colorful, unique characters that you meet during your vacation, each with their own reasons for being in Hinterberg, their own opinions on magic and the dungeons, and differing takes, benefits, and losses that come with their home being a tourist trap. It’s all very real and human without getting too deep and depressing, and toward the end of the game,  is one of my favorite games of all time, so this game having these social and relationship-building aspects be core gameplay elements is very appealing to me. While plenty of games have relationship elements to them, I love it when games like these have deeper relationship systems that flesh out the narrative and lore while using them as ways to improve the action gameplay. By the time I was wrapping up the game, I maxed out everyone’s relationship status just because I wanted to see what they had to say, which is a little bit of a rarity in the games I play. Another area where this game is like  is how it splits its time management system. During the morning, you have the chance to explore small maps that contain dungeons and monsters to whack with your sword. You can also find scenic spots to use the time slot and increase stats without having to complete a dungeon each day, which still gives you something productive to do if you don’t feel like completing a dungeon.I will add that I think the balance of dungeons and non-dungeon activities is a bit skewed. If you wanted to blitz through the game, you only have 25 dungeons to beat, so it likely wouldn’t take more than 30 or 35 in-game days. I did every social interaction I could with the characters and it took me over 70 in-game days to talk to everyone, get their dialogues, and max out their relationships. I know I didn’t do everything perfectly, but I don’t think I messed up my time management that badly. Back to the  comparison, the game will sort of give you the implication you’re on a timed vacation. I can’t remember if the game tells you at any point you don’t actually have a time limit to worry about, but you don’t. This isn’t like Persona where if you don’t do the critical path by a certain date, a teenage girl gets eaten by monsters, or your predator volleyball coach gets you expelled from school. You know, totally normal high school things you’d expect to deal with on a regular basis. The only condition to clear the game is clearing all 25 dungeons, with no real roadblocks, so you have as much time as you want to talk with characters or do other things. If my 70-day game doesn’t convince you of that, the developers have confirmed that there is no time limit, despite how the game might imply Luisa is only in Hinterberg for a “little while”. Don’t worry, relax, and do everything you want to do before you beat the game. I didn’t think the story was going to be much of anything, and without wishing to write a bunch to block out as a spoiler, it proved me wrong. The story starts a little light on the ground without any grand cutscenes depicting shadowy figures enacting their plan. That makes sense given the context and why Luisa’s in Hinterberg to begin with. The story does a good job integrating its characters and gaining some depth and a little bit of intrigue as it goes on. Moving to the game’s combat, it does the job. Sadly, it's largely mashing a couple of buttons until your big, overpowered attacks can be used again, and it doesn’t evolve much past that. You get better gear so your number matches the number on the dungeon, but the only things that change are the magical attacks and powerful Attack Conduits, the latter being something you can change out to attacks you prefer. There are some neat puzzle boss fights that mix the combat and the game’s -esque dungeon puzzles, but those are few and far between the rest of the dungeons. I’d recommend avoiding the highest difficulty, as it doesn’t make the game harder in any meaningful way. It just makes everything take longer. The dungeons and their puzzles help to make up for the iffy combat. The puzzles are fun, usually simple enough that someone dumb like me kept overthinking them until the solution slapped me in the face. They do a great job of making the most out of each area’s two powers you get, even if one of those is just grinding along a rail on a magical snowboard. The dungeons having their own unique vibes to them, even when they have similar aesthetics to other ones, making each one a little treat to go through without feeling like they're taking too long. There isn’t a whole lot of flexibility in the puzzle design, though, which may be a good thing or a bad thing depending on your personal preference. If you like things to be a little more open-ended with multiple solutions, you may feel frustrated to find out there’s essentially only one way to do things. This ended up being one of those games I was sad ended. The fun, charming experience that never had an unwelcome point in it, and it ended exactly when it should have. It never outstayed its welcome and it made the most of the space it had. Even when all I was doing was returning to end the day early just to do social interactions, it never felt tedious or annoying because of how enjoyable I found the characters. If a game that mixes elements of  and  in a cauldron with fun characters and a story that is both silly and surprisingly real, pick this up, kick back, and enjoy a nice game filled with charm.

_childDocuments_.review: General Opinion:Solid 7/10 game though a bit bloated. 26 dungeons were a bit much for this game as it didn't really have enough variety in the dungeons to justify a game of that size and very few bosses. I actually forgot the game had bosses for long time as the time between the first and second boss is filled with like 10 of the general dungeons. I also couldn't tell if there was a timer element or not as the game continually countdown the days while massive issues were occurring in the town, so if there wasn't one kudos for making me think there was. Finally bit for the general review please make the game rewind to before the final dungeon after you beat the game so the player can finish the character stories without restarting the whole title.Story Opinion (Spoilers)*The biggest disappointment for me was the story not because it was bad per-say but they had a very good moral dilemma they introduce but then decide to just paint one side as cartoonishly evil that it ended up falling flat and disappointing. About halfway through the game its reveal magic doesn't like being used as a toy for tourists and is actively rebelling against the town to be completed but the moral dilemma comes in as a lot of people's livelihoods are associated with the town being a tourist spot and closing the dungeons would likely greatly affect the town. The game even presents the dungeons as a great place to relax and find yourself even the main character is greatly affected by the town so it had an interesting dilemma as who are you as an outsider to decide what is good for this town and potentially ruin the lives of many people who live here.Great setup and a hard question to answer, so how does the game answer it? By having the main antagonist turn into the mayor from Jaws. Her stance becomes so unreasonable and her motivation stops having any weight as the entire town basically turns against her and is falling apart. She just doubles downs on it with no great justification for her actions going forward unlike before where she seemed to actually care about growing the town. The message turns into a generic capitalism is bad and respect the environment message with no nuance. The title doesn't show the effect on the town for losing its main attraction and how that ended up effecting the town for better and worse. Everything is better because you decided to force your way through the dungeons for a town the character doesn't really have the claim to make that decision.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this. It has Zelda-like mini dungeons with a really chill vibe and a cool art style. There are also some light Persona-like elements with building relationships for perks and gaining social stats between dungeon runs. The puzzles are where this game shines. They hit the same sweet spot where they're not all trivially easy but also also aren't likely leave you completely stuck. Combat is serviceable but does start to get a bit dull after a while, and it gets a bit annoying how many of the small enemies actively make you chase them around.One thing the game managed to do especially well so far is keep the dungeons from feeling too similar to each other. I don't want to spoil too much, but basically while dungeons in the same area might share the same theme, the game is not afraid to play with mechanics and perspectives, and that keeps the dungeons fresh and creates a feeling of anticipation when entering a new one.One QoL update I'd like to see is better enchantment management. The tutorial tells you they're removable, but they're not removed automatically when you sell old gear, and I didn't see any kind of warning either, so you're likely to lose them unless you buy back the gear and remove the enchantments.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a delightful charm and a wonderful time. It's a very unique experience that's made from very familiar parts but wrapped up and executed in a delightfully fresh way.Yes, the game is basically the action-adventuring of  mixed with the social link elements of  while clad in the very down to earth and realistic themes and story of , and the game knows exactly how to mix and match those elements in proportion to make a fully realised setting that characters can organically grow from while they operate around a core central element for the gameplay and premise. The cast is great, the worldbuilding is phenomenal, and it's all extremely well presented.As a writer, I have tremendous respect for how the developers have taken real life attitudes and politics towards mountain climbing and made a game about that but through the lens of video game dungeoneering. I think there could be a touch more philosophy on the game—like how mountaineering, video games, and escapism intersect with real life—but that's just personal preference and the game is already solid enough; there's clearly a lot of knowledge here with how people and tourists impact the natural environments they flock to, especially mountains where even the most controlled of tourist environments can be lethal hazards. Do you know how many people litter on Mount Everest? Do you know who has to clean all that up? If you know anything about that, then so many characters and themes and events in  will make a tremendous amount of sense to you.All of this is wrapped in a very well executed loop. You go out into the wilds, find dungeons or relaxing scenic spots, go back to town to do some shopping and build relationships with a charming variety of characters, rest up, and do it all again tomorrow. I'd especially like to talk about the scenic spots, because the writing in this game is so solid and really understands why people take vacations and the positive effect they can have on you and how the average working life isn't meant to serve us. It really is masterful understanding of their themes and inspiration that helps to deliver a game like this.On a side note, I love that Luisa's sword has an ergonomic grip and a wrist strap, and I really like how all the slayers are dressed like athletes and mountain climbers. It's details like that that really help to sell a story's themes through their aesthetics.On top of that, dying isn't really a thing. If you die, the screen just flashes black and you end up right back where you started. I don't mind this at all;  is about having a relaxing retreat from life, as Luisa exemplifies time and again, and this helps to communicate that while minimising frustrations. I do have quite a few complaints, however:I think all of these are understandable. All in all, I'm really glad to have played  and kudos to the devs for putting it all together; I am very impressed!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mix between Dark Souls and modern Persona games. A former ski resort town accidentally accessed the dungeon dimensions, events proceeded from there, and now you're on a dungeon vacation and you have vacation stats to build up - Familiarity (with the town), Renown (with monster slayers), Relaxation and Amusement. Pick a biome to open-world explore in the day, each with its own set of magic powers you can resonate with, and then after lunch either run a dungeon for renown and hit points or just spend time out there taking it easy for relaxation and another stat from your chill-out spot.If you played the demo, you know how a dungeon goes. You get light and heavy attacks and a stamina-dependent dodge roll, and biome magic and weapon special attacks that recharge as you fight. Biome magic is also free to use out of combat for puzzle-solving. There's easy/normal/hard for difficulty, but at least on normal, losing in combat (or platforming into a pit) isn't actually the end of the day. You get unlimited retries but each combat instance resets, so you can't just throw yourself at something way out of your league and win by attrition, but if you want to challenge yourself you can keep going until you can beat the whole thing.In the evening, run around the town, give gifts to as many people you're on good terms with as you want to (all gifts will build friendship a little bit but if it was a good gift you'll get something back), and hang out with whoever in the town you want to and have enough vacation stats to manage an intro. There's a nice variety - old tourists, new tourists, influencers, slayer celebrities, townies who are sick of this ♥♥♥♥, townies who are all about this ♥♥♥♥, and one very good boy. You can have an evening for yourself at one of the town's tourist spots too - catch a movie, row out on the lake, pick a local restaurant. There's lots to do and the dungeons are only as much of a pressure as you want them to be.Optionally, stay up a little late (and debuff your HP) to boost a vacation stat in your room in the lonely night hours.The art style is cel-shaded with screentones and has big bande dessinée vibes if those two words mean anything to you, and the music is nicely dynamic, responding to motion through each area and the use of your biome magic.It takes a little bit of time for all the systems to come online, and a few of them are linked to building relationships in town, but the early game didn't feel too confining to me without them.

My particular point of annoyance is a girl, you're forced into a relationship with, who asks if she can sit with you without allowing for an answer. Afterwards, she is the person you have to go to the town festival with or won't be able to go there at all. Whisked away by her for a drink only after the mayor's speech with the “I won't take a 'no' for an answer” method, so you can't even see a single second of said festival. I reserve toxic relationships for a second gameplay, thank you very much.Linear games are okay, if you have great gameplay, which is average here, but the narrative is so forced that I don't get why did they introduce the illusion of choice at all, as it is so transparent.

Thankfully I had another save right before the bug occurred or I would have had to start all over again from the beginning of the entire game.These issues are inexcusable and until they are fixed I cannot give this game a good review.

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful game, nice music, inspired setting, nice player character. Could easily be my best liked game of 2024. High praise to the developers and design artists for that.Why not recommended?Due to sponsorship from the german and austrian state the story is heavily DEI infested. They are even proud of it!Extremely exclusive to normal people. All native inhabitants of the very beautiful town (who built it and fill it with live) are grey stereotype silhouettes from far and faceless if you get closer. They literally dissolve when you walk past them.All white male story characters are silly whiny dorks which are useless. You can guess gender, skin color and gender identity of positive characters. Put it all together and you get the characteristics of your primary contact ... to the local austrian lore and history. Talk about cultural appropriation. This is a prime example. The day has a strict given cycle: Morning talk to your diverse mentor, dungeon delving, shopping, social evening events with shallow or manipulative conversations,  bedtime (TV and books tease you, but are forbidden). _childDocuments_.review: I know this game reviewed well. But I wanted to add my voice to the chorus to really pitch how charming this experience is. The gameplay is like a cross between Persona's life sim mechanics combined with action dungeon gameplay that reminds me of the Zelda games. A few puzzles, a few bosses, a lot of fun general monsters and environments. There has been more and more Persona-likes coming out. But what sets this one apart, is this small touch of the dungeons. Every dungeon has a unique gimmick/mechanic. This is really cool. It makes me interested in taking on every new dungeon, it makes then all stand out in my brain. Every adventure feels just that little bit special. But also none of these special mechanics sticks around so long that it gets boring.Since the game is trying to give the impression of exploring and discovering on a tourist trip, this lack of "sameiness" is awesome. I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still yet to finish Dungeons of Hinterberg, but i can assure you that this is one of many story rich/fighting styled games I've greatly enjoyed playing for hours on end.The soundtracks are amazing, the unique monsters n dungeons, cosmetics n the friendships you make along the way and not to forget the easy achievable achievements as well.Hands down an amazing game to get lost into for hours, deffs suggest giving Dungeons of Hinterberg a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Chill vibe action adventure game. Approachable. Puzzles aren't incredibly tough but dungeons are still fun. On normal difficulty, combat is not too challenging but non-trivial if you wander into an area you're not geared up for yet. Given a choice between paths to an objective with each having a fight, I'd go back and do the other one, too, because I enjoyed the combat but also didn't find it draining of resources. I'm doing new game+ now and upped the combat difficulty setting and it's much more challenging, which is also nice.Mixed feelings about the time management mechanic, with days divided into one part for dungeons and one part for pursuing character relationships. On the one hand, it makes it easier to divide the game up into smaller chunks of playtime, which is nice if you don't necessarily have time to sit down and play indefinitely. On the other, I'm not personally really into having to pick and choose which relationships to develop and having to either leave some behind or else ignore the sense of urgency the plot tried to engender and just "waste" the afternoon dungeoneering periods after exhausting the dungeons and optional scenic spots. I'm interested in most of the characters and what they have going on. I suppose I just wish I'd delayed less on the first run and left more of them for the second playthrough on new game+.Also, it seems like the game just kind of lies to you about being able to speed up relationship development through gift giving, etc? That's... Just kind of weird.Overall, I enjoyed it and I may not finish the whole new game+ run but I'm going to probably at least go through until I finish the remaining character relationships.

_childDocuments_.review: Super chill game. A cute and fun hack n slash with Persona-like(and lite) social elements. I really enjoyed this one. The combat isn't super deep, there's a few options in terms of special attacks and also magic spells (which are different depending on which area you are exploring) but it's nothing super complex or difficult. But it gets the job done. The social system is pretty sweet, its really just you hanging out with a bunch of new people in this vacation town. One of those people is a dog, so the system is already great. As mentioned very Persona-esque, you hang out with people and when your relationships level up, you get special perks that will usually benefit your dungeon crawling. Even though it isn't the deepest, just like the combat it still does the job. In fact I'd say the social elements are pretty close to great. If this game got a sequel or successor I would love to see more expanded relationships alongside combat.You can tell there was a lot of love for this project from the devs. The whole theme is escaping from a mundane life back home to an idyllic vacation in a faraway place where nobody even knows your name. Yet. A little town that used to be quiet until it experienced a tourism boom. It explores concepts like gentrification and its affect on the environment and people who have to live in them. But for me the theme that resonated most was that escape from life back home. Taking a risk and ditching the capitalistic grind of a life of monotonous, unfulfilling labor. That's good stuff.There's also some intriguing mysteries going on behind the scenes, which you uncover as you progress through the dungeons. But even as you slowly peel that away, the game never REALLY drops that feeling of being on vacation for too long. The term "cozy game" gets used a lot nowadays, bevause it can mean different things for different people. I can't get into a lot of those games because it's a lot of farming or grinding resources, never been a huge fan, but I still love the idea of those cozy games. I think this is that kind of game, for me. I can choose to skip the dungeon and zen out for a bit, hang out with the characters in town, and just generally chill out. But I won't get too bored since I can spend an afternoon of my vacation diving into a dungeon and fighting monsters. Sure the combat is a little on the easy side and could stand to be a bit tougher, but its simplicity is also very relaxing. A really good time. Hope to see more from this in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's just get it out of the way; if you're someone who has been clambering for a game that captures the feeling of the traditional 3D Zeldas you need look no further. The actual dungeons in  are an absolute treat. Featuring plenty of unique and awe inspiring moments from all angles whether that be regarding the puzzle design or the action segments. As an FYI the game's structure is based on a calendar system, something that I don't think I've seen before in this kind of genre surprisingly. Through this it establishes multiple areas that you can only go to once an in game day, that feature a different kit for the hero. Those dungeons in said areas then revolve around the associated abilities. The benefit of this is that the player can then pick and dip into different puzzle dynamics to their taste. That isn't to say the different same area dungeons all feel similar puzzle wise- far from it- but it opens up the idea that the game can build up it's puzzle concepts in a non linear way. In fact most of  core gameplay ends up being focused around these abilities you get that are locked to each area. Combat without these unique moves while fun on it's own would start to get stale without them, and enemy groups in these areas also enforce learning/using these spells in subtle ways. Honestly after writing that out it makes me realize how much that points back to the main story as well. Beyond gameplay the sights and sound of Hinterberg are incredible, I would often just get lost staring at the sky in this game. All while being enveloped with a soft, synth focused soundtrack that brings you there instantly. From an immersive standpoint it felt as much like a vacation for me as it did for the main character. Once again just a super well rounded action adventure. Great atmosphere, combat, puzzle solving and everything. One that I feel I'll remember for a long time to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I find the game relaxing.You're not tied to any kind of time-based quest and you can do whatever you want, whether it's exploring Dungon or just sitting around. You also have very good music and a great art style. Admittedly, the game can get a little boring at times, but that's really just a minor nitpick. So if you want to get away from all the fast paced games and just relax for an afternoon, I can only recommend this game. PS: There is a dog that makes the game great.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very chill game that has enough dept without over complicating things. Has a few elements taken from Persona games (social links, a daily calendar with limited activities), but here I don't feel FOMO when I decide how to spend my time. This game just clicked with me and I'm playing it at a slow pace to enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful mix of challenging combat, huge variety in dungeon design (pretty much no two dungeons have the same gimmick), and a Persona style system of social links, all set in a gorgeous alpine village, and with a gripping story about mass tourism. One of the best games, in my opinion, that came out in 2024. Highly recommended. The playthrough is quick, but still leaves you satisfied, and because of the social links I will be going back for another playthrough in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game was mostly fun from beginning to end. It only got to be a bit of a slog once I tried to complete it, filling out relationships, monster club quest (until I discovered a charm), among a few other things. In my honest opinion, do not try to do everything optional. Just talk to those who give good bonuses and who you find interesting. Overall though it was a blast. The combat is fun, and with the spells changing per area, it stays fresh. The music, while not fully memorable, is fitting and often times relaxing. The setting, personally, was amazing. I loved all of the areas, though I always did prefer the alps to the tropics.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.4/10. My game of the year for 2024. _childDocuments_.review: One of the most amazing gaming experiences I've had in the last while. _childDocuments_.review: this game is a little gem that completely flew under the radar until I found it on sale. it sparked enough interest that I ended up purchasing it and still haven't regretted anything. graphics is cozy and clean, while the gameplay mixes a Legend of Zelda dungeon crawler style with puzzles and combat with some Persona relationships with several NPCs that will unlock stores, items and upgrades.but the most important detail is that Dungeons of Hinterberg gives me the desire to keep playing, something that few recent games do.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: If you’ve ever played Summer in Mara and liked it, you’re gonna fell in love with Dungeons of Hinterberg. In my opinion it has similar charming atmosphere, but with a twist - combat! This game has everything a cozy yet adventurous soul could ask for... combat, leveling up, gear, cute dog (BIG + for developer) and some solid RPG mechanics to keep things interesting. Honestly, I’m impressed by how they kept the gameplay engaging most of the time. I noticed it was discounted with 50% off 3 months after release, which usually isn’t a good sign, right? But it allowed more people to check it out, spread the word, and maybe (hopefully) this game will find viral moment. You should 100% trust me  this game definitely deserves some recognition. We need more games like this, a refreshing break from the usual.Pros:+ Charming, cozy vibes, but with combat.  + Beautiful graphics and scenery. + Full translation to my native language - and it’s actually done well! Rarely do I play games fully translated, but it was a pleasure here. + Immersive storytelling - I was genuinely hooked on the story, which doesn’t happen often. + RPG mechanics (stats etc.). Cons:- I had a little bit strange first impression before you get used to the game, f.e. there is specific day cycle you need stick to. - I think friendship leveling system need to be reworked - why gatekeep friendships so hard? I barely hit max level with any character until the end of the dungeons. By then, it was kind of pointless since I was already near the end of the game. And then gatekeeping sales in shops by some friendship levels hit me.. I was a little bit disapointed. - Again - late-game bonuses are meh - The bonuses from friendships (like Hannah, Julian, or even the dog) came way too late to be useful. By the time I unlocked them, I didn’t really need them anymore.- Gifts feel meaningless - gifts didn’t really help with relationships increase. Also, there’s no visible friendship meter, so you’re kinda left guessing if your efforts are doing anything. It was frustrating a bit.But in the end Dungeons of Hinterberg is a great game with a lot of potential. A few changes to the friendship and gift mechanics could make it even better. But if you’re into cozy games with a bit of action, give it a shot! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Well.I wasn't expecting to have this much fun or to find such joy and relaxation in this game as I have. The gameplay itself can be clunky at times and sometimes a little brutal, but it has a decent pacing to it and a sizable amount of spells and abilities to toy with.I wish there was an option to not use a sword, but the sword thing is part of the character you play as. I enjoyed the social system a LOT more than I expected to, and found exploring areas as well as just sitting and existing to be valid ways to wile away the days.I am going to try  to 100% this one. I cannot reccommend this game enough for people who enjoy combinations of rpg, action and roleplaying.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightfully relaxing game with a gorgeous art style. The scenery takes me back to mountains I visited long ago. The exploration, puzzling and simple combat remind me of the best of Zelda games, Ocarina of Time. It seems like since Nintendo discovered the commercial appeal of crafting with Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, we are unlikely to see a simple dungeon explorer like this again so it is a joy to visit the Dungeons of Hinterberg. And the Persona-like social sim in town each day just adds to the chill. Oh, and the music! I bought the OST so I can feel it when I'm at work.Thoroughly enjoying my Slaycation!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game really is something special. When I first heard reviews, I did not think this would be my type of game. I was absolutely wrong about that. The story is great, the combat is really fun, and the way the game has the day cycle really makes you feel that you have choices that actually make a difference in how the game plays out.  The difficulty also always feels just right.If you are on the fence, so was I, and i really haven't put the game down since I got it. Its also a rare game that from almost the start i was interested in trying to complete all achievements, which i feel is also a decent amount of difficulty but not too much. Note: I have not yet beaten this game, but only have a few dungeons left.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve just finished this game, and I think it’s a little hidden gem. Let's start with what you can expect: I’d describe it as a wholesome action RPG with a “Persona Lite” vibe, wrapped in charming graphics.The day is split into four phases, each offering different activities depending on the time of the day. For example, in the afternoon, you’ll explore areas and complete dungeons, while in the evening, you’ll prepare for the next day and build friendships. There’s no time limit, and the game always informs you when an activity will transition you to the next phase, making it stress-free.The battles are engaging, with a modern action combat system, and the puzzles add variety. The game experiments with many different ideas, not all of them worked for me, but I appreciated the creativity, and the variety kept the experience fresh.That said, the game isn’t without its flaws. Some animations can feel a bit stiff, and the dialogue with characters is often disconnected from the story. I also wish the game acknowledged your daily actions more—a dynamic system like the one in "Hades" would have added more depth here.Despite these rough edges, the game's charm, unique scenario, and innovative ideas make it an absolute must-try—especially at this price point. It might not be perfect, but its heart and ambition shine through.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: Alpinist propaganda: the game. Very open ended character growth, magic spells are actually usable in combat AND exploration (tornado is awkward). Coins could be better placed in many dungeons (Tower of Trials is perfection). Wish I had 2 evenings to hang out with the townspeople everyday, there are so many things to do then and "only" 25 dungeons. Each overworld looks good and is magical to experience for the first time, but the feeling wears off after, like, the second time.Dungeons of Hinterberg – pretty nice. I'm waiting for more games by the Austrian Ministry of Tourism.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I greatly enjoyed this game.  It was right at my difficulty level, with combat and puzzles difficult enough to be fun but hard.  I don't normally like much character interaction, but  I came to enjoy it and appreciate the different characters and what they had to offer.  The layers of strategy were fun to figure out.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: The visual, narrative, and thematic identities of Dungeons of Hinterberg are very strong and were compelling for me even when things veered into the realm of obviousness. The game mechanics and elements are on the simple side but not to the extent that they are uninteresting. The game is very adept at leveraging its vision and design to make almost every dungeon a different sort of experience; there's a fair amount of variation and puzzles even within the same areas and I looked forward to finding out what was in store each time I attempted a new one; the limiting the types of magic to each region allowed for a more focused experience in terms of puzzles.The game is a little on the easy side as far as action-y combat goes but that's not the real draw of the game anyhow. Things can be a little grind-y if you're trying to do every side quest but, on the whole, it is a very well-paced game that doesn't overstay its welcome. I would have liked an extra optional area of two with more challenging puzzles but that complaint is less about the amount of content and more a reflection of how I enjoyed the novel twists in the dungeons and would have appreciated seeing the talents of the developer put to further work.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: I tried Dungeons Of Hinterberg because I was looking to play a game which normally I wouldn't. And indeed, DOH is not a typical selection for me, but I am so glad I played it.The game is wonderfully realized.The world it creates is full of delights, danger, mystery and whimsy. The Dungeons are challenging and engaging without being frustrating.The upgrade and character development trees are well thought out and expansive.Some upgrades and perks take you further than others.Luisa starts to get powerful when you have a dozen plus charms shrunk down to 1 slot each.Going for the pro sword, armor, pads and leggings will make the latter dungeons a lot easier on you.The characters are relatable and endearing without being flat. The story has a nice message and the game play is enjoyable.4.5 out of 59 out of 10A+
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons of Hinterberg

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of those rare gems that completely immerses you, making you feel like you could actually live and thrive in its world. The town and scenery are breathtakingly beautiful, to the point where just watching a nature or town scene can bring a sense of peace and awe. I adore the music, the densely packed and vibrant town, the natural progression of time, and the freedom to choose evening activities and build friendships with NPCs. The dungeon puzzles are genuinely enjoyable. It's evident that the creators poured their passion into crafting this game and its world, and that enthusiasm shines through. Truly a delightful and immersive experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the combat being a little underwhelming, I thoroughly enjoyed exploring each dungeon that Hinterberg had to offer. Just like the game’s premise, playing through each day felt like a touristy hybrid of well-constructed adventures and pleasant afternoon downtime.There was no shortage of clever thematic twists to each dungeon. The puzzles aren’t exactly head-scratchers, but they usually do a good job of illustrating the potential of the mechanics they revolve around. Each area’s unique pair of intuitive abilities, which neatly double as offensive options in combat, get put to full use. The presentation between each of the dungeons ranges from admirable to off-the-wall designs. The art style is undoubtedly appealing, but in motion everything feels a little stiff. This is visible in everything from walking to interacting with objects and you can especially feel it during combat.Combat remains rather shallow and stagnant throughout the course of Hinterberg. If you guessed the game was running with the standard dodge-rolling third-person action template, you’d be right. Unfortunately, the light/heavy combos are completely linear and functionally indistinguishable with nothing but a few cooldown conduit/magic moves to mix up the button mashing. New conduit moves are hard to come by, so you’re stuck with the same few favorites for most of the game. As disappointing as combat sounds, the game never really puts uncomfortable pressure on precision during fights, the controls are still responsive despite the tangible rigidity, and fights rarely overstay their welcome. So, for as minimally serviceable as the game's core action is, combat doesn’t detract too much from the overall pacing.The segmented structure of each day is a fun way to break up the action with RPG equipment prep and story stuff. Using this segmented setup, the start of the game is able to deliver new concepts to you on a digestible day-to-day basis. While I did mostly spend my evenings talking to the characters whose relationships were going to net me the tools I wanted the most, I did enjoy pursuing the side stories for the characters I was invested in. It’s just a shame that the length of the game doesn’t quite give you enough space to see all those interactions to the end.Between the opportunity to pick the order in which you tackle the dungeons and the chance to choose the ways you spend your social evenings, Dungeons of Hinterberg gives you a superb amount of freedom. By the end of the game, I felt I had quaintly personalized my alpine monster-slaying vacation.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A charming action-adventure that combines Zelda-like gameplay with social mechanics and Austrian mythology. Great dungeon design, unique powers, and meaningful character relationships make it stand out. Minor grinding required. Recommended! ✅At first glance, this might look like another Breath of the Wild-inspired game, but it quickly establishes its own identity.PROS:Beautiful cel-shaded visuals that make the world popClever dungeon design with satisfying puzzlesEach area has unique powers that combine in interesting waysDeep social system that ties directly into character progressionEngaging story that unfolds through natural character interactionsRich Austrian mythology woven throughout the narrativeCONS:Can't freely choose between exploration and social activities at the start of each daySome grinding required for materialsMaterials must be found in the environment rather than dropped by enemiesPerformance issues on Steam Deck when running on batteryGAMEPLAY & MECHANICS:The game shines in how it handles its powers and dungeons. Each area introduces new abilities that you'll need to master, and combining them feels rewarding. The dungeons are particularly well-designed - challenging enough to be engaging but never frustrating.SOCIAL SYSTEM:Unlike many action-adventures, socialising isn't just a side activity. Getting to know the town's residents is key to unlocking character upgrades and new ways to traverse the world. These interactions feel meaningful and add depth to both the gameplay and story.STORY & CHARACTERS:As you spend time with the townsfolk, you'll uncover both personal stories and deeper mysteries. The game does an excellent job of making you care about its characters while exploring interesting aspects of Austrian mythology. The narrative unfolds naturally through your interactions rather than being force-fed through cutscenes.VISUALS:The cel-shaded art style is stunning and gives the game a unique personality. Each area is visually distinct and a joy to explore.STEAM DECK PERFORMANCE (512GB non-OLED):Even on low settings, the hub world experiences noticeable frame drops when running on battery power. However, performance significantly improves when playing while charging. Outside the hub area, the game runs more smoothly. Despite these issues, it's still perfectly playable on the Steam Deck.VERDICT:Despite some minor pacing issues and material grinding, this game successfully creates its own identity in a crowded genre. If you enjoy action-adventure games with meaningful character relationships and challenging dungeons, this is definitely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I am someone who has a very bad problem with not finishing games. The pace of this game is PERFECT  but I think the smartest design is that each 'biome' uses its own magic spells for puzzles/combat.  Typically, once you unlock the "next spell" you rarely touch the old spells again. This fixes this problem, mostly. The second aspect that fixes this is you dont just progress left to right. You start location A, then dungeons out level you, then you go to B, back to A, to C, event happens to go back etc etc. This pacing allowed the game to feel fresh between play sessions, as I could change what area I was in changing the puzzles and combat scenarios while not having to remember a plethora of different spells.story is solid so far. Nothing ground breaking but more "adult" then you would expect from the graphics. I did buy this on sale but I do believe the $30 asking price is justified with enough content and theyj ust added a NG+ option if youre into those.

_childDocuments_.review: "My dear DoH, you had me at Disable Spiders in the Options Menu."The game's good, too. I guess...
