_childDocuments_.review: Mephista my daughter ♥If there was something that could visually and interely represent what my feelings and emotion were when playing this game, then the perfect example for that representation would be Shia LaBeouf smiling, laughing, applauding and cry some tears of joy watching the big screen. Because that's exactly how I felt from the first minutes of this game, till the end of it.I've waited a long time for this and I didn't even notice when it came finally out... I was browsing and I randomly see it on Steam, I was like "WAIT IT CAME OUT YESTERDAY?!" and I instantly bought it.Talking about something or someone you like it's easy but at the same time complicated, since words can hardly express the emotions you feel and put into something. Don't get me wrong, the game has some downsides, but I still could talk for hours about what I loved about this game, and just use two minutes for the little "mistakes" it has.Maybe I am too emotional when it comes to coffee, or being a barista, or characters that wants to tell a story or try to improve / blend in. I definitely am too emotional, but what's not to like in the story and the characters itself?Let's start from the beginning:This game obviously takes inspiration from Persona and I would say Coffee Talk too. not only from the design, but even from the gameplay and the OSTs you can tell.The game starts and we rapidly grasp how the gameplay and the story's gonna revolve. We can see from the first two minutes the references. Now, what makes this game really interesting, the characters:The protagonist is a very cheerful  magenta haired girl who makes coffee and likes to help. Everything is already beautiful. Wanna know what's even more beautiful?Mephista. If the coffee, for me, makes this game beautiful and amazing, then Mephista makes this game simply wonderful. The voice acting, the outfit, the personality. Perfection. The perfect communist and capitalist demon that follows you around and help you in your crazy adventure of this reverse tower defense.Dr. House (I laughed, and a lot, when I saw this and did not realize the name...). I have to complete his side story, but his voice and character are amazing; he takes our money but not much we can do about it.Goddess Mama (Amen!), the aesthetic of this character reminds me of Arknights. That alone is enough reasons for liking her.There are so many more, but even secondary characters are AMAZING. Like Yua... the style, the colors, the eyes... So much for just a secondary character, I wish it was part of the main cast with a side story.The art is really the kind of style that I love, the colors and the outfits, like I've already said... really my cup of  coffee. The OSTs, chill and vibing at the same time, depending on the gameplay situation.The AMAZING voice acting... without it, this game would've NOT be the same. They really did a top notch job here.The coffee... boy, the art of the coffees, how aesthethic and fancy they are. I would drink them all, in the same day. My heart would explode but I feel like it would be worth it.The references... I don't know if it's just me but I think this game is fuuuuull of references from TV Series, to games, to films... and I absolutely love this.And the characters... The dynamic duo between Affogato and Mephista will always be a memory and I know I'm gonna always have the same smile that Shia LaBeouf had while watching the big screen when I'll be thinking and reading about them (Imma go for a second run for the rest of the side stories). Mephista is just too charismatic fam...Now, about some little downsides...I've played many tower defense in the past, but this is my first time with a reverse tower defense. The creativity of the stages and the themes they have as you progress through the story are perfectly done. The stages are pretty challenging, and that is why after some stages I've decided to lower the difficulty from normal to easy :') I mostly wanted to chill and I'm way more interested on the story and the coffee, but the gameplay is enjoyable even at easy in my opinion; Now, I may just suck, but the shame is that it really is pretty challenging and it's hard to find a way to use the new tarot cards, or the ones that you like if you play at normal. I feel like something could've improved here, but patience.The other problem, which is more personal, is that I would've loved making more coffees. The game clearly revolves more about the reverse tower defense mechanic, and even with that, the game makes you do many, many coffees, but I feel like it could've been more. At the beginning, most of the coffees are just gonna be simple Americanos, and then people are gonna ask for more creative stuff. But, a missed oppurtunity. in my opinion, is that when we decide to spend the morning/evening at The Witchery and work as barista, a time-skip occurs. This is a HUGE wasted opportunity for me, I would've loved to do some coffees and have fun with it instead of just skipping time. But it's alright, it's just a little note.But that being said, I really think the game is worth its price, and I hope for more games like this from the creator, or some DLCs. I really, really enjoyed this game and It kept me awake for the latest hours. I do not regret it at all.I'm even going to do a second run for the rest of side story that I couldn't finish of the first one.Lastly, even if probably insignificant, I really like the name of the game. Affogato, not only just like protagonist or the dessert, but Affogato also means "drowned" in italian. I'm not sure why, but I find it ironic, funny and somewhat poetic too.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sweet take on a reverse tower defense-- You spawn your units, one of each unit at a time, so you really have to be smart in managing their lives, their movement on the field and their targets. If your units get wiped, it's over~ You gotta be smart cause you just can't spam whichever unit.The art is also quite cute, characters look beautiful-- plus they all got personality. Interactions among the cast makes sense, albeit sometimes there are interactions that take too long a dialogue. _childDocuments_.review: I was under the assumption that this game would be more focused on tower defence in a Persona kind of style. But it swiftly turned out to be a mash-up of many different things, which was both fascinating and strange to watch. In terms of the relationship / side jobs oddity, the game is very similar to Persona. You follow the main story, then conduct several side activities to enhance your personality attributes or simply pay off your debts by working at your Cafe. It combines reverse tower defence, which is actually rather enjoyable to play, not too overly challenging, especially with its upbeat melodies. But my problem is with with coffee feature that only appears in the main story. It just feels so out of place and you can't even manually make people coffee when you work there in your free time. _childDocuments_.review: Affogato feels like 50% social simulator (similar to how a series like Persona handles this aspect), 50% gameplay. I can’t say I’ve ever played a reverse tower defense game like Affogato before, but it works surprisingly well. Lots of great ideas that work well together but there were a few mechanics that I felt were not designed too well. Overall more good than bad, if you’re a fan of strategy gameplay and want a nice story, Affogato is worth picking up.    • “Reverse tower defense” was a unique gameplay style that I don’t think I’ve ever seen before. Well designed to be fun, challenging, not too repetitive, and gives you different options of how to play. Would love to see more games in this genre.    • I like the setting. The entire vibe of the game felt very modern between the manner of dialogue, overall aesthetic and in game news articles about the city.    • Characters and stories are well written. I felt invested in what was happening with all of the side story events and main story. Never felt like skipping through the dialogue.    • Jazz OST is a huge +++ for me.    • There’s a mechanic in Affogato around making different kinds of coffee (Americano, latte, macchiato, etc.) and the game tells you to experiment by changing the flavor of the coffee up by adding additional seasonings and such, but it feels like you’re guessing with that system sometimes. If you get it wrong, the customer doesn’t like it and the story continues, but you build more relationship points by giving them what they like. You only do this so many times throughout the story so unless you save and load, sometimes you’ll never figure out what certain customers like.    • Time seems pretty tight in this game for completing side stories. I don’t know if it’s possible to complete all of the side stories in a single playthrough. I was only able to complete 3 before the finale and there was one that I was completely locked out of unless I started a new playthrough because none of my saves went back far enough so that I could spend enough free time with that character. I like experiencing as much content as I can so that was a bit disappointing to be unable to finish one of the side stories.

_childDocuments_.review: Affogato is a spellbinding RPG that masterfully intertwines the allure of magic, the intricacies of strategic gameplay, and the comforting embrace of café culture. Crafted by the talented minds at Befun Studio, this unique offering beckons players to embark on a mesmerizing journey through the enchanting city of Arorua, where every corner holds secrets waiting to be unraveled and potentials waiting to be tapped.Drawing inspiration from the revered Persona series, Affogato unfurls a mesmerizing 2.5D world primed for exploration. Reflecting the essence of this celebrated lineage, players traverse the cityscape’s labyrinthine alleys and vibrant plazas, uncovering hidden treasures, nurturing connections, and peeling back the layers of a narrative tapestry that thrums with intrigue and emotion. This carefully woven narrative backdrop draws players into a realm where every step unravels the threads of a captivating story.In an innovative blend of genres, Affogato reimagines the role of a barista by infusing the nuances of café culture with the interactive dynamics of a visual novel. As players immerse themselves in this richly developed world, they find themselves ensnared by an amalgamation of familiar barista vibes akin to those found in titles like “VA-11 HALL-A” and the engrossing interactive storytelling reminiscent of “Coffee Talk.” However, Affogato distinguishes itself by offering a creative twist that sets it apart from the conventional crowd.The true heartbeat of Affogato resides within its meticulously crafted cast of characters, each etched with distinct shades of realism that breathe life into the vibrant tapestry of Arorua. Whether they play minor roles, shaping the backdrop of everyday life, or take center stage as major players driving the narrative’s ebb and flow, these characters form an intricate mosaic that mirrors the rich diversity of the world itself.While it boasts an endearing and captivating art style, it occasionally grapples with a delicate balancing act. Avatars, character portraits, and in-combat chibi visuals occasionally seem to inhabit slightly different realms, creating a dissonant visual symphony. However, amidst this artistic dance, the character portraits and tarot cards shine as beacons of cohesiveness, capturing the very essence of the game’s spirit and style.The world itself serves as a canvas painted with shades of cyberpunk allure, encapsulated in a perpetual nocturnal atmosphere even within the cycle of day and night. This juxtaposition of beauty and darkness enriches the player’s connection with the environment, adding another layer of intrigue to the journey.Moreover, the game’s soundscape exudes a refreshing charm, with elegant jazz melodies that harmonize seamlessly with the game’s ambiance. A pleasant surprise awaits as players can curate their own café playlist, allowing them to infuse their surroundings with a personalized touch of auditory delight.Delving into café management, players discover a realm of creativity as they wield the power to fully customize their café to their heart’s content. This customization feature is more than mere aesthetics; it’s an avenue for players to craft an environment that resonates with their unique vision, further immersing them in the world of Affogato.While the overall experience is undeniably pleasant, a smattering of clipping bugs has been known to make unwelcome appearances, occasionally punctuating the magical experience with moments of frustration. These unexpected glitches, manifesting during both intense gameplay and pivotal cutscenes, have, on occasion, necessitated a restart, mildly dimming the enchanting radiance of the adventure.Central to Affogato’s charm is its unwavering commitment to player agency, offering an array of choices that cater to a myriad of playstyles. Whether players prefer the relentless grind of progression or relish the intricate dance of cultivating meaningful social connections, the game deftly accommodates and empowers players to curate their very own odyssey, all while subtly weaving their choices into the fabric of the narrative.As the gameplay unfurls into the realm of combat, players harness the potency of tarot cards, each boasting distinct abilities. These cards become the embodiment of playable characters within the reverse tower defense system, weaving a tapestry of strategy and synergy. Whether serving as attackers, defenders, healers, or a myriad of other roles, the cards form a dynamic deck that evolves as players delve deeper into the intricacies of combat, offering an ever-growing spectrum of tactical possibilities.The crown jewel of the gameplay experience is undeniably its combat system. Positioned at the forefront, this dynamic battleground embodies a delicate equilibrium of challenge and strategy. An intriguing paradox emerges as players navigate its intricacies, where the trials are unyielding, and the strategies unforgiving, all within the embrace of an impeccably balanced structure. The unique reverse tower defense mechanic serves as an intoxicating elixir, infusing each encounter with a palpable sense of tension and satisfaction.Ultimately, Affogato emerges as a meticulously concocted medley of RPG elements that culminate in an experience that seamlessly fuses strategy, narrative depth, and captivating visuals. While minor artistic discrepancies and intermittent technical hitches may brush against the edges of its enchantment, the game’s overarching world, the interplay of characters, and its innovative combat mechanism combine to cast an irresistible spell, beckoning players into a realm of intrigue and wonder.Affogato serves as an exquisite fusion of innovation and creative flair, offering an RPG voyage that effortlessly traverses the realms of depth and engagement. With its strategically charged battles, a universe that radiates charm, and a narrative intricately woven around the dynamics of its characters, this game stands poised to resonate profoundly with both seasoned RPG aficionados and those embarking on their maiden journey. Savor the essence of Affogato and set forth on an adventure that promises to infuse every step with a touch of enchantment.

_childDocuments_.review: Great art style and music, I liked the setting and the characters were fun, the stories were solid, the unique gameplay type is interesting and the length feels perfect for a casual persona-lite experience. However, there are a lot of small issues that build up over the playthrough and get more annoying as it goes on.Overall recommend but the game feels like it needed another round of polish and finalization before full release.Some notes:There are a lot of Basic QOL and UI things that seem like easy fixes. Cards still appearing on the upgrade menu when they are at max level, or being able to take the train to the area you're already in for example. The controls are often needlessly clunky... you'll often have to switch back and forth between using the mouse and using keys to scroll through menu options, or you'll accidentally hit a button on the main menu when using controller because there is zero delay between the 'press any key' popup and selecting the options, or how you can't scroll down to the menu buttons on the phone and only reach them by unintuitively scrolling to the side. Button responsiveness could also be improved across the board, with delayed reactions to each press on some menus making the game feel unnecessarily sluggish.The reverse tower defense gameplay feels... underbaked, like it really needed another full round of playtesting and work before release for the amount of time you spend in it.Your units will seemingly randomly develop collision and pingpong off of eachother in the middle of a path for no reason, more frequently with larger group sizes. This is easily reproducible on every map and a MASSIVE headache that can make basic gameplay like trying to put the tank unit in front of the team impossible, sometimes suddenly breaking up your formation while under fire or causing individual units to turn around and run back alone into certain death for no reason. There is no good system to recover from this happening so you spend a lot of time waiting and hackily flipping arrows mid-party in an attempt to reorder them and then again to get them back together. When the game requires pinpoint management and precision at times to avoid things like exploding enemies and area attacks that can be near one-hit kills on units you can't redeploy due to fixed resources, this issue is just compounded.This bug flat out broke missions for me a handful of times, with units stuck against a mid-level checkpoint colliding with eachother and unable to leave that small path (and rendering that checkpoint save unusable).My starting deployment almost never differed and felt locked in by the unit cost mechanics.Re-balancing the costs around the player passively generating a small amount of points over time or on killing any enemy, and having the point generating units be a bonus on top of that, would go a long way towards making this feel better and less restrictive (and also limit the number of dead-end runs where you are still alive but completing the mission is impossible). Targeting enemy units and friendly units felt broken and often didn't work or locked on to the wrong unit and refused to scroll, making some enemy types significantly worse than intended and making recovering units to redeploy them very difficult. As noted in other reviews, the difficulty seems to swing back and forth wildly with some maps requiring multiple retries/restarts or perfect planning on card usage while others later in the same part of the story were an absolute cakewalk and gave you plenty of breathing room in time/cards/points to stall forever and plan/redeploy. This was never bad enough to be a dealbreaker for me, but not knowing if any map you're entering is going to take an easy five minutes or five times that (of if I'd lose progress because of the buggy pathing) made me hesitant to continue a play session sometimes and caused me to take a long break at one point.Money and other currencies feel like they need rebalancing. The rent mechanic was never a factor for me, even with buying out every merchant at almost every opportunity and never doing any side-exorcisms or working at the coffee shop. My cards were all maxxed out around halfway through the game and I never felt the need to level others. I may have missed a tutorial, but earning the 'points' currency and the difference between it and money was confusing and I had none available after spending my stock early on for the most of the rest of the game. Figuring out it came from doing street exorcisms didn't help, as I got a handful for half a day when items cost hundreds.The character stat leveling and breakpoints in such a short game felt overly limiting. For example, I unlocked Natalie's final story missions very early and had to focus on leveling exclusively courage during every single free time that I could so that I could progress it for what felt like over half the game, to the point that I thought the courage stat was bugged and not working properly. The affection stat with the characters seems tacked on, getting it in dialogue is almost random sometimes and I always had the item they wanted to progress in my inventory already anyway. Some shops like the dollar store next to your shop being closed at certain times or having different offerings when you very rarely can choose what time of day you are free felt annoying as well.Again, overall a recommend, but expect it to be somewhat jank.

_childDocuments_.review: While I give this a thumbs up, at the time that I'm reviewing this, having just finished the game, I think I would give it a somewhat neutral review. There are many things that I LOVED about this game. The soundtrack, art, characters, voice acting, are all absolutely incredible, and were a main driving factor in keeping me invested.But there are alot of gameplay elements that I also didn't like, things that felt arbitrary or redundant, and a lot of half baked ideas. Many aspects of the game I could see the potential of, but didn't feel like they were truly explored to the extent that it could have been.(THIS WILL BE SOFT SPOILERS FROM HERE ON)A short checklist of some of my gripes with the game or specific mechanics:- Repetition: Battles very quickly begin to feel mind-numbingly repetitive, and while new battle mechanics shake up things a tad, you still follow the same formula 90% of the time.- Difficulty Balancing: I've seen this mentioned by other players as well, but the game gets WAY too hard for its own good. I played through on Normal difficulty most of the way through, and after saving Ema and Moon, the difficulty takes a DRASTIC spike out of nowhere, standard non-boss story fights took me 10s of retries, and the next major boss took 3 hours of constant grinding to try and beat. Immediately after this, I ran into an optional boss to finish Natalie's story, and with the cards I had built, the fight was not physically winnable. From then on I swapped to Easy difficulty, where I barely had to think during fights at all. The balancing in general needs some major tweaking (I don't even want to THINK about Hard Mode)- Leveling your Cards: It only takes till about beating Chapter 1 to be able to max out 8 cards, meaning your teams potential hits its cap 25% of the way through the game. Either there should be more levels, or they should cost more to do, and be stretched throughout. Yes you get more Cards later, but you can instantly max them as well, as you likely have thousands of points saved up.- Rent/Money Balance: At first, the rent goal seems dangerous, but the game hands you so much from doing required story missions, that it doesn't matter at all. Throughout my entire playthrough I easily had more than double the required amount for rent, and by the end I had probably 50000. Rent should either be higher, or the story missions should give less.- Day Life: In a game about running a coffee shop, I find it odd that the worst thing for you to spend a morning/evening on is running your shop. You get next to no money for doing so, and no exterior rewards or skill points. I wish this part was flushed out more, possibly as a mini game where you have to actually create the coffee a random customer orders, rather than one line of dialogue passing by as you get 400 coins.- Coffee Creation: I was drawn to this game by the coffee making aspect, drawing similarities to it from Val-Halla, but was quickly underwhelmed. Every single drink follows the exact same steps: Make an Espresso, put stuff on the Espresso. I get there are general limitations, but I hoped the game would have more fun with the 'magical drinks' aspect. Also, after beating the game, I probably only ended up making less than half of the drinks on the menu, as characters only repeatedly ask for their favorite drink every time.- Coffee Creation/Chat: This ones more specific, and its a mechanic that I didn't even realize existed until I read some reviews. Apparently every character has special toppings/addings that they like even more for their drink, giving extra friendship points for doing so. But there is no way to infer what any characters 'special tastes' are at all. If these were just hinted at in dialogue with them at random points it would be fine, but you are just left guessing as to which of the toppings they may enjoy.- Relationships/Time: Simply put, there is not enough time in the game to do all the optional characters stories, and its not even close. I was only able to finish Natalie's and Lindsay's stories before the game ended, and there were still 3 others that I had barely started. Perhaps it is possible to do all 5 in one playthrough, but there is no chance anyone will get them all on a casual playthrough.- General Battling Bugs: This is probably what infuriated me the most. During battle, if too many of your characters are on top of each other, they can very easily get stuck, and end up not progressing forward, instead turning around on nothing. I was CONSTANTLY facing this bug, having my party members get peppered from far away while they bumped against each other, going nowhere, like a dog chasing its tail. Some other rarer bugs, enemies that jump around the field (one boss in particular) would sometimes get stuck while jumping, and end up falling in a place they shouldn't, thus blocking a path. Enemies would also continue to attack while reading a cutscene midbattle, so you feel rushed through the dialogue so you avoid dying.- Skills UI: Wish there was some way of tracking how close you are to the next level in Beauty/Intelligence/Courage, it would take a long time to level just one of these up, and was the main reason why I could only do 2 optional stories.- Outfits: This is rather small, but the game gives you only 3 outfits, and you get them all during Chapter 1, with nothing else afterwards. Outfits seem like great rewards to put at the end of an optional story, or for doing some harder battle challenges. Just an idea, felt like another half-baked mechanic.That's all I can think of currently, but again, don't let this long ramble push you off, these are moreso notes for the developers to possibly read and take in feedback. At the end of the day, I still had a great time playing this game, I came back to daily until beating it, and would recommend it! The idea of the reverse tower defense is great, and the main story and dialogue was very enjoyable the whole way through.

_childDocuments_.review: Affogato is a unique take on a reverse tower defence genre with a lot of story elements attached to it. I absolutely loved the characters in terms of their art, personality and story development, especially with how each character's life is portrayed and Affogato's involvement in helping them.The battles are somewhat versatile and sometimes pose a challenge (depending on difficulty too i guess), though some cards feel absolutely necessary in all stages, u still get to be quite versatile with how you use them.I found the whole troupe of a red(its not red its m a g e n t a)-haired witch owning a cafe and helping her clients to be a very interesting approach and the fact that this theme was never lost in the entire story was also a show of good writing.All in all, it was a wonderful journey and I wish to see even better games developed by the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a Persona light game. You have your dungeon crawls (in this case inverse tower defense scenarios), you have your social interactions, you are rewarded new arcana by a mix of completing quests and getting to know people better, and you have a world of interactable locations which can either advance the main story, a side story, or out-of-dungeon statistics that are used to unlock other events and interactions.That said, I did get a little intimidated when it seemed like it may have a cafe simulator as well. However, while coffee making is part of the story, and you do get to interact with the coffee machines, you do not, in fact, have to memorize people's "usual" or complete orders under time constraints.I have only cleared the first of what appear to be four major main story hurdles, but I am enjoying the game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun video game with great art. The story is you are a witch who owns a coffee shop. There are roleplay elements that add to the story, and the game is a reverse tower defense game. Which is actually really cool. This game is fun and the game is not mechanics intensive or reaction time based. Very good relaxing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: Within seconds you're immediately thrown into an intense battle, which ended up being both an amazing tutorial and an insight into the true depth of the Reverse Tower Defence (RTD) game-play. This game won't bore you with strategies either - The details in every card design makes deck-building incredibly intricate yet at the same time, hours of fun. The free-form battle style and the multiple mechanics shines like a star compared to your every-day RTD game.The quality of art and music only makes the game more engaging. Between the distinct 2.5 dimensional characters and the jazz, neon-like background music, Arorua City comes alive and jumps out of the monitor screen. The characters too come alive, each of them more charismatic than the last. They are all weaved into the same story, opening up a whole world of interest.However, all star comes with flaws. It is a constant, as much as a witch has her demon.Collecting the end-game Witch Cards are a significant pain, especially with restricted roaming time and the fact that you have to raise your own stats to even complete them.Given that the game is time-locked, if you aren't careful, you may be permanently locked out of ever completing your whole compendium, with no save file in the past to rethink your decisions.The coffee shop mechanic also feels quite underwhelming. Ignoring the few times in story where you are requested to make coffee, it is entirely impossible to access brewing. Purchasing furniture is also hilarious, because as soon as you finish the final battle you can never re-enter the store again, which renders buying them quite unnecessary.Overall, Affogato is a charming and engaging work with high potential. Given its deep roots into the RTD genre, I can understand why its B-side game-play is lacklustre, but perhaps in the future a more expansive approach could be taken instead.Ah, I still have to pay rent to Dave by the end of this month, so I'll be off again.If you decide to pick up this game, get the most out of its fun, before it all inevitably ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a breathe of fresh air for me, a concept I have never tried before that has been executed quite well, the game has nice graphics and style, the story is fun and compelling, I also enjoy the visual novel like side of this game as well, it doesnt take up 100+ gb of disk space which is getting more rare, its good to see the devs responding to reviews regularly so it seems that the devs genuinely care, to me the game is worth the price and a good casual single player game
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this so much! It feels like the game was created with so much love and care. From the art to the music to the gameplay, everything was on point. I wasn't expecting as in-depth of a story either, so I was pleasantly surprised by how much playtime I got out of the game (especially for the price!). Overall I highly recommend it, and I hope we get more games with these characters in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most impressive debut titles I've ever played, Affogato is a game that executes masterfully on it's refreshing reverse tower defense deckbuilding gameplay, on their own not unique concepts but combined they mix together and create one of the most universal and addictive games I've ever played, It's such a fresh title that I feel no matter who you are if you play it you will enjoy it. It has problems and rough edges but never did they impact my experience in a majorly negative way.Overall I give Affogato an 8/10 and would like to thank the developers for making it, they should be super proud of themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: It's got a decent core gameplay loop; the reverse tower defense levels are have a very polished arcade or flash or itch.io game feel, and you can bounce between that and the social sim/coffee barista elements change things up and get into a good rhythm.That said, the first boss battle is a pain in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ass. It doesn't feel particularly skill building or testing. There's little to no way to understand why it killed me a dozen times except that I should have leveled more before going to it??? It was so frustrating and annoying I considered quitting the game and leaving a bad review. It's a cool game, devs, but you did yourselves no favors with the design of Aoi's boss battle stage. It feels like there's very little to control. You can dodge the AoE attacks... sometimes. You have to manage around the spawning of the guys who attack in a straight line, but sometimes based on where they spawn, if you get unlucky, you'll just get obliterated. It really felt more like dumb luck and rolling the dice until I bashed my head through the wall, and I had a miserable time doing it.The non-boss levels were far more interesting to play, frankly. May update after I see later bosses, really hoping they're all not ♥♥♥♥, because the rest of the game has been a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming game with a fun, but unforgiving (even on Normal difficulty), core gameplay, which is composed of reverse tower defense segments.The story is fully voiced story and accompanied by good music and art, but the story itself is quite nonsensical and the characters don't exist outside their own arcs. The coffee making part feels aimless, so don't expect something like Va-11 Hall-A.
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game so bad, but the UI is constantly breaking on me... I've been soft-locked several times and I wasn't even out of the tutorial section yet. The UX also needs a lot of work.I'm looking forward to possibly playing this again down the line, but for now I simply can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: The game's setting is really fun! I enjoy the cute nightlife aesthetic & range of interesting characters met within this VN. - The game's novel aspect has kind of a cute witchy noir thing going for it.- The puzzle game play is quite engaging. On the more difficult settings it can get very challenging, which can encourage players to complete the story on a less difficult mode first, before returning to tackle the higher difficulty mode. - The coffee making aspect feels a little lacking imo, I suppose it does adds to the feeling of the MC actually doing something cafe related, but that's about all that aspect does. (- I do see where they're trying to go with the coffe making mode & with a little tweaking hear & there, it could make for another fun mini game feature for this VN!)Overall, I've really enjoyed playing this game, ever since I'd played the demo.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome back customer! I can see that you’ve made a fast recovery defeating the wish demon. If I remember correctly, you’re interested in acquiring the same amazing abilities, am I right? Your mana levels are looking impressive, but just so you know, this might be quite a challenging task, and there are a few important rules you’ll need to accept. Are you ready to dive into this exciting journey?You are going to play as a witch named Affogato, with red…magmatic hair. She has made a contract with an incredibly powerful and mischievous demon named Mephista. Together, their main goal is to protect people from demons. Additionally, you are a barista who owns a charming café called ‘Witchery’, where you serve delicious coffee and need to pay for the rent of this cafe:)‘Witchery’ is set in a small city where you can walk around for shopping, upgrades your stats, and complete side story. The game loop contains of three elements: time management, visual novel with coffee-making elements, and reverse tower defense.Time management: This game contains a daily limit system. Each day, you have one free action (sometimes 2 if there’s no story moment). In this action, you need to choose what to do: upgrade your stats for side stories or complete side stories (you don’t use action for shopping). After completing certain side story missions, you will encounter a stats lock where you need to upgrade one of your stats to the next level. Also, there’s a friendship stat for each side story character, but you don’t need to worry so much because if you are collecting all golden chests in the battles, then you will receive almost all presents for everybody and you are able to buy presents to upgrade your friendship and not waste actions on upgrading it. Remember, you don’t need stats for the main story!My disappointing thing about this game is that it has a lock system for side story line. It has 5 side stories. I probably wasted only 3 or 5 actions, and as a result, I could only complete 2 side stories while being in the middle of the others. It’s sad that you can’t complete all of them in a single playthrough (or maybe I just don’t understand how to do this).In the story and side story moments you are talking with characters, and it becomes a visual novel. The art is super good and full voice-acting which is good too. Sometimes you have a choice but it’s only increasing a friendship stat for this character if you make the right choice. Also, sometimes you need to make coffee, usually they are telling what they want, and sometimes not, but it’s easy to understand from their description.Afterward, you need to create a coffee. It’s an effortless process, and you have all the menus and instructions on how to make them. A cool idea and realization.It’s a reverse tower defense where you put your army and need to destroy towers. There are 4 chapters, and in 3 of them, there are different additions to the gameplay. They are logically explained because of the story.I don’t remember a game ‘Anomaly’ too well, but if I recall correctly, you couldn’t separate your army and change the order of your units because of it. However, in this game, you have that ability. If someone has low HP, you can separate them and place them at the bottom of the order. It’s a bit challenging but it’s possible and requires good micromanagement.You can upgrade your units, buy new units or receive them as rewards during the story or after completing side quests.I highly recommend this game if you are searching for a storyline-driven game with interesting characters and not a battle genre that isn’t super popular. However, don’t expect too much from the combat. First and foremost, this game focuses on characters and story.I’m looking forward to your the next game:) I hope that you will continue to make an interesting stories and characters with a good full voice-acting and a cool art style. Thanks for the game!)

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: This game may make you want to get an espresso machine, coffee grinder, and/or a milk frother. You have been warned. The characters are charming, the music SLAPS and the conversations you have with any of the characters makes you care about the NPC's in a way you never thought you would. They discuss real life issues with the current world that are relatable. I don't play many visual novels but this one stuck out to me. And if the Dev's want to release merchandise... specifically a certain coffee shop apron worn by Affogato... I will buy!!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Affogato

_childDocuments_.review: This game had good vibes and interesting gameplay along with very enjoyable character stories to read. Very comfy to play at night with the atmospheric music and art. The feeling of Persona and Va11halla along with the art and environment really nails it.My list of what I felt could've been done better:1) Gameplay is really punishing. I started at hard mode then bumped it down to medium after the 2nd shard boss and it's still pretty hard due to relying on 1 healer only (unless you have Tower too from finishing bond) and not enough Penta. Enemies will just overwhelm you in the beginning of each stage cause you struggle to get your characters out with Hermit as the primary Penta generator since the Penta generators rely on getting more ability cards or summoning characters (and that requires a lot of Penta in the beginning). You can max out your tarot cards early on but it's just raw stat boosts when strategy/trial and error is majority of the game against the enemies piled up with lasers and DoT from water.2) Not enough days to do all the bond quests/social links since level 4 requirement for intelligence, beauty, and courage cost a lot to reach, and thus you're missing out days to finish the bond quests due to lack of these parameters. I could only finish Dr House's story but had the other characters' stories probably 1-3 quests away from finishing due to not high enough parameters and not enough days in the game cause story. Would be better if there were 1 more month of time in the game to properly finish all bond stories and main story. And that way I would also have all the arcana cards ready to fight final boss.3) Cafe and money feels neglected during free time. Since the game encourages to do the bond stories or level up your personal parameters by going to shop you don't get to continue making more coffee just for npc customers, just with characters you already know. Also with all the money you get from main story and bond stories, money gets neglected in use since you only buy bond items which are only about 100 gold compared to your over 20k gold.4) Main story could spend more time with the victims after you save them. Feels shallow that Affogato doesn't get to talk to them more about their issues after their situation is over since it gets patched up very quickly. Also would've like to know more about Affogato's history as a witch.Overall very enjoyable and comfy. Would replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Great Music and soundtrack for battles-Nice anime character arts-Story line interesting even with side stories- Game play was fun, cute units Cons-Normal mode felt difficult especially boss stages-Frustrating long hour of restart if fail stage without save points-Some stages need certain characters from stories to proceed-BUGS, especially the"long line of units stuck in one spot and can't move properly" bugReview-For those who want simple game play and good story, go in easy mode.-Want a challenge? Try normal to get a feel then challenge in hard(quite hard really).

_childDocuments_.review:
Affogato is a RPG revolving around a sorceress juggling with the running of her new café, managing her debts, meeting customers from all walks of life and ultimately helping them overcome their greatest fears and secrets by burrowing deep into their minds. Enjoy a story rich RPG featuring an innovative 'reverse tower defense' mechanic and beautiful anime graphics.

Make critical decisions to help your customers defeat their inner demons by entering their minds and leading them to safety through challenging card-based reverse tower defense levels. Choose your routes and cards wisely or lose your customers forever!

Get to know customers from all walks of life. Lend them a listening ear, hear their stories, step into their minds and help them resolve their troubles. Forge special bonds with those you feel an affinity toward and become the approachable sorceress you've always aspired to be.

Plan each day with care and manage your time wisely. Will you focus on bringing in moolah for your café, honing your skills as a barista, learning stronger spells or bridging closer bonds with your customers? Remember that the clock is ticking and that every decision you make costs time in Affogato!

Making a good cup of coffee is the cornerstone of being a barista. To be a truly great barista, however, you need to understand your customers and figure out which brews are perfect for them. Affogato features realistic coffeemaking simulation. Master the art of making great coffee and you can unlock hidden conversations and storylines!

name: Astor: Blade of the Monolith
detailed_description: Join our Discord About the Game Explore the vibrant planet of Gliese, once inhabited by an ancient race, and now home to their sentient creations – the Diokek. After the ancients’ disappearance, the Diokek lived in peace until malevolent creatures, the Hiltsik, started wreaking havoc among their settlements. With threats of a more sinister force at play, Astor – a young Diokek warrior, must journey across Gliese to solve the mysterious disappearance of his creators thousands of years ago, believing that they may have left behind the key to their salvation. Learn new attacks, abilities and combos, unlock magical powers, and collect legendary weapons as you crush hordes of enemies. Find your way towards the Monolith, an ancient structure holding immense power, and confront the source of the planet’s haunting evil. Will you join Astor on his journey to become the planet's savior? Engage in intense battles against 16 different enemies and 10 formidable bosses across over 20 hours of main story and side quests. Arm yourself with 4 unique weapons, master dynamic skills and combos, summon powerful constructs, and craft your own combat style. Traverse Gliese's diverse landscapes, complete various side quests and uncover remnants left by your creators. Test your skills in combat challenges and conquer New Game+ mode for an even greater challenge. Explore the mystical planet of Gliese and search for a lost history hidden throughout the planet's majestic landscapes, ancient ruins, and old temples left by past civilizations. Using your newfound runic power, shift into the spirit realm to solve puzzles, reveal secret passages, and uncover the answers to save the future. Arm yourself with 4 types of powerful weapons and special abilities as you engage in intense, fast-paced battles. Pummel your enemies with a combination of melee strikes, ranged attacks, and air combos. Switch between equipped weapons at any time–even mid-combo to deliver unyielding critical hits. The choice is yours! Harness the power of the Runic Swarm, an ancient energy used to materialize runic power as weapons or tools in combat. Unleash charged attacks to create devastating finishers, such as the Wall Crush and Runic Cannon, or summon powerful companions, shields, and decoys to gain the upper hand in combat. Your journey will lead you down a path of discovery toward your destiny. Uncover answers to solve the mysterious disappearance of the ancients thousands of years ago, for they created the Diokek, but what deeper purpose lies behind the existence of your kind? Are you, Astor, truly the chosen one destined to bring salvation or destruction? The ancient Monolith holds the key to your answers, awaiting your arrival with the secrets of the past.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mixed on this game. I would recommend it, but only if you understand the caveats of the product you're going to receive currently at time of writing. This game isn't necessarily my cup of tea, but I can see it appealing to individuals who are nostalgic for older beat 'em ups and hack and slash titles. It reminded me a lot of older PS2 titles like The Legend of Spyro: A New Beginning in terms of the overall game loop, where you travel to one area, fight a bunch of bad guys, and then move on to the next objective. If that sounds like your ideal kind of experience, go in with open arms. This is one of the better indie titles I've had the pleasure of sampling.The game is very pretty for what it is in my humble opinion. Delightful color palettes color the landscapes you'll travel across, and the game really does make an honest effort to get you enveloped in its world. Character designs are simple but aesthetically pleasing, though I will say I could go for more variety in the enemy color palettes. They're very dull compared to the rest of the world and characters you'll meet in the opening hour. You will however find yourself wanting to run around the landscape advancing the main quest more than you'll find yourself wishing for better enemy color palettes, though.Combat is very simple, almost as if it were designed with a younger audience in mind. Hard Mode doesn't bring much more of a challenge, parrying windows are very generous, and enemies will huddle around you but you'll rarely find yourself being attacked by more than 1 at a time. In my short time with the game, I was able to stand in front of enemies for a bit before they'd even attempt to engage me. The combat does start to open up more with some of the upgrades that are available, similar to DMC combo modifiers, which will make you OP very quickly just with the ability to launch enemies to juggle. If challenging combat is what you're after, you're not going to find it here.From what I'm able to gather about the narrative, it's nothing world changing either, but I don't think it was designed to be. It's a cozy adventure narrative about being the chosen one and traveling the world to beat the bad guys. Astor is a silent protagonist, and you have your usual tropes like the sweet sidekick best friend, a grumpy village chief, etc. If you're looking for an enthralling story that will make you reflect about it long after the credits have run, I don't think you're going to find it here. If however you're looking for an easily digestible game in terms of gameplay and story, this is worth checking out.A couple of other nitpicks, mostly technical. The game will occasionally stutter but it runs very well outside of area transitions, that's where you'll see stutters and dropped frames the most. I personally had some connection issues with DualSense controllers, ranging from dropped inputs to the game not detecting the controller unless I was in Big Picture Mode (YMMV). I was unable to replicate these issues on other titles, and I'd assume the devs will eventually iron these issues out. I'd also really like to see the devs implement a remapping feature because some of the input placements aren't ideal (Run/Dodge is mapped to R2, for example), and there are only 2 presets for controllers. Gameplay wise, camera sensitivity was a tad high for me and I knocked it down a peg or two, which felt much better. It also feels weird to have an Assassin's Creed style compass when there's a feature dedicated to helping you find your way to the next objective. If all of that sounds like a good time, dive in, if you're leery, wait for a sale. Can't say I agree with the main negative review at time of writing on their dealbreakers (cutscenes aren't really as intrusive as that review would have you believe, the slowdown effect doesn't really affect combat tempo, and getting hung up on broken boxes is a bit silly), but I'll be waiting for a deep sale personally.

_childDocuments_.review: A very commendable attempt at a character action Zelda-like for a new developer. Unfortunately the game isn’t good enough for me to recommend on its own merits. However I do recommend it on the basis of supporting a new developer with a clear vision and talent.I’ll offer some constructive criticism here:1. Combat has a nice flow that is complimented by the combo counter. I enjoyed moving around the arenas and chaining hits together with my long-ranged weapon and my sword. Unfortunately the combat really falls down when it comes to the bosses. The parry is simply too overpowered. Instead of weaving in and out of attacks and using spacing and knowledge of my moveset to beat them, the dominant strategy became standing still and waiting for a parry. Because of this, I was able to ignore most of the bosses’ mechanics and they all just blended together. The final boss was especially bad for this.2. The attempt at a sort of “open-zone” level structure was an interesting idea, but it ultimately falls flat because it winds up making the gameplay feel sparse. Traversing these environments aren’t particularly interesting, and this causes the actual engaging gameplay (combat and puzzles) to feel too spread out. A smaller play space with more gameplay density would have made this a lot better.3. In general, the dungeons suffer from the same problem as the open zones: they’re simply too big. It becomes a chore to seek out collectibles and optional encounters because there is simply so much empty space between them. I would recommend looking into games like Darksiders 1 and 2 for how to pull off dungeons with gameplay systems like this. Despite those games’ dungeons feeling grand in scope, they are actually very compact. They funnel you from combat to puzzles to platforming very quickly. Almost every room has some sort of meaningful gameplay in it. Action-adventure games like these ride or die on how quickly the player can access the next bit of gameplay, and while this game isn’t terrible in this regard, it could definitely still use some tightening up.Anyway, hopefully these criticisms were helpful. I will definitely be keeping my eye on these developers in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: 25 hours 4/10 1 + chapter selection Not yet when I write this. I hope there will be video guides on where to find all the collectibles in the future No No Finding all the collectibles feels as a grind No No No No No difficulty setting NoAstor: Blade of the Monolith is a great Action-Adventure in which you play as Astor. You'll go on a journey to try to understand the world around you. Some crazy things are going on. However, the more you unravel the more confusing it gets until you find the real answers. I keep this a bit vague on purpose because I think that the story hits much more when you experience it for yourself. What I love about Astor: Blade of the Monolith is the story in combination with how beautiful the game looks. The game is much bigger than I would have expected before starting to play it. And the further you get the more powers you unlock to play around with. And very early on you get a mount! Which is so lovely in this huge world. The combat takes a little bit of time to get used to, because the buttons for hitting and heavy hitting are on different spots on the controller than I would expect, but it is quite easy to get used to them and just enjoy the wonderful story this game has to tell. Many of the achievements are for completing the story, and the others are for upgrading everything and finding all the collectibles. There are also achievements for beating enemies with a specific weapon. Most of those you'll already unlock without even really trying to get them as long as you switch to the new weapon when you unlock it. You can always have 2 weapons equipped: the newest weapon and the second one you get to choose. You can switch between them at any moment and they all feel different. The only achievement I struggle with is with finding all the collectibles. Gladly there is a chapter selection system, and during chapter selection, it even shows you how many out of how many you already have. Even more importantly, when you get new collectibles, it is saved and you don't have to complete the whole chapter. However, the chapters are quite big, and sections of a chapter are closed off until you get to that stage or get locked out when you get to the next stage of that chapter. So most of the time you can't walk freely around to search for them through the whole chapter. This is one of the things that prevent me from getting the last few achievements at this moment. I wish you would feel more overpowered after finishing the game, but it feels like the strength of the monsters stays the same, so it is never a walk in the park to go back to a previous chapter and rush through it. On my end, I also have a bug during chapter selection that the game doesn't show where the next objective is. The weird thing is, so far the developers haven't been able to reproduce this and they are busy looking into what causes this. I hope nobody else encounters this bug, as it makes replaying older chapters more challenging than it needs to be. I can say that the developers are very responsive and that I found a few other bugs but those were fixed in just a few hours. I give Astor: Blade of the Monolith 3,5 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game. It's not bad, a 5.5/10 for me personally. _childDocuments_.review: Astor: Blade of the Monolith looks like Zelda, but it plays like Devil May Cry with a huge emphasis on combat and upgrades. It's a very fun game that makes full use of its physics engine and lets you play it basically however you want. Really the only issues with this game are the combat scaling, the fact that it's not very innovative and the lack of any in-depth puzzle element. Starting with the good, the game's art style is very unique and the story, while something you've probably heard before, is actually interesting and easy to understand. Storytelling in games like this is often a convoluted mess, but this game actually tells its story in a very succinct manner. This is a combat-centric game where you are constantly hacking and slashing and pummeling enemies as "Astor" a little doll-like creature who drowns in water. Early on you get the ability to go into an alternate wireframe realm where you can see and pass through certain surfaces. This is cool but it isn't utilized enough. There are a ton of upgrades in this game, including four weapons that all handle differently. The gauntlets are by far the most powerful weapon as they simply deal the most damage. Later on you get a sprint, double jump and the ability to launch a simple projectile. Bashing enemies in this game is a lot of fun as they have a lot of animations. Smacking an enemy backwards, for example, can trigger a unique animation that shows it slammed against the wall. As you progress you pick up both red orbs and little turquoise pyramids that let you upgrade your weapons. You also get "constructs" which are special abilities that let you do things like drop rocks on the enemies or summon creatures like golems and spiders. The game keeps giving you new abilities as you progress so even when the game runs out of new enemy types you're still getting more and more powerful. The game is weirdly easier later on since the enemies don't get much stronger but you get way stronger. Going into the secondary realm increases your damage but decreases your health. Later on you get kind of a "super saiyan" ability that makes you ultra powerful. In addition to this you can also parry attacks and this stuns enemies, even bosses. The parrying is thankfully super responsive and easy to pull off. This game has a few glitches but in general is very polished. The sound design is beautiful and the graphical style perfectly fits the game's story. There are side quests and numerous bosses. The most time consuming element of the game is collecting the extra items like chests and rune fragments. The rune fragments aren't very well hidden but there are a ton of them and they are scattered all over the map. I do wish the bigger maps were more interactive. Early on you go into a desert area that looks very cool but doesn't have much to do aside from kill enemies. What would make this game exceptional would've been if Astor had an inventory, collected keys, solved puzzles, etc. The core game play kind of betrays the aesthetic because this isn't a Zelda-type game but something that's more similar to Devil May Cry. And while that's all fine and well the game really isn't that difficult so you don't get the sort of high-stakes intensity that you would get from a game like Devil May Cry.With all of this said it's a really fun experience. I paid $6 for it and it's worth much more than that, so if you like these sorts of games don't hesitate to pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really pretty and very reminiscent of Zelda games, especially older ones. The tutorial at the start is helpful and eases you in, but the fight mechanics can be a bit difficult in early game with multiple enemies.  Overall I would recommend this for anyone interested in a fun, beautiful, action game where you can smash boxes to a ridiculous number of smithereens and not have to worry about finding your own plot to pursue.

_childDocuments_.review: 30 minutes in, early impressions.The game is lacking polish. Camera movements are jumpy, glitchy areas, the combat is... basic and pretty boring, and for some reason, when you smash a box, it spawns more pieces than it took to make the box. It's like 1000 voxel pieces, super weird, and doesn't fit the art style. When you kill a group of enemies, it does this really weird slo-mo/black and white thing which is... pointless and adds nothing to the game other than some pretend "flare." The beginning of the game is a cut scene every 2 seconds. Honestly, in 30 minutes of gameplay, I've hit 15 of them. Annoyingly, every time you have to use your "spirit" power in the beginning, it keeps telling you. They give you *no* chance to figure it out on your own which is just... dumb. Like, let the player figure it out.I can see what they were going for with this game, but it just isn't ready for release. The lack of polish is everywhere from the way the enemies spawn in, to the jerky camera, the slo-mo/B&W when you kill enemies, it's all over the place in the small details, which add up.It's a shame too because the game has a good base, it's just missing the final month or 2 of polish to bring it all together.

name: Closer the Distance
detailed_description: Closer the Distance is a deeply moving, slice-of-life sim that tells a story about the connections between family and friends in the face of tragedy. Following a fatal car accident, players take on the role of Angela, a young girl from the town of Yesterby, who finds herself watching over her loved ones as they navigate the grieving process. Using her ethereal ability to influence the townspeople she once knew, Angela’s choices will ultimately determine the fate of Yesterby. Closer the Distance combines several key gameplay features for an immersive playthrough. The game's compelling narrative is emotionally charged and highlights themes of empathy, community, friendship, grief, and closure. Choices-matter gameplay allows players to make decisions that affect the outcome of the story, making each playthrough unique. Closer the Distance offers something for everyone, and its emotional depth and engaging gameplay will leave players wanting more. CW: Closer the Distance deals with themes of death, illness and grief

short_description: Closer the Distance is a slice-of-life sim that tells a deeply emotional story about the connections between family and friends in the face of tragedy. Unearth long kept secrets, repair strained relationships, and help your loved ones move on.

_childDocuments_.review: From the developers of the popular  games comes Closer the Distance. Except this time, the team at  have decided to steer away from politics/corruption themes and into a slice-of-life sim about human emotions and relationships. It focuses on the tenderness of grief; how different people process tragedy and how this can impact communities. Closer the Distance is an excellent narrative game that kept me enthralled from beginning to end. Its thought-provoking gameplay had a profound impact on me, despite the immense performance issues I experienced.  A peaceful small town named Yesterby is rocked by the unforeseen tragedy of losing one of its young residents. The townspeople struggle coming to terms with what has happened, and the story follows their individual journeys, as well as how each of their path’s interconnect. Despite being the victim of the fatal car accident, Angela watches over those she left behind, guiding their decisions and pushing them forward, until they are strong enough to continue on their own.The story is clearly, emotionally charged, and immersive, highlighting how different people manage grief. The relationships between characters can be complex but rewarding if you persevere down specific friendship routes. Perhaps the most impressive element was how much impact each of the characters you control has on everyone. How their actions will impact another one of your characters. Whilst the main story is about Angela’s loss, there are many different “side quests” or plots to further explore to better understand other characters. If you neglect a character’s basic needs, they can fall into a deep state of depression and can end up feeling neglected. This can have consequences to other characters who are close with that person, creating a sombre domino effect.I think the best way to describe Closer the Distance is that it plays like  You are responsible for making sure characters basic needs/wants are met, controlling what side quests and activities they do, such as finding a balance between meeting a deadline for a quest and having enough exercise and food. Take this, and add some choice elements, multiple characters and an overarching story about loss and there you have Closer the Distance.I found its storytelling poetically beautiful, but extremely melancholic (I do not recommend playing this while sad). Watch the younger sister slowly recede into her shell and break down, silently, and in solitude. Observe the mum busying herself in pointless activities, only to never be fully satisfied, so she attempts to employ others into her futile tasks. See how these characters closest friendships and relationships suffer because of their actions. Acting as a sort of “God” over the townspeople, I tried to console everyone, to balance their needs so they can be OK. Soon enough, I realised that there is just not enough time in the day to do it all. Sacrifices must be made, which is hard for an amiable personality like my own. Admittedly, this did give me a sense of stress, but in a good way. Waiting for a character to wake up so he can immediately cook food so he can go to work ASAP to meet his project deadline, is kind of amusing, looking back. I felt this sense of stress because I was completely enthralled into these characters lives. I wanted them to succeed, and when they did not, I felt at fault… and that is powerful.Cycling through each character, it is easy to control them simultaneously, always making sure they are doing some sort of task. Although, I would have liked it if it were easier to spot at a glance if they were currently travelling to complete a task, or doing one. Many choices did not have as big of an impact as I was hoping, and often if you did nothing, the storyline would sort itself out without harsh consequences. Perhaps the game would have been too sad and grim if it had brutal consequences to characters actions. Yet sometimes I felt a bit letdown, especially when I replayed specific scenes to see how it played out if I did the opposite. Closer the Distance certainly can have an illusion of choice.Visually, Closer the Distance is quite basic. Characters do not have facial details, with their faces being blank slates, except in their character portraits. The focus is instead on the landscape and environmental details, which are bright and blocky.Dialogue is fully voiced, with the voice acting being especially notable. Delivering believable and heartfelt performances across the cast with the pain in many of their voices being palpable. One small gripe is that sometimes if you lead more than one character to the same location, they will commence their dialogues, talking over the top of each other. They will be having different conversations, but because they are in the same room, we hear each group clearly and it can be hard to follow along with each. My biggest concern with the game was that I had continuous stutters and FPS drops (120 down to 40 and jumping up and down). This only occurred after an hour or so of consecutive playtime and was fixed with a restart, until another hour passed, when I would need to restart again. Stutters were horrid, happening every few seconds, delaying dialogue, watching characters lag in their walks etc. Note that after looking at other reviews, it seems this issue is not widely experienced, but I succeed minimal system requirements  [32GB RAM / 16GB VRAM] 12 hours – 100% achievement completion. No – but there is controller compatibility.Closer the Distance is a melancholic slice of life sim with gameplay reminiscent of  where you are responsible for each character’s basic needs and actions. Its atmospheric and emotive scenes are exceptionally hard-hitting and are sure to strike a chord with narrative lovers. Although its premise is simple, gameplay never felt repetitive, and I was completely immersed in each character’s lives. The performance issues I encountered do not seem widespread across players, but hopefully a fix can soon be implemented. Despite the devs taking a vastly different turn from the popular  series, this is an easy strong recommendation to all story enthusiasts if you do not mind a bit of a sad plot!

_childDocuments_.review: If you love games like Life is Strange or games which have a slice of life narrative, then I am confident that you will enjoy Closer the Distance. For me, it was one of the best narrative experiences I have had the pleasure to play. The plot lines were masterfully woven between the community of characters and taking control of them and steering their destiny felt so immersive. It was a pleasure to get to know the thirteen characters, and the way they were all integrated into the story was cleverly done with different mechanics effecting their relationships, and different choices effecting the storyline. The voice acting was superb and the characters felt alive, especially as there are loads of nice touches throughout the game that will leave you impressed, like the way they turn off the television and turn around when somebody talks to them, or the way they eat at the breakfast table each morning, or simple things like lighting the fires or turning on the stereo to listen to music. The game is full of these little touches which makes it feel realistic and familiar. The small town of Yesterby is a quaint seaside village suffering from the same problems that most sleepy towns face, Lack of jobs, lack of opportunities, and a restlessness amongst the younger inhabitants. We learn of the plights of the town told through day-to-day conversations and through the actions carried out by the inhabitants as we watch them go about their daily tasks. Each character has an independent schedule and travels around the village doing their own things like working or chilling at home. We can view them at any time by selecting their character and watching them and listen to their conversations. You can do this as much or as little as you want, so if you enjoy a rich backdrop and like to immerse yourself in proceedings, you can skip around the characters and be a fly on the wall, or if you want to concentrate on the main story line, you can fast forward time until an important story arc is revealed which halts time automatically and directs you to the event. The characters are so well voice acted and realised that I found myself absorbing as much conversation as I could, and it completely immersed me within their community. The relationships are incredibly well developed with their own histories, personalities, and aspirations. I don’t think I have ever played a game that had this much detail when telling a story and it was all interesting and absorbing. In the evenings, occasionally you will be presented with a map of the town where you can access and view short reenactments of past events. These play out in typical fashion with silhouetted figures and you are able to choose which part of history you would like to watch. Depending on your choice, a task is often added to your bio to perform in the present. It’s interesting and effective how they reveal past events, adding more layers to the story whilst deepening our understanding and empathy of the characters. Within this small community a tragic event occurs that tests everybody’s resolve and forces the community to come together to heal. We examine the relationships between the characters and how this event affects them individually and as a community. If the game wasn’t immersive enough, we then get the opportunity to control certain main characters, making decisions on what to do and where to go. This is driven by certain tasks that are revealed on each character’s bio depending on previous decisions or conversations. There are quite a few achievements attached to these tasks, so it is worth having a look at them if that is important to you and trying to steer events towards them. Some of these tasks will involve you talking to multiple characters and performing various chains of events to succeed. The achievements were very rewarding to obtain. Each character has different stats that you need to keep healthy and a few common traits like sleep, hunger and health that you need to keep a watch on.This might involve you ordering the character to go to bed when they’re tired, or relaxing when they are stressed, or doing a certain task that will improve a stat if it is low. I managed in the main to keep these tasks within healthy boundaries, but I wasn’t quite sure what the advantage of doing this, or the consequences of not doing this, were. Each character has a mood which is shown above their profile picture, so I guess these stats determine that, but again I wasn’t quite clear how it all tied together. I suspect that these moods do effect something, but it would have been nice to have a tutorial on that front to explain it properly. The characters also have a relationship score between themselves, which can either be positive, neutral, or negative, depending on their interactions during the story, and this can affect future decisions or interactions. There are quite a few different things to manage, and I really enjoyed doing them, which only immersed me further into proceedings. .
