But your arrival has broken the silence, Mara Forest. If you want answers, you’ll have to venture deep into the darkness of Crow Country to find them…

_childDocuments_.review: This game perfectly captures the spirit of classic Resident Evil with the visual of PS1 era Final Fantasy. I was impressed by how effectively the game builds a foreboding atmosphere and creates unsettling enemies with such a silly and chunky art style. I had a great time playing this and would definitely recommend it to any fans of classic survival horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: The first play though gave me some trouble with the puzzles from me not paying attention to a quick little thing. It was enjoyable and the story is interesting to keep you going to learn what is happening. My second play through was very fast and trying to find the glass crows was a nice addition into the second play through. I'm looking forward to seeing what i unlock in getting an s rating in my third play through. I would recommend if you like resident evil from the ps1 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country has probably one of the most interesting payoffs for a horror game in a while, and I respect how well it pulls off a lot of things concerning it's puzzles, gameplay, exploration, and story. A lot of things you'll encounter are not new and groundbreaking, but the execution is nearly flawless, and I loved every moment of it. Fantastic experience, and easily a HIGH recommendation from me for fans of the horror genre in general. ( Playtime is about 6 hours I just left it on -- on accident )
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps my favorite original survival horror entry since Resident Evil 4. Crow Country is packed with charm in art, setting, audio, music, and writing. The gameplay is very clean and functional for its perspective. A full run will net you approximately 7-9 hours depending, with new game plus secrets to uncover. That said, there are sadly no ascension levels like those found in Slay the Spire which is a bit of a let down.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: I adored this game. Perfectly paced, terrific to explore, and a visual delight for anyone with an affection for PS1-era graphics.I especially enjoyed the story in a way that I didn't expect. I never expected to be particularly SCARED by this game (one could even say it's more a "Halloween-like" experience than truly a HORROR experience), but the way the story unfolds and comes together in the end really left an impression on me! I hate to compare in reviews, but given the blatant inspiration, it does not seem appropriate: Crow Country left me as excited for a follow-up as Resident Evil or Silent Hill ever did as a kid!To the critiques, I do think certain puzzles were a bit obtuse. A couple of times, I found myself looking up the puzzle not for the solution but for a description of what the puzzle actually was. That is to say, I didn't always know what my puzzling was supposed to accomplish. I also think that this game is convenient in a way that longtime survival horror fans might not appreciate. I really appreciated not needing to worry about inventory management, but I recognize that there was probably some tension lost there.Despite these things though, I had a wonderful time! I even look forward to going for a second playthrough to get that S-rating!
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute "must play" for any fans of the genre. It takes everything you can learn from games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, while subverting a few tropes of the retro survival-horror genre along the way. It's like getting to play Resident Evil for the first time again. It's a real treasure. Pick this up if you love survival horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is an amazing nostalgia trip back to Silent Hill. The atmosphere is tense and dark, and the horror comes through in the story and monsters. There are lighter moments, and everyone seems to be talking about the mushroom puzzle, but honestly it doesn't take away from the loads of care and charm that was obviously put into this game.If you're expecting Resident Evil style brutality or item management, it's not here, and I wouldn't expect it to be.  A lot of people are comparing this to that series, but I feel it fits snugly into its Silent Hill niche. there is no item management or storage, and the unease comes from the story, design, and constantly looming enemies, rather than the constant threat of a game over. TL;DR, read the notes and get immersed. This game focuses on story and mood and delivers on both 110%
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fantastic little survival horror game. It has a very distinct PS1 era visual style, which adds a lot to the atmosphere of the game. It takes a lot of inspiration from the original Resident Evil games, but while still maintaining modern gaming standards (ex. tank controls and analog stick movement are both options). The story was compelling and fun to watch play out, and it even features a pretty big twist at the end which had a satisfying tie-in to the conclusion. The game also has a hard mode for people looking for more of a challenge, as well as a mode that disables damage, for people who are only interested in seeing how the story plays out. Similar to the Resident Evil games, there are also rankings and secret bonus items unlocked after the game is over for collecting and messing around with. I think my biggest complaint with the game would be the weapon switching system, as only being able to swap weapons in a set line would leave me stumbling sometimes trying to get the right weapon out in combat. Plus, while I don't think it is entirely needed as the game has plenty to do without, I think it would've been nice to have just a little bit more to unlock, like maybe some concept art or something like that. However, those are more nitpicks than anything else, Crow Country is a fantastic game that is worth every dollar, especially if you are a fan of survival horror or PS1 style games.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing (but short) love letter to survival horror games in the style of the original FF7 on PSX. There are secrets to get, graded endings, and special outfits/weapons for doing so. Once you get everything there's not a whole lot of replay value, but considering speed running is a thing, YMMV. Definitely recommend if you are a fan of older survival horror games!
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable experience. Modernizes the (frankly) outdated style of old school isometric survival horror with many quality of life changes that actually don't diminish at all from the overall experience. I personally never died in my play through and they literally just added a new hard mode after I finished, so I cannot attest for it but I would play on hard mode if I were to play it again. I don't know how long my play through was because steam doesn't appear to have clocked the majority of my time, but I would guess anywhere from 5-7 hours. Game play wise, the puzzles were fun. Shooting is a bit clunky (aiming is smooth but enemy damage feedback is lacking). Movement is good! Way better than the classics (thank the stars). You can rotate the camera, navigation is easy and intuitive.  If you're on controller you basically have two ways to move, you can use tank controls with the D-Pad or more modern style of moving your character in any direction with the left stick, what's cool about this is that they even have a quick turn implemented for anyone that wants to brave the tank controls. On controls/intuitiveness this game gets it perfect. No stupid inventory management, the only limitation is how many of each type of item you can hold (ie. 5 medkits), I was never a fan of really strict inventory management (fake survival horror fan), so this was a welcome change for me. Hope we see more games take lessons from Crow Country going forward. Only downside for me was that the combat wasn't very engaging, I never felt particularly threatened on the standard difficulty and shooting enemies is a bit dull as there isn't much feedback. I can only imagine this is exemplified if you're aiming with a mouse. I thought the story was very interesting and presented perfectly, it didn't over contextualize or leave everything way too cryptic, it was just a simple plot unfolding logically as the game progresses and I was very satisfied with it! The characters were all a little bit goofy which added to the charm of their silly designs. Speaking of designs, I actually think the characters are the lowest quality part of the art in this game (I think intentionally), the environments are very details with beautiful sprites and colours. It's easy to tell what everything is and I had no problems on that front. Highly recommended for any classic horror fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: A masterfully done tribute to the survival horror genre. It hearkens back to those early classics, but it has very clearly put modern game design lessons to use, too. For a fan of the genre, it's a must-have. And for anybody who wants to try survival horror, I'd say that this is a perfect starting point. Short, but not too short; puzzles that are just tricky enough to pick your brain without being aggravating; and a perfect difficulty - you'll never be starved for resources, but you'll never have a glut of them, either. You just *have* to check this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Pretty much every aspect of it was really well done, the worst I could say is "the combat is rather simple" I guess? (simple combat is infinitely better than being bad combat)If you like survival/horror games, games with really wonderful atmosphere and well done puzzles, or games that endeavour to capture some of the rather nebulous PS1-era "vibe" then I think you'll be as satisfied as I am with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all of the horror games I've tried this is by far the best. I grew up playing the legend of Zelda, and I deeply admire the style of this game since it reminds me of the graphics in those old games such as Majora's Mask, and Ocarina of Time. It truly brings to me a sense of nostalgia, and the inconsistency of monsters spawning brings about an suspenseful feeling. You never  know what is around the corner. The game is not too hard to the point where you need to bring up 50 different walk through videos, and the puzzles are incredibly fun to solve. I heartily recomend this game, and I wish there were others like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast playing through Crow Country! It's a bit of a nostalgia trip reminding me of PS1-style games. Gameplay is reminiscent of Resident Evil 1 and Fantasy Final 7, but plays how you *remember* them playing, not how they actually played lol. I was incredibly invested in the story and took lots of twists and turns towards the end! For the $20 pricetag and 6-ish hours of gameplay, I can't recommend it enough!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Very well paced with a lot of detailed, interesting environments. Plenty of tantalizing environmental storytelling and fun puzzles as well! About 6 to 7 hours long, but more if you want to nab all the hidden secrets and extra goodies. I played, I died, I spooked, I cried. Oh and the sound design was really good!! cawCAW
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic.  I don't have anything creative to say about Crow Country that hasn't already been said, I just want to give it one more thumbs up and encourage people to play it.  If I have one complaint, it's that the puzzles are a bit on the easy side, and often overexplained in-game, but it's a minor nitpick.  An absolute joy from start to finish that should be played by anyone who appreciates horror games.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: A bite-sized RE experience with puzzles that range from easy to moderately challenging without being impossible to decipher (except one) or feeling like you were being pitched a softball. The bits of humor are fun, the story is solid, and the actual art / visual design is wonderful for characters and environment.Beat the game in around 5 hours getting all secrets, so people who aren't accustomed to these sorts of games can expect 6+ hours. Recommend a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful little game. This kind of little piece of love that manages to find a very nice balance between respecting the codes already established and the new QOL improvements that serves the player without reducing the experience through gameplay. Despite easier movement abilities, easiness of the camera movement, you can still fill tension, as the areas are closed. The ennemies look terrifying, I love it. I felt a lot of tensions on my first steps. And little by little I took confidence moving inside the park. Just what you're supposed to feel. The little puzzles are really cool. I enjoyed backtracking some areas to test ideas and look for clues to advance a little more.I'd say the only minus point is the "CRT Filter" look alike that does not improve the retro feeling. I'd love to see an option to deactivate it. Go with your eyes closed, the game is worth much more it's full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played.The puzzles are very creative and different from each other.The controls are smooth (I'm just very bad at aiming in general, even worse with a controller lol).The music and sound design are remarkable.The setting and atmo are eery and on point.And the story is so cool!I liked the game so much that I even cosplayed Mara on stream :DI've never even played the Resident Evil series but after this I just might... :D
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Great nod to oldschool horror games with modern day QoL like no limited saves and better controls (still a option for tank controls), even a option for no enemies for just beating the game and exploring.Game is "short" but saying that my first run took me roughly the same time as something like Resident Evil 1, yet this is a nice low price point.I enjoyed the story, the characters, the map layout is great, puzzles can be a little too easy but at least means you keep constant progression and there's secrets with unlocks for a classic resi/SH score system on beating the game.Easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: A fun survival horror puzzle game! Just finished playing it on my Youtube (link at end of review for anyone looking for a gameplay sample before buying) and came to leave some thoughts here.Story-wise, it's the early '90s and the player character, Mara, has turned up at the gates of the spooky, abandoned Crow Country amusement park. Cue a game of investigation, as she finds her way through the park, uncovering its grisly backstory and encountering a variety of bizarre monsters. Who is Mara? Why is she there? These are questions you'll have and which the game will eventually answer. Admittedly, the twists are a bit predictable (i.e. they shouldn't come as a shock to the player), but I still enjoyed the story for what it was.Getting onto the technical stuff, I quite liked the visuals and general aesthetic of the game; the setting is cartoonish but also grungy and dark. The sound design is fine and complements the visuals fairly well. As for gameplay mechanics themselves, something you do need to be aware of is that the game imitates the kind of tank controls seen in old-school '90s games such as Resident Evil or Tomb Raider - however, there are ways to quickly orient your character's direction if need be. There are also a few weapons you can find in the game with which to defend yourself from the monsters, though be a little conservative with your ammo and/or keep an eye out for environmental means of hurting enemies (e.g. explosive barrels, electrical boxes, etc).Gameplay-wise, Crow Country also has a strong emphasis on puzzle solving. Generally, these are nice and challenging, though look carefully through each area - there are usually notes you can find that provide hints. I did find one or two of these puzzles quite tough - though I'm more inclined to suggest that's me being dumb rather than the game being too difficult.Overall, Crow Country is a good survival horror game. If you like this and puzzle-solving, then I'd definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game. The perfect callback to old-school PS1 horror titles with all the modern accouterments that makes contemporary survival horror extremely engaging and addicting. A great experience for fans of Resident Evil and Silent Hill, and even those who have never played. All around a solid horror recommendation for this spooky season and beyond.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: This game just  fun as hell, and is beautifully put together - the sound design, gameplay and puzzles are all top notchI also found the writing to be intriguing!! Even the little things, such as when Mara is investigating an item are a bit silly at times, which I loveIt achieves exactly what it is trying to do in scratching that old school survival horror itch
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game, love the aesthetic and the story was quite good.My main criticism is that the game's difficulty is a bit too easy. The puzzles lack thinking for the most part and most of them give you the answers outright. In my opinion, the combat is the most difficult part of the game and the main source of difficulty isn't the strategy or enemies. The main difficulty came from wrestling with the control scheme, which frustrated me deeply.Another big issue for me was the map screen needs some sort of room-relative indicator or at the very least a directional indicator for which way the player is facing. I was constantly double checking the map to try and get my bearings on which direction I'm intending to go. Not being able to tell where I am in the room or which direction I'm looking was disorienting.Outside of these two points, I really enjoyed this game. I liked the characters for the most part, the main mystery/story of the game was incredibly well paced. Lore bits were given at just the right intervals and amounts to be concise and not overwhelming. Bite sized pieces of the bigger puzzle really made this game for me.Overall Lovely.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute gem of a game, and perfect if you're wanting to scratch that familiar Silent Hill/Resident Evil itch. The art style is masterfully used and the locales are engaging and spooky to walk through. Combat feels fun and very responsive to control as well. The story is simple but effective, with a good twist at the end and enjoyable characters across the board. It's absolutely worth the price and can't wait to see more from this team!
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished 1st playthrough, of which this is a fantastic game if you like something retro that teases the brain and pulls from both Resident Evil and SIlent Hill. Plenty of secrets to find that are unique compared to most games that I can't mention without spoiling, but that combined with the atmosphere and story left me really enjoying it and going back for some extra playthroughs in new game+ mode. So yes, it offers something different on second playthrough for more replayability. Recommend checking it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent survival horror title, if a little more forgiving than the games it draws influence from. It offers classic resident evil tank controls if that's your cup of tea, but you can also just use the sticks to move the character in the direction you move the stick. Normal mode has an abundance of ammo and healing items, and if you somehow manage to use them all up you can always run around to trash cans/vending machines/your car to get a few bullets/small med kits, so there's really no chance you can get yourself "stuck" because you're out of resources. The developer's roadmap for the game mentioned they're adding a Hard mode, which I'm assuming will increase enemy aggressiveness and limit supplies, putting it more in line with classic Resident Evil games.And none of that is to mention the art direction, which is absolutely spot on. It's like walking around those fixed camera indoor areas of Final Fantasy 7. A lot of recent games try to emulate that PS1 look, but this one really nails it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with only one huge issue:The D-pad is forced to tank controls, and the analogue stick is forced to non-tank controls, without any in-game option to switch this. Tank controls is not the issue I have— it’s the inconsistency. If you’re going to include both movement styles in the game AT ALL, make it adjustable for both the D-pad and the analogue stick.If you want to play with tank on analogue or non-tank on d-pad (like me,) you can simply turn one of them into the other externally to the game via the per-game Steam controller mapping. This is the only large issue I have had with the game and think the rest of the controls and the gameplay are wonderful. This massively glaring issue just stuck with me since it was literally my first encounter within the game, which left quite a bad first impression.Other than that, I think the pacing and the map size are perfect; nothing’s overwhelming, and the atmosphere actually really comfortable-feeling. I think the hint stations should have some sort of dialog to better confirm with the player (and acknowledge he’s about to receive a hint,) as, on first use, I ended up using one by accident, not realizing it was a hint for puzzles. So I got spoiled for something. But after that point I just kept an arm’s distance from the stations to avoid more puzzle spoilers.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: I was not really into the aesthetic of Crow Country at first. I didn't love the setting, the combat controls, the visual clutter and pixel hunts. BUT after a while the game won me over big time. The map design is simply fantastic, and the puzzles are beyond fenomenal. The gameplay really clicked with me by the half-way point and I finished the game in frenzied excitement. I was surprised to see that the story actually came together quite nicely in the end. It's hardly a masterpiece, but a fun tale nonetheless. If you like survival horror, I say give this game a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game, the atmosphere, the puzzles, the art work, the stupid quiz machine.  I am not the biggest survival horror fan by any means, but this game just grabbed me.  Once I started it I had to keep playing and finish it, its a short game for sure, but its super worthwhile.  my 2024 GOTY is torn between Animal Well and this.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend if you're a fan of survivor horror games from the PlayStation 1-GameCube era. A callback to the Resident Evil style horror/puzzle style, Crow Country is mysterious, rewarding, atmospheric, and fun. Please jump right into the Murder of Crows difficulty, its the perfect amount of challenge!
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: As someone with mixed experience with classic survival horror (read: I'm bad at them because I'm clumsy and bad at resource management, mostly), this did a great job of walking the line between throwback flavor and not being too ball-busting for someone with the aforementioned issues. And if you -are- good at survival horror, there's already a speedrun scene and some rewards for playing with more challenge added.Also love the tight-knit story, the well-timed humor without being a non-stop quipfest, and just the general layout of the entire park kind of making sense. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best survival horror homages to classic games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill. While it doesn't do a whole lot to change up the fundamental formula of the games it takes clear inspiration from, it still does enough to set itself up with it own distinctive identity particular with regards to its very bizarre yet thoroughly intriguing narrative. Definitely recommend this for anyone whose a fan of RE and/or SH, particularly the earlier retro entries in those respective games. Indie games just don't get much better than this game does.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful game. It's a little bit short, but excellently crafted.Unique, beautiful art style with an uncommon camera perspective.Everything is carefully designed so that it complements the genre perfectly. It's a really well tuned old school survival horror with a focus on puzzles and exploration.I personally liked the story, it felt different from things we've seen in the genre before, and it kept me engaged and guessing through the course of it.Any complaint about it being too easy is resolved by hard mode.With any luck and if the devs keep adding updates, we get a random mode where key items and codes are shuffled for each run.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't finish games these days but this was the first game in years to really suck me in again!  I love resident evil 4 and this felt  reminiscent in the best way. It took some of the staples of survival horror and turned them into interesting plot elements and story beats like reflecting on all your tools at the end great game
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty solid little game. The story was interesting and most of the puzzles were fun to figure out. The only slight issue I had with the game was that it was kinda easy, I beat the game first try without dying once but they are planning on adding a hard mode so it's not really a big issue imo. Some of the puzzles are pretty clever but a few of them I kinda solved by accident. I'd recommend not using any of the hints the game gives you and going for all the secrets, context clues and notes that are scattered should give you everything you need to figure them out on your own. I'd highly recommend trying the demo if you're on the fence, it takes about 4 hours going for everything (minus the crow hunt thing that's like a new game plus) but it's a very enjoyable 4 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Main story takes around 6 hours to complete, but those 6 hours are consistently good so I wouldn't call that a downside. My only real complaint is that the modern controls make the game incredibly easy.As such I would recommend moving around using the D-Pad to make the gameplay more tense (D-Pad uses tank controls). I plan on playing through once again, using only that control scheme this time.Like the Resident Evil games, this game has extra content depending on how well you do throughout the campaign, so it's very replay friendly.Overall I was very satisfied with this. It was a well made survival horror game hearkening back to the classics lots of people grew up with.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: There is something I absolutely love about PSX and PS2 era horror games. And Crow County manages to capture that lightning-in-a-bottle well. With some cleaning up for a modern audience, it manages to hold on to what made that era of horror games so special.Firstly, the soundscape and visuals. And they really bring you in. The sounds and music aided in the experience the whole while. Each small area in the park felt alive and part of the world you were in. The creatures themselves sounded as good as I could have ever wanted them to. Even in the dark, the noises they would make made it clear what was lurking just out of sight. And the visuals just helped bring you back to the time. This game clearly takes heavy inspiration from PSX era games. A little cleaned up here-and-there, but it brings you back to that time. I will note, I am a sucker for this aesthetic and it won't be for everyone. But for a horror game especially, it aids in bringing out a certain shock and terror from the creatures. It truly elevates the experience to new heights.The gameplay is done splendidly. The movement is responsive and fluid. The shooting can be a little clunky, but I don't mind since survivor horror games aren't meant to be played like a typical shooter. The puzzles are rather simple and the map is large enough to feel expansive, but just small enough for backtracking around to not be too painful. The journey is stunning beginning to end.The story is rather simple, but I enjoyed my time with it. It's a nice set piece that ties the whole experience together. But it is clearly the side piece for everything else which is the starring elements of the game.This game is special. For $15, the price is perfect. The game is rather short, but horror games of the time were usually. But the game wants you to play through it more. And I felt myself drawn back to run through the adventure as Mara right away. I would recommend anyone to pick this game up and immerse yourself in the world. Take in the sights and sounds. And enjoy yourself with Crow County.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best survival horror games I have played in some time. The best monster design, period. Not that long but I don't think it needed to be. It tells a concise story and wraps itself up without feeling as if it was dragging it's feet. I don't have anything negative to say about this game. Pat yourselves on the back, SFB Games.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: This game came across my suggested games and I was sure glad it did. I tried out the demo first and dumped an hour into it. Decided I wanted the full game and have been playing now for 4 hours straight. Its like some one decided to make a resident evil game but on the Nintendo 64. So far I have loved the puzzles as they are not super hard but are challenging enough to make me have to think. The controls are very similar to RE1 or something like Parasite Eve. If you are a fan of early 2000's horror games you are going to love this. These guys have done a great job and it really hit that nostalgia factor for me. Well done.Just finished the game after 8 hours, totally worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: This game has solid writing, interesting puzzles and much more than just nostalgia for the PSX/GameCube survival horror genre. It resonated with my soul, and left me wanting for more backstory.My first playthrough was just under 7 hours, and I managed to find 10 secrets out of 15. The game was challenging enough to keep tension up, while not being frustrating. As a Silent Hill fan, this game scratched a itch I had for a long long time, in a gentle way.Try the demo, then buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the game I hate to have recommend/not recommend rating on Steam. I really do.I would say "very positive" fits better than "overwhelmingly positive" because the game is great, but not in the range of perfection. First of all game is not scary. Not a single moment in the game... ok, well maybe the ending... scared me. I won't spoil it for you, but it is very clever how the game told realistic scare in the game. I was able to kill most enemies in the game and had plenty of med packs to heal. are not hard at all. Some are kid friendly level (literally put the color in order that's displaying next to you) while few of them are flat out annoying ("remember that switch across the long hallway? Yeah, you actually use that here to solve puzzle, sorry that there's no single clue for you")  is okay. I would say it is equivalent to gamecube remake of Resident Evil. Fairly snappy, responsive. _childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible experience all around. Visuals perfectly blend a few different retro aesthetics while maintaining it's own charm, Fun callbacks to it's obvious inspirations. If you love old school survival horror gaming it's a must get. I can't wait to begin my next playthrough with the items I just unlocked
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a cozy survival horror game that can be a fantastic intro to the genre for first-timers thanks to its forgiving standard difficulty, modern control options, and generous supply of ammo and healing items. Purists can also enjoy its hard mode and classic tank control option. Both sides can also enjoy this game's cute retro visual style, intriguing story and setting, and unlockable rewards that encourage replayability. Games like Crow Country, which seem like throwbacks to classic genres but are genuinely fun and well-designed additions to said genres, are quickly becoming some of my favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome neo-PS1 survival horror. It has just enough modern quality of life improvements not to feel like a chore, but not so much as to not feel right at home on an actual PS1 lol. I enjoyed every minute of this adventure, and if you like survival horror, you probably will too. I got an A+ on my first run, but I'll probably go back for the S rank sometime.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing short experience. Really well thought-out map and exploration, fun characters with lots of funny moments. Game still does a lot to put me on edge and got me a few times even without the need of jumpscares. The mystery of it even after beating it makes me want more of this universe. Really impressed, thank you so much to the devs, and thank you to ockaroid for composing the soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches the Resident Evil itch a bit, but not quite.Setting and artstyle is amazing, with decent controls that work most of the time. Dialogues are fun and the story is okay.Seems a bit to easy though. Lots of items/ammo scattered everywhere, with questionably placed explosive barrels or electric walltraps to help further reduce ammo usage. I found myself always having max medkits & antidotes. There is also no inventory management, which I consider to be a crucial gameplay-loop in the Survival Horror genre. Still a great recommendation, but the price is a bit too steep for me ($15 would've been perfect).
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: A small bite sized survival horror game for those who love Resident Evil and Silent Hill. Not entirely long, but it still has tons of repeatability in terms of Ranks, Secrets, and Additional optional unlocks. The main charm is the art style, as the PS1 style effects and soundtrack are amazing. This was a great game to play late at night, even if it's not REALLY that scary, yet it does have some good moments.If you enjoy any of those games above, and a fresh take on them with a lot of charm and love, pick this up

_childDocuments_.review: nice little survival horror indie game. stylistically unique compared to most games and the low res graphics do a lot for its charm and grungy atmosphere. environments are beautiful and packed with detail, although sometimes to its detriment. Music is wonderful and suits the atmosphere, and the compression on the tracks makes them all the better. The game is certainly not silent hill, a little closer to resident evil, yet retains a unique identity that sets it apart from others. I would describe it as survival horror for people who care more about the gameplay  over the 'horror' aspect, but it still has a few good scares that it utilizes sparingly, and never to the point of going overboard.Controls are janky, but feel more like the unintentional jank and intentional jank are at odds. puzzles are pretty good and theres a hint box if you get stuck. My advice: dont overthink any of the puzzles. Reading *and* visual clues are equally important. story is interesting, and has a solid coup de grace. without spoiling anything else, a good game, and i feel satisfied with a single playthrough of 5 hours, and i might play it again just to speed through. if youre interested in the gameplay, definitely pick it up to waste a weekend, especially if it's on sale. the mood and experience alone, however, are worth the full price. the style, art, music, and aesthetics are amazing. it felt like playing an old game that was ported to pc and the only thing that could have made experiencing it any better would be running the game on a CRT tv.

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a very classic survival horror game with a Final Fantasy VII look to it. It's a real fun time overall.It's a bit friendlier than actual survival horror games of the era, letting you choose between tank and 3D controls, and having an item limit only on consumables.It's also a little short and easy. I've only died once because I wanted to see the death animation and it took me 4 hours to complete it. This might all sound like the game isn't worth your time, but it's far from the truth. I just wanted to focus on very few things people might complain about first.Crow Country is really good. I was in love with exploring the abandoned theme park and collecting items. There are a TON of secrets in this game of which I've only found a third. The enemy variety is also pretty nuts, with around 7 or 8 different types or clearly different enemies, along with 4 or 5 different traps. The game clearly doesn't want to be the scariest game ever as evidenced by the Final Fantasy 7-like look, and it is in parts more funny than it is actually scary. That's not to say it doesn't have the understanding of the atmosphere. Enemies might look a little goofy, but when you barely have bullets and are in the dark, it's pretty damn spooky!The story is quite good and reminds me of the original Resident Evil with a few NPCs just hanging around the park, as most of the time story is told through the notes. That said, the actual plot is very different and quite unique, with its own twists and turns, all of which I've enjoyed.One of the things that made me breathe a sigh of relief is a feature that any short game must have: Crow Country does have unlockables. I was really sad that the newest Alone in the Dark game didn't, but Crow Country has a new mode along with some goodies that are given to you based on your rank. Hell, maybe something more too, I've just completed it once!If you've enjoyed Signalis, you should play this game. It's not as out-there presentation wise, but if you like Metroid-y gameplay of old survival horrors, it's a must play!

_childDocuments_.review: Classic RE-style game that leans more into puzzles and exploration of the colorful world, rather than combat. It has very self-aware type of story with quirky, even low-key cute characters. When you enter combat stance you can't move just like in the original RE games, but you get a laser pointer that helps you aim. It's one of the main mechanics of the entire game. You try to headshot enemies (altough headshots are not as important here), you shoot collectibles and buttons, similar to how you shoot off hidden medals in newer RE games.The game also has a few very satisfying puzzles that make you use pen & paper combo to solve them, especially if we're talking about . Great game overall, it's a better game than some of the actual survival horror progenitors.

The mechanics are simple as well with some excellent puzzle design and some fun secrets to uncover. Would love to see this team make a spiritual successor.9/10 Very good game and on my top 5 list for 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: has it all. Weird monsters, a dark story, untrustworthy strangers, a creepy environment, pleasingly clunky combat controls, door puzzles, exploration, resource management, and a bizarre environment that is overwhelming at first but eventually allows you to master it.For the first half, I didn't understand why so many genre enthusiasts raved so positively about this game. I began nursing a (somewhat perverse) intention to leave a Not Recommended Steam review, because I felt a negative voice was needed to temper its "Overwhelmingly Positive" record. Sure, it's good, and it nails the survival horror idiom, and it does everything well, and it's creepy, and the retro graphics and setting, while original in style, evoke nostalgia for the very first games of this type. But where's the innovation? Where's the "aha" moment?  When can I expect the huge meta twist that blows me away, like, it's a game inside a game? Or it scans my Steam account to turn my greatest gaming fears against me? Or I have to plug my controller into a different port? There's gotta be something like this, but where is it? Where's the mindf*ck?As I slowly sank into the second half of the game, I realized what the mindf*ck is: . This is simply an excellently designed survival horror game that does everything right, and like all the best survival horror, once you've been soaking in it long enough, it becomes a part of you.There's really not much else to say - you won't regret playing this and that's all you really need to know.  I do have a couple more comments and then I'll let you get to it.If I felt any disappointment in my experience, it's only because I chose the Survival Horror (medium) difficulty instead of Murder of Crows (hard). Once I got the hang of things, I never really worried about dying, and certainly not about running out of ammunition. Genre veterans, play on hard![Bonus: there is also Exploration Mode (easy), which eliminates combat altogether! If your hands aren't as quick as they used to be, you don't have to deal with getting overwhelmed by monsters and can just enjoy the creepy atmosphere, puzzles, and story. Or if you have a friend who never played survival horror, this could be a great introduction.]When I first became interested in the game, I shrugged and decided to wait to buy it until I finished some other things I'm playing, or maybe until the price dropped. DO NOT BE LIKE ME. If you have a job, this is easily worth full price $20 USD and 7-8 hours of your time.  (Luckily for me, a friend gifted me a copy. It would have been SO dumb of me to miss out on this over $20.)Right now, tonight, support these devs, buy full price, turn out the lights, and dig into a perfectly realized example of what survival horror can be.

_childDocuments_.review: Nostalgic mix of a bunch of classic games with game play modernized to provide a ton of quality of life features you wish those old games had. It's not a very challenging game and definitely more puzzle forward, but the story was way better than I thought going in and the bonus collectibles all provided in game value as upgrades, so never felt like a chore to get.Wish the combat was a bit more robust, like enemies needing to be taken down in more specific ways as currently they are mostly just different health and speeds. Ammo drops are plenty, so you never have to worry about running out of anything. Both are positive for accessibility, so I can comfortably recommend this to more people that likely would pass it over if it was trying to be an exact RE clone. Chances are if you like horror action metroidvania style games, and have a hunger to play a forgotten PS1 classic made in the modern era, you are going to love this one like I have.

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and very refined love letter to the graphics of FF7 and gameplay Silent Hill on the PS1. The primitive models and noisy filter create a genuinely nostalgic and heartwarming aesthetic. The setting of an abandoned theme park is a delight and really helps sell the unnerving "what happened here" atmosphere. The level design is well realised and the attention to detail and interactivity is truly amazing. Click on everything, you wont regret it. The puzzles are charming and well designed. Carefully balancing ambiguity and logic, with well written clues that hide the answers in plain sight just enough to make you think, without straying into obscurity as some other puzzle games tend to do these days. The solution really makes sense and there's a feeling of genuine achievement in finding it.Along with the puzzles are secrets, which may not be vital to the progression of the game, but I assure are more than worth the time and the head scratching to work out. They are slightly more difficult than the progression focused puzzles but they bare some interesting items you wont want to miss. The gunplay / combat is tricky, but that's a key component of this genre. You can't let people 360 no scope zombies like they're on some highlight reel on tik tok, this is survival horror. Aiming and choosing when to take your shot matters. However the game is surprisingly lenient with resources, which means you wont end up having to save scum for the perfect run and wont spend too much time worrying about if you should pull the trigger. So its less focused on resource management and that allows you to relax and enjoy the game more. Overall the game really feels as if it hit its target, everything feels well thought out and realised, it doesn't appear to be struggling to present itself, it's clearly been made by people who understand the survival horror genre. The humour in the writing is re-reassuringly self aware and rewards you for clicking on things the way you tend to in this kind of game. At this price you cant go wrong, definitely worth playing for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The first few rooms serve as an introduction to the game controls, similar to most games, but in addition to that,  In these initial rooms, the player is required to familiarize themselves with the controls and shooting mechanics. Since the controls are straightforward, this brief introduction is enough to make the player feel ready to proceed.The user interface is minimal, with only one small UI element on the bottom right of the screen representing the "aiming" button. When aiming, a reload button appears. When you approach points of interest or interactive elements, a prompt will appear, making it easy to notice. Other than that, the main menu and pause button are reminiscent of Silent Hill and Resident Evil, suggesting direct inspiration from those games.This was one of the main selling points for me. The retro feeling and aesthetic the game evokes clearly stem from a place of passion, not an empty shell. Every location and 3D model has been crafted with love and attention to detail, complementing the simplistic yet well-curated UI. The animations are smooth and fitting, though sometimes they may appear a bit 'cartoony' for a horror theme. For example, Mara's walking animation is so full of swagger that you might forget she's supposed to be investigating a missing person, not strutting down a fashion catwalk.I loved the game's sound design, which perfectly captures a retro feeling. A detail I noticed later in the game is that each character has a unique sound (a sort of beep) representing their voice, adding a distinct touch to their dialogue. The dialogues hit a soft spot for me. The music is also well-designed, with ambient noise creating an atmosphere while exploring, and more intense, "fightey" music during encounters. Sometimes a more intense ‘puzzle music’ may kick int too. It's nothing revolutionary, but it is executed very well. The story takes place in Country Crow, the theme park funded by Edward Crow. I have a grudge against this setting; I'm getting tired of theme park stories, theme restaurants, and similar concepts. It feels like the horror genre is suffering from "FNAF syndrome." That said, I must admit that despite my dislike for the theme park setting, the execution is quite good and i actually liked it.The level design is not overly convoluted. While there is a fair amount of backtracking, which is common in this genre, it isn't too bad. You can unlock 'return paths' that make backtracking quicker and provide new ways to access previously distant areas.We start by playing as Special Agent Mara Forset, who is searching for the park’s missing creator, Edward Crow. During our investigation, we meet and interact with several characters. While I can't reveal much about these characters without spoiling the story, I can say that Mara’s sense of humor is a highlight. Her sarcastic remarks during gameplay are hilarious and suggest that the game creator has a keen awareness of the genre and its sometimes absurd obstacles. For instance, when Mara encounters a box blocking her path, she might sarcastically comment, “Oh, a box is in my way, how on earth will I ever get to the other side?” before simply moving the box. Moments like these add a delightful layer of humor to the game. Other than that characters have their own archs and motives and is pretty standard with some twist here and there.I usually complain in this section about games I review but this one is actually well equipped with different types of foes and traps. The things you have to watch out for during gameplay and the escalation of enemies encounter is right on point.The game is a classical survival horror with unique twists. Its 3D movable camera with an isometric view is a standout feature because key items and enemies can hide behind walls, requiring you to adjust the camera to find them. This view-style blends elements of fixed cameras and over-the-shoulder perspectives quite well.The aim-shoot mechanic, reminiscent of Cold Fear, is a highlight. Holding the aiming button allows precise control over the crosshair. Unlike Resident Evil, there's no auto-aim, but Mara automatically faces enemies within range.The gameplay follows the typical survival horror loop: explore areas, fight enemies, gather resources, solve puzzles, unlock new areas. What sets this game apart are its unconventional puzzle types and the engaging aiming mechanic, which I particularly enjoy.The game features a "decisions matter" mechanic where interactions with characters influence the game's ending. This encourages players to replay and explore different outcomes.The game is also well-suited for speedruns and challenges, adding to its replay value.The absence of cut-scenes and voice acting, along with the lack of a clear objective indicator, suggests that this game may not appeal to everyone. If you prefer games with extensive voice acting or explicit objective markers, you might want to skip this one. Progression in objectives and lore primarily occurs through character dialogues and reading files, so paying attention to these details is essential for understanding the game's narrative and objectives.However, for both longtime fans and newcomers to the genre, the game offers a solid, accessible survival horror experience.The camera occasionally hides important key items, leading players to mistakenly believe a room has been thoroughly searched. This can result in unnecessary roaming and backtracking due to unclear directions.Some puzzles are overly obvious, providing little sense of achievement upon completion, while others may feel overly challenging. I wish there were additional modes like Mercenaries in Resident Evil or Extra-Crisis in Dino Crisis 2 to add replayability.There's one puzzle in particular that still frustrates me to think about. It is irrelevant to the story and game progression, but is unnecessarily difficult. I never unlocked all extras :(It's an exceptional game and definitely worth the price. I thoroughly enjoyed every moment of gameplay, despite getting lost a couple of times due to the camera catching me off guard or my own oversight with objective dialogues. The game's difficulty is well balanced, providing a challenging yet rewarding experience that's hard to match.For me, a dedicated Survival Horror fan, the combination of style, humor, storytelling, and game mechanics is perfect and incredibly refreshing.

_childDocuments_.review: The PlayStation can produce mind-boggling effects.EDIT: Review in progress. I loved the demo and so far the full game doesn't disappoint. Definitely worth checking out for fans of classic Resident Evil or retro horror games in general.Gameplay: They do a good job of emulating the feel of a PS1 horror game with just a couple modern touches like the 2-stick control scheme; tank controls are still available with the D-pad which is neat. The game is rather generous with supplies so far, which does bring down the survival aspect a bit. Also the enemy AI is a bit dumb sometimes.Story: Pretty simple so far. It's easy to get an idea of what's going on if you just read the dialog and notes. That being said I haven't finished the game yet so it's not like I really know what's happening. I personally don't need a super complex plot to get hooked on a game like this.Presentation: I think they nailed the atmosphere. It manages to be both oppressive and campy similar to the original Resident Evil. The visuals are gloomy and the field of view is limited. The music and sound effects are darn spooky.

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a game with an interesting mystery at the heart of it told well through it's environments, characters and notes strewn about the premises of crow country it also gets tied up neatly in the end without any loose ends or inconsistencies. (The one exception is the number in blood, i don't get that one)  I found myself overall enjoying my time with the game and really liked the different areas aesthetics of the theme park, all in all i recommend this game, however i have some points of friction with it. The cutesy aesthetic doesn't mix well with horror, if we judge survival horror by the constituent parts of it's name the horror part is sorely missing out, but in the games defense a lot of survival horror games don't pull off horror all that well either given that these type of games are very action heavy.When it comes to the combat and resource management the aiming system and weapon switching is all very well made and feels smooth, the aiming system in particular is a nice touch. The loot in this game is very plentiful, and it also seems to use smart loot systems meaning that if you're running low on items trash bins or vending machines will provide you with everything you need. As convenient as these systems are i find that they ruin the very concept of having limited resources as they reward a reckless playstyle with more items and give nothing to the players who are conservative with their supplies, i can count on one hand the times i actually found items in trashcans or vending machines in my playthrough, never did i feel that i was low on resources as they are strewn all over the place in heaps.Lastly when it comes to puzzles i did enjoy them and there were none that were obtuse, the only one i did struggle with relates to a door missing a handle which is one of the games 15 secrets, all secrets are cleverly thought out and hide either ammo for the powerful magnum or weapon upgrades that come in handy.The one issue i have with the regular puzzles however is the amount of handholding the game does, in most situations the answer to the puzzle will be written out on several staff notes around the place or very obviously pointed out in text when inspecting an object, this felt rather annoying after a while but is most prevalent in the first half of the game, i wish the devs had added an option to reduce the amount of hints as it made it feel like they had no faith whatsoever in the players ability to come to the correct conclusions.One example is a puzzle that involves getting a code out of a sequence of slideshow pictures, right after i finish this puzzle i notice that the code is plain written on the wall in an adjacent room. This type of thing happens a lot ingame.Overall this is a recommend from me, but this game will not be everyone's cup of tea. It took me a total of 9 hours to finish the game with all secrets on survival difficulty. A controller is highly recommended for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This far exceeded my expectations!In an age of "retro survival horror" that consists of mostly janky 3rd person games with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ "killer chases you" AI and a VHS filter overlaying the graphics, Crow Country actually manages to deliver great puzzles, solid (if basic) combat, a story that becomes more compelling than I'd have thought, and some great graphical touches that genuinely make me think "it feels like a PS1/2 game that pulls off some great effects."Very solid entry in a genre that's lacking this level of authenticity!

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing horror game. Had me jump from a heart attack several times throughout the game and they were all well deserved. I felt tense most of the game yet so invested to keep going. I haven't found all the secrets yet and definitely will be playing more to figure them all out as the puzzles are fun but not impossible. I had a little notebook to write things down and it's so fun to really work through puzzles like that. The art-style is absolutely gorgeous, calling back to old retro games WHILE still being filled with it's own personality. Visually sticking out from a lot of games trying to relive the 'old retro days' by picking a low poly style that feels so well done and genuinely unique. Another thing I enjoyed was how well it played as I feel like a lot of games trying to use the retro look make themselves mechanically difficult or clunky to mimic the old days. Not this game!! I loved how this played and never felt confused or frustrated with the mechanics, anytime there was a mistake it was of my own doing. It definitely feels inspired from games like SH3 or the early resident evils but is also it's own thing. Definitely popping it on my list of favorite games and would KILL to see more games do stuff like this. If you like this kind of game, get it!! It's amazing I promise.

_childDocuments_.review: Classic RE fans, REJOICE! Crow Country is an amazing and very competent survival horror that had me invested from the first time I booted it up with it's fun and creepy theme park setting to it's story setting up mysteries within the first minute that massively pay off. I came for the game play and was not disappointed at all, it has a very tight feeling sense of resource management. It isn't so difficult to be unwelcoming to a survival horror newbie though and plays very much with risk vs reward mechanics with some slight RNG that is mostly avoidable if you wish but overall enhances and compliments the game. The combat is also and extemely fascinating take on classic survival horror combat with RE4esque aiming that I thought would be clunky but was executed very well. This is also the first survival horror game I've played in a good while that has had good puzzles that are challenging and work your brain on a first play without being so obtuse that they're frustrating. The story while a bit predictable was also surprisingly gripping and went in quite unexpected directions. Overall I give this game a glowing recommendation having thoroughly enjoyed my time and ready to play this game again.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic tribute to old school, 90s survival horror games. It's basically Silent Hill or Resident Evil with a FF7 original character model. It has a lot of unique visuals and a very cool aesthetic. I totally recommend to anyone who grew up in the 90s and likes survival horror games. The aiming isn't great but it was fine. You should dodge most of the enemies to conserve ammo anyways. Any old school survival horror fan will tell you that.

Highly recommended to anyone that likes survival horror.Also the music and writing are legitimately quite good, and the attention to detail when it comes to examining objects and secret hunting are above and beyond.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like it could have been a PS1 game in the best sort of way. Played on controller, and for that old-anxiety feeling, opted to use the D-pad over the analog sticks which made the difference for me. Would totally play through again to try for an S rank, or just to mess around with the unlocks.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: What a nice game. It feels like I'm playing a PS1 Survival Horror. It's visuals and aesthetic is pretty much unique, just like the setting: It's a game that takes place in the year 1990, around a abandoned amusement park. How cool, right? Not to mention that the combat, explorations and puzzles are very fun, and the story is simply amazing. Loved everything about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: The term love letter is thrown around a lot these days, and this is yet another instance where it needs to be used. I do feel like this one stands out among anything falling under the "love letter" category. Inspired by the likes of survival horror gems from the Playstation era, Crow Country does more than simply imitate, it re-works and attempts to do its own thing in many many areas, and in that attempt, it succeeds in fantastic fashion. This is the coziest game I have ever played, masterful art direction and musical composition and very fun writing have landed this on my list of favorites. Like all time favorites. You should pick this up even if you don't necessarily like the genre this sits in, it's that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: A curious mixture of hope and dread indeed.This game is top tier retro styled horror at its finest. With a compelling story, unique gameplay and absolutely dripping with its own artistic style. In combination with the top down camera angle & 360 degree turning, this is exactly how modern tank controls should play. If you have a controller, this how the game is meant to be played. With no restrictions on inventory slots and easy weapon swapping, the majority of the game is spent on exploration, monster killing, note reading, puzzle solving, key item finding all whilst trying to figure out what is happening in the park. There are a lot of areas that have optional puzzles as well as optional environment interactions. Their helpful to complete, but are not required to finish the story. If you need help on what to do there's a hint crow in the opening area past the gate, using hits could count against your endgame ranking, but you'll most likely be doing multiple playthrough's for that S ranking.I suppose if I had any gripes about the game is there's no mini map, no way to track your exact location on the map in the area your in, no reminders or recording of your objectives or checkpoints at key moments in the story. But you do have to take into account that this is a PS1 styled game, games didn't hold your hand back then, this one won't either. You also can't move from you place on the map when you aim, but you can completely rotate as well as quick turn into aiming depending on which direction you facing. Might be a stretch if they added in voice acting, but not really needed for this game. Have like a cheesy vibe to it, but its also kinda good too. Maybe add in a leaderboard for speedrunners, showing their overall metrics while they were playing the game.On my first play through I used 39 heals, 5 hints used, 10/15 secrets found, & 0 lives used on survival mode, thankfully rankings are not determined by total death's, saves or overall timed played. You can unlock additional items that'll help you along the way to reach that S ranking, these can be toggle on and off in the pause menu.This is an absolute must play if you looking for a game to scratch that exploitative survival horror itch. You can also play the game "without getting attacked" in exploration mode. I prefer survival mode as its not too challenge, and the looming threat adds to the horror aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite game from 2024. Nailed every point and aspect of gameplay and tone and then added a very necessary hard mode, pleasing both the beginners and experienced in survival horror, created a loveable and funny cast of characters, a great mystery story surrounded by a gorgeous soundtrack and sound design, and then stuck the landing. Freaking video games.... you win again.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game ! I loved the demo and I love the game.The gameplay feels great, the shooting is perfect for a survival horror.The puzzles and secrets are not too easy but I never struggled for too long (yet). I really loved the dungeon puzzle.I really like the art style and atmosphere too.I very strongly recommend !
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Is it weird to describe a survival horror game as charming?, because that's the word that sums this one up best for me. The grainy PS1-evoking pixel filter, cutesy but creepy monster designs, themed environments, atmospheric audio, it's all top notch. I found the balance of the normal difficulty a bit too easy, which removed a lot of the tension from the experience, so if this isn't your first survival horror game, you may want to consider bumping the difficulty up to "Murder of Crows". Otherwise though, I thoroughly recommend this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Love how all of the part is connected with eachother and that you need to finish the puzzle's to access them. Everything in the game is very interconnected and the atmosphere adds to it. Love me a indie game like this. I wonder if there will be more Crow Country content. I'd like a Artbook for this one, if possible.

_childDocuments_.review: is it the scariest survival horror game i've ever played? not really, but the atmosphere is top notch. story can be a little confusing / vague but overall is very good, especially because of how fantastic mara is as a protagonist, and how great her cast of supporting characters is too. puzzles are top notch, they're challenging but nothing crazy difficult like other modern survival horror games like to make them (love alisa and tormented souls to death but some of those puzzles were psychotic)ost is god tieroverall pls support this game if you love retro survival horror everything about it is just so enjoyable

I'll probably do a replay at some point, but I hope this gets a successor!
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun little horror game with a very cozy mood. Pretty much classic Resident Evil with a Final Fantasy VII aesthetic, reminiscent of the pre-rendered background, even if this is done in fully 3D and it all comes together very nicely. Took about 7 hours for my first playthrough. Along with some actions, there are many secrets to find and puzzles to solve. For the puzzles you often have to take note of what is found in certain documents, hinting at or giving you the solution to a puzzle that might be on the other side of the map. I would highly recommend this to classic horror fans, or just lovers of PS1 aesthetics.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep it short since there are a trillion positive reviews on this game and no one wants to read a wall of text.Pre-summary of review:- A clearly resident evil inspired survival horror with an incredible story line that keeps you guessing.Positives:- Resident evil inspired in all the good ways. Limited inventory, dilapidated horror setting, slow moving enemies that take a lot of hits, save room music, etc.!- Great puzzles! Some are a little silly / tongue-in-cheek, but it makes sense because the game takes place in an amusement park and some of the puzzles were in-universe made for children to solve.- The story line is the best I have played in any indie survival horror period. Bar none! it has twists and turns. This is the gold standard!Negatives:- Shooting mechanic can be a little awkward, so don't think of it so much as an action game. The shooting can leave a lot to be desired.- Graphics for environments are great but the characters including enemies look very geometric like balloon animals? Some of the creatures look more funny than scary, like bloody mutant Bert and Ernies. Not a big deal you get used to it!- I think you could speed run this in less than 3 hours. Normal game is maybe 5-6 hours (estimate). It's a short game! I wish it was twice as long. You may find it to be the perfect length though!Post-summary of review:- Buy it now!
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: This is an insanely charming game. I was immediately sold on the PSX era of graphics with a modern touch, brought back a lot of nostalgia and as a fan of the survival horror genre of the likes of Resident Evil this was a great experience, you can feel the love and effort put into this game.The game has great story telling, great atmosphere and great controls, the game play loop is pretty satisfying, the puzzles are interesting and as long as you make sure to read the notes scattered around, their solutions are readily available with a little thinking. And despite the horror atmosphere, it wasn't too scary but the fixed camera perspective, limited lighting, the unnerving music and the various cries of the monsters off in the distance keeps the game pretty unsettling but the game also takes some moments to break that tension with some of the silly remarks Mara will make as you interact with certain objects.Overall the game was a blast to play and I highly recommend it.

Highly recommended for folks who are both new to the genre and veterans too.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well crafted little game. Great and fun puzzles that are actually thematically apropriate since they are part of the setting. Combat takes a bit to get used to but it's also well ballanced and fun while allowing the player to decide if they want to engage or avoid.There are two game modes and if you are familiar with survival horrors then one is easy and second is super easy. Story is very well implemented - starts you with a very basic premise and allows you to explore and look for notes. _childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Cool and engaging tribute to early survival horror games that very much captures what made them enjoyable.  The dollhouse-like aesthetic created from the visual fidelity and camera angle cleverly gives the game its own unique identity while harkening back to techniques that built the atmosphere of older games such as Silent Hill's fog creating a more intimate and moody atmosphere while reducing the need for high draw distance.  My only major complaint is the low difficulty ceiling; it wasn't difficult to beat the game without dying on the first attempt, and then got an S rank on the second or third try.  I never felt like I had to worry about resources running out, which is a large part of the tension of games like this.  Still, it didn't get in the way of me enjoying the game the first time around, but does make it less interesting to return to and master.  Hopefully this is addressed in the upcoming hard mode update.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a mindset that tank controls and fixed camera angles in horror games are bad. I would like to qualify why this needn't be the case, and why isometric free camera and so-called 'modern' free-roam control schemes can actually be worse for such a game.This game, Crow Country, is my case study.So, let's talk about what a fixed camera does. A fixed camera makes it the game developer's responsibility, of what is, and isn't visible, in any given area of a game. This means that the visibility of significant items and visual scares will always be up to the developer, and I, the player, won't 'miss' them due to the angle I'm pointing my camera in, since the camera will always be pointed at what's important. In theory, anyway.Unfortunately, fixed camera angles do come at a particular price: You can't always see threats, beyond scene transitions. This puts the responsibility in the player's hands, of where they are standing, in relation to an enemy, but simultaneously puts the responsibility of where the enemy spawn placements are, in the developer's hands. If the devs want to be enormous ♥♥♥♥♥, they can place a zombie immediately around a corner, blind, where you can run into it. It is then up to you, as the player, to figure out how to take that corner zombie, and lure it into a shotgun fellatio session, rather than letting yourself get grabbed.This may strike you as tedious, bad design, but it's a game of deciding where to have your sacrifices. A zombie you can't see can still be scary, even if it's a pain in the ass. As long as it's not a trick over-relied upon.What's NOT enjoyable, ever, on the other hand--is when you are required to 'herd' the camera, to keep your reticle on a zombie you 'know' is there--and this is where Crow Country fails with its ♥♥♥♥ caught in a woodworking vice.See, in a game with tank controls, your character orients in the direction of the camera. Forward in one scene, is still forward, in the next scene, even if the camera angle changes. This can get a little disorienting until you're familiar with the 'scene' you're moving through, but once you understand the scene (and ergo, understand your unfamiliar surroundings, as you would need to in a horror setting), it's never going to change, and you will be able to memorize when you need to make minor adjustments to your character's turn-angle to help them navigate around obstacles in the environment, like furniture or hungry zombies.Unfortunately, this is a game with a free camera. One with an auto-turn feature, that orients the camera behind your character when you take aim--ala 3d-Zelda Z-targeting. Something you will need to do a lot.What this means, is that any time you want to turn around and aim at something, you're going to have to watch the camera spin. Then, you're going to have to take several seconds to fine-tune the camera with the thumbstick, all while fighting with the aiming system to line up your headshots--and to further complicate matters, many enemies  get randomized 'sizes' each time you enter a scene, meaning you will constantly be having to fine-tune your aim angle--potentially as you're being attacked. In short, you have to deal with the 'zombie around the corner' problem constantly, minus the careful direction of the developers.Add to this, the traps. Oh, the traps.See, traps in games are fine and all--they punish you for rushing around blindly, requiring you to try and keep your cool and get a feel for your environment, to tactically navigate it. This is why exploding barrels are an okay thing in Resident Evil games--yes, they can hurt you if you accidentally shoot one while you're too close, but they also allow you to herd enemies together and reward you for the clever thinking on the fly, by allowing you to eliminate multiple enemies at once.A good example of a well-utilized trap in Crow Country, would be the bear trap. You're rewarded for looking where you're going, and luring the enemies into these, to simultaneously neutralize both the trap, and a monster in the environment.What's NOT a good implementation of traps, which Crow Country does, is littering them every three steps, so that while you're fighting the camera and the aiming system, you're at risk of getting nickel-and-dimed out of your HP by random camoflauged poison-spraying robot crow-heads and chandeliers that have decided to teleport into existence since the last time you entered a room--often in environments like office spaces, that have no business whatsoever hosting chandeliers in the first place. Many such traps, have no redeeming quality whatsoever, and are just there to trip you up and give a cheap jumpscare--worse, you're incentivized to waste ammo just to clean them up.There's always going to be some level of 'inconvenience' to horror, because the horror experience requires doing uncomfortable things. But the uncomfortable things should still feel rewarding to tackle in the right way. There's a problem when you're taking the decision-making out of the player's hands, and making the sheer abundance of traps, combined with the ease of triggering them, to be the responsibility of and challenge to the player, because then you're forcing them to stop every two bloody seconds to line up their camera, take aim, and expend a round of ammo, or else have to navigate an absolutely cluttered resource-eating mess. This is not good. This is taking your player 'out' of the horror experience, and making exploration a 'chore'.Let's take Fear and Hunger as a comparison: Yes, there are stupid rusty nail traps littered here and there in the first couple levels, that can end your run if you don't understand what infection does to your character. They're there in the game, early on, to introduce to you the notion that innocuous things can lead to your death, if not accounted for. They will kill you once. The game then goes on to pit you against enemies that will induce bleeding, infection, or both, and you now understand from your early encounter with a trap, the weight of these afflictions and why they need to be avoided.This is not the case with Crow Country. If I trip over a gas mine, it's immediately time to use one of my five antidotes, and then collect another from the environment--I'm constantly being inundated with antidotes for poisoning. Why? Why does every corridor need to have an antidote to loot, along with a gas trap? I want to emphasize how much worse this is than the "zombie around a blind corner", that gives fixed camera tank controls such a bad reputation. The zombie around that corner has the potential to be a genuine scare. Tripping over the eighteenth falling chandelier, or poisoning myself for the dozenth time on a mine, only to have to flip to my inventory to apply another antidote or medkit, because I couldn't be bothered to stop every two seconds to move the camera and aim at the ceiling or floor, does not scare--it 'frustrates'.The long and short of it, is, Crow Country isn't scary--it's frustrating. For all the love that's been put into its PSX "I'm totally FFVII as a survival horror game" aesthetic, it's lazy. Do yourself a favor and pick up a Fear and Hunger game, instead. And then check out Parasite Eve 2, which basically takes Crow Country and skull♥♥♥♥s it, by comparison. I'm going to guess you got here by way of Silent Hill 3, what with the spooky amusement park setting, but just in case, I'll recommend that one, too, over this.
