_childDocuments_.review: Played this in one sitting. Definitely a refreshing experience for those looking to enjoy a survival horror experience without too much commitment. The graphics and the setting are the main appeal of this game and it really makes it stand out as an indie game. The idea of a horror game taking place in amusement park is one I wish was utilized more. The juxtaposition of an amusement park being filled with monstrosities is reason enough to give this game a try. The controls and the gameplay are simple but provide enough engagement that each encounter still feels like it will cost you if you are reckless. My biggest negative criticism of the game would be the fact that many of the resources feel abundant. There's really no fear coming from a risk of dying when you are supplied multiple healing options that have a chance to respawn. Although I still would recommend this bite-sized 7-ish hour horror game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a must-have for anyone who loves survival horror, especially the early Resident Evil games. This game has an incredible art style that perfectly captures the essence and features of early 3D animation and character design from the 90s. Crow Country is beautifully sculpted to be reminiscent of PS1 survival horror games and the atmosphere fills you with a nostalgic, dream-like feeling. However, that feeling soon turns to dread when you encounter one of the game's many and unique monsters. The gameplay is very smooth and responsive, giving players ample opportunity to survive or escape with the proper strategy and dexterity. The story and characters are also very fun. Along the way, you'll find multiple interesting characters who slowly drip-feed you information. The mystery of Crow Country is very engaging and you won't be able to stop playing until you learn the truth. The sound design is also superb, providing comfort, fear, or loneliness whenever appropriate. While the art style is superb, the soundtrack does so much heavy lifting to make Crow Country an excellent survival horror experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: A cute nod to old survival horror. Absolutely adored my time playing, If you're a veteran to this genre I highly recommend playing on Murder of Crows difficulty.I didn't have much of a hard time on said difficulty, the game is definitely not "Hard" but it does challenge you enough in a lot of aspects to thoroughly keep yourself safe.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a game that wears its influences proudly and doesn't seek to overly stray from the tried and true methods of its predecessors... But it doesn't NEED to. It's a solidly enjoyable experience. There's minor gripes, mostly that some greater puzzle variation would be nice, but overall, it was a nice time and I'm glad to have played it! The visual style in particular was very nice and the amount of level decoration really helped bring the areas to life.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: A totally lovely game from start to finish. I went in expecting a fun homage to retro survival horror, but it manages to be a lot more than that. Fun story, engaging environments, and some amazing meta-commentary on the genre-staple puzzles. Crow Country is a must-play for anyone who enjoys survival horror, and a potential GOTY for anyone who enjoyed the original Resident Evil games.The most amazing thing is that Crow Country doesn't chase trying to BE a retro game, it chases the way those games made you feel the first time you played them. And it hits the mark so, so well.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Being honest: I had a weird time with Crow Country. I feel like it’s a good game and once things got going, I enjoyed it, but it wasn’t a game that quite worked for me out-of-the-gate and some adjustment was necessary.The graphics are awesome, I love the style and the overall art direction of the game. It’s just really pleasant to look at and interact with. Something particularly praise worthy was that items stood out just enough that I knew what I could interact with, but without giving off that “movable object in the matte painting” sort of Tom & Jerry effect. Visually, this game could not be any stronger. I absolutely adored it.I also really like the plot. I like how it handles its main points and how the bits are delivered; it rewards exploration and interacting with the environment, looking for clues.What I don’t like so much is basically everything that has to do with the combat mechanics. It’s by far and wide the most annoying part of the game… And it’s not very skippable, due to the way that the enemy spawns are designed. Most survival horror games, especially those which Crow Country is looking to pay homage to, put an emphasis on avoiding combat, but also have level design that tends to in a way facilitate that. The deal with Crow Country is how it stacks enemy encounters: If you avoid 2 enemies in a corridor, and you go pick up an item, and that item causes 3 more enemies to spawn in that corridor, the new enemies didn’t replace the old ones, they got added to the environment. What happened when I first played the game is that I managed to literally get stuck on a corridor with 8 enemies and I couldn’t get past them, nor did I have enough bullets to kill them and make a way out for myself. I ended up starting a new game. Even if I could have gotten out of that corridor, I would spend a lot of ammo doing so and would likely be equally as screwed in the next hallway anyway… Not a great feeling.The way the game deals with inventory and ammo management is also less than ideal. It has randomized item drops from crates that don’t respawn, so you can actually quite feasibly screw yourself completely out of ammo. And having the feel of an ammo limitation is nice, having your run ruined because you fired a few shots too many in a game that throws hordes of enemies at you doesn’t feel particularly well-balanced. All of this would somewhat be forgiven if the combat was good, but it’s really not…Having said all that, Crow Country is still a game I’d recommend and I think it’s worth trying. There is a lot to like so long as you get into it with the correct mindset. Once I got how the rhythm of the game works, it was a very pleasant journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Because of its genre and low poly aesthetic, I was eagerly awaiting this survival horror title and I was not disappointed. While it does not have limited inventory and saves, the execution and balance is good enough for that constant fight-or-flight decisions that I seek in this genre. The very interconnected map is quite nice and enhances that quality although it is not enough to make route planning a joy as it is easy to clear out key spaces. Although I do like how it handles backtracking by adding random spawns and specially traps which has cheekily caught me off guard several times that happily keeps me alert. I am also happy though that juking enemies is fun specially with the movement boost here as a tank control player. After getting used to its aiming style, I think its gameplay experience is paced and balanced nicely without overstaying its welcome.For its accessibility, the finite hint system to indicate where to go is a good inclusion although it can be cheated with save scumming. Vending machines as resource dispensers when resources are low is intriguing. Having a backup ammo spot as well at the cost of backtracking. While I was not really able to test this as I was a veteran hoarder, I do like these ideas as it preserves player intent and balance instead of having dynamic difficulty.As for issues, the puzzles are okay but the bosses are mostly slow and disappointing without requiring much thought or strategy although credit that the player can escape them. The camera can be a bit jank when loading in as it clips or blocks the path forward which requires occasional manual intervention. Some puzzle inputs feel like it drops inputs due to the animation but not sure. Even if I do like the story and monster's origin, I am not sure the ending choice and context works as it feels devoid of meaning and nuance without the characters talking about it.Overall, I do recommend this neat indie title for genre fans.

Playing this at midnight and finishing just as the sun started to rise really brought me back to my teen years and playing dead space for the first time. Nothing like being hooked on a good horror game with the lights off.

_childDocuments_.review: Technically unplayable - UpdatedOriginal Review:First, it freezes the character for 2–3 minutes every time you shoot, allowing monsters to crawl over and kill you. Second, the controls randomly disable, causing the character to run in circles.Despite the pain, suffering, and dozens of reloads, I managed to play for 2 hours and reach the crypt boss. The game itself is great, but the technical issues make it nearly impossible to play—only for those extremely tolerant of critical bugs.I would recommend the game once the technical issues are resolved, but not in its current state.Update:The solution for the freezing issue on Steam Deck is to enable Proton override in the game settings.I’ve now beaten the game on the hardest difficulty, solved all puzzles, found all secrets, and am replaying to collect crows. With that, I can confidently recommend the game. It’s fun, and some puzzles made me think for a while. However, a few problems remain:1. Aiming:Aiming is very slow, likely intentional since this is more of a puzzle-adventure with horror elements, not a shooter. You’re encouraged to use tactics and evasion rather than dashing through enemies. However, aiming only works in the direction Mara is facing, not the camera. This caused many deaths due to camera and aiming issues, even though the game itself is relatively easy, even on the hardest settings.2. Camera Direction in New Locations:Often, when entering a new location, I’d be spawned facing the exit, causing me to accidentally walk back out.3. Evasion Mechanics:Evasion feels inconsistent. Sometimes you get hit from what seems like a safe distance, at the start of an enemy animation, or even without an animation. Tiny objects can easily block you, and corridors are a death sentence. Despite the plot discouraging killing, shooting most enemies is often the safest option.4. Mushroom Puzzle:Mushroom puzzle is insanely stupid. It’s one of the worst puzzles I’ve seen in any game. I’d have left it unsolved if not for the puzzle completion counter.5. End Battle Glitch:During the final battle, I encountered a glitch where the boss appeared as a large pink spot.Despite these issues, the rest of the game is great, and I enjoyed my time with it. I highly recommend it once you get past the technical problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid. I don't think this gameplay style or narrative benefits from too many arcadey elements like all the extra modes and ranking system, but I understand why it's there. The actual game itself is a lock-and-key style survival horror in a relatively small map that's easy to memorize. As the puzzles themselves are all straightforward the main challenge would've been keeping track of what goes where, but the memo system does that part for you so as long as you figure out the very first step, the game sort of unravels on its own and you'll be done in an evening. I like that pace. It allows the story to unfold pretty naturally. And the story is nice too. Since it's a mystery-thing that hides everything about the who's how's and what's there's not much else to say about it in a review. The characters are written cute and cartoony, the notes are very terse and clear which I highly appreciate. And just to be safe they spell every element out numerous times after the initial subtler giveaways so really no one is gonna be lost on what's going on with this one.What does that get you? A nice comfortable time in a lovingly crafted environment. Oh and the gameplay is there too, it's just what you think it is though.

_childDocuments_.review: I've about done everything there is to do in Crow Country. I played through the game twice, once on my friend's account, once on my own. All in all, I found it to be a very enjoyable game. I'm no expert on aesthetics, but I found the game's environmental design, and the overall look of the Crow Country park to be utterly gorgeous. I was less fond of the human characters, with their chunky, lego-like bodies, but it didn't bother me too much. The monsters look great. Some really disturbing designs, particularly the long-limbed "Spindle".The game had a lot of fun puzzles to solve and chew over. The in-game hint system does a very nice job of guiding you whenever you get stuck. I had to use it three times on my first playthrough, as some of the puzzles are very challenging, and occasionally I would get lost and forget where I hadn't explored yet. The combat in the game was enjoyable, though I almost found it too easy? In both my playthroughs, I never once came close to dying, and the amount of weapons, ammo, health-kits and such made navigating the game world easy rather than perilous. What little damage I took was more from the traps scattered through the map. I really like the traps, and how they slowly become more prominent as the night goes on and on.One of the game's best qualities, I think, is it's story. It's not too complex, but it uses foreshadowing very well and all the dots line up really well, particularly when you play through it a second time. Everything makes sense. A fair few interesting plot elements and a revelation or two. I liked most of the characters, including the protagonist (whose internal commentary on the things you find in the park are very amusing) though I wish I got more time with some of them. Hunting for secrets (and finishing crowquest on my second playthrough) was very enjoyable, though I wish the map would cross out the crows you find once you have the 'secret finder' map upgrade.Game's got pretty decent length, took a little bit over 6 hours for my first playthrough, not bothering with finding all the secrets, and 4.4 hours on my second playthrough where I found all the secrets and collectibles, knowing all the puzzle solutions and where to go. I'd say it's well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is absolutely stellar if you're a fan of survival horror games and have a bit of nostalgia for the classics of the early PSX era. I beat the main story in about six hours, which felt like a satisfying amount of time; not heart-breakingly short, and not begrudgingly long. If the playtime worries you, Crow Country follows the tradition of several other survival horror titles by ranking you on how well you did at the end of the game and giving you some new items to use and tasks to complete on subsequent playthroughs, which is something I appreciate.In the gameplay department, the bread and butter of the genre are represented plenty: puzzles, resource management, and combat, all with some interesting twists that make the game stand out on its own. The puzzles in the game perfectly walk the line between migraine-inducing and trivial enough to sleepwalk through, which is something that (in my humble opinion) is notoriously difficult to nail, and Crow Country hits pretty darn close to the mark. The slow and precise combat controls make for encounters that feel tense but also reward patience and skill, as projectiles deal more damage to enemies that are closer, and headshots are (as you might expect) far more powerful. While there were some multi-monster encounters that got my heart racing, the game's overall difficulty might feel lacking for avid fans of survival horror games - at the time of writing (05-13-2024), the game has a "hard mode" listed on its roadmap, which makes me think I'm not alone in that feeling, and if so I'm glad the developer(s) are keen on listening to player feedback and continuing to improve the game even after release.The game's story was somewhat short and sweet, and the characters you meet are entertaining to talk to if not somewhat odd; the protagonist, Mara Forest, was endearing and I found myself actually interested in the little bits of commentary she had about her surroundings. There are a few plot beats I saw coming, and some others that completely blindsided me, but in either case I was invested and I'm still thinking about some of the implications a few hours after completing the game.Overall, I enjoyed Crow Country a whole lot; someone versed in the world of survival horror classics might get some more mileage out of the game's general vibes, but I think anyone who appreciates a good puzzle-filled horror game will be thrilled with what's here. I absolutely can't recommend the game enough. I'll be waiting with bated breath for the soundtrack to drop for purchase, and I'll be keeping my eyes out for whatever else SFB Games might come out with in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who did not grow up playing those early console horror games (Silent Hill, Resident Evil, etc.) I was concerned about the potential clunky-ness of the ever notorious controls of that era being in this game. Thank goodness that this was not the case!If I had to describe Crow Country in one word, it would be 'accessible'. The game has a combat free mode, the average recommended mode, then hard mode. There is also an in-game hint mechanic if you get stuck, and most of the notes you collect you can read in the save rooms. I found that the puzzles were easy enough to solve, but still enjoyable. It utilizes the classic style of needing to explore to find items to open new paths forward, which I really enjoy. There is a sense of satisfactory exploration that I find so rarely these days, especially with how the different areas interconnect. You are really able to customize your experience how you would like, and I had no issue with the controls while playing this off of my Steam Deck.The plot itself was interesting. The areas you explore were fleshed out enough with notes and environmental objects to give the sense that there was something here before everything was shut down.I played through this game in two sittings, expecting it to take up the evenings of my weekend. I booted it up on a Friday evening and found that I couldn't wait until Saturday evening to finish it. If this game is catching your eye at all - from the genre to the aesthetics - pick it up!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice and sweet love letter to genre and one of the most interesting explorations (for resources) I have in survival horror games filled with nice puzzles and charming aesthetics, but for me game lacks interesting\strange plot or characters and combat design is kinda... there? _childDocuments_.review: felt like i should make a review because the overwhelmingly positive rating it has right now is a bit odd. first off, it looks and sounds f*cking amazing, its more than just nostalgia bait. it has really great art direction and design. its origin might be psx era graphics but it only uses that as inspiration, and goes far beyond the post processing filter shtick most games begin and end on. the environments are brilliant. there is a lot to admire here visually. the music is very good and i would listen to it as a stand alone record no game needed. i wish more games had music as interesting as this that was weirder and more experimental, more ambient, more unique, i'm tired of the cinematic movie stuff in games, so many hammy orchestral scores or Latin choirs..  AAA and indie devs could learn a lot from this one when it comes to sound and music. when it comes to newness, novelty, re-contextualization and experimentation interactive media/games are just getting started. the future is bright and the tools and technologies become exponentially more accessible every year with fewer and fewer obstacles in the way of small teams and bold designers. but we're not there yet. these qualities of the game are exceptional and i applaud them. also the sound design is proper and very well executed. i wish more games had sound as good as this. however, this is a game and the game play is bad. the puzzles are cute but the gun play is not. adding in an adventure mode is nice but for me a middle ground option with some aim assist, higher damage values would've even better. peaceful, normal and ultra-violence is OK but the normal mode just isn't fun to play, it doesn't feel good. the best games don't need difficulty options, they just need to be designed well, but regardless mechanically there is much to be desired.third person shooters always kinda suck (to me) but this one is even more sluggish clunky and hard to groove with than usual. when the market is as saturated with snappy, crisp and euphoric feeling games as it is, its hard to excuse game feel this bad. maybe the devs just couldn't figure out how to make it feel good? either way, this could've been one of the best games this year and instead its just ok. wait till it goes on sale for 5$ and probably opt for adventure mode. turning it into more of a point and click visual adventure novel thing might've been the better option in general...idk. i really wish the controls and mechanics felt good..its so needlessly clunky. with a bit of tuning this could've been an exceptional game. i hope the devs keep going and try again but the overwhelmingly positive rating isn't gonna do them any favors in regards to iterating successfully on the game play itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Played it first time on hard mode which is seemingly a failure of game design.  I've played RE4 and RE4R on harder difficulties with no issue.  Because those games give me what I am missing.  Crow Country refuses to give me healing items.  That's not difficulty.  That's a failure of game design.I avoided enemies when I could.  Again I've beaten other survival horror games on the hardest difficulties multiple times.  Its a failure of the game design to not recognize that I need healing and give me some.  When in critical health you can't run.  Searching trash only ever gives me a single hand gun bullet.  So now I can't avoid enemies, will run out of ammo, and no healing items ever spawn.You might as well tell me to restart the game.  Which I don't want to do.  Because:The game is awful at giving me direction as to where to go or what to do.  There's a difference between handholding and giving me nothing to go on. The map doesn't show me where the computers are so now I'm expected to either remember where they were or wander around until I find them again.  That's stupid.  That's not fun. _childDocuments_.review: A modern love letter to classic survival horror games that forges its own identity within the genre. Crow Country may have a lot in common with the classics like Resident Evil (1996), Silent Hill (1998) in terms of basic gameplay mechanics and aesthetics, but it finds a way to feel fresh through its unique setting, character personalities, and overall production quality. It's great to see that games like this are still being created, in addition to putting fresh twists on the genre. If you love classic survival horror games, this is a gem you can't pass up on. Here's to many more playthroughs!

You can knock it out of the park in one night, but it's still worth the price of admission. My suggestion - turn off the lights, power off the second monitor, and sink into an older atmospher.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just hands down awesome!The game takes place in the 90s, and you play as agent Mara Forest on a mission to look for a mysterious man for some unknown reason at an abandoned amusement park with  a dark past.The game plays like the original Resident Evil games, solve puzzles by finding missing key items while discovering new enemies and traps every time you revisit areas you've been to. The developers understand this formula very well, and do a fantastic job keeping it engaging while you figure out how to progress.There's so much stuff to interact with. Sometimes useful, sometimes just for fun (I really thought I'd get an achievement for playing air hockey with myself in the arcade room).lPuzzles are clever, and unique, and every area you enter just looks really good with all sorts of set pieces, and decorations. There's reason to search everywhere in a room because there's always resources you can use lying around.The game's graphical design is gorgeous for the setting, and matches really well. The sound effects match the art style, and blends in super well.Mara is an interesting protagonist in that she is very mysterious. This whole game is all mysteries, and I can't help but want to solve them all.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Very very good game, not overly challenging but what you're here for is the atmosphere and story over the survival shenanigans, the puzzles are moderately difficult and wont leave you guessing for too long if you're paying attention, the combat is the worst aspect of the game, it tries to do the resident evil 4 approach from an isometric view and it feels pretty awkward, i think a lock on system like signalis has would have suited this game better, the art style and sound is simply beautiful and is very very comfy, this game continues the trend of save theme bangers.the game also isnt too scary so if you're someone who doesn't typically like horror i think you'd be able to really enjoy this one, for horror veterans its the vibe you'll come to appreciate, highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my very first playthrough!If you like Silent Hill (and other old school Survival Horror), this game is right for you. The areas have that "claustrophobic" feel that old survival horrors have, with all the small corridors and tight areas. Resources were plentiful, but I feel like it's not really enough if you're the type of player who likes to clear out areas from enemies (which is a good thing!). it is very good, very interesting. There were a few twists near the end that I like. Nothing major, but I like how there were smaller hints dropped along the way. My only complaint about the story is that I wished the lore of the creatures (and related topics) are explained in more detail. I think it was fantastic. Movement generally felt great and the aiming was good, as in I didn't feel like there were any unclear hit boxes or anything. I do feel Mara runs a little too fast though. Sometimes I just end up bumping into enemies lol.  they were also fantastic. There were some easier ones where the answers were hidden in plain sight, and some harder ones where you had to rack your brain a bit. And I absolutely love how in one of the puzzles, you could clear it using an alternate solution if you found a certain secret and connected the dots together; really love how the game rewards your creativity.I'm rambling but overall ! Would definitely try to get 100% completion some time soon.Really grateful to the devs for this masterpiece. Rock on devs!

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good 4-hour experience for fans of early 3D action games. The game is taking you back to 1998 and it know it. This wouldn't look out of place next to old Resident Evil, Parasite Eve, Silent Hill. The story is good but not quite on the level of those others mentioned. _childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country AKA my average theme park experience. Really solid survival horror game, it knows its roots well and does a good job at living up to the spirit of the series like Resident Evil without coming off as aping them. I was a masochist and played M+K, which I got used to fast but some people may struggle with that, especially as it is tank controls meaning you will have moments where you'll probably take a few hits due to finagling with the movement.That said I don't think the game is hard, at least as someone who plays these games a bit. Honestly though I sort of welcomed that as it made the game feel a lot more cozy to me while playing, which combined with the art style and soundtrack made for a pretty fun night of playing through this game. Managed to get every achievement except the S-Rank one in my first playthrough fwiw. so if you're a completionist it should only take you 1-2 runs (depending how sick you are) to get everything done.Overall it's a pretty easy recommend for me, especially for the price. Looking forward to more updates (especially hard mode!) that'll get me to come back, plus I would def like to see more games like this from this developer in the future.P.S. the soundtrack for this game is killer I can't wait for the full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely pretty great. The style is impeccable, I love the pixel filter and old low poly style. The story is also really good, the game really managed to pull off some great twists that also focus on really interesting plot points. It would be nice if the story was more intricate with more mysterious points and more bits of interesting lore to find, but it was still really good overall. The combat is built around a pretty interesting system that requires you to stand still and trifle with a hard to use aiming system, which I definitely thought was a pretty good mechanic. One thing I will say about this game is that it is a little bit easy, you probably won't find any challenge in surviving as long as it isn't your first time playing games, but it still does a good job at providing difficult and interesting puzzles all throughout the game, which also comes with a fun and limited hint system that helps to alleviate difficulty while staying fair. Overall, I would definitely recommend this game for anyone looking for something to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO GOOD. Pretty much exactly what I love in a survival horror experience, The only thing disappointing is that there isn't more of it. It's just a short but sweet experience. Atmosphere is super creepy and really takes advantage of the grainy, low poly retro aesthetic. The sound design and music is absolutely fantastic; consisting of "save room" melodies, eerie carnival tunes, and unsettling sounds of humming machinery and groaning metal. I really enjoyed the puzzles and the layout of the map. It loops around making backtracking less tedious. The mystery of what's behind the horrors is really interesting and the twists are pretty fresh, in my opinion. Feels and plays like a classic. Easy recommend if you like old school survival horror

Very glad i bought it and I will probably continue playing and try to get S rank, though might take some time, cause i'm very new to gaming >_< Everyone should try this out even newbies like me!

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a beautiful game. It pays homage to classic survival horror games, but it stands out as a unique new experience. The story is simple, the areas are beautifully designed, the puzzles feel satisfying and the dialogue is clever. The game also comes with 3 different difficulty modes and unlocks that add to its replayability. If you're a lover of survival horror, or simply looking for a gem, give Crow Country a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: What a treat this game is. I went into this expecting to ♥♥♥♥ my pants — what I got instead was less scary than I expected, but it won me over with its personality, its cast of characters, the charming art style, and the surprising amount of pathos it was able to bring despite the deliberate and self-conscious silliness of the overall affair. And despite the fact Crow Country rarely takes itself seriously, it’s still able to pull off some great scares. Oh, and the soundtrack is just excellent.Other than a couple of poorly-motivated puzzles (did anyone else get stuck in the Theatre for ages?) I had a great time discovering the various secrets on offer, and I didn’t feel the combat was as clunky as others say. I comfortably beat the game on Murder of Crows difficulty in about 11 hours, and I wouldn’t frame that as a complaint. Crow Country doesn’t want you to suffer — it mainly just wants you to have fun. If you’re looking for something more unforgiving in its difficulty, there’s always RE1.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a phenomenal, and memorable game. The dialogue oozes character, and the visuals are an amazing recreation of that late 90s cg scene. _childDocuments_.review: I´d liken this game to a tasty snack. If you´re looking for survival horror, it scrathes that itch really well. It looks nice, plays well, has some really great music and the overall atmosphere is on point. The story and writing isn´t amazing but still far above just servicable. I´d describe the game overall as charming.Some things to consider though: The game is pretty short. If you rush, then a first playthrough can be done in just above 3 hours. If you take your time and try to get all the secrets, a first playthrough will take around 7 hours. The game is pretty easy as well. As long as you conserve your ammo and avoid enemies you will have no issues at all. The devs are working on a hard mode though, so that might eventually change.I overall really enjoyed playing Crow Country, but I see how the short playtime (for the asking price of 20 bucks) and overall lack of difficulty might be a dealbreaker.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like 90's classic survival horror like Resident Evil, and don't mind the PS1-styled look, this is a safe bet for you. Crow Country is an amazing little indie game, and it is actually the first game I've beaten in 2024. I even went back for an achievement, just for fun. The game is not voice acted, BUT, the story is delivered through small and simple dialogues that are easy and quick to read.The good:- Simple yet engaging story, easy and quick to read- Fun puzzles (feels rewarding to solve without spending hours)- Fun secrets you can randomly discover- Never big chunks of endless text- No bugsThe bad:- Too Short (5-6 hour playthrough)- Only 3 save slots- Some of the controls are a bit wonky and there are no way to remap them. Aiming is (Hold) R1 and shooting is (Hold) R1 + O. Reloading is (Hold) R1 + X. Running is (Hold) O or R2. L2 isn't even used.All in all a great game. I didn't mind the PS1-styled visual, and within 2 minutes I wasn't thinking about it regardless. I wish the game was longer, but that also means it was an enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is an excellent bite-sized horror adventure packing incredible presentation.Puzzles are expertly implemented: while difficult, the answers are always intuitive and can be found via clues from the environment. Additionally, they reward players for paying attention to the story through many hidden 'secrets.'The ambience and lighting is evocative of old PS1 titles like RE, and perfectly sets a creepy and mysterious tone. Conversely, the tight ensemble of characters adds lots of humor by cleverly poking fun at survival horror tropes in games.My only complaint would be that the 'monsters' aren't much of a threat to avoid or fight. However, their designs are fun and reminiscent of old creepypasta stories.Overall 9/10! It's the perfect eerie adventure to binge on a rainy weekend. Definitely buy if you miss old classic horror titles like RE2 and Silent Hill.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet PSX-styled survival horror throwback. Atmosphere was solid, and I found the plot pretty compelling, enough so to make me play through the entire game in a single day. Even having never completed a survival horror game before, this game was quite breezy for me difficulty-wise: I never really felt too starved of resources, the puzzles were enough to make me think a little without outright stumping me, and the game offered plenty of hints on where to go next, both through in-game notes and with an outright hint system.The game took me just under 6 hours to complete, and it seems to have a few replay-oriented features similar to other classic survival horror games (namely new game plus equipment based on your final playthrough performance rank, and some sort of hidden object hunt added to subsequent playthroughs). Relative to many other indie games on the market, this game is a bit content light for the price tag, but the total playthrough time is on par with most other (often AAA-priced) survival horror titles.If you're looking for a traditional (if slightly easy) survival horror experience, can't go wrong with this! There was definitely a lot of care put into this game, and it delivers on what it promises.

_childDocuments_.review: Great little survival horror game. Definitely recommended.Unique visual style that's consistently of high quality. Feels very polished.Not too difficulty on the "normal" difficulty. Strikes a nice balance between mysterious, spooky and lighthearted. The setting of a theme park with more than meets the eye is absolutely perfect for this. Definitely very resident evil inspired. But almost felt more Luigi's mansion like in terms of atmosphere at times. It has an almost top-down camera letting you not view too far ahead, but you still have a RE4 style lasersight you can aim in all directions. Shooting enemies from farther away also decreases damage dealt giving you some risk vs reward.  It gives the game a bit of unique flair even if it's subtle. The aiming is both sufficiently responsive to feel ok and clunky enough for it to feel like a survival horror game. But with the amount of health items and ammo i received I never felt like i had to rely on combat skill too much in the first place. I have yet to try the later addition of a hard mode.If you liked this and are looking for more modern day takes on old resident evil games with some slightly comedic elements. Check out Alisa by Casper Croes and Dead Seater by Zeekerss. The former being very faithful to a PS1 survival horror in visuals and controls and an Alice in Wonderland feel. The latter being a bit more comedic, short and free!Very interested to see if they'll make more games in the style of Crow Country instead of their earlier titles. They're now on my radar.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - A beautiful, well crafted survival horror journey into the wondrous world of yesteryears aesthetics, with a fantastic ambience, fun puzzles, enjoyable story and really good gameplay. If you've any interest into the old Resident Evil, Silent Hill or spooky games from that era, I urge you to stop reading and play the Demo. The least you owe this game is that you give it a chance to impress you, because Crow Country deserves the time of day.I got interested when I saw the dev post on twitter during development, tried the demo during a next fest and was sold. Crow Country is really enjoyable, tightly packed and full of little nods and details that are just really fun to discover! The ambience building is fantastic, the setpieces really fun to explore. Enemies are all so mangled, horrific, jittery, they clash- feeling so out of place compared to the rest of the world around you, it's great!Playing on a controller, aiming felt frantic and enjoyable, especially once you've unlocked the laser sights. Enemies can jump out of many hidden spots and surprise you, or menacingly stomp towards you through the fog of the distance, and both fighting and running can be really tense at times, especially as you delve deeper into the mysteries of Crow Country itself!The story has many threads that all come together for a finale that ties up the whole thing with a beautfiul bow, even reminiscing on everything you've experienced in the game entirely. It's written with love and care, and the game wants you to know that!
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Seems promising, but I find the controller mapping to be uncomfortable even with the limited remap options (can switch a couple of main buttons for shooting). The fact that I can't just remap to what feels best for me is annoying, though I understand this is probably because the developer wants you to experience the game as an old school survival horror game (which, funny enough, all PS1 and 2 Silent Hill games, which clearly influenced this, allow full button remapping, so I guess this game doesn't want to emulate that aspect).I thought maybe I'd play on desktop (initially tried on Steam Deck), but I've read that there is zero mouse support. Controller forces aiming with Left Analog, which I do not like either, so overall, the game just controls uncomfortably for me.Keep in mind that I've barely played enough to really judge the game itself. It seems like it's probably a good time as a fan of old survival horror games, but the controls don't feel great for me and the fact that the developer would prefer people get used to their scheme instead of allowing a custom scheme is mostly what determines my non-recommendation. This is really only a non-recommend for people who might have a similar issue with the controls. Will attempt to continue the game and update my review if my opinion overall changes.

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a game that has managed to dig itself into my brain unlike a lot of other Survival Horror games released in the last few years. It's graphics and setting has nothing but charm and the sound design is atmospheric. The ending also felt like a deserved payoff.  I love this game. Of course any game comes with a little downside. The way the camera moves can and probably will cause motion sickness, luckily I'm not someone who gets sick with that but I can see it being an issue for others who do. The only system I didn't like was the aiming system. It moves slowly and it's hard to get it to stay on target. Anytime I brought a gun out I'd be spun around or aiming the wrong way, not sure if that was a me issue but the movement made it difficult to attack monsters. The monsters were a little lackluster in attacking me, I could run circles around them at times when there wasn't a big amount of them. Sometimes I'd even get a little stuck and be cornered only for them to ignore me for a good second or two before attacking. Also killing off one of the characters made me sad. Besides that the game is great and it's been a long time since I've enjoyed one of this genre so much!

_childDocuments_.review: I was hooked on Crow Country and spent a whole Sunday to complete it! I haven't played much survival horror and I'm far from an expert of the genre. But I played the remake of Resident Evil 2 and I think Crow Country was basically RE2 . Clearly, this game is inspired by classic Resident Evil as well as the horror genre and PS1 era in general. Most people probably know that they're going to like Crow Country just from watching the trailer.By the way, I played this game on hard mode for my first playthrough and wondered if it was much different than the standard difficulty. Hard mode wasn't a walk in the park. There were moments I was scraping by with little to no healing items and ammo. I took a lot of damage when I was careless, which resulted in not being able to run away from enemies. You're only able to sort of limp when at low health, and some enemies can make a gain on you when you're limping. I died several times.I could see a lot of room for improvement in my gameplay as I progressed. Your ranking is a reward for your skill. The game's systems and world are well designed for you to run around in and shoot for a perfect run. I definitely would like to come back to this game someday; I feel like I didn't give myself enough time to appreciate it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a pretty good survival horror game. Mechanically, it's somewhere between the original Resident Evils and their remakes, and is generally faster and with more combat.The aesthetic is almost toy like, because of the borderline tilt-shift camera angle/style and the art style. It almost feels like a Playmobil set, in a way.Good soundtrack and SFX, too.Biggest complaints are the the puzzles (which drift between braindead easy and obtuse to the point of being borderline unsolvable without a guide), the godforsaken traps that inexplicably appear around parts of the game based on overall progression, and a very strange overarching plot that doesn't make much sense and feels like a mishmash of several opposing ideas.Would give it a 8/10 confident and had no problem paying the full $20 for it.Also, like any good survival horror game, it has unlockable weapons based on your completion rank, which gives it some good replayability.Hopefully the devs do a sequel, or at least another game with these mechanics and aesthetics.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, the game is actually good and has an impelling atmosphere that makes you keeping tracking down the secrets that this theme park hides in every corner; but that's here where the game cuts its own throat: since the game itself is short, it is massively stuffed with puzzles, I mean, every damn room has at least one puzzle for you to solve. Some of them are relatively easy and some are made for brain-dead people, but it also has non-intuitive puzzles that will make you quit the game sooner or later. This enormous quantity of puzzles turns the walkthrough less fluid, most of time you'll find yourself trying to remember what you had to do and where you had to go. What I really wanted was to enjoy more of the story than to be stuck in every new room I pass by.Also, there are these  that damage you all the time, since the devs decided to put this kind of "noise" filter that makes it difficult to see what's happening on the screen. God, how I hate those f***ing !Long story short, overall the game is good, it has a good horror atmosphere, some cool challenges and interesting secrets to discover, but the decision of the devs to dump puzzles and more puzzles in the game just to compensate its shortness, to me,  was a wrong move and a poor one. The game could sustain itself without it pretty well.

If you're a veteran for the genre you'll have fun it's gonna be a breeze and if you're new this one is a great starting point. _childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. The atmosphere and overall creative direction are exactly my kind of thing. I've never been much of a survival horror player and I found  a bit on the easier side in terms of difficulty. Depending on your experience and preferences, that could be a positive or negative. Personally, I enjoyed that it wasn't overly punishing. I played on the standard difficulty, but iirc there's a higher level. There was clearly a lot of thought put into quality-of-life features, which is great. Your map shows you which rooms still have unfinished objectives & secrets (once you get a certain upgrade), vending machines are there if you're low on items, and fortune tellers for hints. Aside from 2 optional puzzles, I never felt stuck when playing the game. It was satisfying anticipating where key items might be found or where one might be used. The story is subtle & intriguing and is good at showing you things instead of telling it all. Some things were easier to predict, but the main revelation — especially once you get the final, easily missed info — is super cool. The soundtrack is fantastic & moody and helps solidify the overall tone of the game: that

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best survival horror games I've ever played up there with the classic resident evil games in quality. Loved the music. Didn't realise how perfect a theme park would be for a metroid-vania survival horror game, with an amazing variety of cool places you'll see. The story is a little predictable and gets a little cheesy especially towards the end. but, I had a constant feeling of mystery throughout and the twist was done really well.

_childDocuments_.review: 𝕿𝖍𝖊 𝖜𝖔𝖗𝖘𝖙 𝖌𝖆𝖒𝖊 𝕴 𝖍𝖆𝖛𝖊 𝖇𝖊𝖊𝖓 𝖕𝖑𝖆𝖞𝖊𝖉 Crow Country - it's a the quintessence of what the influence of postmodernism in games can offer, when instead of art the creator makes an empty and talentless product.Despite the attempt to present style, and the desire to please a niche consumer, in its content and structure the game is no better than soulless conveyor AAA projects created by large studios.- Design of the enemies is unremarkable, moreover, they look talentless and miserable. the environment of an abandoned amusement park, with its synopsis pushes towards the presence of diverse and colorful creatures, albeit not completely original, but at least remarkable.Instead, the main opponents of the player are zombies, spiders, slime and a long-armed man who was directly copied from cheap Internet creepypasta.Only the Crayman creatures from the "Thief" universe in design and terrifying appearance beat all the local vein-like losers.It's clear that the author not only failed to use his imagination, he did not even try to do so. the main character could have just as easily fought aggressive cubes and balls.Their behavior and attacks are also pathetic, in normal old-school 3D horror games like Dino Crisis or Resident Evil, each enemy is difficult depending on their abilities.Some are dangerous in a crowd, and some move quickly and jump on walls, some jump out of the water, and some attack from the air, or throw objects at the player. these abilities imply studying enemies and finding the best way to destroy them.Here, all their attacks are the same, except for the fast Pinocchios, all enemies are slow idiots who come at you head-on with one melee attack. the only thing that distinguishes them is the level of damage.Also the enemies are not dangerous, they have no artificial intelligence as such, they constantly get stuck in objects and can't even get close to you.- Game lacks a variety of arsenal as such,all types of guns are a cliche that migrates from one game to another. the author did not even bother to somehow visually update the concept of a pistol - shotgun - flamethrowerDuring the entire game you can find only a few types of weapons, and considering what wretched opponents are here, all problems are quickly solved with a pistol and grenades.- Game has an absolutely wretched and cheap plot, in which there is no intrigue, no interesting memorable characters, no well-tailored dialogues. moreover, almost all the people you meet, except for the detective who arrived on a bicycle, are not at all influenced by the local devilry, and do not even notice that monsters are wandering around the park.The plot does not touch on any themes, does not carry a message, has no depth.There is not a single interesting situation related to the plot throughout the entire game, the player must wander around collecting junk and solving puzzles, periodically suffering in the fight with opponents due to the local miserable shooting.The plot simply exists.And is forgotten a day after completing the game.- Well, the controls are absolutely terrible, it is obvious that the author wanted to repeat the experience of old games. like tank controls. But it would be better if he did not do this, it is impossible to aim quickly, the controls cannot be changed to the button layout and made as convenient for the player, the camera turns slowly.  - The graphic style ... Unlike pixel art, old 3D games looked ugly, this was understood already in the late 90s. So I wouldn't dare call it the highlight of the game, because for me it's just a caricature pile of cubes and diamonds, without any smoothing or style.The main character also looks strange, why this awkward sexualization in a horror game, why is she running around in one dress? It should be cold there, it hits the atmosphere, you don't perceive the horror happening around already at the level of the fact that the main character runs in a white lace dress, as if she is snowflake princess.- The last thing is puzzles, they are surprisingly well done, simple and clear. but considering their simplicity and the above-mentioned huge disadvantages, this is not something that will make you want to return to the game again after a while.after all, the game is not made with puzzles alone, and when everything else is done poorly or very poorly, the only plus in the form of puzzles becomes insignificant.Summing up all of the above, Crow Country is the main dummy of 2024. The author of the game directly promoted this miserable product through YouTubers like The Sphere Hunter and Alpha Beta Gamer. Alpha himself admitted that the author of the game sponsored his video in order to somehow sell own game.That is, there is a place for bribery of media persons with the desire to distribute own product.This is an absolutely terrible and disgusting misunderstanding that is not worth any time and money. This game is an excellent example of how not to make horror-games.

_childDocuments_.review: A whole lot of fun, with style off the charts - the inspirations are clear at a glance, but the visuals stand all on their own with the chunky character designs, creaky decaying atmosphere, and softer rusty edges than one might expect from a horror game. The gameplay is top-notch too, running n' shooting with just enough friction to instill some scares in facing down shambling abominations, and with puzzles perfectly echoing the slightly unintuitive intuitiveness of classic Resident Evil riddles. A little more punch to the story would have helped this be more than the sum of its parts, the very end providing some thrills in this regard but the rest of the game mostly iterates and reiterates the core mystery without too many frills. Still, likely to be one of the best horror games of the year, a fun synthesis of classic Silent Hill, Resident Evil, and Alone in the Dark doing enough of its own thing to stand out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best indie games that I've played and I think it perfectly captures retro horror titles. It has lots of puzzles, most of which being fun to solve. Combat *feels* very retro, which I don't necessarily think is a bad thing. Graphically, the game looks wonderful, and I think it really fits into that "cosy comfort horror game" category. Crow Country felt like a love letter to classic games like RE1 and SH2, the types of games that you revisit for a quick run through every now and then. It's well worth the admission ticket and I'd recommend this to anyone that remotely enjoys horror or retro titles!.

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is an incredible RE-like in just about every way. The puzzles are interesting, generally neither too easy nor too hard. The combat is just odd enough to get your head around at first that you really have to take your time lining up your shots in a way that ratchets up the tension nicely. The story is really engaging and the information you learn about what's happening is doled out at a really great pace. The game is relatively short, but in a way that I really like. It's totally worth the price of admission and doesn't overstay its welcome like some survival horror games tend to.Highly, highly recommend to any old school RE fans out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a delightful throwback to the golden age of survival horror. With its charming retro graphics and atmospheric soundtrack, the game immediately transports you back to a simpler time. The puzzles are challenging yet satisfying, and the story is filled with twists and turns that keep you guessing.While the gameplay mechanics may feel a bit dated for modern players, they're perfectly balanced with the game's nostalgic charm. The exploration of the abandoned theme park is both eerie and exciting, and the encounters with the game's creepy inhabitants are sure to keep you on the edge of your seat.If you're a fan of classic horror games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, Crow Country is a must-play. It's a love letter to the genre that captures the essence of what made those games so special.

_childDocuments_.review: If you, like me, are playing through the absolute treasure trove of indie survival horror games we've gotten over the last few years, Crow Country should be on your list.That being said, I'm a little disappointed. Based on reviews, it looks like this game might have the trajectory of SIGNALIS, a gem arguably up there with REmake and SH2 in the hall of fame of survival horror. I unfortunately cannot give that honor to Crow Country.I completed the game in just over four hours, for one thing. Yes, I understand, Survival Horror always has been and should be a short genre, especially when you know what you're doing. CONSCRIPT for example was a fair bit too long, in my opinion. While Crow Country definitely has a good replay factor, I generally don't replay games unless they really connect with me, like SH1, RE2R, or SIGNALIS. Your mileage may vary, but even considering replays, you might only get 10 or so hours out of Crow Country. Up to you if that's worthwhile at $20, but overall I do think that Crow Country has enough merit to warrant playing.The FF7-esque artstyle is really, really impressive, but I found it a little hard to tell what was an interactive asset and what wasn't- A lot of the rooms are also narrow corridors that make the camera act a little funny. These are relatively small complaints compared to the genuine accomplishment that is making the game look so unique. You won't mistake this game for any else. Similarly, I thought the enemy design was a little uninspired, but nothing too major.The puzzles really shine in Crow Country. Some of the more unique, interactive, and clever puzzles you'll see in the genre are in here, especially the ones that unlock secret upgrades. Some are extremely easy, but all survival horror games have a few gimmes. That's fine by me, and I was pleasantly surprised by a few that had stumped me for a while until I figured them out. I think some memos could be a little more or less obtuse, but the fact that I can't think of any off the top of my head means that I thought they were overall pretty well done.The story comes together by the end, but for 90% of the game, characters by and large act like the events are no big deal. Witty quips and remarks are thrown around like a buddy cop movie. Some really head-scratching dialogue compared to the macabre nature of the enemies and deteriorating park, compared to say, Alisa, which makes its spookier elements fit better into the overall whimsical atmosphere. It could just be that Crow Country doesn't have voice acting and things were supposed to feel like that eerie, dreamlike vibe that SH1 and 2 give with their bad acting, but I can't say for sure.If you're looking for something in the vein of Alisa, pick this up. If you like this and haven't played Alisa yet, go get that ASAP, it's fantastic. If you didn't like CONSCRIPT but still love survival horror, pick this up. If you want another SIGNALIS, you're better off playing one of the established classics like SH1-3 if you haven't gotten to them yet. Crow Country is a bite-sized experience that you can make the most of, but I would say lower your expectations from the overwhelmingly positive reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. Highly recommended if you're a fan of classic Resident Evil and Silent Hill and other games like that.It isn't particularly difficult and the resource economy is certainly not punishing but those things aren't really negatives in my books. The story is great, the creature design is great, the visuals and presentation are great, the game is overall just really enjoyable to play.I'm a fan of the camera implementation, I think that they've captured the feel of those classic games mentioned above whilst avoiding the issues that fixed camera positions tend to have. The gunplay is basically what you'd expect from a game inspired by those old RE and SH games, where you stand and shoot and cannot move whilst aiming. I enjoy that, it prioritises good positioning and punishes overconfidence and getting greedy with how many shots you empty into a monster.My only real complaint is that some puzzles or challenges felt a little too handhold-y, typically the ones that were core to the game's story. I understand the desire to make those easier so that people don't get frustrated by them, but given the audience this game attracts I think it's okay to make them a little more challenging to figure out. It's not the end of the world, though, as there are other puzzles present which do have decent challenge to them. I'd honestly love to see more like this from this team. Creating survival horror with this classic feel and style is hard, especially with how overdone the trend is. This is definitely a worthwhile thing to pick up, especially for its price.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country came out of nowhere for me, its in a genre I dont really play at all and I also hadn't heard about it until a few days before I bought it. Despite all that going against it its been lowkey one of the best games I have played this year, a true sleeper hit. Its best to go into the game blind and not look anything up!PROS:- Gorgeous low poly visuals and lovably crusty filters make this game nail the style its going for, while also not sacrificing any of the horror factor. Monster designs are unnerving, yet also simple, so they dont end up looking too overrealistic or like a visual mess. The environments of Crow Country are extremely varied and every single room is immediately recognizable, an impressive feat considering that the whole game takes place in one location.- Speaking of the horror factor, this game hits a perfect sweetspot of being suspenseful and creepy without going too far as to turn me off. I am a self-identified hater of horror a lot of the time since most horror media is very gory and/or stress-inducingly uneasy. This game nails its tone, with the writing and environmental storytelling touching on some pretty disturbing subject manner while not resorting to jumpscaring the player every five seconds and overfocusing on excessive gore and suffering to get your stomach churned.- Speaking of the writing, the story. While not the most complex thing in the world, the narrative is unique, easy to follow, and is very cleanly self-contained. The characters are charming and have good dialogue, especially the protag who shares a few personal anecdotes here and there when interacting with the environment.- Another writing-related plus is that the puzzle design, which I would say is Crow Country's biggest focus, was absolutely on point the entire way through. Aside from one singular optional puzzle, everything you do in this game feels great to figure out, and nothing is ever too cryptic that I had to look up a guide to solve it. I actually went out of my way to get every secret during my playtime.- Combat is very simple, which is a good thing. The gun controls are perfect for what they are, and the game cleverly signposts to you that fighting enemies head on is not always the preferred way. There's a lot of traps and hazards that you can activate if you have a keen eye that will kill enemies without draining your very limited ammo, and it feels even better to kill enemies this way than by just shooting them over and over, which i definitely think is developer-intended. When you unlock the shotgun midway through, gunplay becomes a bit more enticing, fitting as enemies spawn much more frequently from that point on. Its difficulty is balanced perfectly.CONS:- The backtracking in this game can sometimes become rough, especially during the game's last hours where enemies spawn more plentifully in commonly traversed areas. Mind you, there is a not-very-well-hidden secret item cache where you can get running shoes that double your speed, so the onus is a bit on me for missing that secret location until the last 30 minutes of the game, when i could have really used those way earlier. Maybe some kind of way to non-intrusively hint to the player that they should go back to check the parking lot at some point would be nice.- Remember how I said this game has great puzzles except for one? Well I am dedicating an entire con to this one terrible puzzle since it bothered me so much lol. Spoilers for an optional puzzle: OTHER THINGS:- Game is short, clocking in at 5 hours to 100%. Not a bad thing but something to note if you were expecting a double digit hour experience. I think it is a very tight 5 hours, similar to Luigi's Mansion. Short and Sweet.- The human character models are kind of Lego/Duplo-like in their simplicity, which didnt detract from me taking the dialogue seriously but I could see it happening for others.Overall its an absolute hidden banger that I will be recommending to my friends a lot. Really hope to see more great things made by this studio! Number grade? 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Survival Horror game with a lot of birb!!! :DDD Its my jam >:3If you a Survival horror game fan, I think you're only brought this one but If not, I hope the title alone can convince you to buy this... You play as special agent Mara, who arrives at an abandoned theme park to search for a missing person. It's a classic setting for the genre, and classic is exactly what the game is aiming for. A PS1 aesthetic that is done so well it captures the exact PS1 game in your , not the actual PS1 graphics. That is the first thing I realized when I saw the game. The whole game is a playable diorama, reminiscent of the good old pre-rendered backgrounds like FF7, but with now thanks to the tech we have now a day, you able  to move the camera around this amazing background! It is just so good! The atmosphere is amazing. The game is filled with funny humor and tons of homages to classic games! (There's one Half-Life easter egg as one of the boss moves. Can you spot it??? >:3) Also the gameplay are just to tight! Really good, You use 2D movement with stick and 3D tank control with D-pad. Feel really good!Soundtrack are also on point, I really love Harrison's character theme so much! (Save room theme are quite underwhelming a bit in my opinion)Now one thing I don't like about game ;-; Its just one thing. This game is clearly inspired by classics like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, especially SH3. That answers why there are tons of enemy stuff in one room xD. Enemies tend to respawn along with traps when you leave that said area. This destroys the core of classic Survival Horror, where you need to plan your route. Sometimes, going the long way instead of the shortcut to conserve more resources. And since the respawn rate is so high in this game, there's actually not much reason to fight those enemies... Basically A Horror without Survival part...Anyway despite that nitpick, I really enjoy this little game so much! I can't wait for the Hard mode to be released in the next update!Its such a fine game that made with love and its deserve my God game, God time title! (Also the story are quite fun tho :D)
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a truly amazing must-play survival horror game. It transcends 'throwback shooter,' and completely creates its own identity without ever feeling derivative of any other title. The FF7/Alone in the Dark aesthetic choice for the characters was a fantastic decision from a design standpoint, and it really makes this game feel unique visually, as well.I love the visuals of this game. I love the round character models, I love the pixellation filter put over everything, the lighting, the color schemes going on, I eat it all up. The game is beautiful, nothing feels out of place; if you think the models look silly, I promise you that you’ll forget about it within 20 minutes of playing the game and you’ll get immersed into everything. Every screen in the game is full of clutter and junk, which makes the place feel run-down and full. The monsters are genuinely unsettling and scary, while there is no shortage of cuteness in the game, which tells me that the creators of this game have mastered their craft.The soundscape of this game is phenomenal, truly amazing. Cute-spooky tunes that make me feel fuzzy inside, to harrowing ambient tracks that made my blood run cold, and genuinely calming, soothing music that would help me take a breath to recoup from my outings in the bloody park grounds. All of the sound effects and music have this crunchiness to them, seemingly emulating the limited sound capabilities of the PS1 era, that really help sell the vibe.The gameplay is solid! I can be frank and say that I don’t really think you’re going to be white-knuckling your controller and on the edge of your seat, but I think for the kind of game this is, the action is perfect. Your run speed is great; you run fast enough to get you where you need to go in a timely manner, but you don’t fly through the areas too fast.This is helped by the areas not being too large, as there aren’t really any sprawling areas. Everything’s tight and concise, which compliments your movement speed. The level design is great, though I don't feel qualified to really give scientific, factual reasons as to *why* I think it's good, its just that everything links together in that usual survival horror way in a way that feels natural and satisfying when you realize you’ve just opened a shortcut to a previous area. I will say that I didn’t really feel particularly challenged by the combat in this game. It felt… kind of easy. But never, ever once was it boring at all! I always enjoyed getting to slip past enemies and feel cool, or shoot them to death and still feel cool. However, I will say that I would have possibly enjoyed some optional higher difficulty levels, but the current level of difficulty feels perfect for the kind of atmosphere this game has. The puzzles were exceptional though, absolutely fantastic; they were either just a bit  easy, or just difficult enough to make me get some pencil and paper and work it out, but they never felt so hard they were impossible. There are 10 hints you can use at available kiosks, and they were great hints that were just enough to point you in the right direction without completely solving the puzzle for you.For accessibility, there's 'exploration mode' which makes no enemies or traps spawn, which is great for players who don't really feel like engaging with combat, or who are easily scared or stressed and want to soak in the atmosphere instead. It was also helpful for me, since I used it to just rush through the game to gather footage for my video review of the game. I know of a few people who are the kind that are so easily scared and upset that Exploration Mode would really benefit them, so I'm glad this game provides that option. It's unfortunate that the controls aren't completely rebindable. You can switch between RE controls and modern shooter controls, but you can't rebind the other options, which I understand adds development time to a game and isn't easy, but it's just a bit unfortunate. There's also an option to turn on extra lives, which spawn pickups in the world that let you respawn on death. I noticed the lack of a colorblind option, which I feel is kind of common in a lot of games nowadays, but I'd love for more games to try to include options like that; there are puzzles involving red and green lights, and I'm not colorblind myself so I can't tell if they are the shades that red-green colorblind people can't see, but if so I hope they add a feature to alleviate that. There is also some story significance to a color in the game, it's mild but if that color is one of the colors that certain types of colorblindness isn't able to see, that's another reason I'd like to see a colorblind option.The story is great, it's simple but effective and provides a fantastic hook to get the player interested. The characters are all great, and I really enjoyed how much screen time the NPCs got. Many other survival horror giants kill off characters you meet extremely soon after they're introduced, so getting to see these characters move around the world as the game progresses was a breath of fresh air.Mara is also a very likable protagonist. I like her design, her dress is cute and I like her hairstyle and color. She feels like she belongs in a survival horror game, which I can also say about every other character you meet in the game. She usually has something funny to say, but it never felt overdone or too silly. She does feel like she’s investigating a creepy mystery, but she stays light-hearted and doesn’t let things overwhelm her. It honestly felt pretty immersive to me, because I was never too scared while playing the game, so it helped me slip into her shoes easily.TL;DRCrow Country is amazing. It perfectly crafts its own identity while being very clear about its inspirations, and the stylized visuals, nostalgic music and sound design, and simple yet solid combat make this game an amazing entry point to horror for newcomers, as well as a fresh but familiar experience for oldheads looking for a new fix. I hope this game receives the success and attention it deserves, and I hope you enjoy this game when you play it for yourself. Thanks for reading!This review was modified and edited from my script for a video review I made for this game, with most of the editing done by my friend ProxyAskew, thanks for your help!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game for fans of older classic survival horror games. Limited but rewarding weaponry, which suits this type of game. When you unlock new items for your arsenal, you feel empowered. The combat itself feels difficult but fair (I didn't feel cheated). You legitimately have to choose between running or gunning. The cherry on top for a player like me is that continued exploration is rewarded. The world changes as the story progresses, meaning new secrets might arise in places you've already checked!Fans of puzzles will be pleasantly surprised; this game does not necessarily hold your hand. You have to know what to use and where. Some things are obvious, others not. You can run into the solution for a puzzle an hour before you need to use it. I enjoyed being stumped by this game at times.The game also offers replayability through unlockable items for follow-up playthroughs, survival horror rankings at the end of the game, and multiple difficulties. One may be able to speedrun this game, even.Excellent game in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I played through this game about a week before release so anything I say is based off of that.Crow Country is accessible in a way I've never seen from a survival horror, allowing you tank controls or modern, shoot/reload on face buttons or triggers, resources being limited or easily obtainable, you can just straight up turn off common enemies if you don't want to deal with any of the monsters! I almost completed the entire game in one session just because of how into it I got, exploration is wonderful when the areas feel like they have so much variety. The presentation, I mean, just look at it! (And then when you play the game, listen to it too!)This is a game I expected to like and instead I found out I LOVED. Well worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: Crow Country is a fantastic classic-style survival horror but with added modern conveniences and controls that improves all the quirks and technical limitations of the older games. Additionally, giving it dark comedy and self-aware humour twists that made the game both atmospheric and fun to play through.Follows Special Agent Mara Forest as she investigates an eerie amusement park with dark secrets lurking within it.The game got responsive and precise controls, Mara never does what you don't mean to do (unless you panic and fat-finger the controls). The world-building and atmosphere is fantastic, the cartoony yet eerie atmosphere is impeccable! With fun characterisation across a small cast of characters (not that you'd meet them often), whenever you run into people, it's a good chance you'll enjoy the weirdness of the conversation. The main character Mara often comments on things in deadpan style humour, and she certainly got something to hide, so following her adventure adds some fun to the creepy ride.Personally, a total recommendation, this game hits all the right spots if you like survival horrors!The base difficulty of the game isn't hard, though, but there's an update with Hard Mode, so difficulty may vary. But thanks to that, if you're new to survival horror, this is also a fantastic game to check out., the game's control is precise, you have a top-down view but can still turn the camera around, so the camera angle isn't fixed, letting you get a good view of a room without a stray monster hiding out of sight. The gun controls nicely, there's a mechanic of the further you are, the less damage you deal, encouraging you to get closer.The Puzzles are actually fun! They're not all the same, some of them will require you to note things down or screenshots, and some of them require some little funny deductions, I don't remember a puzzle which I didn't enjoy solving., the game doesn't tell you much, you go to a theme park, and you'll learn more about the story and the park as you explore the area, either through notes or talking to characters. The environmental story-telling is also great, the park is nicely designed, with unique areas and really cool environments that build the sense of a strange and suspicious location that just makes you want to learn more.But don't be mistaken, the game isn't playing it completely serious, as mentioned before it got some dark and self-aware humour, and the game's storyline does have a lot of moments that revealingly parodying the genre or just the developers making some "this is a video game" jokes. I love those moments, giving Crow Country a great blend of creepy and comedic atmospheres.
_childDocuments_.name: Crow Country

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and endearing little horror game that wears its inspirations on its sleeves. You roam around in an abandoned theme park, fighting monsters and solving puzzles. The main attraction here is the park itself: a series of interconnected rooms with secret hallways and locked doors. It’s pretty well done, and pretty easy to navigate thanks to the  amounts of written letters, diaries, and tips littering every floor and wall. There’s this density to it too -- there’s just a lot of detail and stuff all around, which often requires you to do double takes as you enter a new room or revisit an old one.Anyway, the challenge here is definitely mentally mapping the park; knowing where to go next and where the puzzle piece you’re carrying fits. The rest of the game is a little underwhelming in my opinion. Once you sort of figure out how it’s all put together it loses a bit of steam.Still, Crow Country is fun for what it is, even though it won’t exactly turn your world upside down. And that’s totally okay.Thumbs up.
