_childDocuments_.review: In a lot of ways, MW5: Clans is the modern Mechwarrior game I was hoping that MW5: Mercs would be. If you played MW2 back in the day then this game was literally made for you. If you didn't, you'll probably still like it as it's very much designed with players completely new to the Clan factions in mind. It doesn't have the infinite, procedurally generated but all kind of the same missions that MW5: Mercs has, but the storytelling is leagues better, with tons of cutscenes and interesting characters, plus some QOL improvements to the gameplay. The new mech lab takes some getting used to, but once you wrap your head around the omnipod system it's fine. Some of the menu systems are needlessly convoluted though, and the research/upgrade/repair screens are good ideas executed badly. And they feature menus pretending to be NPCs, staring at you blankly. Sometimes things feel a little flat, like some of the music really slaps but a lot of the time there's no music or even much sound at all, and they try a few things that are new to the franchise and cool, but maybe they bump into the limitations of the engine a bit. But the game is fairly long, some of the missions are just so damn cool, the weapons sound and feel punchy, and PGI seems committed to improving and expanding the game with additional content. If you like big stompy mechs, it's a flat-out good time.Overall, if you want to experience the most polished, cinematic and engaging story in a Mechwarrior title so far, buy this game. If you are a filthy freeborn surat, do not, I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what a game should be. It's fun to play.  I've played MechWarrior online and MechWarrior 5: Mercs that was also done by PGI.  MW5: clans they took a much more structured approach then their past MechWarrior games.  I felt interested in the story.  I liked the characters that you follow.  There is a number of twist and turns keeping things interesting.  Plus there is a choice late in the game that will take you through different paths.  The voice acting is ok, I wouldn't claim it to be great.  But it's good enough.  Honestly I'm bit surprised PGI created this based on the other their other two MechWarrior games.  The campaign story in MechWarrior 5: Mercs was just terrible.  The game modes in both MW5:mercs and MWO are disappointing.  The mission variety in MW5:clans is changed up enough that I didn't feel like I was doing the same thing over and over again.  It might not have the same replay-ability like MW5:mercs and MWO have.  But I'm guessing we will see DLC's to explore the other clans down the road.  The graphics in the game look outstanding.  I did experience a number frame drops.  Hopefully they will continue improving the performance.   If you are a fan of MechWarrior I think you will be happy with the purchase.  If you are not, you might want to wait for a sale.  Overall I liked the game.  Well done PGI, Well done.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished campaign, probably will go back for another round after some DLC and fixes.PROS:- In-universe details are great, you can tell PGI really cares about the property- Cinematics are great, definitely a highlight- Voice acting for most of the cast is pretty good, though direction could have been better- Story decent, if a bit predictable- Missions decent, if a bit bloated with dumb enemies that cannot aim (normal difficulty)- Finally, a decent look at the clan invasion in a Mechwarrior game!- Fun, big stompy robotsCONS: (as of Hotfix #1)- Probably could have baked for a bit longer- Performance is awful, even on my relatively strong PC- HUD is a downgrade from MW5: Mercs (where it is still bad)- Custom binds reset randomly- Between mission UI is... organized very badly and tutorialized almost not at all- PGI cannot get cockpit textures or details even close to right and probably never will -- it's bizarre because their art team seems pretty good, but the switches and labels are nonsense- Sound mixing really strange in missions, switching between cockpit and 3rd person really highlights weirdnesses- There's something very wrong with the voice recording of Mia, her performance is fine, but weird artifacts- Some of the voice acting is spotty, particularly on characters with very little lines. The recording of "Aleksandr Kerensky" was.. tragically terrible

_childDocuments_.review: Better and more story than in MW5: Mercenaries, though many of the antagonists are over-the-top villains, grunting and gasping their way through dialogue. I experienced very smooth gameplay, even smoother than MW5: Mercs, with the only issue being my monitors switching between missions for no apparent reason. Mech customization was very difficult and more restrictive than I expected. I'm told that this is similar to MW Online, but I'm not familiar with those mechanics. Most players will need to get used to the default configurations. Any customization is likely to result in a drop in firepower. Gameplay itself is pretty repetitive and (at times) pretty grindy. Nine times out of ten the solution is to slow down and have your team dogpile enemies while moving backwards on the map and dodging missiles. The game definitely approaches missions with a "more is more" approach, with the player team outnumbered 50:1 and still shooting at lots of turrets, tanks, and VTOLs overhead. I found upgrading personnel and mechs to be kind of slow. The game definitely rewards stocking up your team and designating them to targets rather than doing it all yourself. I really wanted to see more variety in the available 'Mechs (there are only four for each weight class) and there's no salvage option. It would've been great to see the other clan battles result in different acquisitions or to equip the IS mech's with clan tech. Wasted opportunity -- maybe we'll see it in the DLCs.Overall -- recommended for players who prefer narrative over micromanaging machines and who love commanding squad combat. Probably not suited for "lone wolf" players who love lots of customizing.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played every MechWarrior game since MW1.  It was literally the first PC game I ever played.  I've been hooked since.  I also spent 3 years playing Piranha's MW: Online and was in the Top 1% of the player base on the leaderboards.  So, I have some experience with the MW franchise.This game is honestly the most uninspired, boring, and bland MW game in the entire series dating back to the original game.  It does what every other MW game does, just worse.  It was clear they spent the majority of their time, effort, and money on the cutscenes.  They go on forever.  This might not be so bad if the storyline weren't so predictable.  Also?  You're going to absolutely HATE all the characters with a quickness.  It's as if you took the most whiny, annoying teenagers and the cartoonishly evil villains they go up against in the cheesiest CW shows and stuck them in a MW game.  I was skipping the cutscenes in my first playthrough just to get them over with.  For the gameplay that doesn't involve being in map and shooting mechs, the game is lazy and, frankly, dumb.  The MechBay is the worst I've used to date.  The game has money so you can buy mechs/weapons/etc,  Why?  You're a clanner.  It'd be like the US Army telling the privates to pay for the tanks and Humvees.  You also get so much of it it serves no real purpose.  I was just buying new mechs rather than wait for them to repair if I didn't have enough techs.  Which brings me to my next point.  The research/upgrade system is awful.  It isn't interesting or fun.  It's just upgrade your weapons or mech.  But it isn't anything you're going to notice while you play the game.  Same goes for leveling your character and NPC teammates.  They're locked into certain abilities which are all boring and you'll never notice the difference if you level them up or not.  Also, the EXP is based on how each teammate does in a mission.  So, the more mechs you kill means the less EXP your NPC teammates get.  So you're punished for playing well.  As far as the actual Mech game play?  It's bog standard stuff that has been copied from every other MW game to ever exist.  Nothing interesting whatsoever.  And like most MW games, you get pushed into bigger and bigger mechs and the only way for the game to up the difficulty is to just throw a zillion bad guys at you.  Which means you get pigeon-holed into taking certain cheesy builds so you can actually complete the missions.  It would have been nice to have missions where taking lighter mechs and using strategy would be the way to go.  Nope.  Max size, max firepower for each mission.  With every mission essentially being "kill everything on the field."  Past MW games would at least have a "Go scout this and escape" or "Kill this one guy and bail" or "Escort these dudes to a dropship" type missions.  This game has none of that.Just wildly disappointing on all fronts. Which, if you know anything about Piranha, is pretty par for the course.  Don't waste your money on this unless you're a diehard MW fan and just absolutely need a MW fix.  Though if that's the case I'd recommend just going back to one of the older games that is actually done well.

_childDocuments_.review: i purchesed this game pre hot fix #1, and since launch this game has had its fair share of issues. that said, if you are a fan of the franchise you will not be let down. _childDocuments_.review: I've always loved a good Mechwarrior game, but I'm quite disappointing I bought this game. It's not that there's not good points about the game. The metagame, which tons of people complain about, I actually like. I think the mechlab is cool, the various things you can unlock to customize mechs are solid, and the repair management is interesting. The metagame is actually pretty good.The story is aright. The voice action is awful. Pretty much every line is delivered pretty flat. I know the Clans don't like contractions, but even the character that uses them delivers lines pretty badly. I feel like it has less to do with the lines themselves and more the voice direction. The other issue is every character is pretty much a single beat character. Your commanding officer is just angry all the time. No one really has any range or depth. Despite that, I am curious about the story itself. I'm an old Battletech fan and I've read the books and they hit a bunch of the cool beats from the books.The mech combat is actually quite solid. Blasting mechs just feels good. The problem is the mission and level design is the worst I've seen in a while. The levels are basically massive outdoor corridors. Mechs run right at you and you just blast them. Calling it a shooting gallery would be generous. The missions are far too short and don't really feel like you've done anything. The scanning mode could be quite interesting, but it's really very shallow. It just makes a mission bothersome. The big problem is the level design, there's tons of backtracking through these corridors. Any time you get into an interesting space that's open enough to maneuver and fight, you pretty much pass through it and end up in another canyon/hallway. As a practical example, there's a mission with three caves around a large open space. You basically end up going into these caves, blasting a bunch of people to scan something, and then backtracking out into the central space. Even though you've opened all the doors, the enemies just wait for you to come kill them rather than coming after you. The central space that's good to fight in maybe has one or two fights.The enemy spawns are also just dull. They spawn in very boring groups and just run at you. You've got five mechs but they often send one or two light mechs at you at a time, so you just blast them and move on. It gets very tedious very quickly, and that's partially because the level design doesn't allow a good number of mechs to move around. The missions are just bad. Really bad. The game looks great and the blasting the mechs is a great time. It's just the process of doing it through poor level design and very boring mission design just ruins the fun. Maybe this will be the game for you, but if I'd realized I was hitting my two hour mark, I'd have refunded it.It's on Xbox Game Pass. If you really want to play it, then go play it there. It's worth the monthly subscription fee, but certainly not the MSRP.

_childDocuments_.review: Most negative reviews seem to be referencing the game's poor optimisation. I've had to turn a fair few graphics settings to low-medium to get the game running at a stable framerate on a 3060, so those complaints aren't invalid. But first impressions of the actual game as a longtime enjoyer of the franchise are extremely positive as compared to PGI's last outing. Don't think it'll overtake MechWarrior 4: Mercenaries as my personal favourite, but the core mechanics and level design are so far improved from MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries that it's hard not to appreciate what PGI have done. The meta-game is also engaging enough and a lot more involved than that of prior linear (i.e. non-Mercenaries) MechWarrior games. Summarily, if you meet the recommended requirements (treat those as minimum ones) and don't mind turning some graphics settings down till the game is patched for optimisation, and have enjoyed prior MechWarrior games, this one is absolutely worth playing. And if you're new to the franchise, perhaps visit YouTube for some basic lore concerning the Clans and Smoke Jaguar specifically; that barred, it's a fairly accessible game and you should play it if it intrigues you.

The AI is MUCH better than Mercenaries, they actually hold their own in fights and will continue attacking whats in their range while on the way to a target you have assigned. Basically, they dont just stop shooting when you give them an order to move somewhere. They simply readjust their positioning to the point you've selected and continue firing at enemies along the way. They even utilize their jump jets to traverse obstacles instead of taking a long walk around.The battlegrid is cool, but I do find myself forgetting to use it a lot. The enemy AI has been pretty fun too, they just dont dogpile you because you're the player, they actually spread their damage around as well. From the few missions I've played so far, I have been having an awesome time. It's thrilling having enemies literally jumping off of cliffs above you and jump jetting into you in desperate ambushes. PGI did a phenomenal job with level design and fight coordination.I run a 4070 Super and dont have many issues with graphics. I have noticed some occasional "slideshow" effects of mechs at far ranges. It goes away when I zoom in to attack, but zoomed out it can be a little weird. Something, I'm sure will be hotfixed. The UI and Menus will take some getting used to. There's not much in the way of a tutorial that shows you where everything is, but as long as you're not scared to press buttons and look for things, you will discover a lot of cool features.Story - 10/10Graphics - 8/10Sounds - 10/10Voice Acting - 8/10 (A little rough at times, but I can tell they put hard work into it)Overall - 9/10Great Job PGI!

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this with the expectations of gameplay like MW5: Mercs and a narrative campaign in the spirit of MW2 and MW4. I also hoped for a step up in acting, writing, and overall presentation. I wasn't disappointed. The Good:- Accurate depiction of the invasion.- Canon characters and events are well handled and faithfully recreated.- Enough good cutscenes to fill a movie.- Briefings are leagues above Mercs.- Plenty of content. - Combat is what you expect from MW5 with options for classic tank controls or FPS/Mechassault. - AI is "better", using their jump jets to navigate terrain, not randomly hop.- Many of the issues with Mercs (lag when new units spawn) aren't present. - Replay previous missions with a batchall vibe for extra pilot experience. (Well bargained and done!)- Haven Kendrick (veteran of Emperor's TTS) was able to flex his talents.- Tons of mechs to shoot at with lots of target variety. - No Ryana/Darius. The Bad:- I don't know how they managed to conceive it, but the mechlab is worse than vanilla Mercs. Send that dezgra chief tech to a solahma unit! - Omnis aren't omni. You need specific hardpoints for gear. If no "omni" pod has an ECM slot for your mech, you can't slot ECM. - The briefings sound like they're over the comms... but everyone is around a table in the same room. - No quickplay option. - AI stays in close formation with you until you tell them to move. This is a problem in a Dire Whale Star. - Not enough things to tweak in the options (graphics, audio modes, etc.)- Small clan mech roster that *really* feels tiny in the Assault class (the nearly mandatory Dire Whale Star). The Buggy (may be fixed by the time you read this): - Rare crash (4 in 42 hours).- Audio has occasional pops (scan mode en*pop*gaged) and doesn't always match the subtitles/animation.- Keybinds have a bad habit of resetting on startup.

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game 8/10. Cinematics are awesome, it gives alot of weight to all characters you meet. And frankly i liked literally all of them. Story is very true to the lore and ups and downs feel organic. Enough to hook me in the whole way. Finished the game in 2 days, in two 14 hour game sessions. Havent done that in a while. Definately the best game PGI has ever put out. Now lets break it downPros:1 - Graphics are great, map design visually is very nice, although it is too linear for my liking. I would've preferred MC:Gold style sandbox missions, where we have objectives and just go about it however we want. But all missions have narration which triggers from point to point which would not be possible to do without linear objectives. Only exception i think is courchevel, the biome feels low resolution.2- Gameplay is solid, classic mech combat. And since there's no HSL, boat weapons to your heart's content.3- Campaign length, lasts 25-30 hours. There's even some variation towards the end.4- Story is 10/10, its not the sort of thing that makes you question life or anything but veery lore accurate. I want more of this. Definately made me root for clans which i never thought i ever would.Negatives1- AI isnt the best, you cant really do much in the way of movement maneuvers. Your teammates always stick to you so you'll lose dps if you wanna hide behind covers and peak for alpha since they will not have LoS towards enemy. There's no tactical element to star AI so, it gets a bit boring. Nowhere near as bad as MW5:Mercs but still subpar.2- Music, again not as bad as MW5:Mercs but still fails to create epic moments. Story is definately strong enough to create epic moments in game by itself, great ost would enhance that even further. Unfortunately fails at that.3- While Mech UI is decent, out of cockpit, it is a mess. _childDocuments_.review: Linux User: Everything seems to work day one about as well as it is for my windows using friends.As a long time Mechwarrior fan I am happy to have the game.  It feels quite different from Mercs in a way you wouldn't expect since it shares the same Mechwarrior 5 branding that mercenaries has.  Friend and I are playing coop and we are about 9 or 10 missions in.  We both agree that if you are looking at this like a Mechwarrior 5 Mercs expansion then you might come away feeling like everything is wrong.  I think that this game is on the core level a different beast.  A heavy focus was placed on rebuilding the experiences around lore aspects of the clans.  The mech selection at first seems small but the omni pod system means that there is a rich set of constraints to use to customize things.  As we are exploring this we have found a very different workflow from MW5:Mercs in relation to Mech configs.  The Omnipod layouts for the First wave clan mechs and the omni pod profiles are good enough that you might not even want to change them.  When you do find yourself in need of changing things your hands are much more tied in some ways but looser in others.  At first you feel like gahh this is limiting my freedom.... And yes it is clanner. You were made to drive mechs not design them. We breed engineers for that Mechwarrior and that isn't your job.  Leave it to the lower casts as Kerensky intended.  There is flexibility to be had in the system but that flexibility is far more inline with what you would expect for an army on the move during an invasion.  You are not dropping 4 million cbills to have a machine shop custom design a new endosteal arm structure so you can shoehorn that UAC20 into the right arm of your Adder.  "No star commander.  I can yank that large laser out and put a pulse laser into the pod instead but I have a forklift not a mechfactory inside this dropship."  The restrictions feel grounded in the world in a reasonable way that isn't explicitly spelled out to you. And why would it be... if you lived in this world you would already know this to be fact.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a long time fan of MechWarrior and Battletech games since the '90s and I love this game so much. It has a really good story, I really enjoyed the majority of the acting and cutscenes. The mouths/faces are a bit weird in some of them but overall very solid story, breathtaking visuals, and good gameplay. There are some bugs that are frustrating, I feel like Piranha Games will iron those out given some time. Performance also can be tough if you have a weaker computer.I took about 30 hours to beat the game on my first playthrough, I did a ton of mech customizations and played the simulator a little too so if you just play the campaign missions and don't tinker with mechs too much you can probably beat it in 20-25 hours. That said, I ended up caring about all of the characters and the story more than I expected. The Smoke Jaguars are not typically a group that gets a lot of empathy and care but you really start to feel the gravity of the situations they were in and the difficulty of their decisions. Add in all of the brainwashing and indoctrination since they were children and a lot of what they did starts to make sense. You get to see the uncertainty and questioning of orders as it happens, see the mistakes of leadership that falls upon the grunts to execute. It's sad but also feels "real".Gameplay is good, I really liked it. Feels like a more polished version of MechWarrior 5 Mercenaries. I do not love the recoil from ballistics but it's fine, I suppose. Some of the weapons feel under or over tuned, that may need some balancing patches. Ammo counts for missiles are really bad and honestly missiles in generally feel pretty lackluster. Lasers seem by far the best, PPCs and Gauss are also really good. Autocannons can be good but take more work it feels.Mech customization is significantly different than in a lot of other games from the series but honestly once I get used to it, I really like it. It also feels lore accurate with how Omnimechs were designed. Some people also complain about the lack of mechs, but the ones we have is lore-accurate as far as what frontline clan units would field in this era. A lot of mechs from MechWarrior Online and other games are either garrison/2nd line units (Clan Battlemechs) or were not available in the Clan Invasion era. Clanners also wouldn't lower themselves to piloting an Inner Sphere mech unless they had absolutely no other choice.This review is a bit random and jumps topics, I know, trying to get my thoughts down while they're fresh. The quick summary is if you want a more linear story focused experience like some of the older MechWarrior games and NOT a sandbox like the last few (HBS Battletech, MW5 Mercs), this is a fantastic entry into the series to sink your teeth into. There's not a huge amount of replay value although there is a branching choice near the end that I want to see the other result! Also the simulator has some challenges you can try to complete and also finishing all of the unlocks for your mechs can keep you busy for a good while. Co-Op is also really fun with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: 4/10 Long version:Story - 6/10So Clans does have a better story than Mercs. However, I should highlight that this isn't winning any Oscars or anything. The story is fairly basic, it's just a good basic. Towards the end, side characters definitely become really pointless and you couldn't care less about them, but at least with the main cast, they actually do do a half decent performance. But again, nothing award winning, but not terrible. Battle gameplay - 4/10LRM and Medium lazer. That's basically the whole game. I think I used SRMs twice ever. Ballistics are basically pointless. All your battles will take place within 800m and medium lazers reach that. AI won't really get too close so you'll always be able to use your LRMs as well. Just put LRM 15s and 4 medium lazers on something, anything, and you'll be fine. You're AI team mates are a bit smarter than in Mercs though. Very rarely get in your way, very rarely get stuck and do a good job of focus firing down enemies on your command, without turning suicidal.Mechlab - 2/10What. A. Joke. Not just because it's WAY too simplified, but the game doesn't reward you much for getting good with a particular mech and will quickly demand you upgrade to whatever is the latest. You never struggle for money and you make any real changes using Omnipods. Even if you use a mech and hate it, you'll unlock something new in 2 missions anyway so who cares. There's 0 reason to invest time into a mech and the mechlab reflects that. In 30 hours of playing, you might spend 30 minutes in the mechlab and 2 hours in cutscenes for context.Progression - 2/10So the game wants you to use a specific mech a ton so you can upgrade it with useless percentage bonuses you won't notice. But likewise, the game is constantly pushing you to use whatever the latest mech you unlocked, because if you don't, you'll be under tonnage, under tonnage, under tonnage. The game just assumes you'll run 5 of whatever the most recently unlocked mech is. The last 3 missions of the game is just 5 Dire Wolf mechs otherwise you're "under tonnage". There's also no reason to save mechs. Just sell old and buy new.Likewise, leveling up characters is pointless. It's just bonuses to percentages and you won't ever really notice anything. And since every character will pilot a Dire Wolf at the end of the game anyway, things like affinities, etc, are pointless. Locations - 1/10There's 3 planets not counting the "jungle" two mission tutorial. Desert, Different Desert and Japan. There are also no nighttime maps, no low gravity maps, no lava maps, no ice maps, etc so basically no environmental modifiers to any of the battlefields whatsoever. Oh, technically there are 2 or 3 "storm" maps which basically just means you can't see very far in front of you. That's it.Difficulty - 2/10I started on Expert and thought it was challenging but pretty good. It's not like Mercs where you can choose harder or easier missions. You simply eat the mission they feed you, which get progressively harder. You're also fed heavier mechs which you MUST eat too, or you'll quickly get stomped. In each mission you'll be taking down 20-30 IS mechs so if you slack a little, it'll burn quickly. Missions are also 15/20-ish min long with NO quicksaves during, so if you fail the mission and have to retry, you can easily waste half a day. I had to bump down to Normal roughly half way through and for the final planet I said F IT and bumped it down to story and even then, still failed one mission. Good notes -I did have several good points, things I actually liked about Clans, but again, upon replaying Mercs, those good points quickly evaporated and I honestly can't remember what these good points were anymore... if I remember and they're still valid in spite of replaying Mercs, I'll edit and put them in but until then.... I dunno man...TLDR; This game tries to have it's cake and eat it too. Tries to really get you caring about characters, who don't stick around very long. Tries to get you to invest in individual mechs, while also demanding you abandon them for 5 of whatever is new. Spend several missions invading and taking over a world, half the time which you actually run away after doing errand missions.Someone else said in their review "Why play Clans when we have Mercs?" and honestly he's right. I've been replaying Mercs after completing Clans and yeah, Mercs is just better in pretty much every single way (except story, Mercs story is lame asf) but that's really it. Just go play Mercs. Clans is what we call "ambitious but rubbish".Quick FYI: 10/10 is buy and play now, even at full price. 5/10 is it's ok, get it on sale or if you're bored and have spare cash. 0/10 is don't even bother, go play something, anything else.4/10

Overall, I am surprised at the B+/A- ish tier cutscenes coming from Piranha granted everyone seems to have Draco Malfoy syndrome, and I am pleasantly surprised the game didn't end at a few points where they could have made a cut-n-dice 10$ DLC. With the increased enemy count, they seemed to balance this out given you are piloting *superior* mechs, but it feels like you are shooting slightly more armored tanks - that is until you run into a bullet sponge boss. _childDocuments_.review: From someone who's tried and failed to get into the MW series a number of times now, this finally feels like a more pleasant step from Mercenaries. It's not just some dislike of the fundamental gameplay systems either, but the actual gameplay in each entry feeling a bit underbaked. Then again, one of the negative reviews says the combat was never the series selling point and the actual game is salvaging mechs, shooting the legs off every other mech for more salvage, and trying not to pick a mission that'll blow your mech in half before you get a chance to grab more salvage than it's worth. If that's true, then I guess I'm not the target audience for the general series, huh. Another one complained about your squad mechs being... too useful? They're significant to your survival, but they can't do everything on their own without wearing out quickly, so I'm not sure where that came from.Tangent aside, there are complaints about the increased linearity, both in mech progression and places to go, and it's true, this game is a fair bit more linear in that regard. In exchange, though, it also feels considerably more polished. The environments, for instance, feel a LOT more interesting to fight on than in Mercenaries, where every map felt like a barren reskin of a bunch of flat or mildly bumpy land, maybe with some cliffs to weave around. Here there's many more interesting geological formations, vantage points and hiding spots, structures to trample through, and probably more I've yet to see. Graphical fidelity is also up significantly, looking like an actually modern game, and helping the prior  point quite a bit.Sure, the voice acting is pretty poor.  And while there is apparently a lore reason that a lot of people aren't using contractions in their speech, it doesn't help much at making them sound less stilted. It's probably a pretty big part of it, honestly, because the characters that do use them correctly sound a lot more pleasant. It feels like the voice actors are struggling in their line delivery by being forced to adhere to this "no-contractions" rule, because what other IP makes characters do that? We get to experience right here why others don't do that. This all said, there ARE moments where it feels less stilted and more... realistic. Never "professional", yes, but at least they sound like what regular people would sound like. Makes sense for a bunch of "rejects" among the elite.Anyway, while there is a fair bit of roughness around the edges, if you're fine with or even prefer some more linearity, give this one a go. Maybe mods or an expansion will bring in a more free-form experience later on.It's nice to be able to full-unload on enemies without feeling bad about "wasting salvage."

_childDocuments_.review: While there may be issues with the performance of the game I expect those issues to be resolved in time.   For me the real problem with the game lies in two places.  The First is mission design.  While Clan warriors in the Battletech universe are genetically engineered super soldiers in advanced war machines, there are limitations of belief, and in many of the missions your small team are wiping out five to ten times your number in enemies and many times with no repairs or reloads along the way.   It is just unbelievable, especially when compared to earlier entries in the series.  The missions often feels more like an arcade rail shooter instead of a Mech warrior game.  If that wasn't bad enough, many of the missions just drag on, to the point where you wonder why they didn't break up the longer missions into two or three shorter missions, allowing you to repair and rearm in between.   This causes real bad pacing in many missions, making them feel grueling. The second issue that makes me not able to recommend the game is the NPC AI.  The AI's both allies and enemies simply charge straight at each other until they literally end up in melee brawls and massive pile ups.  While their is an advanced command interface because there is no time pause when you go to use it to give orders, you will never use it.    There are other design choices that allow weigh the game down but the two above are the ones that make it so that I can't recommend the game at a 50$ price point.

_childDocuments_.review: I have fond memories of this franchise, but I haven't really ever been an avid player. I think as a casual enjoy'er, I never had to drive to really dive into how deep and rich this game is...it was kind of overwhelming. That is why Clans is kind of the perfect game for me. I think people who LOVE the crazy complexity of previous iterations might feel a little restricted in this game, no sandbox here. We have a very focused experience here. This is a narrative driven experience with some leveling and customization options, but nothing as deep as other installments...and for me that is great! I feel like this was what I needed decades ago instead of all the overwhelming sandbox experiences to really start to appreciate the depth of the combat mechanics and tactics you can pull with certain weapons configurations. Also, mech warrior lore is amazing, so to focus on that more is also so welcome. All in all, if you are a long time fan of this franchise, you might feel the combat a bit more constrained. The missions are a little more deep than the sandbox randomly generated ones of the mercenary games. Be more ready for a story driven experience that drives you into heavier and heavier mechs over time. For noobs or casuals like myself, I think this installment is exactly what you need to dive into the greater universe, with some goodsh story telling (it's not baldurs gate 3 mind you) for an action game. Well done and I am excited for this to do well so we can contunie getting great titles like this. The good:Compelling storyBetter than just serviceable graphicsRelatively usable squad controlsMost importantly, I am just having fun...its fun yallThe bad:Missions, while varied, still just consist of mechs jumping over a world bounty and smashing you. Fine for an action game, but lacks some depth that would make it truly 11/10There is, so far, no real going back to your smaller mechs for any reason. No scouting missing in the late game that don't just also having you use your big assault mechs. The Ugly:Clunky UI when in mech customization mode, clearly designed with console in mind...it sucks (doesn't ruin the game but it needs work)Why are their like 5 different types of currency in this game?! Could that be any more confusing?! The UI is so bad for the inbetween mission mode I am mentioning it again...it sucks...so much clicking jesus christ.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a long time Battletech fan and I was quite excited for this game, now that it has arrived, here are my thoughts:*Played through solo with AI, have yet to play it in Co-opTLDR: IF you are a Battletech fan and love the overall story and universe, this game is easy to recommend to you.  If you got friends who are interested in learning more about Battletech, this is also a recommend as well (Co-op)! Even if you are a newer fan, as long as you do not mind some of the gameplay bumps (covered later), you can find some great value in the world building and story here too!STORYThe story is great and is a major step up for the Mechwarrior line of games. You are a Star Commander for Clan Smoke Jaguar and you need to lead your Star through the Clan Invasion. Each of your Starmates is their own character and are fully voiced and they each get great character moments throughout the journey. The cinematics are great and I always looked forward to the next one. A lot of dialogue does happen mid-mission, but its more in the lulls of combat when things are quieter and you are moving to the next nav point which is good for long treks. If you are not familiar with Battletech, namely the Clans, it may be a confusing yet great introduction to them (look up how the Clans speak and it will make following along easier, especially learning the various words used by them). Without spoilers, the game does have a couple of different endings and one of them does deliver a satisfying outcome (need to earn the other ending still). Plus, a lot of named characters from Battletech make appearances here and it is great! No complaints here honestly. I mean we got voiced mission briefings again to boot!GAMEPLAYIf you have played a Mechwarrior title or better yet, if you have played Mechwarrior Online (MWO) or Mechwarrior 5: Mercenaries, you will feel right at home here. It plays okay, but you will notice some weapon systems are better than others for outfitting your Omnimechs. I found the best way generally was to build towards your Starmate's specialties and if they do not have a specific specialization, I found energy weapons and additional armor were the way to go with additional heatsinks as needed. Your Starmates gain XP (as do you) and you can spend that XP on sharpening their skills and making them harder to hit during combat. I did find some things to be kind of meh (Targeting Computers being one of them). It felt like ballistics were not as powerful as they should feel (but they are improved from vanilla Mercs, projectile machineguns!) Missiles could feel hit or miss depending on if it was SRMs or LRMs. Energy weapons feel king here, You could outfit a Nova with a bunch of ER Small lasers and a lot of additional armor and heatsinks and once you researched some of the upgrades for ER lasers, the damn thing can easily swing well above its weight. You do feel powerful as the Clans should feel at this point in the timeline (Clan Invasion). I played through on Normal and only got wiped out twice during my playthough. Be wary of boss encounters, some of them feel ridiculous until you figure out a strategy. If you are struggling, remember that Clan weapons outrange Inner Sphere weapons, so use that to your advantage whenever possible. The 'Mech roster is only 16 'Mechs though and its only front line Omnimechs that were in use during the early invasion You unlock 'Mechs for purchase as you gain Honor. Would of been nice to see more, but its lore reasons. Do not expect much from the AI sometimes. It is better than MW5 Mercs vanilla though. Your Starmates do react and use their range more sometimes than they used to in Mercs. Enemy AI can sometimes be found standing still, making them easy kills if you know where to aim. The game economy is easy to dominate, only thing that truly held me back was salvage parts. Overall, it is not bad, but it could be better.AUDIO/GRAPHICSIt looks good and sounds good when the Audio is there. Voice acting is great and I have no complaints. Cinematics sound great! The soundtrack is awesome and I may have found my new favorite Mech Lab theme out of Smoke Jaguar (sorry Stutter Shark from MW4). Smoke Jaguar is how I envision the Clans: ancient, mysterious, tribal, and powerful and it makes for great background music as you are tinkering with your Star getting ready for the next mission. The graphics are good, in some areas it is a step up from Mercenaries and in others, it is about the same if not a little less. It is still a great looking game. I ran the whole game on Ultra on an i9 13900K and an EVGA RTX 3090 and i ran everything on Ultra with DLSS set to Ultra Quality and I got around 60 FPS and it would slow to sub 30 FPS in some areas in missions. Overall it was quite playable.TECHNICALOkay, I did cover performance earlier so I will not cover it again here. I did have some crashes throughout my play through. Not sure what caused them as it would just pop up Fatal Error and crash out. I could play for about 3 to 4 hours before the crash would hit. Some missions would not have background music when playing, not sure if it is a bug or an intentional decision. You can find some texture pop in, but in my experience it was not terrible. Overall, as stated earlier if you are a fan, its definitely worth a buy! If you are curious and not a Battletech fan, read up reviews and make your own judgement before buying. After all, Mod Tools are coming soon!Sorry if this seems a bit all over, I do not write very many of these!

_childDocuments_.review: Wasn't for sure how much I would like the narrative focus on the game but it did well. Story was good, interesting, almost had that sense of how war changes a person. Lore wise they did a good job, but could have spent a little more time explaining things for new commers into the franchise. I feel like they started to do this but ran out of development time when it came to this aspect, so some things were not explained as time skips forward, or revisited. Doesn't go through the entire clan invasion timeline, but most of it, and pretty much up to the end of the 5th wave. New mechbay system is a nice refresh on the system we have been used to, simplifies things for newcomers but at the cost of advanced tinkering for us vets. Very frustrating when I can't remove jump jets or adjust armor values. But hoping modding fixes that. Game length is a bit short, was able to finish the story in about 35 hours. I don't see any reply either other than coop with friends who haven't finished it yet. Doesn't have the replay ability like Mercs where you can just roam and take on jobs. I really wish we had this game engine in Mercs because its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beautiful and I'm missing that merc experience fix. Like in mercs, light and medium mechs become a thing of the past when you get onto bigger mechs and higher ton limit battles. Overall, I enjoyed the game and hope they expand on it more. It will be interesting to see if they continue the story or tell the story from one of the other clans that invaded. If you're not for sure about the game still, I'd let it cook for a year to see where it goes and get it on sale. Not a must get game but still a damn good enjoyable one that hopefully gets more content like how mercs got theirs.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review after finishing playthrough.Overall score of the game is only a 4 out of 10. So still can't recommend it.The story itself is a 7/10. Not bad but also not great either. To much "telling" instead of "showing" also the character animations look kinda of weirdly proportioned and there is a good amount of artifacts that prevent the cut scenes from being excellent.Mission design and gameplay 5/10. Although the missions are all "handmade" they follow the simple principle of just throwing more and more stuff at you. All can simply be beaten by just eleminating anything moving, no objectives that can really be failed. Additionally the drop weight just increasing over the entire campaign is old boring stuff. Missed opportunity here for some new element getting rid of the doing all assaults in the end game approach. In BT lore pilots tend to stay very long with their choosen mechtype. Would have been nice to see this incooperated into mission design.AI is pretty dumb. Enemy AI will aggro and concentrate on the player even if you command you own star infront of you and to engage first. Own star mates occassionally will do nothing even standing right next to enemies engaging them. Gets worse in the later missions.Map design 5/10. Yeah the maps are no longer just squares like in MW5 Mercenaries, but now all maps are just "tunnels". You are just channeled through them with artificial boundaries limiting the ability to move and position.Mechlab 3/10. Instead of just copying the decent MW5 Mercs Mechlab and add the Omnipod switch functionality they choose to remake the mechlab into an unnecessary mess and by introducing armor pods outright breaking the lore and BT construction rules. MW5 Mercs mechlab was in every aspect better than this new one in MW5 Clans.Mechwarrior developement/leveling 4/10. Same situation as with the mechlab. MW5 Mercs was outright better. You wanted a LRM specialist, you gave a lancemate an LRM mech and he got better in those weapons. In MW5 Clans your star mates have fixed perks you can upgrade with XP points. Way more restrictive and less intuitive to use.Research, chassis upgrade and marketplace 1/10. Those elements are just "bloatware" completely unnecessary in a story campaign driven PVE coop game. Development time spent here could have been just way better elsewhere.Also UI overall is not great and the control mapper doesnt properly support multiple input devices. Its 2024 and the game isnt able to recognize more than one joystick in its own control mapper. A game like MW should by default be able to allow full HOTAS/DUAL Stick multiple input device setups without the need for some third party tool and file tingering.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 150 hours in the game now, and I am going to go over the game. If you're looking between Clans and Mercenaries, my overall suggestion would be Mercenaries. Clans is still a great game though, a lot more story driven. The rest of my review will be below, some minor issues, but there is a few of them.My minor critiques that the game is very linear, no real decision making in it, other than one spot. No play after the story is done, Sim Pod is ok, but its unrewarding as it only awards minor xp for your pilots and mechs. I would like to have seen something like an open sandbox like they do in MW5 Mercs.. The replay value is limited. Too much "currency" to do every little thing in the game, such as pilots, chassis upgrades, omni-pod upgrades, unlock and buy each mech, research is unfulfilling too, takes so much to research things and you can only focus on a few things. Opposing mechs seem to hit center torso often, and that's even moving at max speed and piloting. I wish the game would pause on when there is story breaks in the middle of the mission, battle board, and/or weapon configuration while in the mission. Lastly, I wish they had more mechs available, and it's weird that there is no 90-ton clan mech available.At the time of writing this review, there is a pretty annoying bug in the mission "Voices of the Past" when you get to the end of the map and have to go back to where you started, the bay doors close quickly and can lock some of your pilots out. The only work around that I have tried that seems to work is to send your star to guard on the door itself, get behind them, and when you can see, set them to guard outside somewhere and follow them through. If you don't do it right the other mechs can make it out but you can get locked out. SO it takes some timing. My other suggestion, is to modify mechs with extra armor, as a lot of the missions seem to long and stretch out your durability,Update: The new DLC for clans doesn't seem worth it at all IMHO. It adds nothing for a game that has been pushed a story driven game. It does add new skins and new omni-pod options, but absolutely no new mechs. It adds a PVP mode and a Horde mode, which none of this appeals to me. If anything, this should've been a free DLC, especially for those that bought the collectors edition, like I did. I am posting this here because I am not going to pretend like I got it and didn't like it. All in all, if you want this game, I would wait till it all goes on sale. I don't think $60-$80 is worth the game. The story is ok, but not very deep at all.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not perfect, but it more than lived up to my expectations.For a bit of background, I played Mechwarrior Online from early alpha and while I enjoyed the gameplay the technical issues with it wore me down to the point where I couldn't stand it anymore. By the standards of that absolute gong show, this game is positively polished. Note that this game also chugs to nearly 30fps on a 7800X3D/4090, but hey - it's all relative.In terms of the actual game I had a great time with it. I know a lot of people prefer the sandbox nature of MW5 Mercs but the procedurally generated missions in that game wore thin very quickly for me. MW5: Clans felt like a direct response to that and it did not dissapoint, as far as I'm concerned. I grew up with MW2 Mercs and MW4: Vengeance in particular, and I've been waiting for a very long time for a game to carry that torch.As expected, I spent a huge chunk of my time with the game in the mechlab. You can get up to some shenanigans with the omnipods, sure lasers are kind of OP but it's not like the game is hard, so you can experiment quite a bit. I recommend trying out the researchable solid slug UAC because it's really funny to just obliterate something when you get lucky and it doesn't jam.Story actually impressed me - the voice acting isn't the greatest, and some of the characters (Mia) don't develop a personality until fairly late in the game. But for all the criticism I'll give Piranha - and I've given plenty - I've never once doubted their dedication to the Battletech universe. There's some painstaking detail here down to the individual loadouts of enemy squads, it's very impressive even though I'm sure most people wouldn't even notice or care. The dialogue is a bit stilted and the characters are a little uncanny valley but I was still pretty into it.The squad command stuff isn't quite as fleshed-out as I'd hope but it's still kinda cool. You get access to a tactical view where you can command your squad as needed but to be honest I barely used it. 99% of the time I just stuck to doing the all squad -> attack my target and it worked out fine. One thing I do like, is you can swap to your other characters freely - maybe you've got someone set up to be a sniper, or you lost Jayden's mech to an unlucky series of CT hits. I never came close to failing a mission on normal but being able to take over someone else's mech if you go down is a welcome feature.I haven't had a chance to play it co-op yet, but from my experience in MW5: Mercs I'm sure it's plenty fun. Overall I'd recommend it if you were a fan of the old Mechwarrior games, no idea if anyone under 40 still cares about this franchise these days though.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game, I really did.  But:1:  30 minute missions being capped by boss fights against vtol aircraft that can somehow take over fifty ER Medium laser hits apiece and they send THREE of them at you... I'm done.  Who the hell thought boss fights in a MechWarrior game was a good idea?  If a trio of VTOL aircraft can destroy an entire lance of full health Mechs exist then why do Mechs even exist?  Having to play for 30 minutes just to get back to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hit sponge boss fight is too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ soul crushing to keep going.2:  There is a research mechanic.  In a MechWarrior game... what the hell are we researching you might ask?  Well a percent increase to your energy weapons!  Or a percent decrease to damage taken!  Why does this fall to a lowly squad leader to perform and not the entire scientific might of the Clans?  Well you see... shut up.3:  Voice acting is sub par, not horrible (usually), but more distracting than anything else.4: Tactical map is a great idea, but falls flat in execution.  Using it in the heat of battle is impossible and it is not topographic so you have to already know where the hills and valleys are before using it most of the time.  It is really only good for setting up a firing line for your Mechs, although I should also note that setting up a firing line far away from the enemy and sniping them is extremely effective.  The biggest problem with it is that time keeps going while you fumble around with it (and you WILL fumble around with it as it controls like no other tactical map I have ever used in a game).  This means while you are trying to get your Vulture to high ground where it can use its long range weaponry most effectively YOU are being cored because your just standing there... or you are walking off a cliff.5: The Mech Bay.  What the hell happened here?  The Mech Bay is a complete jumble.  I can't even describe what it was like trying to use the first time, it is made even more horrifying when one considers the completely adequate job Mercenaries did.  Why didn't they just use THAT?!6: Not only is there research but individualized research, or did they call it experience, for individual Mech models.  All the problems of the research system, but now a seperate one for EVERY MECH IN THE GAME.  Which brings us to....7: To much admin.  Like all of the admin.  You have to:     A: Hire Technicians and researchers with "Blue Currency".     B: Assign Technicians to fix mechs.     C: Buy mechs (no salvaging mechs from the battlefield).     D: Outfit mechs individually how you want them (no saving loadouts to copy paste)     E:  Que up research with the salvage you get from missions.     F:  Spend "Mech Experience" on all the Mechs you used from the last mission.     G: Spend Pilot XP on all of your pilots (there are 5)     H: Unlock Mechs using Blue currency because you can't just buy them before that step.     I: Decide if you are going to upgrade your ability to access salvage/ research faster / repair         mechs faster using blue currency.And the entire time you have to try and keep in mind your current Mech Experience currency, actual Money Currency, Honor (blue) Currency, three (THREE) different salvage currencies.......  It is just too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much and none of it, literally NONE OF IT, is explained in game.8:  No in game explanation on what the different mechs are, you just get a stat breakdown.  Minor grip maybe but a simple write up on what a mech is good for would go a long way.TLDR:  This game is a jumbled mess, if you want big stompy robots just go play Mech Warrior 5 Mercenaries... or find a copy of MW:3 or MW: 4 Mercenaries.  They are both really good.Bosses.... why the hell are there hit point sponge bosses....  I need a drink.

_childDocuments_.review: Mechwarrior: 2 and its expansion, Ghost Bear's Legacy, were some of the earliest games I played, leaving an indelible mark on my gaming experiences. Mechwarrior 5: Clans takes place during a particularly intriguing period in Battletech lore, the Clan Invasion. The game immerses players in a world where highly advanced, genetically engineered warriors, known as the Clans, invade the Inner Sphere.The game excels at capturing the rich lore of the Battletech universe. Clan warriors speak in a distinctive dialect, eschewing contractions and using unique terms like "Aff" (yes), "Neg" (no), "Quiaff" (query affirmative), and "Quineg" (query negative). While the Trial of Position is unfortunately narrative-locked, the game features other Clan traditions and elements, such as Elementals, albeit primarily in cutscenes.Despite the limitations in certain areas, the story is well-crafted and engaging. The missions offer variety and challenge, allowing players to truly feel the power of Clan technology against the outdated equipment of the Inner Sphere. The game's linear structure is understandable, as it helps to establish the narrative and portray the downfall of Clan Smoke Jaguar.The gameplay is incredibly satisfying. Piloting a mech feels like commanding a war machine, capable of leveling entire buildings and crushing opponents with brute force. The iconic weapons, like the Particle Projection Cannon and Gauss Rifle, are incredibly satisfying to use. The customization options are extensive, allowing players to tailor their mechs to their preferred playstyle.Mechwarrior 5: Clans is a fantastic addition to the Mechwarrior series. It captures the essence of what made the earlier games so special while offering a fresh and engaging experience. Fans of the franchise and mech combat enthusiasts alike will find much here to enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: About 20 hours in I have a few thoughts.The good:Enjoying the lore-heavy story. Devs really kicked it up a notch in terms of narrative and characters. Choosing Smoke Jaguars for the game's protagonists was an inspired choice and the writers did a decent job using the source material to give us a grounded Crusader perspective on the Clan Invasion from the guys who are usually portrayed as comically evil psychopaths. Also possibly the only game in recent memory that leaned into ComStar's religious trappings, which was a nice choice.Some have criticized the writing of the dialogue but - and I hate to be the one to break it to you - that's how Clanners actually talk. It feels stiff and jilted because if you don't talk like that they batchall you for your pants. I've actually been impressed with the attention to detail, where the only Clan character who uses contractions is the rebellious guy and he gets in trouble for it more than once. Combat feels good and fairly smooth. You are always outnumbered, you are rarely outgunned, which is how a Clan vs Spheroid fight should feel. Most IS mechs will go down with a couple pulls of the trigger, but can you pull the trigger fast enough to get all of them? The scripted encounters feel more meaningful than the rng spawning in Mercs. PPC snipers will hang out on a cliff and harass you from range. Missile boats will keep their distance and focus you down. Locusts and Fleas will try to get behind you as quickly as they can because it's their only chance of survival. Serious overall improvements to HUD, command interface, and cockpit aesthetics. It's so much easier to track things like heat, speed, torso orientation because it's all right there around your targeting reticle. There are numerous ways to give commands to your squad, and the top down rts style command interface is especially cool, although it takes some getting used to to figure out what terrain feature you're looking at from the sky. And while this is a pretty minor thing, the cockpits look so much better. More sim-like, less hyper futuristic, which imo is what Mechwarrior/Battletech should feel like.Sounds design is great. Lots of little details of sounds clearly inspired by previous MW titles. Lasers have hints of what they sounded like in 4. Wooshing missiles sound like a high def version of 2. All the sounds feel a little meatier in a way that really improves the experience. -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The bad:Mech customization is underwhelming, and feels way too limited for what you should be able to do with an omni-pod. I get what they were trying to do in terms of letting you progress to more interesting designs, but even when you get there you're still pretty limited. This can be especially frustrating when you're trying to tailor your squad's mechs to their individual skills. Liam is an ECM specialist and gets buffs to missiles. So obviously you want to give him a mech that fits that profile, but you are limited to mechs that have an omni-pod with an ECM slot. So if you want to give him a Mad Dog with electronic warfare capabilities and a crap ton of missiles, too bad, you can't, the Mad Dog doesn't get an ECM slot. I want to recreate a custom Timber Wolf like the one I bring to the tabletop? Too bad, I can't, because the pods don't have the right slots, even though canonically they're supposed to be highly customizable. Lots of little things like this can make mech customization frustrating and disappointing.On the subject of mechs, the available selection on release is a little disappointing. Sure we have some fan favorites, but there's just not a lot of variety. I was hoping for an Ebon Jaguar out the gate, given it is THE Smoke Jaguar mech. And I understand for the time it might be a little too early with production only starting around the time the invasion force hit the Periphery. But where's the Hunstman, Fire Moth, or Black Lanner? Where are the IIC mechs? I'm sure they have plans to introduce more stuff down the road but I am just underwhelmed by the selection, especially considering how many of these models already exist from MWO.For how interesting the enemy ai has been, friendly ai dumb as hell. Ordering your squad to attack a target means they will close to knife fight range and get shot to crap in the process. Hold position and follow are the only orders worth giving, and even then, sometimes they get real confused when it comes to following. Every single allied mech has a death wish and will get themselves blown up as soon as possible. The voice acting is. Well. It's there. While I have genuinely enjoyed the writing for what it is - and let's face it Battletech has  never been a source of literary masterpieces -  the deliver of the lines could have used some serious polish. Shout out to whichever actors voiced Cordera Perez and Sarah Weaver, though, they're doing the heavy lifting so far. I haven't finished the campaign yet, but I have some early concerns about replayability. For all of its problems, Mercs was an open sand box where you never really knew where you were going to end up. With this game being on rails, and with so few mechs to actually choose from, It doesn't feel like there would be much point in returning because there isn't much that you could do differently a second time around. -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------tl;dr It's not perfect but I have been enjoying my time. If you are just a fan of Mechwarrior/MechAssault games I'd say pick it up once it's on sale, or bundled with a few dlcs down the road. If you are a fan of Battletech and especially if you are a Clanner yourself (freak) it's worth picking up out the gate, warts and all. I don't know if this is the Mechwarrior game crusty old grognard me wanted, but it is certainly the Mechwarrior game nerdy kid me wanted. And that is something special all it's own.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from a longtime Mechwarrior Fan who played almost every game, the Tabletop and RPG and read a lot of the books: I'm positively surprised how well PGI pulled this off. The story seems organic, you get a feel for the clans, nothing so far feels pushed or forced. I actually like their changes to customisation. Only negative is that the Mechlab really is a struggle to use, even for people who know what they are doing. I like how they did the progression, too. Feels like a good compromise between gamey progression and clan lore. The only downsides are for one the bad performance. I have no issues wih a ryzen 9 7900x and a 3090ti to run everything on max on 1440p but your experience might vary. had one crash after 7 hrs. the other one is the lack of mechs. only 16, unlocking ONE every "level" of progression just feels... meh. very limited. These problems dont stand in the way from me enjoying the game though.Thanks PGI, you keep improving! It's been a long journey from the MWO beta to here and I'd lie if i'd say i was always convinced that you could pull it off.

_childDocuments_.review: The only legitimate complaints any true Mechwarrior fan should have about this game is it is slightly buggy and needs some patches. So far no game breaking bugs, or ones that result in mission restart. Mainly minor annoying ones.Now, having said that: this is the best Mechwarrior game made to date. If you are a BattleTech fan and have read the books and have been playing Mechwarrior for years, it checks all the boxes. Full star to command, little bit simpler of mechlab this time around as we are no longer Inner Sphere mercs scrapping along a living, but highly technologically advanced and well supplied Clans. Personally, the best thing about this game is the combat. It is much more fast paced than previous titles, it feels like you are in the books during the Clan invasion scrapping it out. I've been playing on a Saitek X52 Pro HOTAS Joystick and its been working great, just make sure to almost max out your deadzones in the Saitek properties, or it'll be way too touchy to aim. The story (SO FAR) has been excellent. Was cool to see Leo Showers, hopefully we will see others as well. They have kept the story close to the source material so far, and the cinematics are top notch. I am still finishing the game so I will return and edit after finishing the campaign. I give it an 8.5/10. Shoutout to Piranha for going above and beyond with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: My original review was "wait and see". I've waited and saw, I can't recommend it.The game is two hotfixes deep, with only one notable improvement to performance in the first patch, and the game still runs terribly. The store page recommends a Ryzen 5 3600, an RTX 2080, and 16GB of RAM. My computer has a Ryzen 5 5600X, an RTX 2060, and 32GB of RAM. Even at the absolute lowest settings with DLSS set to max performance, this game chokes and dies the moment enemy mechs spawn and when anyone takes damage - which is gonna be happening a LOT. This is a sentiment I've heard shared among other 20 series RTX users, and I can only begin to imagine how poorly the game runs on a system closer to its minimum specs.The tldr is that the recommended specs on the Steam page are incredibly wishful, especially in regards to the recommended GPU. If you don't have at least a 30 series Nvidia card or an AMD equivalent, this game will not be able to run smoothly enough to be enjoyable. I'm really disappointed, because Mercs is able to run flawlessly on my machine at much higher graphics settings.

It's impossible to aim at that framerate - but the ai doesn't have that issue; so you take otherwise avoidable damage because it takes you 3x as long as it should've to kill your enemies because aiming becomes a guesswork of "if I move the mouse this much and press to fire I should be able to... nope missed it by 5 meters because when the next ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ frame got generated, they were elsewhere. Aaaand I apparently took two volleys of fire from that mech and another to its side. There goes my left arm and a few weapons".I WANT TO LIKE THIS GAME.But it's just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ impossible if it plays like this.I feel literally insulted and if I could, I would ask for a refund now.I want this company to make more games because when they get it right (a few months after release usually) they are great but this is just disrespectful at this point.This is no longer a "Made with Unity" indie first-attempt.We deserve better.[[UPDATE, 2 weeks after launch]]2 hot-fix patches into this "semi-aborted batch" of a launch, to borrow lines straight from the game, and things are... a bit better but nowhere near where they should be.Difficulty and other bugs have been improved - and some performance improvements have made the game playable if you drop the resolution to half of what you expected your rig to be able to handle.But you will still run into sections where the fps drops to 1950's cinema level -- and some missions where it is literally unplayable (2-5fps consistently).There is no "Enable/disable ray tracing" option on the game and I feel this is the primary culprit. MW5 was also unplayable with RT on (still is if you ask me) on anything but a 4k+ rig you buy today, but if you disable RT [which, on a personal note, adds absolutely nothing to warrant the performance hit] you can max out graphics on that game at 60FPS with a 3070 in 4k. Not this one though. Not even all-settings-to-mid with DLSS on will save you at 1440p.The game is mostly fun outside of the gaping performance holes that should never have been allowed to happen - or still be a thing so far into its launch window.I want this company to keep making games cause honestly they hit more than they miss overall but... they need better leadership and more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ spine about the state they launch their games under.In 2 weeks time they may patch most of the issues out and finally have the game in a state worthy of launch. Instead we got an Early-Access half-baked project without the warnings, and they have execs on vacation while the poor engineers crunch away at fixing what they likely warned months ago wouldn't be ready - and they get all the blame.There is a good game under all of this.It's just really hard to see it yet...[[original review at launch day +1 follows]]It shows a lot of promise, but unfortunately Piranha has gotten into the lazy exercise of "release whatever and polish it later" habits . Ever since MW-5, every single DLC showed the same pattern. They release a grossly bugged out, unstable, supremely un-optimized piece of ♥♥♥♥ and hope their players have the patience to wait out the month-2 months it takes them to patch the game into actually playable status and I just can't stomach rewarding such ♥♥♥♥♥♥, inexcusable behaviour.The game itself does look like it could be good, but it has major flaws that need to be patched out.Graphics are pretty - but don't fool yourself, just cause this game uses Unreal 5 doesn't mean the quality will automatically be amazing -- UE is a tool, and like any other, it's how you use the tool that determines what you get out of it. Environments are prettier and smoke effects as well, lasers have nicer impact effects, but all around it's not that huge of a glowup. Or maybe it would be if I could play it in more than Medium settings on an 12th gen i7 with an RTX 3070. Even with DLSS turned all the way, performance is abysmal and the framerate stutters unpredictably from 30 to 5 fps, making aiming impossible.Difficulty is also ridiculously inconsistent. I had one of my allies get insta-killed by a spider and two tanks at the beginning of a mission for no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason. I had literally two dozen more mechs to take out after that.I'm done trying for now.I will wait a few weeks for Piranha to finally finish this rushed job insult and give it a try again. Maybe then I can make this a positive review but as it stands, if I could request a refund I would. Do not reward their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ leadership for going the "we can always patch it later" approach or they will keep doing it, laughing at our expense.Wait for them to finish the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ job, and then you might be in for a pretty decent game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best  Mechwarrior narrative campaign based game since Mechwarrior 3 (which took about 10-11 hours to complete and this is around 25 or more). I am a veteran with the mechwarrior games and play competitively with MWO. Some points:- I was surprised to see how good the enemy AI was on expert mode.  This was the one thing I was afraid of because of how MW5 Mercs was. People who are complaining about AI needs to just up the difficulty. This is far better than MW5 mercs throwing 8 million mechs at you because AI and spawning was messed up (I like MW5 mercs but that was such a big issue.)  Honestly this is some of the best single player AI I have seen for a Mechwarrior game (not a high bar to clear but still). When it comes to your teammates you just have to know how to command them It isn't hard. They are especially good at guarding positions. Use the command wheel and battlegrid. It actually helps. When they all go chasing after a target and run into a trap is when you are likely to lose them.- I have not experienced any stuttering or slowdowns. This game runs beautifully for me. I did see the texture load issue but it seems like the patch fixed it because I haven't seen it since. - People complain about the cinematics in how the faces are offputting. I honestly don't know what they are talking about. Is it perfect? No, but it's not bad either. The cinematics have been a joy to watch. Especially if you are one who enjoys Battletech/Mechwarrior lore. - The Mechlab is actually far greater than MW5: Mercs vanilla. Is it better than modded? No of course not. A lot of folks may not be familiar with Clan Omnimechs. The only customization you get out of them is swapping their pods around and mixing and matching them (like in mechwarrior online). You CAN do this in game, but it's not immediately obvious. It only took me a few minutes to figure out the UI. If you have played mechwarrior games before, you will know what you are doing. Newer players will struggle though. They didn't even provide a tutorial. Clan omnimechs don't work like the mechs you see in MW5, and the game should have done a better job at describing Clan tech. A lot of people are frustrated with this but all the options are actually there. You are not limited to the stock omni loadouts! You can absolutely mix and match  the omnipods so you get the hardpoints you want!- Hiring technicians and scientists is a cool feature. I was worried there wouldn't be things to do in between missions and this is actually quite helpful. They have a similar chassis upgrade system like in MW5: Mercs. Except this time you spend mech XP on it rather than collecting things. - The UI is a fair criticism but it's not as awful as some are making it out to be. In five minutes i had it figured out. In no way does that take anything away from the overall game. This is definitely a game I recommend. It's a definite buy for Mechwarrior fans/veterans. New players will enjoy it too because it has accessible options and you can make the game play a lot like mech assault if you want (modern controls vs classic, auto aim, etc). You may be confused with the Mechlab and how these things work, but the stock loadouts are more than enough to succeed.You might be limited to 16 omnimechs but with all the different omnipods and loadouts you actually have a lot of options here. Clan Omnimechs were designed to quickly switch loadouts and fulfill multiple roles (Fire support, sniper, brawler, etc). So think of it as having 16 base mechs but the loadout options each mech has is equal to 6-7 inner sphere variants of the same mech. There are far more options than the stock MW5: Mercs. I think people are being a bit kneejerk with the criticism with the mechlab and simply aren't understanding how it works (a viable complaint). I may edit this review later, but for now... it's a solid game and I have high hopes for it.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: There are only 16 mechs your star can pilot in the entire game. Granted these are omnimechs, so each mech is essentially 3-5 variants of the same mech in one. But still, 16???? Save yourself the trouble, Battletech and MW5: Mercenaries are just better. Buy this on sale. MW5 Clans tries to sell itself on it's story and increased mission depth, general gameplay is overall stronger than in other recent titles, but the game is a linear mission to mission structure deprived of the sandbox seen in more recent titles. This has obvious pros and cons, but the main take away here is that Clans provides a more  curated player experience.On the flipside, this means that the game has significantly less content, less replayability, less customization, less emergent story telling, and (again) less mechs.Also, something about the mech combat feels off that I can't put my finger on. Missions drag on forever, enemies are massive damage sponges that soak up gauss rifle rounds, and at times the mechs feel less like the heavy monstrosities of previous games and more like floaty walking boats. Don't get me wrong, it's still a blast, but something feels wrong about it that didn't bother me about MW5 Mercs.
