_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD:It's another Mechwarrior Game!  I've played every one that was available for PC for some reason.  I played a lot of MW5: Mercs and it's at least as good as that game.Visuals are improved by default over the previous title.  This comes at a significant performance cost.  I can run MW5: Mercs @ Ultra 120Fps, but I hover around 60-70Fps here with AMD FSR on balanced.  And the visual artifacts produced by that are very noticeable.Missions are compelling so far.  I've made it to Rep 9 on Expert Mode.It's an episodic computer animated TV show in between missions.I like the Omnipod system and the research tree system has improved much from the previous game.I really like the idea of the Battlegrid, although its usefulness is limited by the BAD AI.The environment and levels are really nice looking and expansive at times.Damage is more obvious visually and looks nice.  Weapon damage seems toned down a bit and killing takes a bit longer than previous titles on average.  That could be due to convergence issues though.I like the new PPCsTHE BAD: Copypasta of MW5:Mercs.  I wouldn't care about that really.  I mean, it's such a big expansion that they made it a game.  It's not that unusual and I don't have a problem with it like some.  But they didn't seem to spend any noticeable development time fixing all the bugs and visual glitches that have been present in the original MW5:Mercs game for years.  Visual Hardpoint glitches, AI pathing and behavior, flipping out tanks, and mission balance are all problems.  I almost can't tell which game I'm playing.The exact same problems.  If these were new problems I'd understand.  The AI being the most frustrating thing about this game and the previous game.  I could go on about the AI, but it's not worth it here.UACs do not feel nice to use in any format.  MWO is so much better.THE UGLY:why so much TEETHUI and navigation took quite an imagination to design, possibly hallucinating substances.  But that's sort of on brand for the clans.  Action wheel bound to middle click by default is horrible to interact with on PC.  It seems to be a copy of everything you can do with the Fn commands and would appear to be for controller users.  I'm not sure how the developers expect us/them to assign commands with this wheel that covers the screen while mechs are running at 100kph straight at you.  Who has time for that?Weapon projectile convergence is just not.  No convergence to the cross-hair.  Shots randomly go through mechs and scatter uncontrollably.Torso can't look upward more than 45 degrees.  Yet, they put enemies, filers, bosses on high ground consistently.THE TRUTH:I shouldn't have expected real progress.  I'm still going to play it.  Just disappointed.  I thought that the head start the devs were getting by reusing so much of the previous title would allow them to focus on the obvious issues and be creative.Still would recommend for Mechwarrior fans.  So far, I am having fun most of the time.Dear Piranha Games,Thanks for making Mechwarrior games.  Don't you also like Mechwarrior games?  This should have been a win for you.  Please hire the correct number of developers.  Please give them enough time to complete tasks.  Set higher standards.Best wishes

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend it? Yes, but not glowingly. This is meant to be a sequel to a five year old game but quite honestly feels like DLC released in that five year old game's release cycle. It has progressed in some areas, regressed in many others and at no point does it feel like 5 years worth of progress has been made.Let's take Lance mate AI, this is in the regressed column because far more than in the last game they bunch up tight to you and repeatedly shoot each other, and given that the game registers friendly fire as a hit, this is an issue. They are, quite frankly, dumb as a box of rocks. In one example an enemy was behind a rock and one of them was firing away with his ballistic weapon trying to shoot through the rock, wasting precious ammo, in an even worse example - and this has happened several times - the same thing happening except he's trying to shoot through his lance mate's mech, firing away with his LBX 5 into his back, causing significant damage.The UI is unfit for purpose, using a radial menu rather than the key presses of the previous game. Usually a radial menu is superior but try hitting the middle mouse button while in combat to give your AI teammates orders, it's not easy. For example if I wanted to order a critically damaged mech to stay behind it was two button presses, now it's fiddling around with a radial menu and positioning where you want them to guard. It also has a limited number of orders, I cannot, for example, give them engagement ranges or select from different formations to mitigate their disastrous AI. There are other issues as well, such as lance mate mech pictures have been removed meaning I now have no idea where they're damaged, replaced by a name card with a percentage next to it. I'm almost certain in the last game I could have had them engage at long range if I could see they were about to lose a component. They also removed your velocity so you have no idea how fast you're going, nor is the heat bar readily obvious. I had to test with energy weapons to find where it is and it doesn't stand out in combat.That being said there are good points. Acting is vastly superior, and I actually really like the mech bay, it reminds me of MW3 allowing individual components to be removed as well as entire omni-pods. I've also had a single crash which for a modern game is unheard of, although be warned others have had issues so it depends on your hardware. The number of mechs available is limited to a disappointing 16 and I'm on my 6th mission and I still can't buy a better mech than the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Viper I'm in and even when I reach the level requirement the mech I can buy will still be in the same weight bracket, i.e. medium. With more mechs they could have had a smoother curve going from light medium (you start piloting a medium mech but you lead a lance of lights) to a heavy medium. I suppose though I should be glad the likes of the Mad Cat weren't behind a paywall of DLC.One final thing that is up to personal taste. You can chose from two control schemes, classic and modern. Classic is like Mercs, modern moves the legs where the torso is pointing making flanking almost impossible. I highly recommend classic. Clans is a good game but it isn't five years better than its predecessor, and in many cases is worse. As I said at the beginning it feels more like a DLC. For those who have played it, The Witcher 3 came out 4 years after The Witcher 2 and is a monumental step up. This game took an extra year and simply isn't. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Having a hard time to understand all the bad reviews.Are there things that can be improved? For sure.Is the game playable? 11h in, I had not a single bug. No.Gameplay: The game is exactly what's told in trailers/description: A mostly linear, mission-based and story-driven MW experience.If you want sandboxes, multiplayer or skirmish, this is not the game you are looking for (right now at least).Let me tell you, I'm happy they made this decision. To me a well written campaign is worth so much more than any random/sandbox encounters. (And I think MW:Mercs already does this greatly)I didn't play MW:Mercs, but I remember the classic MW:2 + 3 experiences. MW: Clans feels just like a modern version of these.The player will dive into a classic mission-based and mostly linear campaign.Between each mission, well crafted cutscenes and briefings will advance the story.Huge focus on the personalities of the characters and their roles in clan. Well written and with love to detail. In a gaming world where every game tries to do sandbox open world experiences with build-your-story-and-find-32k-endings, this is refreshingly different. Noone would read a book or watch a movie like that. So far, the story is convincing and I'm happy to see a game focusing on one well written plot instead of a thousand mediocre ones.UI could be better, some things are hard to find, but with a few hours into the game, it is working well for me.For us battle mech noobs it would have been cool to add some sim missions explaining the pros and cons of different weaponry as well as strategies to efficiently hunt down enemy mechs.

_childDocuments_.review: Just watch a play through of it. Unlike MechWarrior 5 this isn't a sandbox game. It's just a story that you play through with one branching path and you unlock everything your first playthrough, so doesn't have any replay value. It's also more of an arcade feel to it where the mechs are too fast and it doesn't feel like you're piloting a multi ton mech.There are points in the story that are good, but I also find myself just annoyed at the angsty teen vibes from the characters. They contently say how superior they are to their enemies and how much better their mechs are and talk ♥♥♥♥ about them when they don't come out and fight fair because it's dishonorable... Well it's because you have superior mechs, so why would they come out and fight fair. It's like saying come out and die. It's also a surprise invasion from you're people, so where's your honor when you jumped an unprepared enemy?The game is also not very balanced and thought out. There is also no salvage system in this game, so you only have a small pool of 16 mechs and by the end you'll only be using the only 100t mech you can get from the store, everything else is useless. I would also say that most of the mechs in the game are bad. Almost all of them have most of their weapons in the arms and on Expert difficulty they lack armor. I found myself just throwing on another ton of armor on every point that I could (some parts don't have slots to put anything) and I still lost mech and components.When loading out a mech, every weapon and accessory is available to you from the start and you can buy as many MP lasers, ER lasers, Gauss rifles, AC20's (and it's variants), weapons as you want. No level cap or anything on what you can buy (you have to wait on your level up to get better mechs that unlocks at each level). Which might sound alright for some, but to be honest, you can't really change that much on these mechs. It feels very restrictive with the locked in jump jets and double heat sinks and limit slots on the arm, legs, etc that they give you. You can also swap mechs arms, legs, torso, core, head with EXP that you earn by using the mech to buy these parts. Which is a good idea, but 99% of the time legs, core, head are all the same, but you can still buy like 3-5 different variant with 0 stat difference, or usable slots. It might just be visual, I don't know cause I never bought them.Missile weapons are a lot better in this then in MW5, both in feel and use, but the ammo bins don't have enough missile in them to make them viable to use; given that most missions you're running through a gauntlet of enemies. On the other hand, they did make AC a bit lighter and they don't have as bad ammo problems... maybe the AC 20 bins are a bit low.I also almost never used that tactical map feature of the game. There just isn't a good time to use it.

_childDocuments_.review: MW5 Clans is a huge leap in effort from developer PGI, and it largely delivers.There are significant technical issues present, and players easily frustrated with nonsensical bugs like  or frequent large FPS drops (I have a 7950x3D + 3080, graphics on mixed med/low, maps run around 100 fps but drop to ~50 in firefights, even down to the 30s during enemy spawns) should wait for more patches.The story is engaging, with lots to chew on for franchise fans, and more exploration of Clan society than we've seen in previous Mechwarriors. Voice acting is pretty good, with standouts like Galaxy Commander Perez, and while others have complained about character and face animations, I find them all good to great (keep in mind how low the bar has been set by games like ME Andromeda). The game's interfaces are very clunky and unintuitive, and in this respect is probably even a step backwards from MW5 Mercenaries. It's easy to completely miss the fact that you can mix omnipods from different sets (option is in the component config, E hotkey, when modifying equipment, not on the omnipod unlock screen). There are profoundly stupid holdover issues from Mercs like needing to unbind melee attacks from your AI pilots' weapon groups to prevent your LRM boats from running in to punch the enemy Atlases. The optimal use of Requisition isn't necessarily obvious (max out your salvage capacity, then focus on scientists, to get your upgrade research going early). Issues like this abound.All that said, the shooty mech action is immensely satisfying, building on the good parts of MW5 Mercs, and with the feeling that missions matter this time. It's a worthwhile installment for Mechwarrior fans.edit 20241028 - patch 2 fixed the aforementioned kebyind resetting issue, but performance is still abysmal

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game, worth the money if you're a BattleTech fan or just like robots with guns.The campaign is great, and Piranha deserves credit for the improving their design philosophy by bringing us a hand-crafted campaign with a decent progression system. That being said, I think the campaign suffers from a couple of oversights that take away from an otherwise enjoyable game: 1. For starters, currency is almost meaningless since they give you so much of it. I finished the campaign with multiple copies of every Chassis still in my hangar, and I never once felt the need to sell equipment or a spare Mech.2. Either the difficulty is too easy, or I unintentionally leaned into builds that were OP (Laser spam). I played the entire campaign on Expert Difficulty and I can count the number of times I lost a pilot on one hand. 3. The Tonnage "Limits" are too generous and push the player into bringing progressively heavier Mechs every mission. And if you're not bringing your heaviest Mechs, you'll even get warnings about being "Significantly under tonnage" for the mission. It's as if the game doesn't want you to bring Light & Medium (and eventually Heavy) Mechs into battle for the latter half of the campaign -which is a shame, because these Mechs are otherwise fun to customize and play with.It would have been awesome if they implemented a system that encouraged Mech diversity every mission, such as restricting your Star to 1 Assault, 2 Heavies, etc. Or just made the Tonnage limits more strict so you had an incentive to use the Light mechs for more than 3 hours of the campaign. Peeves aside, I had a good time. Solid 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Mechwarrior at its finest.  A wonderfully lore-deep and well told story, a good variety of mechs (and I assume more are on the way via DLC at some point), and well executed squad combat.  This game is innovative in its genre, and it is refreshing.  I have small gripes.  It could be optimized for performance a bit better.  The overhead map is an ingenious addition to the game play.  But it's weird that it doesn't slow gameplay down in order to let you actually use it, so it is pretty much useless in the heat of battle.  I've heard complaints about the mech lab and I initially agreed.  But after spending some time with it, I get it.  I've done a bit of co-op as well, and this game only gets better with friends.  I hope to do this even more.Bottom Line:  If you have never played a Mechwarrior game, this is a great way to start.  If you are a vet, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★ - Great 28.4 hours Normal (Classic Movement) Keyboard and Mouse + Thrustmaster Warthog HOTAS	• Offers intense, tactical mech battles with a good balance between strategy and action.	• Updated AI mechanics make enemy mechs and their tank counterparts more challenging, especially in larger-scale battles.	• Different variety of mechs from MW5: Mercenaries (Clan focused mechs), allowing for customized builds and unique playstyles.	• Mech movement feels weighty and impactful however may take getting used to for first time players.	• In-game HUD is busy and can feel intrusive to the experience.	• A solidly built story with intriguing lore of the shadow jaguar clan (bad guys) invading the inner circle (cluster full of morally Grey factions).	• The narrative does a great job at immersing players in the struggle between Clans, adding depth to each mission.	• Character dialogue is fitting but sometimes generic and cringe (Why say Aff or Neg instead of Affirmative or Negative? You're not saving that much time.); voice acting is solid though.	• Story missions are varied enough but for people that are familiar with MW5: Mercenaries, can occasionally feel formulaic in structure.	• Visually decent landscapes, especially the forest and mountainous terrains.	• Mech animations are decent; however humans are animated without mocap and often give robotic and uncanny valley vibes that can break immersion.	• Explosion and smoke special effects are satisfying, where ballistic, laser and missile sound effects are punchy and bassy. 	• Both MW5: Mercenaries and Clans are two sides of the same game. Where Mercenaries is an extensive Sandbox experience of full customisability potential, Clans is a decent cinematic linear story experience that restricts you based on the faction you're in. Both are great in their own right.	• A good understanding of loadouts, heat management, weapon groups and mech roles is helpful to navigate tougher missions and maximize efficiency.	• If playing with a HOTAS, expect a lot of tweaking to get the configuration just right. Will need to do some text file editing.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to do this, but this game is very confused about what it wants to be and on the whole I feel like it provides more frustration than fun. The game tries to move more towards MechAssault-style linear campaign and more arcadey gameplay and controls, but doesn't go all the way towards ridiculous over the top action. It also tries to splice in Armored Core 6-style boss fights, all of which are tedious and extremely not fun to play, even on the lowest difficulty. This is coupled with things that you actually need for this type of game, like checkpoints or the ability to save mid-mission, being absent. Get wrecked by the boss? Guess what? You get to play the whole mission over again, even the bad dialogue parts!Speaking of dialogue, woof. The story is so by-the-numbers you know what's going to happen long before it does, and the characters are so bland and cookie cutter I literally could not tell most of my squad apart until the end of the game. The main villain is so poorly written and voiced that It's not even fun to watch him try to chew scenery. Also, just a note to developers: I know you think it's super edgy and great political commentary to make the player commit war crimes and not have a choice in it, but it isn't. It just sucks. It sucks to play, it sucks that I have to do it or the game won't advance, it sucks that anyone still thinks this is a good thing to put into video games in 2024, where we have to deal with this in real life every day on the news. Honestly, the entire concept and story feels like it was done by executive committee. I would not be surprised if the DLC is a Battle Royale Roguelite Cozy Auto Battler. The game does look great, however.

_childDocuments_.review: The female characters in this game are all Triple-A Ugly. Looks like the original model was fine, but then the HR commissar came through and added all the man-jaws and side-shaved haircuts. You can tell they did this after the fact too, because there is a noticeable gap between their lips and teeth. Other than that, you can see how much focus they put on the production value because it is all top notch. The HR ladies just hate other women for some reason and it really shows. This might be the first game where I actually download a beautification mod as long as it isn't over the top in the other direction.I do like the changes to the mech lab, especially the armor by the ton. I know it's different than how it's always been, but on its own I think it's a cool way of doing it. I also like the way they handle repairs and salvage. It wouldn’t make sense having to wait to find the mechs and weapons you want when you are the clan invaders and they couldn’t just get rid of salvage all together, so the honor and research mechanics seem like a great way to handle it without forcing you to endure artificial scarcity throughout the campaign.Unfortunately they also included the omnipod system with fixed equipment everywhere. It just doesn’t jive since now you can’t adjust armor on those sections that don’t have empty space. It will eventually be fixed with mods I’m sure, but I wish they had just started from the ground up with a new system and pushed the lore to the side so we didn’t end up with parts you can’t really adjust because the options are all the same, like 3 torso omnipods all having 2 energy hardpoints. That along with the fixed equipment everywhere really kills some of my favorite mechs, like the Summoner.The training missions were excellent, as was the inclusion of the Summoner for this portion. While I couldn't find any use for it during the campaign I thought it was an excellent way to get a new player used to the types of weapons you can use and all the abilities a mech can have. While it can't hold it's own in any other scenario, it is still my favorite clan mech and I'm glad players get a chance to see it shine here.Speaking of the Summoner, there are some mechs you just have to skip during the campaign since you can't work with them due to all the fixed equipment. And you can't afford to put trash tier mechs into a game when you've only got 16 mechs to choose from. I like the mechs they chose for lore and variety, but some of them just don’t get a chance to shine in this game. They are a great selection of mechs though. Each one is unique and if not crippled by the fixed equipment it would make sense why they were included. It’s also not fair to say there are fewer mechs than any other MW game, since those games didn’t have a different set of mechs for the player and the enemy. When you take that into account, this game actually has a lot more mechs than those other games.It also kinda makes sense why they didn’t include some of my favorites since they might fill the same role as the ones they have now. The Marauder IIC being similar to the Timberwolf or the Warhammer IIC being similar to the Hellbringer with the PPCs/SRMs/MGs. The mechs they have really feel distinct from anything you see on the inner sphere side of things. Still, I’m looking forward to the expansion that gives me all the IIC mechs.The story is pretty good. What you get out of it will depend on what you know of the lore, but basically a lot of what you hear should be taken through the lens of it being Crusader vs Warden propaganda and people not seeing things from the opposition’s perspective without trying to beat you over the head with it.  I really like that we finally got to see the invasion from the Smoke Jaguar perspective for the first time as well. I like the factions that don’t have the plot armor of Clan Wolf or Jade Falcon. Here’s hoping they ditch the modern day routine of small dlc content and go back to the good old days of full expansions like Ghost Bear’s Legacy. I’m definitely a fan of the more narrative driven separate campaigns over the sandbox approach with minor additions here and there. Gameplay-wise, it’s a bit more arcade-y than your typical mech sim approach, but that also makes it more fun and approachable. The on the rails nature of limiting your AO doesn’t really feel that constrictive since the spaces are still wide open and keeps the action on point without feeling limited. There are some boss fights as well which are a fun addition I’m not used to seeing in a MW game. It’s almost like they took some notes from Armored Core without going full Armored Souls which I definitely appreciate. I’m not sure how I feel about losing control of my weapons when scanning, but I like that it encourages you to keep in mind your surroundings. It’s PGI, so 2 steps forward, one step back, but overall I do like it. While it does have a few modern day-isms, like literal space Nazis decrying fascism from the other side (which are actually imperialists) or the fugly haircuts and manjaws, I don’t get the sense that PGI hates its customers the way so many other triple A companies seem to these days, so I can forgive a few minor missteps or annoyances. Overall, this is a good game and it’s a good Mechwarrior game, so you should definitely give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely needs some optimization work. Playing on Linux, Proton Experimental at the time of writing - plays well with some hitching/artifacting in particularly busy gameplay moments but MW5 was the same way when it came out. Audio seems a bit off, with some audio going faster than the in-game scroll, but I'm fairly certain that's a 'gaming on linux' issue as I haven't seen it reported except on proton.db.Gameplay-wise - big stompy robots deliver, if you've played MW5 or MW Online, it's much the same with a higher TTK and more generous heat management for newer players. Some systems (like repairs and research) aren't explained very well, but are fairly accessible once you go through all the menus a few times. In my opinion, it's an easier game to start off the MW franchise with as you're not scraping together a lance of locusts to try and complete a contract - you're given powerful war machines quickly, and you quickly unlock even better chassis after only a few missions. I also have had (so far) no issues with the in-game currency and running out, even when I completely retrofit a mech's loadout, unlike the early game in MW5: Mercenaries.Story-wise, the game is excellent. Fans of the IP will note that PG has spent tons of time to get even the little things right, even down to using the correct rank insignia on the Smoke Jaguar's collars and having accurate uniforms. Cutscenes are amazing and bring the game to life, though you'll have to suspend your disbelief at having a Star Commander report directly to a Smoke Jaguar Khan. The story for the game puts the player in pivotal moments during the Smoke Jaguar invasion, including playing through the destruction of Edo.Some minor gripes - obviously, optimization is a constant problem with PG at the release of their games. Some of the voice acting is a little bit stilted at times, but mostly it's very good - especially when compared with the rest of the big stompy robot genre. Character models (especially Mia, for some reason) go into the uncanny valley territory and just seem a touch weird. The Mech Bay could use a little more explanation for players new to the MW franchise, especially how to use Mech XP and the Mech Specializations.But, frankly, this is the best Mechwarrior game to come out since probably Mechwarrior 2's base game. If you like the genre or have ever been interested in the Clan Invasion era, this game will not disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game is fantastic, and runs perfectly playable at medium settings at minimum system specification. Gameplay, HUD, everything so far is a major improvement over MW5, all while remaining exceptionally faithful to the Setting and Lore.Quick initial reaction after finishing the first 2 intro tutorial levels and watching the related cutscenes. (Which took exactly 60 minutes for me on normal difficulty, which I consider myself fairly proficient at the series after thousands of hours in various Mechwarrior Games.)Also upfront disclosure, I am running at EXACTLY the minimum Hardware specifications (with the exception of having 32gb of RAM)So far, on medium settings, runs just fine. Stable 40fps, which I know, ISNT AMAZING, but again, minimum specifications on medium. It is pretty enough, and perfectly playable. Also no glitches that I can see, no dramatic preformace drops (with one exception for the first 10 seconds or so of the first mission there was some minor asset pop-in, but nothing critical.)I'd advise people to ignore the MANY salty Under-1-hour reviews. Like every PGI game, there is a cadre of salty "fans" that will downvote anything because of some make believe 12 year old slight. And Like every Clan-focused Mechwarrior/Battletech game, there are a cadre of angry grognards that will downvote it into oblivion simply because they'd rather see the series die then have to play as "the other side."EDIT: Also a quick thing I keep seeing in reviews about the dialogue writing. It seems that MANY people have zero clue about the Mechwarrior/Battletech universe lore. The way that Clanners speak can come off as very robotic compared to everyday english (especially the absence of contractions like "can't, won't, isn't" etc.) THIS IS A GOOD THING, it means the writers actually paid attention to the setting and lore, and even address the "issue" twice within the tutorial.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks good, runs well, easy enough to play on Mouse and Keys for what is historically a joystick preferred franchise. Acting and story is also decent enough. I'm playing in the hardest mode and it doesn't too often feel totally unfair, but I often have to go back to the drawing board on my mech loudouts and to overcome challenges which I LOVE as a hardcore souls fan. Occasionally some enemies though, I dont know what to call it but the like the heavy flying VTOL feel waaaaaaay too bullet spongy. There was this airfield mission on the second planet where you have the fight THREE of these things at once and with 3 of them flying around there's no single safe spot to take cover and I really just had to get the end of the mission with most of my star pretty undamaged and it kinda just felt like total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to fight these 3 flying bullet sponges at the end of what was already a pretty hard mission.If you're playing in anything above story mode you are going to need to use the tactical map to create ambushes, set up pincers and high ground advantages, and order your least damaged squad mate to take point. Some might not like this but hey story mode exists. As someone who really enjoys tactical RPGs I love the bridge between the tactical overhead and real time combat. But devs- for the love god if you read this-- I just had to reset the moon mission on the second planet due to objective required enemies spawning under floors and behind walls. TWICE IN A ROW. This type of game breaking glitch is, in my opinion, unacceptable. But as someone who spent many  hours with my dad in the 90s playing Mechwarrior 2 and 3 on the family computer, I love the game so far and it delivers hard on the nostalgia factor. It felt ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nuts launching the first mission for the first time and hearing the classic "reactors-- online. sensors-- online, all systems-- nominal" as I stomped out of the hanger into the beautiful unreal rendered land. The sound design can't be understated either, some of the battles feel straight out of the legendary Mechwarrior 3 opening cinematic. Easily recommend for old school mechwarrior fans-- but devs fix the GD broken spawns! The game came out only a week or two ago from this review so hopefully we see a little bit of polish going forward.Edit--other thoughtsI know its a completely different kind of Mech game but I really liked the way Armored Core 6 did their Mech lab better. You'll run into tonnage restrictions constantly here, often needing to give up super hefty amounts of firepower to bring things like more missiles or additional heat sinks. Meanwhile in AC6- "you wanna run two gigajacked shotguns, have a shoulder mounted sniper, and have legs that make you leap around like a demon? Do it brother!" I also think you should be able to easily tweak your loadouts after a mission attempt, but you have to straight up LOAD A SAVE that's between missions, which feels kinda weird. In armored core customization felt like it was both expected AND encouraged, but it feels somewhat less so here, even though you are clearly going to need to.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a longtime fan of the franchise, this is just about everything you could want from a Mechwarrior 2 successor: well crafted missions, compelling game play, and just the right amount of Clanner cheesiness. It certainly isn't a perfect game - it doesn't do a great job of tutorializing some things, and a week or so after release, there are some frustrating bugs that you many encounter - but it's still a blast to play, and I can only imagine it'll get better in the coming months.If you're new to MechWarrior, you might consider skimming the Wikipedia entry on the setting, and checking Reddit for beginner tips, but even lacking any context on the series, I still think you'll find this an enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: MW5: Clans - A Good Start, But Some Things Just Feel OffI’ve played a good chunk of hours in MW5: Mercs, using a lot of mods like an expanded MechLab, so keep that in mind.German TranslationThe German translation is a bit off in some places, but I can live with that. Some words just don't feel right.Lack of Modding Options and Missing DataThere aren't enough options to customize your mech, and a lot of key numbers are missing. For example, it doesn’t show how much heat I generate from an alpha strike or how much I cool down. I’d really like it if they provided a MechLab-like addon to address this.The damage mechanics feel wrong. There were moments where it took several alpha strikes to destroy a Warhammer (WRM) from behind, even though its rear armor is paper-thin. Similarly, when a full star circles a 40-ton mech and it takes around 15 seconds to bring it down, or if you fire 12 ERMLs (Extended Range Medium Lasers) at a head from 30 meters away, visibly hitting it but not destroying the head—it just doesn't feel right.Small things like an Archer firing its LRMs at my Nova in melee range is another issue that shouldn't happen. The tabletop allows you to fire in melee range with a +5 modifier, but given the size of the Archer and the Nova, and the placement of the LRM launchers, it shouldn't be able to hit.There are a lot of similar issues that make things feel off.On the plus side, it provides a solid foundation for future content. And buying any MW game is a no brainer for me, so i am a little bit biased.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid entry into the MW-franchise, that harkens back to the old school style of the previous games with linear storydriven mission design. The gameplay has been improved from MW5: Mercs and the AI actually feels somewhat competent. The story is well-told, for the most part, and I really came to enjoy most of the characters (Peréz did nothing wrong) and especially the main character Jayden. I found him very authentic and likable, no matter what choices you make. However, I am torn on this game because it can really wow me one second and then leave me disappointed the next. The game can, at times, achieve almost AAA-quality, especially in certain cutscenes and during certain set-pieces, for a low-budget AA-game. However, it can also feel painfully amaturish with poorly mixed and compressed sound (especially during cutscenes!), lacking music and sounds, cutscenes and transitions that end awkwardly, spotty voice-acting at some points, certain poor quality textures and sfx, lacking polished UI, and bugs and glitches (spinning flying tank being my favorite), and etc etc etc. Performance is also lacking. I'm rocking one of the best PC-setups money can buy and firing four UAC/2 at cockpit height made my frames per second tank into the twenties due to the overlapping smoke sfx. However, these I feel like are things that could and should be patched to be fixed, and they have already released two hotfixes that solved some of the more pressing issues. Prianha Games has a solid record of keeping their games updated with patches and DLCs, so I am hopeful it will this case. To summarize: solid core gameplay and a story and characters that is for the most part well-told and well-written, with interesting and somewhat varied mission design that will keep you engaged. However, plagued with poor production quality and performance issues.

PPCs feel very shooty.Things I dislike:Challenge based on tonnage - later in the game you have to slog through loads of heavy and assault mechs and its usually a requirement to exterminate all of them. _childDocuments_.review: Clans takes all of the good from MW5 Mercs and builds on it by switching the formula from a sandbox procedurally generated self guided tour through the inner sphere to a bespoke, curated story with unique and tailored missions.The good: mech combat looks and feels great. The mechlab, while less customizable than MechWarrior Online, provides a robust set of options for pilots to use to configure their mechs.  Missions are well crafted, and the scan function of the mech HUD is well utilized to scavenge for scraps to upgrade your weapon systems.  MW5C is a great representation of the Clan Invasion era of Battletech, and it is obvious that the lore and existing canon is loved and respected by the devs.The bad: Performance is CPU bound - if you have a 10 year old processor like I do, you will be stuck on low settings.  My I5 4690K does manage to run it though, even though it's a 2014 CPU and well below min spec.The excellent: Co-op play is seamless and very fun.  I've spent about half my time in game running around blasting the enemy away with friends, and look forward to many hours of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Joystick support is poor.  I was unable to get Virpil flight sticks and rudder to be recognized (the FAQ states the rudder is supported).  The axis names are enumerated, 1, 2, 3, 4. Axis names should be X,Y,Z.  The arbitrary naming makes it difficult to distinguish which axis is being assigned.  If we want to be software engineers and do something lame, let's enumerate them from "0". "Using letters like normal folk, or the way we were taught in math, never" (please excuse my sarcasm).  Most games, you would select the axis you want to control, then move the stick on the axis you're assigning -- too easy.  I wasn't expecting a hard core sim (God forbid someone were to make a hard core mech sim), but assigning joystick input from devices that are recognized in Windows should be a no-brainier.   I'll wait until this is on sale, and try again with a keyboard and mouse.  In my opinion, without fleshed out joystick support this title isn't worth a full pop $50.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:* They did not skimp on length. This is by FAR the longest MechWarrior campaign in the history of the franchise. For me, playing at a brisk pace, it took 19.2 hours.* The boss fights are a cool touch. They aren't perfect, but I think it's a good idea that should definitely be pursued further in future titles.* Difficulty wise, I found the tuning on Expert to be more-or-less challenging and incredibly consistently tuned. I'd almost always be very beat up and maybe lose a 'Mech, but survive and win the mission. There were no huge swings in difficulty, for the most part.* I actually like the MechLab, for what it's worth. If I wanted endless customization I could go play Mercenaries with mods like YAML. The more limited choices makes each one a bit more meaningful.* Actual story and cinematics, in my MechWarrior game? They really commited to it. It's not perfect, but we've never gotten this much of it in any previous game.The bad:* PC performance is unacceptable. It should not have shipped with so performance issues this large. I have an RTX 3080 and I have to use MEDIUM settings with DLSS enabled and I still dropped below 30 FPS at times. That's just insane. The game looks good but not THAT good.* Audio is quite bad in places. Low quality or compressed files, pops and clicks in some effects ('scan mode enabled'), poor volume mixing, few music tracks, dialog lines that really should have been retaken, etc.* I'm a bit disappointment that none of the missions really require any tactical thinking. You pretty much just keep shooting until everything is dead. You rarely have to make choices, or learn the layout and where enemies will come from/when events will trigger and plan accordingly. It feels like there was more of that in MW3 and 4, but it could be rose-tinted glasses. In general, the gameplay does just start to wear out its welcome at the end.* Tying into this - I think just having every single mech automatically equipped with weightless/slotless JJs would have opened up a LOT of gameplay options. They could have made maps much more vertical and added navigating terrain into being a part of the missions. Is that lore accurate? No, but who cares. Gameplay first.* I do wish there had been more practical use for lighter mechs as you go on. The reality is that later in the game you are just endlessly shooting heavies and assaults, and you can't afford to be in 'Mechs with less armor. Ties into previous point.* I think they wrote themselves into a bit of a corner with Nitpicks:* It does look a bit stupid from a casual angle to open up the omnipod options and see a bunch of duplicate, identical examples. I guess it's there for mod support later, but it looks unfinished.* The briefing map is kind of hard to read. It's low contrast and due to the floating cubes style, it's harder to make out terrain features and boundaries. I get 'rule of cool', but I think they could have made it more clear while still looking good.The conclusion:It's a good MechWarrior game, for all its faults. It's likely the best in the franchise. It's very ambitious. Even though it's clear that PGI doesn't have the experience, manpower or budget of a AAA studio, they clearly poured a ton of time and effort into this project. In some ways it feels like a hail mary. I hope the negative reviews due to performance problems and the mechlab don't kill the series here - and that we still get a MW6. If PGI is willing to get creative and look critically at this game, I think the next one could be a knock-out punch.

_childDocuments_.review: Runs fine with a 4090 (which isn't saying much), frame gen and DLAA, and looks gorgeous.  Everything feels great, but they've taken an arcadey approach, where now it feels more like a shooter than a Mechwarrior gameIt plays like a casual power fantasy version of previous games.  You're not scrounging up rare or expensive weapons, or cobbling together mechs that you salvaged, you're rich and can just buy everything straight up, and of course, the weapons are already the best you can get, being clan weaponsSalvaging is simplified down to getting some number of research points at the end of a mission, and you use those points to research +5% damage to a specific weapon, which not only removes the fun of trying to leg mechs or headshot them to get their parts or weapons, you also end up locked in to gearing your entire team with the same build, using the one or two weapon types you've upgradedThere are only 16 playable mechs, and unlocks for them are gated behind progression of the linear story.  You often only get the next slightly heavier mech after you've already filled your squad with 5 copies of the last one, trying to meet the ever-increasing drop weights, and have very little choice about which mechs to use, because if you're under tonnage you'll just get wrecked.  By the time you finish spending mech XP on upgrades for that mech, you usually can't use it anymore, so that whole system ends up feeling pointlessThe friendly AIs are a bit better than in Mercs, and can aim decently well, but 4 allies is enough to get in your way all the time, and they still will stand in one spot and die instantly if you send them anywhere, or will charge an enemy you told them to target despite having perfectly good long ranged weaponsThe combat is enjoyable and the story seems interesting and well made, but it has to be, because that's basically all that's left.  But that was never what made Mechwarrior games fun, it was the engineering and customization, choosing your missions carefully to manage risks and maximize profit, buying or salvaging better mechs, and gearing them out with increasingly better builds.  Basically all of that's gone, and it's reduced down to a linear campaign with pre-set rewards, where if you never touch the mechbay, you'll still be perfectly fineI don't hate it, but I certainly wouldn't recommend it to anyone that's a fan of Mechwarrior games.  It seems like it'd be good for newcomers and casual players, but if you've played any previous games, you'll probably be disappointed with how much is missing

_childDocuments_.review: After a few hours of playing I can definitely say that I recommend the game. If you like MechWarrior it's a good installment into the franchise. I do have some caveats that I would like to mention though. As well as some good things that I want to note.The good:- The graphics, in general they are very well done. The environments feel good I wouldn't say great but good enough. - Piloting a mech generally feels good. Though still a bit faster pace than I prefer. I much prefer the slower combat of the older games which were built around a joystick as the primary input device rather than the mouse and keyboard. - The clan mech fit pretty well for their chosen clan. - The lore, while not perfect (as no mechwarrior game has been) it actually does pretty good overall in keeping with some of the established battletech lore. With a couple caveats noted bellow.- The clan word... oddities (not sure what to call that)- clan weapons feel like clan weapons fighting the innersphere... somewhat broken and OP at times (this can be a good and bad thing) it means that fights tend to be very quick and don't have a lot of risk to them at least early on.The caveats / neutral / mentions: First I wouldn't call these bad just things that I wanted to note.- The First world you land on "Santander V" is a periphery backwater planet and yet somehow has access to the Raven... yeah gonna say doubt given the raven was manufactured (originally) by the capellans and while was being manufactured by the time of the clan invasion there wouldn't have been a lot of them. Especially not owned in a backwater pirate planet.- I think this is a typo on their part but they say that the Hatchetman was one of the first truly original mechs manufactured by the innersphere in centuries. While that isn't entirely wrong it isn't the most recent or most advanced by far, that would likely go to the Raven, which I mentioned this group some how has dozens of. This might just be a flavor thing on their part and its not technically wrong its just odd that they would mention the hatchetman but not the raven.- They are generally pretty good with keeping to clan customs with words (with a few exceptions), they mention other clan customs but you don't really see them at least early on (i'm only a few hours in so they could later)The "bad":- The enemy mechs. This i think is probably a performance compamize but it takes away from the experiance for me a bit. When mechs are more than like 50m from you they start looking like they are 2d sprites and just do a basic animation. It feels really jank, the farther they are from you the more jank the animation gets. - The story telling IMO is ok. Its not nearly as good as MW4V in my opinion, but its a mechwarrior game the stories are all a little weird. Somehow this just doesn't feel as clean to me. Maybe its just nastalga but I cant quite put my finger on it. Maybe it's just cause its the clans and i'm an innersphere guy. *shrug* Its good enough It just feels like its lacking that spark for me.Overall the game is a good pick if you like MechWarrior. I personally enjoy the game. I do have to say that I still like the older style of the MechWarrior 4 game(s) better. They feel better written and feel like they have a bit more oomph to them overall but for a modern MechWarrior game it's pretty good. I would recommend picking it up and if you worried just wait until it goes on sale. Would recommend, just don't go in expecting a 10/10, maybe an 7 or 8/10, good enough but not perfect. We will see how things go as I keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: In comparison to MW5Mercs, as I feel that is the best way to judge this game... So far after a few missions this is really great. Its leaps and bounds over previous mechwarrior games in terms of story and worldbuilding. The cutscenes are outstanding for a studio of PGI's size,Facial animation and voice acting in the rendered cutscenes is mostly excellent by any games standards, however this quality serves to really emphasise the times when it is a little rough outside of the cutscenes (and we as gamers have come to expect too much) - overall it is quite astonishing what PGI have achieved here.In-mission, graphically and mechanically it feels different to MW5 Mercs and in many ways a step-up. The game as a whole feels more chaotic and 'harder'. I love that it is harder, one of my main complaints about MW5 Mercs is how easy it was.Customisation of mechs at first glance seems limited, however after a while of getting to grips with it I understand the impact our choices have here. It is not as open as MW5 Mercs was, for obvious lore reasons, however I think our choices have MORE impact in this game due to the difficulty spike and other concerns. The omnimechs and the way we earn mechs and mech upgrades in this game in comparison to MW5 mercs is very different. It is an entirely different approach to a game. But considering that we are playing clan mechawarriors it is an understandable and enjoyable approach.AI - now this is a very complex subject. In comparison to MW5 Mercs the AI (both friendly and enemy) in this game has been made more deadly and accurate and less RNG. As far as balance is concerned this makes this game 'faster'. In MW5 Mercs the AI was deliberately more 'RNG', this lead people to call the AI 'bad'. Their lancemates didnt land shots when the player expected them to for example. For me what I am noticing is that the tactics I used in MW5 are no longer working as well, constantly moving my lance is not leading to low repair bills, and I expect that I will need to really up my game as far as positioning and tactics are concerned.This is clearly a great game, thank you PGI.

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed 1 playthrough of this game. I can't really recommend this game for the following reasons:1. Unlike the last game where you can choose which direction you want to engage the objective from, you have a fixed area to work with.2. Just about very mission feels the same. Follow nav points, shoot mechs.3. Boss fights. Each campaign has a boss fight, which is not Mechwarrior.4. Mech customization is somehow worse than Mechwarrior 5 Mercenaries. Sure you get "omnimechs" but they are battlemechs until you earn XP by having your star leader use them, then you can unlock fixed hardpoint omnipods for each of your mech's segments. Don't want MASC or jumpjets? Too bad, they are fixed.5. I have played 969Hrs of Mechwarrior 5 Mercenaries since it first came out, and playing this game I feel like it was just a crawl of the same thing over and over again. I pushed myself to complete it and I most likely wont come back.6. The AI is still stupid, just like in Mechwarrior 5 Mercenaries. I constantly find my star walking in front of me just as I fire a volley of ERLLs. Sometimes they just sit there trying to comprehend the bottleneck (because you're almost always in a canyon) and simply wont engage a target.If you wish to play this anyways, here is my advice:1. Ignore the humanoid Mechs. they are too tall and will eat all the fire.2. Lasers lasers lasers. research extended range laser enhancements and mount only lasers. Ammo can run out. Your lancemates will eat up all their ammo in the first few engagements.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably past the halfway point of the campaign.  Wanted to give my 2 cents.  I am a big Battletech fan and only really played Mechwarrior 5 Mercs so I can't really judge it agains the earlier Mechwarrior games that also featured clans.  There will be no story spoilers.  Game is a solid 8/10.  Gameplay:  If you enjoyed the gameplay of MW5, this is more of the same general thing.  While the bones and core of the game are the same, the supporting aspects are different.  1) Fellow mechwarrior pilots, of whcih you have 4 for a total of 5 of you on a mission, gain xp and you can determine where in their given specialties you can increase.  No choice how you want them to specialize in the end.  2) Mechlab has presets (named Omnipod configuration) that you choose from and it determines what hard points you have and what size.  This is similar to just having different mechs in MW5 but you can mix and match.  Such as having a Prime configuration left arm, and a B configuration right arm, and you can adjust their equipment.  3) Missions are all hand crafted and not procedural generated.  You can go back and run them again in a simpod, but they are all very different.  You don't choose planets and travel there.  You are at one planet each arch and sometimes you can choose between a few missions but you end up doing them all so it doesn't make too much difference.  But, this means there is an end to the game.  Story:  I can't comment much, but I'm enjoying it so far.  It's no TLOU or God of War but it's enjoyable.  The voice acting is MILES better than its predecessor.  Can't say much else but this is purley subjective.  Graphics:  This is unreal engine 5, iirc.  So it looks noticeably better than MW5 Mercs.  I think even the audio is better for every weapon I have used.  It does take a better computer to run it, but I have a pretty high end computer.  I very rarely see a stutter but its rare and over pretty quick.  Bugs: I have noticed some bugs here and there.  Nothing major.  For Example, if you're getting the overheating warning sounds in the simulator and before it stops you exit simulator, the sound keeps happening until you go back into the sim, overheat your mech, and let it cool off enough that the sound shuts off.  In one mission I saw a couple mechs just standing there doing nothing.  None of this is gamebreaking but its just tiny things like that.  I will say there are a few downsides.1) I wish there were more mechs.  Generally one mech for each weight.  LIke one 25 ton mech option, one 30 ton mech option, etc.  Be nice to see some 2nd line Battlemechs.  I know we can't have mechs that, in universe, the clan probably wouldnt have like a Kodiak, but just seeing some 2nd line mechs in fights that maybe i can't use would be cool.  2) Increase in graphics = increase in system performance requirements.  I personally have seen some very very minor stuttering (i have a 3090, a 10700k and mostly ok air cooling). Yet, I have it setup so i am (not max settings) capping my framerate at 120.  I dont know if this is just that 'optimization' people keep bring up in gaming but it seems that way to me.  And I'll list a few minor gripes that didnt really effect my rating but were still negatives.  -No hotkey for switching between chain fire and non chain fire modes in a given weapon group.  This existed in previous MW including MW5:Merc-I dont super enjoy the scanning system it borders on intrusive.  It's just not for me but I wouldn't change it at this point.  Maybe make it so anything that is scannable shows up on your HUD even if you haven't actively switched from scanning to non scanning.  Make scanning only necessary when you have to actually scan a specific thing.-You talk about Elementals but I haven't SEEN them in the game.  UNFORTUNATE because they are cool as ♥♥♥♥ and nightmare fuel for the enemy.  -I can't shoot the birds that fly around.  Want a hidden achievement for shooting a bird with an ER Small titled "Tex Approved".  If you know, you know.  Overall a very very fun game. I recommend anyone that enjoyed MW5 or this kind of Stompy Robot game to get it, but I don't know if I'd put as much hours into it as I have MW5 Mercs since there's no career mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm, what to say, what to say...So, first with the good. Level structure is pretty nice, overall. Same old-school, clunky mech combat that we've seen in previous installments. Customization for each mech is still freaking amazing and in-depth, but not as... how do I say...? Ridiculously convoluted as it could be in MWO or even 5: Mercs. Storytelling was surprisingly good and cinematic (though the physics and facial movements of the characters could be weird at times), and the character development with your star (squad) had me going from hating the entire cast to invested in what was happening around 'em. Of course, it's always a good day when you get to play the Timberwolf and other Clan mechs, too. Now for the meh to negative aspects of the game. Optimization isn't great. Like, at all. Graphical issues from rendering to artifacts do pop up. Lag is a nightmare, though I didn't have it nearly as bad as another friend of mine (even though I've probably got an older processor). Though the story was more narrative focused, which is totally fine, we did lose out on some sandbox elements I enjoyed from Mercs, namely the sheer number of worlds and missions you could take on. That being said, given the context of the game, it does make sense, so it's more of a personal quip than anything else. This also makes me wanna tackle Mercenaries again. Probably the biggest issue I've got with it is the sheer lack of mechs you can pilot, and how you go about unlocking them. Unfortunately, just because you down a mech, doesn't mean you can steal the freaking thing for yourself (which is, from what I understand, what the Clan does, too; taking whatever resources they can). Nope, there are a handful of mechs you start with and a handful of mechs locked behind a leveling system. Again, it makes sense, considering you're a military outfit and not a dude running your own mercenary company, but c'mon... Who doesn't want more mechs to choose from/♥♥♥♥ around with. All that being said, Clans is definitely an enjoyable experience, and comes with a massive improvement in telling the story of a small piece of 40+ years of lore. So, if you're a MechWarrior and Battletech fan, or just a guy who loves mech combat and customization, I'd recommend it. Really curious about whatever the devs' DLC plans are... Or plans for another 5th-generation standalone installment. Rather than "either, or," I'd take both, hands-down.

Fortunately these are just short sections and the game is playable most of the way through. (machine specs: i9 11th gen, 32GB ram, RTX 3060 6GB).Can't wait for the DLCs for this one.

_childDocuments_.review: MW5 Clans is just so much nicer to control and with a smoother challenge ramp than MW5 Mercs (or any earlier Battletech game, really). After quickly 100%ing this game I went back to finish off MW5 Mercs achievements... night and day. Mercs is a punishing grind of mystery challenge levels and waves of nonsense while fighting the UX. Even lance mates pathing into your fire line is worse in Mercs (outside that one duel, you know the one).  After uninstalling MW5:Mercs in frustration (again) I played through a 3rd expert campaign in just 16 hours, it is a good storyline and even the telegraphed pieces serve their purposes.Plays like a great compliment to the Jade Falcon and Wolf storylines from MW2. The endgame is lacking (it sweeps through the last act quickly and then you... replay earlier missions?), and it is a much smaller game overall, but tight and joyous to play. 32 hours on Expert for the first playthrough, but I can't get more than a few missions into MW5 Mercs without rage-quitting. The initial training montage was better in MW2, but not bad here.  A pure newbie might benefit from more mechanics exposition (e.g. why are omni-mechs not fully customizable, instilling the code was better done in MW2).  A few surprise resource constraints (decisions that matter before the player has the information to make those decisions are bad, e.g. salvage for research) and just needs more to do, because I'd much rather do it here than in any of the prior editions.  Just dump us on outreach at the end with random missions and this would rack up the hours - I can't believe I put 150 hours into MW5 Mercs., the quality of life in MW5:Clans is just so much higher.:kurita:

Either way, if you don't like the Battletech universe, or don't care about it, it's probably not your cup of tea. It has succeeded at being what it strives to be - a love letter to Battletech fans.

_childDocuments_.review: ***I want to be very clear. From what I have played of this game I like it a lot. The problem is that it is not quite in a state that I can recommend it yet because it needs some patches. I experience frequent crashes to desktop and with no way to save the game mid mission this makes the game almost unplayable at times. My keyboard bindings also seem to get reset to default constantly for no reason. Considering I use a Razer Tartarus and need to customize my keys for this to work... that's a big issue for me and incredibly frustrating. Once these issues have been patched out, I will update my review.***The actual review so far - I like the game so far, the level design is a dramatic improvement over MW5: Mercenaries. I haven't pinpointed the reason yet, but it also just FEELS better to play moment to moment. I like the level of specialisation and customisation that you can get on each team member and mech. There is a lot more focus on story and character development. It's a focus on my favourite era of the lore and as a refreshing change you are playing this part of the history from the invading clans who are supposed to be the "bad guys" (If you are a Battletech lore nerd, I know what I just said and I know how inaccurate it is, don't come at me. I am writing this for those who don't how deep this rabbit hole goes). The voice acting for the most part is good, not incredible, but good enough. The lip syncing could use some work, everyone looks like they are talking through their teeth a bit but again, this doesn't really ruin anything for me and I quickly stopped noticing it when I got used to it.It's not all great, the parts store is in serious need of some organisation. There is no way to filter or sort the things on sale, just a MASSIVE list of things that you need to scroll through. It's kind of insane to think that they thought this was okay to launch this as it is. There is no way their testers didn't notice this and get annoyed by this as well. Exact same issue when scrolling through your list of mech parts.Due to my aforementioned crashing issues, I am FAR from done this game so take my review with a grain of salt. Things may change in all respects and this is the launch version. I expect many of my issues to be fixed and I am going to put this game aside for a bit, wait for it to get patched a couple times and come back. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: My review is being switched to negative due to the recent DLC announcement, putting multiplayer behind a $20 USD paywall so soon after launch is a big black eye to the reputation and future of this game. Okay, where to start... I got into the Battletech universe through games like Mechcommander and Mechwarrior 4 (Vengeance first then I played Mercenaries) so this is far from my first battlemech rodeo. I'm going to recommend this iteration with a couple of caveats I hope are fixed down the road. First caveat, the customisation in this game is just terrible. The mechlab is a major step back from Mechwarrior 5: Mercenaries and the omnipod system doesn't really do much to offset that. We don't get the level of granularity when customising our mechs and sadly some of the really cool hardware is locked behind very rare slots. ECM is the biggest one here, very few mechs have the ability to carry it with the special slot. Second caveat, the omnipod options are kinda meaningless. Each chassis has one layout that is just objectively better than the rest, usually the one that has the most beam slots because the ER lasers are easily the most powerful weapons. I personally really like running stacks of ballistic weapons like the UAC and LBX, but they just aren't that good. The LR medium laser is by far the best weapon in the game, so the more of them you can stack on the better. Third caveat, the difficulty curve is super messed up. One mission you'll be barely hanging on for survival as you fight wave after wave of heavy/assault mechs, the next it's a walk in the park as you and your allies melt through piecemeal waves of medium/light mechs. I wish the game maintained a more consistent difficulty curve. Final caveat, the research system is just as biased as the omnipod system. You basically just want to throw your resources into heat management, LR laser upgrades and armour upgrades. Focus on those three and you will be basically unstoppable by the end of the game. I recommend this game to both new and returning enjoyers of the Battletech universe, it's really fun and the story is enjoyable (though it will never beat MW4: Vengeance which is hands down the best story in a BT universe videogame) The combat feels smooth, the maps are mostly stunning to walk through and the introduction of the top-down command system made me feel like I was back playing Mechcommander as a child which gave me the warm and fuzzies. I think this game, much like MW5: Mercenaries, will only improve with time and updates. I look forward to all systems being nominal!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Battletech since the early 90's and my first introduction to the Mechwarrior franchise was the first game. I've played all the video games released in the setting and I've loved them all. I think it's possible that this is my favorite installment of Mechwarrior though. I'm a huge lore nerd. I always had trouble finding people to play, so I read the novels as much as I could. I still read the "Blood of Kerensky" trilogy every 2 years or so. I've a few nitpicks with how the lore is handled in the game, but I can honestly put them down to design choices to keep the game fun. There's been quite a few times where something depicted in the books is presented in a way that is different from how I imagined it, but I really like how they did it, and these images will be my new head cannon from now on. The gameplay is crisp and fun. In the lore, we should just be steamrolling enemies at the start of the campaign, but I get they had to balance the game.All that said, I really don't like the mechlab. It's not fun, it's not intuitive, and I feel it kills the whole point of OmniMechs. I've hardly used it and I'm just having fun playing with the Prime models of all the mechs.I do highly recommend the game. It's fun, It's got a great story, it's got great visuals, and it's almost the perfect story driven Mechwarrior game. If you're into the setting, get it. If you want to have a sandbox like MW5, then maybe pass on it until it's on sale, then get it.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10 Worth your time.2 x 14.5hrs play sessions -SOLO77% Achievements Completed on first playthrough.13700K - CPURTX3080 - High settings/DLSS - Balanced  @ 1440p on G-Sync MonitorFps Range (20-110) Story - Not the best, but massively better then MW5 Mercs imo.Graphics - Massively better then MW5 Mercs ( Stock no mods etc ) Lasers, cannons, missiles etc are a visual treat compared to MW5 Mercs (stock), explosions etc. While some areas look very bland, majority of the game looks great.Gameplay - Excellent, all mechs feel responsive to their class and your personal builds and how you pilot them.Progression - Excellent, the linear progression of unlocking more mechs and also upgrading them via mech lab and research keeps you engaged at all times. Crafting your personal load outs are always fun.Missions - Pretty standard engagements - they just get progressively longer and also harder etc. so nothing special to note here.Team AI - Dumb, they will friendly fire you if you get in their way, so, you've been warned. Use the Battlegrid Tac Map and issue your team to always be in front of you so they are the ones engaged first and also out of your way. This is crucial for some of the missions that have only NARROW pathways. But apart from that, they get the job done - be sure to give them additional armour points when setting up their mechs - just trust me on this one. And PPC/LRMS are your best friend in any load out.Performance - I only crashed once, this was in a cutscene. Some missions bugged out, but this was corrected with hotfix (another one on the way) My PC chugged closer to some end game elements (massive battles happening) which didnt take long to settle. Average frames for me were around 65-70fps with the above mentioned settings.Overall - Try not to listen to the super fan boys or lore purists too much in the other reviews regarding the story, or why there are only 16 mechs to choose from. Trust me, the 16 mechs on line up its PERFECTLY FINE. I have knowledge in the  Battletech universe as well, while Im not a gigachad BT nerd,  I know enough about it and still I would give this a thumbs up purely because PGI have made a game that is better then MW5 Mercs in every way.Why? Cause I dont have to go onto NEXUS to download 50 mods to play the damn game.People who are comparing it to a MODDED MW5 Mercs are dumb. You can ask them to go play STOCK MW5 Mercs and get them to tell you how it compares to MW5 Clans and I bet you they cant play MW5 Mercs without their mods.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an early review of the game, I have not beaten the story yet. I have to say my impressions thus far are that of disappointment. Be it the terrible bit-rated sound quality or the bland characters or the uncanny-ness of some of the facial models... I cant find myself getting pulled into the 'story' of this game. The game play itself is typical MechWarrior, and while MW 5: Mercenaries was not a feature complete game at launch, over time the modding communities as well as some of the DLCs have made the replay value and overall gameplay loop very replayable. Since clans is lacking that replayability all it has to offer is its gameplay and story, and as ive said the story and characters thus far feel bland. That leaves the gameplay which is plagued by the same issues as Mercenaries... the terrible AI, the mechlab and its lack of customization (without mods) which somehow feels worse in this game compared to Mercenaries.I have seen a lot of people talk about the attention to detail when it comes to lore and I felt it important to praise that, despite the few discrepancies (what the heck is a SOKOL...?), but I'm afraid that lore detail can only carry things so far. Perhaps mods and DLC will make this game a much better play later just like they have with Mercenaries, but without something that fosters replayability like a career mode that might prove difficult. Pick it up on sale if you're a fan of the battletech universe otherwise just go play mercenaries and use mods.

So they all feel meaningful and you are never forced to "grind" to make progress. _childDocuments_.review: This is a tighter, more formulaic experience than Mechwarrior 5: Mercenaries.A good comparison would be Mechwarrior 4, which had a much tighter roster and mission setup. While Mercenaries has you flying around on your own terms with mostly procedural content interrupted by scripted material, Clans has exclusively pre-built missions. This makes it much more of a tailored experience and as someone who had a mixed experience with Mercenaries I quite like the "things are making noticeable progress" approach that Clans has.Pros:• Story missions give a lot of different experiences that show off what the universe offers in combat and encourages specialist builds. One of my complaints with Mercenaries was that the universe was basically different colors and occasionally different 'mech rosters when you moved from place to place. Clans feels meaningfully different with each mission, in part because it has a very aggressive progression curve and how the combat areas are set up.• Characters and places you get to have a connection to. Now, I'm not going to say that Clans has Baldur's Gate level characters, storytelling, or acting, but it gives you an idea of the drive, passion, and flaws of the characters. The cutscenes are great as a rule, and as someone who's wanted a Battletech movie forever, it kind of feels like we got a stab at one.• Tailored missions are so much better than randomly generated arenas. You can tell where they designed tactical puzzles and opportunities; take cover on the side of the river or dive in to cool off while opening yourself to more fire.• Glorious carnage. With the sheer amount of firepower and Battlemech being thrown around, a lot of these fights are just begging for Duncan Fisher voice-overs. Good aim and a good setup just absolutely melts the IS 'mechs you're up against, and it's a brutal spectacle.Cons:• Less variety than MW5: Mercenaries, especially if you're used to playing with mods that add extra content into the game. Part of this is the fact that the Clans just don't use low-tier stuff, so you're just picking from the high-end gear like ER lasers/PPCs, but there are times when the "upgrades" feel worse (for instance, if you're a staunch lasers fan like myself, you can have some dry runs where you just don't have an obvious upgrade in the tree).• The progression curve is very swift. The simulator missions to replay things and test out 'mechs enforce the weight limits, so if you just want to get a feel for how a new 'mech handles you're stuck in the range/arena, which is not the end of the world but doesn't necessarily map to how the game actually plays, so you can't test if a new 'mech does better or worse in a particular scenario you felt was dicey. I also get anxious with the researches, since it really feels like you're choosing something to the exclusion of other things. I went for ER lasers early in the game, which paid off when I unlocked the Nova and backfired once I wound up in heaver classes with fewer weapon mounts intended for things like ER PPCs.• Performance. My CPU seems to handle the game okay (at least according to performance monitoring), but I'm on a 4070 Ti with frame generation enabled and occasionally I'll have lost inputs and noticeable frame-dips. Typically the drop is closer to 30-45 fps, which feels choppy and can lead to a missed shot but doesn't interfere too much, but I've had the occasional slideshow. EDIT: As of Hotfix #1, things seem to be going a lot better. Still some small dips perhaps, but the part where my system was really suffering last night ran much better today.Miscellaneous Considerations:• Clans outmatch the IS tech during the campaign. A lot of the challenge is "how do I deal with fifteen enemies at once" where in Mercenaries you might actually have to consider a lance-on-lance engagement as something that could end a run. You are superior 1:1 with enemies above your weight class, which gives a very action/arcade feel to many of the combats, even if the gameplay is just a slicker Mercenaries.• Visually, Clans isn't that much of an improvement over Mercenaries on my machine. Some of this might be my reduction in settings due to performance (and Mercenaries is not exactly a smooth and polished high-performance game either). But I don't feel like my complaint with Mercenaries ever related to the graphics. The UI is definitely cooler.• The new tactical options are nice, but I never use them. Sorry, battlegrid, I'm going to still use the function-key commands like I have for decades. Coincidentally, the UI feels relatively busy because the command prompts are always on screen. If we were really supposed to focus as much on our teammates, some readouts for ammo and section health would have been nice (I know you can target them, but that doesn't help at a glance and turns figuring out who needs the repair bays the most into a bit of an ordeal). • The talking head popups are iffy. The headshots feel poorly rendered (I long for the FMV days) probably because the scene isn't fully built out, which makes it feel like a $6 indie game. Between the speaker and the text, it eats up like 10% of your screen real-estate, and while the backing box is transparent you don't need all that. I'd suggest a toggle to a more simple closed-caption format (e.g. "Speaker: Text" in a little box) to keep the screen real estate open.Should you buy?• Clans feels like it has a good chunk of content. I think I probably have a half-dozen campaign missions left, assuming you unlock the last 'mech around the time you finish the campaign. Players don't have access to all the 'mechs and equipment in the game, but you will encounter interesting adversaries and all the Battletech classics throughout.• Low-end machines and non-frame-gen users will probably have awful performance. It's definitely something that falls in places for me, so maybe it is something where everyone has the same dips and performance is better throughout the rest of the game, but you definitely want to have a good rig.• It's very different from Mercenaries. I like most of those changes, but if you want open-world mercenary play this is definitely not the game for you.I like it, as someone coming from the old MechWarrior games. I never played MWO and played MW5: Mercenaries enough to have some experience but never really enjoyed it like the earlier games. I definitely feel like this is more akin to the older games, and if that's what you're looking for it feels good.

_childDocuments_.review: By far the best entry that PGI has made and arguably at least on par with any of the previous entries in the IP. The story is very well written, one of it's strongest points and very lore accurate. There was no compromise made to cater to a 'modern audience' and the growth of the main character into their leadership role is very well executed.The in between mission cinnamatics is solid and while not on the level of a $400 million game is impressive for the size of the Dev team and the budget, with the mocap and voice acting matching the story writing. The hand crafted missions are well laid out and diverse in objectives and the set pieces, especially charging and then cresting the hill on the first mission in turtle bay gave me chills. The in between mission management parts can be daunting and complex and feel a bit clunky at first, but there is a LOT of depth and re-playability there. Once you understand the synergies between the pilot skills, the research, the mech skills, the affinities and the omnipod system you will be able to put together some really brutal builds.The graphics is the best so far, but again, on par with the size of the dev team and optimization wise has the same issues as all new UE5 games. DLSS/FSR + vsync and capped 60 fps is your friend here. I did have issues with the game causing my system to restart, but I am running a SFF system so it struggles with heat and is not the only game that causes this issue. The above settings fixed all crashes for me.I'm not much of an audiophile so cant comment much there but it isn't bad. I use headphones so YMMV.This is a very solid 8/10
