_childDocuments_.review: Edited - I've given this another try on Game Pass and I'm happy to say that with some time and patches, most of my concerns have been mitigated and I'm enjoying it now.  The SOKOL (boss-VTOL) fights have been reined in enough to be manageable in the early game, the uncanny-valley lip-sync feels improved enough that I can connect with some characters and the HOTAS setup is...  well, it's better.  Basically it's the same as MW5 Mercs now and still kind of janky, but it doesn't reset itself anymore.  I'll pick this up again permanently when I can.Original review:It feels strange to say this about a game that I've returned, but I am genuinely excited about where this one is going.  I loved MW5 Mercs and Clans has the potential to amazing.  It just needs more time to cook, I think.  When it's good it's GREAT (PPCs are FUN now, combat in general feels better than Mercs, atmosphere and storytelling are captivating and true to lore) but it also has some problems at the moment and those outweigh the fun for me.  My main issues:  Weird, sticky UI elements where onscreen buttons won't work consistently (particularly in the options menus), a challenging HOTAS setup that resets every time you play, mega-uncanny-valley facial animations ala ME: Andromeda and finally and most irritatingly, some bullet-spongey nonsense bosses that break you right out of the simulation and feel of the game (you can battle through a company of spheroid battlemechs with ease, but one angry boss-VTOL will roflstomp your whole star).  So right now it's a no from me, but I'm looking forward to checking it out again in 6-8 months and am hopeful that I can be super-positive about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly faithful to Battletech lore, from the characters to the events to the speech and culture. Clans is a fantastic uplift to MW5 that brings it into the 4K era. Full of unironically fantastic 80s scifi style music, you'll be pew-pewing your way through a tons of narratively chained missions as opposed to the open format of Mercenaries. Between each mission your Star, has 5 days to research, rearm, and repair. Omnimech tech makes mech customization between missions frighteningly easy, while if you take too much damage, you may want to 'bid on more mech-techs to get your Star up to full strength. There is a lot of customization options, without being overly complicated, eg. adding armor to mechs takes up a loadout general slot, and comes in 'pods' of ablative armor packs, 0.25T, 0.5T and 1T each. Customization is very different as a result to Mercenaries, but it fits the Clan style, they are very adaptable and modular systems. Couple this with 4 Star-mates who have fleshed out characterization, skills, affinities, etc.; eg. Liam can skill up in making ECM more effective on his Mechs, Ezra is better with energy weapons, Mia is better with Ballistics and so on. You can also unlock 'affinity' for a character, to make one of your pilot's skills work 10% better in light mechs, or 20% better in a particular chassis of mech for example. Mech chassis also net you mech XP that can be used to unlock different omnipods for your mechs, which default with "Prime" variant pods for that Mech, with A B C D etc. pods available to unlock that give you access to vastly different loadouts: try switching your Viper to all ER Small Lasers and Armor Pods and go on a killing spree early game. Ditto the Nova. And if that's too cheesy: you can replay past missions in the simpod to unlock more XP and achieve advanced objectives, like beating the missions again using undertonnage and stock loadouts. I'd reccomend this game highly to anyone who is already familiar with Battletech, and it's a fantastic starting point for any curious new players. My only other early game tip is to upgrade your salavage ops ASAP as high as you can bear vs. repair stackup, and make sure you are researching as much as possible as well between missions, because you won't be able to unlock everything in one campaign run, and you will have a limited amount of time, and resources you can collect to do so throughout the story. But that's just more opportunity for replay value right? Heh.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:1. Mechlab is almost perfectly lore accurate, in that most options are simply unlocking and using different omnipods.2. Lore accurate clan mechs, with low armor and ammo, but high speed, firepower, and range.3. They have focused on giving a story this time, as five's stories tended to be more set dressing pablum than anything of interest.4. Game feels really optimized and smooth, and I hope they somehow manage to backpatch this into mercenaries.5. Overall visual upgrade over mercenaries.6. Enemy ai feels improved.Cons:1. Enemy ai appears improved, but friendly ai requires constant micro to no get in the way.2. Missions still feel like a corridor shooter with a skybox.3. No real damage feedback to make you notice/feel when your mech is getting rocked. Most of the time I only notice damage when i move slow from lost leg, or weapons stop working.4. I don't care about a bunch of kids with attitude.5. Mostly lore accurate story, but lightens  down smoke jaguar extremism in order to make them more sympathetic.6. Don't expect to spend hours in mechlab squeezing performance out of a mech. It is lore accurate, but it is still ultimately lacks options (heavy lasers, atm's, etc) likely due to introduction years.7. Difficulty comes from them throwing waves of stuff at you. Ammo weapons (missile and ballistic) are almost rendered useless by how quick you run out, meaning energy spam, which is my favorite, but not necessarily so for others.8. Mechs feel weightless/massless. Some is due to clan tech xl engines, but it feels like playing a weird control fps instead of a mech simulator where I am in a multi ton war machine.9. This is purely a personal gripe, but the main protag has the most punchable face/bearing of any protag I have ever seen.Recomendation:Overall, a flawed but ultimately enjoyable game that shows a key time in the settings history from a side you don't normally see. Still very flawed. Recommend purchase on sale of %25+.

_childDocuments_.review: Its hard to really say if this game is worth it or not. If you're really into the lore of Mechwarrior then this is a really interesting insight into the clan invasion from the perspective of a fresh pilot into Smoke Jaguar, but when it comes to the game play there's so many steps backwards that makes it feel really hollow in comparison to its predecessors. The mech bay has been more or less stripped down to bare basics, you have preset load-outs you can apply or you can individually place weapons and equipment yourself, but you have no ability to adjust the armour values like you can with MW5 or to adjust your maximum armour values when you want to try and make more of a glass cannon mech build, you're stuck with what you're given. You don't capture or salvage mechs, you level up and unlock them, so get used to running light/medium mechs for awhile until you level up enough to get a heavy/assault mech. The mech selections are very limited, obviously these are all clan mechs, but despite seeing the MW5 mechs you come across you'll never see/run any of those or salvage them. Salvage is no longer present in this game in the standard sense, you have different facilities you upgrade over time to take come more "spoils of war" essentially meaning you have to divide evenly between the 3 choices, Mech Components, Weapon Components and Equipment Components. The command options are a great improvement, I would of liked to have this in MW5 when commanding my lance, however the AI is STUPID, while they do follow your commands if you tell them to wait in a location they may end up running through some security wall/tripwire during a sneaking style infiltration mission and give away your position (take a guess how I know this). The UI feels very clunky, feels like there's too much going on my screen to be able to properly see what i'm doing, there are some settings you can adjust to mirror the paper-doll for yourself and the enemy mechs you target and you can put the controls into "Classic Mode" so you can turn and move independent of each other rather than the more arcade like "Modernised" controls they've added. The VA work seems OK in areas, but rather flat in others, I don't get that grandeur I expect from a clan warrior, it seems very much like a bunch of larpers trying to role play, awkwardly. The game is fun in the basic sense, it does tick that box of "hehe mech go boom pew pew" to release the much desired serotonin, but it eventually gets rather samey pretty quickly. I can't see any clear replay-ability value with this as the game is linear whereas MW5 allowed you free reign to explore as you saw fit. I wont return the game as I am having fun and there's a LOT of promise here, but some of the decisions have really left me scratching my head so I'm very in the middle with recommending it at this time.EDIT (25/10/2024) - So, after playing more I am enjoying myself, I do think they need a checkpoint system in missions or the ability to save because having to restart a mission from the beginning is just painful. One thing I did recently discover was that you can individually swap out omnipods from the different load-outs on your mech meaning you do have a pretty decent amount of configuration than before, of course this takes time as you need to unlock the omnipods for the mechs you play but it does mean there's a bit more to the mech lab than originally thought, its still steps backwards in some areas than MW5 but its not terrible. My main issue however is the insane drop in the mechs you can run/play as in comparison to MW5, I understand these are clan mechs only but there are a lot of clan mechs that could of also been put in from the lore/tabletop/other games, something mods for MW5 has achieved. Ultimately, I do think the game is worth it only if you're really into mechwarrior and the lore around the clan invasions as it provides a pretty interesting perspective. If you're kinda on the fence? I'd wait for a sale.EDIT 22/11/2024 - Editing to not recommended. I cannot in good conscience recommend a game where the developers have such bad optics with their first DLC. Game released just over a month ago and already they release their DLC....its paid for multiplayer and frankly I find this a full slap in the face. Why wasn't this included in the base game, especially since this DLC was announced so close to the full games release?If it came with other mechs, some story aspects and new weapons/adjustments sure I can see a reason for DLC for that kind of content, but Multiplayer? Should of been included or released as a free update down the line. They state melee weapons were added but this is in complete disregard to the source material of mech warrior as clans abhorred melee weapons on mechs (Its event mentioned in the first couple missions how "Primitive" the inner sphere mechs are for having to resort to such "primitive tools")

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Mechwarrior PC games since Mechwarrior2 running on MS-DOS in the mid 1990's.This game is a step backwards compared to MW5 Mercenaries and previous Mechwarrior/Battletech games.For one, the voice acting is pretty horrible and not even believable. It is monotone, uninspiring, and boring. I have no problem with them having their own speech patterns as a unique culture but they sound like boring robots who are reading from a script rather than having a discussion. I have never skipped through mission briefing cutscenes before on a brand new game until I got this game. Even the characters are pretty horrible. The main character is an insecure effeminate male, which doesn't make me want to play him.This is a linear game where all the battles are pretty easy, much easier than in previous games. You can literally take out 100 ton mechs within seconds. And there is almost no need for money because you get all the mechs for free and all of the weapons and equipment are cheap, making getting rewarded with money seem worthless. Everything is handed to you on a silver platter. Money, research points, "honor" points, "xp points", etc. It seems like no challenge and not rewarding. It's like this game was designed for little kids with short attention spans.The UI is pretty horrible as well. I do not see how many research points I have, for example, and I hover my mouse above certain points and it doesn't even say what it is that I'm looking at. I used to be able to see exactly how much armor damage and structural damage and whether each mech ran out of ammo after each battle but now I only see status bars. I can't see, for example, whether a mech ran out of AMS ammo after a mission. Or even how many vehicles/mech/aircraft each mech has destroyed or how much damage they did. The entire game was dumbed-down and feels less like a realistic simulator and more like an arcade game. Even the colors and HUD are way too vibrant and large. The HUD is distracting from the actual view. I thought for sure there would be  a way to make the HUD more translucent, but no. Its like the HUD was designed with big crayons and large block letters that interfere with the view.This is a game where everybody who plays gets a gold star and after that, there is no real re-playability that I can see. Oh maybe just to see what happens after the only decision you can make in the entire game, other than that, what? Replay the exact same missions you already have? No that's boring. They should have made it where you can space travel and at least go on random missions.The other thing is each weapon and equipment piece is available to you immediately. Aside from maybe a few like the LBX-AC BF, and perhaps one or two others. There is basically no reason to buy anything from the marketplace. They got rid of rare weapons and "tiered" weapons. So basically you get everything without having to lift a finger. They got rid of the rewarding feeling of finally killing a rare mech and having to collect enough salvage pieces of it after battle to finally have enough parts to assemble the mech into a complete unit, and instead just give you literally every mech for free. After the battle there is no specific salvage you can pick and instead just generic  salvage points, which is totally lame and boring.There are only a few things this game improves upon, such as the "omni pods" which allow you to change the hard points, weapon options and equipment of your battlemech body sections. The ability to add armor to each body section is also welcome, even in increments as low as 0.25 tons. Also the jump jet system has been marginally improved. Otherwise this game is less believable, more easy and less realistic than previous games, also the acting and story is lame, aside from a couple. I think I recognized a couple voice actors from previous games....they were great. The new ones, not so much.This game does not make me want to fork out any additional money for add-on DLC's. I play MW5 Mercs and also Battletech to this day because those are games that you can play over and over again and still enjoy. This one, is not that type of game. which is hard to understand because they could have easily improved upon MW5 Mercs but instead they chose to make a linear game that is worse. So I do not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - needs another 4-6 mos development time to address technical issues. The numerous design and usability problems will probably be fixed by the modding community, so that's another reason to wait before buying.Longer version -Severe performance issues both in and out of combat (including mechlab, briefings, barracks, etc), numerous bugs (does not save keybinds, does not remember weapon groups), even the cutscenes are plagued by artifacts. Enemy AI is not intelligent.Worse still, the Mechlab is excruciating... was any usability testing performed? The Mechlab interface is confusing, not intuitive, and need-to-know information is not appropriately visible when required. For example, resources like 'Mech Exp' are used to purchase omnipods, but the user doesn't see how much of this resource they have while browsing items that require it (user has to click the purchase button to be told that they don't have enough). Also, some screens feature scrollbars within scrollbars. Other screens like the mech overview don't display useful information like heat buildup/s. And pop-up messages / confirmation dialogs have their corresponding buttons far away from the message itself, at the bottom-right of the screen.Like with MW5 Mercs, this release will rely on the mod community to fix such glaring issues. Fortunately the mod community is fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've been raving about the story of this game for some time, especially with my having read the Blood of Kerensky Trilogy!  This game really does deliver on the story line, almost perfectly!  This series' lore and information is a fair bit daunting and a fair bit confusing to some, more so if you're looking at things from the outside, but honestly, after completing the main story, seeing the end of it just made me giddy as hell!  I genuinely enjoyed it all!  I know, I know, some of the bigger sticking points is the optimization, however with a rig that can run almost any game effortlessly, I didn't have too much of an issue, which puts me in a minority of people who had no issues running it beyond just the odd glitches that came up.  Personally, because I didn't have any issues, my sticking points were more with the cutscenes.  Audio was strangely low quality during the cutscenes, and knowing Unreal Engine, something tells me the cutscenes are all pre-rendered, which has me a tad bit upset that we may not even see any fix to it.  However, saying that, there are signs that make me question if it's live rendered, namely in the hair physics.  If it was all pre-rendered, the physics should (hopefully) be pre-calculated to make the cutscenes work without issue.  Thing is, paying attention to some of the scenes, characters with long hair such as Naomi and Mia tend to have their hair suddenly fall into place during a camera change, which leads me to be hopeful that we'll eventually see a fix to the audio since that would suggest it's all live rendered.  I'm really not sure what the back-end looks like with how they made all of the cutscenes, but here's to hoping.  In short, though, if you play it, I *HIGHLY* recommend either DLSS or FSR to help get a stable framerate.  Beyond that, I also highly recommend this game, anyone looking to dive into the BATTLETECH/MechWarrior lore and experience something truly story driven within the franchise outside HBS's BATTLETECH.

Difficulty is wave, after wave, after wave, after wave, (deep breath), after wave of mechs at the weight rate of the mission.  In the least fun scenario so far the whole thing is set up around having to run thru heavy firepower to cut off escaping mechs.  The terrain is nothing but choke points with no room to maneuver, so just charge thru and get shredded.  4 times.  That's it.  Yawn.  I don't like the AI for your friendly's either.  They are just wing man you can order to concentrate fire on an enemy mech.  Not much else.  No real maneuver on their part.  Of course the enemy mechs are about the same.  Concentrate fire on the closest enemy that shot at me seems to be about it.  Of course since you lead your formation, initially you are always closest.Controls, graphics, etc are fine, but the level design and AI are terrible.  I don't mind the stilted speech in the cut scenes because the clans don't use contractions.  That makes the acting sound funny, but I can live with it.What put this game on the shelf for me was the game play.  It isn't bad, just monotonous.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me so sad. It's really fun and everything is good on paper, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the voice acting is bad. Their mocap software must be completely borked too because everyone has ridiculously large mouths.Despite all that, I'm still enjoying it. Missions don't seem as repetitive/boring as MW5 Mercs was. _childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: This game has what MechWarrior 5: Mercs did not. A full single player storyline. The game runs acceptable on even my old 4790k / 6800 combo with some settings turned down. The cut scenes are vivid, the game even on medium settings looks great and overall I enjoyed the game very much. I imagine people who are heavy in the lore would enjoy the game as well from that aspect as there was so much information given my head was spinning.I'd rate it an 9/10Pro's- Looks great.- Full single player storyline with beautifully crafted cutscenes.- Engaging gameplay and mech customisation.- Runs on 4790k (it won't run 100% smooth but the fact it still runs like it does with zero crashes? 10/10).Con- There is one mission (no spoilers) that became a massive slog and took me 4 hours of gameplay to complete on normal with multiple configurations. There were other missions where I had to restart due to not directing my lance mates properly or just going in guns blazing but that particular one was a PITA. All the others before and after were fine and well balanced.I am hoping we see more Mechwarrior games of this caliber in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are good and the story is good.  Easy to finish in under 50 hours of game play. Game lacks a lot of replay value due to the story being very linear. I think it is a good game but MW5: Mercenary's was better because you had more freedom choices and got to travel around the map, you got to manage more resources, and you got to stay with the same Mech's longer.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing Mechwarrior games since Mechwarrior 2 came out.  I believe I even bought MW2: Mercenaries before Mech 2.  As the years go buy and each game comes out, they go from great to okay, to what the hell was MW5: Mercs when it first released?I'm so glad that Clans has come out.  We have a fun game and story.  Granted missions can be hard at times and I'm guessing they'll get tweaked as the months go by, but overall I had a blast playing this game.  I look forward to the dlcs which I hope will continue the main campaign story, as well as introduce other clan stories.  Considering there is at least one branch within the story, it will be good to see both ends of it.One thing however, the devs need to fix the mechlab asap, we shouldn't have to wait for the modding community to sort it out :PI highly recommend this game to be bought.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Rolled Credits on MechWarrior 5: Clans.The GOODThe story was great from my opinion and while there was only a single moment of choice which dictated which path you choose (and ending). It actually felt like an agonising choice when it came to be made.There has been a serious graphical and audio upgrade since MechWarror Mercs here. Though there is a price to pay if you do not have the system to run at full specs.The game had ZERO grind which was really refreshing. Each and every mission was a story mission with the level of detail to make it feel right. Nothing was procedural generated for extra spacing.The Clans felt like they were heroic in their superior BattleMech's against superior numbers.The UNDECIDEDThe levelling up of each Mech and MechWarrior was a little blah. Though it did limit the ability of changing around the Mech's Omni Pods until you have piloted them for several missions. And the interface was confusing and not intuitive when between missions. In the missions everything was perfect in comparison.The BADI did not like being forced to play pregenerated MechWarriors which had specific skill sets. Yes the lance or squad mates had their own personality and story bumps which made them feel real. But I wanted to choose the skills I learn for them. For example, one of the pilots is geared towards ballistic weapons. And I never ever use them in combat in the game. Also the game was short, as it was just shy of 30 hours. But without grind I did not mind it as short as it was.MechWarrior Mercs had a post campaign, free play option as, well, Mercenaries. But because there is zero procedural generation systems built into this game. There is no option for this, this time. And that is a major bummer.The facial animations are REALLY bad. I just found myself looking away at times.I might play again more casually, but at a higher difficulty where I will struggle. Where as I have 450 hours in MechWarrior 5 Mercs due to their post game play (and MODS).Conclusion.If your a fan of MW5 Mercs you will enjoy the improvements here. But understand the post game limits of this.Maybe the game will include something of post game campaigns in DLC later.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the heavy mech on mech fighting and customization of MW5:Mercs, and like me, found yourself left wanting in dialog and story then boy to I have good news for you. And sure some of the visual aspects could be better, and I'm starting to suspect a clanner might die if they smile, this is every bit the game I was wanting. Given its stellar performance on my old pc, I suspect it will only improve from here. Thank you PGI, our faith was not wasted.

_childDocuments_.review: POST ENDGAME COMMENTSOriginal review below stands.30ish hours of linear single player story. A rather cartoonish story, but that's lore accurate to the Honor!  Warrior! Honor! nonsense that is the Clans. I've never liked the Clans and I still can't see Clanners as people, their culture is unworkably nonsensical, but for lore accuracy this is a fun experience. Biggest disappointment is you don't get to fight alongside or against Elementals (the Clan power armor). People talk about them and they show up in cut scenes but that is it.Biggest problem I had was Omnipods. You earn Mech XP with each chassis when you or one of you minions takes it out on a mission. These can be spent on upgrades to chassis maneuverability or omnipods that give you different hardpoint options, and this is not documented at all and I couldn't figure out why I could not buy any omnipods many missions in. Even then you don't get enough Mech XP to experiment with builds for every chassis - I guess that's replayability.Research unlocks improved weapons and armor, and to do research you need salvage. So pouring everything into upgrading salvage early on is vital if you want to put a dent into the research tree.Kerensky's, the currency for buying mechs and equipment, are insanely plentiful. Hitting the 20mil achievement is unavoidable. Never felt a pinch there and wish there was something to waste them on. Being able to buy the all important salvage for example.For the most lore accurate experience I recommend playing on "story" with aim assist turned on and maxed out - you are supposed to be a superhuman genetically engineered Clanner after all.ORIGINALHuge reservations about recommending this product. I strongly do not recommend the digital edition as the content is only usable in the game so you cannot listen to the soundtrack or look at the art without running the game. A strike against the base game is that this is not a finished product as DLC and patches will eventually provide a much more complete product - that's just the way the industry is. If you are willing to invest now and hope it gets enough love from the dev team that this will be a good product then buy. If you are willing to wait a couple of years you can get a more complete game for less money. Right now it is okay. You get a very "on rails" story where you play as naive recruits for Team Baddie and that's fun for a single play through which is the problem with playing as any soldier in an army where you are just following orders. Gameplay is slightly more arcadey than Mercs and the story is full of cartoonish characters which fits because Battletech increasingly leaned towards the cartoonish once the Clans showed up.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: MW5: Clans isn't _perfect_. it's got it's fair share of gameplay issues, some wonky design decisions, and some stilted voice acting and facial animations. But it's a more than worthy successor to not only Mercs but past BattleTech/Mechwarrior titles as well.Pros:+ an interesting mix of electronic/throat singing tracks that fit the vibe of the game+ very pretty looking mech models/cockpits+ sound design is top notch! makes you feel really powerful+ a serviceable story about the beginning of the Clan invasion+ really well-done cutscenes+ a decent linear game in 2024+ very true to BT loreCons:- mech customization feels limited but the pod system opens it up if you unlock them- difficulty spikes can feel out of nowhere and borderline unfair at times- strangely placed boss fights- the game doesn't pause when you open the tactical map; so the emphasis on "being tactical as Star Commander" kind of goes out the window- Your Starmates' AI is... bad. Like really, really, bad. They will crowd around an enemy mech so the risk of them being shot by you is quite high- not all mechanics are explained thoroughly- mech progression is from Light -> heavy and you are not incentivized to vary what mechs you bring to a mission. So the deeper you are in the game you are more or less required to bring the heaviest mechs you can, no exception- Clan mechs feel paper-thin despite being so powerful- if you're not a lore nerd nothing about this will make sense to you- very chunky performance in some places|- HORRIBLE mission balancing

_childDocuments_.review: Look, my only gripe with the game is that the team AI are absolute steaming hot piles of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. They feel worse than in MW5 Mercenaries by a large margin. In Mercs, my Lancemates might not be as good as me, they might not even get anywhere near as many kills as me, but at least they were there as effective damage dealing fire support, which the same can not be said for your Starmates in Clans. The only use for the other pilots in your star, are for when yours goes down and you can take over theirs, which is not something I really did in Mercs, as my Lancemates were good enough to provide cover fire. The only time I took control of a Lancemates mech in Mercs, It was to pilot the faster one to clear out some artillery in the back, which doesn't really have as big of an emphasis in Clans. To be clear, this isn't a difficulty issue in terms of the game being hard, it's just the team AI are that dumb.All of that aside, I do enjoy the story. People can gripe about how stiff or bad the dialogue between characters can be sometimes but they also seem to forget, You are a test tube baby raised in a very rigid (backwards even) warrior society. Of course they are going to be weird! And as for the strange facial animations, I chalk that up to UE5 having strange lip syncing technology, and makes everyone show a lot of teeth in their dialogue.  I've seen this in other UE5 games as well. That's more on Epic than PGI.There's nothing bad to say about the combat (besides ♥♥♥♥♥♥ team AI), as it's more of the same of what you know and love from MW5 and MWO.The graphics of the game looks absolutely great though, UE5 really does look that good, and the devs have taken full advantage of it.The Mech commanding menu... it's alright? I can't say that having more options to command is bad, but this certainly is great either. I sure as hell couldn't think of a better way to do it.If you you could only buy one and had to compare apples to apples, vanilla MW5 Mercs to Clans, I'd say that Clans is by far the superior game in terms of Mech combat, and I love MW5 Mercs.I do have a pretty beefy computer, so I haven't really run into any bugs really. The most buggy thing I've seen so far is that when I destroy a mech, sometimes the mech weight class indicator is still there on the map.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable experience with some noticeable improvements but some annoying detraction's.The visual fidelity is great, however the visual effects for things like blowing sand or waterfalls looks very poor like its not rendering properly.The mech's feel much better, they have weight and the sounds are on point.However there are only 16 mech's and they are very linearly locked behind levelling up.Weapons are vastly improved in terms of their visuals, sounds, and them actually feeling powerful.However you lose almost all ability to edit load outs since you cant change engines, armour allocation, cant remove jump jets, etc.. you are more or less forced into using the omnipod load outs as is.The story is vastly improved over MW5, with acknowledgements to the lore not feeling forced or over explained as if the character has no clue about the world they live in.That said, facial animations and the cadence of the voice acting is very hit and miss. There are actually several moments so far where I have been concerned that Piranha used AI voice models because the cadence and way they were talking just made zero sense.Overall its a nice addition to the mech warrior game series.. but it very much is lacking in depth that you will be accustomed to if you come from MW5 or MWO.

_childDocuments_.review: - The story feels so out of place (Cheesy Teen drama, of kids acting out and debating the ethics of war crimes, Like theres literally 2 missions about saving prisoners you have zero context on if they are criminals or not. I don't think an invading war force that is trying to do create a foothold on a planet would give 2 cares about random prisoners. But ohhhhh the teenagers are throwing a fit so we have to care. Literally when your mech goes through a building you probably just killed a 100 people.)- Performance / Optimization- Day 1 patch, came a day late....- Systematically a downgrade from Mercs... which is weird...- Co-op is extremely lacking, they should just disable it instead of tricking people into buying it to play with their friends and have a good co-op experience because its not here. Immediately started the game with a bad taste.- You can't back out of a mission after failing, you have to keep trying from the start (starting over is fine) but its obnoxious because you want to go back to base to try a new mech deployment.- Environment is too busy, and not flatten for Mechs with Jump Jets imo. Ruins the Level Design- AI is terrible, it was bad in Mercs but it's worse. Enemies and Allies get stuck on environment constantly. Ally mechs are dumb as bricks. They will follow you and watch you fight stuff and not even try to help until you order them to target your target, then they attack at once and one tap the mech target. Hold Position they sometimes try to dodge shots but most of the time sit there like a wall just tanking shots. There is no GO THERE command so you have to use GO HOLD POSITION for that which isn't ideal as previous stated- Battlegrid is extremely lacking in commands/choices... even the time to use it wisely. It doesn't feel like any mission or level was design with this system in mind for it (that ive played so far)- Mission structure/objectives IS STILL BLAND, thats what they were suppose to be fixing in this one I thought with the story?- The Trial were you get killed by the Timber Wolf is legit something every gamer hates, and I haven't seen this in a game in like 15 + years. Like this franchise deserves better, Battletech is really good because it captures a piece of the spirit of this world. MW5 Mercs & Clans & MWO fail to capture the spirit of this world, the grit, the politics, the weight, the immersion. It's really disheartening.---------------------------------------------This game is basically trying to be a sim version of heavy mechs, and yet it doesn't capture this at all, Mercs didn't and neither did MWO.This game desperately needs a new gameplay structure identity. Or new blood to breath in new ideas in this studio.Suggestions:- YOU ARE THE GUARD protecting a city or some such, and its a huge map with immersive sim elements and roaming objects, and you have to go out and do missions for the city and then protect it at different intervals. Legit, this would be day and night more fun then any mechwarrior game I've played in the last 10 years. And you keep all the systems, you get more politics and rich story.- Capture some of the spirit of Helldivers, with being a pilot roaming around the ship, living in the warfront. Then when you deploy you have to go to the hanger and crawl into the mech. STOP WITH ALL THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CUTSCENES FOR THE ATMOSPHERIC AND IMMERSION MOMENTS. MECHWARRIOR IS ABOUT IMMERSION. CUTSCENES RARELY ADD TO IMMERSION. THEY ARE TONE SETTERS OR STORY MOMENTS.

_childDocuments_.review: Hot damn, holy hell, I thoroughly enjoyed this way moreso than I did with Mercenaries.The game has smaller issues compared to its sibling, but nothing as glaring or problematic.As a whole though, the game plays well, and any and all issues I had with Mercenaries here are not present when relevant. Most importantly, the AI won't shoot me a dirty look for so much as looking at them. The story is damn incredible, but not without major speedbumps, and dialogue had some perplexing issues that somehow made it in to release.Clans is really fun. Good, arcadey, challenging fun. It feels like im playing 4: Vengeance again, with a bit of Black Knight here and there in a positive light. If anything, I was pleasantly reminded of that old Star Wars Clone Wars game on the PS2. Or even Ace Combat, 5 specifically with how mechs are handled outside of missions.The issues though are present, but for me at least were not a deal breaker. Definitely more confusing, but there are two I want to address first:I feel like the writer from the sibling game is still around. They are not the main writer, but were definitely still in the room when it came to planning and typing up scripts and story beats. An element of the story flat out did not land for me, but this is only in my experience from a newbie diving in to Battletech. Your mileage may vary on how much it'll bother, but it was enough that if I scored this the story alone would drop this from a 9 to an 8. What they tried missed the mark that noticeably.Secondly, my main issue. It is one of the main Battletech shticks that heat is present. And if you accumulate too much heat, your mech shuts down. For whatever reason, Clans chops away at this and I am not quite sure how to feel about it. When you overheat, instead of shutting down you simply cannot fire any weapons, and your sensors are shut down (And by extension, you cannot order your star). The same if you're legged too, in all other games you, well, limp because your leg was destroyed. In here though, CLAN MECHS have a brief period of stumbling, before proceeding onward like their ankles weren't violently removed by a ball of plasma. This is honestly just not a good decision in my mind and went against how Battletech plays in past games, and even on the tabletop.The only other issue I can think of is the scripting. This one is a nitpick, but its still weird and annoying how subtitles and voice lines at times have separate lines, and on the off chance sometimes the text is correct while the voice has incorrect information.Other than this, easily an owl seal of approval. Solid 8 out of 10, 9 out of 10. I'm still not sure how to feel about my issue with the writing of the story; I can see what they were going for and respect it which has me juggling it still.I just can't wait to see if they'll have DLC for this.

_childDocuments_.review: Ive played every Battletech related release extensively since 1995 and have read every book in the universe, something of an uber fan of the IP. Im not a fan of PGI after my experience with MWO the past decade, but I feel like they put their better foot forward with MW:Mercs. TLDR Version: MW5: Clans is currently only poorly scripted missions filled with irritating dialogue. It has the potential to be more, but its $50 price tag is unmerited. Pros:- The assets are not new but put to good use - mech combat feels good and after some mods, it will be great. Not enough was changed to ruin anything.- It looks nice. Its got some great settings, particle effects, and overall you can get some nice screenshots.- The Clans are a unique perspective and a welcome change to the setting.- The ability to command your team from an overhead view quickly is intuitive and works well.- Not going to be a common perspective but the Mechlab is altered to force you to use the Omnipod system and fixed equipment that is probably annoying to many gamers but commonplace if you play the Battletech game - thats just how it is. Because of that, it forces you to use non-optimized (for a veteran player, that means fun) builds that provide something of a challenge.-Coop is easy to use and hasnt been changed much from the MW5 Mercs system - I can reliably drop in and play with my kid just like with MW5.The Cons:- This shipped unfinished with ONLY a campaign mode (no instant action, skirmish, any form of alternative beyond the campaign).- The dialogue is pervasive and poor. You cannot escape it as it is in every mission, throughout every mission.- Extremely lore inaccurate - from a fan perspective, the fresh-from-the-sibko cadets you play as look and sound like soft, weak ankled teenagers. This does nothing to portray the warrior society and absolute ruthlessness of Clan Smoke Jaguar or the Clans as a whole. Why make the game without doing any research? A good chunk of the Clan books center specifically on Clan Smoke Jaguar and their culture - PGI didnt read and that is all. I cant imagine not doing basic research on a project as specific as this.- Metahumans are used for the characters but are done extremely poorly. This is bizarre - you can follow tutorials on YouTube and create better looking/responding metahumans yourself in a few hours. They creep into uncanny valley territory and you definitely saw better looking humans over a decade ago with far less tech used. It feels like they went this way because its cheap/time efficient to do the basics using metahumans and thats it.Summary:I will play this because Ive played every battletech related game, but without my rosecolored glasses this is a really lackluster release.  They created minimal (and I mean absolutely minimal) new content for this game - I for one like the basic formula but theres no way most gamers will pick this up and not get thrown off by the lack of value and horrendous story telling. The missions are heavily and sometimes poorly scripted, with things that simply dont jive with the Battletech universe or good gameplay in general. I will happily eat my words when they release updates to this and will revise my review when value is added,

_childDocuments_.review: When I played MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries I dreamed for a more story-driven version of the game, one which will include the Clan invasion. Lo and behold I got my dream in MechWarrior 5: Clans. The story is on the level of the BattleTech novels, which means passable to good. The cinematics are very well done. The clan Mechs are awesome and make you feel OP while stomping the poor "spheroids". As a whole the game is a big leap forward from Mercenaries, both in terms of gameplay and graphics.However, there are some negatives. The game suffers from "consolitis" - meaning all menus have 3-4 layers of sub-menus to make it playable on consoles, but a chore on PC. The Mech lab is dumbed down, both for lore reasons (Omnimechs) and for console ease of use. There is little replayability after you finish the story (no New Game+). Also the balance is all over the place, with certain weapon types and Mechs being far and away better than the rest. As a whole for me MechWarrior 5: Clans is a step in the right direction and a solid 8/10, with a potential for 9/10 with some good DLCs and/or mods. Now I find myself dreaming of this game having procedural missions and career mode like Mercenaries. Maybe on the side of the Inner Sphere, playing as a mercenaries hired to fight the Clan invasion? Oh, how the turn tables. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Update after completing the game in Expert mode without Co-Op:My assesment so far is pretty much the same. The game has it's flaws game play wise with a certain lack of strategic depth in level design and combat mechanics we know and love from the old MW games, however the tight-knitted lore and characters make up for it. I felt some fatique though after the 25th mission of wave after wave of cannon fodder mechs coming at me. I wish there was actual radar and use of terrain instead of gauntlet after gaunlet. But still, this is a fun experience if you dont look to close at what might have been a way better game even still. It is for me personally the best Mechwarrior game since MW3 despite its lack of gameplay depth and variety. I will surely play through it again with my MW buddies in Co-Op even though it was hardly a challenge, even in Expert. I look forward to continuing the campaign with better gameplay and hopefully more strategic depth. If the DLCs implement some more tactical gameplay like coolant flush, active and passive radar etc. it could still become a stellar game instead of just a very good game. As a veteran of the original MechWarrior 2 and someone with extensive experience in the BattleTech universe and its novels, I can confidently say that this game is a significant milestone for fans.Newcomers should be aware that it may be a bit challenging to grasp if you're unfamiliar with the lore. However, if you're into sci-fi universes and enjoy diving deep into intricate stories, this could be the best BattleTech experience in the last 25 years.I was skeptical about Piranha Games pulling off a solid MechWarrior title after the lukewarm reception of MWO and MW5: Mercenaries. Yet, after playing for around three hours, I’m pleasantly surprised. As far as MechWarrior games go, this is about as good as it gets.Yes, there are still bugs—something we’ve come to expect from Piranha. Even with 35 mods installed, MW5: Mercs was hardly enjoyable for me. That said, this game has only crashed once so far and has been a blast to play. The story and lore are handled with care and respect for the source material. Kudos to the writing team and voice actors—they’ve absolutely nailed it.In terms of gameplay, there are some quirks. For example, the battle grid doesn’t allow setting waypoints for lance mates, and you can't slow down or pause the game to issue commands mid-battle, making it tricky to manage your squad. There are also strange bugs, like not being able to freely move mechs in the mech lab, audio compression issues in the cutscenes or scrolling issues in the mechbay overview when checking loadouts. Despite these issues, I’m confident Piranha will fix them, though they do tend to take their time.Overall, this is the best thing to happen for MechWarrior fans since MechWarrior 3 or MechWarrior: Living Legends. I’ll keep playing—at least until the next crash—but I’m thoroughly enjoying every moment.I will be updating as I come along playing more of this flawed, yet oh so great game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so hyped for this, until I started playing it, then that hype died rather quickly.Optimization is not all that great, and I am well above spec.But what really let me down was the fact that even though this is called Mechwarrior 5, it is nothing like Mercenaries.Now I understand things are different for the clans, but they reduced salvage to "Here's some components buddy".And by that I mean items literally called that, not weapons, not mech parts or mech wrecks or whatever, you just get "Part points" to spend in your armory which is fully unlocked and all you really need to do is "become honourable".All in all while it makes some sorta sense lorewise it takes away the collectathon fun that I could experience in Mercenaries.Oh yeah and as far as I am in, no random missions, at most a choice between two.Also while I appreciate lore, would love to know what the characters are saying sometimes instead of "Space mumbo jumbo" cause as much as a fan that I am of Mechwarrior, I don't have that ♥♥♥♥ memorized from that one time I might've heard it 12 years ago...I think it is quite misleading that they slapped the Mechwarrior 5 onto this.I get no joy from this game, it simply feels like playing mecha call of duty at this point, very uninspired, do better.

_childDocuments_.review: The narrative focus really comes through here. The voice acting isn't Hollywood quality, but is very serviceable and combines with the universe-authentic Clan dialect ideosyncracies help cover up some awkward writing as verisimilitude for a culture that's grown apart from the Core for many centuries. But the focus on the story delivers real characters with arcs and motivations, that allows the player to invest and develop attachment to them even as we know that they now get plot armor since it's not a rogue-like randomly generated pilot.The engine is more or less the same as MechWarrior 5 Mercenaries, delivering the stompy sense of weight and momentum that has always made me value the MechWarrior franchise over its more directly anime-inspired competitors like Armored Core and Heavy Gear that always left me feeling like I was playing an FPS or 3rd Person Shooter with robot models. The level design has taken a step up over MW5 Mercenaries, offering up variety in environments that get referenced in voice lines and mission briefings, as well as mission design.

_childDocuments_.review: MW5 C is a game that hurts me, as it is a painfully mid attempt to bring one of Battletech's defining era's to life in the action genre, marred by design choices made by devs who followed trends rather than let MechWarrior stand as it's own IP with it's own gameplay.To start, how does it run? MW5 C might be one of the most poorly optimized modern games I've played yet. I know my machine isn't powerful, but that doesn't excuse the optimization of a game built on UE5, numerous other games have done this infinitely better on the same engine while having greater graphical fidelity. This issue is a fairly severe one for gameplay as you could imagine.Gameplay is one of the biggest shortcomings of MW5 Clans. PGI has never heard of a "reasonably evenly matched fight". This directly effects story, but how does it hold up compared to prior entries? Think old style dungeon boss rushes, as a game. A comedic number of enemy mechs on screen alongside tanks and VTOLs. A very unwelcome change in this regard from Mercs is, funnily enough, bringing vehicles to a tankier state. While they don't come in groups of 20 Light tanks with AC/5s anymore, 10 tankier Scorpions is still a rough thing to fight at the same time as a lance of mechs. Speaking of: The number of mechs you face is downright comedic, and ends up feeling like a slog. Clan 'mechs based on ammo tend to not carry much of it, so you will have to re-design these machines to carry MUCH more ammo as a result, or simply run energy heavy mechs like the Nova, Timberwolf, and Warhawk/Dire Wolf. A direct hamper to gameplay is that your Kit Commander in the intro was correct: this sibko was a semi-aborted wreck of a unit. Unless directly commanded, they are next to useless, in fact, it almost feels actively malicious in some instances. It is incredibly common to run into an AI quirk I call: "Star Commander, get down!" where a battlemech will charge directly in front of you in the middle of a fight, frequently eating your gunfire. To add to the frustration of this, even when directly commanded, the AI are braindead. The simplest maneuver I found to make them absorb fire is to order them 100m ahead of you into a defensive position or play 'mech line warfare. A strange addition are what I can only call Armored Core Bossfights involving dropships. Named character fights are typically laughable since the AI on both sides (remind you, in a game focused on Clanners) doesn't respect the batchall (combat duel between 2 pilots) and will just focus fire the one out front. Even customization isn't safe. A downside of the Omnimech design structure is that your customization options are incredibly limited, which, while lore accurate, is also limiting (I care less about this since builds still can be comedic). TLDR: It's trying to be Armored Core 6The story is weak however, not because the source material is poorly represented (this game is INCREDIBLY faithful to Battletech's lore and has a lot to portray faithfully, you get the feeling they love the setting), but because it's a character story where I DON'T care about the characters. Jayden is not a person, he's a yes man Clanner who has never once stood up for himself and when he does once he never does it again, and of the sibko, I think I only actually came to slightly care about Ezra at the very end. Gameplay DIRECTLY hampers the story too. Usually, you find yourself fighting "Insurrections"... who are flying around in squadrons of Leopard dropships while your Clan still has warships in orbit and Aerospace fighters on patrol. This gets particularly ridiculous when you fight a Gazelle dropship over a Clan-held AIRBASE, where no friendly Aerospace fighters are found, or the Armored Core 6 Helicopter boss in a group of 3. It's weak cast also come with equally weak acting, though it actually improves through the game towards the very end. Sometimes, the writing, while faithful to Clan lexicon and quirks, dives into "What's a -well known Battletech thing-?" territory, which has never felt organic in any game it's ever been tried in. But it's not all negative. I like the weird ethereal chanting and mongolian throat singing in the sound track, which helps make the Clans feel unusual compared to the inner sphere, and the combat HAS moments of genuine greatness where you get a feel for what it can be when it's not copying Armored Core. Those moments are what kept me going when the rest of the game was feeling like worse MW5 Mercs. The other thing is that from the perspective of a lore autist, you'll appreciate some of the little weird things (Such as a reference to Alacorn tank crews using beer cans as tension gauges, even though that's 3055 era thing). It's worth a buy if you LOVE Battletech or MechWarrior, but otherwise, wait for a sale and for major issues to be ironed out. Wish steam had a "Wait for sale" recommend, but it's not worth it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: oHH Man.. where to begin?? YES!!!!! (fist pump) ? Yeah that's a good start. Man, this game is something that I've been C R A V I N G for a long time! Let me state that I have only about 45 mins logged in right now and I was hesitant to purchase the game, especially after seeing "mixed" as the current review status. I decided to not read a single review as I didn't want other people's opinion to influence mine and instead just rolled the dice and purchase the game and, man, am I glad I did! So let me briefly shoot some details in case anyone else is on the fence and curious.PROS:+ It's a Mech game! (free bonus point) + SUPER cool story telling so far, no weird gaps thus far like almost every game out there. Heck, most don't even make sense any more.. What happened to story telling and painting the scene?? Not this game. So far, the beginning really makes me feel like I getting ready to actually earn a spot within the ranks. Pretty awesome in my opinion. + Either First Person (inside cockpit) or 3rd person (over mechs shoulders) view options+ Scan mode lets you find stuff on the battle field, REALLY hoping there's cool stuff to be found later laying around. + Can see a bunch of Mechs as purchase/ earn options + Mech Customization. ie: Load outs, color patterns, equipment options, weapon grouping+ Pilots have an "RPG" style feel of "leveling up" and picking skills/traits you preferCONS- A set group of Pilots it looks like so far. Not sure if there's other options, but nothing I see so far. I REALLY hope that there are options to recruit new or rare pilots later- Intro gets you going to learn the controls, then sort of leaves you to figure out "repairing" and everything else once intro is finished. No real explaining going on. - Even though RPG for the Pilots is cool, it doesn't look like there is a wide variety of options for them. Looks like they get an assigned set of skills/traits and can't really deviate from that. Which sucks for "main guy" if you're supposed to be playing him, then why are his skills blocked in and you aren't allowed to choose? - Overhead Map is pretty cool, just not sure how to really command the other Mechs on the team yet? I assume will get easier with playing.-Changing Mech load outs to reduce weight, does not reduce weight for starting missions. Again, I am only 45 mins into playing. Just seen the game had "Mixed" as the review status and wanted to leave a Positive review, because for me.. So far, this game is REALLY enjoyable and adds it's own twist and story that previous games in this same category just seemed to be lackluster at best. At this point, where I'm at, I definitely recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: They have neutered the game. I can only come to the conclusion that the dev team who developed this game have a significant dislike of Mechwarrior games.Salvage isn't, you just can't salvage and reuse what you find. The game feels like it's on rails, holding your hand every step of the way and you can only behave in this very tiny little box of what's allowed, no more. The tutorial ends with a great example of this, you need to defeat mechs in single combat, one at a time, a total of three mechs. One is considered to be just good enough, two is your goal, and three is a dream. So you play it, you defeat the first, you defeat the second...and you get a cutscene of the third utterly destroying you, you're not allowed to even fight it, final result you defeated two. That's how the rest of the game appears to be shaping up, exceedingly on rails, very limited actual choices during the missions. The list goes on, but I think you get the point.The things that made Mechwarrior great, those were all removed in favor of this...travesty that is inflicted upon paying customers by a dev team that appears to want to end the Mechwarrior franchise by removing all of the best elements of it and putting in an absolutely annoying amount of cut scenes and controls that, even when using keyboard/mouse, feel heavily built on a controller. Kind of like it's a port. Absolutely, and by a huge margin, the worst game in the Mechwarrior series. It's not even close. It's just polished mediocrity, to be generous and kind in my description of it. I hope the devs are ashamed at what they've done to ruin this great series of games.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good, albeit repetitive. Story is alright, but they felt the need to make a cinematic after EVERY mission. And there are a lot of missions, missions that don't need cinematics because nothing really advanced in the story. It's like Dragon Ball Z when every 30 minute episode only advances the story 2 minutes at a time. At it's worst, you watch Cpt. Perez or whoever yell madly about how great and holy  Smoke Jaguar is, but at the same time yelling madly about how Smoke Jaguar is being out maneuvered. This goes on for like 10 missions. WE GET IT, he has teeth and is angry! The cinematics look great, but some uncanny valley creeps in from time to time (and why is everyone always mildly shaking? Hmm Clanners are perpetually mad...).  Most all the cinematics are just repetitive filler dialogue within the Sabrecat crew quarters or bridge. I really think the reason this game is $50 is because they spent A TON of production time on making these mostly filler cinematics. The UI is the weakest part of the game. They have these beautiful lived in detailed cockpits that they overlay an obnoxious bare bones oversized ugly ass UI over. It's one flat color too. It undoubtedly is a default Unreal 5 UI asset (this is why it isn't a $50 game imo).The game isn't that well optimized when a million mechs and particle effects are on screen. This is the same problem in their previous title. I'm disappointed they couldn't do better here. I have a solid modern rig and I drop to 30fps with high settings. But most the time it's running 90fps+ and looks range from ok to great, depending on what you're looking at. The environment and cockpit are highlights, but not so much the mechs, which makes me sad. The battles are too frequently close range brawls; mechs just drop in on you, or appear around a building. This means you rarely get that oh so fun Battletech Star formation that just pulverizes enemies from a superior ranged positioning. I think the map design doesn't help this. The maps should be bigger, and things should be spaced out more imo. This would allow more tactics and actually make the battlefield viewer useful and not an after thought. Also, why can't I see the whole map on the battlefield view??? and why is anything more than a football filed away from me hidden? Do they do no recon or planetary topography?? Better map design would have helped the game play immensely. The AI is pretty bad, it just runs up to you shooting, maybe circle strafing on occasion. They pick the nearest target and switch targets randomly. I'd also venture a guess they have massive cooldowns on their weapons as not to injury the player's Star too significantly. I think smarter AI and less but more powerful enemies would really push this game a good ways towards excellence. So yeah, I just ♥♥♥♥ all over the game (see above). But here's the thing. The combat feels good. The mechs feel good. It's fun to start with a small Star of small mechs and slowly move up the "tech tree". Getting bigger mechs, with bigger guns, and growing pilots into veterancy. It feels SATISFYING to get a new big ass mech, and give your prized possession (e.g. your Stormcrow that has been bae the last 5 missions) and hand it down to your best boy pilot. Oh, and did I mention the Clans are back and the focus of a Mechwarrior game?! About damn time.I think this is more a $30-40 game production, but if you're into Battletech/Mechwarrior the excess cost still won't leave you feeling cheated.

_childDocuments_.review: I am only recommending this if you have a friend to play with. I was on the fence with giving a not-recommend but I cannot do that to a universe that I enjoy greatly that still had some shining moments in the campaign.However, I expected much better than this from a company that I know many people have "donated" large amounts of money to. We deserved better than 5 as well.I won't list the strengths but will instead list the negatives because of the thumbs up I have given - take that as you will. 1. The writing is extremely subpar in moments with clear "this could have went somewhere but didn't" and contains a large amount of meaningless dialogue that intrigues you but leaves you ultimately unfulfilled. 2. Your only agency (minus one single decision at the end of the game) is in the core design philosophy of many Mechwarriors / Battletechs - your mech and your build. Yet, PGI will funnel the average player into "all assault / dire wolf" loadout while 100% committing you to maxing your tonnage out with each drop. There is almost zero variance. Drop max or gain little / nothing for dropping less. There was a lot of potential in this game with little realized.The slap-on decision at the end is a joke, followed by ending the game and being told, "replay the campaign to try a different path!"What path? It was a decision that technically bisects for 3 missions or so down a straight linear path. Meh guys.You'll enjoy it as a long time fan of mecha or mechwarrior, but don't get this if you're new to the series - honest opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy where to begin... so imagine a good game like Mechwarrior 5: Mercenaries... how do we improve it? Well for Piranha Games it's simple, dumb down the game to a shell of it's predecessor, don't improve the moronic AI at all because well people don't want good AI, just pretty graphics, right? The voice acting and writing is erm... interesting? I guess? I mean it isn't super bad at least...Mission structure is... well... it's a bloody mess. Salvage doesn't make any sense, the entire "scanning" system just takes away from the gameplay immersion. I'm supposed to be a big bad clanner, not mr. Scanman on a mission here.  Can I recommend MW5: Clans? No I'm sorry but I most certainly can not. All previous Mechwarrior games simply pummel this one into the ground. If you want a good modern Mechwarrior game and don't have it yet, go buy Mechwarrior 5: Mercenaries, it's a lot better and you've got a lot of well made mods that improve on it's shortcomings (Mechlab is HIGHLY recommended). But Clans... sorry kiddies this ain't it at all. Worst thing is, if you didn't like babysitting 3 AI morons in Mercenaries... imagine babysitting 4 of those now... great fun!
