They stay true to the source material and I found myself on at least a half dozen occasions, jaw on the floor, in complete disbelief that something I had only imagined while reading words from print, come to life before my eyes. The gameplay itself is standard for the MechWarrior series. The Clan mechs feel just as powerful and deadly as they should against their Inner Sphere combatants. The out of mission UI leaves something to be desired but it's workable.This is a story driven campaign first, and a MechWarrior smash 'em all second. If you are not particularly interested in the lore or are looking for a more sandbox experience you can give this a pass or wait for a sale, but for me, myself, full price was perfectly acceptable for this experience. It was everything I ever wanted from a Clan Invasion MechWarrior campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: I overall enjoyed the campaign experience... however some very odd choices in game design. The simpod 'live fire' mission ends at wave 3 then starts back at wave 1... why doesn't it keep getting harder? It's the same mechs and same units that spawn from the same places it seems every time. Why stop at wave 3 dropping one dropship worth of units? Why not drop 3 - 5 dropships of units and have us fight em off? Also, no way to easily go back to the fateful decision warden or crusader and replay from that exact point we made the choice? Literally why?There's a ton more that other people have touched on at length, but I'll say if you're a clanner, and you want to experience the invasion again, it's a buy. If you're a casual MW/BT fan... you can just skip it.Also, I was slow af and even left the game open a few times while not playing, and I already beat it in supposedly 22 hours? Really? Why such a short game?
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot, in good conscience, recommend this game at its asking price.While the game play is incredibly fun, the length of the game is way too short.  There are only 2 or 3 missions after you unlock the Dire Wolf, the only 100 ton mech there is.I am showing 44 hours at the time of this review but around 25 of that was me redoing missions because my machine keeps giving me a blue screen of death when I play single player.My buddy and I completed the campaign, with him hosting, in 20ish hours.  That time includes extensive bouts in the mechlab trying out various builds.It pains me to give this a negative review because I am a huge fanboy of mechwarrior type games.  I waited with high anticipation for this title to release.The story was mediocre while it correctly represented the lore.  The animations are okay for the most part.  The mouths of the characters have a strange quality during the cut scenes that is hard to explain.I experienced numerous bugs while playing single player the worst of which was the BSOD i mentioned earlier.  Strangely when my friend hosted we were able to play almost bug free.In short, wait for a sale... I would probably spend no more than $40 usd.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: i've been waiting for a linear Mechwarrior game with a good storytelling for a long while, and even more for a game focused on the Clans. The cutscenes have blown me away, the story is immersive and interesting and i think even players with little familiarity with the Battletech setting might become interested in knowing more. There are several well-edited youtube videos about it. The game may not be perfect, but it's a lot of what i expected and i think the developers worked hard and with passion on it, and should be supported in order to work on DLCs, more stories, more mechs, and more games with better and better quality content.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Love the idea of playing a story driven Mechwarrior Game. The last one I tried was Mechwarrior for Xbox. Thudding around in a 100 ton robot with OP firepower just feels awesome. I'm glad I played this. However, just a few things to mention:- Character voices over radio transmissions cant randomly drop low in volume.- Destroying some mechs has wonky ragdoll physics.- Sometimes the voicelines can be a bit cringey; especially Perez- My NPC teammates would sometimes get caught on terrain; stuck in a rock crevice.- If you are playing Storymode difficulty, the ending missions may seem a bit anticlimactic.Nonetheless, I'm glad I purchased this game and got to dive back into Mechwarrior lore. I hope there is more to come!
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: I love the return to the story driven linear game play like back in MW4. How salvage works is a bit odd but it needs to be reminded you are playing the clans and its even stated in dialog that the inner sphere tech is worthless to them as it isn't any near as good.Love the addition of armor panels to beef up your 'mech with the extra tonnage if your build allows for it. Also highly enjoy the feeling of having better tech. The way you walk across the battlefield and (if built right) just straight fold inner sphere mechs feels right and is alot of fun. Also accurate to what was going on at the time.My major dislike is the slot system Major example where i ran into this was the Timber wolf prime. arms have 2 energy slots. But those slots are for 2 single slot weapons, cant put a double slot weapon in unless i buy a new omni pod load out. Some of that mouth movements in the cinimatics are goofy as the lips move the jaw dose not.You also get an interesting view on clanner society.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Mechwarrior game.  If you liked Mechwarrior 5: Mercs you will love this.  The story-driven campaign structure is a lot of fun.  The missions are hand-crafted and varied.  The mech combat is fantastic.  Your AI starmates are pretty dumb, as usual.  With specific commands they can serve well enough.  Some of the 'boss battles' are poorly balanced.  A few times an odd game mechanic is introduced without letting the player know that something new is afoot.  The game crashed several times before the patch but after the latest patch is it more stable.I just wish it had the open-world of Mechwarrior 5: Mercs.  I wanted to keep dropping my clan assault star.  It would have been interesting if they had provided later missions that needed and used the lighter mechs.  Once I got my Direwhale I never looked back.  Some of the new salvage system did not make sense at first.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, nothing groundbreaking. Shiny graphics that still need some optimization. Compared to MW5 Mercs, we've got a solid story with some good cutscene animation and unique/varied missions. In exchange, the game is purely a linear campaign, no career mode or the like. On the mechs side, you've got mix-n-match omnipods which allow more flexible fitting with some limits.If you want narrative/story with shooty mechs (and likely some future DLC campaigns), get this game. If you want a career mode with a solid frame for modding and replay value, go with MW5 Mercs.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. Played through the campaign and felt more "Glad that's over." than I did "Let's go again."The battles are monotonousness point and click.The missions and maps are linear.AI is bad. Want to kill that mech? Don't shoot at it then walk behind it and open up into it's back.Star mates are terrible shots. On the plus side, they will stand directly in front of your mech frequently during a battle.The main character and the star mates act more like teens with angst than Clan warriors.There is variety in the game.You get two kinds of boss fights. One where you circle a bullet sponge armed with multiple weapons shooting at you. The other is a bullet sponge with multiple weapons that slowly circles you. Good times.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing Mechwarrior games from a very young age. Battletech is to me what Star Wars was to most other kids. While the franchise has had something of a minor resurgence in the last decade Mechwarrior Online, Battletech, and Mechwarrior 5: Mercenaries,  those titles haven't felt like good, quality outings to me. Mechwarrior Online was only ever an arena shooter despite all of the hype before and during its lifetime. I played a ton of it and enjoyed it, but it felt like a shallow dip into the universe. Battletech, while largely being the ideal type of game to me, ended up feeling lackluster to me due to dumb AI and dull optimal strategies. The roguetech mod made it better, but it also made the performance so poor that it was difficult to keep playing it.Mechwarrior 5: Mercenaries also was a type of game that I really wanted out of the franchise, but the execution just wasn't up to snuff. AI was dumb, and the attempt to make it infinitely replayable resulted in repetitive, unsophisticated deathmatches where you would just fight the stuff that spawns magically at a certain distance away from you. It all felt the same in that game despite all the procedural generation, and the story was sooo dull. Literally talking heads. It did not feel like previous singleplayer mechwarrior titles.Unlike all of these other recent forays into the Battletech universe, Mechwarrior 5: Clans has actually executed decently. Adding real actors, motion capture, and a cinematic focuse to the story to the degree that they have is new for the franchise. It is a very welcome and refreshing addition that actually does a decent job of immersing you in the lore. It scratches the itch I've always had of wanting to see a Battletech/Mechwarrior movie / series. The story is decent, and I don't feel like the devs tried to soften the weirdness of Clan culture too much to make modern audiences feel less alienated. They're blabbing about Dezgra and bondsmen and such, just throwing you into the world without pulling any punches, which I really liked. (Granted, I grew up with the franchise and could see some newcomers being like "what on Terra is going on?")The acting is... generally not great. The main actors for your Star, with the exception of one or two, give bland, monotone performances. Like they are reading from cue cards kind of bad. The actors outside of your star are less bad, funnily enough. I liked the performances for Cordera Perez and some of the other important side characters. It was hard to feel for the characters you were supposed to care most for when every time they speak you are reminded that they are very much actors that aren't doing their jobs correctly.The gameplay is good. In line with previous Mechwarrior games. But the core mech piloting and core combat mechanics have never really been a weakness of the the PGI games. It's always been things like AI and a shallow surrounding experience. This game, I feel, has really done a much better job of that, despite the presence of some poor actors.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a HOTAS user don't expect to just load in and begin playing. This is so dam stupid. Why on gods green earth would you not design a SIMPLE ease to bind interface. Instead you have to go through a complicated BS way to install the joysticks because of lazy incompetent DEVS. If the Dev's are this incompetent is the game even worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of Mechwarrior and avid lover of the Battletech universe for over 30 years. One of my earliest gaming memories was watching two Mechs stomp onto the screen during the intro cutscene of Mechwarrior 2....This game pays so much homage to the canon and universe, it's truely a dream come true for those of us who have immersed ourselves in it over the years (and probably a huge headache for those who don't have any context for the story!)When Mechwarrior 5: Mercenaries released I was elated to have a true Mechwarrior game again. The most heart breaking thing about it was that it came lacking a true storyline. Procedural generation on thousands of maps, reused sound bites, pictures, etc really fell short of the story-driven single player experiences I grew up with.This game is NOT what that is. The amount of voice lines, storytelling, and scene setting is amazing. It is very much worth the price, and should be the gold standard by which AAA-level gaming should hold itself too, if not any form of media who inherits a beloved IP with a deep lore and backstory (something modern media companies are too familiar with destroying)Well done. Absolute master class.I pray to God that they extrapolate through DLC with campaigns, storylines, etc. You will have my money, hands down.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically write reviews, but this game hit me right in the childhood - Battletech was the first wargame I ever played and Mechwarrior 2 the first computer game I ever owned.  While is plays different from the old school games (very similar to Mech 5: Mercs) The makers of Mechwarrior 5: Clans clearly did their homework and understood the assignment.  Seeing high-end cutscenes that felt straight out of the Blood of Kerensky and Legend of the Jade Phoenix book series really took me back to the straight-out obsessions I had with Battletech back in the day.  The game has some rough edges - had a crash or two, and some odd choices (boss VTOLs?), but I am having a great time playing 12 hours in. There's been very few games I've played where I wanted to thank the designers (BG3 is one) - but for sheer fun + nostalgia, I gotta say thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Game's actually good despite its janky presentation. Gameplay is much improved from MW5: Mercenaries whether it's level design, encounter design, or just how piloting a mech feels.My expectations were low following MW5: Mercenaries - despite my enjoying its DLC content quite a bit - and I have to say, PGI delivered an actual good game. Not just good for PGI or good for Mechwarrior but actually good.There's an actual narrative here and it is well executed if formulaic; it gives us enough context and momentum to keep us going, something that was sorely missing from MW5: Mercs. It also correctly paints Smoke Jaguar as incompetent fools despite their technological advantages. The plot's also accurate to the established lore and PGI's respect and love for it is evident.The gameplay is what you'd expect following the previous title but with very welcome improvements. Your star-mates will capitalise on each other's work and focus on open components if you didn't order them to otherwise focus something down. The 3D map view lets you order your star around quickly and accurately, enabling you to let your star-mates take a few hits for you. Friendly AI is also much more accurate in general - I never felt hobbled by the AI, but instead felt like I'd failed to order them properly. Level design is also much improved - no longer are you fighting entire pirate regiments assaulting a facility in the midlde of nowhere and instead are e.g. assaulting a position with other stars for support without having the defenders have 50 mechs too many - all the while keeping the challenge up! Overall, very fun and I kept wanting to see what came next and play some more.Some missions have you go up against artillery positions but unlike MW5: Mercs they're not oppressive. I can scarcely believe PGI managed to strike a balance between artillery making sense and not being incredibly annoying. There's also very few missions where you must destroy buildings, and they make sense in context. You're otherwise free to level anything if you want, so this is mostly a remark on the silly and overused objectives from the previous game. PGI definitely understands that players signed up for mech on mech (and vehicle) action.In general, enemies spawn in places and circumstances that make sense. If it looks like you're walking into an ambush, you're probably right and there's probably some way to frustrate the enemy. VTOLs can spawn where you can't see them but you can also catch them lifting off from airbases. Both of these points make your average level feel infinitely more believable than MW5: Mercs.The "strategic" layer of the game is generally simplified compared to MW5:mercs but that's a good thing. Whether your mechs are repaired in time for the next mission or not is dependant on how many techs you have working, how much damage you took and the quality of the tools the techs are working with - never how much time passed (because time between missions is fixed) or some opaque warzone penalty or somesuch. I was never hobbled by hard-to-keep-track-of timelines. Only repairing takes time. Reconfiguring your mechs for a mission takes no time and costs nothing assuming you have the necessary items. I never felt like these sorts of mechanics added anything to MW5: Mercs and I'm glad to see them gone.There's also a research component to this layer. By simply playing missions and finding extra salvage in them you collect stuff you can spend on research, improving things like weapon damage, mech cooling, extra weapon variants, missile spread, etc. Like with the mechbay and its techs you get scientists and lab quality to play around with. And like the mechbay you're never hobbled or frustrated by not being able to do something with your resources. It all comes easily.The Simpod lets you replay missions for extra reward (and extra constraints if you so choose) or test your builds against all manner of targets, whether standing or in actual fights. Really good feature.Boss fights! Not all of them are incredible but all were a cool changeup from the usual formula. I want to see more of this.Is the game perfect? No. Some of the character animations are bad some of the time and the voice acting, aside from a few characters, ranges from mediocre to passable and includes voice work that sounds like it was recorded with a gamer headset. Mech footsteps are almost inaudible at times.Standard Battletech issues like overcooled, over-engined mechs are still present - you can make a decent Viper, but I dare you to make a passable Gargoyle. I value both of these issues less than some because I've come to expect it from these types of games, but I can't give them a pass in a review. The UI in the strategic layer is very bad. It gets the job done if you know what you want but:These might not be negatives for you:Miscellaneous:
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! The narrative cut scenes are outstanding and engaging---they make me feel like I am with the Clans starting Operation Revival. The difficulty level on "Normal" is very tough for me; I have had to restart almost every  mission several times. I am just now on Turtle Bay and have been playing since Day 1 Launch! I am on Honor Level 5 and am VERY EXCITED to reach Honor Level 10 to unlock the Timber Wolf and the DLC Timber Wolf--that was a great way to give out that content. I am hopeful for DLCs related to this narrative where you get to fight back against the retaliation of the Inner Sphere after the initial invasion arc. Thank you for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Exceedingly rare in this day and age to play a story-driven game and at the end of it wish there was just one more chapter. On closing out the last missions, I felt like I'd finished a really great novel. Kudos to the Piranha team for what they have put together here: it is a real achievement. Another kudos for 100% *nailing* the in-universe lore down to almost every tiny detail (I can hardly believe someone read the 1995 Invading Clans sourcebook to find the background on who wins what trials and why for this game).There are some bugs and some typos - yes, and I expect these will be ironed out with time. But the gameplay is solid, satisfying, and a solid foundation for much more to come. If you are a BattleTech/MechWarrior fan, this is a must-have. If not, you'd still be doing yourself a favor picking this up and immersing yourself in a very unique and interesting setting.(Now if only they'd add competitive multiplayer -- but I'd settle for more story-driven DLCs. Bring us the Wolves, Falcons, and Bears!).
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: A major step up over MW5 mercs in terms of single player campaign and story telling. The characters are likeable, especially with Perez who is just unapologetic and fun. There are also so much lore bits in here that makes lore nerds fangasm hard and I'm all for it!Gameplay is pretty solid, identical to MW5 mercs, but generally far more satisfying with Clan tech so you actually have more time shooting and less down time with overheating. The maps and level design are overall superior to MW5 as they are all hand crafted and not the janky procedurally generated crap walking simulator that make up the 90% of MW5 mercs' games that ends up needing to be fixed with mods.Apart from the great voice acting, the sounds are a downgrade over mercs, the SFX are not as beefy and none of the OSTs are memorable, which is a let down.Performance and optimization is dog water, QoL and glitches do hinder the experience and are my biggest gripe with this otherwise solid experience. Would buy as a mechwarrior / battletech fan. Recommend to wait until the game is more optimized and has improved QoL as a new comer
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: I've been on the ropes about writing a review of the game.It has sparks where it is enjoyable, however something about it constantly feels off.The pilots that become part of your crew all feel underwhelming and seem to whine constantly.They all feel like soulless mannequins with gender neutral faces, haircuts and names. There is zero difference in any of their personalities. They always seem to talk with a clenched jaw. Like they couldn't decide on a direction to go with any character and just hit the randomize all button and said good enough.The Sakhan feels like a toxic boss who is always mad and incessantly barks at you. I don't enjoy this personality type in my games. Guy or girl doesn't matter, it's just obnoxious and takes me out of the game."I need a report, NOW!" -Yells every incompetent boss ever-MW5:M's Major Campbell was an excellent leader and I never felt like she was barking angrily as she talks you through missions. It's a subtle contrast and yet, the difference it makes in the game is massive. The Sakhan's tone and inflection and lack of any kind of tact just straight up ruined the game for me. Yes a Khan is supposed to be a powerful figure, but also an inspiring figure. And yet, I don't feel inspired by any of her dialog to be a proud warrior of the smoke jaguar clan. She is just a toxic boss.I played a fair amount of MW5:Merc and the combat was spot on. I don't know why the combat in this game feels so underwhelming. My initial thought on this is the choice of mech that they start you out with. They start you out with a long range mech build and expect you to fight close range mechs and tanks. I figure it's to force you to use your potato ai teamates. The only command I really used was focus my target. In MW5:Merc's I would often post them up for defense ect. So maybe it gets better in other missions. I didn't make it super far.Like I said it has sparks of a good game. You may enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game. I'm a big fan of MechWarrior since Mercenaries. This game bnrings lots of QOL stuff like technicians that auto fix stuff or stuff that's available in the market when I want to try something new. Story is nice, afaik pretty near the lore. Game is just fun. Especially when your lance.. I mean star consists of 5 Nova with 14 small ER lasers.. Who cares if you're significantly under tonnage if everything gets instantly shredded!
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely recommended for anyone who is a fan of the Clans in Battletech!  If you like the feel of the mechs in Mechwarrior Online and Mechwarrior 5 Mercenaries, you'll love this.  I've been a Mechwarrior fan since Mechwarrior 2 back in the day, and I'm glad to finally have modern graphics, great mech feel, and Clans in a new game.The cinematics are way better than I expected, and they include many nods to the lore.  Those who have read the Battletech novels will recognize places, events, and characters that appear in the scenes.I've just, uhm, "finished" Turtle Bay *ahem*, and finally get to pilot a Timber Wolf again.  I'll definitely be back for another playthrough after this one, and I'm excited to see what else Piranha Games will do with Clans.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't have this on my radar, so a pleasant surprise when it came out.  Very good campaign, something that brought me back to the old days of MW3 & MW4.  With some minor annoyances, it's a very fleshed-out MechWarrior experience.  The storyline balances out the need for some minor narrative license while still feeling like an observer of actual Battletech lore.  Very good assets and mech gameplay: made me feel like I was really a Clanner invading the inner sphere.  Only criticism of gameplay is the same with every MW game, you're forced to rapidly upgrade to heavier and heavier mechs, until it's just a turret simulator.  But still, best MW experience yet, looking forward to DLCs or additional games in this line.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Looks great, only sixteen Mechs (for now), framerate chunks at times, story is nice, could have spent a bit longer in development/QA but I don't hate it and will play more of itThis likely could have used a bit more time in the oven. Its the classic MW experience. I've never been a fan of the Clans or their Mechs, but that's my personal taste not a reflection of the game. The framerate goes wonky pretty regularly, the Mechs and available parts feel a bit bland. However, the animated story bits are well made. The dialogue/story is welcome, though the translation can be a little stiff in places (its very obvious in places that english is not the first language of many of the VAs) which isn't a deal breaker for me. My go to strategy in any MW title is: get Locust, death roll at mach ♥♥♥♥, zip off to repeat the process. That's not an option for me in this game (I understand why, still sad I can't).
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this with rather middling expectations, got completely blown away. I've been having a fantastic time overall.Is it a perfect experience? No, of course not, it never was going to be. The co-op is a little bit of a janky mess, the performance isn't great, the scope is more limited than it could be.Is it a better Mechwarrior game than Mercs? Oh, easily. The story's fun, the characters are fun, I'm looking forward to the Smoke Jaguars getting their butts kicked in from the perspective of the guy getting kicked. You *feel* like you're piloting a Clan mech when you're taking on assaults in a light mech. This is the best Mechwarrior's ever been, and it's only going to get better post-launch with updates, DLC, and mods.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: It is essentially the same gameplay as MW5 Mercenaries, except you're playing as a Star Commander for Smoke Jaguar.  Unfortunately this means that there is only the story campaign and nothing else.  Very restricted customization and a very limited range of mechs make this more of a step down from MW5 mercenaries.  The lack of any sort of expanded 'Career' mode that was available previously kills any real replayability.The performance is very poor, and the game has critical bugs; in the first actual mission there's a mini cutscene where some pirates land after surprise nuking your allied mechs, but that cutscene totally breaks the camera and makes it pretty much impossible to fight.  This happened every time I tried that mission.All in all, this game has a better combat map, but that's about it.  The AI is still retarded and giving them any command other than just telling them to attack the same target as you to bring something down quickly will just get them killed as they suicide charge into melee, ignoring any other enemies.The lack of any expanded campaign or actually getting to manage any kind of organization makes this just an expensive standalone Clan centric DLC for MW5.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: When I watched the first teasers I was excited, as you would be if you are a huge Battletech fan.  But I had no idea it would totally blow my expectations out of the water!  The story is incredible, better than any Mechwarrior game I've had the pleasure of playing, and i've played most, and it was so unexpected that I'm still dumbstuck.  But everyone here is here for one thing and one thing only, and that is the mech combat.  It's carrys over the now fantastic combat of MW5 that it has gained over the years and compounds on that with even deeper features that really bring out the spirit of mechwarrior, even if it still isn't as deep as i'd prefer it to be, but I'm sure that after the modding community gets ahold of it then it may soon be perfect.All in all, yeah it's not as open ended and sandboxy as MW5 Mercs, but the incredible story combined with the relatively good voice acting, all but makes up for the more linear mission style.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: So far the game feels pretty good, there are some well founded reviews on performance which I agree with but overall its an excellent homage to the MechWarrior 2 days and makes me happy. PGI have done a good job keeping this franchise alive and well and have clearly put in some thought to the story driven campaign that any die hard battletech fan (or not) is going to love, for anyone who thinks the clanners voice acting is a bit stiff, it's supposed to be, that's how they talk and I think they've done a reasonable job demonstrating that here. Looking forward to seeing how far PGI take this but they've stuck with it and continue to deliver a sound performance.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Its a Great Game! I can say that this a huge step forward in MechWarrior series! First of all, its a cool and epic Clan story, we have very good cinematic scenario with carefully prepared scenes! The game adapt even to them who never plays MechWarrior series before, plus it have a huge updates in a gameplay mechanics and added many new, such a battlegrounds and scanning mode. I'm highly recommend to try this one, and you simply can start MechWarrior adventure from this part! And of course: "All systems nominal!" to everyone!
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not have any sense of pacing or balance. It will constantly throw wave after wave of extremely resilient mechs at you that you simply will not be able to deal with except by dropping in the heaviest mechs you currently have access to. This completely disrupts any sense of diversity or choice in your team composition - you always pick the biggest mech you have with the strongest armor you can fit with the largest weapons you can buy. Each mission is harder than the last, but not in an interesting or nuanced way - the game doesn't pace itself with quiet or less intense missions where you can take some time to appreciate it. It's always in your face, all the time, with no differentiation. I put it down in disgust about the time a mission was asking me to track down mechs that run away at twice the speed of the mechs it forces you to drop in, and immediately fails the mission if they get too far away from you.Do not buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I highly recommend this game.This is by far the best release in the MechWarrior franchise since 4 Mercs.  Also, for those of us that know PGI and what they release sometimes, they have really stepped it up here.  The story is engaging and based in lore.  The environment is beautiful as expected with UE5.  The Mechlab is a bit different than regular PGI Mechlabs and might be a bit confusing for people not use to how you can customize your mechs, the good news is you can completely ignore it if you don't want to deal with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Great action so far.Cool to see lore presented like this, but I started with Mechwarrior 2 so super biased there.Story so far easily the best in a mechwarrior title.Omnimechs done well so far.Responsive hotfixes so far from the dev team.Scripted missions can have way more interesting things going on in them than procedurally generated ones.Cons but I understand:No Firemoth (it would be ridiculous, I know. But still!)No Elementals (yet?  Please!)No Zellbrigen (doesn't REALLY matter against the inner sphere but a future sandbox where you raid other clan OZs?  Please?)Attn haters:There are fewer mech chassis because once you take a mech out on a mission, you can buy a different set of hardpoints and mix them how you like for the next one.  After a few missions it's easy to get all the hardpoints for a particular mech.  You're now a Clan mechwarrior in one of the biggest, baddest Clans instead of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ small-time mercenary limping around the edge of space.  You don't need hundreds of chassis when you can actually change the hardpoints.  Similarly, there's not a giant sandbox (yet?).Cons:Finally had to get a new graphics card.The Mechlab really needs a cleaner interface with fewer screen transitions and clicking, and faster sorting components by part type.  Give me a sortable equipment list on the side and let me drag it into slots and reject it if it doesn't fit.  Let me select omnipods from a small drop-down on the main internal equipment screen above each component.

_childDocuments_.review: At this point, I am only two hours into the game. I am loving it. I played a fair bit of HBS Battletech and MechWarrior 5 Mercenaries, and I am very into the lore. So, I may be a little bit biased. But overall, I am pleased with what I have experienced so far. It does feel like the focus is getting into the story and the battles, and less on management. Which I think is a good thing for what they seem to be going for on this game.Some not so great things. It does seem a little heavy on requirements. I am running an i5-12400 and an RTX 4070 Super. I am getting around 60-75 FPS @ 4k with DLSS Balanced and Frame Gen On with a mix of Maximum and High settings. It could do with a little more optimization to get the framerate up considering all the stuff I have turned on. Granted, this would probably run a little better at 1440p.Performance aside, I did have an audio issue right at the first mission. There was music, but no sound effects. I had to move the audio sliders down from 100 to 99 and suddenly the sound effects started working (did not have to restart the game). I have not had any other audio issues since. One other weird thing, sometimes enemies will bounce after you destroy them. It does not happen all the time, but it is weird to a tank go airborne after you hit it with a laser. I have a feeling a lot of these issues will get worked out over time through patches. However, if you are a Battletech / MechWarrior fan, I think you will enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic storytelling and the cutscenes add so much to the immersion. As a longtime Battletech fan this game is a must play. My only regret is that the missions can drag on a bit, and become predictable. "Oh, the objective hasn't updated yet, there must be another wave inc- yup, there it is". I also wish there were some missions with lower drop weight that force you to go back to smaller 'mechs. It seems like you just need to keep your drop weight as high as possible and as soon as you unlock the next 'mech, the smaller ones get put away and never used again.

_childDocuments_.review: An insult to the community. You've got to be kidding me. Paid DLC only a MONTH after a disaster of a launch. I'd be laughing if I wasn't so disappointed. How about get your base game to a point where save files don't disappear, the game doesn't constantly crash, and you optimize it to a point of being able to be run above 30fps on medium settings with a half decent rig before you start asking for more money for more half baked content?Gameplay is linear and uninteresting. Time to kill is way too short, sometimes you don't even feel like you're fighting giant battlemechs, but an army of elementals. Mech animations are clunky and awkward at times, which isn't the worst thing until you realize that Mechwarrior 3 did it better back in 1999 so there's absolutely no excuse. HUD is busy and hard to read on top of looking cheap and unrealistic. I feel like there was almost no love put towards the actual gameplay mechanics. It feels lazy and uninspired. I'm a big fan. I wanted this game to be great but it's a step backwards in many ways even to Mercs which I didn't think was possible especially given that the modding community paved the way forward with all the community driven improvements. Piranha had the answers to the test and still managed to screw it up.Here's to hoping that the fixes will come in the future but I'm not gonna hold my breath. How unbelievably broken the gaming industry currently is. I miss the old days, boys.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial thoughts is that there is a solid, story-driven constructed Mechwarrior Clans experience here, but some puzzling choices in UI, sound, and a few game mechanics hold it back a little. An overall fun experience that can be polished and improved upon.Positives+ Overall piloting feels more solid and connected than predecessors+ Visual effects are overall well done and satisfying with a few exceptions+ Story script, cinematics, and general atmosphere has been good so far; doesn't feel forced or overly campy+ I like the general base/resource/research management, but the UI is pretty clumsy to navigate and interact with+ Performance has been good on a strong PC (RTX 3090, 64gb RAM, i9-10850k)+ Sound design is almost great (more on this in the negatives)Negatives- Damage feedback for both yourself and your starmates is muted- it is sometimes hard to tell when you're taking a lot of damage, particularly on starmates where the UI indicates a percentage health which is misleading on the status of their actual mech (a.k.a. sure you're at 95% health, but you just got head shot by a gauss round)- In game HUD is highly obstructive (subjectively speaking), would rather have a more minimal HUD to see more of the actual battlefield- Scanning mechanic gets really fatiguing to use, and is just a generally unengaging mechanic to interact with- Overall out-of-mission UI is quite clumsy to use; assuming it is likely optimized for controller, it generally takes a lot of clicks and drilling into menus to do something simple (unless i missed it, there isn't a mechbay UI that allows full loadout editing on a paper doll like nearly every previous game)- The sounds are really muffled - the underlying sound design clearly feels punchy and impactful, but the mastering treatment applies an overly "padded cockpit" effect, everything sounds extremely muddied- Subjectively speaking, the pulse lasers visual design is really ugly

_childDocuments_.review: I felt this was a breath of fresh air. MW5 was good but shorter and felt a little on the lower end of quality as a game similar to if I played the old MWO today which was okay on its own and great with friends in a semi to large clan. It always feels like Piranha bites off more than it can chew and realizes they have to back off from ambitions by quite a bit.However as these games come out I am seeing some big changes that I have always asked myself if they'd ever do. Better cinematic quality for a start. MW5 felt a little sloppy but lead to a massive improvement in Clans. I am noticing they used the DLCs of MW5 to experiment with liked and disliked features for Clans. Which is a positive thing I think. As long as I continue to see these big strides and bigger more tactical battles I will definitely support Piranha on this journey as they have here. The imagining of what this franchise can become is staggering and I truly hope they can achieve it. Clans made me feel like I was leading a star during the invasion and stuck near the bottom of the rung during Clan politics which I found interesting though not quite what I remember from the books it was enjoyable. Getting over any inaccuracies or lack of certain elements makes it easy to enjoy clan mechs VS the inner sphere as a military arm during a conflict where I am not bouncing sides constantly for money. Just a nice change of pace as much as I enjoyed mercs and a significantly higher quality story here. The characters and animations/voice acting was very good quality IMO leaps and bounds better than 5 Mercs. Hit boxes seemed massively improved as well and the customization of mechs was solid especially once you start playing with the omni variants instead of the whole variant to cater a more personalized play style as you would in MWO. AI is much improved including friendlies, lead them and make use of the tactical map and things will flow nicely with arcs of fire and no one stacked on top of you. 8/10 Over all.

_childDocuments_.review: Delivering the Battlefront 2 campaign experience DICE lied to us aboutPlay as the one of the baddest bads in the Battletech universe, Clan Smoke Jaguar in their crusade to conquer the Inner Sphere. While there will be a learning curve for new players adapting to the unique combat of MechWarrior, the action feels intense and well crafted. No two missions are exactly the same. The Mech Lab is an improvement over MW5: Mercs, offering more customization, and while it does suffer the problem of menus within menus, it is not an overt problem.My only real complaints would be in regard to the Chassis Upgrade and Research systems, via which you improve your mechs and weapons. The prices for these upgrades are far too high. Another issue I had was the difficulty of the later missions, even on the lowest difficulty setting, these missions can be gauntlets that will punish mistakes, low-tonnage stars, and non-optimized loadouts, which makes replayability an issue for these levels.As a fan of MechWarior and Battletech, Clans s a must-play. PGI did their homework with crafting a story that fits in with the lore.Solid 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I would rate this at a 8,5/10. Many of the more mixed reviews are due to lucklaster initial graphics fidelity/performance, some of it mitigated via the first Hotfix. Honestly, with DLSS  and DLSS-framegen, you can max out everything with mid-tier hardware like mine and still experience 80-120 fps with no drabacks.Back to the core of the game: you somewhat need to be familiar with Battletech/MechWarrior to fully follow the (mostly well-executed) plot. Or how Mechs work, or how their armament works, or how Omipods work and so on. While the gameplay itself is - albeit due to difficulty sliders - friendly towards beginners, to fully enjoy the game and understand the story, you need to have some undestanding of the lore and the accompanying "lingo". Great and for sure a plus, if you are a veteran, not so great, if you are new to Battletech. I recommend having a browser-tab on  open if you are not familiar with terms such as "quiaff" or "sibko".If you are somewhat familiar to Battletech, though, this is so far the best incarnation of the Clan-plotline to-date. While some ucanny visuales - weirdly enough mostly main characers - and a hunch of B-tier voice acting and dialogues - have to be endured, the story is surprisingly told well with at least AA-tier visuals underlying it the experience.The core gameplay loop is mech-to-mech combat, with a couple of "boss fights" and "cannon fodder" thrown in between - and all of that is well executed! If you are familiar with Battletech/MechWarrior and its video game adaptations, it leans slightly in favor of MechAssault on Xbox then towards it's more Sim-heavy adaptions on PC, especially compared to a modded-MW5:Mercs experience.  There is quite a bit of character- and research-management attached to it, that - due to a knowledge-hurdles - might overwhelm novices to the series, but might just enrich the experience for more veteran MechWarriors.Not to mention, MechWarrior/Battletech is famous for tinkering with the Mechs itself in the Mechlab. While the UI is slightly favoring console-gamers, it is a workable experience for veteran PC-gamers as well. You prefer ballistic weapons over energy- or missile-based weapons? Just switch the Omnipod! More armor instead of heatsinks? Go for it! Plenty of options to adjust the Mech and therefore the gameplay mechanics to your liking!... However, there are still some balancing issues at the time of writing this review, but PGI has been transparent about fixing some of these issues in the coming weeks. Currently, energy-based weapons seem to outperform missile- or ballistics-based weapons quite a bit. Missiles and ballistics spread out damage way too far and suffer from limited ammunition, while the heat-generation of energy-based weapons seem to be too forgiving.All in all, MW:5-Clans is - at the moment - a very well rounded MechWarrior/Battletech experience in terms of gameplay-loop, with a surprisingly good story and well-written characters with mixed visuals. The gameplay leans a bit towards the arcadey, though there is still depth to be found due to MechLab and the ResearchLab. It could do a bit better in terms of handholding for greenhorns, but for anyone just slightly familiar with Battletech, this is a must-buy!

_childDocuments_.review: So,  I will start off saying, This game is well made, I enjoy it very much. But, it is missing some great mechanics the gaming industry has been adding to games. It also, lacks heavily in the customization department. Now here are some why's:Why are mechs so inexpensive in the store? Why do you get a free mech when you "Research' a new mech?Why are the mechs in the store an optimal chassis from the get go?Why are the plants so big, textures so limited and, biomes of limited variety?This game should have a mech bay with weapons and mechs for you to see and drool over. Constraints of level, weight and slots should keep you on your knees begging for the newest tech. When you deploy to the planet, you should have air, land and, sea assets.  You should be able to play Mech Commander style and Mech Warror style. Storms should obscure the battlefield along with radar and commander vision. Being able to choose daylight and weather conditions for each deployment will keep the limited biomes fresh and enjoyable across many play-throughs.You guys are really close, I think. Keep up the dope work. I would love to make war against my friends in one of my favorite franchises, from the Captains chair to an Ensigns kit. To really show my metal in all conditions against the worthiest of foes. Thanks for hearing me out, much love :)

_childDocuments_.review: Enemies tied to objectives failing to spawn or spawning under the ground repeatedly is causing missions to be impassible.   These are critical thing they should have caught before release, but then this is PGI after all.  Par for the course.Even on 'export' mode the AI are just as dumb as MW5 and will often run right into the middle of your star and stand there getting pounding from all sides. _childDocuments_.review: I'd give MechWarrior 6 an honest 7/10.The game has some production value in the graphics, cinematic, and voice acting department. I didn't say HIGH, it just has *some* production value. It has *some* polish, like your cockpit doesn't need to go flashy when you take damage but it does. However, it generally lacks of polish and production value in key places, like audio or music cues missing in many dramatic moments.That said, it's a competent MechWarrior title. The Mechs be stompy, the guns be punchy, the lazers be lazy.And this time some aerospace craft get involved, so that's cool. I have to wonder if the developers are "OK" after making such a game that really, genuinely does not experiment with the mechanics of the series at all.I have to say that I enjoyed it, but this game is still so, so easy to criticize on points that it falls short. Streak SRMs and LRMs underperform. Streak SRMs carry the implementation from MW5, which is flawed and misrepresents what Streak SRMs are. (they are supposed to be genius supermissiles that can do 180 degree turns around walls, doge obstacles / AMS, target specific parts of a mech, etc).It still has a lot of the AI limitations that MechWarrior 5 has, as well has a pretty bad user interface. It also carried over a lot of bar filling ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ from MechWarrior 5 that really didn't need to be here. And, curious by their absence are Elementals or any infantry partaking in combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game, return of a beloved mech universe, this time with the clanners. 10/10, get clubbed by the telephone company.Generally, got it considering Battletech is a franchise that deserves a lot more love, but like all games, this one has issues. Buy it if you truly enjoy BT, however, i'd save my cash and wait for proper QoL/usability changes because the price asked doesn't warrant a game with so many bottlenecks.Compared to MW5, the game has a great graphic(specially cinematics) and gameplay step up, AI behavior as well. However, this also came with terrible optimization. This leads to severe bottlenecking even on rigs good enough to run the game, with big FPS drops even with everything on low, which makes a few missions unplayable considering the lag to aim properly and the precision required to catch modules like the cockpit, torso, etc.18/10/24 edit:Day-one patches nailed the performance hiccups, gameplay A-OK.

_childDocuments_.review: While I will miss being able to walk around a dropship, MW5C goes into OVERDRIVE with the narrative! I felt like in the front seat of a Battletech novel and enjoyed every minute of it! Watching the sibko members in Star develop/change from chapter to chapter was mind blowing and a bit of a gut punch under certain circumstances - no spoilers. I was deeply amazed by how many characters, events, and locations from the Battletech novel series made the actual appearance in the game in one form or another. Also for the better is that every mission area was 100% handcrafted and not generated at random. Some frame-rate issues were encountered and I had to re-adjust certain graphic settings for certain missions. A bit annoying but something I can look past. For commanding my Star (or lancemates), the AI and direction findings is improved greatly - sincerely, thank you much for that!! Gone are the days they would not fire at incoming OPFORs until they were almost dead and then decided to act or until you got around telling them so. That was my big issue with Mercenaries and I am glad to see that fixed. I did not use the RTS style battlemap/command ability often due to how fast the combat became further in the game (because lets be honest, the mech combat sometimes gets crazy fast, haha), but made up for it with the ability to issue classic F1-F5 commands (which also was greatly improved upon by the developers). At a further date: I hope the developers can bring back the walkable and fully explorable clan warship/dropship/mechbay again so I can geek out over the decks/mechs like in MW5 Mercs, and possibly a career mode, too (wishful thinking, haha). While a stand alone game, Clans is a great sequel to Mercenaries in every aspect. Thank you Piranha Games as this game came with a lot of love for the fans. This is a 10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: This is coming from a long time 5: Mercenaries playerPros:- Guns are shootier, mechs are stompier, laser more pew pew, explosions more crisp, etc... Visually and mechanically everything feels great.- More story focused. You play some great setpieces of the Clan Invasion and take part in the harrowing day to day of a Clan Star Commander, especially being the notorious Smoke Jaguar. Old school players will love this more.- You don't have to worry about finance and hiring and logistics like in 5: Mercs because you're a Clan warrior and you have essentially infinite budget. Also the nature of Omnimechs mean it's essentially swapping boxes instead of tearing apart your mechs like before. Small downside is most of your firepower is on your arms (also due to the nature of Omnimechs) because Clanners are stupid and inflexible so you need to relearn engagements (can't really walk in there and torso-twist to block shots anymore)- The battle map is a good step in the right direction (as opposed to having ♥♥♥♥-all), it gives more control over your lance. The original commanding interface (click there to go there) is still there. Combining both methods, IN THEORY it can lead to some pretty flexible tactical maneuvering, though it requires some time and learn and get used to commanding on the fly as you zip about and getting shot at. But you can mini-RTS some scenario, it's pretty fun.Cons:- You play as Smoke Jaguars. - The characters absolutely suck. Even by 5: Mercs standard where you hire and control faceless goons, many of them still have more personality than the characters here. I guess that's lore accurate, considering they're Clanners, and Smoke Jaguars to boot. - Career mode is non-existent. I love the sandbox of 5: Mercs, and people argue that there's no good story missions and most of it are fillers. That's not true, I still remember charging up the hill with the 2nd Crucis Lancers on Tikonov's moon, or dueling a religious fanatic with the mech in bloodied paint after a grueling raid. The whole point of career mode is to sell that soldier of fortune fantasy, and 5: Mercs does that in spades, though not as good as HBS did with Battletech. You don't manage anything here but pick some shallow skill points for your mechs and determined pilots.- Teammate AI is braindead, still. Somehow after 5 years the devs have managed to make the teammate AI even worse. Most of the time they just suicidal-charge into encounters even when they obviously have the range advantage and geared with a generous amount of LRMs and long range lasers, and get torn up by two tanks and a Locust because they have no backups. Or if you tell them to guard a location they will mostly just stand there and get hit, or constantly running into your line of fire. Elite Clan warriors, my ass.- The music in 5: Mercs were awesome. Simple and hard hitting, it was infused with its mythos and you can feel the bravado, the desperation, the triumph, the wonders and horrors of an Inner Sphere mercenary life. Here, none of that remains, and instead it's generic electronic music. Also in 5: Mercs there were the sounds of missile wizzing by, the hiss of laser burning your armor, PPCs striking your cockpit like a sledgehammer, etc... Most of which are neutered hard here. Most of the time you don't notice you're hit until you look at the paper doll. Can recommend because it's fun for seasoned mechwarriors, though it might be hard to market this to anyone else but series veterans. Newcomers might be lost for a bit, but the learning curve isn't as steep as 5: Mercs as it is more accessible this time around, might be even a good stepping point to go back and explore 5: Mercs.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the campaign in 40 hours playing at a moderate pace without rushing anything or playing more than a couple simulation missions. The game run perfectly smooth locked at 60fps on a Ryzen 5 7500F + RX 7900XT setup in 1440p with almost every graphical setting maxed out except the draw distance (doesn't mean performance would necessarily dip below 60fps, just that I have not tested it as ultra settings do not max out the draw distance).In terms of gameplay, Clans retains the mechanics of MW5: Mercs, but transfers the gameplay to a new, far more demanding engine with much more detailed particle effects. This is important in terms of gameplay, because all the highly detailed smoke, explosions and sparks flying everywhere make pinpoint precision aim at desired enemy components much more difficult simply because the target being shot at usually becomes heavily obscured by said effects. Another change is the mechlab: it is both more restrictive and at the same time offers freedom of configuration not available in MW5: Mercs. Configuration is more restrictive, because Clan Omnimechs come with many components locked so you cannot modify every non-engine/gyro/actuator/life support/etc. crit slot. On the other hand, configuration offers more freedom in terms of achieving desired hardpoint combinations as you can swap Omnimech parts freely and can stuff more weaponry into these custom Clan configs relative to Inner Sphere mech variants with fixed hardpoints. Armor deserves a separate mention, because in Clans you cannot configure your armor distribution and bodypart armor values freely: armor can only be added in 0.25-1.0t increments and each increment consumes a critical slot. This is a very significant change as now you may be forced to make compromises between weapons/ammo and armor not just based on total tonnage, but also based on the available critical slots in a particular location. The inability to freely redistribute armor between front/back also means you cannot simply strip all of your back armor and put it on the front. The end result is that most Clan mech configurations are significantly under-armored relative to the maximum theoretical amount of armor they could mount.The story in this game is head and shoulders above anything in the franchise so far, it's an amazing clan slice of life that demonstrates many customs and behavioral patterns like no other game in the franchise has. It also has a degree of non-linearity, introducing a different set of endgame missions based on player story choice.All in all, the game was well worth the full pricetag at launch. Unlike MW5: mercs, the experience has been 100% stable and bug-free. It feels like PGI really jumped out of their skin with this release and delivered a product above what would be typically expected of them and I know what to expect from PGI having played MWO since open beta.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Mission design is fun and I enjoy the interactions between the characters in the Star.- Beautiful environments, Mechs, and weapon effects.- I really enjoy the characters and story so far.- The cutscenes are amazing.- The gameplay is fluid.- Scratches the itch for giant Mech on Mech action.- Improves on the story telling / mission style form MW5: Mercenaries- Despite its cons and need for improvements, overall it's a fun game and enjoyable experience which makes me excited to see where they continue to go with the franchise.Cons / possible improvements:- Mech Bay is not intuitive and omni-pods feel like they force you to play with the presets and discourages customization.- Missions need to have a better start and end. The way your star gets brought in and dropped off is jarring and I miss the proper Mech startup at the start. The missions end in an awful way of simply cutting to black and suddenly you're back at the mission select screen unless there's a cutscene. - Post mission details and statistics could be much better. I'd like to see the actual statistics behind the most damage, kills, etc. Also, adding lifetime statistics to the campaign.- The game is clearly made to be played with a controller and heavily under utilizes the keyboard. They need to take a page from MechWarrior 4 in this regard to what is possible.- The story and characters can only really be appreciated if you have existing knowledge of the clans and background to the existing universe. - Not much is done to explain why the Clan is the way it is, certain behaviors, and words. It could greatly benefit from an Appendix giving some sort of background.- No history provided on the Mechs the Clan uses.- The RPG elements for the characters in the Star don't feel very fun or that they make too much of a difference.- Understanding how you can use your requisition points is not clearly explained, for the longest time I didn't know I had to upgrade my technicians or that I could until looking over the achievements...- Not being able to see my Mech's experience points in the Mech Bay when customizing. You only see what you have if you go to chassis upgrade or select unlock on an omni-pod.- The AI need some work. They're so focused on being in formation that they'll completely turn their back and disengage from enemies while getting shot to try and move behind you. They struggle to help if you're not consistently giving them orders to target an enemy Mech. - Lack of ammo... it feels like you're heavily punished for taking SMS and LRM missiles.- Science research to buff your Mechs isn't very fun or intuitive.- No reason to use light / medium Mechs later in the story, so using affinities for specific light / medium Mechs punishes you later in the game.- Overheating no longer shuts down your Mech, plus Mech shutdown for repairs is just a black screen...- Spoilers in the hotfix... don't read unless you haven't quite finished it like I have.

_childDocuments_.review: I am having a great time with this game. It has an interesting story and characters that vividly portray the first Clan invasion into the Inner Sphere from the Clan Smoke Jaguar perspective. The story is very well told, and the cutscenes are impressively crafted.I played MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries but lost interest because I couldn’t get invested in the story, and the procedurally generated world maps felt dull and too similar to each other. In contrast, the level designs in this game are much better—sometimes even breathtaking.Playing this game reminded me of the Wing Commander series because it makes you feel like you’re part of the Clan invasion, fighting alongside your Star mates, who I grew to care about over the course of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: This is a throwback to the days of MW2, MW3 and MW4.  A narrative, mission-based game that covers the story of the clan invasion of the inner sphere.  Its not an open world sandbox style game like MW5:Mercs, this is a series of missions with a storyline told in the form of cut-scenes.  In terms of positives, the story is actually rather engaging, there is quite a wide array of voice acting skill on display from decent to very good. I was pleasantly surprised, I just wish that the main protagonist had a slightly more compelling voice actor.  The combat is good.  I have a Hotas setup and its working well for me (although I have heard that some people have had issues here).  The mechs feel fairly weighty (especially the heavies and up), the effects are good, and the AI of your companions is much improved over MW5:Mercs.  On the whole its a very fun game to play.Now for the negatives:  The mech lab UI is... poor.  It took me quite a while to get used to it.  The game also doesnt explain how the salvage, research, repair and upgrade systems work which makes the initial foray into the game a little confusing if you're used to MW5 or battletech.  I will add that there are reports of performance issues with this game, but I cant comment on that because for me personally, the game actually runs very well and I've had consistently high FPS throughout.Overall, this game is a really good standalone narrative mechwarrior game in the same vain as the old classics.  The story is engaging, the combat is good, the maps are far better than MW5:Mercs, and the missions have twists, turns and variation because they are all hand crafted.  If it had a better mechlab, better UI, and perhaps some information to demystify some of its systems then I would give it a higher rating.  As it stands its a 7/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: MechWarrior games are like sex—even when they're bad, they're still pretty good. In this case, you've hit the jackpot and scored great sex. _childDocuments_.review: While the story itself is decent, I have to say that this game ultimately left me disappointed. If you enjoy watching cutscenes more than actually playing the game, then this might be right up your alley—but for me, it missed the mark in terms of gameplay.The restrictions on Mech classes are far more limiting than what you’d find in Mercenaries. In fact, it feels like there’s less variety and customization than I expected. One of the few highlights for me was getting to pilot a Mad Cat (Timber Wolf), which is something I’ve always wanted in Mercenaries—except that it usually required mods to make it happen. So that was a nice touch.Unfortunately, the game was an utter disappointment in other areas. Many of the weapons feel useless, and I found myself relying almost exclusively on ER lasers for the majority of the game. And when it came to Mechs, I couldn't even choose which ones or which weapons to salvage, which felt like a major missed opportunity for deeper strategy.The MechLab is a fun little distraction, offering plenty to unlock, but it doesn’t really enhance the core gameplay experience. In the end, this game feels like a watered-down version of a Mech game, and after about 20 hours of play, I was already bored and ended up going back to Mercenaries, which is far superior in comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I'm about halfway through the campaign. Its important to note that PGI is not a AAA game studio, for as much as that term means anything today. This is by far the most impressive game put out by PGI, and while the mechlab and upgrade mechanics are janky, the most important part, the actual gameplay, is top notch, intense, and an accurate portrayal of how much clan tech steamrolls over inner sphere tech. The narrative acting is also somewhat uncanny, but impressive for the likes of PGI. This game is a deep love letter to the battletech universe and is a lore-accurate game that respects the setting and franchise.If you are not deeply familiar with battletech lore, there is a good chance you might get lost. This story puts effort into providing context to who the clans are, why they are invading, etc. but I can't imagine someone going in cold without knowing much about battletech to really fully get what's going on, though I don't think the game suffers too much for that. If anything, this could prompt newcomers to brush up more on some battletech lore if what they see interests them. I can't expect this game to basically become a Sven Van Der Plaank video explaining the star league, the amaris civil war, the exodus fleet, the transformation into the clans, and the intervening succession wars. This is the game we have been waiting three decades for. Its imperfect, but its exciting to see this setting be alive and well after so many years of legal and development hell.I just wish there was checkpointing in-mission, I've been struggling with intermittent crashes.

_childDocuments_.review: This was without doubt my most anticipated game in 2024 - as an older gamer with a limited amount of free time to game I was looking forwards greatly to this, having been a huge BTech fan from when it first came out on tabletop. Like WH40k its the huge lore that is most fascinating to me, and which keeps me interested.Now, onto the game - its a solid meh from me to be honest, for the following reasons.1. Frame rates bounce all over the place, severely impacting game play. I've got a reasonably competitive games rig but seriously? Even reducing settings seems not to help much.2. The implementation of the Lore - oh sweet baby jezus, WTF have you done with the Lore? the Characters dialogue and attitudes/behavior appear to have been written by US West Coast Millennial's who to have never read Clan Lore. This is supposed to be about Clan Smoke Jaguar, the fiercest and most Crusader of all the Clans, a society that has been cut off from the rest of humanity for over 2 centuries and which has absolutely 'gone its own way' and which has mores, attitudes and behavior that is utterly alien to the Inner Sphere.           2a. Where are Clan warfare rules implemented? Where is the Batchall? (for example as a really, really easy thing to implement in game - you should earn more honor for having an underweight Star). Where is Zellbringen? Again, if you stick to this Clan rule you should earn more honor (merits).          3a. Where are my Elemental's?  These are as critical a technology advantage as Omni Mechs, the lack of them is a very serious oversight on the part of the DEV's IMHO.          4a. There better, BETTER be a story arc for Jayden to earn a Bloodname in the next DLC.......4. Kerensky's and Honor (merits) - this system seems to be poorly designed and thought out. There should be an ongoing (impactful) cost for the maintenance of your Omni Mechs and the consumption of ammunition, and the salvage and honor system needs tweaking to make it more of 'cost/benefit' analysis for you to manage. As of now it just scales annoyingly.    5. Boss Fights - really, really? There are much better ways to implement escalating challenges than just cheating on the number of hitpoints and NPC can have. 6. Missions are too linear and also place far too much emphasis on scaling up the tonnage of your Mechs. Make some missions require lighter Mechs for their speed or you can complete the mission by a different route using assault Mechs (for example). Segregate some missions into those where only certain weight classes can be brought. I really, really like playing medium Omni Mechs as the game is just so more exciting imo when you are in a lighter class Omni Mechs.7.  Clan warships DO NOT have artificial gravity and they are arranged with 'down' towards the stern and 'up' towards the bow - think skyscraper as opposed to a factory. Or in other words they do not have the same deck layout as water borne warships. So unless the Clan warships are under acceleration they are in conditions of micro gravity, this may seem like a minor point but it does speak to a wider lack of keeping to the letter and spirit of the Lorre.    Would I recommend it to a BTech fan? Nope, because it does not adhere to the Lore closely enough. To the casual gamer with not a whole lot of knowledge of BTech, sure, it a reasonably good mech game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great mech combat in the tradition of mechwarrior 5 with improved graphics. Campaign is about 20-25 hours of gameplay depending on your play style it might be faster or slower. There is a lot more control over your other mechwarriors than in MW5 merc. although tbh the map placement of units I might have used it once but I am not expert at this.   The customization options for mechs are a lot diffrent from MW5 you need to earn your omni-pods (alternate configurations through a mostly linear mech xp system although this can be sped up dramaticly with lots of pilots focused on one design and meeting kill objectives faster.  But Expect 2 missions after you unlock a mech to unlock new configurations.

_childDocuments_.review: I will not get into what is Battletech/Mechwarrior, it would take me thousands of words to even begin describing it. So, just go look for what is it exactly on the web. Just know that this game set in this universe is just a tiny bit in the direction of a simulation, out of an action game.Mechwarrior 5: Mercenaries had procedural missions throughout the Inner Sphere. Mechwarrior 5: Clans has a scenarized campaign with lots of demos and voice covering. Right now it is the Smoke Jaguar Invasion campaign. But supposedly future DLCs should cover other Clans campaigns.I have read a lot of complaints on the forum regarding optimization, the mechlab, ideologies, whatever, you name it. I did not meet much problems and I do not care about most of the complaints. The game is good, I got what I came for, if for a higher price than what I would have expected.It seems though very easy so far (I am playing default difficulty) but I am not far in the game, maybe about the half. Being cored is very forgiving, repair is very forgiving if you develop your techs, optimiziation is very forgiving if you focus on what the Clans are best known for: lasers and heat management. They are very good for missiles too, but for some obscure reason, the designers decided to have a minimal range for clan long range missiles, which does not exist in the boardgame, but to extend their range. They still have their use though, especially in open terrain, obviously.Be warned that the mechlab might be hard to understand in comparison to previous titles in the brand... and there is near to no point in concentrating on lower weight chassis as the campaign move quickly to heavier ones.Be mobile or die, or stay behind and snipe. Concentrate your fire. Do not fight alone or die alone. Rinse, repeat.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: there was a pretty big issue on launch where using any UI with the mouse was extremely difficult, requiring you to spam left-click to get anything to activate. This seems to have been resolved today with the patch, though I didn't see anything in the changelog that seemed related. I was able to play without issue today, which is awesome!I should also note that I reached out to PG's support yesterday, and they got back to me very quickly, so I'll call that a win, too!As to the game: I really dig it. I have played battletech games I liked more, but this one is new and pretty, and it's pretty fun to play. I'm not quite getting the mid-90s feel of MW2, but I have been chasing that dragon for more than 20 years at this point. There's still a glint of it there in MW5:C.The missions feel fairly challenging, requiring you to be relatively tactical instead of running in full throttle, especially early on as you start out with a fairly light loadout.Others are mentioning things about the cutscenes, and they do kind of look awkward sometimes, but it's not terrible. The mouths seem to have some "pucker" to them, can't quite put my finger on what exactly is weird but it's not so off-putting as to ruin the story. Call it "odd."I am not too fond of the Mech Bay here. It's fine, but it'll take a little exploring to find what data you need and figure out how to use it. I wish it were easier to compare components, too, but maybe I'm missing something.I haven't played too much yet, just a couple hours over two days, but after the launch issues, I like what they've put out.As to performance: I had some slight jank on launch, occasional frame drops but not enough to bother me. After the patch, completely smooth with only shadows turned down to medium and DLSS set to Quality, running at 4k. I was actually quite impressed by how smooth it was compared to things before the patch.Note: DLSS and FSR are not enabled by default. You must go change this yourself.Specs:i9-10900K @ 3.7Ghz3090 (slight overclock)64GB RAMRunning this on a fast m.2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to write.Let's start on the good side. MW5 Clans is an incredibly high effort game from Piranha on the gameplay and story side. Cut scenes are gorgeous and you can really tell the writers did their homework on Clan society. They might have done the Clanners a bit too well, as their dialogue can seem really stilted and awkward at first glance. Which, surprisingly is accurate to the source material. Clanners are weird. Like not allowing warriors to use contractions level weird. Very good work.The moment to moment gameplay is really solid as well. The mechs feel weighty, but agile. You really feel like your mech is a highly advanced fighting machine. No complaints hereNow the bad;The game runs horribly for me and a lot of others. Long loading times, massive frame drops (down into the teens) are incredibly common, and bad hitching and stuttering really break the flow of fights. I can't recommend it on this alone.If they can hopefully better optimize Clans in the future I'd gladly return to it. As it is now though I can't recommend anyone purchasing it on a mid level PC for full price.
