_childDocuments_.review: Alright! This *feels* like Mechwarrior, again. No more cookie cutter terrain, buildings, and missions. The combat feels better. The AI seems to... well... AI! It's not perfect, nor should it be, but it's not plumb stupid, either!The cut-scenes really do give you that Sci-Fi warlord feel. You can feel the universe come alive, and I find this iteration of Mechwarrior actually does the best job at conveying that!After the first 2 hot fixes, I am immensely satisfied! They fixed the controls constantly defaulting on you on PC in hotfix #2. (along with plenty of other fixes)I think my largest critique is like many others are saying. The menu between missions! The whole frontend system, really... Too many layers, not very informative of what you about to get into with some of those layers, and then some menus just have way too much information displayed at you at once, only to go deeper into layers (and lose some of the info from the last menu) like when going from the Mech Lab overview to selecting an omnipod.One last criticism. This might just be how I played the previous games (MWO, and MW5 Mercs), but I do not see a keybind for toggling chain fire! I have to press M, and navigate with the mouse cursor to toggle that in the weapon groups. That takes away from combat, sits dead center in the middle of my screen pretty much, and takes away from immersion. Plus, I put Weapon Groups 1 through 3 on my mouse buttons (left, right, middle in that order) and 4 through 6 is the same, but the CTRL key has to be held down, too. So I'm going to sometimes run out of weapon groups for when I want to chain fire vs fire everything in that group! This is an issue for heavier mechs with diverse loadouts, and multiple lasers, for example. (I have already experienced this in Clans.)But other than that, I love this game! Clean up the menus, especially the mech lab, and add a chain fire toggle, and we are golden!I especially love the new feature of being able to press a key to enter Scan Mode! Keeps me on my toes with switching back and forth when I can to get those extra goodies! And objectives!The overall flow of combat and missions feels really good! It can get intense at times! And not in a frustrating way like in MW5 Mercs.Thank you Piranha Games! I feel like with all the flak you people have gotten from MWO with the "call of duty like twitchy gameplay" improperly distracted from what you were really doing well. I for one thoroughly enjoy MWO. Well over 1000 hours in that one! I recognize the hard work it took to balance that out over the years. I'm a software developer, myself, but not really a game developer because of the extremely detailed QA testing involved. But I can certainly appreciate what I see and understand why it's so important! You people have come a long way since then. Keep it up! And thanks for listening to us... I can tell it's paying off!

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: I have played almost every Battletech/Mechwarrior video game. Yes, even the SNES ones.The Good:- Story is pretty great (devs certainly know their Battletech lore)- Not short, like a lot of games these days that charge 20 more Kerenskys.- The voice acting is definitely a step up from previous MW/BT games.- Gameplay is quick and fluid; you certainly feel like you have a technological advantage over the spheroids.- The level design is 500% better than MW:5 and locations feel like actual locations instead of set pieces.- Graphics are a huge bump up from MW5:Mercs.- Omni parts mixing/matching is kind of neat and makes up for some of the mechlab restrictions.The Bad:- Mechlab is not super robust (lorewise to be expected but still wish it were deeper)- Not as replayable as MW5 Mercs since it is narrative driven rather than sandbox- Limited mech selection (though you do get several omnipod variants).- The unlocks for mechs is gated behind 'honor' before you can purchase them, but don't see the point there since there are still tonnage restrictions, so it just feels like carrot/stick progression gating- Would have also been nice to have a reason to run light/mediums later in the story instead of 5x Timberwolf murder parties- Gameplay may be a turnoff for some who prefer the slow plodding tanky feel, as this is quite a bit faster.The Ugly:- The facial animations are sometimes...well, they exist.The Summary:Overall, this is a great entry in the Battletech video game universe and worth the purchase. I will probably eventually go back to Mercs, because I prefer the gameplay loop there, but this is a very good narrative experience and a good mix between MechAssault-type gameplay and walking turrets.Glad to see Battletech is seeing a renaissance, and I will always be appreciative to Piranha for resurrecting Mechwarrior as a series.

_childDocuments_.review: Way worse gameplay and way less fun compared to MW5 Mercenaries. In MW5 mercenaries I had a lot of mech customization choices, armor vs. heavier weapons, or more ammo, or jumpjets. This was dumbed down for MW5 clans, really all I'm choosing is which weapon I bring or a few special parts that give minor bonuses that aren't worth the weight vs. bigger weapons. Plus the galaxy map gave me the opportunity to find rare weapons so I could explore around and carefully ration these weapons. That's gone now, you can just buy unlimited quantities of weapons and parts, and money is easy to come by.Heat has very little effect, in fact I thought there was no heat system at first as I kept getting hit by flamers and it never had any noticeable effect. This takes away what was a fun gameplay balancing element between ammo based and heat based weapons. In fact managing heat is supposed to be a core concept in MW5 so I don't understand the design decision to dumb it down.In Mercenaries I had salvage options to get rare mechs or rare weapons. Now you just get parts, which are effectively just another form of money you spend on the poorly explained upgrade system. The upgrades themselves are weak and not worth navigating the bad UI, such as +5% to laser weapon range.Framerate is bad despite the graphics not being much better than before. Environments are bad too. Not only less interesting to look at, but the layout of the environments and missions feel low-effort, without much cover or high ground to take advantage of. Destructible cover and cities was a big part of the tactical gameplay of Mercenaries, I've yet to encounter that.The only improvements are the 2D tactical interface to command your mechs, and the story line. Even then the characters are woke, and the acting isn't very good.I don't usually buy games at full price but did so here as I'm such a big fan of MW5 Mercenaries. I'm very disappointed as this game is 1 step forward and 2 steps back in comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: Realiy love the challenge of playing the video game on Expert Diffculty from the start and attempting some of the very hard missions multiple times before succeeding. In order to complete the campaign on Expert Diffculty, the allocation of points into the 6 different areas of the pilot's skillets is very important including how to prioritize loyalty points at various stages of the campaign to upgrade the science lab, mechbay including the effectiveness of the number of scientists & technicians. I find that prioritizing salvage operations  early on is incredibly helpful where at one point I spend around 400 loyalty points upgrading it in one go. You do not need to unlock all 16 available mechs as there are always some mechs that vastly overperform other mechs in the same mech class.Of course as others have mentioned, the mech bay customization is serious lacking when compared to MWO and MechWarrior 5 Mercenaries. I am willing to overlook this as this is the first video-game about the clans in over two decades.  As someone who have been immersed into the books and franchise since Mechwarrior 3 in 1999, i have given this game an Overall score of 85 out of 100. Sincerely hope for multiple story campaign DLCs for this video game over the next several years.

_childDocuments_.review: The takeaway:  if you're looking at this game and are even slightly interested, I strongly recommend it to you.It's clear that this game has downsides:  the cutscene actors look like they are always trembling due to some engine artefact.  The UI for the mechbay and for research is bad, sometimes even very bad.  The RTS-style command screen is pointless without being pausable.  It's frustrating as these problems don't seem that hard to fix, and they're entirely superficial.  Lots of people won't see past that.  But if you do look further, this is a very good game, easily the best MW action game.  There's much more mission variety, the combat is faster paced and more fun, and the story is very good and well acted (which really is saying something compared to some moments in the last game).The first and last of those were major problems with the original MW5, which also suffered from a lack of polish on launch.  Presumably this is down to the resources at Piranha's disposal, but this is certainly a vast improvement on a game I already enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly the narrative driven MechWarrior/Battletech game we've wanted for decades. Ever since I was a kid I would replay MechWarrior 4 Mercs about once a year and still do just for its campaign. The way this game has gone so far I can easily see doing the same for it. I've waited so long for a Clan centric MW game and they've delivered beyond even what I thought PGI was capable of for this. Each cut scene and cinematic is oozing with the series' rich lore, and it's apparent they really paid attention to every last detail to be as true to cannon as possible. Many things shown in-game are the first serious depictions we've seen outside of old line art, and I couldn't be happier with it.I've played nearly 15 hours so far without a single performance issue or bug, it's been fantastic just being able to dive in and play. My only minor gripe so far is that the mech roster is VERY limited. Due to some of the classic omni mechs not having been done by PGI yet, you're limited to a whopping 9 chassis for the entire game. They leaned in hard to the era appropriate front-line omni mechs that would be used by a Clan SJ galaxy, and it unfortunately shows when most missions you're running 2-3+ of the same chassis. This is not a huge deal as the chassis available in game all have their niches and are distributed in tonnage very well, but it is certainly a small pool to choose from.Overall: fantastic game and I have yet to be able to put it down. Hopefully future content adds more mech choices.

_childDocuments_.review: What I felt was better than MW 5 mercs:a) Better graphicsb) Better weapon effectsc) Better Sound Effectsd) Better story driven campaign e) Way better Missions f) cooler cutscenesg) Easy control mode is a nice feature for new playersh) Some occasional boss fights are nice additioni) MISSILE SMOKE TRAILS!!! The game has fantastic smoke effectsWhats not so great about this game compared to MW5 mercsa) A PC that could comfortably run MW5 mercs in high settings(RT off, dlss : quality) at over 90fps can barely  hit 50fps at low to med settings. So if you own a RTX3060 or lower gpu, you might want to try frame generation using the "lossless image scaling" program available on Steam which i personally found really helpful.(practically doubles the fps from 40 to 80 for smoother game play with very barely noticeable visual degradation).b) No option to turn RT off (dunno if its on by default or not supported at all)c) wonky hit detection most of the time. Shots aimed at the head of enemy mechs ends up hitting the torso more often than not.Conclusion:If you are a veteran MW5 mercs player then it might take a little bit of getting used to the changes and limitations of the clan mech bay. The inability to remove locked equipment may get a little frustrating at times. However, I love the game play and the story even though im not even close to finishing it and I definitely  recommend this game to other players who are considering buying it, especially if they loved MW5 mercs.

_childDocuments_.review: This started out being ok but it gets better and better as it goes along.  The rest of my review still applies but now I highly recommend this.  Getting old wing commander vibes.More arcade like than Mercenaries:  The mechs are much more responsive with torso twists, turn speed etc.  In Mercenaries the slower torso turns give it feel like you're in a large machine, mercenaries turn rates and acceleration are slower and you feel like you're lumbering along in an 80 ton mech.  I don't know if it was intentional but it feels less weighty and more twitchy.Weapon graphics are more over the top while melee isn't.  I'm a fan of Mercenaries weapons graphics while in transit to the target.  While clans  PPC hits and LRM explosions are nice it feels less realistic and more cartoonish.  Melee is so underwhelming compared to mercenaries.  The muffed tink when you hit with a melee attack is less than satisfying. The little to no feedback makes it hard to tell if I connected.The red wall fake boundaries are a lazy way to hem in the combat areas of many maps.  Every time the you have left the combat area counter pops up while I am in a fight because the combat area is so tight I roll my eyes.Linear story is more like Mechwarrior 4 which is fine.  I would have been overwhelmed with joy to have an expanded Mechwarrior mercenaries universe with Clans but having to change and introduce everything would probably have been to much.  The story is solid although I don't like the end of the trial of position. Currently just started hitting the heavy mechs and the game is becoming more fun. In mercenaries I really enjoyed the lighter mechs while in clans light mechs don't feel right compared to medium and heavy.Mechs - the omni pod system, repair system are fine.  Having the freedom to change out individual pods and add armor/weapons to preference is probably the best system in this game. Having to unlock pods with experience is probably the dumbest.  The research system makes no sense in the setting except extra grindy fluff.  Clans mechwarrior experience system isn't "Mechwarrior" and that bothers me: piloting, gunnery etc have been replaced with more specific skills.  Having to "unlock" mechs makes it feel like you're being slowed down on purpose...actually all of the between fight tasks feel like you're being slowed down.For advice I would say the thing that helped me the most was being able to modify my mechs to diversify weapon locations and add armor to arms.  The pod system focus on arms for most of the weapons makes it more difficult to get through the rounds of attrition with all your weapons.  Being able to unlock the pods that allow me to put weapons in the torsos helped but adding even a half ton of armor to each arm almost doubles light mech arm survivibility.I (highly) recommend this game, IT"S Battletech.  There are missing components that could have been. The elementals which were so prevalent in the books are missing, and to me are a huge missed opportunity. The writing does a fair job of providing clan culture without outright giving you a history book to read but more history components would have gone a long way.  It would have been amazing to "bid" for missions against other stars but again how much can you stuff into the game.  The invasion feels empty, not enough ships, not enough other stars, not enough of everything. But it's battletech and does a fine job of giving you combat in mechs along the way with a good story that fits into the history.  I'm happy to give you my money for more Battletech that isn't that online abomination.

Functionality wise we haven't lost too much from the base game, but after coming from YAML in MW5 it's pretty stifling.- There's likely little replay value in this game. _childDocuments_.review: O. M. G.!!!  Yasssss!  Love Battletech since the 80's tabletop.  Played every BT and MW game out there.  Still play MW online and MW Mercs, but now this!  Huge story upgrade from MW Mercs, complete with compelling acting, storylines I wanted to listen to and watch (not just spam spacebar to skip),  plot "twists" and one tough decision for the player.  Significant upgrades to MW Mercs!!!I get that some people want every 'mech to be fully customizable head to metal toe, but within the lore, OmniPods are what they are.  Let's look at today's military for reference, a heavy armor tank carries one main gun and 2-3 secondary systems with occasionally an optional extra accessory like smoke grenade launcher, mine flayer etc, but no one tank chassis can be anything/everything.  Why is it so anathema to these trolls that each 'mech chassis is built with hard-wired internal support, scructure, electronics and connections that similarly place some limits on weaponry that can be attached?  You want more dakka?  Pick a different chassis.  You want more pew pew, pick yet another chassis.  Or with the Clan mechs, just try a different OmniPod instead of a whole chassis.  IT MAKES SENSE.  Ignore the trolls, they are just min/max optimizers to the nth degree and aren't fair evaluations of the game simply because they can't mount an AC/20 and nine SPLs on a 40-ton chassis like they theoretically could on paper.Yes, there are quirks with the modding of loadouts within the OmniPods, but does it break the game?  NO.  Even playing the game a lot, I admit that anytime I'd step away for a few days and come back, I had to re-familiarize myself with the various screens and menu options to make changes as a result of the less than fully intuitive modding UI, but that was a minor annoyance worth maybe a half-star deduction out of a 10 stars possible.  Not "this game sucks".  I'm old, and "grumpy against worthless trolls", and 2 bourbons into the evening, so I'm venting against them... this game is DARN GOOD to GREAT.  I challenge anyone who disagrees to a Batchall!  Quiaff, freebirth???

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game that tells a big part of lore for the clan invasion. It looks like the vast majority of bugs have already been fixed, which is great.  There's still a few minor ones which will likely get resolved over the next month. The campaign has a pretty satisfying story arc from start to finish. I feel like they left a reasonable opening for a couple DLC/expansion packs down the road, which is nice. Hopefully there will be some good mod options as well. My only remaining gripe with the game, is the same with most mechwarrior games. That is, it's constantly pushing you into bigger and bigger mechs. After the opening few missions, you'll likely never look at a light mech again, which is too bad. Sure you can replay missions with light mechs, but it would be nice if they sprinkled a few missions in later in the game with weight caps or incentives to use smaller mechs. Not everyone wants to just roll in 100 ton mechs every time.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, it's big stompy robots. So it will scratch that itch.Overall, story line was decent, if a tad predictable. Unfortunately, the linear story with no room for you to wander means this game has very little replayability unless you are achievement hunting, or just want to try different load outs.Speaking of load outs, you will probably be slightly disappointed. It has all the basic weapons that you would expect, and with the research system you have the ability to improve their performance, but you will probably find that almost all of the weapons are underwhelming when compared to lasers. Even with character specialties in the mix, if you experiment you will find that laser boats will simply put out more damage than any other weapon. It's enough of a difference that even just playing casually, you will notice it. I'm a die-hard Autocannon fan, I love using them and I just couldn't bring myself to do it in this game. The vast majority of settings, even the ones they tell you are close quarters, will not be close quarters enough for an AC to really shine. If you try to close to inside 600m, you will get shredded by all the mid range lasers and ppcs, and once finally in close range, you'll find yourself face hugged not only by the enemy, but your own squadmates who seem to have no brain power to decide maybe they shouldn't park next to you while you're trying to go toe-to-toe with another assault mech.Add in that the NPC's have no decision making skills like not wasting finite AC rounds on a plane, turret, or tank that they could have popped with 2 medium lasers and you will quickly realize the ammo capacity is a serious issue for your squad that will lead to them effectively being worthless in long missions. Ammo management is not in their vocabulary. (Seriously - give them lasers or PPC's)Game play is pretty much exactly as you would expect if you are at all familiar with mechwarriors so I won't bother to write much about this except to say that the research and chassis upgrades added a nice touch. Graphics at all maxed settings looks great. Not awe-inspiring or take a screen-shot because it's so beautiful great. But you likely won't be disappointed. Performance wise, I ran into no issues at all. No CTD, no lag, no errors of any kind. Fast loading screens. This is not a game you need to worry about saving at every opportunity in case something causes a crash.In my opinion this is a good game. Always happy to have more mech games to play. Though I would have been happier if the weapons were a bit better balanced and character skills actually made a difference (aside from evasion)TL;DR - Like big stompy robots? Buy it and go blow stuff up. Expect 15-20 hours of fun and no major issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished the campaign on expert so I'll just dive into expectations vs reality. Some of it just Old gamer gripe. Most of my nostalgia comes from MW2.  The narrow campaign maps where you're  leaving the 'map' and get ejected is frustrating and annoying. I miss earlier titles that allowed you to explore and had the ability to 'accidentally' skip a step if you came across the next major point without following the navs.  Mechs spawning in is still lazy. In some maps you actually do see the mechs 'powered' down that you can snipe. However once they take damage they 'should' become active. They don't.  Some of the AI mevchs are on a prescripted run path and if you're not where the developers expect you to be when you trigger an event, the AI just sits there.  So there's several instances of the AI and scripts just falling short. I had a few stutters with the game. People have already talked about it not being optimized. I have a Ryzen 9 7950x with a 4070 TI and 64gb of ram on an SSD. So if i had issues, i'm sure others will. I don't want to spoil anything but 'duels' really should be 'duels' why is your entire team and the enemy firing on you during this?  Tutorial I summoned afriendly during my trial lol by telling them to form on me. Now onto the game in general. I don't grasp why i have money as a clanner. Rank could dictate what weight i'm allowed to have within the campaign. Should have added multiple trials of position.  I personally did a death from above on the second mech in the tutorial and was super excited to take on the third only to get the 'cut scene' ..booo. I'm not a fan of the boss VTOLS. You'd be better off utilizing an assault mech for that type of fight and it won't break immersion.Final note: Once upon a time FASA had relased this tiny third party program that allowed people to use it in conjunction with MW3 and effectively it was the map of the IS with each clan invading and enabling a 4x style of 'build factories, bases defenses, mechs' and you'd then get to fight out those battles. _childDocuments_.review: Added Edits to reflect updatesGame is fantastic. Saw some complaints about lack of customizable armor, but that is untrue. With omni armor upgrades, extra armor can be applied to any slot with open critical. These come in 1, .5, and .25 tons. As for the rest of the game, the gameplay loop feels solid in the scripted missions with just enough challenge. More than once I was worried about when levels were end as my resources were on the brink of collapse. It feels really amazing to make it through those missions. Weapons feel great. They hit with punch and feel weighty when they should. I am playing on classic controls and they feel intuitive. Had to remap MASC from left alt though. Holding that key while ordering your Star around is a disaster. AI has not changed enough from Mercs imo. The enemies are fine and seem to have scripts that make them engage at the appropriate range. Your Star however will cross your field of fire constantly and will always charge to their shortest weapons range. Coop feels good. My girlfriend and I had no issues with gameplay stutter or long load times. Players can now chose the pilot that want to play as and can also occupy a new pilot if they die. Big upgrade and major points here.The downtime aspects are great too. Managing your salvage points to help upgrade weapons is fantastic. You need to assign techs to repair or scientists to help upgrade but you only have so many resources. Figuring out where to invest when is a big part and fun part of the game. Access to new mechs comes pretty quickly, every two or three missions it feels like, so you are never left out of trying something new. There were some complaints about the voice acting and again, I have to disagree here. It feels like how Clanners would talk. The speech is overly formal and a bit stilted. It feels alien and that is a good thing. It feels like they acting crew got it right. All in all, this is a game first and foremost for the fans. The lore is spot on, the feel is spot on, the gameplay loop is spot on. This isn't armored core or gundam. Don't go in expecting that. It feels like a Mechwarrior game and that is something I can really recommend.

It follows the story of the clan invasions pretty much identically to the beats that happened when the clans were originally released into Battletech like 20-30 odd years ago. Some of the plot beats, and ideas of clan culture do feel dated because of this though.So if you liked the older MW titles this is a nice revitalisation and graphic update to the older games, and with the crafted missions it feels more like a successor to MW 4:Mercs and MW 3 then MW 5: Mercs did. The roster of 'mechs is pretty limited comapred to most of the MW games, but it has all the iconic invasion era clan 'mechs (or at least the ones I'd consider iconic).If your new to the franchise and thinking about picking it up, all I'll say is give it a shot if the idea of a mech simulator feels like it'd be fun. _childDocuments_.review: I'll give this a solid 7/10, better than average.Reasoning:The gameplay is enjoyable and flows nicely. The mission variety is another selling point. However, for a mechwarrior game, it is missing the collecting factor. I enjoyed Mercenaries because it was almost like the mech version of pokemon. Gotta collect them all, and you were rewarded for precision shots (legs/head) so you could salvage more of the mech intact. All of that said, if you're looking for an enjoyable stompy-robot shooter, you've come to the right place.I understand that the Clans look down on the Great Houses for losing their technology over the centuries of strife, but that is no reason to cut out an excellent part of the gameplay that increases replayability. Additionally, the honor system is arbitrary. Gate locking your progression based off where you are in the story as opposed to how well you fight doesn't really make sense. They also tie mech unlocks to your honor level. Which would make sense if you could grind more honor for your performance.The roster of mechs is lacking. You gain access to basically 3x mechs per weight class based off your honor level. It's fun at first rolling around in a Timber Wolf against Atlas', but it goes stale once you unlock the walking brick that is the Dire Wolf while you're looking at the sleek lines of a Zeus in your crosshairs. Still, the Clan mechs definitely feel powerful (as they should) against the Inner Sphere rabble. I just wish there was a way to go out on your own and farm mechs for refitting with better tech, or expand the Clan mech roster some.The voice acting is good, but the animations felt like they focused too often on the mouth movement of the characters as opposed to their overall facial expressions. That may have just been due to camera focus or perhaps even my own weirdness, but i found it distracting. Only a few times during the campaign did the voice acting feel like it fell flat, and considering how many lines of dialogue there are, that's saying something. I do wish there was more banter even during the times when you're fighting, but I can understand how some would find that distracting. I'm used to having comms squealing in my ears so it felt odd not having some squad smack talk buzzing around.**SPOLIER** As is common with war games, I found the writing for characters like Perez entirely tropie. He's your standard "controlled by rage and not common sense while completely unwilling to face his own failings" character. The worst part is, your character **light spoiler** doesn't even get to reclaim your lost honor against him. Oh no. He just gets demoted but you still have to work with him later. I suppose in that sense, it really is like the modern day military (US). The worst officers fail upwards while the good officers retire as quickly as they can. I don't want to insult the writers, overall they did a solid job and incorporated nuanced aspects of the lore (such as the speaking patterns of the Clans) that I found extremely enjoyable. I just wish that military characters were written better in games, in general. Colonel Wimmer was a solid character but the ilKhan was your boring standard trope character; overly aggressive against her subordinates while demanding respect without giving any.Hopefully, this receives several expansions (FOR FREE; don't go the way of Mercenaries and charge $15 for light content releases, though that isn't looking good considering they are already charging for paint jobs) with expanded game play mechanics.As it stands right now, a solid play though I would recommend waiting for a sale since it's pricetag is higher than its value right now.I'd still recommend you give it a play through (even though you don't get to ride an Axeman or Mad Cat), but wait for it to be under $30 to get the most for your money.Still, 7/10 and probably the best Mechwarrior game in quite a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the campaign. Kept waiting for it to get good and it just never really did. Nothing new really from Mech5 other than a real campaign with lots of relatively well done cutscenes and good map design. A few bugs and lots of lazy mistakes. They took salvaging out of the game. I'm pretty sure they did almost no playtesting. Some very basic things like weapon tooltips were never looked at a second time. Weapon mistakes: 1) All lasers claim to have 1 second duration, except small pulse which claims 0 seconds. Pretty sure they are all the same though, which almost completely nullifies small, medium and large pulse lasers.2) Gauss is kind of the only decent ballistic weapon. Ultras are laughably bad. LBs have a huge recoil when you boat them so you can't aim. AC10 and 20 velocity is so slow it's too easy to miss. You can also not run an AC20 unless you choose not to put armor on your arm (see armor below)3) LRMs (and tag/narc) are fairly useless. The lock on time takes a while and with maybe... 3 exceptions all your engagements in the game will be in small to medium laser range. 4) All ballistic and missile weapons run out of ammo way too quickly, with few exceptions.5) Like everything else, there is no sense of progression to the weapons. The weapons you start the game with: the ER medium and ER large lasers are the best weapons in the game. Boring. Blatantly stupid Mech and game mistakes: 1) The campaign is so linear you would almost never backtrack and go back to a lighter mech, you always need bigger and heavier mechs. There isn't such a mission as one that would require a faster lance for example.2) The armor system is poorly implemented. You can attach armor nodes to open/free slots on your mechs. This is actually kind of cool EXCEPT the game designers made several mechs that have no free slots on CT, legs or side torsos so they literally cannot be armored up. Summoner is laughably unable to be armored anywhere and therefore is a USELESS mech. 3) There is essentially no money or real resources in the game. The game gives you so much money and parts are so cheap.  Your reward for winning the game is that you get money when you run low? 4) There are LOTS of areas that you can get a mech without JJs permanently stuck and have to restart your mission completely wasting a ton of your time. Watch where you step. (pro tip, hit Y to switch mechs and finish the map but down a mech).5) I played through on expert difficulty. It was not difficult. I died once... and then jumped in another mech and finished the mission. You are not EVER penalized for losing a mech or a companion.  6) The AI is pretty dumb. "We will walk in a straight line to you, about twice as close to you as needed given our loadouts and then slowly sidestep left and right." Your companions are worse. They do not know at all their weapons optimal range and they will make it their sworn duty to walk in front of you every time you try to shoot. Lots of little bugs, one big bug crashed the game on completing a 25 minute mission that I then had to play over. But on the upside my understanding is the game is pretty lore accurate.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so it's fun, it's giant robots beating the heck out of each other and that alone has always been the appeal for me for the Battletech franchise. But it's flawed.People have said that it's not optimised and has bugs, well I haven't experienced that myself. I figure people just haven't chosen good parts for their computer. I only experienced frame rate drops once, and one annoying bug forced me to restart a mission. There isn't as much replay ability as Mercenaries which has always been a let down with the story focused Mechwarrior games. The sound isn't too bad, could be better, the voice acting could also be better, but it's not bad either. But hey, there are plenty of positives about this game.It looks great, it's a huge improvement from the 5 year old mercenaries game. The missions are actually fun and don't feel like the same old grind of the mercenaries game. Boss battles, something new MW, are fun, challenging and sometimes force you start again and rethink your strategy. And that's awesome.As for the story, well I don't know how good that is as I get bored listening to mission briefings and skip them. But the in game chatter and videos are awesome and enough to give you a story. Galaxy commander what's his name is awesome, I just think of him as intensely angry frowny dude and that's enough for me to go 'cool, I wouldn't want to duck around with this man'.At it's core (it's fusion core) this game is awesome and more so for us folks that have been following Battletech and the MW franchise for years and years.Would like to see the clans and the graphics in the Mercenaries though.

_childDocuments_.review: Long time Battletech & Mechwarrior gamer here. MW5: Clans is a great addition to the Mechwarrior franchise.  The lore and story are on point.  Seeing the story from the Clans point of view is actually really cool.  Mission briefings and in mission dialog are quite enjoyable and really add to the flavor of the game.  Some mechs feel big and bulky, while other mechs are quite fast and fragile. Mech customization is fair and uses a hard point system. No, you cannot put 5 ER PPCs on a RT / LT Torso, but you do have many options which keep the game balanced and fun. _childDocuments_.review: This review will very likely change once these issues are fixed, and I have faith they will be.Edit: Day 1 Hotfix did not address initial issues.Edit 2: rewriting intro and cons**For everyone who is using HOTAS: if you are having issues with the UI, launch the game with your set up unplugged, then plug it in once you get to the starting menu**This game is a lot of fun, but it also is riddled with bugs.  They're working on hotfixes, but it will take some time.Pros:- game is beautiful- id totally watch a movie set during this timeframe- wonky character models (unintentionally?) show the dangers of generations of eugenics and cloning.- Somewhat customizable mechs give most loadouts you can want.- Interesting campaign story (so far)Cons- I lose my keymappings every time i relaunch the game (devs gave a workaround, but this will stay here until that is patched).- for whatever reason, my not all my keys register during keymapping.  Mercenaries did not have this issue.- Only 16 Mech chassis- Mech customization for non-weapons is lacking.  Sometimes, I just want to strip my jump jets off for more armor, or weapons.  Audio in a mission even suggests that it was a possibility at one point, but all of the jump jets on the small and medium mechs are hardwired into the chassis - Simulation missions only give (small amounts)XP for replaying story missions.  If you missed salvage you're SOL.  It also means that if you are grinding for XP, you'll be doing the same missions *a lot*.- Simulation missions let you replay story missions with additional challenges.  But are, for whatever arcane reason, limited to max tonnage, despite having no rewards outside of a paltry xp gain.- a lot of campaign upgrades and marketplace purchases are choices that are unrefundable, and with no extra way to get more through grinding/training.- Co-op is plauged with very major desync/lag issues.- There is no Instant Action/ PVP mode (you could even call them Trials!)All in all, what this really makes me want is a game styled after Mount and Blade where you lead a clan or inner sphere faction (or make your own from scratch) and you carve out your own sector of space.  Like Mercenaries, but...more.

There is just nothing in any way engaging after the campaign. _childDocuments_.review: Being back in the saddle of an OmniMech-- even if I'm coming into the invasion of the Inner Sphere from the wrong side of history-- feels good. Clans feels like the logical step towards a more narrative MechWarrior experience. Yes, we lose the sandbox and procedurally generated elements, so a campaign is what it is... But that also had been the case in EVERY modern MechWarrior. MW5 was the exception with its PG'd missions, and needing to let go of them for the sake of a more curated mission experience is just the nature of the beast.The biggest issues we've seen thus far are technical in nature-- performance stutters, some odd co-op behavior, etc. The core gameplay loop is solid, the cinematics look good, and piloting a Clan mech feels like it should. Issues are being addressed in patches, and PGI has been very upfront about what their patches and fixes are intended to address. Frankly, I was ready to be disappointed with the launch, but overall I've been having a blast. Big recommend for any fans of the MechWarrior franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: A promising looking game which is marred by standard PGI game design failings.I have a flight simulator setup on my main gaming PC, and this involves a good number of USB peripherals including joystick, throttle, and many button boxes/panels. For most games that don't use them, I can leave all of these plugged in and the game simply ignores them. For MW5: Clans, if any of these devices is plugged in, my mouse becomes almost unusable in the game menus. The menu options flicker on and off while I hover over them, and are very difficult to click. The only fix is to unplug all of these devices before starting the game.On top of this, PGI have continued their tradition of having no idea how to integrate HOTAS into their game. PGI, if you're looking at this, you need to go and look at any other sim/sim-lite game on the market and see what they're doing. DCS, IL-2: Great Battles, even Star Citizen. All of these have HOTAS configuration that you should consider copying. I should be able to configure my HOTAS fully inside the game. I should be able to assign axes by moving the axis, not selecting it from a list. There should not be a need for a config file to map a small number of buttons into the game. And your game should not lose its mind if there are more than a couple of devices connected. If Star Citizen (a buggy mess of an alpha) can get this right, so can you.I have left a negative review for now, as this is all stuff that was a problem in MW5: Mercs, and there's really no excuse for this to still be a problem in Clans. I will play the game as was clearly intended by PGI - with a controller or with mouse and keyboard, and then I will reassess this review. If the story and gameplay are enough to offset these basic game design failings, I will change it to a positive review.

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't want to read the TL:DR: Having completed the game, if you are a fan of Battletech, or love Sim games with stompy robots, its a buy. If you aren't, it's probably worth a buy on sale or a look at on Game Pass.From here on in there will be some spoilers in sectionsThe story is fantastic on the whole. It is faithful to the lore and, while it might be predictable in places for fans of the setting, it had mostly good passing, with an emotional story with ups and downs, as well as good moments of character growth.The mechs are all fantastic and fun, with a good mix of mechs (with the notable exception of the 90 ton mark, why was the Kingfisher missed?) that had a good mix of omnipods that give each chassis.Weapons feel impactful, autocannons have heft, and when fired in UAC bursts you get a nice visual recoil effect, ER lasers feel like they should and PPC’s have a satisfying smash and a sound that makes you really feel like you are sending celestial lightning to smite your enemies down range.Speaking of audio, the sfx and music are on point and the voice acting is above average for a video game, not quite reaching the heights of say BG3, but serviceable enough that they never feel grating and the game has enough chatter to remind you that there are people involved in your world without the constant chatter that gets old in many other similar titles.The Graphics can only really be described as serviceable, meeting minimal expectations. I have a middling machine (a 7800x3d and a 3070) but at times there were random frame drops and big dips in fps, so much so that at times it really broke the immersion of a fast paced battles.There also seems to be some word issues with mech rendering. I am speculating but its seems like the game does not fully render animations of mech far from your view, likely in an effort to improve overall performance, and while welcome, you can often see this when zooming in. Sometimes enemy mech just wont move smoothly for a good few seconds, making targeting specific parts of mech hard, before fulling loading and becoming smooth again.Staying on visuals, there are time’s where locations just look stunning. You have these moments where you think to yourself, I could really just get out of this mech and build a cabin here and hide forever. However, just as many times the locals just feel boring, and, especially in the middle of the campaign, you start to get board of boxed in valleys and can predict where enemy mechs are going to spawn.Lastly, and this might be pedantic, but pulse lasers just feel and sound like they are from star trek. It totally feels alien to the more hard sci-fi that is Battletech. Honestly they were done much better in MW Online and it seems really strange that they would change them in this way.There is no way around it, the out of mission ui is just bad.There is no way to reference a lot of stats you really WANT to be able to see. This results in a lot of flipping back and forward between menus to find the information you are looking for and then having to commit that to memory.The best example of this is your AI pilots. They each have their own specializations. Like one might be better with ballistics, while another might be better with missiles. The problem is there is no way to see what each pilot is good at inside the mech bay, where you customize your mechs, which causes you to constantly save what you are currently doing (and spend your money to do so) to check on your pilots stats, then go back in to the mech bay to continue your customization. With some things being several menus deep sometimes it feels like you are spending as much time in menu hell as you are on the battlefield.AI pilots, man the AI pilots. I have no idea why they conga line behind you half the time, and have the situational awareness of rocks. They often walk right into your fire, or back into you. God forbid you give them a command to use a repair bay or move to a location. This really stings because it was a notable issue with MW5: Mercs. This should have been an area marked for improvement and being the single player story driven game that it is I’m not sure that the modding support will be there to fix an issue like this in a meaningful timeframe.There are also subtle moments that really take you out of the immersion. There are certain buildings that you come to know just have mechs hidden inside them, and that when you reach a trigger you will spawn them in. Destroyed mechs also just melt away into the ground after you finish the encounter they were in, and when you see it you just can't unsee it.There are also crashes. The game seems to crash to desktop a decent amount, and considering there are no in mission saves, even for the longer ones. It's just criminal. It's also hilariously easy to crash the game in the mech bay. Just try putting a component that takes up 2 slots just above another component.Another issue is the mid game. The level design of the later half of the 2nd chapter is repetitive. You often do what you’ve already done several time (the big ones being the “boss” battles with dropships and Sokols)Also the last chapter feels short (even though the battle of Luthian in the lore happens over around 24 hours, the game does not give you a good sense of the chaotic and fast paced nature of the conflict and sometimes feel rushed  while other times it feels like you are on holiday)Major spoilers are ahead here, so if you don't want to read them, skip this part.With all that said though, I had a really fun time with MW5: Clans and look forward to the continuing of the story with new DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I see big mech fighting games, I'm in. Been a fan of the MW franchise since Mechwarrior 2. This entry however I was cautious, ready to refund it if necessary, however at the moment I can endure a few of the problems I encountered.Plot wise which was my main concern so far has been ok, no real life irrelevant agendas, lore accurate setting and dialogue as well as mech camo patterns. The only question that remains plot wise is why choose smoked Jaguar instead of any other clan that wasn't, you know wiped out? It just feels weird knowing what the end game is going to be.Gameplay wise it is an improvement and a step back at the same time from MW5:Mercs. More agile movement and tracking as well as clan mechs and weapons, environments are more streamlined now allowing you to move freely instead of getting stuck on every rock that's placed in a weird way. UI however is a mess along the mechlab, garbage design that does make it a chore trying to either understand the UI or working on the mechs and find what you're looking for.There is only a single player (or co-op) campaign that is linear. This can either be a good or a bad thing for you. I like the linear campaign but I'm wondering what replayability will it have after beating it once, which was one of the previous title's strengths.As for the horrible parts of this game so far I see 2 things that bother me: the uncanny facial models that shake bizarrely during cutscenes for whatever reason, and the performance which is probably the worst part. I can get north of 140fps maxed out at 1440p however the game stutters a lot, lowering framerate to around 40 in about a second, regardless of where I'm at or if there is a battle with lots of effects in front of me or not. Testing a bit I found that certain specific locations in each map seem to be the culprit, since these areas drop the framerate consistently every time I go there, whether I go alone or during combat, this same behavior occured in MW5:M during launch making me believe Piranha did not learn anything regarding optimization in the past few years and moving to UE5 did not make them any favors either, specially since some of the explosion effects and textures look poor in quality. This issue gets in the way before you start having fun and form what I have seen most people have a worse time with it.Overall I guess Piranha is bound to fix it just like the previous game, but more than that the question is what else is this entry going to bring to the table in the future? Is MW5:M going to be deemed as complete now? Will this one have a sandbox merc game mode?

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics Issues:Graphical rtifacting, stuttering animations, random unexpected frame drops for me and several friends on varying specs of hardware, and even someone with brand new top of the line parts, different settings did nothing to greatly assuage the issue.Audio Issues: Footstep Audio randomly cuts in and out when dialogue is playing.Gameplay Critique:It feels very Un-Mechwarrior in a few ways, they changed how you modify fire groups in mission, historically you could use the Arrow Keys and Right Control to change which fire group a weapon was on and use Backspace to set chainfire, now it is a whole menu that takes up your whole screen, a step backwards from design as far back as the mid to late 90's.Overheating no longer feels like a punishment, running your machine hot in prior titles to the point of maxing out your heat gauge shut down your machine as a punishment for failure to manage your heat or to hit the override in time, now it just shuts off your weapons, doesn't even slow you down. Akin to Piranha Games "Ghost Heat" Mechanic in MWO another system they add that is completely divorced from the setting the game is based on for no good reason.The MechBay felt weird compared to MechWarrior 5's and alot more viually cluttered and a major lore gripe is the ability to add armor to OmniMechs, which is not possible in the setting and one of the major limitations, I think its just not cool to take an Existing IP and just "Change things because" when it give people a false understanding of how things operate if they decide to look further into it, I know there is a difference in how Video Games an Tabletop Game work, but there are some things that make no sense to change and adding non lore accurate equipment to the game is one of the easily most damaging things I have experienced in the community from PGI not respecting the source material.The Movement feels stiff compared to MechWarrior 5 Mercenaries and this game overall feels like a downgrade to the prior title released by the developers, it feels like they did not do anything to internalize the major lessons learned after the botched release of the previous game, the DLC gave hope they they were clawing it back and going to do well but then they throw all of that down teh toilet, you would not suspect that this is this team's second outing with the engine, and after half a decade no less. Unreal Engine is a powerful engine with so many tools, so much documentation, and so many people qualified to make the Engine work and do whatever you need it to and PGI shows no increase in competency after 5 years in Unreal. The Game looks prettier but with an Engine like Unreal 5, that is not exceptionally difficult comparatively, and it still feels like they failed to fully utilize the engine's strengths in any meaningful way.And last but not least, my TL:DR "It is probably going to be an acceptable stompy robot game after a round of patching and a few DLC's, Wait a year or so and for a sale, but it like its Predecessor are very poor MechWarrior games in the BattleTech setting, till showing pale in comparison to their ancestors from over 20 years ago, which is an utter disgrace that with 20 years and the finest engine for making games along with the budget pumped into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: LOVE IT! This is the MechWarrior experience I have been waiting for. It has the fun of Mechwarrior 2 and the story driven feel of a Wing Commander game. The game does a great job of following the Battletech novels in way that has not been done in previous Mechwarrior games. Every mission is crafted and  is accompanied by fully animated & voice acted cinematics. Transparently, I was not expecting this to be good. As a lifelong BattleTech/Mechwarrior fan who has collected every novel ever printed and played every game released (Including the Japanese console games, the unreleased Sega Saturn Game, and fan made games) you can only imagine my surprise... that this game actually lived up to the hype. Kudos to the devs. They knew who they were making this for. The story of Battletech is unbelievably similar to Game of Thrones, but in space. The plot of this game takes place in the 3050 Clan Invasion. This was, in my opinion, the most interesting era of the Battletech Universe. In the early 1990's when the board games and novels for this era were released, it caused quite an uproar. A lawsuit from Harmony Gold (the creators of Robotech) forced them to change all of their mech designs. So they introduced a new line of original mechs and new factions which introduced them-- known as the clans. Mysterious invaders from beyond the edge of known space conquer planets. Their mechs are stronger, faster, shoot further, do more damage, and generate less heat. I would say they are the bad guys, but like in Game of Thrones... every faction is the bad guys. Regardless, In this game, you play as them. During the adventure there are cinematic cutscenes for most of the major events that happens in the novels. Although, some of these cutscenes might feel pretty random to someone who does not already know the Universe's story. The mechs are fun to pilot. You command a Star of 5 Mechwarriors. Your team mates are fully voice acted and are part of the story. (Unlike MechWarrior 5 where you hired, fired, or lost them to a stray AC20 to the cockpit.). You unlock a new type of mech each time you level up. You can customize their loadouts and unlock variants of the mechs. The mech lab is one of the weaker areas of the game's design, but it is (sorta) a little more true to cannon than MechWarrior Online or Mechwarrior 5's systems.  They added A LOT of stats to the game. In between missions you can powerup your crew, techs, scientists, mechs, and even start research to powerup every one of your mechs weapon systems. It seemed a little overwhelming at first, but if you are playing on regular or easy there are really no bad options. There are clearly "better" options. My strategy was to max out survivabliliy and laser range first. Because my Star's mechs take less damage, they do not need as much repair. Another less obvious strategy is to remove some weapons and add more heat sinks. You will do less damage, but your mech will not overheat letting you fire more.... which means you will ultimately do way more damage in a long battle. The Nova is an absolute beast of a mech. IT comes with 6 ER (Extended range) medium lasers in each arm. If you take off two of the lasers and add some heat sinks, it still one shots light mechs, but can continue firing without overheating.I often find myself on the edge of my seat when doing missions. The voice acted chitter chatter on the coms makes every mission feel special. You fight a lot of mechs, and not very many tanks. (This was a huge improvement over MechWarrior 5.)  The game is a little more "arcady" than previous Mechwarriors. For example, you can refill your Star's ammo by simply scanning objects in the map. The game is so immersive that I think this adds more to the fun than it takes away from the realism. Co-op play is great. My friends Dage & Zhoom were able to play through some of the story with me. When a friend joins your game, they take control of one of your Star's pilots. They can customize their mech. It should be noted that whomever is hosting the game is important. Because everyone play's the host's story. The cutscenes play for everyone connected, so beware of spoilers. Also, note that mission briefings do not autoplay for everyone. Each person needs to click and watch the mission briefing (or simply not watch it and wait for the mission to start.) I bought two more copies of the game for my kids, so looking forward to experience 5-player co-op with all of them soon. Overall, this is the story driven Mechwarrior game that I have been waiting to play. I really hope they make expansions which tell the stories of the Wolves, Jade Falcons, and Ghost Bears as DLC. Battle on!Artix

Missions are mostly boring because enemies trickle in and it's pretty easy7. No way to set or create a formation

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very... Mid experience. Would give it a thumb to the side if I could.The Good:- One big thing that MW5 Mercs was missing in my opinion was clan tech. It wouldn't make sense for it to exist in Mercs though, so thus we have MW5 Clans. Playing with the Clan tech is really fun. - It genuinely feels like the developers sat down and actually read through the lore of Battletech/Mechwarrior. It's clear a lot of thought went into making the experience as lore-abiding as possible. Things like the dislike of melee weapons of the constant lack of contractions make it seem like a genuine Mechwarrior product.- I really like the tactical/commander overview, where you can direct your Star through a map interface rather than just looking/locking and giving commands that way. Upon seeing it teased, I thought it'd be gimicky but I found myself using it a lot more than I thought I would.- A major complaint that I hear about MW5 Clans is that it feels to arcadey, with the mechs accelerating and deccelerating way to quickly and not feeling much like a tank. Quite frankly, I don't feel that way. I grew up playing MW3 and MW4 and while I can say those are a lot more tank-like in the way they handle, MW5 Clans doesn't handle much differently from the recent iterations like MWO and MW5 Mercs.The Mid:- The mechlab interface is... not good. It's very clunky, the hardpoints display weird (hardpoint slots versus ACTUAL hardpoints), a lot of clutter and just overall is a pain to use. Only going in mid because once you know how to deal with its quirks, it's usable. Even then, it takes a bit of time to learn and just isn't that great to use.- MW5 Clans doesn't like to hold your hand in explaining it's features. You could be multiple planets in, and not know you can upgrade your chassis. You actually gotta sit there and go explore to find these features. It'd be one thing if they were out of the way like they are and they at least told you about them, but that just isn't how it is. - I'm not a fan of the lack of selection of mechs. Not that the mech choices are bad, but that there just aren't enough of them. It looks like they went for a 4L/4M/4H/4A breakdown, but that leaves out a few of the other invasion mechs. Notable ones left out are the Ice Ferret "Fenris" (My little walking refrigerator), the Ebon-Jaguar "Cauldron Born", the Vapor Eagle "Goshawk" and the Stone Rhino "Behemoth". This is supposed to be supplemented with the omnipod system. Speaking of which...- The omnipod's don't fix the lack of other clan mechs. Not only do a lot of the omnipods repeat, leaving a lack of customization (for example, while the Kit-Fox has 6 choices for R/L torsos, there are only two "unique ones", one with a Ballistic hardpoint and locked JJs, and more armor) across the board. In addition to the repetition, not all of the omnipods are even present. An example off the top of my head, the Shadow Cat only had the Prime, A and B omnipod sets. This leaves out the P (with it's 6 MGs, a favorite of mine to run), the H (which has a missile hardpoint in the right torso, which if it were included could theoretically let you run a 2E, 4M loadout), the D (which would've given the SHC more E hardpoints in it's left arm and left torso, giving it more of a chance to be an effective energy boat), and the Mishipeshu (which while only featured in MWO, would've given an extra ballistic in the right arm). It essentially makes the overall customization of the SHC half of what it was in MWO.- The overarching story is decent, but that was a pre-existing story in the Battletech universe. The story we experience though? VERY VERY mid. The characters almost seem robotic (not because of their lack of contractions, which has lore reasons), and when they do show emotion it seems forced. I think the best way to explain it is, "the characters do things not because it is what they as people would do, but it's what their characters would do." It's hard to explain what I mean, but if you understand than great.The Bad:- The AI tactically seems better than those in MW5 Mercs, but that doesn't help when they get stuck at every little obstacle. It doesn't happen every round, but happens enough to be infuriating. I'll get attacked by a lance of mechs, only to realize two of my star is stuck way back on either a weirdly shapen rock or some piece of debris. I'll have to manually take over control to get them unstuck, only for them to get stuck on something else.- The optimization is really bad. It does look a bit better than MW5 Mercs, but in Mercs I can play on High with light Raytracing and get consistently over 100 FPS without DLSS. In Clans, I have to run DLSS to get consistently above 60 FPS on Medium settings (I have an RTX 3070, which is better than their recommended 2080). Games shouldn't require DLSS to work properly. For that marginally better graphic fidelity compared to Mercs, the performance loss isn't worth it.

MW5 Mercs is simply a more fun, better game than ClansWhat a disappointment :(

_childDocuments_.review: Good:Gameplay is OK albeit faster than i remember mechs feeling, this is probably due to the modern control scheme. -Weapons feel punchy and sound good, for over half being lasers.-Progression if fine and well paced-Mech models look good, some particle effects and terrain is sloppy, will most likely be patched.Bad:Time and time again i trip over "because lore" and this fact actually impedes my enjoyment of this game-why cant i remove jumpjets from this if i don't have any desire to use them > because lore-my fav mech is a Hellcat, can't wait to pilot it! > you fool! you get a roster of 16, and that is all; because lore-why are certain components locked > because lore-oh damn, a Stalker. i kinda want the opportunity to pilot that... > NO! because lore-who would ever use this for mele, i'm removing the arm actuators > no you're not, because lore-i want to ditch .5 tons of armor to slot this better gun > nah, armor is fixed, because lore, but you can add more, that's what you were asking for, no? and also you can't launch overweightI'm sure the dedicated nerds are happy and enjoying the game, but i cannot personally give this a positive review as it currently stands. _childDocuments_.review: In every other game I have played ever (and I've been playing MW since the original), Clan Mechs are awesome. Until I got the 80 ton mech in this game. It's fast (81kph), and has slightly more firepower than a light mech. In other words it's as much  of a useless piece of junk as a certain IS assault mech.Worse, my joystick is useless. If I use the "classic" control method then you turn the mech by twisting the stick and twist the torso by turning the stick. Changing the axis in settings results in no change. If I use the "modernized" method then the throttle control does not work and I have to move using the keyboard. So I have to use kbd/mouse controls which have the crappiest layout I've ever played. Plus the mouse gets overly sensitive in the bigger fights so small moves result in wild swings. Which means I'm forced to leave fighting to the AI starmates. Which also usually results in me getting hammered if not outright destroyed. Why were the controls changed from MW5:Mercs? I could understand if a different company did the work, but it's the same group. WT*!Add in that when you do get repair bays in a mission there are only a few and they only have one use each. So if your entire Star got hammered and everyone needs repairs, you're forced to prioritize yourself and one or two starmates.The story line, haaaaa. Umm. Lemme just say, in every other game, the Clans fought each other, frequently. So the whole "the clans will unify the IS and return peace and prosperity" thing? Absolute garbage. A clan commander bombarding a city from orbit? Bull! Slaughter civies, yeah they did that. But up close and personal (or as personal as it can get from a cockpit of a mech).I'm sure some ppl with top of the line gaming rigs are having fun. But for me, this game is unplayable. Further the game ignores already established lore which further annoys me. 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: First off I'll start by saying that story being implemented well here with cinematic and emotional  (though often over the top) facial expressions; was a breath of fresh air for this IP.Initial game-play felt solid enough. But I must impress how dumb as rocks some of the AI actions are. Worse yet, I've been stuck on a poorly constructed mission where a set of blast doors that you are forced to travel behind ALWAYS seem to block off at least 2 of your squad-mechs behind them and DO NOT re-open. These door are on a timer and there appears to be no code that tells them to stay open if any mechs are left behind them. Worse yet, this door is behind multiple waves of enemies and SEVERAL long winded video logs that get old as you try and finagle the situation. It hurts me to do this, but to have a game released that cant even hold a door open so you can finish a mission speaks of a rush job and I can only give this a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, at the time of writing I have over 70 hrs and I'm still not finished the campaign. I love fiddling with mech loadouts, then testing them in the simulator, that's probably where most of my hours go. The story is great, the voice acting seemed to start off wooden, but got much better as the game went on, I'd even say it's quite good. I really like the way the mech bay works, not totally canon, especially the way the armor is put on, but it adds a little extra puzzle that feels really satisfying when you get a mech just right. The lore is incredible, I just finished reading lethal heritage my Michael Stackpole, and this story is like that book from the enemies point of view. Anyway, fantastic game, highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to mechwarrior 5 mercenaries this game has a very good campaign. I have to say I got completely immersed into the story so far. I have only played a handful of mission and am still at the first planet so take my "review" with a grain of salt.That being said compared to mercenaries this game leans more towards an I guess arcade style compared to the slow and tactical combat of mercenaries. The interface for mech loadout has a learning curve compared to mercenaries, I have yet to figure out how it works, and the scrap system has been changed and now seems to just give scrap points in 3 categories rather than the mercenaries system, which I preferred, since it encouraged tactical hits to leave mechs as intact as possible as to later be salvaged after the mission. The maps also seem much smaller but then again I am at the beginning of the game so we will see how that evolves as I play. As for the performance issues, yeah the framerate chugs from time to time but other than that the game was quite playable for me, I can't say any of the technical issues took me out of it except maybe my PS5 dualsense having double inputs unless using steam input. All in all I have to say that while I preferred the combat and salvage of mercenaries, the story in clans makes it a much more complete package.

_childDocuments_.review: Long time fan of the series, but this went in a different direction than what I expected.  I absolutely appreciate a more prominent narrative focus, but this time I think the game suffered a little for it.  The fun of MechWarrior for me is the endless customization and optimizing your mech for the mission, and this game just didn't focus on that.  We like having to manage the costs of travel and repair, oddly enough.  There are a lot of game worlds where you blow things up for a living, and weirdly enough part of the fun in these games is that you have to pay for it after.  The graphics were great, gameplay was smooth, and the narrative was pretty decent overall.  It's also nice to see this level of multiplayer support for a game like this where it makes so much sense.  That said, this game had a lot of well-done polish, but lacked some of the grit and substance longtime fans enjoy.  Is it fun constantly replacing parts and paying huge repair bills when you barely scrape through a mission on consecutive deployments in MW5:M?  No, but that practicality and sense of consequence is entirely missing from this game so far.I'm also vaguely disappointed in how linear the game is.  Battletech and MW5:M offered the opportunity to just wander around and take random jobs.  That brought both a sense of scale and pretty significant replay value to the games, and extended my personal interest in them quite a bit.  I like having to manage the travel times and costs involved.The amount of DLC and extended support we got for MW5:M has been really fantastic, and added so much to the game and the world.  I have no doubt it's coming, but I wouldn't have minded waiting another year for it to be included on day 1.  Also, I get why the number of mechs we can pilot is limited.  It makes total sense for the story.  Can we have more anyway please?  There are so many in the in-game universe that I get we can't have them all, but I would like more.  At least all of the clan mechs would be a great start.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Clans

_childDocuments_.review: There were quite a few Voice acting Mistakes in the game.....You could tell the whole game was cheaply and hastily done.....Quite a Few of the Clan Mechs were unavailable to get, the Campaign and Gameplay is so Linear it hurts, you can only play as Clan Smoke Jaguar and in the end it doesn't really matter what choices you make.......In retrospect, Mechwarrior 5 Mercenaries is far more expansive with a fully made Inner Sphere to traverse, the ability to choose your starting Employer, an extensive list of avaiable Mechs, various potential Mech pilots, massive Combat Areas that allow you to maneuver how you wish to achieve your objective and various storylines to follow ultimately.  Two VERY different games when you look at them, one being carefully crafted in an expansive Universe and the other hastily made as a Money grab for people who wanted to get Clan Mechs.I personally would suggest the Clan Mech Mod for Mechwarrior 5 Mercenaries......It'll save you $50

_childDocuments_.review:
In MECHWARRIOR 5: CLANS, players take on the role of a newly graduated pilot from the Smoke Jaguar cadet program, thrust into the heart of the Clan Invasion of the Inner Sphere during Operation Revival. This pivotal moment in the MechWarrior universe sees players leading a five-mech "Star" squad across numerous planets with diverse biomes, engaging in an expansive campaign filled with immersive gameplay and intricate combat encounters. 

Armed with customizable BattleMechs featuring cutting-edge technologies, players explore a wealth of tactical options and strategic possibilities. The game leverages the power of the Unreal Engine to deliver stunning environmental details and visceral destruction, making every battle against the tyrants of the Inner Sphere an epic experience.

As the first Clan-based MechWarrior game in nearly three decades, it combines a captivating narrative with well-crafted characters and moral dilemmas, culminating in a dynamic and adaptive combat experience enhanced by a revamped MechLab, Hardpoint, and OmniPod system.

name: Highwater
detailed_description: Highwater is a whimsical, 3D adventure game with an isometric turn-based puzzle-combat system set in a flooded, post-apocalyptic world. Navigate by boat, discover islands, find new allies to help battle foes, and experience a humorous tale about friendship in this melancholic and atmospheric escape. Amid the Great Climate Catastrophe, the flooded region of Hightower has become a kind of safe zone between the two dry regions: the nearly global ravaged land of the War Zone, and the fortified city of Alphaville, where the ultra-rich live behind giant walls. With life on Earth becoming untenable for humans, and rumors of an escape to Mars floating around, Nikos begins a risky journey, picking up friends along the way. First to Hightower, then beyond to cross the impenetrable border of Alphaville, battling insurgents and stealing food along the way. Will Nikos and his friends manage to sneak onto the rocket in time? GAME FEATURES: Rich, Story-Driven Adventure Earth may be flooded, but it’s one heck of a view on the water. With a sense of humor, determination, and some great tunes, Nikos and friends will work together to explore the water-filled environment around them and embark on an adventure to evacuate to Mars and start a new life. 3D Exploration & Discovery Float along the vast waterways freely in your boat and explore the many different islands of a beautiful world where you’ll encounter danger, interact with fellow citizens, gather resources, and fight for a chance to escape to a new life. Turn-Based Combat With A Twist Take on your enemies in a classic turn-based combat system where careful tactics and puzzle solving will help you come out alive. Interact with the environment and items around you: knock down a tree, push a shopping cart into an enemy, or duck behind a turned over car to gain the advantage. Original Radio Tunes The world may be ending, but there's still time to enjoy some good tunes. As you cruise along the water, Highwater Pirate Radio is the key source not only of unique and original music, but also for commentary on your ticket to survival.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played and finished the previous two games in the trilogy and they are all completely different. The first one was a golf-based puzzle game, the second one was a platforming game, and this one is an isometric turn-based combat game. Even though they are different, there is a kind of story arc that links them all together with a familiar radio host commentating on events in each game. In Highwater Radio Nostalgia has been replaced with Highwater Pirate radio, and you will hear some great tunes and insightful commentary as you casually meander through the sunken and desolate landscapes and waterways.  I had mixed feelings whilst travelling in my motorized dinghy. It felt relaxing, with the tunes in the background, and some lovely visuals on occasions, but on the other hand I wanted to explore more and there wasn’t much opportunity to do this. Especially in the first half of the game, the gameplay felt very linear, just cruising along from point A to point B dictated by a crude radar and a map which I couldn’t understand and never used. There were sunken remnants of civilization on show, which occasionally allowed a photo opportunity, but not many places where you could stop and explore, and the places that you could stop were a little uninteresting and only served to pick up some collectibles like books, magazines, and if you were lucky, a booster or new weapon for your team. Exploration was disappointing. When arriving at a destination, there are characters to interactive with, and brief text-based conversations to be had, with the very occasional option of picking between answers. By no means is this a choose your own adventure, but sometimes the option is there. I didn’t feel like I really got to know many of the characters well and didn’t feel particularly close to them or bond with them for some reason. The story wasn’t very moving and didn’t have many moments which grabbed me unfortunately. It was all a bit forgettable. Surprisingly, the most fun I had out of the game was with the turn-based combat which is a genre I don’t usually engage in. I’m not sure there is anything particularly new here to see, but it was done quite well and there were lots of instances where you will need to use the environment to your advantage, or strategize your attacks to succeed. Often, you will feel outnumbered and overwhelmed, but a push of a tree onto an opponent, or picking a fire extinguisher off the wall to throw, using stun tactics, or even rolling a trolley into an enemy, can all balance the odds, and I really enjoyed the puzzle-based elements behind battles.Your team all have different attacks to perform, some melee based, some long ranged weapon based, and even one who can hack robots and either destroy them or take control of them. There’s the usual scenery to hide behind which boosts defense properties and there are boosters to use that can improve movement, damage or defense.
