_childDocuments_.review: The Fuga games get an easy thumbs up recommendation from meThe gameplay is pretty simple conceptually, but it's got just the right amount of variety to make it fun and challenging without feeling unfair. You've got your weapons that each correspond to 1 of 3 colors, and you have to figure out how to use those the right way to exploit your enemies weaknesses. The different abilities and support effects that your party members have add another layer on top, and can really give you an edge in tough battles.And then there's the soul cannon. From what I've seen it seems that people are hesitant to play because of this feature. Yes, you can sacrifice one of your party members (all of whom are young children) to obliterate your enemy if you're in a pinch. In part 2, they doubled down and made it mandatory if your health drops too low. That said, I've never had to use it once in either game. As long as you're careful about healing and take a defensive approach, especially in boss battles, it's entirely avoidable. I wasn't a fan of the "pray to the soul cannon feature" that they added tbh, but you can use it to greatly lower the hp threshold at which the soul cannon activates.In terms of the story, I thought it was very well crafted and interesting. Technically you don't HAVE to play part 1 first, there are some features that will help you catch up if you take that route. BUT, I really would highly recommend playing part 1 first. The maturation of the children from part 1 to part 2 is one of the best parts of the story, and the main "plot twist" that sets up the climax is 100x more impactful if you've played part 1. They're both fairly recent games, and there's not really a downgrade of any sort between part 1 and 2 so you might as well start from the beginning in my opinion.I love both Fuga's, they are excellent from both a gameplay and story perspective and I would highly recommend this series if it sounds at all interesting to you.

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel doesn't disappoint. Still working my way to 100% completion, but I just finished the full story. On a base level, they took the messier parts of Fuga and refined them. Each kid's skillset feels much more unique and attuned to their personality, with attention to how they matured since the events of Fuga 1. Yet you still get the variety of strategic options since multiple kids can fill your base needs (attack, ailments, support, etc). Also, the kids have matured! If a kid from the first game ever felt like "this is my 1 personality trait", that's not the case anymore. Their personalities have grown and changed, and the characters feel much more dimensional. And yet they're still kids.The meat of the gameplay is the same, but it's refreshed by new skills and mechanics that help tie in the world. Last time the children were fighting alone, but this time you're working together with the people you saved before. You see the kids interact with the world much more, leaning further into the great worldbuilding of the first game.One of my favorite improvements in Fuga 2 is the role of the children in the story. In the first game, since you could use any child in the Soul Cannon at any point, no child was necessary for plot development, so no particular kid could be too  important. In Fuga 2, they can still all die, but the way they can die has changed, allowing individual kids (like Malt) to become more important and plot-relevant. And the story. OH, the story. The hook in the trailer is emotional enough, but the full story hits HARD. There are gut punches. There are plot twists that'll break your back. There are complex emotions that really make you wonder what the right thing to do is. And there are multiple endings based on the new Judgement system. This system lets you decide whether Malt is more concerned with saving his friends from danger or stopping anything that might hurt them. These might seem like the same thing. They're not.All of this while maintaining the amazing visuals and music that brought together the experience of the first game. If you liked Fuga 1, you'll find this worth the $40. Support the devs for making their passion project (which they develop AND self-publish, unlike their title anime games which are published elsewhere).

You will be missing a lot of the small details, nods and references to interactions between characters otherwise. And since this game is extremely character-driven, it all matters.I don't feel like spoiling the plot or recapping the basic plot overview so I'll keep this bit short.It is a direct sequel to first Fuga and well worth the play.Plot is solid, very emotional and grabs you by the heart very quickly, much like the original - which one of the two is better plot-wise? - that is a matter of opinion, though the story of Fuga 2 is much more... focused on Malt. This also means that interactions with characters a more advanced and more fleshed out, which is nice.It is a wonderful sight to see how the characters grew...And well, I will not lie, it was nice to see these lovable guys again.I must say - it was wonderful to see how the characters grew over the canonical year between the two games - and the developments all make sense and feel very natural.Let me tell you - I generally despise children in video games - and this series made me deeply care for a pretty large cast of child character - take it as a testament of how well are the characters handled.Gameplay wise - it is very similar to the first one, so if you liked the mechanics of the original, you will like this one as well. There are some nice quality of life improvements, some tweaks to character skills, but everything has a massive sense of familiarity.Because of the plot developments, the major gimmick in form of certain cannon is now more of a looming threat this time around, as you don't control it any longer and if you mess up... it WILL do the thing. If you are like myself - if you easily get attached to such lovable characters as those here... You have a massive extra incentive to do well. Enemy variety is greater as well. You have some old-new and brand new enemies to deal with, greater variety of attacks. Enemies have few more status effects and gimmicks, like group attacks. New tricks up their sleeve.On your side of things - kids have re-vamped kits. Some man different guns now, some of the supporting effects are swapped, but the core of combat remains the same. In terms of difficulty, I found it easier than original. Though perhaps the fact that I played both games one after the other might have something to do with it - I was fresh after Fuga 1, and I had a pretty solid grasp on the game's mechanics by this point. To keep the long story short - get it, get it now along with Fuga 1 - these games are horribly underrated and deserve to be played and cherished.

_childDocuments_.review: Having finally just 100% finished the game, I can confidently say this is a worthy successor to the original game, with some caveats. The plot and characters are, in my opinion, much better this time around. They all felt like one-dimensional gimmick characters in the first game, like how Boron was the fat kid and only talked about food and his weight. Since the game is fast paced and trying to develop 12 characters at once is a massive undertaking, there's still some characters who don't get much attention and fall flat, but I'd say about half genuinely grow and change in at least nominally interesting ways. The plot, likewise, was far more engaging for a variety of reasons that I don't wanna blab too much about, but I think it does a much better service to the characters, and does a better job of writing to the strength of the franchise in general (I've played all of em!) The gameplay is more or less identical to the first game, with a bit of extra polish and some new moves. The delayed bombs are fairly niche but decent, and the new armor ignoring moves are God-Tier for New Game+ runs. The Soul Cannon on the other hand, is both way better and far,  worse. The Soul Cannon now automatically activates on its own if you get low enough on health in a boss fight, and randomly selects a child to put in it, then firing after a countdown. This is fantastic for the first playthrough, it can both screw over your established strategy by taking your star character, and also adds a tough but fair time restriction to really amp up the tension. I nearly lost a character due to playing sloppy and it's easily one of the more memorable moments for me. On the other hand, the fact that the Soul Cannon selects a kid randomly means that it's a massive slog to farm for death scenes in NG+ runs, as you'll be constantly saving and resetting over and over and over and over again until the dice fall in your favor. The game desperately needs to just let the player choose who goes in the cannon for NG+ runs as it loses its gimmick once your characters start getting post-game stats.Overall, I loved the game, and I much prefer it over the first game, however the grind for true 100% was a painful slog that I'm not gonna attempt again anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Since I wrote a big long review for the first game, I figure I should make a follow up for the sequel. There's not as much to say this time though since the gameplay is largely unchanged from the first, for better or for worse. There have been some attempts at balance (RIP in peace my big beautiful boy boron, nerfed into the ground), but stunlocking is still king. The Managarm is an interesting alternative to the Soul Cannon in that you can still use it if you're struggling with a fight, but it doesn't kill a kid so it doesn't destroy the plot. The Soul Cannon randomly selecting a kid and automatically firing after 20 turns if your health gets too low in a boss fight is a cool idea that can add some tension, but it's also annoying when it activates the turn before you were going to do a big heal, so now you're totally safe but have to start the fight over anyway because you won't be able to kill the boss fast enough (this only happened to me once but it WAS mildly annoying).The plot was a definite improvement though, as were the character interactions. Everything felt very shallow in the first game, but now there's some actual character development and Malt gets to actually be a protagonist. The Judgement system also adds a little extra flavor by allowing you to make dialogue choices between being nice or not which not only give you different skills that can randomly activate in battle, but also lead to more character development scenes sprinkled throughout the game. The character interactions in the intermissions also feels better since the kids know each other now and it's not just endless introductions, so their differences can actually show through their dialogues now.But other than that the game is still largely the same. If you liked the first game you'll like this one, and if you didn't like the first game then this one won't change your mind. I got about 35 hours out of it getting the true end on the first playthrough, and then doing a ng+ run to choose the other dialogue choices to get the other epilogue and using cheat engine to talk to everyone and get all their little character vignettes. I've seen people say they found the first game hard, or that this game was harder, but I never struggled with either one, so your mileage may vary. I gave the first game a 6-7 on a true 1-10 scale, and I think I'd probably give this one a 7-8. The game once again had a secret video teasing a sequel, so I'm excited to see the conclusion to the trilogy (though also slightly concerned since the director of 1 and 2 left the company a couple months ago).

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr Fuga 2 is 8/10. Play with the French dub.Fuga 2 is an improvement upon the first one in every way, from gameplay to writing to even some visual effects and with what they tried to pull off. It builds on the first game's formula and expands it with mechanics new and revised. The story is exhilarating, and any summary cannot do the sequel justice, simply that it follows up a year after the first game and examines the cast as veterans of war as they're thrust into new conflict. If you like turn-based JRPGs, I heavily urge you to play Fuga 1 and 2, because Fuga 3 is shaping up to be completely insane in the best ways imaginable.

_childDocuments_.review: In comparison to the first game, there are plenty of improvements 1) the sprinting function, which certainly helped in ruins and going up and down in the tank, 2) the new addition of bombs in the combat were interesting, 3) the forced soul cannon effect when below 50% HP was both exhilarating and added an extra sense of challenge which I thoroughly appreciate, 4) the introduction to town-folk conversations, passerby's and resolution/empathy points that follow were unexpected but effective tools of immersion and spicing of game mechanics.The plot is interesting and as per usual leaves you with lovely cliffhangers.  Character interactions are just as eagerly anticipated too.  The only critics I have would be the following 1) it's easy to pick favorites in the game based on certain abilities, 2) it might be a bit too difficult for some players at first playthrough (though I appreciate difficulty), 3) when in intermissions, you still have to navigate through the tank to do what is necessary, I understand this would be more lifelike, but if at all possible for next game to have an interface of activities would be most appreciated (also, any time a character was changed, you are "teleported" back to the center, instead it might be better to just be left where the previously used character was last).Overall I highly recommend this game; it has an interesting story, lovable characters, and engaging mechanics of gameplay.  Already looking forward to the next installment!

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, I'm a damn sucker for the premise. Probably my favorite rpg I've played in awhile, if not just straight up my favorite ever. I find the mechanics simple yet satisfying. The music is great and fits in neatly. I would also say that the character designs work well for the setting, and that the theme of its story is not only deeper than a "yo I can sacrifice children to a big gun in war let's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ go" (trust me the joke was more funny in my head), but also feels like a reflection on ourselves as humanity (trust me it makes sense). The first game got me hooked in an instant and this one further raised my interest; I can't wait to see what they pull in the third one.I do want to say that for 40 bucks, if you speed through the game or don't care for the story it tells, then I'd wager it's probably not completely worth the price for you. Though, if you were considering buying a jrpg of all things, something tells me that won't be the issue. The 19 hours at the time of review is one playthrough with time taken and breaks while the game was open included, but I doubt it took up much more than an hour of the time, and there's still ng+ with different endings to get (and a collection of cogs? not sure what that's about just yet).♥♥♥♥'s a 9.5/10 in my books (I can't in good faith give anything a 10/10 lmao)

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberconnect2 finally made a sequel to one of my favorite games of 2021. It turned out to be a great sequel in that it did what a sequel should be, be like the first game but with some improvements. It also turned out to be one of my favorite games of 2023 along with Hi-Fi Rush and Pizza Tower. Let's look at the pros and cons of it.Pros:• Great, emotional story• Really good gameplay• Likeable characters, especially Malt, Boron, Wappa, Kyle, Chick & Hack• Improved and new mechanics (judgement system) & animations (the characters actually run in this game) and added clarity to the buff effects of the food for example• Loveable and distinctive art style and character design• Amazing soundtrack• The airship system is a welcome, convenient change• Plays great on Linux via Proton 7.06• No live service garbage• Only $40, not 70$• Complete experience, no unnecessary dlc; only dlc is just some extra items, upgrades, and costumes.Cons:[The cons in this list are mostly nit-picks and some of these cons are techincal problems, especially since I play games on Linux (specifically Nobara Linux) via Proton]• The camera glitch that affected the first game is in this game, but it's not as bad• Pre-rendered cutscenes don't play, just shows color test screen, specifically on the story recap and cutscene that plays when you continue the game (must be an issue with Unreal Engine 4 when it comes to Proton)• Pacing is not perfect• The Soul Cannon automatically being commenced when you're low on health during boss battles is annoying• Don't care for the whole magic hocus pocus spell stuff• Jihl is a fine villain, but Cayenne is meh• Not enough people know about this game  In conlusion, Fuga Melodies of Steel 2 is a great sequel to an underrated gem- coming from a dude who is not an rpg, strategy game fan - and is one of my top 3 favorite games of 2023. It was an emotional rollarcoaster of a game, and it was a really big improvement over the first game. I'm glad that Cyberconnect2 is able to make/self-publishing their own games. I wish more studios can be like IO Interactive and Cyberconnect2.

_childDocuments_.review: "If it ain't broke, don't fix it" comes to mind with Fuga 2. If you're unsure, I'd recommend playing the 3-chapter demo of the original to see if it can get its hooks in you, as really not much has changed. But if you have a winning formula, does anything *need* to change? I'd say no. More of a good thing is... well, a good thing.

_childDocuments_.review: A new addition that adds some new mechanics but is still recognisable to the players of the first game. _childDocuments_.name: Fuga: Melodies of Steel 2

_childDocuments_.review: Recommendation is absolutely contingent on your enjoyment of the first game, because this sequel is more of a chapter 2 than something you can just pick up and understand like a zelda or whatever.But absolutely if you loved the first one, get this.If you were on the fence with the first one... I actually don't know if the new gameplay is interesting enough to really grab you. But things move a lot faster, some enemies have new gimmicks, dialogue choices matter a bit more, and maybe most importantly, the central gimmick of the series is fixed - the new Soul Cannon will force itself to fire if you don't move fast, which also incentivizes using the Managarm.Also since they don't have to introduce a bunch of kids this time around way more of the plot is focused on doing plot things with character arcs and so on.

name: Raiden IV x MIKADO remix
detailed_description: A blast from the past soars into the present! A sci-fi shoot 'em up for the ages! Raiden IV x MIKADO remix combines the original arcade experience with modern-day features, allowing this series to perform like never before. With a remastered soundtrack, vertical screen play, new battle modes, and more, it's time to take off and take 'em down! Experience the return of this classic arcade shoot 'em up as Raiden IV x MIKADO remix soars onto PC! Enjoy an exhilarating lineup of content including brand-new levels, combat modes, play styles, and more. This sci-fi shooter launches gameplay to new heights with a remastered soundtrack and the addition of vertical screen play, allowing players to capture the original arcade experience like never before. Instill fear in your enemies with devastating attacks and earn the acclaimed title of Master Ace! In Raiden IV x MIKADO remix, you'll continue the fight against the extraterrestrial race known as the Crystals in their attempt to take over the world. The arcade classic steps up for its explosive arrival on PC. With this debut comes a suite of electrifying content featuring new levels, frenetic bullet-patterns, and intense gameplay modes such as Arcade, OverKill, Score Attack, and more! The addition of vertical screen play gives players a nostalgic blast from the past, while Double Play mode (the ability to pilot two ships at once) provides an exciting and challenging experience that's out of this world! Soar sky-high with a stellar soundtrack that features live performances and new arrangements, with the ability to switch between classic and remixed songs. With all this and more, Raiden IV x MIKADO remix stays true to its arcade origins while launching the franchise into the present! Play Your Way: Modes such as Dual Play and Double Play take your adventure to the next level! Modern Music: Remixed BGM from the original classic, including live performances and new arrangements! Old-school Vibes: Vertical screen play allows players to recreate the original arcade experience! A Suite of New Content: New levels, bullet-patterns, and modes, including Arcade, OverKill, Additional, Score Attack, and Boss Rush!

Add a jolt to the traditional Raiden formula by choosing from gameplay modes such as Score Attack and Boss Rush, along with Double Play, the ability to pilot two ships at once. Reach new heights by competing against players online in the World Rankings, and elevate your experience by choosing between original or remixed background music, as well as individual tracks for each stage. Twice the Firepower: Pilot two ships at once in any game mode with Double Play! Raiden Remixed: Choose between original and remixed background music, complete with individual track selection for each stage! World Class Pilot: Compete against other players in the World Rankings, and watch their replays to see what you’re up against!

name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun
detailed_description: DISCORD About the Game Play as Malum Caedo, a fearless Space Marine, on his perilous mission to locate a shard from a mysterious power source on Graia, a Forge World on the brink of being overrun by Cultists, Traitors and Chaos Daemons. Scour the place, acquire devastating weapons and holy equipment, and PURGE THE HERETICS in this retro shooter! Become the ultimate warrior of the Imperium, wielding your deadly arsenal to explore the violent and iconic Warhammer 40,000 universe. Dominate the battlefield with the awesome firepower and heavy metal of a Space Marine’s devastating weapons, as you battle against the Chaos Space Marines and Daemons. Take control of the mighty Malum Caedo– along with his faithful servo-skull – and plunge headlong into your mission on Graia. Retrieve the Power Source fragment on the Forge World and cleanse the archenemy from its surface! Roam through bastions, cathedrals, corrupted canyons, hellish furnaces and war-torn environments. Dive into a visceral combat experience, complete with viciously satisfying gunplay, high mobility and buckets of blood to reward your skills. Rely on your indomitable chainsword to eviscerate your enemies. Dash, jump and slice the foulest heretics across the galaxy! Unlock new deadly weapons like the Shotgun, Meltagun or Heavy Bolter and equip yourself with different types of devastating grenades. Show no mercy! Experience a perfect blend of Warhammer 40,000, classic, frenetic FPS gameplay and the stylish visuals of your favourite 90’s titles. In glorious boomer shooter style, unleash your devastating weapons as you blast through an explosion of sprites, pixels and blood. Discover an exceptional aesthetic, with retro cutscenes and pixel art backdrops, paying tribute to a historic era in video games. Want to take purging to the next level? Annihilate endless swarms of enemies in the new horde mode, available for free. Blast each and every heretic standing in your way, trample on their remains and cleanse their foul heresy. For only in death, does duty end.

_childDocuments_.review: If you had to envision a Boomer Shooter with the Warhammer 40k IP being released at the height of their golden era, the inevitable result of that vision would be this game.Definitely one of those games that you just play one level at the time to try and prolong the experience as much as you can to properly savour it. Wishing to see a sequel to the game being announced soon, plus hopefully also see other interesting IPs to get the same treatment by Auroch Digital.-Do you like Boomer Shooters? 10/10 game -Do you like Warhammer 40k? 10/10 game-Do you like both? 20/10 gameFor Terra and the Emperor, glory to mankind!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Its not in Early Access, its just 20 dollars for a rock solid game, better than rock solid. A simple idea, well executed with enough polish and love put into it that there's some nice surprises as well.And its not just a great game for a 40k fan, its a great game for anyone who enjoys retro FPS's. The arsenal is incredibly meaty and impactful, the levels are well designed, the art style is a pleasure to look at, there is great enemy variety, and its a good length (8 hours in and have yet to finish 2 of the 3 chapters).If you are a 40k fan, then this is a must-buy and easily the best first-person 40k shooter available. The people who made this game clearly share a great love for the setting, from the stomping of the power armor, to the incredible sound design of the weapons, to the environments which really capture the scale and feel of 40k.  The game goes one step beyond just being a well executed experience, to having some pleasant surprises, some unique bosses and enemies I didn't expect to see in a game like this, a nice variety of power-ups, and a couple archeotech weapons that are every bit as destructive as you'd want them to be.At long last, we're starting to get games that are truly capitalizing on 40k's potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely good, easily one of the best first person shooter's I've played in recent years. Best 20$ I've spent.Everything feels as heavy and fluid as space marines and their weapons should. All of the guns are useful, and the game doesn't rely on gimmicks like Doom Eternal did.I played on My Armour is Contempt mode (basically the normal or medium difficulty, I do plan on playing the hardest difficulty when I go through to get the rest of the steam achievements)----Some big tips: *Thoroughly* explore the map, you get lots of pickups and power-ups this way. Move constantly but thoughtfully. Most attacks are fast-moving projectiles, so bobbing and weaving between those will get you farDon't stay up in an enemy's face, unless you are going for a chainsword kill. Doing this basically guarantees that you will tank every hit that enemy throws at you.The Plasma Gun is probably your most useful weapon. Some enemies like to group up, and this deals massive damage to groups of enemies. Otherwise it's a great source of single target damage.Don't be afraid to use your "big" weapons. Some enemies, like plague toads and aspiring/chosen champions are *deadly* if not dealt with quickly.----My only gripes with this game is that some stages can be a bit confusing and repetitive, and that there wasn't more boss variety.Hoping for a good DLC
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic! As someone who enjoys the older style of 40k this ticks all the boxes - especially playing as a Sternguard Veteran my first box was the old metal ones in about 2008 so big tick for that! I had a big grin on my face seeing my favourite mini sculpts rendered in this game though I did always feel a little bad for killing sassy Nurgling numerous times. I can't wait to see what Auroch do next as there is a lot of potential for other playable characters, I would absolutely love playing the other half of the powered armour First Company as a Vanguard Veteran and getting a closer look at the Melee/Pistol weapons they utilise. If you like Oldhammer get this game, simple as.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend with a grain of salt!This game is great for what is advertised, a classic shooter with some amazing visuals and the sound design is fantastic!However, the game play loop starts to get very repetitive fairly quickly, and around the 5/6hr mark, I hit chapter 2 of 3 and started to loose interest in it :( The maps dont really help either as they're rather large and loop alot, so I find myself getting lost 60% of the time! 6.5/10 - Worth the money for sure, but kinda lost interest due to repetative gameplay and Getting lost in level design

_childDocuments_.review: The fact game critics rate this game as average/poorly shows that this is the only time Xenos, Chaos and the Imperium should unite under one banner. I don't know what those heretics are saying but this is a damn good game.Amazing Pixel Art? CheckSet in 40K? CheckShooting is satisfying? Check!YOU PLAY AS A SPEHHS MAHREEN! CHECK!!!YOU CAN ACTAULLY RELOAD YOUR WEAPONS MAKING USING THEM ALL THE MORE SATISFYING!!! DOUBLE CHECK!!!!Verdict: The Codex Astartes and the Emperor suggests you requisition this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: I almost forgot games could be fun! I can't remember the last time i booted up a game and after the first level realized i was just playing with a big dopey smile on my face for the last 10 minutes. Everything in this game feels just right, from shooting, to movement, to the satisfaction of exploring every last nook and cranny looking for secret areas. The pacing of this game feels great too, its not overly chaotic and fast paced like the newer doom games, which is why i could never really get into them. Cannot recommend this game enough 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: I am only writing this review because I pre-ordered this game. The game looked good from the trailers, early DOOM, but with a modern engine, modern controls; completely modernized. However, retaining the core element, plentiful gore. I have played through the first level, and I can say I am quite satisfied with my purchase. It has everything that the early DOOM games were lacking in mechanics, gameplay, and graphics. It is worth noting, I have not a single clue about the Warhammer universe, but I do enjoy this game thus far. I will probably update this review in the future as I play more. tl;dr If you liked early DOOM games especially DOOM 1993, but want a more modern take, get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer 40K & shooters go so well together and the retro look of Boltgun is perfect!Fast paced with a wide variety of weapons.Bullet sponge enemies DO exist, but are manageable IMO.The newly added (optional) navigation guide is the best addition so far!Makes traversing the different levels way more enjoyable.For the Emperor!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely insane, this is the studio's first attempt at boomer shooter? No way. Most impactful gore and sound of bullets hitting since brutal doom/brutality. These guys did everything right. You are heavy and you feel it from the visuals and controls, you can even land on enemies and crush them. The guns are impact full and have cool features(ricochet on shotgun). There are so many power ups. Monster variety is incredible and i'm only on the third level. You guys better be making dlc right now, we will buy it instantly. Horde mode with this game too would be incredible. I wil update later, hasty review because im astonished, playing on my school laptop core i7 IRIS xe graphics (integrated). How the heck did these guys pull of this masterpiece?

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game play. The art style is great, the guns feel good. The only downside is the level design is a bit tough, you can end up getting lost and not knowing where to go so you may spend more time per level than usual, but not all the time. Of course I wont have that be a reason to aim towards a down vote. Played many more hours on Gamepass but felt like supporting the game and buying here as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I truely wanted this game to be good but... I'm so bored. Every mission seems quite the same: you gotta go somewhere kill some things, till you get keys to go further and again and again... 30 mins of this feels like 2 hours.It's a shame, because this is a visual banger, but that's pretty much everything good innit.The music is soulless, there ain't any atmosphere, and the gameplay mecanics are way too basics to be really interesting and enjoyable. Do not believe that the story will save the day, the only scenario avaliable is basic as ****. I can't recommand this at all

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could put a neutral rating here rather than a thumbs up or thumbs down. The game is just a little disappointing despite the fact I've put 15 hours into it.Things I like:-Feel of the weapons-Fast paced gameplay-Main menu music-The thudding around everywhere-The tauntsThings I dislike:-Aspiring Champions. Worst enemy I've encountered in a game in 20 years. This guy runs up at you and seems to hit you from 30 feet away for 100 damage. He is completely silent and a bullet sponge. This enemy needs to be nerfed ASAP.-Level design. How much play testing was done? I keep getting stuck on random ♥♥♥♥ in corners. This is not even a boomer shooter, its an arena shooter like Doom (2016). There needs to be no crap in the way to slow you as you race around trying not to get tagged.-Checkpoint saving system. Checkpoints are too spread out.-Though there is a damage indicator, there's no sound effect when you get hit.-Sound design in general. The enemies don't make unique sounds, they all sound the same or are silent. Music during the levels is not great.-Enemy respawns... why are enemies continuously respawning during a boss fight? They spawn so thick you can barely move past them.I've been playing on Hard, and it's very hard to me. I don't get the people who say they are playing on Exterminatus and it's "EZ". They must be crazy, this game is hard AF. I'm not finishing it, I'm setting it aside until patches/updates come out to fix some of the issues.EDIT: See my comment. I am revisiting the game after the recent patch and I'm liking it more now.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Very repetitive. Why is 40k so obsessed with cathedrals? Everything looks like a cathedral. Levels have almost no distinction between them and don't really feel like real places, just hallways and cathedrals. Add that to the fact that secrets aren't really worth it, they don't really give you usefull stuff only temporary power ups that activate when you pick them up, which makes exploration of the levels both tedious and unrewarding. Not worth the 20€ I paid for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: First Impressions:Gunplay and movement is really good. The map textures start to blend in and it's easy to get lost because everything looks the same in the first chapter, but you get used to it and after that it's better. Really good enemy variety. Overall I can't say I can play it for more than 30 min at a time, but that 30 min is fun. On the other hand something like doom eternal you could play for hours no problem, and the gameplay is very similar. With that said on a good price, this game is really fun.UPDATE:I finsihed the game, first impressions where good but after playing it for 10 hours I would say over all its kind of a boring game. It has a really good base and I enjoyed exploring most of the maps but combat is not as fun as I thought it would have been. Small enemies die with one two hits of your weekest wepon and big enemies are just bullet sponges. The bossess are all the same too with different attacks some times.Wepons are also boring outside of the first wepon the boltgun every other gun fills under powered and you hardly get to use it because you run out of bullets all the time. Also jumping around and looking for healpacks on big fights is not fun.Finally you never fill like a bad ass as a spacemarine should fill. For example in doom and doom eternal you ALWAYS fill like a bad ass even when you lose. Because everything around you as also super powerfull you are just one of them nothing spacial.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: This game wants to be Doom so badly that it's really kind of sad... The graphics and style are a quirky novelty for the first 10 minutes and then get very annoyingBig thumbs-up for the D-Rok mix for the music on the title screen, got me nice and pumped! I hit play and it went down hill rapidly from there! The in-game music is annoying, the scratchy "voices" even more so! Many people seem to love it, but I wonder how many of them were alive and playing games when this sort of thing was the norm... probably not many? I was!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: In a word: Tiring. It has initially normal level design, then followed by being hard-stopped and stuck in an arena with a red filter for like 5 or more minutes every 5 minutes, then copypaste that loop over and over again until an extremely annoying boss that you need to play perfectly against on normal happens, then have incredibly annoying level design in the next level with enemies then being spammed Project Warlock style infront of you.There's also an excess of health and armor in areas you don't need it in, but a medium amount in areas you do. Had me thinking about Prodeus's EA levels with how it was laid out, and that's not a good thing.Also, you lose all your weapons on a new chapter, but the game behaves as though you still have them, throwing the str-7 enemies at you when you only have the boltgun...
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would recommend this game, especially for the price. It was not without it faults but was a solid entry to the retro shooters that have been coming out. I played this game on the Steam Deck for about an hour but found that it was very challenging (medium difficulty) with a controller. Probably a skill issue on my part but I enjoyed playing it a lot more on my PC with a mouse and keyboard and didn't find the game overly difficult when I switched.Pros:- Performance on PC - solid 144fps (locked it to that in game) at 3440x1440, did not notice a single frame rate drop during my 10 hour play through (13700K, RTX 3080, 32GB ram)- Performance on Steam Deck - ran perfectly on default settings, mostly 60fps with occasional drops when things got busy, since I switched to PC early on I did not try to tune the settings to get a solid 60fps but I'm sure it would be doable and the frame rate drops did not bother me much anyway (I am normally very picky about FPS)- Combat/gunplay - very fast paced, very fun, good variety of weapons at your disposal, guns feel and sound powerful (definitely a must for a warhammer 40k game)- Graphics - they did an excellent job designing the graphics in this game, modern twist on retro shooters and you can tweak the pixelation and retro video filter to your likingNeutral:- Music - I enjoyed the music, pretty standard for a game like this with a retro filter added, I wouldn't listen to it outside of the game though- Story - I guess there's a bit of a story? Not really engaging, that's fine for an arena shooter like this- Level design - I almost put this as a con, however I personally don't think there was anything inherently wrong with the level design, more on that in Cons section, I did find some areas to be a little catastrophic, as in I would get stuck on stuff on had trouble moving about and dodging during the fast paced combat, I only noticed in a couple areas and it may not bother some, but worth mentioning. Personally I think the levels were great for combat, good vertically, usually adequate cover/room for maneuverability, etc.Cons:- Exploration - They desperately need to add a mini map, or some sort of indication of where your current objective is. I found myself lost and wandering around until I happened to stumble on the correct path forward on nearly every mission in the game. Maybe this IS a problem with level design as others have noted, but I think it could be alleviated without changing the levels.- Balancing - There were definitely some areas of the game that needed some balancing, really just extra health kits/contempt. Some missions were a breeze to the point where I would leave most of the health kits/contempt behind then others would have hardly any for the whole mission. At one point the game saved a checkpoint right before a mini boss area that I could not beat until I restarted the mission because I didn't have enough health and there were no kits once the encounter started, that was frustrating.Final ThoughtsAgain for the price this is definitely a buy, especially if it's on sale and if you don't think the cons I mentioned would bother you. However it's hard to understate just how infuriating the "getting lost" aspect was for me, to the point where I almost marked this as a not recommend. It took me about 10 hours to beat the game and I'm not exaggerating when I say 2 - 3 hours of that time was just trying to figure out where to go because I'm too stubborn to look it up. This game would've been an easy recommend if they just took some extra time (and IMHO they could've even charged a few bucks more) to add a mini-map and do some balancing. It did seem like they tried to add indicators around in some of the missions (one of them was follow the candles, and there were occasionally marking on the walls) but I did not find them consistent or obvious enough to be helpful. That said this game released in complete, working, and solid performing state which is not always the case these days, and I had a lot fun when I wasn't lost so it gets a thumbs up from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: A well presented FPS that suffers from bland level design and mechanics.You shoot, you barge forward, you melee, you can drop from a high up ledge and squish enemies (if they don't have too much health), and that's it.Difficulty on hardest is pretty wack, it's really easy up until you get to the "purge" sections in which the game respawns enemies over and over until it thinks you've done enough. During these encounters, visual clarity suffers as the arena is covered in gore, corpses, pickups, enemies and toxic landmine-esque green balls. Often you will find yourself being pelted with ♥♥♥♥ from every direction and enemies spawning all over the place. This is not fun.Otherwise you end up just going from room to room getting a key to go back and open up a door, no points of interest and every level melds together in a bluey-grey mush of boring level design. Secrets in these levels are basically "go around the back of this wall - secret yaaay!" or you pick up a powerup in plain sight and it goes SECRET FOUND! What.We've had DUSK, we've had ULTRAKILL, we've had CULTIC, we've had HROT, we've had Ion Fury, and this is the best Warhammer could offer? If this game didn't have Warhammer branding it wouldn't have the reception it has had.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty obvious as you play the game that the developers love the WH40k IP - and want to please the fanbase. Fairly priced, good ol' fashioned fun, and tons of things that'll make a 40k fan grin ear-to-ear.(This review was immediately written after a nurgling bent over and shook his ass in my face)
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: The art and sound design are really great, that's about it for the positives. the level design is unbelievably bland and uninspiring. Many of the areas look identical and how you navigate them is again always the same. The secrets aren't exactly "secret". I would describe this game as more of an art exhibition rather than a fun FPS experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Boltgun is an average boomer shooter that starts off strong but ends up heavily overstaying it's welcome to the point where i'm really struggling to keep on pushing through. There isn't enough here to warrant the game being 8-10 hours long. These levels are all starting to blend and mesh together and the combat hasn't evolved at all. A lot of the weapons feel underwhelming to shoot, especially against some of these enemies that are complete bullet sponges. I wish this game was a tightly paced 4 hour roller coaster ride, instead it feels like a very slow and very long train ride that doesn't speed up at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the reviews are memes and not actually reviews, cool.It's a nice concept, but honestly, it's like Brutal Doom lite with a 40k art mod. Having played a ton of Brutal Doom, I just don't see why I'd ever play Boltgun over that. There's something missing here and I can't quite put my finger on it. Other than it having the 40K flair, it's quite generic and I can't recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: If you're living check by check and 20 bucks is a lot for you to spend on a game, I would say look elsewhere.If you have a few bucks to spare and just want a few hours of fun, I think this game is fairly priced and and I recommend buying it. The game also seems pretty lore friendly when it comes to the lethality of enemies as well as the space marine you play as vs certain higher tech weapons. I think 40k nerds will also enjoy it as an intermediate experience.This game is effectively a retro Doom 2016 but worse, unless you're a Warhammer fan or a fan of the retro shooter aesthetics I'd just buy Doom 2016 which is also priced at $20. Make no mistake though for an indie this game is great. I'm looking forward to see what the devs will cook up next and I think it's valuable to give indies some love.  If you're a warhammer 40k nerd your panties will be soaked.Chapter 1 & 2(Early game and Mid game) is very strong and enjoyable. Game is balanced well and smart gameplay is rewarded, using the appropriate amount of power against x target(s) feels intuitive. Most of the maps are visually/aesthetically appeasing and fun to navigate.Diverse enemy types which work very well off each other, creating more pressure for the player and forcing them to adapt to each combination of enemies + room.(Good mix of melee vs ranged threats)Enemy AI breaks often and can be easily exploited, at times it just kills the immersion.It is so incredibly hard to see both enemies and when it comes to navigating the environment in this game. Often times you need to be straining your eyes past all the bright visual affects contrasted with the dark environments just to hit peanut sized human enemies. The contrast is simply ass.The game becomes pretty repetitive and I don't think it has fun replay-ability. This is a one time fun time.Even on the hardest difficulty I felt that the game was giving me too many resources.Later game rooms become more about nuking them with the expectation of having an op weapon loaded than actually navigating them well, too many rooms where it's physically impossible to avoid damageWeapons were fun but underpowered weapons were immediately noticeable and given , you'll naturally neglect a good portion of your arsenal, 40% of your arsenal.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: The game is competent, but it feels like a very polished first draft. Like the devs were trying to ape doomclones without much exposure to that genre.  I don't know how to put it other than it feels like the last 5% of the mechanics that would make the game play loop really engaging just isn't there, and so the visuals and trying out the weapons is all there was to it. Its a decent game but also seriously over-hyped. Worth playing if you love 40k but not sure if I'd bother otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: If gore ain't your thing I recommend you don't play, however if you are willing to accept the ptsd, testosterone and adrenaline the game want to shove through your eyeballs, you are in for one helluva ride. This thing takes everything about guns and pumps it up to eleven, you become a stampeding rino with an arsenal as big as a small countries population. The art is amazing and the game play immerses you in the well crafted levels, it will always leave you thinking "ill just play one more level." This is pure fun funnelled through the chaotic world of warhammer to place a smile on your face and remind you that games can still give you a good time. If any game should be game of the year, this is the one!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10 It's fun ASF!!If you're a fan of Warhammer 40,000, you'll love Bolt Gun, the new video game that lets you experience the thrill of wielding the iconic weapon of the Space Marines IN A BOOMER SHOOTER doom format. Bolt Gun is a first-person shooter that puts you in the boots of a loyal servant of the Emperor, fighting against the forces of Chaos, Orks, warp, and other enemy heretic of mankind. The game features a variety of missions, from defending a fortress to assaulting a space hulk, and each one is packed with action and gore. The graphics are stunning and fun, the sound effects are dense heavy and immersive, and the gameplay is fast and furious. swap your bolt gun with different weapons and ammo types, and unlock new skills and abilities as you progress. even though it's a single player experience The game NEEDS a multiplayer mode, where you can team up with other players or compete against them in various modes. Bolt Gun is a must-have for any Warhammer 40,000 fan, and a great way to enjoy the rich lore and setting of the franchise. It's not just a game, it's a way of life. For the Emperor!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid and fun game. Fun to see recognisable models in these graphics again (we got some of those pixelated goodness back in the day, Chaos Gate and such).I hope we'll get to choose a new character later, maybe from another chapter and maybe in different armour or something to spice things up. I know we basically just see our hands in-game but could be a fun opportunity. Slower not-jumpy terminator armour but maybe you can teleport around instead. Might need its own stages for sake of balancing.I think even a scout could be fun, keeping to the old-marines. But yeah, looking forward to more content if the devs have some planned.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best WH40K games, second only to Space Marines which is still my personal favorite. Where Space Marines is a mix of third person shooter and hack n slash, Boltgun is purely boomer shooter pixel artstyle bliss. It has solid and satisfying gunplay, very old-school level design where the handholding is kept to a minimum, and just captures the power fantasy of being a Space Marine sooo ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ well. That's all thanks to the fantastic sound design where you can feel the weight of each step taken, stomping on enemies, or the splatter and gore of every brutal kill. It's just so well done. Then there's the great weapon variety, how each of them sound and feel satisfying to use. You can taunt as well and there's quite a few which is neat. Storywise it takes place after Space Marines where you're a marine sent on clean up duty and that's pretty much it but the connection is neat.I have very minor complaints with this like how the boss fights are rather meh and having to fight them over and over again was kind of a chore. Also was not a fan of the melee which is better used as a movement tool to zip across the map than to brutally kill enemies. Also no executions was a bummer, would've loved to see their take on this with all the pixelaized glory. Again these are very minor complaints for an otherwise great game and I can easliy recommend this for anyone looking for a fun time. I also recommend playing on Exterminatus for maximum extermination of heretics!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't had so much fun since Doom 2016, it's crazy fun. This is fun to a certain point, but gets really repetitive really fast. Best played for short periods of time. For fans in W40k, this is worth the buy in a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: This game beats ass. I've played various Final Doom mods and pretty much expected this game to be a reskinned one, but I was wrong. It just feels way better and more thoughtful. Shooting and chainswording enemies feels amazing. Level design is intelligent and definitely a throwback to old Doom games. Lots of arenas that have to be cleared before you are able to move on, find keycards etc. Someone in another review said that this game does what Doom 2016 and Doom Eternal tried to do, but better, and he is 100% right. Sound effects are great. Heavy booms and thuds. Everything feels impactful. This game is a great complement to Space Marine 2. More of the same universe and gory fun, but way more streamlined on constant action with very little in the way of cutscenes, or listening to dialogue while going up and down elevators, etc. Basically a full bore arcade experience with the occasional hunting for keycards, which isn't too bad and allows you to breathe. Challenge is good on Hard mode so far. Finding it's got a similar characteristic to Space Marine 2, which is that at times you'll find yourself barely hanging on with just a tiny bit of health. No RaGrEtS buying this game and its DLC today. Good work, devs.

_childDocuments_.review: An audio-visual treat, this is a good game to waste away a day or two on, especially for Warhammer 40k fans. I'm glad to say it's one of the "good ones" in the pantheon of WH40k video games, and I hope the devs continue their work and maybe make a Quake-inspired followup. That said, personally, I found it just alright. Pretty good overall, but it's a bit long with 24 levels split evenly among 3 chapters and a near 13-hour completion length if you go for all collectibles. After the fist few hours, with the exception of excellent new weapons you discover along the campaign, you kind of see everything this game has to offer. Enemy variety is decent, but not enough to carry a 10+ hour campaign; tactics, too, rarely changes, albeit that might be a boomer shooter staple--I'm not well-versed in this genre--and the secrets gifting power almost made them feel like a requirement. They weren't, but gaining temporary overwhelming power is a lot more fun than gaining nothing at all as you play. The level variety, too, was lacking. The first hour is awesome open-air levels and lots of bunny-hopping opportunities, but that quickly devolves into 80% tunnels, factory hallways, and the occasional huge arena that requires holy purging. Still, I ended up enjoying my time with Boltgun, even if I was ready to place it back on the shelf with 1 complete run. It's visually gorgeous, sounds amazing, feels great, and maybe just a bit too long and dull to justify it's length. If you love WH40: get it. If you love boomer shooters: get it on sale. If you love both: it's a no-brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: This kinda hurts to say because I like retro-shooters and a WH40k Doom-like sounds like a perfect match but this unfortunately just isn't it.First I want to say there is a lot to like about the game too, it's not all bad but I personally don't recommend it.I really like the look of modern retro shooters like what New Blood Interactive have been releasing, e.g. Dusk and Amid Evil. This game also has some options for how 'Retro' you want it to look but it literally only has two options, Pixelization, and Color Pallet, so it's a little disappointing there but no big deal. Game looks great overall.Unfortunately though, it's a pretty rudimentary boomershooter that doesn't do anything different in this style of game besides it being a Warhammer property. A lot of games add something different to spice things up. Ultrakill is really fast-paced and focused on intense area battles. Gloomwood is an immersive sim. Cultic allows you to approach encounters in various ways with tight level and encounter design. Boltgun has...taunts? don't get me wrong though, I SPAMMED taunt whenever possible (for the Emperor).I find the levels to be labyrinthine with no notable markers where key doors are and there's no map to chart where I could go next. While I like a good challenge in these games the difficulty seems unbalanced. Some moments it feels too easy and others quite difficult. Part of the difficulty comes from the very subtle indicator of being hit. I don't always realize I've taken big damage because I can't stare at my health mid-combat. Overall, Boltgun is a competent Boomer Shooter that doesn't tread new ground.

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant gem of a game that pays homage to three decades of shooters.The controls and gameplay are simple, and the only real objective is to have fun purging the enemies of mankind as one of the Emperor's Space Marines.If you're looking for the perhaps charmingly contrary experience of a chill shooter, then this is the game for you. All the more so if you find any level of enjoyment in the Warhammer 40K universe. Something that has been somewhat overlooked that I personally find rather fun, is that this is a soft sequel to the earlier Space Marine game which is a nice addition, though you need not fret if you've never played that earlier title. The story is barely relevant as anything other than background information to explain your presence upon the planet.Each level plays out more or less the same. Fight you way through groups and hordes of enemies as you explore the vast architecture of the forgeworld of Graia in your quest to cleanse it of the taint of the ruinous powers. Despite the fact that the game is very confined in its level design, I've yet to actually feel like I am limited in my ability to maneuver while fighting which is quite nice. The enemies too, while fairly rudimentary, will still make you work for your victories and defeat is always an option.The combat itself is simple, with your weapons functioning intuitively and ammunition being plentiful. As you progress you will find more powerful weapons to use and add to your arsenal as you fight everything from random cultists, to Chaos Space Marines, to mighty champions and daemons of Chaos. Even the ubiquitous chainsword is present in all of its gory glory. The biggest downside to the combat, and something I would caution players over, is that there is very little feedback on damage. This means that if you are not paying attention to your health and armor, you may find yourself dying inexplicably, not realizing that you've taken critical amounts of damage from your foes.For the price-tag, this game is well worth getting if you want an enjoyable and novel shooting experience to pass the time with and just have fun.Don't forget to mock and taunt the enemies of mankind as you blow them into gory bits!

_childDocuments_.review: If you are relatively new to the 40k series, Boltgun doesn't care. Melee is extremely lacking and only really good as an ammo saving finisher or to kill cultists with one hit. The lack of a map is also annoying and I have been lost in levels a ridiculous amount of times. Taunting the enemy is a must after every kill to get the full experience. Overall, Boltgun is a great time waster game at a fair on sale price that is easy to 100%. Give it a go!

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the boomer shooter subgenre (Though I prefer the term 'rip and tear shooter') I enjoy this one quite a bit, though I do have some criticisms. I've made it through the first chapter, and I feel I've done enough to give a review on how it plays.The game is fun and visually pleasing, movement feels a bit clunky but I expect that of these games (not everything has to be Ultrakill or Doom Eternal) and a fun all around gorefest with nods to the tabletop game, with added taunts for flavor. However, the game struggles with combat for two reasons. Enemy design and resource distribution. While playing this, you will almost never run out of ammo, as pickups are plentiful and almost always visible around the maps and arenas, though I find this mechanic doesn't make combat repetetive through the use of the same weapons due to the Strength and Toughness mechanic. However, health and contempt (armor) are a completely different story. There are only two versions of those drops that are found in combat, a single point, or 100 points, the prior scattered in lines throughout every arena, the latter hidden away in groups of 2-3 that can fill you up completely mid-battle. Enemies drop 1-5 single points depending on how tough they are and nothing else. Playing on Hard difficulty, I find this system can make resource management annoying, as losing a lot of health restricts me to running around the arena hoping somebody doesn't chainaxe my ♥♥♥♥ off while searching for the medkits. Where other shooters would reward you for still killing enemies despite lower ammo or health with higher amounts of both on kills, keeping combat engaging and upping the stakes even more when low, this one restricts you to running away or playing chicken until the PURGE is over. This system irks me.The second problem with combat is the enemy design. There aren't a ton of different enemies, and the new ones don't come quickly. This is not a problem in and of itself, but some of these enemies serve as little more than damage sponges with slightly stronger weapons or their own form of random annoyance due to awkard hitboxes or attacks. The AI of the enemies is unremarkable, and those that do bring their own tricks to the table feel more annoying than engaging (looking at you little nurgling bastards). Additionally, the two bosses i have fought have TOO much health for too few mechanics. Even going full auto with the strongest weapon I have it took me forever to kill either of them, each of which had at most three unique attacks and simply stood in place and blasted me for a while (oftentime missing because the bastard was too tall or in a bad position) before teleporting away and repeating. With all this in mind, I do still find this game to be good enough to recommend to my fellows who praise the Throne and find reducing heretics to gibs as a suitable form of entertainment. To those who find my review helpful and wish to play the game yourselves after, here's a tip

_childDocuments_.review: Boltgun is a solid 7.5/10 FPS game. It's a bit rough around the edges and I definitely wouldn't call it a boomer shooter, but it does a fine job being a straightfoward, gory, punchy experience.My main complaint is that in order to play this game, you have to sit with the Space Marines, or as I like to call them, the Dorkuses Malorkuses of Warhammer 40K. Not just that, but you have to sit with the Ultramarines, who are like the Space Marines but 300% more annoying. And some of that is justified, because it means you get to wear space armor and shoot giant guns at soft targets, but I would like to play as a character in the Warhammer 40K universe who is allowed to have the aux cable for once. Please give me the opportunity to play as an Ork. Thank you.Anyway, the gameplay is fine - you shoot big guns and enemies explode and die in satisfying ways. There's a melee mechanic, and it sort of works like Doom Eternal's - you can leap towards enemies and then latch onto them by holding down the right mouse button, then revving your chainsword to cut them down. It's super straightforward - levels are more akin to a game like Gears of War than a boomer shooter - not a lot of scenery to check out, just straightforward corridor to corridor fighting with an arena section thrown in to spice things up. The secret doors weren't something I picked up on until later - they're so secret you won't even know they're there unless you physically expect every wall up close for a 'Press E to open' prompt. So if you're going to 100% secrets for cheevos, get ready to give the Emperor's kiss to every wall in every level.Overall, not a bad game whatsoever. Heck, if you need to brush up on playing FPSes with controllers or if this is your first FPS, it's not a bad one to start with. I know I'm going to brush up my skills on the Steam Deck with this game. Eventually. Someday.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: The Emperor of Mankind? He chose me to be his top guy! My name is Malum Caedo, Sternguard Veteran of the Ultramarine Chapter, and the God-Emperor of Humanity actually picked me to lead his holy crusade on the Forge World of Graia. I am a one-man army, an Exterminatus condensed into human form and I am here to purge Chaos wherever it may be found. May the Emperor have mercy on their souls, for I will not!This is a beautiful game with buttery smooth movement and an excellent range of weapons. Auroch Digital have composed a love letter to the fans with Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun. This is a game that has clearly been made with true passion and an extraordinary attention to detail. It boasts strong and varied level design with a surprising amount of verticality and a weapon arsenal to rival any game out there. Tightly paced with wonderfully flowing combat alongside a perfectly meaty feel on the impact of each slug or shell you fire.The only downsides, and these are genuinely minor complaints, are the lack of an auto-map or radar, which become rather noticeable in some of the vaster levels like Grand Elevator and the enemy AI not responding over very long distances. The shotgun should probably hit a lot harder as well, especially at point blank range. I also wish there had been more music tracks in the OST because even the menu music in this game absolutely slaps. All that being said I actually hope they do a DLC that allows us to remove Eldar or Orks from this plane of existence. All hail the Emperor! I cannot recommend this game enough, if you have even a passing interest in old school FPS games or the Warhammer 40K Universe then this is a must-buy.

I felt like this was a good turn in direction and hopefully for their future games. I can only imagine a new game where they give us a doom version of this game almost similar to Space Marine, but add first person and more intense action like doom games (or Trepang2), minus the pixel graphics.- Guns were fun and felt good to use- Gore was spontaneously combustible from meat sticking to ceilings and walls if enemies get blown up.- Chainsaw was very satisfying and felt godly hopping to one enemy to the next in slow motion- Level design really brings out what Warhammer could feel like if you were there instead of from a bird's eye view- Gothic Architecture still looking fire even for a pixel boomer shooter- Is a boomer shooterSuggestions - I'm very hopeful that this game does receive some kind of community update that involves creating custom content like maps/levels/mods like Doom has because why play the game once and prolly not again. _childDocuments_.review: The game is fun. The feel of firing the various weapons is great. You feel the weight of your movements and it has some great charm for a boomer shooter. However, the repetition of the enemies combined with the level layout, the fact that even Exterminatus difficulty just seems to chuck bigger waves of enemies at you rather than, say, improve their behavioral AI or field more advanced units in place of the regular ones, which doesn't do much when the Bolter is thankfully lore accurate in its power, but that serves to the games detriment since they're just throwing more meat into the grinder at higher difficulties rather than giving that Bolter something more toothsome to bite into.These problems alone aren't enough to warrant a downvote for the game, granted, until you consider that you're stuck with the product you buy, since they haven't really made the game accessible to the modding community, which would arguably make this possibly the best Warhammer game to exist and could have propelled it to the levels of popularity that Doom 2 experiences with its robust modding community. This means that there's no way to really spice up the gameplay that's here, even though all the tools exist to create lavish user-made levels. Doesn't help when the DLC looks to be offering the bare minimum in gameplay, not seeming to have much new to show in their DLC pack. My verdict is: buy it on a good sale. It's worth a play, it's satisfying, it's fun. But the fun is limited in the long run with no way to amp it up. So what you see is very much what you get. The enemy roster is limited, the boss is the same in every act, you'll be using a relatively small roster of weapons in comparison to shooters of the past. You'll realize very quick that there's only so much game in this game before you're just going in to shoot a Bolter. Even then... Doom mods and wads scratch that itch all the same, so it's still the superior experience. It's good, but it's leaving so much to be desired I have a hard time recommending it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:+ pew pew pew+ overall great game- few nitpicks and the nonstop action can get overwhelmingLong version:Fairly enjoyable shooter and one of the few games where the power of the 40k weapons by lore actually seems to be somewhat representative. Mainly seen in human enemies actually exploding upon being shot by what are essentially miniature rockets with HE payload and not tanking tens of rounds with their faces (looking at you Space Marine).During the first playthrough the lack of a mini (auto-) map left me running in circles in a few sections, however mostly the levels use either their layout or lighting etc. to visually guide you through the game. What was harder to get used to was the servoskull following you around. Mostly because it:1) provides jumpscares by floating into your periphereal vision2) glows in the same tone that a lot of the enemy projectiles do, making you jump around like a lunaticOther than that the game does pretty much everything right. It has weapon variety. Enemy variety, Level variety. Objective variety (ehh, well kinda sorta). Even playstyle variety. One thing I noticed on my first playthrough was that not knowing the levels, I tended to play more cautiously and even though you can actually fly through the levels in just a few minutes in several cases, playing with near 100% kills tends to make the levels last 20-30 minutes and that nonstop action really wore me out. Modern games do a lot with pacing, but this game is 99% action whether you like it or not, very few areas with any downtime. I didn't mind it, but I found that I could maybe complete like 4 levels in a row maximum. (game has 3 x 8 levels) Usually it was more like 1-2 levels at a time. Sure on following playthroughs it was easier because I knew where to go and where I can skip fights, but for that first playthrough I did have to push myself to keep playing on at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this game every benefit of the doubt, but midway through chapter 2 I've come to the conclusion that it's a pretty mediocre experience.First the good. Sound design isn't bad. The guns sound pretty punchy. Guns also range from standard types to some that are a little different from what you're used to. And none of them are worthless. Graphics are also a high point... kind of? It looks pretty good in the pixelated format and I like the art style. The game is also relatively functional with little in terms of bugs or frame drops. The music is ok too. Not very memorable but it serves its purpose.That's where the positives end. Level design leaves a lot to be desired. Often they're bigger than they should be. You will get lost A LOT as there is also no automap, which is a Boomer Shooter staple. Why is there no automap? Especially since the level direction kinda sucks as well as the environments looking samey. Enemy AI is also particularly bad. By chapter 2 they tend to... not function somehow? And they'll be facing away from you semi frequently on a couple of chapter 2 levels. Enemies have weird hurtboxes as well. Only the center of the sprite seems to have it, so hitting the shoulders you'll find the shots fly through them, which would be a problem if the AI weren't so exploitable. Enemies that lack range abilities will just end up staring at you, or their only projectile attack like the Aspiring Champion is a complete joke and easily avoidable. Since some enemies don't shoot from the center of their sprite, you can often exploit this as well since they'll see you but can only shoot a wall and don't move to get a clear shot. Boss fights were... ok at first. Then they got really bland. I ended up encountering the Lord of Change like 3 times before I gave up on the game. 1st time was fun. 2nd time a slog, 3rd time very boring and tedious. They also continuously spawn enemies in the later fights, which doesn't make the fight more challenging really since they're easy to kill, just more annoying and unnecessarily draws out the fight. Enemies in general also range from too easy to kill, to too tanky with too much health yet they still aren't much of a challenge after a little while.The Mr. Skullhead thing that follows you around is also completely useless and the most it does is point out ammo/health/armor that you're already staring at. Seriously what was even the point of adding this thing to the game? I'd say save your money and buy HROT or maybe Slayers X instead. But if you're a megafan of Warhammer then... wait for a sale maybe?

_childDocuments_.review: Woah, I've only played 7 hours!? Felt like 30 because I was so bored.The only metal song in the game is in the main title. _childDocuments_.review: It's hard to put my finger on exactly what makes me not like Boltgun, since on paper it should be something I'd love: a high-paced boomer shooter with tons of gore and iconic enemy designs from a lore-heavy setting with a stylized art direction.But I think the issue is that everything about it is *almost* good.The guns feel punchy and make enemies explode... except that some of them are useless(plasma gun, calling you out) and that even on medium difficulty enemies rapidly develop tiresomely large health pools. The game flows at its best when there are more, smaller enemies.The areas are fun and enemies are easy to spot... until you move indoors, where the game then gets stuck for a long while, and everything is the same anthracite gray as most of the human mooks. The game should've just stuck to the ourdoor snowy areas, the contrast makes enemies easier to spot and it just looks *better*.The arena battles are a hype way to change things up, kind of like Doom 2016's arenas, after the standard gameplay... until they just get *too large*. Several times I've had arenas where I and the enemies genuinely couldn't find each other for several minutes, and then when I got done I had to spend first another two minutes harvesting all the ammo and health(maybe automate that, please) and then to find the grey door in the grey all that had opened in a grey corridor under the grey stairs.The areas look pretty good... until you start noticing how many copypasted assets there are. It's all the same containers and doors and hallways to the point where I ended up going *backwards* in one area for a while until I found all the gibs that *weren't* pre-placed. As a sub-point to this, this game also has the worst secrets ever. Most of them aren't *secret* as much as they are "go both left and right when offered the T-intersection" or "look behind the box." And most of the secrets are just "more armor and health!!!!" after the first two levels, and even when they *aren't* that, when they're stuff like equipment upgrades, those upgrades only stick for the duration of the level, they aren't cumulative.It'd also help if the game explained how the Mechanicus upgrade worked, because it upgrades the weapon you're holding when you pick it up, and doesn't JUST make it stronger, it also adds a cool bonus, like turning the mediocre shotgun into a great flak cannon(projectiles bouncing off walls and floors). But with there being only one per level, and the game not deigning to tell me what it does for weapons ahead of time anywhere I could find... there was never really any reason to risk it with another gun. Because the upgrade would probably suck.The game has a cool and moody intro that really sets the tone... and then you never hear another human voice for as far as I got in the game before I got bored of it. Cultists and renegades don't go "oh no it's a space marine blargh." Chaos Marines don't go "har har you dog of the false emperor, time for u 2 die 2 day, hur hur" before you crunch them. You don't have anyone on comms offering commentary. You don't have human survivors. You don't have an Eldar or something that you have witty banter with where he calls you an ape and you call him a FOUL XENOS. All there is, is the occasional little five-word text pop-up about how "THIS IS THE POOPIUM RECYCYLIOS." or "SHOOT A BAD GUY."What really broke the back for me, though, was the Lord of Change. Huge, cool boss, the sort of thing I'd really look forward to fighting in Cultic. But as far as I could tell his mechanics involved:No weak spotsNo special abilitiesShooting fireballs at me(like every other enemy)Occasionally teleportingGetting stuck on the geometry because he was wildly oversized for the arena he was inA health pool big enough to drown a herd of cows in. It took so much tiresome, mindless shooting to kill him.I'm genuinely sad that I don't like this game, but I just don't. And not in some sort of visceral, hateful way, but just in a sort of dull, disappointed way because it has all of the parts I should love, and so many glimmerings of talent, but... it just screws up the landing on every single part.
