_childDocuments_.review: Better than I expected it to be - granted I had quite low expectations, especially given the middling release-day press reviews. The marketing leaned a little *too* heavily on the "IT'S A RETRO FPS THAT WILL MAKE ALL OF YOUR DREAMS COME TRUE" side of things, but I can forgive that.This is definitely more CULTIC than DOOM. I am not very good at Cultic, and so this game serves as almost like a "baby mode" Cultic. The mechanics are slimmed down and the levels are shorter than Cultic, and that's okay.The absurdity of the Space Marine is on full display, with the stomping footsteps and ridiculous - almost moonwalk style - jumps. A 40k purist out there is probably going to make some noise about those jumps aren't possible without a jump pack, but it's also impossible for a dude to kick with both legs whilst running and shooting a gun all at the same time, so y'know, FPSs aren't really known for their realism. Even when the 'realism' is the made up frameworks of 40k. Besides, the ridiculous height of the jump is made up for by the poor in-air maneuverability the player seems to have. This is a fine balancing choice, but given some of the other balancing aspects (touched upon later) there's some work that needs to be done.The game needs some refinements though - if we're gonna keep comparing it to Doom, let's compare the HUD with Doom Eternal's. Getting immediate feedback on grenade type and availability requires me (and I DID just lose my glasses so cut me some slack here) to stop and squint. In Doom Eternal I don't have to think about that. There is a subtle shimmer in the bottom of the screen and a distinctive sound telling me I have grenades available.Balance also seems to need some work. The basic health pips only healing 2hp is not enough for a very hectic arena fight. The pips need to heal 10 and/or there needs to be more availability of bigger health packs around. As it is, the rules aren't super fair right now. Enemies do seem to drop health and armour pips *sometimes* but it's not obvious when. Given how much movement is involved, having a small radius of magnet grab for the pips as well would be a nice addition.Balance in this game is just overwhelmingly stacked against the player in ways that don't seem totally fair.With some adjustments here and there, this is going to be a very VERY good addition to the genre and Emperor be praised it is about friggin time that the Machine Spirit blessed us with a good 40k FPS. What on earth was Fire Warrior?!Play it, enjoy it. But be prepared for some post-death "WHAT THE HECK HIT ME" moments. Maybe take out insurance on your expensive mechanical keyboard if you have issues containing your rage.

_childDocuments_.review: In reality I'd give it like a 7 out of 10. It is solid WH40k in both look and soun and it's a responsive retro style boomer shooter with plenty of shooting. It's feels a lot like Doom or Quake which it both its strength and draw back. Boltgun fails to really manage to feel any different from the classics or to really give you that Space Marine power trip. Everything about it is done well, but Doom and Quake did it just a tad better and a long time ago. You get a standard arsenal, a basic all purpose boltgun, shotgun, heavy bolter and the like. While the weapons feel different some are clear winners compared to others and that makes shooting feel slanted because sometimes you have weapons with full ammo that you just don't want to switch to because they're just no good for much of anything except very specific use cases. This makes the gun selection feel smaller than it is. Form me I think if they ever make a real sequel we could see something special. I feel like there are half ideas here, where something bigger was planned. Like you have a chainsword, but all you can do is swing it around with a cookie cutter animation, when you hit something the swing slows down does continuous damage and finishes the attach. But that's it. The melee is not a single step more complex than that. You're not invulnerable when you make these melee attacks and they don't do a lot of damage to any but the weakest foes, they can't be chained and they give no bonus or regenerations. Why would you be given this weak meaningless melee attack? It feels like it was supposed to be built into a bigger melee system where this flimsy swing was the way to start a combo or trigger something of some kind.

_childDocuments_.review: A bombastic shooter that does what it says on the tin. Sure, there are plenty of weapons to use other than the boltgun, but you know what you're here for. And the boltgun delivers.It's a bit of a slog at times, depending on how much in the way of weapon sound effects, power metal and viscera confetti you can take. If you choose to play on harder difficulties, that's when weapon effectiveness comes into play and you need to pay more attention to what you're using against hardier foes.Personally, I had to break up my play sessions with other games, but I finished the campaign on Hard and had a great time doing it. I didn't enjoy the final level. Without spoilers, I'll just say that the scale of the combat arena destroyed my frame rate, and up til this point it had all felt silky smooth.Anyway, this is still easily one of the best video games to come out of the Warhammer 40K universe. Don't sleep on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little mixed on Boltgun. I think the fundamentals of the game are nailed but aspects of item placement and level design could be improved. Overall I'd recommend you pick up the game, just don't expect a new exemplary boomer shooter. Expect a good, heretic pruging time. Oh, also, I played the game on hard so my experience is based on that difficulty. I thought it provided an appropriate challenge most of the time, but delves into poor balance/unfair challenge at times. If you have good experience with boomer shooters its not a bad choice for a first playthrough.What I liked:This game can be quite the power trip. All throughout the game you're over saturated with resources and honestly, it doesn't feel bad at all. Having the ammo you need for a situation or being able to run around and gather what's needed feels amazing. it also feels appropriate for such an over the top universe like Warhammer 40k. Health and armour is a little restricted but I'll mention that later. Movement feels just perfect. So heavy yet mobile. And the sounds of the space marines stomps will always be amazing to listen to. The guns are pretty good. Each weapon feels good to use and have distinct strengths and weaknesses based on the situation you're in and the enemies you're taking down. The weapons have some subtle nuances to each of them making them feel distinct to the game. Enemies have a good variety and can be combined together well to create very tough encounters.What I didn't like:There was an inconsistency to arena battles, but namely in the item placement and level design. For the most part, battles are most fun when you start off with a challenge, have a little panic when something unexpected happens (maybe an enemy spawned in or you lost track of your health and contempt) and you need to full sprint through the horde of enemies to pick ups you can reasonably plan a route towards. However there are a good chunk of arena battles where this experience of intentional actions is disturbed. When arenas are difficult to understand and navigate it not only makes it difficult to move with intent, like when you're repositioning or moving towards a pickup, but enemies can catch you off guard from areas of the arena you didn't even register as being there. Health and contempt pick ups are also placed confusingly in certain battles. Usually they are placed in crates in the middle of an arena, being easy to collect and not very disruptive to the flow of the battle, but other times they are tucked away in a corner of the map or through a back path that makes you go out of your way during fights and wander aimlessly, really ruining the flow and engagement of battles. In summary, the game feel is just great and enemies are well designed to match, but there's too many poorly designed arena and item layouts that brings the experience down from great to mixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like Boltgun, I really do. I've played about half of the game on Hard, and for a bit it was pretty satisfying. The visuals are incredible, the sound design is chunky and really makes you feel weighty, and the gunplay is very solid. The problem I have with this game is just... a lot of the little details. The arenas always drag on a little too long, the winding corridors all look a little bit too similar, the enemies are a little too dumb.The enemies are a big part of my complaint - they just don't act very interesting. Some of them charge at you, others stand still while shooting at you, and that's... it.Also, combat feels weighty and chunky and you feel like a rampaging war machine and then suddenly you fall over dead, because, uh oh, that enemy does like 100 damage per attack. Oh, you thought you dodged it? Turns out melee attacks deal damage the moment their animation triggers, and not, you know, when the animation actually looks like it's striking.The servoskull is both very difficult to notice - when in the heat of combat it's difficult to make out what it's saying in the 5 seconds before its text disappears - and annoyingly intrusive - it constantly floats around going 'look, health! look, ammo! look, enemies!'And on the subject of health and ammo... what's going on here? There's so much ammo. A completely ridiculous amount. I was never, not even a single time, at risk of running out of ammo. I ran out of ammo for a single gun, once, because I decided to use it instead of anything else. There's grenades absolutely everywhere. Just before a group of enemies spawns? Grenades. Right after the enemies? Have some grenades to refill. Fighting space marines? They also drop some grenades. Health (and armor), on the other hand, felt like they went from incredibly scarce to immensely abundant without any rhyme or reason. Some sections I was barely limping by, health in the double digits and no armor, having to peek around corners before I could move on. Others I just walked past 6 health pickups and 4 armor pickups, unable to touch them because I was at full health from picking up the other 3 health pickups and 4 armor pickups that were hidden around.I dunno. I really wanted to enjoy this game, but all these little issues just make it frustrating and not fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Where is my map? Why do I not have a frigging map to traverse these levels!?Do NOT make a boomer shooter and exclude the map, that is an act of cruelty. It does not make the levels more interesting, it makes them less interesting. More frustrating. Less fun. More akin to work than play. This is not the kind of frustration that comes from a well designed maze that simply bamboozles its player, this is the kind of frustration that comes from a clumsily designed maze being annoying instead of fun. I LOVE mazes in DOOM, Wolfenstein, Quake, etc. This is not that. This is terrible maze design, primarily because of the visuals. But, again, you can't shut em off or overlay them and use a map, so the flawed visuals are all you get.Now, without a frigging map, I MUST pay close attention to each area, so I can even have a hope of finding the way out of it. I can't just enjoy the surroundings, I have to study them, to learn every nook and cranny just trying to find the exit. Running over the million pickups I don't need, which still make a sound when you walk over them for some reason. (seriously questionable quality of life choices are all over this game.)There are giant arrows painted on the floor to help. Sometimes. Huge light based visual markers, using the colors of the doors to identify where you are supposed to go. Sometimes. None of it helps the way a bare bones line-structure map would have. The levels are massive, and unfortunately the environment chosen is an imperial city, so a lot of brutalist architecture and repeated assets everywhere means its insanely easy to get lost or even backtrack without realizing it.I might be done for good at the idiotic portal puzzle. That is not fun, at all, it is only frustrating. Really feel like I wasted my gaming budget for the month on this. There are other issues. Chaos faction gets dull as heck after a few levels. Weapons are pretty disappointing. Shocking amount of pickups, meaning you don't have to care which weapon you use, just use whatever. You'll never ever run out of ammo for it. (that might be a 'medium' difficult issue, but its gross. I'm never low on ammo for anything, ever. Least of all the CONSTANT grenade pickups. How many grenades do they think we're going to use?! Makes it kinda boring, there's no risk or challenge. Just a grind, and a bunch of annoying mazes to beat my head against.)Good advertising and hype, mediocre boomer shooter design, bad maze-play.

_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: On hard difficulty, there are way too many spongy enemies that knock a significant amount of health off.  Weapons are not very interesting to use -- for example, the shotgun is underpowered, requires reloading often, the plasma weapon, while lore accurate according to comments, when used close up damages the player and the boltgun is fairly weak unless upgraded.  Upgrading is not explained, weapon/enemy levels are not explained, there is no map, environments, while varied in themes, are same-y, voice acting is good in cutscenes, absent in-game with the floating partner making unintelligible noises forcing the player to glance up and left to read the text instead of maybe having it displayed like subtitles at the bottom, middle.  I bought myself and my friend a copy and he gave up while I continue to slog through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty decent game overall.  Shooting feels great, really good sound effects, a pretty standard affair of guns but they're fun enough.  I found the game to overstay its welcome a bit in the latter half, the game's probably a bit longer than it needs to be.  At a certain point you've seen all the enemies, you've seen all the guns, and yet you still have like 6 more levels to move through.  I would have preferred a bit tighter pacing but ¯\_(ツ)_/¯.  Good game nonetheless, I try to play a lot of boomer shooters and this one hits all the right marks.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is awesome, however i needed 2 weeks just to finish the first chapter because the game is so tedious i would rather watch the grass grow. Yup, i play on exterminatus and i still bored to death. The worst part is the sound design. Why is this game so quiet? Don't come at me with the taunt button, i want to hear EVERYONE shouting like a maniac, are these heretics introverts or what? The music is very forgetable, there is nothing from that epicness that you would expect from it.Guns also, why do they have so weak sound effects?The gameplay itself is serviceable at best, it could be better if the chainsword would be actually useful and if we had a bit more enemy variety.So far this game is mediocre at best and it is highly overrated for no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the first act and dont think i'm going to continue.I have like 3 main problems with the game.>The big one so far is performance. For a game that looks like Doom with a simple 3d environment and 2d sprites and a lot of fog in act 1 why the game fluctuates between 40 and 110FPS is mind blowing. This ♥♥♥♥ should never drop below 144 its almost impressive how poorly optimised it is.>Weapon balance / enemy balance is not great. All the weapons all have drawbacks like the plasma gun overheats and needs to reload, the shotguns got shot range and long reload (seriously its like 4sec), the heavy bolter doesnt need to reload which is nice but it slows you down when firing so the regular bolter becomes the go too weapon for progressing but its limited to 150 rounds and 1 tiny frog will eat a 25 round magazine from it as they have almost as much HP as a chaos marine. Theres a mix of fast, slow and slower projectile speeds so a lot of the time meaning you either get instantly hit or they clog the arenas - also theres a few hitscan attacks from bosses/mini-bosses that also ruin the flow. But then finding the secrets makes the regular bolter do more damage than the plasma gun with no drawback making all your weapon choices backwards...>The maps aren't amazing. They arent as bad as many people say they are, but they do have problems. Some are dark which combined with the purge red screen tint makes it very hard to see, theres lots of cramped areas which leads to a low of corner hugging with the shotgun/plasma, theres just a lot of stuff to get stuck on in the arena's and theres a lot of back tracking through intuitive areas trying to figure out where to go while in other games its either linear or completing a side area would have a shortcut at the end to take you back to where you were seamlessly.What makes boomer shooters fun is running around, dodging stuff, combo's stuff, being flashy, and having fun, but thats hard to do when your in small cramped areas, hitscan bosses you have to hide from, theres no weakspots to aim for and you cant play how you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: WH40K Games have been really hit and miss, so I am glad to see that Boltgun really hits a lot of the right spots. there are things the game lacks, for example there really isn't much of a story (kind of in the boomer shooter fashion), and there are a few quality of life issues. But as a simple, adrenaline filled, power-fantasy game? its par excellence. Boltgun reminds us that videogames are supposed to be fun.some misc notes: -The guns and the kills are extremely satisfying, everything sounds and feels great. You can practically feel the crunch as you mow enemies down.-Atmosphere and art design is cool as hell-Enemy variety is interesting and engaging.-Where the hell is the mini-map? this has to be one of my biggest gripes with the game. in boomer shooter style, the level layouts are not clear or intuitive to navigate at times. I spent 20 min on one map just trying to find the exit. not cool.-We've seen Imperial worlds in quite a few 40K games now. I think its high time GW takes us to a few other corners of the galaxy. Massive space cathedral factories are cool and all but they're all starting to blend together. Well worth the 30 bucks, and no cut content masquerading as micro-transaction, or missing content on launch. You get what you paid for. Love to see it.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Marketed heavily as another "Boomer Shooter" (don't blame me, the advertisements ACTUALLY refer to it that way), Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun actually plays as an interesting combination between an arena based shooter ala Doom (2016) and newer, pixel based shooters. From the NEW: mobility is key and jumping, dashing, and running around the arena is basically required to not be cut down from the hail of grenades, toxic spit, and gunfire coming from the forces of Chaos which you're pit against. From the OLD: there's secrets to be found with items that offer full health boosts, weapon enhancements (some of which will last an entire level), and new weapons all of which offer different effectiveness against different enemy types. Speaking of weapon effectiveness, an interesting and novel approach to the current "Boomer Shooter" formula is that defense and armor ratings (taken straight from the Warhammer 40k miniatures game) will vary based on enemy types and switching up weapons mid-fight based on the makeup of the enemy waves is encouraged because of it. The story does carry on from Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine although this is mostly a nominal connection and playing that game is NOT required to enjoy what story does exist in this game. True to the older games which Boltgun plays tribute, the story, such as it is, serves more as a justification to kill countless Xenos and Heretics rather than build on the story set by Space Marine.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say. I just love the nostalgic mix of of old school shooter with some new age particle systems. The whole game is like DOOM 1999 2.0 with better graphics and better lore. Playing with the controller and the force feedback rumble makes everything better.  8.5/10  PS: EXTERMINATUS is the only way to play. Otherwise all the other difficulties are noob modes.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Not just a generic boomer shooter with a 40k skin, DOOM sweats and Dusk fans have a lot to enjoy here, especially if you're a 40k fan.Your Space Marine feels powerful and heavy and this is worked into the mechanics nicely. Guns feel good to shoot and sound good too, they definitely live up to the lore. Playing my first run on the hard difficulty (second hardest) provides a good fast paced challenge, the game is not afraid to crush you if you don't keep up, I'll definitely start again on the hardest difficulty once I'm done.DOOM Eternal fans will rejoice at the weapon switching available, I encourage everyone to try cancelling the shotgun pump animation by switching to your Bolter and back again, big PB-Rocket feeling there.Performance is overall solid and I spend most of my time locked at max refresh (5800X+3080 @1440p180Hz, max settings) although I get some heavy frame drops when a lot of enemies and particle effects are on screen, (seems to happen most when using the heavy Bolter) but these are luckily short and infrequent.Overall this is a very cool game made by a talented team that clearly understands the raw fun of a good boomer shooter.Big recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent, but EXTREMELY overrated. I've no idea why this title sits at "overwhelmingly positive" and has reviews like GManLives claiming it's "ridiculously good". It really is not - it's just... decent.It's another boomer shooter but one that feels pretty good to play. Unfortunately it doesn't really do anything noteworthy either, sometimes even falling for design mistakes we should have moved past ages ago in my opinion. The first thing Boltgun struggles with is to fully embrace the niche: just add what the game needs - do not add which doesn't add to the experience the game is trying to go for. The pixelated shading on the weapons (which do receive lighting, so they're actual meshes just "pixelated" through shading techniques) are cool, and I understand they want to highlight them in some way. But reloading adds nothing to this title. The same goes for sprinting. Why? Since Quake we've accepted that the player just always sprints in these games regardless of the situation. Just prune the sprint key. Grenades? Sure, but why several and requiring a key to alternate between them? Just why? More is not always better.The dash is very flavorful, being able to only charge AHEAD an not backwards or laterally, but it's also way too limited for regular use as a result. The weapons feel good, but most are somewhat pestered by needing to be reloaded (let me reiterate: why?). Movement feels accurate. Controls feel responsive. The movement speed feels good. Visual clarity is mediocre at best, with excellent feedback on hitting enemies but almost no feedback on getting hit yourself. Melee feels good and is probably the strongest part of the game: it's a variation of the typical "Call of Duty-knife" where the player immediately tracks the target to be hit, then interpolates to its location over a few frames. Better yet: it briefly slows down time when charging, allowing you to accurately pick a target you want to hit. It's smart, feels good to use and compliments the game. Sound design is surprisingly good. Music is good. There is minor incentive for quickswapping.Besides the severe lack of feedback on receiving damage there are other big issues at play here: the map design is just bad. Surprisingly bad actually. Not putting too much effort into hiding the secrets is completely fine with me; I always skipped them in Quake and Unreal tournament because they took away from the pacing, but in Boltgun you really just run across them by sheer accident. What is less forgivable is the weirdly looping back linear corridors that the game seems to absolutely adore. It's often quite confusing what exactly the game wants you to do and I've run the same circle over several times in 3 out of 5 maps simply because I missed some keycarded door earlier in the same section. But the arenas where the player must "purge the heretics" (several waves of enemies) are just atrocious. The game has a tendency to throw excessive resources your way when you don't need them, and barely any when you DO need them. You can quite literally make the game 20 times harder by accidentally walking into an arena with little health, as god forbid there are any actual resources in them. The arenas also add nothing to the game: instead of just walking forward you now essentially walk forward once, then backwards as it spawned a bunch of fodder straight in your back (which is also awful as you receive barely any feedback on getting hit) and then forward again. Why? Look at Doom Eternal: make USE of the arenas when you are going to add them. Add means to quickly traverse them, add paths to traverse with resources on them. Boltgun does none of those things; it's just a big open, closed off section with no incentive to go anywhere but sit besides some piece of geometry and shoot the things until they stop shooting back.I mean it's not a bad game. The weapons feel good. The movement feels good. The sound design is great. But it just doesn't really do anything specifically well design wise. It's "just another boomer shooter". One of the most perplexing games to see receive such immense appraisal.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: An okay boomer shooter. Game feels good to play and looks great and if you're into 40k you're gonna really enjoy how faithfully it captures that look and feel. Level design is a little bad but is basically carried by having a 'draw a line where I should go' button ala Dead Space that you can use to just have the game tell you where the next door is.Only real complaint is that enemies can be kind of spongey and they give you a cool mechanic where you can slow down time and dash forward with a chainsword, but doing so is almost always a bad idea because unlike other games with similar designs, you aren't actually rewarded for rushing in. If it worked closer to Doom 2016 and doing up-close melee kills gave you temporary invulnerability and health back, it would probably be a lot more fun.Get it on a sale. It's fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun is an insanely fun game. It is a boomer shooter set in the incredible Warhammer 40,000 universe however even if you don't know anything about Warhammer this is still an incredible game the story is interesting and it connects to the Space Marine 1 story line however the connection is small. The story mode is good however it isn't something that will blow your mind, most of the enjoyment comes from the action packed and gruesome fast paced gameplay all with the Warhammer coat of paint. My favorite mode is the Horde mode which is a wave based arena shooter that progressively gets more difficult as the waves go on and it gives you access to more and more of the game's arsenal. If you love Warhammer and boomer shooters than this is 100% worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall fantastic but there's some weird underlying issues that this game has that are really problematic for this type of game even if they make sense to a logical degree.Main Pros:The game has a fantastic template with a lot of things to do and all of them are very fun. Game is an absolute 9/10 from my initial impressions and I don't think anything about that is going to change by playing the game more. My main issues:1.I know Space Marines are 8ft tall genetically engineered death machines but most enemies are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ small I can't see them 30% of the time. it also makes enemy types and variants virtually impossible to distinguish from one another because everything is like 2ft tall to me. Having larger pickups would also be really helpful.'2. There is also an almost unacceptable amount of vagueness when it comes to actually knowing what anything is or what it does. THIS COULD EASILY BE SOLVED BY A CODEX OR AN ACTUAL TUTORIAL. There's a lot of picking things up and not knowing what it does and having no way to find out.3. The HUD is a mess. Everything is too small, barely readable, and in strange locations. ALSO 1/3RD OF THE HUD'S ELEMENTS ARE NEVER EXPLAINED AND I DON'T HAVE A SINGLE CLUE WHAT THEY DO.  Reading you ammo or grenade count is virtually impossible unless you stop and check and then squint really hard. Even having the option to customize the HUD is not a thing. 4. Having enemy variants and then having some enemies that can have multiple completely different looks or color palettes that are not different variations is a cardinal sin.5. Moving over an item pick-up always plays the item pick-up sound every time even when you haven't actually picked up that item because your stores of said item are full.Other than that this game is really good and I could easily recommend it to anyone even with the issues that it has.

_childDocuments_.review: A very faithful boomer shooter. It is not really a "good" one, but it is just very "faithful" to the genre and the time. That is to say, this game carries over a lot of, probably too much of, good but also at the same, bad or obsolete designs from the old school boomer shooters. That is not only limited to its visual style.This game reminds me of the time when I have nothing but classic  and  to play for the whole summer vacation, but that time was not made of only enjoyable moments. For example, getting stuck in a particular encounter over and over, drawing own map with pen and paper, or getting lost looking for keys for days are certainly not pleasant memories.If you have experienced the 90's FPS era and wholeheartedly enjoyed boomer shooters (I did not really), then this game is well worth trying and probably will bring back memories. Otherwise, the game could really use some design tweaks or QoL improvements to bring the experience on par with more "modern" shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: "I will finish what Captain Titus started!" 7/10 - Room for improvementWarhammer 40,000: Boltgun is a movement-shooter spinoff to the "Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine" and offers an entry for this Genre into the Warhammer 40K universe. If you have played games such as the older "Doom"-Titles or other modern retro shooters such as games like "Dusk" or "Ultrakill" you might feel right as home, with some differences to spare. The game follows a health-kit/armor econmy system. Cautious play is incentivised, hyper agression such as in Ultrakill or the modern Doom-Games does not work out.If you are more interested in a detailed review:The grafics and artstyle are well done, the devs clearly put effort into it and during many levels you will feel the sheer size of the Warhammer 40K universe. The rich pixelart is commendable as the degree of style stays consistent throughout your experience. The level-design sadly undercuts the visuals, leading to repetitive gameplay in corridors which blend together during the given selected chapter. The leveldesign tends to be hit or miss, in bigger levels and arenas you might need to use the navigation system on your companion to not loose track of where you are supposed to go. In smaller arenas the level design can lead to claustrophobic impressions, as enemies are often spawned in around you during an arena-holdout. This specific way to spawn the enemies combined with the lack of distinct sounds can lead to you beeing suprised by melee units spawning behind you and taking half you HP off before you notice why you are taking damage, which can be fatal in smaler rooms, as your melee options are limited to a chainsword which does not anywhere the damage you take while striking back. middle-sized Maps tend to work the best, both for enemies as well as gameplay. In regard to the audio it can be a mixed bag as sadly many sounds drown another out or are not distinct enough so that the gameplay experience might suffer because of it. Main issues are in this regard that while weapons have clear sound and sound quite good for a spinnoff which was supposed to generate hype for Space Marine 2, the lack of destinct enemy sounds leads to a mixture of effects which make it hard to differenciate between them. In this regard games like "Darktide" do the job very well, sadly in "Boltgun" you will miss many of these often important soundcues.While the details on the maps are well made and the design is consitent it yet felt to me that the game often lingers too long in already traveled terrain so that many levels bleed into each other and often have little distinct identity. To me to felt as if the game could have used different scenarios like beeing outside / inside / on a wall looking down more often, which is in my eyes a lost opportunity.As game-stability goes, the game runds smooth, over the course of 9 hours I had only a single crash which did not loose me any progress due to the games autosave feature. Manual saves are also an option, in later levels i had to use it, as a few autosaves could have softlocked me, if not for my experience with the genre and its ressource management.I played on the Normal difficulty and could go through the game nicely, Bossfights and later chapters were challanging.I am yet to play the "Forges of Curruption"-DLC, so i cannot comment on that part yet.According to the steam-archievements less than a third of players reach beyond the first chapter, which suprised me.Overall the game does many things right and holds it own identity, yet could improve on the shortcommings listed above in the future with DLC. While I enjoyed it im not certain if I would replay the main-campaign for the same reason. Id would most likely rather return to Ultrakill or try out other games within the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Yep, it's pretty good. Gameplay is satisfying and I feel like I'm playing Brutal Doom in the thick of it. I'm used to hitscans, though, so the projectiles felt a little floaty but I eventually got used to it. I particularly like the taunts and over-the-top pixelated bloodiness of the firefights.The only downsides in my opinion are a lack of multiplayer, horde modes, and a map - please, holy Sigmar, give us a map. Some of the levels can be really confusing if you're not careful, and I sometimes will spend ten minutes wandering around looking for the next gate or door. Plus, with a present lack of a horde mode or multiplayer (pvp and/or pve), replayability will be somewhat low.All-in-all, a pretty decent FPS. Even if you aren't into the so-called "Boomer Shooters" it's still a pretty fun game to hold you over until the next retro FPS or Warhammer-themed game comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best 40k games I’ve played.The gameplay is fast paced as you would expect from a “boomer” shooter and mistakes cost you health and the shame of hearing an angel of death grunt in pain. The game is not very hard though, not even in Exterminatus (max difficulty). I found the fights in the game to have a good balance between easy and challenging, which is good because it lets you blow off some steam after a fight that costs you a few deaths.The art style looks pixelated by default but you can adjust it a little bit. I didn’t find the default pixelation to get in the way of me seeing projectiles and dodging (on 1440p), especially since everything everyone shoots is bright colored.Sound design is top notch. The sound of your steps and any movement, like jumps and falls, sound very heavy yet you remain nimble. The feeling you should be getting when playing as a space marine. The gun sounds and enemy death sounds (like when they explode) are great to listen to also.There are 8 guns and all of them feel great to use but my personal favorites are the boltgun and the heavy bolter. Both of them are a treat to shoot because of the sound design and the damage feedback on enemies (humanoid heretics explode in meaty chunks).You also have a taunt button to say some stuff a space marine would say. Which you should rebind to an easily accessible button like a mouse thumb button so you can spam it during combat.About story/lore. There isn’t too much. I’m not an expert in warhammer lore either but I was playing this live and some guy came in to complain about the lore/setting in the game. This person was complaining about having chaos space marines, daemons and cultists together. I don’t really know if its lore is accurate or what but I don’t really care because the game is awesome. Maybe it was a copypasta. In any case it was funny as ♥♥♥♥.Game score: Must play / 40k.

_childDocuments_.review: Being a fan of WARHAMMER mainly the stories and the video games as my painting skills for the miniatures is somewhat poor. I had always wanted a WARHAMMER video game fitting the mould of Doom and Quake yes, we had 2003’s WARHAMMER fire warrior but it was no Doom or Quake. Fast forward 20 years and my dreams had come true I saw the trailer for Auroch Digitals WARHAMMER Boltgun the art style the music chosen for the trailer got me really excited for it to be released and I purchased on PC Day one.The story for Boltgun follows the lead character Malum Caedo a Sternguard Space Marine of the Ultra Marines purging his way through the heretics on Graia where dastardly rogue Techpriests have been experimenting with Drogan’s power source which just so happens to open a rift to all the forces of Chaos to invade the forge world. This also gets the attention of Chaos sorcerer Tumulas Samael who now seeks the power source for his own evil doings.Boltgun has a playtime of around 8 to 10 hours for the base game split across three chapters containing 8 levels in each (24 levels) containing secrets areas and for the achievement hunters out there 21 achievements to get so plenty to do.The levels follow the format of corridors and some outside areas where you have some scope to stomp around dealing death from above or on ground level, level one you your pod with your fellow squad members gets damaged in the descent and you are the only survivor you start with just a chainsword and a servitor that will accompany you and help to guide you through the game. This level is more of a tutorial you have some enemies to obliterate with your chainsword until you work your way into an inside area with corridors to go get your first gun the Boltgun this rapid-fire death bringer mows through the heretics with great satisfaction and will be your staple weapon due to low ammo counts in some of the other weapons. When the second level comes around you will be introduced do a new enemy the Chaos Space Marine these can take a bit of a beating compared to cannon fodder you faced at the beginning if the game. Sometimes the levels can become a little frustrating as you need to find keys to open doors and there at times some back tracking or you cant seem to find your way and accidently back track but this didn’t take away from the fun for me other than one level Sanctum Magistratum the last map of chapter 1 the warp gates you have navigate is very much like a maze and I found myself going in circles many times until I finally working it out thankfully the rest of the levels didn’t give me any frustration like that one.Now for the weapons but first I must say at the end of each chapter your weapons will reset so you will start with just the chainsword and your Boltgun.The Chainsword – I didn’t find myself using this weapon that much I tended to use it on the cannon fodder and found it be useless against Chaos Marines and demons for the most part.The Boltgun is a steady gun that will mow through cannon fodder with ease and deal punishment to the tougher enemies.The Shotgun does what any shotgun does destroys what’s in front of it a nice punchy weapon but with a low ammo stock best used in corridors.Plasma Gun. This is a rapid-fire gun that does a great deal of damage to near enough everything, but you will run out of plasma charges quite quickly.The Heavy Bolter this is one the standout weapons for me blasting away with this you just see life bars being deleted before your very eyes but again run out of ammo quickly and the weapon draw is a little slow.Vengeance launcher this is a good weapon is fires explosives that stick the enemies brilliant for clearing hordes of Nurgle. (The jumpy little bastards).The Meltagun similar effect to a flame thrower I found that this worked well against pretty much anything close range like the shotgun.Volkite Cavalier this is like the plasma gun but instead of firing rapid-fire shots this fires out a lazy beam where if the fire button is held down it will be a continues beam.Grav Cannon, you get this weapon late into the game probably a good thing as it just obliterates everything this is a Volkite cavalier on steroids.The enemies there are a few some like to moon you if you miss them, and some just have a death wish.Light enemies  Autogun CultistHeavy Studder CultistCultist ChampionPlasma Renegade ­Nurgling or the jump little bastards as I call themBlue Horror –Medium level enemiesChaos Space MarineLesser plague Toad –Pink Horror –Flamer –Screamer of TzeentchHeavy enemiesChaos TerminatorExalted FlamerAspiring Champion/Chosen ChampionPlague ToadSuper-HeavyAmbullAncient AmbullLord Of ChangeGreat Unclean OneSorcererWhilst playing this game I did not come across any issues with frame rate or crashes this held very steady for me.On the 18/06/24 new DLC is coming a Horde mode and story expansion which I will also be reviewing. _childDocuments_.review: So as a disclaimer, I have returned this game, but not because it was bad.  More just that I don't feel I get the same enjoyment out of the genre as I used to back in the Doom/Wolfenstein days, so don't feel I'd get enough value personally.I would happily recommend it to any who are into old school shooters, warhammer 40k or simply just high octane FPS games.The graphics look gorgeous for the style, the weapons feel like they have solid weight and they are as devastating as they 'should' be in the lore.  The combat is fluid, smooth and fast, so realistically everything you'd want from it.That said...  The gameplay loop is where I felt it dips a bit and I feel this is more where personal tastes come into it more than anything.  What I experienced in the game, it's quite simply "Move to this location.  Shoot everything.  Move to next location.  Shoot everything.  Find key. Open door.  Shoot everything."  There wasn't much to it beyond that, which tbf was pretty much what the deal was in the old school games as well.If that's the sort of thing you're looking for, I'd strongly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game, but a few things are really disappointing to me.The biggest letdown is the level design, both visually and from a gameplay standpoint. Warhammer 40k offers so much potential for stunning, engaging level design, and while this game has the occasional standout scene, most of it just feels like pointless copy-pasted sludge. The levels also don't flow very well, especially compared to other boomer shooters. The secret hunting isn't as involved and organic as it could be. There's basically no intractability in the levels.The other main problem for me is the overall muddiness in the visuals and audio. I really love the spritework on the player character and the enemies. The pixelated textures on the environment look great on their own. But there is an overwhelming fog that just drenches everything in visual mud and drains the life out of everything. It gets worse during the arena sections, when the player character literally sees red.The sound design for all the individual elements is also great, but the mixing just lets it down and makes everything sound muddy. The music especially lacks any clarity or punch. The big action moments are really let down by the muddiness of the audio.Still, it's a fairly fun shooter set in the 40k universe, and if that's all you want, then you will get it here.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: I know the reviews for this game are positive, very much so, and initially the game is great, engaging and the novelty factor is through the roof. However I think most of the reviews would also consider this a "good" game rather than a great one, 7.5/10 rather than 9/10, something where Steam reviews do not make any distinction. In terms of pros, what you see in the trailers and the gameplay videos really is what you get, no more, no less. On the other hand I have refunded my purchase for two reasons; one being performance being a little bit choppy, which, when the game is a retro shooter as it is and with the graphics you see in the videos, is completely unacceptable. The second reason, and the more pressing, is that it just isn't fun. You shoot stuff, blood spurts out, you shoot more stuff. There doesn't seem to have been any effort in pushing any boundaries of the genre at all (I get this is a retro shooter but something like Selaco is as well and that felt far more fulfilling). The arena mobs feel lazy, as if the developers needed to pad out the game time in some way and I feel no desire to come back to it, unfortunately. It has promise and I may come back later. The bolter is absolutely awesome as well. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Game with a lot of potential, very fun for the first few hours, but ruined by a constant swarm of bullet sponge enemies with lackluster weapons to deal with them. On top of that, each 'boss' fight increases in ridiculousness as you progress, spawning countless nurglings, plague frogs, terminator marines, and more tanky baddies that make it more of an annoying chore to take care of with your (pretty weak, comparatively) weapons. I can't help but think there's a good reason why so many owners of the game failed to complete it, despite glowing reviews. 40k fans are desperate for something that isn't a pathetically transparent half-baked cash grab from GW, and I can understand why they gathered around this game with positive reviews.If you want decently-balanced fun with challenging gameplay at higher difficulties, pick up Space Marine 2 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unpleasant from top to bottom.  The level design is boring and repetitive from the textures to the layout to the gameplay.  Maps are identical rooms pasted together with thin hallways where you'll get constantly ambushed by annoying enemies.  Most levels have some kind of issue where you have to backtrack through an area you've already cleaned out or find some button or hallway that's extremely easy to miss in order to find a key.  I get that they were going for old school, but games like Duke 3D still had a map.  Here you just get to wander around listening to your footsteps.The gunplay feels cheep with enemies spawning out of nowhere to sprint at you or being nearly hidden in an alcove above you somewhere.  The weapons are either underpowered for anything but the cannon fodder, don't have enough ammo, or some other annoyance like the long wait for the grenade launcher's projectiles to actually detonate.  The boss rooms keep respawning enemies so unless you want to run out of ammo, you need to focus on the bullet sponge in the middle of the room and not the hoard of nonsense coming after you.  The game also runs out of new bosses two thirds of the way through so you just keep having the same boss battle repeatedly throughout the last chapter.The music is irritating, the little skull following you has a couple good jokes, but is otherwise irritating, the overall theme is just bland with nothing but stale factories connected with gothic archways and the occasional featureless desert to break up the monotony.

_childDocuments_.review: Thought it would be another fps masterpiece but it turned out to be surprisingly mediocre and overrated.  What a shame, i love the 40k universe, and seeing it get its own boomer shooter was something very exciting to me. The gunplay, controls, feeling are incredibly good, and that's Boltgun's biggest qualities. However, it's really not enough to redeem the whole game. The gameplay loop is poor and gets stale pretty quickly. You do one arena fight after another, again and again in places that all feel -and sometimes look- the same. Levels are usually bland corridors and arenas. They're uninteresting to roam despite some occasional nice scenery. Even the secrets aren't good. And i know what you're thinking: "." Well, yes, sortof. BUT the craftmanship behind good shooters is what makes any encounter or place stand out as unique. It's what makes a 3D world feel real, alive and tangible even with archaic textures and geometry.  Boltgun completely fails at this and playing it became a chore before i reached the end of the first chapter. The difficulty and balancing certainly didn't help: most of the time, the "Hard mode" is way too easy. And then there's sudden odd difficulty spikes with a few mundane mobs being able to easily kick your ass or previous bosses coming back as normal enemies. Last but not least: bullet sponges. Way too many of them, specially when you get closer to the end.I don't know if i was setting the bar too high but there are far better games like that for the same price or less. I'm not saying it's particularly bad at all. I just can't bring myself to recommend it solely because of the aforementioned flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy. Where to begin with this. Boltgun isn't a BAD game, but its a heavily flawed game that becomes more apparent the more you play.The good things first. Visually the game is excellent across the board. Sprites, animations, even the lore accurate architecture are all very detailed and look great. Sound design is top notch, from the chainsaw sword to the iconic bolter that fires literal anti-material rounds with rocket propellant for maximum damage, is just "chef's kiss". Even as a mild fan of 40k, i respect the effort to keep everything faithful to the source material, but obviously focusing on fun factor first and foremost. Now the bad news. Boltgun is a SLOG to play on anything other than easy or normal. I play all boomer shooters on the 2nd highest difficulty, Boltgun was no exception, but i REALLY wish i did make an exception. Level design is terrible. Just straight terrible. Early on the game focuses on very large open areas, with some set pieces to showcase some of your skills, like the charge move and the ground slam. Both these skills are useless after the first chapter with enemies having much higher health pools, and those enemies being far more frequent. The enemy variety is vast, but the enemy attack patterns are very similar. Most enemies have insane pathing and shot prediction, this wouldn't be so bad if the game didn't throw 30 enemies at once in some arenas, and some enemies are just sponges that take FAR too much damage. Most "Purge" sections quickly turn into cluster ♥♥♥♥♥, with several dozen enemies constantly shooting you. I think the devs knew this too, thats why they added obscene amounts of healing and armor in each arena.I never thought i'd reference Far Cry New Dawn ever again, but here we are. Enemies have strength levels indicated by the symbol next to their life bar. Your weapons have a strength level too, the lower the strength the lower damage you deal regardless of what range. I hated this awful system in Far Cry, i hate it here. You'd think a shotgun in close range would be a safe bet for consistent damage. NOPE! That Chaos terminator is level 5, your shotgun is level 3, have fun wasting ammo! You can technically level up all your weapons, but only one per level and from a secret upgrade you have to find, and the upgrade goes away at the start of every new level. This isn't the same as Doom Eternal, where every weapon is a chess piece that has a specific function for a specific enemy type. All this system does it make you run with 1 weapon for as long as you can, then swap to the next strength leveled weapon. Basically Plasma gun the entire playthrough. I rarely used the bolter, the literal name of the game, thats how bad it is.I bet Boltgun is great on easy and normal. Charging through enemies, leaping around with the chainsaw, squishing non-believers while singing praises of the emperor. On hard or higher, i just wanted it to end. This is even worse knowing there are better alternatives out right now. Prodeus, Brutal Doom, Postal: Brain damaged, just to name a few similar games. I give credit where its due, Boltgun is a top tier game game worthy of the praise. No early access, bug free, solid price to playtime ratio, and overall a fun time. But after coming off of HROT and jumping into this, 2 different styles of game, sure, but HROT has a focused vision. This game is all glitz and glamor but mediocre once you take off the makeup.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game today and to review it is quite simple, so here it goes.To have a doom-like game in this day and age goes against almost every conceivable industry practice, we moved away completely from colorful, fast, metal blasting power shooters to realistic, slow, brown modern shooters that feel repetitive from the moment a new one hits the market. Although we've had the new DOOM (2016) and DOOM Eternal as a breath of fresh air, I feel like while loyal to the originals they still lack the nostalgia value of the graphical representation.As for the Warhammer 40.000 take on it, I feel like it couldn't have been a better hit. I'm a massive fan of the hobby, plastic space army men addicted since I was young, building, painting, the lore, the whole charade. This game has quickly risen up to my top games for the Wh40k franchise..I completely support the use of 2D sprites and simplified yet really well thought out geometry and textures, these art assets can be done in a quicker manner, with lower costs to the developers and possibly the promise of more content more often, we don't need 100 gigs worth of vertices, 4k textures and physics based hair, simplicity in design will model any artistic vision if done well, and this game has it in spades.The gameplay is as expected, fast, impactful and reminiscent of boomer shooters like DOOM, Quake, Serious Sam, Duke Nukem 3D and the likes. While 90s kids used to eat them for breakfast, it's true that those who haven't played them when young will feel some discomfort (in the form of motion sickness) due to the speed at which this game wants you to move in, remember, you have to move fast in order to dodge projectiles, break line of sight and gather ammo consistently, this is the whole point of doom clones.The guns are iconic and while games from this genre have the tendency to powercreep the later discovered guns, completely overshadowing the first ones, this title has done it right, each weapon has a purpose due to the level design and enemy design, they will nudge you to use a specific weapon without you even realizing it: Long Corridors? Heavy Bolter, you'll kill everything in your path; Open Area? You can freely use explosive weapons and grenades without damaging yourself; Short Tunnels with low vision? Shotgun! Lots of small enemies that die from a single shot? Bolter! Giant enemies that pose a great threat? Grav-gun! You get the idea.With very few cinematics this game tells the story of a lone Sternguard Veteran attempting to kill anything in his path in order to seal shut a warp gate from which chaos spawns, all with a totally intended comedic slip as to why a single space marine was sent for this mission, due to the . This is all you need to burn the heretic.The following are more or less nitpicks but they do still exist:This game is a blessing from the Emperor, if you're a Warhammer 40.000 nerd that also thirsts for DOOM nostalgia, get on the bandwagon, the devs deserve it.Just please add multiplayer and modding support, it's all I ask.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I tell people prices are too low to justify the required work involved, but this time it's the other way around. This is just another DOOM clone! There are so many open source tutorials on how to create this kind of game on the internet, there's virtually no engineering skill required! These games are usually free of charge or no higher than a couple of bucks.It's also glaringly obvious from the game start menu and initial cut scene that there will be more skill sets (aka Space Marines) to choose between with which to play. If they really go to introduce those as charged DLCs I need to recommend this game even less.So please be aware that everything about this game is easy money for developer, publisher and Games Workshop.That said, the gameplay is smooth. 40k slaughter and DOOM style were meant for one another. Artists and level designers also did great work here, though the former mostly had to copy what already existed in the GW franchise. Yes, it means that I see very little innovation of any kind here, all departments considered. However, if you like the franchise and look for a way to support the parties involved financially, here's your chance. That's pretty much why I accepted the price, should you be wondering.

_childDocuments_.review: Boltgun is a love letter to the 90s shooter era, only with the volume dialed up to 11 and a massive power fist smashing the button for good measure. If you loved DOOM, Quake, and RTCW, you’ll find a home here amongst the skulls, the screams, and the endless pixelated carnage.Forget RTCW’s knife, forget Quake’s axe—this game gives you a chainsaw on a sword, and it’s basically the medieval weapon you never knew you needed.If you’re nostalgic for the days when your screen was a kaleidoscope of pixelated blood, gore, and enemies that looked like they were birthed by a high-speed blender, Warhammer Boltgun might be your new best friend. Imagine if DOOM and Quake had a high-octane love child, and they raised it in a gothic monastery with a stack of grimdark Warhammer lore. That’s Boltgun in a nutshell, except this child has also been bench-pressing heretics since it was old enough to hold a Chainsword.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the worst experience and least fun I had with this game in this year. Lets knock out the positives first: the pixelated art is amazing and shooting heavy weapons for short period of sessions can be fun. I say can because you cant play this game for a long time because its get very repetitive very fast and not fun fighting same enemies. The fun ends here. The biggest problem of this game for me was how terrible level design is created. Most of the time you feel lost and try to find the way out. Some layers of same level repeats itself to the point where you get even more confused where to go. The enemy ai is bad to. Smaller enemies spawing behind your back. Some of them just standing there doing nothing and waiting for you to come and shoot them. Encountered one bug where the first boss was stuck on a stairs and couldn’t move. The biggest slap is how dreadful and painful “music” is in this game if you can call it music in the first place. The meniu music greets you with beautiful metal cover and….nope we can have nice things here. Have the rest of a game some beats and poof I don’t know how to call them. Sounded more like regurgitating vomiting sounds.

_childDocuments_.review: There are many things I respect and appreciate about this game despite finding some elements that do frustrate me. There are levels where the progression is all over the place. Mind you, I did finish Chapter 1 and plan on finishing the game. But one level in Chapter 1 required some sort of understanding that maybe, just maybe, was out of my knowledge when it comes to Warhammer. Secondly, this is a Warhammer game so this isn't a true "boomer shooter" since it relies on weapon stats rather than the conventions you associate with other FPS. I don't play FPS for stats or RPG-elements. On the technical side, this game tends to slow down from time to time in tight corridor with a lot of action which isn't great at all. Not to mention that, sometimes, failing to land properly makes the landing sound stack which can be defeaning.However, the gunplay feels meaty and that is thanks to the aesthetics and overall destruction caused by the weapons. Each weapon feels good to hear which is very hard to do. Enemy variety is certainly better than it has any right to be and that is probably thanks to the lore. I'm not someone who knows much about Warhammer but I understand its reputation as a tabletop strategy/role-playing game so I just treat Malum Caedo as the Warhammer's Doom Slayer which is almost accurate because Malum can speak. Also, each secret being a temporary reward in power is great and does encourage exploration.There's some to dislike, but lot to love. It's Warhammer to a fault but I would take a mode that does away with the RPG elements and focus on the strength of the genre.

Cogitating..." or something like that, or "Try looking for the key in adjacent rooms", surely my blessed space marine brain couldn't have come up with that? Or, best thing ever - "Suggestion: Lost?". _childDocuments_.review: This is going to probably be the most negative positive review this game gets. It's... fine. It runs, doesn't crash, doesn't have any weird bugs, and the retro aesthetic is kinda cute. But a lot of it feels like an absolute slog. Level design is atrocious, just press N until you get wherever the next room is, don't waste your time trying to make sense of it. Enemies start out fine but just get too needlessly tanky and uninteresting/frustrating, felt like everything gets one free shot on you before you have time to wear them down, and boss fights are just one big guy standing still with a huge health bar that you have to pump hundreds of rounds into before they give up. Not to mention visibility is pretty poor, the gore, explosions, and short draw distance mean a lot of the time you're getting shot at by things you cannot see (especially the plasma gunners who are wearing black, their projectiles are easier to see than they are).And on top of all this, your weapons aren't very imaginative or fun to use. The boltgun is good against the smallest enemies but everything else can tank a magazine, and the plasma gun is good against everything else. All other weapons are either useless, or worse than the plasma gun but decent enough for magdumping into bullet sponge enemies. I also found the melee system to be awful, never really got the hang of it and anyone I wanted to chainsword seemed to also be able to hit me back, defeating the purpose. So, yeah. It's a game. If you've never played another game in this genre it's probably good. Compared to something like DOOM 2016 it's awful, but that's a high bar.

_childDocuments_.review: You pretty much get what it says on the package - A retor shooter with a Warhammer 40K paint job.And I had a great time with it - The game makes you really feel like a Space Marine stomping through a horde of heritics and demons in the name of the Emperor!I played on my steam deck and it was great, but I think all the boss fights I needed to change to my pc, make of that what you will.- Controls feels absolutly great, you feel like a Space Marine stomping around, but it still feels fluid and fast.- Art style is great, it calls back to the old Doom and Quake without looking old. - The melee charge feels great-  The game is not always great at telling where to go next. I'm not asking for a map or a big arrow pointing to the door but why can't the servo skull indicate direction or something?- Armor and Health pickups seems a bit off - There is either to few or to many, giving a weird dificulty curve.- The secret pickup where, for me at least, either fine, inconsequential or found to late to be of use...- While they story is not the most important in a game like this, the lack of voice acting meant that the story pretty much disapeared - A little more voice acting would be awesome!- Given the setting and the iconic melee weapons Space Marines has access to, a few more melee weapons would have been awesome.- An option to make the Servo Skull give a hint for directions

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think this game deserves its current "Very Positive" rating here on steam. I can see how it's perfect for people who wanted exactly what it is but for the rest of us who were maybe expecting a better rounded game with great retro flavor it will fall short.Now, while I actually enjoyed Boltgun I still have to give it a cautionary thumbsdown when answering steam's question "Would you recommend this game to other players?". Here are a few points to consider if you are not sure if it's for you:On the positive side it has great retro visuals and a pretty decent soundtrack with great sound effects and the action feels awesome once you get going. And if I had to list its one redeeming quality it'd be its auto checkpoint system. It's an awful turnoff when you need to keep quicksaving every minute just in case. The game seems to have a 120fps cap and I didn't have a single crash in my 10 hours playthrough.Now the bad stuff:-The absolute worst is how padded the game is. Around halfway trough you'll have seen every enemy type (including the final boss) but one.-There's no automap and in some levels you'll be stuck for minutes at a time looking for a door or switch you missed.-Weapon vs enemy-level system makes big enemies way too bulletspongy if you don't have the right ammo.-I got stuck into walls 3 or 4 times, no big deal.

_childDocuments_.review: I can only tolerate Boltgun in about 20 minute increments. It is repetitive, tedious, and ultimately underwhelming. You probably already know that this is Warhammer 40k's take on a "boomer shooter." To that end, the first level is fun. It's a homage to the original DOOM and keeps things light. You'll mow down Chaos cultists and rip and tear your way through the level with a bolter and chainsword that **feel** powerful. However, the farther I go the less fun I find myself having. I find it really telling that 5 months after release only 1/3 of players stuck it out to the first boss. Things start to grind down almost immediately. You notice the music isn't satisfying or reactive. The trailer and main menu set the tone for a rocking shooter in the style of DOOM 2016, but what you get is a lot of chanting and quiet moments even as you're blowing enemies to bits. It is tonally mismatched for both a 40k game and a boomer shooter. Tonally, there's nothing to push you forward. This is especially disappointing because the arena-style PURGE areas... don't have any big musical cue to announce them or get you excited for a big fight. Just a babbling servoskull. It's really embarrassing. There's a weapon "strength" system where certain weapons work better against certain enemies. So a lot of enemies end up as bullet sponges if you don't use the right weapon against them or just in general (looking at you Plague Toads). So uhh... good job taking the worst ideas from Doom Eternal's Ancient Gods DLC and basing the entire game around it, I guess? Also, weapon swap animations are long enough to prevent most quickswap combos which... for a boomer shooter is just really embarrassing. There are a lot of minor things, but they start to stack up. The damage feedback is really weak, so a lot of times you won't realize you're being hurt at all unless you take massive damage in a single hit. Space Marine 2011 and also DOOM (the games this is based on) gave you health for meleeing enemies. Here melee is basically part single-target stun and part lunge attack. Health pickups are usually static in the world (though some enemies might drop 2 HP pickups and ammo).There's also a lot of minor quality of life stuff. You can only restart from checkpoint if you die, if you restart a level at all you only start with the boltgun (if you play the levels sequentially you keep your weapons, but not any upgrades), the game is awful about telling you what the powerups do (there's a token in every level that upgrades each weapon in a unique way, for example). And the list goes on.   The bigger issue, I think, is the level design and encounter design. The first level is 1-2 minutes. The second level is 6-8 minutes. Third level 10-12 minutes. Fourth level 18-20 minutes. And so on. Levels often reuse assets, as well as shape sometimes making you play the same piece of scenery from the opposite direction. The fifth level has you play the same section of bridge and battlements TWICE. On top of this, there aren't enough assets to make areas within the same level look unique. Everything blends together, sometimes because you're walking over the same assets in the same layout twice or even three times. That, combined with extensive level times it feels boring and undeserved.It's really embarrassing level design.  There's also the problems of PURGE areas which reveal a lack of combat momentum. A lot of them are absolutely gigantic compared to the number of enemies that spawn to the point where you're actively trying to find enemies in a moment where you should be overwhelmed --and that's on the hardest difficulty where *more* enemies spawn; on standard difficulty the empty feeling is much worse. Add onto this a weak draw distance or deliberate fog effects and purge moments are less high intensity trials (like DOOM 2016) and more walking around a big empty area waiting for things to happen. It's really embarrassing. Within these levels, the encounter design is really bad, again lacking momentum. It's rooms full of enemies, mostly guys with guns or daemons with slow-moving projectiles, usually on the same axis. How does Boltgun make rooms more difficult? They add more enemies. There's not a flow or synergy between how enemies are placed or what encounters contain what kinds of enemies. It is a zerg rush approach to encounter design and it's another part of what makes boltgun so unengaging. It's not just that every room looks the same, but the encounters feel the same.So we have kind of a trifecta of serious, unavoidable issues. Boring tedious level design, boring tedious music, and boring tedious bullet sponge enemies.  Between these issues we have a ton of quality of life issues that get worse as the weapons and enemy roster expand. I wanted to love it, but I can't.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The most recent update did help with #5, but not enough to make my rating positive yet.On the surface this game is amazing. I like a lot about it, and I keep coming back and wanting to like it. However, once you get into it, you start to realize how shallow it is and many small frustrating or poorly designed things start to mount up and overwhelm the good.1. I don't know how it is possible, but somehow all the guns simultaneously feel overpowered and under powered. I think the effects, gib, etc. makes them feel really good, but then you get swarmed by 50 enemies who aren't hard or interesting, and you find yourself fumbling through your guns and none of them really get the job done like you want them to.2. Reloading is AWFUL. This is not the kind of game to have reloading. I like to swap guns fairly often (and the game even encourages you to with different armor level or whatever) and I find 3 or 4 times through the battle I just have to run away, cycle through all my guns to reload them, then go back to the fight. THIS ISN'T FUN. Especially for the shotgun, PLEASE take out reloading. Please please please.3. There are too many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ items everywhere! No item feels impactful or even memorable when you pick it up because there are so many scattered around. Literally half the time I am playing this game, I am running around picking up stupid little powerups that are scattered EVERYWHERE and... I just don't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ want to. Then, you run around picking up little ♥♥♥♥ just to find a room that fills you up on most everything anyway. WHY? Why would I want to run around picking up 10 different items that give me +10 HP when you could put ONE somewhere with +100 that I can give a ♥♥♥♥ about when I find. It's not fun.4. The enemies aren't different enough. The men shoot you. The ugly aliens run at you. THe big men shoot at you and grenade with a bunch of HP. The big aliens shoot fireballs at you. THAT'S IT. There are so many types of little different guys who seem to do the same thing. Why? None of them are memorable because none of them seem different. Have one throw a net around you if they get close! Have a suicide bomber. I don't know, just ANYTHING except another hard to see guy who shoots you.5. The damage you take isn't clear in several ways. As I am battling, I have no idea how I am doing until I look down at my HP and armor. Sometimes I will look down and be almost dead and have no idea why. Other times I'll be battling for ever and still somehow be full. I also have no idea which attacks do more damage. Maybe there's an indicator or the screen flashes more red for more damage or something, but I don't see it.6. The level designs aren't great. The buttons you need to press are often easily missable. I ran around one level for about 30 minutes once just in awe of how I had absolutely no idea where to go. I thought, "I'm NOT this stupid, right?" Then I finally find this tiny yellow button behind some crates I had to press. I'd been back there a couple times jumping around and missed it. It sucks. SOLUTION: Once you haven't done your next objective after about 30 seconds, have a non invasive arrow or something to point you to the next objective.7. THE SLIDING MOVEMENT!!! Oh my god you need to fire EVERYONE who thought it was a good idea to have the entire game feel like you are on an ice rink. I miss SO many shots because of the sliding. It's awful. Remove it.TLDR: Slidey movement, too many items, uninteresting enemies, it's not very good in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool beans, rule of thumb for boomer shooters, especially modern ones, is to not tuck away supplies for surviving arena fights in back alleys or in enclosed spaces. Call me a nitpicker, but it's piss poor map design to have all the useful pickups be found AFTER the fight is over and it's safe to scrounge for ammo and the like. (Looking at you, full magazine of Kraken rounds I found AFTER both the Chaos Terminators were dead)
