_childDocuments_.review: As a recently converted 40k fan and lapsed-but-still-game-for-anything old-school FPS fan, I had high hopes for Boltgun going in. The trailers looked great (if a little obnoxious with the voice-over), and I'd heard plenty of fawning reviews. Hell, I'd absorbed enough hype to actually buy and play a singleplayer game, something I barely ever do anymore. After a couple hours of actual playtime, though, my hopes were kinda dashed, having just gone through a first chapter that seemingly had all the ingredients for fun but couldn't deliver.The core of the game, to be clear, is phenomenal. Movement is fast and responsive, the weapons all feel great to fire, the visual art and sound design on everything are phenomenal while still being recognizable in the middle of an intense shootout, the gore is excellent, and it gets the ineffable feel of the 40k universe and its inhabitants just right; it's a very solid foundation all around. A massive amount of care clearly went into crafting it, and as a purely artistic work it feels like it came out more or less exactly as intended, a perfected version of the audiovisual experience it wants to be.The problem, then, with that first section of the game is twofold: it's very easy, and all the weapons you get are fairly straightforward. After you get your bearings, you very quickly get to a place where you just spend every level walking into crowds of low-tier fodder enemies emptying your generic machine gun into them (which works well enough that it seems impossible to balance a game around; I get that it's the literal name of the game but it's simply too good at everything the game asks you to do), occasionally switching it out for your plasma gun that works like a generic rocket launcher or your generic heavy machine gun (and ignoring the generic shotgun entirely, because the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boltgun does near-identical damage while having none of the drawbacks that make shotguns interesting to use). The game drip-feeds you new stuff at a snail's pace, but doesn't have any other means of varying things up, so ♥♥♥♥ gets monotonous real quickly. If the game were harder, full of John Romero-style level design ♥♥♥♥-yous, but the weapons stayed the same, it'd be much more engaging as a skill challenge, like how classic DOOM is; if the game were just as easy but all the weapons got crazy alt-fire modes or special effects and there were tons of off-the-wall powerups and you were being introduced to new ones of these things every half-hour, it'd be a fun sandbox to stomp through while constantly delighting yourself with novelties, kind of like modern DOOM crossed with a Just Cause game. The first approach would be good for making the most of what's already there, while the second would be good for living out the space marine power fantasy like the game seems to want to kind of do. As is, though, effortlessly turning enemies into paste is fun for an hour or two, but it gets old fast after that, and the game seems to have little else up its sleeve. I guess it replicates the space marine experience of walking forward and holding down your trigger until everything is dead, but if so, I don't see how those guys live for hundreds of years without entering some kind of existential ennui.Those were my criticisms after completing the first of three episodes, and going into the second one I didn't have high hopes that things would turn around. But, shockingly, they did! Almost immediately, the game starts stepping up the difficulty, throwing actually tricky combat encounters at you and not giving you so much ammo so that you have to be even slightly judicious with your weapon use. Later on, it also starts giving you actually fun and interesting weapons, and in the third episode piling on completely ridiculous numbers of enemies that are pretty fun to chew through. I started dying occasionally, and scraping by by the skin of my teeth enough to keep me on the edge of my seat. The game becomes a pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ solid shooter, with the only remaining issue being that the maps can sometimes be really unintuitive to get through, necessitating use of the slightly condescending navigation guide mechanic. Given its quality in the latter two-thirds, it's a real shame that the first few hours are such a drag, because it feels like a great way to turn people off before they get to the good part. Looking at the global achievement stats, I think this is genuinely what happens, as not even a third of players get to the end of the first chapter, and after that completion drops off even more precipitously before eventually leveling out to just the people like me who pushed through. I feel like a lot of 40k fans with not much shooter experience have been lured into buying the game because it advertises itself as being Epic, and they're all huge marks for anything Epic, before getting bored in the first chapter and losing interest once that initial shot of Epicness wears itself out and there's nothing behind it until chapter two. On the other hand, I guess I'm glad that the stellar artwork, sound design, and movement and shooting mechanics aren't wasted on a totally worthless campaign. Give it a shot, if you're willing to wait a couple of hours for the real fun to begin.

_childDocuments_.review: Abstract: Boltgun is a fairly solid New Doom clone with 40K set dressing. It nails the look and feel with Brutal Doom levels of gore and chunky weapons but lacks the kind of polish that prevents it from sitting up with the all-time greats in the modern boomer shooter revival.It surprises me 40K has never had a traditional FPS, not even in the halcyon days of licensing Doom, Quake, or Build for your game. To get this out of the way Boltgun is far more inspired by Doom 2016 than the original: classic Doom was defined by its map limitations which made it more arcade action like Gauntlet. Doom 2016 brought verticality to the franchise with simpler, more compact maps and massive arenas where you take on waves of monsters. This isn't a negative just don't go into Boltgun expecting a maze-like Ultimate Doom or even Quake experience.What Boltgun gets right from the very beginning is game feel. You move swiftly with heavy screen shaking footsteps that really sell the concept of being a roided-out one-man-army in power armor. The basic starter "pistol" is the boltgun, canonically an automatic submachine gun that fires miniature explosive warheads with a recoil that would shatter the bones of a normal man. Every gun is a visual spectacle, it punches with a weight you would expect from the well established lore, and enemies gib in a shower of grime and gore. Playing this game feels like the way 40K is written and despite the low-poly environments and billboard-sprite enemies the aesthetics have never been replicated better.Gameplay is pretty standard for the genre, you advance through rooms taking out swarms of enemies and collecting keys then face the occasional locked-arena battle. There's no advanced enemy AI, they are as smart as the foes from Quake, but just in the first 4 levels the sheer variety of enemy types is pretty staggering and they serve their purpose of forcing the player to move and prioritize targets. This is the rare shooter I recommend veteran players start with Exterminatus the hardest difficulty. You will die, a lot, but scraping through a fight by the skin of your teeth is an amazing feeling and there's a built-in god mode for when you get too frustrated and just need to progress.What keeps Boltgun in the solid 8/10 range is a series of minor issues that mount up. Damage feedback is practically nonexistent: you see a blue-arrow telling you the location of damage but it's entirely possible to lose 3/4 of your life in a single shot and the only notification is if you look down at your health. Sound design is great everywhere except enemies and with so many varying types it becomes important to pick your targets. With the maps quickly getting filled with blood clouds and splattering brain matter it becomes very difficult to discern targets. Too often I'm ambushed for no fault that enemies have no discernible barks. A hulking chaos terminator is as much a master of stealth as a greater plague toad.Enemies also don't have a "pain" state, a very important concept in Doom that many shooters foolishly gloss over. This stun-state that interrupts an enemy's action is why it's an important consideration in Doom to switch between the shotgun, chaingun, and plasma rifle. With no such state in Boltgun you end up in scenarios where the game encourages you to melee and bull rush enemies only to take a face full of hot plasma immediately afterward. Cultists humorously hesitate, throwing up their arms in mercy as you attack but no other enemy has a similar state of shock. If melee attacks were an automatic stun it would encourage more rushing headlong into the fray but as it stands, at least on the higher difficulties, the best strategy is guerilla hit and run tactics which feels totally against the tenets of the Adeptus Astartes! Suffer not the retaliatory acid blast from the demon I just chainsawed.So Boltgun is a great experience but not an amazing one. It's a game I'll happily beat but unless the issues with feedback get addressed I can't imagine I'll put the time in to master it. It's a undoubtedly good 8/10 experience, it just falls short of the likes of Dusk or Ion Fury.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a 'mixed' review type, because that's how I feel about this game. On the one hand, I enjoyed it enough to complete it, but that's not to say that it wasn't a tedious process getting there. The gunplay is nice, but most of the enemies are bullet sponges, so it becomes a chore killing them when you start getting further into the game. The level design isn't great, and you'll find yourself running around a lot, trying to find the corridor/door that you're supposed to go down to progress to the next part of the level. I really enjoyed the first few hours of this game, but like another reviewer has said, you kind of hit a wall after a little while - it's hard to explain unless you've played it. The developers have clearly put a lot of work into this game, and for the price I feel inclined to recommend it, but there are a lot of things that could easily tip the scales.

_childDocuments_.review: The game would be quite the gem if it werent for one incredibly glaring problem:This game has some of the most horrific level design and absolutely NO MAP.You will be playing and progressing just fine, then completely dead end in a sandbox with no doors in or out, no portals, no switches, no keys, no ladders, no stairs, no enemies, nothing. Just wandering around, grinding along the walls looking for a developer FU switch theyve hidden, but nothing. You'll spend hours trying to figure how the hell to get out of areas so you can progress, then shut off the game and come back days later when you feel youve got an hour or so to kill trying to find your way out of their dumbass level design only to shut the game down again and wait until you feel like going through that process again...All of this hassle, and even their lazy design could be completely bypassed by an....um....i dont know.....maybe.....sort of....like.....one of those things theyve had in games since early dos games......an um....Oh, that's right! A MAP.Only play if you enjoy being hooked by great effects and gameplay and led right down a dead end hallway of f'd level design...

_childDocuments_.review: this has very satisfying gameplay, i see why the game is named "boltgun", that thing is like a damned sniper in this game for most of the enemies! i love these sorts of games where you play as a big chunky space marine running around destroying everything, this game (as you probably couldve guessed) has Doom / Quake styled game play, with a very retro nolstalgic art style, whats more is if you dont like the pixel art, you can customise how "retro" you want the game to look, you can make it look modern, or straight up 144p if you really want! this game has a lot of customisation so you can get the game to look *just* right to your liking.i really like this game and im very glad i bought it, its not often i buy games on the 2nd day of release due to being quite sceptical on them (most games these days seem to always never work as intended on release.) but this game has no issues from what i found, maybe a few frame drops when you're in a full purge and gets loads of gore piles and enemies running at you, but that's about it.speaking of purges, this game will certainly get the blood running and can quickly overwhelm you if you're not prepared, so always be sure to stay topped up on health to PURGE THE HERESY! you may feel like a god, but you're still human, and you will die.i'd recommend it for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer boltgun KICKS ASS, it's probably the best example I have seen of a Warhammer FPS.Action is explosive, you will not get bored killing things in this game. It's as brutal and violent as you could ever ask from a Warhammer title. The game makes you feel powerful without taking away any of the challenge. This is not a mindless shooter, taking some inspiration from DOOM Eternal, certain guns will work better on certain enemies meaning you're always switching your gun to best fit the situation. So you will have to keep focused and pay attention to your surroundingsHowever, that doesn't mean you have to play this way. If you just want a game where you easily rip and tear enemies in the Warhammer universe there are cheats in the accessibility menu that have no penalty. If you want to play that way, no judgment, its there if you want it but you don't need to use it.The gun-play is extremely good, though its a boomer shooter, its a boomer shooter with a lot of modern conveniences as somebody who is addicted to ADS in games I was worried that this game wouldn't have any, however the game makes it extremely easy and comfortable to aim without ADS. Getting melee kills with your chain-sword is satisfying as you'll automatically lock on to the closest enemy and maul them without second thought, and you can just chain kill lower level enemies this way and it is beyond fun.(I have only had a few problems with this system where it would randomly lock on to a stronger enemy behind the lil guys I was trying to melee kill)Main problem I have with the game, and this might just be a skill issue, but because its a boomer shooter there's not a lot of hints on where to go and getting lost is pretty easy (something my servo-skull endlessly mocked me for). Its not like the doors are easily hidden its just that there's a lot of winding hallways and it can get a bit confusing. Though that could just be me.Getting lost isn't too much of a problem though because there are secrets to be found that all benefit you during game-play, a majority of them are power-ups. Though only a few are permanent and a lot of secrets are hidden in purge zones which means by the time you find them all the enemies are gone and you wasted a power-up.There's a lot of different enemies that all look unique and provide different challenges, (I know that doesn't seem like a big deal but I have played a lot of shooter game where there is a lack of variation in enemies) so you'll always have to adapt based on the situation In summary Warhammer 40K: Boltgun KICKS ASS, its a well designed thoughtful boomer-shooter that does a great service to the Warhammer lore, and pays great homage to the shooters of old
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: The game suffers from many terrible design decisions as a retro shooter. One major core problem is how there is no thought or any care put into the enemy placements most of the time, they are just placed so randomly. In many retro style shooters of new and old, you can observe how the developers usually designed and placed their enemies on the levels in meaningful ways that made the ecounters interesting and fun. The enemy variety is also very lackluster. You have guy who shoots at you while standing still and the same guy but bigger and more health. Similar story with melee enemies. This makes the game feel incredibly repetitive and more like a chore than a fun challange. Shooting at the same boring foe, trying to deplete their absurdly large healtbar. The damage they dish out is also very inconsistent and the visual feedback of getting hit is very poor. Often times you are on full health and suddenly you die or notice that you barely have any health left. This poor feedback indication makes enemies like Aspiring Champion and Plague Toad particularly annoying, combined with their large healtbars.The levels are pretty but the art is repetitive and it's way too easy to get lost in them. Be prepared to wander around a lot. Keys are often placed right next to doors requiring them, defeating their purpose altogether. Despite how they look, levels are unmemorable and just as shoddily designed as the combat encounters.Overall, the game looks and plays like a fun, gory shooter but really stumbles with poor design decisions. The fact that only 8% of players on Steam beat the game at all really speaks volumes of just how quickly it becomes stale.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has three chapters and less than a third of people who bought this game have completed chapter one which is somewhere between two and three hours long. Completion rates drop down to 15% and 11% for chapters two and three... At first it's hard to understand why because your starting boltgun is great, combat is fun and the levels are fine. Unfortunately it's all downhill from here; levels become endless key hunts, the maps are copy pasted, progress is slow because you constantly get lost and every new weapon you find sucks compared to your starting one. Oh and secrets are completely pointless because they're just temporary power ups so if you've already cleared the level there's zero motivation to secret hunt when you know it won't benefit you in any way since health and ammo don't carry over between levels.I eventually made it to the final level in chapter one and noped out. There's some portal puzzle you have to solve which involves running into portals over and over and over and every time the environment looks the same. Imagine watching Die Hard and then all of a sudden McClane has to spend half an hour tediously walking through a mirror maze. That's what this feels like but worse. I'm supposed to be a space marine dispatched to purge the most dangerous threats to humanity but here I am walking through purple doors like the worlds worst Portal rip off.Even if I could drink an entire bath tub of vodka, solve the puzzle and make it to chapter two I still wouldn't be enjoying the game. Combat is fun if you use the boltgun but the rest sucks. Exploration is horrific, map design is trash, the story is non-existent, enemies are brain dead and there's no challenge beyond getting swarmed. I would refund if I could but this trash blue balled me just long enough to tip me over the two hour mark.Seriously, don't buy this game unless you hate yourself or will literally buy anything with 40k in the title. But still, this is bottom of the barrel even for a 40k game. In fact, it's so bad I'd actually rather play Darktide than this which is such a bad game I'd rather play Back 4 Blood.... God I hate games sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: It is the 41st millennium. For more than a hundred centuries the Emperor has sat immobile on the Golden Throne of Earth. He is the Master of Mankind by the will of the gods, and master of a million worlds by the might of His inexhaustible armies. He is a rotting carcass writhing invisibly with power from the Dark Age of Technology. He is the Carrion Lord of the Imperium for whom a thousand souls are sacrificed everyday so that He may never truly die.Yet even in His deathless state, the Emperor continues His eternal vigilance. Mighty battlefleets cross the daemon-infested miasma of the warp, the only route between distant stars, their war lit by the Astronomican, the psychic manifestation of the Emperor's will. Vast armies give battle in His name on uncounted worlds. Greatest among His soldiers are the Adeptus Astartes, the Space Marines, bioengineered super warriors. Their comrades in arms are legion: the Astra militarum and countless planetary defence forces, the ever vigilant Inquisition and the tech-priest of the Adeptus Mechanicus to name only a few. But for all their multitudes, they are barely enough to hold off the ever-present threat from aliens, heretics, mutants - and worse.To be a man in such times is to be one among untold billions. It is to live in the cruellest and most bloody regime imaginable. These are the tales of those times. Forget the power of technology and science, for so much has been forgotten, never to be re-learned. Forget the promise of progress and understanding, for in the grim dark future there is only war. There is no peace among the stars, only an eternity of carnage and slaughter, and the laughter of thirsting gods.10/10 - May the god emperor bestow upon us multiplayer co-op

_childDocuments_.review: I've almost yelled out FOR THE EMPEROR! many times.I've got my nitpicks with some things, but overall a very enjoyable FPS.The movement is fluid and when you run your every power armored step rumbles the controller.Map design is fun, especially now that they've added a guidance button that shows you the way forward. Some people call this "hand holdy", but if not getting lost for 30 minutes in a classic FPS then hold my hand harder mommy. There's one level that's basically an Escher-esque warped in on itself castle with teleporter doors you need to find your way through. I didn't even try the navigation button on that one, but the game's visual language makes it somewhat clear where you have to go without being completely obnoxious.The weapon variety is fantastic, and they feel great.The boltgun is fantastic, and friggin better as it's the titular weapon of the game and the signature gun of space marines. I also love the heavy bolter which feels chonky with every round fired after a fraction of a second delay in raising the weapon. There's a plasma rifle which will hurt you if it hits too close as it has a small AOE. IIRC there's 8 weapons in total in the base game, the chainsword, plus 3 types of grenades, though only the regular frag and krak grenades common. The chainsword mechanics are awesome. If you press the button you raise the sword while letting it go swings it and starts ripping the enemy to shreds which they can break from the higher their health. Two things that make it so enjoyable is while you have the button held before an attack if you look at an enemy it will slow-motion the game and then when you release it you zoom forward like you have an assault pack (jetpack) sort of which can get you up to higher platforms or across small gaps, but usually just closes the distance extremely quick.If you love the 40K aesthetic; this is a solid first person shooter worth the price you'll most likely enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: A great experience only set back by small flawsVisuals, music, sound design, gunplay... they're all great. But I wanted to tell you about the issues that make this game shy of a masterpiece.- Lack of map: For a game that has intricate level design, and you need to collect colored keys and backtrack in order to open doors, sometimes it's easy to get lost, especially since some parts of the levels look similar. Even adding a simple map would go a long way. - Weapon reloading: This is a fast-paced, old-school, arena-shooter. Having to reload your gun, absolutely kills the pacing in some combat situations. Please add an option to toggle off weapon reloading.- Plasma gun quick swap: Like DOOM Eternal ( one of my favorite games of all time ) you can quick swap between weapons, which is freaking awesome and make the combat very fluid... unless you use plasma gun in your combos. Then you need to watch it's animation play till the end, then you can switch to another weapon. It's very odd to me since you can quick swap between every other weapon and I hope they patch this in future updates.- Health and ammo pick-ups: Enemies mostly don't drop health or ammo, and when they do, it's in very small amounts. So you just have to take whatever's in the arena. That's fine by itself but there are moments that you just running past large sections like a headless chicken in order to find something but there's nothing, so you feel like the game being a bit stingy. I would have loved to be able to gather health or ammo by chainsawing enemies. That way you had to play more aggressively as well and keep the combat going.- Arena balance: Pretty self explanatory. There are times that a small arena is filled with enemies to the point that you can't move or use certain weapon with splash damage, and sometimes in large arenas, you literally have to go looking for enemies and you just end up running around for minutes. Adding/removing enemies in certain arenas will solve this issue.Again, this is great game and I'm really happy with my purchase but I just wanted to highlight some issues that I saw with the game. Some of them might not be important depending on who you ask but some of them are absolutely necessary to fix in order to maximize the quality of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Boltgun is a retro-inspired first-person shooter game where you battle corrupted humans, Chaos, demons, and occasional native aliens. The levels are generally linear with periodic arenas, reminiscent of Doom (2016) and Doom Eternal, where you must eliminate all enemies before progressing.The game is divided into three chapters, each with its own visual theme. However, I found the level design to be uninspired and flat, lacking both engaging gameplay and visual appeal. This contradicts the common criticism that the game's levels are maze-like and confusing. Personally, I never felt lost or in need of a map, possibly due to my experience with retro shooters. Nevertheless, I must reiterate that the level design leaves much to be desired—it's simply boring! While there are some cool set pieces that capture the grandeur of the Warhammer 40k universe, the majority of the levels appear to be created by a skilled yet amateur level designer.The enemies in Boltgun have distinctive visual designs, but their behaviours lack variety. They all home in on you regardless of their chosen attack method. The unique aspect lies in their armour rating and damage output. The armour rating mechanic introduces a fresh element to the genre: each weapon is assigned a strength rating. For instance, the bolter has a strength of four, making it a decent all-rounder. When an enemy comes into your line of sight, their armour rating is displayed above their health. So, if you encounter a Chaos Space Marine with an armour rating of four, your boltgun will deal normal damage. However, if you face a Plague Toad with an armour rating of five, your boltgun's damage will be reduced. In theory, this mechanic should encourage dynamic gameplay, where you need to utilize a variety of weapons to defeat your foes. Unfortunately, it doesn't quite work that way, as some of the weapons are nearly useless. I won't name specific weapons, but it becomes apparent which ones are strictly superior for their intended roles when you play the game.Regarding the art design, Boltgun excels. The team have done an excellent job in creating a cohesive visual experience that fits perfectly within the Warhammer 40k universe. The graphics, while not mind-blowing, maintain detail even through the intentional retro filter.On the other hand, the sound design is a bit iffy. The sound effects are great and impactful, just as you would expect, but the audio engineering aspect is abysmal. When I initially played the game, I genuinely thought there was something wrong with my headphones. All the sounds blend, with the overpowering music creating a chaotic audio mix that assaults your ears. It's like playing an old RTS game where dozens of sounds play on top of each other, resulting in an incoherent jumble of frantic noise. In the end, I decided to mute the music, which made the game more bearable.In terms of difficulty, Boltgun is a breeze. I completed it on the hardest Exterminatus difficulty without breaking a sweat. While there were a few arenas where I died multiple times, those instances were rare. The game is overly generous with pickups, providing plenty of ammo, health, and armour as long as you're not rushing through every exit. This isn't necessarily a criticism, as not every game needs to be a challenging slog designed to test your patience. However, unless you're a complete newcomer to shooters or this genre, you'll have no trouble progressing through this game. Keep that in mind.Now, let's discuss performance. Unfortunately, this game ran poorly on my system, despite exceeding its requirements. I experienced massive frame drops, stuttering, and occasional one-second freezes. I believe the frame drops are related to alpha effects like explosions and fire. To be clear, the frame drops were a constant issue throughout the entire gameplay experience. This significantly detracted from the enjoyment of the game, but I persisted, nonetheless. If you encounter severe frame drops, I recommend requesting a refund, as the situation is unlikely to improve.Finally, do I recommend this game? Yes, if you're a devoted fan of Warhammer 40K and/or the shooter genre. However, it doesn't offer anything particularly new, and it falls short in certain aspects—most notably in level and sound design. Despite this, it never becomes dull to obliterate heretics and demons. Furthermore, it's important to consider that the development team is relatively small, so let's not judge them too harshly.EDIT 07/07/23: I realise that as a whole, this review is quite negative, yet I recommend it. I initially forgot to discuss the satisfaction from shooting weaponry and killing enemies. Weapons are punchy, heavy and truly do feel like they have impact. Enemies can be gibbed, and it's a gory game. No, it's not like Brutal Doom, but it's certainly gorier than a lot of other games out there. This is important as it adds to the 'punch' factor of weaponry. I'll add to my conclusion here that the general gameplay and art design saves it. It's fun, it's punchy, you — sigh — feel like a Space Marine. If anything, wait for a sale.

(honestly, this should be the whole review, you judge these games by their shotguns and this one is useless)- why have a taunt button?- why are the power-up useless and instant? Except the gravity grenade that is not instant and deletes bosses, but never even hidden (you didn't beat the game, if you used it).- why is everything a gothic-industrial catherdral?- why pay for something that plays inferior to most Doom wads and Quake maps?- why did I waste money and 12 hours of my life on this?TL;DR, Don't buy, trash game with devs trying to ride the boomer shooter hype and 40K fanboys with an unispired, badly designed shooter. _childDocuments_.review: The battlefield is ripe for the taking, and Warhammer 40K: Boltgun stands as a testament to the might of a true retro shooter in the modern era. In the endless sea of pathetic, soulless modern games, this gem emerges, crushing the competition beneath its iron heel. Like the grand shooters of the 90s, Boltgun delivers a pixelated experience that brings the past roaring into the present, striking terror into the hearts of its adversaries.The narrative simplicity of Warhammer history. In this glorious digital war zone, you are an elite space marine dispatched to a distant world, your mission clear and unyielding: eradicate the heretics in the name of the Emperor. No convoluted plots or overwrought storylines, just pure, unadulterated war. The setting and story are quintessentially Warhammer, staying true to the roots that veterans of the lore will recognize and newcomers will quickly come to revere.Prepare yourselves, soldiers, for the combat in Boltgun is . The pace is fast, the enemies plentiful, and the arsenal at your disposal is as varied as it is deadly. The level design and atmosphere are meticulously crafted to , demanding both precision and brutality. The Horde Mode, in particular, is a relentless onslaught of enemies, providing an endless stream of entertainment and significantly boosting the game's replay value.In an age where modern games stumble under the weight of bloated budgets and massive development teams,  This game stands as a towering giant, demonstrating that true quality and entertainment do not require endless resources—only a commitment to excellence. The developers have created a masterpiece that shames the so-called "advanced" titles of today, proving that sometimes, the old ways are indeed the best.As the modern gaming industry succumbs to the drivel of nonsensical, woke ideology, Boltgun stands resolute, a beacon of sanity and quality. It does not pander, it does not compromise; it delivers a pure, unfiltered Warhammer experience. In this sea of garbage, Boltgun is a precious gem, gleaming with the promise of true entertainment. , Warhammer 40K: Boltgun is not just a game; it is a triumphant return to the glory days of gaming, an experience that both honors and elevates its predecessors.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending tentatively. I haven't finished the game yet, so maybe some of my complaints will dissipate later into the game.For clarity, I played the game on the hardest difficulty ExterminatusLets start with the good: + Great setting and atmosphere+ Guns feel good (amazing actually)    + Weapon variety (I won't spoil all the weapons you find, but they all feel space marine worthy and just about every weapon 1 shots a cultist)+ Enemy variety makes for varying gameplay+ Game looks pretty great (some enemies look better than others, but they all look the same after being hit with a plasma gun :))The mid:+- A lot of the difficulty of certain enemies comes from their health. While you'll rarely ever have to look at cultist for longer than your cross hair moves across them, a chaos marine will take around a full boltgun clip to finish off. That in itself isn't an issue, it's a chaos space marine after all. But it becomes a bit of an issue when you have to also fight lesser plague toads, who have a way higher than expected health pool, and can hit harder than a chaos marine. Don't even get me started on tzeentch screamers. They fly, have a ton of health, and due to the nature of using 2d sprites in a  3d environment, their hitboxes are pretty hard to find if they're above you.+- There's a lot of ammo. Like tons of it. I've only left 1 encounter where all my weapons weren't topped off. This isn't necessarily bad since it just means I can shoot more, aim/think less. But I still expected to be a  punished for only using the plasma gun in a room that teleported in tons of enemies. +- The melee is awesome until it isn't. It feels great to finish off an enemy with the chainsword, or to gib nurglings with your dash, but these tools are so situational that you'll almost forget you have them at times. The chainsword does great single target damage, but if there's other enemies in the room, you're better off not going for melee since you're not invulnerable during it (and some enemies take a while to die to chainsword). And while the dash is a good tool to get through enemies, it doesn't  do that much damage. It's more of a "get away" tool than a "get in" attack.+- Ranged is always the best option. This is mostly due to the melee issue listed above. Since this game lacks traditional hitscan type enemies, just about every attack is avoidable. You might think this allows for close range combat since you can easily dodge projectiles, so you can bob and weave your way into shotgun range (think doom 1, weaving through imp fireballs) while this might be true for individual projectiles, most enemies in boltgun have fully automatic weapons, creating a bit of a bullet storm that goes in your general direction, making getting into close range significantly harder. Certain enemies also have reaaaally good close range options that make getting close even less appealing. This leads to the ideal combat encounter against almost every enemy being: strafe shooting a target from 30+ feet away.+- The shotgun sucks until it doesn't. I won't outright call the shotgun bad. It has it's uses, and the game itself says it's Strength 3 (where the boltgun is strength 4, and plasma gun is strength 7(I think)), so it's not being advertised as this beast of a weapon. But I will say it feels bad to use in a lot of situations. Chaos Marines? Probably the slowest way to kill one. Tzeentch screamers? I weep for you. Now, if you use it against cultists or other low health enemies? Pretty good at clearing them out. Probably the best weapon to clear them if you don't feel like using the plasma gun to kill groups. Not quite what you'd expect a shotgun to be in this type of game. However, there is a silver lining. There's a secret item you can find in levels that will buff your currently equipped weapon in various ways. This buff lasts for the entirety of that level. I honestly couldn't tell you what it does to the other weapons, but it makes the shotgun feel stronger than the super shotgun from DOOM (2016). With the upgraded shotgun, Chaos Marines? Swiss cheese. Exalted Flamers? Extinguished. Tzeentch screamers? Still pretty annoying with their hitboxes, but you get the idea. This is  to what I expect a shotgun to be like in a boomer shooter, but it has the opposite issue of being  good.The Bad:- Encounter design. While actually shooting the guns and killing the dudes feel good, at times the game just feels like a shooting gallery. Round a corner. Cultists. Shoot them. Open a door, chaos marines that spend more time laughing at you than shooting you, shoot them. The most interesting thing the game will do is teleport enemies into the room you're in when you're out in the open, prompting you with a mini fight or flight scenario. While it's more enjoyable than the standard enemy placement the game has, it's not really good. It's a bit cheap. Now, I'm not opposed to cheap enemy tactics in my boomer shooter. I played Blood, that game rules, and those cultists are as cheap as they get at times. But there's something lacking in Boltgun when it comes to how enemies are placed or appear, it just feels uninspired. More of a "Hey, look. Here's more enemies" versus "We placed enemies here to make you change your approach"- The purge event. Similar to DOOM (2016)'s gore nest rooms, you will occasionally (often) enter a very large room with tons of ammo and health pickups. This will almost always be a purge room. In a purge room, you will have to face several waves of enemies that teleport in more and more as you kill them off. I believe that there's a preset amount of enemies that spawn in, but it feels endless. To finish the purge event, you have to kill the "big enemies" of the purge (i.e Plaguetoad, Terminators, Exalted Flamers). To be blunt, these encounters suck. They really drive in the bad encounter design I mentioned previously since the spots that enemies teleport into is always the same, and will happen the moment a threshold of enemies killed gets passed. This means that you can kill a cultist, and turn around, walk forward, and get shot by the cultist that reported in directly behind you. This isn't a challenge of having better positioning, as you're good position can instantly turn into terrible positioning as soon as enemies teleport in, but more a challenge of spawn memorization and movement. Good movement will carry you far, but it doesn't really feel good to have to move around enemies that may or may not teleport in at any moment. The only good thing about these encounters is that there's usually enough health and armor scattered around that you can fully heal twice before running out.Conclusion:While I definitely talked more about the cons than the pros, I do still like this game. It really does feel good to shoot dudes in this game (unless your using the shotgun, but I digress). Ultimately, if you just want a game where you shoot the dudes and they die a lot, you'll like this game. If you're looking for a more well designed game with thought out enemy encounters, I'd say pick up Cultic or Ion Fury.

_childDocuments_.review: This game delivers far beyond the easy sell that is a WH40K boomer shooter. The IP is known for its schlock, but this may genuinely be one of the best retro-style FPS games in recent memory, if not all time.The movement is fast and fluid while still feeling weighty as a space marine should, making it very fun to zoom and bounce about the nuDoom-esque arenas you find yourself fighting in. The chainsword and dash offer glorykill-style abilities that don't feel gimmicky or intrusive to the flow of combat, and are useful not only as weapons but as movement techs as well. Shooting feels great with punchy, impactful weaponry which combined with the enemy variety makes combat very engaging and satisfying. On top of that are the delightfully indulgent particle effects/lighting and beautiful spritework; the carnage you find yourself in is eye candy to the point that it almost goes against the source material. Nearly everything about the core gameplay in this title is just delectable.No game is perfect, however, and there were definitely a few things in this game I should note. The little skull guy who follows you around is annoying, unhelpful and says half its dialogue at the wrong time. Some enemies are way too sponge-y far what they are. The bosses are very mediocre (though that's par for the course in the genre) and recycled frequently. A majority of the weapons are "kill big guy quickly" standbys, making your arsenal feel less like a swiss army knife and more like a knife, screwdriver and multiple sledgehammers.My biggest gripe with the game, while still not huge, is the level design. As previously mentioned, it utilizes nuDoom-esque arenas where players must clear out a gauntlet of enemies before they may proceed. It's not everyone's cup of tea, certainly isn't mine, but at the very least the arenas are large enough to stretch one's legs in and allow for decent combat flow in their design. Their size also means scavenging about for health and ammo when in a pinch is still very much a gameplay element within them. Outside of these arenas, it can also be hard to tell at times where the game wants you to go. The levels are not labyrinthine by any stretch but the repetitive environments and semi-awkward routes can make it feel like you are backtracking when you are in fact moving forward. It doesn't help that blood-splattered corpses are used as intermittent set dressing, so looking out for the breadcrumbs of defeated enemies is not wholly reliable either. That being said, it wont be long before you eventually find your way. Oh, and the secrets are kinda meh, only just barely out of the way. I find most of them by complete accident.Gripes with level design and other minor things aside, this is already one of my favorite retro-style shooters and I'm not even a fan of WH40K (quite the opposite, in fact). It stands more than well enough on its own, and needs not rely on its imperial coat of paint.

_childDocuments_.review: I can see why people would like this game but for me I feel it doesn't innovate enough.The first few levels are pretty fun but by the first open encounter I could immediately see the games glaring issues.For one after the first few levels the dash mechanic is all but useless not doing enough damage to effect anything above fodder enemy's and not giving enough control to be used as a movement option.Furthermore the big open areas and purge rooms are designed really well for ultra aggressive gameplay....its just too bad your not given any good movement options with your ground movement being limited to wasd and your air control being basically non-existent.The only movement options you have are the previously mentioned dash which cant be used midair,cant be controlled simply setting you in a strait line for where you look,has an incredably short range for how long you have to wait to use it,and immediately stops if it bumps into anything including stairs.And the  chainsaw which isn't horrible....but not exactly  terms of movement I think a fair comparison would be the green arm from ultrakill or the meathook from doom eternal where you pull yourself towards an enemy.The big difference being you can only pull yourself in a strait line so if the enemy moves a bit or has some kind of railing in front of them you just cant do anything overall the best use you could have for this is when you already midair using it to get a bit extra height something that you could do with a simple double jump but idk warhammer lore so that might not be an option.Although my biggest gripe is the lack of ability to heal yourself. I played on the highest difficulty so im not sure if this isnt as big of an issue on lower difficulties but healing is nigh impossible.The only healing options you have are medkits and armor pickups hidden away in secret areas and very tiny health and armor pickups dropped by enemy's.These small drops are worthless you'd need to kill 50 enemy's to equate to one health kit.The lack of movment options and effective healing makes the cool ass designs of these arenas basically worthless as it is strategically better to just sit in an enclosed room and wait for the enemys to come to you or you run the risk of just dying to some nurgling stuck on a stairway suddenly appearing along with a bunch of gunners killing you before you even realize what happend especially since the gunners blend into the background soo much.Its clear to me these issues are covered up by the games very flashy display..too flashy I cant even see what im doing half the time theres soo much blood shooting around I cant tell if im shooting an enemy or a corpse if it wherent for the universal health bar id have no idea if an enemy was actually dead or just close to being dead because I cant see ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.While this review might sound very negative i really feel like this game could be good with a few changes those being to give the player better movement options and possibly give them a way to at least increase how much health they get back from pickups like idk maybe the chainsaw makes them drop health even if it doesnt kill them giving more reason to use it later on when it does piss poor damage compares to the inflated health bars.Again the level design looks great and it can be alot of fun to just jump aorund in it even if the game incentivises you to basically stay in one area and not move and im sure on lower difficultys this is possible but If your game cant scale with difficulty and still feel fair and fun that just shows that there is a problem with how the game works fundamentally.

_childDocuments_.review: What I wanted: Warhammer 40k Doom with modern sensibilities but nostalgic retro style.What I got: Warhammer 40k Doom.If you wanted to play Doom again, you didn't need my review to convince you. You already bought it. You're already enjoying it. The guns and demon splatter are as great as they've ever been. Welcome to 1993. If you wanted to know if there is something more here, there isn't. Same 2 hp health pickups that still leave you starving and serve only to taunt you while cluttering the world with false promise. Same frustrating level design with no map or UI help. Same maddeningly hidden and ultimately underwhelming secrets. Same arcade style level times that make you wonder if you're bad for taking so long, especially if you were looking for those secrets. Same grueling difficulty. Same outdated experience that has undoubtedly been improved upon immensely over the years. None of the fantastic voice work I'd come to love from the great Warhammer 40k titles like Dawn of War and Space Marine. No interesting lore or compelling story. No customization or upgrades. No sleek new take on the brutally simple classic Doom. Nothing to set it apart from its nearly 30 year old progenitor. No little spark of life. Just the same old notes I didn't actually want to hear again.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. I wanted something like this for a LONG time and now it is here.First i want to make clear, what this game is, because some people i have talked to still do not have the right mindest:This is an  shooter!This is as old shool, as it gets. No XP, no skills, no RPG-elements, just you, your gun and the enemy.Don't expect something like Doom: Eternal, or something like that. This is more like Quake, but 40k.This doesn't mean, that this game is easy, far from it. You can certainly die, but the strategy you have to apply here is more along the lines of: Ammo conservation, movement and using the right gun for the right case.The game also throws a lot of enemies at you and a lot of different types of enemies, so you have to be a quick thinker. Especially in bigger fights, you really want to use the right tool for the job. You certainly can use a big gun for trash enemies, BUT that means, that you won't have the ammo for the big bad boiz.Just retro eye-candy :)This game may be retro, but it does not look terrible. It really nails the old look, with textures, animations, the enemies being sprites and even a filter, that kind of emulates this old 16-bit color palatte-look.The guns and projectiles look awesome and feel awesome, killed enemies just leave a HE-UGE mountain of gore. This game is just as bloody, as you'd expect it.The game also has (MILD SPOILER) The game has little touches, like an idle-animation, where your char starts reading the Codex Astartes, when standing still for a while...just...great :D , especially since you are an Ultrasmurf :PThe nice thing is, that the game lets you fine-tune this. There are sliders in the options-menu, that let you customize the retro-look. This is just a love-letter to 40k and old-shool shooters :)Some light and Dark here.When it comes to you, it is just amazing.The guns sound beefy and have a punch to them, especially the Bolter.It really sounds like the "automatic RPG-Launcher" it is.Your char stomps around, like a heavy walking tank and the best part:You can taunt at enemies and curse their heretic existence. That's just an awesome.On the other hand, you have the enemies, that do not do much, except grunting. Goes in-line with the "old-school shooter"-vibe, but still.Aside the sound:There are A LOT of them. Not just in numbers, but also in variety, i was pleasantly surprised. Just so many heretics, Chaos Space Marines, Terminators, Champions, Demons, you name it. Some enemies also have some specialties about them, that go in-line with the lore:(Mild gameplay spoiler)The only thing to complain about is the AI.The enemies are sometimes pretty braindead, especially when engaged on distance. It is like they do not know, where the bullets come from.Aside that, they just swarm you. They do that well, i have to say. Sometimes you are just overwhelmed by the mass of enemies, so you have to stay on your toes.Aside that, they do not do that much. Range enemies stay a bit back and shoot at you, about to be expected, but yeah.They do not really take much cover, or deploy smart strategies, but again: This is not really in the spirit of this game, one could argue, but still.The guns are one highlight for me. This is one of the BEST feeling Bolters ever. It just sounds great, looks great and everything, that is not wearing Power-Armor, or is blessed by Nurgle, is turned to mush by 1-2 shots. I have been using it even in cases, where it may not be the smartest gun to use, but it is SO SATISFYING oh my god.So satisfying, that the other guns kind of get overshadowed. Not, that i did not use them, but this game is called "Boltgun" for a reason.Each Gun has a STR-rating and each enemy has a DEF-rating. Matching, or surpassing the latter with your gun, gives you additional damage, where using a gun, that is too weak, lessens your damage. It is a nice system and a neat nodd to the tabletop.You can also find temporary Upgrades for your guns, like a machine-spirit, that adds to the STR-Value of your Bolter, different ammo types for the Bolter, like Dragonfire and Kraken rounds, which just fits neatly into the lore.You can really see, that the Devs put a lot of thought into it, especially, as i said, into the Boltgun itself.I also want to talk a bit about the levels.Again, the game takes HEAVY inspiration from 90s shooters, which comes with good...and some bad things.There is a lot to look at here. Initially, people were afraid, that there may be just one dark corridor, after dark corridor and while there are a lot of them here (Kind of dictated by the setting) the game also has some grand setpieces, that really make you feel like "Yepp...this looks like 40k!".From a manufactorum with rivers of molten metal and promethium to Plasma generators, hab-blocks, spires, demon twisted realms, a desert and industrial complexes, there is quite a bit of variety here, that actually left an impact on my memory.Like 90s shooters, this game suffers a bit of "Where the F- do i go??"-syndrome.The levels sometimes are mazes and while there is variety, it still is 40k, where every corridor looks kind of the same. I do not blame the DEVs, that is just something setting-related and it is not like the games of old do not have that problem.Doom 1+2 certainly had this issue too, so did Quake, where it is just mazes and more mazes.Be prepared to get lost! Just as a warning.This is, where the game falls flat...at least for me.It is..."serviceable", but really forgettable. It is rather a mix of 80s synth...electro...music...It fits the mood and is interactive, based on what is happening on screen, but not one track stuck, except the menu-music and the credits, which ARE heavy metal tracks.I am a sucker for good game OSTs...this one ain't one :/So far i can only say, that it runs well, plays well and it did not crash once.I have tried it on two PCs and the weaker of both was:Core i5 1240016GB DDR4 3200 CL16 RAMAMD RX 6800Win 11All @4k 120Hz Free-Synch (Samsung Q80a TV) and it ran butter-smooth.The frame-rate sometimes dipped maybe to 100 FPS, but rarely.The game apparently uses Unreal Engine 4 as its base and it seems to run juuust fine. About to be expected?Yeah, but tell that to the AAA-Industry, with their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ optimized PC-ports.Even for a "retro"-game, like Boltgun, a good performance is NOT a given, sadly.So i am happy to report: This game works just fine! Boltgun does nothing new. It is just an old-school shooter and that is all it wants to be.However you know what?Sometimes that is enough. They really knew, what they wanted, they set realistic goals and they achieved them gloriously.It isn't anything ground-breaking, BUT it does the things it does really really well.It also is surprisingly long with around 15 hours, so you get a lot of fun out of the 20 bucks i have spent.I highly recommend this game, if you are into old-shool shooters and/or Warhammer 40k.

_childDocuments_.review: Boltgun, while refreshing in its functionality, performance, and commitment to an old-fashioned feel, does not provide an experience that isn't available somewhere else, and it fails to build or improve on any of the games in this genre that have come before it. It is clear this game is not without vision, many aspects of its design are tight, but it still leaves much to be desired.I've played a more-than-average amount of Doom Eternal (probably in my top 5 favorite games), and I've dabbled in other games similar to it, naturally leading me into the "Boomer Shooter" genre around the same time that it began to explode around 2020. Many of the new games coming out around that time were iterative, new, strong, interesting, compelling, balanced, and fun.When I saw Boltgun and read all the glowing reviews, I had high hopes that this would be also be a well-designed, well-balanced, fun and fair boomer shooter like the others that I had come to love. To my disappointment, I was wrong.For everything that this game gets right (and it does get a lot right) it gets about two things wrong. It's guns are all visually interesting, but almost none of them are really usable and lack an effective use case. Its movement is fast, fun, and smooth but most arenas encourage hiding and picking off individual enemies.Enemy designs are unclear and hard to differentiate during gameplay, taking damage is VERY poorly communicated, leading to many deaths that feel instantaneous. Enemies spawn in randomly, in unfair locations, and without warning leading to cheap and unfair deaths. Utilizing movement seems futile in many situations, since so many enemies are often present on screen shooting projectiles at you that it becomes nearly impossible to attack at close range or to attempt to outmaneuver them. The end result is a play style where you use the boltgun at a distance to pick off enemies one by one.Level design is at best average, and at worst borderline juvenile. The consistent color and design palletes do contribute to the 'boomer shooter' feel, but the lack of notable level design features leads to levels that feel repetitive and confusing.The weapon sandbox is poor, with many weapons being sympomatic of the developer's clear worry about creating any one overpowered weapon. The shotgun, which at first seems like it should dominate, fails to outperform the boltgun at any range. The plasma rifle was so unbelievably bad I thought I was using it wrong; turns out it's just terrible. I cannot speak to the rest of the weapons, as I did not play for long enough to experience them.It did not take me long to realize that this game wasn't good enough to hold my attention. I've had so may better experiences in better games in the same genre, that this one didn't seem worth it. If this is your first foray into boomer shooters, you may enjoy this, though I *strongly* suggest you play Doom Eternal, Dusk, or Ultrakill first since those are proper introductions to the genre.If you, like me, have spent a lot of time with this genre, then you're better off skipping this one. Unfortunately, it just isn't worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive fan of Warhammer and boomer shooters I should absolutely love this game. It looks awesome, it plays very well, the sounds and soundtrack are both superb and yet I am not 100% sure I really recommend it at full price. It gets repetitive quite quickly and just about after an hour or so you feel like you've seen everything. Obviously a game like Duke Nukem or the classic Shadow Warrior has more variety to play with than the 40K setting, but that's exactly the problem. It basically is either space hulk or gothic cathedral when it comes to level design, with a few outdoor sections in between. _childDocuments_.review: Just exhausting, frankly. Which is amazing because it does so many things *extremely* right.All the movement feels great. There's a sense of real weight without losing responsiveness in the controls, achieved mostly by sound design. There's heft to the shooting, borrowing smart small design choices like an audio cue for hitting enemies, which comes in really handy with how chunky the graphics are. Oh yeah the graphics - just stunning. Pixely and beefy but with touches of modern tech here and there that accentuate the old school look rather than take you out of it.Basic controls are great. It feels awesome to plow through the smaller enemies with the tackle, the chainsaw attack slowing time momentarily so you can pick a target, et cetera. Et cetera! Just lots and lots about this works exceptionally well.But misguided level design and poor enemy design completely fail to capitalise on the super crunchy and satisfying fundamentals. There is way too much open space in levels and way too few enemy behaviours that know what to do with it. You constantly find powerups that last X seconds and then just kinda scurry around looking for someone, anyone, to shoot. Your movement options usually has you running circles around most of the opposition, while tougher enemies are bullet sponges rather than requiring anything exciting in the way of strategies.What's ironic and frustrating in equal measure is that the game succeeds at the really difficult parts and drops the ball entirely when it comes to the more obvious areas of design. Not to diminish encounter design of course, but the reverse of this game's situation is much more common: Everything feels good except the minutia of playing  the game.It goes on forever, too. No amount of eye candy could distract from the samey shooting, and I spent the back half of the game mostly wishing it would end.The nitty gritty is here, though. If they recognise the shortcomings and make a sequel to this, it could be something genuinely special.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give 0/10 points I'd rate this a 5/10. The game functions well and combat is good. However this game commits a cardinal sin at every chance it gets. It never fails to do so. It literally spams enemies at you to the point that you get frustrated and never mind the "PURGE" encounters which spawn enemies in every corner possible. I played this game to completion on Exterminatus difficulty and guess what? Too easy. The only way this game creates any semblance of a difficulty is what I mentioned previously: This game could've had a fifth of the enemies it does now and been just as difficult if not even more difficult with one simple change: enemies deal a lot more damage. However that's not going to happen as the only way you make this 3 hour game a 9-12 hour game is with the "purge" encounters and a **** ton of enemies. In any case the whopping 11.1% completion rate for this game speaks the truth for itself. The truth is its boring. Spamming mouse1 at a never ending horde of enemies is boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey hey, another cash-in on the modern-day return of the boomer-shooter.And like its ilk, it captures no charm or individualism that genuine olden-day boomer shooters captured.The game's hardest difficulty is too easy, there is a death-blow immunity system that allows your stupidity to be forgiven. One note is that trying to use the chainsword or charge attack are useless on hardest difficulty, and they aren't even that much more useful on lower ones. Also, the charge attack has no sprites; you just walk into people fast. Embarrasing.Enemy choreography is trash. Simple animations with low frame counts means it's nigh-impossible to read when enemies are about to attack, especially when the average enemy attack is just a wall of projectiles you can't see through anyways.Feedback for taking damage is vague and hard to read, meaning you'll be dying and not knowing it unless you constantly babysit your health number.It's games like these that really make me wonder what the average playtimes end up being within the genre. I bet everyone looks at this game, calls it awesome, but doesn't actually play it because, deep down, this game (and practically every other modern boomer shooter) is actually just boring and uninspired lmao. It's just the cool, "in" thing; to suck on the toes of nostalgia. Honestly, how far into this game do YOU think the average player made it before going back to Warzone or Tarkov or something? lmaoOnly a third of this game's customers even finished Chapter 1. Lmao, no ♥♥♥♥.This game is nothing at all that anyone needs or wants, but we lie to ourselves.The state of the gaming industry is so trashed that we eat up mediocrity.Worthless to me, but if you were gonna buy it, spend no more than 5-10 USD.

_childDocuments_.review: So, how is the much anticipated W40k:Boltgun turned out in the end?/// Let's start from the pros of the game ///-Developers perfectly nailed the style and feeling of old-school doom-like gore shooter. The controls, weapon feeling, art style are all top-notch, the game has a much fleshed-out gameplay cycle and a perfect shooter core, which keeps you interested all along-Combat. Rapid-paced, bloody, FOR THE EMPEROR! You are playing as a space marine, an eight-foot tall, power-armored, bio-modified human, whose organism is rebuilt with a single purpose - to kill violently. And oh man, you DO feel like a space marine - you're fast, tough, hit hard, and fit into the category of a super-soldier perfectly.-Equipment and weapon designs are balanced, different and provide an actually intuitive way to utilize all 8 weapons in a nice cycle. All of those look, sound and feel just as they should lore-wise - extremely pleasant-Authentity - from highly different, yet defined levels to enemies, pickups and your arsenal, everything is soaked in W40k style. There is very much attention to details, and making sure that the game follows 40k lore, rules and ideas. As a boardgame fan, I am much pleased with how much this game sticks to its franchise.-SD support. Well, officially, lack of thereof - but with kind of minimal efforts the game runs on Steam Deck, and performs well there. I played it fully on Deck, and with gamepad+gyro controls it felt so nice-2k23 game, released as a full, cooked product, that wasn't miserable on launch. Such games are more rare than Mechanicus STC nowadays.//But not everything is still perfect out here - so let me pinpoint some cons//-Abscence of a map, linked with the level design. Latter would be awesome, if the game would actually tell you where to go. Yeah, yeah, hardcore aspect, but in the end it is just annoying to clear an area in 5 minutes and then wander for 10 more to find where to go next. Visual clues for the ways exist, but sometimes they are hell of an unintuitive concept here-Difficulty issues. I played the game on Hard, and while general difficulty is pretty much dope, some areas are basically poor game design. When a game spawns you in a small, confined room with 1 armor pickup, spawns a bullet-sponge boss that endlessly spawn tough enemies that eat all your ammo, it is way too much and unpleasant. Difficulty is good when you can overcome it with tactics and skill, neither can help when in a confined chamber two melee champions are spawned behind your back, and 4 plasma gunners shoot you straight after spawning with pinpoint accuracy, while boss hits you with an auto-lock hitscan ray. No tactics, nor skill will allow you to dodge this - which is extremely annoying and leads to cheesing several rooms as the only pleasant strategy-Not so much of a con, but more enemy variety. There are numerous enemies, but all of them are already introduced in chapter 2 of 4. Not critical, but more variety in second part of the game for sure won't hurt, especially in scope of the fact that only two chaos gods are featured out of fourOverall, while having its flaws, game is a wonderful example of developers' craftsmanship and attention, and I really love playing it

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit hard to pinpoint my earliest gaming memories, but games like Wolfenstein 3D and Doom I/II are definitely among the most vivid ones. Back then they were not "boomer shooters", but just "games" - and revolutionary ones at that, that I got to play after preschool on spare PC with a black & white screen in my father's office.With all the nostalgia I have for pew-pewing pixel sprites, you'd think I'd get into the genre sooner. Oh well, at least I got to start my boomer shooter journey by purging some heretics.Let's knock off visuals and sound first. Yeah, game obviously looks like a pixelated potato, but it's still a pretty potato. Weapons and enemy sprites got some nice detail to them. Levels are well designed and visually consistent, overall atmosphere fits quite well with the oppressive, massive, future-gothic architecture of 40k. Audio consists mostly of gunfire, enemy screeches and metal music. Nothing extraordinary, but competently done.Story is... present? Boltgun is a kind of sequel to Space Marine, but the whole narrative consists of barely few sentences boling down to "you need to secure this macguffin, go and shoot anything that moves". Who cares anyway, we're here for the gameplay.And the gameplay is where Boltgun shines. It feels like exact middle point between Doom II and Doom 2016. It's quick, snappy and responsive. Enemy variety is good, with each type having unique behaviour, from cultists using various weapons, through various demons, swarming nurglings and frogs jumping around to charging champions and teleporting terminators. There are also few bosses presenting a unique challenge. Gunplay is solid, each gun feels quite different, with a few having unique mechanics affecting you as well - like overheating plasma gun damaging you, or heavy bolter slowing you down. Each gun can also be upgraded by finding a secret Machine Spirit. They're all affected differently, so it's not just a straight damage boost. It's also limited to one gun at a time and lasts only for the current level, letting you experiment and find your favourite pew-pew stick to upgrade. My personal choices were heavy bolter and, later on, grav-gun.There's also the chainsword, and while there are some creative use cases for it, it's mostly there as a last resort backup. Unlike modern Doom, it doesn't make enemies drop extra resources.The game can provide a fair challenge, even for seasoned FPS players. I really enjoyed the way they solved higher difficulties - rather than turning enemies into bullet sponges, they tweaked the spawns - so you'll not only face more enemies, but different combinations of them as well. In addition to DLC, latest patch also added a horde mode, for the ultimate heretic-purging challenge.Warhammer 40k games are in a bit of a weird state right now - there are games from a dozen different genres and rather mixed quality, kinda like with Star Wars before EA bought exclusivie rights from Mickey Mouse. Thankfully, Boltgun is one of the good ones and I've throughly enjoyed the time it took me to 100% it and its DLC. Would purge the heretics again.

_childDocuments_.review: Looked at all the hype...finally got it. I like a lot of the old games because I'm fairly old and played many of the classics since computer games were ever a thing. The game has a lot of good things going for it, and with a few patches it could be a really cool retro style shooter. But at least on my modern gaming computer, I have constant graphic issues. I set the graphics as I like them and play, and the game constantly changes the colour palette and pixelation mid game. Sometimes this gets so bad, its like all the colour richness gets cranked to the max. I reset the graphics and the problem recurs again and again. Sometimes you cannot change this without quitting and restarting the game, But when it happens, you can't see anything clearly and you end up dead. Sometimes the sounds cut out or bug out, usually the gunfire. Another thing this game does, which is kind of garbage, is that the enemies constantly track you through everything. This includes walls, pillars, floors, crates etc. This means that as soon as you move slightly into view there is already a shot, projectile, or strike waiting to hit you. It's like the environment is telling every enemy exactly when to shoot or strike you, when you are about to emerge from cover. You can mitigate this somewhat by dashing around, strafe jumping etc or just tanking the damage (if you can afford to) and killing relentlessly and look for health. Maybe this is a condition of playing the game on the harder difficulties, as I haven't tried the low or normal difficulty. It's just not something you would find in a well-made game, and comes across as a programming error. I can definitely see why people will like this game in general, but due to the aforementioned, I can't recommend this game unless its fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of torn about this game.On one hand it's an excellent Warhammer 40k game, on the other hand it's a mixed boomer shooter.For the Warhammer 40k part:The weapons are "realistic" and powerful. The boltgun feels like an automatic rpg, the plasma gun behaves exactly as you'd expect it.The decorations and general iconography is spot on, techno-gothic as it should be, metal containers mixed with giant statues and cathedrals.The music is a tad more cyberpunk/futuristic, not the usual gregorian chant infused machine sound we've come to expect from 40k. It works but it's nothing special.For the boomer shooter part:Gunplay is fantastic, enemy killtimes are spot on, weapon variety is just right.Enemy variety is good.Pickups... hoo boy there are waaay too many pickups. Sometimes you can barely see the floor from all the hp/armor/ammo.Map design is probably good but it's hard to appreciate because of the samey looking corridors and walkways. Some splashes of color help a bit to find your way out of the maze but spending 80% of the time hunting for keys and re-re-re-revisiting the same areas to find said keys is PAIN.Marking ledges with yellow paint is a nice touch.If they removed the key-hunting aspect the game would be way better off, especially as there are some really nice looking maps like the suspended platforms or giant AA guns you can actually climb.The graphical style is unique, retro-inspired with configurable pixelation. A standout feature for me.All that and a reasonable pricepoint earns a recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, Boltgun, what a gift. It’s Doom, but on Emperor-approved steroids. Imagine if you threw Doomguy into a blender with a Space Marine, added a hefty dose of chainsaw bayonets, and served it with a side of holy zealotry. That’s Boltgun.Pros:You’re a Space Marine with a boltgun that sounds like a thunderstorm in a gunfight.You explode heretics, mutants, and daemons by the literal dozens. They don’t just die; they evaporate into blood confetti.The game encourages reckless aggression. Strategy? Tactics? That’s for people who aren’t wearing 300 pounds of power armor.One-liners that make you feel like the lovechild of a tank and an exorcist. “Purge the heretic” has never sounded so good.If you turn your brain off for too long, the game turns it back on with violence.Cons:There are no cons. Only heretics would claim there are cons.Ok, fine, my fingers might fall off from holding down the fire button, but it’s a small price to pay for delivering the Emperor’s wrath.You will probably shout, “FOR THE EMPEROR” at your screen at least once, which may alarm the neighbors.If you love the Warhammer universe, retro shooters, or if you just have a primal urge to paint the walls with Chaos spawn, then buckle up and prepare for righteous carnage. This is pure, unadulterated bolt-spam bliss. Go forth, and remember: Only in death does gameplay end.

_childDocuments_.review: As cool as this game is, the combat feels samey. Nearly every enemy dies before they can even pose a threat and the ones that don't die in a single hit are incredibly spongey and have poorly telegraphed attack patterns. The problem with this game is a general problem I have with 40k in general is that everything is too powerful so nothing feels powerful. In the 40k universe you're either absurdly powerful or you're so weak you turn into paste when a single bullet hits your body. 40K fans would love this game, but Boomer Shooter fans like me aren't very impressed. Levels feel samey and more-often than not lack direction so you can end up wandering around for half an hour trying to find your way because nothing is visually distinct in these maps. There are no landmarks to find your way because everything is the same grey and brown corridors with skulls. Also these levels are all super linear with only one path through with secrets scattered about it and sometimes I end up finding secrets thinking I was supposed to go a particular direction and when I find the actual path i'm supposed to go it feels more like a secret than the secrets do. For all the polish, great art, and general good quality of this game the 73 score it has on metacritic is pretty accurate. This game is Mid. I regret spending 20 dollars on it when I could have bought something else I would have enjoyed far more than Boltgun. Wait for this game to go on sale, don't waste more money than you need to. I don't even know why I was hyped for this game in the first place, I'm not even a 40k fan. It looked really fun to play but it turns out I'd just about rather play anything else. I'm still going to finish this game, but so far it has not impressed me.

_childDocuments_.review: Boltgun is not hard.Full disclosure, I completed this on normal difficulty; not too hard, not too easy. I see a lot of complaints on Plebbit and other sites that it's hard even on normal, which is genuinely nonsense.Boltgun was one of a spate of games in the boomer shooter genre that came out in the same timeframe, and therein lies the secret. This isn't an ultra-tactical battlefight shooter. If you take it super slow and screw around there are points where the game will paddle your ass raw. Keep moving. Take resources. Reload. Shoot, shoot, shoot again. Occasionally enemies will get close, so punish them with your chainsword and keep going. If you stand around you'll get overwhelmed. Every fortification is temporary. You are the Emperor's Angel of Death, and you need no such things for long.It's exciting and action-packed. If you like boomer shooters, I highly recommend this one.Word of advice: gib enemy corpses if you can. Champions can't revive if they're dismembered and Pink Horrors also can't divide if they're dismembered. There is never too much violence.

_childDocuments_.review: After 14h and beating the game on exterminatus, the points I made earlier still stand.Pro:Gameplay feels super smooth; melee weaves easily in; weapon swaps are fast; movement is on point; kills feel rewarding; I personaly like the soundtrack.Con: Gameplay is repetitive to a point it's no longer fun; too many arena-style sections; boss battles are tedious and unimaginative (the first time each boss is encountered it's somewhat interesting, but after the 3rd, 4th, 5th time it becomes repetitive. The worst offender is the final battle)If you like the 40k-universe, you will probably like this game. The enemies are well known but not seen often in a shooter. If you don't play on exterminatus, enemies are probably more forgiving, and you can just experience the marine>everything else gameplay. If you have not heard of 40k, I can't see a scenario where you would pick this over any other retro shooter.
