_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good retro shooter overall. Nothing really special to it, but the game manages to provide this brutal power fantasy you only find in these kind of FPS. Gunfeel is good, feedbacks are punchy and violent, controls are responsive, all the core mechanics are well made and satisfying.But it's not perfect though. Level Design is on the weak end of the spectrum for this type of game. There isn't any level that particularly stands out during the campaign, and many encounters are redundant and plays likely the same. Might be due to the large amount of "arena" room where you're locked in and must purge everything that moves. It is definitely a repetitive game, and the developers didn't do much to hide this.Still, it's brainless fun and cathartic violence, I'm fine with that.

_childDocuments_.review: I can only recommend this game if you're like having to be forced to play easy or if you're a DOOM pro.Why do I say this? Well, lets take a look at the achievements, the most notable being the percent of people who've completed chapter 1.  "Why have only 30% of the people who've played the game beaten the first chapter?" You may be asking, to that I answer with terrible balancing. Chaos Space Marines will throw volleys of grenades at you, Aspiring Champions will resurrect if they get close to you (REGARDLESS if they deal damage or not), Pink Horrors shoot orbs that you've really gotta dodge, and nurglings will throw volleys of vomit at you which does enough damage to annoy the Scheiße out you.Now lets look at what you have;A Chainsword: An elegant weapon for a less civilized age; perfect if you want to dodge attacks, kill enemies that get really close, or if you just like melee. A Bolter: Perfect for dealing consistent damage at all ranges. An Astartes pattern shotgun: Great for thinning out swarms of enemies such as nurglings and cultists, or if you like close combat. A plasma gun: a weapon that if fired consistently enough, will shred even Terminators, I don't recommend using it in close quarters though. A heavy bolter: Imagine the minigun from TF2, a weapon you have to rev up before firing, but increase the damage it does, and decrease the spread. So far the second best weapon that I've found to be effective against nurgling swarms.A meltagun: Basically a flame bursting shotgun which shreds most targets, ammo for it isn't really common.A Vengeance Launcher: Just as a man who lay his life down on this planet said "That sounds promising." It DOES sound promising, until you use it. Just imagine a worse of the plasma gun, but remove the consistent firing benefit.A Volkite Caliver: Essentially the best weapon if you're looking for damage and consistency paired with piercing. The best weapon I've found to be effective against nurgling swarms, also it explodes enemies upon death.A Grav Cannon: Imagine the BFG 10000, but mixed with the Volkite weapon's(Mentioned above) dps, however, finding ammo for it will be extremely scarce.And 2 grenade varients: Fragmentation and Krak grenades.These all sound like very fine weapons until you've encountered greater daemons such as Great Unclean Ones and Lords of Change, who I will not talk about because of the fact they would turn this review into sky scraper length.In short: This is a fun pick for you if you're a pro at fast paced games that require ammo management.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is a neat throwback to the PS1 days and it's super fun to sprint around at 40mph destroying all and sundry. However after a while the cracks begin to show. The level design is boring and uninspired - while it's cool running around an Imperial hive city, the sad fact is that every area looks the same leaving the player both bored of the aesthetic and frequently lost. When the early game's minibosses show up as more regular enemies later on, the space marine power fantasy stops dead as your tactic becomes "pour 4 bolter magazines into this plague toad, dodging occasionally". Really wish I could recommend this game as it starts off incredibly well, but the shine wears off far too quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: The retro feel of this game fades very quickly, you get used to the look and then it's just boring. The biggest problem is the immense amount of back-tracking through empty areas to get to the next populated place on the  map. I don't recall any of that while storming through Doom or Quake, I'm not sure what inspired them to go that route.There is some fun to be had, and they set the price appropriate to this kind of game, but any time I think if playing it I remember the big empty spots and all the fact that I spent more time looking for the next section than actually shooting things and, well, there's so many better things to play or do.

_childDocuments_.review: Boltgun is a love letter to WH40k and oldschool FPS games like Doom, Hexen, Dark Forces, etc. It's a game that knows exactly what it is, and does it flawlessly. Boltgun makes no qualms about what it is and doesn't attempt to be anything else. Modern game design should take notes. The game is purely delightful to play. It feels like playing Doom, Doom 2, Hexen, Dark Forces, or something along those lines for the first time again.It also feels like being a space marine, mowing down ranks of heretics - admittedly, from a lore perspective, impressive as they may be a single member of the Adeptus Astartes isn't likely to wade through a sea of daemons and chaos space marines (cultists, sure). But in spirit? It's absolutely there. Is it perfect? By no means. And if oldschool shooters or WH40k aren't your thing, you're probably not going to enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent Nu-Boomershooter with an 40k Aesthetic. If you like the Doom 2016 style of Boomershooter where you move from Arena to Arena and kill enemies until you are done while searching for secrets on the way you'll probably get your joy out of this. Doubly if you are an 40k Fan.Biggest pro's are the Artstyle (Throne, some of those areas look amazing), Arsenal (We get a Gravcannon and a Volkite Cavalier. Don't think i've seen these in other 40k games yet) and flow of Combat. Biggest con's are map layouts where you will find yourself constantly lost, overuse of a specific enemy Type (Nurglings) and the OST is pretty bad aside from the Main Menu and Credits Track (Which are from D-Rok, no less.)Biggest con however is the performance. Last fight especially i found myself constantly in sub-30 territory on an 1660S, I5-9400F with 16gb of ram. A retro looking game should definitely not drop into those territories even on weaker hardware.All in all, Boltgun unfortunately misses a few thinks to make it great. Hard to pinpoint what those things are, to be frank, but i would've probably not bothered finishing it if it weren't for the 40k thematic. As a standalone game, detached from it's IP, it's one of the more bland nustyle boomershooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent boomer shooter with a 40k kick. Delivers beautiful pixel art and visual effects with chunky, brutal sounding and feeling movement and weapons. The only (very minor) critique is the game is quite easy and ammo/health pickups are very common, Hard is recommended even for people not particularly good and Exterminatus even if you're only 'kinda good' at shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of the warhammer 40k series, but i find it interesting still. Coming into the game i thought it would be like doom, but it resembles more like what i would  think the old doom games were. There is a feature called a purge wich is where lots of enemies come. Instead of getting excited it annoyed me, so i don't really recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Fun! A heck of a lot of Fun.It's just as fun as Prodeus, with the main character/movement being really nice and fast.I love a lot of the mechanics. The main weapons feel perfect and a lot of levels are nicely done. Prodeus has more replay-ability, and some unique/cool weapons that are more unique/distinct.So both have ups and downs, but overall for me the best boomer-shooters, besides good old (Brutal) Doom.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok. It isn't as amazing as a lot of people are making out, but it's certainly fun. It's not a full on retro shooter as most make out either. It's like DooM meets FPS from the 2010 era, its ALL arena survival fighting. Enter area, doors close, kill EVERYTHING in arena, move on to next arena with small connecting bit of level inbetween. I HATED this era in FPS because it was companies finding ways to make their games longer, at the cost of actual content.Sound is great, same for music, but it highlights a problem I shall go in to a little later on. The sounds are as stated, great. Everything ((except the bolter)) has a nice some nice mixing to it, each weapon also has little a unique little sound when you are running low on ammo, about to blow your plasma rifle up all that type of thing and its very welcome, especially when you are in the middle of a fight. Very nice to be telegraphed that when i'm low. Music GREAT! Rock, metal, synth mixed very well together, I shall be buying the soundtrack later on down the line.Gameplay is, eeeeehhh adequate. As stated above move to arena, kill, move on to next arena but the movement is nice at least... perhaps TO GOOD at points, the air control is VERY responsive and moves nicely in every direction you want, perfect for someone like me who loves jumping down from above on things lol. Bosses are fine, they do their job but there wasn't much balancing going on. Take the first chapter for example, they throw a lord of change at you on mission 6/7 I believe it was? Then 1 mission later throw the actual "boss" of that chapter at you, which is a sorcerer.... who you can chainsword to his FAYCE and get rid of him in seconds, even faster if you picked up the infinite health powerup. So yeah chapter bosses are weaker compared to the "miniboss" thrown at you earlier... bad balancing.Shooting can be a tad annoying. Unless the enemy is bang on in the center of your crosshair you arn't hitting it, even the shotgun has to be almost dead center to hit the thing with it's spread.. that's fine, but why does the player's hitbox have to be 2x the size of the enemies? I do get sick of plasma shots SOMEHOW hitting me despite being a clear foot away to the side of my screen.No crouch.... why are FPS games going backwards in terms of controls?The levels themselves are actually very well put together despite what alot are saying, they are fine to navigate, but everything looks, HORRIBLY boring. It's the same grey corridors over and over, there isn't a lot of variation. I thought this might change when being flung into a chaos area, but nope. Same walls, same banners almost, EVERYTHING EXACTLY THE SAME just with some cool purple "chaos" effects slapped around. There is no gore inside the levels, there is no creeping masses of flesh, there is nothing that makes you feel you are going insane and there is no "warping of reality", infact nothing to make you feel "off". Hell there is BARELY any spikes in chaos areas... It's just more grey, with some purple. Not a very good colour palette IMO, especially when you have planets like catachan in the universe but here we have desert, snow and grey..... Now, my gripe. The trailers show off 2nd ed looking stuff, its marketed towards the 2nd ed mind set, even showing off 2nd ed marine, bike and other boxes, your character cracking his kunckles inside a damn suit XD a floppy disc, it even had tracks from DROK! ((yes I own it mwhahaha, haha, hahaha...)) but there is NOOOOOOTTTTHING 2nd edition found inside the game. You are what looks like a primus smurf ((choosing smurf was also a bad idea, no one gives a crap about them....they are smurfs)), you have the latest edition bolter, the latest plasma etc etc and after they showed SO MUCH about how it was geared to my era of 40k? It did not deliver... It's Catholics in space, which a lot of us never liked that change, rinse repeat till you get bored....All in all though, good game. NOT worth its full price tag, definately get it on deal, because I refuse to pay 20 pound for what is effectively, DooM with some added bits ((also not very well optimised either, a 2d game should not make my computer hit 70c..... THAT'S TERRIBLE!)).
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun - very fun and the old school aesthetic with buttery smooth controls, excellent design - but I will say one thing that does take me out of the full 40k experience is that this game was really affordable and consumer friendly - but aside from that this thing kicks ass and is well worth your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was an "in between" selection:Not great, not terrible. If this game had any other theme than WH40k it would not be nearly as successful. I WANT to like this game but its enemy variety and gameplay is repetitive and gets old fast. The weapon variety is also lacking and does not feel as "punchy" as it should. Enemies do not have any sort of real strategy and can mostly just be ran past without any real consequence besides the level end screen not showing 100% enemies killed. (I dont care for completing levels 100% anyways) The major criticism that everybody seems to share is that there is no minimap. I agree that no minimap is slightly frustrating and leads to some serious backtracking in an attempt to understand what you are meant to be doing, but on the other hand, I sort of enjoy that feeling of exploring aimlessly and figuring out where to go. But to each their own, I understand that this may not be a popular opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best boomer shooter (by which I mean, modern shooter aping the style of retro shooters) ever made. But that's only because Prodeus doesn't punish you for dying, otherwise they're basically the same game with different skins (And that's a good thing!™). If you liked Prodeus, buy this game. If you like this game, buy Prodeus.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Prelude: this is one of those games where I wish Steam had a middle ground option for recommends.Tried a few times to enjoy this game and it's not happening, not even the 40k trappings are going to end up keeping me around.I think it comes down to level design and pacing. In its retro shooter pastiche, Boltgun failed to capture why the labyrinthine style of map design was compelling in classic DOOM and such. The levels feel perfunctory, they're there because it's a video game as opposed to a space that I want to poke and prod at with mechanics.In terms of pacing, Boltgun tries to have arena and set piece sections that are epic slug fests but they are not built up to at all. DOOM 2016 and DOOM Eternal are masterpieces in how levels are paced leading up to their arena sections. This game is not. The play loop so often can be summed up as wandering around convoluted levels collecting obligatory keys with sporadic combat and then all of a sudden any kind of flow is disrupted as you're locked into an arena.This game could have been so much better if it didn't rely so much on aping the boomer shooter formula and had done some of its own things.That being said, it does capture the 40k vibe fairly well and I love the look of it for the most part.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: We're currently in the middle of an retro-FPS resurgence, frequently getting spoiled by high quality titles such as Dusk, Amid Evil, Cultic, Turbo Overkill, Prodeus... the list goes on. Given this fierce competition, it's hard not to feel underwhelmed and disappointed by Boltgun, with it's poor level design, mediocre gameplay and unmemorable soundtrack.The levels, while at times visually impressive, feel bare-bones and labyrinthine, with no minimap function. Expect tons of samey corridors, square rooms and repeated sections and assets. Also, bloody caves! I don't know why so many boomer shooters insist on making the same dull, brown cave levels. I assume they must be simple to make, but tend to feel like filler, and a slog to play through.The gameplay loop is a bit of a one-trick pony and gets old fast. You've got your standard arena wave fights broken up by corridor fights with weaker fodder enemies, in between disorienting keyhunts. The boss fights feel especially underwhelming. These big baddies don't have many unique mechanics and mostly spam adds for you to deal with while occasionally pelting you with some sort of projectile. The pickups are especially odd. You'll find copious amounts of ammo and grenades scattered haphazardly across nearly every surface. I'm honestly wondering if the devs used an AI program to distribute pickups, as there doesn't seem to be any rhyme or reason behind the placements.The combat itself is perfectly serviceable, most of the weapons are reasonably powerful, look good and feel/sound satisfying. The baddies will explode into a shower of gibs and blood in a very entertaining fashion. This is somewhat negated by shoddy AI. There are 3 primary behaviors, enemies will either stand around doing nothing, run into your face, or teleport around. This dance makes combat feel kinda sluggish, which is a problem further accentuated by overly large arenas with enemies spaced too far between. A lot of time will be spent trying to figure out where the next enemy wave even spawned. There's also very little feedback in terms of player damage, as there's hardly any indicator for when incoming damage is occurring, and where it's coming from.Overall, a fairly mediocre experience with not much going for it besides the Warhammer theme. For fans of the franchise, you could do a lot worse as far as 40k games are concerned. If you're looking for an amazing shooter, you probably won't find it here. I'd personally recommend waiting for a big sale, or instead playing one of the better boomer shooters out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: In all seriousness, the gameplay is rinse and repeat. That will be a hard bargain for a lot of people I'm sure. So if you're really on the fence about it, while it's on sale is a good time to try it. But if you love the Warhammer 40k universe, the blood, the gore and the sweet sweet sounds of weapons making your enemy pop, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: This game lacks a minimap, a navigation system, and a feature to highlight the path to the exit. It doesn't even provide arrows or signs for guidance. The floating servoskull by your side is entirely ineffective in giving directions, mapping the area, or leading the way.While this isn't inherently problematic, the game's relative linearity often forces players to backtrack extensively to open gates after locating their keys. The color palette makes it challenging to identify certain corridors and passages at first glance. Moreover, the designers have repetitively employed the same patterns and layouts throughout the same and even across different levels. This frequently makes orienting oneself within these layouts quite difficult.The combat isn't the most challenging aspect. In fact, it can be quite entertaining, though the abundance of 'combat arenas' in what's supposed to be a 'boomer shooter' game was unexpected. The real difficulty often lies in finding the path to the exit. Wandering alone through a desert level in a constant search for the correct route becomes tiresome and far from amusing.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Boomer shooters can be fantastic, and Warhammer 40K Boltgun was just that. I had some hiccups with difficulty spikes on my trek through the campaign, but this game felt fresh, and I loved the gameplay loop and aesthetic. Warhammer 40K and Fantasy are IPs I would love to get into. Unfortunately, most of the games in the Franchises are strategy, which is okay, but I love it when we have options like Boltgun, which are great entry points for people like me who are new to the franchise. As we make our way through the game's three acts, we lay waste to various enemies and proclaim glory to the emperor with our chainsaw blade and unique arsenal. Boltgun is a short experience, but it was a great time and a way to get my foot in the door with Warhammer 40K.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Boltgun is a well-made boomer-shooter that is great for those days you want to turn your brain off and just shoot some heretics.The game is worth buying on a 50% sale as it is only about 10 hours long with little replay-ability.The gameplay of boltgun feels great.This is firstly because of the weapon design. Weapons look and sound powerful, even though enemies may get spongy depending on the difficulty. The game has 8 unique weapons (excluding the chain-sword and grenades): The bolter; you will be using it for most of the game and feels amazing.The shotgun; works as you imagine. Unfortunately used little in the later game.The plasma gun; could use a little bit of a buff in my opinion, but remains a cool weapon.The heavy bolter; LMG. Once you press the trigger, don't let go until all heretics are purged.The grenade launcher; the bane of the nurglings.The melter; an anti-armour shotgun. Sends any chaos marine back to their foul gods.The laser; works as you expect. By far the longest range of the weaponsThe gravity gun; a late unlock to tear the heretics a new one.All of these weapons look, sound and feel unique from one another and give much needed variety.The game has an armour system which indicates which weapon should be used for which enemy. Even though it rewards picking the right weapon for the job, I found ammo so plentiful that you could easily brute-force your way through most engagements using whichever weapon you prefer.The grenades are very basic, but still well done. Frag grenades have decent range, impact grenades great for single target and vortex grenades for when you are in a pinch.The charging is great as a movement tool but I found the damage and distance too lacking to be used in combat.The chain-sword is cool but quite dangerous to use as you are locked in place while cutting through an enemy, making you an easy target.The enemy variety in this game is quite limited.There are three main factions in the game; Undivided soldiers, Nurgle daemons, Tzeentch daemons.Undivided contains the common soldiers with shotguns, machine guns and plasma guns and the chaos marines with basic soldiers, terminators and aspiring champions. Which, expect for the aspiring champions who are mainly a melee enemy, all fire slow moving projectiles.Nurgle contains nurglings, lesser toads, toads and gunships. Which fire arcing projectiles or melee (expect for gunship).Tzeentch contains blue horrors, pink horrors, flamers, exalted flamers, screamers and ambulls. Of which the pink horror, flamer and exalted flamer all fire slow moving projectiles and the rest are melee.Even though there are alot of different enemies, which all have well-made sprites and animations, the variety in fighting them is very lacking. As I listed above, most enemies are melee, or fire slow moving projectiles. (A notable exception being the aspiring champion who can run faster than you. You will need to melee him to stun him giving you time to shoot or get some distance.)This means that the variety comes from finding the right weapon for the situation you are in. Since the weapons gradually unlock further into the game this means that for most of chapter 1 you will only have 3-4 weapons, which I believe explains why so many people struggle to continue after this chapter. During chapter 2 and 3 the weapon variety increases and I found these to be more enjoyable because of it.The game has 6 biomes:MountiansGothic buildingsCanyonsVaultDeep vaultShip maintenance/storage decksThese biomes give some nice visual variety and do differ a bit in gameplay (inner ship is more vertical and cramped, etc).The variety in objectives is quite low. You will be doing one of 4 things in this game; A boss fight, doing an arena battle, running to the next arena or finding a key. Since the game is mainly about killing heretics this is fine and I imagine other objectives that don't involve purging the unworthy would get annoying. The story is quite simple and the levels do feel like they tie into one-another for a continious crusade.The game has 3 chapters, each containing 8 missions. Most missions are around 20-25 minutes. Some levels are mirrored or require back-tracking but I found the variety in areas fine.There are a total of 4 different bosses. I found the boss-fights quite tedious. Especially the first time fighting a lord of change and the final boss-fight.This is because enemies seems to spawn infinitely until the boss is killed, which meant I ignored and kited enemies while just shooting the boss. As nearly all enemies fire projectiles, this quickly turned into a bullet hell and since the bosses have too much health, this was annoying. The bosses looked and sounded great and had cool and fitting attacks but as you need to kill the boss as quickly as possible to survive, most fights I spend chipping at the boss from a distance while kiting the onslaught of enemies.The difficulty of this game only affects enemy health and enemy damage. Because of an unrestricted quicksave and quickload feature you can brute force your way through any engagement. I would recommend, for your own enjoyment, to only save after an arena. This makes deaths have more meaning and can make the moment you charge a terminator with 3 hp to get the health-pack he is standing next to unforgettable.I have no nostalgia for boomer-shooters as I am too young to have played any but I did find the visual style charming.The game ran fine which is to be expected for any computer.The achievements for this game are quite easy to get on a first playthrough. Most require you to just complete the game on the highest difficulty (exterminatus) which as I mentioned before is doable for anyone with constant quick-saving and quick-loading.The rest of the achievements require you to find secrets, hidden items which give you a (sometimes temporary) boost for the current level. Most of these are easily found with a bit of exploration but others are behind hidden-walls. These are very well hidden and require you to either check every wall or use a guide. There are great video-guides on youtube showcasing the locations for the secrets but I wish I wasn't necessary.In conclusion I find Boltgun a solid 7/10 game for a weekend. The game is easy to 100% in around 10-12 hours if you get all the secrets on your first playthrough.This makes the 22 euro price tag a bit too steep in my opinion; I recommend this game on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Short little review.Boltgun is underwhelming. The 2D enemies in a 3D environment combined with the monotonous color pallet and poor lighting leads to awful visibility and boring repetitive levels. Once you play the first three levels you have played the whole game, nothing new is thrown your way. Buy any other boomer shooter; Boltgun is nothing new or exciting.

_childDocuments_.review: Super happy with this game, The lower level units are some of the hardest to kill, the harder units are fun to kill, lots of 8bit gore. Fantastic. Complete game, just works, very responsive. A game you can jump in and out of with limited time. _childDocuments_.review: What Space Marine should've been.This one doesn't disregard the lore, AND you get to find cool upgrades for your guns.And it makes me feel more brutal than Space Marine did, by having you glory kill your way into health.It goes further than that though: When Pink Horrors die, Blue Horrors spawn in their place, and that's a neat thing from the tabletop that just reinforces how well crafted this game is.Including the STR profile of your guns also just fills my warm heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this was a huge disappointment. Maybe I came in with too big expectations, after seeing how this game was praised EVERYWHERE. So the good - the gameplay, gun and shooting mechanics are terrific - that's what made me come back and give it one more shot after the other. But good lord, after a couple of hours, it gets so boring - "walk here, kill some folks that are mostly the same, UHH KEY! Use it to open door. UH a YELLOW KEY! Go find the yellow door". It becomes so monotonous, it's actually painful. Now I can understand if they wanted to get also the bad parts of a boomer shooter, but I still think the map and gameplay design is lacking. Plus, there's no map. So you end up walking around more than shooting. Warhammer Walking Simulator 2023.Such a shame, because the first hour or two I was absolutely sure this would be a blast, because in it's core - it could have been such an awesome game.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Boltgun is ok, it has some awesome visuals, the gunplay for the most part is pretty solid and the overall experience is fun. There is a good game here that many will most definitely enjoy but for me personally i feel this game has not done enough to be a good boomer shooter.The general gameplay is pretty much your classic good old run and gun doom, the game puts you into a level with your guns and you kill everything on the screen. You are searching around rooms for keys to unlock doors and collecting ammo and health to keep you in the fight. It's really that simple. Just a small note that I have only played the majority of the first chapter, in total there are 3 chapters. The level design is pretty cool, plenty of cool arenas and narrow spaces to put your shooting skills to the test. These levels are quite big; each level took around 15 to 20 minutes to complete. One big issue which isn't exactly uncommon for these kinds of old style shooters is there is no map or objective markers, you are left in the dark. There is this robot that I guess is supposed to help you but mostly it's gone then suddenly swoops in near a door. It does nothing and it seems pretty useless, it would have been great if they had some kind of map or basic quest marker, maybe not enabled by default but something for general player experience. Another thing in regards to level design is the arena battles, you are put in these situations where you must kill waves of enemies until everything is dead then the blocked door while unlock, this is a great concept and it works some of the time but in the later levels of chapter one i had some pretty poor arena battles, i had one room where i was left able to stand still for ages waiting for something happen, i realised that several of enemies got stuck on a ramp and even then there was maybe 3 basic enemies trying kill me, compared to earlier arenas where i couldn't get a break. The enemies are ok, nothing overly impressive, some do really keep you on your toes but many are just standing there ready to be shot to death. The weapons, well the 4 that i used were very good, punchy and they all had an aggressive feel. The gunplay and movement is fine, you cannot really go wrong with the tried and true old school movement shooter gameplay. The game also adds in this dash which is a little clunky mainly down to how it locks you in place once you dash. The game also has a chainsaw as your secondary attack this is actually pretty awesome as it really pushes for aggressive attack strategies. It would have been cool when using the chainsaw on an enemy if it dropped shields or health as a reward for pushing towards your enemy. I think mainly what this game has done has avoided so many good quality of life improvements that modern gaming has to keep this game super retro. Retro is good but quality of life and making the players time with the game smoother is super important. Outside of the game there is pretty much nothing, level select and of course the settings menu, you do have 4 difficulty modes to play on however. One point I will make is that this game would really benefit from something like upgrades for weapons or your armour. I know it's a boomer shooter but something to make the gameplay just a little deeper would be great. The game does have achievements which is good, however they are very barebones. The art is awesome, retro, gritty, colourful and sharp. Everything has a solid look to it and the environments do feel very immersive. The enemy sprites also look great and are very readable. Even the weapons look really awesome. The game also provides settings to make the game look slightly more modern if you choose to have a cleaner looking game. The game's soundtrack is pretty weak, I'm surprised since Doom was so influential to video game music, I was expecting they would focus on having much stronger music. The weapon sounds and overall audio is fine however, guns, footsteps and enemies all sound super awesome and everything sounds crunchy and dramatic. I did not experience any bugs apart from of course the enemies getting stuck/failing to chase me. As for performance the game run alright, i saw some reports before i played about some FPS issues and i initially thought that these must be false since looks so retro with such little to render on the screen but to my surprise, no in the later levels of chapter 1 my 3080 and I7 was struggling to maintain 70/80 fps at some points. Hopefully this gets sorted, other than some points of low fps the game ran solid at 144 fps in the other areas of the game. If you're on a lower end pc even though this is a game with retro visuals you may want to avoid this as it seems to be performance heavy. In conclusion, I am pretty shocked to see this game be a little shallow and lacklustre. I recall looking at the FAQ saying there was no horde mode, no multiplayer and there are no further chapters planned. Thinking that hopefully the game stands up on its own but the game is just so empty compared to other boomer shooters on the market. It surely wouldn't be much trouble to pull together a little horde mode and understandable multiplayer is something much harder to create however it would have been a great addition, even if it was co-op. Other than these games let downs id say its worth buying if you are a big fan of warhammer or boomer shooters, there is fun to be had here, it just depends on what you expect here. The pricing is not terrible but it could be cheaper for the smaller amount of content this game offers. Hopefully the development team can give this one a few well deserved improvements until then i will be submitting a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: I'd be worried by how much I'm enjoying the blood, guts, and gore.But then I remember they're heretics.This game has been blessed by the Emperors light, It is ridiculously fun. The movement feels great, the guns feel great, the art is an amazing retro comboand the graphics look somehow even better.       10/10If only all Warhammer games could have this level of quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Doom (2016 & Eternal) with original Doom graphics set in the Warhammer 40K universe. Quick movement, jumping, climbing, a little bit of jet-pack boosting, lots of secrets (power ups or special weapons), plenty of guns, chain-sword melee, gory giblets galore, and fast paced combat that can be challenging but always leaves you wanting to taunt the enemies again before you slay them for the glory of the Imperium and the grace of the Emperor!Very few cons... some enemies have near instant attacks that feel cheap, the classic SlowMovingPlatform + MissedJump = Wait, and no map... so you must remember colors/ symbols/ objects in each level to figure out where you need to go next after slaughtering 100+ enemies in a 10 min chaotic battle, escaping a maze, secret hunting, or trying to find a locked door once you have the key. Minor annoyances, nothing more.Considering my introduction to the WH40K universe was another shooter as a blue, heretic murdering, demon slaying, overpowered weapon carrying, power-armor wearing, death machine (SpaceMarine), I hope this game gets a sequel and brings more people into this brutally bleak, yet charmingly ridiculous setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: Game is meh. Character is weighty in a way that doesn't feel good with the amount of precise platforming you have to do. Aesthetic is pretty cool. Seems to be some shader compiliation stutter.Would've given it a weak recommendation considering the low price, but I just quit at the portal level. I bought this game for satisfying shooting to good music. Instead I got skidrow Portal.Don't appreciate a garbage portal puzzle with ass platforming putting the brakes on what little good the game had going. Would refund if I didn't get to it just outside the playtime window.Overall, only get this if you have a strong Doom itch to scratch or really like Space Marines.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun

_childDocuments_.review: So, the game doesn't do a whole lot *terribly*, but it doesn't do a whole lot *great* either. I'll list what I like first:The look of it - perfect pixelated graphics. Gun sounds are nice, too. Preface: I played the first 4 levels and stopped there so I could refund it. The discussion board peeps are already saying that people aren't allowed to say their piece about the game until they get beyond level 4, but you know what; I don't want to because it's not fun anymore and it lost me before I got further in. That's called bad design, I'm afraid. It's like being told to watch a whole season of a TV show because "it kinda picks up halfway through season 2". Sorry, no, not doing it. I'll miss out instead.So here's what's been annoying throughout the first 4 levels:- You can hardly tell when you take damage, the effects are not noticeable most of the time.- The secrets are...there. No upgrades, just temporary buffs. - It's an arena shooter most of the time, so you walk from Arena A through some corridors to Arena B. It makes the level lose its own identity and purpose. What's the story in this level? If you don't read the loading screen text, you missed it because you can't tell from the map itself. - Some floating Crash Bandicoot-like mask trying to fill in the gaps of the level's story with text. If I stopped and read that thing's generic mumbo jumbo about how it spotted a health pick-up that I can clearly see on my own, I'd get nowhere. -NO MAP. NO MAP STATS. That's right, you get lost, good luck. The levels are big and can disorient you. It's not *terrible*, but did the devs just...forget to add it? - The ost starts off great with the main menu track and then it drops off from there. - Why is the shotgun so bad? In fact, what's my incentive to use anything but the boltgun? The plasma gun doesn't feel great either, though it does decent damage. It just doesn't feel "good".- You're a sluggish marine with what feels like a jetpack jumping on the moon. Moving fast and making quick turns is difficult and often not possible. Even when you run, it's like you slide a bit. This, combined with the poor damage response on your HUD, and you can quickly die to what feels like something dumb and outside of your own doing.  -Pickups *ev-e-ry-where*. It covers the whole screen. Most of the time I pick up like 50% of it before everything's filled to the brim.Again, there are better boomer shooters out there. Prodeus in particular outshines this game in most departments in my opinion, but Cultic, HROT and Brutal Doom are worthy mentions as well. If you've played through those already and this game is on sale, sure, get it. But before you do that, there are better games out there for you, in my opinion.Final edit: Just wanted to thank the edgy people who dish out clown awards so I can upgrade my seasonal badge! You guys are the best <3

_childDocuments_.review: Feeling a light-to-mid 7.5 on WH40K Boltgun. Pros:- It feels and plays pretty much like what you'd expect from a DOOM-like or any other retro-inspired FPS developed using the Build Engine, GZDoom, ETC. It's basically DOOM's gameplay and Quake's level design with a WH40K skin slapped on top of it, so of course it plays great.- I've literally never consumed any sort of WH40K media until Boltgun, but the devs did an amazing job making the player feel like a sentient, hulking weapon of mass murder and maiming. Each step the player takes is accompanied with the clod of heavy, metallic footsteps, but players using controllers that have rumble on them will be treated to a slight rumble as well. Always having access to the chainsword just adds to the feeling, while also providing players with a competent melee option when the need arises. Bungie should be taking notes, because this is how I always imagined the Master Chief  feel like. - The sound design and music are both good, bordering on great. The space marine sound design alone was enough to win me over, but the most of the guns sound good, and the OST is pretty solid as well. Neither the sound design or OST will be winning any awards any time soon, but I don't have much bad to say about them.- The art direction and graphic design are fantastic. The devs really nailed the mash-up of 90's FPS games and WH40K into a very visually striking package. The environments are well-modeled and will treat the player to some interesting set-pieces throughout the campaign. - The game ran at a rock solid 120 FPS on my 7800X3D/4080 Super rig.- Solid suite of resolution support and accessibility options.Cons- As is the case with a lot of DOOM-likes, the level design can be a bit bland and uninspiring at times. They player will often see themselves navigating through a series of hallways, just to arrive in a slightly larger area with some enemies you've gotta take out, or a larger arena where you're basically hit with waves of enemies  until you kill them all. - The enemy variety leaves a bit to be desired and can make the game feel like a bit of a slog as it goes on. - Every good FPS game needs a good shotgun, and the shotgun in Boltgun is trash in almost every sense of the word. It gets the job done against weaker enemies, but it doesn't feel good to use, it doesn't sound right, and the reload time is cumbersome.- The blue horrors might be one of the most annoying enemies I've ever encountered in an FPS. They're up there with mechcrawlers from Selaco for the most annoying in recent memory, at least.- I kind of wish we were given more graphic options to tweak. Maybe I'm just a bit spoiled having just finished up Selaco and experiencing its impressive number of graphic options.- Having to set run to auto-toggle is annoying, especially in a fast-paced DOOM-like. - The simple gameplay loop and cookie cutter level design can get repetitive after a while.

_childDocuments_.review: PURGE THE HERETIC!KILL THE XENOS!TERMINATE THE CHAOS FILTH!THY FOES ARE AN ABOMINATION!!!WE ARE THE ADEPTUS ASTARTES THE MAILED FIST OF THE EMPEROR AND WE SHALL KNOW NO FEAR!BLESS YOUR WEAPONS AND GO!Ok its a Warhammer 40K game i kinda had to do that. I will start by saying part of me wishes this was done in the same graphic and 3 dimensional style as a more modern shooter but in the same gameplay style as it it is done a modern doom like retro shooter. That being said the Warhammer 40k universe does lend itself well to a doom style retro shooter having a Sci Fi Gothic vibe with buckets of blood and gore. I've been playing video games in this universe since the first PC Space Hulk game back in 1993 though I've never played the tabletop game but i love the universe. This game is top notch with great graphics reminiscent of FPS shooters like Doom, the first one that is. Controls are crisp and the movement feels heavy but fluid as i imagine moving in a suit of space marine armor would feel like and of course your armed with a variety of Warhammer 40K weapons such as bolters, chainswords, and shotguns. I did particularly like that the developers chose to set it up so that you wield chainsword and boltgun simultaneously as space marines are often depicted and have a moving semi auto lock on when you hit the chainsword button on your controller when near an enemy. The gameplay is fast and furious with multitudes of enemies and buckets of pixelated blood and gore but dont expect a really substantial story it is not that kind of game. In short i think the game is great and fun for a retro FPS shooter and a worthwhile investment especially if you catch a sale like i did. So what are you waiting for grab your bolter, bless your weapons and go the forces of chaos never rest.

_childDocuments_.review: Its pretty meh.The visual style is good to solid, but the gameplay is absolute generic meat compared to all other possible picks on the market right now.It reeks like big publisher wanted to jump the boomer shooter hypetrain and get its piece of cake, by applying a license instead of quality.The game lacks variety, there are no alternative modes for you to be challenged (like NG+ restarting with all guns and at higher diff.), no ironman mode, nothing.There is no way to upgrade or unlock new characters.The game even implies there are several to pick, as it shows you a character in the starting screen, listing that characters abilities.And honestly, more characters would basically increase the games value by a lot without having to use your brain too much.Have a heavy guy (Terminator?) that is slow but powerful and comes with heavy versions of each weapon, add a melee guy with stronger melee and faster movement, add a guy with jetpack and small handgun versions of each weapon and the bolter does have infinite ammo.Or whatever.It could all be there, but isnt.Enemy Variety is ok, but not special. You just get upgraded versions of each type all the time. Small poison frog, big poison frog. Weak fire mage, big strong fire mage with blue shots.The game is ok, but honestly, spare your money for any of the far superior games around the New Blood publisher.Hell, even rather go for Wrath Aoen of Ruin. Although unfinished, i had more fun and playtime with that one and it showed far better gamedesign.Especially regarding level design, Wrath and other games like Dusk or Amid Evil allow for more open spaces and different paths.Boltgun is super limited and linear.The game is ok, but pretty boring pretty fast.I went into it very enthusiastic to play a boomer shooter and gun them all down.And while i could, it felt so generic, i stopped after half an hour, later forcing myself to finish it.

name: EVOTINCTION
detailed_description: Media Reviews About the Game A Fruitless Pursuit of Eternity. A Glimpse of Evolution and Extinction. A Solemn Song of Life. Near Future. A virus of unknown origin breached the network of an isolated, self-sustained research facility and community named HERE. Inevitably, the core unit of the highly-advanced AI system that runs the facility got infected. As a result, those harmless service robots went out of control and started to attack humans. Dr. Liu, Head of R&D at HERE and one of the architects of the system, decided to go back into this lost facility to search for possible survivors while attempting to identify and fix the underlying issue. A one-man infiltration into an AI-controlled rampart. Utilize the kaleidoscopic hacking skills the doctor masters to cope with adversaries. Disable the security system remotely, rewrite IFF IDs, or manipulate rogue AI's behaviour... Do what you can to avoid any unnecessary encounters. Make your way in stealthily and neutralize all threats one by one. Go deep into the heart of the facility to face the core crisis! 'Genie' - those everyday service robots will be your most common opponents. Each of those service robots has its routine patrol, and the AI system behind their behaviours also coordinates the efforts of those robots to maximize their efficiency. In addition, the doctor will encounter certain killer robots specially-engineered to neutralize any threats to the core system as he gets deeper into the facility. Could the infected AI be to blame for everything? Or perhaps there are additional unidentified reasons lurking somewhere? All will be eventually revealed along with the doctor's investigation... Not your traditional protagonist, Dr. Liu, an ordinary researcher who had absolutely zero combat training, will have to infiltrate the facility on his own. Not a specialist in melee combat, nor a slick gunslinger, the doctor is just an average joe when it comes to 'combat'. However, as a tech-savvy researcher, he is able to hack, disrupt, and manipulate all these rogue AIs to guide himself through this dangerous automated facility. Long-Range Signal Disrupting, Radio & Electromagnetic Jamming, Hologram Illusion, Malware Implant, System Takeover, IFF Spoofing… Make use of the doctor's full arsenal of gadgets to hack a way inside and out!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is polished, the graphics are amazing, the gameplay is very fun and satisfying and the story is interesting, if a little confusing (then again, I never bothered to read the audio logs and documents I found so that might just be me). However, I do have a complaint: this game just doesn't have enough content to justify the price. I beat it twice, got both endings, got every story related achievement (somehow, I have no idea) and beat every level on S-rank and all that took me 12.5 hours. I just don't think that's worth the 30 dollars that it costs (I got it at a discount, but still to expensive in my opinion). However, other than the price, I think this game is definitely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, its some sort of an "advanced walking sim". Basically a walking sim (like fort solis, tacoma, and so on) but with stealth elements and enemies on top. So, you are sneaking around, using hacking-abilities to distract/stun enemies, trying to navigate through the station without getting caught. The station itself is fairly linear, you are making your way from room to room. The story is mainly told through audio- or text-logs. Nothing unheard of or really innovative, but overall still a solid and nice little gameHowever, the price tag of 30€/$ is just too high for such a game. I would not recommend it, thats just not a good deal. Wait until some sale or discount or whatever.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a unique genre I've never experienced before, Stealth & Hack, that the developers did quite well. The stealth mechanic worked good, avoiding the various sensors on dangerous infected robots roaming the hallways trying to get you. While hidden you had to scan the area for possible things to hack. There were a lot of abilities available to choose from when hacking but only so many could be equipped, giving you the option to play around and find what was best for any given situation. A couple of minor bugs caused me to restart the game, but they were few and far between. I recommend checking out this game if you are into the stealth genre!You can view my entire review (& more) here:

_childDocuments_.review: Just so disappointing.  I was SO excited for this title, but while graphically beautiful, the story is a muddled mess and the controls are wretched.  I died repeatedly, not because I screwed up, but because the controls reacted so badly (or were so ridiculous) that escape was just not possible.  Additionally, so many things about the situation are unexplained, or explained so poorly that they may as well not have been explained.  Why is there a timer?  How do I add time to it or cancel it?  What the hell do I do when it autosaves with 10 seconds on the timer?Add checkpoints that are just too far apart to be fair and we have... well, whatever this is.At this point, I'm so burnt out that I don't even care anymore.  I'm so sad about how far this is from what I was expecting, and I just cannot recommend it.

name: Akka Arrh
detailed_description: A cascade of words, color, shapes and sound flows around your turret as you desperately fight off swarms of inbound attackers. If enemies penetrate your perimeter you need to zoom into close range combat and beat them back, adjusting to a completely different perspective in the blink of an eye. Welcome to Jeff Minter’s Akka Arrh . This modern take from the fine developers at Llamasoft combines the intrigue of an incredibly rare Atari arcade prototype with a unique creative vision that delivers a wave shooter that is insanely addictive. Akka Arrh drips with Minter’s sense of humor, love of psychedelic color, and ability to create games that are a joy to play. Key Features: Pure arcade bliss! You'll be thrown directly into the action where combos, high scores, and survival are your only goals. Create massive chains of enemy explosions and rack up ammo for precision shots to keep a combo and your rings (or life force) protected. Lose them all, and it’s game over. Start from the beginning of the 50 unique levels, or pick up where you left off to power through to the end. Accessibility! Sensitive to flashing lights or just not a fan? Not to worry, as there is an option to disable the more intense visual effects so that the experience can be enjoyed by a wider audience.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of Jeff Minter's games going back to the Commodore 64 and have followed his stuff since then. So when I say that this might be my favourite game of his, I wanted it to be in context.Akka Arrh was originally an Atari arcade game that never left the prototype stage and wasn't officially released, though there are versions you can play now, including in the Atari 50 collection. It's a very hard game to explain as there's never really been anything like it before or since. The simplest version is that it's a 360 degree shooter where you're essentially a turret in the middle of the screen and trying to keep enemies away from said turret. If they touch it, they'll go underneath it and try to steal your pods. You can then drop down into the turret and try to take out the enemies that got in before they can steal them. If you run out of pods, it's game over, but you can gets pods back by achieving certain goals.You can launch bombs which reset your score combo, but create shockwaves within certain areas of each level that will kill most enemies that touch them, which will also create their own shockwaves. For each enemy killed by a shockwave, you get a bullet for your secondary gun, which fires much more quickly and doesn't reset your combo. You ultimately want to be able to use this as much as possible to score the highest in general and also to unlock extra bonuses. There are also various power-ups that will spawn and give you extra temporary abilities or just points bonuses.Even all that explanation doesn't convey what it's like to play this. You should watch it in motion to get a real idea of it. As usual, this has Jeff Minter's acid trip type visuals, which are understandably polarizing. I like them, but I don't blame anyone who thinks they're too much.You can play this with a controller, but that adds an extra layer of difficulty in my opinion and the game really benefits from the dexterity that a mouse provides. Like many Jeff Minter games, there's a unique mechanic where you can not only start a new game from the last level you completed, but you can also start with a certain score, which you can increase the delta for by replaying older levels and doing better at them. It's a really smart and clever system where unlike traditional arcade games, it doesn't force you to start from scratch with every new game, nor does it make you start at a later level, but with no score, meaning you couldn't be competitive without starting over anyway. It's a different kind of accessibility feature that you don't see in basically any other games of this type.As I said, you really should see this in motion to understand just how cool and different an experience it is. Unfortunately, like many releases from "New Atari", I think they're priced this way too high and it hasn't gotten the exposure it deserves as a result. As a huge Jeff Minter fan, I don't mind paying full price for it, but I do think most would probably be best to wait for a sale. But if you like arcade style experience and different ones, don't miss this!
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Llamasoft games since Llamatron in 1991. To a casual observer many of their games might look like simple shooters with weird visuals, but they're so much more - they're about experimenting with the rules of shooters in interesting ways, leading to unique gameplay experiences. Akka Arrh is one of their best and most interesting games in years.
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking to buy a genuine Llamasoft game for some time but haven't had a PS4 or VR helmet. Last game I paid for was Llamatron on the Atari ST.Akka Arrah works really well on my Intel HD4000 laptop and I am enjoying it hugely. You might control a turret in a tower but there is alot of movement from the enemies, from the tower and the explosion planes. Don't worry that there are limited shots, you have many and gain more by dropping bombs. It's a bit like Doom Eternal that way. I often have over 130 bullets just ready to be used. The difficulty level starts relaxing, then manic and then a bit more relaxed then. There are nice vector style affects. Anyone who enjoyed his previous work will love this .
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t think I like Akka Ahrr, but I do recommend it.I came into Llamasoft’s work as very much a twenty-first century American human slightly afraid to get spat upon by the beasties, but also enough of an animal lover and video game fan that I brought a towel. I started extremely intrigued by Christian Donlan’s Eurogamer review that compared Jeff Minter’s creativity style to an oil painting and gave Akka Ahrr five gold stars. Thus christening it Essential, I simply couldn’t ignore the entire Jeff Minter / Llamasoft journey.So I set out to undo my ignorance and start in 1982 with Digital Eclipses collection, Llamasoft: The Jeff Minter Story. Boy, has it been an enjoyable education, even if all of the games aren’t my jam. Thus, the journey is very recommended: especially pairing both Akka Ahrr and the Jeff Minter Story as a complete experience.I should say what works and doesn’t work for Akka Ahrr before I sign off. My favorite thing is when I get perfect clarity: know what I need to do and that execution is the only gap needed to cross. Akka Ahrr constantly divides you between an assortment of priorities where the joy comes from discerning the order of importance correctly. With time, I could develop this skill, have my enemy particles driven before me and hear the lamentations of their fragmented pixels. Unfortunately my motivation just isn’t high enough to do so. For the ones who that perfectly scratches their brain itch, I see how it lights up like rainbow gold.So again, not for me; but I recommend the ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: Just what you expect from Minter. Score attack addiction with his "best level score" carried over from Space Giraffe, cacophony of audio and visuals with some really nicely synced effects, blending of chilled and near impossible levels rather than a boring linear difficulty curve, and a slight disconnection from reality while your hands just have to take over proceedings.
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: I think Akka Arrh might prove to be my favourite Llamasoft game.So much more than the twitchy arcade blaster that it might seem from the trailer, it's a game that demands accuracy and a careful rationing of your weaponry, closer perhaps to Missile Command than anything else.This doesn't make it chore to play though, as the right shot in the right place at the right time can set off gorgeously satisfying chain reactions.It does require you to pay attention and learn its ways, to a degree not seen since Space Giraffe, and I can see how easy it would be to bounce off of it and declare it too hard, but it's super rewarding when it clicks.My only real complaint is with those little bastard bullets that fly off the screen, turn around, and fly back again at speed.  Unless you spot them being launched and deal with them quickly it's very easy for them to take you by surprise in a way that can feel a bit unfair.  There is an audio cue when they turn around, but it's easy for that to get lost in the din - and it is a glorious din that deserves to be turned up if you can. The pacing's spot on, too, building up the chaos and tension, then throwing you a nice, chilled level or two to let you cool off.Anyway, get it, and don't be put off if for the first few games you feel like you have no idea what's going on.  Akka Arrh speaks a language worth learning.
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: One of Jeff's most original games, and in my opinion one of the best because of it.  It's a little less 'loud' visually and aurally than Space Giraffe and such; more of a mellow vibe overall... which while different, is less of what I play a Minter game for. YMMV on that.  Great fun with a track ball.  It's nice to see him making more than tweaked up Tempest and tube shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Llamasoft game.  You like the other Llamasoft games, you'll love this one.  This game does give you a chance to ease into it with the tutorial levels before the game says "you've had your fun, now I have my fun" and ratchets up the difficulty.   With practice I've found my scores have improved.One thing I would've liked is to have the global highscores a little easier to find.  I've stumbled into them, but it seems like you need a game controller to happen upon them.   As a mouse keyboard user, I can bring up the local scores, but can't for the life of me bring up the table that shows my score relative to other players UNLESS I use a game controller.Annoyances with the highscore table aside, if I have to sum up Akka Arrh in one word.... Lovely!
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: I can't write the review this game deserves. The controls are simple: you shoot bombs and bullets. Bombs are free, but each bomb you fire resets a points multiplier. And firing bombs also gets you bullets to fire. So bullets are not limitless. Keep as many as you can for a bonus. That's the way this game gets into your mind.You defend pods: lose your pods and the game ends: go "downstairs" to defend your pods from intruders.Fast-paced, lots of audio, lots of stuff going on. Hard, but never too hard and never ever too easy.Jeff Minter takes something relatively simple and keeps craftig and coding until he's made you a game that gets you in the well-known "Zone". Play with mouse & keyboard..probably the best experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: Llamas!  Everywhere!!!  7.9/Camel.- PRETTY EXPENSIVE, LETS BE HONEST.  - THE MULTI LEVEL MECHANIC IS NOT VERY WELL DONE - IT WAS AWKWARD IN THE ORIGINAL - BUT THE ORIGINAL WAS LIMITED BY TECHNOLOGY.  ANNOYING IS NOT CHALLENGING.  + IT'S REALLY QUITE BEAUTIFUL.+ VERY MORISH DESPITE THE BASIC GAME ELEMENTS (SHOOT STUFF, KEEP AN EYE PATTERNS TO SHOOT MORE STUFF).+ NO NEED TO GET HIGH TO HAVE A PRETTY WACKY EXPERIENCE. Look - this game should not work.When I say work I mean be playable or popular at all.I got into this with my extreme Proto Game purchase with the Atari 50 years release at the end of last year.  Akka Arrh as an arcade game I never saw - if the back story is on the level, I am not alone in this.  Jeff MINTER appears to have more of a connection to me with Commodore 64 games - but I was very young.  I missed out on the likes of Gridrunner and Tempest which should never be ignored in the pantheon of computer games.  This game involves bombing enemies which come at you.  The secret sauce to this is that some explode and leave a pattern of destruction which sets off chains of more destruction.  Add in some enemies need to be shot rather than bombed and that there is an ammo limit and this becomes very tactical.  All this is portrayed through a very psychedelic lens with a suitable and interactive soundtrack which is affected by the chaos you generate fighting off the waves of attackers.  It is very simple by todays standards - but totally compelling and oddly therapeutic.  One aspect grinds - your gun turret is powered by a series of orbs that are in the 'basement' area of the layered playing area.  Switching to that is awkward and chaotic - not in a fun or challenging way.  It carries on the theme from the original, but 50 odd years seems long enough to come up with a more effective mechanic for it.  Over priced and a bit flawed - but brilliant as a drop in and out shooter (and oddly calming and refreshing for a shoot em up game).
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remake of an old 80s Atari prototype game that sadly never got released (but it's now included and playable in Atari 50th Anniversary Collection), shake it never got released because I give it high marks for innovative gameplay. Imagine Defender & Missile Command having a child with other random shooter elements mixed in. It's unique because there are muktiple levels of gameplay that keep you bouncing between levels to rack up highs cores while also defending the pods that you need to keep to stay alive. And apparently the developers of this one are golfers because there are numerous references to golf scoring...As this is a Llamasoft remake, if you've played Tempest 4000 there is a heavy emphasis on 3D/psychedelic/neon graphics effects-of you're photosensitive or epilectic be warned because this game could trigger seizures (there is an option to subdue the effects but it's really not enough). They also add a lot of music/voice effects that is both unusual and rewarding when you figure out how to get really high scores. It takes a game or two to get the feel of the controls (simple but they are customizable) and gameplay  but once you get into it, having to switch between two levels keeps you on your toes.While this is a good remake and fun to play, you might want to get Atari 50th Anniversary Collection and try the prototype first but it's not mandatory. I wish there were more options to tone down the graphics/3D/vector effects even further to make it easier on my eyes and senses but this is still worth picking up on a sale for the unique gameplay and what could have been if Atari had released this in arcades.
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique take on a shooter. I would best describe the game as Missile Command, except the cities are in the center, and you have a laser that can catch stragglers. Granted, that's an oversimplification of the entire thing. Llamasoft's style is here on the visual department, with bright neon lights assaulting your eyes in the best possible way throughout most of the gameplay. That being said, you can now disable the harsher side of the graphics, which is great, even for people without epilepsy who would need a break from the game. The one downside to the game is that it doesn't feature a soundtrack: it uses various instruments and chord progressions that change throughout gameplay to create a symphony that accompanies the on-screen destruction. This is fine, but it simply does not compare to the masterpieces that are the  Tempest 4000 and Polybius soundtracks.The game is good. It's different from what you might be expecting out of a shooter, but it's a lot of fun to play. It's also weirdly relaxing
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: Akka Arrh is a retro/ancient style shooter released in 2023, and I know that "retro" is the goal here, but seriously, Atari has been a triple-A company and they should know better than to dump such primitive garbage onto Steam and charge such exorbitant prices.Gameplay is really basic stuff... you have a "shoot" and "bomb" control, and the game doesn't even feature proper graphics, it really does look like a failed video game project from 1982.  Remember... this was released in 2023, around the same time as Hogwarts Legacy, Sons of the Forest and Company of Heroes 3... so to have such crap graphics from a company with a brand like Atari is just some kind of joke.  And the price tag!  Is this a deliberate insult to gamers???From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The graphics here are some of the worst, laziest attempt at video game "art" I've ever seen.  It's hard to suggest this game even has graphics.  It's just untextured, basic pixel blocks and blobs, the kind that an infant child might be able to create in 5 minutes on MS Paint.  It's clear the developer didn't even try to produce any real graphics for the game and just phoned it in.  It's unclear why such a lazy approach was taken, whether it may be caused by lack of talent, budget, or motivation to do their job properly.  It also doesn't matter... what matters is that this has resulted in a game with zero visual appeal for gamers.  It's an immediate failure on that measure alone.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic low quality vector art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the mediocre 2D visuals.The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, left handed gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only  players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 50,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.Reviewing SteamDB to check how popular this game was with players reveals a surprise... there's a modest spike in player counts for the game.  But this only happened once, around the same time that trading cards were applied to the game... so this is just card idlers getting their cards and moving on.  A closer look at the numbers shows the game just has a couple of players every week running up the game and idling it for cards, then deleting it.  We must ask how it benefits gamers for there to be so many games like this, with no merit as a serious game, that only generate sales from people idling and selling the trading cards.Akka Arrh has the cash grab price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "Dead by Daylight", "7 Days to Die" or "The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.  There's also thousands of free, superior quality games on Steam.It's absolutely unacceptable for any company to charge $20 for garbage where the developer didn't even try to do any computer graphics.  I have little respect for your average amateur developer working from home, but even they can do better than this tripe.
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a look at what game design might've done had 'realism' not got in the way then this is for you. Its a somewhat trippy game (at least at the beginning). Who knows what it gets like later on?Your turret defends against incoming enemies and they chain react - sometimes so much you wonder if the game might be playing itself, but then you get stirred in and it needs you to prod the mayhem on. You dont want to keep on using the bombs but theres a definate risk reward going on. Wait for more aerial enemies and get a free shockwave off them? But if they hit the turret you might reset the score multiplier and steal a pod. Its very polished (though the high score table could do with commas!). You definitely want to turn single button off and have two buttons for bullets and bombs. Score: Iridis Alpha
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: tl'dr it's a very solid well made game that's not going to be able to appeal to everyone with it's many quirks overall 7 out of 10 I'd say definitely get it on sale for 10-15 dollars if it looks interesting to you                                                                                                                                    On to the main review +Very unique game play unlike any other shooter I've encountered in my life  Nice aesthetics  Interesting backstory to this game as well  Many different control options to customize it as much as you want  50 levels which is a lot of levels  Arcade mode to see if you can survive all 50 levels  Doesn't take up much space so it's efficient which I appreciate- Biggest flaw is that it's quite abstract in the rules and there are many  Gets too frantic like the arcade version if you don't use a mouse   Doesn't zoom out far enough and lost pods because the enemies sneak up on you  Not the most intuitive shooter or game on the market took me about 2 hours to be able to completely understand the game and now it's just getting better at the game           Overall a very solid game that's just too unintuitive to make it a stone cold classic but considering it's a reimagining of a failed arcade prototype and it's this good I can say for those who are willing to put the time into understanding this game will find that they will like this game it just takes time, effort, and patience to be able to get anything out of this game it just means that unfortunately that not everyone will be able to like this game but I'm glad Atari allowed something like this to be made and shows that the games industry isn't afraid of still taking risks which is something we need
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play it the more I understand it but it feels like I'm always just falling short of getting the really big scores. Speaking of which, this game would be 100% better if it had high score charts, feels like that's an essential thing for any arcade style game. Other than that though, it's easy to recommend to anyone who's enjoyed Minter's previous works or those who just enjoy an innovative new shooter!
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

_childDocuments_.review:
A cascade of words, color, shapes and sound flows around your turret as you desperately fight off swarms of inbound attackers. If enemies penetrate your perimeter you need to zoom into close range combat and beat them back, adjusting to a completely different perspective in the blink of an eye. Welcome to Jeff Minter's Akka Arrh.

This modern take from the fine developers at Llamasoft combines the intrigue of an incredibly rare Atari arcade prototype with a unique creative vision that delivers a wave shooter that is insanely addictive. Akka Arrh drips with Minter's sense of humor, love of psychedelic color, and ability to create games that are a joy to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Akka Arrh

name: Withering Rooms
detailed_description: Withering Rooms is a challenging 2.5D horror RPG set in a procedurally generated Victorian mansion that changes each night. Explore Mostyn House to gather weapons, distractions, magical artifacts, keys, and crafting materials. Take on a huge cast of monsters and bosses - overgrown undead, invisible ghosts, devious witches, axe wielding madmen, and many more. Discover secret passageways, dusty attics filled with treasure, and even the ever-changing Byzantine Labyrinth that lies beneath Mostyn House. Take the sting out of death by performing rituals to preserve items from night to night or permanently level up. Meet a cast of strange friends, merchants, liars, and witches each with their own agenda. Cast a wide variety of spells - create hex traps on closet doors, enchant suits of armor to assist you, or create a decoy mimic of yourself. Greater dangers - and greater treasures - await you in the hedge mazes, tombs, caves, churches, and ruins beyond the Mostyn House grounds. Steam Deck: Withering Rooms has been played start to finish by multiple people on a Steam Deck and we believe it meets all of Valve's Steam Deck Compatibility guidelines. We are waiting on a Steam Deck Verification review from Valve.
