_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't bad, but it's very frustrating, which makes it hard to recommend.One significant issue is the overly minimalistic control scheme, which makes basic tasks like accessing the map or navigating menus feel tedious. An even more pressing concern is the overall game's design; as you advance, confusion often increases due to fractal-like structure of the game — each time you unlock a door, you are likely to face multiple locked doors immediately afterward. This principle  also applies to puzzles and items; players are inundated with an overwhelming number of items, documents, and locations to explore. While many puzzles are relatively straightforward (with some exceptions), they typically depend on basic pattern recognition and would be easy to solve on they own, the challenge primarily stems from the excessive number of objects and overall visual clutter. A most common puzzle type in this game involves 4-digit codes linked to specific dates; there are numerous such puzzles, which can make navigating related documents quite frustrating. Many of these issues could be mitigated by removing items and documents that are no longer relevant. Lastly, there is a minor  problem involving a section where a which feels counterintuitive.The presentation is appealing, and the atmosphere is dense; however, completing and enjoying the game demands a considerable level of patience, which I unfortunately do not possess.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and bizarre game about the labyrinth of the mind, told through the lens of a loving homage to Resident Evil where the combat is replaced with cerebral challenges. It's the ultimate escape room filled with some of the most mind-bending puzzles I've ever witnessed; every one of them with their own special "a-ha!" moment. You will get stuck, and you will start to pull your hair out and feel like you must've missed something, but when it finally clicks and you understand what all these shapes and symbols and numbers really mean... there's no better feeling.My iPad is full of pictures of puzzles on my TV and the random scrawling of a madman. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A captivating, enigmatic masterpiece! “Lorelei and the Laser Eyes” is a real gem in the world of video games! From the very first minutes, I was totally immersed in its mysterious, spellbinding atmosphere.The graphics are simply magnificent. Every scene is a visual work of art, with meticulously crafted details that reinforce the game's dark, intriguing atmosphere. The play of light and shadow creates an immersive atmosphere that immediately transports you into Lorelei's unique world.The music and sound effects are perfectly in tune with the game's environment. The soundtrack is mesmerizing, adding an extra layer of mystery and tension that keeps the player's interest at its peak.The gameplay is innovative and stimulating. The puzzles are extremely well designed, offering a rewarding intellectual challenge without ever being frustrating. Each puzzle solved provides an immense sense of satisfaction. What's more, the game perfectly balances exploration and puzzle-solving, making every moment captivating.The plot is deep, rich and superbly written. Every character is well developed, and the story constantly pushes you to find out more. Unexpected twists and surprising revelations keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish.“Lorelei and the Laser Eyes” stands out for its originality and ability to create total immersion. The game doesn't just follow the conventions of the genre, it transcends them to offer a unique and memorable experience.In conclusion, “Lorelei and the Laser Eyes” is a must-have for all fans of puzzle and adventure games. It's a masterpiece that richly deserves to be discovered and savored. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a deep, mysterious and extraordinarily well-realized gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: is quite possibly the best puzzle game in existence. Mind you, it takes plenty of patience and reams of scratch paper for note-taking, but everything about this world is . Many games of this complexity are obtuse, forcing you to fight  itself -- not so here.   solve itself.It gives you a log of every unsolved puzzle as you find them, crossing them out as you make your way through one-by-one. It keeps an index of your discoveries, allowing you to quickly and easily reference (and cross-reference) any  information you come across. knows that the beauty of a good puzzle, the fun of solving a mystery, is not about ripping your hair out trying to find one hidden detail...but is about piecing together a narrative, one step at a time, culminating in a climax so satisfying that you can't help wonder how you didn't see it all along.If you can't tell, I . Regardless of its mastery of the puzzle genre, this game is also a visual and auditory treat, with stunningly surreal set-pieces and a haunting score. Do yourself a favor and dive head-first into this masterpiece -- and don't forget to bring a notebook!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT : After finishing the game and finding solutions to certain puzzles online or elsewhere I further stand by my review that unless you know certain details before hand good luck figuring out some of the more non contextual puzzles in the game.I am glad I gave this a try, however I am not so glad to have had to rely on outside sources to get intel on how to solve things in game.....This is one of those situations where I would have loved a neutral option.The game is great while you are getting it and making connections in your head and maybe on paper if you so choose, however once you get stuck, good luck, you can try all sorts of things and still not get it even after a couple of days of trying.I can understand if there are some cases where you can back track and make references to, but in my case that was really not the case.Puzzles without a reference or context are simply not fun. Having spent two days pondering what the answer could be, I finally decided to check online and the answer made me feel like I either should have been sad I didnt think of the most stupid solution or proud of the fact that I finally gave in and checked for a hint/solution.Besides some of the more dumb solutions to certain things, it was certainly fun until I had to find a solution from else where and not within the game itself.For those of you that love puzzles and can think out of the box for everything, this is definitely the game for you, for anyone wanting to try their hand at a puzzle game or if this is your first attempt at something like this, this maynot be the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Beat this game tonight and absolutely loved it. The varied gameplay, soundtrack, visuals, and story were all fantastic. The puzzles were sometimes quite hard, but extremely satisfying. I streamed some of it for a friend and we had a great time solving puzzles together. It's so fascinating how different people approach the same puzzle from such different angles. I wish I could erase my memory of the game to play it again fresh. Highly recommended. The only small quibbles I had were 1) like many other reviews have said the menu system could really use a dedicated back button, 2) the minimalistic controls worked okay for the most part but on a few puzzles made things confusing for me where I couldn't solve it for a while because the way to manipulate it wasn't intuitive (the music box was the biggest one), and 3) opening up the notes that were black text on a solid white background was causing me eyestrain (solid white screens can set off migraines for me but this may just be a me issue). Minor issues all though!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere and some real head-scratchers for puzzles, all make this really vague and oblique puzzle game a pretty memorable experience.Tips for anyone wanting to play: many puzzles can be solved on your own with lateral thinking, others can be brute-forced, and some are really oblique and obtuse if you're not a genius. Pet the dog, and "cheat" with a guide if you need to; it doesn't make the game any more comprehensible in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: After playing their previous game, Sayonara Wild Hearts (and becoming one of my favorite games of all time) I was extremely excited for Simogo's next game. And though the gameplay is very different, Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is an absolutely amazing puzzle game, and like SWH, unlike anything I've ever played before. If you enjoy puzzle games or adventure games, you owe it to yourself the play this game, it's absolutely fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a phenomenal experience from start to finish! My playthrough clocked in at around 13 hours, and I had a great time the whole way through. The puzzles were incredibly satisfying to solve. The game recommends you use a physical notebook to write things down, and while my notebook ended up looking like the scrawls of a madman, having something simple to look through on the fly was really useful. None of the puzzles are too difficult, but there was so much variety and  always another puzzle to be solved if one was giving me trouble. The controls are extremely simple, with just directional inputs and an action button (though a back button would have been nice). This game just oozes style. I loved the fixed camera angles and the game goes a lot of places (both physically and story-wise) that I was not expecting. Enhancing the experience was the incredible soundtrack, and some of those songs will definitely be joining my playlist. Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a gorgeous puzzle game that I would recommend to anyone who is in to games where you have to think, but it still manages to be an approachable, wonderful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★One of the best puzzle games I've ever played. The puzzles are brilliantly designed and some are complex enough to actually require a pen and paper. The controls are simple and everything you need to play the game is explained through the various notes and documents you can collect in the game. The immense satisfaction from solving and unlocking the story is addicting. I always kept playing to solve "one more puzzle". Almost everything in this game is a puzzle, which makes you feel intelligent and fully absorbed into the otherwise simple gameplay.This game has awesome soundtracks! The atmosphere is haunting and full of mystery as you try to uncover the story of Lorelei and the Laser Eyes. The story can be confusing and the puzzles can feel a bit challenging at times, especially in the beginning, but never give up, and it will be a truly wonderful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: once you start figuring out what the game wants from you and how to solve the puzzle, it just clicks into place and it just goes and goes and goes... there's a very smooth momentum to it. the words that come to mind are "snappy, elegant, patient, cheeky, clever" for me... im not very good at words, but i hope im making sense here. it was thoroughtly enjoyable all the way through, i very rarely felt genuinely stuck on something, and whenever i was, there were 25 other things i could go work on instead. and when you finally solve that puzzle, its so satisfying, it sounds like sunshine on a wednesday...
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I bailed at 90%. I can't believe I got that far through a game and then quit. But from 80% I was just trying to push through. I decided that, actually, I didn't need to sink any more time into doing something I was hating.Early game is good - the puzzles are achievable and there are always a couple of 'next steps' to follow up.Late game is incredibly tedious. By now the single spacebar control is driving me mad (just give me a way to escape out of menus and a fast travel as nothing new turns up in walking around endlessly) and the final puzzles are just annoying. I had no idea what I needed to do to get finished, and the guides just sounded tedious. I'm gonna watch someone's walkthrough.I wish I could retrieve the hours I spent on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game's story is revealed in bits and pieces with every puzzle you solve and following all the clues, solving these puzzles, and figuring out the 'truth' was a satisfying exercise. The game's design of allowing me to refer to any piece of text I had seen before meant that I could focus on solving the puzzles rather than having to track down the clues again and again and was appreciated. Adding all that to great visuals and music as well as an outstanding atmosphere (though sinister and eerie) and this was a complete package as a game. However, I would still give my world for a back or cancel button.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, just wow! This game exceeded my expectations, it's not just "cryptic story puzzle game" as it may look on the first glance, but also a well-crafted one.Puzzles may look basic on the beginning but later on they'll require you to be more aware of surroundings and clues you can find scatttered around. It's not just about logical thinking but also utilizing all information you have, yet there will be couple of times where you have to take a leap of faith. Most of the time there we'll be multiple places where you can go, so you don't have spend all the time in one place in case you're stuck.Story may be quite confusing, not going to lie, so I would recommend do not concentrate much on it, you'll still have alot of fun during play.There are two moments I kinda disliked though:Aside of that it's great game I would like to recommend to anyone who's looking for great puzzle challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei & the Laser Eyes is a fantastic immersive adventure game that is both challenging and satisfying to play. Its many puzzles will leave you stumped for certain, but the achievement of progressing through the game is incredibly satisfying and engaging. This game really feels like a modern imagining of a point-and-click adventure game without the sluggish pitfalls that can come from that genre. The game is well-paced, with natural breadcrumbs that effortlessly lead you through the incredible story as you slowly piece together what is truth, what is fiction, and what lies between. I wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone interested in the mystery or puzzle genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I am the perfect customer for this game. I love escape games, codes, weird stories, searching through documents and I LOVE when I'm forced to use a pen and paper to solve enigms. I believe games with many puzzles and codes have to establish a very strong trust relationship with its players. If you play and at some point get stuck on something only to find out the response is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, odd, or forces you to try 10 results to bruteforce your way in, you won't trust the game anymore. Which means each subsequent puzzle for which the answer isn't obvious will be upset you to the point you will stop playing.I did everything in the game. I did not feel that way ONCE. On top of that, it's not that often you play a game that absorbs your attention so much you forget about time. I ended up playing until 4am because I wanted to uncover MORE of what was hidden.I just feel like I spent 20 hours in a very, very high quality Escape Game that plays with its medium in many ways. If that's your kind of stuff, give it a go!To devs just one feedback - please consider adding a "return" button on controller to quickly get out of a menu or any interactive element.Thanks for making this game, I loved every single puzzle in it <3
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei is undoubtedly a solid puzzle games. The game provides a lot of puzzle variety and is sure to scratch the itch for most avid puzzlers. There is a good range of puzzle difficulty that has a general pace of ramping up towards the end. For myself, I found some of the mid-game puzzles to be the most challenging. The controls and UI for this game are smooth but, undoubtedly frustrating. The lack of button mapping makes this game a slog at times, which may turn some players off entirely. I did get used to the menu navigation eventually but overall I felt it was a poor design choice. A big turn off for me was the constant usage of "tank control" segments. I would guess at least 20-30% of the game uses that control scheme. I thought it was a cool gimmick at first but, I quickly grew tired of it. I became frustrated when the game kept assigning me tasks to complete in those areas. The game has a beautiful art style. Lots of noir elements juxtaposed with retro 8-bit style graphics. It does feel a little bit unnatural at times but still looked great. Overall, I did enjoy this game but would not consider it on the same level as Obra Dinn or Golden Idol like some of the other reviews claim. If you are a freak for those games like me, I would recommend you check out this game for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Such an exceptional experience.  I'd absolutely recommend this to any fans of puzzle games.  The design is exceptionally clean, the puzzles are perfectly tuned so there are no red herrings, and the story has a lot of larger things it's trying to say.  This is one of those rare games where you consistently feel really smart every time you solve a puzzle, while also having no puzzles that I would describe as being unfair or obtuse.Get this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A labyrinth exists to prolong a path.A maze is for getting lost.And you will be lost. Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a game about tearing your way through a web confusion, insanity and death to discover a buried truth.It's a game about games, art about art, a reflection of the people who made it and the people who play it.Have you ever wondered what happens when the snake finishes gobbling up its own tail and consumes its own head? The answer is: it becomes magic. This is the type of game Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is. If you think you're up for it, I implore you to delve into the maze yourself and see what's waiting for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I did the first couple of puzzles, thought the game was way too easy, and then entered the hotel... I can't wait to delve into this more tomorrow. In the meantime, I can already tell this is something special, and I've had a lot of fun getting acquainted with the world and presentation.Edit 1:7.6 hours in and I'm not even halfway done with the game. I'm loving the puzzles, the world, the mystery. it's all great. get this game
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game expecting to enjoy the puzzles, but what really captivated me was the story. It puts forth some very interesting ideas on the nature of cinema (and of art as a whole). I found the puzzles to be good but nothing outstanding, although they were really good at guiding you through the story, because they are often embedded within the objects and environments you come across. The art style, music, and presentation are immaculate, as is always the case with Simogo (I still have Sayonara Wild Hearts's soundtrack on repeat).Sadly, the game does suffer from clear controlling issues. The developers decided to stick too hard to the "using only one button and one directional input" mechanic, which makes navigating menus pretty annoying (you have to scroll all the way back up just to press "Exit"). This also means that there is no way to back out of a puzzle; you have to intentionally screw it up in order to get out, which can get very frustrating if you did not intend to enter the puzzle in the first place.Even with these glaring issues (which I hope the developers consider fixing, although I don't hold out much hope), Lorelei still managed to captivate me with its thought-provoking story and outstanding style. I recommend it to anyone who doesn't mind pattern recogition-style puzzles, and doesn't get too frustrated by a clunky user experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Such great puzzles, and so many of them! Very impressive overall. Lorelei and the Laser Eyes looks good, sounds good, and is just generally captivating.The story was a bit hard to follow, but there's this bit at the end that kinda "forces" you to understand what happened. Things aren't very clear until you sort through everything and piece it together.Nevertheless I loved exploring the hotel, the mazes, and everywhere and just solve puzzle after puzzle. It's the kind of game that pulls you in so many different directions - you can be trying to solve one puzzle, but all of a sudden realize the solution to another and bounce from on sequence to the next.Pen, paper, and lots of patience are a must.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: 1 word: gemIf you like mystery/puzzle games, think no more, just play it. It is similar to Obra Dinn's level of quality:artistic direction? checkatmosphere? checkpuzzles? triple checkmusic? not omni-present, but when there's some, the impact is therestory? like most of these kinda games, it is a puzzle itself that will keep you guessing until the endHonestly, the ONLY "bad" point about it is the lack of back button when menu'ing, but that would go against the design of "1 button gameplay" they went for, and you get used to it.Take your time and enjoy a piece of art.Ab imo pectore
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei earns a spot in the short list of games that I wish I could immediately replay again, akin to Outer Wilds and Obra Dinn.Nearly everything is designed, organized, and executed flawlessly. The stylized atmosphere is haunting with a mix of modernized Resident Evil, feelings one must have of perusing an old magic shop, and being lost in a maze-like mansion full of secrets. The puzzle variety is wonderful and rewarding, a mix of simple, opaque, and a few 1000 IQ challenges to boot - a true delight to puzzle enthusiasts.No game is perfect. The menuing can be tedious. As others have said, the rapid screen brightness shifts can be pretty jarring.    Arguably these are design decisions and not actual negatives.If you're interested, don't wait for a sale like I did because it's likely not coming.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid lover of puzzle/escape room/mystery games, this game is exactly my cup of tea. I was interested because some reviewers compared LatLE to Return of the Obra Dinn/Professor Layton, but rather than that it felt more like a large sized escape room game.I enjoyed the difficulty of the puzzles, and I like that I can go and do another puzzle before coming back to a previous one I was stuck at (which was usually because I was overthinking it). It really paid off to not look at guides even when I felt that I was stuck (there are helpful spoiler-free guides if you're really stuck). I really enjoyed the noir style and atmosphere that the game built up, and the music really helped to build the mood. I was really confused at the story but it helped to reread through everything after unlocking them. Highly recommended to go in blind!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: With Saynoara Wild Hearts being one of my favorite games of all time, I was extremely excited for Simogo's next game. I had also played Year Walk in the past and enjoyed it as well. Lorelei exceeded all my expectations. This game was everything I want out of puzzle games. Simple quick one screen puzzles all the way to overarching, complex, wide sweeping puzzles. Interesting story and lore to piece together throughout with an amazing and satisfying ending. Play this if you like piecing together information to reveal the truth.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent pure puzzle game with an interesting mystery, elegant visuals and a couple of exceptional ideas and gimmicks.The difficulty is just right. Some puzzles may appear too hard, but it's usually because you're not supposed to solve them yet - explore first and find required information, then go back. This is, in fact, one of things I'd like to see improved in Lorelei: it would be nice to know whether or not we can solve a puzzle. We, the puzzle enjoyers, aren't exactly known for liking to give up after all. We can spend quite a lot of time inventing plausible solutions even when lacking necessary data.Another thing: because you interact with the game with only one button (plus directional ones, of course), navigating the menus is a major pain. There is no "go back"/"cancel" button on your gamepad/keyboard, which means that to go back to the game after checking your inventory or clues, you need to select the "go back"/"cancel" button on the screen every time. A "map" button would also make things more pleasant. I bet in someone's head the idea of "minimalistic controls" sounded cool and artsy. Well, let's not do this again.Since I'm already complaining, one minor thing, this time completely subjective: I think the story would "feel" better if it was told in a more down-to-earth way, with a bit less notes/letters and more dialogues. As it is, even though you learn a lot about some characters, it's hard to actually get to know them, to like or dislike anyone in the game. Because of that the story doesn't "hit" or make you "feel" anything besides the feeling of "that was interesting".All that doesn't change the fact that Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is an absolute must-play for any puzzle-solver. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I've felt like a hog that found an unexpected rose. I kept my hat on and boots off, always walking in a straight circle. This game is like blood that flows through the veins. I don't doubt there are geese, who say all ducks are swans, however, lending an umbrella to a salmon is a fool's errand. Even the greatest artists can make a badly controlled omelette, nevertheless, even a bad letter will end somewhere. Moreover, the hammer has no directions for the anvil. Even a delicious soup can stain the shirt.I'm a hiker who asked for a bigger forest. I hope this milk cow will not be lined up to be shot. Sometimes too much milk is too little milk for one canary. The mystic filled my heart, the flute didn't blow smoke, the chef didn't count the mice. The bishop is happy, and the saint is not sad. If you are pondering, I bring you this advice: keep your antenna up and never plow sideways.Sometimes the thumb is a way out of hand and this thumb is pointing up.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't like puzzles, you probably won't enjoy this game. This game is like sitting down with an activity book of logic and math problems, and flipping through to solve different pages that look interesting. Eventually, you'll have to solve the harder one, but by then you'll have a better idea of what type of solution the game is looking for.The game designers used repetition in an ingenious way. Several numbers will appear again and again, either as outright solutions or a step towards the solution. You might see that a certain pattern needs to be entered and because you've seen it again and again, you'll know that the pattern will be based on a specific number in some way. The puzzles also blend seamlessly into the story the game is telling. Because certain things repeat in just the right way, you'll easily piece together a narrative of things that happened as you slowly reveal the "truth."The controls bothered me initially, as the game insists upon using just directional buttons and a single action button. The D-pad and any analog stick will act as your directional buttons, and a any other button will act as your action button. This can be annoying in the menu as there is no back button. You have to always navigate back to the X. By the end of the game, I realized the advantage of this system. Solving a more abstract puzzle, I intuitively understood that the action button would do something without needing to be told.The story was fantastic. It was filled with mystery and fantasy but was ultimately about learning to accept reality and maybe forgive past mistakes.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I applaud the creators of this game, a game that puts a show for the cosmos. The story is captivating and enigmatic, the gameplay is absolutely phenomenal and the puzzles are intuitive yet challenging. I recommend this masterpiece of a game to everyone who loves to crack codes while having unique and innovative experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing Lorelei and the Laser Eyes with no guides, pushing myself to figure things out but believing the developers give everything needed in the Photographic Memory and really capitalizing on any and ALL numbers, interactive objects, and symbols I could find. I absolutely refuse to look up guides and though I sat stumped a few times, it really only took about 20 minutes of thought to come up with some kind of progression or movement. I just kept telling myself to never expect it to be typical and to always seek the most complicated way forward or go back to an item or memory I had already used. I absolutely love this game. It's a masterpiece in my opinion. I hope there are more like it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: For the asking price, you get an insanely stylish and atmospheric piece of meta-text on creating art, an interrogation of what the creator owes the audience and the “systems” that finances it, which also a reflection on how we engage with film, modern art, digital art, and ultimately serves as a self-reflection on itself, its historical gaming inspirations and the studio that made it, all told with a healthy dose of mysticism, mystery, and the misdirection. Also a banger puzzle game with in depth blader mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 14 hours and 8 pages of hand-written notes to solve this thing - and I loved every minute of it. None of the puzzles are especially difficult in themselves. But they hit you with so many different areas to investigate and avenues to explore that the resulting overwhelmed confusion prevents you from getting to the core of them. I spent most of Lorelei and the Laser Eyes understanding its internal logic. Which is exactly the right combination of actual logic and magical thinking to make it just work for me. The puzzles are of the "really good escape room"-type and manage to be quite unique despite their sheer amount. The visual design and atmosphere bring the entire experience home for me: The entire game is filled to the brim with eerie vibes. It's haunting. Its puzzles haunted me throughout my day. Just as Lorelei is haunted. And now, I'll leave the rest of the game's secrets to smarter people. Godspeed, discord servers of the world!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Never before has a game made my jaw hit the floor so many times. I've played puzzle games for years, and designed multiple puzzles myself. Genuinely, I cannot think of a SINGLE puzzle that felt off or obtuse - and for this puzzle box in a puzzle box in a puzzle box in a puzzle box in a puzzle box of a game, that's damn impressive.If you love puzzle games or escape rooms, pick this up immediately. So many moments of genuine "how the hell did they design something like that" and just a perfect experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I'm always in search of puzzle games that really make me think, and this delivered. Six pages of notes, cross referenced, color-coded, and a really satisfying story throughout. (yes I wish there was a back button but ah well) Played at the same time as a friend and we kept texting each other cryptic updates. I haven't solved one of the doors, but by god I will figure it out
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing puzzle-style game. When someone asks, "what's it about?", I don't want to answer them. I recommend going in blind and just letting it all unfold. It's confusing in the best ways possible. It's thinky but makes you feel so clever. If you like solving puzzles in video games, this is a game you will almost certainly love.There are some dark themes/subject matter, but the game itself isn't scary at all. No jump scares or other similar horror-style elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Damn, what a game. Definitely scratches that "The Witness" itch, although this one isn't AS open ended and is easier.There was always something to do. When I got stuck with one puzzle, another path was waiting for me to be explored, containing 3 more  riddles. The game stays very criptic, so for most of the time, you're not quite sure what's going on. Very easy to develop a "one more puzzle" syndrome. It's a good idea to keep a pen and paper on hand.I strongly recommend it. First run finished with 99% completion and I'm going to go back for that last 1%.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptionally well put together atmospheric puzzle box that was extremely compelling all the way through. The game's story and themes are woven deftly into the game play and exploration.  You are given all the tools to succeed from the start. The game treats the player's intelligence with respect and provides minimal to no hand holding.  I'll be keeping an eye out for any future offerings from Simogo!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A thorough exploration of the fictional bodies of work of a slightly unhinged and an upcoming artist.The monochromatic presentation is regularly punctuated by creative set pieces and novel perspectives in an otherwise formulaic environment.This game really benefits from having a guide or friend handy to give you spoiler-free hints as there is no built-in hint system. The single-button controls can be a bit tedious but you get mostly used to it. Take the "pen & paper" hints serious since this will cut down on otherwise repetitive painful navigation of the collected hints.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic.The atmosphere oozes personality and tension. I'd describe a lot of it as 'Resident Evil without the zombies' and that's honestly a great vibe in my opinion. I like settings that rely on creeping discomfort rather than cheap jumpscares, and this game delivers on that. The music is used sparingly but one song in particular is probably gonna be stuck in my head for weeks.I was worried the narrative would be Twin Peaks levels of incomprehensible, but it's actually pretty easy to put together. By the end I had a very solid idea of the events that had transpired and there weren't any huge plot holes or unanswered questions. Obviously I recommend going in blind and piecing it together for yourself, because it really adds to the whole experience.Of course, the crux of a game like this is the puzzles, and LatLE aces this. Puzzle difficulty is always going to be a subjective  issue, but for me the game hit the sweet spot of 'challenging but not frustrating'. The open-ended nature of the map means if you're stumped on one puzzle, you always have the option to step away and try something else until the answer comes to you. The game is very generous with keeping track of things for you, from listing puzzles you haven't solved yet to a perfect recollection of every document/image you've read. But it also recommends taking notes on a pen and paper, and doing this really enhanced my experience. I managed to beat the whole game without looking anything up and I am very satisfied with that.It's not a completely flawless game. I got lost a lot trying to remember where particular rooms were, and the control scheme being limited to 'directions + 1 button' is a bit odd. But neither of these was enough to stop me from devoting two whole days playing it from start to finish.If you're even slightly interested in puzzle games, this is an instant recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing new addition to the open-ended puzzle exploration genre. If you like games like Outer Wilds, you should definitely check this game out; hits the exact same itch. The whole game has a wonderful creepy atmosphere, while never really being a horror game.The puzzles are challenging, but not unfair. _childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Very good puzzle game with challenging yet crunchy puzzles. Cool visuals and imagination as well. It's kind of a cross between a puzzler, Suda 51, David Lynch and Alone in the Dark (no combat though). An intriguing set-up and story keep things interesting as you progress. The puzzles are mostly well-judged in difficulty with it rarely feeling unfair or bs, and they are very satisfying and there are tons! Like other good puzzle games of this ilk, you usually have a load of puzzles available so if you get stuck you can try somewhere else. I do have some gripes. The controls and movement are a bit clunky but retro in feel. The menu does a great job of cataloguing clues, but its frustrating dipping in and out of it constantly with no dedicated back button. Same with the map, no map button. I also got very stuck a number of times simply because the game didn't highlight interaction options well enough, for example interactible objects with no button prompts where there were actions I didn't know that I could do. It's also easy to miss documents with the page-turn option, and some items in the world like notes can be easy to miss because of the specific angle you need to be for them to highlight. It would be good if some of these things can be ironed out.Overall though this is a top tier puzzle game with a lot of style, maybe not in the very top tier of the GOATs but definitely up there. Definitely recommend to those who like crunchy puzzle games with exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically a massive Resident Evil-style puzzle box mystery mansion, except instead of zombies you get ambushed by even more puzzles around every corner. I'm not even kidding, the sheer density of puzzles in this game can be overwhelming at times! If you were looking for a Layton-esque puzzle collection you can really sink your teeth into I'm happy to report that this is exactly that.♪ I dream in black and white, ♪♪ See it all through Laser Eyes ♪
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Within two and a half days, ive put ~26  hours into this game. I am a voracious puzzle game player, and will usually sit with a pen and paper and start and finish a puzzle game in one setting. Try as I might, I could not do that with this game. This game felt like the love letter of puzzle games. Imagine just the puzzle aspects from all resident evil games, combined with the storytelling elements of the Rusty Lake franchise, but even then those comparisons dont do any of these games justice. I have now completed this game, and used up a third of a notebook for all my clues, and am a bit listless on what to do next. After discovering 100% of the truth, I now need to find another game to fill the void. Truly an excellent game, that I never felt was boring, dragging me along, or there was unbalance in the puzzles. 200/10, if I could remove this game from my brain and play it all again, I would.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely pretentious, but it's a game about insufferable artists, so it fits.  My only complaints about the game are that it is extremely dense and involves a ton of lateral thinking and there's nothing to point you in the right direction if you get lost and don't realize the mouse in the cupboard contained the clue you'd use atop the mountain. _childDocuments_.review: Incredible exploration puzzle game, if you're a fan of games like Obra Dinn, Golden Idol and Chants of Senaar I'd recommend this one. I spent hours in a fervour trying to unlock the entire house. I consumed all of the documents trying to understand what the hell was going on with the characters. The aesthetics are really great, I really like the black and white style overall, and the noir-inspired cutscenes. I love Nero's silly idioms. Descending deeper and deeper into the maze of mystery was super compelling. Puzzles range from easy to hard, and I felt like the game had a good balance between giving you hints and just letting you go at it based on stuff it's already taught you. Some of the puzzles I got genuinely stuck, and I enjoyed going away and thinking about it before coming back. Minor downsides were the clunky menu navigation (I understand the reasons why for accessibility but man was it tedious scrolling all the way to the back button). And sometimes, the black and white made the puzzle a bit harder than it should have been. This game consumed my life for the better part of a week. I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: What started with "Ohhh, I see." and the occasional "Eureka!" swiftly became a pile of 30 some-odd discarded sticky notes packed with scribbles and even an envelope for a bill I happened to have nearby. This game is an evolving masterpiece of an atmospheric thriller mixed with some of the best and most intuitive puzzles I've ever seen. The game is equal parts cinema, game, and art piece with its subject matter being much the same. It reads like a modern Hitchcock movie written by an A24 scriptwriter that did a few extra tabs of acid than normal, and the result is something unlike I've experienced prior. Let the game speak for itself and whisk you into the puzzle box of a Hotel where you're sure to encounter the spectacular, add a few wrinkles to your brain, and get lost in time. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: To briefly speak about the product, think , quite the minimal hand holding too, but more approachable than it may look despite the arcane look of it all, impeccable presentation and sound design too, and quite lengthy, it is great.To speak about the art, to speak about the game, and to speak about the maze, it will definitely take longer., to me, is the untarnished outcome of human expression, clean of any impurities and external factors, therefore,  is not only unfeasable, it is impossible, it is beyond our capabilities, since to be human is to be flawed.Then what is art that isnt ? every other kind, real art, fake art, good and bad art, art for yourself, for someone else or for no one at all, illustrations, theater, poems, literature, music, cinema, videogames of course, they are all our imperfect progeny.Describing games as  can be quite reductionist, its very effective to get people's attentions, the marketable side of it not only cannot be ignored, it has to be respected to a degree, but to say movies are pictures + music, while not completely incorrect, clearly misses the point.Lorelei and the laser eyes is about art, it is about the passion for the game, and it is about the passion for its players. It is a game about games, and about illustrations, theater, poems, literature, music, cinema, it is about recognizing patterns, and solving puzzles, it is about yesterday's news and about dreams in black and white.I will undoubtedly remember this maze, this shattered and scrambled work of both simogo as authors and its fictional characters, and its characters drive towards this unattainable .And that is as close to the  as we will ever get.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely one of the finest adventure games of recent years. The presentation reminds me of Killer7, with its abstract visuals and stylish graphics. _childDocuments_.review: Surreal and wild puzzle game. A hotel absolutely crammed with puzzles, where you pick at individual pieces and gradually open up more, which is very satisfying. _childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 5 hours in and having a lot of fun. I don't feel like I'm near the end either. There is a lot to explore, unlock, and unravel.  I have never made this many notes playing a game in a long long time.The game really does deserve all of the comparisons to Obra Dinn, Outer Wilds, and The Witness. I say that because it's that kind of game which is completely magic for the first playthrough especially, with different categories of puzzles to solve. It's very good at challenging you with enough variety that if you get stuck, you can go somewhere else and feel smart instead. It's not all one kind of puzzle either, the game introduces these different puzzles with satisfying "a-ha" moments. Some of these puzzles are spatial, some memory, some lightly mathematical (mostly just addition), many lateral thinking, and some staring at the same screen until it just clicks. The game also engages a sense of nostalgia for games like Resident Evil with the fixed camera positions and even some . The only downside to this is occasionally walking back to the previous screen by mistake.Aesthetically this game is pretty perfect too. No issues with hardware for me either.

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a mind-bending puzzle adventure that immerses you in a surreal world of illusions. Set in a mysterious European hotel, the game challenges you to solve cryptic riddles while navigating fragmented realities and uncovering the enigma of the laser eyes.The game's atmosphere is captivating, with each scene presented as a shifting monochrome tableau highlighted by splashes of red. Puzzles are dynamic, shifting in perspective and visual style to match their diverse types. The unsettling ambient music enhances the atmosphere, perfectly complementing the beautifully designed hotel—a maze of levels and rooms, mirrored worlds, and layers of locked secrets.One of the standout features of Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is its narrative. You play as Lorelei, summoned by an eccentric artist to a remote hotel in Central Europe. The story unfolds through fragmented notes, scripts, letters, and memories, creating an enigmatic and immersive experience. The storytelling is minimal but brilliant, with many narrative elements looping back into the central themes and puzzle solutions. As you progress, the initially opaque story becomes clearer, revealing the game's genius in building its central narrative through puzzles rather than exposition. It's exceptional work from Simogo.The puzzles in this game are excellent, requiring deduction and the referencing of previously found materials via your "Photographic Memory." Most puzzles boil down to pattern solving using basic arithmetic, roman numerals, Latin, zodiac signs, while testing your attention to detail. The hotel is rich with environmental clues, and you'll need to pay close attention to every detail. Repeating themes and number sets are woven into both the narrative and the puzzle solutions, creating a deeply interconnected experience. However, the relentless barrage of puzzles can be exhausting. Despite the minimal yet compelling narrative, the game sometimes feels like an endless puzzle gauntlet.Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a fantastic game, standing out as one of the best narrative puzzlers out there, destined to become a cult classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: If you can't tell by the name alone, this is a pretty weird game, I can't claim to understand what's going on so far, but I'm really enjoying the puzzles and aesthetics, and that alone is enough for me.If you like other Annapurna games, this is another great game from one of their teams, an indie team that definitely deserves the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: The most refreshing puzzle game I've played since . It was truly breathtaking seeing this game's tapestry unravel piece by piece. This game does a terrific job of building the narrative through the puzzle solutions too, and the final stretch of this game proves that. A couple of the shortcut puzzles were needlessly obtuse though, and they stuck out because the design for all the main puzzles was sublime.My main gripe with this game: THE CONTROL SCHEME. The 'one-button-does-everything' method is fine for controller-users, but why in a PC game do you not allow me to use my mouse to navigate menus or press buttons? Why can I not use my keyboard to input a string of of text or numbers? Why must I navigate 3 LAYERS DEEP into the menu just to see the map? The controls of his game very nearly ruined the entire experience for me as I felt like I was constantly fighting them. PLEASE AT LEAST ADD MOUSE SUPPORT.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER:  I have not finished the game. I have given up on trying to play it anymore because of 2 reasons: how tedious the game already is at the very start of the game, and how filled with filler "puzzles" it is, even at the very start of the game. TL;DR: In my opinion, the asking price does not fit a game that ultimately doesn't have enough interesting puzzles, nor a good enough plot line to keep anyone hooked, and it genuinely feels like the developer believes the intended audience are a bunch of idiotic monkeys.This is a weird experience.Basically, if you do like puzzles, not matter what form they take, and don't particularly care about the setting or story the game is trying to sell to you in the background, then go ahead and give this a try. Just be warned that a lot of what this game considers a puzzle is probably not what you're looking for, if your goal is to stimulate your mind with a problem that has a logical solution that you NEED to think through.As an example, there are, at the very start of the game, a lot of puzzles where the answer is quite literally on the screen, either literally hanging on the wall in the form of a picture, or inside a book. These puzzles also require you to do a small amount of basic math.And not a single one of these "puzzles" are fun. By far, my biggest complaint after 6 hours of playing is that way too many of these are filler for the sake of filler, so many damn doors are standing in your way for no reason other than to frustrate you, the player. I say "for no reason" because the solution to many (if not all) of these puzzles is inputting the same exact number over and over and over again but through different mechanisms. You want to open this box or that door? Figure out which buttons correspond to which number, and that's it.This all just feels like the developer is calling you an idiot. "Hey, the solution is right there! You have eyes, don't you?" Yes, I also have a working brain and nobody on this planet likes feeling belittled, even if that is not your intent. The moment your game is released to the public, Death of the Author applies all throughout, and while your intentions may play a part in how people ultimately feel about your product, but ultimately, you only ever get one first impression, and if it is a bad one, then that stain remains forever.It makes the experience feel like the developers decided to knowingly be needlessly tedious for no reason other than "because we can". Add onto this the fact that, despite it being The Year Of Our Lord 2024™ , we are only ever going to use a single button to interact with everything, which makes the experience infinitely worse because you, the player, do not have dedicated buttons to go back in menus or cancel whatever it is your doing, or only interact with specific things the way *almost every single other video game on the market has taught us is possible.*Now, I understand that there are those developers that have a very specific vision in their mind that they want to realize, and it can be incredibly artsy and pretentious and all that good stuff, and I do not have an issue with that... In principle. In practice however, I believe that developers need to realize that games need to be a compromise between the developer's vision and the act of actually playing the game, how easy and engaging it can be, etc.This developer has thrown out every convenience known to the game's industry to be as artsy as possible without managing to actually land on being interesting enough either in premise nor execution of any other mechanic.I will compare this to another game that requires knowledge to beat: Outer Wilds. In that game, the player isn't even given a tangible goal at the start, you simply explore a solar system at your own time, while being given an inciting incident that links to a mystery. The game is incredibly simple in all its mechanics and execution, and once the story is known, that is it, there is no more to do. But the entire game revolves around actually figuring out the specifics of this mystery, a constant loop of "I must find out why!". It manages to instill into the player an intrinsic motivator as the driving force, figuring out clue after clue, mystery after mystery. And it works perfectly!Comparatively, Lorelei gives the player a known goal pretty much at the start of the game, and then continues to hold the player's hand throughout so many puzzles, while leaving a bunch of them unexplained, because to solve them you'd need knowledge from later down the line. But every time the player reaches a new room and finds a good number of puzzles to be as brain-dead easy as possible, while others are nigh-incomprehensible for that moment, it just leads to a growing feeling of Ludo Narrative Dissonance (a fancy way of saying that what the game wants the player to feel is entirely at odds with what the player is actually feeling while playing the game). And the game only gets more frustrating as it drags on. Every single new room has at least one new puzzle, and when the choices for the solution are between the two extremes of "the solution is right in front of you, just squint a bit" and "makes no sense right now, come back in, say, 5 hours, after you've found more random books or memos with random pieces of information that may help", it just feels like a waste of time to play.So yeah, DO NOT BUY if what you're looking for is either a serviceable story with puzzle elements involved, or actual interesting puzzles to solve that require you to think at a level higher than "what's 2+2?" and a story you do not actually care about.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game in all detail it deserves to avoid spoilers (which'd really steal that pure joy of exploration) and schizophrenic vibe.So I just leave my blob of utter adoration here: it's so pleasurably stylish, very engaging for “just” a puzzle game, and with all that analog clock and rotary dial (which could possibly offend a whole bunch of zoomers, though).Imagine if Kentucky Route Zero, Signalis (ok, Silent Hill for our consolian friends), Twin Peaks and the most recent glamorous incarnation of Ripley had an orgy under an eyeroll from The Path.But wait, there's more: buying this one actually provides you with three more minigames (fierce and not that byte-seyesed) — it's the only opportunity to play at least some version of brilliant SPL-T for non-Apple users.The one and only real flaw of this one is obvious: no special “back” button makes all the manipulations more annoying than it's justified. Also, the ending (although very beautifully executed) is quite questionable,Trigger warning: focus-hungry, puzzlicious and coffee-propagating.All in all it's a wonderful family (or party) game to share (if your fam is into existential horror kinks).

_childDocuments_.review: Simogo released yet another wonderful game, this time being a puzzle game set in a mystery with a very artistic approach that Simogo is known for.
