_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei is a thematically artistic, trippy and atmospheric experience with some varied and clever puzzles. Considering how the game appears to be highly refined and carefully designed, I must conclude that its control and camera systems are a deliberate choice. They are meant to induce unease and claustrophobia, and are thematically apt in some situations. Having said that, I personally felt that the fixed camera angles, reminiscent of the very first Resident Evil and Silent Hill games, detract rather than enhance. Here, I must admit to my personal aversion for retro art styles and control schemes. They are best left to respectfully reign where they belong - in the past!The puzzles vary in difficulty, but where a couple of each type would suffice, there are a dozen. This inflated, fragmented puzzle count is often pointed out as a feature. While this statistic, along with the aforementioned control scheme definitely pads game play time, it dampens the impact of the interesting premise that is setup at the start. Towards the end I was scrambling to get to the conclusion, drawing no pleasure from what are supposed to be it's best puzzles. I am left wondering how much better this game may have been if it were half the length and the control scheme were differently implemented.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a brilliant game and teeters on being an unquestionable masterpiece. any complaints i have are extremely minor, and the game has stuck with me in the exact way Outer Wilds has. this is, in fact, the closest a game has gotten to that feeling Outer Wilds gave me. that said, this game is a more focused, personal story than a grandiose story on the scale of the universe. it was a great game that only ever has grown on me, and i am amazed at how often i reflect on the ideas and experiences of this game. rather than life and death, this game touches on art and creation. i absolutely adore it and highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I keep thinking about it, and when I'm not playing it, I want to be playing it. There are a couple things I would change - adding a back button to the controls and allowing the player to adjust the screenspace effect - but even without those changes I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it. A+++ will probably play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a puzzle box.Note that I didn't say that the gameplay is solving puzzle boxes (though it does involve that on occasion). This game unfolds like a puzzle box, one piece clicking open to reveal a new set of obstacles to work through, which then click together to open the next set. It's very satisfying, and even if you get stuck on one thing there's almost always *something* else to go work on.The atmosphere is spooky without being scary, if that makes sense. It made me jump a few times, but (with one exception) it was much more that I was honed in and my focus was broken rather than an intentional action on the game's part. I do have a few complaints - the entire game is five buttons (four directions and confirm), and this makes menuing a bit of a hassle. A B button to go along with the D-pad and A would have been nice, so that you could close out of a menu without going allllll the way back up to the X at the top of the page, or back out of a puzzle you don't know the solution to without having to input a blank answer. In addition, one midgame mechanic annoyed me a little - I'll be vague but will still place in spoiler bars. All in all, an excellent game, absolutely dripping with atmosphere, and actually interesting and satisfying puzzles (less common in games than they used to be). Highly recommended for escape room fans.Pen and paper, a calculator, and a camera/screenshots strongly advised.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a big fan of Simogo ever since Device 6 on iPhone. Unique innovative and memorable gameplay has always been the core of what they provide. And Lorelei continues the trend.I'm nearly finished with the game at this point. I've been playing with my girlfriend, and we both have our own perspective on certain puzzles, and remembering certain details, which has helped make things easier, to a point. The game still has frustrating parts, where we don't know how to proceed. Sometimes, you need to take a step back and re-evaluate what information you currently have and what you are looking for, and how to reconceptualize the information in a different light.The story within the game, and the story the story is telling, seems a bit pretentious, but I think that is intentional? But where does the "story" and the story differentiate? Whose eyes are we looking through? All-in-all, I strongly recommend this game for any puzzle fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well designed atmosphere meets intelligently created puzzles. The level design is built beautifully. Getting stuck on a puzzle leads you to focus elsewhere. Before you know it, your solutions cascade into each other; a domino effect has never been so satisfying. The Hotel feels like REmake's mansion, down to the trails of paint, locked doors, and cryptic puzzles. The references feel like a tasteful homage rather than overt references. The notes provide great background information about the surrounding characters in this mystery and dangles just enough to get the imagination going. Although, the SH2 influence can be seen, the ending could stand to learn some lessons from it.   All in all, pick this game up if you like puzzles or taking extensive paper notes. FIXED CAMERA ANGLES ARE BACK WITH A VENGEANCE, BAYBEE.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I just hit a brick wall with this game where I realised I wasn't having fun any more (For reference I got to about 70% completion).This game emulates many older videogame styles, from puzzle design to controls to movement. And personally I think it suffers for that*The puzzles*As you explore more of the environment you unlock more and more information, and find more "puzzles" where those pieces of information will be useful. Unfortunately, you will quickly reach a critical mass of having a huge amount of info and a wide variety of puzzles to solveEarly on this is fine. Later on, any single piece of information in your entire backlog of documents could be used for any puzzle. This creates an exponential issue, where if you've come back to this game after a few days, reminding yourself of everything is going to take hoursSome puzzles can be solved just by looking at them. Some require you to come back literally a dozen hours later, making this issue even more noticeableSome system to mark information as having been "used" to solve a puzzle would solve this. As it stood, I fell into a rhythm of looking through all the puzzles, all my info, solving what I could, and resorting to google or steam forums when I get stuck for more than an hour with zero progressI should point out however that there is no "Moon logic" here. Every puzzle solution genuinely requires you to understand it and I praise thatHowever if you fail to understand a single puzzle, there is no way to progress except to stare at it for hours or google. And with google right there, players are going to use it. Gone are the days where the barrier to entry was buying a cheat guide from your local game store, and so this level of potential frustration just isn't a good idea any moreThis style of puzzle system will appeal to some, and I think those people are those who miss old-school puzzle games. Alas, I am not one of those people*Controls*Very janky, and I think deliberately so. In some sections that I won't spoil, this is done clearly on purpose. But there is essentially only one button in this game, which I have yet to see anybody praise. It's fiddly and annoying and I hate it, making an already inherently frustrating experience nearly unbearable*Visuals and vibe*This is where the game shines, and is the reason I kept playing for as long as I did. The story has plenty of mystique, and the characters are charismatic despite being mostly confined to text and a few cutscenes. They say a lot with a few words and I am very here for itIt's striking and cool and intense and these aspects of the game I love, and wish I could have enjoyed its conclusion. But it wasn't enough to keep me going after so many trips to google*Conclusion*I think this game is a warning that it may be wise to take a "Best of", rather than copying everything from the past. If we could have had just a few quality of life features in there, this would be a game that a lot more people could enjoyAs it is, this is a game for hardcore puzzle purists who are willing to suffer through its tortuous lack of playability, and for nobody else. I find it extremely hard to recommend, and so my review must be negative
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A deeply compelling experience, a must play for puzzle/mystery game fans. The puzzle design here is excellent, a great mix smaller, straightforward logic/number puzzles and larger, overarching puzzles comprising symbols and information found throughout the game. It's also really successful as a mystery game, and the thrill of discovery when the pieces start to come together is reminiscent of Outer Wilds and its ilk. There are horror elements as well, and though they are relatively tame, I found them extremely effective.What sticks with me the most after completion though is the narrative and themes. This is one of the few games I would genuinely describe as Lynchian. Various characters that are described or interacted with seem interlinked, perhaps as fragments of a single person's identity. Stories within the story can cross over with the "real" reality your character occupies. There is the sense that you could be in an experience unmoored from the linear flow of time, perhaps a dream state or a simulation. Or maybe it is a concrete reality, with illusory elements overlaid atop a solid foundation of verifiable truth? In the end I felt the game provided just enough answers to reach a very satisfying conclusion, while leaving enough unexplained to keep me contemplating its mysteries long after the credits rolled. Unforgettable.Fantastic soundtrack too!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phenomenal game. I'm a puzzle enthusiast, especially with respect to Myst-like games. While this game doesn't quite scratch that itch, it does fill its own niche without comparison. The game scaffolds puzzles in complexity and interactivity all while successfully maintaining an engaging story throughout. The game never veers too far into obscurity, making puzzle solutions near impossible, while still keeping them challenging. Just a fantastic game all-around, second only to the Riven remake for my GOTY (2024).
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unbelievably good.12-20 hours of dense, fair, rewarding puzzles, plus a fantastic atmosphere, story, and sound design to boot. The payoff to the  puzzle solidified this as a game that I will be benchmarking other puzzle games against for years to come. I truly do hope the devs address serious accessibility concerns, but anyone who is skeptical of trying this game for fears of an 'inconvenient' or 'confusing' control scheme, I urge you to push through. Do what the game tells you to do. Read everything, internalize it, take physical written notes in the real world. The photographic memory is one of the greatest additions to a puzzle game like this in recent memory, but you don't need to navigate the menus at all if you have everything you need on your notepad in front of you. The Steam Guides put out, even this early, are *great* at providing hints and nudges without telling you exactly what you need to do for every puzzle. No shame in peaking at those! You're likely overthinking the parts you're stuck on anyway.A piece of art exists in itself and for itself, but you should experience this game. It's a piece of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: thought this was a neat puzzle game but turns out you can just die and lose a bunch of progress (in fairness they do say that but wow do they mean it) - menus, ui, and movement are slow and clunky so that was the straw that broke the camels back and i gave up after that, good ideas wrapped in bad execution sadly
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: ( This game requires you to be involved with the story and its setting to fully be fully completed and understood. It contains many text documents that expand the worldbuilding in relevant ways to understand the plot and solve the final puzzles. If you don't like reading, and theorizing about what you've just read, DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME. For its and your sake.)Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a beautiful essay on the nature of art and its relationship with artist, audience and capital in the format of a puzzle adventure thriller. It presents itself in a gorgeous black, white and crimson package, reminiscent of noir cinema, which perfectly complements its themes and plot. And it will absolutely  every last ounce of attention your mind can offer it. In the best of ways.While I was playing, I didn't have a single moment to be bored; there were always puzzles to solve, documents to read, theories to ruminate on... and even while I wasn't playing, thoughts about the Man with a Gun and the Woman with Laser Eyes plagued my mind in the most unexpected of moments. That's one of the best parts of Lorelei and the Laser Eyes. It'll never leave you hanging, without a thread to follow... if you know where to find that thread.One thing I have to agree in with my brethren in the negative side of the reviews is the controls. Made to be played with one hand, writing notes with the other, you can play the game with just WASD and Space, or the Arrow Keys and Enter. Which sure, doesn't make a great difference while walking through the map, but... can truly make menuing and puzzle-solving tedious, especially with the lack of a "Back" button. But otherwise... this game might just be contender to GOTY, if seen by the right eyes and spoken of by the right mouths.Truly recommended if you're a fan of narratively-driven puzzle adventures, especially the most old-school of the lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not like the Witness - which in my opinion is the puzzle GOAT. Progression through this game is dependent on solving simple math problems via clues found in the environment. The Witness taught the player a coherent and evolving logic language unique to that game world; this game teaches you to walk around, slowly, while looking for numbers to plug into easy math problems. Reminds me of escape rooms. The controls are unacceptably terrible as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most brilliant puzzle games I've ever played. Your brain will activate neurons that have been long dead in order to complete some of the stuff in this game. The presentation is great, especially later in the game with the bug reports, quiz club and everything. The game starts slow, I actually played a couple hours on release and then lost interest for a few months. There should have been something more to hook you in the start, most of the cool stuff comes later. And a few of the puzzles are almost impossible to solve with the hints provided. Also a search function in the "photographic memory" would have been hugely helpful but maybe too much. Often you will get stuck because you know what to look for but not which of the 1000 documents it's located in and you will sit there and flip through documents, missing what you're looking for due to just the volume of text.But those issues aren't that big in the whole picture. Very good game for puzzle enjoyers. It's been a while since I actually had to take notes for a game and not feel like an ret*rd doing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Obtuse puzzle design, a vague and uninteresting story, and agonizing controls make for a unique but overall infuriating experience. I hate to put down what is realistically a very well made game but I found myself annoyed more times than I did really enjoying most of anything. Maybe its because my brain just doesn't operate like a normal person's or maybe its because most of the puzzles expect you to have access to some kind of mental rubric I just don't have.The photographic memory thing is cool in idea, but in practice, its a cluttered network of letters, posters, and other documents that the game expects you to remember every last detail even though it all starts to melt together by the halfway mark.I didn't hate all of my time in this game. Some of it is really well put together, but the constant need for slow-walk backtracking and remembering why 1947 is important to Side Character Number 3 gets old very quickly.6/10 - Maybe I'm just stupid, idk.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I don't like 'escape room' games where you find codes to unlock boxes to get keys to unlock doors etc. This one is something else. It's stylish and smart. The puzzles start very easy, but soon ramp up in difficulty.If you have to play one game about solving logic puzzles, this is the one.(also the UI is fine, grow up, your fingers won't fall off from pressing up a few times)
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Some interesting people with completion rates of under 18 hours. Lets be honest, they've just used a walkthrough... much like the people those twitch players who just happen to know everything - it's rigged trash. What's the point in playing this type of game if you're just going to use a walkthrough? So ignore trying to beat their times - they're not real, just trash people. So what's good about this game? It's fantastic > logical puzzles that make sense, and I've got a huge excel spreadsheet and enough screen shots to sink a battleship right now, but I'm genuinely loving it. This is some of the best puzzles I've seen in a game for year - genuine brain ticklers that make you think and when you get them a real "A-ha!" moment. I've not felt cheated once by a puzzle while playing and only once was stuck enough to refer to a walkthrough - which was clever enough to give hints not full on spoilers - had a real "oh" moment and on my way I went.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I would've played this so called "masterpiece" more, if there wasn't one tiny problem. This game doesn't have any concept of a "cancel" button nor it has any way of controls remapping, so in order to quit any kind of menu you should navigate to the corresponding element every time you interact with anyting - this includes status menu, notes menu, savegame menu and all the interactable objects that obviously are found a lot in this kind of game. In order to quit the status menu you should navigate to the "cross" menu element and press the "action" button, but if you're interacting with a clock puzzle you should navigate to what? Any ideas?At first I thought that this was some problem with the keyboard controls and the game is meant to be played with a controller, but when I switched to gamepad I couldn't believe what I saw - all of the buttons (A, B, X, Y, LB/RB, LT/RT, Back/Start) were mapped to one single action, that is some ridiculous sh##. It's not like the developer had no buttons to choose from, it's like they didn't even care. This one "action" button tends to perform all of the actions in game - if the character is standing in front of some interactable object, the "action" button will trigger it, if there's none - the "action" button will open the status menu. What have prevented the dev from assigning separate buttons to different actions the way it's done in other similar games? This games mostly copies other games like Silent Hill but fails to implement such primitive systems they had implemented in their days way better. I have no intentions to encourage such a lazy work in this important part of the game, for this only this is a negative review.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: remarkably crafted puzzles with an impeccable atmosphere and deeply cryptic yet engaging story. i've been playing through this one together with some friends and it has forged a bond between us the likes of which are only comparable to those that are forged in war. there is truly no bonding experience like sitting in a call together for hours scribbling notes about cardinal directions while you're all trying to figure out how to add words and translate numbers. i'm never going to be able to look at the numbers 1847 1963 or 2014 without getting traumatic flashbacks to the many long nights i've spent meticulously combing through miscellaneous documents trying to figure out what the hell i'm supposed to be doing. if you enjoy puzzle games you'll adore this one but if you're less experienced with the genre you may want to consider easing your way in with some gentler titles before coming back to it (and you should definitely come back to it). sincerely can't recommend this game enough to anyone who loves the feeling of uncovering a good story little by little in the way an archaeologist slowly pieces together ancient history. this game made me realize im stupid
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A good puzzle game with fixed camera reminiscent of early Resident Evil with creepy atmosphere. At times it can feel a bit aimless. There was a point where you're supposed to input several puzzles at once with no telling which one is incorrect, which felt frustrating. I think I felt the most enthusiastic about it in the middle, the start and end felt like bit of a wet fart.Finally I want to talk about the controls - they are infuriating! There is one action button which is bound to EVERY KEY, which performs a contextual action. Then there is Escape to open the menu. There is no back button, no map button, no using keyboard to input letters. Navigating menu involves you pressing a button to go through all the many documents both to access them and to exit back to the game. Puzzles cannot be exited directly, only by inputting a wrong combination. With padlock puzzles, accidentally going past the number you wanted to select means going the long way again. In some menus, the menu loops, in some it doesn't. In some menus, holding an arrow key keeps the cursor going, in some it doesn't.Striving for accessibility only to make the game more tedious to operate for everyone does not seem like the way to go, guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks game for deleting 3 hours of my progress. Seriously expected more from you.Sure you can say the game warned about 'lost time'in a game full of cryptic references and multiple eras and times. The devs can simply get bent. I don't think I have ever been so out-rightly infuriated by such objectively terrible design.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I always like to say that Annapurna never misses, I'm so happy that they haven't dropped the ball with this one, Lorelei and The Laser Eyes was a great surprise to me, I didn't know what to expect at first but few minutes after playing I knew that this game was special, not only because of the "seeded" puzzles, making it more fun to replay, making it every playthrough a different experience, but because it took me back to a time when you had to rely on things of the real world to play, took me back to when I had to write down answers in games, Zelda Puzzles, GTA Cheat Codes, etc. Lorelei and The Laser Eyes sometimes feel just like an interface for the real game happening in your notebook, that's such a great feeling. Loved it!Another thing that I have to say is that, as a puzzle game, Lorelei is one of the best there is, very similar in a way to Tunic or Outer Wilds, where your knowledge is what prevents you from moving forward, Puzzle Games like that you don't see very often. The puzzles are not necessarily hard, but they challenge you to think without making you feel very dumb. Lorelei is the best mix of puzzle box and escape room and for that, one of the best games I played in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a mystery, but it is just a stylish puzzle game.It feels like the devs don't respect their players :- open ended puzzle games gated by items have the issue that when confronted with puzzles you can't solve yet you have no way of knowing that (and the hint system that could have helped is useless)- latter half is clearly rushed and asks for a lot of backtracking (Quiz Club is the summum of unfun).- no skip/forward button for cutscenes/animations replaying (Quiz Club again...)- the controls feel very clunky with only one button to navigate menu- unnecessary bladder/coffee management to move slightly faster- no special thanks "You, the player"... it is petty, yes. but for such a small team, it is telling a lot about their mentality.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really like this at first, but my wife did, so we kept playing. It's engaging enough to keep me playing, and I like playing puzzle adventure games together, but I don't think this holds a candle to Myst, the Outer Wilds or The Witness. It definitely doesn't feel as cohesive as other games in the genre, because the puzzles feel arbitrary -- puzzles for the sake of puzzles -- rather than being deeply tied into the world and the story. But overall it was still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really disappointed with this game. I saw the rating, and was prepared for a great puzzle game. In my opinion, this is not a great game. I wouldn't call it bad, it has a soul and distinct style, I just think the approach to puzzles and game design is what I would call cheap.In general i'm a big fan of puzzle games and Outer Wilds is one of my favorite games. And I was so excited to start, having pencil and paper ready.But I would say fairly quickly, I lost that excitement.There is a big problem with the game introducing too much to the player.For some puzzles there are rules that the game introduce to the player, that I think the game itself breaks, which leads to a bad experience. And there are some puzzles, which I would describe as just straight up badly designed, or poorly thought out.A bad puzzle in a puzzle game is much different from for instance a bad boss fight in a action game. In a action game, you had a few lousy minutes, but then you move on. But in a puzzle game, if you can't solve a puzzle, you are stuck, and you need to look for help. And if the solution to the puzzle is not logical, you lose faith in the game. That's why it's very important that a game like this has no poorly designed puzzles, and that the game itself is very strict with the rules it introduces.I lost faith a lot in this game, that is why I leave a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: The controls are awful the the puzzles are way too obscure to care. I doubt I will finish this game. I am so done with it! It expects you to notice details like an upside down 6 under a mans armpit in order to determine the password to a computer is arm. I made that up but it feels too similar to the ♥♥♥♥ this game asks for.To reiterate, the controls use a thumb stick and one button. All I ask for is a back button! DON'T MAKE ME MANUALLY GO BACKWARDS! It is such a pain and makes me not want to view the manual notes cause it is such a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ way to view them.Skip this game if you do not want to wander around for far too long looking at puzzles you can't yet complete because you walked away from another thinking you did not have the answers.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I get the feeling that despite my intense hatred of this game, Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is operating 100% according to the developer’s intended vision. It is supposed to be this hard, this frustrating, this stagnating. You’re never supposed to feel like you’re actually progressing. You are intended to spend hours on a single puzzle just trying to figure out how to give the game the solution. I am certain there is a very small group of people out there, maybe folks who compete in competitive jigsaw puzzle tournaments, who will find Lorelei and the Laser Eyes to be their favorite game of all time. I also do not think many humans out there will be able to complete it without help from a guide. If you have played through The Witness or The Talos Principle and thought “I wish I could get a version of this that would make Albert Einstein sweat,” purchase Lorelei and the Laser Eyes immediately. If you are anyone else, please trust me, your time is better spent elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't used a pen and a notebook to solve puzzles in a game in decades, but Lorelei and the Laser Eyes got me back in the habit. A fair amount of my playtime for this game is from me having it paused while sketching out clues and putting together connections on the paper in front of me.It's been so long since a game came along and challenged me with puzzles that managed to creep up just to the edge of frustration for me, but never felt unfair... (okay there's ONE puzzle that's just rude, but only one is fewer than many good puzzle games out there)And the STYLE in this game... the atmosphere generated was just exceptional. _childDocuments_.review: So peak. You don't need to use a single thing outside the game to solve it, just be sure to check libraries and your notebook thoroughly. Some documents have multiple pages. Having a pencil+paper on the side is also a pretty fun way to visualise and solve puzzles. Not necessary but it leaves a really fun set of cryptic scribbles after you complete the game.Don't want to spoil anything but the story and presentation are 10/10. Go in blind and crack some codes.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah this is 100% my type of game. Think Resident Evil / Silent Hill vibes, but instead of surviving against enemies you are trying to figure out all the puzzles and lore that tie the place together. This is a game where once you figure out a rule, suddenly you get on a roll before you hit your next roadblock. Its satisfying to see the solutions to all these puzzles come to mind, and that if you had been paying attention you could have  figured them all out from the start.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei is a visually striking and challenging puzzle game. I liked how the seamless the world of the game was to explore with clues scattered throughout. It was thrilling to finally find a clue pertaining to a puzzle that I had discovered several hours earlier. As the game progresses it becomes harder to track all these things (the game even recommends using handwritten notes) to the detriment and I will admit to looking up a few puzzles towards the middle of the game when I felt overloaded with information but ultimately the intriguing narrative was enough to keep me engaged and eager to unravel the mysteries within.If you're into escape rooms or puzzles with exciting narratives attached, I'd recommend checking this one out
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I somehow forgot to review this game when I finished it, but the game has been on my mind ever since. It was very satisfying to solve puzzle after puzzle, seeing how each one led to the next, like falling dominoes or a rube goldberg machine of puzzles. The story was extremely unique, kept me on my toes, and left a lasting impression by the end. The specially made notebook was very useful and makes for great keepsake of the game. I also love the addition of randomized puzzles for each playthrough; it adds some replayability and supports the theme of jumbled, fading memories.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: So while the following will contain quite a bit of critique: yes, this is a very good game and it is highly recommended. The art style is exceptional, the writing is really good, the story is engaging, and the game is just oozing atmosphere.That being said, there's some conflict between gameplay and narrative here. One of the main themes of this game is a maze. Mazes are great from a narrative perspective: they portray confusion, loneliness, being lost, the question of choice. However, as a gameplay mechanic, they are purely annoying. There's is no cleverness involved in solving a maze. To be fair: you get a map of the maze right at the beginning, but switching to it is quite annoying. So in the end, I just made a screenshot of the maze and put the game in windowed mode...As a puzzler, the game is also not that great, because it is too easy. The puzzles feel complicated at the beginning because you are immediately confronted with a lot of puzzles you simply do not have the necessary information for. In some extreme examples, you are confronted with a puzzle right at the start which you'll eventually solve when you've done about 80% of the game. That however is not being made clear at all, so I often spend a considerable amount of time looking for clues in the room or in my "photographic memory" for puzzles which you simply cannot solve yet. In the end, I felt a bit cheated that these puzzles are actually obvious once you got the necessary information.Also, this game could have been considerable improved with some simple changes to the interface. As already mentioned, quickly switching to a map from your memory would greatly reduce the annoyance of the maze. Likewise, that you cannot quickly exit out of puzzles with simply pressing escape or similar is also annoying.Again: I still highly recommend this game, but as a puzzler, it is a bit lacking.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: "Before I go, I'll see it all through laser eyes."Back on May 9th, I purchased Animal Well the very second it dropped and had a blast playing it to completion accomplishing it's true ending in about 30 hrs. Fresh off the heels of this victory, I decided to purchase Lorelei and the Laser Eyes because of the good albeit small amount of press it was receiving. However, due to overall puzzle fatigue (if you've played Animal Well, you understand) I fell off of it after about 5 hrs, but with a plan to return eventually. Well that time is NOW and I must say I am very glad I did.Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is an atmospheric, "survival-horror-esque" (quotations are important there), third person escape room puzzle game where you control a mysterious woman visiting a hotel in search of answers. I've never experienced such a since of discovery from a video since I played Outer Wilds back in 2023. The atmosphere, the music, the imagery, the cryptic story, they all come together in such a strange way that ended up leaving a strong impression on me, but let's keep things concise.Firstly, I want to touch on the gameplay because I want to avoid spoilers and it's one of the sections I have the most to say. To preface, it is advertised that the player should play this game with a Pen and Paper in tow to jot down any notes, thoughts, iconography or anything in between. I don't believe I would have enjoyed this experience as much if this idea wasn't brought to fruition. The feeling of scouring your own notes in real-time (and in my case attempting to decipher my handwriting) made me feel like a real detective attempting to uncover some long lost case, and the moments where I would remember something and frantically rip through my pages trying to make connections... wow, no game has challenged me in such a way. Outer Wilds comes close with it's in game computer, but having to actually engage with it outside of the game world was immaculate. It's design like this that makes me adore video games as a medium, and remember their unique place in the world.However, I must also talk about another aspect of gameplay, SPOILER this is my main critique with the game and I'll just get it out of the way now. Um, the controls in this game are not good. If you aren't aware, as per the in-game Instruction Booklet, "When pressing any button near an interactable object or another character, the player character will be able to interact and take contextual action in different ways." Sounds fancy, right? Let me tell you they aren't kidding about this quote by the way. Every face button, interacts. Every Trigger/Bumper, interacts. Every stick, moves the character. Every directional input, moves the character. Both menu buttons open the pause menu. The glaring issue is that there is not differentiating any of the buttons. Since all four face buttons act as the "interaction button" there is no "back" button. You will very quickly need to adapt to navigating to the exit button to leave menus, otherwise you will just open up something else in said menu. Same goes for the puzzles, however, in this case the puzzles do not have exit buttons, you need to attempt the puzzle in it's entirety to leave the puzzle. Sometimes, it's harmless, other times it borders on plain tedious. It kind of boggles the mind that this design was intentional but I digress, it didn't ruin my experience. I bring it up because I can definitely imagine this being someone's straw that broke the camel's back because these puzzles are NOT... easy.Moving on from that dissertation of despair, let me get back to glazing this thing. The overall feeling this game evokes out of you is also immaculate. This is NOT a horror game, but I'd be lying if I said I felt 100% safe at all times. The ways things are said, the way the environment exists around you, the SOUNDS things make, it can all be a bit... unnerving don'tcha think? I remember having to take a step away from the old computer box because the sound of a window shattering had my stress at an all time high. These feelings are further exuberated by the Survival Horror esque camera design. The camera does not follow the player character at a fixed angle, but rather cutting between points as you arrive at different points of interest, very akin to classic Resident Evil games, which just drills even deeper feelings of dread into your subconscious. Going to bed after finishing this game was an oddly terrifying experience.Lastly, the narrative on display in this game was my personal highlight. I had a bit of a unique experience because I never restarted the game after taking 6 MONTHS??! Wow time flies. Sorry. I never restarted the game after taking my hiatus from it so basically my memories from that first experience were foggy which I was aware of. This lead to misremembering key information, and also trying extra hard to keep track of things. This lead to arriving at theories that I was very strongly opinionated about and was ever so wrong about. Regardless, I enjoyed this because I was very closely entwined with the story, paying attention to every single detail, jotting down thoughts whenever new information revealed itself, it was a very immersive experience. Couple that with the atmosphere and you've a damn good game on your hands. I won't talk about specifics of the story but the overall design of it was very mesmerizing for me. The parallels, symbolism, and entangling of time lead to a web that was an overall treat to experience and de tangle.Overall, Lorelei and the Laser Eyes was some "gas" as the cool kids like to call it nowadays, and it has arrived in my higher echelon of puzzle games. Greatest appreciations Simogo, ya'll are rad.Ab Imo Pectore,Quidam Guido online
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game.  Every puzzle can be solved with information that is in the game.  Some are quite challenging and require a few layers to solve.  Was able to complete the game without looking up any hints or walkthroughs.Menus are a little tedious at times.  There is a lot of information to digest.  Some of view points, perspectives and navigations can be quite tricky.If you are into puzzle games and are not freaked by mild horror this one is definitely worth a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute gem of a puzzle game with such a distinctly magical feeling.You will overthink the puzzles and kick yourself you solve them, it is one of the only puzzle games where being tired will actually help. Story is incredibly esoteric at first and builds to a satisfying, emotional, and cohesive payout. Sound is very subdued at first and builds as you play and explore the game. Controls are super simple, slightly annoying at first but quickly forgotten. Go in blind, you deserve to discover this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Extraordinary experience. When it's flowing, it is a deeply nourishing puzzle experience. Considering how much of the game is number puzzles and combination locks, that's saying a lot. The lack of a back button is inscrutable and annoying to the very end (because you'll be opening the menus a LOT) and puzzle difficulty bounces around dramatically, but the rest is so good it becomes a petty complaint. A lot of love went into every detail and it shows, each creative choice performed with absolute confidence. The world, writing, and presentation are full of that "weird but with hidden meaning" type of storytelling that make me feel dumb for needing a plot guide after finishing since many parts are up to interpretation, but that I'm so glad that people are willing to run the risk of creating to push the artform.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good narrative/ puzzle game. It is pretty much pure puzzles but in a very interesting narrative framework. It is an excellent game and genuinely worth the price. It is probably closer to outer wilds in the sense of solving little puzzles to get the big puzzle solved and with narrative playing a large part of the puzzles. It does have a mix though- some puzzles are pure maths/logic and detached from the narrative altogether.The game has good twists or moments where the stakes change, and the vibes and art style is top notch. Definitely has very strong themes throughout the game too rather than purely solving a mystery.I really think you should buy it if you like puzzle games/detective games. If you liked outer wilds, blue prince, case of the golden idol, obra dinn then this is a vey similar sort of game though substantially different in its own ways. Personally I really do not have any substantial criticisms, its a really addictive 20 hour game. Strong recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Just 100% completed the game about 5 minutes ago.Holy. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. ♥♥♥♥.I was NOT expecting that story. This game is an absolute masterpiece in storytelling and atmosphere. Also, the puzzles in this game felt so satisfying to do fully blind without any help; I got stuck on I think two of them, but you will eventually have an epiphany and be able to solve every puzzle in this game.In all, it is well worth it's price. I would have paid $60 for it, it is just THAT good.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Soft recommend. While I love the setting, especially the witty comparison between "Last Year at Marienbad" and Resident Evil's camera angles, there's a reason we set aside obtuse puzzle design like this, and even by the standards of old-school puzzle games, the overall momentum needed to solve the game doesn't really cohere until pretty late in the whole thing. Fun if you're a nostalgic puzzle fan, great atmosphere, could be a lot better as a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up a  while ago off an indie recommendation video, and honestly? I was kinda bored with it at first. It felt like I was being given information about things that were run of the mill for this style of game, just to be given a puzzle that was "1963 but backwards". So, I dropped it for several months until I got my new SSD installed, and was batch downloading games from my list.A week or so later, I'm in a quiet, late night call with some close friends, and figured I'd just put it on in the background to entertain us.What I did not figure was a  as I got absorbed into the ACTUAL puzzles and mysteries behind the game.Without spoiling too much, Lorelei does an incredible job of making the experience of discovering the solutions really satisfying. They start simple; small detours, a keypad with an obvious hint, etc., before diving into the deep end with solutions that get so creative towards the end of the game, it makes the quantum physics in Outer Wilds feels like putting the triangle into the square hole. You don't even get to consider thinking outside the box because they already took it away and used it for fire kindling hours ago. There were even a couple of puzzles that admittedly, I would never have figured out as quickly if I didn't have a few friends watching me play and giving me theories.That being said, the ending segment dies down in complexity compared to the actual Resident Evil 2 style blackbox that makes up the bulk of the game. However, this actually winds up being a good thing in my eyes. I like flexing my brain but after , I'm more than happy to just put the triangle block where it belongs.As an additional side note, the aesthetic and art direction of the game is just a VIBE. It has absolutely... NO colors, save for the same shade of pinkish red used in several places. A lot of the texturing is also done with these arts-and-crafts picture overlays that look just... cool.In terms of actual "complaints" and things to keep an eye out for as a potential buyer, this is a pen-and-paper  game. The notepad app will not help, and I don't care how good your mouse drawing is, no art program is going to help you visualize things the way you need it to. Lorelei gives you an in-game record of all the notes and signs you read, but I still had the notebook open on my desk the  playthrough, constantly flipping back and forth between pages to connect information I found hours ago with information I found minutes ago to solve the puzzle I found NOW.It also has a somewhat redundant system related to coffee. You eventually unlock the ability to use espresso machines at various places around the hotel. They give you a temporary (key word here) ability to run when moving in the same direction for a while, but you only get to use it three times before you have to use the singular bathroom in the basement to empty your bladder. Frankly, as nice as the speed was from time to time, I think I'd rather just not have it at all at that point.If you can make the time and patience to sit down and genuinely engage with the game as it presents itself, Lorelei will show you an experience that can only be described as art. Which makes sense, because as far as I'm aware, that's what the entire design philosophy was. Bring the trusty red string and thumbtacks, turn out the lights, maybe bring a meal to the computer with you, and enjoy a truly transcendental piece of media.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Where do I even start with this one. It's incredible. It might even be perfect. I just finished it a few minutes ago and I'm still sitting with it, but it's clearly a masterpiece. A heavy focus on incredibly clever puzzles, resident evil style map and exploration, and a surreal, spooky vibe that pushes against the boundaries of genres and the video game medium itself. It's a beautiful puzzle and a carefully crafted mystery.This is a game you need to play with a notebook and a pen in front of you. I have at least a dozen pages of crazed notes that are only comprehensible to me. But the design and pacing of all the puzzles are really wonderful, and the whole game builds towards a beautiful finale that will stick with you long after finishing the game. A blend of cinema, video games, and art that isn't quite like anything you've ever experienced before in any of those mediums.If you play one game in 2024, let it be this one. It's as close to perfect as any game I've ever played!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I have awful sense of direction so my playtime isn't representative of how long it'll take you to finish the game. With that out of the way....One of those puzzle games that makes you feel jolly good about yourself for working out all the solutions. Sometimes, all you need to work something out is a new frame of mind, seeing it in a new way, than trying to brute force it with other information. In a way it's sort of  perfect information, there are some bits you need to know that the game will tell you if you look, but some of the solutions simply require you to observe and think. At first, I thought some of the solutions were put in slightly the wrong place, but once I worked out how they came together it really blew my mind, some of the game is so well planned that even going back to look at some of the other clues gives you such fresh perspectives and information.I'm not sure how to interpret the story still, but the story that is told concretely to you is extremely compelling and emotional. Deeply enjoyable, starkly stylish, elegant, unencumbered and highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: If you are searching for a mysterious travel with puzzles in an old RE style gameplay, this game will have you covered.Artistically the game is beautiful from it's story, to it's visuals, it's music and it's puzzles. This game is beautifully crafted in every aspect and will keep you busy for a lot of time looking for details and opening paths as the story is really interesting.It's been a while since I played a game like this one and even though I'm losing my hair with it's puzzles, I want more of them.This game is made for the OCD people... Come in with the puzzles, hmph! come in with the puzzles, hmph! come in with the puzzles, HMPH! COME IN WITH THE PUZZLES!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Never has a game made me oscillate so much between "I'm a moron" and "I'm a genius!" Incredibly challenging but, as a puzzle lover, deeply rewarding to compensate. _childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend for anyone who enjoys puzzles and dark stories. The gameplay and atmosphere are amazing, and the puzzles are very well thought out. While there were one or two puzzles I didn't like, most of them are great. They complement each other well and reward attentive players. The entire hotel feels like a beautifully designed puzzle box that slowly unfolds. Even though progress can feel extremely slow at times, the constant flow of puzzles makes it incredibly rewarding.The only drawback is the story—I’m not a fan of run-of-the-mill psychological horror, and this game leans heavily into that - you can see it from the very beginning!But yeah, overall it’s one of the best games I’ve ever played

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding, another best-in-class effort from Simogo. Not for everyone, but what is? If you want a tough but extremely fair puzzle game, an entire escape-hotel rather than a simple escape-room - this is for you. Fans of Obra Dinn or Golden Idol will find this right up their street. Everyone else, at least go play Sayonara Wild Hearts to at least see what the studio can do in a completely different genre
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is one of 2024's best adventure games, and one that I'd easily recommend to those who are keen on number and logic puzzles.The story and setting are shrouded in mystery and relishing in a nostalgic, horror-ish theme. Your character was supposed to meet someone at a hotel, but the hotel lies abandoned. Something terrible has happened here, and you have to get to the bottom of it. Doing so involves navigating every inch of the hotel and beyond, gathering clues and solving puzzles to open doors to new clues and more puzzles, interspersed with glimpses of the central mystery.The whole thing is intricately layered and punctuated with fun or disturbing story events. It's a testament to the developer, Simogo, that the game remains challenging but fair throughout, and I always felt like I was making progress even when I couldn't make any sense of the puzzle eight rooms earlier. Overall, it's a rare gem among these kinds of games. Think Professor Layton with more a focused plot and puzzles, or Flower Sun Rain with much less walking. Easy thumbs up from me (but only if you like number puzzles).
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is an intriguing mystery puzzle game where every element aligns perfectly with the dark and enigmatic atmosphere. The game weaves together suspense and mystery, drawing players into a world filled with cryptic clues and surreal visuals.Each puzzle feels thoughtfully crafted, encouraging players to engage their intuition and deduction skills. The fragmented narrative keeps you on edge, with every new discovery hinting at deeper layers of the story waiting to be uncovered. The game’s visual style—evoking film noir aesthetics with its stark contrasts and striking use of red—adds to the tension and gives a sense of timelessness to the experience.I highly recommend Lorelei and the Laser Eyes to fans of puzzle games and mystery. It’s a challenging, immersive experience that rewards patience and curiosity, and it stands out as a unique entry in the indie game scene.

_childDocuments_.review: Device 6 is quite possibly my favorite game for mobile devices, ever. So although I'd heard good things about this game previously, it wasn't until I saw a trailer that mentioned that Simogo had also made Device 6 that I really got excited.Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is not a sequel to Device 6. Without getting into spoilers, I don't think either game could meaningfully have a sequel; they said what they needed to say and then finished speaking. But the style, writing quality, awareness of medium, and commitment to execution of a very specific context make it feel like a spiritual successor in the best way.This game is committed to the bit that it is a work from an older era, from its monochrome color scheme to its manual saves to its Resident Evil-style cameras, but it plays with this narrative conceit constantly in a way that's very satisfying. I haven't watched enough experimental European cinema to tell how spot on the portrayal was, but I have read some Calvino and I got Calvino vibes.It's definitely the kind of game I can't imagine without pencil and paper (I recommend lined or grid rather than blank paper), because you will be taking notes constantly. That isn't to say the game won't keep track of things for you--it keeps track of almost every image and document you come across, one anachronism I'm grateful for. But all the solutions are your job as the player. Most of the puzzles felt fair, though I did come across a few that felt like the "you get it or you don't" kind, which is always a little disappointing.The game is very even-handed in how it approaches the central mystery, though. I can't speak for other players as to what should or shouldn't be considered a twist, but there was nothing about the narrative that felt unearned or out of the blue. The proverbial skeletons in the closet all have tells.The ending wasn't exactly what I expected, but it was appropriate, meaningful, and stuck the landing. More of a lateral move from what I was imagining rather than better or worse.That said, my gripes:The controls leave something to be desired. They're very simple... so simple, in fact, that the complexity typically handled by controls is shifted to other parts of the interface, often without adequate explanation. For example, I became temporarily stuck when I first interacted with a padlock I didn't know the combination to, because there's no back button or dedicated enter button. Turns out the intended behavior is you interact with the bar of the padlock.There are also a few segments where the control scheme is differently mapped across the same buttons. Most of the game maps directions relative to the camera, so up / down / left / right is upstage / downstage / stage left / stage right. But other segments map it differently in ways that can be disorientating. The way my playthrough went, I had to switch between normal gameplay and two different sections with different controls back to back, which was disorienting and made normal gameplay harder to execute. Perhaps this was done for narrative reasons or to explore a certain theme, but I disliked it heavily.I also want to warn anyone who might have photosensitivity or visual issues. There are sections with large chromatic aberrations, choppy low-res animation, warping and subtly moving environment textures, and, worst for me, several sequences involving a small, bright flickering effect on the player character and full-screen jitter. I think the devs' intent with the jitter/flicker was something like "cool glitchy effect," but I have an eye disability that typically isn't an issue in puzzle games, and this effect directly interfered with my ability to focus my eyes on the screen and understand what I was looking at. I don't think any of the effects are bad enough to provoke a seizure (though IANAD), but there's no way to reduce them or turn them off. So make informed decisions.Overall, this is a really cool, ambitious game and I'm glad I played it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: CONTENT WARNING: MATH.If you're in the middle of the Venn diagram of people who love puzzle games but hate maths, I would caution against this game; certainly a number of the early game and optional puzzles which unlock shortcuts will require understanding of geometry and basic algebra.Personally, I kinda enjoy maths so this didn't put me off at all, but felt it was so prominent in the game that it was worth front loading the review for those who it may concern.This game is kind of like a grown up Professor Layton with a much more creepy tone and a narrative connecting all the puzzles. As a result, the puzzles generally take place in the context of the game world in the form of entering codes into keypads or padlocks and sometimes more complex mechanisms.As for modern games, it is comparable to games like Obra Dinn and and Chants of Sennaar insomuch as a core element of the puzzling is trying to connect a much larger picture. It's almost metroidvania-y in a way, where you will encounter puzzles you have no idea how to solve, only to return to them later with the knowledge (or tools) to pass them with ease.Another core element of this game is remembering stuff you saw/read one time maybe 10 hours ago and recalling it as relevant seemingly out of no where to solve a puzzle in the mid or endgame. The game *does* provide a complete log of every text document (book, letter, poster, menu, etc) you read throughout the game permanently accessible in the inventory menu, but honestly that doesn't help much when you read the relevant thing 3-4 days ago in real time and had zero idea of its relevance at the time to even know that's what you're meant to be going back through your notes for this time. And yes, this still impacts the game even if you take non-stop IRL notes on paper which I did.This was the weakest and most frustrating part of the game for me (and I'm not saying too much here as to not spoil the particular part which caught me), but there was a super relevant word mentioned one time in a really early game document that I had not committed to memory that ended up becoming a hard-blocker for me progressing in the game (other than the shortcut doors, there is almost nothing at all optional - you MUST solve EVERY puzzle to progress to the end) and after hours I gave up and I looked it up online and had an "OH, THAT!" moment which kind of took the wind out of my sails to be honest.Of course in a game like this YMMV wildly, so even someone fresh off completing the game could read this and have no idea what I'm talking about. I suppose what each of our brains randomly decide to retain will be inherently unique to us, but this was the only time it happened to me in the entire game so soured what was an otherwise thoroughly satisfying puzzling adventure. The final puzzle at the end was also really cleverly put together; requiring you to summon from your brain/notes three sequences of "passwords" which you could only possibly know if you'd solved essentially every part of the game correctly up until this point. And honestly "really cleverly put together" could describe the game as a whole. Overall, an incredibly well constructed puzzle story game and I will definitely be keeping my laser eyes on what Simogo does next!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. The vast majority of the puzzles are very well weighted in terms of difficult - I suspect everyone will have a couple of absolute head scratchers but you never get bogged down as there are some many paths. The vibes are magnificent too - great setting, backdrop and intriguing story. Some great mini games hidden away too!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this fever dream of a game is good. Remember the feeling you had playing "Year Walk"? Prepare for that but much, much longer and more confusing and magical. Amazing things:1. The style. This is a piece of art. Both visually and with respect to the story. It's dark and haunting, yet weirdly realistic, due to all the details added into the descriptions of items to flesh out the background for the story.2. The puzzles. They are never hard, and most often the answer to a puzzle is neither too far from the puzzle nor requires many steps. But they are a little bit... surreal? Like the story itself. I relied on intuition more than trying to construct one true solution, and it usually worked.3. Controls. I absolutely love minimalist controls, even though occasionally you have to flip through a few menu items to get where you're supposed to be. But you can play with one hand.4. The EXACTLY CORRECT amount of help. The game saves all important images for you, and lists all the tasks you have to do, but never too early, and never in a too specific way. This is honestly a massive help, because even with the map the hotel is huge, and I would have had to keep a list of everything unsolved. P.S. You do still need pen and paper.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent dark puzzle mysteryI picked this up on a whim because I love a good puzzle mystery, and the vibe felt very Halloween-appropriate. It sucked me in more than expected though. The strongest single point I can make is that all of this game's design choices and systems work together to immerse you in the world it weaves. I saw a recommendation somewhere that name-checked "The 7th Guest" and that feels appropriate.Some other assorted things I liked:+ Lovely aesthetic / art style+ Good pacing on the unfolding mystery+ Great variety of puzzle style and difficulty+ Using an actual notebook outside the game to solve puzzles felt weirdly satisfyingAnd a few things I didn't:- The commitment to a single action button felt counterproductive (a "back" button would have made many parts of the game much smoother)- Some of the control scheme changes were awkward to navigate- The "run" mechanic felt pretty clunky in both introduction and executionIn some spots I genuinely couldn't tell if the game was trying to _be_ modern art or poke fun at it. But it worked for me either way.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply one of the best games I’ve ever played; this sits alongside the likes of Submachine, Obduction and Riven in my personal favourites list. I almost missed out because Steam said `This game doesn't look like other things you've played in the past’. Really??? I love this type of game – a brilliantly imagined, weird world, a coherent story, visual style and music, great puzzles that are challenging but never the kind that require a degree in maths. I really appreciated the `photographic memory’ and the `mental notes’, which helped to avoid the endless backtracking that turns too many games into a chore. I was hooked, wanted to succeed but didn’t want it to end. I hope this is up for awards because it certainly gets my vote.

_childDocuments_.review: This was recommended to me by a YouTuber (who primarily plays Adventure games and Metroidvanias) who declared this her GOTY for 2024. While it is indeed very well made, it's also very frustrating and very narrow in appeal. Unlike certain other big name recent releases, this is a true "return to form" and is the best traditional Adventure game I've played in a long time. However, the puzzles get more and more complex, weaving puzzles inside of puzzles, that eventually you'll have to complete almost every puzzle just to finish it. Highly recommended for point-and-click fans but even my non-Zoomer brain hurt while trying to finish it, even with outside help.Almost all of the puzzles are logical and thought-provoking, avoiding the 80-00s tropes of arbitrary "use a balloon and string to restart a generator" types of absurd puzzles. They range from "find the missing number" to algebra equations; while it starts out simple enough, providing an open-ended mansion to traverse full of seemingly optional puzzles, the pieces eventually all come together for the finale. The problem is just trying to figure out which square piece fits into that final square hole... You will eventually need a guide just to figure out where you're supposed to go next, never mind how difficult the equations get.Using a guide isn't really cheating because there is so much randomization that you'll almost always have different problems and answers than other players who played through it. The biggest hurdle is trying to find out the logic of the puzzle and how to navigate it with the knowledge and tools that you have. On one hand, this is excellent for replay value or playing through with friends, but on the other hand your notebook will be useless on repeat playthroughs outside of possibly helping you remember the structure of a puzzle.This is unironically the Dark Souls of traditional Adventure games. The 5000 pieces of this cinematic puzzle eventually make sense, but you'll definitely need help along the way. Lorelei would've greatly benefited from some kind of hint system; I would've loved to see a multi-step hint system, akin to what other players and game guides offered along the way: one free hint per puzzle, a second one that consumed some kind of resource, and a third hint that possibly locked you out of achievements related to that puzzle. It's a very well made game but by the end I was genuinely fatigued by it. While it's not my personal GOTY, I still really appreciate the amount of love and care that went into it. Recommended if you have the patience and IQ to solve what is probably the most challenging game this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes
