_childDocuments_.review: This is most likely my game of the year. Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is an exclusive member of the prestigious indie-puzzler club that’s currently occupied by games like The Outer Wilds, Return of the Obra Dinn, and Tunic, in that it beautifully blends complex puzzles, knowledge-based progression, curiosity driven exploration, stylistic panache, and a non-linear mysterious plot to make an incredibly immersive and memorable experience. Seriously, I started this game two days ago and it consumed me from the moment I got going (to the dismay of my wife who wanted to watch movies this weekend). It also scratches a very specific itch for me in that the vibes feel heavily influenced by Suda51 games like Killer7. I'm surprised I haven't seen that comparison more often as that niche crowd would *love* this.I think the less that’s said, the better, as this game is best experienced blind. But I will say that it’s rare for a game to have me taking so many notes. Throughout the entirety of the game I had a notepad with me that I scrawled on, and by the end I had 10 full pages of cryptic solutions that I was constantly flipping back and forth between as I continued to unearth patterns. So suffice to say, I believe this game will resonate the most with players who are willing to take their time with pen and paper. But wow! What an experience!!! Games like this are what I’m always hoping to find and it’s so delightful when catch me by surprise. I knew it was a puzzle game, I just didn’t know it was going to be THE puzzle game, you know?
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: When I started the game I didn't know I would love it so much. Beginning was a bit difficult because I couldn't figure out what the game wanted from me, but that went over pretty quickly. Puzzle solving felt very satisfying and logical. Never so difficult that I had to look it up, but still challenging. So much so, that I actually got out my old notebook and made pages full of notes.Apart from the puzzles you get an interesting story, beautiful musical pieces, and  well.The only downside is that there is no "back" button in the menu, you always have to navigate to the "X" to close it. It's not a big enough issue to lessen the fun, but why?
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, cool atmosphere, solid puzzles, chill music, incredibly frustrating menuing. Wait. So the game isn't perfect, the longer it goes on the worse it starts to get. You have more documents which means more searching through stuff for answers if you took breaks in between and don't remember what has what. As things get more complicated it becomes harder to tell if you just haven't worked it out or if you are missing the correct item/document needed to solve it. As an example there is a clock with symbols on it very early on, but I couldn't fully solve it till I was about 80% done, then there is a piano puzzle too which I thought I would need something to translate what was there but the solution is actually in the area from the get go. The game also lacks a hint system of any form, if you get stuck at a puzzle (the damn piano) thats that. Either you eventually work it out, or you have to look up a hint/answer which is always sad. There is even a call for advice, but as far as I could tell it was always nonsense. Just a slight hint towards something that could be completed with the items/info I had would have made things way better. The menus are extremely clunky and annoying (my fingers hurt how many time I had to spam buttons to get around) and the achievements are also really bad, there are a bunch you get for 100%ing the game, great love it. Then you have to get an annoyingly high score on the little mini games you get   and then the ever frustrating speed run, with much of the game randomising each playthrough (though not in a way that makes it fun to replay right after you finish) Lastly while I could see where the story was likely headed early on, I wasn't a fan of the ending. The game is still going up as one of my favourite puzzlers of all time, but these few things really bring it down. 8/10 game, 9/10 if they fix the menu garbage (yes it can be that bad) 7/10 for all achievements, making me replay a game that has no true differences is always a sin.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ what a Phenomenal game. Puzzles were engaging, and wonderfully challenging while managing to never frustrate me. The worst it got was me stopping for the night when I couldn't immediately think of a way forward, just to figure it out a bit later. The story was amazing. Interesting, and wonderful, and tragic, and I love it to bitsHighly Highly Highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This one got me fairly obsessed. Had to bing 20 hours over 4 days.It may very well be the best puzzle game I've ever played.Staging, design, and atmosphere above all are exceptional. The scenario and storytelling are masterpieces.Subtle audio made me appreciate every single moment of music even more.Puzzles are preety hard, had to look up a few of them to get to the end of it.Might not go for 100% as its mostly collectables. Solid 10/10.Thanks for the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game.  A lot of repetition of theme without repetition of mechanics helps make it feel like a total experience rather than a series of separate puzzles.  Often you'll see the same answers without them being the same solutions, driving you to think about the meanings of these repeating patterns.  Very cool game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. I haven't had my brain melted like this since The Outer Wilds. This game is HARD. And you will probably have to bang your head against the wall more than a few times, but solving the puzzles in this game is just so rewarding. In addition to the puzzles, the overall vibe, art, music, intrigue of the whole thing is just really addictive and makes for a game that draws you in.I don't think this game is for everyone and I get the UI navigation complaints (I adapted after the first hour), but if you are looking for a new challenge inside a stylish world, pick this up. It's right up there with some of the best puzzle games around.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most captivating, bizarre, and challenging puzzle games I've ever played. The plot is completely off-the-wall in an amazing way. It kept me hooked enough to play for like 6 hours straight - which is good, because this game involves a lot of memorization, and it's easy to forget what the heck you were doing when booting up the game again.The game invites you to keep a pencil and paper on hand, and they really mean that - though you might only use them towards the end. Your character has a photographic memory, so everything you see and every task you need to complete can be referenced from the menu. It is a godsend, and it is in fact a very necessary feature, because there are seriously more than 100 puzzles, with difficulty ranging from instantly solvable to borderline sadistic. But all of them are ultimately FAIR, and they feel incredible to get right. I'm amazed at the amount of puzzle variation they were able to fit in here.I admittedly caved in and resorted to internet help for 3 of the puzzles, but I am genuinely pleased I was able to keep it that low. Some of them are just plain hard. If you have a friend who has played this game, and you find yourself stuck - ASK A FRIEND FOR HELP FIRST. Don't jump right to a guide. Anyone who has beaten this game (with enough recency) should be able to nudge you towards answers without outright spewing them at you. Clicking open a lock with your own wits always feels better than being given a skeleton key.Anything else I could say would just be general praise of the writing, art design, music - all of which are a perfect match to the setting they've created, but are better experienced than read in a review. The last puzzle game to give me satisfaction like this was Outer Wilds, which was also published by Annapurna. The entire staff of Annapurna resigned amidst bureaucratic in-fighting like the week before I finished this game, and that feels like a huge loss to puzzle game lovers and the gaming industry in general. A+ work by Simogo here.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best puzzle games I've ever played. Incredibly well crafted, with so many surprises to be uncovered. Loved the visuals, EASILY the best soundtrack in a game this year. There's plenty of meat on the bone but never overstays its welcome. My only real complaint is that the UX feels like it was lifted directly from a phone game. Navigating through menus is clunkier than it needs to be. That would be a nitpick if you weren't using the menus so often. Regardless, a fantastic game and as of right now, my game of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A great puzzle game with a neat art style and a few rough edges.I really enjoyed LATLE. Its puzzles strike a good balance between being intuitive and abstruse enough to be challenging. There were only a few instances where a solution made me groan which is a genuine achievement relative to many other games in this genre. The art style is really appealing and I also appreciate that the game has a fairly compact install size and runs extremely well. I liked but didn’t love the level design, which is interesting enough but doesn’t quite establish the same level of identity as the mansion from resident evil 1 which I assume was a significant influence. I also liked the fact that most music was diegetic and could be toggled via various record players. However the fact that music is localized to rooms made this less impactful than it could have been which was a bit of a shame.This game employs a one button gimmick which is at best unobtrusive and at worst very grating. Without a dedicated back or map button, tasks which should take a few inputs  might take 10+ depending on context. I also found movement to be a little clunky; rather than a typical “glide and slide” approach to collisions, your character stops dead when you contact a wall, making near misses of doorways a lot less natural to recover from. This is a pretty minor problem since movement isn’t the focus of this game, but it is a frequent annoyance.  There are also a few areas where the control scheme shifts from camera relative to tank controls and the implementation feels honestly terrible. I found this probably deliberate clunkiness kind of endearing for some reason though so I didn’t really mind.Aside from mechanical complaints, there is one sequence which involves answering tons of trivia questions which is extremely and uncharacteristically boring. Given how solid most of the other puzzles are I’m not sure what they were thinking. There are also a few puzzles which act as significant bottlenecks if you miss them, either due to them functioning non deterministically or blocking progress on other puzzles. I don’t see this as necessarily a big design problem, just something which made the pacing slightly less good on my play through personally. I definitely recommend this to anyone who enjoys puzzle games or games with unusual presentation.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I finished this game for the first time.At first, I was drawn to the Noir retro art direction. The control was bit of weird, but I had quickly got used to it. I was expecting some mind-boggling puzzles, and I got what I want. Even though the game feels too much, the art style and side quests are interesting enough to make me managed to unravel the foreshadowing and secret little by little. My personal favorite puzzles are the piano puzzle, the music is beautiful and worth to play on loops.Pink maze(third person), Art pieces are really hard but very enjoyable. I wish there's DLC  for an alternative ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unmistakably unique and very dense. It’s about art, creation, passion, madness. It’s fantastic and can be read in many different ways, both literally and symbolically. It gives you something to think about. The mood is also superb, this mixture of vintage with high concept art, occult and even retro cyberpunk.I also liked that puzzles require lateral thinking. You need to join information from distinct sources and be creative in noticing and interpreting patterns.What I didn’t like is kind of baked into the formula - it is easy to get stuck, even one single puzzle can make you unable to finish the game. (Fortunately, walkthroughs are available). 95% of puzzles are great, the remaining 5% somewhat soured my taste at the end, but I guess this is somewhat subjective. Let me complain a little:- One item is hidden in a screen you have no reason to expect even exists, I mean .- One puzzle I didn’t get because of the atrocious font .- One puzzle I actually did solve myself, but the answer was so stupid I felt like it didn’t count, - Some of the optional door puzzles feel like they operate on rather obtuse logic.- One puzzle got me confused because I was actually too good at seeing patterns, Overall not a big deal, the rest of the game more than makes up for that. I've never played a game which as a whole would feel so much like a maze.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil, but the zombies are replaced with more puzzles. Challenging, but remarkably fair compared to the vast majority of other puzzle games I've experienced. Your resources are within the game, clearly marked, and intriguing to follow. Even as someone that gets frustrated easily and tends to look up guides, this one is rather fun to figure out without relying on ciphers or ARGs or 'gotchas', making it a strong recommendation for anyone wanting to wrinkle their brain but hates pulling their hair.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzling and beautiful. Hard to recommend to most people. The story is obscure and hazy, only revealing itself slowly, through obscure riddles.The art direction is impeccable, with a style unique and daring that seeps through every aspect of the game. The main gameplay is exploration and puzzle solving. Remembering where things are and figuring out which information is required, which puzzle can be attempted is part of the fun and quite interesting. I'm not a fan of the 1-button control, I don't think it adds anything to the game, and having a dedicated "examine" and "inventory" button would be nice, navigating the inventory and coming out of it is slightly frustrating. Not much but over the whole play through it never gets smoother.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, I was surprised by some of its ideas and how they change by the end of the game. I'm going to go the other way than most reviews and say there isn't really a problem with puzzle difficulty in this game. Actually, perhaps the main issue with this game is how tied to progression that information is. This is certainly by design, but it means there are multiple examples of the following: you get a seemingly open-ended puzzle that shows elements from information you already gathered. You try to solve it, maybe for an hour or more, and then you finally give up and go try to progress in a different path. Much later, you receive new information and realize that the puzzle was *never* solvable until you learned this, and the information you first received is basically just a codex to apply this new information to the puzzle. That's my main issue with Lorelei. If something is not explicitly called out by the game as optional, and you don't know how to solve it almost immediately, the safe and optimal thing to do is just walk away from it and do something easier. I wonder if many reviews talking about the puzzle difficulty never realized that what they were trying to solve had its only solution gatekept by a separate nesting doll series of more straightforward puzzles. If you keep this in mind when playing the game then I think you will have a smooth experience. Puzzles that don't need currently unavailable information generally get their difficulty from requiring spatial thinking.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely do recommend, game is an 8.5 lean 9 from me.Moderate to lower high difficulty puzzles that all made sense, consistent themes and presentation throughout, great satisfaction when a clue you picked up hours earlier all of sudden clicks because you understand the game's rules.I don't have any major complaints about the main story and execution, the game lost a point just because there's a handful of nitpicks that stacked up. The music was largely unremarkable, the side content was shallow and going the extra mile to complete it didn't have a substantial payoff, the art was a bit too simple repetitive, and the story was simple and not really that interesting in hindsight (the big dopamine hit came from the solving puzzles and revisiting complex puzzles later). Completely acceptable for a game of this budget and scale, just the annoyances combined docked a point.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: It was a fun game with challenging puzzles. All was going well until I forgot to save for some time, Maze Man appeared and it wasn't possible to save near the computer! I failed, got game over, deinstall. Please respect people's time and add possibility to save at any moment.Right now it's 3/5. With reliable saves I would give it 5/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a gaming masterpiece. Historians will study this game as a lesson in game design. This game is basically a giant IQ test. Not for the faint of heart. Reminiscent of Monkey Island games (specifically reminded me of Grim Fandango, especially with some stylelized sections with intentional awkward control, likely a nod to Grim Fandango), but it is mostly an IQ puzzle game (unlike Monkey Island games). You will need a pen and paper for this game.The fixed camera angles make for a cinematic masterpiece. Reminiscent of Squaresoft's late 90's games. I wish more modern games "dared" to do fixed camera angles. It's always amusing how much better games looked back then when developers were more constrained. I'm so tired of boring third party chase cam games that all look the same. So this was extremely refreshing.The overall style and graphics are also a masterpiece. Everything was done so right.Puzzles ranged from trivial to head-scratching, but so very rewarding once solved. The story is also surprisingly good, with a great ending that actually felt rewarding. The game is also much longer than expected, especially at the end. Whenever I thought it would end, another puzzle was in the way.Loved that my reward for solving puzzles in this game was (most of the time) more puzzles.The only annoying thing about this game is the achievements. Some of them force you to play the minigames, which I do not like. And one achievement is a speed run achievement. Because of this I didn't bother 100% the achievements. But don't let that stop you from enjoying this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this was good. I think the critical praise plus "overwhelmingly positive" overhypes it a bit. But, it's evocative and the difficulty is just right. Give it a little bit to get going. Many of the puzzles (and almost all of the early ones) are very standard "escape room" logic, but they get more creative as it goes on. The game has a system for record keeping that tracks the information that you find, although you almost certainly will also want / need pen and paper for multiple solutions. It also has a couple of systems (maps, "mental notes") for tracking unsolved problems, which can be very helpful. (However, there is one critical puzzle that doesn't show up on this system. I was blocked here for a while, and reading comments after I finished, it appears to be a common place to get stuck.)
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: It was close for me, it really was, but this game has Return of the Obra Dinn beat as far as I'm concerned.This is THE Puzzle Interactive Media Experience of..... well, I was going to write the decade but, the decade isn't over, and it's still selling it short. The Crew at Simogo is back and with a bang. Their previous title Sayonara Wild Hearts ranks as one of the best presented and scored games of all time for me and Lorelei and the Laser Eyes delivers on that front as well, all the while being one of the most well-thought-out and clever pieces of interactive media that I ever had the pleasure of experiencing. It is THAT good, full stop.This isn't a Review, it is simply a wholehearted recommendation of this game. If you have any passing interests in puzzles, mysteries or math, this game is going to be your Game of the Year.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is like if you took the Resident Evil mansion, took out all the creatures and replaced them with more puzzles, an eccentric, possibly gay director (?) and a maze made of lasers.Despite its title, your eyes aren't portals to a dimension where only giant lasers exist and just glow slightly sometimes. I wrote a letter complaining about this only to receive an intricate puzzle box that, when opened, was just goatse.In terms of story: don't worry about it. You don't need to know about how the game is a meta-commentary on modern art, you only need a basic understanding of key characters and dates.The game does a wonderful job of having supplementary information for people who don't know alchemy or roman numerals.Overall I'd rate it in a very obtuse and artsy way.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic puzzle game with brilliant atmosphere and a mind-bending mystery at the center of its story.I think the most notable aspect of this game is its puzzle design and pacing. The game unfolds beautifully, a maze of lock-and-key puzzles that develop more layers the deeper you get in. Some of the puzzles might be a bit obscure or obtuse, but there are always other ones to switch to and focus on while you let them marinate, and much of the game's environment finds ways to encourage you to be focused, attentive, curious and also to think outside of the box, helping you put yourself in the mindset necessary to find that lateral twist that turns a puzzle into a solution. As a result, this game managed to manufacture the most genuine 'ah-ha!' moments for me of any adventure puzzle experience I have played in recent memory.Putting it more concretely, I got 22 hours of delight out of this game. Out of all of that, I only felt honestly stuck twice, both near to the end of the experience, and neither for very long. There was exactly one puzzle that caused me genuine frustration. I had to kind of brute force it, narrowing down to a handful of possibilities and then trying all of them until i got the right one. There were two puzzles that successfully tricked me and I had to back-track to understand how I had gotten the answer wrong, and both felt satisfying rather than annoying when i realized how I had been tricked into giving a wrong answer. There was only one puzzle I needed to look up the answer to, and it was an optional puzzle that I looked up after finishing the game because it was the only thing left between me and 100% completion - and even with that puzzle, I looked up a hint, not an answer, and the hint got me to the answer in a way that still felt pretty good. In between each of those moments, my main experience of the game was a continual sense of forward progression, slowly and pleasantly following a bunch of different threads out of order until they all started to come together. The atmosphere, story and aesthetic of the game did also agree with me very strongly. The limited color pallet, magical realism, meta-fictional framing, and non-linear storytelling are all things I personally really like. The story and the way it was presented were really interesting to me, and struck me as having an elegant combination of complexity and simplicity that complimented the puzzle gameplay quite nicely. Even if that isn't your cup of tea, though, I do think that the puzzles in this game are some of the best, and that the way they are presented is stylish and charming.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this game is a must-play for any fans of logic puzzles, mysteries, and compulsively reading every little bit of information the game gives you. It's solidly constructed and completely solvable within the game - no outside knowledge needed. Once I started I was hooked (except for a brief break right at the end when I got frustrated with the final puzzle (it turns out I had just mistyped something))Some random notes:- This is not a horror game. While there's some supernatural spookiness (and I don't want to give too much away about that), the game is much more about the mystery than the horror. Nothing is really scary.- There are a few places where you can suffer an instant game over, but they're clearly telegraphed. So save often. If you're paying attention and at least skimming the various documents the game gives you, you should be fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Rare instance of a puzzle game that made me feel hopelessly stuck, yet unwilling to look up solutions. Lovely cascading solutions towards the latter half, culminating in a gimmick-free comprehension test. Would've found 100% of the truth if I hadn't ignored the guide and spent all my American dollars on a gachapon machine. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying this so far (25% in). Lots of fun puzzles, plenty of nice lateral thinking stuff, nothing's felt obnoxiously hard so far and I've had a lot of great "oh that's for THAT puzzle!" moments so far where I got really excited as I discovered something new. Very *weird* game so far aesthetically and story-wise, is maybe the one caveat. Hasn't bothered me but might bother others.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A very special game, the narrative remains fairly vague and obscure yet is intriguing throughout. The puzzles, which definitely are a main focus, are varied, with a nice progression and I'd say a light-medium challenge overall (if you like that sort of game). Usually they are quite logical and rewarding (so you can feel smart, without ever getting stuck for long). I personally enjoyed it immensely, so would definitely recommend. To the negatives: a drawback are the controls, which are a bit cumbersome when not playing with a controller (no mouse, just navigate via arrows/enter for input). There is also no inbuilt hint system, which is understandable but might have been useful for some players - all unsolved puzzles are kept as a list and get crossed off one by one, but there may be instances where it isn't clear what the game wants you to do next, leading to frustration.There's no save-anywhere-feature, which I as a busy person would have preferred, but save systems (save  at certain locations that are spread out over the mansion) is servicable.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a wonderful gem of artistry, design, and craftsmanship, possible only in the format of a game. It's one of those experiences that solidifies games as the intrinsic art form that it is while being wholly aware of its role in 'art,' whatever that means. A joy to play, to listen to, to experience, to complete. I felt like a genius at times, an idiot at others, but I was always enthralled and motivated to keep going, finding solutions to puzzles while taking a shower or going on a walk, the game nearly always being on my mind. It's going to be strange not having to mull over some of the games mysteries or puzzles now that it's finished, but something tells me I am going to be thinking of Lorelei and the Laser Eyes for many years to come
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: If you're at all into mystery/puzzle games, this is a game you probably want to play.The atmosphere is impeccable, from music to visuals to vibe. The puzzles are never too spicy and just tricky enough to feel satisfying to solve. The overarching mystery works really well, and you're given more than enough hints to figure things out yourself before the actual reveals.Overall an excellent game, bravo, signores, signoras and signorinas of the development team. You produced a great piece of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Another amazing game by Simogo! A truly mind-boggling (quite literally) but yet somewhat easy experience. This is what I love about puzzle games. Most puzzle games gets you to think a little bit with a somewhat obvious solution at the end. This one makes you write many things down, realise not everything's important then scrap it whilst finding out the answer you hold is not relevant until later parts of the game. And it doesn't help you at all in the current parts.Also, just want to thanks Jonathan Eng, Daniel Olsen and Linnea Olsson for your beautiful ingame soundtrack. It compliments the game really well and adds a lot of depth to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: 很奇幻的後設+解謎元素不建議中文很像自動翻譯甚至句子被吃掉--------------------------------------I think this is a philosophical game that explores observation and creation.“Given the nature of spiders, webs are inevitable. And given the nature of human beings, so are religions. Spiders can't help making fly-traps, and men can't help making symbols. That's what the human brain is there for - the turn the chaos of given experience into a set of manageable symbols.”―Aldous HuxleyIt illustrates the author's journey of pursuing self-transcendence through creation, only to realize that we can only exist within the experiences we create, and that we can only observe our experiences through self-reference (1982: which is more true—the reality around us, or the one on our screens? & 1932: we must observe the observer, too). Without self-observation, we do not exist.Conversely, , creation must be observed and distinguished (1957: Can white exist without black?) in order to exist.Similarly, the entire game, as the author’s creation, lacks the consciousness to observe itself. It is through the numerous observers—i.e., the players(laser eyes)—that its reality is reflected (1953: Who would you be, and where would you stand, if you were on TV?).Of course, my review, just like this game, cannot escape my own experiences. It can only reflect how I observe, experience, perceive, and understand the game. Likewise, my re-creation of this review, based on my understanding of the game, can only be reflected through the understanding of other players.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Design: Delightfully Non-Linear, multiple methods of progression are available at almost all times.Atmosphere: Creepy and intriguing, brings to mind Resident Evil 1 (to extreme degrees at times)Puzzles: Clever and intuitive, often-times the solution is in front of your face, though that makes the relatively few times where you cannot proceed without additional information stick out.Can you pet the dog?: Yes.  And you should.Update/Edit:Having now finished the game and confirmed that the ending is wonderful, I will list the only two nitpicks I had with this title for the sake of completeness.  Neither of these are deal breakers and I'd still recommend this whole-heartedly, but they are minor pain points nonetheless.1. There are certain documents you can pick up that are multiple pages, indicated by an arrow on the side of the screen suggesting you can turn the page.  However, for whatever reason (perhaps the way the game darkens at the edges for a cinematic vignette effect) these arrows can be hard to see.  Twice during my playthrough of this game I looked for some additional documents or books I hadn't found yet, thinking I didn't have information to solve something, when in reality I just didn't realize a document I had found had multiple pages.2. There was a point in this game where I didn't have all the information necessary to complete a series of end-game challenges because I had overlooked clicking on a source of information in a place I'd already been.  Searching the game from top to bottom to just find something I didn't click on was not a great time: perhaps a reward for doing the optional map puzzles could be highlighting un-interacted with items on various floors?
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This was honestly a fantastic experience from start to finish. This game was a fantastic brain teaser and looked great while doing it. I'll likely be thinking on various elements of the story that was told for the next couple months. Also since a good chunk of the puzzles are semi randomized from what I've been told I can do it again in a couple months if I'm so inclined. Also, just a tip, but definitely use a notebook or something while you play. Improves the experience by a ton.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my first ever Steam review but wow, this game is a masterpiece. If you love games that challenge your mind, this is for you.One of the best games I have played in a long long time, I can't recommend it enough. Whilst this game likely won't get the mainstream media attention it deserves, the developers should be proud.So often these days, games forget about the content side of things but this game hits the spot for practically every criteria you could want/need in this genre of gaming.I look forward to whatever this studio produces in the future. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Killer7 x MENSAThe puzzles were great and if you like puzzles it's worth the price. Cool to see how many times the same set of dates and names can be worked into puzzles. The maze sections were tedious. Did get stuck at a couple of points because I missed things in the environment, and without looking it up probably would have been stuck for hours. Doesn't need a hint system but maybe some way to ask if you have all the information required to complete a puzzle would be a good way to handle getting stuck. Story was okay. Mysterious but it gets laid out for you in the end which I appreciate. The conclusion was a bit underwhelming. Good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite games of the year so far! I very much like manors filled with unique and genuinely varied puzzles and secrets, and this is exactly what this game provides! I definitely got stuck a fair few times, but when I did it was almost always my fault for not figuring something out, rather than the game being overly obscure. Overall, I deffo reccomend it to any fans of escape room style games! ^w^

_childDocuments_.review: Believe the hype ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥I didn't pay this game any mind at first because Sayonara Wild Hearts is not my type of game whatsoever, but that was a mistake. _childDocuments_.review: How we view the art we make will never be the same as those who consume it. There’s no possible way to account for how every person will respond to something you make, so how do you convey something so great that it goes beyond those internal contextual barriers? Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is single-handedly one of the greatest video game experiences I have had in this genre and ranks highly among everything else i’ve seen in this medium of art. Please do yourself a favor and just buy this game, and go in as blind as possible. You will not regret it. Congratulations to the team at Annapurna Interactive, you have made something truly special that I wish I could wake up and experience for the first time again and again.(Edit) Its been almost two months since I finished this game and I legit cannot stop thinking about it. This game is incredible.

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is very likely my game of the year.This game takes ideas and questions about making and consuming art in all its forms, the nature of memory and time, introspection and self reflection and somehow manages to fuse it and represent it seamlessly with its environments, narrative and puzzles.  It's so freakin' stylish to boot!The game feels unstuck from time, anachronistic and nostalgic all at once:  it isn't lost on me that 70% of playing this video game is actually stepping away from the screen to use a plain old pen and paper to piece together information and timelines - like decoding an old diary.The folks who made this game should feel very proud, as it is a work of art in itself.  Thanks for this wonderful experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is a masterfully crafted puzzle game that manages the trick of feeling like a throwback to a more punishing era of gaming, without ever forgetting everything we've learned about making something enjoyable. Moreover, it's a love letter to the joy of figuring things out, and the history of how both games--and people--have gone about creating it. Even when that very joy can only exist because of the frustration of working through something that refuses straightforward explanation.The answers are always fair. To the point that, if you can't solve something, it's refreshingly comfortable to know that you either need to play further, or take nap.If you have fond memories of sitting down with books of brain teasers, this is what that book looks like when it gets folded into a digital origami hotel. Complete with a dozen deep ideas hidden in drawers and under carpets, where you don't need them to enjoy the game. But, they're there, if you want them.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a puzzle design masterpiece. If you're a 90's kid, and you're used to having a paper and a pen by your side when playing puzzle games, you would most likely have a brilliant time! There were so many times when I stared at the puzzle in front of me for a while not having a clue, until I reached that sweet Eureka moment and felt wonderful about cracking the puzzle. To me Lorelei and the Laser Eyes felt like a tasteful strong puzzle cocktail, and I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is an unbelievably good RE1 style puzzle game. The puzzles are all complex but fair and you are gonna need a notebook for this one. The game respects you and your time and exploration and does not hold your hand whatsoever. Highly recommend, definitely one of my favorite games of this year and one of my favorite puzzle games yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic puzzle game. Went in blind zero expectations and was just blown away. The game is surprisingly simple and while there is nit picking to be done, scouring through notes and quick drawn scribbles of notes i took a few hours ago. But its a simple game with a simple interface. The story itself while integral to the puzzles, it isn't terribly easy to follow. Not that it hinders the game in any way as its your typical artistic metaphor ridden story as most puzzle games tend to follow. Regardless the puzzles themselves are rewarding to complete with lots of ahah moments and I'm very thankful for the lack of mind numbing head slamming that would have me looking up guides. As well as the overall progression and level design keeps things fresh and interesting, giving an open floor plan puzzle box that gives you enough direction to keep you from feeling overwhelmed while also making sure not to hold your hand the whole time. Overall just a nice time I pretty much sunk my teeth into this in the span of two days. Took me about 20 hours to complete. Although I am a slow gamer and like to soak in the scenery so it might be like 15 hours, Worth every penny,Would def recommend checking this one out. Will have me desperate for a new puzzler for a long while.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute must play in my opinion, one of the best games that I have ever played, and certainly the best game I have played in years. Normally I don't try to 100 percent games, but this was of such baffling high quality and peaked my curiosity so hard within it's tiniest of details that I just had to go for 100 percent, to become the investigator that the game wants me to be, and 100 percent I did, and it was 100 percent worth every dollar, for all the value that is displayed. Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a fascinating murder mystery game, taking inspirations from games of a Resident Evil style, but rather than having mostly horror with some puzzle solving, Lorelei and the Laser Eyes puts puzzle solving at the forefront, while retaining such a creepy, spooky, dark, mature, and serious tone for it's endeavors. Everything that you do in this game is of the upmost importance, and has to do with a puzzle, a clue, a solution, aspect of the story, an achievement or objective, etc... It might seem like an overwhelming game with its incredibly challenging puzzles that are bound to require actual writing with pen and paper on the side. However, one of the best aspects of this game is the fact that this is a nonlinear game. If you ever feel that you are stuck, don't understand how a puzzle works, if the game is too hard, etc... you can always go somewhere else to continue solving another puzzle or make another discovery either via puzzle solving or via exploration, that can even help you and aid you with a puzzle that you might have been stuck on. This game rewards being stuck on a puzzle and going somewhere else, when in most puzzle games, this would be outright punished. The fact that this game was enjoyable even when I was stuck on puzzles is a remarkable achievement. This even affects the overall puzzle design to where the puzzles in this game are simply astonishingly well designed and so interconnected. Not only are the puzzles unique in every instance, but they also evolve, change, and introduce new ways to solve puzzles all at the same time while making more and more connections between each other, like solving an actual mystery, even in different mediums. Best of all, the answers to puzzles are completely random and unique to a save file, meaning that every play through is going to be different, as well as locations and other aspects of other puzzles, which was a brilliant move that makes using guides next to impossible and adds to the replay value. Everything in this game has a synergy that not only connects its' unknown time and setting of this hidden haunted hotel alongside its' awesome puzzles, but also with it's excellent thick, black and white with select color, filmic look, with its' imperfections being brought to the spotlight with such excellence that it seeks an applause with grand gestures with its' incredible emotion filled and rather bleak but colorful tonal qualities of its' music, expressing different eras and styles to add to this effect, or the overall aesthetics of the hotel also being a blend of time periods with its decoration, furniture, etc.... that requires such craftsmanship and showmanship. You never really know when the game that you are playing takes place, you never really know what is real or not real, and you never really know what is going on within the sublime story until the very end, which makes for an uneasy feeling throughout alongside mixes of dreadful yet euphoric symbolism and imagery. I never wanted this game to end, and this is even after 30 hours of play time. This is a 10/10 game and a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Starring: Some weird dude who's probably David LynchI took a gamble on this game due to the glowing reviews and the likes of Sam Barlow highly recommending it. I won't lie that I was skeptical given Simogo's last game being Sayonara Wild Hearts which lacked interactivity despite its great style. Good thing I took a gamble because I hit the jackpot.As with most other reviews for this game, I'll try to avoid giving much away because I believe going in with minimal expectations is wise. Needless to say, the game is a puzzle exploration game where you explore a hotel and try to unravel a bizarre mystery. I heard someone describe this as "Resident Evil but with puzzles instead of zombies" and I think that's one of the most accurate descriptions. You come to be deeply familiar with the hotel as you explores its nooks and crannies and slowly open it up. The game is practically a rat's nest of information for various puzzles. Puzzles fall back on certain themes and ideas, but consistently force you to determine where the answer is hiding. It's a really cool method that feels incredibly intricate and encourages you to engross yourself in the game's setting.I won't lie that I did look up a couple hints. The shortcut puzzles can be too obtuse to understand at times and I just felt as though staring at them for ages was not in the spirit of the experience. I did also look up an answer for the piano puzzle, as it felt a bit obtuse (all the information you need to solve it is in the room with you), and I did look up how to finally solve the supercomputer puzzle when I was about 98% of the way through it as I struggled to interpret some of the final pieces and wanted to wrap things up. You may view that as cowardly, I view it as "I gave it an honest try and didn't want to sit on the puzzle for ages".I need to emphasize though that, for the majority of the runtime, I didn't look up any hints. I trusted that I could decipher things and would simply come back later if something didn't make sense. And that mostly worked! It was a constant stream of "Eureka!" moments that had me feeling clever as I slowly peeled away this game's layers.Presentation is really cool with artful camera angles and a sharp use of reds in an otherwise monochromatic game. Controls are definitely a bit janky though. There are directional inputs, a start menu button, and an interaction button. That's it. So every single thing you do from accessing your recorded information to inputting numbers on a lock is done with basically one button. While I appreciate the attempt at minimalist design, it does result in some annoying navigation issues from time to time.I do need to emphasize though that these control issues are a minor complaint when considering that this game is essentially the new gold standard for puzzle design. It's so deeply compelling with its narrative and puzzles interwoven and the ways in which it asks you to flip your thinking and re-assess what you know are so damn cool. Also, I just wish more games would utilize numerical puzzles like this.Simogo have developed an insanely large and well thought out title and I hope that we get another from them some time. More than anything though, I hope this is the starting point for a new breed of puzzle design.This game is truly a one-of-a-kind experience with a mesmerizing narrative and engrossing puzzle design. I'd score it 9/10.Highest recommend FFO: Return of the Obra Dinn, The Case of the Golden Idol, Resident Evil, logic puzzles, and auteur projects

_childDocuments_.review: Behind the theme, the game is about 2/3rds IQ-test type puzzles, and 1/3rd finding connections in documents and the environment. It's not a game about exploring one particular puzzle mechanic and one could make the criticism that they just glued together a bunch of random puzzles with the art theme. I'm not going to be so harsh. Actually making puzzles out of modern art is a clever way to give you what you've always wanted, a definite meaning hidden within the art that you can arrive at with logic.Between story/lore and gameplay, I'd say story pulls you through more. Some puzzles are fun, some more an obstacle to finding out more about what's going on. Not that the big reveal at the end is hard to guess at. In fact the end sequence was something of a disappointment to me after the excellent final puzzle.Worth a playthrough, mostly for the strong theme.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I play a LOT of puzzle games. Very specifically I play a lot of puzzle games that try to have as rich of a story as this. Every game I play is unique, wonderful, brilliant in its own way.This game? THIS game is maybe in my top games of -all time-. The puzzles are phenomenal. The storytelling is unbelievable. This game is a marvel. This game SHOULD win awards. Every part of this game has a meaning. Nothing is wasted. I 100% this game because I NEEDED to, not because I'm a perfectionist. I cannot stress enough that if you are questioning whether or not this game is worth it, it IS. This game is worth the full price tag. This game could easily have been $40 and it would feel worth it.Congratulations on creating a masterpiece. I really, really hope this isn't your only game. And thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly compelling in gameplay and narrative; the internal consistency and repeated themes/symbols create a satisfying mystery to unravel. I highly recommend having paper and a writing utensil on hand to help with the puzzles. Be aware that this game is almost entirely number and pattern puzzles, and that memory challenges are not to be taken lightly.Also, the game tells you that money is a limited resource; while this is technically true, it's worth also knowing that a) none of the things that cost money are required to complete the game, and b) you actually can buy everything if you find all of the money. If you want to know what to prioritize:-Gameplay is only affected by coffee, which will make you run for a while instead of walking everywhere.-To get 100% of the "Truth," save your money for stories and games.-Figurines are only for an achievement, to my knowledge.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Cool little adventure/puzzle game that elevates itself up on really, REALLY strong presentation (unsurprising from the Sayonara Wild Hears devs) but it helps that the meat of the game is also just, really solid too. Lots of number puzzles and some more traditional puzzle game-y type puzzles from time to time too set in a maze of a hotel that slowly opens up the more progress you make in the story, and progress in the puzzles is directly tied to progress in the story so it's always constantly there and revealing itself piece by piece. I do think some of the puzzles are a bit of the flop - I don't know why this game has a failure state and I don't know why one of the puzzles it's tied to are really annoying and kind of random memory/observation puzzles - I tried to put the same amount of energy into each of them and some of them gave the most obvious questions on the first go while others gave me really obtuse ones like 3-4 times in a row, it's just. Not fun. Running puzzle box solutions back to the appropriate boxes is also a little scuffed. The UI, as many others have said, is kinda weird and not great but ehh you get used to it.And I think the amount of things this game does well more than make up for any little nitpicks I could have - I definitely found it compelling enough to power through it in like, three long sessions of getting lost in the puzzling flow state so. Absolutely worth your time, another Simogo banger.

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is an exceptional puzzle game with its intricate narrative and challenging gameplay. Simogo's  offering blends the complexity of a labyrinthine mystery with the satisfaction of unravelling its complex puzzles. It's a journey that swings between  frustration and blissful elation, demanding us to think critically and delve deep into its enigmatic world. From the stunning visuals and beautifully haunting soundtrack, to its thought-provoking storyline, every detail of this game feels intentional, creating an immersive atmosphere that completely draws you in. Whether you're captivated by its dark, surreal settings or its relentless puzzle-solving, Lorelei and the Laser Eyes offers an unforgettable experience that both challenges and rewards in equal parts.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing.I normally wouldn't go for such a puzzle-heavy game, but I had to see what the fuss was all about. And I'm really glad I did.The mechanics are dead-simple. You walk around and solve puzzles with the narrative objective of figuring out "the truth." The puzzles draw you in, bit by bit, and by the time you reach the objective you are pretty heavily invested in putting it all together.Incredibly well-designed and executed. Everything you need to figure things out is there. You just need to evaluate (and re-evaluate) your preconceptions and adjust according to what is provided: See it all through Laser Eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece. It looked stylish, I really enjoyed their last game (Sayonara Wild Hearts) and I love a good puzzle adventure game. I went in blind (which I recommend), and my expectations were exceeded. Two things I especially love about the game : 1. It achieve such a good balance of letting you figure things out for yourself, both for the story and the puzzles, but also being generous with the solutions. All the notes and documents you find are useful in some ways, but it might not always immediately be obvious how. I often read back old files (and my own notes) trying to figure out a new puzzle and had some "oh wait, I think I know where I can use that" moments.2. The story and puzzles are intertwined in very clever ways. Usually in theses types of game, the puzzles are there for fun, but don't connect to the story. The story will progress once you completed the puzzle, but they have nothing to do with each other. But in this game, the puzzles constantly references events from the story, which help you understand it better, which help you solve puzzles more efficiently. I thought it was very clever from the devs. You start seeing patterns and by the end, you will probably have a good understanding of what went down.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best game i've played this year.It's very much a puzzle/mystery game, with lots of lateral thinking and exploration, and it does everything it tries to do excellently.Aesthetically it's great, and the sound design and music is fantastic; the story is enigmatic and interesting, and the puzzles are just super fun.Even after finishing, I was thinking about the game and the ending, and during the game, I was thinking about puzzles that stumped me even when I wasn't playing the game.I'm sure you'll know if this game is up your alley or not by looking at it, but I think it's brilliant, and another hit from Simogo
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

The puzzles in general have a pretty good difficulty, I did get stuck in 2-3 places and it is a bit frustrating to figure out where to go next but I just tried to find some general hints online and that gave enough ideas
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A cryptic, cerebral, and engrossing narrative adventure by way of a puzzle box game, with a dose of Resident Evil flavor included. Lorelei's mysteries and puzzles fit together and intertwine brilliantly to make for an intensely satisfying experience for those who like their games to require cleverness, mental flexibility, and note-taking. The artistic vision, art direction, and overall aesthetic quality here is superb, and the themes -- including the purpose of art in capitalist society and the fragile nature of human memory, of madness, uncertainty, obsession and deception -- are quite interesting. Highly recommended for folks who aren't put off by the Annapurna Artsy™ style.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: The quintessential artsy videogame, but this time around it kicks ass also ludically speaking. A boundary pushing puzzle game like you haven't seen one in quite some time, maybe even since the birth of this industry. I say this mainly in terms of ideas and new ways to communicate via game interaction and related mechanics. The control mapping is a little bit problematic to say the least, but it's not so important due to the nature of the work. What it lacks from this aspect, the art direction compensates perfectly. Conceptually and aesthetically the game takes inspiration from all sorts of other media: literature, theatre, cinema, in particular from the works of Federico Fellini and David Lynch. If you like to navigate across every expression of creativity and question yourself about the contamination and influences that occur, this game suits for you. Simogo has once again proven the potential of videogames as a powerful and unique tool by which we can express art and at the same time reflect upon its limits and aspiration. A true gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is often described as a puzzle game, and while that is true, it's not how I would describe it. To me, the game is a uniquely interactive narrative experience unlike any other I've seen. Narrative games are special in that the audience can interact with them, adding an extra level of immersion. This game has taken that philosophy and pushed it to its deepest level. It is truly a work of art and a masterpiece.It's hard to put into words what makes it so special, as it's not as simple as "this game has branching dialogue choices", which it does not. I think the easiest way I can put it is that it takes seemingly pretentious ideas, such as "art is a reflection of the viewer", or "a piece of art is better left unexplained" and turns them into logical truths. It proves these ideas to you as if they were your own, and it does so beautifully.Every piece of the game, from the puzzles to the interconnected narrative, are meticulously crafted in such a way that even the simplest of things have immense meaning that change as you progress through the game. By the end of it, you'll have an entirely new perspective on every single word you've read previously.While I would recommend it as a puzzle game, because that is the majority of the gameplay, it's truly defining feature is the story it tells and how masterfully woven it is.I hope that this game is recognized in history as a piece of media that helped to define and push the idea of what is possible in interactive storytelling. It seems like that was the goal of the developers, and all I can say is that they are geniuses. One of a kind, even.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I almost gave up at around 50% because there were too many puzzles, but then I realized that none of the puzzles are actually complex or time-consuming. The game provides very clear hints, and the real challenge is . Some early puzzles can only be solved later or in different spaces, and the interplay between . This  is exactly what I love. The maze is the core element of the game, and it is presented in various beautiful and stunning forms. My only tip is to be sure to use the in-game maze map as a guide; it really helps with navigating the maze as well as providing hints to some puzzles. Finally, Simogo's visual aesthetics, interaction design, and soundtrack are as beautifully crafted as ALWAYS!

_childDocuments_.review: Cool as hell, challenging and inventive, love the style and the general vibes and spookiness of the hotel you get to explore. i will admit to feeling a little overwhelmed when I saw what the full scope and breadth of the final puzzle would entail and that's why I did not beat it. _childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I've not yet finished the game but i am halfway done atleast. It's a very unique puzzle game. Emphasis on puzzle, it has a lot of puzzle-boxes and conundrums you'd find in one of those brain teaser books. But in a good way, mostly atleast.The puzzles aside my only real gripe with the game is that it's easy to get stuck. And it's not obvious if a puzzle is solvable yet or not. Like something you think you'll need later information to solve, might be solveable immedietly, but you won't know that. things to do are already marked in a little menu, so it'd be great if there was a way to know if something was "ready" yet or not. _childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best puzzle games of all time. If you enjoy games like The Witness or Animal Well and don't mind a bit of light horror thrown in, I cannot recommend this game enough. Be aware that while the horror elements are effective, and you can technically "die", it never requires dexterous movements or quick button presses to survive, even when it may seem like it does. This is a game anyone can play, so long as you can solve some pretty difficult but accessible brain teasers.

_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant, fairly length puzzle game. It's less solving one central mystery and more a collection of well presented riddles.The presentation is the highlight and well executed. The writing is distinct and keeps your interest. Some of the puzzles, especially in the earlier part of the game, can be quite satisfying to solve. I liked that it was spooky too. I enjoyed the ending song quite a bit. Really strong ending.The end portion is a bit of a slog to get through. I could have done with less of the repetitive puzzles to figure out the final goal. Some puzzles were kinda dumb (the piano one comes to mind). Some quality of life things could be improved, even things as minor as being able to go from one end of a list of documents to the other end more quickly. One critique about the overall structure is that the game is less free than it initially seems -- you do have to solve all of the puzzles and it's possible to get stuck if you don't want to look it up. It won't be considered one of the greats, but a confident and distinct experience if you're in the mood.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: This game is *extremely* heavy on flashing lights, and they cannot be turned off. This is my main strike against an otherwise marvelous game. While it's deeply integrated in the art style, it's *not* essential, and I hope the authors put in the work to make this game available to a wider demographic.Anyway! Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a puzzle adventure in a point-and-click-ish style: seek information, solve things, unlock areas, repeat. While all of it is well done, its main strength is its storytelling: like the team's prior work Sayonara Wild Hearts, Lorelei deeply integrates its emotional conceits into the presentation and the gameplay. Playing is experiencing, just as intended.The story is highly surreal, deeply unsettling, and *occasionally* mildly gory. I was impressed by how well it all came together in the end—the story wrote some checks I was certain it couldn't cash, but by the end, everything came together, and the truth of the world hit me hard. (I think some people will be disappointed by the direction they choose? But for me, especially in the context of the execution, it was *perfect*.)That's all I'm going to say! This is a GOTY contender for me: a story that hits hard, using the full breadth of the medium to do it. It's a bit tricky at times, and I recommend using hints if stuck for *too* long, but for someone like me who adores puzzles and pathos, it was just right.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely enjoyed this one. The story isn't massively deep or complex but the puzzles certainly are. I did find myself looking up not necessarily solutions but some kind of understanding of the logic for a couple of puzzles because I locked myself into thinking a certain way and could NOT break out of it. There's a few bits and pieces to go back and replay for achievements but honestly for the price and the length of the game, I'm super happy and feel I more than got my money's worth.This is a big one for me because there is no Accessibility menu in the game, and the game has not particularly done anything to reduce the need for one. There's one very large section of the game where the camera swings wildly (and given you are making a lot of turns, that's about every few seconds) and is an absolute nightmare for folks who suffer from motion sickness. Every time you move from one section to another the screen does a violent glitch effect and during portions of the game, this effect continues for sustained periods of time. It's bad enough in the single glitches but this is really bad design when there is no ability to remove what is a serious migraine and epilepsy trigger. I would strongly recommend folks who suffer from migraines or epilepsy to check out gameplay online before purchasing.OK I know every other review brings this up but it IS a really frustrating feature of the game. The controls are just directions keys (WASD), and space. That's it (aside from ESC to bring up the pause/exit menu). Interacting with objects? Space. Want to check your inventory? Space. Want to close dialogue? Space. It can make navigating some of the puzzles incredibly irritating as you're reaching for a back button that simply doesn't exist. I read that the devs did this for accessibility reasons - simplified buttons to make it so everyone can play with limited dexterity. As someone who has issues with fine motor skills, I did not find this helped with accessibility in the least. There may be others who find otherwise - disability is not the same for any two people - but for me all it did was make me annoyed every time I had to spin my character around to open the inventory rather than trigger a puzzle or item. For moments where you're going back and forwards between inventory and a puzzle... not good.The good of this game far outweighed the bad for me. As I mentioned, it was a great length and I loved the puzzles. The artistic design of the game is phenomenal and I loved the experience of the black and white with splashes of pinky red. The soundtrack is STELLAR (but I wish there was consistently more of it and that it didn't just disappear when you click on a puzzle). I found it very engaging and looked forward to every session. I appreciated that the game rolled out all of the information you needed to get through it, even if I sometimes got frustrated because I couldn't do things in the order that *I* wanted to. It was perfect for scratching that itch of wanting to do some serious thinking. Take your time with this and enjoy it :)Save often. Save everywhere. Save every time you solve a puzzle or unlock a new area. Just do it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting puzzle game that oozes style and originality. _childDocuments_.review: Tightly written puzzle game with a good level of difficulty - certainly not easy but the puzzle solutions were almost always logical and made sense. Puzzles are largely "escape-room" style - most of the gameplay involves extracting number/word combinations from puzzles to open various doors or locks to progress the game. Anyone who enjoys escape rooms will find a lot to love here. The horror elements are also fantastic. My only criticism is the controls; navigating through menus is particularly annoying as there is no "back" button, so you waste a lot of time trying to check your in-game notes. I ended up taking photos of documents etc on my phone rather than relying on the in-game notes for this reason, and that saved a LOT of time. Take your own notes and you'll have a blast!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I've played in years. Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a game which shamelessly wears its inspirations on it's sleeve, taking elements from PS1-era survival horror games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill and making something entirely its own. You're stuck in a mansion filled to the brim with puzzles and locked doors, but it's not brain-eating zombies you're worrying about here; instead, it's your own lack of brains as you try to wrap your head around the myriad mind-bending mysteries contained within it. (If you're a huge scaredy-cat like me, worry not; there's no real scares in this game beyond some mildly unsettling NPCs.)The quality of the puzzles cannot be overstated, but if I had one central critique, it's that the game can often bounce wildly between difficulties without much rhyme or reason, even by the end of the game. The frequency with which it jumps between simple math problems and incredible leaps of logic is a bit frustrating; the shortcut door puzzles (though thankfully optional) stood out to me the most here. Some of them were incredibly simple, others left me boggled as to how you could possibly solve them without a guide. Regardless, the puzzles I considered actually incomprehensible were few and far between, and most of them were fun enough brain teasers that always left me with a satisfied feeling whenever they guided me towards my next area of progression.The interface leaves a bit to be desired; Laser Eyes has a very interesting one-button style of interaction, but that also means the game foregoes having a "back" button. Most puzzles can only be exited by putting in an answer, which is kinda annoying if you have no idea what you're trying to guess. Navigation around the mansion is often cumbersome, and while the game provides handy maps for most of its areas, they weren't quite as useful as I would've liked. There were a few instances where I was left frustratedly walking around the whole mansion looking for the next piece of progression that I knew existed, but couldn't remember the location of. Walk speed is also painfully slow, and while there is a way to increase it for a duration, it's pretty cumbersome and also a bit easy to miss. I didn't unlock it until I was well past the halfway mark.I tend more towards critique in reviews of games I really liked, and Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is one such example. I expect it to go criminally underappreciated, but anybody with a taste for puzzle games owes it to themselves to give this one a shot. I'll definitely have to look into Simogo's other games if they're half as good as this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely remarkable game! From the sound design, to the visuals, to the absolute heart and soul put into the puzzles as well as the story, not once did this game fail to cease my attention and challenge my thinking. This is surely one of those games that I wish I could play again for the first time and truly appreciate every aspect of it with a fresh pair of eyes...
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Holy brainteasers Batman!Where to begin?The compelling puzzles?The incoherent-yet-grabbing storyline?The gorgeous black-and-white-and-red graphics?Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a game that will grip you nearly instantly, keep you engaged for several hours (it took me 24h to complete the story) and fill you with existential dread. A horror puzzler with no monsters, save the monster within yourself.And all that from a little-known Swedish company? Just wow.I cannot recommend this game enough; with the caveat that it is, at times, fiendishly difficult. Yet no matter how tough the puzzle, it never feels unfair. All the pieces are there no matter how little they may make sense at times. The control scheme is also something you need to get used to; the only (yes, only) relevant keys are WASD-Enter (or the arrow and space keys) - leave your mouse to the side! In conclusion;-If you like puzzle games-If you like somewhat pretentious story lines-If you enjoy video games as artThis is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid atmospheric environmental puzzle game; I really enjoyed my time with it.Don't expect any puzzles that are too meaty -- much of the game reduces to "put the obvious clue in the nearby input device", so you won't be working your brain too hard, but the atmosphere is well-done and the puzzles are enjoyable enough if you like this sort of thing. _childDocuments_.review: Great game, I was thoroughly obsessed for the 3 days it took me to finish it. The puzzles were great, just the right level of challenging but not unsolvable. Some reviews here are saying there's a lot of maths, but as someone who is definitely numerically challenged I didn't find it so bad. It's got a really unique style and aesthetic, and an unsettling atmosphere without burdening you with cheap scares. _childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser EyesScore w/o Context: 95% TruthThe Context: Whenever I write a review I usually step back for a few days and try to think through what the game offered up. Mostly, this ends up with me having a similar opinion of the game as when I rolled credits, but occasionally I see connections that I didn't during my initial playthrough. Lorelei is the epitome of the latter, a simple puzzle game at first glance that forces you to make connections you didn't even notice were there, and a rare one that rewards a replay to catch missed references.Upon starting up, you're immediately left to your own devices without your name, purpose or even moment in time. Everything in this game must be found or intuited, from the biggest mysteries to your bladder size. While I had a bit of trouble with it, I think the one-button control scheme ultimately simplifies what could be a complex mess of exploration. Everything interactable is highlighted, and any document or possible puzzle solution is memorized by your character's photographic memory, cutting out large swathes of potential confusion or back-tracking frustration.This frees you up for the meat of the game, the puzzles. I found them to be almost universally fair, with very few esoteric stumbling blocks. Anytime I was stumped, the solutions could be found in my memories, if I looked carefully enough. If I couldn't find one, there were plenty of other possible avenues to explore in the winding hotel grounds.Of course, eventually all of these avenues lead to one final solution. The story being told in these stark hallways is one of metaphor and loss, of art and mystery. The sharp graphical style leads your eyes to certain places and phrases, while the numerical repetition in the puzzles leads your mind. The layers are purposeful, and when the plot was finally laid bare, I could only appreciate the detail of each line. Lorelei is worth your time, and your eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is as perfect as a game can get for me. It is a mix of everything i love.Very cool variety of puzzles ranging in difficulty, with a couple that I figured out randomly throughout my day while not playing. Most of the puzzles unlock a deeper layer in the mystery, increasing my excitement whenever something clicks when solving them.The story and the mystery it revolves around are extremely intriguing. The game has a distinct "vibe" reminiscent of some of my favorite properties like "Twin peaks". The presentation is very unique.
