_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a rare accomplishment: not only is it an amazing puzzle game in its mechanics, but the entire story and setting are themselves puzzles that must be unwound to discover the mystery hidden deep within under many, many layers. The game is very intuitive and gives you many tools to aid you, but does not hold your hand and solving the puzzles is up to you, but they are quite satisfying when you make the connections. Most puzzle games have good puzzles but a mostly boring world to trudge around in, but this world is endlessly fascinating and draws you in instantly. If you are a fan of puzzle games even in the slightest, this is a must play!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Wow wow wow, this is a very good puzzle mansion with a very strong art and story direction. While I am still coming to grips to the story, most puzzles are difficult and obscure enough to feel rewarding to solve. Thankfully it does not rely on obscurity too much; instead, it tends to use known information and references as clues and solution making this feel more knowledge-based specially specially in the later puzzles. Encouraging the player to keep a pen-and-paper close in hand with its own handbook is awesome and pretty good advice with the need to make cross references. Even with a guide, some puzzle solutions are randomized to let players understand the problem is very much appreciated. In terms of difficulty, this is on the more difficult yet fair spectrum but it is not just its puzzles that make this standout.The mystery and aesthetics accentuate the experience even further. Specially, the fixed/tracking camera and monochromatic visuals with strong red colors just looks good as a film enthusiast. Of course, it has more with its various diagetic console and games providing a wide tapestry of references. Also, the reference to other games such as  just make me smile. Going back to the story, It is not simply the what, who and why but when as events and characters occur non-linearly. While not a fan of the limited save, I do like how it meshes with a little risk and tension specifically from the stalker and prevent guessing in the trivia section. Overall, the variety and context make this like no other.As for criticisms, the most tangible ones are the lack of a sprint and menu/cancel button. Having to unlock and refresh sprint may be novel but I feel it was monotonous and uninteresting. The lack of a menu/cancel button feels jarring as pressing any button accidentally opens the menu and cannot be closed quickly without iterating through the items. An one button game feels strange as a gimmick considering most controllers and consoles have 4 buttons available and seems to be another unnecessary restriction. Both these issues just hamper the immersion and takes some needless time to get used to without any reward which just baffles me.As a knowledge-based puzzle game, I do criticize this for a lack of a hint system. Creatively, I respect the choice for not including it and taking the risk of a niche title; however, I do wish it had a system to check if a puzzle could be solvable with known information at least as I tried several times to solve a puzzle and moved on figuring out later I wasted my time. I think this can be done with the entries in the photographic memory and perhaps spending some limited currency as well. Again, I do like the difficulty and obscurity but I think a middle ground can be created for a better experience.My last minor issue is the inventory system. I just wish it can be sorted, customized or discarded as it tends to clutter up and make it harder to use more relevant items. Why keys are not discarded on use is beyond me. Also, the item descriptions are rarely used for the puzzles so there is much less reason why to keep them and can be saved instead in the photographic memory section if really needed. Honestly though, I would do away with the inventory since it is not a strong part of is appeal or experience specially with most items being used once. I can admit it does give the protagonist some nuance but not worth it.This is a niche game requiring patience and determination to get through. This is a contender for my personal game of the year if not simply a game of its year and I strongly recommend this for players willing to undertake the mental challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A surrealist escape room with a hypnotic style that looks like nothing else. It's an absolute masterpiece in puzzle design that never leaves you feeling lost but does not hold your hand at all. You'll definitely need a notebook to write down information and work out solutions, and I'll treasure that wonderful little artifact. An total package of a puzzle game, with brilliant design, a great setting, and vibes like no other. PS If you like this, you should seek out their iOS game Device 6!

_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I've played in ages.  Requires some real lateral thinking, but it uses its theme and recurring elements to really reinforce the connections you make between things, allowing puzzles to really come together in surprising ways as you progress. _childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game but I was helping a friend with the game while streaming. This game is a love letter to adventure mystery puzzle games like The Curse of Monkey Island or Loom, and it performed flawlessly. This is a game where you can sink hours upon hours, don't expect to try to complete the game in 1 sitting. My friend and I did it in 2 streams, for a total of 18 - 19 hours to complete, using some hints on the steam guide section. If you're streaming this, I suggest using some hints since it might make the flow of your play through smoother. Otherwise, do this game blind. You will not regret sinking so many hours trying to understand how a puzzle works and getting that feeling of gratification from figuring it out. On top of that, most of the puzzles in the game are randomly generated, so don't expect watching some person playing the game and think that the solution that they get is the same solution that's going to be for you. Honestly this game is amazing and you should definitely play this blind. 1 tip I would give you is to find every note and make sure to read every note. I would say all of them is pretty important to the story as well as  needing them for solutions to puzzles you haven't encountered yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Really unique puzzle game, the ambiance makes for a lot of it. It gets a bit eerie at times and can make you uncomfortable, you might like it or hate it ! Overall puzzles all seemed fair as long as you're still good on your school knowledge :)My only 2 peeves with the game is not about the content but about control/interface : - No B/Back button(and Close Button while we're at it) is a terrible idea, even with a joycon, you can fit at least a second button. It makes navigating menu awfully clunky and can also get frustrating on some puzzle where you can only cycle in one direction...- For a game that relies so much on memories/documents, not being able to pin at least one in a corner of the screen feels like artificial difficulty by just making you go back and forth between puzzles and memories.I do get the incentive for doodling on a notepad but i ended up spending a lot of time actually screenshoting/snipping the game to get the view of the key information needed for the puzzle instead.Heck, i even used Paint a lot in the event to scribble over my screenshot !
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: "Lorelei and the Laser Eyes" is a masterpiece!The world is mysterious and intriguing. You wander the hotel and its surroundings, unlock room after room, open shortcuts. You collect maps that help you navigate. You read books that explain the many important concepts, be it roman numerals or zodiac signs. You find documents like police reports, magazines, letters, journal entries, reports. They all contain the clues you need to solve the next puzzle - and unravel the puzzle that is the story itself.Read every word, understand every word. Take a close look, and don't miss the details. Remember concepts, and be aware of crucial story details. Keep pen and paper at hand. Then, puzzles are solvable within reasonable time. Intuition and gut feeling can be useful. The occasional puzzle may seem challenging or even impossible to solve. Always keep in mind that this game is non-linear; you just may not have enough information yet, and you can always come back later.This is a game about art. It's the statues, phonographs, movie posters you encounter everywhere. It's the magazines, movie scripts, video casettes you collect. It's the media installations you visit, it's even the money you find. Then again, this game is also art itself. It experiments with highly stylized visuals, it plays around with different camera perspectives.Everything is entangled, connected. Layers, worlds within worlds. The ultimate maze. What is reality, what is fiction? Eventually, everything makes sense. For the most part.I do highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: You know that feeling of disorientation you get when walking out of a cinema after watching an intense 3 hour long movie?Lorelei And The Laser Eyes achieved this for me. (in over 16 hours of gametime)I read every piece of text there is in this game and got rewarded by kind of, but not really understanding the ending.The disclaimer that you need pen and paper to play this game is true. I had to write down so many notes, calculations, drawings, dates, ... i managed to fill 3 Pages with it.Be warned though: This game DOES contain light Jumpscares and a constant feel of unease while playing.10/10 would recommend to anyone interested in detective/puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is An Experience™ - go in and get lost in the weirdness, the spectacular visuals, the headscratching puzzles. Speaking of: the puzzles fun the gamut from simple to incredibly dense but the game provides a load of resources to give you all the pieces you need to solve everything. My biggest complaint is I often had TOO many things I wanted to do as puzzled opened doors (often literally) elsewhere on the map - but thankfully the "mental notes" feature acted as an in-game to-do list to help me stay focused without risking losing bits I wanted to follow up on later. Bizarre, aesthetically rich, and exactly the level of suck-you-in puzzles I want from a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best puzzle games ever made in my opinion. The sheer scope of it is staggering, everything is so interwoven and it makes you feel incredible when you start solving puzzles back to back after being stuck for a while. Been a fan of Simogo since Year Walk and it's amazing seeing how far you guys have come!If you're a fan of puzzle games I cannot recommend this enough, please check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Takes a little bit to get fully going, but there are few games that have drawn me in as much as this game's mid-late game sections. Not every Puzzle is a hit but the average is very high with some real Gems in there too, and I was a big fan of the story, especially the ending and how it was presented.If you like puzzle games and the vibe or theming is appealing to you I highly highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: have not finished this yet but this is a really wild ride. the hotel feels like a giant escape room where you're constantly connecting the dots between random stuff you saw in room A and random stuff you saw in a hallway on a different floor 5 hours later. the vibes are off the charts. music is absolutely stellar when it needs to be. i wouldn't classify this game as horror but it definitely gets pretty tense and unsettling.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes delivers a unique experience blending puzzle-solving and narrative-driven gameplay. Set in a mysterious hotel with a striking monochromatic style, the game immerses players in a dreamy, Lynchian atmosphere. The integration of story and puzzles is one of the game's strongest features, with players required to solve combination locks, find keys, and decipher clues hidden within documents scattered throughout the hotel. The puzzles are generally well-crafted and test the player's attentiveness, though some felt arbitrary or lacked contextual clues.The gameplay encourages players to take extensive notes and screenshots, evoking a nostalgic experience reminiscent of old-school puzzle games. However, the game is not without its flaws. The lack of a back button and the need to input wrong answers to exit puzzles can be frustrating. Despite these minor interface issues and occasional pacing problems, Lorelei and the Laser Eyes offers a rewarding journey culminating in a masterful final puzzle that ties everything together brilliantly.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Making art *about* art is extra hard because the fictional works of art inside your story have to be convincing. One of my favorite things about this game is that the movies and games inside the game all absolutely make sense and have a plausible aesthetic. They all really work for me and in fact tickle the part of me that took film theory and had to watch a bunch of bonkers stuff from the 60's.I loved the puzzles and only had to look up a hint on one single thing in the game. It was definitely challenging and required copious handwritten notes but all the puzzles seemed like they were drawing from the same logic, like nothing felt too far out of left field for a game like this. I see people have complained about the controls and lack of a back button in menus, but it didn't even occur to me to be bothered by that. Overall this was an incredible challenge and a great experience, and I'd highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A great game in its genre.Good puzzles, cleverly incorporated into the world, and a strong atmosphere.Having your own notebook will probably greatly help you and is very satisfying to review when the game is over.However, the navigation in the menus is questionable.for example, a back button would be better when using a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A bold, confident, (seemingly) effortlessly stylish and hauntingly confusing puzzle game, it feels to me like Riven meets Killer7.The puzzles all revolve around the narrative, itself in pieces and in need of reconstructing through the act of play. By the end, you'll be intimately familiar with all the actors and themes, and the final quiz is liberating in how "obvious" it all is - after you've spent a maddening time figuring it all out, of course.Most of the puzzles will live rent free in your head before and after solving them, and you'll cover pages of crazy scribblings that'll look like a confusing conspiracy theory board to the casual onlooker - but really, it all comes together and makes sense! It does! Talking at length about any of its design choices or details would be spoiling the experience, so it's really best to jump in as blind as possible, with the firm belief you're in for one of the very best and smartest games of 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Stylish art, intriguing storytelling, challenging "escape room" style puzzles and best played coop.The world is a joy to navigate. The layouts are fun to learn, explore and are euclidean enough to reason about. While the controls are a bit... choice they are something that is easy enough to get used to. By using a "one button control scheme" that excludes a "back" button they made the menu navigation a chunk tedious but definitely adds to the otherworldly sense of place and is accounted for in the layout of the menus.Where Lorelei differs from other puzzle game success like "Obra Din" and "The Case of the Golden Idol" is in the way it prompts you and the types of questions it wants you to answer. The puzzles are more independent from each other, more focused, more "notice the pattern" or "enter the code you found (usually close to the question)" and less "think about the world and make deductions". Calling it an extended "8th grade Math class and IQ test" might be too reductive for how varied and engaging the puzzles are, but it's not too far off either.Playing this in a coop setting, with players sitting in front of the screen and discussing the puzzle, should also be a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Game of the year for me, lots of puzzles, some easier than others, many building on lots of different sub-elements, almost all completely fair (just one puzzle where I had to look up and am unhappy with the answer out of 200+).Outside the puzzles the game creates a really eerie atmosphere, somehow both incredibly disjointed and cohesive at once with a genuinely intriguing story that comes together brilliantly by the end.High recommended for anyone who like a bit of a mystery puzzler.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Challenging, captivating, charming, it has all been said here in the comments and reviews and it all rings true. What a delight and kudos to the team for realizing this vision! Maybe adding a back button that functions after trying to enter a solution and failing one time. The idea behind not having one is to force the player to find out how to 'enter' a possible solution. And a map shortcut would also be helpful. Otherwise perfect and daring game of which the memory will stay for a long time to come!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I will start stating: I REALLY liked the game. Great puzzles, with an great story and an AWESOME noir style, which charms you until the very end. The good part is really good, so I will not extend on them. If you like what I mentioned, I think you should give it a go.However, there are some things that bothered (and sometimes even infuriated) me. First, the controls, which are mentioned in many reviews. Think of navigating on a website with a horrible interface. However,  you are in a game, and you constantly have to deal with it. It may not seem too much of a hassle, however, when you have to click 3+ buttons hundreds of times just to access a map, it kind of stacks up. I don't know the reason the devs decided to implement the system this way, however, it did not contributed to my experience in any positive manner at all.Secondly, avoiding spoilers, some systems you discover very early in the game are REALLY crucial to the overall pacing, and if you do not get them, you are going to have a real bad time navigating. I'm not saying the game should do like a generic open-world and just point it, but maybe be a bit more insistent about it? Third: many objectives depend on information you don't have at the time, which is great. However, the problem arises because it is very easy to miss a single clue in this game, since in many times you just stumble upon them. Then, you must pass hours exploring every section of the game, because the in-game tracking system (the "Mental Notes") do not give any hint on that matter, and you NEED this clue to progress in the game, without knowing how or where to find it.Well, by the comments, it seemed I hated the game, but quite the contrary: I loved so many aspects of it. It is so charming, and has so many clever puzzles and reasonings. That's why I fear that some people can be discouraged to finish it, and miss on the great things it has to offer.Overall, I had a GREAT time. Very charming, very smart, very caring. Please give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Like it so far. The riddles feel good and strike a good balance between challenge and accessibility. It’s getting complex at 20% puzzles solved and I hope I’ll figure it all out without getting lost.The art style is sleek and this game is a great showcase for what cognitive art games can be. Thanks for making this!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games of this year. Every puzzle, every key, every lore piece is meticulously placed giving an incredible sense of exploration. Seeing everything you gathered during the game coming together in this bigger story is amazing, some tips you get that you won't use during hours until you randomly encounter the place and it just clicks. I can't give this game enough praise. Daniel Olsen also delivers an incredible soundtrack this time again.My only complaint would be just like any of the other reviews, I don't understand why the control scheme works this way. I don't know if it is aimed at a mobile platform, some weird game collector's overpriced dumb one-button portable game console like Playdate, or just simplified enough that anyone can play it no matter what. Either way, it doesn't make a lot of sense. But don't get me wrong, this does not reduce how good this game is by any means, it's just weird.With all that being said, this is easily a 10/10 game. Play it, write every piece of evidence that you think might help you in a notebook and just let your brain cook.This is definetly going to my favourite games list, thank you for this incredible experience Simogo.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Looked through every corner of the game and wrapped credits still wishing there was more. A masterpiece for fans of the puzzle genre, bonus if you loved stuff like OG Resident Evil (puzzles and pacing, not combat) and the visual style of Sayonara Wild Hearts. Much like SWH, an excellent "Video Game" on the surface, with a touching human introspection as the custard filling. Can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was right up my alley, I loved it. I really like puzzle games that don't hold your hand and you need a pen and paper to complete. I was surprised at how difficult (yet solvable) a lot of the puzzles were. They were the perfect difficulty where they give you everything you need to solve it but you really need to think until an epiphany happens, and it's an amazing feeling when you finally figure it out.I was hooked by the story and atmosphere but just know it's very surreal and abstract. Kind of like if David Lynch played Professor Layton and Resident Evil then was like "I can do that."I'd give it a shot if you like games like Return of the Obra Dinn, The Painscreek Killings, or The Case of the Golden Idol.Overall I give it a 9/10 and I'll be analyzing the story and ending for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: this is probably going to be my game of the year.from the twin peaks/the shining inspired setting through to the art style, reminiscent of something like killer7 or other works by suda 51, everything in this game feels like it was specifically designed to appeal to my sensibilities.i don't think i've ever played a puzzle game this intricately designed and lavered that seemingly tries to push its players away as much as it's trying to pull them deeper into its mysteries. trying to have a conversation with the player about the relationship between the artist and the audience through both its story and the experience of playing it. i'll be thinking about it for a very long time
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: i really enjoyed this! if you're a fan of the walking-around-doing-puzzles style of game you'll probably like it too. this is definitely one of the better entries in that genre. plots a pretty fun meditation on the "nature of art" and all that sorta stuff. it's written well enough and very stylish so it doesn't come across as too pretentious imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games like Return of the Obra Dinn, this is right up your alley. There is an over-arching story that unfolds as you get further along in the game. However, the ending feels a little lackluster after all the effort you've put in solving puzzles to get to that point. To me this wasn't the biggest deal as I really enjoyed the "journey" of getting to the end. Really one of the only improvements to the game would be adding a back button to the menus and puzzles as other reviews have also suggested.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game a lot.  I've played Device 6 several times and have never been able to find anyone else match the well crafted, difficult but intuitive puzzles, the chilling atmosphere, and the interesting narrative like that game has.  It gave me an itch that nothing else could scratch, and now finally ten years later the same folks have come and done it again.  The highlight of this game is definitely the puzzles.  Despite the well organized codex of information the game maintains for you, definitely want to play this game with a notepad you can write in, which is my very favorite kind of puzzle game.  It definitely draws a lot of inspiration from resident evil, with you exploring a strange manor, finding weirdly shaped keys and unlocking new hidden passages.  It's so difficult to find a well crafted puzzle game of this caliber, and for anyone that enjoys that kind of thing, I highly recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: At the start of the game I was frustrated by all the locked doors I couldn't solve and the lack of any sort of direction, but it was SO satisfying to watch all the information come together and realize the note you just found is a clue for the lock you found hours ago. Every piece of Information you find is important eventually. The controls were annoying at first but I got used to them pretty quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: An "Oops All Puzzles" Resident Evil written by Italo Calvino and directed by David Lynch. A delightful, dense addition to my "notebook game" notebook, yet polite and obvious regarding what you need to track outside the game.Could be elevated with voiced dialogue, smoother collision meshes, an option to exit puzzles before attempting a solution, and dedicated "Interact" and "Introspection" buttons.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is, without doubt, one of the finest video games I have ever experienced. I went in blind, and that enhanced my playthrough immeasurably. Put simply, if you enjoy puzzle games, this is one of the all time greats. It is a sprawling, delicious puzzle box, with a dense, often 'meta' plot that kept me hooked for the 26 hours it took me to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Instantly a new favorite of all time. If you like puzzles and logic games, this is for you. And it's got a great mystery and noir aesthetic lavished on every facet of the experience. My only quibble is the lack of accessibility options and the omission of a back button, but overall my experience with the game was extremely positive.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: 8-9/10? really fun and satisfying puzzle game. i enjoyed exploring the hotel, solving little puzzles everywhere and opening up new areas, and i think the game is really well paced + close to perfect difficulty (for me, at any rate - i'm not a hardcore puzzler enthusiast but i am a veteran). the game's aesthetic presentation also rules it's SO stylish & being able to keep information in your inventory to be called up at will is great. the narrative i'm less hot on but that's personal preference... i worked out where it was headed early on and am just not as interested in it as i expected to be.my caveats to this recommendation are:- controls - everyone mentions this probably but where is the back button!!! i'm not sure if there's a dedicated map button that i didn't find but having to go in and out of inventory to check maps did suck. this game is also CLEARLY designed to be played on controller; i have one on hand but it's annoying to start playing a game sold on pc and just go okay my experience will be worse if i play this using kbm. the tank controls in some sections are also really rough- other accessibility - lots of flashing visuals in here. i am not very photosensitive but the Vision puzzle hints for the penultimate sequence gave me a headache bc they're lowkey flashing/swirling the entire time and i needed to stare at them for ages :(
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: not done with it yet but 10 hours and ~65% into the game and this is a deliciously opaque puzzle mystery. Anyone familiar with escape room puzzling conventions will be at home with this one.  Some folks have complained about the minimalist control scheme (1 stick, 1 button) but I like how expressive they make it... although not having a back button is mildly annoying when navigating nested menus.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wild ride. I couldn't stop thinking about this when I stepped away from the computer.There are some rough edges here and there, like the lack of a dedicated back button and some passcode locks that don't make it clear what they are even asking for, but these issues aren't enough to change my overall opinion. In a weird way, the game wouldn't be what it is without those wrinkles.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the kind of person who is down to sit down and just grind out riddles and escape room puzzles back to back this game is going to be right up your alley but this is definitely not a game for everyone.  The visual style and presentation is all great, and I never got hard stuck at any point in the game save for one puzzle that roadblocked me because I failed to read an extremely obvious note for a long time.  If this game looks like a game you might like you're probably right.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of the best puzzle games to come out in the last 3-4 years. Great atmosphere, great story, great puzzles that you can 100% solve without having to look anything up. Maybe there is room for improvement on the controls but that is the only thing that stops me from giving this game a perfect score. Bonus score for referencing Silent Hill and Twin Peaks.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic puzzlebox of a game.The puzzles have a nice difficulty, where you have to think, make connections, or even pull out the ol pen and paper. You never feel like you stumbled on the solution by accident, which is very satisfying.There is no bruteforcing this game (well you can, but its prohibitively time consuming), which, if you're out of ideas, could be frustrating.The story is very obtuse, but you slowly piece it together for a satisfying conclusion to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes is a truly special puzzle experience, from one of the most underrated studios out there, Simogo, who I first noticed when checking out Device 6 and Year Walk. On your way to unravelling the story you'll definitely want a notebook by your side (even with the ability to keep any documents you read memorised through the character's photographic memory), as many puzzles have solutions elsewhere, and there's no hint system. Reviews may mention the one-button control scheme as a downside, and while it surprised me at first too, I honestly got used to it pretty quickly and barely noticed it after an hour or two. Everything flowed quite smoothly, and that's with the art style being pretty unique and daring on top of that, as it's mostly black and while with bits of red, which give an interesting contrast and help important parts to stand out.Lots of excellent atmosphere as well, despite there not being any enemies to fight, and it only draws you in further and pushes you forward, to the next puzzle, to the next story beat.Expectations are also played with, in a good way, where you're never quite sure what will happen next, and just as it seems like you've got the story figured out, another curveball is thrown your way to keep you guessing.I only got truly stumped maybe once or twice in the entire game, and even if that happens to you, you often have multiple leads to go on at any given time, so you can almost always leave a puzzle for later if you don't know the solution right away.While this game definitely is not for everyone in multiple ways (and Simogo said as much, they do not expect everyone to be able to finish the game), those that it does capture are sure to delight at the experiences and feelings it gives. Entering and peeling back the layers in the story, thinking about puzzles every which way, and having those "Aha!" eureka moments are irreplaceable. If you think this game is remotely something up your alley, I'd really encourage you to give it a try.Simogo has yet again created a wonderful game, with a striking artsyle, excellent soundscapes, interesting narrative, and of course engaging and unique puzzles. Such a game I will not forget anytime soon, as I'm listening to "Enneahedron" on repeat, wondering what Simogo will come up with next...
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much! It's stylish, the puzzles are well-done, and the story is a bit unhinged in a good way, full of twists and turns and symbolism. If the sound of a room escape game with a House of Leaves/film noir mashup aesthetic sounds like something you'd enjoy, you should definitely play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to explain what makes Lorelei and the Laser Eyes special.Maybe it is the monochromatic visuals, maybe the (mostly excellent) puzzle design, the amazing atmosphere, its soundscape including an incredible soundtrack, its pretentious but great writing. Or maybe it's how all of its pieces fit together. It's not perfect, and it's hard to recommend because it probably appeals to such a small group of people. The only thing I can say is that I loved almost every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game boasts a plethora of excellent puzzles that require knowledge of the environment, characters, story and things like the zodiac, math and the Greek alphabet. Luckily, your character has a photographic memory, so any information you acquire can be consulted whenever you wish. In essence, all puzzles are about pattern recognition - the challenge being that you'll need to figure out what pieces of information to pull together to be able to decipher the pattern. Barring a few more frustrating and vague puzzles, the vast majority are very enjoyable. The game respects your intelligence and will make you work for the answers (pen and paper are a must), which is what makes it all so satisfying. If you get stuck on a puzzle, just walk away and try another. Remember that sometimes you may not have the right information yet to solve it - several puzzles are dependent on solving other ones first.Aside from the puzzles, the art direction is just stunning. The black and white minimalism of the environment - only occasionally broken by shocks of red - works together with a beautiful score to create a very strong atmosphere. The game isn't scary, but it has existential horror elements. I would classify it more as a scifi/fantasy mystery. The narrative deals with topics of (very vague spoiler) If all this appeals to you in the slightest, please check it out. You won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately a satisfying constant brain teaser with a gorgeous artistic style and great atmosphere.It's not perfect. Got lost a few times, wandered aimlessly a few times more, looking for that one little detail I missed (that I occasionally always had with me) but it's still nice to have a puzzle game that makes you feel smart that manages to be difficult and clever, but not insurmountable.The game's puzzle design is to be commended. I got through the whole game while feeling like I overcame actual challenges with proper logic, and I never felt forced to look up solutions. It's quite impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to put into words how much fun this game is. Not cause I can't, but because I don't want to.If you like classic adventure games like Secrets of Monkey Island, Myst and King's Quest, but want a more logic based approach to the game (rather than spamming items in random locations), then Lorelei is the game that will scratch that itch near flawlessly. It is a mix of the exploration from Resident Evil (without the horror) and the logic-based puzzles from the previously mentioned games.To say more would be a disservice to the game itself. So that sounds like your cup of tea then trust me: buy this game and play it blind. Keep a notebook and pen handy by your side and allow yourself a day or two to stew on puzzles. A deep, rich meal of which you should only take small bites off one day at a time. And that's the best praise that I can give it.5/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I love puzzle games. I don't generally like abstract stories with a lot seemingly left open to interpretation in lieu of actually presenting a cohesive narrative. Because of these facts I played this game with cautious optimism. It did not disappoint.The puzzles are good for the most part (with one strong exception, ), but what the creators did brilliantly was weaving the story and puzzles together. From the start the game hides answers in documents that each hold a tiny snippet of the overall tale. While the answer is fairly simple to deduce at first, it sets up the expectation that paying attention to what you find is important for both story and player progression. It manages to ease you into the difficulty of the later puzzles, meaning you know how to look at the clues, and feel clever when you get the right answer. The story itself is what blew me away at the end, and elevated this from a good puzzle game to an amazing experience that I won't soon forget. I may be in the minority of people that didn't put everything together until the final puzzle gave me  enough context to figure it all out myself. If so, I am glad to be a dullard, because the feeling of satisfaction I got from the confirmation to my final solutions was something few games have managed to give me.In the end there were still some elements that are somewhat vague and open to interpretation, but I found out that it doesn't bother me when the overall story is sound and clearly present. In fact, I even enjoy speculating on some of the details that were less explained. I don't hate mystery. I just think it should not carry the story in the end, and I feel the creators of this game understand that. There are a few decisions made in making this game that I cannot understand. There is no auto save, and saving can only be done at certain spots in the game (though these are plentiful.) This is a problem because at a few unexpected points there is a chance at a game over. The game does warn you about it, and I can imagine they did it to create tension in those moments, which it sometimes did for me, but it means that if you don't frantically save at almost every opportunity, you risk losing some or a lot of progress. In a puzzle game like this, that is just frustrating, since it's nothing more than a chore to get back to where you were.The controls are also very simple. A bit too simple, in fact. All it uses is directional keys and a confirm key. It works, but I cannot figure out why there is no cancel button. It makes going through menus a slog, and it makes inputting the solution to some puzzles more tedious than it needs to be. You get used to it after a while, but I cannot help but wonder why they chose to do it this way.If you like escape room style puzzles that build up in difficulty at a good pace, this game will probably scratch that itch. I imagine it would be less enjoyable if you have no interest in narrative, since you need to understand it at least to some degree to progress at certain points. The game is trying to tell a story, and I think it's better for it.

Honestly, the amount of "Ah-Ha!" moments were incredible, especially when you have been trying to figure out what to do next only to realize that two things you didn't think were connected actually were. _childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly brilliant, unprecedented, and unlike anything I (and I'm pretty certain that you, the reader) ever played.Gorgeous art direction, fantastic puzzles front-to-back (and with hours upon hours of JUST puzzles, that means A LOT), extremely open-ended exploration for fans of the genre - but it's not really possible to get stuck and not know what to do.The story is wonderful, and the storytelling is unlike any other. Ridiculous, absurd, beautiful and immersive - the story is a puzzle in itself - one that you'll have no choice but to piece yourself in order to understand.Simogo did it once more.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Simply one of the best puzzle games I've ever played in every way.  The theme keeps you intrigued, the classic style of gameplay lends itself very well to the genre, and the puzzles are just perfect.  I think this is the first puzzle game where every puzzle made sense, but wasn't so easy that I solved them right away, leading to plenty of those satisfying "Aha!" moments.  It was also sufficiently challenging, but not so much that I felt the need for guides or hints.  Simply Perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: YES play it!This is, in my opinion, the best puzzle-based game out there. I am enthralled by the story, you glide from one puzzle to the next organically, your mind is almost awake, always working, thinking about all the details you've learned and how they can help you solve X or Y. You wake up in the middle of the night with an epiphany for puzzle 17 (there's a cool puzzle book), you fill up PAGES of notes...It gets the silver on my GOTY list!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: An extravagant, headscratching, beautiful adventure game.The design and setting of this game work like a huge, interconnected escape room where every puzzle you solve and door you unlock gives you another puzzle, another door and some information that drives the story forward. It's an anthology of classic riddles and brainteasers (cyphers, arithmetic and geometry, roman numerals, wordplay...), most of which are not very original or difficult, but there's a ton of variety and the puzzles are contextualized and intertwined with the narrative in amazing ways; this makes the game very pleasurable to play through: it compels you to solve one puzzle after another with its intriguing presentation and well balanced, non-linear progression.Even the story is a big riddle to interpret: it's very cryptic, surreal and you won't leave with all the answers; but the style, the pacing and the events are captivating: it always rewards you with enough information to keep you interested; oftentimes it goes in unexpected directions or touches important themes, but it does so without ever leaving the enigmatic realm of its setting, creating an unique and thought-provoking type of meta-narrative.Extremely recommended if you want to get lost in a gorgeously crazy mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I've played in the last few years. It's tougher than the usual fanfare but nothing felt cheap or unfair, realizing the answer truly felt like unlocking a third eye. The art direction is also stunningly striking and well committed. This is definitely one of those games that digs deep into your brain in every way
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: When I started playing it, I was a bit put off by the frustrating controls (please add a dedicated Back button) and not too sure about the escape room style padlock puzzles.However, by the time I finished, I had 10 pages of notes in my notebook and I couldn't stop thinking about this game and listening to the soundtrack. Very Twin Peaks-y.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: We're 10 hours (and countless pages of scribbled notes) into playing Lorelei and the Laser Eyes and it's a great non-linear puzzle/mystery game with Twin Peaks-esque vibes.I'd say its metaphysical antics are fourth-wall breaking except it's hard to know which wall is the fourth one when the viewing angle keeps changing and the walls are only enumerated with upside-down Greek letters.Update: We finished Lorelei and the Laser Eyes and it's overall really good! Like an incredibly intricate escape room set in a giant space-time folding mystical mansion. We clocked in a 33 hours and ... 42 pages of dense scribbled notes, neat!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Another amazing game from Annapurna   Interactive (and kudos to developer Sumomo!).  It’s weird, mysterious, and loads of greatness!  The game is like a mixture of twin peaks, silent hill, and Alan wake series (without combat).  Great mystery and great puzzles.  Makes you feel like a detective!  I’m only 43 percent done with it, so I have lots to go, thank god! Highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Being stylistically on point and with challenging, yet (mostly) not frustrating riddles, this has been a delight in the first ~65% (according to the in-game counter) of the game I played.I would describe the atmosphere to something like the Rusty-Lake series, even though the visuals are quite different and some of the riddles are much more directly brain-teaser-y than the mostly strange-mechanism-tasks found in that series.There are some explicitly signaled solve-or-reload-from-checkpoint events, and for me these are not as enjoyable as the normal gameplay mode, but that is so far the only thing not perfect I can come up with.As it seems like there are lots of parallel tasks, there is a high chance that there is always something else to pivot to when you get stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Going in blind is the best thing you can do for yourself if you are interested in this game. It does have a fairly somber atmosphere almost throughout the whole game but not too scary (unless you are otherwise sensitive).The game recommends you play this game with a pen and paper in hand, and it is that type of game forssure. The photographic memory mechanic keeps important info always at hand, so minimal backtracking is ever required. Story will lands its beats sporadically, but the drip feed of the mystery just adds to the atmosphere that I believe the game executed well on. Don't come in here expecting a clear cut story without investment. You will be in the dark to the larger plot points until later in the game when all the pieces you collected start fitting together.

Go in blind, do your best to avoid looking up any puzzle solutions, and let yourself become lost as well. After all, is that not the point of a maze, Signorina?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a triumph. An intricate puzzle box with gorgeous artistic direction that tells a feminist narrative about art, trauma, and the auteur.That being said, I do have to disagree with many of the other reviews I see here. One real strength of the game is the puzzle design, and I've seen many people talk about the piles of notes they generated to play the game. While you're entitled to note down whatever you want, I think a real strength of the game is that you DON'T need to take very many notes, the puzzle design is so elegant that you really don't need to. In my playthrough I took notes around 10 times total, and mostly to help memorize sequences of things that were longer than 7 units. In general, though, what you need to solve a puzzle is usually directly in front of you, and when it is not the game helpfully uses Lorelei's photographic memory to record everything you interact with to aid in puzzle solving. Very helpfully, if you ever interact with anything in the game and it ISN'T recorded by Lorelei, you know it is only meant to be used on a puzzle that's immediately in front of you (though beware: the inverse is not always true!). You end up accumulating a huge trove of information, but it's always easy to sort through and what information applies to which puzzle is usually extremely obvious.There are a variety of puzzles, but many of them follow a general structure which is also very streamlined. They are by-and-large "escape room" style puzzles, with a lock-and-key approach. It flows like this: (set of information) -> (cipher or rule) -> (lock input). The puzzle design lies in figuring out elegant and intuitive ciphers or rules to apply to the information that forms the "keys", and the team has done an excellent job in figuring out straightforward and rewarding examples of this. I often found myself overcomplicating puzzles which were otherwise actually very straightforward. The ways they change this up throughout the game is also very elegant: there's a fun room with a bunch of locks where the code is always the same, but the way you input it into the lock changes. Many reviews have also complained of the control scheme, which is a "one button" game (actually, it's one button plus directional input). These complaints consist of minor things like not being able to hit the B button to exit out of a menu and things like that. What this control scheme opens up, though, is accessibility. This game relies on pretty much 0 pre-existing game knowledge, and I think we'll see it becoming very popular with people who don't normally play games. It'll be a lot easier for those types of people to play it if they only need to remember movement and one button, as opposed to the normal controller or keyboard setup. It's a smart design choice which I hope will open up the game to a wide audience.Overall, this is a real masterpiece. I do think the only prerequisite to enjoying this game is that you likely need to like puzzles at least a little bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is marvellous stuff - simultaneously innovative and artisanal. The trailers don't do it justice. The level of skill and learnedness it takes to make something like this is astonishing. There's so much to rave about here. Three things in particular deserve attention, imo: the extremely effective yet subtle jumpscares, the deliciously creepy retro sequences, and the use of passive, unobtrusive repetition to induce player learning.I desperately hope that this will be a commercial success. Please buy the game and help make that the case.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is a soft recommendation with a big caveat:I stopped playing Lorelei about five hours in. The puzzles just became too much work to push through to see the end of the intriguing story that the game had set up?So why I am "soft" recommending it? Well, you can't deny the craft and artistry that's gone into this and I think if you enjoy puzzles, you will REALLY enjoy this. I'm largely apathetic toward puzzle games and steer clear of experiences like MYST and RIVEN and this game is definitely in that camp. You have to break out a pencil and paper. You need to have a calculator. Get ready to do some math. You'll often come across puzzles you can't solve until you find another key item/bit of information.For a lot of people, that's exciting. It's a fun scavenger hunt and brain teases. But to me, it feels like ultimately equivalent to being stuck in a college course I'm not particularly enthused to be taking. BUT, that ultimately comes down to player preference vs any flaws in the design here (outside of the odd absence of back button???).So yeah, how much you enjoy Lorelei will entirely depend on how much you like puzzles. If you're apathetic or mildly allergic to them, yeah, you might want to steer clear. But for puzzleheads, I imagine this is one you don't want to miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. The puzzles are nothing revolutionnary but they are very logical and never felt unfair. They also have a lot of thematical coherence along with the story, while adding a sense of nostalgia for those kind of brain teasers you'd find in books or magazines.The story and atmosphere are probably the best part of this game. Contrary to what it might seem at first, this game has a carefully crafted narrative and is not the kind of game that just throws random ideas and themes and ends up open ended. Understanding the story is a puzzle in itself, and everything here, documents, locations, dates, names has meaning that helps progressing towards it. All of this culminates into a very satisfactory ending.The single button controls are kinda annoying though, but nothing is ever perfect I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many different reasons why I loved this game. For example, cerebral-type puzzles like in Tunic, but  more concentrated, or the extremely deliberate control scheme that I can see why it would annoy people, but I fully bought into it (it's sort of hinted at why in the game), or maybe it was the fact that I had to take real, physical notes. I loved every single minute of this. I have a pile of sticky notes like 3 inches high with all of my puzzle solutions on them. Having a pen and paper next to you makes this game possible, I definitely couldn't have done it without one. I love games like that. It respects your intelligence and is highly confident in what it's trying to do. If you love puzzle games,  play this game. You owe it to yourself. Every decision it makes is purposeful and I love it to pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Thought I'm only a couple hours in, I can already tell this is going to be one of the greatest of all time possibly in the puzzle genre. Simogo puzzlers always have that certain charm, but the presentation on Lorelai and the Laser Eyes is perfect and I can't wait to delve deeper into the puzzles. This is a game I can't recommend enough for those who enjoy some thinking.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like an escape room meets Sleep No More; the vibes are off the charts and I find myself pouring over notes the game has provided me (as well as those I have written down) to squeeze out any other answer to allow me forward, and after enough strain I am able to figure something out, rinse and repeat, Brilliant game both in puzzle design and in aesthetic and theme, highly recommend if you are a fan of puzzles and dark atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is an outstanding puzzle game.Usually, I either feel like the game was easy, or end up looking up at least some puzzles. Lorelei managed to make me both feel like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ genius while making every single puzzle feel fair.I found the game's approach to puzzles very unique. A somewhat spoiler-free example is this: a lot of the puzzles revolve around three particular years. Sometimes you have to decipher some strange symbols on the screen, and simply knowing that what you are looking for is probably one of the three years makes you see the pattern that you probably would never ever notice otherwise. In short, puzzles that would have been obscure and unsolvable when put in any other game somehow become natural, quite straightforward, and yet beautiful and entertaining.This is my personal GOTY so far, and out of the "usual suspects" this year I've already played Animal Well, FF7 Rebirth, Infinite Wealth, Balatro and Unicorn Overlord. This one tops all of them for me. Devs, do you know what would make this game even better? The addition of a functioning "back" button!BTW, 12 hours for 99% truth uncovered. I am pretty proud, to be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an extremely focused, dense, and intertwining experience and I need more things like it in general. The puzzles in the game can be really difficult and downright frustrating to figure out but they're absolutely not outside the scope of what one person can figure out which is a breath of fresh air when so many games have puzzles that seem to require an entire community of hundreds to piece together from minute details. You're given the information to complete every puzzle and it's made clear what information is important for completing those puzzles. Another thing that's great about the puzzles is the sheer variety. Some are basically just straight up math equations while other are much more abstract in how they convey information to you. Some puzzles make it pretty clear that the solution to them is in the same room while others require information that's found scattered across the map but it's always pretty obvious when you do and don't already have the required info. The presentation for the game is also absolutely phenomenal. The surprisingly wide array of settings and visuals echos the variety of the puzzles and every one will catch you off guard when you first come into contact with it. The disjointed and abstract nature of the presentation also pairs really well not only with the narrative but also how the narrative is told. Bits and pieces of an incomplete story are strewn about everything is about something else yet it all somehow embodies the same central ideas and themes of seeking closure and meaning in the face of uncertainty.The game is very very obviously not for everyone and if you don't think that you'd like it then yeah you probably wouldn't, but if you've got a pretentious bone in your body then I implore you to at least give it a shot. Lorelei and the Laser Eyes left a very strong impression on me that won't go away anytime soon. Ars longa, vita brevis, so go play Lorelei and the Laser Eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: FLAWEDI haven't finished the game yet, but at more than 90% completion, I think I'm well within my right to write this review.To make a long review short, I wish steam would let me put down a gray option because while the good parts of this game are really good, I feel like I'm fighting to like the game.In essence, it's an "open world" puzzle game where you try and solve puzzles (sometimes related to the environment they're in, other times based on information you've found accross the manor).As you've most likely noticed based on the trailer and the other review, the presentation is top notch with only one glaring exception (I'll come back to it later, I want to start with a positive). I'll also praise some puzzles in the game for being extremely creative with their environment use. It really knew how to reward me for really paying attention to the surroundings of the puzzle.When it's an environmental puzzle that is. My main gameplay gripe with this game is that most of the puzzles are of the "key A for door A" variety with key A being a longwinded document you have to parse to figure out which part is which. The writing is excellent, don't get me wrong. But for every one clever puzzle that comes from putting context clues together, ten of them are simply "read the document and advance". I also really don't like how some puzzles can trigger a game over. Not because I'm afraid/tense (Saving is free as long as you reach a computer so there is no reason not to save at every single one you find) but because I know that if I die, I'll have to mash through a lot of cutscenes to get back to the point where I was. It's especially egregious since some "puzzles" where you die are as simple as "What is the color of Henri the IV's white horse?" meaning if they stumped me, I only felt annoyance at knowing that I had to scower the whole map again to find the one hidden piece of paper hidden under a couch.This is also where the open world nature of the game hinders it in my opinion. Not only is a lot of it based on observation (and it can get really annoying to look for a grey splotch on a grey background) but I also find the game really bad at telling me which puzzles I can actually solve and which puzzle I have to come back later to. The first time I looked up in the discussion forums how to solve a puzzle (at the 80% completion mark, give or take) I was basically told that I was trying to solve an unsolvable puzzle and that the one thing I put aside for later was actually solvable.My other minor gripes with the game are the shortcuts and the screen transitions.the former are unlocked by solving extra puzzles whose are either really easy or rely on math (I am not good at math). Unfortunately, that means that if you are unable to solve one of these, you could end up having to go the long way around every time you want to double check something, always walking in front of the same mocking locked door.As for the latter, they're the one visual flair that I openly hate. At first they're fine but after a story event (trying not to spoil), the transitions are turned into glitched effects that trigger every single time. Once or twice is fine, but after longer play sessions, my eyes end up killing me.But, with all that said, I still want to finish the game. and that's all thanks to the writing. It is excellent. Some scenes are beautiful and the mystery surrounding the manor is extremely well put together. Said scenes are also helped by a really nifty soundtrack that, unfortunately, only plays in certain rooms and certain events.If this novel of a review tells you anything, is that it's one mixed bag that I'm struggling to reccomend but also struggling to diss. In the end, Steam requests a yes or no and I can't find the heart to put a no, but be warned that my thumbs up may be misleading.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the full game with 16 hours of game time, I will say this game is magnificent.This game is certainly not for many people. The game will ease you into simple add/subtraction puzzles and all of a sudden you'll be doing scientific equations out of nowhere.Since this game is not fairly popular, it was hard to find guides on certain things I was struggling with which prolonged my game time. The story is a hit or miss. I didn't really follow it but I did get a grasp of what was happening. You can pet the dog. I really enjoyed that.Controls can be wonky. Especially since the game requires you to open the menu so much and there's no back button for some reason. I'm not really sure how the devs missed that crucial detail. There is a classic Resident Evil easter egg in the game and it was hilarious encountering it.There is 1 puzzle in the game that made me want to pull my hair out. I spent 3 hours on it. Devs, you know what I'm talking about. Never add something like that to your games ever again. Definitely a 10/10 if you want to twist your brain A LOT. I had to throw out a notepad for 99% of the game. Felt like I was back in school, which is a good thing in this case.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly brilliant blend of different ideas and styles and concepts into something beautiful and unique and new. The puzzles are well designed, and while I still haven't finished the game, the "aha" moments right before wildly wonderful cutscenes are definitely gonna stick with me. It's the best game Cosmo D and Swery never made. I can't recommend it enough. Can't wait to get back in and melt my brain and lavish my eyes again.Edit: Just beat it. 10/10. 2024 might be the best year for games yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A bizarre but captivating puzzle box that just keeps getting more complex as I play it. The game evokes old-school design with some modern quality of life keeping the game from feeling clunky or deliberately obtuse. Puzzles get increasingly challenging as the game progresses, but they never become frustrating or require massive leaps of logic in the entire ~20 hour runtime.If you are into puzzles, you owe it to yourself to check this one out. And don't forget to bring a pencil and scratch paper - you'll need it!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: finished the game and i will say that playing this was very refreshing from other types of games i've been playing. the story is great especially for a murder mystery, which is something i dont often look into. puzzles are definitely a challenge and i'd bring in my fiancee to help; i did not want guides whatsoever (but got hints instead but yknow). i'd spend a single day with the game running for over 8 hours just cause i'd be stuck on a few puzzles; highly recommend ![OLD] only got 2 hours so far and i really had to lock in when the pen and paper had to be whipped out. also lots of math... struggling but it feels good solving the puzzles
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more of a puzzle game with spooky vibes than it is a horror game, but it also happens to contain the scariest/stupidest jumpscare of all time I actually screamed lmaoLorelei is unlike anything I’ve ever played before, like you’re reaching into an alternate dimension where game design conventions diverged down an entirely different path and pulling this game out. More games that trust the player enough to let them get stuck and figure stuff out on their own please!
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

_childDocuments_.review:
The stage is set. Imagine an old baroque manor, perhaps a hotel or a museum, somewhere in central Europe. A woman wanders in search of answers. 

An international auteur. What does he want?
An aristocratic artist. Who killed her?
A vagabond illusionist. Who is he?

And you, the wandering woman. Why are you here?

Watch carefully, observe. Numbers. Patterns. Puzzles. Are they all part of a macabre game, a complot, a simple treasure hunt?

We invite you to take a journey into the nightmarish surreality, and answer these questions to solve the enigma of "Lorelei and The Laser Eyes".
_childDocuments_.name: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes

name: Invector: Rhythm Galaxy
detailed_description: From Warner Music Group and award-winning indie game studio, Hello There Games, comes the next exciting chapter of the critically acclaimed rhythm game series, Invector: Rhythm Galaxy. Navigate breathtaking, celestial worlds to the beat of chart-topping hits from today’s most popular artists, including PinkPantheress, Charlie Puth, Duran Duran, and more. Discover fresh new tracks from tomorrow’s biggest stars on a cosmic trip where every note guides your way. Play solo and master the beat of every song or put your party in hyperdrive with up to 4-player local multiplayer, where exhilarating head-to-head competition comes to life in your living room. And with a range of difficulty levels to choose from, Invector: Rhythm Galaxy offers a fun challenge for players of all skill levels. Turn up the volume and light up the stars this summer. Invector: Rhythm Galaxy launches July 14, first on PC.
