_childDocuments_.review: - 9/10This is an in-depth review for the game Live a Live, by Square Enix and historia.GAMEPLAY: 8/10   You play the game as seven different characters, from the stone age to the distant future, in any order. This game is a lot like Octopath Traveler, with many characters and an interconnecting story.   In fact, this game is Octopath Travaler's predecessor. Being released in 1994, it has never been released oficially to the west until 2022.   As stated, you have seven chapters to play before you go to the second act of the game. The chapters vary greatly in tone, mechanics, gameplay and story, providing different experiences and feels for different tastes.   The battling is done inside a grid, where positioning is key. In this game you don't just simply take turns attacking. You can move around, attack, wait or even pass your turn to an ally. This mechanic adds another layer of depth to this turn-based RPG.   There are plenty of status and damage types, and while this may seem overwhelming at first, some chapters are very good at teaching these mechanics to the player.   In fact, this is an excellent RPG for beginners, as the inicial chapters take care of explaining basic RPG mechanics in an easy and intuitive way, with no slow or boring tutorials.   The game respects your time, and there's no need to grind for levels. Battles and bosses never feel too easy or too hard. Also, the moves are very varied, creative and some are very funny.   On the other hand, you have a modest run time from the game: approximately 30 hours. While this is fine by me, some people may not consider this to be enough, because other RPGs provide way more entertainment time (Tactics Ogre Reborn, Legend Of Zelda TOTK, Elden Ring, Dragon Quest XI).   Though I would remember you that 30 hours is the industries standard.   As you play different chapters, you really don't have a way to make many builds. Even in the second act the characters are oriented to an optimal play style, and one or two can be somewhat changed to fit another playstyle. If you like messing around with builds, this game is not for you.   You have a limited pool of items, compared to other games. There are enough, but not plenty.   I  also missed having a button to sort my items in the menus. It felt like a mess sometimes.GRAPHICS: 9/10   The latest release of Octopath Traveler II and now Live a Life consolidate the HD 2D style. The character's pixel art is very expressive and beautiful and the 3D textures of the overworld compliment the sprites very well. Moves' and powers' VFXs are rendered in a very beautiful and colorful 3D, making this game feel a little more modern.   Menu interface is organized, beautiful, and most importantly, makes a lot of sense. It's simple but intuitive.   You can smell from the beginning of the game that Live a Live has an unique art direction, one that has a lot of personality and probably will age very well.   While I can't personally identify any flaws in the graphic department, I believe the HD 2D style still has a lot to show and improve, in order to really be flawless.SOUND: 10/10   This game's music was composed by acclaimed game artist Yoko Shimomura (Kingdom Hearts, Mario and Luigi, Legend of Mana). Rumors say that the original .midi files were lost and so the music was composed from scratch.   The orchestral tone of the music ranges from epic, emotional and even scary and it's not a strech to say that it the music carries the game.   The voice acting is clearly competent. The english voices are good, but if you like anime - play in japanese. The japanese voice acting carries a ton of emotion, and may even make you cry at times.   The SFXs are great too and really improve the game's quality. The characters' screams, hits and sounds have depth and impact. The buff sound is amazing to listen, too!   It even has a jukebox if you want to listen to the game's tracks.REPLAYABILITY: 5/10   Once you have played the story, you'll see that it is very concise. It has a definite beginning, middle and end chapter. you can make some changes in the last chapter and even get a total of three endings, but for most people beating the game once will do.   There's not much that's subject to player's choice in this game and, therefore, not a ton of replayability to be had. But it's in-line with most RPGs in the mark.ACHIEVEMENTS: 10/10   If you like achievements, there are no dumb or stupid achievements in this game. All are story related and none is hard to get. You don't have to fear buying this game if you are a completionist.   I've wanted to play this for a long time, but the dated graphics and bad translation from the SNES versions were a deterrant to me. Now I finally had a chance to play and all I can say is that I super recommend this game!   A pure gem to be enjoyed by newcomers and old timers alike!
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: I still have a few things to go but I can recommend Live A Live. It's a unique JRPG with both a unique combat system and a unique approach to its story. The game makes some decisions I was annoyed with but other than 2 sections (not whole chapters) it's a good time that isn't too punishing or grind heavy.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: The absolute gall of Takashi Tokita to direct two of the best JRPGs of all time (this and Chrono Trigger) within less than a year of one another. This remake was an absolute treat and absolutely the best way for me to experience this for the first time. One of the chapter's endings actually brought me to tears, it was downright beautiful. The one issue I really have (besides not really liking Edo Japan or Prehistory all that much) is that the game is only ever really hard in small moments, and there isn't any difficulty setting to account for that. But if you're not looking for a challenge and you just want to experience an absolutely transcendent story experience, brought together by a fun, if not remarkably challenging combat system, you owe it to yourself to play this game blind. I will treasure this experience for as long as I live.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: If i could explain Live a Live in short, I would say its what Octopath Traveler tried to improve on but didn't and its clearly evident.  The game starts off pretty basic with 7 story lines focusing on individual characters but bare with me. I wont spoil it but it improves greatly after that. Although the experiece isnt really long in comparison to Octopath (This game being only about 20 to 30 hours unless you're a completionist), the game nails the story line and the turn based RPG elements that we've grown ever so accustomed to. it was a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: A legendary classic, with terrific updated graphics and music. I quibble with their need to redo all the game's formulas without really surfacing what they are, especially when so many of the damage formulas are *very* obscure and confusing, but considering number go up = damage go up and the original was even more obtuse, it's hard to complain. And Megalomania really is that hype. I personally recommend pulling out a guide once you hit the final chapter, but that's just my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remake/port showing all the other subpar ports out there how it's done. Having never played or really heard about Live A Live I went in blind and I'm better off for it. The only suggestion I might make is looking up which chapters to start with as some of the chapters can be more story heavy and may not be the best introduction.The performance is stellar even on potato laptop hardware, the sprite art is amazing, and the 2d/3d effects have really been mastered looking at Octopath 2 and Live a Live.Highly recommended for any JRPG fans or newbies alike.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: The comedy in this game is really good it made me burst out laughing a couple times. though be aware that the game isnt as long as normal rpgs its really short so if you want a long game to occupy you this isnt the game you want for the price they're selling for but if you dont mind the price and length then this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: An unique take on the RPG genre with a lot of heart. The game consists of 7, pretty short isolated stories, very referencial on movie tropes, and thus play very differently to eachother. On one story you gotta infiltrate a castle with the game becoming a non-lineal stealth mission, and the next you're welcomed with a full-on Street Fighter like character selection.The visual conversion from its SNES days to the 2D HD style worked great as well, retaining the spirit of the game with a fresh look. I'm hoping Square follows this trend with more of their older games (Maybe Treasure of the Rudras or Bahamut Lagoon?). The same treatment went with the music, Yoko Shimomura made some bangers once again.As for negatives, I believe the game leans too much on the easy side, with only a few optional fights giving any challenge, and one of the later chapters had a lot of flashbacks that for its short length felt unnecessary.But yeh! Overall I'm very pleased with the game and I hope more people get to give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't recommend this game enough, each of the characters bring a unique type of story telling and gameplay element that keeps things fresh. The presentation is 10/10, from the colours, the environments and the character sprites are just gorgeous. The way the story come together at the end is an amazing payoff that makes the foreshadowing throughout each of the stories make sense. For a game that I only saw a singular screenshot of to be interested, this game floored my expectations and then some. Each of the stories may be short but that doesn't mean the game itself is short.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: I heard about this game here and there but it was always put to the side while I checked out other games but after hearing that an hd 2d remake for the game was announced I didn't have an excuse to not check it out now and I can see why people were hyped for this remake.I love how updated everything is without losing much in the translation, and now with the steam release it feels refreshing to play at a high framerate with no slowdown.Fingers crossed for LAL 2
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: ive bought this game 3 times, twice on Switch and once for PC. I don't regret any of it. Each little story shows how good a short story can really be in just a few hours of gameplay.Voice acting is really good, but I wish it was more consistent. People who get VA'd in chapters only voice some of their lines, it's weird. Should have gone the 8path 2 route where ALL cutscenes are voiced fully.But aside from that, it's a short and fun little treat of a game. Oersted and Streibough should hate kiss. goodnight
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: A great short-but-sweet JRPG with some very unconventional ideas that generally work very well and one of the best payoff finales of any game I've played. As usual, the HD-2D style is gorgeous and the music remastering is perfect as well. The voice acting is very good in both languages, although the English text really does not line up with the Japanese VA which can diminish the impact of lines on occasion.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: I played this emulated almost 20 years ago thanks to fan translators since this game never came out in english, and I was just blown away by this amazing remaster of such a legendary classic. Everything about this, it's just pure care from the developers, while keeping true to the original. I'm so happy they decided to release this to PC.Now if only Namco would hop on the bandwagon and release all those legendary tales games stuck on console. Perhaps one day we will see Tales of Destiny 2 in official english..
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent, unique RPG made up of several bite-sized 1-3 hour RPGs (influenced by various genre tropes) that eventually link together for a big conclusion.Has good individual stories and a really strong greater narrative, an incredible soundtrack by Yoko Shimomura, surprisingly good voiceover, some really nice-looking 2.5D visuals and a functional PC port, because that's something to make note of these days, apparently!100% recommended for people like me who can't typically stomach 80-hour RPGs and want something short and satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: It's a faithful and beautiful update of the original SNES game. The $50 price tag is a bit much even for a big fan of the original game though. I really enjoyed the original but bottomline, this in its core is still an older game and it shows. The hefty price tag puts it in the same range as Octopath Traveler and it's even MORE expensive than Dragon Quest XI. What??? As much as I enjoy LAL, the completion time for this game is much shorter than current Sqeenix or older Square games. Most folks will likely play this once and put it away forever, unless you really enjoy replaying LAL the full price is too much. $30 is much more feasible. (I bought my key from GMG around that price point) I 100% the game in about 23 hours, but might take longer for those new to this game.Differences from the original:The immediate obvious standout is the Ocotopath-like aesthetic. It makes the game look really gorgeous with the amazingly detailed background. They also managed to make the behemoth from the space chapter actually intimidating and scary. The new soundtrack is wonderful as well. The minute I hear that opening intro given that orchestral treatment it gave the goosebumps. Megalomania still blows my mind. I'm slightly sad they don't give you the option to swap to the original OST, but it's fine. Some really big name voice actors were hired to voice EVERYONE (except Cube), probably where most of the budget went.  The The ability to skip cut scenes is pretty sweet. There's an additional boss in the final chapter. It's not some super difficult EX dungeon type boss, more an additional story related thing in the final chapter. The localization is ok. They did make some slight changes but I think it's still within acceptable range. Runs well on Steam Deck for those that are curious.
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

_childDocuments_.review: Seven different stories featuring different protagonists, time periods, and gameplay styles await. In The Wild West, a wanderer with a bounty on his head fights for his life. In the Twilight of Edo Japan, a shinobi undertakes a secret mission. Experience these tales in any order you choose—the adventure is yours to control. What other stories will you uncover on the horizon...?
_childDocuments_.name: LIVE A LIVE

name: Voidwrought
detailed_description: Join Our Discord! About the Game The coming of the Red Star heralds a new age. Emerging from its cocoon, the Simulacrum is driven to collect Ichor, the blood of the gods, from the monstrosities who hoard it. Voidwrought is a fast-paced action-platformer with tight traversal, varied abilities, and formidable boss battles. Find and equip powerful Relics and Souls to customize your playstyle. Excavate into the rubble of the Gray City to construct a shrine filled with loyal followers. Delve Beneath the Surface Descend below the star-scorched surface and explore the multidimensional depths below. Witness the corrupted revelry of the Court, lose yourself in the icy tunnels of the Old Waters, and discover the grim fate of the Abandoned Expedition. With sharp controls, engaging exploration, and deep lore to discover, Voidwrought is a dynamic addition to the modern Metroidvania genre. Unleash Ancient Artifacts The world is filled with treasures sought by the learned, the brave, and the mad. Scour the halls of your shrine, rend the corpses of defeated deities, and hunt in the hidden corners of the cosmos to find objects capable of granting unique powers. Discover and equip over 50 Relics and Souls, from spectral weapons to passive buffs, to match your preferred playstyle. Build your Shrine Some still cling to the original faith. From a tiny cult, expand your influence and excavate further into the ruins. As you expand your shrine and followers, new secrets, rewards, and horrors come to light. Features Experience smooth, satisfying movement and tight controls. Explore atmospheric, hand-drawn biomes, from the star-scorched Surface to the biomechanical Abandoned Expedition. Fight over 70 enemies and 11 formidable bosses. Customize your playstyle with over 50 active Relics and passive Souls. Expand your shrine to discover new treasures, abilities, and secrets. Enjoy a rich, foreboding score by Anima: Song of the Abyss and Vigil: The Longest Night composer Jouni Valjakka.

Discover and equip over 50 Relics and Souls, from spectral weapons to passive buffs, to match your preferred playstyle. Build your Shrine Some still cling to the original faith. From a tiny cult, expand your influence and excavate further into the ruins. As you expand your shrine and followers, new secrets, rewards, and horrors come to light. Features Experience smooth, satisfying movement and tight controls. Explore atmospheric, hand-drawn biomes, from the star-scorched Surface to the biomechanical Abandoned Expedition. Fight over 70 enemies and 11 formidable bosses. Customize your playstyle with over 50 active Relics and passive Souls. Expand your shrine to discover new treasures, abilities, and secrets. Enjoy a rich, foreboding score by Anima: Song of the Abyss and Vigil: The Longest Night composer Jouni Valjakka.
short_description: Voidwrought is a 2D action-platformer set in a hand-drawn world of cosmic horrors. Explore the thawing ruins of the First Civilisation and strike down the gods that dwell there. Grow your powers, uncover ancient artifacts, and expand your shrine amid the wreckage.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece?. It is a decent Metroidvania, and there can never be enough good Metroidvanias. But it is probably no masterpiece. The game was programmed by a small team - essentially just three people. A typical indie game, even if the experienced publisher has ensured that many of the usual rough edges have been sanded down. You can also tell that fans of the genre were at work on this game. The visual similarities to the genre primus Hollow Knight are not entirely coincidental. The three developers are not rookies, of course - all of them have previously learned their trade with other developers and have now written their first game together.Deeply hidden in or under a mountain range is a mysterious city. Few attempt to enter, and even fewer have ever been seen again after their attempt. We play a - rudimentarily human-looking - creature that hatches from the sacred egg cell. A talking statue tells us to explore the city and awaken its siblings... the Keeper of the Shrines explains to us shortly afterwards that the city is inhabited by corrupt beings and that he will support us in setting things right (and silencing the Council of Elders). He also wants us to gather followers around us who will support us. It's all very mysterious, but some things are explained during the game, at least if you pay close attention and follow the conversations. There are always encounters with friendly creatures with whom you can talk about several points - or you can just keep walking without spending much time on unnecessary chatter (and thus never understanding the story). Information you find is automatically noted in the compendium. You can find out a lot about your enemies and the strange town by reading through all the entries.At the beginning, we can jump and strike with our claw-like hands. No dash, no double jump, no roll. All this (and much more) has to be learned first. As is typical of the genre, you have to continuously improve your character in order to stand a chance against the (relatively soon respawning) monsters. To do this, you can find and equip relics and souls. Dying enemies often leave behind Ichor, the blood of the gods, or other resources. A map is automatically drawn, and unusual locations are marked. The level of difficulty is quite high, especially at the beginning, but surprisingly it even gets a little easier as the game progresses. This is mainly due to the higher damage you can deal. At the beginning, your attack hardly deals any damage, and you must hit your opponents several times before they die. Of course, this often means that enemies can easily hit you, causing you to lose your life and wake up at the last save point. In general, you will suffer damage even if you only touch your opponents. The first skill you learn is a roll, but rolling through the enemy without taking damage is not possible. Your roll will be stopped by the opponent, and you will take damage before the enemy has even struck. The roll is therefore only suitable for getting away from the enemy to safety. Or to roll through narrow passages. Jumping onto the platforms is tedious. Even with the non-moving platforms, I always miss the mark, not to mention the moving platforms. Mega Man was easy in comparison! The bosses are quite interesting and, with a little practice, can be beaten. Provided you have the right timing and location, you can hit the bosses' vulnerable spots at the right time and eliminate them - and collect nice rewards for doing so.Hand-drawn Metroidvania that contains varied environments and challenging boss battles, with tight controls and full of hidden secrets to find. It is no new Hollow Knight, but a well-made representative of its genre, made primarily for experienced players who are not afraid of a little challenge. Lots of jumping in dangerous environments and a variety of different enemies are your daily bread as you explore a mysterious city.

_childDocuments_.review: I just about 99% Voidwrought recently. (missing one item on the map because of tedious collectable tracking + extremely hidden breakable walls)A very good attempt of Hollow Knight wannable Metrodvania.The art and map design is good overall, but there is some pacing issue + frustration in the beginning~ mid point of the game.One core issue of this game is it's TOO OPEN in the beginning of the game.  A good Metrodvania , like Hollow Knight, will start the game with a semi linear progression path , and branch out to open world AFTER they give you sufficient tools to traverse the world. In Hollow Knight's case, the normal pathing you'd take is Green Path -> Mentus Lord , which grant you access to air dash and wall climb . Unless you do some sequence break via poggling , you're are pretty much blocked off venturing into other Biomes UNTIL you go through Green Path and Mentus Lord. Dev make sure you have means  to traverse the rest of the world.Voidwrath does not do that.  Around 80% of the crucial traversal methods are either optional unlockable , or hidden at the edge of the world . I literally get Wall Climb and Double Jump after I already explored like 95% of the world already.  This makes my whole exploration a tedium to get through obstacles because I simply don't have the tools to traverse the world, and lead to lots of needless backtracking. Sometimes I venture into couple biomes without any means to progress and have to just turn back multiple times.Also bosses become too easy later on because our weapon upgrade is too op and our character has way too much health.  Healing is kinda weak in this game because you can't replenish the flask easily , and they don't heal much, so in return , dev just gives you so much health you can pretty much trade blows with bosses until they die , which take away all the challenge in the game.Some other minor issues including way too many extremely hidden breakable walls at very random spot with zero hint makes 100% completion super tedious .  Charms locking to 3 without any method to expand the slot kills the diversity of the build . We should be able to expand the charm slot later on, but given the bosses are so weak, maybe that's not very necessary, but nevertheless a wasted potential .Relic has some balancing issues too, with around 20% very good and 80% completely pointless. Also no means to upgrade the damage of the relics too = another wasted potential. Overall this game gives me an enjoyable 20 hrs~ adventure , but with some tweaking and polishing, it could have been so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: is a 2D action-platformer inspired by similar souls-like metroidvania games, and developed by Powersnake. Taking place in a hand-drawn world of cosmic horrors, you play as a shapeshifting protagonist on a mission to dethrone a lineup of false gods who apparently all missed the memo on staying in their divine lanes. But it’s not all smiting and slicing; you also get to expand your very own shrine, because who doesn’t want a cosy cult base for your loyal, slightly unhinged followers? With smooth controls and customisable playstyle,  satisfies the thirst for those looking to explore yet another fascinating labyrinth in the metroidvania subgenre.Rating: ★★★★☆The game is fast-paced, action-platforming at its finest, where you’ll dash, leap, and cling to walls like a caffeinated spider. With multiple multidimensional worlds being your playground, every nook and cranny could lead to a hidden treasure or secret room, making the exploration aspect of the game one of my personal favourites. Additionally, there’s dozens of collectible artefacts to choose from to support your playstyle, but once you reach the mid-game, the overall difficulty takes a nosedive. Nevertheless, between slaying false gods and digging up rubble to expand your shrine,  offers an entertaining experience—even if it gets a little too comfy later on.Rating: ★★★★★ stuns with its hand-drawn aesthetic, blending eerie beauty with cosmic horror in every frame. From the opulent, corrupted Court to the chilling depths of the Old Waters and the grim leftovers of the Abandoned Expedition, every area is a visual gut-punch. The game also serves up a collection of eerie enemies that could be straight out of your darkest nightmares—or your weirdest art class. Honestly, the world of  is like exploring a haunted art gallery where every exhibit might try to kill you—and you’ll love every second of it.Rating: ★★★★★The beautiful and spine-chilling soundtrack in  also enhances the game’s overall atmosphere. From the sinister hums of exploration to the heart-pounding battle themes, it’ll make you feel like you’re living in a nightmare... but a really well-composed one. It’s like your own personal soundtrack to existential dread, with music that pulls you deeper into the void.Rating: ★★☆☆☆With deep lore filled with forgotten gods and doomed expeditions, the world of  feels like a dark fantasy mystery novel you can’t put down—if only you had all the chapters. Its backstory is well written but cryptic, and the main story itself is a bit… elusive. With no clear narrative to follow, you’ll often find yourself wandering a lonely, desolate world, piecing things together like a detective without a case. Furthermore, the characters each carry a sense of mystery, with unique designs and backgrounds that spark curiosity. However, despite their potential, these characters are often underexplored with limited dialogue and involvement in the main story. Overall, while the lore is intriguing at best, the lack of a concrete storyline can leave the experience feeling empty and detached.Rating: ★★★☆☆ took me about 12 hours to reach the true ending, which, compared to other games in the genre, feels a bit like leaving a buffet just as you’re getting started. There’s no New Game Plus yet, but if you’re the kind who loves tinkering with different playstyles or making different choices in side quests by starting a brand new run, there’s some replay value to dig into. As a proud completionist, I squeezed an extra 8 hours out of the game by scouring every dark corner and crevice, which I honestly found to be an enjoyable aspect of the game. Now, considering its cost and playtime, I’d say it’s worth it even at full price—especially with plans for new content on the horizon.As a fast-paced action-platformer,  excels in diving headfirst into cosmic horror with its solid gameplay, stunning visuals, and a mesmerising soundtrack. The combat is slick, the customisation is satisfying, and the lore is well written—though the main story is about as clear as a foggy abyss. While the mid-game difficulty takes an unexpected coffee break and some fascinating characters don’t get their time to shine, there’s still plenty to love for metroidvania fans, especially if you enjoy searching for hidden treasure in every corner of a beautifully-crafted world. Short but packed with potential,  earns a thumbs up from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, I can't recommend this game.The first two bosses were challenging and interesting. The next two were average. And the rest (including the last one) I managed to kill just by continuously pressing the x button. They were definitely doing something in the background, but you can just ignore it, there's enough health and damage to kill them before they kill you.The slime wall-climbing ability provides access to almost the entire map, making the latter abilities almost unnecessary (the final mandatory boss can be killed before getting the wall-jumping ability).Slots for passive skills are too few, and they themselves cost too much at the merchant, there is no motivation to farm resources further.The logbook shows how many items are collected on which map, but fully explored rooms are not marked on the map itself (like in biomorph). At the same time, there is no special item, ability or at least the possibility to get a mark on the map with a missing item (as in crypt custodian).Also, I wouldn't classify this as a flaw, but some of the enemies and locations are so similar to their Grime counterparts that it's on the borderline between homage and lazy design.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty decent metroidvania with some caveats: -After the first first few boss fights you'll be so powerful that you'll just face-tank every boss (I killed the final boss on my first try, with 90% of my health still remaining..), the game would be a lot better if it was more difficult.-On the one hand, you've got a lot of non-linearity for a metroidvania which is great, however one ability in particular make others  irrelevant.  It was the third or fourth ability I found and it opened up most of the game.  ..So later when I got some of the more standard movement upgrades they were not very impactful because their role had been fulfilled with this better ability.  --To obtain the big damage upgrades you are required to do some logic puzzles, which is not the sort of thing I like in videogames.  I was able to fiddle them for 15 minutes and eventually get lucky to solve them, but I can see someone else just throwing in the towel out of annoyance.  It's always dangerous to insert that sort of thing into a different genre.. People buy this seeking a metroidvania, not a puzzle game.The music was a bit light/soft but it added a nice ambience and did actually contain some metal.  My favourite piece sounded very different to the others; The market area sounds lively and like it came straight out of Blasphemous 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Tough choice for me. But since I kept playing and beat the main story it has to be at least kind of good, right?The short version: The beginning will feel pretty unfair. If you are willing to go through some frustration in the beginning and have enough patience until you reach a certain point in the game there is a good chance you can enjoy it later on. If you concider yourself a treasue hunter and exploring is your jam then this is for you. The exploring aspect in Voidwrought is great. Secrets can be very hidden. If you are here for amazing combat keep searching for another game. The long version:To be fair, I started playing right after release. And the beginning of the game was soooo frustrating. Especially the first 5 gameplay hours in my case. The pacing in general didn't feel great and the difficulty balance between early game and end game is way off. The early game:There is just nothing to block or dodge any damage. The only thing you can do is to keep your distance since you don't have any abilities yet, start really low on health and don't do much damage. Often I found myself in tight spaces where it's basically impossible to avoid damage. If you're standing in the wrong place you take damage just because an enemy spawns inside you. Not once throughout the whole game I managed to avoid that. There is literally no time to react once you see where they spawn. I mean I just started the game, go at least a little easy on me.Plus I have to say the movement felt slightly off in the beginning. I can't exactly put my finger on it what it was but I got used to it later. Combat sometimes don't seem to make sense since there is contact damage and you have to guess where the hitbox starts and ends. For some enemies, especially the first boss, it's not really clear.I really wanted to love this game. The graphics are stunning! So I tried again and again.Pretty early I noticed that the world is just too open to explore. The map is not blocked off enough by something where you need a specific ability first to proceed. You are not guided to the areas where you'll find the upgrades you need to properly explore the world. 80% of the map I feel like I used cheesy methods to make my way through. Hoping to find at least one of the precious ability upgrades. I actually ended up twice in a place where I couldn't get out anymore because I simply didn't have the right ability found yet. I fell down while fighting mobs and couldn't get up anymore. Reloading the save file was my only way out.Well, that lead to A LOT of backtracking and wandering around headless, me guessing where I'm actually supposed to be or where to go. I felt so lost for a long time. The markers didn't help either. They told me where the bosses are - great. But how to get the abilities to be able to reach them? Good luck finding them early.The end game:Since I was searching a lot for the abilities and couldn't find them I focused on finding secrets instead. I got my health bar complete. I also found all places where your damage will increase before I was fighting a lot of the bosses.Means now I don't need to watch out to not take damage anymore. I simply can stand inside the chaos and spam attack. My damage and my health are high enough to do that. The boss fights: No challenge anymore. Just spamming the attack button. The end boss of the story I defeated in maybe 30 seconds by simply pogo jumping on it. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯Btw, the last abilities I found were double jump and wall climbing. If you've seen the map already you will feel my pain.So would I recommend playing it? Not really to be honest.I feel like it needs a very specific type of player that will be able to enjoy it. I was patient enough in the end and I like exploration. Since I focused on the exploration part for at least 70% of my playtime I was able to enjoy it. That's the only reason why I give it a thumbs up here.Overall if I look at the big picture and consider all the above I wouldn't recommend it to a friend. The pacing and the difficulty imbalance definitely left a bad taste in my mouth.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Voidwrought has solid fundamentals. Its two major influences are Hollow Knight (gameplay, art style) and Grime (environment aesthetics, music, mood). Voidwrought does well on all those fronts, so if you enjoyed those aspects of Hollowknight and Grime you'll probably have a good time with Voidwrought. That said, Voidwrought falls a little short of those predecessors without adding anything novel to the genre.One thing that frustrated me about Voidwrought, and this is my personal preference that you may or may not relate to, is being confronted with possibly important decisions with little/no context and no help online. _childDocuments_.review: Tentative recommendation. The artstyle, sound design, movement, and lore are gleefully and unashamedly inspired by Hollow Knight to a degree that is perversely shameless. Unfortunately they're also worse than Hollow Knight on every axis. I do not begrudge someone taking a shot at the king and missing, but when so little is done to differentiate themselves it makes the comparison stark, especially when the dash is all but a T-pose with some lines behind it and the grappling hook sends you in random directions. Boss designs are fairly striking with unique attack patterns and visual design, but unfortunately the vast majority of of them are HP sponges who tend towards Touhou projectile spam and the healing in this game is both slow and anemic. The map is fairly well laid out, with void shortcuts offering interesting ways to blip across the map though the actual fast travel system has an extremely slow animation for reasons I cannot fathom. It would be remiss of me not to mention that I had a fairly non-standard experience with the game, as I used an attack that makes a projectile you can pogo off of to skip straight to a midgame area and got both airdash and the Carrion-inspired ooze power very early. I did not find double jump until I had 95% map completion. I believe you are intended to find double jump about a third of the way into the game. I did almost every area out of order and the game was surprisingly cool with that, though it certainly didn't help the HP totals of the bosses to fight them with a below-average number of damage upgrades. I gave up on the final boss because even with every health and damage upgrade it was still an uninteresting war of attrition. This is not Radiance. You don't get opportunities to heal from successfully hitting the boss. Dial it back a bit. Overall you could do worse, though even among B-tier metroidvanias I'd recommend HAAK, Biomorph, Moonlight Pulse, and Zau before this, to say nothing of Nine Sols.

_childDocuments_.review: Voidwrought is a highly competent Search/Action game, with an appealing artstyle, and an interesting world.  I will be honest, Voidwrought does not do anything you haven't seen before, but it knows what it wants to do, and does it well.  It is a Search/Action game that leans heavily on the "swipe your sword down to bounce of enemy heads and spikes" mechanic that you have probably seen before, most likely in Hollow Knight.  Especially early on in the game, you are not very agile and have somewhat limited movement options in combat, and mastering the downswipe is essential to getting through the first few bosses.  I had fun playing through Voidwrought, mostly on Steam Deck, and I really loved the art, especially the look of the main character.  Once you are powered you have a lot more abilities that let you move through the environment at a faster pace, making it a breeze to go back and look for more secrets, and there are quite a lot of secrets.  Good game, looks good, enjoyed playing it, well worth the purchase.7/10

But when you do find collectibles, they aren't even rewarding - why is there like 5 types of currencies for the same shop items? And the special attacks were mostly meh, not satisfying to use.The game offers nothing new for me at least, it felt a bit tedious and perhaps even AI generated. Sry for harsh review.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello everyone! Following my play-through of Voidwrought, I wanted to share my thoughts on it!As always, a video review has been created, which you can watch by following this link: For those who do not wish to watch the video:Playtime: 8 hours and 30 minutes with one ending (an additional two to three hours for the second ending)Completion Rate: 89%Pros:- The setting of Voidwrought is just drenched in Lovecraftian dread, featuring some of the most beautifully hand-drawn biomes I have ever seen in the genre, with each area evoking its own brand of degeneration and existential terror that results from the tainted touch of grand abominations beyond one’s understanding. Special note goes to the various characters that populate this sanity-shattering realm, each one standing out in terms of design and, at times, personality!- The world is not only beautiful but also home to an ungodly amount of secrets and collectibles, from health and damage upgrades to powerful accessories. - The game features a sort of base-building cult-themed mechanic with which you expand your home area piece by piece according to the number of followers and amount of Ichor you have at any given moment. By doing that, you open up new paths that may lead to collectibles, hidden areas as well as new NPCs that will offer assistance to you. I have to admit I truly enjoyed that aspect of Voidwrought and found myself constantly curious as to what sort of secret I would be discovering with my next expansion.- The game’s map is very user-friendly and functional, with clear distinctions between biomes, proper marking of special rooms, such as save, fast-travel, ability acquisition and vault points, as well as, thankfully, the option to place your own manual markers of diverse visual styles, which was a life saver since Voidwrought’s exploration can be quite challenging, especially when it comes to finding certain hidden rooms concealed by breakable walls that can be tricky to spot. I didn’t get to find anything that allowed me to see collectibles on the map, so I highly recommend you start using the manual markers from early on.- The game also features a very handy fast travel system that unlocks within the first couple of hours, which allows you to jump around the biomes via some special rooms. You can also unlock one more form of fast travel via the base-building system, through which you can use the game’s mirror save points to travel between the save point of your base and the last save point you used in the map, which can be helpful at times though I didn’t use it that much.- Voidwrought is one of the most open-ended metroidvanias I have played recently, featuring an incredible degree of non-linearity, meaning that you can go about the discovery of the world by carving your own path to a large extent. That means you can find creative ways to access areas for which you may not have the proper ability to do so at that moment, for example by pogoing off enemies to reach high places even though you may not have the double jump or climb ability yet, something that offers an immense sense of freedom.- Combat wise, I’m glad to report that Voidwrought tries to go the extra mile with significant success. On a basic level, you get a lightning-fast melee claw combo with which you can tear your enemies apart in satisfying fashion. On top of that, you also get the aforementioned relics, which bring a variety of different effects in combat, such as producing light beams that set your enemies on fire, augmenting your claw damage and throwing explosives, among others, effectively bringing ranged attacks into the mix. Of note here is the responsiveness and accuracy of the pogo mechanic, which I found incredibly useful against certain enemies. Healing is carried out by pressing down a specific button which allows you to channel your healing shards and restore your hit-points.- Boss-wise, I’m beyond elated to say that the bosses I got to fight were not only visually stunning but incredibly fun to duke it out with as well, each one featuring a healthy range of attacks that kept things interesting and required good observation of certain animations that telegraphed each move-set in order to make sure you emerged victorious. Main bosses aside, there are also several optional big bads for you to discover and take down, which is a big plus.- I do wish to mention one more thing that I truly enjoyed to see in Voidwrought in terms of quality-of-life functions for the players, and that is the region tab located in its menu. The reason I make special mention of this is because this tab actually shows you the completion progress you have in each separate area, which makes it easier for you to track your progress if you intend to go for 100%.Cons:- In terms of platforming, I didn’t really experience anything extraordinary here, though, to be honest, part of the reason for that was the aforementioned climb ability which, once acquired, pretty much makes traversal of the environment quite trivial and can be used in place of most other abilities, with very few exceptions. In essence, even though there were some acrobatic segments that would have been a bit challenging otherwise, they were made easy by that particular ability that had me jumping off walls like a madman without a care in the universe. I have mixed feelings in relation to that skill since, on the one hand, it made the whole world my playground but, on the other, it reduced platforming difficulty to nearly non-existent. That aside, I do have one more minor complaint here, and that has to do with an area called The Void. During the preview I made a month ago, I mentioned how platforming in that biome was a bit finicky due to the platforms being lined by eyes that didn’t match the actual circumference of the platform, which led to me constantly being unsure if I was landing on solid ground or not and resulted to a few falls that could have otherwise been avoided. In this final version of Voidwrought, The Void got much darker and visually rough, which made it even harder to know where you’ll be landing, though I will admit that the developers increased the number of platforms across it so, ironically, I didn’t fall to my death as much as I did previously. Still, I would have preferred a more visually clear area.- I do feel the obligation to mention that Voidwrought features what I like to call cage-fights, which refers to the fact that, from time to time, you’ll get locked inside a room and have to fight a few waves of enemies before you can move forward, which I know is something that some people may not find appealing, though I didn’t mind it.- Though I did enjoy the bosses, I did feel like their difficulty became progressively easier the more upgrades I acquired to the point where I could face-tank the attacks of most of them while dealing lots of damage with my basic combo as well as relics. I still had to be careful for a few of them, but nothing compared to the earlier boss-fights which could quickly end you if you weren’t careful.- The overall feeling of gradual reduction of difficulty as I got progressively stronger kind of chipped away at the oppressive atmosphere of the game's world.- I did not like the rotatory puzzles you have to solve in order to open the vaults. I consider them too complex and a momentum stopper.All in all, a great addition to the genre!

_childDocuments_.review: For the price I guess you'd be a grinch to grumble, but I'm not sure what happened here.Started off very well, and then kinda just loses it in the middle. The art is great, the combat and initial bosses are well done... but then the sense of balance goes nuts. You get way too many health points and because of how the game mechanically works, you just stand there pummelling bosses with very little to kill you before you outdamage them.As for the ending... what the hell? I just randomly did an excavation thing and the worst final boss I've ever seen comes out of nowhere and the game is over? This feels like such a promising project that was cut way too short and had a diminishing sense of scope.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine, not a bad game by any means. Music and art are great. Gameplay is very obviously inspired by Hollow Knight.Game is quite short and quite easy, though. If you're into Metroidvanias for the map exploration and movement upgrades and collecting I would say it's a buy. If you want a brisk, competently done by the numbers metroidvania I'd also say buy.If you're into them more for tension and satisfying combat I would say pass. The combat has promise but the game is laughably easy after like 2 or 3 bosses. If you want a game that's longer than ~13-15 hours, I'd pass as well (took me 10 to true ending, a couple of those hours was rescouring map to unlock the true ending).

_childDocuments_.review: After 15 hours of game play i'd give a recommendation of buy this game, especially at a sub $20 price.  Standard flair Metroidvania with upgrades, exploration, and backtracking as you get new skills.  Character motion feels good and while combat start off hard, it quickly gets easier as the game goes.  Map is a great size and most of my playtime has been backtracking and trying to 100% all of the areas.  If i have to give it a con it would be the hard to find secrets. _childDocuments_.review: This is not a bad game. It's just definitely not a good game. Everything in this game felt tedious and boring. Once you get the ability to turn into a blob, all other means of travel aren't even necessary to beat the game. In the 7 hours I played, I beat every boss, got every portal except one I didn't feel like hunting down, and fully upgraded the hub. This game felt like A.I. made it after being fed the description of "Metroidvania" and "Lovecraft". Everyone that got this game was like me, and wanted something to tide them over until Silksong. This, unfortunately, wasn't it. Go play Nine Sols instead, that game is worth every cent.

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal little metroidvania. If you enjoyed games like Hollow Knight or Blasphemous, you'll definitely enjoy this one. It feels a little weird at the beginning, but, like most metroidvanias, really begins evening out and opening up once you grab your first few abilities.It quite clearly draws a lot of inspiration from Hollow Knight, you can tell just from looking at it, but you can draw a lot of inspiration from something and still end up having it be really good. It's fun. The map is big and well designed. It has a lot of secrets. Boss and enemy design, variety, and actual combat are definitely big winners in this game. It's not super hard- at least towards the end. At the beginning it's quite punishing, but once you find some health upgrades and some good Relics, it very quickly stops being hard. The final boss is... a disappointment? To be honest, unfortunately. Especially when compared to some of the other bosses. The true final boss if you fulfill a few objectives is definitely a step up, but still not amazing from a gameplay standpoint. From a visual standpoint though it's a huge improvement. The world and worldbuilding is also quite fascinating, and honestly, with all that in mind, the trip is very much worth the mild disappointment of the destination, in my humble opinion.Got... just about 100%- not quite but basically 100% aside from a few things here and there- in about 12 hours. I'd say it's worth the price of admission, though my $20 is not your $20, so if you feel like that's not worth 12 hours, then you can wait for a sale. This game is definitely worth a look, though.

_childDocuments_.review: This game goes down on my sleeper GEM of 2024! I grabbed this on a whim, and am extremely happy I did! Controls at first feel a little slippery, but once you unlock a mechanic or two, everything feels amazing! I love the art style, and the combat can be a bit infuriating at first, but with a few passive abilities, like dodging iframes, makes this an extremely agile to mold to your play style. I HIGHLY recommend this game! A very true METROIDVANIA. There are soft gates for progression, but if you're creative and lure enemies to areas, there's not many locks from letting you openly explore. It's both good and bad. I was completely avoiding the goal for days, which took forever to get back, but if I just followed linear progress a little longer, I would have had the ability to warp MUCH sooner. Still an AMAZING experience so far. I'm looking forward to finishing this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Voidwrought is an amazing metroidvania that is done justice, If you're still waiting for Silksong, then I suggest you hop right into this game.It has brought so many good memories of my hollow knight days, very solid controls, fun mechanics to use almost in every section of the map, lots of hidden secrets and lore to unravel.The boss art and designs were flawless, truly loved it, the soundtracks were top notch, I enjoyed every bit while 100% the game. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty nice game that's heavily inspired by Hollow Knight and leans in on the Lovecraftian elements of it. It holds your hand up to the first boss and then just sets you loose. It doesn't do the thing HK did where you need to find and purchase pieces of the map, but the number of branching paths creates the same feeling of being lost that people either love or hate. There's lots of hidden stuff and backtracking, and that's boosted by many traversal challenges having multiple solutions. So, things you miss on the first pass might be very different than someone else's play through because you had different power-ups or found a clever way to use oneMy complaint is that the later bosses have a lot of RNG spam, ambiguous hitboxes, etc. They're still mostly pattern-based, but the developers added annoyances to make them seem harder and are then going back and nerfing the health and damage of the bosses (and in a few cases toning down randomness) to balance completion rates. It ends up feeling like you're being graded on a curve. It's not a huge issue, but I could see it being one for people who want Soulsborne bragging rights or who still fall on the wrong side of the curve

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent Metroidvania in just about every way except difficulty tuning. The first boss is going to be rough on casuals (especially due to the weird hit/hurtbox). However, the world opens up afterwards and a little bit of exploration and the Assassin soul make you an unstoppable killing machine in a few hours, capable of face-tanking anything, including the final boss.+Colorful and well-animated+Really good music (on Steam, Bandcamp, and Amazon)+Great sound design. I love some of the sound effects.+The "base building" was kinda neat+Smooth movement+Huge open world after first boss and a bit of shrine unlocking+Two forms of fast travel+Couple of minor puzzles+Boss, save, and fast travel rooms usually obvious from doorway design+Multiple relics and souls to customize your playstyle+There IS an item to add iframes to your dash+Journal to track details on enemies, areas, journals, completion %'s+Multiple endings, and you can see all in one playthrough+Devs are communicative+Demo available+Can fast-scroll credits+Took me about 16 hours to nearly 100%, using a guide only to find one envoy+There are some minor choices to make, leading to replayability~Enemies are very spongy at the start~Some enemies have unusual hit and hurtboxes~No punishment for death. Only throws you back to last save room.~Game gets progressively faceroll easy after first boss if you explore~I found some of the earliest souls to be the most powerful~Likewise, only a few of the relics seemed useful to me~No boss health bars~No difficulty options, low or high~Hard to restore health between save rooms (only a problem early on)~Map isn't incredibly detailed (similar to Super Metroid)~Limited number of map mark types~100%ing is rather difficult and grindy, even with the item that shows map~Story is pretty vague-Unskippable splash screens-Loud noise after loading a save (I think it's from one of my relics?)-The cadaver enemies' acid puddles are nearly impossible to see-Envoys could have been a bit louder, per their journal entry-A few item descriptions are unclear or even misleading-How to unlock fast travel is poorly explained-How to properly finish game isn't well-explained-Analog sticks don't work in menus (at least on my controller)-Your icon on map can block marks you're placing-Endings are underwhelming, at best-Can't place map marks in unexplored areas. Would have been nice to have dotted lines for void passages.Played on:Win11, i7-14700K, RTX4060 Ti 8GB, 32GB DDR5-6000 @ 1920x1080Using PowerA Enhanced Wired Controller for Xbox Series X|S

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game worth your time. I had a lot of fun with Voidwrought - it's beautiful, plays well, and has a great sense of exploration. I think its nonlinearity is a bit detrimental though, I was quite far into the game when I acquired what felt to be some of the core abilities.Player movement feels mostly good, although you do retain a bit of momentum before coming to a stop making it feel a bit "slippery" at times, especially when trying to land on a single tile block. I did get used to it pretty quickly though, it wasn't really an issue after the first hour or so of play. Speaking of movement, I found this game's version of , although creative and interesting, to be painfully sluggish. I understand the intent with this ability from its visuals, but it was so cumbersome to move in this form I dreaded every time I had to use it. I really think it could be 2x the speed with half the acceleration and deceleration times.Hitboxes and hurtboxes seem fine on regular enemies but don't seem to line up with the sprites on some of the bigger bosses. At times it felt like a bosses hurtbox disappears entirely when it transitions from one attack to another, meaning if you're pogoing attacks you just fall into the boss and take damage (even though your attack sprite was well and truly in front of the boss sprite). The bosses go from challenging at the beginning of the game to extremely easy once you have some attack and health upgrades - the attack upgrades felt appropriate for regular enemies though as they are pretty spongy at base damage.A final and very minor gripe is the movement speed that the currencies fly towards the player. You can outrun these, and often I found myself waiting at each rooms exit waiting for the money to catch up with the player so I don't miss out on it. It's only for a second or two of course, but when it is every single room you definitely notice it.Those points aside, the pros vastly outweigh the cons with this game and I recommend Voidwrought. Smacking stuff is satisfying, the visuals and sound design are top notch, and it is a well crafted game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a less binary way of rating games on Steam. I don't hate this game. I think there are plenty of people that would like it. But it is not what I want out of a metroidvania in terms of gameplay.In my opinion, the controls aren't particularly tight, but maybe that means something different to me than to the developers. I can't tell you how many times I've landed, hit the health button, and it doesn't start charging. Maybe that's my own lack of coordination but it doesn't  like it.Probably I'm just not keeping up with the times, and maybe I'm just getting older, but when I game I'm not looking for something brutally difficult (I know, "git gud"), I'm looking for fun. Now, is it satisfying when I eventually killed the first and second bosses? Sure. Would I rather they were a tad easier? Yup.For instance,  and I think it might actually be really fun - and around the difficulty I'm looking for. There are some cool mechanics but my after-work exhausted brain just doesn't have the patience for it. I end up rage-quitting after a dozen attempts only to come back a few hours later and do it again.With that said I think the art, music, general aesthetic of the game is phenomenal, and frankly is really what's keeping me playing.Edit: Alright 15 more hours in this feels like a pretty solid Metroidvania to me, other than some general scaling issues. Like some others have said, the first bosses feel too difficult but the later bosses feel too easy. Still a fun, beautiful game to get lost in.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fantastic until the Time-Lost scholar boss. Finally, I thought someone made a Metroidvania where it was not a Dark Souls die fest but more about exploration like Metroid. This game was it, then it came. The boss is so hard for no good reason. There is no save point close to it. I like how you beat the first version (which takes three million hits including special items) and then two more appear throwing scrolls in eight directions with no way to avoid them. Also, there are no block/parry, or dodge-through attacks so, yeah....... The game flowed so well up until this point. In good conscious I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't how you do Metroidvania games. This game left such a bad taste in my mouth after the first boss took over an hour for me to beat due to its 5 phases, inability to heal myself, and a rinky-dink weapon that might as well have been a pool noodle. _childDocuments_.review: If this was a bad game I'd call it a Hollow Knight rip-off, but since it's good that means it's a loving homage to Hollow Knight. Really great art, movement is satisfying, there's some upgrades I haven't seen before in this genre...It's very non-linear -- I was going to say that it's a game with a lot of potential for sequence breaks, except the sequence breaks are so prevalent I think it's just non-linear. It seemed like there was at least two obvious paths to get everywhere, with a more available if you're good enough. I wouldn't be surprised if the speed running/challenge running community keeps this game alive for a long time.The only big criticism I'd level is that you get way too OP by the end if you collect everything. Honestly I'd suggest, to improve your enjoyment, to stop collecting health upgrades after you hit 6 or so, and don't equip the vertical laser spell, because it makes boss fights waaaay to easy.Speaking of, the boss fight design is kinda meh. I liked the Prince, but most lacked variety and the inability to respond to cheese (like the afore-mentioned space-laser).

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little Metroidvania very reminiscent of Hollow Knight that's occupied me for the better part of two weeks. Set in a Post-apocalyptic Aztec-Egyptian cityscape whose inhabitants have been forced underground following an unusual solar advent, with a nice mix of old fantasy and technological aberrations in its undertones. Gameplay is very simple in that you have a basic attack and two special abilities you can swap out as you find new ones, but I found it engaging enough, when backed up with the exploration and a great OST (please go listen to it if nothing else). At about the halfway point you become sufficiently upgraded as to render environmental hazards the biggest threat, so it may be a bit to easy for those experienced with the genre. My build started engagements by deploying a censor that rendered all enemies in an AOE more vulnerable to damage, then lighting my surroundings on fire with a jar of pitch. Cleaned house against most skrunklies and was very satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Metroidvania game at a great price.  When I first played the demo several weeks ago, I didn’t like it.  I thought the controls were too floaty and didn’t like the fact that you couldn’t crouch/duck.  I went ahead and bought the game after watching an in-depth review.  I’m glad I bought it.  It has turned out to be a fantastic Metroidvania for its price point if $20.  It’s not the same caliber as more expensive games like Hollow Knight or Bloodstained, but that is to be expected for a game at this price point.  Lower priced games tend to have smaller much smaller production budgets, and that’s something that you have to take into account when comparing a $20 game with a $40 game.  Things I would have liked to have seen are a few hints scattered around on where you need to go next.  There was too much wandering around aimlessly trying to figure out what to do next.  I also felt very overpowered after getting a couple relics about 1/4 of the way through the game.  The combo of the two relics made just about every boss fight a breeze after acquiring those items.  Those items (aim sure the developers know which ones I’m referring to) should not have been available until well past the mid point.Exploration was a blast.  It was always fun finding my way into a whole new area after thinking I had the map pretty much opened up.If you’re on the fence, do yourself a favor and give this game a try.  It is one of those hidden gems that seems to have mostly flown under everyone’s radar.

_childDocuments_.review: I previously left a very harsh and nonsensical review that is now deleted. There are aspects to Voidwrought I do like; the art style and the overall atmosphere are amazing. I never made it far enough to see how the gameplay progressed but I'm hoping someday I will. This is one of the first Metroidvanias I've tried to play, and I found it hard to get lost and easy to progress right up until I got to The Council. I was recommended this game on Reddit as being a good beginner Metroidvania but this is not the case. The Council is a ridiculously challenging first boss. Now, I expect to die at least a few times until I learn the pattern, but when there are multiple phases, inconsistent hitboxes, and platforms that don't let you land on them half the time, it gets pretty frustrating. It's not like I've never fought a difficult boss before, The Lingering Will from Kingdom Hearts II was a very satisfying boss to beat. Dev, I'm hoping you implement some accessibility features to lighten the difficulty of The Council, or just make the fight less difficult as a whole (but that might make people who love the difficulty mad).

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it doesn't commit the cardinal sin of the genre, which is having terrible controls. It does, however, commit the 2nd worst sin, which is being very boring. There are some frustrating design choices here. Why put a save point just far enough away from a boss fight to make running back to the fight a repetitive slog in its own right? Unfortunately, I played just a bit too long to get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Voidwrought feels like a game made by artists. The game looks great, but unpolished. The menus look like something somebody threw together in an afternoon, but the rest of the game is gorgeous. The lack of polish is everywhere. Game design, level design are all mediocre, and a lot of it seems like they're trying to play it safe and just pulling game design elements and puzzles from other games without thinking how they should fit together. Enemy designs are beyond boring; this game makes extremely heavy use of contact damage as the primary threat in the early-mid game sections. You don't come into interesting enemies until way late in the game. The writing and narrative follows the same direction too: it's too much style over substance, and worst still, the actual storyline (both endings) are about as stock standard as it comes: you either sacrifice yourself for the bad ending or take over the baddie in the good ending. There's nothing complex about it, which is criminal, considering how great the actual setting could have been.Now I'm sure you'll think this game sucks based on the amount of negativity in this post, but honestly, this is an average metroidvania that has great visuals and a setting that tickles the brain in all the right places. It's definitely enjoyable, just not mind-blowing. It's a fun weekend kinda thing, but I highly doubt it will generate its own legacy the same way Blasphemous, Ori, Hollow Knight, Metroid or Castlevania can. This will forever be relegated to the bin of hidden gems, and solid B-tier games when you've finished all the greats.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to be able to recommend this game to others, I really do, but I can't. It feels bad to say that after only 3 hours of Gameplay. But two of those have been spent on the same single moment.Firstly, the good, the art, while very hollow-knight clone-esque, is still unique, and the world (what I've seen, at least) is unique, with the surface world being an unexpected twist I did enjoy.Unfortunately, that is the only good part so far. The combat initally is standard fair, let down by high enemy health pools and a the "relics" that add spells being expensive to get from the merchant, which leads my to my second complaint in the initial few areas. The blatently misleading item descriptions. The first boss drops an item that, according to the discription, can be used for the games fast travel. What the game doesn't say initially is that the item DOESN"T. WORK. So you'll waste several minutes trying to figure out why you can't access it, Then, you have to backtrack all the way to your starting location again, be told why it doesn't work, and go find the thing that makes it. All of this has to be done with 1 single health refill/flask per life, as unlike hollow knight, you have no way to refill a charge, and each upgrade requires 5 collectibles, which you're unlikely..This leads me to the killer of my interest in the game, as that frustration was made worse by the Second Boss of the game. An Overtanky, fast, 4 phase boss fight, that expects the player to have mastered the floaty movement, perfect Pogoing of moving objects, and using the slide move (that cannot be used to avoid other enemies as it doesn't have Iframes for contact damage) and, on top of all of that bull, also spawns in enemies that take 6-7 hits to kill, and that prevent you from dodging due to the above issues. 2 of the 3 hours of gametime have been spent fighting this boss, constantly dying for all of the above reasons.I'm certain from some of the reviews, that there is much more to see in the game, but none of that matters when I'm trapped behind a ♥♥♥♥ boss, and don't have any incentive to go and explore, as it's a backtracking slog without the fast travel.If you're willing to slam you're head against the brick wall, go right ahead, but I can't recommend it as it stands.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really beautiful. Unique monsters, NPC, biomes, relics, and etc. What I like the most are the immersive music, and the fair difficulty of the bosses (you get overpowered if you roam a lot, so I'd say it's fair). During the first five hours of gaming, and MAN! Couldn't really get my hands off the controller.  And tomorrow's my exam for Immunology and Serology T^T. You know it's good when I sacrifice my study hours for a game! (Well, that's just academic negligence.) Anyway, I'm dropping a good review 'cause I really want people to appreciate this hidden gem! Enjoy the game, and wish me LUCK! ;)Edit: I didn't nail the exam, but I certainly nailed three bosses today. Worth it.Edit 2: 10+ Hours of game play. Okay, I've figured out some things that some people would like to know before buying this. I have four concerns: First of, controls are a bit "rough". When I say rough, you couldn't really control some mechanics like when you want to heal; there would be a two seconds delay before healing especially when you just ran or attacked, or even unleashed a skill. It's really awkward and might affect the overall game play, and yeah, what I'm talking about when you are fighting a boss. Second, I've encountered some game-changing bugs. These are those that might affect the player's experience when playing: 1. The objectives displayed on the map disappears randomly, like which bosses would you fight or places to go; 2. NPC(s)   appeared late than it was supposed to; 3. NPCs dialogue will disappear after interacting with a "stone" in some occurrence.  These are all of the bugs I encountered so far. Now, for the last part; this is just an opinion and preference. I suggest that when you die, there would be a marker placed on the map where you died. In some cases, I get lost a lot when finding the place where I died (not because I lost some money which is not a thing in this game) because I often die at a hidden area or mini bosses. There's also this inaccurate information on the mini map, it's not as smooth as I expected, your icon will just blink when you enter a new area. Overall, there's a lot to improve, but I would still recommend this game. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of promise and manages to be both visually and atmospherically stunning, but there are issues holding it back which make hesitant to recommend it.- The first major issue is that this game can be rather challenging. I could tell from the trailers this would probably be the case, but I was met with Souls-like boss difficulty quite soon after launching. And while the bosses aren't hard to a frustrating degree, it was tougher then I expected going in, which I found to be somewhat misleading.- The second major issue is exploration and objectives. Not only does this game do little to nothing to give you any sense of direction, often causing long hikes into new areas where nothing exciting really happens, but the exploration is also heavily reliant on backtracking after unlocking new abilities. This is of course nothing new for Metroidvanias, but the exploration here is tedious, as even with fast travel, getting from on area to another takes far longer then it needs to, causing multiple hours to be spent just trying to get back to old areas.There is a certain charm to this game, one which I still feel is there despite these things. That said however, the Metroidvania genre is vast and offers plenty of darker, more atmospheric titles that can scratch the same itch while having less tedium.

one of the best OSTs on my drive, mixed with fantastic ambient and effect design and a somewhat unexpected art-style that still manages to transport the cosmic horror (Giger meets Lovecraft) theme perfect.the main issue in hindsight is that the game kinda pushes you into a direction (at the start) where you end up in a place you realy should come back to later. meanwhile i recommended the game to two friends, who ran into exactly the same area(s) i stumpled upon (early); with the only difference beeing me already knowing where they should go instead. this might/will lead to enemies feeling very spongy in general; bosses and trash alike. as a general hint: Vaults. they are the most important thing imho. . each vault upgrading your general damage output substantialy and i do mean substantialy. i don't know the exact numbers, but it downright feels like a 30 to 50% net damage increase per vault you solve/unlock. this out of the way: i absolutly love the game (now).in a crowded genre (2D metroidvanias) it sits on the top. the world design is stellar and everything is filled with lore and athmosphere. every item has it's very own lore fluff text, npcs are out of this world and alien while still feeling conceptualy familiar and often enough hitting the cosmic horror note of indifference to "normal" live forms.the toolkit has mostly familiar stuff, but all with it's own void/cosmic-horror theme. instead of turning into a Samus-bomb-ball you turn into a black-mass-of-void-energy, instead of a slide across the floor you turn into a mass of tentactles and black void energy, etc. . the same goes for your spell- and perk-kits. there is a metric ton of different spells to find. from throwing bombs, to casting energy beams, summoning circles of light-balls or casting a gigantic sword.perks aren't just perks, they are "souls" and got most bases covered. you can even sorta kinda a solely spellcasting build using perks. the alien design of the protagonist and the world, the spells and collectables all together create a wonderfull picture that despite it's comic book grafic, feels still thick with cosmic-horror athmosphere (and some of the stuff is still brutal in all the right ways).as a metroidvania it also works once you get the early game going. there is hidden stuff everyhwhere and the world and it's mechanics cryptic in all the best ways. when it comes to exploration i think this might by now be my favorite in the genre.think Bloodborne, meets Alien, meets Lovecraft/Giger. you will talk to absolute outofthisworld-things, with deranged outer-plane-beeings and scientists that went to far. in a way even having different factions that you can "help", that all seem to have their very own motive (like the Grandbazaar and the Grey Pyramid).meanwhile not just improving your character but also re-building The Shrine, which opens up new options, like shops, upgrades or collectables and much more.there are still some issues, like some bosses beeing to much; to much stuff thrown around, to fast; and also some boss-ways are to long. which feels kinda like a waste of time. but the power-grind you go through it real and you will have a much easier time once you get some spells, vaults and traversal skills.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid entry into the genre. It has the pleasant quality of a well made Metroidvania where you always have something new to discover and new areas to explore, with new powers metered out at basically a perfect pace.
