_childDocuments_.review: I love this game's art style. I'm definitely bias towards purple hooded figures as well so that gets extra points. The music and overall atmosphere is awesome. In fact, they deserve more than a quick mention. I was playing this game on my Steam Deck at work. Sometimes I'd have to leave the game paused for a bit while I worked and I loved every track that played from the OST.The movement and vibe are definitely inspired by Hollow Knight and it's welcomed. Combat is simple, but certain enemy designs still make for great fights. This isn't in reference to the "regular" enemies you come across though. 90% of your combat is stabbing your weapon at an enemy that barely poses a threat to you. But the boss fights I've had so far were pretty challenging. And the "dance" was really fun with these bosses once you understood what you had to do.I know metroidvania fans either love or hate linear gameplay. I'm more of a fan of when games "nudge" you which way to go towards the next objective. This game has moments of "uhh where the heck do I go next" but also has moments where it literally highlights your next objective. So it's a toss up so far.I'm 7 hrs or so deep right now, so I'll probably update this review once I complete Voidwrought. As of now, 7.5/10. Overall it's fine and not something I regret getting into. It's not a top contender, and that's fine too.This is one of those games where I criticize it, because I truly think it could be great. I definitely have some feedback. I can tell a game has potential when I find myself criticizing it to myself or even complaining, but still playing the game 6-8 hours a day. Voidwrought is that. I have 18 hrs played now, and while I love certain things, other designs or decisions are questionable.Combat is simple, I don't mind it, but most enemy encounters are also simple. There's plenty of cool little spells/relics available but I haven't ever needed to switch off the first damage increasing Relic they give you and this one I bought from the main hub vendor which sends out a vertical red laser. Everything gets obliterated by that build and I haven't ever needed to rethink my setup for different situations.I don't mind "cage matches" in metroidvanias but I think this game could have sacrificed a few of them and instead added more bosses. A lot of these encounters I just spam my red laser and pogo all the enemies to stay safe in the air. I want to have trouble with a boss fight, then have that lightbulb moment when you figure out the right Relic and soul combination that'll give you a sweet advantage against that specific boss. This hasn't happened yet in my 10+ hours.The slither ability is bitter sweet. When I first got it I was excited because I immediately recalled areas I knew I could backtrack to with it. That's great design. But then you keep exploring and this same ability trivializes everything. You even pass by areas you could tell were designed with a double jump or grapple point in mind, but who cares I'll just jump on this wall here and slither on over. It's also not satisfying or fun, you're really just slowly slithering everywhere lol.I LOVE that fast travel is introduced early and fast travel points are plentiful. I love that save rooms and fast travel rooms are easily spotted while exploring with their purple/gold glows. I think the map is designed well and aside from the secret walls, it does a decent job of telling you which rooms you haven't been to yet. I think the excavation mechanic at the main hub is pretty creative and really enjoyed "coming back home" with money to see which new areas I could unlock.I'm going to end up completing and maybe even 100 percenting Voidwrought on my steam deck, and I'll recommend it as a 7/10 game. But I think it could have been a top contender with a few tweaks and couple more months in the oven.I haven't 100%'d the game but I rolled credits after beating the "last" boss. Quotations because I'm assuming there's a "true ending" finale. The last few bosses were way too easy to defeat. I didn't die to them and I think that's an issue. I'm not some god tier gamer, these bosses just had very simple mechanics and low hp, or my damage was very high. Either way, that satisfaction of defeating bosses and unlocking new abilities or finishing a game was just not there because of how simple these fights felt. I rolled credits without unlocking all the traversal abilities. I find that to be weird. I don't mind when there's post-game content, but I think the pacing in this game could be looked at. I was missing more than half the relics and crests (spells and perks) as the credits rolled. That makes me feel like I missed out on content before completing the game. But the incentive to unlock all these missing items is lacking because what do I need new spells for? The bosses are defeated. I think it's fine that the map is massive, but more often than not, backtracking and exploring wasn't as fun as it should be because you're pretty set once you get the slither ability and another that lets you punch out these purple bricks that often block important pathways. So I felt like I was exploring pathways _just_ so that my map was complete and not because I was excited to see what new upgrade/unlock was waiting for me behind the next secret. And speaking of secrets, there needs to be an ability that reveals all secret walls to the player once they've completed the game or something. It is _not_ fun walking around an already explored map and having to hit every wall to see if it breaks down to reveal another path. There needs to be more hints for the player that wants to 100% your game. Their time needs to be respected. There's already interactive maps to help players like that unlock everything, but 3rd party resources should not be required in my opinion.I enjoy this game, but I really want it to be great one day. I'd love to revisit it and experience any new tweaks/patches/updates/content. If any dev reads this, I hope I don't seem too harsh. I really think Voidwrought is good, but I want to see it excel. You have an awesome foundation here.

The world is pretty open and you can get powerups in different orders so it has good exploration.  Good music and sound.  You get a lot of different relics, which are essentially this game's magic, I felt most of them are pretty useless however because they are simply weaker than your basic attack which was disappointing,  There were only two I found very powerful for combat, and one that made travel easier.  Another thing I hope the devs change is make shops cheaper, I completed the game with 100% of the map complete but I only bought maybe half the items in the shops because I simply didn't get the cash, and that's with the item that increases money gain equipped most of the game so if you want everything you're in for a grind.So overall, if you like metroidvanias you'll probably find this decent. _childDocuments_.review: To get this out of the way, Voidwrought is very much inspired by Hollow Knight in almost all aspects of its gameplay though it manages to carve out a unique visual identity of its own (despite having a very similar style) and the overall mood feels strangely both similar and very different. You play a character that feels like a copy-cat of the main protagonist from Dead Cells going through a world eerily mirroring the decaying insect kingdoms of Hollow Knight, only here it's pyramids, zombies, and a very strong Lovecraftian vibe with you on the side of the monsters.As the game can't escape comparison to Hollow Knight, the brass tacks are that the game is around 10 to 12 hours long (took me 13 though I'm a slow player), the only difficult bosses are the first two, with the biggest spike the second one. After that, you collect so many skills, power upgrades, and health upgrades that you likely will beat every boss on the first try with the final boss almost comically weak by the time you reach him. Not sure whether that was just an overall bad balancing job or they didn't care anymore making them difficult enough (visually they all look gorgeous though).  Plot is dished out like in all Soulslike-inspired games via cryptic item descriptions or opaque diatribes from the various NPCs you meet. The game is very generous upon death, whatever you've collected and explored on the map will remain even after spawning at the latest safe points, so in theory, you can do a death run but given the low difficulty you don't really need to. There's lots of stuff to buy (relics are subweapons/spells, crests are power-ups) and various things to do. Even after finishing the game, I know based on the achievements I'm still missing at least one region and 2 or 3 bosses.This is really the biggest draw of the game. Exploration is king here and unlike most metroidvania, you can easily bypass bosses and just go spelunking, though with the adverse effect that by the time you get back to the boss you bypassed you're likely so overpowered he's a complete pushover. Still, every new area feels distinct, with its own set of enemies, and it's fun going around and just mapping out the game.Still, I hope they either patch the bosses somewhat or introduce a hard mode to make this more of a challenge compared to the joke that difficulty is at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: The latest review (51h of play time):This game is incredible. Despite some complaints about the late-game difficulty (e.g. it becomes too easy to play), I enjoy the exploration-based reward system. It's a great balance for both casual and speedrun players.The pros/cons remain the same as below.Final score: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Updated review (15h of play time):I must admit, my original negative review was completely unfair. I apologize to the developer team for my hasty judgment. I encourage anyone reading this to spend more than two hours exploring the game before forming an opinion. Many design choices that initially seem questionable will become clear as you progress through the gamePros:- An amazing exploration experience. After 15+ hours, I'm still enjoying it immensely. I can't recall another Metroidvania that encourages exploration as much as this one, prompting players to revisit seemingly familiar areas. Sometimes using differen routes! - Gorgeous graphics and music- Challenging bosses and unique "unusual activities" that you have to do to power upCons:- Some platforms still feel a bit too small and slippery.- While I understand the design choice, the inability to climb edges by pressing 'up' can sometimes makes platforming unejoyable.- A few elements feel out of place in terms of size and visual style, as if they were hastily added to fill space.- The default controller mapping feels a bit awkward. I remapped dash and other actions to make it more intuitive (a subjective preference).- After acquiring powerful abilities, some collectibles become less essential.Overall Score: 4/5 so far.I'll update this review once I've completed the game.Original negative review (2.8h of play time):I waited for this game and I really wanted to love it, but the mechanics, "slippery" platforms and the fact that the game was deliberately designed to use some structures that if permanently destroyed will not allow you to reach some artifacts is just bad idea in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. According to the ingame timer roundabout 10 hours with 86% completion. Overall I really enjoyed it. A few things still missing. At least one boss (according to the handbook there should be one more "herald") and also a few pieces of the map are still missing and so are som relics, souls and other collectible stuff.I think, it is a pretty cool Metroidvania. Not the best I've ever played but by far not the worst. The combat is fun although the mechanic is pretty simple, but I like the enemy variety and the relics add a nice touch to the combat.At the beginning it can be a little bit challenging and for my taste some of the standard enemies take quite a lot of hits, but there is a progression mechanic which will help here and actually makes the game way easier. For my preference even a bit too easy - especially in regards of the bosses. It doesn't need to be on dark souls level but at some point I didn't even need to avoid the boss' attacks anymore. As long as I am constantly hitting them, I can finish them sometimes even without the need to heal. It shouldn't be like that, in my opinion. I don't feel that I actually "outsmarted" the bosses or that I was playing quite well. It felt like that I just had more HP and made more damage while smashing the attack button.The "final" boss for example is ridiculously easy (I actually believe/hope, that there still is something left, when completing the game 100%).The big star of this game however is the exploration and map design. I really enjoyed exploring the game world and finding new secret passages and even whole new kinda secret biomes, solving the few puzzles and finishing some of the souls-like cryptic quests. Quite some nice surprises are waiting here and it was always exciting for me to go deeper and deeper. The eerie art style and atmospheric dark music helps a lot here.The metroidvania typical progression skills are mostly pretty much genre standard, I would say, but it is well integrated, although it feels like the controls are ignoring sometimes the input, which can be annoying from time to time. But what I did like the most about this type of progression system is that it doesn't feel so linear like a lot of other metroidvanias. I am not 100% certain, but at a certain point it is pretty much open and left to the player how they will progress and which abilities they will get next. In some cases it feels like you can also easily sequence break the game (for example when using the "bounce attack" to gain some extra height) but I am quite certain that this was considered to happen and adds some additional nice ways to progress throughout the game.

name: Parcel Corps
detailed_description: Skid onto the sun kissed streets of New Island, where three bicycle courier corporations are vying to become the biggest, most profitable business in town! Pick a side then lock handlebars forming two-wheeled rivalries in pursuit of market share, influence, and a modest income. But this honest struggle to make ends meet is swiftly threatened by the arrival of Rich Villainé, CEO of crude oil exploration company Polar Petroleum PLC. Villainé’s political ambitions place him on a collision course with New Island’s bicycle messengers. As the details of his maniacal plan become clear, it will be up to you, humble player, to *checks notes* save the world! All while delivering delicious food, valuable parcels, and sensitive documents in 32 minutes or less… 3 Factions Sign away your soul to one of three rival courier corporations: Anglo-Australian start up Wallaby Wheelers; Brooklyn’s own East Coast Couriers; or the ultra-professional, pan European, Das-la Post. Free-flowing cycling Negotiate levels with a stylish, expansive skillset. Catch air from rooftop ramps, slide under articulated vehicles, defy gravity by riding along walls, and create your own lines through a bustling, vibrant city. Triumph over totalitarianism! Embark on a journey satirising the gig economy, media influencers, big tech, and more! With an outlandish villain and totalitarian government to overthrow, it’s up to you to save the world one parcel at a time. Colourful, stylised city to explore Fight for control across 8 different regions, completing jobs for demanding business owners and legally-distinct-from-recognisable-IP-but-just-in-case-our-legal-email-address-goes-to-a-defunct-inbox side characters. We’re sure you’ll agree there’s more than enough here to justify our very reasonable suggested retail price!

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend the game itself, I do think it is too expensive and for its price there are some omissions that I don’t quite understand. Mainly there being no graphical settings to speak of which in 2024 and at a $35 tag that’s pretty nuts. It’s steamdeck playable but it varies from the 10fps range to 47fps range and it destroys the battery. I went down to 23% in 80 minutes. Compared to bombrush cyberfunk I could get 6 hours out of. A lot of this I think rally is tied to that annnnnd the biggest caveat being…It’s an always online game which is very strange. It is cool to see other riders around the world but it doesn’t make much sense as you cannot customize yourself you all named characters that you pick from so it’s always online simply for aesthetics and to challenge other riders. Again not a huge deal exactly but for deck it is bad and for preservation it’s also bad. I recommend it because it does work well, the satirical comedy is pretty good and let’s be honest we don’t get extreme sports style games often if ever so for that reason I’m on board. I almost wish it was early access because while the foundations are good so far I don’t really no how expansive it gets. The map doesn’t seem all that large, customization is just on the bike, tricks are pretty much just bar spins, wheelies are very strange and not super intuitive and are hard if not impossible to land in due to it being tied to jump. that said I am early on but I do struggle to want to hold onto it simply for the price. At $20 this is an easy recommend. At nearly double ehhhhh I dunno. It’s release season and while it stands out for what it is there are a boatload of good games both aaa and indie coming out in rapid succession right now and I’m not sure it’s price is proper. It is fun though for sure.EDIT: with more time playedAfter spending a few more hours with it now on my desktop as well id say everything still stands and a few new things have cropped up.performance on the PC is not great im running a 13700k and a 4080 and my fps has topped out at 75fps at 3440 x 1440 ultrawide, this to me is unacceptable for how it looks and the fps fluctuates pretty wildly generally though it is playable i just don't understand why its so bad for how it looks and i find it does affect control latency at times even if the frame rate itself is manageable. world does have more to it than i thought however it is zoned, so for the performance again it is concerning, id think a seamless open world would make this so much better overall as just riding though everything at once would feel good even without an objective but it is all sectioned off. I would Rather have a Thought out Tightly Designed smaller world than a Large open one with no direction but i cant help but wanting more out of the current design choice as i think the zones are Good i just wish they were together for a Next step experience. objectives vary by how the Package is handled, some you trick to mix, some you cant drop in speed, some you cant take damage, ext. however this is kinda the game, there hasn't really been much deviation in the past 6 hours or so and id guess there wont be much more for the duration. from zone 1 to 2 the Objectives were exactly the same. get 3 shops on board then 7 then 10 then do rushes til you get the next zone. this is fine in theory but id still prefer opening a bridge or something like in GTA and just cruising over to the next instead of loading in. customization still hasn't been much of anything. even for just the bike going into the second zone i haven't found or unlocked any new items for it or decorations still just the same from the first. to that end bike parts don't seem to change anything other than cosmetics so the bike itself doesn't have stats or change in anyway. rider doesn't either, you don't get new skills, new stats, new tricks, anything really at all. So the Soul this is another thing i Find it lacking, its also something i think Cyberfunk Struggled with but to a lesser extent. This game has so many Weird and Wild Shop owners, like half ape creatures, Talking Oranges, a guy with Pizza for a face, a Robot like some out there creatures. but the world itself does not have any of this, every npc is just The same kind of cut and dry regular person, the zones while they look good and are sorta of themed its twords like commerce or construction it isn't like Embraced by how weird the characters are if that makes sense. like the world exist but these characters don't feel like they exist in it they feel completely separate. which is a shame because they are wacky and interesting and i just want the world itself to feel like they belong here, think of like borderlands, or platoon, or sunset overdrive. every part of those games feel like a universe everything belongs to here i do not feel that and i wish i did.  again i still like the game as a concept and less so as an execution but i really am struggling to understand where $35 price tag comes from. if its the Live Action cut scenes peppered in maybe but i would have forgone that for a much more Robust and cleaned up experience. im gonna keep checking in but i really hope they refine this rendition because it is something id like to personally see succeed.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, there is enjoyment to be had in this game. And I could see people liking this game more than I did, but it just falls flat for me. I have 2.5 hours in this game at the current time and I have requested a refund as I’m not sure the level of fun I’m at is going to increase or just be drained the longer I play.Riding around on your bike and delivering packages is a lot of fun, but while it seems they have nailed the core concept every extra degree seems to break. The general gameplay is to go to a business, pick up a job (can start here after you do the initial business mission), and deliver a package. This is pretty much the basic mission and eventually you can start doing missions for businesses with fragile packages,missions where you deliver multiple packages, missions that require you to go back and forth between customers and businesses, missions that require you to maintain speed, missions that require you to do a few tricks (but not too many), and a mission that requires you to put posters on walls. And all these missions by themselves are fun if not maybe a little too easy, like I spent some time grinding rep and it felt very brainless to get from point a to point b delivering one package. But besides just fun and an excuse to traverse the map, why are you doing these missions?Money is the biggest motivator in this game (there is a second one but we will get there). And money is seemingly spent on cosmetics like I expected, though I’m sad I don’t think you can customize your character at all. I really thought the cosmetics I would be working for would maybe be hats, clothes, and maybe different models, but it's all spent on your bike. Well I didn’t get far enough to see all the bike upgrades and cosmetics, but the ones I had access to already weren't enough of a carrot to dangle in front of me. Not to mention the fact that when you go to the bike customization menu you cannot buy cosmetics where you can see how they would look on your bike, instead you have to engage with the phone menu that takes a bit of practice to do while riding your bike (though I do think that makes sense). And that small separation between where to buy and equip made me immediately disregard my want to personalize my vehicle. I will also state I didn’t feel I had an incentive to particularly do any job well as I don’t think doing a job faster or maybe with more tricks got me any more money or loyalty. There was no S ranking a job or anything so it only really behooves you to just get the job done and collect the measly cash prize. But there is a second reason to do the impromptu jobs besides money.Besides impromptu jobs there is a second mode called delivery rush, which is probably what you expect. It's a mode where you have about a minute and can take 3 jobs at a time from anywhere. It can be a lot of fun the first few times around a map, frantically trying to find jumps and wall rides to get around obstacles quickly before the time limit. And doing impromptu jobs before and after these rushes allow you to get more extra time from businesses you have high loyalty with which can help you keep going for a while. But my problem with this mode is as far as I can tell it throws out all the interesting job types. Instead of having to deliver one package that requires you to maintain speed while another requires you to go back and forth between the pizza place and customers, it's always just “get package, go to customer, make it before time”. Which means you have now been grinding to get stuck doing the most basic mission a ton of time in a min (plus extra time you now get to keep getting). And besides that being a kinda fun incentive to see how many jobs you can do, the only real reward is some loyalty with businesses, and money.What I want for rewards is not money but cosmetics. Like what if each level of loyalty with a business (you know the places that have recognizable theming and mascots) gave you merch? Like lvl 1 loyalty gives the badge that lvl 3 gives, lvl 2 could give you buddy that could replace your bell on you handle bars, and 3 could give you a livery or something (also if the game does have this farther in then I’m sorry but I maxed 4 business and never saw anything like this). This is also assuming that we can’t in the future get items you can put on your character because I know people would love to ride around looking like the goofy mascots that represent each business. Like the world this game takes place in is hilarious and fun to see and be a part of, so let me be a part of it.All in all the game manages to accurately simulate a worker who is forced to do a menial task for little pay who is determined to do it the best, but manages to fall short at trying to get me to clock back in for one more ride.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: The first-week patch has fixed pretty much all of the issues I had with the game. What a blast. I really hope people give this a second chance, because there's very little with this level of flow out there in this genre - it's clear they put a HUGE amount of thought into making a game that occupied a space between Jet Set Radio and Crazy Taxi, and it builds on both in new and interesting ways. Traversal feels great, it's the kind of game you could just play for ages because it's just funamentally FUN.Old Review: The core ideas of this game are absolutely great, and it's a blast to play. That said, it appears this release came in kind of hot as there's a few fairly disruptive bugs in place as of day 1. I'm holding out hope they can get some patches out, because this game deserves to have a long and wonderful life.

_childDocuments_.review: Early impressions, take this less like a full review and more like a guide to know if this game's for you.The gameplay loop goes like this: you explore a decently large area discovering businesses that give you parcels to deliver. You start by doing individual deliveries and eventually unlock a "rush" delivery where you have to pick up and deliver multiple packages in whatever order you want, I think this gameplay loop is great, you familiarize yourself with the map by doing relatively easy tasks and the game lets you tackle a more challenging one whenever you feel ready for it,The moment to moment gameplay is also good, if a tad janky. The environments are full of shortcuts, hazards and terrain to do tricks off of,  Since you'll be going back and forth a lot, you'll naturally get better at using the world around you to keep your speed up. Your bike feels somewhat floaty and traversal overall feels less polished than something like Bomb Rush Cyberfunk (which is a high bar to pass, to be fair), but it's still fun,The game's tone i'm less pleased with. It goes for a hyper corporate, tongue in cheek style of humor which is fine but a lot of the dialogue is overly long because of it. I think most of the tutorial messages and explanations could've played as audio during gameplay but instead they feel the need to pause the game... Kinda kills my momentum.Since i'm not that far into the game, i won't comment on the pricing.
_childDocuments_.name: Parcel Corps

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. But there are so many little frustrations in this game that make me want to stop playing. The biggest offender is the failure state. I’m okay with failing in a traversal game like this. But when you fail you have to sit through the same unskippable cutscene over and over again. There is also no restart button if you have a bad start to the mission. You just have to sit through it again and again. Sure. You can skip some cutscenes. But I do not understand why you can’t skip the last cutscene. And I don’t know why we can’t restart a mission. Another failure problem is the animation for getting on your bike after a crash. It’s funny the first time when you pull a bike out of your backpack. But man is it so slow and frustrating the 100th time. The lack of options for this game is telling that this game might have not had enough time to bake. The performance is poor on the steam deck and while it is not verified, this is a game that should work on the steam deck. Lastly the worlds are too small for the traversal at hand. They are so tall vertically but do not give the player any room to breathe. I would have enjoyed a flatter world that was much bigger than the maps provided. Also this games maps are almost all the same. It would have been nice if it was just one larger map. Then I feel like the vertical space would have been utilized more. I would highly recommend bomb rush cyberfunk over this game. That game knows how to create a world that has room to breathe and the traversal mechanics are much better.
_childDocuments_.name: Parcel Corps

_childDocuments_.review: There are problems. No graphics settings or controller rebinds, a pretty annoying comment section on everything you do in the top right of your screen, very little customization/things to buy, and only 7 real tricks (grind wallride barspin tailwhip wheelie wallplant bounce). I don't know about performance because my monitor is 60 hertz; I literally could not run this game above 60 fps if I wanted to.Despite all this, this game is enormously fun!! I've only unlocked 3/8 areas so far but all of them are huge and distinct. Parklands is an open grassy area next to a college campus, Old Town has older architecture with a huge central cathedral, and the Consumer District is full of restaurants and construction workers. The map design is amazing with fun shortcuts, routes and memorable landmarks. Games normally aren't funny when they're trying to be but the comedy tag is real! I really do hope people still try this game because it fills a very niche deliveryman market I've wanted a game to fill for so long.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't even enjoy the game. There are an unforgivable lack of in-game settings for a game that is asking $35. - I cannot change any display settings other than display resolution, VSync, and motion blur (at least they have those). - I cannot change which display the game runs on so I simply cannot play this game on my TV (which this game is made for). It's locked to what my computer considers my primary display with no ability to change it in-game (and I'm not changing how my computer is fundamentally set up each time I want to play). - I cannot navigate menus without using the controller. Sure, having the game-play only use controller makes a certain degree of sense, but this is a PC game on PC... why can I not change settings and things with my mouse?I very much wanted to love this game and to play it on my TV while sitting on my couch but this game won't let me do that. As for now I will be refunding the game and I will try it again further down the road when there are actual in-game settings that allow for, you know, actual changes. If these complaints are addressed, I will change this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Parcel Corps

_childDocuments_.review: I wish we could leave neutral reviews. I am a huge fan of flow state games and i have to say that this game is one of my favorite games when it comes to gameplay. It is a ton of fun to ride around doing wallrides and grinding around looking for new paths to take as you play. The problem i am having is that there seems to be an issue with the multiplayer for me. I will sit in the multiplayer lobby for 10 plus minutes and never get anyone to join. When i do the quick search it just throws me into a lobby alone. Another problem im having is that it is pretty difficult to find much information on the game so i have not been able to find if this is only happening to me or to others as well. I tend to play games like this alone but this game can get pretty repetitive so i was looking forward to having some fun playing aganist others. I have waited for an update but nothing seems to have changed so far. This is really off putting since the gameplay is fun but gets kinda stale pretty fast. The game likes to have you play some interesting mission types as you unlock different shops to do deliveries for but then wants to focus on this delivery rush mode where you only get to do the basic transport mode during a time crunch. Its still a fun mode but it feels like the addition of these other mission types are wasted since you will probably only play them a few times in order to unlock delivery rush (which you have to play and level up in order to progress.) With all that said i would say that it is still alot of fun and something that i recommend if you like stuff like JSR or crazy taxi but you may want to watch some videos to make sure you will like the missions before you commit.
_childDocuments_.name: Parcel Corps

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely feel kinda scammed.Parcel Corps has plenty enough minor annoyances, but I was hit with a progression bug 3 hours in, right after the refund point, with what looks like no way to get around it outside of either restarting the game and hoping it doesn't happen again, or just waiting until a patch and hoping my specific bug gets covered among the veritable sea of other bugs that are seeming to plague this game.The game itself has plenty of redeeming qualities- The movements and speed you can achieve when really understanding the controls, the smooth nature of the tuck and wallrides, even the simplistic trick system is something I can enjoy, kinda makes nostalgic for the system in Sonic Riders.But the second you try and slow down to adjust a barely missed landing for an objective, you can't just back up and fix it. Accidentally slam into a wall and gotta turn around? Good luck if the quick turn actually feels like working this time. Or if it gets too sensitive and leaves you tailwhipping a good 2-3 extra times to slam into a car and fall down again.Or the fact missions have no way to retry immediately, leaving you to fail and ride all the way back to try anything over.I really wanted to love this game, and as small as the dev team is, I can understand why it released as is. It's a miracle games are released even when backed by billions of dollars and 50x what these people have.But Parcel Corps is very clearly an unfinished game pulled from the oven before it was ready. Doesn't matter how big or small the studio is, if you're going to charge me money for a product I should at least expect it to work as intended

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: This review originally was focused heavily on the performance issues I was experiencing while playing this game. I had mentioned enjoying it, but I was getting FPSs in the 20s, which is rough for an actiony game. After receiving the developer response, I dug into forums to find the force vulkan option (use launch option "-force-vulkan" and doing a bit of riding around for shaders to recompile, these issues have been resolved!! I am now getting 60-75 FPS on my mobile 4060 at 2880x1800 on the same machine just by changing the engine.With the above fix in place, I can highly recommend this game like I was hoping to!! Definitely force Vulkan if you are having issues!!This game is a lot of fun!! I really enjoy the speed boost coming from performing tricks mechanics. It really reminds me a bit of Rollerdrome (a top 10 game for me) in that way. You must do the stylish things in order to succeed at your otherwise unrelated goal. The City itself is a lot of fun to ride around in. There are a lot of areas where the city very clearly was designed for you to follow a few selected paths, but your move set is useful enough to experiment a lot with making some stranger ones. Probably my favorite trick so far was jumping off of a railing over a pond, hitting a small rock in the water, and rocketing off of it to get to the end!! It is a blat to chain the movement together.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the characters and world in this game, reminds me a lot of Jet Set Radio and crazy taxi, but in a modern context with bicycle couriers! Plays smoothly on my PC (nvidia 3080 and AMD Ryzen 9). The NPCs have crazy designs and fun dialogue, the bike controls allow for a variety of different tricks and ways to traverse the world. the level design is well thought out and lets you decide on different routes around the place to deliver your packages. As i progressed the main story-line, the quests give different sorts of challenges with the types of items you deliver which is cool. I look forward to unlocking more of the map as i go.Would be nice to have some extra graphics options, but still an enjoyable game without these. Some text is a little hard to read at times, but neither of these issues take away the fun of this charming game.

_childDocuments_.review: It hurts to post this, especially at a time that studios are laying off tons of people or shutting down entirely, but the game wasn't ready for prime-time. I love the commentary, the art, the satire, the self-awareness. I pushed through the main campaign, hoping to get to a place where I felt confident of giving a positive review, but I never got there.First, there are bugs. They range from the funny (having characters morph into other characters during a run) to the deeply frustrating (having the mini-map freeze or repeatedly dying on respawn). I should have known this was going to be the case when I encountered bugs in the tutorial. But as we all know from Bethesda, bugs alone do not a game tank.But it does from baffling design decisions. The controls are counter-intuitive, inconsistent, and clumsy... and cannot be re-mapped. Before a patch, the player could not skip cut-scenes (this has been addressed... kinda... sometimes) or restart a run (again, addressed after a patch, kinda). Sometimes the spawn locations are at police checkpoints. Schnoz already covered the issues with map layout (missing a trick and not being able to recover). Etc. But the truly troubling series of decisions involve the reason we play these sorts of games (like Bomb Rush): the flow state. It's almost as if the devs were afraid of it, so they erected as many barriers as possible to restrict the fun (cars are more slammy than bouncy, tons of clutter to slow you down, plenty of dead-ends, walls that are a little too high, etc.) The most egregious of these are the hard edges. Walls/corners needlessly have columns/edges/molding that juts out, prohibiting getting too close or wall-riding.A patch won't fix that.And it's a damned shame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game should be welcomingly familiar to any Jet Set Radio or Crazy Taxi alumni.  Tonally it's wearing it's disdain for corporate inauthenticity and dehumanisation on it's sleeve, visually it's low on detail but high on style, and mechanically the movement flows quickly and satisfyingly from jump to grind to sprint.Occasionally there's a bum line-read from a minor character and it's a bit buggier on launch-day than I'd like but thus-far it's all been cosmetic so I can't say I'm particularly put-out by any of it.Also you get bonuses for destroying surveillance cameras so bonus points for blade-running.  Splendid stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost this is an enjoyable game. After looking at the reviews regarding an inability to change display settings and performance issues I was a bit hesitant, but upon playing I have had zero performance issues, not even a little hiccup and I do not have a powerful system by any stretch. The game does not appear to use AI up scaling (DLSS) so comparing to to games that make aggressive use of that from triple and even double A studios is wildly unfair. As far as the lack of graphical customization, the game has the settings that most people actually adjust in lighter games (like this) Motion Blur and VSync. The gameplay loop is as expected, go here, get thing, go there, deliver thing. It brings me back to the days of Crazy Taxi and earlier task driven games like that. The world thus far feels good, it's fun and quirky and wildly on the nose. The story doesn't feel too compelling but it doesn't need to be. Looking at similar games like Crazy Taxi, Skate3, the pro BMX games of old (Dave Mirra, and Mat Hoffman) and even Riders Republic to a degree, none of these games have a truly compelling "story" just a go here do this and have fun and be creative in how you get there. Mechanically the traversal is unique and very sound. The control scheme takes a little getting used to but referring back to similar games, did anyone load up a Skate game and be able to traverse the world and do all the tricks in an hour? Did you get the S license in Crazy Taxi your first time playing it? Like these games, if you give it a second and learn the flow you'll be wall riding to new heights (quite literally) in no time.All in all I genuinely do encourage anyone who enjoyed the previous games mentioned or any task driven/extreme sports oriented game or that just enjoys unique modes of travel in games to give this game a try.Also, please acknowledge that this is an indie dev, not a massive triple A studio. Give it a try, communicate with the devs and they will 100% listen, this is probably the first time I have seen a dev reply to this many reviews on Steam and make a genuine effort to work with people in this way. P.S To the team at Billy Goat, thank you for your work on this game and putting it out. Game Dev isn't easy, 10 fold if you're trying something unique and trying to build the wonderful world that you have. You have brought me plenty of enjoyment with this game and I hope more people find the enjoyment in it that I have.

_childDocuments_.review:
Skid onto the sun kissed streets of New Island, where three bicycle courier corporations are vying to become the biggest, most profitable business in town! Pick a side then lock handlebars forming two-wheeled rivalries in pursuit of market share, influence, and a modest income.

But this honest struggle to make ends meet is swiftly threatened by the arrival of Rich Villainé, CEO of crude oil exploration company Polar Petroleum PLC. Villainé's political ambitions place him on a collision course with New Island's bicycle messengers.

As the details of his maniacal plan become clear, it will be up to you, humble player, to *checks notes* save the world! All while delivering delicious food, valuable parcels, and sensitive documents in 32 minutes or less...
